name: SUMMERHOUSE
detailed_description: SUMMERHOUSE is a small-scale building game and a love letter to the feeling of long lost summer afternoons. Craft a neighbourhood of tiny, beautiful lived-in homes in a variety of settings: the sea, the city, or the mountains. While there are some little secrets to uncover, there are no rules, and you can’t win or lose. Just chill out, build to your heart’s content and soak up the atmosphere. If relaxation and creation are your thing, this is a game for you :) Please keep in mind that this is a small game with no goals or challenges, created by a single person🙂

_childDocuments_.review: SUMMERHOUSE is a quaint and relaxing little game with an enchanting art style.Or rather, it's about 80% of a game.Keeping in mind that it's a one-man project, there are certain glaring things missing from it that I personally would have made sure to add before release.- The ability to simply click to drag an object to move it is just a strange feature not to include, and makes every action twice the amount of work it should be.- The available selection of items to decorate with is simply too small most of the time. Some strange choices were made by the designer of which item varieties there are enough of and which not - there are three parasols, but only one (strangely huge) plastic chair and one plastic table to put under them. There are several advertisement signs but only one lamp, and none of them light up at night. Even just different colour varieties of items to pick from would add loads of artistic freedom.- The UI falls short. There is no scroll bar and scroll sensitivity is low. Items of wildly different sizes show up as the same size in the menu, so you have no idea what you're getting. Items are also highly pixelated in the menu to the point of being unrecognizable at times. Menus will frequently reset to the top half the time, and several times they bugged out completely.- The textures of placeable items frequently clash with each other's meshes. Certain items that are supposed to be stuck to a wall can not be put at the correct depth to actually stick to the wall, either sitting inside or floating in front of it. Side scrolling reveals that the sides of any wall block or roof block are completely untextured.So after that laundry list of problems, do I recommend the game?Yes. It's gorgeous and meditative. It's an impressive effort for one man to have made. Really, my only hope is that the author continues to fix the problems above and add more items/colour options.With these issues adressed the game would be simply excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extremely cute house building game. One thing however, I did find it a little frustrating if I place down an item then wanting to move it, I'd have to delete the item then go back into the item menu and select it from there. Another thing is I wish we could choose the colour of items. Certain items are one colour in menu (take example the graffiti) then it's a different colour once you place it. The tutorial is also a little lacking. It can be confusing sometimes with the popups. I think there should be a quick tutorial to show how to play the game.Overall though, I enjoyed playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Chill.Basic.And super relaxing.A little house/neighborhood builder.No pressure, no time limits, no mobs coming to wreck what you build.Just pixelated creativity.Pick your map, and build your dream house or farm or row of shops.It is basic- don't expect a million choices like massive city builders might have. But see what you can create with what is there, and what new blocks and character you can unlock to use.Well, it can be played with one hand. So there is that.No text or UI scaling.No color-blindness settings, which could be an issue for people with certain forms of color-blindness. You will have to rely on your computer's system settings for color-blindness settings to adjust things.The art may be difficult for some people with low vision to be able to easily tell the difference between different blocks or decorative items- even with pixelization toggled off.There is no voice acting, other than the developer giving a very short "Hi!" at the beginning of the game, right after launching. Nothing that affects game-play. Should be very playable for Deaf or HoH players.Controls are a tad awkward and not intuitive, can be a little confusing at times.**************************************************************************************************All that said, the game is by a solo dev, and is very new.It runs well on my older desktop (i9 9900K/2070 RTX Super/ 16 GB DDR4 RAM/ Windows 10), but I wouldn't count on it running well on an absolute toaster (see the required system specs on the store page).There are some guides being published for the game, some are helpful, some not so much (true for any game on Steam).Very casual and chill creative art experience for killing time and just relaxing. I see a user-defined "city-builder" tag some gamers have applied, but it really isn't that. It is a creativity thing, not a "build and manage a city" thing.Don't expect an AAA studio game experience, expect a cute, casual, chill indie game experience, and enjoy it for what it is. Definitely recommended for folks who just want something creative to relax with after a long day.Full price is worth it, on sale, snag it right away.(Quick edit to fix a few typos and autocorrect fails)

_childDocuments_.review: So, I bought the game the moment it released, and I think I am going to sink a lot of hours into this game. Its a relaxing, creative building simulator. Build your house how you want it and make it however you want!Think townscaper, but just the house. During my playtime I could just feel myself relax to the music and the visuals. Even when I made something that arguably looks bad, It still has its charm in this game.The only real feedback I would have is to have more blocks to make your house even better. Or give tools to the community so they can create more models on the workshop to be used in the game.All in all, I can recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxing and simple straight-to-the-point sandbox game about just laying back and enjoying that warm, digital breeze while building some houses.I can't help but love it.It's not the type of game to keep you engaged for the "long run", instead more like a "fun run".Sincerely, Summerhouse is best enjoyed in small, few, compact sessions with a hot cup of coffee on a hot summer evening.Strong recommendation!

_childDocuments_.review: Easy, fun, relaxing, heartwarming. You can tell someone put their whole heart and soul into this game from the second you open it up. This might be my favorite little building game ever, and it JUST came out!! Absolutely incredible. I highly recommend this game. If you're even slightly skeptical about a new release, don't be. Try it. Do it. You'll be so happy you did. Believe me. Besides the heartwarming description, the designs of the pieces and depth of the blocks are AMAZING. 3d pixel environment blew my mind. Its absolutely gorgeous. I am personally begging you to play this game and just relax for a little while, breathe and smell the roses and remind yourself that its okay to zone out and build a summer house.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice and entertaining little building toy, but there aren't many pieces to play with or backgrounds to build against which limits your creative options. You unlock a few bits but it needs quite a few more imo, lots more building types, roof types, etc. You can build a lot of different buildings but they all look kinda the same few types. Also, they're confusingly ordered and if you turn off pixellation fx on the main screen, the catalogue images are still pixellated. so it becomes a bit of a guessing game what size thing you're going to get or what it will say on a sign. I can't imagine anyone can tell the difference between the 6 wooden building blocks without using trial and error to learn the order -- they're just different brown smudges in the build screen. It's charming and I liked it but it's pretty limited, feels like it's a cool digital Fuzzy Felt, but with only half the pieces. More pieces and backgrounds and it will be better for it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Beautiful aesthetic and great concept but the user interface (UI) needs a bit more work.I played with a mouse and keyboard - not sure if it is better on a controller.I found the UI a little frustrating - from the fact that you can only build in a line or straight up (even though blocks seem to be 3D) to the really counter-intuitive and laborious way of finding the blocks you need (you have to scroll through the whole list each time and it doesn't remember where you last were - so you can't easily get the next block in the series). This game could be absolutely wonderful with just a little more work and testing. I'm also confused why some blocks like doorways seem to be only place-able slightly in front of other assets, but not in them - e.g. grated doors that show the background through the gaps until you put a wall behind it- where then it just shows bricks instead of being a doorway in the wall; or graffiti only being visible on some parts of a rock formation but not on others.I can see how this could be relaxing and I found the new blocks popping up delightful (if again feeling a bit random on what pops up and what doesn't). However, for me the UI issues were a bit of a deal-breaker as they caused stress and frustration.I do hope the creator keeps working on it and fixing some of the bugs at least - I look forward to seeing how this evolves (if it does)The way it is now though, I don't think I can recommend it. I hope that changes!

_childDocuments_.review: SUMMERHOUSE is an Incredibly calm and relaxing game. It's open-ended design allows for a lot of creativity. Although there are a couple limitations in the game, they end up furthering the player's creativity by forcing the player to think outside the box and come up with new strategies for building their summer house. The game has beautiful graphics and a pretty nice option to change them if you aren't particularly fond of the pixelized style.Although the game could benefit from some improvements to the UI, better explained controls, and having other controls explained at all. The ability to disable the UI by pressing 'H' now has a pop-up, which alleviates some of my problems with the UI, but there are still improvements to be made.Overall, this game is a nice, relaxing experience that I am sure I'll return to at later dates to get a fix of that cozy juice. The first update gives me hope that we will see the issues I brought up addressed fully with time, but nevertheless this game is an immediate recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: is a creative pixel game where you build small-scaled lived-in buildings without restrictions or limits to your creativity. As an artist, first and foremost games in this genre tickle my fancy. In  you craft small-sale lived-in houses, cafe’s or stores without restrictions or limits. Choose from four main environments; a lake, the city, the desert or a grassy scene. The game also has some secrets to uncover as you play and pair certain items together. If you're stuck on getting certain achievements or unlocking secret items browse the community guides, there are some very helpful ones to guide you! You can build whatever you can imagine in this game. Place objects anywhere you wish and change the depth of them to make them come forward (like 3D) or recede so parts are behind others. You can change the weather to suit the mood you're in, whether it is a moon-lit night, a sunny afternoon or a rainy day. Plant trees, grass, flowers and place rocks. There is some wildlife and insects such as butterflies, birds, a cat and even a ghost. There are lots of save slots (20) so you can do lots of different creative designs and not feel like you're running out of room. I do hope they put out some dlc in the future or add mod support for more content to allow us to build even more things or have more variety. Content such as animal packs or more lighting options. But what is included is a good selection to start with. My first design…but check out the Steam community or subreddit on Reddit for some truly epic builds. This game is truly relaxing and enjoyable to play. No restrictions, pure creativity and beauty. A wholesome game for everyone to enjoy at a great price with very high re-playability. 🎨

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and soothing, tiny city builder; a very enjoyable game that lets you build anything you want in a variety of environments.Combining different objects might unlock a new variation of one of the objects used. You can change the weather or time to see your creations in a different light. While there are no limits to what you can build, you still might run out of ideas as there aren't that many things to build with, so hopefully more will be added in the future. It would also be nice to see some different environments to build in or more weather options.Overall, I consider this a perfect game to unwind and be creative with when you just want a break from stress, so I definitely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a game I was so excited to try when I first saw it previewed.  I think this is more of a creative exercise than a game, in that there are no goals - simply a blank canvas and building blocks to play with to create a cute scene.  It's so very intuitive and I think ANYONE could get in this and make a really nice looking scene easily, that's how well done this is.I've spent an hour and a half just playing around, with no real goal - just placing blocks and seeing what the end result was.  I even built one scene entirely by hitting the "random" button and placing whatever piece it gave me.  The end result was always pleasing to look at and fun to put together.  It was also really fun to discover new "character" blocks by placing certainly blocks together.  The art is gorgeous, colorful and a joy to look at.  I think if you are someone who enjoys being creative OR you're someone who likes to have something to mess around with while you do other things (talk on the phone, listen to something, etc) this is going to be a hit with you.  It doesn't have to be a time sink if you're looking for something short to do, or if you want to spend literal hours with this, you absolutely could.I encountered no bugs, no issues and the game is solidly well made.  My only wish is that it will get an update or DLC with new environments and building blocks.

If you seem to find this game boring, perhaps you lack imagination... A great way to spend time unwinding for the sake of a couple quid!

_childDocuments_.review: Personally I think the game has a good premise and I really love the game, but it comes with a major flaw that I can't seem to work around. I think that if they had just added a feature like controlable length and height to roofs and walls, and maybe ability to change texture and colour, it would be amazing for the game. So at the moment I wouldn't recommend this game to people, but if it did get an update with new stuff and more variation I could definitely recommend it to someone.

_childDocuments_.review: More of a sandbox builder than a traditional "game", SUMMERHOUSE is perfect for winding down & relaxing. Other than the achievements for unlocking specific building elements, there is no objective to the game - you simply build to your hearts content. While I would like more variety in items to build with & perhaps environments, at the price point of $5 USD I feel like this game offers plenty.My only complaint with the game is the difficulty navigating the menus to find the exact items I want to use. I am not sure how to make it more efficient but I often found myself looking in the incorrect category for specific items.For anyone who needs some downtime & a game where they can chill without stress, I would absolutely recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because it was on sale and recommended to me based on other games I like (Dorfromantik and Stardew were the lead ins). I sincerely hope this game gets things added to it like more backgrounds and assets, more unlockable pieces, because I LOVE IT. I opened this game expecting nothing and spent 6 hours when I should have been sleeping just building to my little maximalist heart's content. What a fantastic cozy game, I would happily pay for additional content. I've truly been enjoying what I've seen so far. I would love to see this game take some chances on backgrounds and more fantasy and modern fantasy inspired pieces, or the ability to recolour assets/use asset colours from different maps. But, that being said, very greedily, this game is lovely and so chill. The unlockable pieces with people and animals are charming and they add such depth to a 2D game. The gentle breeze helps the game feel immersive and cozy. I will be playing this over and over for a very long time. Fantastic concept, wonderful execution, thank you for Summerhouse, I love it. I definitely hope to see more for this game in the future but if you're on the fence, get off and come play Summerhouse!

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a cute game that is littered with problems. I REALLY wanted to enjoy it but the game makes it so hard.Why do NONE of the pieces line up? You basically need to make the houses like the ones in the promotional images or cover up every single join with other bits and pieces. Did you think there would be a stone walled roof that matches the brick pattern you used for the walls? Because there isn't. Did you think the smaller wooden walls would match the pattern of the bigger walls you used for the base? Because they don't. There are also only a handful of pieces you can use to build. It's so limiting to have a single wooden roof, and that wooden roof doesn't match the wooden walls. It needs to be completely covered in signs and other bits to make it look at all neat. WHYYYYY does scrolling take SO long? It would have been simple to just make it faster but it's painful trying to scroll down the menus to do anything. Especially if you want to swap back and forth between things further down the menus. The trailer also seems a little disingenuous, although probably not intentionally. "You can build houses in a variety of levels, such as the sea, the mountains, the city, or the desert." Yeah you listed the only 4 locations. It really makes it sound like there are more than those 4. I hope this doesn't discourage the dev from making more games, It seems like they really liked this game. But it feels more like they built a game for themselves.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly not sure how I've already spent seven hours in this game. I feel like I blinked and suddenly I had 5 adorable little meticulously decorated villages full of little people, each with their own little back story that I made up in my little brain. I am thoroughly enjoying Summerhouse and it is honestly the most relaxing game I've ever played. I would love it if the developer continued to release updates in the future. It might be nice to see more characters to unlock or new building block types or even the ability to re-color some items. It would also be great for my little aesthetic brain if the grass didn't clip through objects that are built on top of it. And honestly, with a game this affordable and engrossing, I *might* be willing to buy DLC if the developer released it. Now excuse me, I have to return to the game. There is a cat sitting on top of an air conditioner that I need to figure out how to unlock.
_childDocuments_.name: SUMMERHOUSE

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:- Low cost.- Nice art style.- Unlocking the new objects was quite fun.Negatives:- Controls are really bad - to find something to place you can either right-click a dozen times to get to it (and you will probably overclick and need to go round again).- UI is really hard to use - the objects are stored in thrown together menus that scrolls painfully slow.- No further customisation tools like the ability to recolour.- No convenience tools that would be expected, like the ability to move something that has been placed.- Unlocking new objects has bugs that meant I had to spam objects to trigger them to be unlocked.It lacks a lot of content, which isn't terrible for a low cost game, but it isn't relaxing to play because the controls are horrendous. _childDocuments_.review: Probably a skill issue, but I just couldn't make anything that looked even remotely good. There should be fine controls over everything you place, re-coloration options, moving something after it's been placed, scaling objects, rotating the camera, and so on. I would cut it some slack if these were complicated features, but they really aren't. It hasn't been out for that long, so maybe these things will get added, but I'm not holding my breath. I should also mention one bug that, while techincally minor, is incredibly annoying, namely opening up the object picker and nothing being there. _childDocuments_.review: When I was little, I'd play the original SIMS game with my big sister. I was always terrible at keeping families alive, but even at a young age, I was pretty good at designing houses. We would demolish the preexisting house, enter the //rosebud cheat, and I'd have free range of constructing a new place. Then, she'd control the family and I'd watch. One summer in college, I took the world's most boring computer class, and I'd spend most of class designing random things in Google Sketchup (not part of the assignments, but I'm a kinesthetic learner and the class was SO. DULL.). My dad was an architect, and I guess I inherited some of his aesthetic know-how.For some people, a nostalgic game might be an arcade style beat-em-up, a remake of a classic, or something modern with an intentionally low-polygon count. For me, it's a game like Summerhouse. Although you're only constructing things on an XY-axis plane, the simplicity of the options make it my ideal cozy game. I've only pulled it up 3 times so far, but it's such a relaxing experience that it's become my go-to stress reliever. Anything more complex in nature would be too intention-heavy for me, but this is more like building something out of Legos with pre-2000 choices of blocks (something I've also used to keep my hands busy when I'm getting a bit too fidgety). I highly recommend Summerhouse.
_childDocuments_.name: SUMMERHOUSE

_childDocuments_.review: SUMMERHOUSE is a simple game that allows you to be creative and get lost in a different, peaceful world for a bit. Even though (as of now) the elements are limited, the possiblities to create something fun and cute feel endless. As mentioned before, the elements are limited but you can move them around freely. The dev already added some new elements the players were asking for to the game and there's even more to come. It's a bit difficult to like up things perfectly every now and then but I see it as a challenge to make it work. The game comes with achievements and lets you unlock fun details by using certain element which only adds to the cosy vibes of the game. With each block you place down, the town comes alive more and more. The playback function is great to watch back your building process and is also a cute feature to maybe even record some kind of speed build in the future. I received a free key for the game but I'll definitely gift the game to some of my friends. For the price of 5€ this game really is a steal and I can see myself spend many more hours on building and decorating tiny houses. So if you feel like supporting an indie dev - this is your sign.

_childDocuments_.review: Only a week into release and this game is already fantastic! _childDocuments_.name: SUMMERHOUSE

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very cozy and has a great atmosphere in general. I enjoyed building a few cute houses in all of the different biomes and testing out the different architecture you could create with the pieces. It feels like a pretty unique game style wise which I think was pretty cool.Overall this game is a good, cheap cozy game. However, I found it to be a bit buggy. I ran into several bugs:- Background layer shows on foreground- Main tile menu is off center constantly, sometimes requiring a full restart of the game to reset- Blocks randomly have a hitbox and prevent placement on top of one anotherGenerally, I got bored of the game very quickly. I didn't feel like there was enough to do in the game, even though I love sims and cozy games with very little to do. Mostly because it seems very infrequent that you get a new tile to use, so you're stuck for the first several hours with the same small number of tiles to place. Additionally, there's very little depth of field in the game so you cannot make that large of a house, especially upwards, most houses can't be more than 3 stories tall. Like some reviewers stated, it feels more like a thought experiment/design project than an actual game given how limited the gameplay and options are. Additionally, I found the controls to be extremely frustrating and I had to research what they were in the first place, this should've been in the settings menu. I received this product for free with a review code, so I can't complain too much, but I don't know if I could recommend buying this game when there are so many other cozy, chill games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a sidescroller house building game focusing on street-view. It's very relaxing with the sound effects and calming music tracks; very great to escape from a stressful day.The UI and controls are confusing at first, but I got used to them pretty quickly - you don't get an introduction for controls at all; figured them out by myself. A few community members shared more detailed controls :)Next to a bunch of different blocks to choose from, you can change the day/weather: sunny, rainy and night. Sadly you cannot scale stones or stone patters :(After unlocking all hidden figures, which you get by placing certain blocks close to one another, there isn't much to do but building houses - the concept behind Summerhouse - obviously.=> short note for Mac gamers like me: The game itself runs without any lag at all! But the device heats up and the fans get very noisy.
_childDocuments_.name: SUMMERHOUSE

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really nice. Utterly relaxing and satisfying. _childDocuments_.review: First I just want to say I received this game as a gift from a friend who thought I'd really enjoy it. I love the graphics. It's definitely a very very chill vibe, but I think it needs something more. I don't personally like that once I finish building a scene/house/etc and I want to make another one, I lose all previous work. I wish there was a gallery or save feature where you could keep all your previous work in one place to look back on, or even return to if you wanted to update it. The game feels a bit redundant right now. I may not be creative enough when it comes to a game like this, but it feels like it needs more options and variety added (maybe this will come with future updates and I'm jumping the gun, we shall see.) Overall, if you love games that allow you to have a creative outlet for creating houses (i.e. the Sims franchise), then this game probably would make you pretty happy to get.It is not a bad game whatsoever, but it missed the mark for me (at least at this time.) I wanted so badly to like it more than I did, but as I've said above, maybe that will change with future potential updates.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little scene builder. Absolutely delightful in execution - the graphics are bright and cheery (and I found I actually preferred to play with the pixel filter off because it looks really nice without it too), the environments you can build in are beautiful,  and there's extra building objects to unlock. It's really nice, especially on a cosy afternoon where you don't want to think too hard and just want to relax.
_childDocuments_.name: SUMMERHOUSE

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game; it's chill, cozy, and creative! It has the feelings of a My Summer Vacation game, or a dreamy little town like out of a Studio Ghibli movie. It is relaxing and fun with a calm ambiance. The stylized pixel graphics and lighting are beautiful. My only qualms, which are QoL suggestions that I hope the dev fixes in an update, is that not every item shows up in the search feature, nor do colors match when placing the item (i.e. the door is red in the menu when you select it, but it's actually green when you place it), there is no option to change the color of an item, the search isn't organized logically or labeled (i.e. window items are not placed together; roofs are not all together), it takes forever to scroll through the search menu (it's like dial-up internet download speed slow), some of the items are essentially indiscernible—I truly can't tell what some things are supposed to be (label the category of what the item is, please), and there are no hints for combinations to unlock new blocks.
_childDocuments_.name: SUMMERHOUSE

_childDocuments_.review: Like the addvertisement says, it's minimalistic. No tutorial, no goals, no achievements (other than some little unlocks), just chill music, relaxing vibes and some fun pieces to build houses with. There is a lot of variety you can get from what is available, although the wooden house options are somewhat limited.For the price this is a steal if you ask me. Maybe the most memorable game i've played in two years.
_childDocuments_.name: SUMMERHOUSE

_childDocuments_.review: I am clean, distilled and pure this game washed away the bad of many hours on such games as fortnite, valorant and siege. (ok maybe I'm exaggerating as that statement is probably taking it far) I feel whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't afford therapy? Just buy this game instead.Surprisingly fun for how simple it is. Fun fact: you don't HAVE to start your house on the ground. Build the castle in the sky you deserve.You can turn off pixelation in the settings and the art becomes even prettier.Experimenting with different blocks will unlock you characters. Not sure what i did but there's a chicken sitting on my trash can now. Metal.You can adjust the speed of your build replay in the settings. if you make video essays or lo fi music you can save footage of your builds and use it as B-roll for your videos.As far as I can tell the below features aren't in the game yet. I'm still on my first hour so i could be wrong. If I'm right, I think adding these features would put this game in a league of its own:-Please add ability to select blocks with arrow keys so i don't have to use the mouse. For me personally it's distracting to have to move my cursor to select a new category then again to select a block, then again back to where I want to place the block. If I could use the up/down arrows to choose a block category, and then the left/right arrows to quickly cycle through the blocks in that category, I could choose from any of the blocks available without having to move my cursor which for me is a huge increase in work flow.-Please add text generator for the signs (maybe the chicken showed up because my sign says "Hotel")-Please add custom colors and resizing of blocks (blocks can be pushed closer or further away with "Q" and "E" but not actually made smaller or larger.)-This is all as far as I know, correct me if I'm wrong about any of it.Incredible game for 5 bucks. Hoping to see different architectural styles as updates/DLC content.

Definitely has potential to grow bigger by increasing item catalogue, backgrounds and maybe being able to resize or recolor items (even if they do slightly change based on the area you are building in already). _childDocuments_.name: SUMMERHOUSE

_childDocuments_.review: Such a cozy game! Really beautifully made and so relaxing to play. My only comment is that there's a "limit" to how much you can advance/push back items in certain spaces which can make it a little annoying to place things right where you want them since the game works in a single perspective. (I know that these items can go back more sometimes but it would keep snapping to the front for example).  I hope that eventually the push/advance tool can just do it for the whole depth of the area instead of "set" areas, and/or a tool to manually move items left to right would help a lot (maybe arrow keys?) so that you're not struggling to line up your mouse to get juuust the right spot. Alternatively, you can utilize the randomizer to acquire a random piece to use in the construction of your house, but that didn't seem as enjoyable to me. _childDocuments_.review: It's hard for me to look at something that costs $5 and consider it obscenely overpriced, but this does it. I got this on sale and it still wasn't worth it. I don't know if you can technically even call this a video game. If you somehow don't have wallpaper engine, get that instead, it's cheaper, provides more utility, and you will have an infinitely better time.The only reason this game is successful is due to the marketing and graphics. Which by the way, the graphics aren't even that good, the warm lighting and pixel filter absolutely carry and makes it look significantly better than it actually is. (Which usually wouldn't be a complaint from me, but the only thing you're paying for realistically when you buy this game is the ability to look at the graphics.)One of many examples of how you can just genuinely make a bad game, but as long as it fits into a certain genre or "aesthetic," and you market it correctly, people who don't know any better will buy it with a smile on their face. They will then proceed to basically rationalize to themselves about how it was redeeming in any possible way because the marketing was so effective it practically brainwashed them. Just look at the playtime of all these positive reviews, a majority of them have less than 5 hours, and multiple have less than 60 mins.

_childDocuments_.review: While I commend the developer's effort in creating a game centered around relaxation, my overall opinion remains negative (I really would like to click button neutral). The concept itself is commendable, particularly considering it was crafted by a sole individual. However, my initial excitement waned quickly after just 20 minutes of gameplay. The experience proved more frustrating than relaxing due to several issues. The arrangement of objects lacked intuitiveness, and the absence of options for seamless object connections detracted from the experience. Additionally, the transparency of objects like doors and windows hinted at a lack of polish, particularly noticeable in a game where aesthetics play a significant role. Despite acknowledging that some aspects may be subjective, the misalignment of windows and doors felt particularly jarring. I found myself longing for a control panel to clarify functionalities such as object rotation, which further added to the frustration. Simple tasks like setting up a fence proved needlessly cumbersome, as objects behaved unpredictably. Furthermore, the limited selection of maps with challenging terrains added to the disappointment. Despite these drawbacks, I must acknowledge the fair pricing of the game. However, it's possible my expectations were inflated by enticing screenshots and the creator's promising announcements. In summary, while the game's concept and visuals are appealing, its overall execution leaves much to be desired, appearing rather sloppy.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely idea, the sort of thing that is right up my alley. I love building games, but I don't like this one. And that's a shame, because it's obvious a lot of love went into it. But it's just too simple to hold my attention and warrant me spending much time with it. All building is done on a single plane, meaning you can't rotate left/right. Also, there's a very limited amount of building blocks you can use, and you have to access them by either right clicking endlessly to scroll through each item, or slowly scroll down a dialog menu. It's just a chore to pick items, and when you do, their utility is very limited.I just got done playing Enshrouded for over 100 hours. That game has a similar aesthetic, they're both beautiful games, but Enshrouded's voxel system does everything this game does but better. One of the most frustrating things about this game is that the building blocks don't have any reaction to the blocks around it, meaning you can't play around with merging them together.To put it simply, the game is far too simple. Perhaps you'd enjoy it if you don't have more advanced building games to play, but if you do and you have experience with them, you'll likely find this boring.

_childDocuments_.review: This is hot garbage.The interface is genuinely terrible.Different wall pieces cannot be flush with one another when brought all the way forward. Wall pieces do not tile, so say you want a two-wide stone block wall ... there's not spacing between them, no 'mortar', and so it looks exactly like you've placed two wall pieces side-by-side - not like a wide wall.Some objects can be placed further forward by placing 'in front' of other objects. Most cannot. Why this is true is utterly opaque.The screenshots and video suggest the objects are 3D. Which they are - with textures on only one side. So when you move the camera left or right, you can see that your stone block house is just a movie prop.There is no fine control. You're just hoping for the best.There are no real camera controls. You cannot change the angle of the camera at all. It feels like you're in a neck brace. Left, Right, Up, Down. That's it. Probably because these are not 3D pieces for art purposes. If you could move the camera, it would be even more glaring how poor the art is. This is all very strange because ... why not just make it 2D? We're wasting electricity by using the 3D engine and getting no benefit.There are no physics. Consequently, nothing 'settles'. Objects won't look as if they are in a 'real' space. You must hide all of the problems behind other pieces. The people and animals do nothing. They don't come and go. They don't interact with the environment. They are just props like everything else and exactly as flat.Quite damning that the videos are edited in such a way to suggest the camera is more useful than it is. Pushing in, pulling out, panning ... except that the videos carefully do all of this so that you aren't constantly seeing the completely blank sides of the objects.If this were free, it would be interesting. As it is, especially with the camera movement in the videos, this is a bait and switch. "A tiny building game about beautiful lived-in houses. No rules or restrictions, just pure creativity." The only true word in that tag is 'tiny'.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: - Very cute & relaxing cozy game- You can turn pixelation on & off - The lived-in vibe is nice. I build a lot in the Sims & this feels like a less frustrating version of that- Unlockable blocks to add some life to your builds- Lots of save slots for your favorite builds- It's kind of mindless (in a good way). It's a fun way to just turn off your brain after a long day but still be creative without using too much brainpower- Chill musicCons:- Can't change colors or sizes of blocks- Flipping signs will cause them to be backwards- Sometimes it's hard to place something exactly where you want- Would love a bit more variety on blocks, but I am content considering the price- A scroll bar would be awesome. It takes a minute to scroll all the way up or down- Some weird bugs where I can't see the gallery of the block I'm using without opening another gallery first (for example, if I'm building walls but want to change the type, sometimes the gallery will be blank when I open it. I'll open the roofs, exit out, open the walls again, & it'll work).Final thoughts: - I got this game on sale for under $4. Even the full price seems like a good deal. _childDocuments_.review: A highly relaxing casual game, perfect for keeping you occupied while listening to a podcast, or simply to de-clutter your brain. This is not a particularly good house-builder, nor a powerful sandbox game, but it is more like a sort of creative therapy – you can put more-or-less most blocks/items right next to each other and it always seems to work aesthetically, making this game an altogether whimsical experience. There are some clear points for improvement: certain items don't seem to align properly with each other (perhaps snapping could solve this), the 'flipped' signs also flip the text, and it would be nice to see a few more blocks added in. Your limits are quite literally nonexistent and you can structure homes/stores/churches, whatever, like that. Its a great casual game and real cheap too, so whats stopping you from buying. My only nitpicks are no rotation button, I find that the walls you are given to be a bit bare, and rotating could help spruce up walls made from several and offer more exploration/variety. _childDocuments_.review: After around 10 hours in the demo and another 7 after release, I've fallen in love with . It's an adorable and extremely cozy game to spend a few minutes or a few hours with here and there, and one which I would highly recommend if you have any interest in creative building games.Summerhouse's immaculate vibes begin right from the main menu screen, where the creator gently welcomes you to the game's bright visuals and relaxing soundtrack. The soundtrack and sound design are subtle, but make up the heart of the game's quiet atmosphere and provide pleasant feedback as you slowly build. There aren't a ton of pieces the game gives you to build with, but I think this is actually a strength. The quote "the enemy of art is the absence of limitations" is often attributed to Orson Welles, and it applies to the art people build in videogames as well. The best building games are those that force you to build interesting structures by imposing some kind of limitation, like for example Valheim's structural integrity mechanics. I think the limited tile library that summerhouse has achieves a similar effect,This limitation helps the game maintain a consistent style regardless of who is playing, but still allows for a lot of creative freedom. Everything you make matches looks great together because of the limited themes and colour palette, which also differ slightly between regions, giving each one a different feel. There is no system preventing tiles from overlapping, so you can really go wild with possible combinations of different objects. All in all, excellent game and excellent experience. This little indie project has the best building of any new game I've played in the last few years, so give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: is very neat and vibrant, generally fitting the calming vibe this game has, while also giving the player the choice to switch between a pixelated and shape-oriented kind of version. is really greatly executed, giving you some restrictions, but just enough in which you can move comfortably around, without having to much leeway, resulting in something that makes you think about how you create and doesn't get boring as quickly as it would otherwise.There are still some points in which not enough leeway is given for my liking, but otherwise it's a great middleground so far. on the other hand are a bit iffy.The game is fairly new, so the amount of stuff that can be unlocked is excuseable, the way in which you unlock new building blocks is quite restricting and hard to find out on your own without any guidance.Especially for artistic oriented players or people who use things in only one constellation, some things just can't be unlocked, so far the  being the worst offender for that problem. it's also executed quite well, the replay button being a great addition, but there are definitely still features missing and/or desired for.I'd love to see a more complex replay system than the one already in place, more options and variety, as well as, and most importantly; objects which can be rotated or that have a side-view, enabling bridges, other entrances to a garden and other uses.Generally a really calming game though with a ton of potential, can't wait to see what's to come if the developer is building upon this!

_childDocuments_.review: A small game with a lot of creativity is the best way to describe it. You start with just making a small house as you're just kinds thrown in and left with only your imagination and some basic instructions on how to use the program. You soon realize you can do more then just a simple house. I ended up making an entire city block of buildings on the outskirts of the city map. The story in my head was the area was the final stop on the bus line, a tiny forgotten part of town but each square foot was bursting with people with little clues on who they are. The final building at the far end past the end of the street was a series of ruins due to a fire burning it down years ago with the sign of it being a store long ago. The building next to the ruin is an apartment building that is slightly off as it was damaged with one window covered in green vines and window planters as the landlord loves plants. Below is a corner store and bus stop sign with a notice on the community board from the city detailing how the bus stop would be decommissioned due to low service to that location and budget cuts (not an actual feature but if I could actually write flyers and make them zoom-in capable I would do that). The windows at night are alight with neighbors and people hanging inside, outside on rooftops and terraces, watching the city in the distance.If you're a fan of these kinds of games that don't hold your hand and just tell you to make something, I think you'll really enjoy Summerhouse. Its a slept on cozy game at the moment that needs more attention.

_childDocuments_.review: "SUMMERHOUSE" is like a cozy hug for your gaming soul, perfect for those moments when you just want to relax and let your creativity flow.It's all about simplicity, which is a breath of fresh air in the gaming world. Whether you're dreaming of a quaint cottage or a bustling little town, this game lets you bring your vision to life without any pressure.Unlocking new building blocks feels like discovering hidden treasures, adding a sprinkle of excitement to your creative journey. And even though the initial options might seem limited, trust me, you can still whip up some seriously charming designs that'll make you smile.Visually, "SUMMERHOUSE" is a treat. _childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful little game!  It's more of a toy, or, more appropriately, a tool for the imagination.  Unlike a city builder or a town builder, this is an open canvas to let you express your dreams and hopes in the form of a little community or cluster of homes and shops.  This is as simple as games get, yet it has the very core of wonder and wanting to know what comes next that you get with a much bigger and more complex game.  I truly hope games like this continue to rise and take-off because we need more games like this.  I'm going to be playing this a lot.Pros:  The game truly does feel like when you were a kid, playing with construction toys like Legos or Lincoln Logs.  This is pure creativity with little blocks and windows and decorations, without boundaries, which, at least for me, is very stress-relieving.Cons: For such a simple game, complaints feel a little petty, as there aren't really many "bugs", other than a bit of a lack of variety in construction options and, at some point, you yearn for more interactive characters, but for what this game is, I'm not sure if that's a fair "con", rather just a thought about the future.  Sometimes the trees and environment clips into your structures in a very unsatisfying way.  There is a slight sense of wanting MORE progression while playing, other than little touches like having a character move in or unlocking new items.  But for the price, these are nit-picks.TL;DR: A very simple "game" without many rules, in the spirit of the construction-style toys you played with as a child, where you build a house, or several houses, or a building, or a cafe, and so on.  It's a bit overly-simple at times, but there's not much to dislike.  Great game for relieving stress or just letting your mind drift away!

_childDocuments_.review: A nice relaxing game if you're like me and love the aesthetic of cluttered streetside shops and alleys. Once you've played 20 minutes, you've seen all there is gameplay-wise, but that really only matters if you're constantly looking for new things to stimulate you. I think the biggest improvements that could be made on this are:The UI could definitely use some improvements, as clicking between available items is a drag. Maybe if you held right click it would pop up with a list of the things of that category you could scroll through with the mouse wheel? The search function could also use a bit of a speeding up.This is an easy request to make as there are only 4 stages and I'd love to build in more environments. Hopefully you can add more in the future as it would spice things up more.There's a solid foundation for the controls, but the z-axis messes with it more than necessary. Some objects don't seem to go as far back as others, leading to frustration when a background element will only stay up front. You can move stuff forward and back using Q and E, but it seems like it locks itself to certain areas which causes issues when you can't place things exactly how you'd like. Honestly this is my biggest gripe so far. So Friedemann already mentioned in another review how he ran out of time before being able to add more roofs, so knowing that may make some of the other gaps in connecting styles make more sense. Having more pieces thematically fit with each other would be very cool, as there's already a good amount there. Another thing that's more of a personal dislike is that a lot of the pieces don't fit with each other in terms of z-axis width, and since you're looking head on its mostly fine but if you want something to have a bit more depth it can get very annoying. One more thing here, it would be cool if combining brick walls or other walls with a pattern didn't just overlap them onto each other, but generated a fitting brick pattern where it connects.Overall the game is really nice and I hope you keep expanding on it and adding more stuff. For $5 it's a good time!

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine who will live in that place, the shape of the building, what their day-to-day life will be like? Maybe you are too late and there are only a few ruins left of what once was. All the answers are in your hand.Cozy game about imagining and customizing buildings to our liking, with a more than decent variety of elements and a total of 4 biomes in which to build our scene. At any time we can alternate between day and night, as well as a rainy day. Adapting the environment to our taste according to the atmosphere we want to recreate.The pixelated aesthetics, like Cloud Gardens (noio_games), suits it wonderfully. But if by any chance you prefer to disable it, you can do it at any time from the settings menu.There are times when we need to disconnect from so much open world (icons, missions...) and so much action, and this is certainly one of the best experiences available for that. The music alone is highly relaxing 👌Oh, and I almost forgot, although it's a "do what you want, at the pace you want" experience, there's a progress system that consists of unlocking "blocks" with people and animals to give more life to our scenes. Although I have to say, it's somewhat random.

name: Yars Rising
detailed_description: RUN, JUMP, SNEAK, AND HACK YOUR WAY TO THE HEART OF THE MYSTERY From the renowned development studio WayForward Technologies, Inc. (Shantae, River City Girls, Advance Wars 1+2: Re-Boot Camp) comes Yars Rising, a 2D action adventure exploration of one of Atari’s richest, and best known classic titles. In WayForward’s experienced hands, the Yars franchise becomes an expansive mystery solved through 2D platforming action. Take control of the young hacker Emi Kimura, who is hired by a mysterious patron to infiltrate the shadowy QoTech corporation. Run, jump, sneak, and hack your way through challenges as you slowly unravel a complex secret shrouded in intrigue. Emi grows in power throughout her adventure, allowing her to retrace her steps and reach previously inaccessible and secret areas. Her evolving hacking skills are critical to solving stimulating minigames that reference the innovative gameplay from the Atari 2600 title Yars’ Revenge. The deeper into the QoTech facilities Emi ventures, the more expansive the sci-fi mystery becomes. A colorful cast of hacker allies help Emi discover her connection to a distant alien race and unlock powers unlike anything she could have imagined. Yars Rising celebrates the Yars franchise in WayForward’s distinct style of anime art, humor, retro game mechanics and storytelling virtuosity. Features: 2D Platforming Action: Emi must jump, blast and sneak her way past waves of robotic and alien enemies. Her latent powers are revealed as the game progresses, granting her wild augments and biohacks that let her reach previously inaccessible areas. A sprawling, interconnected map allows for hours of exploration Sci-Fi Intrigue: A seemingly bottomless mystery takes Emi from drab office buildings into hidden underground labs, and even to the farthest reaches of space as she uncovers the dark truth behind the QoTech corporation and discovers her own personal connection to an alien race. Challenging Retro Minigames: A series of hacking minigames pay homage to the original Yars’ Revenge, which fans love for its top-down, quick twitch gameplay. Stealth Traversal: Emi can’t always shoot or jump her way out of a jam – tense sections of stealth gameplay force her to duck into the shadows to hide from relentless security guards. Classic WayForward Aesthetics: With fantastically rendered 3D environments and an ensemble of captivating characters, the WayForward team brings Emi’s story to life as only they can. Play the OG: Discover the first game in the Yars franchise by playing WayForward’s modern take on the Yars’ Revenge, accessible right from the main menu.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played most of the metroidvanias on Steam as its my favorite genre of game, but this one is a painful not recommend for me.  The game has a pretty high level or production value.  The visuals and graphics are vibrant and well done, the music is pretty great, and there is tons of voice acting.  The problems start to show once you start getting into the meat of the game, or lack thereof.I'm very surprising reading a lot of the positive reviews for this game after spending 2.5 hours playing this, I've decided to just stop for a variety of reasons.  For starters, there is a ton of loading screens in this game when traversing between rooms.  I don't think I've ever seen anything quite this disruptive to game flow from any metroidvania I have played.  It seems to push a 5 sec loading screen between room transitions whenever there is a change in the music.  Save rooms are a big offender as they are plentiful, you will have to do a 5 sec load to enter a save room, tell the save point you want to save, watch a few second animation, then another 5 seconds to leave the room.  As you wander back and fourth around the map, the frequency of loading screens just crushes the flow of the game.  Again, I'm really surprised none of the other reviews here are harping on this.Speaking of traversing the map, the game outright tells you where to go next all the time.  You can't turn this off and it kills me when metroidvanias do this as it crushes any sense of exploration.  The joy of exploring is further crushed by map markers explicitly telling you every single path you don't have that ability to unlock and which ones you do.  Some people may like this feature, but when the game is basically leading you around by the nose as much as this one does, and then shows you every single place you can and cant go, it kills any sense of what makes this genre fun to me. The game is generally very "by the numbers" and feels generally uninspired.  It feels like the most basic a metroidvania can be and still be classified as one.  Maybe the target player is super casual and wants to have their hand held this much, but it feels too restrictive and linear to me personally.  The one thing that really sets the gameplay apart is the massive number of hacking mini games required to open doors and such.  The novelty of these also wore off quickly, especially combined with a bug I had with the KBM controls.The game's default KBM controls are completely weird, basically one of the devs decided to just put the buttons on the keyboard with where they would be on a controller without thinking it through.  As such, you have WASD for movement, and arrows for actions.  Having jump button be the down arrow is truly weird.  That being said, the game lets you remap the controls as expected by any game in 2024, so great!  The problem is that if you remap movement to the arrow keys, the game ignores this for the hacking mini games and pretends its still WASD.  I'd like to believe this will be patched.After playing for 2.5 hours, I was totally bored of being led around by the nose, listening to the main character non-stop trying make cutesy commentary, and sitting through tons of loading screens breaking up the flow of the game.  There was also never really a moment where I felt challenged at all.  The bosses I did fight were very well produced and flashy, but pretty easy leaving you with a "that's it?" feeling when they died.  My save file says I'm about 35% through, so I'm guessing 7 hours for a full playthrough collecting everything?  For a price tag of $30, that's a tough sell.  It's a shame because the game visually looks solid, and the music is full of bangers, and there's a lot of effort put into the story with all the voice acting (sometimes a bit too much), but as a metroidvania fan it was very generic, generally linear, full of loading screens, and it just failed to grab me.

_childDocuments_.review: When it was first announced, for about a second, I turned away from it but then I realized that this could be something way different and way more interesting than the usual "same 'ol, same 'ol". Nice to see a fresh new take on the franchise. You got some that say "Not my Yars" but it is actually more Yars than you may think. You got your original 1982 release, the 2011 rail-shooter *cough* Panzer Dragoon *cough*, the re-imagined version on the Atari 50 collection and Yars Recharged in 2022.I know it may look to cater to a different younger audience but there is something for all (including us older generation). Good story that keeps flowing and just when you think it's over - it still keeps going! Quite a few "callbacks" to other Atari games and the soundtrack is pretty cool too with lots of variety. The hacking stuff is a little meh but whatever, not a deal breaker. WayForward put some work into this - they didn't just put something together quick and push it out there. Overall, I like it and think it's very fun - especially for this old Atari guy.
_childDocuments_.name: Yars Rising

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to give a tldr for this game, it's pretty much baby's first metroidvania. I'm not saying it's not hard, actually a bit of the opposite. At times this game really gives you a challenge, especially during the Yars Revenge minigames during the game which start off easy sure, but later on are pretty difficult.What I mean by "baby's first metroidvania" is that if you've never played a metroidvania before, you would most certainly like this one (and probably start with this one). It's a very accessible metroidvania, so accessible that you can even give yourself invincibility during the Yars minigames (though I opted to not use it for that true Yars experience). There is a bit of backtracking you have to do, though not excessive... until the end game where I was like "is this really necessary?" It wasn't cumbersome, just a little annoying since where you have to backtrack to there are no elevators for specific parts of the map (elevators allow you to traverse the map faster). It got a little annoying to the point where I used the save point as a "teleport me back where I need to go" type solution because I would travel down a long path with no elevator and finish the objective there, then deliberately die to respawn where I last saved, which would save me a lot of time having to run all the way back up. A little annoying but not too bad.My main criticism with the game is the final boss, which to say the least, is a little bs. I think the move set of the crystal (?) is strange. It moves around sporadically and feels a little bit unfair because you can't really "see" when it will attack you, it's just random.My other criticism is that there are no boss health bars for... some reason. I dunno why there aren't any, but at times I'm just blasting the boss with my Zorlon shot and I can't really tell how much damage I've currently dealt to the boss.But other than that, it's a very good game. The music is the show runner here, clearly, and is just absolutely awesome to listen to. And the music features Moe Shop like waaaaa??? Absolute peak.The art is also absolutely fantastic, and the VO I especially liked. The protagonist is quirky yet extremely charming. They really chose the right voice actress for this game. Some of the dialogue is a little... um... funky frfr no cap. I think some of the dialogue is meant to be ironic which is pretty funny.This game is priced absolutely . $30 I would say is very fair for a game like this, and I think perfectly justified. Overall, I had a lot of fun with this game (and had this game on my radar for a long time now, and was my most anticipated game so far). I give it uhh... um.. a 9/10 I guess. Minor problems, but still kicks some Qotech ass!
_childDocuments_.name: Yars Rising

_childDocuments_.review: So I've played this game and have almost fully completed it (currently stuck on the final boss).  So I feel qualified to discuss it.Yars Rising is a 2.5D Metroidvania set in the Yars universe. For those of you under the age of 40, Yars Revenge was a game released for the Atari 2600 that a large portion of you have probably never heard of. This game apparently takes place in the same universe as that. Somehow.Anyway, you play as Emi Kimura, a hacker trying to steal data from a cyberpunk megacorporation called Qotech. You get caught, discover weird alien powers, and then go on a rampage through the tower and the surrounding city, doing hero stuff.If you aren't familiar with how a metroidvania works, the clue is in the name. Games like Metroid and Castlevania only allow you to explore a small part of the map at first, until you gain more powers and methods of traversal that then open up more areas for you. This both gives you a reason to explore every nook and cranny of hte map, but it also means there's a lot of backtracking to places you've already been.  And there is very little in the way of fast travel. All this backtracking can get tedious.That aside, the combat feels pretty good. Controls make sense and feel tight. Enemies are varied enough to keep you on your toes. Everything looks and sounds good, with a great city pop/retrowave soundtrack (always a strong point in Wayforward's titles) The main character, Emi, looks good too, and she has that sort of adorkable personality that'll grab attention from a lot of players. The voice acting is a little cheesy, but seems to fit the atmosphere they were going for so I won't count against it.Is the game fun? I've been enjoying it. There's a good challenge, lots of secrets to find, and while the plot is a little stupid, it serves its purpose. Is it a must-buy? No. Definitely not. But if you like metroidvanias and the game looks appealing, I'd say put it on your wishlist and wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Yars Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing for about 4 hours and so far there are a ton of really great things about this game and 1 very bad thing.The controls are very smooth and intuitive. Animations are nice and detailed with character and enemy movements. The colors in the game are absolutely beautiful. The use of classic Atari Yars for the hacking mechanic mini game is such a good idea and never gets old. The art style is full of charm from the characters to just the simple detail of using the Atari rainbow pixels as her projectile. I know some people say it's a little simple when comparing it to other metroidvanias, but I honestly don't mind that. Not everything has to have extreme layers and depth to be fun. The method of equipping items by managing your Yar's pixel space with Tetris style blocks is a cute and fun way to manage character upgrades. The soundtrack is a banger. I enjoyed multiple tracks and appreciate that the game tells me the track listings as the come on.Combat is very reminiscent of Megaman and just feels good mash the shoot button.Also seems like there is a bit of a slow burn here which after about 4 hours there is still plenty to chew on. Very cool.All of these thing make this game excel in my opinion. The game isn't trying to reinventing the wheel or anything, but in the department of style and vibe, it kills. It's just fun to look at and play.The bad part. The main character's dialogue is absolutely insufferable. I can't stress enough that without this I would have nothing really bad to say about it. The rest of the game is very lucky it's got all these positive things, because I almost stopped playing just because of the dialogue. In fact, the only thing that kept me from quitting for good was someone suggested I see if I could turn off her dialogue in the settings. Apparently some dev agrees with me because there is literally an option to turn her commentary off which saved the game. You still have to see the text pop up and you still have to deal with her dialogue in cutscenes... but this is a setting that is REQUIRED unless you want to hear Bubsy levels of annoying quips throughout the entire game. I'm sorry to whoever put work into these lines, but almost every line from our main character is an attempt at quirky humor and it falls completely flat every single time. She is not likable in any way and comes off like every obnoxious ostentatious person in front of you in line at Walmart who has to have everyone notice they are funny and interesting like they are auditioning for a Joss Whedon movie. I can't tell if it was written by an AI or someone so terminally online that they've never talked to a real person IRL and for whatever reason it's only our main character who is this bad. Also there is the HILARIOUS NEVER BEFORE DONE joke about the fat character needing snacks... riveting. Please stop doing this sh*t. I mean, on god that's pretty sus.However, aside from this. The game is REALLY good is packed with charm is all the other departments. Definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Update after 100%:My full review of Yars Rising can be found on my website, which I can't link here due to Steam policy — just search for Demajen. The review is 2700 words long and goes into a lot more detail about why I can't in good conscience recommend this game when there are so many better and cheaper Metroidvanias around.If you absolutely love the Yars franchise and the hacking minigames, go wild with this one. If you don't know squat about Yars or found the hacking minigames intrusive and slowed down the pace of the metroidvania game you thought you were playing in the demo, don't touch with a barge pole. (There are over 40 of them in the full game, though thankfully there's only the one you have to do in a boss fight!)Absolutely not worth the price. 100% completed in 7 hours and 10 minutes.The Voice Acting attempts to carry a mediocre and rote plot, with twists you'll see a mile coming, and the kind of exploration you'd find in a one-man indie effort --- actually no, that's an insult to indie devs.I've played a few Wayforward metroidvanias at this point, and every single one of them has been better than this overpriced snoozefest. Grab it on sale or, better yet, get any of the later Shantae games or Mummy Demastered instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Yars Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Very mixed recommend. A decent metroidvania that unfortunately overstays its welcome quite a bit by committing a few cardinal sins of the genre towards the end:All of this culminates in an absolute slog of a last fourth of the game in which you need to go back to four places in order to use your new "I can go underwater" ability. A completely baffling decision that destroys the story's quick pace. It's entirely unnecessary and ends the game on a really sour note, when the rest of Yars Rising is a very okay metroidvania that lacks juice and exploration but makes it up with style, a smooth difficulty curve and a banging soundtrack.Definitely needs some touching up in order to be more accessible to people and more fun, but a great effort to revitalize the Yars licence! I enjoyed the hacking minigames that are straight up stages from the original Yars' Revenge on the Atari. Thirty bucks is too much, but wait for some updates and pick it up on sale - or better yet, pick up the soundtrack right now!

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty much the definition of a 7/10. pretty competently made and well playing game, neat characterstyle, some humor (though it can be cringe).it has a really great OST that is worth checking out.Little to complain about other than price and the amount of loading. moving between different sets of zones needs a little loading screen, its only like 5 seconds but it adds up and makes backtracking really annoying, especially because sometimes these zoneswitches can be chained so you run through multiple loads in a row. with a game like that i dunno why no option to just load it all into memory exists - it would make it feel a lot smoother to move around.one other thing that is a shame: game does not support 21:9 aspect ratio

_childDocuments_.review: Had a great time with this game. Game is very charming. Voice acting is well done, especially on the main character. Delivery matches the humor well. Had a lot of fun listening to Emi make jokes about the game itself, and overall I feel the experience was enhanced by the voice lines. Be aware though, if you think "millennial writing" is cringe, you'll probably think the opposite. There is an option to turn off the quips if you don't like them.Music is fantastic. Not sure the exact genre but imagine something you'd hear in a hip clothing store. My only gripe about the music is that it changes when you hit a loading screen, which is pretty often, so it's rare to hear more than 30-40 seconds of a song at a time. Controls are solid, no complaints really. The wall jump is similar to Super Metroid, where you have to wait for Emi to start sliding down the wall or it won't work. Takes a bit of getting used to.I am a bit disappointed that most of the movement upgrades felt underwhelming until you found their corresponding augment. Wall jump feels limp, super jump doesn't go very high, and the dash is short with a lot of endlag. After placing the upgrades they feel much better. I also wish the base crawl speed was higher, and the crawl speed upgrade wasn't even a thing. Seems like a silly thing to intentionally nerf so that you can fix it with an upgrade later. It's never required, so IMO it should have just been faster from the start.Hacking sections were hit or miss for me. I felt that some of them, especially later in the game, were excessively annoying. I preferred the hacks earlier in the game that were quicker and easier, almost like a Wario Ware micro game, not the longer obstacle course style of the later hacks.Gameplay is fine. The game is pretty easy overall so I hope hard mode changes that. It's honestly nothing special, but the exploration paired with the voice lines kept me engaged. Boss fights are a nice change of pace and well designed. Backtracking is thankfully kept to a minimum. You can choose to explore each area fully before moving on, or just grab everything when you find yourself going through that area again later on. None of the upgrades are so crucial that you need to have them ASAP.I really enjoyed the upgrade system, it's designed so that you can build Emi pretty much any way you want. You can choose to focus on the normal gun, missiles, movement, survivability, etc. It's sometimes a pain to swap things in and out constantly, but I didn't find that to be much of a problem until late in the game where certain hacking upgrades become nearly mandatory. Overall I really enjoyed my time with this game. Is $30 kinda high? Yeah, but I think the production value was adequately high as well, so I'm not mad about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Very decent Metroidvania game, good for people who don't usually play them but the Pro Mode (New Game+) does provide harder gameplay so you will get your $30 worth.And YES it does tie in with the original Yars game! _childDocuments_.review: While not a very fluid and satisfying side-scroller, the level design kept my interest with a variety of different challenges, unlocking traversal and combat abilities before I had time to get bored. The throwback hacking minigames are nearly all distinct too, some particularly challenging. Can't say I'm crazy about the quip-filled dialogue, but typical of WayForward there's a corny English anime dub charm to it, and I appreciated how Emi gave fresh commentary when exploring and revisiting parts of the map. Excellent background music--I wish the save point sound effect didn't drown it out.My biggest complaint would be the same of River City Girls 2: Loading screens. WayForward should remedy this in their next project. From the player's standpoint, it's hard imagining why small and relatively simple 2D environments require seconds to load. Plenty of Metroidvanias with busier environments exist, and they maintain a more seamless presentation.
_childDocuments_.name: Yars Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This is a metroidvania with all the secret finding removed. This is an action platformer interrupted by old-school shoot-em-up styled hacking minigames that grow increasingly tedious. The bosses are either extremely easy or obtuse.Overall the writing is probably the worst. The story itself is fine, but the game spends the first half deprecating itself by pointing out how weird or annoying certain things are--lasers are its favorite target--that when it decides that it wants to try taking itself seriously in the last act it's already trained me not to even bother getting engaged. It feels insincere in the most patronizing way, like Joss Whedon's writing but without any charm.
