_childDocuments_.review: I understand that I'm in a very niche audience that this game targets, but I'm disappointed that this game isn't more popular than it is. First, I think I need to clarify what I mean by "niche audience". This game is a metroidvania that involves a LOT of hacking minigames involving gameplay from the classic Atari 2600 game Yars' Revenge. So if you don't like metroidvanias... or you don't like Yars' Revenge... you probably won't like this game. The core game is a metroidvania, but you have to hack a LOT of terminals to open doors, activate platforms, and unlock various forms of powerups and upgrades. So there's no avoiding both styles of gameplay as the mix of both styles are the whole point of this game.I will say that the store video will likely put a lot of fans of the classic Yars' Revenge off. At first glance, it looks like this game has NOTHING to do with the original plot of Yars' Revenge. I don't want to give any spoilers, but that is NOT true. The hacking minigames are great little bite-sized chunks of Yars' Revenge gameplay. Some minigames are simply the classic "fire the Zorlon cannon at the Qotile" objectives like in the original game... but many of them go beyond that. You'll also have objectives like "destroy the centipedes" or "use the ion fields to help you navigate the maze". While all of the hacking challenges focus on the gameplay of Yars' Revenge (), they are all varied enough to keep the numerous challenges fresh. Not once did I approach a terminal and think, "Oh no. Not another hacking game." Many of the variations are also references to other Atari games like Centipede, Black Widow, and Missile Command.While you often have to hack to open doors and activate platforms to progress in the game... many of the challenges will provide powerups for your character that are typical to a metroidvania-style game... while others can provide upgrades that you can equip. Equipping upgrades reminds me of the upgrades in Tron 2.0 where you install programs on a disc. You have a template in the shape of a pixel Yar, and the upgrades have shapes that you have to place inside the template to be active. So you can't have all of your upgrades active at once. As you progress, you'll find better upgrades, or similar upgrades with a smaller shape allowing room for you to equip other upgrades. Red upgrades are for health (raising max health or raising health drops by enemies), orange is for offense (like shot damage and shot speed), purple is for hacking (like 3-way shots and cloaking when hacking terminals), etc. You can adjust these whenever you want... so if you find a hacking puzzle difficult, try installing more purple upgrades. When having trouble with a boss, try installing more red and orange or maybe green (movement) upgrades.The graphics are great and the sound is superb! The music is really different from what I expected, but it's fantastic! The dialog can be a bit campy, but it's not bad. Emi does make various comments throughout gameplay... however, once she makes a comment or cracks a joke, it's done. She only says it once. It's not one of those games where she says something over and over again. So while there's an option to turn her comments off, I never had the urge to do so. In fact, I have to admit that some of her comments made me chuckle. So I think it's worth leaving her commentary on.So is this the best metroidvania out there? No. Not at all. But if you like metroidvanias and you also happen to like Yars' Revenge, I think you will probably really like this game. I certainly do. I've already completed the game, completed the bonus hacking challenges, and completed the game on professional mode (hard mode). So I liked it enough to 100% it... and I could see myself playing through it again sometime in the future. This game gets a thumbs up from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Yars Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Solid action-adventure platforming metroidvania game from Wayforward! Controls well, and offers decent variety in platforming activities through different power-ups you obtain throughout the game. Some of the hacks can be quite frustrating, but I don't think I was stuck on any for more than 10 minutes. Standout for me is Wayforward's usual fun/snarky dialogue, colorful cast of characters (no one talks like that Refresh...they only type like that ;) ), and the AMAZING soundtrack. I played for about 2 hours initially and then went and immediatley bought the soundtrack. If you are familiar with their work on the Shantae games, this is classic B&B of Wayforward. There isn't anything here that will redefine the genre, but if you are looking for a solid gameplay experience with a decent amount of post-game content (as well as a harder difficulty mode), pick this up and you will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review: Yars Rising was a mostly enjoyable venture into a world that was crafted from a 1982 Atari game. The story was quite enjoyable and that was at least partially due to it being masterfully voiced. Each character had a unique personality and that came across well. The map was well designed and fun to explore. The stealth elements weren't overbearing which for me was a plus since I'm not a huge stealth game fan. The platforming was pretty decent with a bunch of upgrades you'll earn as you play. Hacking was retro inspired and something I had a blast with but it might not be for everyone. The weakest link of the game to me landed with it's combat which wasn't bad but wasn't great either. The enemies felt fairly generic and none of the bosses were overly spectacular either. The last thing I want to mention is the soundtrack which is pretty much worth the price of the game alone. Absolute bangers on here!For a more in-depth breakdown of Yars Rising please see my included video review!

_childDocuments_.review: Cute art style, a funky main character, challenging boss fights, and occasional breaks to play an "old atari game" style hacking game. The gamefeel is as good as most Wayforward games, with this one borrowing more from the metroidvania genre than most of their past works. It's good, and while I haven't finished it yet I'm getting the feeling that it's not very long. Not every game needs to be long though.
_childDocuments_.name: Yars Rising

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has been gaming for 25+ years I'd say i have a pretty good appreciation for retro games. The Atari era did pass me by as I would have been -13 years old at the time Yars' Revenge came out but I can still respect the roots of gaming. Yars Rising does exactly that by respecting the history while also bringing it to a more contemporary setting. The game is a Metroidvania at its core as you explore the Qotech building with various upgrades you find scattered around. They improve movement and your combat abilities so its very satisfying to find new ones as you get them pretty often. However this game is a little sneaky because it has a 2nd game hidden inside it. The character you play as is a hacker called Emi and you will be hacking almost as much as you will be exploring. The twist being that the hacking games are actually Yars' Revenge levels! Every single one will have you doing mini challenges in a new version of Yar's Revenge and they are such a treat! Some are very challenging and there are even a few other hidden Atari games inside those hacking games as well! The characters are fun and well written, the music by Megan Mcduffee is always a treat, and the expanding on the lore of a 1982 arcade style game is commendable. I really appreciate how Wayforward kept the original games spirit alive with this. I do hope more people try this out as it is one of those games that's just a genuine good time with lots of charm.
_childDocuments_.name: Yars Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable game with an absolute banger of a soundtrack that I ended up also buying. The hacking segments added a lot of challenge and were a lot of fun, even if the platforming bits were a bit easy. Will admit that the last boss was a bit disappointing though, I managed to beat him after my 3rd attempt and I was left feeling a bit "Huh, is that it??" afterwards. Overall though a brilliant game from Atari that won't disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: Yars Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I freaking adore this game and I hope it's successful enough to sustain the series with at least a sequel or two, even if it might have to stick to being a constrained-budget title to continue existing.This aesthetic is going for a specific kinda of neo-retro-futuristic anime-esque cyberpunk sort of world, you can tell if you'll vibe with it from the trailer footage. If the visual and audio aesthetic does vibe with you, you're in for a great time because the game is pretty consistent in its flavor with catchy music that feels of the era, and a handful of references to other games that also very much feel of their time.Because this is a Good game. It is a very competent and distinct Metroid-style side-scrolling action-platformer with backtracking through environments for new paths and hidden secrets. It's also got a lot of very fun variations on the original Yars Revenge gameplay in the "hacking" minigame segments which I enjoyed quite a bit. I think quite genuinely anyone who is able to finish this game would be able to play the original version of Yars Revenge with little additional guidance.But I want to emphasize that the game is Good, it is not Great. * It doesn't have a greater meaning it wants to get across- it's very much just trying to remind people that Atari and its IP exists. and that's not a message one can do much with after they're done playing.* It lacks in terms of accessibility options (why on earth is auto-fire/rapidfire not built in? And no, the one hacking-only upgrade does not count. Though the option to be able to try the hacking many games as many times as one wants as an _option_ is pretty cool). * The game is very much lacking in "sauce"; as in, the game doesn't have cool momentum-preserving tricks to play with, or much advanced movement tech in the way of dash-cancels, dash-jumping, an inifnite-run, slope-boosts, etc.* Boss Intro Splash Screens cannot be skipped at all, so if you struggle on a boss during a low-HP playthrough, you are going to have to wait through the splash every time.* There is no Speedrun mode, no built in option to show a timer on the HUD, nor any option to auto-skip cutscenes after having finished the game once or twice. (If you are a completionist, you will want to finish the game twice.)And while it's a competent Metroid-inspired game on the whole, it seems to have followed the roots of the genre closely enough to inherit most of the genre's worst design flaws and very few of the mechanical upgrades and refinement that have been seen from indie Metroid/Vanias in the past two decdaes. For example, * There are boss where you die and then you get sent back to the loading room and walk back to the boss room and re-watch the boss intro with no-means to skip it, wasting almost an entire minute per retry instead of just quickly resetting the one room. * Or having crushers that will mis-register and insta-kill the player if they are zipped upwards towards certain walls due to hitbox overlaps. Or generally *requiring* having to manuaklly backtrack to elevators and portals in order to fast travel between those points with no option to immediately warp to a known save point. * Or you have the ability to customize your augmentation loadout to help you deal with specific challenges that are being a pain, but there's no option to save multiple loadouts or quickly recall them. There's just so many of these rough edges that feel like at least one person on the team should have noticed before launch.All in all I think the game is worth playing and I look forward to seeing more fanart of Emi. Like, the vibe of this game really *really* hits my tastes just right. The characters's tendency to make silly jokes and self-aware comments kinda remind me of Bubsy a bit, which I enjoy, despite how loathed he and his games are on the internet. ALSO THERE WAS MORE THAN ONE TIME WHERE I LOOKED AT THE NAME OF A BOSS AND SCREAMED AND WAS SO EXCITED FOR THE DUMB BUT VERY TARGETED HUMOR. I freaking LOVE that. There's a boss around midgame that particularly just :clap: I freaking loved that reveal.
_childDocuments_.name: Yars Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Yars Rising is a sequel to Yars Revenge (released in 1982 for Atari) and turned into a Metroidvania game.The game's strengths lie in its creative hacking minigames, which offer a unique twist by drawing inspiration from Atari classics like Yars' Revenge, Missile Command, and Centipede. These minigames are engaging and varied but become repetitive over time, which can detract from the overall experience. Players unlock new abilities and upgrades through these hacking challenges, but the limited visual variety and overly familiar environments can make the gameplay feel.Boss fights and power-ups are notable highlights, with some battles showcasing tight, strategic design. However, the early emphasis on stealth mechanics is widely considered the game's weakest point, detracting from the otherwise fun On the positive side, the soundtrack stands out, featuring city pop-inspired tracks that give the game a distinct energy and make even its duller moments more enjoyable. The music, contributed by a variety of artists, has been praised for its catchy tunes that stick with players long after they finish the game​(In summary, Yars Rising brings a nostalgic yet modern take on Atari's legacy, but the lack of variety and underwhelming environments hold it back from reaching its full potential. However, its creative hacking mechanics and strong soundtrack make it an interesting, if not groundbreaking, entry in the Metroidvania genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review after spending more time with this game:I've definitely fallen in love with this game after getting stuck into it.From the top the first thing that captures me is the music. Its just so freaking good. It makes me want to put in headphones and crank up the volume. Only complaint here is that a few times playing in bed on the Steam Deck has resulted in the music getting me way too energised to sleep.The next thing i love is the art style and visuals. I'm not at all an anime person and have never seen the appeal so this game was already something i wasn't sure about yet i've really fallen in love with the vibrant and bold visuals that this game uses to present itsself, from the character and environment design to the overall UI design. Its just really very good and feels very video gamey in the best way possible. This combined with the music and quite frankly awesome sound design (your weapons, skills, the voice work, footsteps) all just add up to make this feel like a very well polished video game that brings back memories of the bold visuals and punchy sound effects of the old arcade machines i saw as a kid.Gameplay is where i felt the game lets its self down a bit.  The movement / controls feel great. Everything is very tight and responsive, i even enjoyed the exploration / map design but some of the combat felt very simplistic and perhaps a missed opportunity. But the more i play the more i just get into the groove of what this game wants to be. It's not trying to present its self as an overly complicated or challenging metroidvania with punnishing combat. Instead this game is more of a casual game that offers fun exploration with moments of challenge (boss fights and some of the hacking mini games) with an overall focus on navigating the map.A metroidvania's main character is always the map and this game presents that very well. Early on you get a very easy to read map that shows you where you have been but also places you still need to explore. At certain points in the game you find yourself just going away from the main mission objective and starting to explore and backtrack and trying to unlock things that were previously out of reach to gain new skills. I spent hours doing just that and its been some of my favourite moments in the game.So overall i have really been enjoying my time with this game.I've got quite a few of the most recent AAA releases all sitting in my backlog waiting for me to finish this game - because it's this game that has been the one i want to load up each day when i get some free time to play. It just feels great to play and makes me feel great to play it.In-fact after playing this i went and bought a whole bunch of games made by wayforward.I really hope that this game sells enough to see some sort of expanded content or story either as DLC or a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: I recieved this game from a streamer doing a giveaway for steam codes on the day of the games launch. That being said I enjoyed this game a lot! the 2.5D artstyle allows for some really cool perspectives on enemies and enviornmental hazzards while also being able to flesh out character and level design more than a straight 2D game can give. The chracters are cute and have an artsyle that I personally enjoy and the levels are very detailed and immersive. The soundtrack is amazing and I find myself listening to the megamix on Wayforwards youtube frequently I honestly don't dislike a single song in the soundtrack. The gameplay is pretty stock standard for a metroidvania game you get power ups then proceed to have puzzles/enviornmental challenges and enemies that require those powerups. There are quite a few secrets that provide an in game reward (such as power ups, ammo capacity, and health/damage increases) as well as plenty of secrets that offer a trip of nostalgia for anyone that's played any old Atari games. The story while nothing flashy is still cute and serves its purpose of fleshing out characters while giving the player a purpose to progress forward. All in all this game is very charming and entertaining. I enjoyed every minute spent playing and hearing the ever sassy and manic Emi interact with the world and plot points that developed. my only gripe with the game is that I wish it were longer I have almost 6 hrs on record at the time of the review and I have beaten the game with about 85% completion. I do intend on playing through the harder mode that unlocks after beating the game and seeing what further challenges or secrets that may have been tucked into it. If you enjoy metroidvania games give this one a shot and I don't think you'll be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun metroidvania-type game! It's on the shorter end as far as games like it go, but I think its length is great. It's much more focused on the story than exploration, and I appreciate it when games like this don't have the player needlessly backtrack if the world isn't interesting enough to make the player want to go back and explore areas they didn't finish before.I liked the characters (mostly) and I think the voice actors with a great job with the pretty mediocre script they were given. If they hadn't done such a good job, I think I would have been a lot less interested in the story of this game. The music is also very good, usually blending right into the background of what you're doing. Sections of dialogue (typically at bosses) play out the first time and do not play again when you die and retry the battle, with one exception. I liked this, mashing through dialogue every time I die isn't fun to me. Granted, this game isn't super difficult or anything so I didn't die all that much but still it was an aspect that I really appreciated! The exception is the final boss, which without spoiling anything is a bit of text to mash through. I mentioned I don't think this game was very difficult for me, but the hacking sections do have a much higher level of difficulty compared to the combat. I really liked how they always had something different in them, it almost never felt like I played more than one that was the same, or didn't at least have a weird spin on a previous challenge, which is really saying something because there are a LOT of them. These are optional, and also grant invincibility if you choose after a certain number of failures.The game also looks great! I think the visuals are nice, and there are some comic/manga panel style cutscenes that really look good!Some things I did not like were how the game controls at times, but really specifically the ledge grab. 99% of the time in the game it plays very well! But there are a few sections where you have to navigate a room with very strict timing, but the ledge grab requires you to jump, usually go higher than the ledge you're trying to grab, KEEP HOLDING the direction you want to go as you fall back down (otherwise Emi won't grab the ledge), and slowly pull yourself up after needing a beat for the grab to... resolve(?), and then keep going. There was one segment where the character model would be pushed through the floor and snap onto where I pulled myself up because the platforming didn't have enough time for the pulling up animation to finish but the game recognized that I made it to where I was trying to go.Additionally, some of the dialogue wasn't for me personally, like I said I think the VAs did a fantastic job but there were a few lines that got my eyes rolling.Overall, I think this deserves to be played! I don't think it's a masterpiece or anything, but if you like metroidvanias and want a shorter one to play this will certainly do the job. Also if you like games that feature a female protagonist that has her own agency and is allowed to actually be a character etc. this game has that as well! I enjoyed this.

Beating them without any biohacks is quite a different expirience, and also there are a some unique challenes. Supernova took me some hours on the course of several days to beat.Overall, not an ideal, but pretty enjoyable game. Do recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great little game, i think if you like Wayforward games, you will like this one.  also, if you like *really* old school games like yars revenge, but you like *somewhat* modern games (Symphony of the Night -> onward) you will REALLY love this game.  It really has a nice mix of both styles of gameplay, and the just fabulously hilarious dialogue and character design that is standard for wayforward.  Also the MUSIC soundtrack is top notch!  it really has that kind of 80's vaporwave pop vibe that is just timeless.  maybe the graphical style is a liiittttllle bit lacking... it's hard to say what's wrong with it tho... like the graphics really fit the vibe, but they seem a liiiiittle bit generic... but it's really hard for me to come up with a constructive criticism... all in all it's a solid 9/10 if you like a good "metroidvania" and that signature hilarious wayforward dialogue and characters.  it's no shantae and the pirate's curse,  but really, what is?

_childDocuments_.review: Great modern revival of one of Atari's classic games. In summary, it's a Metroidvania with the gameplay of the original Yar's Revenge interspersed throughout in hacking minigames, all while you confront a corrupt corporation with the police in their pocket during an alien invasion. The story has so far kept me engaged even if I'm not finished with the game, which was not something I was expecting. One of WayForward's biggest leaps forward (hardy har har) graphically too, completely 3D, full voice-acting, the works, and in general the stylization is fantastic. Although maybe that's mainly cuz of Atari's budget, WayForward tends to reuse engines and tech they've used on other projects for Shantae. Makes me excited to see the next new Shantae game, besides Risky Revolution obviously.All-in-all, highly recommend.

I didn't hear a single repeated line in my entire playthrough and she talks ALOT,The other standout feeature is the hacking minigame. which is always a variation of the namesake atari game Yar's Revenge. hacking is used to open doors, disable security, and acquire upgrades, If you don't enjoy this little minigame, it will probably get on your nerves very quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't necessarily doing anything much grander than any other Metroidvania, but it's a really fun one, especially if you love old Atari stuff. It took me 20 hours to do pretty much everything the game has to offer, which includes two playthroughs. It's pretty short, so if you judge a game's price by its length in hours, it's probably something you'll want to pick up on sale. If you judge a game's price by its overall quality, it's well worth the 30 bucks (personally I would price the game at 25, but I'm not going to complain about price when the game is really fun and I feel like it was money well spent). If you like Metroidvanias and Atari games, this is a must-play. If you're only into one of the two, this is also a really good bridge into enjoying the other. The only big flaw I could find in the game is that Emi can be very annoying, but you have the option of turning off the in-game quips and skipping the cutscenes. Also definitely a "Best game soundtrack of the year" contender.

_childDocuments_.review: Wasn't a bad game, okay really.Story:Wasn't anything much, just something about an alien conflict that didn't get much expansion on. _childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty decent, I had a lot of fun with it, although I think several aspects of the game fall just slightly short, both gameplay and story-wise. I will talk about some of the unlockable abilities and plot points, so if you with to remain spoiler-free, proceed at your own risk.Starting with the story, it remains very simple, stop the bad guys with a couple small surprises along the way. However, it feels like the developers wished to push the story a little further, but had to cut some corners.One of the early boss in the game is the Black Widow, a spider lady once human that was experimented on and augmented to the point she had no humanity left. Black Widow senses that the same is happening to the player’s character Emi, the implication being that the DNA rewriting augments the player collects through the game puts Emi at risk of losing herself. A theme that we see again both in the soundtrack -such as ‘Who am I’ and the augment screen with the Yars version of Emi slowly fading in a little more with each acquired ability.Sadly, this theme isn’t explored further past this early boss fight, which is a bit unfortunate. I feel seeing Emi fight to keep her humanity and how much of herself she is willing to sacrifice to save the world would’ve made a nice twist on its otherwise simple structure.Gameplay wise, the game has a nice balance between 3 differents sections, the regular traversal of the map, jumping ans shooting your way through enemies and obstacles megaman style. The stealth segments where the player must avoid  guards far too resilient to be taken head-on until the end-game. And the hacking mini-game which make you play classic Yars with different scenarios and objectives.I’ll focus on the normal platforming segments which make the bulk of the game. The gameplay is solid but never gets too crazy for a Metroidvania. You won’t be vaporising screens full of enemies as would a fully-powered Samus Aran, and the addition of a triple shot power up -something available for the hacking mini-game funnily enough- would’ve really helped making the player feel that Emi is getting stronger.My biggest grip with the gameplay however is the Dragonfly Dash. The dash ability in a games is always on the biggest mobility option you can give a player. However, the Dragonfly Dash stops to a screeching halt after launching forward, making it feel clunky and barely usable for quick traversal. This dash would’ve greatly benefited taking a page from Megaman X’s dash, with the ability to smoothly chain them together without stopping and cancel in long jumps/ A fluid dash like this would make backtracking in a Metroidvania map much more satisfying, and would also allow for more complex boss patterns.While my review focuses on what I personally perceives as shortcomings. The game was still a blast to play through. I can only hope these points could be improved upon if the game gets a sequel.

From the renowned development studio WayForward Technologies, Inc. comes Yars Rising, a 2D action adventure exploration of one of Atari’s richest, and best known classic titles. In WayForward’s experienced hands, the Yars franchise becomes an expansive mystery solved through 2D platforming action.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, let's get the important stuff out of the way first. The remaster could be better. There are no video options beyond brightness, and the keyboard and mouse controls are only rebindable with a utility you have to use before you launch the game, though mouse sensitivity and camera speed can be changed at any time. I get that this is using very old tech and probably a nightmare to reverse engineer for modern standards a decade after the fact, but it is disappointing.All that being said, I am very, very happy to get to be able to play this again without having to dig out my Xbox 360. This game was envisioned as a radically different project, but Shadows of the Damned remains charmingly absurd in spite of EA games demanding an overwhelming amount of change during production. Is it a must play? No, but its a Suda 51 game. That means at the very least, it's you're going to have a weird and memorable time one way or the other.Edit: Unsure if Steam will let me link this, but a modder on Github has already uncapped the framerate, among other improvements. It's still very early obviously, but nice to see!

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the game twice so far (on Steam Deck OLED). Once on Normal and once on New Game+ (Normal). Pros:+ God-Tier Soundtrack.+ Fun story / characters / writing / lore.+ Solid action gameplay. + 60 FPS on SteamDeck OLED. Cons:- 2D segments are kind of boring (and obviously in place of cut content).- Beating the game on Normal or harder does not unlock the achievement for beating the game on Easy. (So dumb when games do this.) - Final third of the game feels kind of rushed and slapped together. - New Game+ mode does not let you skip the non-pre-rendered cutscenes. - New Game+ mode does not let you begin on a harder difficulty. (New Game+ Normal was pointlessly easy.)- Unless I'm missing something, there are no PC graphics options aside from Gama adjustment. The game runs smooth, but some aspects of the visual presentation are annoying.Final Thoughts:I enjoyed SotD:HR about as much as the first time, when I played on PS3 back in the day. That is to say, the 2D side-scrolling areas still bum me out and the game really loses momentum towards the latter third. I think those 2D areas are such a bummer because by the end of the third one it's super obvious they're representative of cut content. (Probably "because EA".) So when the remaster was announced I was really hoping they'd go in and add the missing scenes. Such a missed opportunity. All that said, it feels good to have modern access to this game and I really hope we get a sequel. SotD: HR is still a wild ride and if you're looking for a quick, over-the-top action romp, overall I totally recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to recommend Shadows of the Damned mostly because it's a Grasshopper/Suda51 game and I want those to sell, but it's a game that becomes increasingly difficult to play when you know the entire story behind it.In the late 2000s, Suda51 went to EA with a pitch for a game called Kurayami, which would have been a new entry (and also the second one released in the West, after Killer7) into his Kill the Past series. As I understand the story, EA accepted his proposal but then demanded that it be changed into another game entirely - that game being Shadows of the Damned - at the behest of their C-Suite, then led by John Riccitello. Suda never forgave EA or Riccitello for it, hence why he later went on to publish a manga called Kurayami Dance that showed what Kurayami would have been. You can see the covers in the remake of The Silver Case, they were published in a magazine called Comic Beam and have been fan-translated. This is why the antagonist in No More Heroes 3 has the surname "Riccitello", by the way.Personally, I would rather have had Kurayami, a game that definitely had things to say, over this game, which is a pretty generic shooter full of ♥♥♥♥ jokes. It's not a bad game, just a very generic late 2000s shooter that really should have been so much more.  Even so, you should still buy it - and then go buy The Silver Case and The 25th Ward and play both of those instead - because Suda is worth supporting and because I want to see the real Kurayami some day, along with a full translation of the PS2 version of Flower, Sun and Rain.

_childDocuments_.review: This is where gaming peaked, games like this aren't made anymore but sadly PC ports way worse than the typical 7th gen era ones are for some reason. They've literally just loaded up the original UE3 project and clicked compile for PC and call it a day. Obviously these options should be there but they aren't and I just went straight into the game without worrying about it, the only thing I really miss is 21:9, that aside I'm honestly not that bothered about the lack of options, it plays more than well enough, it looks more than good enough, aside the initial shock I'm not really missing anything, FOV would be nice but since its locked to 16:9 anyways I can live with it.TLDR: As bare minimum port as it gets of a really good game and I don't think its worth missing out on just because of missing options, I think the price is fair and on the plus side this is 1:1 the exact same game as the original, no censorship, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ just locked to mostly 60 FPS at your desktop resolution. It depends on your expectations and I completely understand why many aren't happy, for me though this is kind of what I've been asking for, I hate butchered and overpriced remasters a lot, yeah this isn't a remaster, yes it is falsely advertised as such and no I don't care because I just want to play these games without dealing with ebay scalpers or experimental emulators and this works for that perfectly, in fact better than most remasters that try to go above and beyond yet end up missing the mark by a lot, this is what I want more of again, great games for a fair price, hella fun and thats all that matters.

_childDocuments_.review: KURAYAMI IS ALIVE, YET AGAIN!I have played Shadows before on a ps3 emulator, but didn't replay it before the release of this game like I planned to. What I can say is that for the most part from what I can tell, this is the exact same game with no major differences or changes, or anything missing. Which is good, expected from a remaster, and probably the best GHM remaster we've gotten so far in that sense. The addition of a New Game plus is great, very much needed for a game like Shadows, especially since you couldn't skip cutscenes in the original game. You can now in this remaster, but only some, stuff like boss introductions and enemy encounters or whatever, it's pretty selective. The costumes are also a very nice touch, however I think it's very strange that you only get Kaido Wataru's outfit after beating the game, when Demon Garcia gives you a double damage bonus, and you can select it from the start. Only Demon Garcia has a bonus like that and nothing else. Why make Kaido's outfit only selectable after beating the game if it doesn't have one? Seems very strange to me.On the issue of bugs, I didn't encounter too many that wasn't related to Eight Hearts's chain and cape freaking out every cutscene or animation, but it wasn't often enough for it to become a problem. There wasn't any bad texture pop-ins that I could tell, which the original game had horrendous amounts of due to it being an Unreal Engine 3 game from developers who had little to no experience in it. There was however, one crash I had after Justine's bossfight, which happened the moment before I was to load into the next area, making me do that entire chapter again. It only happened that one time, so it wasn't too bad, but it's still very frustrating. I didn't encounter any horrendous framedrops either, the game ran at a solid 60 my entire playthrough, but I can't say for everyone else, since I was also pretty lucky when it came to the NMH1 and 2 ports, so results will vary.My biggest problem with this game is the fact that you cannot select a new difficulty upon playing on New Game Plus. You're stuck with whatever difficulty you chose for that save. Ontop of the fact that the achievements for completing the game on each difficulty don't stack, makes that very frustrating knowing you have to play the game 3 separate times just for those achievements, and makes the extra hard difficulty redundant since, like the original, you don't get anything for beating the game on Very Hard. With some extra fixes and ironing, this could be even better. A couple changes and more additional content would be nice to see in the future. 25 bucks isn't bad but considering how little extra content is in this game and how short it is, I'd wait for a sale unless you really liked Shadows or any Grasshopper Manufacture/Suda stuff. This is a very good PC port.

_childDocuments_.review: Some games attempt use their interactive capabilities to deliver a powerful emotional punch. Some games do it poorly: Metal Gear Solid 3, despite its excellence, has one such bad example, with the "Press X to kill mommy/lover"-thing towards the end.There are two games that I would argue deliver such emotional payload effectively, that have made me have a sudden irrational need to inhabit the character and do something that would pretty clearly not contribute to a "win" condition. This was one of them. The other one was ICO, so we're clearly in good company. In ICO, the game persuaded me to jump off a bridge out of love. Towards the end of the Shadows of the Damned, I drank 43 bottles of sake in quick succession out of desperation, before accepting my fate in sorrow. That was really powerful.As of writing this, I have not yet finished this remaster, but I can attest that it is a very good port: you will have a better experience playing this port than the original, and so far there's nothing missing.As for the game itself, it is a tremendously stupid game with some moments of pure brilliance. The end of the game made the whole thing worth it for me, and some of the stupid jokes still make me laugh. I wish it took itself a bit more seriously, because you get some of the best storytelling there is when the game is firing on all cylinders.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm here rather for the Shinji Mikami stylish action, and not so much for the Suda51 weirdness, and so far I'm having a blast. The depiction of hell is quite interesting, looks like traditional Spanish slums, and reminded me of DMC2 levels. The protagonist in motion reminds me a lot of Benicio Del Toro with voice acting sounding like Manny from Grim Fandango. Also would like to mention the sound direction by Akira Yamaoka, it's stellar and atmospheric. I don't want to talk much about humour, but the dialogue about a strawberry ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ had me smiling like a weirdo.I think the price is great and the execution also good - stable 4K /60 FPS, beautiful textures, and not particularly buggy (although I feel like my left stick is drifting...). The shooting impact has good animation, but otherwise some rare and minor animations seem not smooth enough, as if the game was programmed with 30 fps in mind. Which at all doesn't distract from fun. I'm early into the game and am wondering whether there is also the mechanic of adaptive difficulty implemented, similar to re4. With that said, I think I'll have to drop this game, because the girl of the protagonist is mostly displayed in lingerie, and for some reason she is too sexy, and I'm feeling horny while playing and after. The game makes me too horny, while there should be no horny there, and frankly I already have an in-game Boner to play with. P.S. It also wouldn't hurt to finally have some ports of more over-the-top Japanese action classics, such as God Hand or Madworld, especially if those are not as horny.

_childDocuments_.review: Game itself is great, I enjoyed it on PS3 and platinumed it with pleasure. Full of dark humour, gameplay is pretty typical for such a game from that era. Garcia is likeable, Johnson brings funny dialogues. Music is top notch (Akira Yamaoka composed soundtrack for this title). In general - it's a fun game to play, which you can finish over the weekend. I'm happy that Shadows of the Damned left 7th generation of consoles and came to modern platforms. What I'm not happy about - is the fact, that this is very lazy and poorly implemented port of the game with assets taken straight away from old consoles (you can tell even by looking at button prompts image quality). There is no resolution option nor framerate change (locked@60). You can't even change such a basic option like full screen to borderless/window. It's straight port of a game from 2011 with console's options left as it is. I can't recommend Shadows of the Damned: Hella Remastered (title should be "Ported") in this state. _childDocuments_.review: So, a new Suda51 game dropped on PC, aaand... it's not the best one, far from it. It was produced by EA, and you can tell. Gone is Suda’s distinctive, classy style, replaced by basic sex jokes seemingly aimed at the average American audience. The style here doesn’t feel as cool; instead, it leaves the impression of something trying too hard to be edgy, which is the opposite of Suda’s usual flair.Gameplay-wise, it feels like a lesser version of The Evil Within 1, with some really annoying gimmicks, silly QTEs, and awful boss fights that overstay their welcome (good luck trying not to get bored to death by the first boss...).But - but - it’s still kind of fun. The combat has that "Mikami" signature style, and the soundtrack is probably one of Yamaoka's most unique works. These two aspects carry the whole game.The PC port is decent - barebones - but it works. You'll need a mod to unlock the framerate (locked at 60 by default) and to adjust the resolution. SpecialK is also required to get HDR working, which looks great with the game’s vibrant colors.

_childDocuments_.review: In the modern day SotD is a refreshing experience: it's a hodge podge range of different elements from a difficult development cycle that demanded extreme compromise from its creators. The game's janky and breaks just often enough to be both a little grating, and a little funny, but underneath the funk and crude humour lies a genuine sincerity and authenticity to the world and its characters. Akin to Lollipop Chainsaw, the crudeness appears to be a misdirection where the sex, gore and bawdiness plays into an underlying tone which, whilst not deep, has more going on than it initially lets on. Garcia's constantly tormented by the Demon King, and the torture and flaunting of his girlfriend in front of him are as much a statement about the Demon King's power, and Paula's helplessness, as it is how he dehumanises all for the sake of his pleasure. Garcia's a sincere and honest man, and though he externalises his love of the overt and bawdy in dialogue and how he dresses, he's also earnestly tender about his love for Paula, as melodramatic as it is. That's just how open and honest a character he is. The game plays upon  Like most of Suda51's work, macho men and beautiful women tend to have more going on beneath the surface. There even appears to be a few DMC 3 references - Mundus, Garcia, Paula and the .The gameplay's serviceable for what it is, and though it lacks the depth you'd associate with older Shinji Mikami projects, it fits with the newer  style shallowness. If you dig into the mechanics there's enough to keep you interested and mixing up your play style - e.g. rolling into enemies removes the enemy's shadow giving you both a defensive and offensive move in one that maintains the pace of combat. I wish you were able to cancel quick turn akin to RE4 for fast 90' angle amendments, that you could revert the Dentist back into the Teethgrinder as an alternative form, and that difficulty achievements stacked, but eh, is what it is.The game's also got costumes which I'd recommend checking out - selected by pressing 'continue' on the menu, selecting your save file, and then amending the costumes in 'costumes'. Whether you're here just for the bawdiness, a bit of tank controlled combat, or for the fairly curious world created, if you're a fan of Suda then this game's worth checking out. As always check out the PC Gaming Wiki for a few quick fixes to widen the game's fov, remove the vignette, etc etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignoring the barebones port aspects, the best way I can describe the game itself is the janky transition from RE4 to The Evil Within mixed with middle school humor.That isn't an insult as I do like the game, but it's a clear 7/10 if I've ever seen one. In so many ways it feels like a PS2 and a PS3 game simultaneously. But I'd still recommend it to anyone who already is interested in it. It at least tries to be something unique and pulls it off well enough and overtly that it's too charming to hate and is only $25 full price.And there's already a community patch that unlocks the fps and fov so that helps a lot to. Otherwise, do not expect the port to be anything other than literally the console experience and lack of settings put on PC.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadows of the Damned: Hella Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, the PC got Shadow of the Damned. To complete the major Grasshopper collection the only 2 games left are Sun, Flower, Rain & Michigan.The remaster lacks graphic options, but as I always play in 1080, it was very comfortable for me. Overall, the graphics are still good thanks to special visual design, so I see no problems with it. However, in some cutscenes, the sound felt a bit flat compared to in game one.The game is great even in 2024 and shows that some game designs are timeless. You can clearly see how Q Hayashida created Flemming as a mix of En from Dorohedoro in terms of position and Shimada Death from Dai Dark in terms of design. Many ideas of bones and darkness would later be realized in Dai Dark.Really wish Suda51, Shinji Mikami, Akira Yamaoka & Q Hayashida would collaborate on some new project. Hopefully, it would be possible.Now I am hyped for the Killer7 Full Edition announcement and the new Grasshopper project. Or maybe God Hand for all modern platforms because it is a great game. Those are the games people need to play more in our modern age.Thank you very much to all the teams working on this project.

_childDocuments_.review: Classic game. I played this on PS3 back in the day. I've been wanting a PC version for a long time, and now we finally have it!This is a very basic port, without graphics options. But it looks fine. It is the original game running at a higher resolution (your native monitor resolution). You can use DLDSR to get better anti-aliasing, but the game is pretty good looking in terms of native image quality. Again, this is the bare minimum in terms of options, but it works and runs well.The game is capped at 62 fps for some reason. I use RTSS to lock it at a smoothly frame paced 60 fps.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadows of the Damned: Hella Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: As a first-time-experiencer, this game blows me away with how fun it is. It's like RE4 meets Suda51's crazy gameplay and storytelling with a (very dope) humorous approach. I've been meaning to play it ever since it came out for the PS3, but finding a copy for a reasonable price was the most challenging. This port is smooth (constant 60 FPS), has skippable cutscenes (great for achievement hunting, which I plan on doing) and retains Yamaoka's badass music unlike the Lollipop Chainsaw port. Now this is a console game through and through, meaning that this port doesn't give any accessibility options; be it windowed support or graphical tweaks aside from gamma adjustment. It only allows you to adjust sensitivity, music and language options. Overall, I wouldn't say it's a lazy port, considering it runs flawlessly so far, no crashes, no bugs. Plus the price is definitely fine for an oldie resurrection. Definitely give this punk game a go if you're on the fence, controller recommended!

_childDocuments_.name: Shadows of the Damned: Hella Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: Does what it says on the can, a solid remaster of one of those overlooked games from the PS360 era.Back in the day I enjoyed Shadows of the Damned for what it was: a functional, competently designed third person shooter riffing on the Resident Evil 4 formula with more straightforward level design and some neat mechanics. If the game was just that it would be a decent 6/10 worth a playthrough, but what elevates it is the world building and sense of humor.It kind of plays out as an Adult Swim parody of the Divine Comedy with tons of dark humor and, believe it or not, legitimaly funny ♥♥♥♥ jokes. That may sound vulgar and, don't get me wrong: it really is, but it goes really well with the buddy movie/road trip dynamic between the two protagonists and the depiction of the underworld the game presents. The sense of humor goes beyond the surface level jokes and dialogs and it actually contributes to building a rendition of hell that is as funny as legitimately interesting, with goat heads as a natural light source and tons of other weird aspects that you'll get to experience during the adventure. It's the world building and the constantly wacky and outlandish ideas where one can feel the involvement of Suda 51 the most. It's also one of those games that really put the extra effort into blending the mechanics, items and collectibles into the narrative and themes, which I also appreciate.Everything contributes to a game that ends up punching well above its weight despite being a pretty basic third person shooter thanks to its wild sense of creativity and how it permeates almost every element that is presented during the experience. Not the best action game ever made, but certainly a very memorable one!
_childDocuments_.name: Shadows of the Damned: Hella Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: A 7/10 Classic from the Xbox 360 era made by Shinji MikamiThink of Resident Evil 4 with some added humour & gothic horror mixed in.The game still holds up really well and game-play is still a tonne of fun. Just to note that this port is fairly barebones when it comes to video configuration which I suspect will disappoint some folks but what I can say it runs great on the Steam Deck without any messing around.60 FPS locked and plays great in handheld mode also.For more, you can see my YouTube Video covering the Steam Deck specifics.

name: Aquanox Deep Descent
detailed_description: Aquanox Deep Descent is a first person underwater vehicle shooter, in which players control a variety of customizable ships to engage in fierce battles in the dystopian deep sea world of Aqua. In the near future the Earth's surface has become uninhabitable. What remains of humankind lives in former mining and research stations, deep below the surface of the sea. Born and raised in the only world we know, the loose network of underwater settlements, torn by the war for resources and dominance between various factions. Take control of a team of highly trained fighter pilots and experience an epic story in the dark world of Aquanox. Send your enemies down to Davy Jones' Locker with well-aimed torpedoes, shrapnel blasts, mines and more in a journey that takes you across the world's oceans and into the deepest trenches of our Earth. Fight - Action-packed vehicle shooter combat that supports a wide variety of play styles   Co-op - 4 player drop-in co-op, with four unique pilots who are all involved in the game story Customize - Choose and upgrade your ships, making them fit your preferred playing style Explore - Discover the deepest corners of the ocean VPP - Classic multiplayer modes like Deathmatch and Team Deathmatch Dogfighting The Original Series Aquanox Deep Descent is a re-imagining of both the gameplay and world of the original AquaNox-series. The Aquanox-series has its roots in the game Archimedean Dynasty (German: Schleichfahrt), released in 1996, which was followed by AquaNox in 2001 and AquaNox 2: Revelation in 2003. All games are vehicle-based shooters set in a dystopian future where mankind has had to flee the surface and live in underwater stations in the oceans. The AquaNox games were powered by the groundbreaking KRASS Engine that lead to the popular benchmark AquaMark.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game for the coop-campaign, as coop playable games are somewhat rare. We got really into it and had lots of fun for a few hours. The bad surprise came the next time we wanted to pick back up and loaded into the game. To find out that the coop-guest does not get saved, all their progress, items and money are just gone. According to the devs, this is what they wanted and had planned.If they don't want to save the coop player, they could have at least "cloned" the host inventory+money to the coop guestz player, instead of starting them over from nothing. Should have been easy to do that, right? Well we haven't touched the game since.

_childDocuments_.review: (ADD) is a semi-open world shooter set underwater, after the world endured the "Last Day" - an apocalyptic event where most of humanity perished and the rest was forced into oceanic depths. Players impersonate Kaelen, one of the chosen few to be preserved in stasis for centuries, now woken up by unclear circumstances. After a dangerous escape, he and his companions - left without most memories - decide to embark on a quest to find the answers about their past, forging alliances and facing many dangers along the way.🟩 🟥 🎮 Gameplay is divided into Exploration, Combat and Station Business.Is performed using a DSF, which means submersible vehicle. Roaming the oceanic floors has no movement restrictions, as the ships can go in any direction just as airplanes, just with more friction. The world is divided into sectors linked together by jump-gates, some of which cannot be used until a certain point in the story. Each zone often has an Outpost to dock into for supplies an d quests. There are scattered piles of loot which give out crafting resources or rarely weapons and lore data. There is no fast travel and the pacing of movement is rather slow, which along with backtracking can be a chore.Is performed in a first-person fashion, using up to two weapons simultaneously on all ships, while also turrets or secondary abilities if available. fights mainly focus on dodging / strafing away from enemy fire while dishing out damage - too bad enemies are not nearly enough competent to do this reliably most of the time. ADD uses cheap tricks like spawning a mass of enemies around Kaelen out of nowhere, or cramping fights into shooting gallery style tunnels to create more difficulty. There is a good variety of guns and abilities or use, though the really good ones are few and outclassing all others, which is disappointing. Enemies feel repetitive and generic, with three or four archetypes of fighting styles across the board, the rest just change weapons or ship models, each faction has no uniqueness to them at all. Bosses are just utterly annoying trash, recycled ad nauseam - and bullet sponges. The fact players can spam healing indefinitely as long as they can craft some is cheesy and unbalanced.Is done at any outpost. Players can buy and sell resources at the market, craft ammunition and healing, upgrade their ships modules or buy new ones. This gameplay part is simple and works as expected. At stations one can also interact with NPCs to receive primary and secondary quests to complete in the world. At no point there will be enough money, even by completing everything, to get all upgrades and weapons; which is unsatisfying. Some NPCs are there just for lore's sake and are really forgettable though, often even sharing the same models or voices. Again, recycled stuff, yay.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR 6/10, adequate 6 DoF combat game, some flawed mechanics and absurd story, but looks half decent and some what enjoyable.Longer thoughts.With fond memories of the originals and Archamedian Dynasty, I backed this on Kickstarter.The end product...is a bit of a let down.But, ignore the outright stupid things people have said about this game.(I've given this a positive review to counter balance them a little and because Steam doesn't have a "Meh" rating yet)"It should be a mobile game" - Sure, try controlling it on a fricking Samsung/Iphone!"It's too murky, where are the sun rays" - It's the bottom of the ocean, what did you expect?"The AI is rubbish" - To an extent yes, but never game breakingly so.The graphics and atmosphere are pretty good, with some nice touches like water seeping through damage cracks in your canopy.Every ship and every cockpit upgrade looks pleasingly different and can be enjoyed, with a pointless free look mode.Sound and music are also decent, lots of good muted thumps and clangs of things hitting the hull.Game play is okay, very much built around a console controller so keep your flight sticks away and don't expect any exciting dogfighting.Be ready for lots of 6DoF strafing around foes, chucking fire at each other, spamming special abilities and using repair power ups.There are some immersion breaking things (hah, water pun!), like the narrative is that you are a squadron.You aren't, it's only ever one of you.And instant spawning hostiles, right in front of you, inside a sealed facility, with no in setting mechanic for it, is just crappy.There is a rudimentary salvage and credits based economy, which to be honest feels a bit bolted on.Sure, you can scour wrecks and on occasion will find special weapons, but they are barely worth the effort.The range of ships if reasonable, but the fact you get them at set points, along with unlocking their upgrades, further highlights how pointless the economy system is.And there is one big flaw with the weapons setup.You can switch any weapon out on the fly, in case you run out of ammo and don't have time to craft more (you being able to craft ammo inside your fighter, is kinda stupid).But, because you can't scrap or sell any weapons you don't like or are just plain redundant, you will end up cycling through junk to get what you actually want to use.How your fighter is carrying 12 different guns at once, on switchable mounts, is beyond me.Better option would be to ditch all of the resource and economy and just restrict you to carrying either a pair of weapons (with cool down or reload delay) or 4 different weapons and that's it.The only really bad part of the game, is the plot.Not just because it's fairly predictable sci fi bilge, but it's also badly told.Factions pop up with little explanation or back story, same with science and setting stuff.Your characters possess knowledge they could not possibly have and NPC's know things about you for no apparent reason.There are a handful of fairly dull side missions and totally pointless dialogue choices, which have no effect on game play, ending or even mission order.And to cap if all off, your best of the best type main characters, are just really, really dumb and unlikeable.The finale will leave you pretty cold, as there is no real resolution and you will have developed no emotional attachment to the characters or story.Maybe get it when heavily discounted, play it through once, then forget about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aquanox Deep Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I bought that game hoping for a good underwater/exploration/adventure game, I finished it just now, and unfortunately, it was lacking in every way.The world design: Aqua is boring. Especially if I compare it to Subnauticas many biomes. Aquanox's plot takes you across multiple oceans all over the world, however if you've seen the first zone, you've seen them all. Always the same design, again and again, for everything, zone; bases; ships. Furthermore, I know Aquanox is supposed to be pretty bleak, but constant poor lighting gets taxing after a while.Gameplay: My friend, do yourself a favour and download a trainer so that you can have unlimited boost, the game is a slog. IA is cyberbrain dead. The game might be difficult at the beginning but ships become OP fast. And the missions basically amount to fetch and scan. Much, Much more customisation for the subs would have been appreciated, they're basically the pillar of the game.Plot: Serious Sam is more engaging. No, seriously.Final word: What I, as a gamer expect from a game (especially a solo campaign game) is for it to create the impulse/interest to want to follow its plot to the end, for that, the gameplay and the plot has to evolve throughout the game to keep it from stagnating and keep play on their toes. Aquanox is supposed to be this dangerous post apocalyptic place where we fight for survival. I didn't get that feeling. So random steam dude and dudette that bothered to read this review, i advise you to pass this game and look elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Aquanox Deep Descent

_childDocuments_.review: I'll get this out of the way since some have the wrong idea about this game...this is an arcade shooter so don't go expecting some kind of underwater submarine simulator with realistic physics.If you played the previous Aquanox games or Archimedian Dynasty, then you will also like this.It recreates the great atmosphere of the previous games and adding it's own flavour to it, but still trying to keep things old-school.To some it might seems too old school and not exciting enough since it lacks the open world aspect. The gameplay consists mostly of getting missions from someone on a station and then doing those missions in a linearish fashion and on the way you are free to explore the current area you are in and collect crafting materials or shoot thugs and the likes.With the mentioned crafting materials you can either craft yourself ammo and submarine parts or trade them at various stations you come across your travels.Combat is pretty straightforward shooting with your typical assault weapons, shotguns, snipers and rocket launchers and other tools at your disposal. The enemy AI is not particularly smart as it is aggressive and enemies tend to gang up on you so you got to keep moving constantly to avoid fire which makes the combat hectic at times.Story tells the tale of 4 individuals who have been awakened from cryosleep, have lost their memories and need to find out what is going on. If you play a solo game, you only control one of them even though the other 3 are with you in dialogue but are of no help in combat. If you on the other hand play with your friends via co-op then they will take the other 3 individuals spot and can help you with your endeavours.Have not finished the game yet, but after about 17 hours in the BETA and about 10 hours on the final version, I'd recommend this. Yes people have different opinions and some can see straight away it's not for them, but I would suggest playing this for a few hours at least and see what it has to offer....you might be surprised.

_childDocuments_.review: Usually I don't write reviews before I am done with the game, BUT: - You fire a shot, it does not even create a flash of light in the cockpit. Aquanox 1...dynamic lights. You saw it illuminating the walls, ground...other ships even.- The loading screen says AVOID OPEN AREAS....which? Its all tunnels.- The fishes look all the same and like made in 1996.- No plankton or air bubbles, rays of light making the scenery more dynamic.- No enemies outside of missions...you travel to a gate...slowly through water, with nothing else to do.- Not enough weapons. I miss the plasma, the laser gatling, the sizzler!! Mortar...- The UI is a pain. Side mission activation with SPACE key only, mouse will not do.- Story is ok, voices are ok...you want to go on and find out what happened. Good one!- Enemies...they all just hover in front of you. I am really wondering, WHAT took you guys so long? No dog fights, no allies distracting the enemies creating a bit of locomotion...nothing.- Explosions look ok, should be more like IMPLOSIONS though, like in that last  Why?? Under water!!It feels emotionless, loveless...I really looked forward to play this one, could not wait to download it. But this is really notworth the long wait guys!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mad. Aquanox was one of the first games I remember getting as a kid, nearly 20 years ago now, and by sheer coincidence, I've had the good fortune of playing through the first one again not more than a couple weeks ago (at time of writing this review), and loved it's smart writing & appealing visuals. THQ Nordic clearly didn't do the same at any point throughout this game's development cycle. Complete spoilers below, so TLDR: Deep Descent is bland, visually uninteresting, boring from both a gameplay & storytelling perspective, and is a pale shadow of the original game, adding in huge, unnecessary plot points that actively derail Deep Descent's claim as a prequal to the original. Gameplay-wise, you have a million weapons all strapped to your ship at once, speed is the only ship metric that matters, and the claim that you can customize your ship is a complete lie - you upgrade your parts as soon as they become available, with no choices or trade offs between them. Prepare yourself:-Why does this game look so boring? Why did you go for the darker, more depressing atmosphere of Aquanox 2, rather than the vibrant, soulful feel of the original? Why do all the environments look more or less the same? Why do all the faction ships look similar to each other, and not visually diverse ones like the base game? Why can I not tell who's shooting at me from a distance without the help of the HUD text telling me who's who?-Why are all your characters bland and soulless? Why is everyone a generic gruff, hardened soldier/survivor type? Remember in the original, how your main character was a bit emotionally deadened, and everyone teased him for it? Remember how wide-eyed Lisa & Piccolini, and drug-loving Harper helped offset your seriousness? Remember how you could write areas like the Tornado Zone, that could fit both no-nonsense warlords like Ivan King, AND way off the top characters like Jones, the king of drugs, into the same space? Remember when you could write characters with soul... or who could voice act something beyond serious lines?-Why is the story so generic? Wake up from cryo in a ruined world (*cough*Fallout 4*cough*), a gruff stranger saves you but is reserved and has a dark past, the main villain turns out to be closely related to the person you befriended in the beginning, and there's some magical McGuffin that'll magically put everything back together. I seriously called the "biont queen is actually your friend's wife" part from a mile away, and just about every other plot twist for that matter... except for the part where you introduced aliens into a series that's made no mention of them previously, and then DIDN'T LET US SEE THEM IN THE END. -Why are there essentially no dialogue choices except for say 3 in the entire game? Why make us manually select dialogue options like it's an RPG, but only make one available at any given time? Why not just have the characters talk by themselves, like in the other games? Why is the ending so unsatisfying? Why does it feel like you guys suddenly ran out of budget, and/or patience?-Why are none of the gameplay elements of the first game reflected into this one? Why is the Vendetta called the Stingray, the useless ground-based weapon from the second game? Why can your starting scout ship carry 76 torpedoes, when the heaviest bomber in the first one could only carry something like 18? Why do you have magical, instantly-regenerating health & shield packs? Why install the cheap "last breath" cheat system that instantly saves/heals you, at low health, and regenerates after like 20 seconds? Why is EMP virtually unavoidable, and massively crippling compared to every other ability? Why do the AI aim so badly sometimes, but is pinpoint accurate at other times? WHY IS EVERY GUN IN THE GAME ON YOUR SHIP AT ONCE? Remember how the previous games had limits for that exact reason? Why do you make us cycle through 14 different guns at once to get to the one we want? Why do you keep the outdated spare guns around when we have more powerful ones available that completely invalidate them? Why is the upwards thrust so sensitive that half the time when I just wanna move upwards a bit, I end up using a boost and smashing my ship into a ceiling? Why is speed the only ship metric that matters for everything that isn't the final boss fight? Why is the beginning ship the most optimal one to use for 90% of the game? Why do the bulkier ships have their upgrade availability gimped so badly?-Why is there basically no mention of resources or logistics in this game, beyond scavenging? Why are there no companies like EnTrOx or the Neopolis Drakes around, or even the scantest whispers of them? Why is every ship a combat ship... where are the transports of the original? Where are the ships that are supposed to be scavenging resources from the environment? Why are there no civilian ships roaming around? Why is everyone you encounter directly tied to your quest... why does it feel like the entire world revolves around you, instead of you just being a part of it?-Remember how you were gifted a ship in the beginning of the first game, and this was a huge deal, because it's cost was more than you'd make throughout the entire game? So why are we given like 6 ships for free in this one, with nobody batting an eye? Why do we not even have to buy them like in the first game? Why do most of them come so late into the game that they don't matter? Why do they appear suddenly in our inventories, with no pretext or mention of it by anyone? Hell even the second game had missions specifically dedicated to you getting new ships, and made a big deal of doing so-Why are there very little mentions of politics in this game? Remember how the corporations were doing shady things behind the scenes, like outlawing sleep, partially because the world's so strapped for resources & manpower? Remember when you could have discussions with all sorts of people, from warlords to random tourists, all who actually had opinions? And remember how there were a few reoccurring joke characters to balance things out, like Jones, the Neopolis waiter, and the one scientist lady who kept mistaking you for her assistant? Remember humor in general? -Why are you so stingy with upgrade availability? Why slowly build up the upgrades for the bigger ships, only to unceremoniously dump the last 33% of their final upgrades on us at the final mission? Why not let us buy them at our own leisure, but make doing so more costly for the earlier stages of the game to balance things out? Why BS us with marketing material saying we can completely customize our ships, when in reality all you can do is buy straight upgrades? Why are there no trade-off upgrades/side-grades? -Why is the world building so inconsistent? Why do the bionts feel like they're a pest threat, instead of the lurking superpower that rarely showed themselves in the previous game? Why do the bionts pilot slick, ultra-techy ships in this game, when in the previous ones they were basically reconstituted scrap heaps? Why do ships travel through both man-made & alien warp gates... why are we not using the Dipol Drive system from the first game? Why is a young Emerald Flint introduced in this game, but every settlement is like a pitstop? For reference, Neopolis is a hamlet in this game, but Flint is like 10 years old... so you're telling me that in the span of say 20-25 years, Neopolis grow into a mega city, and both the enormous Gulf Stream turbine field & the Brainfire Station are constructed in that time, when the world's clearly so strapped for resources? I don't think so, budThere's probably more that I'm missing, but I think I've ranted enough. In short, this game's at best boring, unbalanced, & uninteresting... and at worst it's a bit of an abomination, scantly tied to the original and by no means a satisfying prequel by any metric. Stay far away from this one, and try the original instead.2/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a backer of this game since its inception ... what I wanted was Aquanox 3, what I got was years and years and years of waiting, radio silence from the devs, project almost being scrapped and ultimately a lot of money wasted on a VERY mediocre game.Let's sum it upGraphics: Not bad, not great, definitely not year 2020World: Single zones connected via jump gates, no interconnected world, nothing to really explore, lifelessEnemies: There are 2 types of enemies - those in subs like you ... and nanofauna. The subs are at least somewhat interesting to fight, they swerve and avoid your shots, but they're only ever a challenge in large numbers and that's what the game tries to constantly throw at you. The nano fauna are mutated sharks and mantas and eels ... they just charge at you. Their movements look unnatural, they have terrible hit boxes and are just annoying to deal with. There's also a big boss whale in the game that you have to fight multiple times ... the same way each time. Enemies also just randomly spawn in in front or behind you. The AI is stupid.Gameplay: It's standard "Descent" gameplay. Ego shooter in floating space. There's not much room for flashy plays or sneaky suprise attacks. You're immediately spotted when the game wants to and there's barely any cover to outplay your enemies. The standard approach is thus just fire and forget and use healing and shield items frequently.You will go from station to station on your quest ... and you can also do side quests, but why? They're just boring "destroy x" quests and often not even voiced. Just filler content.During the course of the story you will unlock new subs and new sub parts. I've never switched from the original sub, because all other subs were subpar and most of them were so much slower and had less "dodges" (which you can use to propel yourself forwards, thus making traversal quicker) ... the game is slow enough as it is with you just aimlessly travelling from point A to B. When I finally unlocked all upgrades (automatically starting the last mission) I was no longer allowed to dock anywhere to change ship and equip them, so ... thanks for that.Since there is no point in playing after the story is complete anyway that's just a total waste of space ...Apart from main and side missions there is no content in the game. You can find resources in the game world ... very unnaturally. But there's no trading, no sense of free roaming, no conflicts, no pirating, nothing. Even the mission variety is just "destroy this" or "collect this", that's it. A few missions were somewhat fun, but only because the rest were so terribly designed. Hint: If your idea of good mission design is to start at point A, go to point B in order to reach C in order to reach D, then spend 1 minute collecting something, only to make the exact same trip back, wasting 15 minutes, then you're a fool.Obligatory difficulty spike for the final boss included of course.Story: Started out okay, ended in typical quasi-religious, quasi-environmentalist nonsense. The characters remained faceless throughout the game. The only real persona was Okabe, a friendly captain, but even he wasn't exactly "great" and his story, my god. The ending just felt completely rushed and made NO sense at all.Presentation: Dialogue is either just in-game and frequently cuts off, because of invisible triggers you can't know about, like reaching a certain location before you should ... Otherwise you just speak via unanimated pictures to people on ships and stations. Nobody really has anything interesting to say. The story is just contrived and you will forget about pretty much everyone very soon.Where's the variety in mission design? Where are the cool, memorable characters? Where's the interesting game world you can explore? Where's trading (no, selling resources you find in the world isn't trading)? Where's your own armada or a bigger ship perhaps even? Where are the interesting underwater battles between the factions? Where is the point in this game? Why are "we" supposed to be a squad of 4 people, but you're only alone? So many ideas just rushed to get some sort of final product out that got delayed over and over again anyway (or rather just dragged on).If Aquanox was your inspiration, then what is this? Heck, even the music sucks.I'm not saying never play this game, but if you're not really looking for an underwater ego shooter, skip it ... or wait at least for a deep discount. Disappointment. Play time is about 8 hours for the main quest by the way.
