_childDocuments_.review: This is another example of "i wish there was a maybe rating".Preface - loved all of the older aquanox games (Archimedean Dynasty,  Aquanox 1+2) and not feeling this one, thus the mixed aspect/not liking it.TLDR: another game suffering from the 4 player co-op disease, if you have mates that want to play this. It will be a fun hour or two, otherwise i would give it a skip unless its heavily discounted/sale (50% at least)Gameplay - gone are the old levels, and now the game focuses on a world to explore, which would be decent IF it didnt consist of underwater caverns 99% of the time with an aspect of scavenging, which makes me feel like im playing an ubisoft lite sandbox.Ship movement: feels (and is) slower then all previous titles meaning its slower to drive forward and avoid weapons fire (they did improve the 3D movement/strafing though to compensate).Weapons: rely on crafting and scavenging for ammo, as well as a significantly reduced variety (gone are the infinite ammo vendetta's, plasma's and entertaining weapons)Combat: my style in previous games were like a jouster, i would fly by, drift/engine off, unload doom and then turn around and repeat. This game forces me to play uncomfortably close to the enemies (due to weapon travel speed, ship movement speed and level design). Also, did i mention the basic cannons have ammo?Environment: Do you want underwater cave A or B? all jokes aside it does look pretty, but its missing the cities and filtered sunlight rays of the previous games to convey the aspect of humans adapting to survive underwater with the surface out of reach due to factors.Ship customisation: it falls into aquanox 2 territory with only a couple of different subs, HOWEVER in order for variety they allow you to equip and upgrade different parts of the sub to help with making it your own vehicle. For most people the progression will be lacking as they will just update their current sub to be the "little sub that could" instead of exploring different options.Story: while i cant comment on endgame (both avengers due to reasons and this game) due to time played, the story is standard insert yourself here, you were a military/merc/fighter that was put on ice with your squad for reasons. You wake up with no memory of why or where you are other than a "follow me" by the person that pulled you out of your cold embrace. You then join up with a ship and form a rag tag group of mercs to do stuff until you recover memories (got tired of playing after this point due to character interactions, story + gameplay and stopped).Overall: if you have played and enjoyed previous aquanox games, this wont feel right and i would've recommended the devs used  a different name then aquanox. Single player feels like a chore ticking off every quest/map marker. Squad/4 player co-op seems to be fun for an hour or two unless people get REALLY invested in the game or setting (both of which feel weak and lacking to me).I would give it an 6/10 as it is above average, works, no bugs and a small bit of fun, however it lacks the characters and story that previous aquanox games had.PS: if you made it this far you deserve an e-cookie

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Archimedean Dynasty, I was bitterly disappointed by the Aquanox games.  All of the subtleties of the original were wiped away.  AD had great upgrade system, which allowed for more tactical play.  Stealth elements that actually worked, where all you had to be was quieter than the enemy, and they would look right through you, allowing for ambushing tactics.All of that was wiped out, among many other things.Then I hear of this, after the Kickstarter ended.  And while I was annoyed about that at the time, I now consider that a relief of sorts, as I would almost certainly pledged more than I payed for this.The graphics are great, really well done.  But sadly that's about it.  I remember seeing these preview screenshots of this deeply customisable ship building screen, where different parts can be swapped out, each one having its own stat modifiers.  This looked better than anything we had before.Come release, all of that has gone.  No stealth that I can see, though I did have some successes from approaching boats from the rear, they just seem to know you are there by magic inside a certain range.Active or passive sonar?  Nope, none of that either.When you do get the new ship with turrets, which is very early one, can you command them to target your target, fire free etc.  Nope, not even that.  AD had that and it came out 25 years ago.Anyone who has played AD will well remember that mission where you had to enter the currents of a canyon lined with turrets.  You had to power the engines off, and drift pass them with active sonar off.  This is a dumbed down shooter, just like the original Aquanox sequels were.I honestly think, and have for about 10 years or more now, that gaming is going backwards, and its in part because of multi-platform releases like this.  They have to be dumbed down to support a console audience.  How can a game of 25 years ago be far superior to the dross that gets released now?  It's not talent, as you can see that from A:DD.  They have programming talent, and clearly talented graphical designers.  Sadly, what they also had in spades was very poor design decisions, and perhaps an agenda to meet a certain demographic.Only those that have played AD will know my pain.  Also take a look at Subwar 2050 if you want some underwater action.  Don't both looking for nuanced gameplay here.Such an opportunity to be had here, and they totally dropped the ball.  So disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: I read several reviews before buying the game, all telling the same: the game´s bad, dont buy it. Bought it anyway since I am a huge fan of the first part of the series Schleichfahrt / Archimedean Dynasty... Now a couple of hours into the game I must accept: nostalgia is a bad adviser. Shame on me.The game is quite stripped down concerning features and general scale. But Aquanox its not a triple A title. So I guess thats ok. They nailed the atmosphere and the general wibe of the game. I played the game on easy, since I am only interested into the story, the world and the atmosphere. So I really REALLY wanted to play this. But the gameplay is sooo bad, it broke the game for me to the point I had to stop playing. My major complaints in the gameplay are:- Enemies spawn out of nowhere 5 meters before (or even better behind) your ship, if you trigger a script point. - All enemies always fly straight to you, stop 10 meters away and shot straight at you. Thats the complete mechanic behind enemies. No dogding, no manuvers, no nothing.- As a consequence there are no dog fights and no real diving action. The fighting is just a pain in the arse. The standard fight looks like this: fly to a checkpoint, 10 enemies spawn out of nothing, all enemies start shooting at you,  you run for your life behind any obstacle (brute forcing doesnt work, even on easy). In many cases the flashmob will eradicate you within moments.This gameplay is zero fun and often really frustrating. I really can´t get my head around, how the original Schleichfahrt from 1996 !!! had far better gameplay. Thats just ridiculous... Budget limitations cant explain that.Pro Tip for any devs reading this: google "core gameplay loop" and start reading.

_childDocuments_.review: Aquanox Deep Descent is the attempt to revive an older franchise. It began with a game named Archimedean Dynasty, released in 1996. 2 Sequels followed, under the new brand name of Aquanox.All of those games were quite similar to the "three degrees of freedom" space simulation games that came up roughtly at the same time, but tried to put themselves apart by not going up, but rather down. All three might be considered aaa titles considering the amount of work and effort, as well as content they provided at the time. Even though their success probably fell short of that.Aquanox: Deep Descent tries to be a prequel to all three original stories, as well as a reenvision of the world they created. It contains many more modern takes, especially on gameplay and presentation, while attempting to retain the feel and flavor of the older parts. The maps have grown. Movement is semi-free, permitting exploration of different maps with different visuals and highlights. Fallen ships and random pirate locations invite the player to take a look around in a vibrant world with many interesting details. Mission design feels immediately nostalgic to people who have played the prequels, ships feel distinctly different and can be upgraded as the story progresses to stay useful throughout the game. Besides having to fight the resistance of the water, making your first ships quite clunky you ride currents to quietly go around enemies and watch out for your surroundings as building debris from the sunken cities are just as dangerous to your hull as the walls of thight canyons and undersea caves. Gameplay (in singleplayer, as I have not yet tried multiplayer) is good, although sometimes the difficulty jumps up or down a bit too much (the game stays comfortably playable even at hard difficulty, though). The story is short if you are used to Story RPGs and even compared to some shooters, with 6-8 hours of gameplay if you rush through the missions without paying mind to sidequests or exploration. It is also a bit predictable if you pay attention. However it is not badly told and references a lot to the other games, which is fun for fans of the series and should make new players take interest in the pre-"sequels". Aqanox: Deep Descent is not an AAA title. It is the attempt of a small team of original developers and aquanox-fans-turned-game-designers to tell a new story in the universe, on a shoestring budget (for todays standards), while balancing amount and quality of their content. I hereby thank the development team for delaying their game for almost a year to work hard on polish and presentation.The game has become, to me, a trip of pure nostalgia to one of the first games I ever played, and I loved every minute I played (and will probably love it some more). It still has unpolished spots, AI enemies, story and amount of content fall short compared to modern titles. But a player can immediately feel the devotion that went into this project. And I sincerely hope that we can see more of it in the future. After all, the world of Aqua is vast and has barely been explored yet.To those interested in the Prequels: Aquanox and Aquanox Revelation are available in the Steam store. The games are outdated and might need some tinkering, but will run on modern windows based computers. In order to get everything working, check out their respective guides and the steam forums. Most problems are covered there. If you want to go to the roots, Archimedean Dynasty (Schleichfahrt for the german speakers out there) is available on GoG, including a prepared Dosbox environment and lots of help to get it running. Story-wise it is the best part of the series, so I can immediately recommend it to anyone. Just keep in mind it is almost 25 years old, so don't expect your warthog flight stick to immediately work with it.

_childDocuments_.review: --Caveat Emptor, for Steam review length restriction reasons, I will TRY to put the rest of it in replies, I may fail spectacularly, however--Alright, this is going to be long, because I am... seething.If you had been like me and you've been waiting for Angel Tears, if you had been like me and wanted a bigger, greater Aqua, this is not it. This is hardly Aqua. The red flags in the game make you extremely suspicious if you had played the original trilogy. So, the first segment of my review is for those who had played the original three.The Archimedean Dynasty was a decent narrative, even if a little dull, but only because of lack of voiceover, that would help you digest the walls of text easier. Aquanox fixed it, bringing along not only a lot of good voice talent, but also very deep, colorful and memorable characters. Both the Archimedean Dynsaty and Aquanox would leave you with something to think about, was never afraid of articulating the conflicting points of view, wasn't afraid to show everyone had their tendencies, weaknesses and delusions. Leo van der Waal? You would think he's but a greedy tycoon, a shark of the waters of Aqua, except it just turns out he found the controls to an orbital WMD and what did he try to do? Defend it from everyone else getting their hands on it with his very own life. Even if he had failed, his motive was not selfish, because he knew if it were to fall in anyone's hands, the consequences would be catastrophic and he was right. Sool? There's every reason to hate him, but you can understand why he had the charisma to sway people to his side. Dopamine Harper? He's avaricious, but he also understands that he's nothing without his team having his back, nonetheless it's best to take his opinion with a block of salt, because he in the end values money more than any other consideration.Additionally Aqua had it's own red herrings, that you had to be wise about. But let's move on. Then there's Aquanox 2: Revelation. The Aquanox 2 experience was depressing for many reasons, but nonetheless the game was identifiable as still Aqua. The worst parts of A2 were the pretence of balance, the absence of big battles, the story was limp and had it's own major plot holes. Which is why Deep Descent stands on very poor footing in terms of writing, as it clearly takes the majority of the lore from Revelation and yet fails to stay in line within the lore set by the A2, Let's just forget McGregor for plot convenience, shall we?-The first gripe is the fauna. Aqua is a pretty dead planet. You have small species, plankton and of course sediment. Crustaceans and sharks only being introduced lately into the menus of an Aqua resident, through the contributions of genetic scientists playing G*d. Humanity is constantly struggling to keep these ecosystems alive.-No word about EnTrOx... Oh, you know, just the company that held the sole monopoly for methane hydrate, or "burning ice" as Sergei Chang has put it, which EnTrOx after receiving a dose of democracy started to distribute evenly across all factions. So, no word about ENERGY shortage or underwater current farms. No word about how EnTrOx held the SOLE MONOPOLY on the jumpship technology and for the longest time being the only ones with capability of dipole jumps, in other words, TRANSPORT issues were discarded for plot convenience, or rather gameplay inconvenience. And lastly, the OXYGEN issue, something that is also a valuable comodity and pressures of the depths making everyone rely on HeliNOx gas, which are the only mixture that allows anyone to breathe in the insane depths of Aqua. Oh and also, not even the throat implants? Ones that are vital for human survival. I'm sure being "cryos" from the past are exempt to breathing issues.-The EnTrOx point actually has something else to point out - the original trilogy, the first two games in particular would always try to explain the life in Aqua through technological means, basing itself on real world physics, science even the sociology if you take into the account to take a look at the extreme poverty of the majority of Aqua's population. HeliNOx is an actual gas and divers who dive particularly deep use it to avoid decompression sickness. It is theorised that dipole pulses can actually be used for... Teleportation or if you feel more comfortable saying so - jumps. Then there's synapses, Extremely Low Frequency, etc, etc. none of it is mentioned in Deep Descent. We had ELF since possibly the 60s if not before that, using massive antennas to communicate with the nuclear submarines, but certainly, the game set in pre-Archimedean Dynsty era will have much better technology than that, that'll be discarded for no reason at all in favor of ELF. Which you really should read about, by the way, it kind of drives the locals near it insane in best of cases, however they always have a spike of Leukemia cases.-Actually, speaking of technology - what about the Machina Antarctica? Basically an entire faction IN THE ANTARCTIC that has existed in all three games, that are basically dedicated scientists?-What in the name of Fudd's Gunshop Blue Falcon ammo is Atlantian Alliance? Why did it have the necessity of being Atlantian Federation's predecessor? It's not even explained how did they change from Alliance to a Federation. Same goes for the IPF. And Shogunate is 404 not found.-Remind me again why do Bionts need human pilots to their ships if it is canon that the wreckage of their ships reassemble themselves if it has not been completely DISINTEGRATED, hence battlefield cleanups are absolutely necessary? They just need shards of ships, not necessarily a pilot. Unless the Biont Bomber looks inviting to you. Or maybe you recall their ships looking like flying pieces of wreckage, making them indistinguishable if they really try to hide?-Lastly even Flint's connection to Nemo doesn't add up. Flint was a genetic experiment, that was spliced with dolphin DNA, he also had test tube sisters Ruby and Sapphire (IF I remember the name of the second sister correctly). It was why it was so funny when Mad Sam Korhonen posited that he may have raped and impregnated his mother (which is a test tube). Having said that, Flint was well aware of who he was and who his parents were, the way the "little" him talks doesn't make sense in that regard, even if those concepts needed to be taught to him, he would of not put things the way he did. The epilogue cutscene also doesn't sound like Flint at all. Emerald "Deadeye" Flint was hardly ever edgy or serious, if anything he was easy going and would usually carry a good sense of humor and wit. And when he would become serious, that's when he would sound intimidating. The way he talked to Nemo if they were as close as that doesn't add up.-There's more plot holes than in the roads in Michigan, but these are the most egregious ones.

Just to give you that added "pound your desk in frustration difficulty". THERE'S MORE! instead of having to BUY or BUILD your new sub design what if we just GIVE it to you?!4) Weapons that are nearly identical in damage! because who hates having a FAVORITE weapon but someone else's is superior in range, or damage, or some silly thing like that?!5) Truly unique biomes! but not so "unique" that you get lost in the environment, because we wouldn't want you getting sidetracked from your missions. _childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, the only thing that is good about the game is the name and the fond memories of the old games in the francize. The story is so bad a highschool student could have written a better one as homework, the combat is incredibly repetitive and boring, weapons are dull, ship designs are ok, visually, but have very little impact in gameplay and the only way the designers thought they could make something challenging was to spawn enemy subs right on top of you, while you were already fighting 3 or 4 enemies. I was close to the ending, but I just couldn't convince myself to waste more time on such a failure of a game.Buy literally anything else, except this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Waited 5 years for this game to release.It got a good story, great lore, good graphics. Gameplay itself is OK, not great, but still fun.If you play a little longer (~6-7h) you'll get really great ships that are WAY more fun due to better agility and speed, weapons with more bang and the story gets a boost and the graphics and missions are tuned up.It's not an AAA game but fun for a mission based shooter :)- The game is not as good as Schleichfahrt was, but an OK succecssor to Aquanox 1 & 2.- The voice actors are good, even in German.- Graphics miss one or two things like global illumination and lighting effects on the surroundings. The water effects and deep-sea-feeling is well done.- Level design is good in terms of visuals, but a bit repetitive from time to time. Later on in the game the levels look vastly better and immersion is nice.- Enemy AI is nearly nonexistent. There are no dogfights as in the previous games. I hope this will be sorted out in an update, but my hopes are not high with THQ Nordic (aka JoWood).

_childDocuments_.review: Simple Answer - no it has not.TL;DR at the bottomIt's an ok game.It has nice gameplay. The zipping arround in your spacecraft/submarine is on par with aquanox - or even G-Police if anyone remembers that (and that was on the Jupiter moon of Kallisto!)The maps are gorgeous.The mystery to get from a to b and explore stuff is there and that is nice.the cavesystems are interesting... butBut is it really Archimedean Dynasty/Aquanox?No... definetly no.The original game from 1997 didn't introduce any magical beings from outer space to judge humanity.The reason humanity lived in aqua was just coz the surface got destroyed.The Polar Ice melted and everything is underwater now and the surface is uninhabitable.End of story.In the original game box (yes there were cardboard boxes back then) it had a brief history of the world of aqua.The history was in a booklet and about 4 pages long.The Devs back there really had their ♥♥♥♥ together.Neopolis for example was a big underwater city, and not a 'station'here have a look at thatIt had no Jump portals and super magic space portals to get from on part of the aquasphere to the next.well yes it had 'jump stars' which were in generel just harbors for the jump ships, which just had a special engine (dipol engine) that made the ship go fast in open water, but it still needed a few days to get across the ocean.nothing too wild.it all kind of made sense and was pretty much doable with todays (or even 1997s) science and engineering level.(i'll put the history of the world of aqua at the bottom....)not much in this game makes any snse.What really made me want to quit right there was, when i had to ... ok spoiler territoryalso rant! the only thing that made this game playable for me after that point was, that i imagined it to be somewhere else.on another planet.maybe naboo from star wars, or that planet from subnautica 4546BThen it kind of made some sense.This game does not feel anything like the world Archimedean Dynasty.As i said, it's an ok game. With gorgeous level design. but it does not get the world right.Aquanox at least had the game universe correct, even if it introduced new enemies from an 'hollow' earth and some major fish monsters.Just look at these videos from the original game and you have to admit that the franchise kind of jumped the shark with this one... or even aquanox 2 did it...tbh, this would've been better aquanox 3, and should've taken on the story of aquanox 2 which had it's major cliffhanger back in 2003.and here we have the manual of the game witht the history of course.in german - but google translate will get it right for you.I find it kind of sad, that a fanproject has the history and the universe more correct than a game dev studio with people involved whos only job it is to get this stuff right.Please respect the IP.This game only makes sense if you take it, and put it in its own universe on another planet, but not earth.The Marianas trench for example has a real big power plant in the original game ;) not some Mystery science station.Here we have a map of aqua, with the stations of the gameworld of AD and AquanoxI really want to like the game as part of the aquaverse... but i can not... and that makes me sad.TL;DRsummaryBut why the Thumbs down?All of this has nothing to do with the world of aqua, and it also makes the mistake that even George Lucas did not do with Han Solo and desecrate the body of .And i'm for sure not gonna pay 10 Euros to get the Video that makes me link everything together.It makes me sad.I will probably never play trough this again...other than let's say archimedan dynasty or Aquanox, which i just played in order to hype me for this one.and that can be bought for 4 euros on  - and is fore sure the better game.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original Schleichfahrt and Aquanox 1&2, this game is a major disappointment.Some negatives I see are:- Gameplay is not fun in any form. Enemy AI does little else than close in on you and then attack like a static turret. Sometimes they just spawn direcly behind you. No interesting core game loop.- You do not have AI mates if you dont play it coop. This also means that every enemy in range will just shoot at you no matter what. There is no skill involved here, if you wanna survive on the highest difficulty all you can do is retreat as soon as the enemy spawn, sit behind a rock and exploit the terrible ai.- They butcher the lore. A major turn off because I intended to play it for the story.- Gameplay design choices that are just plain bad, like a useless crafting system or the inability to remove weapons from your ship. Health system is broken, as you survive as long as you can spam out repair kits and shield kits. Overall, combat feels like a bad joke.- Progression isnt fun, upgrades are not interesting, not enough variety. You get guns that do more damage, and a ship with more hitpoints.- The story is bland and feels forced. No mystery here, no lore that keeps me interested.- They do the Han Solo in terms of unnecessary and forced lore - Extended ending to connect the story of the originals and this one in a paid DLC.... Almost everything mentioned above was done way better in the orignals. They are more fun, have a better story, have actual gameplay, progression and variety. This is sad.
_childDocuments_.name: Aquanox Deep Descent

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this.So. After having played several hours coop with my friend my experience can be summed up with "meh". The shooting is okay, even though the balancing is all over the place. Sometimes you just steamroll the enemies, sometimes you die without even having time to react.Graphics overall are passable.The story is serviceable if somewhat incoherent. Like how did the sc's know that the pirates in prince Abuls mission were really rebels?? What?? And they learn nothing about the world and don't ask?The German voice acting is good.The worst part is honestly the coop functionality. It "works", but only just barely. Coop feels more like a crappy mod instead of something the game was built around.And generally there are a ton of small things that just make the game feel terribly unpolished. Like why can I only leave dialogs with tab? Why do  keep the crew members on the tupilac repeat the same sentence over and ofter after you have asked about a topic? I could go on.So, in the end would I recommend the game to someone? No. It does nothing really well and a lot of things badly. It makes me wonder if it has gone through any kind of playtesting. So many things are just baffling.I should add that interestingly we didn't really encounter any bugs or technical issues, which is nice. Just underwhelming design and lack of polish throughout.

_childDocuments_.review: A flashy shooter game that borrows the Aquanox name and throws some names and events in from the old Aquanox lore to lure you in, but has none of the worldbuilding that the old games had.The characters are wooden and boring. Remember Iwan King, Amitab, Atahualpa Jones? Yeah, none of that here. It's all just I'll-help-but-first-do-me-a-favor people everywhere, not an ounce of character between the lot of them.No landmarks either (think El Topo's Asylum, or Brainfire from the old games), just gate-base-cavern-with-stalactites-other-gate, rinse, repeat. Brownie points for the salvageables and broken gear on the seafloor though, it could really sell the atmosphere if the devs had bothered to actually make one.TLDR: It just comes off as a lazy attempt to cash in on a cult favourite.

_childDocuments_.review: Strange.... this game feels like the same Aquanox from 2000's. Linear dialogues, same boring shooting underwater. Yet 2000's Aquanox felt more authentic and the story was interesting to me. Emerald Flint was the boss.Here.... it is the same, yet it is not... in a bad way.I suppose childhood experience can never be same again.Edit 14/08/2022I was a small kid when i first played AquaNox 2001. Yet I still remember how awesome that game was.The story was superb. Very simple but it was gripping! Characters were unique, every little dialogue between missions was awesome in terms of voice acting and the way they were drawn. I can see how Massive poured their souls into everything they made.Ship designs were awesome too, Sure, when you boot up Aquanox 2001 now all the structures feel dull but hey, back then they did not)The combat and the music were awesome. Torpedo mechanics, sound of underwater combat, Dipol arrivals - awesome. Again, the characters were memorable and interactions with them too. I mean I still remember that poor guys from Dead Space 2 who dies in the very beginning after waking Issac up. Here, when Ishmael or whatever his name is dies - like I give a damn)))The best part of this game - some times the visuals are awesome. Good job to designers of the underwater caves. Yet if we are in the ocean - why does it feel so cramed and small? I am very disappointed, but then again I understand that Child nostalgia is hard to beat. The ending to this game is also very strange. VERY STRANGE.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Aquanox (2001), I've been looking forward to playing this for a while.  I probably should have heeded the 'mixed' review status.Graphically, its quite beautiful.  With details cranked, it runs silky smooth on my modest gaming rig.  The look of the game creates a nice atmosphere that is fitting for the world of Aqua.  The cockpit view modes are especially cool here.  As you take damage you start to see cracks form in the cockpit and water spray in.Unfortunately that is mostly where I run out of positive things to say about Deep Descent.  The sound design is bad on multiple levels.  Moving around the world of Aqua sounds ok, though its a far cry from games like Subnautica, or even the original games.  The soundtrack is weak and completely forgettable.  The music tempo tends to raise and lower as enemies are within range; this can happen multiple times within a few seconds and can be annoying.The worst crime committed here, however, is the voice acting.  Truly awful...among the worst I've ever heard in a game.  The writing does it no favors either.  The original Aquanox had excellent VA and is one of its redeeming qualities.  I can't put into words how disappointed I am with Deep Descent in this regard.  The difference in ambiance (versus the 2001 game) is notable as well.  There are also audio glitches; sometimes the voice lines just don't play during a conversation sequence (perhaps this is a positive given how bad the VA is).While the ships HUD design is nice, the UI / menu system while docked is bland and uninspired.  It's basically as generic as you can get, with the context menus being especially unintuitive.  Combat is average... not great, not terrible.  I wish I felt a bit more impact with the weapons.  Enemy variety seems low, but I'm only five missions into the game.I really don't have much to say about the story except that I don't feel invested in it.  Bad VA and writing is probably the primary factor here.  There appears to be no cut scenes...even Aquanox had an intro movie.  I'll update this review if I ever finish the game.  Based on what I've seen thus far, you'd be better of playing Aquanox (2001) or Archimedean Dynasty.

_childDocuments_.review: short version: not as bad as you think for a retro shooter.long version: sometimes when I see a lot of hot reviews it makes me curious as to whether a title could possibly be that bad. In the case of ADD (heh) I think the game's flaws are somewhat overstated, and where the problems really lie is in sticking too close to the original game's formula & presentation, while missing the 90's throwback attitude & over the top, frenetic quality it had. put simply: nobody who loved Aquanox back in the day wanted a more somber & slower paced version of it in 2020. So there's that.Taken on it's own merits? the intro level where you're in an underarmed pod is really annoying, after that it's a decent retro (emphasis on the word retro and everything it implies) strafe & dodge arcade shooter w/nice visuals & immersive sound design (high marks for sound, in fact). the shooting action and exploration are good (and tense sometimes); you will need to get used to the game's 3D movement & combat- mastering dodge is essential, and you probably won't want to be playing this w/mouse & keys. the story & characters are... eh, forgettable (the voice acting varies, it's on par w/the other games), the ingame economy & salvage feel a little underdeveloped, & the most frustrating aspect of gameplay is figuring out which sub configs work best, and you get no help, there (protip: save before you upgrade). Bottom line: not recommended at full price, but for under 15$ you could certainly do worse.(thinking out loud: post apocalyptic questing is so freaking tired at this point. but a futuristic undersea game like this where the focus was rescue? saving trapped divers/miners, doing emergency medical tech, putting out dome fires, spot welding hull breaches, cleaning up chemical spills, protecting wildlife, etc? I think something along those lines would be awesome.)

_childDocuments_.review: I have this game for the sole purpose of playing coop campaign with a friend. The game advertises itself as being a coop game where you can play the campaign with friends. What it does not say is that only your stats will be saved and if you try to pick up that campaign with the same friend another day, which is totally normal, then you will have your cool stuff you've worked towards in the game but your friend will have lost everything and start almost from scratch.The coop campaign mechanic is completely abnormal and the omittance of this fact until you have played beyond the refund point is dishonest.For an old school singleplayer experience then this is an alright game. The graphics are dated but it reminds me of Decent from the 90s. As a coop game do yourself a favour and avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, even if it was the most perfect underwater combat sim it would still be a gigantic disgrace to the amazing flavor, atmosphere and writing of the original AquaNox games. And I don't think it is a fantastic underwater sim, personally it feels pretty bland to play to me and has disappointing limitations, but I'm not an underwater sim enthusiast, I don't really care about that all that much. If this invalidates my opinion for you, cool. I'm an AquaNox fan and I love the games for more than just fun action, and certainly for more than whatever claims to underwater combat realism they might have or aspire to.What I care about is that nothing that was interesting about the first two AquaNox games is here.And it didn't have to be that way, it didn't have to be a disgrace to the AquaNox name and world. You can't bring Helmut Halfmann from the dead, and maybe the budget of this project wouldn't allow to hire some big shot writers, but it was still possible to employ more adept writers and storytellers for the project and do a better job. Most of the better storytelling in gaming comes from mid-size and indie developers after all, at least in my opinion.This game does not benefit from its association with the AquaNox series and the series sure as sharkshit doesn't benefit from this sequel. So even if there are people who prefer this game to its predecessors in every way, I'd like to think that ironically we'd be able to agree on this point.So what i'm trying to say is if following up Halfmann's brilliance was too much to ask for (which, really, it is), the absolute least they could've done is just make this game a standalone title and not taint the fantastic legacy of a very unique series of outstanding sci-fi games.I had my expectations low coming in. I expected disappointment, I expected it to be underwhelming and not true to the previous games. I bought it to sadly chuckle at the game's expense. But the joke was entirely at my expense, and there was no laughter to be had, only the dull, profoundly unsatisfying sadness.
_childDocuments_.name: Aquanox Deep Descent

_childDocuments_.review: The ships somehow mange to be too slow and too fast at once, they move slowly, but turn way too well for that. As a result it doesn't feel like proper action and not like a proper "simulation" (like the original, Archimedian Dynasty) either.This leads to the enemies to behave like glorified turrets, with a litte bit of swaying in the water and maybe slowly (since ships are slow) closing in on you or following you. Because the ships turn very well and move slowly, it's impossible to get behind or flank an enemy. Thus they always stare at you, you stare at them and you trade blows with each other.But worst of all is the spawns: Enemies just spawn wherever they want, for the story often they appear out of nowhere around you or in front of you, and for the open areas they just spawn at random points at random times, so you might be salvaging something and then an enemy spawns behind you and attacks you.And then there is the story, it's often confusing and stuff is simply skipped. Several times they tell you to board a capital ship, and after doing so, without a cutscene, or explanation or anything, you just get a loading screen and end up in a different area.For a game that took so much longer to develop than announced and promised, it is sad to say that the game would have needed more time...

_childDocuments_.review: Well I played all the old parts of Aquanox and I give this one a thumb up but it is rather borderline. The game has a good atmosphere but the fights are not dodgefights but rather going out and in cover and shooting all the time. Not very tactical and even on hard the game is fast finished (less than 20 hours). The upgrading of the ships is fun, but there are not enough missions even to upgrade any ship completely.The game design is not finished, the last 5 missions you cannot change your ship anymore, that is a boomer because I choose a fast fighter that made the end battle very hard. Also it is a decent story there are several missed oportunities. However, the atmosphere is good and thats a big plus, no bugs as far as I could see and the game runs very smooth on max details on my older rig.If you can live with the static fights I and liked the other aquanox it is a worthwhile game. I hope they make another part and improve on the mist oportunities and show a more complex mission design.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:++Fun Combat: New additions to your arsenal and a decent AI pretty much carry this game. Most of the tricks you can do, the enemy can and will do as well. Taking cover and healing up, dodging your rail gun shots with their pressure jumps, deploying counter-measures to avoid torpedoes or rushing you down with their shotguns and charge modules. That being said, about 90% of the enemies are weaker fodder and might die before they get the chance to amaze you. Fewer, stronger enemies would have been appreciated.+Decent graphics: Much brighter and colorful than the predecessors but I welcome the variety. Also, the ships' cockpits are very detailed and nicely animated.+Good performance: Game runs smoothly, load times aren't longer than a few seconds and I only had one crash during my playthrough.+6 different ships with a decent customization system: You can also upgrade previous ships so if you get a new one that leans in a direction you don't particularly like you can stick with your old one, no problem. Now, if only the game wouldn't throw about 50% of the upgrades at you in the last two hours...Cons:---A thousand minor bugs and imperfections: It really feels like one day the devs were told: "Get this done tomorrow - kthxbye." This ranges from small issues like UI issues to big ones. For example, at one point a character sacrifices themselves and it's supposed to be this big moment and then the dialogue gets their name wrong.-The soundtrack (while okay for the ambient tracks and even the lighter combat sections) is severely lacking during the more dramatic moments. Imagine Final Fantasy 6's bossfight and instead of Dancing Mad it just plays the generic combat theme. It also doesn't hold a candle to the previous games kickassery.-Bullshittery: For example, the game has a tendency to (re)spawn enemies in your face - this would have been so obnoxious on a higher difficulty. None of the typical "teleportation" or "cloaking" technology as an explanation either. Also sometimes the usual map borders that slowly damage you are just straight up invisible walls. And sometimes they insta-kill you.I could go on and on about every single thing the game gets wrong and then makes up for somewhere else, but in conclusion: It's just barely good enough for a recommendation if you're a fan of this series or genre. Riddled with frustration for everyone else.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand why this game has such bad reviews. I absolutely loved the first game. The second would've been better if they didn't limit you to three ships for the bulk of the game. Yes, Deep Descent feels different than the originals. Those games were also put out almost two whole decades prior to Deep Descent.  However, I just spent the last 12 hours playing this game. To put that into context, the last game to hold my attention for that long was Sekiro. (No, I'm not comparing the two.) It's fun. It gives you options on how you want to play whether you prefer to be fast and nimble or a tank. ((( They kind of put a lot of favor into a specific ship. Play and find out why.))) All in all, it's worth playing. I might even replay it since I didn't get all of the upgrades.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite releasing in 2020 being in development for about 5 years, it feels very unfinished and dated. Still, I had fun, and I like the story and gameplay, even though it wasn't as immersive as one would expect.There's more cons than pros, mainly because it's a low budget production and I expected more for the price. I know some people would refund the game after seeing how little effort the team put into some of the content, so I think these points are worth mentioning.DISCLAIMER: I haven't played previous AquaNox titles, but I am a fan of Freelancer and other games in its likelihood. Pros:- The gameplay is unique and fits the setting: a nice blend of FPS close quarters combat with 6DOF. However, don't expect it to be anything like a space sim.- A very nice variety of weapons and DSFs (Deep Sea Fighters) to choose from, allowing for many different play styles.- Each DSF (Deep Sea Fighter) is unique and has its own HUD, which made "dive into the game" a little more when I noticed it.- The story is interesting, and it's the main thing that kept me invested in the game. There's just a LOT of content to be played. Cons:- Conversations are linear, no free choice, despite there always being a list of replies with only 1 choice most of the time...- Cutscenes are literally colorized storyboards rather than actual in-engine scenes, with a lot of re-used sprites, even though we see animated 3D models of people in stations as background props.- The game always acts as if there's 4 of you, even when you play single player. I'd expect bots to fill the gaps...- Some of the names, places, and character designs seem like temporary content that should've been replaced in the final version.- Some of the descriptions are written in broken English.- The voice acting sounds cheap, the actors often overact their roles, and not all voices fit their character's description (e.g. a Russian guy, from the game world's Russia, with perfect British accent)- There's not much side quests, and not enough random missions ("Gun For Hire") to fill in some progression gaps.- You need certain materials to craft consumables and survive intense battles. You need the same materials (some of which are relatively rare) to upgrade your DSFs. It ends up forcing you to stick with a certain DSF for longer that you'd like to.

_childDocuments_.review: The original two Aquanox games had great charm, and a fun sound track. This third installment has neither. It feels like a muddled mess gifting frustration. It is a shame that a year after launch, it still has blocking bugs (in the first real mission the AA repairman can get stuck and not trigger the repair sequence, which I only know exists because I looked things up online to see what I was missing - should have called AAA instead). It's not just the game play that is a frustrating mess, it is the story. Apparently, you play a crew of four people who have awoken from cryo-sleep. That could be a compelling story if there was any interaction with them besides the occasional pop up during a mission, or, you know, even just an introduction that said "This is Freddo. He's on your team." No, you have to puzzle that out as people deliver wooden dialog in the middle of combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Came back to this game after playing it roughly a year ago, and ...I can only sigh. I've loved Aquanox since I was a kid, and always hoped for a continuation of the underwater world. It had a lot of potential, and in a lot of cases I feel it's similar to the OG games where you zip around in your chosen ship and shoot things.I can't help but cringe when I see obvious spelling errors, and it's a peeve when what I read is not the same as what's being said. What's the point then? You have to read the key bindings to realise that you can dodge to the sides instead of the generic up and down, how to turn on secondary weapons in the hammerhead, etc. It grates me when I'll get constant reminders to follow a damned pipeline in a mission but not tips on how to pilot the sub? Make it make sense.It also irritates me when I'm listening to MAIN STORY dialogue and it gets cut off because I got too close to a SIDE QUEST area.Not to mention that certain achievements are STILL broken despite the number of complaints. It's sad when players have to create software to get something in the game that should be obtainable by normal means!Anyways, it's an okay game if you couldn't be bothered with the nit-picky problems that stick out like a sore thumb at times. I went a little crazy at the easter eggs in the game, but playing it the second time around is a bit dull and frankly, disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Go here, press E to interact, shoot enemy ships, press E to salvage, shoot enemy ships, go here, press E to dock, do some super minor ship changes, press E to undock, shoot enemy ships, repeat.  For a game that's all about the deep sea it sure is shallow.  The combat feels awful, and that's about 90% of the game, locking on only ever tells you the shield/hull of the enemy ships, also lets you fire homing missiles, but it doesn't give you a leading reticle in case you want to attempt to hit a moving ship, or do anything else for that matter.  The "resource management" feels so weak, you go up to random wrecks, wait a few seconds for your ship to scan it, then press E and loot everything in it.  You can then dock at stations/ships and sell it, or use it to "upgrade" your ship (replace 1 module for another module).If you plan on playing coop then be prepared for the non-host players to basically be NPC's in the game.  They don't get to see any of the cutscenes, they don't get to see any of the conversations, only hear them.  Half the time they're not even part of the objectives, while I was playing the host was stuck in one spot while talking to a ship, and I was zooming off ahead going to the area he was going to be escorted to.Never played the original Aquanox, so I've not got the rose-tinted glasses some people might have at another game from a series that was solid, but I'd avoid this title if possible, maybe on a deep deep deep sale (~90% off or more).Also terrible idea releasing DLC day one that instantly has an exclusive ship, AND story content locked behind it.  Shoddy business practice and it's definitely going to come into account if I see a game by Digital Arrow out there in the wild in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: JOTTING DOWN RANDOM THOUGHTS AS THEY COME.When I see THQ Nordic, I automatically expect a lot. I have never played any of the other games leading to this one. That said, I had high hopes for this.Doesn't feel immersive. I was expecting a Subnautica-feel and environment with a battle element to it. Whenever I dipped my head below the water in Subnatica, I immediately had waves of anxiety hit me. Being under the sea should be intense, at least to some degree. With this, considering the game's premise, should be the same. Nope.Voice acting is over the top. Heard the exact same exclamation twice within a 5 minute span. Felt like I was playing an arcade game.On easy, it's easy to die from attack rather fast rather than easing me into the game. It's like my ship is made of paper. That's not fun. When an AI ship tells me to go on and he will hold back the enemy, that should be my option. If I start to help and shoot at enemies, I expect them to take damage. Just because I chose a different direction should not matter.I have hope, if the team is willing to keep making things better in the form of updates. I saw No Man's Sky come back from the dead to become a wonderful game. Subnautica was in early access for 4 years while the team worked on it. If Aquanox: Deep Descent was an early access game, things can be forgiven, knowing that things will progress. Such is not the case here and that leaves me with reservations about recommending the game just yet.If the devs are planning to call it all good and let the game stand the way it is, it should not be more than a $15 price point. As for now, I'd recommend waiting on the game for a while. Wait and watch.

_childDocuments_.review: To me, this game feels like a mix of Descent and Freelancer with an underwater theme, but more linear. The maps have "portals" to go from sector to sector, but the sectors are smaller than the sectors in Freelancer. The gameplay sometimes feels like one of the Descent games when you're inside some caves or buildings with narrow hallways. I liked the story. It's not as good as the Freelancer story, but it's okay for me. I've played the other Aquanox games and you can "connect the story" at times, but this game feels more like a retelling of the original story than a prequel or sequel. The only thing it lacks for me is replay value. You can host your own Multiplayer Team Deathmatch game with bots, but since you can't customize vehicles in this mode, you'll get bored quickly. I think most people will play the "main game mode" and follow the story, since that's the only way to customize your vehicles.The combat gameplay is okay for me. I really liked some of the weapons and utilities, like the missile barrage and the EMP. The combat feels a lot like Descent because of the 6DOF (Six Degrees of Freedom) movement. The graphics are also very good, only the flashlight looks a little weird to me (but maybe it's my monitor's brightness setting).The main thing I miss from the other older Aquanox games is the Instant Action mode. Sometimes I just want to jump straight into the action in a scenario. I think fans of the older games may or may not like this game, as it sometimes feels a little different from the older games (not in a bad way to me, just different). There are side quests and other small activities available, but they feel more linear than the other games. You can loot the scenario and sell the loot, but it's a very simple and limited mechanic, and it doesn't have nearly the depth of buying and selling goods that is available in Freelancer.Overall, I enjoyed the game and plan on playing it through the story when I have time. I like some side quests, so this might take a while.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played much of this game, but then i really don't have too.One of the first games i played on PC was Archimedean Dynasty, i utterly loved it, and i've played Aquanox 1 & 2. So understand me when i say that this game has very little to do with any of them.Now others have gone and criticised the graphics and gameplay, and while i myself think they are fine i can see where these people are coming from.My problem with the game is that they've completely ruined the world of Aqua. Archimedean Dynasty was a game dripping with lore establishing the world, the nations, their people and the events that lead up to the story you played through. None of this is represented in this game. Instead the nations have been changed, and frankly they're very shallow stereotypes. The Bionts the main antagonists of Archimedean Dynasty have been changed from an mysterious unknowable force to something nondescript that flings insults at you just like any other enemy in the game. And where before the world's infrastructure and technology was well defined and believable this has been replaced with fantastical systems such as jumpgates and alien(or perhaps celestial) technology.On top of the trash they've done to the world building the story is rather stupid sci-fi shlock and the characters very poorly performed. It also makes no sense for it to have 4 protagonists when only one of them (the dullest one as well) really interacts with the world.I don't know whether or not i'm going to give up on the game tho. I have yearned for so long for a sequel to this series that it's hard for me to enjoy it as such but at the same time there are soo few games set in this sort of world that mayhap i could enjoy it as it's own separate entity as the gameplay (for me) is fun enough. Still i will not recommend anybody buy this, you certainly won't be missing out, and for anyone who was a fan of Archimedean Dynasty or Aquanox i tell you in definite bold terms: AVOID!

_childDocuments_.review: This game simply put is NOT ready for release.  I have played it for at least 2 hours and already received the refund I asked for; why you may ask?  Simple, it doesn't even hold a light to the original Aquanox which I actually still own physically (and play).  Here are some issues:1. The factions don't really have ANY exclusive looking ships, all of the factions I've seen so for have same-ish looking ships and same-ish AI behavior.  This was not the case in the first Aquanox ALL THE FACTIONS LOOKED DIFFERENT!  The Crawlers, Bionts, Scavengers ect. had their own ship designs (capital ships, Freighters, bombers, fighters you name it)2.  NONE of the player ships from the original Aquanox made into the game which is a huge loss of points for me, would have loved to seen ships like the Skipjack, Voodoo Breath, and Succubus 2 again with a HD update.3. _childDocuments_.review: I received a review key from the developers. I may be negatively biased towards games that take place underwater (with the exception of Subnautica) because I love the space theme and play a lot of simulators like Elite: Dangerous, so I often find combat and movement in the ocean to be too bloated and boring. [This game was played through Steam]If you like underwater shooters, upgrading submersibles, and traversing the deep blue, then you will probably enjoy this game.The aesthetics are okay - the amount of detail in the world and its inhabitants is good, but feels a bit dated for a 2020 release. I noticed that the Steam in-game screenshots may be concept/refined stills because I have been unable to recreate those visuals even when playing on the highest graphical settings. The combat visual and auditory effects are decent, but again feels slightly lackluster. The music - with explosive, intense, and gripping tracks - is easily my favorite element of Aquanox, and I highly recommend you check out the OST at the very least.You can play with controller or keyboard and mouse - I preferred the latter, especially for movement. The tutorial and first few missions are great at teaching you how to play the game, however, I encountered a very unfortunate bug where I had to ram myself against the NPC I was supposed to be following because he got stuck against a wall (and the entryway wouldn’t open until he was close enough). This, among many other things, made the game feel unpolished, and I was very surprised to see other people encounter this problem in the very first mission (which should have been playtested). The learning curve is minimal to moderate depending on your aiming and shooting skills - enemies will not normally try to dodge you, so you can juke around and blast them away with ease. You can, however, get overwhelmed by enemy fire if you just stay in one place and soak damage. Aquanox is a lot like Matrix, but underwater - you “awaken” to command a submersible and journey across different territories using “special” (avoiding spoilers) waypoints. There are side quests you can do and many upgrades you can purchase to outfit your various vehicles. There is a lot of dialogue - both voiced and text - however, I did not like how you can sometimes get locked into speech chains even if you already heard them. Combat is okay - I struggled to play through the game because the gameplay loop quickly became: lock on to enemy -> shoot while juking -> spam repair/shield -> lock on to next enemy. Since you aren’t in outer space (or even in open air) you can’t do aerial maneuvers that make dogfighting fun and exciting. Instead, you can boost in 6 different directions while the enemy crawls toward you firing all weapons. I was uninterested in the combat after the first two missions. Fortunately, the weapons (and submersibles) you unlock early on help to change things up, however, this could not keep my attention for very long.If you really like being underwater and want a fairly easy shooter that allows you to customize a submersible, then you should watch some gameplay videos before deciding to try the game. At its current state, I cannot recommend this to others. Do not recommend.Cheers,DJSF For more reviews, .If you'd like to support me, please visit . Thank you for your consideration.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't say this game would fit nicely into everyone's library considering it's not a typical 6-DOF shooter but it's Aquanox with all its pros and cons. I'd like to point out a few specifics for this particular game as a standalone product and not just a sequel to the old series though.+ sound design is very good+ slow movement works perfect for battle encounters+ atmosphere is cool+ scavenging is simple but adds to the immersion+ keeping an eye on health and shields and using kits and abilities to survive still works better than 'energy relocation' in Star Wars Squadrons+ a team of pilots on the ship narrative wise works far better than a single person. good choice - i don't feel motivated enough to use resource market- story progression should be a bit higher considering the core gameplay have been paced down imo- would really like to be able to save manually in hubs 'cause it's logical to save your progress in safe environments- would be cool to have all menus visible on the cockpit considering we have a separate panels for them (as of now in-game cam aligns with a black panel on the side of a character and zoomes in when you look into quest log or inventory)
_childDocuments_.name: Aquanox Deep Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Good atmosphere, very good feeling from controlling vehicles underwater. Actually for 25 EUR I am quite positively surprised about quality of game. It is story driven, semi- openworld, crafting, upgrading game. There is safe zones, bigger ships, where you get quests, upgrade your shuips, buy parts etc... There are also secondary objectives, which gives nice credits and you can buy ships upgrades. Somehow I am satisfy and I will keep comming back to finish this game. So far 5 hrs in and I really quite like it. It is not bad game. It is better than aquanox 1 or 2, so if you lieked them, you can safely make this purchase, price is fair.
_childDocuments_.name: Aquanox Deep Descent

_childDocuments_.review: All in all i enjoyed playing Aquanox Deep Decent, After 20+ hours here are my pros and cons: + Graphics, sound and environment are well made.+ Feels almost as good as the original game 'Schleichfahrt'.+ Individual ship configurations.+ Crafting or buying your equipment.+ Story is ok. Emerald Flint as young boy? So this happens all before original Schleichfahrt?+ Blowing things up underwater ist fun!- Story feels hastend at the end.- No ship changing possible at end game encounters, docking without changing ship and loadout - why?- Lower half of sonar is almost always not visible. One has to dive nose down to see it all. Not nice.- Support characters feel lame and not fleshed out.- Dialog is extremly linear with no options in choice.- Weapon change is a bit tedious, especially in fights. i seem to remember that this was smoother in original Schleichfahrt.- No more sniper mode. - A lot less careful crawling and sneaking to turn off turrets or mines as in the games predecessors.- There is only one type of torpedo and three different launchers. I miss the torpedo variety from the other games in the series.Conclusion: If you liked this series so far this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Aquanox Deep Descent

_childDocuments_.review: It is a game that I have missed the KickStarter window to pledge in however, from what I've read about, ADD had plenty of problems for its launch. I jumped right in ADD two years later and I did encountered a few technical issues, namely the crash to desktop ones. Another big gripe with the game is the bare minimum support for UltraWide screen. While the screen is properly set in the UW format, the submarine HUD is way too close and lacks FIELD OF VIEW option. The only way I could remedy that was to play in a smaller resolution and that stretched the display considerably. This is such a shame that many modern games still can't support ultrawide screens however, I do know Digital Arrow is a small indie developer team and I could somehow forgive them... something I just cannot do with FROM SOFTWARE with their AMATEUR PC Porting... meh!OK, back on track...Like the description says, the Earth is in ruins and the only way humans survive is in underwater bases. They roam the ocean floors to scavenge resources while trying to stay alive against the other factions doing the same as you.Gameplay is very arcade-y and I don't recall any other game similar to this. I had good fun playing with the different upgrades, weapons and other submarine variants. You get to see how they pilot and move around. I would say the pacing is often OFF in ADD. You start slowly by avoiding most fights since your starter sub is so damn weak. The pacing issue is the game only unlocks the sub upgrades as you advance in the story. Some side missions do give you weapons so they are worth doing in my book but the poor locking mechanism for the sub upgrades was annoying. I would advice you save the game manually as often as you can. While ADD offer autosaving feature, they are far apart sometimes which makes you replay big portions of the game... irritating!The game visuals are pretty decent. Audio voice acting is fine and I keep hearing ACT MAN whenever the main protagonist, KAELEN, speaks. The music is good also. The story get's the job done. It's not outstanding but it could had been worse I guess.Then again, the biggest pro for ADD is the gameplay itself. The dogfighting in underwater is pretty cool itself and makes you think which weapon to use after each encounters.Without further ado, here's the pros and cons rundown:

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the series and played all predecessors including Schleichfahrt/Archimedean Dynasty. I was exited to play the new game but was still patiently waiting for it. It didn't matter to me that they had to postpone the release several times.Now, I downloaded the game and it started out weird right off the bat. Why are the main characters waking up from cryostasis controlling a submarine? (They don't even seem to care and don't ask questions). Ok never mind, that's just the start.Oh wow, the game instantly throws bionts in your face? Hardcore! WRONG! Those are just normal ships with some pilots in it. No horror of the bionts you know from the other games.The level design also throws me off... too much stuff to bump into, it feel narrow and crowded even when you're now just in a canyon. Also why the hell is the top now blocked by this stupid nano stuff instead by radiation?!And the most stupid thing is this module which let's you instantly accelerate to high speeds to RAM ENEMY SHIPS. Did you forget you're basically sitting inside an old piece of junk? Suicide much?Making/Bying weapons also does not make sense. I found one new weapon and could by it for 500 credits. The second one would have cost me 20k? For what reason?Nothing is explained, Dialogues don't make sense from time to time...This is the first game I'm trying to get a refund for and usually I stick with bad decisions but as a fan of this franchise I simply cannot allow myself to own this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the first Aquanox (still playing through Aquanox 2 at the time of this review) I can say that this game actually stands as a rare example of a good reboot/prequel. In terms of gameplay Deep Descent has a blend of semi-open world exploration and vehicular combat. Personally I loved the combat in this installment as it felt like a good modernization of the original. I will say to those playing on mouse and keyboard that the game only tells you how to dodge vertically. I found out in the final boss fight how to dodge horizontally by accident. It's double-tapping the shift key while moving with "wasd."Each of the available submarines available have a series of upgrades including changes to the hull, shields, engines, and fins. I admittedly would have preferred some trade off among the upgrades, such as higher armor at the cost of speed, rather than direct upgrades with no trade offs. But this is a minor gripe in my opinion and I always enjoyed seeing how the view from the cockpit would change with a new hull upgrade. As for the story and voice acting, which seem to be the most criticized part of the game from what I've seen, I thought they  were passable. The Aquanox setting has always been a character unto itself and the writing does a good job capturing that in my opinion. The direction and overall narrative felt a little jarring at times, but no more so than in the original. When it comes to the voice acting I thought that the characters were alright, with the only weak performance coming from one of the main characters, Kaelen, who very much feels like a charismatic cardboard cutout at times. Though this may be to give him enough voice to have agency while being blank enough for the player to imprint onto and feel active in the world. I would contrast this to the original Aquanox, where most of the characters were voice acted well enough to keep me invested...and then we have characters like Brewmister whose dialogue I always skipped or Boston Harper who was so obnoxious that his dialogue alone would break the setting for me at times.If you're new to Aquanox this might be a good starting point, and it's still worth playing if your enjoyed the previous entries as long as you honestly acknowledge what those games were and what this game is. The setting is honestly fascinating and something I've greatly enjoyed, and Digital Arrow did a good job presenting it for a reboot/prequel. But Aquanox has always had a smidge of camp and flat acting. It's like a good novel getting adapted to a sci-fi channel original series. Overall, you should come into this game and the others in the series with an inverted view, learning to enjoy the setting while viewing the characters as backdrop. 7/10 - Would headbutt a whale with a DSF again.
_childDocuments_.name: Aquanox Deep Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a review. Just my impressions of the first 2 hours of the game:It's not very good. There's no sense of exploration or fun challenge. Narrow levels, lifeless enemies, mediocre shooting. There's an interesting story underneath everything but it hardly seems worth the effort given the problems with the gameplay. It's just a total snooze-fest and I have no desire to finish it. I don't know why they decided to make the game so linear but it's just mission after mission (so far) of bland corridors and soulless combat.

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't know this series, then it is an okay game. If you love Aquanox, then this will dissapoint you. Not because of the gameplay (It is average at best) but because of the storytelling. It just skids all around without rhyme or reason. Your crew doesn't seem to have any reason to do, what they are doing. It feels like a lot of dialogue has been left out.[Edit]After playing Aquanox 1 & 2 again and then Deep Descend, I can say, that this is an okay game.My original review was fueled with nostalgia and the gameplay is far more polished in this one.Still the characters don't really "feel" alive.
_childDocuments_.name: Aquanox Deep Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Will update review as I go through the game.Was a fan of the original Aquanox and Aquanox 2 games due to the music, shooting mechanics and oppressive underwater atmosphere. This, unfortunately, seems more arcady and less polished than the previous games.- Some of the art in the game is downright low quality which hints at a rushed/sloppy product. - The dialogue lacks humour and intrigue. - the graphics look... foggy? I was lucky to remember to put on the headlights, otherwise I would have simply stopped playing. The colours also seem washed out. Maybe this was intentional but I don't want to play a pastel painting. - There's a glaring control issue with moving downwards and upwards being bound to the same key as boosting in those directions - lots of unintentional boosts and hitting rocks. - the shooting reticule lacks the enemy movement prediction reticule. This is a massive oversight by the developers since half the fun of shooting in these ships is having to choose homing weapons which deal less damage vs. non-homing weapons with which you have to anticipate where the enemy ship is moving. Takes 50% of the fun out of the shooting mechanic. - can't do a upside-down 180 by just steering the ship up and over its head- mission variety is lacking. Escort this and shoot ships. Go there and shoot more ships. I've yet to see a single mission where you're sent to explore caves filled with traps for example. - the NPC enemy AI just sits there. Combat is pretty much strafing to avoid fire and shooting at enemy ships which hardly move. It's different for boss-type enemies so I don't understand why they had to make regular enemy ships be so retarded. - no decent ultrawide support - you lose 10% of your top and bottom screen view if you play on an ultrawide screen. On the plus side this does somewhat feel like an Aquanox game so if you're nostalgic for that sort of thing, it's worth a buy.There's so much wasted potential here.A start where you have a run-down ship and are basically doing tow-truck and garbage disposal work. Then a lucky break that nets you your first low-class fighter sub. Electronic bassy bombastic music playing loud as you try and win battles by lining up your movement predicting reticule just right while avoiding torpedoes. Meeting new friends along the way and uncovering a mystery that might help solve the ecological crisis on the surface. But no. You're defrozen, thrown into a decent combat ship, given a crew and a mothership from the very start. Hope this gets better as I make it to the midgame and endgame.
_childDocuments_.name: Aquanox Deep Descent

_childDocuments_.review: After all those years in silence they actually released quite a good game. Not perfect by any means but not as bad as most reviews would make it seem. We have got a story, stations, quite good combat, ship upgrades and so on. Lets see how it develops and how the story unfolds.. looking forward to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aquanox Deep Descent

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun for a while but it is not the evolution of Aquanox that i hoped for. The graphics look outdated and the ultrawide resolution chops off the top and bottom. The fights are a bit lackluster compared to the older titles and sometimes unfair when you play alone. I reccomend this as a nice trip of nostalgia for those who loved Aquanox 1 & 2 but unfortunately Deep Descent doesn't live up to it's predecessors.
_childDocuments_.name: Aquanox Deep Descent

_childDocuments_.review: As others have already commented on the AI seems to be very limited, in the very first mission the AI that is supposed to guide you got stuck trying to go around a corner and kept going into circles. Controls are also fairly clunky and not fluid, I tried both mouse+keyboard controls as well as a gamepad and neither made me feel like I was really have good control over my craft. This goes further than this simply being underwater instead of in the air or space as I have played other games under water that feel much better. The graphics under water are also nothing to write home about, in fact it didn't really convey being under water to me except for there being fish. Finally there is something of with the feeling of scale. In the tutorial I felt like I was looking through a camera and steering a remote toy and when the missions finally started this didn't get much better as the enemies also feel like they are way too small to actually be real crafts.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly the game managed to be pretty boring.I lost interest after some hours because there is practically no story and even all the characters feel disconnected.The only thing interesting is the combat, but that feels boring too, because the AI seems not be able to do anything but looking at you - no maneuvers at all. So there is no real other engagement than shooting into the front of them - Even the synchro sounds not motivated.Graphics sometimes look like a distort filter and everything is too bright.Even the first Aquanox games had aim assist (lead pip)..You always have all guns with you and you cannot sell any. Must mean, that in the end you have to switch 10+ times to cycle from one to the other liked weapon..Ui (Inventory, etc) is clunkyOne moves like there is no water at all, more like in a space game or in "Descent", to be honest: it has more with that title in common.I'm pretty sure it would be possible with that engine to have implosions somehow, but here they look like (not spectacular) explosions. Anything else could have been made but those little bubbles all around, to have an indicator for being under water...Everything on the game just feels unfinished and kind of "rushed" out, which also makes no sense, as the devs wrote in late 2018 that the game was near completion and only fine-tuning would be done. I clearly cannot see why it was held back for another 2 years.Seems to me the "lowest effort possible" made, to not let people backing the kickstarter believe / have arguments to be a scam...There was clearly no "love" put in it (and if, i cannot tell what it is (maybe hidden code)) - Feels like grabbing into fans pockets just for the name of the game.A friend watched 10 minutes and decided, he didn't want it as present from me -> unfortunately good choice for both of us.(Maybe it's like Bethesda and Skyrim, where mods have to correct everything to make it fun some day...)

_childDocuments_.review: Solid effort! If you're a fan of the first 2 games, you'll feel right at home with this one. 13h on Hard difficulty with lots of exploring but never a dull moment. Let me put it this way: finished SW Squadrons main 8-9h campaign and while i did like it for it's authentic SW feel (yes, it's that good in replicating the universe to it's tiniest nuts and bolts), i totally loathed the controls and can't say i had an overall "awesome" experience. Aquanox DD? Pfff, easy to pick up and the combat is a blast no matter the ship, the weapons (very diverse and punchy) or the power ups used. Yes, the AI might be a little on the "easy" side and yes, the story might not be everyone's cup of tea (I liked it) but it has nice production values (great sound effects, very nice soundtrack and an overall more than decent voice-acting), I encountered 0 bugs or crashes, it has a fair price and it's a ton of fun (there was even a free trading cards booster pack thrown into mix lately)
