_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty decent and has its flaws but is still worth it. The game looks good, movement is responsive and swift, and your not questioning if you missed an item to progress through the story. I could only stick with a 7.5 or 8 out of 10 for one or two major reasons for me but maybe small for you. Otherwise a 8.5 feels about right. Shout out to the Devs for including Moon Samurai (a game I was hoping would be backed on kick-starter and hope will be back soon)The little flaws to me are combat and level Design (not all levels)...along with the abundance of particles (aka where is Leah). Fighting is fine until your on a wall hoping to not drop to the bottom for the 10th time along with the fact its hit for hit rather than hit dodge hit (maybe the AI is too quick). Level Design seems to be centered around EXACT movement with close to no forgiveness such as wall running but let the whole animation happen before you have 0.02 seconds to jump. We did ask for tight movement however so its ok.The environment outside the platform level is absolutely pleasing. I am into the story, the characters, the hacking portion, and I find the "challenge the ghost" feature cool (Fishy you S+ show off, you have ruined my confidence lol) Should you buy? I think the playtime is about 10 hours for the main story plus Leah is a hacker so just buy it or lose your information forever. In all seriousness, the game is worth the price tag. its a great casual play with competitive aspects. I'm sure I'll get over the combat, particles, and level design issues I previously mentioned. Thank you devs for turning a casual ghost to a speed-runner ghost. I'm currently trying to get into the Cafe, only an hour and some change in, expected way less (got way more), and somehow keep thinking how do these S+ people do it while watching them leave me in the digital dirt. See you Ghost around and Fishy...I'm coming for you.Update: Have to shelf it...some levels are in conflict with the mechanics. I actually am to blame...this game is good, not perfect but it is aimed towards hardcore/extreme gamer...i'm casual at best. Got a few S+, watched replays, and my lord the obsession is there. Its been fun.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, fast paced precision platformer with a major focus on speed, precision, and even sprinkles in combat to keep things fresh. This game is great in many ways, Time trial mode allows you to view ghost as well as race alongside them to try to maximize your score/timer. The controls are fluid and very sharp and precise and the music is very fitting for every stage and the cyberpunk setting.Pros: Strong gameplay, decent story mode, mostly fully voiced as well and the VAs showed up to perform.Cons: mechanics and controls can be a little hard to understand at first, learning curve to get S+ may be daunting for some, some levels are a bit too short.This game is very fun overall hopefully more people start to pick it up. For me? It filled a void that Celeste had left but also offered some new things that could take itna few levels above Celeste amd other precision platforms. I recommend for players who'd like a decent challenge

_childDocuments_.review: A mediocre action platformer whose platforming stage design and arena like combat stage designs never reach the heights of its inspirations like Dust Force or N+ with the additional issue of awkward controls and momentum use that never feels right and a dull narrative and hub section to explore.The story features a cyberpunk setting where your extremely annoying character has been diagnosed with an incurable disease and is told about a new possible treatment that involves going into a digital world created from her mind where completing the challenges she faces there can reduce and reverse the spread of her illness. You explore a hub world where you find two types of challenge rooms, one focused on platforming that has you attempting to reach the end as fast as you can while maintaining a synch combo by constantly collecting pickups and destroying enemies that don't attack you and the other room type offering a more closed off combat focused test where you have to destroy all the enemies and collect all the pickups with the enemies now being more varied and having different wats to attack you. Your performance in each stage is ranked getting an A or an S rank will give you 1 or 2 items needed to progress the game by allowing you to access more areas of the hub, while getting an S+ rank gives you an item used to access more advanced challenge rooms for side content.Platforming gives you a dash ability that can be performed on the ground and in mid air and a double and triple jump along with the ability to run up walls, run along ceilings, and slide down steeper slopes to gain speed. Your attacks consist of a light attack that is quick and does one damage, a slower heavy attack that gives you more range and hangtime in the air that does three damage, and if you find a pickup to charge it a gun that can be aimed in a direction in slow motion that damages or destroys anything in its path. Destroying enemies in mid-air refills one use of either a jump or dash and in certain stages they have to be destroyed to allow you to advance to the end. Your only real hazards in the platforming sections are falling off cliffs and areas of the environment that are red that you can basically think of as spikes in a lot of other similar games (even being similar enough to many games in that they have extremely questionable hit detection that not even the game seems to understand as it frequently will partially move the camera and your character like you landed a jump while it also kills you and moves you back to the checkpoint). Everything about these stages is generic with nothing new or interesting offered, worse it just all controls awkwardly requiring you to hit down to make use of sliding or to drop from ceilings (and I mean DOWN, no touching right or left at all like in a normal game or it just isn't going to work) your running speed and momentum rarely feel right and some of the more frustrating moments had me eventually having an Angry Video Game Nerd moment where I realized "You can just walk over it" (do nothing and she will probably get by it by herself, usually the movement was a bit too questionable for guarantees). If you die you can be taken back to a checkpoint, which can lead to moments of confusion as you aren't informed about where these checkpoints are and when you spawn back in the camera is probably in a completely different place than when you were last on that spot. Many of these stages also waste time by having the first half be some simplistic thing easily gotten through with no effort before suddenly throwing in some more usually moments you aren't going to be ready for unless you know they are coming which will then force you to replace everything else after you die to try to get a better score.The combat stages give you all the same abilities only you have aggressive enemies attacking you in a large but enclosed area where you need to take a path that will allow you to kill everything and pick everything up as fast as possible for the best ranking. Some enemies doing things like launching seeking missiles at you and the wall climbing remind me of N+ but there is nothing fun or interesting about these stages as the enemies almost never pose any threat and their attacks can be destroyed with your own. Even when I thought I did badly time wise on these I was often given an S+ ranking. The times I found myself most likely to be hit was when one started up their attack animation when they were barely on or not on the screen yet due to the camera.Some side activities see you trying to reach harder to get to areas in the hub areas to collect floppy disks for more setting details and discovering more out of the way harder challenges to get video game cartridges for an even more annoying version of Skippy from the Expeditionary Force series. Other than that, the hub area really offers nothing apart from some decent visuals and constant needless references to other media instead of doing much for its own setting.Even if I were to think about it being entirely just me having problems with the way this game controls and moves and I was able to control everything with no issues like I can in most in games, while it would certainly make the game less frustrating, when compared to similar titles it still wouldn't be offering anything interesting in any area and therefore still wouldn't make it very good.I supported it on Kickstarter and was added to the credits as a backer and as a character profile in the game.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: This game puts me in a weird place for "recommending" because, do I recommend this game? Yeah, I do recommend Dustforce, the game this is obviously inspired by, self-admittedly so since there's an explicit shout-out to Dustforce in game. Eden Genesis is Cyberpunk Dustforce. If you liked Dustforce, you'll like this game. If you haven't played Dustforce... go play that first? It's cheaper, bigger, better, and comes with a full level editor and community levels?That's the thing, when you make a game so obviously inspired by another game, it's impossible not to hold it to that standard. And I don't think Eden Genesis plays quite as good as Dustforce, or at least, the rough edges felt more visible. It's not a direct copy, mind you, it adds a second action charge in air, a genuinely great stomp that's leagues better than Dustforce's, and replaces the super attack with a beam attack that lends itself well to some solid platforming puzzles that are completely original to this game. Tack on an increased sense of speed and a secret-filled overworld map, it's definitely its own thing, even in spite of its similarities.But then there's some flaws that shine through the more you play - the aforementioned stomp, for one, which is mapped to "down + jump" or "down + dash" and likes to either not work in specific scenarios (trying to stomp off a ceiling while in a booser), or triggers when you don't want it to (trying to jump right after a downward-angled beam attack and just getting a stomp). The beam is also a pain to aim sometimes, eight-directional is already a problem Celeste had and basically mandated that game be played on keyboard for optimal precision. It's not as frequent an issue in this game and I did play through the entire game to 100% on controller, but misaimed beams came up frequently enough that it was a nuisance - and it's even more awkward that there's absolutely no delay or time to reorient yourself after using one, which can lead to what feel like cheap deaths. I also frequently experienced a failure to cling onto ceilings, even when I was bumping my head against them, and I swear that in Mirror Mode I was having dropped inputs - never felt this way in standard mode but it was happening all the time in Mirror Mode, I dunno if it was just a psychological thing but whateverrr.And when I say Dustforce is "bigger" I mean that it just, straight up has more levels. There's 41 main levels and 14 expert levels in this game for a total of 55 levels, but around a dozen of those main levels and one of those expert levels are combat rooms, the worst type of level in Dustforce we really didn't need to carry over, much less this many times. I dunno, I don't like them. But that's compared to Dustforce's four sets of 16 increasingly difficult levels each, on top of the three tutorial levels and a bonus world of 7 more levels pushing it over the 70 level mark. With levels in Dustforce also trending longer than some of the pitifully short easier ones in this game.The level design's also super hit-or-miss, because there's just, lots of moments that feel really inelegant even when you do nail them. A lot of the standard levels feel super slapdash, even replaying them at a higher level of skill, and while there's some that are cool they're mostly confined to the endgame. The expert levels are also pretty hit or miss, with a few of them actually being really cool and fluid and interesting to figure out while others feel finnicky and bad no matter how many times I play them to S+ them. I'd like to highlight the final level of Xanadu in particular, which feels like it was made on a bet to make the most awkward and nitpicky level design imaginable without making it too obvious the level designer was trolling. Truly atrocious level, that one. Genuinely think it's harder than the super secret bonus level, too, which is. Something. I could ramble on all day about this but it's hard to explain when something just -feels- bad, and while the game has more than its fair share of levels that feel good, between the number that don't and the combat levels generally feeling bad, it's a very mixed bag of levels overall.The presentation is also... while nice, visually, even if it doesn't have a ton of personality, it can get reeeeally cluttered, especially with some of the visual effects like the aforementioned beam attack or some extreme zoom outs that can make it easy to lose track of where you are. There's also, bafflingly, a few levels with a sharp orange background, y'know, the same color as all the cubes you're collecting and enemies you're smashing, which just makes those handful of levels especially awkward as you struggle to even see what you're doing sometimes. The music is... fine, the story's... not great, there's like, an entire second story going on in the background that has little implications on the main plot, which resolves without really resolving anything and doesn't feel particularly satisfying, but it's an edgelord cyberpunk plot that doesn't really have much to say anyways so, whatever. Uhh. The voice acting can be pretty shaky, too, but it's, whatever.I probably sound really critical here but I liked the game enough to 100% its achievements, which is, y'know. Perfecting all the levels, twice, and doing an entire second playthrough to speedrun it. It's fun to get caught up in the level-to-level flow and the game on the whole feels good to control even despite my nitpicks......but it's just, slightly worse Dustforce at the end of the day, so I can really only recommend it if you've already played Dustforce and are hungry for more.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun getting into Eden Genesis! I'm not very co-ordinated so I found it a bit tough but folks who play these kinds of games more often would have no dramas at all. It's quite forgiving in the mechanics and I managed to get a decent way into the game despite my lack of skill. It is a LOT easier on a controller and Steam will prompt you to use one when you go to open the game so there is fair warning. I tried to muddle through with keyboard for a bit but I couldn't get my head around it. Connected a controller and it was instantly better. The voice acting is great, music is beautiful, and the graphics are gorgeous. It's a delightful game that I think anyone who loves retro games and platformers will genuinely love.

_childDocuments_.review: Tentative Recommendation. I think with a few tweaks, this game could be wonderful as the gameplay itself is pretty solid. I love the flow, but it does feel like it's missing a really clean design. Here are a few things I've noticed in my handful of hours playing so far:• Aerial dash favours left movement over down, so you have to let go of left to down-dash onto the left-facing slopes.• Down dash is linked to both down and dash as well as down and jump, which can cause you to die if you're not careful.• I've bound dash to R1, which is also the interact button, which appears is unable to be bound.   - When I'm trying to dash away from terminals 'n' such, I'll often end up locked in lengthy menu transitions by accident or dialogue I can't skip.• R1 also opens the doors. But in this instance, it prioritises the dash instead, making me run away from the doors I'm trying to open unless I hold down.• Jump being dynamic makes it hard to judge how long I have to press the button to get the right height to catch ceilings or clear ledges at times (skill issue on my part).• If a ledge is 1 tile, you're unable to climb over it in the same way you would with a wall.• If you go too fast on a stage, the run isn't recognised on the leaderboards.I think if most of these concerns are tidied up, this game will be a fantastic experience for both veterans and newbies to the platform genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely like the game. There's a simple story guiding us along and a brief tutorial, which is always a plus in these types of games. The levels themselves are dynamic and quite challenging if you're aiming for an S+ rank, sometimes even a bit frustrating, but that's part of the fun. I'd love to have more upbeat music during the levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Eden Genesis

_childDocuments_.review:
Eden Genesis is a platform game focused on fast-paced trials, quick reflexes, and a rich story in a cyberpunk world dominated by neon lights and corporations. Take control of Leah, a young cyborg lady, and overcome challenging trials to liberate her corrupted mind!

A cyberpunk adventure

In the not-so-distant future, corporations rule the world providing ways of increasing the physical and intellectual capabilities of the common folk, at a high price...

Those who wear cybernetic implants are doomed. Their lifetime is coming to an end in a matter of time, but luckily for them, there may still be hope. The biggest tech conglomerate just announced a promising solution for this terrible disease!

You play as Leah, a young cyborg lady who joins this experimental treatment to find a cure for what is killing augmented people. Overcome the trials to unlock your full mind potential and eliminate the corruption born from the implants that are destroying your neurons.
_childDocuments_.name: Eden Genesis

name: Manic Mechanics
detailed_description: It’s time to dust off your overalls and hitch on your toolbelt in Manic Mechanics – a chaotic couch co-op game where you and up to three fellow grease monkeys pay a visit to the car-obsessed Octane Isle. Your mission? Work your way around the island’s six neighbourhoods – from the rust buckets of Betty’s Scrapyard to the spooky shores of Banshee Bay – challenging the Master Mechanics that rule each part of town. Repair as many cars, trucks, choppers, tractors, mini-subs (and even UFOs) as possible to prove your worth in this hectic race against the clock. No two games are the same as you work your way through 40 unique garage levels, each one more challenging than the last. Completing a garage is one thing, but mastering it and beating your best score requires coordination, skill and determination. Octane Isle is a great place to visit, whether you go solo or bring along your friends. In co-op mode, up to four players work together as a finely-tuned machine, tracking their team’s best scores, unlocking new characters and discovering hidden secrets as they explore Octane Isle together. Or maybe you'll choose to head straight to the Versus Arena, split into teams and decide once and for all which crew truly rules the workshop? Whether you choose co-op or competitive, the action unfolds across local, wireless and online play. Just about anything can happen on Octane Isle... the faster you work, the more chaos is unleashed. Fuel ignites, tyres explode, robots short-circuit, cows stampede and aliens abduct, but with teamwork, skill - and maybe just a little luck - you'll earn the right to call yourselves a Manic Mechanic! Features Manic arcade action 40 levels Six unique neighbourhoods Local and online couch co-op Local and online versus mode

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of games like Overcooked and Moving Out, you're going to enjoy this one!It captures the enjoyable essence of those titles and introduces a car mechanic setting, making it an absolute blast to play with friends. When you collaborate effectively, assigning roles and mastering the game mechanics, you'll find yourselves in a seamless flow. The game offers engaging level progression and consistently stays true to its theme. We encountered a minor glitch where our characters appeared in the same color, but aside from that, our gameplay was smooth and issue-free.Overall, a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Manic Mechanics

_childDocuments_.review: While there are a fair number of Overcooked-style games to choose from, Manic Mechanics does a fine job of standing out from the crowd. It takes great advantage of the car theme, creating fun and frantic scenarios inside of levels - the minigames that are required to repair each part add some distinctive fun. Even making driving around the map is joyful. The ugly character design and lack of online matchmaking are weaknesses compared to Overcooked. That's right, there is no online matchmaking. You can play online with friends, but that's it. That's a bit deceptive since you'd naturally expect to be able to play with random players in an online game. Still, local matches and online matches with a friend are a blast.Overall, Manic Mechanics is a nice alternative to Overcooked, especially if the car theme appeals to you. For more details, see my full review at .

detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition Deluxe Edition Contents: -Ys X: Nordics -Summer Adventure -Azure Mermaid -Endless Voyage -Heroic Captain -Sacred Beast Roo Costume Set -Eyewear Set: Cool -Eyewear Set: Fun -Ear Accessory Set -Extension & Color Set: Vivid -Extension & Color Set: Wild -Display Stand Set -Headwear Set -Horn Set -Scarf Set -Shield Set -Marine Companions Set -Ironclad Battleship Set -Nosfleet Ship Set -The Pikkard Set -Deck Decoration Set -Sail & Hull Color Set -Ouch! Sail Set -Ouch! Flag Set 23 Costume/Attachment DLC Items *Includes content that is also sold separately.Beware of duplicate purchases. About the Game Experience the latest action RPG featuring Adol Christin, a legendary adventurer who left behind over a hundred adventure journals for posterity, now on Steam! Who are the immortal beings known as Griegers appearing around Obelia Bay? Take control of Adol and Karja to engage in fast-paced battles, utilizing steps and dashes to defeat your foes! 【Featured Characters】 ■Adol Christin He's the main character of the story, a vibrant adventurer with fiery red hair and eyes full of curiosity. Adol left his first adventure land, Esteria, at age 17 and was believed to have set off for Celceta. However, according to one of the adventure logs found in his family home, it's revealed that he had visited Obelia Bay with the former thief Dogi before heading to Celceta. ■Karja Balta The sole daughter of Grimmson, the leader of the Baltan Navy. Karja leads the rough seafarers in piracy with confidence, earning her the moniker 'Pirate Princess' among the people of Karnack who have seen her in action. While she possesses elegant features, she is armed with a hatchet and a round shield, displaying a ruthless, Norman fighting style. 【Major Battle System Overhaul!】 The all-new “Cross Action” system allows players to fight in two modes depending on the situation: a speedy solo mode in which the player controls gameplay supported by a partner who attacks automatically; and a dual mode in which two players simultaneously control a series of actions to engage in a turn-based battle against a powerful enemy! ■Enhance Your Skills with Increased Proficiency and Unlock Advanced Skills! Improve your skills by using them frequently, thereby increasing their proficiency and power. Certain skills, when leveled up in proficiency and meeting specific conditions, can unlock even more potent advanced skills. ■Combo Skills Get a Power Surge with Proficiency & Revenge Gauge! By successfully guarding against enemy attacks, your Revenge Gauge fills up. Activating skills in this state boosts their power based on the gauge's multiplier. As skill proficiency enhances the base power of skills, unleashing a combo skill at maximum proficiency and a full Revenge Gauge can deal immensely more damage than regular solo mode skills. ■Teamwork is Crucial! Explore dungeons and interact with Raven Marker Stones to temporarily release the mana bonds linking Adol and Karja. During this time, control Adol and Karja separately. You’ll need to strategically switch between them, coordinating their moves from different positions to overcome challenges effectively. 【All-New “Mana Actions” System】 The game also features the “Mana Actions” system, a special ability that greatly expands the freedom of the player in fields and dungeons. 'Mana String': Use a string of Mana like a pendulum to reach faraway places 'Mana Ride': Allows you to glide on a grimble board 'Mana Burst': A Mana attribute attack released by a charge attack ■Spin the Threads of Fate! Nornir's Spindle: 'Mana String' Harness the power of Mana Strings to swing like a pendulum and reach far-off places with this dynamic mana action! Upgrade your Mana Actions to strengthen the strings, enabling you to manipulate objects and activate switches in dungeons. ■Ride with Style! The Grimble Board: 'Mana Ride' Soar and slide over the ground on the Grimble Board in this thrilling Mana Action! Glide over water, race down Mana Roads at high speed, or launch through the air from wind pockets for a fast-paced experience. ■Unleash the Power of Mana! 'Mana Burst' Release elemental Mana attacks with charged strikes! Adol uses fire and Karja ice to not only damage enemies but also to aid in exploration--burn away obstacles or create icy platforms. ■Enhance Your Perception! 'Mana Sense' Reveal hidden elements of the world with the ancient Druid Monocle. This Mana Action lets you detect enemies, uncover hidden gimmicks, and find buried treasures. As the Druid Monocle gets stronger, your Mana Sense sharpens, allowing you to slow down time and overcome challenges like impassable doors and treacherous walkways. 【Sail a Ship!】 For the first time in the series, Ys X allows players to become a ship’s captain! This adds an exciting new element of challenge to the adventure, such as exploring vast regions of the ocean using nautical charts as guides, and sometimes challenging enemy ships to naval battles! 【Land the Big One on the Open Seas!】 Engage in fishing at designated spots on water surfaces within fields and dungeons, where you can spot the shadows of fish. First, select your bait and fishing spot to begin. Once you get a bite, you'll need to quickly press buttons or manipulate the joystick according to the situation. This will increase the fishing gauge at the top of your screen. When it's completely filled, you've successfully reeled in your catch! 【New Features Exclusive to the Steam Version!】 Supports 21:9 ultra-wide monitors and frame rates exceeding 60fps! Enjoy a wider field of view and smoother gameplay. Preset settings tailored to your gaming environment are also available, ensuring a comfortable experience even on the Steam Deck. 【Engine Powered by DirectX 12】 With improved performance and support for Intel® XeSS, NVIDIA DLSS, and AMD FSR, you can experience the beautiful world of Ys X at higher resolutions and frame rates than ever before. 【About the Game】 The story takes place in the northern sea Obelia Bay, a bay filled with countless islands of all sizes. Adol Christin, a young adventurer who has explored the ancient kingdom of Ys, encounters two factions: the “Normans,” seafaring people known for their powerful warriors, and the “Greegers,” a mysterious group of immortals that threatens the people of Obelia Bay. Ys X: Nordics depicts a brand-new adventure in the northern sea Obelia Bay, featuring the young adventurer, Adol Christin, as its protagonist!

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: While I was not involved with this port or have ever done any work for CLE, I want to make it clear that I have helped test other PC Falcom games from their competitor, NIS America, on a voluntary basis, which might affect my judgment here. This review was written independently however and I bought this game with my own money.I usually do not post my reviews, but the state of this game warrants it. First of all, I want to make it clear that I am not the targeted audience of this product, as I do not speak Chinese or Korean. I bought this game expressly for the purpose of examining the port and not really for playing, as I don't speak any of the supported languages.Now, with that out of the way, let's go over a port that mostly reminds me of the first PC port of Ys 8 way back in 2018, which, in short, was released in an unacceptable state, so much so that it had to undergo a full-on overhaul later on.In my preliminary testing yesterday, I can mostly explain the poor performances seen by many. Firstly, the game only appears to support three total resolutions behind the scenes: 1080p, 2160p, and some 8K resolution. This can be spotted by analyzing a frame with something like RenderDoc or just looking at the game config file, which has a setting called "MaxRendering."This setting is changed on the fly when you change resolutions in the launcher and seems to round up. So, if you pick 720p, it will select "2K," which is 1080p here, 1440p selects 4K, 5120x2160 selects 8K. This is likely part of the reason why so many have issues and partly why the performance is so poor on the Steam Deck, where I am seeing frame rates in the lower 20s. The Aspect Ratio support advertised in official CLE marketing is, from what I can tell, nothing more than smoke and mirrors. The game claims to support 1280x800 in the launcher, but in actuality, it's just a 1920x1080 image squished a bit vertically so the game can stretch it out.Resolutions aside, the game itself seems woefully underdeveloped on the technical side. GPU utilizations are way below expected values across the board, suggesting a bottleneck somewhere along the lines and this is on a top-of-the-line AMD Ryzen 9 7950X & RTX 4090 system. Though I am seeing the same on the Steam Deck, so it's likely a universal issue. It's tempting to blame the DX12 renderer for this, but I've got no concrete evidence for that. All I can say is that the current state of things is unacceptable, and I can't see how XeSS can fix this either, unless CLE and their likely subcontractor improve performance somehow.As an example, when I first booted up the game on a monitor set to 4587x1920, the game defaulted to 8K, and the game ran at 47 to 50 fps on a 4090! Here, the GPU utilization was also way below max, so a bottleneck is likely present. At 8K, it could be a lot of things, but that's just another issue with the game only supporting three resolutions.If I manuelly lower the resulution to lower levels instead of doing 8K rendering it get's a bit better, but stil way below what my hardware statistics suggest should be possible.Lastly, I want to touch upon the controls. How do you release a PC port without keybindings for the native input method, namely Keyboard and Mouse? I see in the known issues this is being worked on, but at that point, why not delay the game, because things clearly weren't ready, as is evidenced by XeSS being delayed mere days before release too. I could go on and on, but I think I've made my point clear.Regardless of nationality and language preference, I cannot in good conscience recommend this game in its current state. I hope for all of you who only speak the supported languages that this port offers that CLE gets their act together because I've heard great things about this game otherwise.I will try and update this review if/when anything changes in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Ys X: Nordics? A New Horizon for the Adventurer Adol Christin! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)Note : With the latest update, Ys X: Nordics has undergone substantial optimization, transforming the gameplay experience significantly. Thanks to the implementation of DirectX 12 and new upscaling technologies like DLSS and FSR, the game now runs smoother with higher frame rates and enhanced visual fidelity. Players previously troubled by performance issues will find that the game now handles beautifully, even on ultra-wide monitors.Ys X: Nordics is the latest action RPG in the Ys franchise, featuring the iconic red-haired adventurer, Adol Christin. This time, the game takes place in the mysterious Obelia Bay, a northern sea full of scattered islands. Adol embarks on a new journey, accompanied by Karja Balta, the Pirate Princess. The narrative focuses on their encounters with the Normans, fierce seafaring warriors, and the enigmatic Griegers, immortal beings threatening the region. The game introduces several new systems, including the Cross Action combat system and Mana Actions, giving players a fresh perspective on exploration and battle mechanics.The most significant feature in Ys X: Nordics is the Cross Action system, which allows players to switch between solo and duo battle modes. This adds both depth and flexibility to the combat, making encounters fast-paced and dynamic. Adol and Karja each bring unique abilities to the battlefield, and their synergy becomes key in taking down tougher enemies. The system is satisfying, especially with mechanics like the Revenge Gauge, which rewards defensive play with enhanced offensive power. However, for players new to the series, these mechanics can feel slightly overwhelming until they get the hang of it.Exploration in Ys X is enhanced by Mana Actions, which allow you to traverse and interact with the environment in creative ways. Mana Strings let you swing between platforms like a pendulum, while Mana Ride offers a thrilling glide over terrain and water. These mechanics make moving around the map more engaging, but the islands themselves can feel visually repetitive. Unlike previous entries, such as Ys VIII, which offered diverse and visually stunning landscapes, Ys X’s island environments often feel too similar to each other, slightly diminishing the sense of adventure.One of the game’s highlights is its optimization on PC, featuring support for ultra-wide monitors and frame rates exceeding 60fps, all powered by DirectX 12. The integration of DLSS, FSR, and XeSS ensures smooth gameplay and beautiful graphics, making Ys X look and run better than previous installments. Even though the game generally performs well, some players may experience minor stuttering in certain areas, though it’s far less of an issue than in past Ys games.Ys X: Nordics continues the Ys tradition of exhilarating combat and storytelling, while successfully introducing new features like the Cross Action and Mana Actions systems. The dynamic battles and strong character focus are highlights, offering a refreshing experience for both series veterans and newcomers. Despite some drawbacks, such as repetitive environments and a steep learning curve for new mechanics, Ys X delivers an engaging adventure that fans of action RPGs won’t want to miss. While the game doesn’t quite reach the heights of Ys VIII, it still stands as a worthy addition to the beloved series.If you’re a long-time fan of Ys or looking to dive into the series for the first time, Ys X: Nordics is a solid entry point. For more reviews, game recommendations, and RPG content, be sure to follow our  and stay updated on future adventures with Adol Christin!ヽ(´• ω •`)ノ

name: Piczle Cross: Story of Seasons
detailed_description: The critically acclaimed Piczle series presents Piczle Cross: Story of Seasons; addictive nonogram logic-puzzles celebrating the beloved farm life game series Enjoy the bucolic charm of Story of Seasons while relaxing and exercising your brain with classic logic-puzzles. All your favourite villagers and bachelors, tools and crops, animals and upgrades in nonogram form will provide you with countless hours of puzzling! With 350 puzzles featuring a wealth of different Story of Seasons mainstays you’ll have a veritable pasture-full of puzzling pleasure! As you clear puzzles the seasons progress, your farm expands, livestock appears and crops grow.  5 unlockable collage puzzles celebrate Story of Seasons’ festivals by combining dozens of puzzles into a bigger picture. True to the Piczle series, Piczle Cross; Story of Seasons provides the most feature-rich and option-abundant experience available to cater the puzzling experience to your exact liking. From hiding away the timer to correcting your mistakes, from choosing the puzzles’ themes to managing how completed clues are marked off, you can play exactly how you want. There is no wrong way to play! Clearing specific puzzles will unlock entries in the in-game 100+ page almanac that celebrates all your favourite characters and critters from the Story of Seasons games.  Keep an eye on your progress with detailed statistics and achievements. Replay puzzles to improve your time, or to hone your skills without using helpful gameplay options.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to start off this review with saying, I play every Piczle / Nonogram game I find, and have not played Story of Seasons, also at this point I have finished most of the puzzles in this with no hints and such.The game is clean, it had great features that Nonograms should all have. There are some nice little features with advancing the farm as you do certain puzzles,  however you don't get to really decide which ones they will be as they don't reveal until after the puzzle is complete, and there is little to no change at all to the farm in the background.My biggest issue with this game is that the puzzles most of the time look NOTHING like what they were trying to depict. Most of the puzzles (especially the 15 x 15 ones) are all people / characters from the game which have had weird changes or extra lines put in which get faded out once you finish the puzzle. This is horrible. a large part of enjoyment of doing the puzzles is seeing the pictures they become. In this aspect, this has by far the worst nonograms I have ever done.TLDR. Great features to the puzzles, absolutely HORRIBLE pictures from the puzzles. I would not recommend to anyone. 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: My main point of comparison to this as a picross game on pc would be Hatsune Miku's Logic Paint S. You wouldn't think there's that much to differentiate a picross game outside of the theme. But this one actually offers a lot more in terms of features. A lot of accessibility options to fine tune what kind of hints you get. The game can even count blocks for you. Not sure if these features are in mainline picross games, but this feels a little more advanced.The theme is subjective. If you like Story of Season games, you will be happy here. That friends of mineral town farm theme is baked into my subconscious. The unlockables are pretty nice. I think more art would have been nice, like concept art or event photos. But that's not really this game's fault if the art doesn't exist.Also the developer is very quick to address issues and responsive to feedback. I think the asking price is fair. If you like story of seasons and picross, this is a no brainer.

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming game with quality logic puzzles. If you love Picross games, you can't really go wrong with Piczle Cross. The Story of Seasons franchise is used nicely and it was a delight to fill my farm with all the cute animals as a reward for solving puzzles. There are some nice quality of life features here, such as displaying the amount of filled in tiles on a spot of your choice (this was in frequent use during my time with the game).I feel this title was well worth its price. I didn't encounter any technical issues. I completed all the content in 48 hours (some of the time I spent looking at the animals with a stupid smile on my face and checking the illustrations/bios in the almanac). _childDocuments_.review: Great nonogram and I really enjoyed my time with it. I like to complete nonogram puzzles without any of the assist tools. Two things made this is a little more difficult compared to my favorite nonogram series: Picross. 1) the numbers indicating how many blocks are needed in each row will grey out as long as all squares are filled in, even with an “x”. In Picross, the numbers only grey out when you have the needed number of squares filled in (even if they’re wrong). In Story of Seasons, you could fill in whole rows with “x” and the numbers would grey out. This means you might think you completed the row only to find later that you’ve made a mistake. 2) there’s no “maybe” option to fill in squares. You can only fill in squares as a “yes” or “no”. Picross has a third “maybe” option that lets you plan more without committing. Still, Story of Seasons is a ton of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Piczle Cross Story of Seasons is a delightful and charming puzzle game that expertly combines the addictive nature of Picross puzzles with the heartwarming Story of Seasons theme. With over 300 puzzles to solve, this game offers hours of engaging gameplay and a relaxing experience for players of all ages.The collaboration between the Piczle and Story of Seasons series is evident in every aspect of the game. From the vibrant pixel art to the charming character designs, the game exudes a warmth and coziness that fans of both franchises will appreciate. The attention to detail in the visuals is impressive, with the puzzles revealing adorable scenes of farm life, seasonal festivities, and beloved characters from the Story of Seasons games.The gameplay mechanics are easy to grasp, even for newcomers to Picross puzzles. The tutorial provides a smooth introduction to the game, explaining the rules and controls clearly. As players progress, the puzzles become increasingly complex, offering a well-balanced difficulty curve that keeps the experience challenging yet enjoyable.One of the standout features of Piczle Cross Story of Seasons is the inclusion of various gameplay modes and customization options. Players can choose between standard Picross puzzles, Mega Picross, Color Picross, and even Micross puzzles, providing a diverse range of challenges to keep the experience fresh. Additionally, the game offers a plethora of accessibility options, such as the ability to toggle hints, auto-fill completed rows and columns, count the cells option, and adjust the color schemes for colorblind players.In conclusion, Piczle Cross Story of Seasons is a captivating and relaxing puzzle game that successfully merges the best elements of the Piczle and the Story of Seasons series. With its charming visuals, diverse gameplay modes, and accessible features, this game is recommended for fans of Picross puzzles and the Story of Seasons franchise alike. Whether you're a seasoned puzzle enthusiast or new to the genre, Piczle Cross Story of Seasons offers a heartwarming experience that will keep you entertained for hours on end.

_childDocuments_.review: Good enough as a time waster, but the UI is not very smooth or as functional as it could be. That doesn't sound so bad, until you're trying to do your 60th puzzle and "right-click to go back" isn't working like the screen is telling you it will.The "farm progression" is also barely a factor. Most of the puzzles you solve don't impact the farm at all, and when you can see something added to the farm, it doesn't add much to the experience. Watching your farm animate is much less fun than watching a 00s screensaver, say. I would also like to add: there is a lot of guessing in the later puzzles, I would guess as a way of adding artificial difficulty. If I have to guess at your puzzle game, it's not  a puzzle game. It's a guessing game. That bit feels unsatisfying as well.I like that they took a risk and made this, but I'd like to see another attempt with a bit more heart. I wonder how well ConcernedApe could iterate on this concept, sigh.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big Picross/Nonogram enjoyer and I fell in love with Score Studios through Piczle Cross Adventure. I loved that it had exploration and RPG elements, and when I heard he was working on another Piczle Cross, I was expecting more of the same gameplay. Piczle Cross Story of Seasons is much more puzzle-oriented. So far in my playthrough I haven't encountered any adventure or story elements. It's pretty much exclusively puzzles, with images themed around Story of Seasons. There seems to be a good variety of puzzle dimensions, including collage puzzles comprised of smaller puzzles stitched together. The features are very good, including accessibility options like accommodating for colourblindness and convenience options like automatically filling out a row with X's when the necessary cells are coloured in. I've never played Story of Seasons so the Almanac doesn't have as much of an impact on me, but the theme is very cute and the music is nice. You can see your farm grow as you progress through your puzzles, but I wish you could interact with the farm more. I like that there are in-game achievements. The stats page is cool too, you can see how many cells you've filled in, and each completed puzzle shows your time as well as whether you used any hints or other help features. It currently isn't Deck Verified but it does perform well, which is to be expected since it was also released on Switch. Only issue is the text of the Puzzle Categories page and pop-ups are small but they're not really important to the gameplay.Overall I am happy with this game because the puzzles and features are great and it runs well on Steam Deck, but the previous Piczle Cross Adventure game set my expectations so high that I was disappointed in the lack of story and adventure elements, and I think it would've been so cool to be able to interact with the farm ourselves. If you enjoyed this game, I strongly encourage you check out Piczle Cross Adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: There's quite a bit of content for the price, and while the game isn't *difficult* by any means, even when turning off all the QOL features that make it even easier and more approachable for those who have a harder time with logic puzzles like these, it does still offer some semblance of needing to think on the puzzle while still being very fun and soothing to play. With the SoS music from games I've spent years playing, it's particularly great when I've expended all my energy doing errands and need something low key and relaxing to play.With the addition of the QOL features, the game can even be sort of completely brainless, just clicking every square until you get the correct ones if you're super tired but still need something to focus on without losing the low effort energy vibe as the game kindly doesn't penalize you for incorrect squares or accidental misclicks like most nanogram games in the genre do.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming little nonograms game to wind down and relax whenever you need. I really love the fact that every puzzle you complete "unlocks" items for the farm, which flourishes and evolves in the background as you progress.Pros:- The farm evolves as you play, making the experience even more rewarding.- I love being able to unlock entries in the almanac and see iconic and loved characters being unlocked.- It has ALL the options and QOL of various nonogram games floating around, but you have the choice of using them or not as you want.- I'm 9 hours in at the time of this review and I don't even have a fourth of the puzzles completed... Meaning the game has a LOT of contents, making it well worth the price. And I like to think I'm kinda fast at completing them.- On PC the graphics are really pretty.- At the time of this review, the game is not yet Steam Deck certified, but I can confirm that it works very well (with some caveats that I will cover later).Cons:- You may lose track of time playing this game and realize that 3 hours went by in a flash. Beware.- The 25x25 puzzles can be a bit small on a Steam Deck screen, but it certainly beats the same types of puzzles on, say, a phone screen...- Some color schemes can lack a bit of contrast, making it a tad bit harder to read the numbers on the sides. I mainly notice this with the winter theme (without using the accessibility modes).- If you plan on playing the game on a Steam Deck, do not apply a FPS limit, at least not a the time of this review. The dev is working on it. :)Overall, the positives far outweight the negatives, and I strongly recommend this game to all the Picross/Piczle/Nonogram fans! And if you're new to nonogram puzzles, fear not, they're very simple to understand and this game can be a fantastic introduction to them!

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a nanogram game of the month, you can easily grab this one.If you've never played this type of puzzle before, the rules are really simple. Each puzzle is made up of an empty grid that must be filled in according to the rules set out by the numbers on the top and left sides of the grid.The numbers indicate how many squares in a row or column need to be colored. Zeros and digits that fill the entire length are always the simplest and most effective way to begin. Then you just go from there to see where the numbers match. The only catch is when there are many numbers in the same row or column. In this situation, there must be at least one empty square between the group of numbers.The puzzle settings that allow you to tailor the experience are my favorite feature. You can enable the option to fill in rows and columns with zeros, mark numbers completed, and even auto-correct if you fill up the wrong squares. This makes the game playable at all skill levels.There are over 250 puzzles, and you can play any you want. The theme of the game is farming, so most of the solutions depict something you find on a farm. It’s also connected to a well-known farming game series, which can be seen in the almanac that you slowly fill up with images. The fun part is that the farm in the background changes and grows when you complete a couple of puzzles.

name: Arranger: A Role-Puzzling Adventure
detailed_description: Arranger: A Role-Puzzling Adventure follows the story of Jemma, a small-town misfit on a journey of self-discovery. Venturing out beyond her stiflingly cozy confines, she finds an inspiring world - but also one ruled by fear, and a strange, immovable ‘static’ force. Can she disrupt a culture of stagnation, and find a place to fit into it? Gameplay takes place on a unique, interconnected ‘grid’ that spans the entire world, snappily uniting movement, exploration, and combat. Anything on the same row or column as Jemma moves when she moves, and can ‘loop’ around the edge of the grid - creating both a playful sense of chaos, and a regular stream of small, thoughtful puzzles that twist and play with the central mechanic. Features: Unique, interconnected gameplay “grid” that snappily unites movement, combat, and exploration. A story-driven adventure about a small-town misfit on a journey of self-discovery. A breezy RPG without XP or inventory to manage, where everything is handled in-world. A nicely-sized campaign with some optional challenges, and various assist options so that you only get as stuck as you want to be. Debut game from an all-star development team, featuring the artist behind Braid.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is worth your time and treasure. I have issues which I'd like to discuss a little below, but this game is, no order: beautifully paced, fascinatingly designed, gorgeously painted, challengingly simple, and on the whole a delight. The "arrangement" mechanic was taken to such perfect lengths, without excessive gimmickry or abstraction. The level design moves hand in hand with the gorgeous paintings, giving a thoughtful narrative flow at the player's pace, capturing the wonderment Jemma experiences on her journey. Every tile radiates thought, care, attention, and skill. Movement feels delicious and slick, and as the speedrun tools suggest, fast movement once mastered becomes a complete thrill. The colors and compositions of all screens felt rich and whole. And the character designs featured a vast array of kinds of bodies; the artists took care to explore the tiniest details of their art. I must now, having frontloaded my compliments, spend a bit of time on my gripes with the writing:This is a young adult story. It is not wrong to write a young adult story. The dialogue blossoms with the sort of corny wit that i don't enjoy, but can respect. Every so often, certain lines struck me deeply: "If it's easy, that probably means someone is paying for it" and "it's not easy here, but we'd rather be ourselves" are both fruits borne of effective characterization and wit. However, as a whole work, the writers seem to have settled on a sort of self-consciously-wholesome lowest-common-denominator YA style. Every NPC encouter, after the starting area, involves giving or receiving a overstated moral lesson. Merriton's quest is a embarrassingly simple "you do be on that phone though" twitter metaphor. Flax begins with two deeply hollow and memorable NPCs, and then gives a fable of conformity and diversity i remember from pre-teen cartoons and children's books. There is nothing wrong, again, with writing for a younger audience; not everything has to be for me. However, there is a way to write for a younger audience *well*: without condescention, without unavoidable overtness, and without cloying kitsch.  Gemma's fundamental problem -- *that she has no way to act in the world without disrupting it for others* -- could have played host to all kinds of strange, particular, wonderful stories. Instead, we get a parable of apathy and privilege, change versus static. I would encourage the writers in their future projects to write timeless, write subtle, write reflexive, write as mature and subtle and rich and particular as their own lives. Had to get that out. Hate the whole wholesome thing. But this game still owns. Worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: At times like these I wish Steam had a neutral or "not for me" rating. Arranger is by no means an awful game, it's just one I personally found really disappointing, shallow and lacking in the actual *puzzle* department.The puzzle gimmick of shifting one row or column of the entire world at a time seemed interesting and relatively novel, so I went into this game expecting mind-blowing puzzles that would use this mechanic to its fullest potential. Unfortunately, that was not the case. At regular intervals throughout the game, it introduces a new gimmick, gives you 2-5 or so screens of relatively basic puzzles for you to play around with it in, just enough for you to get a feel for it. Then, just as it seems like things are finally going to get even remotely challenging and interesting, the game cuts the progression short, takes away your shiny new toy (sometimes it's the first and last time you will ever see it!) and moves on to the next one. As a result, the game never gets challenging. If you're at all puzzle games-savvy, you will likely breeze through every single puzzle in the game without struggle. It took me a little under 4 hours to 100% the game and see everything it had to offer and not once did I feel challenged.I did not care for the story, the characters or the setting at all. The tone of the dialogue and writing felt extremely smug and obnoxious (I guess some people would call this "millenial writing") and was an active detriment to the game. After the game's second town, which was a paper-thin cringe-inducing allegory for social media (complete with robotic "blue birds" that deliver letters for people who never go outside), I decided that I couldn't care less about how the story went and began mashing through every NPC interaction and piece of dialogue from that point onward until the end of the game.The music is nice and pleasant. The art is a bit hit or miss; the environmental background details and occasional comic book panels were nice to look at but the character sprites themselves don't animate and just wobble back and forth slightly in a way that ends up looking really unflattering and cheap.Overall, Arranger might be an alright game for you if you want something casual and non-threatening with an interesting core gameplay mechanic to play around with for a few hours, and if you have a high tolerance for its particular style of writing. But if you want intellectually interesting and challenging puzzles, this is not the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: What an awesome and unique puzzle game where you go on a puzzle adventure, but you move the world when you move around and solve many puzzles that way. It takes around 10h to complete and has many missable achievements.  10h 3/10 1 I wrote  No Yes, many achievements are missable. However, the game has a handy-dandy system to skip puzzles which makes playing through the game a second time a breeze. In my guide, I listed the achievements per area so you hopefully don't miss out on any.  No No No No No Not sure, I didn't use the system that let you skip puzzles in my first playthrough. So I don't know if you use that on a puzzle that is attached to an achievement, if that achievement still unlocks or not.  NoWhat an awesome game! It made me feel super smart, while also with moments super stupid. In Arranger you move the area you walk on and solve puzzles that way. And they are round, so if you leave an area at the top, you'll return at the bottom. With this mechanic, you'll solve many many puzzles in this awesome adventure game. You'll never fight with weapons in your hand, or open locks with keys in your pockets. The items lay around on the floor and it is up to you to move them toward the objective. It takes a bit of time to wrap your head around it, but it is so well done and unique. What took me the most time to get used to is that you can move items from within buildings outside by just moving them along with you. I also have felt stumped on some puzzles for a while, especially in the later areas and in the optional dungeons. What helped me when I was stuck was to remind me which info I had on solving the puzzle and what am I unsure about or what am I missing. There were like 1 or 2 puzzles I solved by luck by just moving around. However, there always is a solution, you just have to see it. The story in Arranger is interesting and funny. I love that they added a story that made sense and also made fun of that your character is the only one who moves around in such a weird way. You'll meet a lovely bunch of interesting people, from good to evil people and from clumsy to skilled people. The variety and the amount of characters you'll meet is crazy for such a short story, but they all fit in and made sense to be there. Another thing that I love about Arranger is the kind of achievements. Sadly it has missable achievements, which I'm not a fan of, but it has unique achievements. Achievements that make you explore the world a little more outside the main story. Achievements that make you do silly things (especially looking at the achievement for stealing a golden toilet). It is also nice that the game has a system to make replays so much faster by having the option to skip a lot of puzzles and dungeons. It took me around 10 hours to unlock all the achievements. I give Arranger: A Role-Puzzling Adventure 4 out of 5 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.It's a great puzzler that feels fast and reactive to play. I appreciate when a puzzle game achieves this, because it provides a similar satisfaction that playing an action game does, while still feeling more focused on teasing your brain rather than your reflexes.What's really brilliant about the game design is that it does not allow for fail states and therefore doesn't need a reset button. Its reactive gameplay stems from extremely simple controls (I found myself switching to just using arrow keys over starting with a controller, because it felt even faster and more precise to play that way) but this simplicity does not limit its puzzles from still becoming complex.Never too complex, mind you. Even with occasional head-scratchers, the overall difficulty feels more on the gentle side, which works in the game's favor. It does tell a story that - much like the gameplay - starts rather simple, but does get a bit more involved later on. If you were stuck on one puzzle forever, the pace for moving through the story would be hindered. It's a tight balancing act, and Arranger handles it wonderfully.Speaking of the story, there were plenty of moments that made me smile or chuckle. It's a funny game, even if comedy isn't its primary goal. Part of that is helped by the utterly charming art. I genuinely think that visually, this might be my top favorite game of the year. And that includes other heavy hitters on the visual front like Hauntii, ANIMAL WELL or Nine Sols.A big reason for that is that Arranger FEELS like a comic. Loads of games manage to LOOK like a comic, or include comic panels as cutscenes separated from the gameplay, but Arranger goes a step beyond. It builds a patchwork of comic panels that, at times, pop in and out of existence to create the scenery, while cleverly blending perspectives and levels of detail. All at once, you can clearly read the interactive parts of the game, while finding yourself centered in its larger world, and also taking in lovely details such as woodland critters observing your every move. It's absolutely brilliant, and maybe the game's biggest achievement in my eyes. Oh yeah, and the music and sound design is good, too.All in all, Arranger is a perfect blend of unique ideas and concepts that doesn't outstay its welcome. The gameplay and narrative go hand-in-hand, and together with fun, innovative visuals combine into one of 2024's best games around.

_childDocuments_.review: A first look:I was fortunate to win a copy of Arranger on X—previously known as Twitter—thanks to the wonderful people from the Latin American Games Showcase (@LAGShowcase)!I'm so used to regular character walking that I feel like I started a little wonky and insecure, but it didn’t take me long to get the hang of it, and before I knew it, I was zooming around through the maps, sliding left and right, up and down, and sometimes just all around. I even tried to take a ‘shortcut’, or however I should call them, to speed through faster, although I am not a speed runner and was doing that for fun. Simply because, why not?Perhaps some talented souls out there might put down amazing record times.I loved the art style and the music, but the puzzles were something, too. Sometimes, they were a little too challenging, and they had me scratch my head for a while or even ask my friend if he saw it cause I sure as heck didn’t. Some clicked immediately, and a very few… I.. I’m not sure what happened with those. It’s almost like I accidentally solved them while planning to position myself on a specific tile, and boom, solved. We were baffled a few times in voice chat about that but were not mad about it since it was convenient! (and funny)So, all I can say is that I had an enjoyable time playing through this one, and after finishing the game, all I could think of was how I really, and I do mean really, would like a second Arranger. I want to know more about them and everyone. About their gift of sliding and other lore-related stuff. And I know there is only so much you can do with this gameplay, but still. I really wouldn’t mind seeing more of it. But I guess that is something time will tell! Meanwhile, I’m watching to see what Furniture & Mattress LLC  has in store for us next time!
