_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: After upgraded my RAM to 16GB DDR4 from 8 GB DDR4, no longer had any performance issues, including the stuttering issue.Despite some annoying performance issues (in particular, a stuttering issue due to the default resolution setting and way too many loading screens), Bannerlord takes all the quality of life improvements of modded Warband and improves it further with new systems.Pros:1. Notables system makes questing, diplomacy, and relations more interesting.2. User Interface is vastly superior to Warband.3. Captain's Mode makes multiplayer fun for people who only played single player in Warband.4. Clan management allowing for multiple parties and management of characters (which fits the gameplay better than Warband's player character focused management).5. Introduction of armies and minor factions (like the Warband mod Prophecy of Pendor).6. Archery now viable for non-aimbotters. 7. Character customization much more polished.8. Polished tutorial and tooltips giving more direction.9. Cows are now a resource in your inventory rather than a map unit that runs away from you like a chicken.10. Battles end once all enemies are fleeing or dead (unlike Warband which needed to wait for all your men to recognize that the battle was over and cheer 3 times before you could leave).Cons:1. Performance is pretty bad. Game has a memory leak that causes extended play sessions for those with < 16GB of RAM to lag. Using the default resolution setting of desktop resolution causes massive frame drops and stutters (fixed by manually setting to your monitors resolution). Game is CPU heavy, not GPU heavy and appears to be optimized for single core performance (read Intel CPU's, doesn't like my Ryzen 5 CPU). 2. Lots of gameplay bugs (text errors, got some weird quest issues where a Lord I was looking for didn't appear on my map, had a similar issue with a caravan I was supposed to be escorting). 3. Multiplayer servers get overloaded at peak times (lose connection to servers). Summary: The gameplay loop is the same as Warband, which is exactly what I wanted from it. With the better modding support and the already set plan for new features (like ambushes), there is a very strong foundation here.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into purchasing this game after playing Mount and Blade: Warband a significant amount.  I fell in love with giant sandbox of that game and really hoped that this game would carry that same feeling.  Now after putting a couple days worth of game time and familiarizing myself more with the systems and gameplay I can honestly recommend this game.This game has flaws that I can easily acknowledge.  Its companion system is bland in that they are almost all warriors and the few that are not are either capped in tactics, medicine, or rogue.  By capped I also mean that because they have no attribute or focus points into that specific area it is very hard to get them past that area if you want those companions to become more specialized in what you hired them for.  The governor system is dumb as well as there are no companions that would be suitable for it as those are located in a different area.  The city management system is much more fleshed out than the previous game but at the same time still a bit lackluster as all cities will end up being built the same way.  The siege system introduced was really cool at first glance, but the AI always destroy your siege engines before you even really get a chance to use it in battle or they just rush the defenses so there is no buildup of tension at all.That all being said, Bannerlord makes marked improvement in areas compared to the first game.  The combat is familiar yet at the same time more difficult and refined and the simulation battles are a real treat now rather than just two armies rushing at each other and hoping for the best.  I have also really been enjoying the trade systems and going from place to place bringing goods and selling them to markets.While I listed many cons of the game I did so to warn buyers that the game is not complete.  Please keep in mind that it is an Early Access(EA) game before and after you purchase it.  It is hands down one of the more fleshed EA games that I have played and the developer team has done an amazing job at updating after release.  Never before have I seen a team release patches everyday for over a week after the game has been released.  It shows dedication and love for the game and those who bought it and I sincerely look forward to how the game develops in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: As a combat nerd from Warband I expected Bannerlord to  add on new and challenging mechanics while keeping the same free feel of combat from Warband. If you are new to the series you may not understand what you are missing out but if you are a returning Warband vet you will understand that the combat mechanics feel incredibly clunky and restrictive. Here are the issues I have with the mechanics:1. CameraCompared to Warband the camera feels incredibly stiff, as if you are walking around with a barbell around your neck. - When you use the ~ key (which is natural to Warband players) to look for flanking cav behind you, there is an incredibly annoying delay in the camera rotating back. - The camera shake feels out of place for a game series which gained popularity for its clean mechanics, this does nothing but make it more annoying to play the game, and harder to get "locked in" to the mechanics.- Using ranged and throwing weapons makes the camera go funky, and there is some sort of murky motion blur that occurs when trying to attack moving targets that was not present in Warband.- inability to tilt and pivot your entire upper body with the camera removes a key feature present in warband making combat feel even slower and stiffer2. Feinting changesIf you have not seen Warband feinting then you will not understand how much more simplified the feinting system is in Bannerlord.-Lack of in-swing directional changes makes the entire combat system incredibly slow and diminishes the range of attack strategies.-Changing your static blocking position is a poor replacement for the previous feinting system which had far more visual and audible cues and strategies.3. Combat DelayIn Warband, there was no delay between your clicks and your in-game actions besides the speed at which your weapon "reloaded" (and there was no blocking delay whatsoever). This allowed you to get into a tempo during fights, and combat felt realistically fast paced and involved a great deal of skill, reflexes, and talent to master. In Bannerlord they added a sort of unnatural blocking and swing delay which gives the game a feel similar to Chivalry or Mordhau, where timing, spam attacks, and mass spam in numbers has becoming the meta.-Block and attack delay completely destroy natural feel of combat known to Warband players.-Skill ceiling has been lowered to accommodate a more broad, casualized audience by appealing to mechanics from games like Chivalry and Mordhau. -Strange unique movements when repeating or chaining various attacks feel clunky and random.-Stance system is a poor replacement for greater diversity of animations present in warband.4. Class/Meta imbalancesBefore some keyboard warriors get riled up trying to claim the moral highground by saying "cav and archers were always overpowered", understand this; yes, cav and archers were the "damage dealers" in the competitive scene while infantry was just there to "hold the line" and stay alive, yet in bannerlord there are several issues which compound to make infantry nearly completely useless.- Shields are seemingly made of vibranium, taking an excessively long amount of time to destroy, therefore slowing down combat and making it near impossible to pressure a "turtling" infantry without archers or cav.- Movement is a lot slower compared to warband, and the movement debuffs present when shielding or moving backwards simply make infantry an even greater target for archers and cav.- Cav bumps send any ground units flying to the moon. Yes, I know that in warband cav bumping existed but it only stunned you for a split second, and you had to go max speed in order to knock someone over. In bannerlord you can be knocked over, thrown backwards and stunned for 3~ seconds by a cav at a slow canter.- Spears take several hits to kill most charging cav. Even when you stab a horse which is charging you at max speed in the face, it simply stuns it for a second in bannerlord, while in warband any fast charging cav would be killed in one shot if met with a spear.- Skirmish mode mechanics are stupid for a variety of reasons. It managed to take away the enjoyable parts of warband siege mode and battle mode and combine the annoying parts into a frankensteinian cluster ♥♥♥♥ of nonsensical proportion. 5. Minor Grievances -Throwing weapons move at the speed akin to a small child meekly tossing a rock, meaning aside from point blank range they are useless, removing medium and long range strategies.- Spears (or infantry momentum) are extremely underpowered and serve little purpose-Current game modes seem like various iterations of mob-like deathmatches with little strategy-Due to spam-like strategy of the game (from poor combat design), there is no benefit to using any weapon(in melee) except the hardest hitting 2h weapon you can find.-Audio cues for successful landed hits sounds like you are hitting a wet pillow.-Slower movement speed makes the game feel like you are trudging around in mud and gives massive advantage to archers and cav.-Set classes instead of being able to customize your loadout make the game feel restrictive (and unoriginal - concept prevalent in many other titles in this genre) in terms of what choices you can bring to the battlefield.Update 10/25/2022The Native Multiplayer side of things has seen little development for two years since the Early Access began. Servers crash constantly and often remain offline for days, weeks, and there has even been times that they are not fixed for entire months. Taleworlds clearly focused all of their resources into the Singleplayer side of things, as there are only 3~ Multiplayer developers, and only one seems to be doing anything. Multiplayer is NOT in a full release state, it is still in a Beta, not even Early Access state. Mods are the only redeeming quality for this game, so I would recommend to all newcomers that you WAIT for a couple months before buying, unless you are simply buying for the Native Singleplayer experience.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Good game, and unique still. Technically a bigger, better Warband with massively upgraded visuals and better engine, but lost some of the charm underway, and could really benefit from mods to make it less repetitive.Blah:Well, mostly it's Warband, but better engine, better visuals, larger battles, less jank, more refined. Somehow, the old wonky Warband was more enjoyable to me, though. There, I would ride around with 20-30 elite cavalry troops and hunt bandits and sea raiders for a good while before entering service of any king, and taking on the responsibilities that come with all that. After joining a faction, I'd then get just one village. To get a castle, I'd really have to be strategic about it, and then really dig in and work to defend it. Claiming (and holding) one of the cities, that would take even more.Here, there kind of isn't any middle ground, or that sense of achievement. Early game just riding around with some troops, there's really not all that much to do (unless I guess you want to get into bandit life), there's just the same looters and some bandits (maybe it's a difficulty setting, idk, I didn't start a new campaign just to see if there was a setting that would make them scale up over time or something). After I tired of the early game of leveling up, and smith grind, and hunting for small bandit troops I'd steamroll - I joined a kingdom, and the ruler just dumped 3-4 enemy towns, 2 castles and a bunch of connected towns on me in short succession. And just like that, now I'm basically waging war against an entire faction by myself, and managing politics to avoid revolts in all the settlements, etc.Somehow, despite this being larger and more refined in basically every way, it ends up feeling *more* repetitive than the old Warband gameloop. In large part, I guess it's due to this being all scaled up, which fundamentally changes the way the game plays.In some ways that's good, in other ways, it's lost a bit of the magic to the core game loop, that Warband had.I definitely see why people are upset the updates have kept breaking mods, because the game feels like it's screaming for mods to add some more diversity, and the updates don't actually feel like they've made much impact in that regard, since it was in EA.At this point, the game is already really well polished, and it seems like it'd be better if the devs treated it as a foundation for modders to have fun with, and stop breaking mods with meaningless updates and making modders give up due to the constant maintenance.

_childDocuments_.review: I do highly recommend this game, it's very fun. I myself am likely to put some more hours into it after I write this. However, I do not want to write a favorable review as I planned to once this game came out in full, as this game is releasing in less than a month as of the moment of writing this, and it still feels very much unprepared for a full launch. AI bugs, graphical errors, and promised features that are still missing are all huge parts why this review is being written, but an almost equally prevalent factor in why I'm writing a negative review (and a factor almost nobody is considering) is the fact that when they release this game, even if they implement all these features and fixes they promised so long ago on PC post release (which they won't), I know for a damn fact console players are going to still be playing the very first ever launch, because that's exactly what happened with Warband. I'm proud of this studio for growing as much as it has and making such a novel game series as MnB, and especially proud of them for finally ditching the old engine and starting from scratch with something more modern; it can't have been easy. But that doesn't give them an out for over-promising: a trend that has been far, far too common in the gaming scene for far, far too long.

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to the series, a game where you can spend hundreds of hours into it and it still has replayability. This game is great, but i could be generational which is honestly the frustrating thing about it.While i do recommend this game here are my critical points to it:- Diplomacy between Kingdoms is absolute lackluster and they immediately declare war upon you if they see your Kingdom announced if you don't immediately get about 6-7 clans pledging to you.- The world itself has so much potential but the interactions are absolute lackluster at times. Bartering is almost comically bad until you get your Trading skills to 300 and can barter for Fiefs with other Nobles.-  the Level and progress System is not optimal and starts to get very obnoxious at higher levels. I would have preferred if Talesworlds would have stuck to the level system of Warband.- Unlike in Warband, most Battles feel not important because in a blink of an eye, the enemy shows up with an even bigger Army after you defeated the first one. Also the pacing of the wars and the game itself is off for the inheritance and generational system that it wants to implement. Entire Kingdom get destroyed without the first ruling generation to even die.- Mods in this game often cause the game to crash for me or not even make it able for me to start. Surely Talesworld can provide better tools to the modding community than this? Because Mods in itself could make the game generational.Even tho that is a lot of critique points that i have for the game, the greatness of it is clearly there to see and i adore the concepts it has and all the improvements compared to Warband. I am just greedy and want even MORE out of this game like for example, not only smithing weapons but also Armor yourself? But thats wishful thinking on my part. Anyway you see it tho, this game can suck the life out of you without you noticing in it's current stance and still has so much room for growth and as mentioned before, become generational.

_childDocuments_.review: HIGHLY RECOMMEND TRULY INSPIRED AND GREATLY INVOLVED GAME WITH EVERYTHING YOU COULD WANT OUT OF A MEDIEVAL FUEDALISM TYPE GAME.If you remember that old online flash game Feudalism, I present to you it's high production bigger brother. You control your own character which works their way up the Feudalism Food Chain in one of many ways. You can gain Renown through trade, combat, or bureaucracy.Combat consists of 1st/3rd person fighting with your player character as well as using the command screen to direct your legions in strategic ways to win the battles. Enlist interesting NPCs to act as your sergeant’s and help delegate various responsibilities of your clan. These NPC can then be given command of your various platoons as they fight for you on the battlefield.Swear your allegiance to a kingdom and join them in siege warfare (or send your troops to fight in your stead). Then after your kingdom conquers a new castle or village use your political influence to sway them into giving you command of it. Create your own kingdom, and forge your own alliance, or declare war.Overall, this is a truly stunning game. I’ve barely had it a week and it’s just amazing. I love the mix of 1st person combat with real-time unit commands. I cannot believe how much the factions declare war, form armies, siege castles, and declare peace with or without my direct involvement. I’m working on a battle-hardened king who proves himself through feat of combat and tactical prowess, Winning Tournaments across the lands. However, my next playthrough I’m considering a Roguish Backstabbing and Cunning Bureaucrat who creates and uses leverage as his sword to sway lords and kings alike into his bidding.

_childDocuments_.review: It's more Mount and Blade, but polished. Tale Worlds has added new systems, such as Smithing and criminal activities, while iterating on existing systems from Mount and Blade: Warband. Overall, this game is wonderful for anyone that enjoyed Warband.That being said, there are two "issues" I have with Bannerlord that I think people should be aware of:1) The game is definitely in Early Access. It isn't totally finished. Tale Worlds releases hotfixes and patches at a blisteringly fast pace.2) Long time single-player only Warband fans may be dismayed to learn that "auto-blocking" is not present in Bannerlord and may not ever make it into the game. The combat system is very reminiscent of Warband's combat system. It is also built on the concept of directional attacks and blocks. The lack of auto-blocking creates a learning curve that can be intimidating to those who, like me, played all of Warband with auto blocking enabled. 70 hours in and I feel like I can somewhat reliably block most of the time. That being said, I find the game extremely unenjoyable without a shield. RIP two-handed axe builds. :(

_childDocuments_.review: Bannerlord is a fantastic game that truly justifies its price. However, at first glance, it might not immediately pique your interest. I recommend watching plenty of videos or giving it a try and returning it if it doesn't suit your taste.I purchased Bannerlord when it was at version V1.0.1, and I must say it had numerous bugs and missing features compared to the current version. The developers have done a commendable job in improving the game, but there are still areas that could be further enhanced or added. It seems that the game is considered "finished," and updates might not be as frequent as before, possibly limited to DLC releases.Now, let's dive into what I like and dislike about the game.The game offers four possible roles: Ruler, Vassal, Mercenary, or none of the above. While starting as none might not be the typical choice, you'll likely gravitate towards joining a kingdom or creating your own eventually.However, I believe the developers should include more roles, such as a soldier, thug, caravan guard, lone knight, shopkeeper, farmer, and others. These might sound mundane, but they would add realism and allow players to expand their character's story as they see fit.Regarding fiefs, there are two types: Castles and Settlements. While players can manage these holdings, there isn't much to do with them. You'll find yourself spending little time in your fiefs, as there's no compelling reason to linger. Most interactions involve basic tasks like upgrading the fief, reinforcing the garrison, stashing items, or completing quests.This is where the game falls short in the roleplaying aspect. The lack of interaction with NPCs is quite disappointing. Taking a break and spending time with the in-game characters is a missed opportunity, as there are no meaningful interactions or conversations available. Even a simple feast event could have a significant impact on the game's immersion and experience.When it comes to modding, the game offers a rich and diverse range of mods created by talented modders, covering various aspects of the game. Notably, the "Improved Garrison" mod stands out, significantly enhancing castle and settlement operations.However, the major drawback of modding is that with each game update, mods tend to break and become incompatible with the newer version. Frequent updates, including hotfixes, can obliterate mods, leading many modders to stop creating great content until the developers find a solution to this issue. This is unfortunate and hampers the modding community's potential to contribute continuously to the game's improvement.Regarding diplomacy, it is surprisingly limited. The game lacks essential features like non-aggression pacts and alliances, which are commonplace in many strategy games. The Kingdom menu, despite being crucial for rulers, feels lacking and requires more improvements to give players more agency and options for managing their realm effectively.The side quests, in my opinion, are underwhelming in terms of quantity and quality. Many of them can be tedious and unrewarding, making it unappealing to send companions to complete them. The time it takes for companions to finish quests is also frustratingly long, far exceeding what a player would take to complete the same tasks. Even more frustrating is how companions can fail quests despite being given elite troops, which should theoretically ensure their success. Such inconsistencies raise questions about the quest mechanics and create frustrating experiences for players.In conclusion, I believe that Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord is a great game with the potential to become even greater. While there are areas that could be improved, such as addressing mod compatibility issues, expanding the diplomacy system, and enhancing the side quest mechanics, I understand that implementing these changes would require considerable time and effort from the developers.It's important to acknowledge that game development is a complex and challenging process, and developers often face limitations in terms of resources, time constraints, and other factors. Calling developers lazy is unfair, as they work tirelessly to bring players an enjoyable gaming experience while managing various technical and creative challenges.Ultimately, as players and fans of the game, we can provide constructive feedback and express our desires for improvements. While not every suggestion may be feasible, developers often listen to the community's feedback and work towards making the game better over time. Let's appreciate the efforts of the development team and look forward to the potential future updates and improvements that could elevate Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord to new heights.

_childDocuments_.review: The long awaited Mount and Blade II: Bannerlord.  Bannerlord keeps to it's original formula that made the previous titles so successful, while adding new features, and perfecting the old ones.  I 100% recommend this game, but read on to be sure.This game is in early access, and due to that you have some bugs, incomplete quests, which disappointed me at first.  The first day I actually ran into a bug that broke my first save completely, and I had to completely restart.  I was upset, but I dove back in, knowing it could happen again.  It is also worth mentioning, that since release (as of this review, Day 3) there have been two patches to fix many of the bugs.I had a lot of fun, and could not put the game down.  I spent 31 hours, and have just completed my first campaign.  The entire map is owned by the Southern Empire, but I felt it was much too easy for them to take, they never lost a single castle or city once they took it.  The beginning for a player is slow, and difficult even on easy settings.  The grind is real, and you will lose all your men, and have to start all over multiple times.  Welcome to Mount and Blade, that is what makes this game so fun; there are risks, but the rewards are amazing.On the flip side, late game is extremely easy, almost too easy.  At the end of my 31 hours, I own 6 cities, and not even sure how many castles personally, and now I have over 10m Gold, more than I could ever hope to spend, and I make so much there is no real challenge.  If I were to lose all my troops, the next city over has so many available, it takes me 3 minutes to completely recreate a full fighting force.  Same with influence, I could completely run the empire with how much I have.  All to do what though?  No enemies to fight unless I fight the empire I am in, and they are way too powerful to take on, tournaments but I have all the gold I need, which is not necessarily a bad thing, there has to be an end game, but there should be some bigger challenges than steam rolling everybody.The game needs to be rebalanced, the starting game needs some work, and the end game needs a lot. The main quest, chasing after the 10 nobles, is really difficult, as they keep moving and it is hard to pin them down, and the main quest is a bit lacking as of right now due to Early Access, I just wish they had worked more on it before releasing.Over all, fantastic game, and I am about to begin my second campaign, and I look forward to all the updates that comes!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the playtime and my playtime in Warband, I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who isn't a fan of the series. Warband itself stood firmly on the fact it had just the right mix of things as the only game in its genre to stand out as there were few other games in a similar setting and role, but Warband also had its share of jank and poor design choices. Luckily a large part of that was smoothed over by modifications.Bannerlord took about ten years to develop, then released in an early access phase, and still hasn't seemed to fix a lot of issues. A lot of development resources seems to have gone to overhauling things like graphics and the character generators while core gameplay systems didn't get the attention they needed. The real core of the game, the battle system, is probably about the only thing that is well done, though that's not hard considering it was also present in Warband.Is awful. The only way to make any significant amount of money is margin trading, spamming low effort quests, or selling loot from battles. Workshops and other long term income projects are never worth the investment and attention required to maintain them and even the most profitable workshop will make you less than 1,000 denars a week which is virtually nothing. Troop upgrades also suffer from a similar type issue where upgrading troops is dirt cheap but the same gear they're wearing is magnitudes more expensive.Skills became both better and worse. On one hand, the skills themselves were completely overhauled into new categories and a "perk" system was introduced which allows you to choose one of two (or sometimes just one) benefit at certain landmark levels. These benefits are interesting and can change up some considerations of how you play, but overall a lot them are flatly better than another in 99% of scenarios.A decent number of skills are useful: All combat skills, riding, athletics, steward. You can raise these just by using the related action.Some skills are useful but stupidly difficult to train: Trade, charm, tactics. These take forever to level even if doing what they're used for and investing in them. Don't expect them to budge very much.Some skills are both nigh useless and are also abysmal to level: smithing, rougery. Skills like smithing and rougery didn't get the amount of content they needed behind them even if they were supposed to have content. Smithing/crafting boils down to a UI minigame of playing with sliders until you get a weapon with correct stats and rougery is only involved in about two places.Not a lot has changed since the first game which I guess is good. There's still the same attack/defend directional and chambering, though chambering doesn't ever seem to be clearly explained and either you 'get' it or don't. Sieges are better in the fact that AI is not forced to funnel through a predetermined entrance or exit. AI for the most part without any orders will try to have ranged units hold the walls and melee units hold entrance points, but giving any orders immediately turns everything into a mosh pit and it is very difficult to intelligently order groups of soldiers to do things during a siege. Majority of the legwork is easily done by you if you get your hands on a siege weapon or just an advantageous position.Honestly not much improves here without a ton of mods. It always seems like the developers never play past the initial few weeks in a game since once you start massing power the amount of tedium involved in managing things like garrisons, buildings, and patrols becomes immense. Many things like diplomatic effects or certain laws signed into power have minimal effects or effects that are actually broken in vanilla.I would only recommend this if you want to actually sit down and install 100 mods and spend a lot of time tweaking configs to find an ideal difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Having about 450h in total on the earlier games in this series, the base concept has been enough to draw me into the world and put me into the shoes of a lord or lady in Caldradia, or any of the modded worlds (starwars, GoT, Warhammer, etc for example). getting this game as a present i knew i'd like Bannerlord, since it'd at least be as good as the original, but propably missing the old classics like the NPC:s from the old games, due to it being set at an earlier "start date". Having only seen some yotube videos, maybe a trailer here and there, i didn't know what else to expect, other than maybe fancier graphics and new gui elements.when i started playng this game for the first time, i was supprised af when i realized that Bannerlord has completely re-immagined everything! in a good way. Taleworlds has sat down, and thought about how to make the concept better, and they actually delivered! the game is indeed more than just warband ported over to directX12!!to put it into a word, i'd say bannerlord is "dynamic", or "most dynamic" if i had two words. when i got to playing, i decided to start off my dynasty by trading some sheep to a nearby town, since a villager told a rumor about trade prices. after savescumming my way to that town (since i had put the dificuilty too high, the dificuilty settings are about the same as in warband with some extra features), i made a neat profit. i thought "well, i could propably repeat this and make a fortune", but i realized that the prices had changed. in warband the prices change all over, in every marketplace in a town, for every good depending on how much you sell of anything, magically, somehow the horse merchant caring less for your cabage because you sold gloves to the general store the same day. in bannerlord how ever, each good, or good category (even better) have a supply and demand system, this means that the prices for all goods are DYNAMICALLY generated for every town and village! i was amazed by this. the villages also are specialised, meaning that your geographic proximity to any good is in a way a market factor for how much a town wants a good! the game doesn't hide this, you can see each transaction that happens in towns by lords and the like on the map if you have visibility. this game is perfect, this game is my dream. this game is a better version of victoria 2's economy! this game is the dream! and this is just the first feature i found!there are a lot more features hiding in this box, and i want to discover them all! <3

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. I've been playing this game for quite some time now and I can say that while I would still tell potential buyers to wait for a sale, since the price is a bit too much for the state of the game currently, I can wholeheartedly recommend this game especially those who were big fans of Warband. The things that I have complained about (see below) are now being fixed and the game is running on my low end PC much more smoothly than when the game was first released. The current 1.0.6 patch removed most of the lag and stutter that I experienced whenever I played. Though there are still some stutters especially on combat, loading screens are still pretty annoying and it seems there is still some memory leak problems judging by how my PC wants to die every time I restart my game, they are all bearable now. With how the devs have been working non-stop to optimize the game, I have confidence that all these problems will be fixed in the future.Original post 4/2/2020: Though it breaks my heart to say this, I cannot on good conscience recommend this game in its current state. Lags and stutters in and out of combat, incomplete quests, a lack of stuff to do in the world, bugs galore and oh my god so many loading screens are the reasons why I recommend for people to either wait while the devs iron this game out or buy it on sale if you really want to try it. Having said that I do not regret buying the game just disappointed by it somewhat. There is potential here, and I liked the snippets of game that I was able to play before I surrendered to all the problems I pointed above. I'll keep an eye out for their progress.Some people are saying that we should cut them some slack since the game is in early access and to that I say it's been a DECADE since warband and almost EIGHT YEARS since they first announced a sequel. I'd say it's normal to be disappointed when this is the state of the game they give us after all that waiting.Update 04/05/20: The devs just put up a patch addressing the memory leak issues. What I can say is the game is playable for me now but still the problem has not been fully addressed. Playable does not mean that there are no more lags and stutters. Also, the problem of the game slowing down after a couple of hours of play is still there. It seems that these problems are specifically prevalent to people with only 8 gigs of RAM, so yeah. For people with RAM lower that 16, don't buy this game yet and don't believe the recommended RAM of only being 8 GB.

_childDocuments_.review: It's simply not worth the price tag. There's fun to be had here, but that fun comes with a lot of frustration. You'll be fighting back bugs and performance issues the entire time, and personally, the combat AI is not fun to play against in this game currently. You'll constantly be blocking and backpedaling as clumps of units converge on you and simply never stop attacking and leaving you with a such a narrow window to counterattack. The updates come out rather slow and nowadays most of it is focused on combat for multiplayer. Bug fixes are a plus though, but there has not been a massive singleplayer content update since launch.Most singleplayer updates are tweaks or small additions. In fact, some patch notes are features and mechanics that are already present in Warband, such as the distribution of experience to all units after a battle, awarding experience for being in tournaments, etc. I get that people want to be forgiving when a game says "Early Access", but the price tag also says $49.99, If you came here looking for a purchase worth 50 dollars, you'll be very disappointed. But if you like kisses and a promise that it'll get better, then hey this might be the purchase for you.Wait for a sale, or at the very least wait for a large content update.

_childDocuments_.review: Troop command system makes it quick to issue orders to troops but does take some time to learn, this allows the player to get involved in the battle and still command the troops effectively.Direction based approach to attack moves, rather different to most games but once you get the hang of it it is definitely a more intuitive and interesting.Large scale battles with a couple thousand troops all with their own target and animations etc.Partake in sieges attacking or defending, your actions can change the tide of battle just watch out for those arrows.Large focus on tactics in battle enables experienced players to defeat much larger armies than their own if they use terrain and troops effectively, while also keeping the enemies challenging in evenly matched battles.Engaging political system that allows the player to really affect the world for better or for worse.Players can buy workshops or receive taxes from fiefs to passively earn currency allowing them to focus on things they want to do rather than always worrying where their next meal is coming from. Currency is still something to watch though, grow your armies too large or loose too many fiefs and you can find yourself paying your troops more than you are making.

_childDocuments_.review: Catches the spirit of original M&B really well while infusing the formula with gorgeous visuals with a huge attention to detail. Having your opponent clutch at his throat as your arrow pierces it, or thrown spinning in the direction of your double handed axe swing is immensely satisfying. The game feels big right out of the gate. The greatly expanded Calradia is stunning. The new combat system (which, read: is manual blocking only now, no auto mode), is at first daunting but you quickly realize the expanded level of depth it allows makes learning the combat system much, much more rewarding. I really encourage people not to let that sour the game if you're used to Warband easy mode.There's a few rough patches here and there, a model or two with inverted normals, bugged quests and borked siege AI, but otherwise it's significantly more polished than most EA titles and anyone arguing otherwise (especially coming from Warband) is absolutely talking out of their ass. With that said: the game's flow and balance really isn't tuned yet. While impressed, I've found myself less engaged than Warband. From looters being irritatingly hard to catch, tournaments being less obvious, and generally the world feeling more complex but less transparent, the game needs tuning badly. Some of the UI is poorly thought out, delivering huge chunks of information with important data being slow to identify. And there's some questionable decisions in areas such as character banners- the colourful, feudal banners that very clearly identified characters are gone and replaced with single colour flags with a simple icon overlayed. This is pretty boring to look at (yay, all the Vladians are red... not), but also makes it hard to identify characters. As a result of this, I don't think I would recommend this game to newcomers just yet. But if you're a Warband fan, there's still plenty to enjoy here and it's clear a lot of love went into the game.Although. WHERE ARE MY BATTLE BANNERS TALEWORLDS? I WAS PROMISED BANNERS!

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked MB WB or classic you will love this game. Mount and Blade II: Bannerlord is challenging Strategy game that puts you in the role of a soldier of fortune/mercenary captain trying to find your way in the troubled lands of Calradia. The paths to renown are many, you can be a poacher, a thief, a cruel raider, a defender of the meek or even aim to conquer your own castle or plot of land. Much of it is alike the classic experience, with some great improvements. The travelling now is smoother with the time controllers and the pointers that you can add to aid you tracking your targets, now the reports update more quickly. The combat is fluid and engaging, with some moments of frustration and pure chaos. The strategy element got also revamped making the experience even better. If you want to immerse yourself into a medieval game of strategy combat and trickery, this is your place.

_childDocuments_.review: It's what you came here for.If you like Mount & Blade, it's Mount & Blade.I will say, as far as the single player campaign is concerned, this game is ever so slightly more streamlined than Warband, but it's not an outright replacement like they had probably hoped.If you like the new graphics, siege engines, and the extra details (quite tiny) with combat logs, then you'll like the game. As far as the structure of the game goes, it's identical to a modded version of Warband, basically.My big problem with it IS the streamlining. While there is hardly any of it, I do miss the ability to talk to any prisoner or soldier in my party. Now you can only talk to significant NPC prisoners and party members. There may not have been much for them to say, but I always remember Mount & Blade being full of optional stuff like that.Also, while I'm not sure if I have the right to complain about this, I did somewhat expect there to be some new functional dialogue and interactivity with the people and towns. As far as I can gather, the game doesn't really do much to add on to the original Warband system. It mainly clones it, very slightly streamlines it, and adds a new coat of paint.TLDR: It's more of the same. It's the reason why I like it, and it's the biggest problem.

The sandbox and roleplaying in here is a poorly veiled lie.-Economy is "buy fish at coast then sell at plains", this makes sense for food only and is so boring by the time I maxed the trade skill to buy towns I realised I'd rather watch ice melt than make a trader character again. Workshop income is broken, makes no sense and it's never clear why your workshop in a fully supplied town makes pennies.-Relationships don't make sense, every character is the same with no personality, lords are so stupid they will sell you their only town for 2mil while being in one of the most powerful kingdoms.-The AI doesn't adhere to the same rules as the player, it cheats. Lords can just spawn armies out of thin air. So why the hell should I bother trying to outplay the economy of a rival faction if their armies apparently don't even need to eat? _childDocuments_.review: Being a fan of mount and blade for more than ten years (yes, well before warband, in fact being a fan when mount and blade was still little more than Zendar), I have waited more than ten years for bannerlord. Is this a disappointment? Maybe, because expectation over a course of ten years tend to be extremely high but is this a game worthy of recommendation? Absolutely. Some of the plus and minuses of the game:PLUS:a) graphic upgrade, maybe not stunning but well enough to convince us to move from warband to bannerlordb) Medieval simulation. The feudal system has been greatly enhanced giving you a feel of how a nobody moves up hierarchy. It's more difficult alright but whether this is good or bad is a matter of taste per se.c) Horse movement --- more realistic, now you dun become a tank without proper practices and the right horsed) Trading system --- maybe it's more difficult to make money by trading because of the new system but it's definitely make the world setting more real. And there are more caravans to loot (sensible too),e) battle and sieges are WAY LARGER now and fighting in an army makes much more sense now. MINUSa) You are no longer a superhero. Clearly, the developer has switched from a single player focused game to a multiplayer game focus. Do I like this? maybe not but I gotta say, this is not a reason for not recommending. Now, you just have to fight in formation or you won't last against two or three enemies (unless you topped your skill)b) Slower progression --- the progress is much much slower now. Especially without the focus point. I guess this is still undergoing balances but for a singleplayer experience (i'm only singleplayer person), this seems to be a little time wasting.c) bugs ---- still some to go. Many who began with warband would find this unbearable but for a player who has followed through mount and blade from its humble beginnings, I am actually quite impressed with how finished this game already is. Probably because they spent ten years and charged 20 times more than they did for mount and blade (in beta or alpha).Overall, highly recommended for both new players and veterans. Ignore those negative reviews, most of them are because of the bugs (some of the bugs are indeed game breaking, like CTD) but considering this is an early access and the potential (and the development curve of this predecessor), just buy. Lastly, I CANNOT BELIEVE I ACTUALLY LIVE LONG ENOUGH TO SEE BANNERLORD RELEASED!!!!! WOW!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: While a fine game, Bannerlord feels hollow and extremely repetitive, with the only real activities being to complete repetitive quests, fight in simple battles and trade. I don't care if its in Early Access, the game has been in development for at least 8 years and this its sad to see that this is the product of all that time.The simplest way to describe this game is repetitive, and very few actually new and fun features being added. Warband was a fun game, but just slapping new graphics on it and some minor improvements is not nearly enough to justify a $50 price tag, especially when so much still needs work.The kingdom stuff is abysmal and as deep as a puddle, the combat quickly gets stale and very little actually feels improved upon. From a sequel you'd expect that there are at least some good additions but instead we see a barebones and hamfisted crafting system. We see a cumbersome and overbearing UI. We see loading screens every 2 seconds just so we can see the terrifying models of whoever we're about to fight. The game feels amateurish at best and gutted at worst.For new features, why not include a weather system that effects combat, ambushes, genuinely well-written companions or even just actual quests. Yes this is Early Access but right now the game suffers from Outer Worlds syndrome where people want it to be good so they just repeat it over and over with cries about how its simply the best when in reality all that's here is a mediocre product that barely improves on the original and could never get out of Early Access. I hope the game improves, I love mount and blade and something great is definitely here but right now its a garbled mess that doesn't feel actualized in any way, it seems the game has been in development hell for sometime and without a clear direction the game is going it seems like they were more or less content to add a bit to the kingdom side of things, throw on a fresh coat of pain and call this a sequel.Don't think of EA as an excuse for the problems this game has, this is a time where we NEED to criticize this game if we want to see something truly great be a successor to Warband, after all thats the real point of Early Access, not to just ship an uninspired product.

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom line up front:- If you put hundreds or thousands of hours into the previous title (Warband) and want more of the same. This game is for you. The developers appeared to have followed a "Don't fix what isn't broken" philosophy.- If you were expecting an entire different game. You might be disappointed. Specifics:The purpose of this review is to give you straight to the point info.- The world map will look very familiar. some settlements have almost the same names as warband. The map is bigger and has more details such as mountains, rivers, etc.- Combat is harder(or just different). No auto-block as of now, so if you plan on using a two handed weapon I suggest you spent some time in the tutorial to practice directional blocking. Some of the AI's attacks seem to hit through shields (probably a bug). The overall speed of combat seems a bit faster than warband. Even vets of Warband will need some time to master the combat again.- Commands in battle give you several different formations options and commands. Closely resembling the Viking Conquest expansion of warband, just a bit more complex.- The quests seem to follow the same basic setup as warband just different text and scenarios.- the worlds is more alive and immersive. Several more NPC's. The taverns actually feel like taverns with patrons, bards, etc. You can interact with certain objects like siting  in chairs. Very good for those that like to roleplay.-  There are many bugs and CTD's. Some game breaking, but I expect these to be patched out over the next few days. - I have a high-end PC, so I can't speak much to the performance on Low - Mid range rigs. I run maxed out settings and have not experienced any slugish or stuttering even in 1,000 man battles.(Specs for those who care)Motherboard:          MPG z390 Gaming Pro CarbonGraphics Card:	GeForce RTX 2080 Ventus 8G OCCPU:                        Core i7 9700k 3.6GHz (4.9 GHz Turbo)RAM	                TridentZ RBG 2x16 GB (32GB) DDR4 Memory	                2 x 1TB (2TB) M.2 2280 SSDMonitor	                Predator XB1 Ultra HD 3840x2160 4kI hope this review has been informative. Feel free to ask questions in the comments.

_childDocuments_.review: I really hope to turn this around to a thumbs up at some point, but I gotta say as a lifelong Mount and Blade fan (1000+ hours into Warband easily) it definitely falls short for me in its current state.  There just isn't enough going on here.  To be honest there's more difference between warband and with fire and sword than there is between warband and bannerlord and I wouldn't even recommend fire and sword either.  On top of that a ton of features are just completely missing.  Smithing for instance you'll create a character that is geared toward smithing and it doesn't warn you at all that smithing isn't currently implemented, but then you get to midgame and realize you wasted all those starting points to smithing when you try to smith and just... nothing at all works.  The ranged combat seems slightly improved but the melee combat has regressed.  There's a lot of features just sort of missing as well from the original, for example no camping on the overmap.  I don't know... kind of just underwhelming especially considering how much time this game has been in development.  I hope they turn it around but until then I don't recommend the game, warband is just a better game still.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is really a massive disappointment for the amount of time it was in development, TW seriously dropped the ball on this one. The graphical design and looks of the game are great. The new map is absolutely massive BUT the game is utterly a wasteland when it comes to actual content. Quests are so far and few between the world just feels so damn empty, and the few quests you do run across are the same cookie cutter quests over and over again. For the amount of time it took to make this game the sheer lack of content and creativity when it comes to content in game is really pathetic.The singleplayer is extremely boring and repetitive with no *real* sense of direction in which you or the game are going. Bandit hunting simulator 2020 can sum up this game as a whole. Every hotfix or update they add to the game seriously damages something else in-game (Mostly the economy). The combat is extremely clunky and hard to learn. much harder than warband, you'd figure they would have atleast made the combat better in some way but no, no real changes at all besides graphical, the combat honestly feels worse than in warband. Horse mechanics and handling are still terrible, was atleast hoping for horses to no longer rear back when hitting something, always felt so silly and unrealistic, They really should have made horses ragdoll and eject riders when colliding but they couldn't fathom that in the 8+ YEARS it took to develop this dumpster fire of a game.Overall I really wish this game would have stayed in development, I feel the playerbase forced their hand to pushing it out too early and it ended up biting them in the ass big time, which is extremely sad. They really should have taken more time to flesh the game out, because in its current state its astonishing that we waited this long for such a flop of a gameHopefully modders will be able to revive this game, otherwise its dead in the water.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so i believe it was time to refine my review a little bit. Before reading this, I want to note that I am a massive fan of warband, I have played warband for basically 6 years and have amassed over 700 hours on it playing mods like AWOIF and Third Age. Furtheremore, consider that the game just was released and is in early acess, thus prone to bugs and issues. What I truly love about the Mount & Blade series is that they aren't just games, they are a story generator. Want an example?Meet Beorn, my first playthrough of Mount & Blade Bannerlord, a Sturgian (Slavic / Nordic) who recently lost family members. Due to coming of age and becoming an adult, Beorn is determined to seek out his glory and wealth in the world of Calradia. He begins in the divided Empire which replicated the Byzantine Empire, here he begins doing shady deals with merchants and business owners to make some cash. Sure he attracted the attention of the guards, but he made enough to bring together a group of recruits. After spending time trading, doing oddjobs for merchants, and killing local bandits, Beorn felt ready to play the games of war. He joined Garios, the leader and warlord of the Western Empire as a mercenery. As he wished, he would quickly see battle as the Western Empire declared war on Batannia, the celtic and gaulic like faction. He spent roughly a year working as a mercenery, taking parts in sieges and massive battles. His warband would many times be slaughtered by the enemy, but within weeks he would have more men ready to fight. Making a wealth but no name, he left the Western Empire, it was time to go back to his homeland. He finally arrived in the cold north known as sturgia, where he spent time killing sea raiders and increasing his renown and wealth. But before he knew it, he would be accepted as a vassal to raganvad, the leader of sturgia. Now in a world of disarray, what will Beorn do next?P.S. This game has so much to it, and even with 10 hours of gameplay after the first day. I look forward to playing it more. Sure there are bugs and issues, but that is expected from a game in early access!

_childDocuments_.review: If the game is lagging and running horrifically, change your video settings from Borderless fullscreen to Fullscreen. I went from having to run the game in 1600 resolution on low settings to everything on Ultra High because of this!!!There's some memory leak as well so recommend people restart the game and reload their save in a long play through!In terms of the game itself...As many other people have said, the game does look and feel like warband 2020, a modder potentially could created the graphical overhaul, but the actual gameplay and new content is lacking. Now there are some things which I know they are going to release later but it the game feels like it's in beta because of the lack of depth. This relates to quests, character stories, content & the main questline (since it's meant to be the introduction to the game) so far is such a letdown. Cons:- Zero dialogue - literally nothing voiced- The same, almost to the letter, question and answers as Warband in conversations- I've been extremely lucky with crashes but the RAM leak mentioned above is a killer, if you're on 8Gb you may be ok but be prepared to give your computer some time off!- Repetitive, quests, etc. is all the same as warband why not freshen it up.- Battles, AI isn't great, it's just run at each other and hack to death.- They've actually removed some better features from other M&B titles like stamina, i've literally no idea why. - The quests are killers.... go speak to these 20 people scattered across the map which it takes ages to get to- The tutorial (even though I sunk 1000s hours into warband I wanted to see new features, there were 0) was missing huge amounts of info. Kingdom view, encyclopedia to name 2.- Characters in cities play no role other than repetitive quest givers. None have any personality whatsoever and the dialogue is so dry that I cared about no one - oh that's my brother, who cares.- swinging arcs are mental. There's no glancing like warband, it's damage related but you can hit someone side on sometimesPros:- It's Warband 2020, if you liked warband, you'll like this- I really like the trade system, it's been updated, not amazingly but some small features which make a difference- Graphics, controversial with some people but I love the graphics, yes theres some clipping and shields go through capes etc but it looks nice.- Terrain looks stunning, desert, forest in the background of battles is amazing.- They've focused on the campaign map to battle map and matching- Tactics look better (minor improvement) but it's easier to see formations- I like the focus points and skill trees, basically you gain focus points as you level which don't increase attributes but the speed you learn the skill. You then have attribute points every three levels. Much better levelling system- There's crafting, it's not fully implemented yet but the beginnings are there. - I can't wait for the modding to start... ACOKs please <3.... also a warhammer based on total war would be awesome. Overall i'm giving the game a positive because although the basis is there for an awesome game, they've really not changed too much from warband and what they have changed (re combat) is not the best. Here's hoping however that there's a lot to change with this being in early access but I am hoping so much and have every finger crossed that more content is coming soon.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't play the original game but I did know what it was about and have been looking forward to the updated version. Note I have a high end system i7 9700k, 32 gigs of memory, an RTX 2080ti and playing on a 4k monitor.It's always a good sign when you keep having more fun as you play a new game and that's been my experience with Bannerlord so far. Honestly I'm still not very good with the combat yet but I've learned to work with that, and that's one of the things I love about the game is that it gives you the freedom to work around your weaknesses and still be successful. Their are parts of the game I don't care for like the arena, as it picks what weapons you get to use, no thanks, but you can simply ignore those parts. I really enjoy growing my little band of solders bit by bit while I level my smithing and try to make some money. The freeform game play is something I find fun but if your looking for a more structured rpg then this might not be for you.This is a very demanding game hardware wise and I think even the recommended specs look a little to low to me. I recorded a peak memory usage of 12 gigs and my 8 core CPU had a peak package usage of 78%. I would be concerned that systems with less then 16 gigs and or a low end or older cpu may have issues as for me I haven't run into a single bug yet with 21 hours in game and play at a rock solid 120 fps at 4k.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of a kind. There are literally no other examples of this game or even slightly alike game except the older games in the serie. The experience that the game has to offer is pretty good if u don't mind grinding. Battles between thousands and thousands of soldiers are  really fun and tactical aspect of the game shows itself at that point. But in order to join those battles, u gotta grind your ass out. I am not saying its hard or something but you gotta do the same thing from beginning to end. Thats really unpleasant part of the experience. But commanding your own army, real time commanding of course, and also fighting alongside with them makes u feel powerful. Fighting animations, mechanics physics needs tons and tons of work. And this is a game published in early access after 10 years of development. But they are working hard I will give them that. They are updating the game all the time just for little twiks and balance changes. Online game mode tho really promising it wasn't like that in previous games. They were more like cs 1.6 rough around the edges. But they took a big step forward with bannerlord. Even though we lost the norths now we have a grand story(still work in progress btw). If you are into medieval games  you have to try this one.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a finished product that  just needs some polish. In 4 hours of play i only encountered one bug. When i went to attack a bandit camp it said i had to wait tell nighttime. So the game had me wait tell night and then i attacked. It went into a loading screen and i waited for 10 minutes and the game didn't load had to alt f4 out of the game. Other than that one bug everything has worked perfectly. Its a much improved mount and blade. If you loved Warband than Bannerlord is a much buy at any price. No need to wait for a sale support the devolper they won't be abandoning this game. This devolper can be trust to make a good product and keep updating there game and improving upon it. Look at what they did with Warband it had allot of content added over its lifetime. Also once the games fully released and the modding starts taking hold. This game will shine bright.(above is 4 hour unchanged review)(below is 105 hour review)The game is very playable with many bugs and frustrations related to early access. This dose not mean the game is not enjoyable or unplayable. It just means its early access and some features are missing or need tweaking. Siege Towers your mean stand at the bottom and hump the tower only using one ladder. The devs are trying to fix this and claim a recent patch has. I tried the recent patch and the problem still happens but the AI dose seem to get up the one latter faster and sometimes use's a second ladder. They do not however use all 3 ladders like intended. The devs are aware of the issue and are trying to fix it. Ladders work but your men will stand in a clump waiting for the battering ram to reach the gate before charging the wall and lifting the latter's up. This just allows the archers to slaughter your men. A work around is for you as the player to rush to the wall on your horse dismount and lift one of the ladders yourself. This triggers your troops to charge the wall and start lifting the ladders before the battering ram reach's the gate. Battering Ram breaks down the gate but instead of the AI from the ram attacking the inner gate they all rush to ladders or towers while only a few if any stay to wack a mole the inner gate. This is another bug or bad AI. Each siege equipment has its own group of NPCs assigned to it. To attack that part of the castle. So your attacking on multiple vectors. This dose't work with the Ram as intended from what I've seen. I've noticed on some castle/city siege maps siege tower ramps don't connect to the wall and are in mid air. Which means the towers useless. The devs are working to improve siege AI and mechanics and overall sieges are way better than in Warband and are generally fun and well done. The conspiracy quest is totally broken and makes AI empire's declare war on your player kingdom or the kingdom your fighting for non stop. After signing a peace treaty that same empire could declare war on you within seconds after a peace treaty, days or weeks. They really need to fix this quest.As for player kingdom your kingdom will declare war on AI empires randomly without player input. This is so frustrating your getting dragged into wars you don't want to fight. You either have to reload a save or run down a lord and ask for peace treaty. Which that AI empire could declare war with you seconds after signing said peace treaty. I highly recommend downloading Diplomacy Reworked Mod. It allows you to talk to faction leaders from your player/faction cities/castles and ask for peace so you don't have to track a lord down. Allot of the issues I've had with the game can be mitigated with mods. The modding community is already strong. However the devs are amazing and are releasing consent patch's. The devs are listening to feedback and are very invested in there game. This game is early access and the devs will be working to finish it over the next year or so. Its playable its fun its enjoyable. I definitely recommend the game. Once its fully finished the modding tools will get released and this game will shine bright. And will expand beyond imagining. Allot of mods from Warband where great if you loved that you'll love Bannerlord.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the original Mount & Blade games and someone who never played this until it was officially released, it's a ton of fun and absolutely worth it. There are a few missing features, like needing to rest your troops, making camp, and manual party troop category sorting. But there's also some new features like clans, better diplomacy, and kingdom management.
_childDocuments_.name: Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely unpolished, unfinished game that is riddled with bugs or crashes. From the start, there is virtually no campaign and a minimal, half ass made story. There is a serious lack of weight in some of the features that quickly become obsolete. Interactions with NPC characters are cookie cut, generic and repetitive. Not to mention, due to a lack of depth with a succession system, there is no real consequence when removing an NPC from the world. End game becomes mundane instantly as the kingdom management system is abysmal and holds no true value to the success of your empire. There is no "diplomacy" with other nations, simply due to a lack of content in the diplomacy menu. AI controlled clans within your kingdom are basically useless and constantly need saving as there are no command options other than to gather everyone into a single large army. Being labeled and designed as a "sandbox" experience, this game is seriously limited by the lack of content, or honestly the quality of content, in almost every aspect of the game. Some would argue that sandbox is what you make of it, I would be be one of those in support of this view. However, ultimately, Bannerlords open world experience is choked to death by the limitations in development. With myself having over 150 hours in this game, obviously there is still some fun to be had. However, in all honesty, it feels like hollow shell of a game. This is why I would have a hard time recommending another person to spend money on a product that lacks well over half of its features.Several patches have been focused on multiplayer issues when the single player needs SO MUCH ATTENTION

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I start... This game is everything I remember, but even better! The quality touch ups are on things like giving commands in battle to just a general aesthetic. I Wouldn't say Cons! BUT!I will say there are several bugs that I've come across at least. For example yesterday I was playing really late, and I was in this town in some Aserai Town. And this kid was walking around. Sounds normal. But get this. He was walking in the air! and I had to do a Conflict Resolution quest - as we do as Bannerlords. So as soon as I pass this levitating child, he looks at my character, dead into my screen. And I freak out! I've had a couple blue screens as well as random dialogue errors in certain quests. Other than that, here are the Pros that have come out of my 27 hours. Exciting Battles. Meaningful relations with NPCs and Quest Givers. Interesting Character Creation options. Great Battle command controls Epic BattlesInteresting Micro-Managing in your Party: Hiring, to Recruiting, to Loot Management./ Trading The Quests can become fairly repeatable but this isn't bad because it allows you to farm resources! I find that later on they do seem to get harder. The success rates of your skills decrease which makes the game make you succeed in different ways. As you amass power it feels great moving around the map. Everyone is running from you, or you see a lower enemy faction hero moving around. You fight him, take him as prisoner, and sell him for 2000 gold.  What I mean is, this game makes you become very lucrative. You have to feed your people, and sometimes make tough decisions. I thought it was a good idea to have 3 Parties, but i couldn't sustain it financially. So I dropped it into 1 Party, and now I have about 100k and running. Quest I find are fairly doable and as soon as you get a hang of the world and factions. You can really start playing freely. I've been playing for about 27 hours. I haven't even completed the 2nd Quest. I've been leveling my clan, and gathering resources. My biggest hurdle yet has been raiding. I do not participate in looting villages but Bandit Camps are fair game. Only when they have low amounts of people in them! like 12 and under!Otherwise they seem impossible. Maybe its just me. My character specializies in Social and Negotiations, except Family Feuds...Anyways so far a 8.99/10 experience. I would recommend to anyone that wishes to get into Mount and Blade or returnees. Its the same beast!

_childDocuments_.review: Having never played Warband I don't have the ability to compare Bannerlord to it. That being said, I have found Bannerlord to be a lot of fun even though it definitely has its fair share of problems. The devs have been very good about patches since release and are making strides to get the game to where it should be, hopefully that pace and progress continues far into the future. The combat and battles are the bread and butter of the game for me, its just a lot of fun to command an army with some basic orders and then be able to wade into the fray yourself either atop a warhorse or on foot shoulder to shoulder with your troops. The settlement/kingdom management side of the game has just enough to it for it to be a good compliment to the army battles but it still has a ways to go for it feel complete. For me the game scratches a similar itch to the Total War games but provides a more personal RPG focus rather than a tactical one. If the game sounds at all interesting to you I think its well worth the asking price even with the balancing problems. With some patience you will figure out the games quirks and still enjoy yourself even if there are some frustrating aspects. This game will only get better with time and has plenty to enjoy now. Highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: There are two perspectives on this game. As a veteran, and as somebody who's new to M&B. I've played all the M&B series, but didn't finish viking's conquest due my old laptop being too sh**ty at the timeTo anybody who's never played M&B before, this game will be lots of funs, worth hundreds of hours if not thousands. The combat mechanics aren't typical like other games, and can be considered quite unique in its own way such as couch lancing, siege engines, and multiple weapon types. You can experiment with different builds on different situations and approaches, allowing for re-playing to be possible. The economical and political system also seems to stand out when compared to other titles, the games tries to make you to be more involved with it, rather than being another 'hack, slash, conquer' type of game. It makes you think to make decisions and how can it actually affect your progress and/or the kingdom's progress. Overall, the game's mechanics and systems are very unlike other games and allows for high re-playability as the game is more adaptive rather than having a single meta to finish the game.In the perspective that this game has been undergoing 8 years of development and compared to older M&B titles, (especially warband), it definitely lacks quite alot. The game itself is still very fun, but I expected more knowing that the game has been given quite alot of time for development. the combat mechanics are still rather similar to warband despite some reworks that i understand some veterans might dislike, but i personally think it's fine, because it feels different, not worse. They put some new economical and political features, allowing some better and more impactful decision-making. Siege has been drastically improved with very refreshing features to see that were not expected before and they feel much more immersive. Graphics are very good, despite minor optimization issues, the game is still very playable.But in alot of aspects of the game system and mechanics, they feel very unfinished. Combat AI is still very clunky, AI troops tend to either only stay still defensively in formation and move around slightly without any proper strategy, or simply charge you recklessly with infantry accompanied by cavalry at the sides. Although it's not as bad as warband, it still needs to be worked on in order to allow more effective defensive and offensive maneuver decisions. Troops in sieges also seem to be way more clunky in so many ways, they only proceed to climb 1 or 2 out of 3 ladders in a siege tower, defensive for some reason do not fire 50% of the time, and AI barely uses the defensive siege engines. Micro-managing fiefs are nice to see, they give out civ vibes but i personally do not feel like they are sought out that well. I can't put to words how many times did i feel that the game is unfinished and has the same warband's clunkiness feeling.Overall, the game has alot of potential but still feels rather disappointing how many parts of the game still feels very similarly unfurbished like warband, although it has been in development for so long. Don't get me wrong, the game is still tons of fun, it has new features, reworks, and quite alot of improvements. But when you compare this game to warband, it has way too many similarity to it in terms of "unfinished touches" given it's been in development for 8 years. I still have love for this game thrive and hopefully it gets better on official release. It has huge potential, and would be simply perfect if they stop repeating the same mechanics and bugs that were in warband.TL;DRIf you havent played M&B, you'll find this game awesome with some forgivable clunkiness to itIf you played other M&Bs, it'll definitely bring up that old fun in you but don't expect too much of it

_childDocuments_.review: It has been several months since I reviewed this game (April 2020) and a lot has changed, so I am changing my review:Overall a huge improvement to Warband. If you liked Warband, you're going to like Bannerlord.-The clan voting system is cool, and the devs have done well to expand on it since release. Players can now force a vote to declare war or sue for peace by spending influence, which gives some control over warfare compared to release. The policies still don't feel overly impactful, though, so there is room for improvement, and I'd like for the devs to add a system of political intrigue similar to how factions work in Crusader Kings - the ruling clan needs to carefully keep their subjects in line, or they might get overthrown.-Having played the beta, the tactics in singleplayer feel worse overall. I'd like to have the ability to form units like in multiplayer and command them as such. A battlemap would be a really nice addition, too. Update: Unfortunately, this aspect of the game has still not been changed. Battles for the most part play how they did in Warband, with a few additional formations added.-There should be a lot more minor castles vs major cities, like in Warband. Wars in Bannerlord can be extremely crippling because it's very easy to quickly lose 1-3 cities in a short amount of time. Update: I'm not sure if they added in more castles since release, but it sure feels like they have, plus with the ability to sue for peace, wars don't drag on as long. The devs have worked hard on curbing snowballing, and compared to release, wars aren't as much as a one-sided curbstomp anymore.-Sieges seem to be reaaally buggy - especially when it comes to ladders, where sometimes the attacking army will erect them but not use them, leaving them just sitting outside. In one battle, as a defender I had to literally open the gates of the castle because the enemy weren't scaling the walls. The ability to delegate units would be useful in offence, too. Update: Unfortunately, this aspect of the game has barely been improved. Ladders are slightly more reliable but siege AI is still terrible.-Please for the love of god cut down on loading screens. I'd rather go back to simple dialogue screens if it means cutting out the loading screens. I once captured 5 lords in a row and the fact that it loaded between each of them, even if quick, was infuriating - Update to this, the devs added in a quick dialogue screen!-Also stop kicking me out of dialogue. If I ask a question and they answer it, but I want to keep talking to them, please for the love of god don't kick me out of the dialogue screen Update - this no longer happens.Once the political system  is expanded I'll have no complaints with this game, just now the entire clan system feels very hollow and inconsequential.Do note that while I focused entirely on the negatives in this review, the game as a whole feels a lot better to play than Warband. The ability to command armies of your own vs relying on the Marshals as in Warband is a simple but effective system to giving the player much more freedom in waging war.The game is still not perfect - there needs to be more politics, and sieges need to be worked on - but the game has come a long way since release and it shows.
