_childDocuments_.review: I AM recommending this, but not without some criticism and caveats.First, the good: -the story is well-done, if predictable, and the voice-acting adds a lot of emotion to the story that wouldn't be there otherwise.-the visual presentation has some interesting ideas, and a couple of levels do actually challenge deductive skillsNext, the bits I found needed work:-the overall gameplay loop is... a bit easy, once you figure out how to scan for time chunks. There's an easy exploit I discovered where changing days back and forth resets your action rolls too, taking away a significant amount of the meter management challenge since you could easily do this until you get the lowest possible time expense.-In fact, the only resource that TRULY matters here is time. Everything else can be managed or reset, and I feel this limits the design a bunch.-The actions and revelations feel a bit disconnected and nonsensical. Why would stealing someone's medical records reveal their grocery shopping habits, for example? It all feels like very loose flavor text over a very basic numbers game, and eventually I stopped reading what I was doing and just scanned for the lowest numbers.-the mask  resource you get from a couple of the recover actions further simplifies gameplay, effectively removing attention gain in a way I think held back the difficulty.Less fair criticisms:-I feel like focusing entirely on timeline management was a bad idea. It limits how invasive you feel, and the ui implies files and documents to flick through that you can't actually open or peruse. This alone would have added a lot of invasive sleuthing options to the gameplay loop, and I could have easily seen this taking on a similar approach to Papers, Please or Hypnospace Outlaw where you have to match private information on a time budget.As is, all you're really doing is playing a simple tile guessing game with a weekly planner.-The ui visuals felt out of place. The main character looks a bit older, and I feel a more analogue UI design may have fit better than the cyber-hacker futuristic paranoia thing we had. Grimey crts, old desktop towers, more of a glaring/otherworldly/retrocomputer green vibe than the calming digital blues. Granted, this would run the risk of leaning too hard into the somewhat played out trend of analogue horror, but it may have fit the characters and concept a bit better and added some good tension-building.-the characters you stalk could have had their blankbody portraits slowly -fill up- with details as you grow more familiar with them using some simple png overlays on the limited paranoia poses they take. This would have added a lot, but been somewhat of a burden to add since keeping track of the various necessities like age in the generative system may have been a bit of a puzzle to figure out.-The intended emotion as stated by the developers was to feel like you were invading people's lives, doing something truly wicked to the people you stalk. To that end, I think adding some kind of response system would have added a lot. EG, if you get paranoia too high, perhaps they start ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up at work, making them harder to track as they erratically try to dodge your pursuit. Something like that, where your victims are more impacted by your actions, would have sold the sickness of what you do a bit more. As is, it's only really evident in the cringing character portraiture, which is depersonalized to such an extent that you feel alienated from these characters even as you circle in for the kill.-The ritual component of the game feels a bit strange at times, it's a very direct memorization game but sometimes there's very little in the way of information to glean from what's right or wrong, especially whether or not characters live with others. It's fine with the single mistake you can make, but it is odd how limited it feels. The animation for puncturing the heart could also have used a bit more impact, but that's more of a personal quibble I'm having as an animator.OVERALL, however, this is a pretty interesting concept. I do hope they build on it going forward to create something more elaborate!If you're going into this for time management puzzles, you're unfortunately not going to find much to tickle the brain. There's the bones of a great concept here, but it feels limited by its execution.

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Scaffold is a developer I admire, putting out tight, short games that are small in scope but big in ideas. Life Eater, a "horror fantasy kidnapping simulator," falls into this wheelhouse well. You play as [REDACTED], a poor man with an obscured name tasked by a mysterious god, Zimforth, to sacrifice one or more people of a specific quality each year, or the world will end. Maybe, if Zimforth is even real, that is. The story's drama comes with Johnny, who is captured early in the story and locked in the basement by [REDACTED]. We follow these two over several years and their subsequent sacrifices, seeing how their kidnapper/kidnappee relationship shifts while the weight of Zimforth's demands on [REDACTED] grows heavier.The gameplay for Life Eater focuses exclusively on these sacrifices, opening up a blurred-out schedule (think of a TV guide filled with static) for your potential victims' week. To capture them for your god's ill intent, you must select a time slot within a sacrifice's schedule on a given day and choose how hard you want to essentially spy on them while simultaneously managing both how suspicious you're being (fill up the bar too many times, and you're arrested: game over) and how long you have to complete the sacrifice (each spying attempt takes a little bit of time off the clock from the world ending, as does resetting your suspicion meter). There are a handful of other mechanics, but for the most part, the game is a puzzle of piecing together information to determine the correct victim based on a few vague hints from your cruel deity.After a successful kidnapping, specific organs and bones must be plucked to "water the flower" of your vile lord, requiring further reading into the victim's traits like their hair color, whether they commuted, and if they lived alone. These aspects must be memorized before kidnapping, as the timeline vanishes once they're on your basement butcher's table, and you can't check to see if they use the toilet more than once a day for your hungry god. This gameplay is intended to make the player feel invasive, prying into these innocent victim's lives and most vulnerable moments.While an interesting mechanic and story concept, Life Eater struggles in its execution. The game is played across 10 levels, each being bookended by voice-acted storyboard-esque cinematics explaining the progression of [REDACTED] and Johnny's relationship, but rarely given a real sense of the extended time passing each time we meet them. While the game covers a decade, these characters feel like they, at best, spent a few weeks together and only a cursory glance into their ongoing and tormented lives. Part of this is bumping up against the tight scope of the game, with limited time to spend with these characters. From a narrative standpoint, it's almost antithetical to the game's premise, which focuses on delving deep into a stranger's life and their many insecurities. We can see how long a stranger stares at the wall to the dot, but what [REDACTED] and Johnny, our main characters, get up to in their private and intimate moments, mostly left up to a few scant impressions throughout the game. It's not enough to ruin the narrative, as it remains impactful throughout, but it invariably leaves the player wanting more of this drama. That's not to say that these narrative choices aren't without merit. This lack of information dovetails with our lack of understanding of our main character himself, who only appears as [REDACTED] when named in the game. He is a nameless stooge whose wants, desires, personal thoughts, and even his name are rendered meaningless under the weight of his god's demands. I didn't quite feel like the game landed on a strong narrative conclusion to these themes, but it certainly leaves plenty to think about.While gruesomely novel and challenging, the gameplay suffers from an extremely tight scope that can lead to a frustrating experience. Many levels are vague on how to solve them and even what needs to be solved in the first place. For example, one of the levels requires you to find two relatives among four people living together, but the key to this information can only come from picking a random spot on a single day of the week to discover a clue. This led to a brute force "trial and error" style of play where I figured out where the hint would likely be and spammed those scheduled time slots for every character to see what popped up.Likewise, once I reached the sacrificial portion of the game, the specific criteria always remained the same, so it became less about analyzing the victim's individuality and more about "Did this person have kids or black hair?" every time. If I didn't discover how often a person went to the bathroom or whether they drive to work, you are allowed one bad guess before failing the chapter and having to restart with a new randomized schedule for the potential victims. This happened a lot!This is a very tight, short game that can easily be beaten in a couple hours (maybe a bit longer if you're struggling on some levels). It's atmospheric, with excellent voice acting and some memorable character dialogue. While some horror aspects are extensively present, too much of the gameplay feels divorced from anything too gruesome or invasive to strike me as offputting despite what the premise implies (although ruminating too deeply on the actions [REDACTED] is implied to perform may leave you with some dark thoughts of your own). Instead, this game feels much more like a tragedy as we watch [REDACTED] struggle to live with the many barely understood burdens placed upon him.That divorce between "information" and "individual" does feel intentional to some degree, with [REDACTED] continually referring to his victims as "beasts" to further dehumanize them and reduce his guilt. We, too, as players, learn a lot about these victims' lives and the specificity with which they live, but much of it is superficial. They are weak and flawed human beings, but they are all faceless and interchangeable outside of our god's vague whims. The sense of randomness in all of these events, from [REDACTED] being chosen to the victims Zimforth wants, to even Johnny being at the wrong place at the wrong time to kick off the game, lends to the true sense of dread at Life Eater's bloody heart: terrible, awful things happen, and there's no reason why.I would have loved to see a larger version of the game with a few more mechanics or systems and a more elaborate story that was at least double its length. I would have also loved a more elaborate tutorial and guidance instead of mainly relying on guesswork and brute force for many puzzles. Tailoring the criteria for the sacrificial portion of gameplay based on the actual generated nuances of a character instead of unchanging criteria could have also elevated that sense of learning about these victims.However, Life Eater knows the fun in its core conceit has a limited shelf life and avoids becoming too tedious or having to ramp up later level's difficulty by remaining short and sweet. This crux of Strange Scaffold's development model, where putting out games at a healthy pace while remaining in scope as the priority, has resulted in a growing library of incredibly creative and genuinely original indie games. To that end, I'd argue that a brief stint into the cursed world of Life Eater might not hit all the marks but strikes quite a few, which might be more than enough.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be one of the most terrifying and depressing games I've seen, but it in a good way. While this game is very short (around 2 hours of gameplay if you only do the story mode), it leaves a lasting impression. The story is accompanied by amazing art and even better voice acting, which makes it hit even harder. Don't want to make any spoilers, so I'm just going to say that the ending actually made me cry.While the story and visuals in this game are amazing, I do have to mention that the gameplay is rather shallow. It felt to me like there wasn't much effort put into desinging it. Most levels felt repetitive, and to beat the game, all you really have to do is basically randomly guess at what time some specific events happen. It really felt mostly as just guessing, as while there are some clues that can guide you in the right direction, they are very sparse, and I can only remember 2 examples of them (both being different people having same action lengths in their schedules). It really feels like there's a lot of missed potential there. Also the game often feels inconsistent with how different actions are placed throughout the days and how long they last. Like how a person only walks to work, but never walks back. Or how some people have the most random stuff in their schedules (like spilling a drink every Sunday at 1pm). I guess it would make sense if it wasn't actually a schedule but just a single week in their life, but the game seems to imply that this is, in fact a schedule. The resource managment in this game also felt extremely underdeveloped. You basically just have to check every single item in the schedule to see their time costs (which are simply random) until you find the one that costs 0.5 hours. Then you just investigate, and check everything again because of course the costs for everything get rerolled. The risk percentage is basically irrelevant with how easy it is to get rid of it, how you only get strikes with a certain chance and how you need 3 strikes to lose. And you also have access to anonimity points that you can use to investigate without any consequences at all. All of this makes losing by getting caught seem impossible, which removes all stakes.With all of that said, I still think that the game is worth playing. While the gameplay is not particularly captivating, it doesn't feel terrible, and with how short this game is, you won't have time to get bored with it. The main value in my opinion does come from the story though, so if you're not really interested in that, you might want to skip this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely not a game I would recommend to everyone. However, if it looks like something you might possibly enjoy, you'll likely end up having an even better time with it than you anticipated! At first the game play is pretty clunky and confusing, but once you get the hang of it it really clicks. The process of using your intuition to investigate your targets, processing each bit of information you unlock to try and anticipate and uncover the dynamics between them is a really satisfying puzzle. R̷̢̆̍à̴̭̂l̶̪̅̏̊p̵̮̘͂̑h̷͓̭̣͌̇̄ and Johnny are great. The way that their relationship progresses really kept me invested in the game. It's not hard to predict the events that will transpire at the climax of the story, but the way that Life Eater ties it into the game play made the emotional impact so much greater. The game doesn't make any hints as to whether or not Zimforth truly exists, or if any of this is necessary, and that's a good thing in my book.I really liked the art style, which suits the game incredibly well, but was especially immersed by the soundtrack. There's not a lot of variety, but what it lacks in quantity it more than makes up for with atmospheric quality.My only complaints are that I wish R̷̢̆̍à̴̭̂l̶̪̅̏̊p̵̮̘͂̑h̷͓̭̣͌̇̄ and Johnny had their own personalized silhouettes during year 10, and I would have liked to see maybe like, 3-5 more years before the ending. I appreciate that the game doesn't drag on too long, but I really enjoyed the more complex puzzles and wish there were more of them! There is an endless mode, which I haven't check out too much of, but from what I've seen those puzzles lack the complexity that the later years of the story mode have.All Hail Zimforth!!!

_childDocuments_.review: *Spoilers*Interesting premise, but half-assed execution.You get given a target: e.g. "Kill the drifter of the group" and a blank timeline for a set of characters. You then can investigate different time periods of the people's day to try to figure out who has the characteristic you're looking for. Except ultimately all you do is randomly investigate the time periods you're given and then hope you happen to select the literally 1 time period that has the single relevant clue. The rest of the time periods are like "Sleep" "Eat" "Work" "Shower" etc and then, they'll be one single time period that has a different description that immediately tells you if this is the right person or not. So, yeah, the investigation aspect is incredibly tedious and not really a puzzle but is more just a "pick random time periods and hope you find the right one" simulator.What about the story? Well it starts interesting but pretty quickly becomes absurd. The MC somehow kidnaps a young man from the middle of a store because the guy "saw him" (never explained.) He then proceeds to keep him locked in his basement in a tiny animal cage for multiple years. After each level we get more dialogue between the two.For a story trying to take itself seriously, this is seriously dumb. MC constantly tries to talk to him and be friends with him, literally sitting next to the cage and watching shows on his phone with the guy at one point. But as far as I could see he never gives him... pillows? Or a blanket? Or books? Or a TV? Or a bigger cage? He also performs all his vivisections on the victims right in front of the guy for years and never thinks to like, put up a screen or something? It takes the guy like 6 years to ask for some headphones so he doesn't have to hear him sawing the people up. Like I said, it's just very half-assed. If I were going based on their conversations I'd think like maybe 1 month had passed but the game is trying to convince me it's been 7 years.Not to mention that the story sections themselves are incredibly short. Like, maybe 45 seconds worth after each mission.I'd avoid this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I am recommending this game with the caveat that you get it on sale, it does seem a tad over priced at $14.99.It is a very short horror experience which you are the murderer stalking people to sacrifice to your god.  It has a eerie atmosphere and very appealing visual design.  The story and voice acting are pretty decent.The main game-play loop is also pretty good though does feel a little bare bones near the end. The main story does not feel like it ups the difficulty that much as you go on, remaining petty much the same throughout with a few minor bumps in some levels.As such once you've beaten the main story it's pretty much done. You even unlock all the achievements just by playing the main story.  The unlimited mode is more of the same loop from the main story and doesn't offer much else. So unless you really love the game play loop it doesn't offer much else.The game's concept is very interesting but does feel like it could have been expanded just a little more to give another layer.  As said above, I do recommend this game just for the experience and how well it is put together but get it on sale as I don't think it's worth the full price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often like doing reviews for games unless its just for a friend, but with the small amount of reviews i'd like to throw my coin into the pond here. I recommend it! Stop reading these reviews and go in blind.The gameplay is interesting if not a little shallow, as a lot of the schedule doesn't randomize you can easily identify who your target is after a very small amount of time. Generally about 1-2 tries if you manage your time well enough. Another issue I do have about it is the fact that your success can also sometimes just be random, with how the stalking methods you are given will take either between 30 minutes to 6 or so hours. Now to say the gameplay is bad isn't really fair. The concept is very interesting and something that I like a ton, the same can't exactly be said about the ritual part of the game. This might be a bit biased, but in my experience I always found that the only variations I had to look for was just, do they commute or do they live alone. Most of which can be found out extremely easily. All in all, the gameplay is simple and interesting with a decent challenge in some of the later levels (That or i'm just a bit of a dummy) On another front I do think its a bit silly that your stalking options sometimes reveals things that make no sense, like a phishing sext finding out that someone is taking the bus or specifically sleeping in. The fact critical information is also locked behind a level 3 stalking option which basically just tells you "Oh this is critical info" which sort of railroads the player.Now, I wont touch much on the story as frankly its amazing, and seeing as the game isn't really much game the story really is the highlight. First! I'm happy that it didn't fall into the similar tropes that a lot of stories like this do, while the story in itself is simple that doesn't mean its bad by any means, like I said I think its great. The voice acting as-well does a lot for the story and is absolutely top notch in my opinion. The only small gripe I have is that the game takes place over 10 or so years, this isn't super well shown in terms of visuals. Johnny doesn't look much older beside his hair growing longer, a change of clothes over the last 10 years would be nice I imagine. Ralph as-well doesn't look much older either, but that isn't really a huge issue in the slightest. Especially for a short indie game like this. So 8.5/10 I loved it, also I suck at writing reviews :)

_childDocuments_.review: the story's good but the mechanical complexity wasn't as much as i'd hopedi know that this is going to make me sound like a psychopath but spying on people and kidnapping them was just too simple. you clicked timeslots and picked appropriate options while balancing time and awareness. and then, once your meter was full, you just hit "abduct person". you didn't have to play for *when* or *how* to abduct them, you just did. you'll notice on a lot of time slots there's a little label that said "unarmed". i notice that my first victim was, indeed, sometimes *not* unarmed. so i'm like, okay, cool, i'll have to pick a time where they're alone and unarmed in order to successfully abduct them. nope, i just press a button.similarly, the ritual was pretty much always the same. at first i thought that i needed to take detailed notes about my victims' lifestyle, but a few of the ritual questions never really came up and the rest of them were the same ritual after ritual after ritual. it would have been a lot more fun if each ritual had randomized questions that kept you on your toes and made you have to really think rather than doing the same ritual over and over again.still worth it for the novelty and for the story, though. fantastic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ voice acting for !@#$% and Johnny, absolute props to those two.

_childDocuments_.review: A very compelling little game. It's more a puzzle game than a horror game, as it's not particularly scary in any meaningful way. What it is, though, is a suspenseful and intense narrative interlaced with clever and thought provoking puzzle design between those two parts. Because the pules operate rationally and rather consistently it never really feels like you are trying to abide by some unknown moon logic, though I would argue year 9 is probably the weakest puzzle, as it has the least structural sign posting to determine how you should solve it, the other 8 puzzles as is are great.What REALLY works, though, is the underlying tragedy of the narrative, that I won't delve to far into. What is worth saying is that the game does a lot with maybe 20 minutes of spoken dialog to build up two compelling and tragic figures.
_childDocuments_.name: Life Eater

_childDocuments_.review: This is a one of a kind game, truly an experience to play.  The story is captivating being that you play a serial killer who needs to sacrifice his neighbors every year to satisfy his God to prevent the end of the world. The unique gameplay consists of stalking and learning about your potential victims in the form of a video timeline (similar to premiere pro) making it a puzzle game to plan out the right opportunity to kidnap the victim without being caught by police while also getting to know the victim enough to preform the ritual right. The art and the voice acting is top tier with beautiful but haunting imagery and emotional scenes.  The only complaint I can think of is that it wasn't longer because enjoyed it so much. But you can tell this was a labor of love so if the creator felt like the story was done then so be it.  I hope to play more like this and I implore you to try this awesome game!

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me *feel* things. I went from "I should probably delete my Google data." to "oh god, what do I have to do?" to "No...no no no no".An emotional experience through and through, I loved how uncomfortable this game made me feel, how intensely the story is shown to you in both the gameplay and cutsvenes both. Highly recommend to anyone who enjoys that sort of sensation. In slightly spoiler comments about the gameplay, I think the game-as-game is a bit hampered by the ritual objectives being the same every year, but that being said it honestly aided the game-as-immersive story aspect. As it went on I found myself more detached from the beasts, less worrying about every detail of their lives and more just what the ritual required. My notes went from obsessively detailing their schedules to scribbled marks to denote where to cut...this game's atmosphere definitely gets into you.I would definitely be interested in seeing endless mode introduce new (randomized?) objectives you have to figure out to enhance the puzzle aspect though, I'm definitely interested in digging into the puzzle aspect of this game as much as I enjoyed the story aspects as well. _childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend Life Eater, but with some caveats.What I liked: - The atmosphere. The art is gorgeous and suits the tone perfectly, the voice acting was great, and the game is overall very stylish. It was neither overstated nor understated; the visual and sound design complements the gameplay beautifully.- The gameplay itself. I only got really stuck on one level, but I liked exploring and developing strategies to use my time better.- Story integration. The concept is engaging and I think it ties well into the player's actions.- The writing. The cutscenes aren't super long, but they show a believable set of characters that I grew to care for.What I'd like to see added:- Levels of zoom. Neither of the current zoom levels work particularly well for me - a decent chunk of my time in-game was spent switching between the full timeline and the up-close one so I could read what my victims were doing. I think a middle ground would have been nice.- More complex puzzles. I only got really stuck on one level, and I would have liked to use my brain a little more. The time management aspect of the game makes it harder, but I'd like to see more puzzles in general.- A cutscene for losing. Granted, this would have really annoyed me at certain parts, but I'm curious to see what might happen should the player fail. The option to restart is fine, but I think there's a good opportunity to increase the tension and solidify why we're doing what we're doing.What I didn't like:- The final level is of a challenge and more of a choice. It makes sense narratively, but it was kind of disappointing. I enjoyed how the actions the player could take changed, but I felt cheated out of a real 'win'.- Some of the information in the I feels useless. I've fully completed the game and I don't think I ever learned what the faces on the downtime activities represented.- The earlier levels were pretty easy and I don't think there are enough of the later ones to make it worth it. I felt like I was in a tutorial for the first third of the game.I liked Life Eater. The story was compelling and I enjoyed the gameplay, but I think it'll be far more worth its price once Endless Mode is added. I don't see much value in replaying the levels that already exist, but there's a solid base for a game I can see myself losing lots of time to.

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Scaffold continues to make really unique games with great premises. I think that Life Eater, like many of their other games, is a really banger 6 or 7/10 game. It's good, but lacks polish. I beat that ♥♥♥♥ all in one day and regret nothing. I want to be clear, because I'm mostly going to be complaining about it- I absolutely recommend this game to anybody who is interested in it. The game feels unsettling in precisely the way it wants to. Barring some logistical questions  I did really enjoy the narrative. Also less so a narrative complaint, but you'll have a time limit study someone's schedule and kill them, except the time limit is shorter than a week. It's a little weird that I can find out precisely what someone does five days from now when I only have three. It could sorta be handwaved as finding out stuff that was already scheduled, but then there's so many spontaneous events that that couldn't be true.As I said, I do think it needs some QOL. I didn't realize I could zoom in the timeline until literally the final year (which is sorta my fault, it gives the option on the screen the whole game). The tutorial doesn't explain what the skull tokens do at all (when you perform an action to reduce suspicion, you may be granted one depending on what action you take, and you can spend one of these tokens to perform an action without gaining any suspicion). After kidnapping a victim, you have to pluck organs out of the meat constellation. If you kill the wrong person, it doesn't tell you it was the wrong target until AFTER you pluck out all the organs, so that's an extra step that might not even matter if you did a previous step wrong. If you kill the wrong person, I would've preferred if the game just told me right away. Moving on from the QOL stuff, I think the gameplay would be more interesting if the meat constellation had different requirements after every murder. I don't know if there was some mistake, or if this was intentional, but you'll be told like "if the target has a commute, take this organ, if not, break this rib" or something (I don't remember the exact requirements) but every single year had the exact same parameters every single time. Giving me different parameters to keep track of would make me pay much closer attention to somebody's schedule.Little rough around the edges, some of the art looks a little awkward (it's mostly good tho), but great idea, great tone, and short enough to be worth checking out. I was engrossed the whole time. A great little horror story that may require you to gloss over some of the details that don't quite work.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not often you get to describe a game which involves stalking and ritually sacrificing strangers as an absolute *delight*, but Life Eater absolutely is. The game play loop sees you manage your time as efficiently as possible to plot out the lives of ordinary strangers in stark and sometimes horrific detail, unpicking specific details to allow you to sucessfully perform a harrowing ritual to the demanding, dark god Zimforth and hold back the end of the world for another year. This is all juxtaposed against a (surprisingly) beautifully illustrated narrative with standout performances by both Jarret Griffis and Xalavier Nelson Jr as the two leads - the glimmer of time spent with them in the cutscenes adds a wealth of humanity and heartbreak to the whole experience. The main campaign runs for about three hours, but assuming that the promised endless mode adds some more procedural puzzling and allows us to delve further and deeper into the lives of truly awful, or tragically innocent victims, this game will be an absolute winner.I can't cook up any comparisons, there are no other games quite like this. I just can't wait to see what the Strange Scaffold team come up with next!

I was afraid it'd be over-the-top dark and edgy, but it was just enough. _childDocuments_.review: I have no idea what to say about this game. It feels like a proof of concept, but the concept doesn’t even feel fully thought out. The tutorial is entirely unhelpful in explaining how to play, and what little gameplay there is feels like it has no thought put into it.The premise of this game is that you have to kidnap and kill a target given to you by a god. In order to kidnap someone, you have to learn about their weekly routine by choosing methods of surveillance. You have a set amount of time to learn this, and your actions cost time and increase the chance of getting caught. But the entire thing plays out in this menu that looks like a video editor, and there is no connection between what your actions are and what information you discover. For example, why does DDoSing someone’s home network let me know that they spent 30 minutes peeing? How does entering a target's home not immediately get me caught, and why does it tell me what they spent the 4 hours away from home on? And what is even accusing someone of a crime supposed to get me in terms of information? None of this has any meaning and I lost interest almost immediately in the mechanic.Once you actually kidnap someone, you are tested on their schedule in order to properly mutilate the body, but you have no chance to actually go back and review the information. On one hand, being able to back and review the information would make this section of the game a complete waste of time, but I don’t know what I need to make note of before I get to this part so I literally have to just sit there and guess or write the entire target’s week out in a notebook. Neither one of these options is preferable.I can’t tell you what the actual story is in this game. I was done after the first kidnapping. The best part about this game was the description of its premise on the store page.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly suggest this game however it is not for the faint of heart or those looking for a sad ending. My only suggestion is I hope the developers would give the game a happy ending.I've had psychosis and delusions for the longest time back in 2020 till now. I am on medication; this game is the most accurate depiction of what it feels like to have hallucinations when you're unmedicated. Out of all the "psychosis/schizophrenic" games I've reviewed so far, this is the one that stood out. Ofcourse the killing part isn't accurate at all, however, it's scientifically true that you can indeed inherit aggression or need for violence when you feel like a higher, most powerful entity is controlling you. The gruesome visuals and the unpredictable moods were highly accurate and relatable for me. I would have the most intrusive thoughts 24/7 and sleepless nights with mood swings, unregulated behavior, etc.I used to think I was talking to spirits and they would tell me what other people were thinking of and I isolated myself from the outside world for so long. I never knew what was real or what wasn't and was in a constant state of mania. I have never reviewed any other game but I truly had to comment on this one. This drew a strong sense of comfort (ironically) for me. I think the developers researched or really thought this well and through when making this game.Spoiler:Also, when (redacted) protag said how Zimforth doesn't communicate consistently but happens every year can be very relatable since Zimforth is a hallucination (theoretically) and (redacted)'s brain cannot keep track of a specific date per year automatically, so it makes a lot of sense.The creator knew what they were doing when it came close to the ending. Genuinely broke me. I love it.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game in 110 minutes with all achievements. I refunded, because a $15 should have more than 2 hours of content.Very interesting concept with rather poor execution. The story begins strong. Our main character has a panic attack in the beginning and kidnaps someone that his God wants nothing to do with. Zimforth, the God in question, wants the MC to remain anonymous, and the MC doesn't want to kill more than necessary. As a result, the MC keeps his hostage in a cage, and they provide commentary and moral judgement to our MC. Unfortunately, the story doesn't evolve much from there. Even though the game is about knowing your victims, you never really see or interact with them outside of the silhouette in the gameplay UI. The game cuts from your kidnapping them for your ritual, to them being dead immediately. The entire story is just you talking to Johnny (the man you kidnap).I was hoping that the ending would save it, but the ending is really predictable and anticlimactic.

_childDocuments_.review: Life Eater is an amazing game with an interesting premise and a rewarding gameplay loop that's deceptively simple, yet has a lot of depth in the small details the player will have to pick up on to solve puzzles as they progress. The story perfectly balances showing and implying, and, without spoiling anything in specific, I'll say it caught me off-guard more than once in ways I loved. It took me about 4-5 hours to beat the main story, and the new endless mode offers replayablility.I've only played the endless mode a bit, but the puzzle component of gameplay seem to be well balanced to offer new challenges from the amount I've played. It's a very fun gameplay loop that I'd love to see more stories told through, honestly! Great game, loved it.

_childDocuments_.review: I love a horror game that  is more than just jump scares (although this one still has a decent amount of gore). The narrative is short, but there is an endless mode if you're interested in the puzzles. The puzzles are a bit tricky, trying to decipher clues to who you're meant to sacrifice using essentially scheduling software. In terms of narrative, performance, score, and art design...it's all great. Now some from the mixed bag. For a game about time management, you're likely to lose simply out of negligence for seeing your own clock run out or getting caught one too many times. I didn't even grasp what the little heads meant until the final three levels (it means you can cut your risk for some tasks). There's a lot of information up front, and it'll take you a decent amount of levels to piece together ways to optimize your run. However, you can even go back and revisit specific levels if you want to try and get better (or hunt certain narrative achievements).Frustrating at times, but if you want to try a puzzle that finds new ways to challenge the mind without tweaking the game play, this one's worth a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Thoughtful psychological horror with some unique spins on familiar formulas. Investigative gameplay that actually gets you thinking pretty hard as you solve levels. It'll make you feel awful and uncomfortable, but that's the point. It's not for everyone, but if it's for you, then it's  And though not without its flaws, it was still , and the experience is going to stick with me for a while.This is a game where you're the threat. Yet instead of the usual more gratuitous approach where you're getting a power trip out of killin' some dudes, you're intruding on people's lives to kidnap and sacrifice them to a god that you don't even like serving, feeling uncomfortable and guilty about it the whole time. This game will make you feel like a monster, and most of the horror really comes from your head more than it does the game.The gameplay mechanics are pretty unique, but also don't feel totally foreign. You go through a timeline of potential victims' day-to-day lives over the course of the week to learn more about them until you know them well enough to kidnap them. You always have specific sacrifices to target, but it's not always clear who they'll be, and you sometimes have to figure that out by watching multiple people and choosing the right ones. You figure out the information you have to by slowly uncovering that timeline with actions, which all take time to do and up your suspicion levels to varying degrees. There's things you can do to lower your suspicion levels and not get caught, but everything you do takes time and you're on a time limit. So it's some mix of puzzle, strategy, and resource management. After you've learned enough about them to take them, you perform a ritual where you destroy or remove the victim's innards in specific ways based on traits that you've observed and need to keep note of.That's the gameplay loop. Though certain elements are slightly overutilized and some cool micro-mechanics are slightly underutilized, it's still solid and fun, and a refreshing approach. I often found myself disturbingly immersed in the investigative portions, and some levels are really good shows of what this style of gameplay can do. I really enjoyed figuring things out and that information isn't spoon-fed to you- though I do think some mechanics could have been indicated with just a little more clarity.The story and dialogue are also heavy hitting, and I think that's something that really elevates the game. There's interesting things going on with the brains of the characters, and they're sympathetic. The whole situation in the story is a simple setup but it gets you wondering more and more as it goes on. You'll have questions and you won't get answers, but you will get clues. Stories that leave a lot vague are also something that's not for everyone, but if you appreciate some things being open to interpretation, you'll probably like it. I'm not going to say anything too specific about the story or characters, this part is honestly best experienced with minimal prior knowledge. But I will say it definitely left me thinking, it will probably keep me thinking, and it actually made me feel something. There's this unnerving atmosphere and air of tragedy that lingers throughout all the  cutscenes, with cool art and a great soundtrack to boot.I recommend it if what was described here sounds like your kind of thing, and especially if you want a refreshing and more unique kind of horror experience. I personally really like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short: A short game with an amazing story, lots of heart, soul and effort put into the details of the game. _childDocuments_.review: This is the first comprehensive review I have given a game because I think it deserves it.I thoroughly enjoyed this game, but I feel as though there are some key aspects that make the game less compelling and entertaining.I'd say the story is a solid  The voice acting as well as the art is absolutely phenomenal. Xalavier Nelson Jr. and Jarret Griffis did an amazing job in making both characters feel human, even after all the atrocities Ralph commits. However... The endings are very very underwhelming, and it feels as though the consequences of your actions are not important, especially because the difference between the obtainment of the endings is just who you do the ritual on at the end. I really wish there was more impact felt for your actions. Otherwise, the story is well fleshed out and well written.As much as I hate to say it, the gameplay is a  (which was just added recently). The first time you start a level, it is quite fun and entertaining managing your resources to carefully uncover your victims routine. But the moment you discover the "pivotal detail" in your victims schedule, the gameplay becomes monotonous, and if you happen to lose and restart, you know exactly what to look for on one day at one time. It renders all of the mystique and intrigue of your victims essentially meaningless, as all you need to do when you find your specific target is to just fill up the bar to finish the ritual. I finished the base game in about two hours, if that gives you an idea on how the gameplay loop may be easy the moment you grasp how the game works.Endless Mode slightly redeems the main boring aspect in the game with "randomized" schedules. As a result of the statement above, the  If you want a short, compelling game that really makes you think, this game is for you. If you want a game that challenges you by thinking and adapting to others, as well as a solid puzzle game, I cannot say this game would be a good idea for you to purchase.  does a fantastic job at making you question yourself. Throughout the game, you go through a journey of self-doubt and questioning, debating on if what you're doing even matters. The worst (and best) thing is the thought process' you may go through if you consider what you would do in Ralph's shoes. It is an existential masterpiece of a story, but it falls short in the gameplay, and the rather lackluster conclusions to the compelling storyline.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the concept behind the game (essentially Stalker/Serial Killer simulator) is really cool. I didn't like that there's such a weird incoherency between the "Time[1]" left before sacrificing someone (where Time is basically a resource you can expend to learn more about a target's habits and errands) and the "Time[2]" that represents, well, the target's day-to-day schedule. By this I mean you can learn what a person is doing on Tuesday at 10AM [2], wait an hour [1], and learn what they're doing on Monday 8PM [2]. I feel this adds a layer of confusion that, maybe with just a bit of renaming resources or reframing the problem, could have been avoided entirely. Also some resources are plainly not named at all (afaik) - you can expend a "token" to study a person's whereabouts at a certain time [2] without spending any of your own time [1] resource... what's that token represent? Am I hiring someone to stalk them for me? What's  going on, in-universe, when I do those actions?I also think the objective at the end of levels could have been made better. Once you find the person you want to sacrifice, you have to perform a sort of "ritual" where, based on a few questions (does your target sleep enough? Do they have children?), you will inflict a specific bodily harm to them. My issue with the ritual is that it's the same questions for every single person in the game. At first, I thought the questions would be different, and so I really went out of my way to learn EVERYTHING about my target before committing to the ritual in case it'd be on the test, trying to memorize their entire schedule and habits. You know, ! By forcing me to remember so much information about a single individual, the game was actually putting me right where it wanted me to be! That was only for the first couple of levels, however - as I realized it was always going to be the same interrogations over and over, I ended up not caring as much about learning who the victims were, and just going over the same tiny mental checklist of expected questions before ending the level.That said, the voice acting and the artwork are really awesome, and the story was captivating. I'm a little disappointed in certain mechanics being the way they are, but it's still a pretty innovative game, and I'm definitely keeping an eye out for future releases from you.
_childDocuments_.name: Life Eater

_childDocuments_.review: A harrowing puzzle game where it's hard to know if you're doing the right thing but you KNOW that you MUST.It's worth playing for vibes alone, and the idea of the game sort of has to be seen to be believed because it all works incredibly well. However it is remarkably short and only gets challenging towards the end. It feels like an idea that still had more to explore but then the game ends. Perhaps it'd need to change the flow of the puzzle gameplay to explore its ideas more, as it is quite rigid in its design. Still, it made me feel something. That's pretty good, though what I'm doing is far-from-good.
_childDocuments_.name: Life Eater

_childDocuments_.review: I think that this game was phenomenal. From the premise, the voice acting, the pacing and even its overarching themes had me twisted by the end of it. I was hooked from the very moment we were tasked with our mission, it was simple, and a good way to start introducing us to the flow of the game. It doesn't take long before a simple 'stalk this person, find out where they are' becomes much more of a deductive puzzle using the people around your target to understand when to strike. It blends beautifully because through this game play you also uncover stories around these victims even if they're blank faces without voices to the protagonist. The internal strife he goes through as an unwilling servant is captivating, it made me question what was and is real in the world as a whole. Don't listen to the people who found the gameplay 'repetitive' or 'boring'. They aren't reading in between the lines and appreciating every aspect of the game as a vehicle for both atmosphere and story building. The voice acting and visuals have only added everything to this underrated gem of a title. I sincerely hope people will see this through the lens less of a serial killer simulator, and more of a highly narrative driven story.
_childDocuments_.name: Life Eater

_childDocuments_.review: Slow start and i didnt understand everything at the beginning, but I really got into it as it went on, and I got invested in the story, really good time, unique gameplay and i'd say its pretty well executed, although I definitely see potential to explore the gameplay more and add more scenarios. As it is right now, still a great time!
_childDocuments_.name: Life Eater

_childDocuments_.review: A short but gripping story delivered through a simple resource management style of gameplay, where you must avoid rousing too much suspicion from your 'prey' while simultaneously figuring out key information from their schedule so that you can properly complete the ritual in time for your God. While the gameplay isn't challenging or complex, it complements the story well enough that it doesn't feel repetitive or chore-like, as there are small variations throughout the chapters. One thing that I particularly liked was the voice acting, so kudos to the voice actors for really selling the characters (the small details like the nervous chuckles and such were great). Overall, this has been an interesting tragic horror game that has satisfied my craving for a reluctant villain-type protagonist, if only for a brief evening.

name: Dragon Throne: Battle of Red Cliffs
detailed_description: Dragon Throne: Battle of Red Cliffs is an epic real-time strategy game that depicts a turbulent and chaotic time in Chinese history. Three individual campaigns allow you to control the kingdoms of Liu Bei, Sun Quan, or Cao Cao, warlords who played a pivotal role in Ancient China. Lead your kingdom and develop new technologies, establish strategic alliances and create a mighty army in an attempt to unify the nation. This real-time strategy game features a unique period in Chinese history and is based on the classic historical novel, 'Romance of the Three Kingdoms', written in the 14th Century. Play the game and experience the thrill of being a heroic conqueror in that chaotic, war-ridden time. Warriors choose from more than 40 different skills. Multi-map system enables you to separate battlefield and city development. Use domestic policies, diplomacy, science, trade and other management factors to affect your Kingdom's overall state. Unique Profession-Transference system enables laborers to be trained as sergeants and then, if needed, revert to laborers again. Tech-Tree is composed of over 100 items extracted from the social reality of the Three Kingdoms period. Engage in 3 campaigns that allow you to change the destiny of China.

_childDocuments_.review: Some people may run into audio issues. I fixed mine by disabling full screen optimizations and setting compatibility to Windows XP SP3. Running on an Ryzen/Nvidia/W11 laptop.1. Find your dragonthrone.exe Steam folder (DRIVE:\Program\Steam\steamapps\common\Dragon Throne - Battle of Red Cliffs).2. Right click dragonthrone.exe and click properties.3. Under the compatibility tab, check the box with "RUN THIS PROGRAM IN COMPATIBILITY MODE FOR:"4. Click the drop-down and select Windows XP (Service Pack 3).5. Optionally click the check box for "DISABLE FULLSCREEN OPTIMIZATIONS".5. Enjoy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Travel back in time to one of the most important battles in Chinese history with this sequel to "Fate of the Dragon." The Battle of Red Cliffs was regarded as a great milestone in the Three Kingdoms period. In July, 208 AD, after pacifying the north, General Cao Cao mustered his troops and headed south with the intent of unifying the realm. After a series of quick victories Cao Cao had become so arrogant that he completely underestimated his rivals Sun Quan and Liu Bei, and failed to take advantage this precious opportunity to unify the realm. On the contrary, he suffered a huge defeat even though his crack forces greatly outnumbered the opposing forces. After the Battle of Red Cliffs, the division of the realm into three parts began to take shape. [Strategy First]

name: MARVEL vs. CAPCOM Fighting Collection: Arcade Classics
detailed_description: The legendary crossover hits are back! Jump into this collection of arcade classics from the fan-favorite Marvel and Capcom crossover games! Dive into an action-packed lineup consisting of seven unique titles, including heavy hitters like X-MEN VS. STREET FIGHTER, and MARVEL vs. CAPCOM 2 New Age of Heroes. The collection also includes the rare beat 'em up game, THE PUNISHER. Each game in the collection can be played online or co-op! Whether you're new to the series or you played back in the arcades, players of all levels can enjoy these timeless classics together! - Smooth Online Play! Compete in heated ranked battles or play for fun in casual matches. Create a lobby with friends and battle head-to-head, play co-op, or spectate other matches. However you choose to play, rollback netcode makes the experience smooth and fun! A High Score Challenge mode is also available. Aim for the top of the global leaderboards! - No Experience? No Problem! This collection boasts a number of beginner-friendly features such as adjustable difficulty levels, One Button Specials, and training modes. Plus, players can save and load their progress almost anywhere and pick up right where they left off. - Additional Features! Players can view more than 500 pieces of artwork from all 7 titles along with never-before-seen development documents used to make the original games. The Music feature contains over 200 tracks from the original arcade games that players can listen to at any time! - Included Games X-MEN CHILDREN OF THE ATOM MARVEL SUPER HEROES X-MEN VS. STREET FIGHTER MARVEL SUPER HEROES vs. STREET FIGHTER MARVEL vs. CAPCOM CLASH OF SUPER HEROES MARVEL vs. CAPCOM 2 New Age of Heroes THE PUNISHER

_childDocuments_.review: Confirmed: Runs on Linux PopOS with various Protons.Confirmed: Can opt out of any data collection and easy to change at any time.  Privacy Policy is explained much cleaner than most.Confirmed: NorimaruThe gods bless, this game shows care and respect for the originals.  The additions of the training modes to bring it up to modern Quality of Life for fighters is very welcome.  There are some bug fixes for MVC2, but not too many (in a good way).  I really appreciate the multiple secret character options filtering out Mech-Gouki or Anita for certain sessions, or just having an easy select of them for my old-man brain.Complaint 1: I prefer button "map by press" rather than the "map by left/right cycle", its faster with less thinking when you are not using an xbox Controller.Complaint 2: While the screen filters are top quality, you cant see them as you select them in the menu, and they are labeled A, B, C, etc.  It takes some back and forth to find what you like.  NOTE: The Saturn look is Filter G.Complaint 3: Menu selection sounds in the metamenu area are a pain with headphones....They sound like they hit the 18kHz range.  ouch.So, you are at the end of this and wondering "Is it $50 good?".  Yeah mostly, if you love at least 2 of these games, I think enough love and polish from the devs shines through to justify the $50, especially if you know the effort to run these before this.  No Ragrets here.

_childDocuments_.review: People will complain about this just being an emulator port. Newsflash, the people who have been playing these games are well aware of what they're getting into and new players if you come across this review, please feel free to stick around. These games have been riddled with licensing issues due to Capcom & Marvel no longer being buddy buddy. Flash forward, Disney buys Marvel, MVC:I comes out... we all know how that turns out. This collection represents not only the realization of how important these games are in gaming, but to express interest of more games in the future. The last time MVC2 was available on a console was back on Xbox 360/PS3, and the other games never made there way to consoles in any capacity. Sure there is FightCade, but getting this shows both Capcom & Disney/Marvel how much we need a Marvel Fighting game again and most importantly a GOOD MVC game. Thank you for coming to my Ted Talk.

_childDocuments_.review: You get 7 faithfully ported Arcade games from CAPCOM covering the Marvel Universe largely comprised of the familiar X-Men and Avengers members with some other superheroes and villains in the mix. 3 of the games are entirely Marvel, with 4 being crossovers between Marvel and CAPCOM rosters. And 6 of the 7 are versus fighting games, with the odd one out being The Punisher which is an old school beat 'em up game much like other CAPCOM classic Beat 'Em Ups including Final Fight or Captain Commando. And wow, the rosters in this compilation are stacked! The biggest title boasting a whopping 56 characters. That of course being Marvel vs. CAPCOM 2. the crème de la crème. The very reason I'm sure a lot of people are buying this. But make no mistake, the other titles are not to be overlooked. There are some characters exclusive to certain titles. Some have different types of rulesets and features. Hell, if music is your thing, I'd say you'd want to check out everything else over Marvel vs. CAPCOM 2! If you like fighting games but find them to be very difficult or too technical, the Marvel fighting games from CAPCOM might be your ticket to easing into this genre. The games are generally a lot more forgiving than the core fighting games from CAPCOM like Street Fighter and Darkstalkers. they still reward practice and tact over sloppiness of course. But the games can sometimes be so chaotic you can get away with some button mashing even and not look like a total fool. And if you're really just that  bad  then the game also has optional assist buttons to set you for special moves with ease. But practice makes perfect so they say, and each of the fighting games includes a practice mode. Each game comes with an assortment of customization features, with options such as attack power, cpu difficulty, number of rounds where applicable, unlimited or limited continues, screen filters, easy unlocks for hidden characters, and lots more. You can basically custom tailor each game to your liking when playing in single player. I found the difficulty adjustments to be extremely fair for each title whether looking for a challenge or wanting to just roll through each game with little effort. The only game I thought needs some work from CAPCOM on balancing the difficulty adjustments might be X-Men: Children of the Atom. The CPU seems a little over the top aggressive no matter what difficulty you pick. The only real notable changes I saw in adjusting the difficulty boiled down to the health of the CPU, and not really much else. All the other games though handled just fine!As for other extras, not much has changed in the overall packaging that brings everything together. It's very similar to CAPCOM Fighting Collection. You have your gallery with tons of artwork and concept art, a music player to listen to all of the music from each game, practice modes for the fighting games in the collection complete with visual hitboxes, rollback for online play, and the normal odds and ends to wrap things up. It's a clean package overall. If I had to change anything I would love to be able to listen to the game music when say browsing the artwork gallery for example. Sadly the music from the soundtracks only play within the music section and nowhere else. Instead you have standard music made specifically for the compilation piped through in a loop everywhere else. One thing I hope CAPCOM patches in is a quicksave slot unique to each game. As of now there is only 1 quicksave slot for the entire compilation. That means if you do a quicksave for The Punisher for example, and then want to quicksave Marvel vs. CAPCOM 2 later, well, your only option to make one for MvC2 is to overwrite the quicksave for The Punisher. Tat's kind of a bummer. Now to kind of bring up a common complaint I've seen... the price. Yeah, that thing. In usd it's $49.99 at the time I'm writing this review. I'm not going to sit here and BS you. That's not cheap for some people. I get that. But at the same time it's neither an unfair price. When I look at the games in this collection and realize how long they have been buried in the vault. When I look at the prices of these individual titles on places like eBay, well... But wait, that's not a fair comparison, since these are arcade ports. Right? Well, arcade machines are just a bit more expensive then the already ridiculously overpriced copies these games go for in the individual console releases. I'm not going to try and convince you that $49.99 is not much. For some people it is. I'm just saying it's a fair price for what you get. And is this collection worth getting? Yes. Yes indeed. It is worth getting!

But the memories I hold with these games and my mother are unmeasurable. I love you Mom and I miss you everyday. R.I.P. Nostalgia never felt so good, thinking of you while I replay these games!

_childDocuments_.review: A near complete versus series package, but it's inexcusable that this game does not have cross-platform support.All the great fighting games you remembered going to the local arcade and feeding them quarter after quarter is here. Training mode for each game offers the essential features such as dummy recording, and playback, while also letting you see hitboxes - which is a rarity. However, missing features from previous titles such as the frame bar, and replay takeover keep this from being a "great" training mode.Online experience is overall solid, with rollback netcode allowing for smooth play across greater distances. However one thing that is surely holding this title back is the lack of cross-platform support. With the performance of the game being fantastic on the weakest console (Nintendo Switch), there's no reason to not believe that it isn't attainable across Steam and PSN either. This game is also coming soon for XBox Live and I see the lack of cross-platform support as a MASSIVE missed opportunity to unite the communities together as such a feature would make this collection infinitely more accessible and valuable than emulation (FightCade II).While I can't, in good conscience, give this collection a negative review, I refuse to call it "complete" until crossplay is achieved. Otherwise, the 4 communities will remain divided and I predict that the overall numbers will start to dwindle and make their way back onto FightCade. I cannot stress this enough...:PLEASE ADD CROSS-PLAY SUPPORT CAPCOM!!

_childDocuments_.review: And while it's great to have a package of really all the classic Capcom Marvel fighters tied up in one nice bow, Early feedback indicates that it's a great version of the game boasting low latency that's similar to the DreamCast version of the game - often considered the tournament standard and the best port of the game to date.For background - the DreamCast's hardware was based on the original arcade's Sega developed Naomi hardware, which essentially meant the Dreamcast version of MvC2 was running *almost* natively on *very* similar hardware to it's arcade counterpart.The PSN version on the other hand ran at a slightly different speed and also at higher input latency due to emulation.  Essentially the PSN/XB360 ports were emulating the Dreamcast version.  This included multiple filters, aspect ratio adjustments, and some visual bugs that weren't present in the DreamCast version.  Indications seem to point to this being pretty close to the DreamCast version.  Having played it myself a bit already, it definitely feels better than the PSN version did.  Sprites, sound, everything looks and feels correct - I didn't see any visual artefacts or glitches. I personally did not play the DreamCast version much so I can't comment directly on how similar it is, but I did play it quite a bit when it was in the arcade (RIP Gameworks at Grapevine Mills Mall) and it seems pretty authentic to what I remember.If you're a casual Marvel fan like I am then this is likely now the best way to experience these games.  The UI presentation, and organization of titles makes them feel authentic while giving you a few bells and whistles that we haven't typically seen with previous ports.  It's a nice homage to the series.I also appreciated having an officially released ROM of The Punisher - a game I completely missed in the arcades.  It's about as superficial as most coin-op beat-em-ups come; being a variation of the Final Fight formula with a slightly more "mature" theme.  But it was fun to run through a few times.If you pick it up - I recommend playing through them once chronologically.  It's interesting to see how the games evolved from the first title up to MvC2 - and they definitely changed pretty dramatically throughout their run.At 39.99 it may be a hard sell for anyone who's not a true fan or hasn't sipped from the nostalgia goblet, but I'm enjoying it quite a bit.  Having access to a great set of Marvel ports on Steam is just more convenient for me than Fightcade and fits my use better than anything else.  Really glad to have this collection and looking forward to future Capcom Fighting bundles!

_childDocuments_.review: Lemme get the obligatory "It's Mahvel babeeeyy" joke out of the way. *ahem* IT'S MAAAAHVEL BAYBEEEEEE!!!Now then...Marvel vs. Capcom 1 was the first traditional fighting game I remember playing back when I was 11 years old and Marvel vs. Capcom 2 on the original Xbox was how I learned how to use special moves and hyper combos for the first time. It is so surreal seeing a game franchise always shrouded in legal and licensing hell to finally have a modern collection available for modern gamers to finally see what all the hype's about and to promptly get their ass handed to them by people online.Considering that this is just an emulation of the old games, there isn't much to expect in terms of performance issues. Everything runs great and the CRT filters they offer to the CPS2 games look super crisp and look very nice. MvC2 on the other hand feels a little rougher around the edges. The internal resolution is the same as it was on the Dreamcast and everything looks really pixelated. I appreciate them keeping things as close to the original as possible, but I think having an option to scale the internal resolution to your monitor would be nice.Having a whole slew of concept art and high quality promo art by the art legend Bengus is great and is a highlight of the package. Never before has his art looked this good. Though I wish there was a bit more of a showcase of the series' history. Perhaps some interviews or a timeline of events like the Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection had.For people who have played Mahvel in the past, you probably already own this. For newcomers to the Marvel vs Capcom subseries, be prepared to learn a lot of new mechanics not present in Street Fighter. Playing MvC2 after months of 3rd Strike made the game feel like everyone was fighting on an oil slick. For newcomers to the genre as a whole, if you put in the practice and play with people around your skill level (or have someone who is good at the game teach you the ropes) I think it'll still be a fun time!

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought I would see this day. At long last MARVEL VS. CAPCOM 2 has finally been freed! It would've been worth it if it were only marvel 2, but that they brought EVERY classic marvel game really sends this collection above and beyond. Seven great games / great online with high-functioning rollback netcode. They even made sure not to forget about things like secret characters and the alternate stages exclusive to the console versions of MvC2. The only nitpicks I have are that it feels like some MvC2 stages online are more likely to appear than others. I get carnival seemingly every 2 or 3 games and I haven't gotten the alternate river stage once. Its final missing piece is CROSSPLAY. With that being said I'm still ecstatic that I can finally play a crown jewel of gaming history again. Welcome back marvel 2. Here's to hoping you stay for good!

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this is actually a pretty good collection, though (just like many games these days) the pricing is a tad too steep.I do have two massive complaints, though.1. The default settings kinda suck. The resolution (800x600) is way too low, and the ugliest scanline (I think Type D) is chosen by default. Even worse is that you can't save your changes and have to constantly change it every single time you open the game. It's also very tedious to change every single button/video configuration for each game, and there should be an option to change the controls for every game at once. (Except for probably the Punisher, since that game is a beat 'em up and not a fighting game.)2. I don't know if it's the fault of the original arcade version, but MVC2's sprites look way too blurry and low-quality. I also have to dock a few points for not including widescreen support for these game, MVC2 especially. (If I remember correctly, Capcom Fighting Collection does let you play Hyper Street Fighter 2 in widescreen.)Overall, 8/10. Pretty good, but please at least somewhat fix these glaring problems.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel vs Capcom Fighting collection: Arcade classics-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------It's Mahvel Baby!!!A blast from the past, the Marvel Vs Capcom fighting collection is a love letter to all fighting game fans. The roster is stacked, the animations are slick, and the soundtrack? Pure nostalgia.Each game brings its own flavor, whether you're a beginner spamming Hadoukens or a pro pulling off insane air combos. Sure, some mechanics might feel a little dated, but that’s just part of the charm.Get ready to mash those buttons, call in your assists, and scream "HYPER COMBO FINISH!" at the top of your lungs. This collection is a must-have for anyone who loves chaotic tag-team action.In the words of Magneto, "Welcome to Die!"… again and again.Grab your stick, grab your friends, and enjoy the madness.CAPCOM PRESENTSMarvel Vs Capcom.And it lives on !!!!!!Enjoy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite my limited time with the game cause of circumstances I can give it the following review:Gameplay:Mechanics are insanely deep and free flowing with every single game in this collection. This is a marvel vs capcom treat and the developers know it, giving you multiple arcade original artwork from the cabinets themselves on how to start playing these games.As an added bonus, all arcade modes are easy to finish and to practice with the help of save states and unlimited retries. Pulling up a movelist mid match, no matter if online or offline, works fast and lets you quickly look up your moves to get to know the character in a fast pace.Otherwise what can I say that hasn't been said:THIS IS MAAAHVEL BABYYYY, you be hitting people with combos as long as the trip from sun to earth and back or getting reset as if you were a bugging super nintendo in the 90s.At the same time between all of this broken mess are characters that give you upwards to unlimited potential and tricks while the ones down lower on the tiers still provide decent fun in games like marvel 2.Story:Maaaan this is comic book stuff. With some insights from the artwork gallery you could probably piece together what the lore might be here but honestly, not knowing anything about the X-Men or Marvel super heroes in general is kind of a hard task nowadays with them flooding popular media and culture. This is mostly interesting for the nerds under us who love both IPs to the fullest.Art and Sound / Presentation:This is old school capcom at its best. - Incredible Spritework - Stunning animations - Overall charming visuals (even while some of them might look dated!) - Incredible OSTs for all the games with Capcom smashing some hits in there   (personal recommendations: Magneto's Theme in XvsSF or the Cave Theme in Marvel vs Capcom 2)The overall UI is pretty good and the menus are nothing to write home about but it is good enough to not be noticable in any bad way possible.Overall TL;DR:This is a peak game even for the price tag. You're getting each game for about 10 bucks with bonus artwork and behind the scenes sketches for the game's development. You should get this game for Marvel vs Capcom 2 alone but who wouldn't mind listening to its character select theme on repeat in the music gallery until he drives himself insane?Happy gaming on this one, let's bring back Marvel and get Marvel 4 rolling!

_childDocuments_.review: 24 years later and the promised "ride" has still not happened... Unless they mean those air combos. One of the finest collections of classic fighting games you can buy... BUT (and it's an enormous but) this game is unplayable online unless you put in a LOT of practice first solo or with friends. It's an unfortunate reality of all classic fighting games that they become extremely hard to get into for newcomers and the capcom vs series is one of the worst for it.On the plus side at least you can turn off certain things now like the seizure inducing white light flashing that was in the originals designed to grab your attention in the arcades. It's truly a product of the 2000s and late 90s with some of the head-scratching decisions of music choices and character balancing which would never fly if the games were made today.Which reminds me! This game is 100% a test to see if people will buy a marvel vs capcom 4 and they would for sure!A lot of games can get carried by the brands associated with it and this is a classic example. Strip the famous characters away? and it's a game of mostly zoning, inescapable frame traps, anti airs, and infinite combos to learn (that the devs totally intended guys! Honest!) so you can style on the other person and force them to just sit and watch.If all that sounds like a good time or you know what to avoid? Go for it! Everyone else? You are going to get more salty than a fish butchers at opening hour.Oh yeah and it has The Punisher beatemup too which is nice....

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 The collection we've been wanting for a long time!First of all, thank you so much for releasing this collection on PC, Capcom and Marvel. Marvel VS Capcom Fighting Collection: Arcade Classics are full of classic gems. I played some of those games on an emulator (Sorry, Capcom and Marvel.) because I really wanted to play those games. But playing these games on an emulator is difficult for me because of the laggy input and low resolution. And if you want to buy the OG games with the outdated consoles on Amazon or eBay, it gets very expensive. It's not worth selling your two kidneys for games that you don't know will work properly. I will never buy from scalpers. Not even in 100 years. Actually, I could wait until this game is discounted to -75%. But I pre-ordered the game to support the developers and this franchise (fighting game crossover) in general (maybe we'll get a new Marvel VS Capcom game someday. Fingers crossed.). Licensing a comic book/cartoon character is more difficult than licensing a video game character. That's also why licensed games are delisted one to five years after a product is released. (I don't know when this collection will be delisted, but I hope it never happens)._______________________________________________________________________________Now I would like to give a short review of each game. X-MEN CHILDREN OF THE ATOM: It's ok. It feels a bit slow. And the CPU in arcade mode are damn cheaters. EVEN ON LEVEL 1. MARVEL SUPER HEROES: Much better than the previous game. But it also has the problem that the enemy is OP, even on level 1. X-MEN VS. STREET FIGHTER: Excellent. The gameplay is smooth and fun. ^^MARVEL SUPER HEROES vs. STREET FIGHTER: An improved version of X-Men VS. Street Fighter. The gameplay is amazing and smooth. It's cool that other Marvel characters are playable. MARVEL vs. CAPCOM CLASH OF SUPER HEROES: The fact that Cyclops is not playable in this game is a crime. But it's still a good game. MARVEL vs. CAPCOM 2 New Age of Heroes: I'm finally able to play this wonderful game. But the final boss is a damn cheater. THE PUNISHER: This is an unexpected bonus game. A great beat em' up game. I love it. _______________________________________________________________________________There are also a few problems that I would like to mention:The first problem is that the one button special moves and other control settings only work with controllers.If you want to play it with a keyboard, you somehow can't use these features.The second problem is that the win rate is not calculated in the final results of X-MEN CHILDREN OF THE ATOM and MARVEL vs CAPCOM 2 New Age of Heroes. Only “0 Wins” is displayed. Is this a bug or is it only displayed if I use the save state regularly? (Source:  ,  )To sum everything up, this collection is great. Also, the existence of this collection make me so happy. Is it worth the 50 bucks? Well, that depends. If you only want to play the single player content, you should wait for a discount. But even then, it's still cheaper than buying from scalpers. I would like to thank everyone who has supported the #FreeMVC2 movement, especially Maximilian Dood who started this trend. Overall and a message to Capcom:In general, I'd like to thank Capcom and Marvel for releasing this collection (and more collections in the future) on Steam. My wishlist for games that should come to PC is now almost complete.However, there are four games that I really want to see on PC. Whether it's a port or a remake, I'll leave it up to you, Capcom. These games are Okamiden, Viewtiful Joe, Tatsunoko vs. Capcom: Ultimate All-Stars and Asura's Wrath.I'll be looking forward to playing more of your older games. And thanks for bringing Marvel VS Capcom and Capcom VS SNK back to life! <3
