_childDocuments_.review: Words cannot describe how happy I am right now. The MVC Fighting Collection is a dream come true for fans and newcomers of the series alike. I still remember to this day, besides MK Armageddon, one of my very first fighting games was the MVC Origins and MVC 2 port on Xbox Live. It was my first true experience with the franchise and as a kid, those games blew my mind away. Especially MVC2. Similar to Armageddon, the roster size of MVC2 was massive. It was to celebrate all the previous Marvel and Capcom crossover games to that point and man, what a fighting game.  Years later it is still unrivaled in terms of gameplay mechanics, speed, combo potential, and presentation. I remember watching Maximilian's streams constantly, seeing an MVC2 port being a "dream come true". Years and years of streams just to finally have this happen. Not only that, but to have a port with all previous crossover Marvel and Capcom games, all with rollback, lobby and tournament settings (both online and offline), a gallery for art, music, as well as an insanely well-done training mode for each game with frame data and AI opponent customization. It is all perfect.Thank you Capcom. This is a brilliant package. Pick this one up folks.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Those madmen actually went and unpatched the Juggernaut glitch. A lot of my below complaints about this port's UI and interface still stand but it's clear the people who worked on this genuinely care and that deserves a ton of respect. Definitely show this your support!-----I purchased to support these games. I love these games. Capcom please give rollback to MVC3 and please, please give Eighting a billion dollars to make MVC4, thanks.Overall I'd cautiously recommend this if it wasn't for a few major gripes. The collection seems solid.  The non-MVC2 games look great, run great, and are fun to play even if you're just being a shameless button masher like I am. Personally I’m even finding myself preferring playing them to MVC2, which frankly speaking has always been very MUGEN. I've only played with my wife, so I haven't tried online for them or MVC2 or personally seen the problems people report with the online yet.But there are some other problems with the collection itself. The menus lack some QOL features, for instance. One thing I noticed immediately is that, as far as I can tell, there’s no controller test, and you assign your inputs with a left to right scrolling menu, one button at a time. You can’t, for instance, select your Light Punch button and then press Y to assign it to the Y button - you have to go to LP in the menu and scroll over to Y. This is pretty silly and I expect better from a fighting game collection these days, especially since a lot of people will want to use leverless controllers that have reassignable pins and don’t have marked buttons.  The real kick in the pants in this collection though is, strangely, MVC2. Considering it's objectively the main draw of the collection and what most people are putting down $50 just to play, me included, there are a number of oddities. I have to assume it's because it's the hardest to emulate since it's emulating a NAOMI board, which is effectively a Dreamcast, and not the CPS2 boards used by literally every other game here.First of all it looks terrible. What blew my mind is that's just dead on accurate to how it actually looks when displayed in raw pixels - MVC2 really did just display the sprites  badly, because the NAOMI board/Dreamcast is 3D hardware. It's not made for 2D games. The developers just lazily plastered the sprites onto MVC2's bizarre 3D environments as chunky, stretched, heavily aliased billboards. Check it in Fightcade or another emulator yourself - I did.You probably never noticed this either because CRTs disguise the jank. Hell, I have a local arcade I go to where I'll sometimes play MVC2 and it’s never looked this bad to my eyes. The real problem is the CRT filters are hard to use and don't disguise it well. I have no idea why the filters are listed as letters like "A" or "J", and why the menu where you change them covers the entire screen so you can't compare them at a glance. This is something that Capcom developers got right back in the day with games like 3rd Strike: Online - just have the filter menu at the bottom of the screen so you can preview the whole image without backing out.On top of that, the filter also filters the game's UI. Which, duh, but the more aggressive filters make things like the text on the healthbars hard to read. Having to make a tradeoff between readable text and the game looking decent doesn't feel especially great. I think it's possible to actually fix it and have the UI filtered/overlaid separately, but I think this is really a problem with the filters themselves. The NAOMI board is different hardware - it'd be smart to use different filtering techniques than the ones that are designed for the CPS2 games.Putting that aside though, since it is admittedly how the game looked, my real problem is that this collection of arcade games isn't actually arcade perfect. Nobody is going to play this game over the long term over just using Fightcade if it isn't the exact versions people have been playing for 20 years. My team is BB Hood/Commando/Juggernaut since it's one of BB Hood's best teams and she's the character I've been playing since I was a child, but this version fixes the Juggernaut glitch that is core to her TODs... so this already low-tier gimmick team now is even less viable.From what I've read, this is apparently because this is just the game running as it always was “supposed to,” and they didn’t actually alter any code. But the job of an emulator is to replicate the original hardware 1:1, flaws and all. NES emulators have sprite flickering, SNES games like Star Fox and Earthbound have slowdown. But even those are visual issues, not gameplay ones - even more accurate emulators seek cycle accuracy because anything less can result in behaviors that aren't true to hardware, and can even prevent games from being able to be completed. When you’re emulating a fighting game in particular, inaccurate emulation resulting in changes to the character’s gameplay (and so the meta) is a complete failure in a product selling itself as a collection of fighting games.There’s no actual reason for this glitch to stay removed. The Juggernaut power-up glitch isn’t like other glitches in the game that could cause issues in a mass-market online title, like Gambit cheesing matches by leaving the screen and never coming back, or Ruby Heart hard crashing the game. These make sense to patch out, if not philosophically, then at least in the game’s online modes so that people can’t use them to grief. The Juggernaut glitch doesn’t allow players to grief, it just benefits a very bad character in a way the developers didn’t intend, allowing him to serve a role in a couple of low tier gimmick teams.As strange as it might sound, I hope that Capcom unpatches the glitch and any other glitches accidentally "fixed" by poor emulation. No matter how much I want to support this series, no matter how much I want them to make more of these games that were a part of my childhood and young adulthood, what’s the point of an arcade collection if the games aren’t as 1:1 as possible to the arcade ROMs? I am glad to support an official release, I just hope that Capcom is paying attention to the feedback and will give this some more polish and stricter arcade accuracy.

_childDocuments_.review: The Marvel vs Capcom franchise is a peculiar crossover series, one that outsiders likely shrug their shoulders at its absurdity. Behind the curtain though exists a legacy that stretches more than 20 years and brings several icons to the brawl. This new edition of the Fighting Collection: Arcade Classics revives seven Capcom games featuring the Marvel cast, but the most notable of these are Marvel vs Capcom: Clash of Super Heroes and Marvel vs Capcom 2: New Age of Heroes. While these two games are the stars of the bundle, Capcom represents other notable fighting games released in partnership with Marvel (with the exception of the beat-em up, The Punisher). The collection mimics both the look and feel of the arcade games, includes accessibility settings for new players, and introduces online functionality with solid rollback netcode. And the in-game gallery features deep cuts of artwork and music across all the titles. While I do think the bundle is worth the value, I acknowledge that only die-hards may stick around long enough to savor all this package has to offer. But make no mistake, Marvel vs Capcom Fighting Collection: Arcade Classics will take you for a ride.Review Score: 8/10For a more detailed review:

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely lazy port. No crossplay. No wifi indicator. Changing the setting to 5 bars only does nothing. The only reason to buy this game is in the hopes that marvel vs capcom 4 comes out. The netcode is horrible. Characters glitch everywhere. I don't know how it is possible for them to make this netcode worst than the 2008 version that was on the xbox 360 and the playstation 3 but they did. Horrible, and lazy, implementation of rollback. It feels like the awful street fighter 5 rollback. I feel bad for anyone that is introduced to the amazing "marvel vs capcom" series through this half hearted port. Capcom does not deserve this fanbase they have. We have stockholm syndrome. We will accept anything from them because we miss these legendary games so much, and we want the series to continue. They didn't even try, they just added a UI, and imported some roms.I really hope they patch the netcode, because no netcode should be this bad in 2024. Good luck guard cancelling anything.

_childDocuments_.review: PSA: If you play PC fighting games using a PlayStation controller prepare to be disappointed. Even though it says full support it DOES NOT!I prefer a PS4 Dual Shock controller when it comes to fighting games because I like the feel of the D-Pad on that the best. This game does not register the D-Pad at all. I even tried the PS5 DualSense controller, same thing. Its stick only. It doesn't end there!The buttons are reversed. By default square should be light hit punch and triangle should be heavy punch but its reversed for some reason so you will have to setup a custom control layout to correct.The Xbox controller works great. Everything works as its supposed to but, for me, the XBOX is the last controller I would want to use for a fighting game.If you are like me and prefer PS controllers for fighting games either skip this or wait till Capcom fixes this.

_childDocuments_.review: The collection is fine, and it definitely shows that people have worked in this release and it`s not just copy-paste release.HOWEVER, I only care about MVC 2 online. And right now that is completely unplayable, it functioned fine for about two weeks and misteriously after some people were reporting "not getting any matches"... capcom decided to fix this by merging the entire american continent in to one. If you filter connection by bars it doesn`t work... region lock doesnt work either. You are forced to play ranked matches against lagging people. Great.Everyone is in full copium mode and still speaking about how wonderful it works... and in reality you will get constantly getting matches WITH RED BARS FROM THE ENTIRE CONTINENT, slowdown, bad rollback and an overall awful experience that will for sure ruin any enjoyment you could possibly get from playing this particular game online.WHEN IT WORKS PROPERLY it's awesome... but for misterious unexplainable reasons the routing sucks and sometimes I cant even play (AT ALL) with people who live one hour away from me.Also, quitting in ranked is 100% free, turning an already toxic and opressive game in to an awful mess of an experience.As it is right now, I would 100% recommend you go to fightcade and pirate the ♥♥♥♥ out of every last capcom property included in this collection (since 35 buckaroos is not cheap for something thats been emulated for over two decades).Again, when you are playing arcade alone, single player, it`s the best most stable version of the game (tho the ps3 version wich I absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hate looks at least 2-3 times better and that is pure shame).Sigh, you played me with this one capcom, played with my illusions and dreams and so my review is AVOID AT ALL COSTS, ONLY BUY WHEN IN SALE.

_childDocuments_.review: One week later: matchmaking seems to be working. Can't tell with lobbies since they seem abandoned from the initial bug wave. Sound issues still exist in mvc2, and built in visual nerfs in ranked by design for all games (sigh). Game crashes periodically after matchmaking. I'm past my refund period, but I'm reluctantly recommending this since it's the simplest way to play these games online currently if you're not technically savvy. Day 1 review: Broken matchmaking. Can't connect to lobbies. Sound issues in mvc2. Another game with a 60sec confirmation timer for people to troll you with in matchmaking. Already wasted an hour to get 3 matches, so now i have to sit and wait for a patch to spend my last 40 minutes game testing before I pull the trigger on a refund. Fine if you're a collector I guess if you dont mind wonky ps2 era sound on an arcade port. Great gallery, so worth it as a digital artbook if you're into that! :)

_childDocuments_.review: The built-in DualSense controller support is broken, forcing you to use Steam Input, which usually means additional input delay which i find in other fighting games i play. Also if you want to change the button icons to match the PlayStation layout, there is no in-game setting for it. You will need to follow these steps:    Right-click Marvel Vs Capcom in your library.    Select Manage > Browse Local Files.    Open Config.ini.    Find the line that says Button Prompt = X360.    Change X360 to PS4.    Save the file.    Start the game to see if it works.I will update my recommendation once these changes and fixes are implemented.

_childDocuments_.review: If you use a KEYBOARD (which is a lot of the PC community).  Please note that the control options you get are extremely limited and PAD players get more options.  There are no settings to allow you to map PPP, KKK, LP+LK, MP+MK, HP+HK buttons for KB so this makes many aspects of all of the games in the collection inconsistent.  Without playing with these, after 30 minutes I'm getting hand cramps and dropping a bunch of combos.  I can't wave dash, triangle jump, or quickly call assists consistently.  Keyboard users need these options!  They are literally available on every other Capcom Fighting game.  While I don't use this, mapping 1 button specials is also not part of keyboard controls.  There are issues with online matchmaking as well.If you intend to play this game on Keyboard, I strongly recommend NOT purchasing the game atm.

_childDocuments_.review: No ping or jitter info, no wi-fi/vpn indicator, no flag, no connection status before a match, no way to block teleporting Magnetos and other evil doers... It's ghastly. Delay based netcode fighting games from the 2010's had some or even all of these things. FBA based clients like GGPO and Damdai's Supercade had them and they are ancient history. What's Capcom's sorry arse excuse when Fightcade has been providing all of this vital data and more for years? And what is this about not losing points in ranked? That's crazy.

_childDocuments_.review: The main reason for getting this collection is Marvel vs Capcom 2. Fortunately after the recent patch, it now is more or less arcade perfect without crashes or freezes or softlocks. While absent at launch, Juggernaut glitch is back and present. Anakaris curse infinite does not work in the training room, but it works in actual matches. The matchmaking has been greatly improved with games appearing usually under 20 seconds.There is another game that doesn't have the revision the community prefers, but I don't know the details. Personally, I got this for Marvel vs Capcom 2, and the other games are a bonus. For that one game revision, there is Fightcade as an online community alternative.As for the expectations of a $50 collection, the port is more simple without the quality of life features that newer fighting games around that price tend to have. Training room is more basic rather than something modern with great features. For example, there's no quick selection for characters or there's no save state feature. There is also lackluster support for some features. Keyboard binds don't support macros like the controller bindings do. You will need to use an external program to get that functionality. The lack of crossplay will hamper the longevity of this game too, but there is Fightcade for that.For a release that's $50, there could be more love and care put into it. Otherwise, it is functional with the biggest complaints at launch now resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: Main reason for the thumbs down is the censorship. If it's "not an issue" as I see other reviews and discussions saying, then it shouldn't have been removed, but because it was removed it must have been an issue. It took more effort to censor the idiotic things they censored than it would to have just left them in and listened to a minority of people gripe about them.The second reason is the price tag. I purchased this to give it the 2 hour play test to see if it was even worth it. In my first few fights on MvC2 they were fine. No issues. Then I'm paired up against Sakura and Captain Commando as Gambit and they're just walking through my Ultimate when Sakura call's in CC. Or Sakura will freeze in place when hit but CC will take all the damage.3rd, and I didn't really look all that hard, but I couldn't find a way to enable the D-Pad. I dislike joysticks very much for fighting games.4th the menu's suck. I couldn't find the exit button from the main menu, granted, I didn't try that hard, but it wasn't intuitive so I just alt-F4'd out of it rather than deal with it.5th These are the arcade mode games it seems like, so there's no unlocking characters as you play. I'm not in this for the online play. I just enjoy beating up the computer. This ties in with number 4. Since this is arcade you have to set your difficulty at the main menu as opposed to changing settings in each game. So there is no personalizing each game to how you like it. I think I'd rather just play the Fightcade or ROM versions than this overpriced censored emulator.The effort needed to put into these games would be to LEAVE THEM ALONE AND RELEASE THEM AS THEY WERE INITIALLY RELEASED. Hell, I wouldn't mind a $40.00 price tag on an unaltered release of just MvC2 as it was released on the Dreamcast. And to the crowd that keeps crying "this is why we won't get MvC4!" Good. It's not worth it as they clearly can't be bothered to just re-release an old game like it was back in the day. Why would you want a new game when they can't even get their act together on a simple re-release? MvC3 wasn't that great and MvC: Infinite was a dumpster fire in the middle of a train wreck. With all the pandering and woke BS that Disney is pushing out you won't have anything meaningful, and the way Capcom is going in their development of fighting games we'd just get nothing but 1 button special auto-fighters with some stupid grind hell mechanic and $20.00 per character DLCs, 50 nonsensical costume options, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ soundtracks, dumb-ass hype men/announcers in the fights and garbage rosters.This isn't even worth the nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played any of these games as a kid. I was introduced to the franchise through the original mvc3. Have fun with the game, and invite some people over. If are very good at mvc, these games also have online, keep in mind I couldn't land a single hit on anybody in mvc2 online.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually, Marvel vs. Capcom: The Fighting Collection strikes a balance between its retro roots and modern expectations. The games are faithfully presented in their original 2D sprite-based art, and even the more dated titles still manage to hold up reasonably well, thanks to the HD upscaling and filters that are available. However, it’s important to remember that these are still games from the late '90s and early 2000s, so don’t expect cutting-edge visuals. The charm here is in the old-school look and feel, which is perfect for players looking to experience the magic of arcade cabinets in the comfort of their own home.

I'm liking this (these) game(s) a lot, I bought it for MVC 2, but I have been learning how to play all the other games, and I think I'm doing okay, that is, unless my best isn't good enough. I love these games, and I hope I can work my way up to playing more ranking matches so I get more opportunities to experience this with everybody. If I had a complaint, maybe get Cross-Play in there too? I don't know. All I know is its Mah-Vel Bay-Bee! What do I really have to complain about?!

_childDocuments_.review: Finally having (mostly) arcade-perfect versions of these games all in one place is really incredible. X-Men: COTA was a transformative game in my childhood and sparked a love of both X-Men and fighters; X-Men vs. Street Fighter blew my mind by combining two of my favorite franchises. I haven't played MvC2 since owning it as a teenager on Dreamcast, but the muscle memory is still there and it's a blast online and off. The games all play well, online is now in a really solid state, and you get incredible value for the cost. Sure, MvC1 and 2 are the most  games in the collection, but I think all of them have their place, with X-Men vs. Street Fighter being super underrated. The extras are straightforward but a nice addition. With another collection on the horizon next year, I hope Capcom keeps the train rolling. This is fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long time coming, but the fan requests have been answered to have not only the first two Marvel vs. Capcom games available once again, but several other Marvel themed fighting games from Capcom as well.Several display options are available such as different scanline options and borders, and adjusting the difficulty of each game to your liking. The games play buttery smooth and I didn't notice any lag during my hours of play on my Steam Deck. I unfortunately can't give my thoughts on online since I'm not up to snuff with the most expert players in experience, but I've heard great things about it.Using mostly the controller for play, input was on par and I liked how super moves are more accessible with hotkeys now as it saves a bit more time for me when playing through the arcade modes of the games. As for graphics, they look nice and sharp and have been touched up a bit for modern gaming.For what it's worth, and how strongly requested these games are, the $50 pricetag seemed understandable. Definitely pick it up in case these games get delisted again.

_childDocuments_.review: A MARVELOUS TIME CAPSULE FROM THE PASTI have nostalgia for only some of the games in this collection. I have played the PS1 versions which are regarded as different compare to the Arcade releases. Even then I never played a whole lot of them and was more attracted to games like Tekken 3 or X-Men: Mutant Academy 2 because of those games being in 3D. Therefore, this review will come from that perspective. This collection offers six games which are;THE PUNISHERX-MEN: CHILDREN OF THE ATOMMARVEL SUPER HEROESX-MEN VS. STREET FIGHTERMARVEL SUPER HEROES VS. STREET FIGHTERMARVEL VS. CAPCOM: CLASH OF SUPER HEROESMARVEL VS. CAPCOM 2: NEW AGE OF HEROESEven though I have played many fighting games, I’m not a real connoisseur or expert of the genre. In terms of multiplayer, I like playing locally with other people more than online. Unfortunately for this game I did not get to play with other people like before so this review is not going to be critical and is mostly having a casual look on this collection.THE PUNISHERThe first arcade game that formed the partnership between Capcom & Marvel. Honestly for me, this game is most unappealing in this collection. The Punisher is a fun beat-em-up game where you can control either The Punisher or Nick Fury and fight enemies in order to defeat Kingpin. Mowing down enemies with weapons littered throughout the stage is satisfying and can get surprisingly violent and edgy which is uncommon for me to experience in a Capcom game. The main reason why it feels the weakest in this collection is mainly because it is standing side by side with the fighting games. This is not a fighting game and is included in this collection as it is the start of Capcom’s & Marvel’s partnership, giving birth to the Marvel vs. Capcom series.X-MEN: CHILDREN OF THE ATOMThe first fighting game that will pave the way to MVC and features X-Men characters based on the X-Men: The Animated Series TV Show. I’ve played this game on the PS1 and other than some UI changes, the game feels about the same to me. I didn’t play this game a lot back then because there is no Nightcrawler which is present in another X-Men fighting game I played a lot.  I will say the art and music in this game is probably the best out of all the other games in this collection. Maybe I just like Magneto’s design and stage music too much, I don’t know. Gameplaywise, this game plays a bit similar to Street Fighter having the traditional 6 buttons and 1v1 fights. This game is pure fun but can get pretty tough after getting used to the later games.MARVEL SUPER HEROESThe next fighting game after X-Men: COTA. This game is just pure fun that gives a glimpse on the state of Marvel Comics back in the ‘90s especially when it comes to Thanos and anything related to the Infinity Gauntlet. I played as Spider-Man and fighting against Thanos is funny for me because it is a totally different story compare to the modern interpretations of these characters especially the MCU’s version. Gameplaywise, it is fun. The Infinity Gems is a neat gimmick to turn the tide of battle. I’m not much of a fan of the artstyle honestly with its more kiddish and childish themes. I’m more of a fan of X-Men: COTA’s more metallic edge and splendor.X-MEN VS. STREET FIGHTERThe first Marvel vs. Capcom game. As a first attempt, this game is a solid and fun experience. You get to pick and play as two characters in a battle unlike the previous games above which are the traditional 1v1 situations. There is no Team Assists yet at this point. Gameplaywise, this game feels much more faster and chaotic. Artstylewise, this game have not yet manage to blend the two brands of Capcom & Marvel together, making the characters having conflicting art styles at times.  MARVEL SUPER HEROES VS. STREET FIGHTERAt first, my impression of this game is quite negative. This game on the surface seems to not offer anything new, bland menu design, bland artstyle, reused stages, and weak final boss. But what made me appreciate this game more is, well, this game is just fun to play. Team Assists is first implemented here and I have a moment in this game where it finally clicked on what made Tag Team Fighters fun. Looking up on the game more, there’s a lot of secret opponents hidden in the game. These parts of the game are the reasons why I don’t hate the game as my initial impressions.MARVEL VS. CAPCOM: CLASH OF SUPER HEROESThe next game that I have nostalgia for from the PS1 era. The third MVC game in release order, but the first MVC game by name. Nostalgia or not, this game is one of the best games I’ve ever played. I love the chaotic energy this game exerts in each moments of gameplay. This game adds more stuff you can do with the Tag Team mechanic. I’m not sure if this is only on Arcade Mode but it is kinda a bummer that I cannot pick Special Assist characters which are characters that can only be used as assists. I will say the final boss is kinda cheap. Almost made me hate the game, but once I finally defeated him and enjoy trying out other characters, I became fond of this game even more.MARVEL VS. CAPCOM 2: NEW AGE OF HEROESThe one, the only, the champion of this collection. I have never played this game and this is the best game in this collection. While MVC1 have 2v2 with 1 Special Character, this game just included the special character, making the game 3v3, and holy moly the 3v3 fight is real. Tag Teams feels more like real teams, assists being one button, having a large roster including every character, makes this game even more the largest amd tougher to juggle.  The only flaw I found for this game is the story and finale. The story is kinda nonexistent. Other games have character endings that shows a glimpse of life behind the fights that usually shows whats the story all about. But here in MVC2, the final boss is weird and unexplained, and then the finale hits then it just cuts to credits which can be disappointing. Honestly, I think the real story is locked behind Online, something about a guy named Wazzler.MARVEL VS CAPCOM FIGHTING COLLECTION: ARCADE CLASSICSThis collection offers the best presentation for these games providing not only the games but also the Museum and Music Player. The Museum features many old artworks that gave more context and behind the scenes stuff for these games. The Music Player is… well, a music player. The devs went unnecessarily hard with the original tracks made for this collection though. The music is great in all of these games.Another great feature this collection offers is the Fighter Awards which is more than just a normal ingame achievement system. The awards not only provide achievements you’ve done but also achievements you can do and gives hints on the secrets and parts that are hidden in the games. The Fighter Awards is what made me aware of MSHVSF’s secret opponents, XCOTA hidden opponent, and also the differences of roster between games. This is not a normal ingame achievement system but also a helpful objective list of stuff you can do in these old games which can sometimes contain very obscure ways to tackle the hidden content.I also love the simple way of this collection providing guides and tutorial for each game; Marquee Cards. There’s no modern tutorials for these games and you have to read each provided Marquee Card that are scanned from marquee cards in each game. These cards provides the basics and guides on how to play each characters of each game. I actually love this aspect since not only it sets the tone for these games but also enables the player to participate or experience how the game is played back in the past. This is a surprisingly superb collection and maybe one of the best collection I’ve ever played. Overall, a great collection for great games.5/5

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing these on the arcades as a little kid back then. Bought this almost solely for MVC 1 and 2. I don't even play online, though I hear the matchmaking is good. I also love Juggernaut and I appreciate them patching his glitch back. They literally patched the game to break it, which is quite funny, but this speaks volumes on how authentic of an experience they want it to be (similar to the original).Lack of crossplay might put off some players (though I'm not discounting that they might eventually update it in the future) but in the case of being the most accessible version of MVC 2 and all the other titles, this is a great case for the preservation of these games in the future.As a busy person, I also really like that I can pause the game anytime, save my progress and load it right from the state where I left off. Honestly, these classic games are my small pops of entertainment in such a busy schedule. I know that these are classic emulator features, not to mention that I also played some of these games in Fightcade, but having all of these titles and those functionalities in one package with some extras (the museum!) is a huge quality of life improvement for me. I can just boot up steam and have a quick arcade run for 15 mins or so before going back on my tasks.Lastly, an arcade stick is optional, but it adds so much to the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: In the first week or so there was trouble with online matchmaking. _childDocuments_.review: A marvelous collection full of nostalgia showcasing the legacy of Capcom's Marvel VS. Series. Keep in mind the games are emulated, so take that into consideration. (Which isn't a negative thing, it's differences from an "Arcade perfect port" is negligible at best) Training mode, ROM selection, Rollback Netcode makes this a buy for fighting game enthusiasts and marvel fans alike.This doesn't replace the community that Fightcade has built but it certainly is great to have the ability to purchase these titles that otherwise previously had no legal means of purchase for nearly a decade from their re-release in Marvel VS: Origins and MvC2 re-release on PS3 and 360.Honestly it's a great collection; there are minor gripes in terms of Quality of Life improvementsTake for instance: Button Configuration -- I wish it was button confirm instead of a slider to choose it's function.I also would have liked the Arcade Start Button and Menu Start to be the same button but to open the Menu ---- it would have to be a Long Hold Press.When setting the game to 4:3 and not full -- the borders do not stretch to fill the space so you have an odd black border between the art and the game.Again these are minor gripes, I'm grasping at straws here to find something negative to say -- the overall package is fantastic and cannot be understated.The inclusion of The Punisher is nice but I was hoping they would have added the X-Men: Mutant Apocalypse and Marvel: War of The Gems beat-em-ups as well.Part of the package is the robust collection of SUPER HIGH Resolution art and complete OSTs for each of the titles which is a really nice inclusion. The addition of the original arcade marquee and controls info is fantastic and a nice touch.Marvel VS is back and it's great to see it's re-release handled with great care. It certainly is a great time to be an old fighting game fan.First SVC: Chaos, then Marvel vs Capcom Fighting Collection and then Capcom Fighting Collection 2 --- Bringing classics like Rival Schools -- excuse me, I mean the sequel, Project Justice, Power Stone 1 & 2 as well as Capcom vs SNK 1 & 2???? There's no better time to build a Steam Arcade cabinet!

_childDocuments_.review: I was really enjoying the game, my grandma who's deal with the early stages of dementia, which she developed after my grandpa passed, saw me playing. She said "whats that?" So I showed her the game. We then went to her computer I created a steam account for her and downloaded MVC, the first video game shes ever played! Next thing I know shes in the lab doing sick combos, making these awesome team comps. She's having so much fun! Her speech is improving! She's remembering things forgot 10 yrs ago! She's beating MY butt in the game! So I encourage her to go online. She's a little nervous but I've seen the things she can do. I know she will body these fools. After about an hour into her online adventures, "he" appeared. The Wazzler. I said "no ma ma!" "Do not challenge that man!" And she turned and smiled to me "What's wrong? It'll be fun?". This "Wazzler" was relentless! Hitting her from every side. Mix-ups I wouldn't wish on my worst enemy. With every blow she clutched her chest. I screamed "STOP!" "YOU'RE HURTING HER!" and that's when I noticed his mic was on. He said " Whats wrong granny? Oh you gonna learn today!" "Welcome to the real world" After the match I rushed her to the ICU. But it was too late. Curse you Wazzler! CURSE YOU!!!!Good game 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: With these collections, I base my rating more on the thought and care they put into the presentation than I do with the actual games themselves because everyone knows they are all-time classics.  On that note, I have only dreamt of owning legit versions of these games with MvC1 being at the top of that list.  I gave the Street Fighter 30th Anniversary collection a negative rating because it felt janky and like a lazy cash grab.  In contrast, with the Marvel vs. Capcom collection it seems like they put a lot more effort into making this a cohesive package (but still not as good as the Playstation 2 SF collections), even including a hidden gem that I nearly forgot about (but loved as a kid) with the Punisher.A couple really nice touches in this collection are all the filters (G is my favorite so far), much more robust training modes, nice looking move lists, and QUICKLY getting into the games.  I know it may not seem like a big deal, but I couldn't stand waiting through all the UNSKIPPABLE company logos in the 30th Anniversary collection every time I loaded that up.I haven't tested the online yet which I hear isn't doing so hot on PC, so I hope it doesn't die off soon.  I also don't like how under Controls, it doesn't detect if you have a Playstation controller (only the A,B,X,Y annotation) or that you have to change the controls for EVERY game.  Still, once I changed one, the rest of the games were quick to rebind.  Not a huge deal, but slightly annoying.I guess the biggest pro is that most of these games, at least in arcade perfect form, have never been available for consoles I've owned, so to have them ALL together in one bundle is a huge deal.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid fighting engine and very engaging. If you like high chain combos, average/'above average' reflex required fighting, and challenge...this collection is the one.I'd go as far to say that if there was 1 fighting game left on the planet and people from the future picked this game up and had no concept of fighting games but played this collection... they'd be very inspired to make fighting games - a golden standard In my humble opinion.'The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim' equivalent for fighting games both aging like fine wine.For perspective: I'd say i'm pretty average at fighting games, hear me out...I've toggled back and forth between a controller and keyboard playing this game and I'd say unless you've been playing games all your life on keyboard or controller there is a mechanical/accuracy/precision ceiling you're hands are going to hit that will translate into missing input to clear mid/long combos. Performance will vary on your part, not for lack of knowledge or mechanical skill (you know what you want to press, and you know you pressed the right buttons) but for some reason your character whiffs/'doesn't execute' because you slightly missed a button or your finger slid a bit early/late off the buttons/keys of your controller/keyboard:Conclusion: if you have a fighting joystick I'd says this is 100% worth picking up or if you're a keyboard/controller god. If you're an average controller/keyboard gaming warrior with 70%+ gaming mechanics... you will feel your limits... if you have the will to face that failure time and time again and not get frustrated by your lack of precision/accuracy due to your tool... I'd say with 68% confidence that this game might be for you - If you end up really liking this game you'll probably want to buy a joystick(I'm definitely feeling my limits, mechanical/precision issues be damn3d). :(* If you love fighting games and have never played a Marvel Vs Capcom game, this game is a must buy/try.* If you like games with deep depth or love to experiment, this game is for you.* If you never played a fighting game ever, this is a perfect place to start.* If you're  a casual gamer I'd say it's worth a shot!!!!*!!!! If you don't like challenging games or complain (on reviews) about balance issues, this game may not be for you at the current time of this review - I mean no offense and am not tying to turn people off to this game. These games are very fun it's just that MVC2... a new player is like a baby lamb walking into a forest of wolves unless you get matched up with another baby lamb consider yourself fresh meat ;)This is my first review of a game... I probably should've kept it shorter -_-... I hope this helped in some way, remember to take breaks, take care :)

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: you get to beat up superheroes and animeCons: you can only do it using superheroes and animeIn all seriousness, this collection of games is deeply awesome, and good on Marvel and Capcom for rereleasing them with some nice tweaks and updates to make them more enjoyable than ever.Pros: + MVC2 alone is worth the price, one of the best fighting games of all time+ 7 great games for $7.14 each, a bargain no matter which way you slice it+ Features that make it friendly to casual players and newcomers+ X-Men and Fantastic 4 characters available thanks to no stupid Fox Embargo+ Better than UMVC3 (which is still really good) and MVCI (which is just okay)+ Entire MVC series now available on Steam+ Nice nostalgic 90's games+ No microtransactions or DLC+ The Punisher beat em up included+ So many fun potential teamups you can put together in the crossover games+ Each game has a good amount of fun characters you can use and play through as+ Rewards short play times+ Insane replay valueCons:- Would've been nice to include Capcom's Marvel SNES beat em up games (X-Men Mutant Apocalypse and Marvel Super Heroes War of the Gems, but this is technically an arcade collection, and the better/best Marvel/Capcom collaborations are still otherwise all here)- Spider-Man and X-Men arcade beat em ups would be cool too but those weren't made by Capcom so can't fault them there- Would've been nice if they maybe updated MVC2 so you could use characters who were omitted from the previous games (Cyber Akuma, etc.) but this is an extremely small and petty gripe when MVC2 is already a fantastic game with an insanely big and awesome roster- Having a hard time thinking of any other cons, honestly, there's so much to love here!Hoping Capcom will learn from the success of rereleasing these games, if the Capcom Fighting Collection 2 for 2025 is any indication hopefully they're listening. At least MVC2 has Mega Man, Roll, Tron Bonne and Servbot which is close enough for now I guess)Can't miss this, worth it at full price, been a long time coming and so worth the wait. The few cons there are being so negligible that they pale in comparison to the pros, this is easily a 10/10.IT'S MAHVEL BAYBEE!

_childDocuments_.review: Excluding The Punisher which is already a strong positive due its lack of previous ports but not being a fighting game, if you expect any of these games to have some sense of balance, tough luck. Prepare to get bodied online with infinites, massive differences between tiers, and a roaming Justin Wong at all times.HOWEVER, these games were the foundation for many current fighting games and others yet to come. Flashy attacks, vibrant stages, a lot of hype matches, and the list goes on about this legendary group of Marvel games. I am speaking to those who never experienced the 90s era when these games came out, as despite their massive flaws compared to overbalanced current games in the genre, the fun factor barely fades away once you get the hang of it. We are talking of that kind of game that if you can win matches with the worst characters, you deserve a crown king/queen.Obviously the latter might vary not only of the player, but the game itself. Children of the Atom is the slowest and more experimental design wise, while MvC2 is absolute chaos with everything going on screen. MvC1 might be the middle ground and a good starting point for newcomers on the other hand, as solidified most of the franchise's mechanics but you don't have to worry much about insane power tiers.To be honest, this compilation and others by Capcom is about the legacy of this series. The gallery alone is a huge proof about it, showing development files and sketches on an INSANE resolution. I recommend it to just play it for fun and go with a casual mindset. However try to do so online, as despite the roaming players that experienced these games for decades is way more entertainment than to just face the CPU, since depending of the game the AI can be either a boredom turtling stall like in MvC2, or read inputs and pull some BS like in COTA.In summary, if you are expecting some highly competitive fighting game, is a yes and a no. It is competitive even if one or two characters dominate their respective games, but requires a lot of practice the veterans are used to for years. But if all you want is some the greatest capcom games in your library to have a blast with friends, getting bodied by Maximillian and others, and learn a few basic infinites, then is a strong recommendation if you grew up with these games or not.

_childDocuments_.review: This is superb. Worth every penny. These games are the best of the 90's arcades in my opinion, which makes them some of the greatest of all time, and not just on a relativity scale, I'm talking in terms of timeless raw ingenuity in gameplay mechanics. Hard to believe now but SF was massively more popular than Marvel in the early 90s, and these mid to late 90s follow-on collabs were Marvel getting a foot in the door in the arcade game player vs player fighting scene that Capcom created, whilst Capcom advanced the complexity of 2D fighting games at the same time. But even SF was on the way out at the time to new 3D arcade machines like Virtua Fighter, and all those other early 3D fighters that are absolutely dreadful and unplayable by today's standards. So with the growth of home consoles and the new 3D arcade era kicking in, these games largely went by the wayside in the arcades for most; people were aware of them, but those that did still visit the arcades were putting their money into Daytona USA and Virtua FIghter and the like instead. And yet in retrospect, it's these games that remain solid in terms of both playablity and graphics, and stand out from the 90's. They still look, play, and sound amazing. They really are quite brilliant. If there's one complaint .... these are retro 90's arcade games, there really should be a 4/3 or 5/4 border-less mode, for those with monitors of those resolutions—something so little from from Capcom, really could add so much for fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this collection for a bit. I've always avoided emulation so I've never really gotten to experience classic Marvel Vs. Capcom.So to REVIEW the game, or should I say games. Marvel vs. Capcom Fighting Collection is a great collection! These aren't necessarily the best versions of each game, but the FGC (Fighting Game Community) has finally been granted legal access to these games to play on modern hardware. I've played a number of fighting game collections mostly for Capcom but a few SNK ones. The key to a good collection is: offering games that have been "gone", quality emulations, and bonus features. The MvC Fighting Collection nails all of these qualities very well.So the games being offered are quite comprehensive. It's every single Marvel game produced by Capcom from X-Men: Children of the Atom to Marvel vs. Capcom 2: New Age of Heroes, not to mention The Punisher beat em' up. I want to be in-depth with my somewhat casual experiences with these games. I'm not a pro, I primarily play Street Fighter games. Let's go in order.THE PUNISHERThis game was fun, a surprising violent beat em' up similar to Final Fight with its gameplay and more. You play as/or with The Punisher or Classic Nick Fury. You beat up goons as they come your way. You have a variety of weapons to wield, from simple melee weapons like knives and bats, to firearms like pistols and assault rifles.This game isn't too long, but it was enjoyable. I would recommend playing through it if you at least enjoy beat em' ups a little bit. 7 out of 10.X-MEN: CHILDREN OF THE ATOMThis game really makes you feel like a mutant. This game is volatile, a lot like the other titles in this collection. Each playable character has a really unique feel through their normals and their specials. I'd argue that Cyclops and Psylocke are the most simple to use, but they each still feel very distinct. For my first arcade playthrough I used Psylocke because of her agility and easy to use kit. Despite all my praises for this title, it definitely feels very unbalanced. This game is fun, but sometimes it felt impossible to beat without abusing the save states. 6 out of 10. I don't really have to return to this title.MARVEL SUPER HEROESThis is my least favorite of the titles in this collection, but I still think that it's a unique game that you should play. This game has the smallest roster other than X-Men: Children of the Atom, though it does reuse X-Men: Wolverine, Psylocke, Magneto, and Juggernaut. This game has the unique gimmick of Infinity Stones. Collect and use each stone to grant your character a unique buff. It's a mad scramble to hold on to the Easter eggs! I played as Spider-Man for this one and it was okay. The infinity stones were jank to use. I appreciate the new editions in this game like Captain America, Iron-Man and Spider-Man, but I am disappointed with the gameplay itself. 4 out of 10, surely I could get good, but I have other titles in this collection to get good at.X-MEN VS. STREET FIGHTERFinally a team game, and the first crossover in the collection chronologically! This should really be called X-Men vs. Street Fighter Alpha, good thing I like Alpha. I enjoyed this title, the team up supers were really fun to pull off. For this arcade route, I played as Charlie Nash and Rogue. I'm very happy with the roster for this one, even though I think Charlie is an odd choice, I still think he's pretty cool. Rogue is definitely the stand out character for me, her ability to "Kirby" every characters' abilities is well implemented. The final boss, Apocalypse, was fine. He gets reused in the next title but he's a passable boss. I enjoyed this game, but I think I'd probably play the main MvC titles over this one and the next one. 7 out of 10.MARVEL SUPER HEROES VS. STREET FIGHTERA lot of the game feels like the previous game. Which is a good thing. The roster to this title is a little weird. We're reusing some characters from X-Men and Marvel Super Heroes but somehow we got weirdos like Shuma Gorath and Black Heart returning. Why didn't we get Iron Man back, but we got Omega Red?I played as Wolverine and Sakura for my first playthrough of the arcade. This game is literally the same as X-Men Vs. Street Fighter when it comes down to the gameplay. Nothing from the original Marvel Super Heroes game returns other than the characters. The one new edition is after Apocalypse, we fight... CYBER AKUMA! This game still gets a 6 out of.... wait, we got Norimaro back also? Alright it's a 7 out of 10.MARVEL VS. CAPCOM: CLASH OF SUPER HEROESThis was the game I played first in the series back in 2012. Getting to play this game was magical. This time I decided to run Gambit and Strider, cool guys team. This game and the next have the same celebratory vibe as each other. Let's celebrate the history of our respective franchises. In this title, we have a somewhat small feeling roster, but our cast has grown past just Street Fighter and into the other Capcom franchises. We got Morrigan from Darkstalkers, Jin from Cyberbots, Captain Commando from Captain Commando, Mega Man and Roll from Mega Man, and Strider Hiryu from Strider! This game feels great. The cool thing about this game is the assist characters that you can summon. We get characters from previous Marvel titles as well as obscure Capcom characters that get new sprites! The final boss, Onslaught, was difficult so I used save states. 8 out of 10. I would actually come back to play this for nostalgia.MARVEL VS. CAPCOM 2: NEW AGE OF HEROESOh, MVC2. How much I've heard about you.... Mahvel 2 is the game of all time. The game I want to learn and get better at. With a staggering 56 character roster, we get essentially every playable character into this game. Sorry Norimaro! This game definitely has a distinct vibe to it compared to the other titles. The soundtrack and art of this title are on another level. I actually played this title first when booting up the collection, and I still think it's my favorite. My first team consisted of Captain America, Ryu, and Star Gladiator main character, Hayato. My second team consisted of Ruby Heart, Psylocke, and Spiral. This title plays the most different compared to the others. With only four attack buttons we're given two buttons just for assists. Though, my favorite thing about this game is the diverse roster, like I said, everyone basically returns plus some new editions, notable on Marvel's side are Cable, Marrow, and... that's it. For Capcom, it's Jill from Resident Evil,  Darkstalkers B.B. Hood and Anakaris, and the new "original characters" they made for this game. Ruby Heart is really cool and stoic, Son Son is a neat reference to a classic title, and Amingo is Amingo, we love him and the others. The boss is completely original to this game... and it was a little disappointing? Abyss is fine. Hard but manageable. For this game it's a 10 out of 10 for vibes, but 9 out of 10 for actual gameplay.MARVEL VS. CAPCOM FIGHTING COLLECTIONThis is a great collection with a variety of features and content to browse. The museum is pretty great, I wish we got even more art, but this is enough to satisfy my collector's appetite. I haven't played every games' online, but I did play some casual matches of MVC1 and MVC2 and it's amazing connection wise. Fun-wise, I lost every game. Goes to show how much experience with CPUs does towards actual wins. I want to get better, but I know I'll be left in the dust unless I start investing time into this game which is time I might not always have, I've got Street Fighter 6 to grind. I love fighting games, and I'm very happy to have finally gotten to play one of the greatest. This collection is a 9 out of 10! Quick aside, I wrote like 4 whole pages worth of review. I had trouble actually uploading the review so this is chopped down. Bro, I spent like 2 hours on this lol.

They also added a bit of QoL like 'easy secret character selection', which essentially just means all the secret character codes are automatically active; you can toggle it off if it bothers you. There's also one beat-em-up in the collection with the Punisher.These are mostly still fun games (♥♥♥♥ boss Magneto in the first X-Men game though), though the price point is at quite a premium; no doubt because of Disney's cut.  Personally I kind of regret paying full price at launch for this, I'd wait for at least a moderate discount.

Fighting games struggle to sell copies and maintain a playerbase on pc so I'm hoping that in the future crossplay gets patched in, possibly when Xbox gets this game and Fighting Collection 2. I spent hours playing casual matches, and the nostalgia hit hard, reminding me of the countless hours I spent with these games growing up. Now, as an adult, I can still say: this game is WOW. It’s fun, competitive, and timeless.Capcom, you knocked it out of the park with this one. In my eyes, you’re legends. The vibrant colors brought me right back to the early '90s, and I hope this collection draws in a lot of new players to the FGC (Fighting Game Community). This is a game that’ll continue to impress for years to come.

name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami
detailed_description: REVIEWS "Personally, I'd recommend Duck Detective: The Secret Salami . There's a button that makes you quack." - Bloomberg, Jason Schreier "The Duck Detective may crave bread, but I crave more Duck Detective!" - GameLuster, Kate Mitchell Jewett "In concept and execution, this game is an absolute delight ." - GAMES hub, Leah J. Williams About the Game Aggretsuko meets Return of the Obra Dinn in Duck Detective, a cozy mystery game about a down-on-his-luck duck searching for answers in a sinister sausage-based conspiracy. Join the Duck Detective on his latest, greatest case: Inspect and interview suspects to learn their hidden secrets, then use the information you’ve gathered (plus your own de-duck-tive reasoning) to locate the suspect and bust the case wide open! A 2-3 hour long mystery game! Interview suspects, fill in the blanks and crack the case! Fully voice-acted! Throw bread to the fine beak of lady justice! Judge everyone on first impressions, just by looking at them really, really hard! Get them to admit things by staring! Do ducks blink? You don’t.

_childDocuments_.review: "I've QUACKED the case!"To get the obvious out of the way, Duck Detective is a great little game and well worth its full asking price.In the game you take on the role of the eponymous Duck Detective, hired on to uncover the mystery of a stolen lunch while studying your surroundings and the colourful characters that inhabit the game's office environment. The premise is a relatively simple, but manages to get a ton of value out of that simplicity by mixing just the right amount of hearty humour with an excellently voiced protagonist that has a bit of seriousness mixed into his lines. All in all the game's audiovisual presentation is great, though the lack of character animation that has them looking like cardboard cutouts does add up over time. Oh, and there is a dedicated quack button. It makes you go quack! That's immediately a bonus point in the gameplay category right there!As for the gameplay, the core of the game consists of looking at objects, chatting to people and collecting the keywords that allow you to piece together relatively simple fill-the-blank sentences that add up to form our detective's reasoning, which allows the game to move onto its next scene. I was a bit slow and brute forced a few words here and there, but for the vast majority of the puzzles it's a perfectly reasonable chain of logic and association that lets you piece together the information you need.Duck Detective is a great game about ducks, salami and secrets and I heartily recommend it! Here's to hoping we get a sequel involving a certain sidekick character, too!Playtime: 2 hours (A single full playthrough)Ratings (1-10)Visual: 8Audio: 10Story: 10Gameplay: 10Overall: 9

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Definitely buy and play, if you understand English, like investigative games, and have a sense of humor.It's been a long time since I've enjoyed a Steam game so much. For one thing, it's cheap, at just €10. The game is fairly short; I finished it in 2.5 hours, after a bit of a struggle and doing all the achievements (they're all done automatically as you progress, except for one) and taking the time to read carefully.The strong points are undeniably the story, the characters and the acting. A perfect blend of talented writing and dubbing. You really get caught up in the case and the suspects. Unfortunately, it's too short, but what a pleasure to listen to the voices of Sophie, Laura, Margarette, Freddy and the Duck Detective.Finally, the music! Buy the OST on Steam with the game, you won't regret it! If you like the typical jazz of noir series, you're in for a treat! It can get a bit tiresome after a couple of hours, but it's still very beautiful and a great addition to a chill playlist for studying or working.The game is therefore very short on playing time. The gameplay is also very simple. You'll be moving around three rooms. The game can be played with the mouse alone, without even needing the keyboard.If I had to point out any shortcomings, it would be that far too often, when you want to talk to a character, you click on the wrong button. Mouse movement is fine, but could still be improved. Above all, the translation: the fact that the game is only available in English will put off many people for a game based essentially on reading and comprehension. Even me, who has an excellent level of English (C1, twenty years' experience), was taken in by certain turns of phrase that made me waste time. This game deserves to have translations as soon as possible. Note that I didn't encounter any bugs.

Sure everything made sense and was logical in the end, still I feel I had less trouble deducting things in Case of the Golden Idol for example.But maybe this is just me being blind and/or stupid.However, the setting, the story, the art design, the voice acting, the soundtrack.. everything else in this game is on point and I really enjoyed it.So I am hoping for a sequel or at least a gameplay wise similar game from Happy Broccoli Games!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Of course as you can see, the game is very cute and has fantastic voice acting! But I was also positively surprised by the puzzle solving, it was really fun! Collecting key words to fill out a form is a solid approach, and the tips the game gives you don't give too much away. It's more a "maybe think about x again" type of deal.I really really hope we get more Duck Detective games in the future, this was a really good foundation!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: I can't help but be disappointed. I enjoyed the game, I really did. But just one case that takes around 2 hours to solve? Even if it's relatively cheap I kind of expected more than just 2 hours of fun. The sudden end spoiled the entire experience for me and now instead of recalling that I enjoyed the game I actually regret spending money on it :(
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little cozy gem with salami, bread, dedicated quack button and thick atmosphere.Can't say that puzzles were as smooth as they should (especially Deducktion phase is very unintuitive at places despite you knowing the right answer), but it's no biggie. The only downside is that it shorter than some bus rides, but at least it's not overstaying it's welcome.Bread out of 10, will quack again.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Such a good game!The art style is amazing, the moody soundtrack and voice acting is SO good! Puzzles were not too challenging, but some were pretty tricky.I really hope there will be either a DLC with another case or a separate game, I really want to follow our dear Duck Detective in more adventures! This has to become a game series!P.S. I'm about to buy the soundtrack too. Just SO good.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun and very short game that I absolutely want more of ASAP. The music was pitch-perfect, the characters were unique, and for a few hours I could rack my fellow duck brain in solving a very silly and well-thought out puzzle of a case.Oh and, while it's a short game, the thing is fully-voiced acted, featuring modern VA gem Sean Chiplock as the Ducktective and THE BDG Brian David Gilbert as Frederson. The devs clearly know quality, buy their game now.Whether it's a sequel game, or just some more individual cases released now and then, I want more.There's a deduckated Quack Button.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: While relatively short (mainly based on how fast you can solve the deducktions), the game manages to be a fun experience with cute characters, clever writing, great voice acting, and boasting a technical depth not often found in puzzle games. I'd recommend it even with its full price tag, as a nice brain teaser for people of all ages.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: The game is short but fun. Worth it for the price -- the puzzles require you to pay attention but aren't in the "how were you supposed to know that?!?" range. I haven't tried replaying it yet... there aren't many decision points, so barring coming back to it after a few months I doubt the replayability is all that high.But it isn't much money -- and it left me most certainly wanting more. More cases, more sequels --  As such, I have to recommend it. If you're looking for quick, casual fun and just a game to duck into, this game is all it is quacked up to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Saw it advertised.  Figured I would give it a try since it was only $9.99 and had a positive rating.  Two hours later, I can say it was cute but not for me.  A noir detective send up, The Duck Detective allowed for little actual mystery solving as the majority of the work is done through a mad-libs style interface where you fill in the major happenings in the story.  It is a simple little detective story with forgettable characters, tropes galore, and plenty of frustrating moments of trying to get all of your clue phrases from people so that you can solve the story.  While it did have some cute moments of animal humor, the vast majority of the game was repetitive and unrewarding.  I found myself committing to the slog so that I could just get it over with.  There were no real moments where I was glad I played the game aside from the first five minutes when I found out that you could make titular Duck Detective quack, he had an addiction to bread, and had a deep voice that made me chuckle at first.  If you are really bored, this might be fun for you but if you are looking for a really great detective romp, look elsewhere.  The best part of the game was the Paper Mario style art design that allowed for a whimsical take on a gritty noir mystery.  While it wasn't for me, it might be something that others enjoy.
