_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: This game is short and I completed it in about 3 hours. Just because it is short does not mean it is a bad game!The voice acting, music and graphics were all very lovely. The mad lib style of filling in the clues was a lot of fun. I thought the story was a fun silly cozy adventure and would love to do more cases with the Duck Detective.I highly suggest you pick up this this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: We all need our bread, in one way or another.Adorable characters including our hard-quacking duck detective. Figuring out the clues for his deducktions for a story that was not as straightforward as it seemed - tho lunch stealing is indeed a heinous crime by itself. Great ost was perfect for that noir feel. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective is an adorable detective game that absolutely oozes with charm. The mechanics of figuring out a case are fun, although they can sometimes devolve into trial and error.My only major complaint is that this game can be over far too quickly — I beat it in just under 2 hours. You should expect to spend 1.5–4 hours on a single playthrough depending on how quickly you can solve the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- I like the art! The Paper Mario-style 2d characters in the 3d environment work well- Lots of spoken dialogue with good voice acting.- I liked the magnifying glass examinations, uncovering little details on each character was fun.Cons:- It's really short. I unlocked all achievements and finished the game in 2 hours. And there's little reason to replay it, as you've likely exhausted all the dialogue when trying to find more words for the de-duck-tions.- A bit too easy for my liking. It tells you exactly how many things to find on each person. All the puzzles are fill-in-the-blanks from a small list of choices. I think if there was a bit more content, it would be an easy recommendation. As it is, I had fun playing it, but I wouldn't recommend the game to others.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Overall really fun game and I look forward to future Duck Detective adventures! Like the other reviews it is a bit short but the story wrapped up well. The colors were fun and vibrant and the range of characters were relatable to an office environment. Also the innuendos of the bread made me laugh more than I probably should. I'd recommend this game to other friends even if it only took about 2ish hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective is what I usually call a perfect game. It picked one concept and properly exectuted it : nothing more, nothing less.Every aspects of the game work together to offer this engaging story. The music, the characters, the dialog, the art, the humor, you can feel that everything was thoughtfully made.Yes the game is short and some solutions are a bit far-feteched, however I enjoyed my time tremendously and I do hope we get more investigations in the future !
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game, very polished and fully voice acted with cute art! Fun story and nice deducktions. It felt a bit short however, but it's also not an expensive game so it's worth it in my opinion. 8,77€ for about 2.5hours of gameplay is good enough I suppose. Especially when that gameplay is tight. Hope they release more, like another case or so!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game has charm with it's art style and fitting music, but that's about all I have nice to say about it.I get it, fun little indie game and what not, but I just couldn't bring myself to complete it.  The characters are flat and unlikeable, the voice acting in this game is awful.  It sounds so overly cartoony like and exaggerated on top of being too loud sometimes even when I turned it down.  It's like they shifted between normal talking voices and yelling.  The gameplay doesn't feel very detective like.  Comparing to ace attorney, you can search clues and find out information without having to go through every dialog prompt and investigating every bit of detail, so when it comes time to prove the truth, it feels rewarding because you can't just place everything in and hope it works if you are missing a detail or two.  Everyone's name I couldn't figure out, I just placed in random ones until it worked.  I don't want to bash what I am sure was a fun project for this developer.  I paid for this and could easily refund it, but I won't out of respect for that.  But I also think it needs criticism and it's charm of being a cute game is not enough for me
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Who could've thought finding out who stole someone's lunch could lead to such a thrilling case. The characters play their parts well, the music and voice acting are sensational, and the clues make playing detective rewarding for being inquisitive and almost nosy. Eagerly looking forward to a sequel case for our daring Duck detective!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Breezy and quick little detective game! This is only a single case, but it's fairly meaty and interesting despite the humorously low stakes. You'll need to use a good amount of logic and intuition--it'll often seem like you don't have enough information, and that's when the game will expect you to make some deducktive leaps. Easily beatable in a day, so highly recommended for a fun thinky game.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute game! 10/10 voice acting. So... Why is it a thumbs down?Downsides? It's short. Finished the whole game and all achievements in about an hour. With the given price it's okay, although, without the sale I'm not sure I would buy it given it's current content. The puzzles were very linear and the plot twist was fun, but odd. It would be much better if they added a bit more story and content but right now, given the price compared to game duration, I'd wait for it to go on sale (40%) or for a content update that adds more cases.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: this game is short. I am posting this right after getting 100% so yeah only about 2.3 hours and I took breaks.But otherwise this is a pretty great game. They are serious about the duck-tective being hard boiled, I had thought this would be a fun game for kids and while it is pretty pg, it would probably not be very fun, as the humor is very much playing to an adult audience. The de-duck-tions are pretty precise and tricky, and require a good bit of actual problem solving (at least on hard mode). Biggest complaint: a lot of the clues are just left where you found them in the office, so you have to walk all the way back to them to look at them again, which just seems tedious. There is also no fast travel between rooms.Best feature: every line that I can remember was voice acted and done well by good voices! I am someone for whom audio will sell a game faster than good graphics, but this has both amazing audio and good ascetics!Over all: good game which play's its premises straight.P.S. Well play devs on the variable ending! That was a remarkably cool feature!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: I have been eyeing this game since the minute I saw it, so I was so excited when it was released. This game exceeded my expectations. The story line, graphics, and music were all 10/10. I played this game on Stream and all my chatters had such positive things to say about the game! The jazz music really sets the tone for duck mysteries to be solved. I like how the developers inserted different ways to play the game. You can have it on story-mode or play with a bit of a challenge. The game definitely made you think and look at every detail! This game was so well thought out and developed. Highly Highly recommend!!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: A fully voiced acted adorable point and click game. The fill in the blank mechanic is new for me and it's effective as a narrative helper as well. I also love the magnifying glass use in observing the characters. Overall its a great cute deducktive point and click game that is just the right length. Hoping for sequels, need the duck to get over that bread addiction.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet little detective game. The story and dialogue were legitimately funny, and there were only a couple moments where we got genuinely stuck. My daughter and I played through it in a morning and we're really hoping there are more cases made eventually! And the duck "facts" were a joy every time.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: A very smooth and enjoyable experience, though it's not exactly challenging.It's a detective duck, don't expect it to be much more than that. I think this might be a great detective game for the whole family though, it looks and sounds lovely, and there are plenty of hints if you need them.obligatory gravity falls reference
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game with distinct art style and very clean graphics. But for $10, it is extremely short and it's a little unclear how some of the deductions were supposed to function. I deduced some things that were important, for instance, but that didn't have their own deduction (such as the motives of the sheep), while the larger deductions could sometimes be made without all of the information necessary because of a simple matter of wordplay guesswork. Well polished esthetically and game function wise, but I think the bridge between the story and the series of most reasonable deductions to make upon finding out certain pieces of information needs some work particularly for the price and considering there was only one case to solve in the entire thing. Definitely recommend if you just want somethig cute to kill a couple hours with, but maybe on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: You are a duck ducktective. A deep-voiced, down-on-his-luck, feathered-fella (with a crippling bread adducktion) who is trying to make a living quacking cases. You go about it methoduckally, gathering clues by conduckting interviews and observing people and objects. You then complete your deducktions in your notebook by filling in the missing words with the correct clues. While the story is surprisingly unpreducktable, you don't have to be a valeducktorian from Duckmouth College to solve the mystery. The game induckates when you've gotten something wrong, but you won't have too much of a problem... unless you happen to be me and you happen to brute-force the deducktions like an uneduckated thug. One thing though, the game does feel shallow as a pond. But if you're searching for a short yet pleasantly riduckulous experience, this game fits the bill perfectly. I must also mention that there is a deduckated "quack" button. So waddle you waiting for? More duck puns perhaps? I think I've made my case.P.S. If you're thinking, "What the duck did I just read?!" I respectfully suggest consulting a ducktionary.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: I Quacked the CasE!!!! I can finally go home and eat that sweet sweet... succulent bread;; *shivers in delight*Honestly, this is one of those amazing shorter games that is just a pleasure to play through and through. Voice acting is really really good, top quality stuff, characters are super cute, art is very stylistic and pleasant, and the detective work (altho super easy at first, and you can guess most of the stuff, sadly) is actually really nicely done, and if you can put the whole case together on your own without guessing, it feels amazing.10/10, would be a bread addict again.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the only ones I feel genuinely deserves a review. The characters are charming, the mechanics are amazing, and it is so satisfying to solve all the mysteries. I played through this in 2 hours, and my only gripe is that there isn't more to play! seriously, if you have a free afternoon and a few bucks to spend, this is absolutely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: This does have good voice acting (but in this day in age that's an industry standard), but the game lacks much animation or expression in the characters as aside from 1 character all of them use the same still image in the whole game. The mystery is pretty solid and will take some time to think through everything, but overall it's an okay game. Side note I don't see the point of who u can choose to arrest as it barely affects the ending at all. In my case I booked everyone involved in the crime
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely fantastic, simple, and short detective game. I played co-operatively with my 7-year old daughter and we had a blast. The puzzles were complex enough for me to think but simple enough for her to contribute to the solutions. The writing is whimsical, atmospheric, and surprisingly complex for a shorter game. The voice acting is incredible, especially a certain reptilian creature.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun way to spend a couple hours. The voice acting was great and the fill in the blank style "deducktions" were fun. Reminds me a bit of the Detective Grimoire series. I do wish that we had one more clue for the finale so it wouldn't quite feel like such a leap of logic, but the puzzle is by no means unsolvable.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: It was a very cute game with a ton of charm and incredible voice acting. The art is very nice and to be honest I only got the game as it made me think of Duck Detective from the cartoon Gravity Falls. However, there are some cons worth mentioning. When you play the game you have to get every single piece of spoken information from every npc to get clues for your ducktection and if you don't have every single one you can't solve the ducktection you are working on even though you technically have the ones that you need. This is something that I personally find to be very annoying since I got stuck even though I had put in the right answer only to then go interview one of the npcs about a item I had in my inventory just to get a word I wouldn't even have to use. The second con is that I am disappointed with how short the game is. I hope they release a follow up that is longer than this game as I genuinely found this to be very frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10This game is unique and fun, filled with some quirky characters with entertaining voice actors. The art style kind of resembles Paper Mario, and the protagonist is a comical take on the noir detective genre. The mysteries were enjoyable and it makes you feel smart when you piece information together. The overall premise is humorous and it didn't feel like a drag to play through this game to the end.The problem I have with this game is its length. I don't mind a short game, I actually love them now since most games require 80+ hours from me to complete. A game that's short and sweet is awesome, but this game was so short it kind of left me wanting more. This whole game feels like the tutorial for something bigger. I think realistically a Duck Detective game has the potential to be about 6-8 hours without outstaying its welcome. It was kind of a bummer that the entire game takes place in the same location focusing on just one small crime. Had this just been the intro section and then you move on to other areas or other mysteries, I think this would be a real winner.Still, for $10, it's a pretty good deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much, from the story to the characters, and especially the voice acting. The voice acting in this game is magnificent, especially Duck Detective. I loved all of his lines and how they were delivered. My only gripe is that it is so short. I really hope there will be a sequel one day with a longer story. I can still wholeheartedly recommend this game to everyone. You can really tell how much love went into this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective game feels so alive with such exceptional voice acting. There were moments where i literally gasped at the intensity in the performances.The design is simple yet stunning. The game's noir style perfectly sets the tone for a feathered mystery.I am hoping for a sequal. Don't want this duck to hang up his hat and coat, he should have more mysteries to solve!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliantly written story of lies, liaisons and lunch. The investigation system underpinning the story is really well implemented, but it's the story, acting and vibes of Duck Detective that carry it into the realm of something special. Fingers crossed for another chapter in the Duck Detective's tale soon!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: I fell for the hype but really once you get beyond the cute aesthetic, it's an extremely basic game with almost no deducktion required, very shallow ""puzzles"" and a quite tedious system for discovering new words to put in your journal (speak to everyone, fill out your journal, speak to everyone again, repeat) - It's also super short, I expected more than one case to solve to be honest, and some more backstory on our duck protagonist. I don't really see this game being worth more than 5 bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, hilarious af, and with an epic mystery... at least for the Eastern states bus network! The delivery of its story is sometimes messy, mixing up real clues, with false clues, with just unintended noise... which can create moments where the de-duck-tion system must be "bruteforced" to get to a conclusion, often, on mysteries you had not even considered.Messy but charming, I can't wait for the next crumb of Duck Detective's epic quest!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of my favourite detective games!It's got that big thread that you think that you are following and you think to yourself "oh, this is so easy... XYZ is the culprit. Why can't I just end the game now?" until there's a small plot twist that makes you think "oh, wait, no! XYZ isn't the baddie! ABC is the one! Ok now I can end the game" - until the same happens again shortly after.It's cute, it's funny and the devs definitely knew what they were doing and they did it really well.This makes me really excitied for a Duck Detective 2 or whatever the next game from HBG will be.Also in terms of time: around 2 to 3 hours for this type of game is absolutely fine because it's basically meant to be played in one sitting. I'd rather have a good story that's neatly ended in a short time, than a 20 hour detective game where I can't even remember what I set out to do in the first place, after the third session.Also shoutout to the VAs! Y'all did an amazing job. I personally loved Lizzie Freeman (or Yanfei from Genshin Impact) and Annika Maar (who was also the director for the game) with their respective roles.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Quacktacular Fun!Got this game for my birthday (shoutout to Henrik) and I’m totally quackers for it! The mystery of the secret salami had me hooked from the start. The dialogue is full of puns that will make you quack up, and the puzzles are egg-citingly clever. Controls can be a bit webbed, but once you get the hang of it, you'll be gliding through the game like a duck on water. If you're looking for a feather-raising good time, this game is a real quackquisition!P:S. Quackle up detectives! The mystery won’t crack itself.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on its release on a whim and it was definitely a great game choice! The overworld reminds me of Paper Mario and all of the characters are unique and charming. I loved getting to solve the mystery and observe things about people in this office job. I did struggle a bit with some of the Deducktions but I feel like they weren't too difficult overall. It's a very fun and easy to play game, and I definitely enjoyed my time playing it!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: For 10 bucks a fun, funny fully voice acted game with at least somewhat decent puzzles. Grab it, if not now, on sale.But its not a very deep experience, it is 1 case (which about 3? interwoven mysteries). And say compared to Phoenix Wright I wouldn't say its the same as a case from that game, more like 1 of the interludes between court room scenes. But its still a fun tight experience that obviously knew what it wanted to be and didn't waste my time with a bunch of unnessacary fluff. The only thing I'm unsure of, is if there is a sequel in the future would I want it. I think as much as I enjoyed this taster, it would have to be a fully meal, one where we got to know our leading duck more that had more of a interwoven world rather then this isolated set piece.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting detective game. Short and sweet, basically a movie-length (perfect for completing in a single seating). The deducktions are fun to figure out, with enough misdirections thrown around that a few solutions seem plausible at times. Loving the narrow scope, not forcing you to run around multiple locations and randomly try stuff (the most tiring part of a classic Point and Click game).The story is cute and fun, loved the characters (especially our bread-addicted protagonist), done in a classic noire style. Priced very fairly, does not overstay it's welcome or get boring. Plays smoothly with a very unique art style ("2d" characters moving about a 3d environment),  works great with a controller. Absolutely recommended if you are looking for a fun brain teaser.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective: The Secret SalamiA fun case to crack! Identify the employees, chat them up for clues, and uncover key words to solve the mad-libs-style mysteries in your detective journal. The game’s charming visuals and quirky humor make every moment delightful. The plot thickens! Highly recommend! Thank you for this game! > the only negative is the game is too short! I want more! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: I recently played this game and loved several aspects of it. The music, voice acting and illustrations were charming. The characters had this "paper feel" that reminded me of Paper Mario (nostalgia hit me hard), and some clues were challenging to solve.However, I can't recommend the game because of how short it is. There's only one case in the entirety of the game to solve. There's no character development and no deep connection with any of the characters. It's not that I need those things, but considering I’ve played more complete games on this platform for the same price, this one left me feeling a bit underwhelmed.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective was some of the best money I've spent on a game! I enjoyed the immensely, and you should just buy it too. The animation is so cute, and the duck facts for the loading screen are so funny. The story is genuinely well-written, and the voice acting throughout is great! If there was ever DLC for this, I'd buy it in a heartbeat.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't want to come off saying that Duck Detective is a bad game. The art style and visuals are great, the audio and voice acting are solid, and the mechanics behind the mystery gameplay are engaging.  And the low price point certainly lines up with the short play time.  But seeing that this is currently rated as Overwhelmingly Positive, I can't really bring myself to say that I recommend it.The title character, Duck Detective, is woefully underutilized.  On paper, it is such a great character concept, with a catchy name and a striking visual design.  But there is very little relevance to the Duck part of the character.  I can only name three things: There is a dedicated Quack button, a core detective mechanic is a pun in which you make DeDUCKtions, and the character has a drug-like addiction to bread.  All of these are experienced within the first few minutes of the game.  For the rest of the game, nothing about being a duck is relevant, not mechanically, not narratively, not even for comic relief.  This game could have been Dog Detective or even Human Detective, and it would have been a nearly identical experience.  None of the other animal characters have any relevant animal quirks either.  For a game that screams "You are a DUCK!", they really don't seem to embrace that detail.While the core mystery solving mechanics are enjoyable, a lot of the execution doesn't really come together.  There were a number of moments throughout the game where I felt like I had all of the information available to me, but I still didn't understand what DeDUCKtion the game wanted me to come to.  Because there's no penalty for getting it wrong, and you are just immediately informed when it is correct, there's incentive to just keep guessing until you stumble into the right answer.  Even after seeing what some of the DeDUCKtions were meant to be, I still didn't understand how you were supposed to come to that conclusion.  The game clearly marks everything you can investigate, so I feel confident that I didn't just miss something.  It would have been much more satisfying and enjoyable if the details of the case had come together more cohesively, instead of just arbitrarily coming up with conclusions that seemed entirely out of left field.Those two major elements left me unsatisfied with the Duck Detective experience.  If $10 is no object and you want to see the game with the cute duck, by all means, go for it.  But if you were hoping for a genuinely great duck-centric mystery solving game, then maybe just keep your fingers crossed for the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little detective game.  Talk to the suspects, investigate the scene, put everything together and solve the case.It's fun.  As you gather clues, you pick out words from people's statements and fit them into the paragraph at the end of the chapter to describe the action and put the story together.  And it finishes up with you gathering everyone together in one place to lay it all out in front of them, as all the best detective stories do.The art style is very cute, the voice acting is first rate and the puzzles are mostly fun.  There's a lot of humour and the characters are enjoyable (Laura is awesome!)  The only drawback, I'd say, is the last couple of deducktions (Yes, that's how it's spelt) where the word template is sufficiently complicated that it's hard to know exactly what the game wants you to say.  There seemed to be a few alternative answers that fit all the clues (and the final solution), but weren't the required solution.This is not a long game - I finished it with all achievements in about 2 1/2 hours, but I enjoyed it thoroughly and could easily play it through again in a while, just to spend some more time in the world.With the comic strip art and animal actors, and the fill-in-the-blanks word puzzles, is this a good one for children?  I'm not sure - the crimes are presented in a slightly surprisingly grown-up way, and as noted before the last puzzles could be frustrating for youngsters.  Maybe one to play with your kids, rather than just sitting them down and leaving them to it.I got it on sale, and honestly wouldn't feel bad if I'd paid full price for it.Final point - the soundtrack is excellent, and will be getting a lot of play from me, even when I'm not playing the game.  Just a good, noir-ish album.

This makes for a frustrating experience. The de-duck-tions are extremely linear. I would discover something or make a connection long before the game would let me enter it. _childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective is a very charming game that comes off as the love child between Untitled Goose Game and the Sam and Max series. The characters are goofy and instantly memorable, the premise and plot are equal parts silly and compelling, and the art, music, and humor are all executed to a highly polished degree. There's also an attention to detail that made me smile like the magnifying glass revealing more detailed drawings of the characters or the little doodles on evidence that add touches of humor. My one and only gripe about this game is that it is woefully, painfully short. The game only has a singular case for you to solve and I managed to finish it in 2 hours. Even for the price of $10 it feels like the amount of content is a bit lacking. I would have happily paid $15-$20 had the game consisted of multiple cases or had the case of the secret salami been a 10+ hour playthrough. As it is I was extremely charmed by the world of Duck Detective but was left extremely wanting as I felt I didn't get enough time with the characters or the story to really feel a sense of satisfaction. I would recommend this game if you are okay with a very very short but charming game. Hopefully there will be future content or DLC added to flesh out the game. If this is the beginning of a series of games my only suggestion is to make the content a bit fuller and richer but otherwise no notes.

_childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami is short. All told, there are just about a dozen "deducktions" to make. As I write this the game has been out for five days and 70% of players have beaten the game, suggesting a majority of players beat it in one sitting, like I did.It's cute, and the voice acting is good, but it wasn't very memorable since none of the puzzles were all that challenging or surprising. I did need to use the in-game hints a couple times, which are well designed: They gently suggest which clues you should pay attention to without spoiling the real puzzle.I felt like a lot of my time was backtracking (to see if the suspects had any new clues) and waiting for loading screens, which seems strange because there are six rooms total. I think they did a good job with the characterization of the characters, but the paper-doll animation was very plain. Having them cycle between emotions (e.g. surprised, suspicious) would do a better job of drawing me in to the story. Feels bad giving this a downvote, since it was made with some care, but can't really recommend it as is. Definitely "almost there"; I would have enjoyed it more if it had another act, or some side mysteries to solve just for fun. The gimmick is good, but not good enough to give the rest a pass. Buy it on sale, maybe you'll like it more than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami is a game where you play as a detective down on his luck, willing to take any case available to get back on his feet. The gameplay is simple. You go around the various rooms and investigate different items to gather clues to piece together the case one step at a time. While the gameplay itself is simple, in my opinion the fun comes from the part of the game where you use the clues you've gathered to slowly put together the pieces of the puzzle and progress the story. The game is not too hard and if you ever get stuck they have a recap/hint feature that recaps everything you know so far and also tells you where to go to find the next clue(s). The game does a good job of not falling into the trap where you find out who did it very early on and have to slog through the rest of the game in order to get to an ending you aren't surprised by. Instead it gives each character their own reason to have done it so you are left still guessing until the final few moments of the game.As far as the audio, artstyle and voice acting goes, the sounds in this game are all very appealing to listen to and the artstyle reminds me a little bit of the paper mario games. The voice acting is done extremely well and there was never a time when playing where I thought the voice acting was poor. All three are 10/10In my opinion the only reasons I have for someone to not get the game is if you either don't like detective games or the game is too short in your opinion to justify the price. The game is definitely on the shorter side and can be completed in only 2-3 hours so the $10 price tag may be a little steep for some. In my opinion, the game has enough polish and charm to justify buying the game even at full price, but that is up to everyone to decide for themselves.Overall this was a very short but very fun and charming little game to spend some of my weekend playing. I hope that the developers consider adding another story as either a follow up game or dlc and I will definitely keep an eye on their future releases.

From the moment I stepped into the whimsical world of anthropomorphic animals, I was captivated by the game's charming visuals and engaging narrative. The clever writing, filled with witty dialogue and unexpected twists, kept me invested in solving the quirky case of the missing salami. Each character, with their unique personality and backstory, added depth to the storyline, making me genuinely care about the outcome. The puzzles were not only challenging but also infused with a sense of fun, encouraging me to think outside the box and explore every nook and cranny of the vibrant game environment.Beyond entertainment, Duck Detective has had a profound impact on my life. It inspired me to embrace my curiosity and creativity in everyday situations, reminding me that problem-solving can be both enjoyable and rewarding. The game’s emphasis on teamwork and friendship resonated with me, fostering a deeper appreciation for collaboration in my personal and professional relationships. By immersing myself in this delightful adventure, I learned the importance of viewing challenges from different perspectives, which has significantly influenced how I approach obstacles in real life. Ultimately, Duck Detective: The Secret Salami is not just a game; it’s a trans-formative experience that has enriched my perspective and filled my life with joy and inspiration. I think I want to become the next duck detective after playing this game

_childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami is a short, sweet game that needs less short or more sweet. What's there is nice, but it feels underbaked.This game as having two support beams: Gameplay and tone. And if just one was improved, or just leaned into more, I think that would be enough to support the downsides of the other. A light breeze can knock it over as it is.So first, gameplay. The literal gameplay is just walking around, obtaining words, and figuring out which words to put in what order, but the actual gameplay is that of deductive reasoning on your end, sometimes compared to The Return of the Obra Dinn. This game isn't trying to be Obra Dinn, obviously, like, OBVIOUSLY. But it is basing the core of its gameplay on providing scant information to the player and have them be the ones to put it together. However, most of these deductions weren't done via evidence and investigation, but through relevance. You're given new words as the game goes on, and so most of the time, it's just figuring out what new words you're gonna use.Furthermore, the information given ranges from basically just writing out what your trying to deduce, (e.x. trying to figure out someone's name, and the "information" given to do that is just their name tag), or is so obscure that the conclusions reached from it, while not an unreasonable leap of logic, are unsubstantiated. And because the game only progresses from the words obtained through conversation and investigation, it told me that I didn't need to pay attention to other things. And frankly, that's kinda true, because I was able to beat the game through guessing, without completing the external deductions the game expected of me.Next, tone, which I describe as aesthetic and writing. It's sad the most charming and hilarious bits of writing were the "tips" featured in loader screens. They had a fun tone that was just not present in the rest of the game. A game called Duck Detective: The Secret Salami made me expect some cartoonish logic and comedy, but it was pretty muted. Not absent, just, yeah, just muted. I think they really really should've leaned into the absurdity of the situation and tone.The vocal performances helped the charm of this game, but they weren't enough to save it.While not a bad way to spend 2 hours, I wouldn't call it a good way either. I didn't hate anything, there was plenty I liked, but a lot I was disappointed by.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an interesting one. The art style is incredible, and the voice acting is so compelling! I had a really good time with this game.... for the first 30 minutes.As the story progresses, the de(duck)tions you have to fill out become increasingly difficult. At first, the increasing difficulty is super fun. It makes you really feel like you are delving into a case. As you progress through the game, though, things sort of feel like they are falling apart. You are faced with de(duck)tions that are full of random words pulled from every which way, making it feel more like sorting through red herrings gathered out of context than discovering clues. The vault puzzle in the office should be logical, but it doesn't seem to have been playtested well- the O's look like 0's, BD looks like Birthday when instead it is Bus Driver, and the number of bus drivers is the number total, not the number present, meaning that you have to account for a note on the floor in a random place that offhandedly mentions that there are four bus drivers. The last couple of de(duck)tions are really difficult to deduce on the regular mode due to the lack of character and object interactions available. Your detective journal says it has all of the words you need to fill it out, but you don't have any of the information about what has happened, and the game has no more information to give you. A lot of the de(duck)tions have to be finished with trial and error or wild conjecture instead of hard-won evidence. It feels disorienting, frustrating, and unfinished. This game is also pretty short. For 10 bucks I had around 2 hours of playtime total, which isn't awesome. I wish there was more than one case to uncover, but I respect that this game was made by a small indie studio, so they probably didn't have the time/budget for that, since game-making is a tricky business. Maybe a free DLC down the line would make up for this issue and allow the game to finally come into its own after some bug fixes.Despite my gripes, I feel like this game has serious potential. I was frustrated with the gameplay, but I really wanted to enjoy the story and the characters despite that. I really hope this studio keeps trying and grabs more playtesters to make this game or their next awesome. Hopefully this review was comprehensive enough, but if you have any questions or need for clarification, feel free to comment.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:This game is a fun little gem, that only takes a couple hours to complete, but is a good time throughout. 10/10 because the game absolutely nails what it sets out to do.Pros:+ Story:A short little tale about a lunch thief. Or... Is it actually a deeper tale with more more intrigue???+ Voice Acting:The voice acting is stellar! I didn't expect literally the whole thing to be voice acted, but it was a really nice surprise.+ WritingThe writing is pretty stand out as it manages to somehow combine a dumb plot about interpersonal office relationships with a gritty noir crime drama.+ Deducktions:The investigative and puzzle elements are simple, yet fun. You can figure out basically everything just by talking to everyone and investigating all points of interest, but if you can't the journal will tell you how many elements you have wrong. So worst case scenario it could be easily brute forced if you don't want to rely on the hint system. Any way you slice it, you're not gonna get hard stuck on something here.+ Art Style:I love the paper-craft art style. It feels like playing a pop-up book mystery, but not meant for kids. And having things become more detailed visually when you inspect them is a nice touch.Cons:- Length:I know the game is so short (about 2 hours) because it's a fully voiced indie experience, but damn I wish it was longer. I wish there were more cases to solve and I would gladly pay a higher price for it.Review:I loved this game! A short little story driven experience that I honestly wish there was more of. I expected it to be silly, but I didn't expect the Duckdetective to essentially be a Max Payne type, but addicted to white bread instead of pills and alcohol. That extra element of more cliche, gritty, noir stuff juxtaposed with the visual style and comedy of the ultra low stakes case really sold it for me. Good time all around. Perfect 10/10 since the only complaint I had is that there isn't more game for me to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Great short and cheap game to play on the side - can be worth it, if you don't brute force or dodge the main mechanics.Also worked like a charm on Steam Deck. Firstly, it has to be said that the game is not extremely long, nor does it have a very high price tag. For me, this is a great shorter game to play on the side!I've also had the game running on the side on my Steam deck (it appeared to be fully compatible BTW) while talking to my partner and her brother about various things.Apart from that, I have to say that I really liked the VA, the character design and especially the story.While playing, I had the feeling that I was doing some real detective work. Sometimes something is somewhat obvious, sometimes you have to think outside the box to interpret the clues correctly and get to the solution.Overall I had a great time with it and it was totally worth it for me.Of course it will be different for everyone.Some players report that the puzzles were too easy for them or that the game offered too little content - however, you have to be fair and take into account how this opinion came about:Many of the negative reviews at this point say that they finished the game too quickly and didn't have enough clues to find the right solution, so they preferred to solve the puzzles by trial and error.I personally tried not to use guides or trial and error approaches, because for me that undermines the point of the game, but everyone can decide that for themselves.And sure, I found myself stuck in the story at times, but by changing perspective, observation and deduction I always found the right solution in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've cleared the arguably bad puns out of my system, it's time to delve into why this game got a thumbs-up from me. Told in a lighthearted, humorous tone that persists throughout the gameplay, our main character, Eugene McQuackling, begins with a fatalistic outlook. He is a recently divorced duck who has lost his previous job. Things look bleak as he receives no messages or calls and has no cases to solve. He struggles to make a living as a self-employed ducktective; money is tight, and he cannot pay last month's or this month's rent. To make matters worse, he's feathers deep into a bread addiction. Just as everything feels like rock bottom for our protagonist, the phone rings – a case! This could be life-changing if he manages to solve it. It could be his big breakthrough! And so, our story starts as we see McQuackling arrive at his destination, where things take an exciting turn as a straightforward case has more to it than meets the eye. At the beginning of the game, you can enable auto dialogue. Following that, you are given another choice regarding how you would like to experience the game. You can select either "detective mode" or "story mode". In my playthrough, I chose the detective mode, so as we advance, my experience and review are based on that choice. I still need to play the story mode, but they are likely similar.Of course, it wouldn't be a detective game if the gameplay didn't revolve around that. The game is set in one location, with five indoor and one outdoor spaces, where your investigation begins. The main gameplay mechanics are the de-duck-tive skill and your observation abilities.You'll investigate people and occasionally revisit them for more information while observing your surroundings for clues. This allows you to pick up buzzwords that are added to your journal. However, it doesn't track who said what, so you must remember some details.One of the sepia' noir’-vibe scenes vs a full-colour cutscene:Once you discover enough buzzwords with your skill, you can complete the page and move forward. This way, you'll piece the story together little by little. Some may already know this from games like Golden Idol and Obra Dinn. However, I never played those, so this was new and exciting for me. As a bonus, you'll receive an adorable stamp when you solve your journal page. It was simple; most felt intuitive and easy, but it got a little more complex towards the end.I had only one problem, and that was with the vault. I know I saw two of the three hints somewhere; alas, I couldn't be bothered to find them again, and I don't recall ever seeing the third one. So, in the end, I chose to brute-force the vault. Honestly, I'm not even ashamed to admit that. A good detective gets the job done at any cost, right?Wrapping up, I enjoyed the visuals. The soft background and the characters that almost looked made of cut-out paper or cardboard made them really stand out, especially when our ducktective waddled around. I enjoyed how a close-up scene image became clearer when you hovered your magnifying glass over it to see objects in greater detail while looking for those precious clues. I also thought it was great how the sepia "noir detective movies" were integrated as cutscenes, giving me the feeling of being in one of them.The music was incredibly complementary, with its jazzy, smooth tunes. Even if a massive murder scene were to happen, I would still be cosily vibing to those tunes, feeling mellow and relaxed, ignoring everything that is going on around me. The power of a great soundtrack!The voice acting in the game was genuinely outstanding. The voice actors delivered their lines with incredible skill and emotion, bringing each character to life in a truly impressive way. I was thoroughly captivated by every performance, and I loved every one of them to bits. Despite its short duration, I thoroughly enjoyed the game. Its delightful combination of humour, intrigue, and charming characters captivated and entertained me. So, you are searching for an entertaining and laid-back game with a hint of challenge. In that case, I wholeheartedly recommend Duck Detective: The Secret Salami.Meanwhile, I am genuinely curious about Happy Broccoli Games' upcoming projects. I would eagerly welcome additional episodes of Duck Detective or Kraken Academy 2—or perhaps an entirely new creation!  If you enjoyed reading my review, kindly give it a thumbs up. Your support would mean a lot to me. Disclosure: I received a free game copy and wasn't paid to write this review. _childDocuments_.review: is a cozy, mystery point-and-click game with fill-in-the-blank elements developed and published by Happy Broccoli Games.  You take on the role of Eugene McQuacklin, who once worked for the police department but is now a private detective.  On top of that, his ex-wife divorced him and now he's struggling to make ends meet, all because he got addicted to bread.  (Yup, you read that correctly. lol)  Anyway, as Eugene, who we'll call the Duck Detective from here on out, is going about his business, he gets an anonymous call to come to the nearby bus company because apparently, someone's lunch got stolen and the caller wants to know who committed the crime.  Having nothing else to do and needing the money, the Duck Detective makes his way to the bus company, using the last of his bus fare to do so.  Upon arriving, he finds himself stonewalled by uncooperative witnesses, and he has to investigate locations and items to find clues about the identities of the bus employees.  Also, he may end up stumbling upon an even bigger crime than a stolen lunch, but I'll stop my synopsis here to avoid going into spoiler territory.Regarding the gameplay, it is mainly a point-and-click game, so you use your mouse and keyboard or a controller to move the Duck Detective around.  I mostly used my keyboard with the arrow keys and the WASD buttons.  You interact with items or enter rooms by pressing the E button, and you can search items for clues by first using the Q button and then moving a magnifying glass with your mouse to find hidden clues, which you then press with the E button.  There is a tutorial as well as a Help guide that explains all of these functions.  Of course, you can talk to people, observe them for clues, and even interrogate them about certain items that you might pick up along the way by pressing the R button.  In addition, there are fill-in-the-blank elements, mostly in the form of deductions (or deducktions, as the Duck Detective would call them) that are in the detective's notebook.  Once you find enough clues, you'll be able to fill in the blanks with the appropriate words.  Also, there are some Steam achievements, which count towards a user's global total, and Steam trading cards.With the story and gameplay all done, I'll get into my thoughts.  I enjoy cozy, relaxing games a lot and if they have a mystery element to them, all the better.  Also, I wanted to play a short game, so  was the perfect game.  First, I enjoyed the story a lot.  I liked the Duck Detective as the main character.  Especially with the English voice acting, the Duck Detective really fits his role well, and even more so, as a down-on-his-luck character.  However, that doesn't prevent him from doing his job, and he admits as much that he needs the money.  With the story itself, I like how it progresses as the Duck Detective is initially investigating a case about a stolen lunch, which ends up uncovering a way bigger crime.  The detective is definitely being put to work.  Also, his interactions with the characters at the crime scene are great.  At first, the other characters refuse to talk to him on the pretense of being busy or other similar reasons.  However, once the detective can figure out their identities, then they'll open up to him.  There is one character who's way more open initially than the others, but it turns out that he's a huge fan of the Duck Detective.  Without spoiling the ending, I liked following the detective during his investigation and finally, figuring out the major perpetrators of the crime and how it all ties into the stolen lunch.  Towards the end of the game, you can even choose whom you think the detective should have arrested, which I thought was a nice touch.With the gameplay, I really liked the point-and-click and investigation elements.  When you first start the game, you can choose between detective or story modes.  Detective mode is the more difficult option since you're given fewer clues.  (For review purposes, I chose detective mode.)  Anyway, I like how you can interact with items and find out more information about them, which can lead to valuable clues.  Also, there's a gameplay aspect in which you have to make deductions in the form of fill-in-the-blank.You have to wait on these parts until you've gathered enough clues, but they're doable to complete if you think through the sentences logically.  Making correct deductions will help the Duck Detective ultimately solve the case.  Personally, I enjoy these kinds of gameplay aspects where you need to think clearly, just like a detective.  Regarding Steam achievements, I had no problems obtaining all of them on one playthrough although there is one missable achievement if you don't explore everything thoroughly.In regards to the art, I love the style that is present, especially since the character sprites are in the paper-cut style that reminds me of certain games.  The sprites are colored well, and the rooms are drawn and colored well, too.  With the music, the tracks are great to listen to.  They give off that whole mystery, detective vibe going on, which is totally perfect for this game.  Also, as I mentioned earlier, there is English voice acting, and yes, all of the characters are voiced.  This is such a great addition to an already wonderful game.Overall, would I recommend ?  If you enjoy cozy, relaxing games with some mystery and point-and-click elements and don't mind a short game, then this is totally perfect.  I bought this game when it came out, and I'm happy that I finally got around to playing it and sharing my thoughts.  If there's one downside, I'd say that I wish there were more cases to solve, but who knows?  This could be start of a great mystery series, and I'd completely support it. ^^

_childDocuments_.review: Are you a fan of ducks like me? Do you dream of becoming a duck yourself? And do you love spending time in a cozy, chill game, playing a cute point-and-click adventure while solving mysteries? If so, then you definitely have to take a look at this game! 🦆 The first thing that grabbed my heart was the adorable art style, with Eugene, our ducktective, donning a classic detective outfit complete with a trench coat and hat. This charming look perfectly captures the essence of a classic detective. As you play the game further, you'll find that its point-and-click mechanics allow you to explore, collect clues, and arrange them in your notebook to form correct de(duck)tions (I love this pun!).In addition to the delightful visuals, the game features a variety of characters whose names you need to guess by matching clues from the “Suspects” section of your notebook. The fully voiced characters add depth and personality to the game, enhancing the experience. While many on my stream have fallen for Eugene’s deep voice, I must admit, I have a soft spot for the quacks!Speaking of quacking, the game has a totally hilarious feature where you can press a button to make Eugene quack! It's such a fun addition. Adorable duck? Quack. Strange case? Quack. Need more evidence? Quack. Brain not braining? Quack. Another fun aspect is how easily you can knock over trash cans. Just walk up to a trash can, and it will tip over, scattering trash everywhere. It's chaotic, refreshing, and you even get an achievement for knocking over enough trash cans! The developers encourage it, so go ahead and knock over every trash can you see—in the game, of course.For achievement hunters, this game is a treat. It doesn’t have many achievements, and they’re quite easy to complete. For content creators and streamers, I finished the game in one stream (around 5 hours) even with my turtle pace and lots of chatting. It's a short but entertaining game, perfect for some brain-frying fun with your community!There are so many things I adore about this game, and I really hope Happy Broccoli Games makes a sequel. I've grown so attached to Eugene and look forward to more of his adventures, If you love ducks, cozy mysteries, and charming adventures, this game is a must-play! 🌟

_childDocuments_.review: When you need a private eye to locate your missing lunch, who do you call? Duck Detective! Duck Detective: The Secret Salami is a short game featuring Eugene McQuacklin, alias known as Duck Detective. You play as the Detective, short on cash, and wanting back a relationship he'll know he'll never get. Fortunately, money comes with an invitation to the Bear Bus. Someone's salami has gone missing. It's up to the detective to solve the case. I'm a fan of Ace Attorney games, and honestly, this is a real step up from those. Of course, I mean, I'd be worried if a lawyer game had more "detective-ing" than a detective game. The game requires you to make de-duck-tions, which basically allows you to look for clues, be it objects from scenery or people. The voice acting is bloody amazing, I love the detective's voice. I also love the Janitor as well. Although a short game, it's absolutely worth it to pick it up and play. Put on the best detective hat you can, stay away from the bread, and find clues, as you discover: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective: The Case QuackerDuck Detective is a detective game (clearly) about finding a lunch thief, and stumbling into a large-scale conspiracy. You interrogate a cast of fun characters, investigate clues, and make "Deducktions" to solve the many mysteries of BearBus's office. The Good:-The Voice Acting. Hands down, the best part of this game are the voice actors. Each line is delivered with so much exaggerated emotion that I couldn't help but talk to everyone. And I'd be foolish not to mention that every single line of dialogue in this game is voice acted! They could have gone the easy way out and recorded some grunts or talking noises to play over everything, but they went above and beyond to have each of the amazing voice actors read every single line. -The Writing. The writing in this game is amazing, and that makes each character a blast to speak with. They all have their own unique way of speaking, and this makes sure each character distinct and memorable.-The Investigations. I love how the player investigates each item to find clues, it was always exciting to find a new interactable item just to see what new information I could gleam from it.-The Deducktion System. I love how this system is handled, and it allows the player to feel like they're quacking the case like a true duck detective. Since they take the form of vague fill in the blanks, it allows the game to guide the player to conclusions without holding their hand too much. The Bad:-Game Length. This game is very short, with my completed playthrough only lasting 2 hours. Granted, it is a high quality 2 hours, but 2 hours nonetheless.-Hint System. While a well-made hint system is incredibly difficult to make, I'm afraid they missed the mark. It only gives you vague ideas on where to search, but when you've already collected all the clues you need for a "Deducktion" you're on your own. They do not give hints about the correct answers, only saying things along the lines of "I should check my clues" which was a bit frustrating near the end. The... Confused?-None.There really isn't anything in this game I have mixed feelings on, which is a pretty good sign in my book.Overall, Duck Detective: The Secret Salami is a great little detective game. The writing is fun, the mysteries are engaging, and the voice action is nothing short of phenomenal. The $10 price tag isn't egregious for the short play time, but if you're frugal with your funds, I'd wait til it goes on sale. I definitely recommend this game to anyone who likes detective games. P.S, If we ever get a second Duck Detective game, I'd kill to have Freddy come along as a sidekick.

_childDocuments_.review: A tight but charming deduction game with just the right amount of challenge for its scope. The simple system of sort of madlibbing clue words into a pre-composed logical thought balance guiding the player and distracting them with valid (and sometimes silly) options to make sure you really know the solution to a Deduc(k)tion. Duck Detective gets every element right for its premise from the crisp, inviting visuals and the tone-setting noir soundtrack, to the intriguing if ridiculous mystery premise and down-to-earth writing. The clues are carefully laid out as to not be obvious (in fact some are quite clever), but there are no leaps in logic that aren't grounded in what's presented. If you're struggling, the notebook makes it clear when there's more evidence to be found if you're missing something.If you're looking for a fun mystery and a fair challenge, perhaps for a plane/bus/long car ride or just something for your detective brain to chew on, I'd highly recommend it! _childDocuments_.review: I love playing detective. I love ducks. This game was literally made for me. Jokes aside, this game is truly incredible.The gameplay in Duck Detective: The Secret Salami is fun and engaging. You waddle around as the Duck Detective, investigating environments and interviewing suspects to solve the mystery of a stolen lunch. Clues you obtain throughout your investigation are used to make deduc(k)tions which progress the story, similar to how it's done in the Detective Grimoire games. It's a good way to make sure the player doesn't get immediately overwhelmed with information.I'm impressed by how creative the game is, too. Every character has a cute "overworld" design, but they become hilariously detailed when you investigate them. Everyone has a unique & believable personality, and the voice acting helps to sell them (Brian David Gilbert plays the crocodile??). The music nails that Jazz Noir feel, smoothly transitioning when the player switches between waddling around and investigating. Little things too, like knocking over pens and bins when you bump into them, help to sell the world.The main complaint I see repeated in the reviews is that the game is too short. You can probably finish it in 2-3 hours. I did too. The game also isn't too challenging. I agree with what these points in the reviews, and I can understand if you think the current price is too much for only a few hours of content. I thought it was a reasonable price because the game's concept is original, but also because "true" detective games are a niche. The game has some other shortcomings (e.g. at least one plot hole by the end that I've observed) but these didn't detract from the game. Overall, I think HBG have managed to create something special, and I'm really eager to see whether Duck Detective comes back in any sequels or DLCs.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this a lot more than I did. I was in the mood for a point-and-click mystery and while this is cute and the characters and voice acting are fun, the mystery leaves a lot to be desired. I really liked the mechanics of how the investigations are done and conclusions are reached, but the vast majority of clues are spoon fed to you. Literally, there are screens where you can't move on to something else until you find all the clues. That makes the few times that there's a subtle clue so easy to overlook, not because it's hard but because it doesn't have a neon sign flashing "CLUE HERE!" in your face. But, if you do miss them, it also doesn't matter because you can just keep guessing at solutions until you get it right (and some of the solutions more or less force this approach since the wording doesn't always make it obvious what you're supposed to be concluding). When I finished, I actually checked to see if I'd accidentally turned on easy/story mode, but it was still off, which makes me wonder how much easier it can be.Hoping this studio follows up with a better mystery and maybe a harder mode. I don't want it to be impossible, but I also don't want to feel like an eight-year-old.

_childDocuments_.review: Good gravy, I can't believe I have a higher total play time on Bad Rats than this masterpiece."Duck Detective: The Secret Salami" is an isometric point-and-click adventure game which plays similarly to games like those from the "Sam & Max" series and, to an extent, the "Sherlock Holmes" games by Frogwares: You analyse your environment, interrogate other characters, solve puzzles and piece together the mystery of .The voice acting and soundtrack definitely give it that film noir feel, while still retaining a whimsical but original look with the whole "cardboard cut-out" visual aspect to characters in the overworld. I do like the fact that the game doesn't try desperately to make the game feel funny () or solely rely on overused gags, so I'd like to think that speaks volumes about the visual and writing quality and how it naturally exudes humour. The  inspection was definitely the highlight for me in regards to those two attributes.The difficulty of the game is also interesting. There were a couple of puzzles that took a good amount of brainpower to make sense of the clues given, so it's good to see a kind of push-and-pull when it comes to the different puzzles the game has to offer. When interrogating other characters or interacting with the environment, they can sometimes give you false clues (or "red herrings", if you will) so sifting out these from the actual clues gives the deducktions a certain level of depth that I wasn't expecting.One aspect which threw me off a bit was the fact that dialogue isn't tracked in the sense that other characters can say something important but only ONCE and if you misheard or forget about it later on, then tough luck. Fortunately, the game is rather forgiving when it comes to the completion of deducktions, but there were a couple of times when I basically just had to brute force the available the options because of that.The game itself is certainly something you could finish in one night. To me, this is a good thing because it means the developers have focused on delivering a high-quality experience across the whole game end-to-end, rather than having a game with twice the content but with quality that drops as it progresses. It also lends itself naturally to an episodic approach for future titles, especially since there are a lot of things in this game's world building that aren't explored in great detail.In terms of price, the game is... average on that front, at least when looking at it in terms of cost vs. total game time on completion. In my locale, the game roughly stands at the same price as "Sherlock Holmes: Crimes and Punishments" which easily took 10+ hours for me to finish. Granted, "Duck Detective" is a new IP (I think?) from Happy Broccoli Games and Frogwares have been making these "Sherlock Holmes" games for over a decade now, so perhaps that's not exactly a fair comparison.. It combines the charm & comedy of the old "Sam & Max" games with the core mechanics & plot depth (or thereabouts) of the "Sherlock Holmes" games by Frogwares to create a unique experience that will be a challenge to top if there is a sequel/second episode in the works. And if that's not enough - How many games do you get to play as a case-hardened duck detective desperate to make ends meet in both his personal and professional life? I thought so.And one more thing:

_childDocuments_.review: I've often maintained that length is not the be-all and end-all (wa-hey) when deciding whether a game is good or not. Just as a TV show that's 100 episodes long won't necessarily tell a more interesting story than a series a tenth the runtime, a short game isn't a bad game. Often brevity is in fact a strength, as it can feel like the game respects the player's time enough to not waste it with grinding or padding. However, when a game is only an hour long and is being sold for nearly a tenner, that raises an eyebrow.Duck Detective is a fun game, filled with charm and some decent puzzles. The voice acting is well executed and the visuals are pleasing on the eye. But it's over before it ever has the chance to become interesting. The central plot is intentionally dull (that's kind of the joke), but there's no twist to serve as a punchline to the setup. It's an everyday ocurrence being treated with the gravity of a pulp crime novel, but nothing happens to build on that joke. The puzzles themselves are okay,  though it's too easy to bruteforce a lot of them. The game uses a similar system to The Case of the Golden Idol, which had the same problem, but the variables in that game were complex enough to obfiscate their solutions. In Duck Detective, there is often only one arrangement of your clues that makes any grammatical sense, so it's a more test of your ability to structure sentences than make deductions.Being intensely critical of Duck Detective's puzzles or plot is missing for the forest for the trees though. Yes, both may be quite basic, but that's not really the point. Duck Detective is a comedy game, so the most important question should really be "Is it funny?" And the answer to that one is "Yeah, kinda." I chuckled a few times, smiled a few others, but without bit more meat, it's hard to feel like you're really getting your worth here. But again, I'm being too harsh.Ultimately, Duck Detective is fine for what it is. Everything is executed with competance, but I can't help but wonder how much better it would have been multiple cases instead of just one. The surprise moral decision at the end feels like evidence that that might have been the plan all along, but I can't spend too long wondering "What if?" If you've enjoyed games like Detective Grimoire and Tangle Tower, you might like Duck Detective too. Just don't expect the next Obra Dinn or anything.

_childDocuments_.review: A great ducking time This down-on-his-luck detective (with a very serious bread addiction) has been hired to quack the case of a lunch thief. As he begins using his skills of deDUCKtion, he begins to uncover the mysteries of a much larger and much more sinister sausage based conspiracy. Help this Duck solve the case by interviewing and inspecting suspects, then use your deductive reasoning to solve the case. This was such a fun game and had me chuckling with every animal pun, kicked trash can, and humorous interaction. I mean *spoiler* they even rickroll the player. The animation was excellently done and the art style was so incredibly charming. Not to mention, the voice acting was superb (featuring many individuals we know and love from the anime English dub community). If you thought you’ve heard Eugene McQuacklin’s voice somewhere else - he also voices Diluc in Genshin Impact among many other familiar anime shows. The gameplay was interesting, it took me back to Beacon Pines where you would need to investigate the area, find certain words, and then put those words together to create the correct narrative. I played the game in Detective Mode so there was less information and hints when you were incorrect. I’m not sure if it was different in Story Mode, but there was a sort of imbalance between really easy puzzles and difficult puzzles. There were times I didn’t even need to go around and talk to the suspects in order to complete a deducktion, because the word order just made sense. Other times I felt completely lost and went over and over all of the clues I had gathered only to just start guessing which words went where until I got it correct. I completed the game and all of the steam achievements in a little over 3 hours. It’s incredibly short, but I I think I’d rather see a Duck Detective series with different cases to quak rather than one really long game. With the animation, story, and voice acting this was well worth the low price. So, if you are looking for a cozy mystery noir game with lots of laughs, don’t hesitate to pick this one up!

_childDocuments_.review: i really really wanted to like this and at first, i really did. the music, voice acting, and art is all lovely and has no right being this awesome for a little indie game. the mechanics of the game of picking up clues, interrogating suspects, solving codes, and examining things are all fantastic, but it felt like at the end.. everything fell apart. it was like they got tired and wanted to speed run it to the end, with clues that didn't make sense and solutions that felt obvious being completely incorrect. there were things that could have been pressed with suspects or expanded upon, such as the OTHER crime going on in the background that the detective ignores in order to solve this one. i see a lot of potential here as a fan of the ace attorney series, but with how short the game is, it feels wrong that the ending was so rushed. would i recommend the game in this current state? no. would i play future installments, updates, and/or sequels that might perfect this formula that they have? yes. absolutely. again, there's a lot of love in the art, music, voice acting, character designs, and a great deal of potential here as many of the questions are fun to solve.. just poorly executed at the finish line where it matters most.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is , in my opinion! Why do I say "surprisingly good", though? I had some doubts about whether Duck Detective was going to have a good story after playing its demo. However, I'm happy that the story it tells is silly yet intriguing. Also, the detective work is really nice - it FEELS like you're making cool deductions on your own, especially if you're paying attention to your surroundings. If you weren't super impressed by its demo like I was, I would say still give it a try because it gets a LOT cooler right after where the demo ended.You're a duck, binging on bread (junk food for waterfowl, don't feed them bread please) and you've been asked to solve a minor crime that spirals into a conspiracy. If that sounds cool, go for it and try the game out!There are a few strange leaps in logic that you need to make to get through the game but it becomes more apparent what Duck Detective is expecting out of your thought process as you go along. As I mentioned before, you should be able to figure out the whole story if you carefully observe your surroundings, but be prepared to brute force some of the fill-in-the-blank puzzles the game has since it's sometimes not apparent what exactly it's asking to you deduce.On a separate note, the voice acting is really good, but it's brought down a bit by some bad voice line volume balancing.All in all, great game, and I really want to see more stories around this Duck Detective fellow - I was fully expecting more plot around his ex-wife but maybe that'll have to be for another game in the series? :D

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my God, this was one of the most fun games I have ever played. Ok, let's put this game into context. This is a project by a small team of four, that have even outsourced the music and a part of the text. Also the game is at about 8 euros, so they don't ask for a fortune, nor they charge you 20 dollars for cosmetics. It's small indie project that it's price feels more like a support to the studio rather than a price. So what is this Ducktective? You play as the Eugene McQuacklin, the Duck Detective who is called by an unknown person to investigate a stolen lunch. The mystery is delves deeper as you uncover more of the clues and the story. The gameplay is simple, just investigate and interogate everyone, uncover every clue (that is automatically saved once you uncover it) and use your own deduction to fill the gaps in the De-duck-tion sequence. The puzzles are not hard and some of the de-duck-tion sequences can be brute forced, if you get 8 or 9 pieces of info right. But the game is extremely witty and funny and the voice over is amazing. It almost feels like a satire, and this cute bread-addicted detective that is at the same time so serious and so ridiculous that I'm amazed how they came up with this beautiful characters. The only flaw of this game is that it is short. You'll need only 2 or 3 hours to full investigate the mystery. So, some may question its value for money, but personally I think it is worth it. Kudos to the writer and the whole team for this very short but very fun, almost heart warming game.

_childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective was a short, but rich experience. _childDocuments_.review: I would absolutely recommend this game!  The voice acting and art style were on point and I found some of the investigating, deduction, and clue gathering fun, addicting, and even bit challenging at times. While it fails to muster any real consequences for getting interrogations or deductions wrong, I thought the game did a great job at forcing you to really pay attention to all the clues found in both the evidence collected and environment. I only had two gripes with the game overall.  The first complaint I had with the game had to do with its length, as it is really short and I wish there were more cases to solve (even though I know the title is just "the secret salami"),  The second issue, as I mentioned earlier, is that there are no real consequences for guessing or deducing incorrectly.  Not everyone will agree with this, but I just think it would enhance the detective experience so much more! All that being said, if I were to give it a score I would probably give this game an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth the full price of $9.99. The hints and the solutions don't come together in a satisfying way and though everything seems to be presented to you in an obvious manner, I was often left scratching my head at what the game wanted. The graphics are very cute and the controls are pretty easy, but unfortunately that's not enough to save it. Do not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good as a foundation for a detective game, and nice as an "episode 1" or tutorial case. Also, I personally found this case a bit easy and never really got to a point where I had to stop and think much; it was fairly steady progress, which is great for an "episode 1" but a little disappointing for a full game.It can also be a little too easy to just trial-and-error the entire deduction system and bypass any need to think about the case at all. However, ultimately that may just fall on each player's discretion whether they want to actually figure things out or just brute force it, though the temptation to brute force it may allure some and rob them of the experience of actually making the deductions.Overall it's fun and I hope more cases are coming.
