_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. It didn't take itself seriously what-so-ever, which is precisely what made it so great. It was short and I finished it in around three hours, but that's not because it was easy, mind you. I just couldn't put it down. The hidden schemes unveiled nicely and the character interactions made my classmates laugh just by looking over my shoulder. Putting together the pieces of the case by filling in the blanks with drop-down menus was a great choice. It prevented the plot from becoming overwhelming and confusing, as they often do in detective games. I recommend it 100%!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Grab your fedoras and trench coats, folks, because Happy Broccoli Games has served up a real feathered masterpiece with "Duck Detective: The Secret Salami." For three hours, I waddled through a web of intrigue, mystery, and delightful duck puns, and let me tell you, this game is the crème de la quack.From the moment our beaked hero hit the foggy streets, I was hooked. The noir atmosphere drips with charm, capturing the essence of classic detective tales while adding a feathery twist. The storyline, centered around the elusive secret salami, had more twists and turns than a duckling on ice. Each piece of dialogue is meticulously crafted, with puns landing as gracefully as a duck diving for breadcrumbs.I truly wish I could reexperience "Duck Detective: The Secret Salami" all over again. It's a duck-filled delight from start to finish, and I can’t wait to see what Happy Broccoli Games hatches next. If you’re a fan of detective noir and have a penchant for puns, this game is an absolute must-play. Here's hoping for a sequel that quacks us up all over again! 🦆

_childDocuments_.review: What was supposed to be a perfect crime has gone a-RYE, for when the bills start to pile up, there is only one duck who can quack the case... EUGENE MCQUACKLIN!I can safely say this game is perfect in every way, shape, and form. Compared to other games in the genre, Duck Detective carves out a space in the genre while also using the same cliches that make mysteries work. The art style is so adorable that it's hard not to like every character in the office, even though some are especially dubious in nature. The music and sound in this game are tremendously well-crafted, also shame on the devs for not allowing us to buy the soundtrack.The only mystery left unsolved after completing this game is how the team made such a memorable and showstopping experience. I wholeheartedly recommend this for anyone who wants a casual game they can dive into and get lost in while uncovering the mystery surrounding the salami bandit. Absolutely amazing job Happy Broccoli Games, I hope you make more games like this in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely LOVED this game! So many good things I have to say!- Art Style: I adored the cute sticker-style art for all the characters! Very reminiscent of paper mario, and the environment was nicely designed. All of the art assets were clearly made with love, and it shows!- Gameplay/Story: Finding clues in this game is definitely the easy part, as it tells you what areas you haven't fully explored, characters you still need to speak to, and the number of keywords you're missing. The hard part is putting them all together and piecing together the mysteries! I definitely found myself getting stuck a few times trying to figure out how everything connects, and I think the devs did a really great job of striking a balance between "Oh, that was pretty obvious" and "WOW, I would have never thought of that!" - Voice Acting: I absolutely had to make mention of this. I really wasn't expecting much going into this game when it came to the voices, but I was super impressed at how the voice actors brought these characters to life! Duck Detective and Laura were a joy to listen to, and the other characters had really great performances overall!- Length: The game is definitely on the short side! I finished it in about 2 and 1/2 hours, but I enjoyed every second I was playing. If you're looking for a cute and comfy game to spend a couple hours on, THIS is it!Thank you for releasing such a wonderful little game. If any additional updates, DLC stories, or sequels get made, I'll absolutely keep an eye out and check it out! Much love to the development team <3
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: So disappointing. It's two hours long and I didn't even want to finish it.On the positive side, it looks nice - the Paper Mario style works really well, the UI is clean and the main character's voice acting is great (although some other characters sound like they're doing a bad impression of an accent - the janitor has the worst English accent since Al Pacino in The Local Stigmatic).But it just doesn't hold up as a detective game. The story itself is boring and the "collecting clues to make deduc(k)tions" mechanic falls apart quickly. Half of the game is trying to guess what the game is thinking as it hasn't given you enough information to form a proper conclusion, and the other half is the game propelling itself forward by inventing things out of thin air. The most effective way to play is to brute force answers by picking the words which look like they'd fit the sentence most closely.The process of collecting clues is also tedious. Examining characters to find out more about them is mildly interesting (although it's nothing more than pointing to a feature and the game using it to leap to a conclusion on your behalf) but traversing the small environment is slow and the map, which tells you which characters or items you need to interact with at that point, is inconsistent - it shows a coffee machine and a work bag as apparently important items, but you can't interact with either at any point.Not for me unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw "Duck Detective," I thought it would be a shameless knock-off of the popular Frog Detective and other subsequent comedic, animal-based detective games.I'm happy to say that I couldn't have been more wrong.Duck Detective is a hilarious detective game with an emphasis on deduction. You walk around the small environments and gather clues and talk to suspects. When you have everything you need (or at least most of it) you can go into your journal and piece these clues and pieces of evidence together to try and formulate what exactly happened. The game doesn't hold or your hand or make anything too obvious, and there were several points where I had to stop and rethink certain events that I thought I understood.But what keeps the game from being a dry puzzler are the characters. They're all funny and fun, and despite the humor the game isn't afraid to dip its toes into some darker themes and elements on occasion. It also does a good job of world building despite taking place entirely in one building.This is a surprise hit for me, so good that it's actually one of best games of 2024 so far. Do yourself a favor and play this game. Or check out my full video review below.

Paper mario style art/cutouts can be nice if leaned in to, but the way it is portrayed here seems to see it as a negative, meaning that all visual clues are irrelevant. _childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective is a fun detective story that expertly straddles the line between silly and serious. Every single line is voice-acted, adding to the charm and atmosphere of the game.The gameplay is linear, with new interactions unlocking as you solve key questions about the situation. The general pattern is that you talk to characters and inspect objects to uncover words that you can use to fill in the template statements. You can also obtain pieces of evidence to ask characters about. Once you've gained enough information, you need to put it all together to reach a conclusion.Overall, this was a charming game with pretty unique mechanics. However, for the price that I paid (USD$8.99), I expected some more gameplay hours. I went through every interaction possible (including those that were unnecessary to solve the main puzzles) and completed all of the achievements within about 1.5 hours. I would love for this game developer to come up with more of the same type of cases, but I would be leery of paying as much for them as I did for this game.Some feedback (with spoilers hidden):

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing VA, good comedy, lovely art style, and interesting plot. I really dig the fill in the blank mechanic as a detective to figure out a deducktion. Speaking of deducktions, that was my one complaint/issue with this game. I found it incredibly confusing to figure out the deducktions near the end. It could be that i'm just dumb and was overthinking it way to hard but I found that there was just way too many options to pick from that it overwhelmed you and made you overthink every blank spot. *NOT A REAL SCENARIO* For example instead of using the characters name, lets say Sophie, the correct word would've been "the salami bandit". While both words are technically correct, the blank only accepts "the salami bandit" and  in the moment it misguides you and forces you to think over the other blank spots and ultimately leading you to overthink the whole deducktion. Another thing is that I wish you could rewatch/review cutscenes. There are hints that are only visible in cut scenes that you can only see once and would greatly assist in your investigation, but since its not possible to review it I got lost and it took me a longer time to figure things out. Overall great game, I genuinely had a good time and am exited to see more from this studio

_childDocuments_.review: AVOID | LACKING | MAYBE |  | COMPELLING | UNMISSABLEDuck Detective: The Secret Salami is an investigation-focused point & click story game. This game is short and sweet; it's fun throughout its entirety and doesn't overstay its welcome. The characters are all unique and interesting, and the gameplay is straight-forward (it plays very similarly to other games like Return of the Obra Dinn, even if the atmosphere/graphics are quite different). The music was great and added to the overall sleuth-y vibe to the game. I finished the game in just under three hours. I recommend completing it in one go (perhaps two, if needed) to stay engaged with the story. Given its duration, I feel like the price is pretty fair, but I would probably suggest getting it on sale because of this.If you're looking for a casual story-driven game to spend a few hours enjoying at once, then this is a cozy pick to be sure. It's not very challenging, but I also think people are unlikely to get everything correct on their first try. This game is simply fun.

_childDocuments_.review: (no spoilers in my review) Very cute game! Very much like an interactive short story. I hope they release more of Duck Detective. The music is relaxing, there's an option for dyslexic font for the captioning, and the mystery was challenging enough to keep my interest, but not so challenging it caused stress. The game has an interactive environment that can be played point-and-click so it's also pretty accessible in that way. This game doesn't take very long to play, and to be honest I don't think it'll be as interesting the second time around if I played alone again, but I still think the price is great for the storyline and artwork. Would probably be a fun game to play with another person sitting next to you, so that ups it's replayable factor. I'd say it's appropriate for older kids, depending on their maturity level and basic deductive reasoning skills. There are a few vague innuendos but nothing blatant.

I fully recommend it!The only thing that bothered me a bit was that I didn't always feel that I had the information I needed. So sometimes it felt like I got a deducktion right only because I tried something that happened to be correct by sheer luck.Still, I would love to play a longer adventure with Duck Detective, maybe with multiple cases, or a bigger and longer one. _childDocuments_.review: I don't know why adorable animal detectives have become a trend, but I welcome it. _childDocuments_.review: The game is VERY short, and I feel like I wasn't the target audience at all. This is something a very young child would enjoy as an introduction to gaming. The story is too simple, you only get to solve 1 case, I was half expecting after solving the mystery to have more cases to solve, or for the story to evolve in some way, it felt like an "intro" mystery to get you accustomed to how the game plays out. The voice acting is great, and I liked the characters, I'd love to see the game expand in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: 2,5h without a guide 3/10 1 There are guides on steam with the solution. However, you still have to find the clues yourself.  No Probably the one to kick over all the bins. However, you spend almost the whole game in that building, so as long as you do it before solving the last puzzle you're fine. No No No No No I think that you can play on story mode without missing out on the achievements, but I didn't test this.  NoWhat a lovely game. It is such a delight! It reminds me a lot of "Frog Detective' but with some mechanics of "Obra Dinn" added and as an extra treat, the game is fully voice-acted. You (Duck Detective) get hired to solve the mystery of the stolen lunch, however... there is much more going on at the company you visit to solve this game. It has a button to quack and it the loading screens are short, but when they are there, they will throw funny duck facts at you. Duck Detective is so well done. I love how you could see how many clues to find for each objective/person. This stopped me from overthinking it when it wasn't needed. It was also nice to see that the game kinda tells you when you have enough clues to solve part of the mystery. I suck at this type of game but this one was just great with a wonderful production. What was a lovely surprise is that at the end of the game, it tells you how others judged the characters in the game, which was nice to see, and while I voted differently, I can totally understand the scores at the end. Achievement-wise this game has only one missable achievement, which you can complete almost the whole time you play this game as long as you don't fill in the final solution. That achievement is for kicking the bins in the BearBus Office. There are 9 bins (the one in your own office you can kick over but doesn't count). All the other achievements are story-based and can't be missed. I give Duck Detective: The Secret Salami 4,5 out of 5 stars and I hope we will see sequels in the Duck Detective series!

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels much less fleshed out than I was expecting. It feels like answers don't really come naturally in this game. It expects you to waddle around checking everything then just guess by putting words into a sentence, or shove names together until it works. Like, okay, that's Freddy. Cool. How was Duck Detective supposed to deduckt that? You don't go "oh, this guy must be Freddy, and I think that because [evidence]" you actually go "I have five first names and one of these is going to work if I guess" and it does. A few times I went "Okay, I know what's happening. But how does Duck Detective know what's happening? How was the dev expecting me to piece together this info based on what he is observing?" And I couldn't think of an answer. I think I'm expected to just guess.It seems the dev wasn't expecting people to do things out of order either. If you approach the door in the reception office before talking to the receptionist, the game gives you a voice line as if you've already spoken to the receptionist. Stuff like this happened a couple times. Lacks attention to detail. Kinda sucks for a game that reacts to nearly everything by giving you some voiced lines, but the voiced lines can be out of order if you don't do things the "obvious" way. I thought we were investigating, not being led by the nose through a story.If you're just looking for a silly couple hours, and aren't expecting anything, this would probably be fun for you.However for me in the end, I feel like this game is a cute concept, but not detailed enough gameplay to be fun. It's like one of those Youtuber games. Surface level gameplay, but ultimately it's just an avenue to deliver voice acting from familiar people. I wanted Phoenix Wright, instead I got Word Jigsaw Puzzle: Celebrity VA Edition with a Quack button. I refunded, but maybe the game is cute enough for you to not be bothered by its shortcomings. It's not a bad game, but it's not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: A single word I'd use to describe the game; charming.Duck Detective is a delightful sleuthing game; the office relationships were fun to unravel and speculate about, the art style was unique and pleasing, but what really sold me was the voice acting, especially Duck Detective himself. The gusto his voice actor put into the lines had me laughing many times.It took me roughly 3 hours to complete the game, which for its price I was perfectly happy with. _childDocuments_.review: This was a great little game. Though short and heavily scripted, there's a delightful array of well-voice-acted characters that make this a deeply enjoyable experience. It's a great game for couples, I'll say! Cutesy in a fun way.My only critique: maybe a little short for the price point. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. It's made with a lot of love that shines through in everything: the art, music, dialogue... However, the actual detective work isn't very satisfying. You mostly need to fill in blank words in sentences. Quite often, the types of options you get matter more to finding the solution than the actual in-game clues. Some deductions are hard to piece together from clues (at least in my experience) but are easily guessed from the sentence structure and how you can fill the blanks. When you get them, it doesn't feel rewarding. Other deductions are very easy to get instinctively right based on clues, but it's easy to get stuck on a nearly correct answer. The worst example, without giving any spoilers, is a deduction where you might think you need to select a name but you actually need to choose "The Bandit". If you choose a name, even if it's the correct name of the bandit, you can't proceed. Also, the option "The Bandit" is all the way at the bottom making it easy to overlook that it exists. In the end, the deductions weren't very satisfying and it felt like a bit too much gaming the system and not enough actually being challenged to solve the puzzle. I do hope they make a sequel. If the actual deductions are a bit more polished, it'd be a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Joy is an emotion, overwhelmingly seen as a positive one.It is therefore no miracle that this game has the rating fitting for that description, because it invokes precisely that, which I spoke of: Joy.Duck Detective: The Secret Salami is a shining example of what can be achieved in todays gaming industry, with ingenuity, wit and creativity.While Happy Broccoli Games could've happily went the same way as so many other studios nowadys and release "The Prolougue" of this game for free, Happy Broccoli Games made the correct move as to release the full game to a reasonable price. Not to be overly critical of other games, that releases Prologues, but can we get back to calling them, what they are? Demos. There is no shame in that.The artstyle of Duck Detective draws you in, without gripping you by the throat. If it were me, I'd even lost the elements that were 3D and stick exclusively with that paper cut silhouette aethetics.The plot and dialogues are funny. And by that, I mean genuinely funny, not riddled with overly used puns or double entendres. It is refreshing to see a game that takes being funny serious without pestering the player with being one or the other.Special mentionings need to be made toward the voice acting. Supreme job all around. The characters came to life, they were vibrant, unique and lovable. Everyone in their own right.I for one would very much like it, if we saw Mr. McQuacklin again.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective: TSS is a cute investigation game where you as the titular character are hired to solve a small mystery and end up being pulled into solving a larger one.The first thing that jumps at the player is the appealing visuals. With a very colorful cartoonish style and characters that deliberately look and move as if they were cut out of paper that give the game a very distinct style. The game is also surprisingly fully voiced.The gameplay is not just regular point and click adventure fare. As you talk with characters and examine objects you gather information, which you can then use to solve clues. The game automatically gathers these, and then it's your job to figure out how to properly place them.The flip side to this is that despite the game gathering all the info for you and keeping it stored in your notebook it still expects you to pay attention. As you move around looking at stuff and talking to characters you might forget the context in which certain clues were acquired. This will undoubtedly cause some players not to fully understand how the protagonist reaches some conclusions. But the game isn't cheating, all the info is there if you're observant. Thankfully, the game allows you to properly look at the clues in their original context and interrogate characters more than once, which I suggest you do if you feel stuck rather than trying to brute-force the solutions.The one slight against the game is that it's a bit too short. It's only about 2 hours long, give or take, and it only has one ending (albeit with a couple of variations). But considering the production values and the price I think it's pretty fair. I'd still like to see more cases, whether in DLC or a sequel, because it's a fun experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: I was hoping for something cuter and more charming, similar to The Frog Detective series, but I'm not too overly disappointed with what was in this experience: wonderful voice acting, very basic but excellent graphical design choices, and, of course interesting characters with casual but somewhat deductive work required to solve the main mystery.It's only about an hour and a half long, so it's definitely something that could be expanded on in the future with different titles, perhaps with a little more difficulty for those who enjoy piecing together puzzles and investigations while remaining casual for those who prefer to play the story mode. Personally, I believe it was a little too short, but that's mostly because I'm interested in detective games that go on for about 5 hours and have many secrets woven into the main story alongside interrogations and all that stuff. If you want a more casual and cute approach, it's certainly enjoyable, but if you're looking for something with a little more depth and substance in terms of gameplay, you'd probably benefit more from a different detective game with a bit more length to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: A great detective game with game play akin to The Case of the Golden Idol. You need to figure out the clues and complete the sentences to complete the deducktion! Doing it this way is great as it strikes the perfect balance between not being too difficult while also allowing the player to use their own reasoning to piece the puzzle together themselves.The voice acting is genuinely amazing, a little over-the-top but that completely works for the wackiness of the game. I particularly enjoyed Sean Chiplock's performance as The Detective Duck, because he really sells the confident image the Duck wants to portray, while also showing that The Detective Duck seems to actually lack confidence in his abilities as a Detective.The game is full of very silly humour, which mix really well with the characters, the setting and the story.My only complaint is that there wasn't enough, I wish this had more than one case; but hopefully we'll see more of The Detective Duck in the future.Charming game, with funny dialogue, amazing cast of voice actors and solid detective gameplay! 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve seen my fair share of animal detectives over my years: Frog Detective, Chicken Police, Tails Noir, even Pikachu has found his way to sleuthing and investigating.  Most of these titles bring a certain characteristic to the table, be it charming humor, determined wit, or a real thinker of a good puzzle.  For Duck Detective: The Secret Salami, the opportunity is there to grab all three, but takes empty grasps at all of them.For Eugene McQuacklin, the road traveled has been a tough one.  Recently separated, down to his last dollar, and looming on the last hit of toast he said he wouldn’t do, the Duck Detective is contemplating selling his badge to make enough for rent.  Approaching his lowest moment, his phone rings to the tone of a concerned individual looking for a sleuthing intervention regarding…something, the detective was too busy getting out the door to take in all of what he was supposed to be there for.  But fret not!  Eugene’s powers of deduc(k)tion will help fill in the blanks and help him crack the case of the Salami Bandit!You arrive at your destination with little info but a lot of questions, and to that you’ll use your deduc(k)tion skills.  You’ll start interacting with the diverse cast of characters who are employed at the BearBus station, from giraffes to cats, buffalos and bears.  Each character is fully voiced and comes with a range of emotions on how their day-to-day is going at their workplace.  You can choose to talk to them which give you small quips on their current state, interrogate for additional details, or inspect their demeanor: all to add “clues” to your notebook to work out your deduc(k)tions.These are tackled with a fill-in-the-blank style puzzle, taking in all the clues found throughout your searches and piecing them together to get closer to solving the big puzzle.  At first these are pretty cut-and-dry and help understand the situation at hand but diving into the later puzzles where you start getting deeper into the Salami Bandit’s hands the expectations of piecing these together become a little tedious due to how open some of the deduc(k)tions are.  The beginning ones may have 2-4 gaps in the puzzle, but the later ones have you almost completing whole sentences with nearly 30 words to choose from that could realistically fit multiple scenarios though you’re only needed for one specific detail.  It becomes less of an A-Ha moment and moves to jamming square pegs into round holes to figure out exactly which part they want you to talk about.The whole case runs a little over 2 hours which I felt was a fair amount of time to dedicate grilling six different staff members and investigating clues in essentially 4 rooms worth of content.  Some of the puzzles outside the deduc(k)tions were very clever, specifically finding out Margret’s work computer password, but there were very few of these to chew on outside of the heavily leaned on fill-in-the-blank criteria.Where most titles within this genre find a niche to latch on to like explained before, the problem I found with Duck Detective is that it doesn’t quite hit any of the goals you would expect from this kind of game.  There were very few humorous bits to progress the character traits and motives, the flexing of your brain muscles never really hit a good elasticity as the puzzles are either cut and dry or do too much to be obtuse, and the wit from the main detective doesn’t carry enough to feel motivated to push through this case to its fullest.  There is a good foundation with the art, style, and presentation, but if there ever becomes more of the Duck Detective, and I do hope there is, it will need to pick what style of detective it wants to be and to stick the landing like I’m sure it can.  Otherwise this detective might be the thing it’s trying so hard to stay away from: Toast.

_childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami is a delightfully charming game that’s short, sweet and leaves you craving for more.First off, the voice acting for this game is phenomenally well done and adds so much enjoyment to the experience. The delivery of each and every line is fantastic and the dialogue itself is quite witty and fun. I cannot praise the voice acting and dialogue enough, it definitely boosts the entertainment factor of the game.Next, the art design in this game is simplistic and carries a lot of personality. I’m a sucker for art styles like this. The 2D characters move in a cute, choppy manner on a 3D background that blends together quite nicely. The environment is filled with bits and bobs you can investigate for clues, but doesn’t feel cluttered or jarring either.The story is actually a lot deeper than I expected it to be and that’s not a bad thing. I was lured in thinking this would be a simple case of silly office drama and was surprised at how much more there was beneath the surface. You do have to dig around a bit and do some critical thinking to see the bigger picture, but there’s a story mode that makes uncovering the plot a lot easier if you’re not into deductive reasoning and connecting the dots.The music direction was fun and enjoyable. It conveyed each scene well and contributed to the positive experience. I do appreciate the fact that the music isn’t distracting in any way. It may not be super memorable, but the fact that it set the ambiance without being chaotic and overwhelming is nice.The way the characters are portrayed is also quite nice. No, they aren’t really deep by any means and most of them do embody typical office tropes, but you do catch a glimpse into their personal lives in the information you glean from your surroundings. I think there’s enough variety in their personalities and design to make each one stand out in their own way.The lead, the aforementioned Duck Detective himself, is a wonderful protagonist. He’s very likable and makes you want to root for his success. He also has several relatable aspects to him that I think many people can identify with. He may not be perfect, but he’s definitely a good guy just trying to get by.I absolutely enjoyed collecting clues by investigating the area and questioning the characters. You basically collect clues and then piece together deductions by filling in the blanks. I will say that sometimes putting the clues together in a way that makes sense can be slightly difficult if you’re missing any relevant information, so make sure to go back and check areas and speak to characters every so often for new information.While the duration of this game is quite short, I don’t actually think that works against it. It’s something you can do in one sitting and the achievements aren’t difficult to get. I absolutely would have enjoyed it even more if it was longer, but I’d also be worried that if it was too drawn out it might dampen the overall experience. It doesn’t overstay it’s welcome, so to speak.The price point is fair, in my opinion anyway, for the product you’re receiving. I don’t have any real issues with the game’s performance and I played it on my Steam Deck. As I said above, it’s a short experience, but I consider this an investment of what’s to come. I can only hope there are more installments of Duck Detective in the works because I would gladly pay more for a longer game with multiple cases to solve.Finally, there’s a dedicated quack button and that is just fantastic.I hope this review was helpful to anyone on the fence about getting the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective is such a charming and fun little adventure to play through. From the art style, music, as well as the writing, the game is teeming with personality. And while I do have some issues with the product, it's an absolute treat from beginning to end.To begin, the visuals and music. They really drag you into the experience. The art style is unique as well. It certainly made everything pop when you're playing the game. How transitions would dim the lighting to give off that noir style. The music just aids completely in making you immersed into this world. Or, the world of duck detective. Despite how ridiculous the set-up is, the main character keeps things grounded to a point. It made me smile seeing this journey continue to grow as we investigated, all while playing as a gruff duck who's down on his luck. The music, sound design, art; everything works to engross you into this world.The story is simple, but did grow to be something fun. Though once pieces start falling into place, it does become fairly obvious what is going on. But the discovery prior I found to be lovely. In addition, the writing itself is teeming with personality. Every character felt alive in the world, especially the main character. I wish there was more interaction in terms of talking with the other characters, but the main writing was good.The gameplay is where my only big conflict comes in. You investigate and find key words. Then, using what words you find, you solve the mysteries to move along the plot. I think the system is very cute, but it does leave me wanting more. For example, there is no fail state, or penalties, for forcing one of the mysteries. Because the game tells you what words are generally incorrect, it gives you a guide to brute force all of the puzzles. In addition, there is nothing stopping you from doing this. Personally, not sure what could be a solution since this does suit the lighter gameplay throughout. But it did leaving  a lacking impression on me as I played through the game.Outside of that, I lovely the aspect of roaming around the little environment. I adored how you could look clues over and get more information out of that. How characters names weren't given and you needed to piece them together through the clues you collected. I just wish, in addition, there was a little more to explore and maybe just more interaction with other characters.Despite that issue, the game is lovely. For $9.99, it's at the perfect price to pick up and play through. The game is also fairly short, sitting my playtime at 2 hours. A perfect little gem that came out in a year full of incredible titles, thus far. If you find yourself a little interested, absolutely pick this game up!

_childDocuments_.review: A recently relapsed bread junkie is two months late on rent and spends his evenings pining for his recently divorced wife. Desperate to make ends meet while wallowing in his depression, he gets a call for a job and steps into his Duck Detective shoes. As he arrives at the workplace of his client, he realizes the colorful cast of suspects hide even more crimes beyond a missing lunch.Duck Detective is an investigation game where you guide the eponymous character through the headquarters of a bus service. Explore the scene while examining suspects (both verbally and visually) and delving through the clues strewn across the messy workplace. As you do, you'll collect little 'word bubbles' to organize your thoughts, similar to The Case of the Golden Idol. You take these individual thoughts and organize them to fill in the blanks of the questions asked during investigation, from discovering who your initial client is along with their coworkers to the true events that led to the initial crime being committed.The game is visually pleasant and fun. The environments are vivid and the little interactions with it (like knocking over a pencil holder to the rain effects) makes it exude a jovial charm that is simple but fulfilling. The characters are similarly cute and cheerful, with both simple sprites and more detailed representations. While they don't do more than waddle around physically, the voice acting really elevates the designs. I don't think there is a dud in the cast (love Laura's manicness). The deductions themselves are pretty simple, much easier than Obra Dinn's sprawling 9 chapter mystery. The game is fairly short and the clues are flagged in game so there isn't any need for pixel hunting or accidentally missing one. I did like how each item investigation did a short little deduction train (tanline on the ring finger -> missing wedding ring -> divorced?) as it helped convey our Duck Detective is actually somewhat competent rather than a bumbling fool who accidentally gets things right.The one thing that irked me was the end, where we HAD to pin a crime on someone. There were several crimes, but we only had to arrest someone for one of them . We could arrest multiple people, but we HAD to arrest at least one. The only other "bad" thing is that its so short. I would have loved three or more cases, especially if they were all this high quality.Overall, 9/10 game. 3 hour timespan for $10 is pretty good, and I hope we get a sequel (hopefully longer).

_childDocuments_.review: Whoever voiced The Detective Duck did a phenomenal job. "Detective Duck" is an enjoyable and humorous detective game with puzzles that are challenging, but not overly difficult, making it accessible to a wide audience. The game starts with a simple premise: solving the case of a stolen lunch. However, this seemingly trivial investigation soon leads Detective Duck into uncovering a much more serious crime.The voice acting, particularly that of Detective Duck, adds an extra layer of charm and immersion to the game. Each character has a distinct personality, and their interactions are often hilarious, keeping the tone light-hearted despite the criminal undertones.The puzzles in the game are well-designed, striking a balance between being thought-provoking and fair. They require keen observation and logical thinking, but they never become frustratingly difficult. As you gather clues and piece together the mystery, the sense of accomplishment is immensely satisfying.The storyline, while initially appearing simple, unfolds into a complex narrative with unexpected twists and turns. The case of the stolen lunch is just the tip of the iceberg, and as you delve deeper, you uncover a web of deceit and intrigue that keeps you hooked until the very end."Detective Duck" is not just a game; it’s an experience that combines humor, mystery, and engaging gameplay. Whether you are a fan of detective stories or just looking for a fun game to pass the time, "Detective Duck" is sure to entertain.

_childDocuments_.review: Stylish detective game, similar to  in its deduction systems, but with a unique pun-packed noir aesthetic. _childDocuments_.review: Despite the short playtime of this game, it's very well worth the full price!You play as Eugene McQuacklin, a private investigator set out to uncover the mystery of the missing salami. You interview a colorful cast of characters, taking their statements and using your keen eyes of observation to come to conclusions about what is happening around you, finding different items and keywords to take note of in your journal, solving the mystery piece by piece.The story is unique and engaging, all the characters are fun and memorable, and the voice acting is just phenomenal! I still find myself quoting the game's funny dialogue even today. "ANA! I'm a different duck now! I haven't had a slice of bread in weeks! YOU HAVE TO BELIEVE ME!"The art style is a mixture of 2D cutouts in 3D environments, a combination which I find myself loving as more games of this style come out and in this game it works very well, with the cartoony Duck Detective waddling along the vibrant and detailed areas of the Bear Bus office.The soundtrack has the perfect blend of film noir style jazzy tunes, fitting for the overall mood of the game as you uncover the mystery with the down on his luck P.I. protagonist.Some of the puzzles near the end of the game made me have to try to brute force through a few of them a bit, but overall the puzzles are pretty simple and fun to figure out.Highly recommended! This is one of the few point and click adventure games that has come in recent years that is an instant classic and honestly I am DYING for a sequel or at least a DLC for more de-ducktions! Also, check out the studio's other game Kraken Academy! I played it after playing through Duck Detective, and while the two games are quite different thematically, both of them are very fun and engaging with unique storylines that leave you wanting for more!

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, but I can't recommend it. a lot of people want a sequel and I do to, but I probably wouldn't buy one... why? this game has fun and unique (to me at least) little puzzles for solving the plot points and continuing forward on the mystery front, but there's very little challenge. not the worst thing in the world, certainly better than having too obscure of clues for people to find or making connections that beggar belief. but the simplicity and briefness mixed with the quality voice acting and fully developed art style left me feeling like I had played a demo of a much larger game, but I already bought it... and I finished it in one play session...which brings me to why I probably wouldn't buy a sequel or more follow-up games, if this was level one of 4-5 levels in a ~$30 game I would probably be giving it rave reviews, but being game one in a 4-5 game series... I couldn't invest my time into game 2 without knowing for sure that games 3 through 5 were coming out and I would have some sort of satisfaction or overarching story to care about. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that, while I've had a Steam account for about 10 years, I've played a grand total of 4 games on it. Once I got into MMORPGs, I didn't really have much time to spare for games outside of the one I was playing at the game. However, I watched a YouTube video (by Pushing Up Roses) about how cute this game was, and I just so happened to have a few weeks of extra time, so I thought I'd give it a shot. She wasn't wrong in her assessment that this is one of the cutest mystery games ever! The artwork is adorable, and the voice acting fit each character so well and really brought them to life. And I was pleased when I found out that all those trash cans I'd been knocking over for fun were actually part of an achievement, though I'm surprised there was nothing for all the water bottles scattered about...I will say, as someone who likes puzzles but doesn't have much experience with them, I did struggle a bit with this game. There were times when I was just going back and forth between characters and clickable items trying to figure out what to do, because I knew I hadn't gathered all the clues yet, but couldn't figure out what I was missing. And there were a few puzzles where I had solved it correctly, but didn't put in *quite* the write word ("message" vs "letter," for example). I did have to consult a guide a few times, and it was a bit frustrating knowing how close I was to solving it, but I was just one word off.However, I feel like most people who have experience with this type of game will probably not struggle as much as I did with the UI or the fill-in-the-blanks, and despite my troubles, I did really enjoy the game :) Overall, I recommend this game for people who have some experience in puzzle games, but you definitely don't need to be an ace detective to enjoy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and sometimes funny, and always full of personality.Every character has an instantly identifiable archetype — but not without some nuance, as you will discover while spending more time interacting with them and investigating. In particular, I love Laura's and the titular Duck Detective's voices and dialogue. Both voice actors add so much detail to their characters' emotions and I had a lot of fun.The 'fill in the blanks' way of solving mysteries is great at preventing brute force trial and error guesses, but its implementation in this game can be confusing to play. For two of the later Deducktions, ~80% of the text were blanks and I had to guess a bit.Though the header of the Deducktion tells you what the Deducktion is about, it can still be confusing — and not in the puzzling kind of way, it's the '100-pieces jigsaw puzzle of the sky' kind of lost.Overall, it's a great detective game and I recommend this game. Looking forward to more mysteries with McQuacklin!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, snacky (pun very much intended) little game, well-worth the $10 pricetag for ~5 hours of wholesome deducktions.  Gameplay consists of interviewing suspects, investigating clues, and then correctly filling out a Mad Libs-style section in your notebook describing what has occurred.  The art style is simple but effective, and the voice acting, especially that of the titular detective, is greatly entertaining.  My one regret is that there is just the one case to solve.  Here's hoping Happy Broccoli will put out a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a recently divorced bread addicted duck detective who just received a job from a mysterious client to solve the most important of all cases: WHO STOLE THE LUNCH in the office fridge. But, soon you will realise the plot is much thicker than a regular sandwich.This is a very short detective game with excellent voice acting and actually rather amusing story. It's very short and could be completed in about an hour and a half. It's a bit expensive for the game time, but it's very fun and I hope we will get sequels.
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun, but rather short detective game. The gameplay and controlls are quite intuitive (you even have a QUACK button!) and the puzzles are fun to solve and logical, but also not too easy. The zoom mechanic was pretty fun to discover some of the character's details too!I love that the game is fully voiced! Always nice and appreciated if you don't have to read through tons of dialouges and it also adds to the character design and the overall atmosphere, if you actually hear the characters talk.I'd love to play a sequel of it at some point, if the devs have any plans for it!
_childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: Duck Detective is a fun, cozy indie game that hooked me with its quirky humor and charming character designs. _childDocuments_.name: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazing one off story, beautifully written, voice acted and puns a plenty."The early bird always catches the criminal and this case isn't always gonna be a walk in the pond."Contained in one big story the Duck Detective leads out for hopefully an express mystery over stolen lunch but all is not what it appears. What's hiding behind the charade of this failing bus service, could the lazy crocodile who steals everyones mugs be in on it or has the overworked cat been taken advantage of for too long?Solving each case is such a terrific experience, each discovery is interlinked between the characters and offers comedy throughout, if it's not the Detectives inner monologue it's secret messages between the computers, post-it notes on the noticeboard or complaints in the suggestion box.Truly a remarkable puzzle to solve and fully engaging whether you take it on the storymode or experience detective mode for something a little more challenging.Would love to see sequels of the Duck Detective in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Feeling mixed on this one, probably due to my high expectations, but it's certainly worth the $10.Story - 5/10 - With a name like "Secret Salami" I expected something a bit more satirical and over the top.Gameplay - 7/10 - I enjoyed the mechanics of uncovering clues.Sound and Music - 6/10 - The music was great, but the voices were hit and miss for me. name: Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit
detailed_description: Jump into the pit and immerse yourself in a new chapter in the Five Nights at Freddy’s universe. Oswald wishes his town, and his life, weren’t so boring. That all changes when he explores the ball pit in a rundown pizzeria and finds himself in the past. However, Oswald’s deepest desire will have an unexpected cost… Survive five nights of terror in this chilling adventure game. Travel between time periods, gather clues, and outrun the threat relentlessly pursuing you. Move swiftly and stay hidden, and you may just survive. But be careful—it’s not just your own life that’s on the line. Oswald’s father and children from the past could all meet their end if you don’t save them. KEY FEATURES Experience the heart-pounding adventure of a beloved entry in the Five Nights at Freddy’s franchise, Into the Pit. Solve satisfying puzzles intertwined with an adrenaline-fueled story. Immerse yourself in a narrative experience. Try to save your friends, your family, and your own life. Uncover secrets that span decades. Discover different endings. Escape the clutches of the animatronic creatures wreaking havoc across time.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has been a FNAF fan since I was literally 10 (via watching gameplay and now that I'm an adult playing some of the games myself), I say this game is awesome. The pixel art is amazing, the music and sound effects are good, and there is references literally everywhere. Also, a shout-out to how quickly the devs respond to bugs.I really liked this and hope that there are more games based on the books in the future because this was super cool!

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly well made, the art style and animation truly are one of a kind. It's smooth, and has been eye candy for me my entire playthrough. _childDocuments_.review: FNAF meeting Clock Tower is something I never knew I needed. A very interesting game, especially with the secrets throughout. However it's a little questionable how you have to beat the game once to unlock the 2 harder difficulties. I think the third difficulty should have been unlocked from the start as you may want a challenge at the start that the base 2 difficulties can't provide. But the amount of customization with the difficulties, even down to disabling a specific alarm is such a great idea, providing you with your own "custom night" here. Would be down for another game like this in the future, especially if we can get more unique perspectives in this universe like maybe playing a day guard for once.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Very good graphics, everything about the game looks really good and I just adore the pixel style they usedCreepy, not the scariest Fnaf game you can find, but is scary at some moments.I really enjoy repairing and playing the arcade machinesBuilds on what was in the original book in a very good wayAnd overall just a fun fnaf experienceCons:1: Some fetch quests, doesn't ruin the game, but I still wish they weren't there. The main ones I'm talking about being the get the Teacher's book fetch quest that means nothing. And the distracting Jeff mission, to find a rat trap, to catch a rat, show the rat to the customer, and then you can continue with the game2: The animatronics in the game don't do much, I don't think we ever even see Foxy, and Freddy and Bonnie don't do much, and Chica just has the abilities of a Staff Bot from Security BreachOverall, a great game to celebrate fnaf's 10 year anniversary!
_childDocuments_.name: Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: Only about halfway through the game but absolutely love it. Great FNAF game, very new and different. Great for gamers looking for a more old school style scary game. Much scarier than Security Breach and on par with the originals. Similar to sister location in the sense that each night duration is not defined by time, but instead by task. However I am enjoying myself far more with this game than Sister Location. The jumpscares themselves are not the scariest, but the suspenseful lead ups are. The constant paranoia causes for an on edge experiance. Love the art style and the controls are very refined. Even with the 16-bit graphics, you can tell so much work was put into this game. I can already see myself replaying this game over and over to beat the game on every difficulty as well as getting every acheviment. The long time fans will have their minds blown with the references to the lore, however that knowledge is not required to have a great time playing.l Perfect for newcomers and veterans to the FNAF franchise, very unique but I am welcoming it with open arms, hope we get more games like this one!

_childDocuments_.review: This game came literally out of nowhere for me and was an incredibly welcome surprise into the FNAF lineup. I cannot get over how freaking GOOD the environment is in this game, especially in the Pizzeria. It's very similar to the sounds and feeling I have at the Pizzeria I work at and I felt just so totally engrossed. Kudos for that!The gameplay itself is a bit of a refreshing take compared to what the series is used to and the pixel art is absolutely gorgeous. I have not read the book this game is based on, but I felt like I didn't need to to enjoy it and the story. This has quickly become one of my top favorites in the franchise. While it's also a short game, taking me about 5 hours to complete while also exploring my first time, there's reason to start multiple playthroughs as there's plenty to offer for various secrets and endings to find. Kudos to the development team! Hope to see more FNAF games from you all.

_childDocuments_.review: I lost my money to have this game for me and my friemd and honestly I am not really happy about it. The whole game is just about doing random uninteresting stuff while going from point A to point B. Ain't really funny, yk? Not to mention that I got scared only one time in this "horror game". Graphics are great, I agree, but the story is weird and does not really fit to FNaF, especially this time travel bullcrap or whatever it was. Speaking of music, well, it's fine, it's not very good, but ain't bad, music here is just okay, imo the best one track was in the puzzle solve mini-game.This game isn't terrible, but it ain't that great, I'd give it, like, 5/10, mostly because of graphics. If I could get my money back, I'd def do it.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so this is a semi review mostly just my thoughts on the game.Personally don't care for the story I've never read any of the fazbear frights books but I still love the idea of this innocent child jumps into a pit and comes out with his father replaced with daddy springtrap. The game has incredible Pixel art with the animatronics and the pizzaria as a whole. The human character feel a little off especially Oswald but it's just my own personal preference.The games atmosphere is incredible but it loses it's pressure the more you play but that is ultimately due to something I've noticed during my third replay Springtrap is incredibly dumb.I also don't think the higher difficulties removing hiding spots really helps with that feeling honestly it feels kind of cheap. Springtrap can lose you when you hide mere meters from him and left to do a mini-game which get quite boring after the repetition of the game sets in.I also think the first play-through doesn't use Freddy or Bonnie enough being only rare occurrences. Something I have to give credit for is the fact you can make your own custom difficulties from the aggression of chica and springtrap to the chance of Bonnie and Freddy messing with you. The difficulties of the mini-games, the battery life, if you get warnings of springtrap entering rooms and if you can use hiding spots and noises giving the player the power to make their own into the pit play-through adds so much repeatability for those looking for a challenge.Something I think would've been cool is like Resident Evil games when you complete the game on a higher difficulties you get cheat codes you can use in another play-through. Maybe springtrap is really tiny or maybe you run twice as fast something simple like that would bring a new level of fun.The game is incredibly short though which I think is a good and bad thing. It's good because you can replay it more but bad because the casual player will not get their Moneysworth. But overall as someone who dropped Fnaf after 3 and disliked SB/Ruin I think this is a great step forward.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished Five Night's At Freddy's Into the Pit, here's my review:As someone who have read the book and fell in love with the into the pit story line, I knew whenever I saw the trailer wile back. I said to myself I NEEED THAT.Now having played through the game + did a couple of endings (will explore more) I think the game is fantastic. I love the art style, the 8 bit, 2d look and game play is great. It has tons of content, even when you complete the game. I am looking for all achievements, secrets, alternative ending and there is an extras tab.A lot of the game play involves hiding and running from "The Rabbit", I found this very stressful and fun. I also love how open it feels. There are many different places you can go to, even though most of them aren't usable, until it shows up on your "Quest tab". I want to say a great job the team of mega cat studios, y'all did a phenomenal job capturing the essence and atmosphere of 'Into the pit'.I found a few bugs here and there.Example: after I saved a kid and it told me to go to the entrance, I got killed. I respawned and I went there and no one was there, So I had to jump in and out of the ball pit. Which was annoying.I also want to say that I experienced a bit of lag in the ending. It might just be my interview but as far as I know I should have a stable network.

_childDocuments_.review: In my first hour of gameplay I was not prepared for the sight of a crying kid crammed into an endoskeleton, head exposed begging to be let free. This game has the most visual storytelling and structural storytelling of a FNAF title and all the little nods, winks and callbacks to other FNAF media helps translate this book’s story in ways it deserves I really want to see more games like this and I want more FNAF games in a bold and charming artstyle like this that’s so fitting for the time period which the games are based within. This feels like a fan game in all the right ways - FNAF’s Sonic Mania and Into the Pit is a great example that maturer fear still works in modern FNAFAlso plays really well on the steam deck, good job on the optimisation!

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly hooking for a FNAF game. It's not "scary" but FNAF never was to me. The game's not too overwhelmingly gigantic and doesn't become super difficult, making it more fit for players of all kinds. It's also pretty easy to 100% the game and get all 3 stars, which makes it more welcoming. The art style and the story it tells are wonderfully made. Also there's a cat.Issue: Getting most endings require you to look up guides. The things you need to do for that just don't make any sense and there's no way someone would just stumble on those on their own without having seen guides or videos of people playing it beforehand. I think games where you need to rummage through the files and data to be able to beat it are counterproductive and not what a game should be.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I don't have any dislike for the franchise or anything. I'm just one of the few that don't get how cheap jump scares that don't actually scare you are considered fun or thrilling as someone who prefers titles like System Shock, SOMA, and many other atmospheric horror elements that get your heart pounding and keep you on edge without doing any of that.I've never bothered to play through prior FNAF titles because I've seen others do so and it was only capable of making you feel on edge for a short period of time before becoming frustrating rather than thrilling and entertaining for the harder nights. If it makes sense, it felt more interesting to watch someone else play it than to play it yourself because that was exciting.  In my perspective, FNAF Into the Pit fails in a number of areas. The gameplay is quite simple: run, hide, retrieve, and escape. There isn't much else to it; the mini-games are relatively empty, the ambience is a little weak, and the only thing that really jumps out is the beautiful pixelated graphics and it doesn't feel like they do a whole lot with it as a leading element. Unless you're a die-hard FNAF fan who is deeply invested in the rich lore created by Game Theory, Markiplier, and the fandom as a whole, I don't see much here to be excited about. It's an overhyped franchise, yet it resonates with a lot of people these days. I would consider sudden loud noises and cheap jump scares to be complete garbage because they aren't really authentic when it comes to horror. Almost every game is the same, same style, same gameplay, same over-hyped median. It's very short and didn't feel all that fulfilling.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent pixel artwork with impressively fluid movements and animations for what is commonly known to be a choppy, skippy style inherently due to the classic limitations of the generations-old pixel art that was the pinnacle of our abilities. The controls are simple and the hiding mini-games are stressful in a good way. This game breathes a little bit of fear back into the franchise notorious for losing that scary whimsy after the first hour of static image jumps-cares. Not a huge game, but likely secretly huge thanks to yet to be discovered lore and secrets...like interacting with a candy machine 100 times for about 5 hidden messages and a secret mini-game like the FNAF games of old. The audio design is outright disturbing...ly good. Proper sound design is a key element of any horror media and they include accessibility for the hearing impaired for these important cues as well. CANDYCANDYCANDY

_childDocuments_.review: Solid horror game with stealth elements. Sound does a solid job of tracking which direction nasty things are in and when they're on the move. Rewards patient play without forcing you to sit and wait for minutes on end.Various optional minigames were a nice diversion. Story is nice, without getting in the way of gameplay. Encountered no bugs or roadblocks, and didn't have to grind away at any particular section just to get through it. Curious to see how the higher difficulties change that, but glad that people don't have to get frustrated over RNG-based gameplay just to reach the end.The audiovisual side is fantastic. _childDocuments_.review: Into the pit feels like what ive been waiting for from the series for a while. the gameplay, while not necisarily hard, is engaging and puts up enough of a challenge to keep you on your seat regardless of how skilled you are. i think this is probably the first FNAF game ive found to be re-playable outside of a yearly visit. not just because of the gameplay but the surprising variety of customization there is to the difficulty settings you get after your fist playthrough. ive already had three playthroughs and ill probably play it more in the near future. thats all also not taking into account the secrets and side stuff ether by the way. One issue i always had with starting a fresh Freddy save is how boring it can be replaying early nights, a feeling that gets worst as your understanding of the game grows. but with this game, each situation is a little different while still having a difficulty curve. earlier levels have less characters, but have more areas locked off, making the threat still present if much more manageable compared to later levels. the fact the custom difficulty options apply to the entire game and not just a single night like in the past makes this really a treat to play. i can see the challenge community getting alot out of this. couple that with good visuals and an amazing ability to make you on edge throughout its runtime some seriously tense moments, and i genuinely believe your into this franchise this is a must play. i hope mega cats makes more freddys games like this cause it feels the work really well with the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit is a pixel art gem that delivers far more than its simple aesthetic suggests. The game's environments are meticulously crafted, creating an atmosphere that's both nostalgic and unsettling. What starts as a straightforward adventure quickly reveals itself to be an expansive thriller, packed with secrets, collectibles, and varied challenges that keep you on edge. The ability to customize difficulty levels adds another layer of depth, making each playthrough unique. Whether you're a fan of the series or new to it, Into the Pit is an engaging experience that proves a 2D game can be just as immersive and thrilling as any 3D counterpart.
_childDocuments_.name: Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best FNaF games of recent times. As an avid fan of this series I have been excited for this one, and I am pleased it proved worth the wait! The animation is fluid and the pixel art is beautiful. It has great gameplay and feels very satisfying. It is the perfect mix of difficulty, so you have to think to figure out what to do, without being impossible to play. The immense amount of easter eggs this game is so fun to see, and it is very re-playable. The pacing feels great, and the story is a great adaptation of the original novel. It is also actually pretty suspenseful, and I am often surprised by jumpscares, which is a rarity for me. It is a breath of fresh air in this franchise, and I highly recommend it. I hope MegaCat Studios keeps working with this franchise, I would definitely play more Fazbear Frights stories!

But it does leave some to be desired, like the sounds being too hard to discern with how the music amps up when you just need to listen the footsteps and the doors opening and closing. _childDocuments_.review: Generic "look for things and hide from the roaming monster" survival horror game glazed in a unique 2D perspective and a good art style. I'm not a huge fan of the genre but it was ok. There was a bug for a lot of people (including me) that prevented you from progressing in literally the last 5 minutes of the game. It's fixed now but it was very annoying having to wait hours for a fix so I could finish the game.Pros:2D works surprisingly well for a survival horror game.Graphics are really nice, especially the more detailed cutscenes.Great sound design to know where the enemies are.Loads of minigames.Very organic tutorial that gets you into the main game quickly.Cons:Very generic repetitive survival horror gameplay.Some objectives are poorly designed, at one point you need to capture a rat and an npc tells you that Jeff's Pizza is full of them. So you go get a rat from Jeff's, right? Wrong, it's in Freddy Fazbear's for some reason. Why have the npc point you in the wrong direction? It's annoying.The true ending is too obscure to discover without a guide, someone has to have datamined one of the steps, it's so random.Two of the threats get removed near the end of the game, why is the last level easier?Eleanor narrating the trailer is just clickbait, this game has nothing to do with her.No Foxy, could they not think of one more unique mechanic? They could have made him chase you at random points during the night.6/10, decent game for the price

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the best FNaF game we've recieved in years. I love the gameplay, the puzzles felt very well put together and even though it would take me a while to solve, I managed to do figure everything out myself on my first playthrough after thinking on it for a while which is always a good sign. The game has so much love and care put into every inch of it. From being able to play the arcade machines to finally getting to see one of the most iconic FNaF events in history up close, this game has it all! You can even find a few hidden secrets about some pretty big FNaF characters. I'm personally a huge fan of the books so all of the references to other books was cool but even if you haven't read any of the books the game still is engaging and references other parts of the franchise a lot! This game is by no means dependent on you reading or even enjoying the original Into the Pit story. If you're a huge FNaF fan, this game will feel like a dream come true with all sorts of references and secrets and if this is your first FNaF game, it'll be a wonderful introduction to this world and some of the mysteries this franchise has to offer. A stellar game that makes me incredibly excited for the future FNaF games from Mega Cat Studios

_childDocuments_.review: Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit - An In-Depth ReviewIntroduction"Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit" marks another chapter in the expansive lore of Scott Cawthon's Five Nights at Freddy's universe. This book, written by Scott Cawthon and Kira Breed-Wrisley, is part of the FNaF series of novels aimed at expanding the terrifying world of animatronics and hidden horrors. Released in 2019, it delves into the story of a young boy named Oswald, who finds himself entangled in a nightmarish adventure that intertwines with the eerie lore of Freddy Fazbear’s Pizza.Plot OverviewThe story follows Oswald "Ozzy" Kincaid, a twelve-year-old boy who feels isolated and overlooked in his daily life. His father is always away on business, and his mother is too busy with her own issues to pay him much attention. Ozzy finds solace in a dilapidated local arcade where he discovers a mysterious ball pit. When he ventures into this ball pit, he is transported to different times and places, each associated with the nightmarish animatronics from Freddy Fazbear's Pizza.As Ozzy navigates these different environments, he encounters various characters and situations, each revealing more about the dark history of the animatronics and the sinister events tied to them. His quest is not only a fight for survival but also a journey to uncover the truth about his own family and the connection between his life and the eerie events surrounding the ball pit.CharactersOswald "Ozzy" Kincaid: The protagonist, Ozzy is a relatable young boy grappling with feelings of abandonment and the fear of the unknown. His character development is significant as he transforms from a passive observer to an active participant in his own fate. Ozzy’s resilience and bravery are tested throughout the story, and his growth is a central theme.The Animatronics: As with the games, the animatronics in "Into the Pit" are more than just mechanical monsters. They embody the haunted spirits and tragic stories of those who once interacted with them. Each animatronic, from the familiar Freddy Fazbear to lesser-known entities, brings a unique horror element to the narrative.Supporting Characters: The secondary characters, including Ozzy’s family and the individuals he meets in the various timelines, serve to enrich the story. They provide context to the animatronics' backstory and help to unravel the mystery surrounding the ball pit and its connection to Freddy Fazbear's Pizza.ThemesIsolation and Belonging: A recurring theme in the novel is Ozzy’s struggle with feeling isolated. His journey through the ball pit becomes a metaphor for his quest to find a place where he belongs and to understand his place within his family and the broader world.The Past’s Impact on the Present: The novel explores how past events, particularly those involving trauma and violence, have lasting effects on individuals and their environments. The animatronics are a manifestation of this theme, with their haunting presence reflecting the unresolved issues of their past.Courage in the Face of Fear: Ozzy’s courage is tested repeatedly as he faces terrifying situations. The novel highlights the idea that true bravery is not the absence of fear but the ability to confront and overcome it.Atmosphere and Setting"Into the Pit" excels in creating a chilling and immersive atmosphere. The settings are vividly described, from the rundown arcade to the eerie, time-traveling locales. The sense of dread is palpable, and the novel effectively builds tension through its detailed descriptions and suspenseful scenes. The shifting settings keep the reader on edge, as each new location introduces fresh horrors and challenges.Writing StyleThe writing style is engaging and accessible, making it suitable for both younger readers and long-time fans of the series. The prose is straightforward yet effective in building tension and conveying the eerie atmosphere. The alternating perspectives and time periods add depth to the narrative, although some readers may find the shifts between timelines a bit disorienting at times.Conclusion"Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit" is a compelling addition to the FNaF universe that successfully combines elements of horror, mystery, and adventure. It offers a gripping narrative that explores themes of isolation, courage, and the haunting impact of the past. The novel’s atmospheric setting and well-developed characters make it a worthy read for fans of the series and newcomers alike. While it may rely on some familiar tropes and can be complex in its timeline shifts, it ultimately delivers a satisfying and suspenseful story that enhances the lore of the Five Nights at Freddy’s franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: While Five Night's at Freddy's: Into the Pit may look like a dinky NES game with no depth or longevity, it's actually one of the best entries in the entire FNAF series. It has linear objectives but an open world with numerous areas to explore to some extent depending on your progress and the time of day. There are arcade-like minigames that can be found at the pizzeria provided you've repaired the arcade cabinet, each of which aren't super long but can make for a fun break in between quests. The story is fairly short, taking just a few hours, or longer if you decide to do some exploring which I highly recommend. The story is solid which is a relief as that's a large part of what keeps us coming back. There are countless difficulty options and game settings to play around with to make for a truly unique experience each time you play through. All in all, I highly recommend you give the game a shot and I hope you enjoy it as much as I do. Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Overall very polished and wonderful game, and spooky too! Took me back to the feel of playing horror games from 10-15+ years ago. If you rush the game, you will complete it in about 4hrs, but as someone who has taken my time to explore all options, find all "side objectives", and stealth through the game properly, I've more than doubled the gameplay time just doing the main story once (and I'm going back to try to find the secrets and alternate endings now as well!).Full review (mild maybe-spoilers only if you know the book - I'm not going into detail at all though):I love this game! The art and overall adaptation is great. The story and gameplay loop works really well, and I was surprised to see how they were able to seamlessly "translate" the book to game form with minor (imo), but intelligent changes that keep the core story and flow intact while turning what would be a fairly mundane story into something engaging for gameplay.The sound design is also fantastic, aside from the occasional "intense music" being a bit too loud. You need to listen closely to more easily traverse the "spooky sections", and sometimes the music that intends to create tension is more annoying than anything, as it makes hearing footsteps difficult. It is very easy to tell the distance and direction of said footsteps to help you comfortably navigate threats, unless you're feeling brave.There is plenty of hidden mini games and secrets to uncover, at least 5 endings, and 2 more difficulty modes to unlock once you beat the story once (with sliders for the enemies to adjust the game to your own liking if you'd prefer that as well)! Nightmare mode is a proper hardcore mode that resets you to the beginning if you die, and also takes away a lot of your hiding places, while making the AI more aggressive.

_childDocuments_.review: Into The Pit, like most Five Nights at Freddy's titles, is more so an experience than a game. While it has game elements, it is its narrative, told through environmental cues, dialogue, minigames, and especially secrets, that pull you in.If you don't know or don't care about FNAF, Into The Pit is a decent side-scrolling adventure game with a simple, yet compelling story and charming aesthetics. It has a beginning, middle and an end, it has a satisfying gameplay loop that gradually grows in difficulty as you advance in the 5-nights week, and it has multiple endings for those who enjoy looking for them.If you happen to be a FNAF fan, this game is a delightful fan-service. Seeing the now iconic characters in a different medium is exciting, there are references to multiple FNAF titles, and lots of interesting secrets to uncover, including a potential clue as to the next Mega Cat FNAF game, likely based on another FNAF novel--something that was also hinted by the original creator, Scott Cawthon. The perspective of running from the animatronics, rather than defending yourself against them in a static place, is a welcome change from the original formula.The game starts to show its kinks if you are a completionist and you seek to conquer all its achievements, as this will require multiple playthroughs that are repetitive in nature. While the difficulty ramps up considerably, the same starting principles apply throughout the achievement hunting, and winning or losing becomes more influenced by luck, rather than skill. A few bugs may also surprise you at inconvenient times, possibly cutting back some of your progress. After 16 hours and 5 complete playthroughs, I was able to get all the achievements, but there is no way any one player will be able to do it all without looking up a guide on a couple of issues. Much like the original FNAF titles, this one has incredibly obscure secret requirements to achieve certain endings and conditions that I cannot fathom how the playerbase managed to encounter them, let alone in such a short amount of time (within a day of its release).While I can see some extra unrealized potential with the concepts utilized in its design, Into The Pit was a thoroughly enjoyable addition to the Five Nights at Freddy's franchise, and I am most happy that it's still possible to experience the series' universe in new and refreshing ways. If you enjoy games of this kind, and especially if you are FNAF fan, this game is worth a try.
