_childDocuments_.review: Full Review (No Game or Book Spoilers):As a huge FNAF fan (it’s been 10 years, I'm getting old), I’m here to give a complete review of Into the Pit.First, let's talk about the book. I read it as soon as it was released and available in my region (12/26/2019), and damn, that book was amazing. The main highlight, aside from the third use of the Spring Bonnie suit (first as Springtrap, then Glitchtrap earlier that same year, and the third being a rabbit that strongly resembles Glitchtrap but doesn't have a confirmed name), was how the book focused more on the "magical powers" of the Pit rather than the animatronics. In my opinion, the Pit was written in a terrifying way, making any scene involving direct interaction feel completely different.But do these feelings of the Pit carry over to the game?Answering the question and diving into the game review itself: No, but in a way that incredibly supports the game's essence.First off, the game is similar to The Coma: Recut (the most popular title I know with identical gameplay), where you walk through a place with various hiding spots while threats roam around. The Pit is used primarily as a means of travel (I'll leave it vague to avoid spoilers for new players, but you'll understand how it works as soon as you start playing), and it somehow becomes a safe spot for the player, losing its essence for the sake of everything else.How are the game's aspects and gameplay?To explain fully: you walk through an establishment divided into rooms with threats moving from room to room, trying to find you. To protect ourselves, we have two extremely important tools: audio and hiding spots. The game's audio cues are crucial (as a side note, they provided incredible accessibility support, allowing people with disabilities to play using audio cues displayed on the screen comfortably) and indicate where the animatronics are, one room away, with footsteps, door noises, and music being very relevant. As the game progresses, more animatronics are introduced to hinder you and make Glitchtrap (we'll call him that for simplicity) catch you, each with a unique mechanic and different ways to deal with them, shown to the player in a very clever way.What's the game's length?If you’re a bit of a coward (like me) and like to play it safe or even if you’re a Dishonored player who likes to carefully analyze AI pathing, the game should take about 3-5 hours, depending heavily on how much you want to explore, complete side quests, and collect items that have some relevance but aren't strictly necessary. If you rush through, playing aggressively, it’s possible to finish in as little as 2 hours.How are the graphics?Pixelated graphics tend to appeal to many players but might make some hesitant or discouraged from buying the game. Before I give my opinion, I have no issues with pixelated games—I really enjoy old RPG Maker horror games, but I don’t do well with ones with fewer pixels, like Pokémon Crystal, for example—.In my opinion, the game's graphics and animations are simply spectacular. The animation is jaw-dropping, especially for a game that wasn’t even announced much before its release. They pulled off a masterpiece, and all the art and environments are amazing. I strongly encourage those hesitant to buy due to the graphics to watch some videos beforehand and get a glimpse of this artwork.Is the game worth the price?I’m from Brazil, and at least for us, the game is priced similarly to FNAF 1 to 4 combined, R$60.00 (equivalent to $10.90 at the current exchange rate), which I’ve seen is almost half the cheapest price for us in conversion. Honestly, if you’re a fan of the franchise, I sincerely think it IS worth paying that price, or I encourage you not to watch anything about the game and buy it during a future sale. But to answer the question, is it worth the price? For me, it was. I had a lot of fun, the graphics are very intriguing and well-crafted, the puzzles and exploration are very enjoyable, and I liked the story. As I said, for a game that was announced just days before its release, it’s spectacular in my opinion. But honestly, I think it should be cheaper—I would pay without complaining or noticing that the price is "above the range" if it were 1/3 cheaper (in dollars they set the price absurdly high and should cut at least $6-8 off the price).How about the achievements? Are they easy?I don’t plan to platinum the game, even though I enjoyed it—I’m not the biggest fan of this style of game—but I plan to replay it and might change my mind about platinum. I’ve seen the achievements, and they aren’t too difficult; most just require time and patience, like collecting items, replaying several times, spending extra time looking for your cat, or just falling... falling MANY times. I didn’t find most of them fun, per se, and they require some additional runs, which isn’t a problem if you want to see all the endings by yourself... Oh, that’s right, the game has multiple endings too!Final Thoughts and Rating:Into the Pit was the last thing from the 10th-anniversary week, and it drove social media crazy. The game is just the right amount of scary; it’s fun and keeps you wanting a little more of the story and some fun things in it. I didn’t find its replayability that interesting, making getting all the endings a somewhat monotonous task due to repeating the same things—again, this is just MY opinion. The price could be lower, but I don’t regret paying that amount for the game; after all, FNAF will always have a place in our hearts, and the game itself is very good, though a bit short. Taking everything from this review into consideration, I’d give FNAF: Into the Pit a 7.8/10. They could have used some scenes better, giving the story more focus and a scarier tone, making the player feel more of the protagonist's emotions and putting them in a more fearful situation with the events than just hiding or running away from the rabbit (sorry Outlast fans). Overall, I recommend trying it, and for fans, playing it and reading the book that inspired the game.I hope this review was helpful and brought someone Into the Pit!

_childDocuments_.review: A yes or no recommendation is tough for this one so let me clarify: If you are a hardcore FNAF fan and want to keep up with all the lore, then yeah, obviously I recommend Into the Pit. If you are a casual fan or even just looking to get into the franchise for the first time, Into the Pit is probably a skip for me.First off, the graphics and sound design are incredible the whole way through. Major props to Mega Cat for what they accomplished here. However good you feel the trailer looks and sounds, the game lives up to that expectation. Unfortunately, the game has pretty intense performance issues (which may or may not be linked to using a controller based on patch notes?) but jump scares and animations still look great. As for the gameplay itself, I again give them props for taking the franchise in a wholly new direction. Approaching the game as a 2D horror game in the vein of Clock Tower, The Coma, or Detention was a great idea. The trouble is that none of the puzzles or horror here are all that interesting and investigation is basically non-existent. Throughout the whole game, you are pretty explicitly told what you are supposed to do via objective clues. The few times these are vague are usually more frustrating than thought-provoking. That said, I imagine the younger target audience might find some of the time-travel elements entertaining. For me, I just had trouble not comparing it unfavorably to Day of the Tentacle.The horror comes from Springtrap chasing you around places but it's hard to be scared of him since he's remarkably easy to avoid. Despite what the trailers show, he actually runs slower than you do and the game even is built around this, with one particular point in the game seemingly requiring you to just run around him to progress. Once you realize that you can just go around him at any point in time, he becomes entirely trivial and the game never becomes any more difficult. Even as more animatronics start showing up, they seem to just make noise alerting Springtrap, rather than posing any direct threat. The flashlight is also entirely useless, making resource management a non-issue. The flashlight flickers constantly while using it and each battery is used up in somewhere between 10-15 seconds. You can always see Springtrap's eyes, even in the dark, so I preferred just running through the dark rather than using the entirely unreliable flashlight.I will say that there are moments of inspired gameplay here. Several of the nights, you have to get out of your house, with several options available from the start. As you use escape paths though, they become blocked off for future nights. This forces you to find new ways out each time. I loved this concept and honestly wish it was expanded on in the pizzaria. Instead, they seem to switch things up from night to night by just locking certain doors and opening others. You never know which are open or closed though without simple trial and error and there doesn't seem to be any actual logic behind it that I could determine. Despite hints at further areas to explore via a world map, the Pizzaria and your house are the only two places that ever require any level of exploration, with the other locations only serving to house NPCs to talk to and items to obtain.The story of Into the Pit is an interesting beast in itself. As with all FNAF games, the plot is ultimately cryptic but it does offer more of a narrative than pretty much any other game in the series. Ozwald has a goal and works to complete that goal throughout the game. This is never left to interpretation and is pretty straightforward. What's less obvious is why any of this situation is happening. If you're playing to understand why there's a time traveling ball pit, why Springtrap is impersonating Ozwald's Dad, why nobody else sees Springtrap for what he is, well, just know those answers won't come easily. I won't say they aren't in the game, that's more for online theorists to figure out, but I certainly couldn't figure any of that out.If you are a fan of FNAF and just want more FNAF content, I think you'll be happy with Into the Pit. It's different than other games in the franchise but trying something different is good, especially from this side-story made by a partner studio rather than Steel Wool. If you are hoping to finally get the answers to the franchise, you likely won't be finding them here. I can't honestly even tell you if this is canon to the main games or not even after seeing all the endings. If you aren't a FNAF fan though and just love 2D horror games, this might be a good introduction to the genre for kids but it won't be much more than that. The puzzles and difficulty are remarkably easy, even on the hardest difficult (there are only two), the story is simplistic, and the game is quite short (I finished the game and got all the endings in 4 hours and that was taking my time casually looking around for everything).

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played any of these Five Nights games (so my comments here are completely unbiased), but seen this one get mad good reviews so thought I'd give it a whirl....meeeeh? It's alright.I'll start with the positives:SOUND DESIGN - is frigging great. The music is great, the ambience is great, the monster's mechanical garbles are great. Really immersive.Art Direction - The retro pixel graphics pair great with the eighty's story line and arcade-like game-play. The characters's animations have a peculiar sense movement that I've never really seen before, fluid but static, gives the game some personality. Colour has been used beautifully too, vibrant neon brushstrokes everywhere, again leaning into this retro-eighty's thing.Story - Its okay, has more substance than you would imagine from looking at the trailers.The Bad:TINY MAP - the world and areas are very small, with only 2 of the areas having more than 5 rooms (but less than 10). This gives the game a boringly claustrophobic feeling, which no, doesn't add to the horror.REPETITIVE GAME PLAY - entire game consists of avoiding enemies and 'pick item up from over here and use it over there' puzzles. There's also a little bit of 'stealth' allowing you to create distractions through noise or hiding from enemies. This gets really old, really fast. From the point above, as the world is so tiny, you end up just running around in tiny circles to escape the monsters, then hiding, then running around again, that's it really. Only a tiny fraction of the environment is interact-able, it just sucks the fun out of the whole game.As a big fan of horror games, this was just average, and really makes me question the significance of Steam's 'Overwhelmingly Positive' rating, but I'd still recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: POSITIVES:To start with the positives, I think that the art is good quality. I don't particularly love the art style or anything but there are impressive visuals and animations to this game. That being said, there aren't as many full screen cutscenes as I would of liked, the bulk of the story is carried by boxes of text over regular gameplay, with maybe some sprite animations taking place. Another positive is that, at least for me, there were no bugs. Can't really go on a big rant about that but yeah, good job devs. Another thing that I like a lot, and this is super specific but its good so I'm gonna mention it, is the sound design when hiding from Pit Bonnie in the suit, very spooky sounds, very good. That's where everything positive for this game ends for me however.GAMEPLAY:The biggest crime this game commits is its gameplay. So for your controls you have your usual WASD to move around, sprint, interact button as well as your flashlight, which is pretty much the extent of your abilities. Its not the worst games have done more with less, so how are these things used to make you feel like you're leaving an impact with what you're doing? Well to start off with the flashlight, actually useless, completely a waste. There is never a moment in the game where the flashlight is required, in fact there is never even a moment in the game where I'd want to use it. The light is forced to either point left or right and literally doesn't help with seeing at all, there's literally a whole battery finding mechanic but I never recharged once due to how little I used the thing.Next big thing is interacting with stuff, in terms of actually playing the game you'll mainly be using the interact key to hide from stuff. If you're chased to your hiding spot you'll enter a minigame which is better than just sitting there, but even so, pressing W A S and D to swat spiders? Holding space? Pressing F to flash? These just aren't intense at all, but to be fair I haven't played on higher difficulties. However, I was also not given the option to, I'm aware harder difficulties are unlocked after beating the game, but, I didn't enjoy anything the first time, so now it can't really get much better. But anyways, back to the hiding mechanic, you can spend and awfully long time hiding sometimes, especially if you're being hunted by someone I'll mention later, which is just super boring and made me wish you could literally fast forward the game. Anyways walking and sprinting are pretty standard, no problems there, except for 2 things, mainly to do with sprinting. So first off, sprinting literally never had any consequences in my playthrough, it really doesn't make enough sound to trigger literally anything. Secondly, the fact that you trip if you run for too long. Don't get me wrong, ANYTHING is better than stamina, dear God, but you'll literally never run away from anything long enough to trip, its always just doing random objectives and then falling over, which isn't a major complaint but its still like, man, I wish that he wouldn't do that. DANGERS:Consider this spoiler territory, so if you stop reading and haven't played the game... Just watch a playthrough on Youtube, I've already gave my thoughts on the gameplay. Anyways, there are a WHOPPING TWO ENEMIES in this game, you heard me right. These include Pit Bonnie and Chica, and only them. Now for Pit Bonnie, he serves as the one that actually kills you, he can see you or hear you, and if he does he'll come running. This can be swiftly countered by just going the opposite direction, and hiding. So yeah, that's it for him. Now I don't mind Pit Bonnie, but I DO MIND Chica, she is nothing but a complete nuisance. What she does when she sees you isn't really the problem, she basically alerts Pit Bonnie, which obviously isn't as bad her straight up killing you, HOWEVER, she has one wacky quirk which makes her super annoying. If she comes into a room that you're hiding inside, she will stay there for like an entire minute, just doing nothing, waving her arms around like she's trying to find an invisible object. I'm also going to mention the noise makers here too, because yes, they're good for luring Pit Bonnie away from where you're trying to get to, but also, as someone who will interact with anything and everything I come across without the patience to inspect what it is, triggering these accidentally is incredibly easy, usually serving to make things take longer than they need to. This could be easily fixed by requiring the interact button to be held or just using a different button. I have no idea why neither Freddy nor Bonnie do literally anything apart from be a blockade at one point, but being real, seeing how Chica turned out, its probably for the best.NIGHTTIME:Probably the thing that shocked me the most, not in a good way. The most repetitive and blandest thing that I've ever seen in a game. So, here's the formula that is done literally every single night. You for the most part always end up in your bedroom once night begins, once you spawn, its time to leave the house. The most interesting way of leaving is by going up into the attic, and having to take a ladder all the way to the garage, which is interesting because its kinda noisy and you cant run. THAT is the most interesting way, as every other way basically involves going to an exit and just leaving, with the attic requiring a rope that you'll probably just find before you need it. Overall these sections are just super unmemorable, Pit Bonnie is a complete non threat as long as you don't burst into a room that he's already inside of. Every time you escape the house you immediately go to Jeff's, and into the ball pit. Now, whats going to happen almost every single time is this: You're going to enter the past, need to save a kid, an animatronic is guarding the way, so you have to leave the pit, go do a fetch quest, come back with fetched item and remove the animatronic, save the kid, then get chased back out of the pit. Every single time. Zero big differences. This makes it feel like absolutely no progress is being made, because nothing different is happening, you do an objective just to have to do the objective again the next night, and again, and again. You never get any closer to finding your dad throughout any of them, only finding him on the very last night. This game play loop is exactly why no smile appeared on my face after the first hour, because after the first hour and basically seen it all.OVERALL:My experience with this game was hope in the beginning and despair in the end, and I cant even expect any fans of the game to really see where I'm coming from especially with how well received the game is. I just think its a shame because the developers can do a lot better, they clearly have the talent to make a good looking and polished game but when it came to decisions involving the gameplay and everything around that it was just the bare minimum. There's talk of more official games coming in this style and if that happens I'm going to be watching on Youtube as maybe watching someone get excited will trick me into thinking its good and save me the price I had to pay for this game. Which I'm also going to mention now because its a ridiculous price for the amount of "unique content" this game offers, which is pretty much just fetch quests and poor stealth. Rating this game I'd say 3/10, it gets points for the visuals and the polish as I said before, but nothing else about this game was enjoyable. If the day comes where a second FNaF game like this made, please focus on making every segment different and stay away from boring as hell fetch quests and swap them for more puzzle elements and action sequences rather than slow monotonous stealth. Hopefully with all this written down I can stop festering the hatred I have for this game and just move on from it, once the hype dies down at least.

_childDocuments_.review: This is genuinely one of the most terrifying and emotional Five Nights at Freddy's games since the fourth one, nothing short of immaculate. I'd say it's my favorite FNaF game, and I've been a longtime fan since 2014. From the story, music, pixel art, sound, every element about Into the Pit is everything I could've wanted and a LOT more. I haven't finished the game yet, but if you're hesitant about purchasing thinking it's an simple spin-off game with nothing much to it, please do yourself a favor and pay the $20! It's MORE than worth it!If Into the Pit proves anything, it's that it IS possible to please both veteran and new FNaF fans. It's a matter of finding the right balance and telling a great story that isn't too obscure and tedious to dissect. I'd prefer for a story to be more direct for me to appreciate it and comprehend the lore easier. Let me emphasize that it does not detract from the fun of figuring out how it fits into the overarching and ongoing timeline (that's admittedly ridiculous at this point), I understand that's a niche associated with this franchise. However, it's important to tell a great story upfront and then hiding extra "lore bits" for any lore seekers out there. It's essentially the issue I had with Security Breach's method of conveying its story via obscure easter eggs that don't make any sense and relying on the player to figure it out. I'm happy to report here that the writers outdid themselves to closely align with the books and game lore, respecting the source material Scott Cawthon fostered before Steel Wool took over and [debatably] disjointed the story to take a more "rogue AI" approach.FNaF: Into the Pit's story is full of passion, heart, and horror that's quite memorable. There's plenty of dark elements embedded that horror fans will appreciate, something that's been missing from this franchise for a long time. It sent chills down my spine, making me wonder how YouTubers like MatPat are able to show certain scenes on the internet without being demonitized (no spoilers). I digress.Thanks for all the memories over this past decade Scott Cawthon; all the internet trolling, obscure teasers, and sheer kindness will never fade away with the legacy of this iconic video game franchise that brings joy to fans from all parts of the globe. Happy 10 years!

_childDocuments_.review: This is without a doubt the best Fnaf game to come out in YEARS, dare I say since the original Help Wanted. Even if you only have a cursory knowledge of the series, you'll have fun with this one (so long as you don't question things like why totally-not-Springtrap is an eldritch monster now). What really stands out about it to me is that despite not having the classic "office" gameplay of Fnaf, it still  like a Fnaf game (unlike Security Breach imo). You can hide from totally-not-Springtrap, you can distract him, but you can by no means fight him. He constantly feels like this oppressive force that could ambush you at any turn, making you at least the slightest bit anxious whenever you enter a new room. I also like that all of the classic animatronics do something different when they come into the picture rather than all of them doing the same thing or just being another kill condition (thus taking focus/menace away from totally-not-Springtrap), though I'm still not sure what Freddy was supposed to do. No Foxy is also sad but like I get it.That being said, the game started to fall apart for me a bit around the fourth day.  This whole part of the game threw the pacing off for me, turning what was a tense encounter into both a grindquest and pure guesswork in an an otherwise very intuitive game.The process of getting the good endings also felt a little contrived. Overall, though, these are just minor complaints. The game is fantastic, with multiple difficulties, accessibility options, and achievements to keep you coming back. It manages to be scary, intriguing, and just a little bit goofy, everything Fnaf should be. The game is fun, the spritework is gorgeous, and the memes of totally-not-Springtrap ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ your mom are hilarious. It only took me about five and a half hours to beat the game, and I got stuck on night four (see above) for a while. Take that into consideration if you want to buy the game at full price. I think it's worth your buck if you're a Fnaf fan, but if you're not as into the series you might want to wait for a price drop.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is at its scariest, with its masterful sound design that pushes every game in the franchise out of the way. The atmosphere and tone are incredibly dark and dreadful. (example: the shriek-like melody that plays when the power goes out, the blood-curdling unnatural human like breathing from The Yellow Rabbit) Alongside that, the game sets that tone in your face, while cranking it up later with blood, some gore and dead corpses being shown to you. Something modern FNaF tries its hardest to avoid and cater to children with a LACK OF HORROR, censored content and many other changes other than being a bland overly colorful poor jumpscarefest (cough cough SB).The graphics. OH WHERE DO I EVEN BEGIN?? This game uses a pixel artstyle, no, not those fake pixel minigames from previous fnaf games (they're also replicated well here), this game uses genuine pixel art and animations that look and animate beautifully and look absolutely stellar. This is a game that everyone at Mega Cat Studios poured their heart and soul into, it absolutely shows and will get the attention of other people looking to collaborate with them, hell, maybe Scott will collaborate with them again? Overall, i love this. It's absolutely horrifying and beautiful to look at.The gameplay: holy its actually a game with well designed gameplay mechanics and isn't a bland horrorless walking sim??? I haven't seen this in god knows how long besides the VR and Fanverse (TJOC) games. This game as you play teaches you the mechanics before you realize it's a tutorial (now that's a well done tutorial). Before i finish this review i'm being visited by my cat. Did i mention you can pet the cat? I'm getting sidetracked. Anyways, the game utilizes stealth mechanics, you can hide, use distractions or be intentionally loud to try and access an area (which is hella risky), crawl through vents, or just run, at the risk of tripping which can alert others as if running wasn't noisy enough. You can also use a small variety of items to help yourself. Repair things, complete objectives, provide power to smaller things, and more. Another thing to mention, yes, this game is 5 nights, and despite taking place in the same locations, the game succeeds in not feeling repetitive, something previous games have fallen to some criticism of (especially Security Breach). This game has a day and night set up where it'll start during the day, then later begin the night. The days are typically a lil' shorter and are there to help progress the story, this is an adaptation of the books by the way. The real horror attraction, star of the show, the meat and bones, begins during the night when having to go Into The Pit (insert low quality ba dum tsss) where you will have to find out what happens yourself because i'm not spoiling the game. Verdict: This is the best game in the franchise, period. This feels like a more return-to-form-and-embrace game. It goes back on what made it so special, specifically on what made it so scary, and cranked the horror up a ton. The gameplay and graphics are at (in my opinion) at their supreme form. I did not have any issues with the game. Mega Cat Studios is an example of a studio that has both love and talent, and both focuses and nurtures them equally to make the best game they can put out. This is a team with passion, this is a team that loves and plays games, and knows what makes a good game. And they delivered. Congratulations and well, SUPER well done, Mega Cat Studios. I cannot wait to see what you make next, and i wish you the best success.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the mechanics are very underutilised for how much explanation there is. The first night goes on about how the power can go out and you need to go back to fuse box backstage, but that is the only time it ever happens. You get a sketchbook explaining Freddy's and Bonnie's mechanics, but they never appeared a SINGLE time across all of the nights, apart from the scripted Bonnie encounter.The noise mechanic is also strange as if you make a loud sound and leave the room then Springtrap will know where you are immediately and tunnel in on your exact location, even if he never saw you enter that hiding place. Not that you need to use the noisemakers anyway, I only needed to use them in the 2 scripted/required uses, but Chica will camp a door with no way of knowing that she is on the other side.The autosaves in the first few nights are fine, but they stop working correctly on night 4 and are non-existent on night 5, meaning you have to do all of the daytime parts again. This would be fine if there were any threats during the daytime, but instead you are just running around though empty rooms 80% of the time because the game doesn't explain what you need to do. 2 of the places you can go have pretty much nothing there apart from a single interaction.The dialogue/quest logs are also difficult to read, and the game only supports x-box button prompts with no option to change to ps4 prompts, which lead me to die several times during quick time events. Most of the tips/hints are not helpful in any way. Achievements also show up in game when you get them, which personally i found to break immersion, especially with how many there are for doing normal actions, like flicking light switches.This does not even include the gameplay, which is very repetitive and involves just running between rooms to pick up a key item and take it to another room, which is fun for the first 2 nights but gets boring and frustrating VERY quickly. Springtrap is easy to avoid, but at times you will not know a door is locked (no way to tell before reaching the door) and get stuck in a room or corner with no hiding place. Springtraps pathfinding is strange at times as well, where he will be a room behind you and then somehow appear in the room your entering. There are also softlock bugs that require you to restart, which is especially in night 4 where there is only 1 autosave location.Its a shame because the art and music are great but everything is underutilised. I understand going for each ending would be longer, but from my research it only includes playing a few more minigames and picking up a few items, which isn't worth playing the full game several times over for a extra minute of epilogue.Not worth the full price for a 3 hour game, get it if its on sale. I was hoping this game would be a turn in the right direction after security breach, but it seems like it isn't unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: This game at times felt like an annoying and long fetch quest, AND SO MANY BUGS. For example, I needed something to break open the fridge while Spring Bonnie was chasing me. I saw a hammer in the arcade, but when I tried to grab it, nothing happened. Nearly 20 minutes later, I could suddenly grab the hammer. Awesome, that's just awesome.Another example: I walked into a room and heard the sound effect for when Spring Bonnie sees you. I went up to a door, spamming 'E' for my life, but nothing happened. Then, 7 to 10 seconds later, he just teleports into the room, and I die. It feels like not a single beta tester played this game. I wish I had counted how many glitches I encountered, but it might have been in the triple digits.I really wanted to love this game, and I gave it the benefit of the doubt. As I'm playing it, my friends are watching my screen share, saying this game is unbelievably bad. I had high hopes for this game, but it feels super rushed and almost like one big fetch quest. It's really saddening how unfinished this game feels. This game needed beta testers, and I was reading the credits—I didn't see any. If someone can correct me on that, please do.Also, I hated the fact that Spring Bonnie's speed would change depending on how far away I was. That's just unfair. I'm running, thinking I'm far away, but as I try to go into a vent, Spring Bonnie was just out of sight on my screen. That's insane. Again, I really wanted to love this game, but it feels unfinished with so, so, so many bugs. If you're reconsidering buying this game because of my review, let me tell you something: this game could have been great, but two things are holding it back—SO MANY BUGS and bad design. If anyone from Mega Cat Studios is reading this, please fix your game.

_childDocuments_.review: Never really cared that much for fnaf played the original way back and thats about it, but when i looked into this game i decided to give it a try and to my surprise its really good. Probably one of the best installment in the franchise, very story driven focused and relaying on exploration to solve objectives. In addition to having an amazing pixel art style which is by far my favorite thing about this game. 2D game mainly, but has great jumpscare moments that switches the pov to first person which is really cool. New difficulties to unlock and multiple endings for some replayability. Only problem i had is the objective gets repetitive over the course of the story, but overall would highly recommend this to any who wants a decent horror game not just fnaf fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't really know what to expect when this game was announced, but was really pleasantly surprised. Its a lot of fun! This is easily the most visually polished and beautiful FNAF game, and is probably better as a gameplay experience than most of the mainline games too. Its fun, relatively spooky, and an absolute ball buster on Nightmare mode, which I am too much of a baby to attempt. I enjoyed hunting for secrets too, and theres a surprising amount of stuff to find. This game will probably take you about 6ish hours for your first play through, at least thats how long it took me, only dying once or twice and getting every collectible and secret on "normal" diffcult. To be honest, I just wish there was more game over all. I really, really, really hope Mega Cat are given the go ahead to make another FNAF title, because this was fantastic and I think they did an amazing job. I would love them to adapt some of the other FNAF books - maybe the comics? - or something original in the universe. Good game, 8/10, Bonnie is the best.

_childDocuments_.review: I must admit I put myself on a game ban due to recent games I just bought. But seeing this dropped early I had to buy it. While playing it, it is rather late so I'm going off based on the small amount I've seen so far. I will try and refrain from spoiling as much as possible!!I am playing the game on Steam Deck even though it's not verified for it yet. So far I've had no issues at all. Everything works well and responds as it should. I was worried I might have to delay playing it if it didn't work as I play most games on my Steam Deck now but for now, I've had no issues with it! I enjoy pixel horror games! And this hasn't disappointed me at all. I can admit I'm not the greatest with horror games but pixel ones, I can handle. The scares I have received have made my heart race. The jump scares that you don't expect just from exploring the area got me a few times. The graphics are so detailed. I can't find any issues with the art style used at all. It just fits the game so well. The music helps create the atmosphere of the areas you're in. The fact that I'm certain you can hear heavy breathing in the background that just adds to the tension of the game as a whole.Springtrap is horrifyingly terrifying as he should. I was constantly on edge trying to avoid him in the short time I have played. Having him appearing appear at one point did cause me to panic and hide when I shouldn't have which resulted in my demise in game. The way he moves is well crafted, a mix of robotic and human like movements. It makes him feel alive but not.  The miniature cut scenes that are very well detailed such as when he does catch you or when you're hiding in certain places and he's looking for you. The QTE as well when hiding in spots when he's in the room makes it more dangerous as if you don't time things right you can still be found in a hiding spot.There are also two modes in the game so for people who want more story rich game with what I assume also has less jumpscares is available and with him barely appearing to chase you down. That's my current thoughts so far. I do plan to update this review when I get further in game or complete it.

_childDocuments_.review: as someone who has played these games since a child and has multiple tattoos of these characters, i would recommend this game to other nerds. as someone who is a huge fnaf nerd, i can't necessarily say without bias that this is a solid game for people who are not fans of the franchise- but from a biased pov, this is one of the best games i've ever played. it definitely goes in my top 3 for fnaf, and that's big coming from an old time fan like me. amazing job to the team. there are still some glitches that i'm sure will be worked out, such as sometimes doors not opening when you run into them or the door button not appearing, but this is a brand new game and i'd expect some mild annoyances with that. i just got the true ending, and it made this game 10x better for me. i found myself feeling blissful playing this game- it is a scary game, but as a longtime fan, this is the most happiness i've felt in awhile just that there is another one of these games for me to play.

_childDocuments_.review: FNaF: Into The Pit is a much needed return to form for the FNaF series, which has admittedly started to lose its scare factor significantly. While the scares themselves from dying aren't too freaky, the atmosphere of this game after the tutorial is definitely deserving of the title. The story is based off of and expanded upon somewhat off of the spin off FNaF book of the same name, and it is a very well made story telling the tale of a child who discovers a time traveling ball pit and must fend off an animatronic following him around for five days. There are also plenty of secrets in the game as well for players to discover, as per tradition with this franchise at this point.Overall, props to Mega Cat Studios and Scott Cawthon for the game adaptation of Into The Pit. A very well made game utilizing a professional pixel art artstyle, well animated animations, and very engaging and thrilling gameplay. I definitely recommend, very much worth the $20! Surprised it isn't more tbh.

_childDocuments_.review: so review timethis game is a stealth horror game, you cannot rush this game and solve its puzzles, patience is required to wait for opportune times to move and snake aroundif you do not have patience and waiting and observing and listening, i highly discourage this gameif you do have patience you will more than likely have funthere are a few issues and bugs here and there (this is still a day 1 release so fair enough on that front)one issue i will point out Spoiler for day/night 5this and a few other issues do kinda make it a little frustrating to play, (had a moment where a predetermined cutscene threw me onto springtrap into a unfair spot where i had to redo the sequence again)other than these issues the game is fun, scary and interesting to play and explore while also telling a unique storyi really like into the pit, it puts fnaf in a new era for games and this is a welcome addition to the fnaf games lineup

_childDocuments_.review: I love the idea of adapting the "Fazbear Frights" books into games and "Into the Pit" delivers on the idea with only a few minor hiccups. The art style was not my favourite, some parts look good others goofy.  I still appreciate all the detail and effort went it into the art. The animations in particular are quite great especially in the hiding segments. The game play of "Into the Pit" is  a standard adventure game affair with some simple puzzles and stealth mechanics. Said stealth mechanics amounting to a bunch of repetitive mini-games, which while there are quite a few, none are very engaging.  My only gripe with the puzzles is that I wish the game leaned into the time travel gimmick more or at all in this case.I don't think non-FNAF fans will enjoy "Into the Pit" but as I fan I personally enjoyed my play-through. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: A good game tarnished by a bad achievement list.The game has good art and sound direction and was overall a stable and fun experience for my first playthrough. The story feels forgettable and at times felt like there was intended to be more depth to it that got cut. I would agree with some that the price may be a bit higher than I would expect (in my region it's $20, though I would have felt it more suited at $15).My biggest gripe is the achievement list, and not because of the difficulty but because of how tedious the setup is. There are several achievements for getting different endings, including getting the same ending on the highest difficulty and getting any ending on the second highest difficulty. Doing the highest difficulty achievement, however, does not award you the achievement for doing the same exact thing on a lower difficulty. So in order to get all the achievements, you have to do the same thing multiple times across multiple difficulties, which is tedious and boring.If the devs fix this, I'd consider updating my review. Otherwise, I'd skip this one if you like getting achievements and want a game that doesn't overstay its welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: After five years of ups and downs from letting other companies take a crack at FNaF, Mega Cat Studios comes in with my absolute favorite just in time for the ten year anniversary. Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit is a fantastic entry into the series, and is well-worth the price of admission for the polish alone. It takes the design of classic point-and-click adventures and puts it into the context of a pixelated Freddy's minigame, with stealth mechanics! And that's not to mention the fluid animations, the eerie sound design, the beautiful art style, and the crazy secrets - it's clear Mega Cat Studios did their homework on the series.  Being the first Freddy's game based on a book, and thus separate from the game-canon timeline, it allows this game to stand on its own, meaning only a general knowledge of the concepts in FNAF are required to jump in (to the pit) and enjoy. As a result of this, though, the story isn't technically new, so anyone familiar with the book Into the Pit will already know what's coming, so I'm curious how this will play with people who don't know what happens. On that point, though, I do love its story. It's sweet, and hits at the heart of what Freddy's has been about for a while. I have never been a huge fan of the way the books approached canon, though, being a sort of parallel universe, but after playing this, I am much more open to them. It's nice to wipe the slate clean and just take in the universe that Freddy's has become. If I were to come up with any issues I had with the game, it would be the relatively simplistic nature of its item system, and the little impact it has on the endings. The items are pretty straightforward, meaning you'll collect something, then more than likely use it within the next five minutes. I hope that in a sequel there is a bit more depth and diverging pathways, but nevertheless, this was still a very fun experience. To close, I highly recommend playing this game for yourself. It's a breath of fresh air for this series, and I hope this is a good indicator for what more there is to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely brilliant Five Nights at Freddy's instalment, and one of my personal favourites - Into the Pit is a thrilling journey from start to finish, and it pulls no punches with the subject matter at hand. This game is genuinely freaky. Seeing the Yellow Rabbit luring kids, locking them in freezers, standing over corpses, blood, the spine-chilling sounds of kids screaming and crying... Into the Pit is genuinely disturbing and is super direct with its story and subject matter, marking a refreshing change of pace in tone for this franchise, which usually opts for a 'tell don't show' kind of storytelling. After 10 years of this, it's FANTASTIC to get something entirely different. It is insanely cool to be able to see the macabre so unfiltered within this franchise, really making the subject matter it deals with feel that much more potent, and I hope this continues within the franchise as a whole, as it really elevates the 'horror' of the horror game.Artistically speaking, this game looks incredible. Some really impressive sprite work is at play here, with some super detailed cutscenes that make it almost hard to believe you're looking at pixels.Content-wise, this game is much longer than I expected, with a good 4-5+ hours if you're going for completionist. There's tons of secrets to discover, which absolutely nail that classic FNaF vibe. Get digging!The use of the ballpit from the story translated into a puzzle-solving gameplay mechanic was genius. Going back and forth from the past to the present to grab items and use them in different time periods had me grinning from ear to ear. Every single bit of story from the original book is covered here, and is adapted into gameplay in a way that's nothing short of genius. You'd think that the book was written to *be* a game, and not vice-versa.I think my only gripes with this game would be some unfair checkpoints that can set you back a lot of progress, and some *very minor* visual bugs... Which will likely be patched out in the coming weeks.Sound design, tone, storytelling, visuals, UI... everything comes together in a beautiful blend of artistry that really puts this game up near, if not *as* the franchise's best. Seriously guys, pick this one up. Mega Cat deserve this success, and I hope they can continue to work on this franchise for years to come, and lay down the path to the future of Five Nights at Freddy's.

Combining first-person and third-person aspects causes this game to amp up the amount of creepiness, on both an artistic and intellectual approach. From sound design, to animations and art, everything has been handled so well and i can't help but want more of this!Two things however i did not like:One of them being that there is no breathing room for the player. You are on edge all the time. In your house, in the pizzeria and even in some parts of the map that you should feel safe in, you either have to hide or run away from things. This really makes the game repetitive and i hope that if they do adapt more fnaf books, they can improve on that.My second issue with the game are the endings. So far i reached 3 endings and only one of them left me satisfied. The endings don't have much build up and are presented in few pictures, kind of like security breach's ending but with more dialogue. I feel that for a game like this where its been amazing from start and its progression, the endings fall very flat and it could have been fixed with more interaction to leave a better taste for the players when they log off. but i really think that these issues could be improved on very easily and i really REALLY hope that this studio continues on making fnaf book adaptations!! Until then i would love to check out what else they have been doing outside of fnaf. I had a great experience, i sincerely wish the best for the team that worked on this <33

Slight context error that could use fixing.- I had a few times where I would enter a room with no knowledge of an enemy being in there (no footsteps or gurgly vocal sounds) and would sometimes be in a part of the map where I couldn't hide which resulted in me dying, could be a skill issue though hahaApart from these issues, one big, rest minor the game was fantastic and I would highly recommend it even if you've never read the book (I haven't).

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I knew from the trailers that a pixel art 2D survival game focused on horror was up my alley, but they freaking DELIVERED on this game. As a longtime fan of the series since fnaf 1 dropped my freshman year of college, I absolutely love this one. I think Fnaf 1 is my favorite game, followed closely behind by Help Wanted, which is now CLOSELY followed by this game. It was THAT good and fun and creative. If you like the novels, it’s a solid adaptation with good references to other stories. If you just like the idea of a horror adventure game, it’s fantastic. I would genuinely recommend it to a non-fnaf fan. The self contained story is absolutely great on its own. I love that unlike another game I was looking forward to not being made by Scott, this one has SO MANY working arcade cabinets and other fun things to immerse you in the environment (which is a huge part of the appeal of these games). And the secrets have been so fun to find, I ended up getting the 3 star ending myself on the first playthrough but I felt like I was rewarded for the time I took to find everything for it. Overall, huge recommendation and cannot wait to try the harder mode. It actually seems doable, I maybe died 3 times in the game, so I am up for the challenge! Well done all involved, it was super rewarding and fun!

_childDocuments_.review: If you adore the books and want to see one of the stories articulated into a good-looking and simple game, it's for you, if you want something scary or riveting gameplay, you should look elsewhere.It has beautiful visuals, great sound design, and an amazing atmosphere, but that's where it ends for me.I think the $20 price tag isn't justified whatsoever, I could see it easily for $10 and maybe even $12, but with how intensely this game is driven by its very short narrative (That isn't to say the story is bad, I did enjoy it while I was going through it initially) despite giving almost no real direction in the later nights, alongside how simple and unchanging the gameplay loop throughout all 5 nights are, I really don't think it was worth it for me, especially with how short it is.All the power to you if you enjoyed it, but I really did not find the gameplay challenging or even interesting. _childDocuments_.review: Casual Review:This game on its own is great. A first time experience is great. basically this is a great game. great sound design, visual design, animations the lot. Just great.Review from a completion perspective:This game is fundamentally flawed, 3 achievements locked behind a ridiculously unnecessarily hard challenge. The audacity of the developer to add a "speedrun" timer for a game that is absolutely NOT optimised for speedrunning is ridiculous. Too many dialogue box mashing is involved and a really long stupid prologue/tutorial that YOU CAN'T SKIP.Nightmare Mode, WHY would you develop this mode to delete your save file. The mode is already hard enough with the aggressive level of springbonnie AND lack of hiding spots and breakable distractions. WAS THE PERMADEATH/DELETE YOUR SAVE FILE REALLY NECESSARY? Literally, everyone HATES IT.I got all the way to Night 5 on this mode attempting to get the 3 star achievement and lost it all to a single wrong click. So I used S.A.M. and gave myself the last 3 achievements because if the GAME wont play fair, then I wont either.Please update this game to remove the permadeath and only have it as an optional feature for those who actually want to suffer through it rather than people like me who just wants to finish the game by getting all collectables including achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: I really really really enjoyed FNAF: Into The Pit. From the start of the game, I was instantly taken by the art style, as well as the story straight from the beginning that left me hooked throughout my entire first playthrough of the game (5.2 hours) I ended up playing through it in one sitting. You play as Oswald, who is so far, my FAVOURITE fnaf protagonist in the entire franchise, absolutely no competition. I really enjoyed the subtle details on the sides of the screen when Oswald gets more and more stressed throughout the game. His sprite really encapsulates how anxious and nervous he feels, especially during some sections of the game.I was not expecting this game to be as good as it is. Although I did experience some bugs during my first playthrough, it was still immersive and enjoyable to play, didn't take me away from the game at all. I really like the usage of the ball pit for quests, as we can switch between different times whenever we want in order to find items, finish quests, etc. I also wasn't expecting that more difficulties to be added and to be able to change settings after my first playthrough.I do think that the endings are a little too short for the amount of effort you put into getting different endings. For most people, it simply isn't worth it to get all endings when the endings are so short. While I share some sentiments about them, I actually don't mind playing through the game again and again to get all of these different endings and achievements.This is one of the games that I would be happy to play again and again to 100% the entire game, and this game has extra hard difficulties! This is also the first game that I've ever written a review for, so sorry if any of this is unclear. All in all, I would recommend this game AND the book because this game definitely made me want to buy it. Also, a steam game profile would be awesome...

_childDocuments_.review: Into the Pit is a solid entry in the FNAF franchise. It's actually got gameplay and content, and lives up to what it promises. Wouldn't recommend it to a newcomer, but if you're a disappointed FNAF veteran, you might like it!The hide and seek mechanics have some depth, featuring minigames for hiding (Pandemonium would be proud) and a sound/awareness system that influences how the main threat behaves. While not as deep as something like Amnesia: The Bunker, they're fine for this relatively short FNAF game. Do wish the harder difficulty settings were available from the start, though...Alongside your main objectives, there's also a variety of minigames, collectionist stuff, tidbits of lore, and juicy secrets. More than the average FNAF, actually.The art for this game is absolutely phenomenal and worth mentioning, being the sole reason I picked this game up. Clean UI design, excellent lighting, and buttery smooth pixel art animation.Game is overpriced as hell but so is everything these days. Get some friends in a voice chat stream, give the game a run-through, and you'll have some fun.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10I originally uploaded this on how long to beat however I figured id upload it here in hopes that someone from the dev team actually reads it.I never thought that 10 years later id still be a fnaf fan. Sure, I may not be as much of a fan as I was when I was 9, but the series still holds a special place in my heart, as well as capturing my attention any new game (or movie!) releases. This whole week I had been egarly anticipating the release of this game, as well as celebrating by enjoying all the fun surprises shown over the week. With the day early release of into the pit, I was excited yet had my expectations measured. Ive never read the into the pit novel, and honestly didn't love what was shown in the pre release media. However, after completing the game once I'm happy to report that this game is very much a great game and honestly one of the best the series has to offer.The story starts off with a bang with a really cool inciting incident and mystery for you to solve. I think the pit is a fantastic plot device and really has a great supernatural feel to it. As the game goes on however, I do feel like the story loses steam a bit as you kinda just search for your father, however thankfully it really does pick back up towards the end of the game. I talked to really as many people as I could, as well as interacting with everything I could find, and I gotta say I do love the kinda character everything has. I think Oz is a really great character and really manages to pull of the series signature style of humor. I do wish that the story had a few more reveals however, most of all really just whats going on with spring bonnie? Is purple guy inside him? Is it his ghost? Why is the ball pit teleporting Oz back too? I hope however that these are answered within the other endings and hidden lore that I may have missed.The gameplay in this game is simple, honestly pretty simple to what was found in security breach, however I think that this game does a great job at ramping up the difficulty as the game goes on, and more animatronics are added as well as the others becoming more aggressive. I love all the different hiding mini games and while I wish they had a little more variety, I think they do a really great job at keeping the tension high as you hide. I think the noise meter mechanic is also really fantastic, and I wish that it was utilized a lot more than it actually was, as really towards the end of the game I kinda just ended up ignoring it.I really think that this game looks and sounds amazing. I love the kinda open world aspect of the game, and while it wasn't really utilized very much, I do think it helps add to the sense of scale this game gives off, which is something I was worried about. Each location looks fantastic, especially the pizzeria which is just dripping in atmosphere (literally). I think each of the animiatronics look fantastic and are animated really well, giving off quite a robotic yet cartoony look. All of the animations in this game look fantastic and polished really, which is a stark contrast from SB. I really think one of the best elements of this game however was the sound design though, which really returns to how it was in the original Cawthon games. I love how you can hear the footsteps of the animitronics not only off screen (also in the direction in which they are) but also thru doors, which helps you get jumpscared less. Really all of these aspects kinda come together to make an honestly surprisingly scary game. Sure, I don't think its nearly as scary as the first game or pizzeria simulator, but I actually did jump and get frightened a few times while playing this, which I didn't think would happen from a 2d pixel game.When I was 9 and in my biggest fnaf era, I remember playing those gmod or roblox recreations of the fnaf 1 office where you had to run and hide from the animitronics and wishing that one day a fnaf game like that would be released. Then I played SB and thought to myself, this is exactly what I wanted back then, but its not really scratching that itch I've had for so long. Now I know why that is. SB was filled with frankly just poor decisions, average if not bad gameplay, and an honestly mediocre story. This game, has none of that and IS the fnaf game I've been wishing for all these years. Sure its not in 3d first person, but honestly I could easily see this game being made in that format. The gameplay is basic yet really fun and engaging, especially for its short runtime. The story is also really great and has a great central mystery that makes me wanna dive back in and explore the game for secrets like I did with the Cawthon era fnaf games. The environment and world this game creates not only looks but sounds great and creates a scary presentation that continues throughout the whole experience. Hell, id even argue that this game is detached from the other games and not really weighed down by all the confusing lore like SB is, making it a great jumping on point for new fans to the series. Overall, this is finally the evolution that I was hoping for all these years. This is a fantastic game and I highly reccomend fans of the series give this one a try. While the Cawthon games hold a special place in my heart, and I have a hard time saying that this game is better than those, I will say that this game is easily up there along the best in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: ---------- takes the eerie, animatronic horror the series is known for and pairs it with a narrative-driven twist that pushes the franchise into new territory. Whether you're a veteran of Freddy Fazbear’s haunted legacy or a newcomer, this entry offers a fresh blend of classic terror and intriguing storytelling.At its core, Into the Pit retains the signature mechanics that define the FNaF series: monitoring security cameras, managing limited resources, and surviving relentless animatronic threats. However, this installment expands the gameplay with exploratory segments, allowing players to investigate the pizzeria and its surroundings during the day.The story revolves around a young protagonist, whose name is Oswald, who discovers a mysterious ball pit in an old, dirty and not-so-good pizzeria, one that serves as a portal to the past. This seemingly innocent setup quickly spirals into a nightmare as the protagonist finds themselves entangled in a sinister mystery involving mechanical figures with their own life, and a haunting connection to Freddy Fazbear’s murky history.The visual and audio design are standout elements. The dilapidated pizzeria exudes an unsettling charm, with flickering neon lights and crumbling walls that suggest untold horrors lurking just out of sight. The animatronics are more grotesque than ever, their designs blending a mix of retro nostalgia and nightmare fuel.Sound plays a crucial role in building tension. Subtle creaks, distant whispers, and the chilling hum of animatronic servos create a constant sense of dread. The soundtrack, when it does appear, is sparse but haunting, perfectly complementing the eerie silence.The game doesn't seem to have much minuses. The only thing I would think would be a problem for some people is that the game might have a very confusing story for a new player who isn't familiar with FNaF. revitalizes the franchise with its mix of classic survival horror and narrative depth. It pays homage to its roots while exploring uncharted territory, creating a chilling and memorable experience for fans and newcomers alike. _childDocuments_.review: This is such a good step in the right direction for upcoming FNAF game's atmospheres. Five Nights at Freddy's 1 was very special, there was nothing like it and it had this sense of nostalgia mixed with uneasiness. This was completely diluted past a few games, and I am going to directly blame Steel Wool's vision that FNAF is about robots screaming in your face. FNAF's atmosphere was lost for a long time, reintroduced in Help Wanted, then lost again. This, though. It really does it. The ♥♥♥♥♥♥, beaten up and disgusting Jeff's Pizza is such a wonderful location. It makes you miss what Freddy's Pizzaria used to be, even though you've never been there. The weird sections in your house where it just doesn't feel quite right. The main character's constant state of unease. It all adds to the atmosphere very well. However, this game has a lot of problems. The one that got to me the most is that the ending is balls. It sucks. It's so, so bad it's actually insane. You're handed a crappy, nothing-burger ending if you don't do a bunch of hidden criptic stuff. And that's your ending. You play like, 5 hours or so of game, just to have like your character be grabbed then it shows them strapped on a chair and then roll credits. What is this? It almost seems like a bug, it's ridiculous, and it made me completely uninterested in chasing the other endings. I don't know where to start to get the other endings, so I guess that'll be it then.The gameplay is also really bad. Not the mechanics themselves, they're pretty alright. But the gameplay loop, oh god, it's awful. They didn't have enough content for a full game and it shows. You kinda just run back and fourth and back and fourth, trying to figure out what specific item the game wants you to get in what specific place. It's like a fetch quest simulator. You do all that, to then get to the place and find out that this night's plot is that there is a kid screaming and you have to find them - again. It's always the same every night.So, despite all those complaints, why am I recommending it? Because it delivered in everything I wanted from a FNAF game. It's unnerving, atmospheric and grimmy. It looks beautiful and it can be intense sometimes, even more so at the beginning, however much less at the end. I recommend it for FNAF fans, for anyone else though, I don't think you're going to have a lot of fun.

I loved the sound design in the game, it really makes the game feel more alive and honestly more creepy. Into The Pit also is the first game that actually motivated me to go through more than one playthrough to get all the endings. Over all Into The Pit is such a solid game and is one of my favourite installments of the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is alright, maybe. Has it's elements of a fnaf game, though most of it is simply the classic uninspired story of some middle schooler in a town that's haunted or whatnot. Gameplay is about what you would expect from this type of game - just bunch of fetch quests where you bumble around until you find the right room, except there's always someone looking for you, very neat.But none of that really matters if it's scary though, right? Well, it's not. If you found security breach scary you might like this, but it's less so than even that.First, the atmosphere. It frankly feels like they barely even tried. It feels like they paid most of the attention to the story and feel of the game, which again, is meh at best. Of course, there's the dark rooms and loose wires and whatnot, but generally most of the gameplay happens throughout fairly well lit rooms with basically no scary ambiance. I honestly can't even recall if there was any ambiance. I think possibly there may have been some vaguely spooky background music, but thats about it.And second, there's basically no build-up to any of the scares. They either happen out of nowhere during some cutscene (not scary) or after you fail to run away from an animatronic. If you pay attention to the sounds while you're doing one of the aforementioned fetch quests, you'll have a fairly solid idea of where all the animatronic around you are, so any scares you might receive are going to be very light. But if you do get caught off-guard, a simple jump sound will play and then a fairly soft sort of drumming will continue on while the animatronic gives chase, until you either successfully hide away from whatever was chasing you, which frankly is very easy to do as the animatronics are very slow, or receive a very expected and boring jumpscare. This is not scary. tldr: mid story, mid gameplay, less scary than security breach (exploring caves in minecraft is scarier than this ♥♥♥♥)I'd consider playing it through though if it was like 6 dollars, maybe.

_childDocuments_.review: Into the Pit does a great job of portraying the story of the book it chooses to follow with its character, environment, and sound design. The game's story, just like every other entry in the franchise, follows similar themes and attempts to expand the story with different characters. Although the game is a must-pick for die-hard fans, the gameplay becomes somewhat repetitive after a while, and the objectives are almost the same every night. _childDocuments_.review: FIVE NIGHTS AT FREDDY'S: INTO THE PIT is the next terrifying chapter in the FNAF saga, developed by a new-to-FNAF studio, Mega Cat.This game, rather than continuing the story of Steel Wool's games, is an adaptation of one of the very first Fazbear's Frights book stories of the same title. It takes us back to an unknown time period where we play as Ozwald. He wishes his life weren't so boring, he spends every day of his school break going to the pizzeria in town, Jeff's Pizza, eating pizza & staring at the grease stained walls.Just like every other day, he's taken here by his dad to chill and eat pizza for a little while before his dad returns to pick him up, but while sitting at his own table eating pizza, he overhears the chatter of the family sitting next to him where they talk about an old ballpit that managed to give one ringworm, and something else that they don't mention. Curiously, Ozwald decides to find this old ballpit and hide in it before his dad arrives to play a prank on him. He finds it and swiftly jumps into it and...What!? He hears many kids playing & talking with loud music playing all of a sudden. He jumps out of the ballpit and... this doesn't look like the rundown room he was just in! He sees a weird assortment of animal characters on the wall next to the ballpit and numerous kids in the room playing. Confused, he runs out of the room and this definitely isn't Jeff's. The building the same, but with much different decorations and... a band on stage? The band is made up of 3 characters, a brown bear, a blue bunny, and a yellow chicken, all singing & dancing as the kids around you dance to the music and cheer them on.What happens next is for you to find out... this game is 100% worth a purchase! Mega Cat knocked it out of the park with this and I love it so much, it's definitely top 3 FNAF games and might even be #1. It's a much different style than what us FNAF fans are used to. It's not point & click like Scott's games, and it's not 3D free roam or VR like Steel Wool's games. It's a pixel art game that has a very appealing style and the gameplay is great!FNAF games always have a story, but to me, they never feel completely story driven. This game is different, and I guess that's expected since it's adapting a book story, but something about it just makes it feel much more story driven than any game in the series & I love it. Maybe it's the amount of dialogue, I don't know, but it's great. I've already gotten all 3 endings and I loved every moment of playing this game, and I can't wait for the community to dig into it with all the theories they come up with. Does this game confirm that the Fazbear's Frights books are canon to the games? Does it confirm that the books are actual books or games in universe? I don't really know! I'm not a FNAF book reader so I don't know all the details, but I'm seeing a mixed consensus about what this game confirms to be canon. Guess I'll have to wait & see!Scott Cawthon has already mentioned wanting to see Mega Cat adapt another FF story, and I'd love to see it. They truly made something great here & should be played by both FNAF fans and non-fans, it's just a good time with a hint of mystery! I'd love to see them not only make more book adaptations, but also see them make new chapters in the currently building story, I feel they could do really good with it & there's tons of potential there! Of course, they'd have to communicate with both Scott & Steel Wool to ensure lore stays consistent, but I think it'd all work out! Hopefully we get to see that soon!This game was originally slated to release on the 10th Anniversary of FNAF, August 8th, but after accidentally releasing in Japan early, they released it EVERYWHERE a day early in classic FNAF fashion! This truly was a great anniversary drop for the series as it's an amazing game, and it's also pretty scary! The atmosphere is absolutely great here & gave me the chills in some places. I hope Mega Cat does get the opportunity to make more games in the series, whether it be book adaptations or a brand new game building the current story, I will play it on launch. Mega Cat did great.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a fun and fresh new take on the franchise. You never want a game to be too hand-holding, but sometimes, the game felt a bit confusing as to what the solution to something would be. It wasn't always intuitive to know where to go or what to do. Again, you don't want it to be hand-holding, but it also felt random in what it needed at times.The other problem with the game is probably the saves. The saves being locked behind specific story beats meant that prolonged periods of side activities and losing meant losing all that progress. I wish there was a manual save feature, or more frequent autosaves. Although doing so probably would've hurt the already low difficulty bar.But overall like a 7/10 experience.

_childDocuments_.review: FIVE NIGHTS AT FREDDY'S: INTO THE PITFive Nights at Freddy's: Into The Pit, this game is absolutely amazing...This game has the concept from the Fazbear Frights: Into The Pit book, but it expands on it further so it has it's own take of the story. I was honestly worried it would of been a one to one copy of the book. Springbonnie is my absolute favorite character in the franchise, i'm so glad to see a game with him in it as the antagonist. For those that never read the book, this version isn't William Afton, this is an agony creature created by the evil that happened at the pizzeria. There's definitely some references and straight out of the book scenes/areas, but it works really well with the game, like a compliment to this masterpiece. No words can express how much i love this game. Everything about it has a constant uneasy feeling, even being in your own house isn't safe!There's a lot of ways to hide in this game, chests, tables, closets, vents, Golden Freddy suit, beds. That's just a few hiding spots! I honestly hope they continue the Fazbear Frights games, including this 8 bit style and free roam in general.Into The Pit has a School, The Mill, where Oswald's dad used to work before it was shutdown, Jeff's Pizzeria, The Library, It has no purpose in the game since you can't enter it other than looking at it from the outside and talking to 2 kids, and Oswald's house.There's collectibles around the locations you can grab, items to fix arcades, dad's personal belongings, and many other retro items.For those who read the book, you already know how the game will end. (Hint: Collect all of dad's belongings before saving him).I absolutely love the 8 bit style, one of my favorites when it comes to gaming! They nailed everything, from cut scenes to just walking around the locations. I was so impressed by the amount of detail they put into the game, especially for a spin off, definitely worth all of those years in the making! The main title screen is also very nostalgic, having Springbonnie twitch ever so often inspired from the older FNaF games.There's stars in this game like the older ones, a total of 3 with some other secret endings that don't give any. Some of the arcade minigames has easter eggs in them, keep a look out for those!Along with Springbonnie, you also have the main og cast, Freddy, Bonnie, and Chica. Foxy was never introduced in this game unfortunately. As the nights progress, you'll start seeing them one by one. Their cut scenes are very well made! Each animatronic has their own unique way to be lured out, they also each have their own way to catch you. Chica will alert Springbonnie to your location, Bonnie hides under tables in hopes of catching you hiding in the wrong table, Freddy will look through doors, blocking the way, if you try to go through the door he was spotted he will scream at you. They don't actually kill you.This game is just perfection, 12/10! Happy 10th Anniversary FNaF, it's been a journey throughout the years!
