_childDocuments_.review: It hurts me to say this but this is one of the bigger disappointments for me when it comes to games that I've been looking forward to.Coming into it, I have had huge expectations, not only does it come from the gaming franchise that I love the most, I've heard nothing but good reviews, from how fun it is taking the more supernatural side of FNAF, how it comes from the novels which is always a banger, it takes a different approach with its gameplay and I was all for it, it was ticking every box of mine when it comes to "My type of horror game".I've even read reviews where fans who aren't even into FNAF or had never enjoyed the original gameplay fell in love with this one, and that made me feel even more enthusiastic for it.And what do you know, for the first couple of hours they were more than right, I had an absolute blast and fell in love with the game... That is until I learn more of the game it starts to leave a bad taste on me.There started to be what I first thought as glitches, until I realized that it's more of a weird design that I find very questionable to keep in the game, why would you ever let the "monster" chasing you STILL be active and is able to roam around normally when you are in dialogue, or in events that forcefully puts text on your screen that you cannot skip and have to go through that results you to only being left vulnerable to die? Imagine the many times I have died to that, back-to-back-to-back, and that wasn't even me playing the higher difficulties yet where they just get unfair.Having to take big steps, going out of your way to meticulously gather all the requirements, activating the secrets that makes no sense whatsoever and would have had no way of finding out how to do so if not for the guide, just to get: only a 2 second ending that adds nothing whatsoever to the lore, in no way does it even fulfilling for the slightest.You constantly get stuck on literally nothing while running, you could just have to take a wide step because the hitbox of this item on the ground is so large when in reality it should've just been a thing in the nackground that the character ignores.What I especially hate about this game is how doors are just magically locked for no reason while just a second before this wasn't, at one point I had to unlock an already locked door without any reason of it ever being locked, you get chased as they spot you in the perfect place to trap you, and out of nowhere every single area that was unlocked just a moment ago is now locked? for what reason, holy hell I am indeed a huge fan of having dialogues that force your character to stop that you can't skip, thinking to yourself "Ah, I should do this." for a little puzzle without me interacting with anything  while I'm in the middle of a chase after being spotted.Don't get me wrong, this game has all the tools and the potential to be a great, fun game, a good mixture of fanservice, lore, horror and just plain-out fun... but it really just came off to me as a very repetitive game with almost no content past the first few hours that force you to go through the exact same exhausting gameplay, missions and whatever else, back and forth back and forth just to get something in the middle of a night, to then get rewarded with literally nothing, no sense of fulfillment whatsoever.I don't know if the fact I am an avid enjoyer of FNAF and have been kept up with its lore would make this game worse or better for me, regardless, I really just didn't enjoy it and it ended up feeling like a chore. This is the only FNAF game that I would express my disappointment towards it, for a franchise that I unconditionally love.I know reading this out loud might make you think that this sounds exactly like any other FNAF game on face-value, but trust me, this one is just not as replayable nor is it fun to go through again and again.It feels way more unfair than challenging, it's polished but you only get incredibly questionable designs, and just.. it flat out feels like a rage game, or a troll game of some sort.I find it hard to recommend this but I do believe it's not bad either to try, It was again, a very different experience and I still do believe most FNAF fans would love this game, it just so happened to disappoint me a lot based on my expectations and the reviews.This is honestly one of the only few games I regret ever buying.But I will say it one more time, it's not a bad game overall, if anything, it'd fit the "it's so bad that it's so good" category at best, but it just ended up to me feeling like a chore of a game.

_childDocuments_.name: Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazing entry to the franchise, and gaming as a whole. Whether or not you're a fan of FNAF, be it the games, or books, or just a gamer who enjoys sidescroll/snes style graphics and horror, this is WELL worth the price tag. It takes a short story and expands it into a full game in a way that should be praised. It ticks so many boxes for FNAF fans: the music, the setting, the easter eggs and references; and detached from FNAF, or if you're someone who has NO investment or knowledge of the franchise at all, but enjoy this style/genre of game, it's got a great atmosphere that keeps you on edge, a gameplay loop that isn't in itself difficult, but when coupled with the music and lighting, and the ever present fear of where the creature is, especially as nights progress, is fantastic. It's great for a one time play for the story, but also gives built in speedrun timer, and higher difficulties and added difficulty sliders to tweak it for more of a challenge if you're someone who enjoys testing their abilities. 10/10 am playing again.

_childDocuments_.review: "Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit" is a captivating and chilling addition to the FNAF franchise that fans of the series will undoubtedly enjoy. This game masterfully blends the eerie atmosphere, engaging storyline, and iconic characters that the FNAF series is known for.From the moment you start playing, you're drawn into a world of suspense and mystery. The game successfully keeps you on the edge of your seat, with every corner hiding a potential scare. The plot is intricately woven, offering new insights into the FNAF lore while also introducing fresh elements that keep the experience exciting and unpredictable.The game mechanics are smooth and intuitive, making it easy to immerse yourself in the experience without any technical distractions. The visuals are appropriately dark and haunting, perfectly complementing the sinister tone of the game. The sound design is exceptional, with eerie audio cues and ambient noises that heighten the tension and make each moment more intense.One of the standout aspects of "Into the Pit" is its ability to balance nostalgia with innovation. Longtime fans will appreciate the familiar themes and characters, while new players will find it accessible and engaging. The game does a fantastic job of building on the foundation of the FNAF series while also pushing the story forward in exciting new directions.Overall, "Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit" is a must-play for anyone who enjoys horror games or is a fan of the FNAF franchise. It offers a perfect blend of scares, storytelling, and gameplay that will leave you wanting more. Whether you're a seasoned FNAF player or new to the series, this game is sure to provide a thrilling and unforgettable experience

Maybe I'm wrong and there is a way to save but I haven't seen it.Has multiple endings, that's cool, definitely better than Security Breach and well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I get started let me preface this.Mega Cat Studio's you lot are the absolute best, responding quickly and efficiently to feedback and bug reports, I really appreciate how vocal you guys have been in discussions regarding bug reports, so this may hold a little sway in my review from how outstanding you guys have been.To get the Short Attention Span People here right out the gate.Is the game scary: Occasionally.Is the game great: YES.Is the game worth the price: In my Personal Opinion, No.Overall Rating? Solid 6.5/10. One of the best FNAF Experiences available out there with quite a bit of replay-ability due to the difficulty settings and advanced settings, but bogged down by the fear factor wearing off quickly and how short the game generally is, as well as the game's asking price of £16.75.Are they gone?Alright, then lets get started.First off, the Art Direction and Aesthetic of into the pit is absolutely stunning, the mix of pixel art with some honestly impressive lighting is absolutely stunning, the characters look great and generally feel expressive, especially my boy Jeff.The game world feels lived in, for what little you spend roaming around. The Students roaming the halls of the school, occasionally going from room to room, plus the occasional customer in jeffs pizza.Now to where my biggest critique comes from, The Horror, Keep in mind I played this all on frightening which was the balanced experience, but the fear factor in this game significantly falls apart very quickly when you realise most of the jumpscares are artificial and most of the 'threats' aren't actual threats, besides the creature, also the significant lack of rooms that force you to use your flashlight makes the flashlights existence questionable, other than to stun the creature, if he finds you under tables.The variance in difficulty of the hiding minigames is also questionable, I always found myself running to vents because their minigames were simply the easiest to react to and the most available to me, thus making my experience with the creature always lack luster.I almost never encountered Bonnie or Freddy, I always dealt with Chica slowing me down by her refusing to leave a room or being in a room I need to go to, forcing me to leave cause the creature books it to the room I was in.But the worst of all is the creature as a whole, Whilst arguably the best selling point of the game, his AI is an absolute joke, the noise meter does arguably nothing unless you are in a room close to him or you've maxed it out, so you can get away with running around with no punishment until its close to max.You can also pace behind him without him noticing you if his back is turned, and my least favourite part of his AI is the fact that if you gain enough distance from him and hide in something, he will almost always walk past, or trigger a minigame, not kill you outright for hiding in the same room he is in, so you never feel legitimately punished, he will only ever outright kill you, if he is in frame when you are entering the hiding spot.His AI needs to be touched up upon and made a little smarter and his pathing needs improvement.How do I feel about the story however?Its... whatever really, the story isn't really all that breath taking or memorable, taking what seems to be a take of the first incident William did when killing the 6 kids, since the importance of the number 6 is thrown everywhere in this game, but that's whatever, I generally never got invested in the books stories and the same generally applies here, I can't realistically see a little runt like Oswald being able to push over or punch a 'person' in a suit twice his size, it feels unrealistic and generally put me out of the experience and its endings.My Biggest Problem is the asking price of £16.75 in the UK, which for a 4-5 hour experience imo is personally absurd, £8.50 would have been fine, but £16.75? unless you are hoping on the average player to rip the game apart for secrets or grind hard on nightmare difficulty to justify its price, I don't see a reason for it.If the game is less than 8 hours in my personal opinion, I do not think it should have any right being higher than £8 and unfortunately that's how I feel here, as much as I love the game, I CANNOT recommend buying it with this asking price. The Difficulty choice and advanced settings to make the game harder imo do NOT justify its price.Outside of this Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit is an amazing FNAF experience with some pretty decent scares, however it does have the misfortune of them wearing of quickly, if you are deeply immersed into the FNAF Lore, this game is definitely for you, however I cannot recommend the game if this is your first entry into FNAF.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only on night 4 at the moment, but I wanted to share my thoughts so far!First of all, the art in this game is gorgeous. The animations on all of the characters are fluid, there's a good amount of clutter that makes each environment feel lived-in, the lighting is great, and overall it's just really good pixel art. Some objects even have idle animations that play as you walk by. It really reminds me of old-school point and click games where they'd have random objects with their own unique backstory, which is amplified by the fact that you can investigate most of the objects found around the world and get a little bit of text about them. This makes the game feel even more lively, it's like playing a very descriptive book.As for the gameplay itself, I'm really enjoying it so far. The stealth mechanics are fun and interesting, and the little minigames you have to play when you hide are a great added feature and extra incentive not to be found in the first place. Sound lures are a nice and very much needed feature as well, it's very difficult to explore without them. I also really like the side activities  They provide a nice rest point between the typically fast and dangerous  main quests. Another feature which helps even out the pacing of the game is the fact that you need to go to School or do something in the house before you head to the pizza place. Into the Pit really does something that most other FNAF games haven't done, it builds a world outside of the animatronics.I'm also a big fan of the story. Every character is interesting in their own way, and I always felt bad for Oswald's father. I've never read the book but this game does a great job at telling the story itself. Even the little references to the original games which I consider to be a part of this entry's story, they really show off how much respect Mega Cat has for this franchise as a whole. There's honestly nothing about the story I find boring, every part of it is enjoyable.I do have a few small tweaks I would love for the game, which are more-so nitpicks but I do think that they deserve consideration. The most important one is that objectives can be a little unclear, such as  If objectives were a little bit more clear, it would make the game a lot less tedious in that regard. One other slightly annoying thing I've noticed so far is Chica's walk cycle. She loves to stick in the same few rooms and she idles for a good 20 seconds in the area. She also isn't lured by noise which makes her very annoying and unpredictable, along with significantly lowering the amount of time you have to look around for objects required to complete your task. Other than that, I think that the game is extremely well polished and all of the gameplay is very well thought out.Overall, Into the Pit is a fantastic entry into the franchise. I'm really loving the gameplay and story, the art is beautiful, and it's so nice to see an official FNAF game in this style. I do hope, like others, that Mega Cat adapts more of the books in the future (me personally, I'd love a Twisted Ones game). If you're a FNAF fan, you'll love it, and even if you aren't, this is just a great horror/stealth game in general and definitely worth the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a brilliant step up from the most recent mainline games. This is the direction all mascot horror should strive for. This game is unique in every way. The art style takes pixel art, something this series is familiar with, and completely turns it on its head. The animation is so fluid and breathtaking, making every jumpscare feel unique and horrifying. Speaking of, while I wouldn't call this the scariest game ever, it's scarier than any mascot horror before it (besides VR) and feels just as fresh as FNaF 1 did 10 years ago. I love the game but it isn't without its faults, I haven't gotten the secret ending yet but the main ending did feel a bit rushed in the end. And Springtrap was defeated in an underwhelming way. The directions the game set up also felt a bit vague, leading to me being stuck a few times. None of these destroy any enjoyment and there's even a chance the ending improves for me. All in all, this was the best 10th anniversary gift I could have ever asked for. Maybe even being the best in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best FNAF games out there!Into the Pit truly stands out in the franchise with its beautifully written story and atmospheric depth. The narrative keeps you hooked from start to finish, and the tension is palpable throughout. The atmosphere is incredibly well drawn out, pulling you into the eerie world and keeping you on edge. Very ominous and I absolutely adore the pixelated style—it adds a unique charm that complements the horror perfectly.If you're a fan of FNAF, this game is a must-play. I highly recommend it! I look forward to more games produced by this studio in this format, and I'm hoping they might delve into more adaptations of the other FNAF books in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: While it was cool to see the FNAF franchise take a different route like this, Into the Pit is a really bare bones game once you look past the nice spritework. The game presents itself as a story driven experience, as opposed to previous entries which were more about gameplay with the story told through easter eggs and the like, and yet the story of this game is pretty much nonexistent, once you've gone back in time and seen Springtrap replace your dad, you've pretty much seen everything. The game has the player constantly going back and forth from point A to point B while occasionally having to avoid Springtrap, but all you end up doing is going on meaningless fetch quests to progress to the next meaningless fetch quest, the game is so short it can be beaten in one sitting and yet it still manages to be 90% padding.The segments where you have to run from Springtrap get old really quick, it basically just boils down to knowing where the hiding spots are, so long as you don't accidentally back yourself into a corner, you're going to evade him easily, and by that point it becomes more of game of praying he isn't in the room you need to be in because then you'll have to run away and then go all the way back.As I mentioned above, the story is lackluster to the point of not even being there, the first day/night is pretty interesting, but then the only story events you get beyond that are seeing Jeff attack a rat or finding a kid hidden somewhere and then getting chased out, it introduces quite a few characters and locations early on that are forgotten about completely by the second half of the game.Since FNAF 3 the series has had multiple endings, that's just how it goes, and that's cool, but when two of the endings are just glorified game over screens, I should not have to start the whole game over again to collect all the "dad items" just to get the good ending, it lacks any form of replayability as the gameplay gets stale halfway in, so why the hell would anyone want to replay it to get the better ending? There's no motivation.One thing I found kinda fun was the arcade machines you can fix up and play, but when the generic retro arcade minigames are more fun than the core gameplay, is that really a good thing?Now I don't know the story of the book, I haven't read it, but there must be more to it, surely? I doubt the plot of the book is made up of 90% fetch quests.Overall this game really feels like some old shovelware title dressed up in nice pixel art, it's a good direction for the franchise to take in theory, but the execution is just not worth anyone's time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is polished and stylish. There's a lot of attention to small details, little hidden visual things, and beautiful animation; unfortunately the game is bland to the core. The gameplay boils down to linear fetch-quests and shallow hiding mechanics. There's even pointless quick time events while hiding. Mini-games are underwhelming, and opportunity (and reward) for exploration is minimal. The story is nothing  really engaging or interesting either.The game isn't scary either. _childDocuments_.review: All the style of FNAF and the charm of old school side scrolling graphics. It has a few good jump scares but it feels more like a puzzle game than other entries to the series. It's a short game, though, so expect around 4-8 hours tops. Oh, and if you are a completionist, be careful before you enter the final day (it's clear). _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game so far; absolutely love the gritty retro style. The audio design is top-notch as well. Very immersive; the older style graphics allow for a unique horror experience not commonly found in today's market. I'm also a big fan of this particular story from the books. I was not so sure how well it would translate into a game, but so far all the important details (even the smaller ones) are there!So far I'm loving everything about this game, with only one exception; I wish that there was an accessibility option to increase the size of the dialogue text. I heavily appreciate the dyslexic font option, but was surprised to see that (as of writing this review) there is no way to make reading the on-screen text less straining on my old lady eyes. This would become especially straining if played on a TV from several feet away. Please add this as an accessibility option! The game would be perfect if not for that.UPDATE: I wanted to update this review after having completed the game. There seems to be a massive memory leak issue where the game will keep taking more and more RAM over time. If you're a slowpoke like me, this could be an issue. It was running slower and slower and load times were becoming really unbearable. Checked my performance monitor and the game was taking nearly 9GB of RAM and climbing rapidly (for a game like this, that's crazy). Restarting the game revealed that it is only supposed to hover around a few hundred MB to a GB of RAM, but the usage gradually increases over time. This will very likely be fixed in a future patch, but I wanted to mention it. Restarting is a temporary solution to this problem in the meantime, but that can be frustrating as the game does not allow the user to save whenever they want; checkpoints are automated. Easier settings increase the frequency of automatic checkpoints, but that saps out a lot of fun and frights for me.With all of that out of the way, I didn't really encounter many bugs. There was only one game-breaking bug that I experienced during a certain section of the game that required me to restart. Without spoiling anything, there was a part of the game towards the end that had me interact with an object that erroneously made my player character disappear. He was unable to be seen or move. I could open the inventory and main menu, but I was locked out of continuing. Again, this will likely be fixed in a future update, but I wanted to mention it here.The game is fantastic, but it isn't quite fully cooked yet. Is it worth the money, even despite these flaws? In my opinion, yes. The game was a lot of fun and I'm looking forward to discovering more of its secrets in my second play-through. If you're a fan of the series, and if you love older style adventure-type games, don't miss out on this gem. There's also juicy lore bits riddled throughout for those who care to look... If you crave that sorta thing like I do, you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Five Nights At Freddy's initially released with the simple concept of being attentive towards a few cameras and ensuring that you would survive the night from possessed animatronics in a run down and clearly abandoned pizzeria that still feels the need to hire security. Since then, it's become a global sensation that has spawned multiple sequels, spinoffs, merchandise, films, and more. Now with Five Nights At Freddy's: Into The Pit, the series takes the animatronics for a new spin and puts them in the guise of a pixel-art driven horror narrative adventure where you play as a child who simply wants to get his father back after he'd been abducted.FNAF Into the Pit does a wonderful job tackling the atmosphere this franchise has been known for, with a tone that's oddly inviting thanks to its animal-based animatronics that are far from cuddly. Into The Pit keeps the essence of FNAF alive throughout, while also giving creative flexibility and freedom to exploration outside of the usual environment we've come to know throughout the years. Playing in the shoes of a young boy named Oswald who's sick of pizza by this point, you'll be attending school, visiting an old mill, a library, going home to sleep (which is not as safe as one would expect), and, of course, visiting the restaurant. For the most part, you'll be able to go freely between these environments, though unfortunately a lot of these places besides the pizzeria itself don't really hold much value. Oswald's home you'll become familiar with, but frankly the other locations seem like an afterthought, especially the library which only really serves one purpose throughout the entire game. I kept visiting it thinking something would happen - maybe a hidden cutscene or trigger some sort of side event - but it was ultimately all for nothing as there was a small thirty-second segment during Night 4 (of 5 total Nights/Chapter in the game) throughout my 6-7-hour playthrough, and that was it.Even though these various locations mostly felt like window dressing, however, they were all fairly well designed as the pixel art here is really exceptional, and the animations that coincide with it is truly satisfactory. Not just the characters themselves but everything surrounding them from the cloth of a table to the swaying of a balloon to the rolling of a ball and virtually every single detail that makes up the foundation of the art direction of Into The Pit is wonderfully constructed and animated, bringing a level of depth and polish that should be commended and looked at as setting a standard for something outside an HD-2D environment that Square Enix, for example, has come to wonderfully perfect. The time and effort here is all on display, and the game seamlessly weaves all of its love for FNAF, its lore, and tones into a package that I would argue makes it the best FNAF game of its entire property, spinoff or not. It's a great entry point for anyone looking to get into FNAF after they've heard about it for so long, and even just a great game in general for those that want a genuinely awesome horror experience for the weekend.Not only do the animations keep you infatuated with everything happening on screen, but the sound design here is truly phenomenal for those that are wearing headphones. This is where the game truly shines and comes into a league of its own, with deep thuds of footsteps from these heavy machines being heard doors away as they travel from room to room scanning the areas to look for any children to torment. Its droning ambiance, squeaks of a floorboard, screams in the distance, and so much more completely embody your surroundings when the headphones are on, and these are all ineffably mixed in a way that keeps things focused and cohesive, keeping the heavy weight of its atmosphere on your shoulders without it becoming distracting.Rarely does FNAF: Into the Pit feel like it's fighting against you. It's a well designed game that is clearly proud of its accomplishments and puts it all on display as you're playing. It never feels like it's dragging out, and even when you're going from place to place back and forth in a metroidvania-esque fashion, it's all smooth as no locations and their respective rooms ever feel overly large or unnecessary. Every room in the pizzeria and the house was used intelligently, and despite a map, the player should be able to get acquainted with each area fairly quick and be able to remember where everything is without much fault. Everything in Into the Pit simply made sense, and its floorplan is a big benefit to that. Though admittedly there was just a small few of tasks that may not have been immediately crystal clear as it may not be made apparent to some that it's okay to leave the pizzeria during some segments to gather things from other locations. Once you wrap your head around this, it becomes straightforward and understanding. There was only one time I accidentally got an alternate ending because I left the pizzeria a little too early, but that was only because I wanted to make sure what I needed wasn't elsewhere.For those that love retro horror, Five Nights At Freddy's: Into the Pit is a must-play. There's just something that marries beautifully about the genre and art direction of pixels that, when done as well as it is here, really gives off a special experience that remains memorable, all without sacrificing the actual horror itself. Don't let the pixels fool you -- Into The Pit is still every bit as terrifying as any other Five Nights At Freddy's before it, and distributes its scares tastefully and cleverly throughout the game. The scare factor here rivals even the most prestigious of horror titles, and it's yet another thing I can't help but truly appreciate about Into The Pit as someone who loves the genre and art form deeply.

_childDocuments_.review: FNAF: Into The Pit is a fantastic addition to the FNAF Series. With its chilling and frightening artstyle and gameplay, Into The Pit is definitely more scary than other recent FNAF Games. However, the jumpscares and enemy chases can get repetitive after a while but can still make you jump in fear from time to time. Oswald and his father are some of the most interesting characters in the FNAF Series with a good amount of character development for such a short game. Throughout the game, it becomes more and more clear that Oswald's father is just a chill guy who wants what is best for his son and his family. It makes you feel more compelled to go through the game to try to save him because you know that he actually cares about his family and is just doing his best. Oswald's commitment to saving his father at any cost highlights the bond the two have. My only major issue with FNAF: Into The Pit is its lack of manual saves, if you get screwed over by rng or not knowing what to do then you are forced to reset at the point that the game last saved which can be anywhere between a few minutes and around half an hour (can be longer if going for the more difficult endings). Outside of this however, there are very little issues with the game, the game is very polished and relatively bug free. Overall, FNAF: Into The Pit is a Strong addition to the FNAF Franchise and I would highly recommend this game if you are interested in good horror games.

_childDocuments_.review: My first recorded jump scare happened during my twitch steam of this game. Worst part? It wasn't an animatronic 🤣I'd say I became a "fan" of FNAF about 3 years ago. I love the lore across the universe Scott Cawthon has created. It's fascinating but I couldn't play the games. No jump scares for me. Then the trailer for this game came out and I was like "This one I could try.". So, I did and loved it. It's a pixel art game which helps softens the scare, but the audio design did a terrific job at being terrifying.Here, you play as Oswald. A character not previously seen in other FNAF games but a main character in the "Into the Pit" book from the FNAF Fazbear Frights series. If you hadn't guessed by now, the game is based on the book. It's a very interesting and entertaining story. Since I haven't read the book, it's all fresh to me. It is a semi point and click game that moves with WASD with normal point and click mechanics along with minigames and stealth mechanics (and jumpscares).The game has SO MANY easter eggs for fans of the franchise.Going back to the sound design, they did an amazing job at maintaining the suspense and thrill throughout the game. I always felt like I wasn't safe and it was because of the score and sound effects. You become hyper aware of every single sound. Claps for sound design. 👏👏I'm probably 1/3 through the game and I'm so excited to keep playing. Even when I know it'll raise my heart rate, and I will likely scream a few times.I livestreamed on YT and Twitch if you'd like to check it out (and my jump scare).Yet, I highly recommend you try it out for yourself before watching a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: Best FNAF game in the entire franchise, maybe except Help Wanted and Help Wanted 2. It is incredibly well made, and everything in it (Story, gameplay, art, sound, everything I'll go on to explain) feels like such an incredible and fresh entry in the franchise.It's pretty scary I guess? I jumped at certain points, but it feels more like an adventure game than an ambient horror experience. It still has way more horror atmosphere than Security Breach, and it's still quite scary.The art is amazing and incredibly done, absolutely lovely to look at. Even better are the jumpscare animations, like the close-ups in this game look so good. You can see the love in the art.The environments are absolutely incredible. The environments all feel so lively. Seeing kids walk around in the school, seeing only a couple people eating at Jeff's Pizza at a time due to how run down it is, it's all so amazingly crafted. The fact that you can listen into so many different conversations in these areas makes the game feel so fleshed out. The dialogue is just so fun, especially when it's coming from someone random and not one of the main characters. And man, the sound design. The sound design is just so good. The ambiance when the lights go out, the running of the yellow rabbit, Oswald running, how the people scream in the game when something bad is going on. And the main show of the sound design, the yellow rabbit's noises. He says incoherent words with heavy distortion and robotics layered over, but you can here certain phrases such as, 'Come back". And especially the yellow rabbit's growls and breathing, it sounds so deranged and monstrous, really puts the game on edge. This also helps if you can't see him, or wear he's going, because you can still hear him (Which helps on harder difficulties).This game is absolutely amazing from it's environments to it's sound design to the story, everything about it is such a fresh and incredible ride for this series and I genuinely cannot say enough good about this game. I am genuinely amazed and so unbelievably happy with this game and I hope Mega Cat gets to adapt more of these booksThe game does a pretty good job at explaining and showing whats going on for people who don't know the Into The Pit story already. So if you haven't read the story, don't worry, the game follows it pretty well. The game adds some of it's own content, but most of the time either to include other parts of the franchise, or add more gameplay. Overall, the story is fun, and it can work for everyone. It follows the original story from the book well enough so that newcomers who haven't read the book can play, but is also distinct enough from the book, so that people who read it will still be surprised and excited.The gameplay is pretty good, only complaint is that the game can get pretty boring when you learn how the AI works. It goes from keeping you on your toes, to a puzzle game of strategy. My first playthrough on Frightening was the first way, keeping me on my toes. However, trying to beat the game on Nightmare mode with the three star ending, made me have to strategize. Tripping on purpose and then going through the vents to lure the yellow rabbit away, it adds another element to the game that makes it not just scary, but instead quite fun. The game adds something new each night, new animatronics, new rooms, new items, new routes, so the game doesn't feel repetitive. The only thing that feels repetitive are the hiding minigames. If you are in a chase, and hide in something (While the yellow rabbit is still in the room behind you), you have to play a minigame. I swear, you do not know how many times I've swatted spiders. So. Many. Times.Getting all the different endings was super fun, seeing all the different cinematics and secrets. Also seeing references to things like the other Fazbear Frights stories, and the Helpules minigame are quite fun. Overall, the game made me want to get the endings, due to the different outcomes, such as (Ending Spoilers!!):Now, some of the extra content:There are certain ways to get alternative music on the title screen and more, such as getting high scores on all the arcade machines (It tells you in the menu what these scores must be). This is just a small extra, but a nice one.Along with this, after you beat the game on Frightening, you get two new difficulties. Terrifying and Nightmare. Terrifying removes some hiding spots, and Nightmare removes a ton. Along with this, both of these game modes make the AI way more aggressive, meaning that the noise meter can be only risen a bit, and he can be alerted. Along with this, it makes the AI faster, thus in Nightmare mode, running in a straight path is certain to let the yellow rabbit catch up and end your run. And yes, you heard me, END YOUR RUN. Nightmare mode has permadeath. This is why Nightmare mode is the hardest. These difficulties are fun, and while you can just brute force your way through the game, on these difficulties, especially Nightmare mode, you have to strategize and be careful.Now, if you know me, you'd know that if I think a game is good and I love playing it, I wanna 100% it. So, now I'm gonna talk about the achievements!The achievements in this game overall are very fun. Achievements for the endings are all good, and certain achievements let you see certain mechanics in dialogue. I love achievements that give you new outlooks on the game. Hide-n-Seek World Champ requires you to use every hiding spot once, while in chase, survive, and complete the minigame. This made me play hiding minigames I would've never played otherwise. Achievements like A Master Of Stealth made me play the game carefully to beat it without being caught. Some of the achievements that give fun and extra dialogue are Who You Gonna Call? (For Calling 911), answering the phone when it's ringing and talking to Phone Guy, and more. Then there are difficult achievements, such as Good Job, Sport, require you get the three star ending on Nightmare mode. Achievements like these really give you more knowledge on how the AI works, and makes the game feel entirely different. You can't just brute force, or get in chase and hide, because there are so little hiding spots, and all the hiding spot minigames are way harder. Overall, the achievements in this game are challenging and fun. Only problem I have is that the permadeath in Nightmare mode feels like a cop-out. Like, they couldn't figure out another way to improve the AI, so they just said "Screw it, make it that so when they die their save gets deleted!". I find that as a cheap way to make the game harder, rather than to continue improving the AI so it can understand when Oswald is trying to trick him.Scott already said in an interview that he wants Mega Cat Studios to adapt more of the books into games, so I'm hopeful and excited for that!Art: 10/10, Sound Design: 9/10, Environments: 9/10, Gameplay: 8.5/10, Story: 9/10If this was too long to read (Probably was), then overall, I'd give this game an 9.1/10. It is really fun, unique, and interesting to play. One of the only FNAF games where I wanted to play more because I genuinely loved it, not just for lore reveals. I'd totally recommend it. This is not just good compared to other FNAF games, this is amazing compared to other games in general. I'd recommend it even if you haven't read the books, so don't be on the fence about buying it for that reason. It's one of the only games in the franchise I can see people who aren't FNAF fans playing, due to how well made it is.

The autosaves are pretty frequent, which I really do like, as otherwise I'd be really suffering, but I feel like Springtrap(or Yellow Rabbit Agony monster, whatever) is really everywhere, and I wish the game made a difficulty mode that was even EASIER, just so I could focus a bit more on exploring without having to worry about a giant, ugly, wanna-be William Afton killing me every two seconds. _childDocuments_.review: Hello? Hello, hello? Uh, I wanted to record a message for you to help you get settled in on your first night. Um, I actually worked in that office before you. I'm finishing up my last week now, as a matter of fact. So, I know it can be a bit overwhelming, but I'm here to tell you there's nothing to worry about. Uh, you'll do fine. So, let's just focus on getting you through your first week, okay?Uh, let's see, first there's an introductory greeting from the company that I'm supposed to read. Uh, it's kind of a legal thing, you know. Um, "Welcome to Freddy Fazbear's Pizza. A magical place for kids and grown-ups alike, where fantasy and fun come to life. Fazbear Entertainment is not responsible for damage to property or person. Upon discovering that damage or death has occurred, a missing person report will be filed within 90 days, or as soon property and premises have been thoroughly cleaned and bleached, and the carpets have been replaced."Blah, blah, blah. Now that might sound bad, I know, but there's really nothing to worry about. Uh, the animatronic characters here do get a bit quirky at night, but do I blame them? No. If I were forced to sing those same stupid songs for twenty years and I never got a bath? I'd probably be a bit irritable at night too. So, remember, these characters hold a special place in the hearts of children and we need to show them a little respect, right? Okay.So, just be aware, the characters do tend to wander a bit. Uh, they're left in some kind of free roaming mode at night. Uh... something about their servos locking up if they get turned off for too long. Uh, they used to be allowed to walk around during the day too. But then there was The Bite of '87. Yeah. I-It's amazing that the human body can live without the frontal lobe, you know?Uh, now concerning your safety, the only real risk to you as a night watchman here, if any, is the fact that these characters, uh, if they happen to see you after hours probably won't recognize you as a person. They'll pr- they'll most likely see you as a metal endoskeleton without its costume on. Now since that's against the rules here at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, they'll probably try to... forcefully stuff you inside a Freddy Fazbear suit. Um, now, that wouldn't be so bad if the suits themselves weren't filled with crossbeams, wires, and animatronic devices, especially around the facial area. So, you could imagine how having your head forcefully pressed inside one of those could cause a bit of discomfort... and death. Uh, the only parts of you that would likely see the light of day again would be your eyeballs and teeth when they pop out the front of the mask, heh.Y-Yeah, they don't tell you these things when you sign up. But hey, first day should be a breeze. I'll chat with you tomorrow. Uh, check those cameras, and remember to close the doors only if absolutely necessary. Gotta conserve power. Alright, good night.

_childDocuments_.review: While I'm not a fnaf "fan" per-say (I played 1-3 and this one, and watched a play through of Security Breach) I can honestly say that this one has been the most fun single player FNAF experience I've had so far. FNAF 1-3 weren't particularly "fun" in the traditional sense primarily because you were completely static and had a very limited amount of influence on your surroundings. Moreover, it was a far more terrifying and exhilarating experience and was better experienced with friends or as a means to get your blood pumping. Security Breach seemed fun, but there being a Large portion of the game that disallows saving to proceed and make progress, to me, really felt like a slap in the face. Also, the laser gun really seemed to harshly gut the challenge and tension built up until it so I wasn't necessarily that into it. But this game, being pixel art which is something I personally love, being top down isometric allowing for a full range of motion and full view of the environments, being metroidvania adjacent with the constant revisiting of different locations, obtaining new items and abilities along the way, and ultimately having a far more linear sequence of events with a minimal amount of obtuse Easter egg hunting really had my itch scratched and ultimately me walking away with that afterglow feeling of having had a good time. Also, it was pretty cheap being only $20 without discount for a Licensed and Cannon FNAF game. So yeah, recommended.

Any player with a brain will connect dots well before certain gameplay elements are introduced, and instead of rewarding the players intuition and perception it gatekeeps objects for progression for only certain points. I understand this is an indie studio thats why the expectations were not high to begin with, BUT for 20 dollars i expected at least the bare minimum from a 2024 pixel survival horror. I know it recreates the book and has to adhere to the source material, but from a game perspective you feel as if you are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around for 5 nights until the game remembers the initial objective. The only enjoyment you will get out of this is if you are a FNaF fan who is excited to see the story adapted and of course... the secrets. BUT. FROM A GAME STANDPOINT DISCONNECTED FROM THE BIAS OF FNaF's CATALOGUE. I am thoroughly disappointed and sadly cannot get a refund. Watch this game. DO NOT PLAY IT you will waste your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Some things I enjoyed were the visuals, sound design, stealth element, mini-games and instant steam deck functionality. Some things I did not enjoy were the story, unnecessary backtracking and item fetching, certain mechanics, and lack of animation variety. I really liked the new art style they went with this time. Although it is not as scary or atmospheric as classic FNAF or VR, it made the game feel more casual which is nice when I just want to play something on my Steam Deck. It was also cool to see how they translated the Freddy Fazbear and friends to pixel art.Something that consistently stood out to me while playing was the screams and crying they put into the game. The UI/progression noises were interesting as well. They could've gone with some classic beep or boop but decided to go with this crazy Springtrap scream noise which was pretty cool, a good example of thematic sound design. It was also interesting to hear the contrast in different areas of the game. Some moments in the school, like when the kid laughs at Oswald, it's a bit-crushed/reduced sample rate type sound but then when you get into the pit the sounds become more "real" and it definitively added to the immersion of being transported back to 85'.Please do not come for me you crazy FNAF sickos but this story was, at best, minimally fleshed out. You have a time-travel device where your dad gets pulled in by some killer animatronic rabbit and the best we get is a search and rescue plot? No exposition, no clues about why it's coming after Oswald, nothing? Perhaps I'm just not a FNAF theory enjoyer to the point of where I understood the hidden meanings of events in this game but, as with the movie, things are confusing for people that do not already know everything through exterior research out these games. One thing that did consistently pissed me off while playing this was the door opening mechanic. When you're running and hit the door sometimes you automatically go through, sometimes you don't; It depends on the angle or something. Normally you press A to open the door, but what's annoying about that is that there no flow. You stop, Oswald opens the door, then you go through. It's a painstakingly slow animation that, when paired with the unnecessary amount of running around for items, becomes grating quickly. I'm not completely positive whether or not this is a latency issue or not but I felt that there was a fair bit of time between when I pressed a button and the action went through. I felt this with most actions like the door, the spiders, the flashlight, picking up items, etc. I would've preferred more fluid motion of Oswald than seeing him pick up an object or whatever. Pretty pleasant experience. There's a fair amount of replay value with adjustable difficulty that I might try out considering the toughest beginning difficulty was a breeze, I can easily see this being  FNAF speedrun game. I'd recommend this to all my fellow FNAF enjoyers and enthusiasts alike. I will be on standby waiting for the theory videos about whatever is going on in the pit.

_childDocuments_.review: Since this game's announcement, I was worried it would be a rather dull retelling of the original Fazbear's Frights story. Fortunately, after completing this game, I'm glad to say that I was proven otherwise. It's not a super complicated game, nor mechanically in-depth, but what it lacks in complexity it more than makes up for in sheer amounts of polish. I was blown away by how much effort was put into each corner of this game. The pixel art and animation in this game are incredibly impressive, and they help to aid the atmosphere that the developers set out to create.I don't remember every detail about the original book this game is based on, but I'm pretty sure it's not an exact retelling of the original story. While the major story beats are mostly unchanged, there's still enough content in between the most important parts that it avoids making the game feel too dull.I've only played through the game fully once, taking around four and a half hours to complete, which is not a bad length for what this game sets out to achieve. However, it seems that a bulk of this game's content comes from replaying the story on harder difficulties. With the ability to toggle a built-in speedrun timer present in the options, it seems that the developers push for replayability, which I find welcome in any game.I think this game is worth any FNaF fans' time, as it's clear that the developers put all of their efforts into making sure that this game captured what made the original story so engaging, and is a great way to re-experience that story again.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews, and when I do, they’re not this detailed. But here I am. I also wish to state that there should be a neutral recommendation option on Steam because I feel very conflicted about this game. On one hand, this is the first FNAF game I've ever played (even though I'm very familiar with all the lore), and I was really excited to start it up. What I found was a fun yet interesting experience.I loved the sequences and puzzle-solving elements, like how you need to visit specific areas to obtain particular items. For example, there’s a sequence where you need to lure out Bonnie by playing his guitar. To do that, you need new guitar strings, which you find at the mill, a place that makes perfect sense because it’s where the trash is stored. But then there were moments that left me utterly confused, like figuring out how to lure Freddy out of the security room. I thought I needed to flash him with a flashlight or use a camera flash because the sketchbook we received from Gabriel mentioned Freddy was sensitive to light. I vaguely remembered a guy selling crackers at the library on Day 2, but I forgot about him. Without looking it up, I would never have figured out that you need to play a few minigames, redeem a voucher, use the redeemed retro gift to get crackers, and then use those crackers to blind Freddy. And you don’t even have to plant the crackers somewhere or blow a fuse behind a crate—you just need to have them in your inventory, which I find pretty dumb. Sometimes the puzzle-solving is masterfully crafted, but other times, it becomes your worst enemy in progressing through the game.Then there are two other issues that hit you hard if you’re unlucky: the checkpoint system and Springtrap’s spawning. I understand that every game needs a balanced checkpoint system, but Mega Cat Studios spaced them so far apart that it’s brutal if you die. For example, if I die in the middle of a night, I respawn back at my house, which is frustrating if you take escape routes other than the window, especially if the ladder is your last escape option. At least put a checkpoint after leaving the house, so I don’t have to redo so much. Please, for the love of God, just make the checkpoints a bit closer together. I don't know how I can finish this game on the second hardest difficulty, especially with the other issue: enemy spawning. Sometimes I walk through a door and die instantly. Before you suggest it, yes, I listen for sounds...there were no sounds! Other times, enemies spawn and trap me in a corner. For instance, I needed to reset a fuse to restore power, but Springtrap was waiting on the stage. As soon as I entered, he became aggressive and chased me, forcing me into two rooms: the backstage and basement, neither of which had hiding spots that night. This wasn’t the first time something like this happened, with him trapping me in a room with locked doors except for the one I came through, and GUESS who came through that door as well with a YELLOW RABBIT SUIT.Lastly, I know the game was released just nine days ago as I write this, but there’s a bug in my save file during the end sequence where there are two Springtraps, even though there’s only supposed to be one, and he’s in the ball pit with my father. One of the Springtraps is in the hallway where you need to go. Half the time, he’s chill like that and doesn’t attack (I even posted a screenshot on Steam) but the other half, you can't do anything but get killed. I hope these bugs get fixed soon before I start trophy hunting.In conclusion, yes, I might have crashed out while writing this, but I think it's important to highlight these issues. Does this mean the game is bad? No, you can definitely play it. Will you have a good time? Likely. Will you have a smooth experience? From personal experience, unlikely. If you're an OG fan of the franchise, it’s a good game with a great story based off the book. having very subtle and clever references to other FNAF games while also sprinkling new Lore crumbs for us. But if you’re an average player, I’d recommend holding off until some bugs are fixed and certain game elements are rethought and redesigned (hopefully, they will be). Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: Frustratingly cryptic objectives, glitches ranging from annoying to unplayable to softlocking, and a just out of reach sense of enjoyment. It has its redeeming qualities, from art style to story, but it can't save it from the core of a game: the gameplay. Just wait for a big patch to drop, and even then, its not worth the $20 price tag in my opinion.Edit time! Not gonna edit my original part, instead have some clarifications + new thoughts:- Frustratingly cryptic objectivesThis worked on tandem with the glitches to provide an upsetting and frustrating experience. Like, for example, when i could clearly see the rat i was supposed to capture, but the game glitched and WOULD NOT let me capture it, leading to several deaths and a LOT of searching elsewhere before it finally let me. Other objectives are bug-free but are hard to reach in the first place, made harder by certain bad parts of the animatronic AI (Chica's specifically).- GlitchesJust look at other reviews, from the night 4 completely disappearing when leaving monitors bug to un-interactible required items.-Out of reach enjoymentThis game has too little emphasis on either part. It wants to be a horror game, but also a narrative driven one using daytime segments, and that drives a sword down the middle, dividing your place experience and half-baking the ideas present. I would've loved more stuff about the kids at the school, the town itself, or about the state of the town in the past world. Leaving the pizzeria in pit-world would've been VERY cool and feels like a missed opportunity.Yes, the big patches dropped, and I applaud them, because it mostly addresses the glitches present.I bought this game on launch day to avoid major spoilers ruining the point of playing the game, AND to stream it on release day for the extra views. I am in a tight spot financially, like a lot of others, so buying a game instead of using that money for, say, food, is a huge decision right now. That's why I said it isn't worth the $20 asking price. $10 feels more approachable, but I understand developers have to be paid fairly, and I'm all for that. But that doesn't erase or invalidate that opinion.@SonicMaster519 has a point: People can be critical of games. I myself am a huge and long-running FNAF fan AND Theorist, but I can see a game's flaws. You are free to disagree, but the main negative replies here barely contribute any conversation because "ooooooh its a puuuzzzleee gameeee" is just an obvious fact. An obvious one that gets overlooked because the FNAF fanbase is so huge it is omni-genre'd, causing players of all backgrounds to check out these games.That's all, thank you for the awards, that's all.(pssst

detailed_description: Bring the heat with a threesome of fun in Jackbox Naughty Pack . We’ve Seen How You Play Our Games We know you’ve been begging to burst out of the box. It’s time to set your party aflame with a brand new pack of three adult party games that will bring some harmless heat to your next weekend hang with friends. It’s the perfect pack for your next college party, grown-up game night, bachelor/ette celebration, or hump day gathering. Play with your phone or tablet - no special controller required. All three games support 3 to 8 players and 10,000 audience members. We’re spreading the love around the world. All Jackbox Naughty Pack games can be played in English, French, Italian, German, Castilian or Latin American Spanish, and Brazilian Portuguese. A Threesome of Fun Fakin’ It All Night Long (Social Deduction): Fakin’ It returns and this time we’re putting it all out there. Everyone gets a secret task except the Faker, who tries to blend in. Find out which of your friends is the best liar… and SO much more! Featuring new categories like “Finger Blast” and a brand new “remote play” mode. Who doesn’t like a good Finger Blast with their friends? Dirty Drawful (Drawing, Guessing): It’s Drawful, but dirty… It's Dirty Drawful. Hosted by the one and only Drawful Owl, as you’ve never seen her before. We’ve taken the game that you love and added prompts to ensure your drawings are both terrible and titillating. This game has everything:, sex, drugs, and other things that we absolutely cannot list here! Also, if you can’t commit to a relationship, or a drawing, we added an undo button just for you. Let Me Finish (Presentation): Let Me Finish is Jackbox’s new presentation game that examines life’s serious questions like, “Where is the mailbox’s butt?” or “How does this avocado get aroused?” Everyone gets a chance to speak their mind, but will others pick up what you’re putting down? Content Warning Jackbox Naughty Pack contains mature themes and explicit content. It is not intended to be played by children. This game contains references to consensual sex acts, light drug use, non-graphic violence, and crude language. Jackbox Naughty Pack Key Features The more the merrier: Customize your game with content filters, streamer settings, or accessibility options. It’s good to be bad: Discover the next inside joke for your group chat. You have to be an adult to play this game but you don’t have to be mature about it. Find your flavor: Variety is the spice of life. With social deduction, drawing, and debate-style games, everyone walks away satisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not gonna lie, this is extremely disappointing as a hardcore Jackbox fan. First of all, there are only 3 games for this year compared to the 5 games every other year has gotten in their respective party pack (at least the price for this was somewhat reasonable for what it offers). But the worst thing about this pack is that it just isn't funny. Which is shocking considering Jackbox games are famous for their great sense of humor. However, this game just comes across as trying way too hard. Every single joke in each of these games is begging to get a laugh yet only resulted in groans from my party. The thing that makes Jackbox games so great is that the maturity of the games depended on those playing. If you wanted to be family friendly, you could play family friendly. If you wanted to be dirty, you could play dirty. And all of the dirty jokes are funny because they would come from players trying to twist the innocent Jackbox prompts into something dirty. Anywho, now I think it's time I get more specific and discuss my issues with each individual game.Easily the best game in this pack however, that isn't because the game is dirty. It's because Faking It is a great game on its own. The original Faking It is one of my favorite Jackbox games, despite it's many issues. And this new rendition fixes almost every issue I had with the original game. Specifically, the remote game feature is easily the best thing about this sequel (I'd love if they'd go back and add it to the original). This would easily be a 9/10 or a 10/10 if it wasn't trying WAY TOO HARD to be dirty. Every single thing in this game from the animations to the sound effects are 'adult jokes'. And all they do is ruin the experience. This especially sucks because without them, this could easily be one of the best Jackbox games.It's just Drawful. That's it. The only difference is that every prompt is now 'adult-related'. The strangest inclusion of this game is the undo button (something the Drawful series is known for NOT HAVING). Aside from that, it's just another Drawful game. You're not going to get any more out of this than you do with Drawful, Drawful 2, or Drawful: Animate.This game may genuinely be the worst Jackbox game in party pack history. Hell, I had more fun playing ZEEPLE DOME than this. Not only is it painfully unfunny, but the gameplay loop is an absolute slog to get through. Players get absolutely NO time to draw on the screen in order to prepare for their presentation but also, most prompts don't even allow for much creativity and are, as I said previously, painfully unfunny and just plain weird. Genuinely, not even halfway into the game, everybody in my party just wanted it to be over. Presenting wasn't fun, nor did it allow for any creativity. This game is just absolutely atrocious and I'm shocked that no playtesters gave the same feedback.Overall, this pack's release deeply saddens me. This pack's existence just feels straight up wrong. Watching the animations in Faking It and Dirty Drawful feels like Jackbox taking their iconic characters and just absolutely mutilating them. I was already worried when the pack was announced however, I kept my faith in the Jackbox team. I know how creative and funny they can be and I figured they'd find a way to do something unique with the concept of an adult Jackbox Party Pack. But instead, we're left with an absolute slopfest of an original game, Drawful but less funny, and a genuinely good Faking It sequel hindered by the juvenile humor found throughout it. And that is the word I'd use to describe this pack. Juvenile. It feels like they hired a bunch of middle schoolers to create a party pack.I'm genuinely worried about the future of Jackbox Games. After the absolute mess that was the launch of Party Pack 10, the company desperately needed a win this year. But this is an even bigger disaster of a pack than 10 was. I can at least appreciate the team for trying with this game but it just wasn't it. I'm honestly even considering refunding it because this feels like a waste of my hard-earned $20. Please Jackbox, cook with Party Pack 11. I know you guys can do it. And it sucks that I have to be this critical about one of my favorite game companies, but it's the truth.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I have 10 hours in this game currently, and the more I play it, the more I can understand critiques for ‘Let Me Finish’ in particular, but a 27% positive rating on Steam genuinely baffles me. Here’s what I think of the pack after playing it with three different groups:♥♥♥♥♥’ It! All Night Long:I don’t think there’s any denying that this version of ♥♥♥♥♥’ It is vastly superior in pretty much every conceivable way. That’s the one thing most people can agree on. Remote Play not only makes it way more accessible, but is also a much faster, and more intuitive mode for displaying player answers so they don’t have to remember everyone’s actions (except Thumb Shot) and allowing time for the Faker to discern whether their answer will get them in trouble shortly before everyone else can see it.	The original ♥♥♥♥♥’ It used to be among my least favourites with immense anxiety as the faker when being silently judged for 9 whole seconds before even being able to defend your answer with Same Room gameplay. But with both the Remote Play mode, and the naughty prompts really defining a target set of expectations, along with these prompts being on average more opinion based, the riskier prompts in this version ironically make me feel  comfortable playing this version as the faker.	8.5/10Dirty Drawful.The game said it. It’s Drawful but dirty. It’s hard to describe, but this is simultaneously the best version of Drawful, and the worst version of Drawful. Let me explain.	Here’s why it’s the best version of Drawful: Each player now has an additional colour to work with. There’s also a new ‘reroll prompt’ button in the drawing phase. Pacing is generally faster in most areas, animation is no longer here (thank God) and the  reason why this is the best version of Drawful: an ‘undo’ button (which can also be turned off via a special setting.) Due to the less filtered nature of the prompts, lying is also generally a lot easier in this version as well. Emotes are also here, and they can prove to be fun… in small doses at least.        And here’s why it’s the worst. The removal of the ‘Make Your Own’ mode and ‘Friend Mode’ from Drawful Animate. The more I think about it, the more reasons there are to  add these modes to this Dirty version of Drawful, but I do miss them. Secondly is… also the emotes. If you play this game with the wrong group, particularly online, the emote spam can get quite annoying due to each emote having their own unique sound effect. You can turn down SFX volume in the settings, but I would appreciate a setting that targets the volume of emotes specifically.	In short, this is easily the best version of Drawful as a  game, but in terms of a full package with extra modes and content, Drawful 2 and Animate are superior when talking exclusively about that metric.	8/10Let Me Finish:The brand new game. The presentation-debate game where you argue your points on weird raunchy arguments. Usually about object anatomy or kink analysis.	We’ve never seen a real debate Jackbox game like this before, and it handles the turn-based argument structure of the game really well, and forces players to be creative in ways we’ve never seen from Jackbox before. Arguing is simply just fun, especially when handling inconsequential opinions. But if there’s one thing that brings this game down, it’s the lack of variety in prompts, with a dash of cringe-factor.	Each image has three accompanying prompts, levelling from NICE, to NAUGHTY, to NASTY. The problem is, you’ll only be seeing one ‘NICE’ prompt in one game, and if you play again with the same players, you won’t see any ‘NICE’ prompts for the rest of the session. Singular ‘whereis’ images suffer the most from lack of variety, and most prompts from these images boil down to ‘locate the butt, locate the penis, locate the vagina, locate the titties.’ When most singular images boil down to those prompts, it’s a  breath of fresh air to get a ‘dress-up’ prompt or something else.	‘Lineup’ images suffer less from this issue, and as such are a lot more engaging as these mainly focus on personality analysis, but are still mostly sexual.	The argument aspects of this game are really fun, and have produced the most laughs out of all games in this pack in my experience, but the prompt variety isn’t as much as you’d like. I’d like to see this game get some extra prompts that are edgy, but not necessarily sexy.	Still a pretty fun time, but I wouldn’t play multiple games of this in a row.	7/10A couple more things I’d like to point out. This is an adult pack, and to force the players to be naughty while still being fun is something that very few existing Jackbox games can do. To everyone asking for a dirty Quiplash or a dirty Trivia Murder Party, what you are looking for is adult DLC. One of these games is too open-ended to work as an exclusively naughty sequel, and the other is a trivia game, and limiting the trivia to just things about sexual anatomy, obscure kinks and drag queens narrows the appeal of the game tenfold. I promise you, if either of these games got naughty-specific sequels, you would hate them more than the games in this pack. Please take more than three seconds to think about why your proposed naughty-sequel could work. Most of them don’t, believe me, I’ve spent a long time thinking about this.	Secondly, this pack is waaaay better in person, or with people you know. ♥♥♥♥♥’ It ANL requires you to know your players, and Let Me Finish requires you to be confident with speaking. If you only play these games online with strangers, you won’t find much value here. (hmmm maybe that’s why this pack is getting review bombed, maybe all these other reviewers are chronically online minors)	Thirdly, not only does this pack have a very specific target audience, this pack also has the worst price-per-game ratio from a Jackbox pack to date. Still way more efficient than buying standalones, but I digress. So when considering this pack, ask yourself  do you want an intimate naughty pack?All this to say, these are the reasons this pack is getting review-bombed; and quite frankly, it doesn’t deserve any of it (apart from maybe the price thing, I can get behind that.) You knew from the start that this pack had a specific target audience. And if you’re not the target audience, what authority do you have to clown on this pack for reasons that this pack shouldn’t have to consider? You are allowed to be negative in these reviews, but please think critically about why you think what you think, and if your reasons even apply to this pack as an adult package. Especially if you're reviewing after less than an hour of play. Play through all of the games so that you actually know what you're talking about.Thank you for coming to my Ted talk.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game on the first day of release, was kind of disappointed first of all of it only having three games although it's not in the main "franchise" of party packs 1-10 - so I get it. My honest review after playing it for two hours in a Discord call tonight:# Faking It All Night Long (the first game which Steam somehow wants to censor)It was really fun in the beginning. I've never played the SFW version myself so it might've just been like the normal one. Overall it was fun, but I wouldn't recommend it among a collective group of "friends-of-friends" if not everyone knows each other. That probably goes for the normal one too.The prompts were creative, the visuals and the ass-slapping on screen made us all giggle the first few times... Everything else looks to me like the normal SFW version in pack 3 (from the looks of it).# Dirty DrawfulIt was like any other Drawful game, but with NSFW prompts. I generally don't like the Drawful games, and I didn't really like it more here. There's funny prompts to what you are supposed to draw, but the colors you get is like drawing on the moon with wet diarrhea on your paint brush.We were also SO ANNOYED by all the emojis with sounds, and myself got a headache when the group spammed it constantly. You start to wonder if you have like 20 tabs of porn open in the background randomly moaning, or if your house is being hit by anvils again - like any other day obviously, but then you look at the screen being filled up with weird emojis covering anything else happening on-screen. We could also not turn this off during presentation of the drawing or when the narrator was talking. It even sometimes covered up who guessed or made a prompt, the actual prompt etc. - but our group collectively shared half a braincell, so it might've been "human error", whatever that means.# Let Me FinishA complete waste of time. "Which one of these kitchen appliances gets satisfied by pimple popping?" and the only fun thing we did was draw non-proportionate shafts on everything. And I mean everything. Even the dishwasher had one, with some really hairy balls. And, "How would this mailbox 69?" - the hell? This one was actually kinda funny to get for the first time, but still; what the hell.And no, it would not work as a SFW version. At least not better than this. I would imagine prompts being like "Which phone is the best?" and then you still just draw penises everywhere.# Cumclusion - the conclusion but I accidentally came multiple timesIf you either* like Faking It (the first game in the 3-game pack)* like the creators* have a collection of all party packs (like me), or* would like a peek at the Jackbox characters' oiled and firm buttocks once every half an hour (this is where I came)then go buy it. _childDocuments_.review: Really didn't want to leave a negative review. Jackbox is one of my favorite game developers out there. I always have an amazing time playing these games with friends and family and keeping an eye out for the annual release. I'm even one of those weird Pack 10 defenders.But this pack was not it. Even after seeing all the negative reviews, I was still willing to give this game a chance. But when I got on a call to play with friends... it really wasn't great.First off, let me get this out of the way: the new ♥♥♥♥♥ It is good. It's really dang good. The new question types and remote play options are great additions. Even with the sexual prompts, this was an absolute winner.The other two games weren't so great. Dirty Drawful is just Drawful again but with kinkier prompts, not much to say there. But good God, Let Me Finish is probably the worst game Jackbox has ever made. I absolutely mean that, worse than Zeeple Dome. It felt like a really unfunny game of Cards Against Humanity. No comedic timing and the only punchlines are just "haha penis funnie!" The first prompt my group got was something like "Which of these bird statues masturbates to Twilight novels?" Like, what am I supposed to do with that? Got to the point that we had bigger laughs taking the piss out of the game's prompts than actually playing it properly.I commend Jackbox for doing what some fans have asked for in their customer surveys. But knowing what I know now, we really didn't need this. A lot of the comedy of Jackbox comes from sexual responses from players to otherwise normal prompts. It's all about the creativity and comedic timing. When every single punchline has to do with boobs or sex, it gets old REALLY fast. It's not just uncomfortable for people who don't like sexual humor, it's boring for people who DO like it on occasion like myself.If this game goes on sale for like $10, definitely get it solely for ♥♥♥♥♥ It All Night Long. But I can't recommend this as an entire package at the price they're asking for.I really hope Jackbox bounces back from this. I'm crossing my fingers that the Survey Scramble and their next project are fun and high-quality. After the mixed reviews of Pack 10 and the abysmal state of this pack, they need an absolute banger.EDIT: Great job Steam, censoring "Faking minus the letter g" but "masturbate" is totally fine lmaoooo

_childDocuments_.review: The Jackbox Naughty Pack is Jackbox Games is an ambitious pack by the company as it is their first M-rated pack going more explicit and lewd. This pack definitely is not for everyone but is still a fun time when playing the right people.FIANL: To be completely honest, this is my favorite in the whole pack and expands on the concept of social deception and the OG even further. Even though I would've preferred a tamer sequel first so everyone can do the remote play option, I see why Jackbox instead opted for a spicy sequel. There are still plenty of regular prompts mixed in with very lewd and explicit ones as well. As well as new categories! Overall, it's a great improvement on the OG adding quality of life improvements. With the best thing being that it is streamable with the remote play.Dirty Drawful: Although I do like the premise of Drawful, I do feel that Dirty Drawful is pretty uninspired and a disappointment. The prompts are definitely quite lewd and I'm not fully comfortable drawing certain explicit things. Though that is just a preference of mine so don't take that point to heart. There are other changes such as more color options, using emojis, and switching prompts, but I am still not a fan of the deliberate typos. And the prompts are too weird for my taste. And I know this might be like a rant, but I really don't like that there are player-specific prompts in the game and no option to turn that off because that can become painfully uncomfortable. And I do make it a strong point of mine to not direct sexual, inappropriate commentary to specific players. As I want people I'm playing with to be comfortable as well. I have no problem with raunchy, sexual humor, but it can easily cross boundaries if it's directed at someone. Because you don't know how they will handle it. That all said, if you do love Drawful and don't mind being lewd with your drawings and forgive aspects that I've mentioned, then Dirty Drawful should work for you.Let Me Finish: Being the only new game in this pack, Let Me Finish I think will end up being quite underrated. It is a presentation game so having people able to vocally present and/or on VC is a must for this game to work. There is no Present For Me option so yes, it is mandatory. This definitely does not make it a bad game by any means however, and the reasonably short timers allow just enough room to string together a few jokes without it being stretched out to a point where the joke runs thin. Plus, the option to jump in at any time even if it's not a round you started off is a huge plus in my opinion. The prompts and the images are quite funny too so being able to twist those into something even more ridiculous appeals to me.Overall, I think this is a fun, experimental pack done by Jackbox that goes even further for a great mature experience. Despite my disappointment with Dirty Drawful.
