_childDocuments_.review: As an avid Jackbox fan, this one is a huge disappointment. It takes two previous games and one original game and applies a naughty theme on all of them, and... well, I feel like it doesn't get the "naughty" theme across as much as the "what is up my fellow degenerates" vibe. It just doesn't feel right if the game is providing the horny prompts as opposed to the players providing the horny answers. But that might just be my own preference.The games themselves are... Well, they're fine, in a sense... But going over them one at a time:It's Faking It, but naughty. This one got the best treatment out of all of the games in this pack, since it now supports remote play, something that wasn't supported in the first game, so you had to do some huge workarounds to get it working remotely. Honestly, if the we could have the prompts from the first game and apply it to this new version of the game, I would absolutely love that.It's Drawful, but naughty... That's it. Nothing more to it... I guess it does have an undo button, something that the previous Drawful games didn't have. Beyond that, I would argue that every other version of Drawful feels more fun to play.The only original game in the pack and it's bare bones. You're given pictures, and you're supposed to make drawings on them and then present your argument for the prompt. It feels like the very base of an idea for a game, the place where you start building a game upon, but there's just nothing beyond that. In its entirety, the pack does have fun games to play, but there are much better versions of those games already available in previous packs. If you don't mind fiddling a little bit with Discord (or whatever communication app you use) to play a game of Faking It remotely, then the original, in most cases, is more fun to play. If you want to play Drawful, any other version of that game is about as good, except with less raunchiness. And if you want a presentation game, Junktopia, Talking Points and Patently Stupid all have so much more to offer than Let Me Finish.To finish off, I do not write this review because I think the games themselves are bad. I just think that the naughty theme does not exactly work with Jackbox games as a whole, and the games that have been included are either inferior versions of games we already have, or there are already different games that work so much better available. So the question I leave you off with is: while the games in this pack can be fun, why would you buy this when there have better alternatives for sale for many years already?

_childDocuments_.review: After going in with an open mind and playing the games a few times each. I must say that I just don't understand the review bombing that this game is getting. I don't think this is the best jackbox pack in the world, but I don't really think anything it does really makes it deserve the 28% positive rating it has on steam as I write this.Faking it all night long - 9/10Faking it was always a jackbox game that I thought always had potential, with it just being unfortunately stuck in pack 3 while the team was still trying to work out the audience of their games. So just the fact that they bring it back here, make it playable with 8 total people instead of 6, and make it fully work remotely is just perfect. My only biggest worry here is that the prompts would be too out there, something I was worried about on the whole as I watched trailers and reviews. But after a few rounds, I think the tasks and prompts aren't as bad as I feared, actually making this into one of the all time greats of jackbox I think ♥♥♥♥♥ it deserved to be. I'm glad at least most people seem to agree this is the best of the pack.Dirty Drawful - 8/10I mean its drawful, but dirty... Its not a bad game but its the least interesting of the pack. I do like the features of bringing in a new color and an undo button (which you can toggle on and off in the settings menu, i'm guessing this was put in so that people drunk off their mind wouldn't draw incoherent nonsense). Honestly there is a bit of novelty to feeling like more answers are on the table and could be real compared to some drawful games, especially after they kept the naming schemes of prompts from drawful animate (which you can also have swapped out once per game when in the drawing phase if you wanted to make something else, I feature I kind of think should be in every drawful from now on ngl). Also the addition of emotes are neat, but I feel like there should be some settings to lower their volume or turn them off if players want that.Let Me Finish - 6/10This game honestly fluctuates for me depending on the group I play it with, it definitely takes a creative mind to get some real fun out of it, but even then I feel like the groups of people I've played it with considered it fun or a neat concept. So the people saying this is one of the WORST games in Jackbox's ENTIRE LINEUP just feel out of touch to me (Like have any of you even PLAYED Lie Swatter or Zeeple Dome???). I did see one repeated task while playing it a few times, which might have just been unlucky on my part. But I think having a quick paced presentation game like this is pretty neat, and players being able to jump in and speak their mind if they want is a pretty interesting addition. Also I saw some people say they don't show the scores until the very end, but actually you can check them at any time on your device, honestly pretty cool feature that I also hope returns in some other games.Miscellaneous thoughts: I think the soundtrack for this game continues on with Jackbox excelling with different types and ranges of music recently, with a more jazzy feel for this one that heightens the themes on screen. I also like that there is a button for the VIP to switch to another game after completing one, like I didn't even know that was doable?? Another cool feature I hope comes back honestly.So in the end, I'd give this pack a solid 7/10, and I don't think that is bad at all for 3 games in one pack for $20. I get that it might not be for everyone, but saying this game is straight garbage just makes me feel like people are growing a fatigue for jackbox in general. Like I just want to stress, this is NOT JACKBOX PARTY PACK 11, this is clearly something smaller and more experimental, made for fun if anything. I saw plenty of people complain about the fact that there is only 3 games for $20, which I guess I do agree that the price could be a bit lower for these. But honestly I do find it strange that people have the Jackbox Party Starter at an incredibly positive rating when it also does the same thing of having only 3 games in one pack, and even then those games aren't even original, and even THEN, the games they picked are all represented in pack 3 anyway so whats the point? Also another point I want to mention right at the end that I found weird is how there is a good chunk of bad reviews made for this game that have a playtime of 1 hour or less, hmmmmmmmmm, suspicious...TLDR, Faking good, Drawful strange, Finish requires creativity, price could be lower, but pack doesn't deserve this amount of hate.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally gave this pack a thumbs-down on day 1 because I thought the games it had were weak, especially the new one. They just released a major patch update that addresses most of the problems we had for it. Every game has more prompts, and FI:ANL and LMF both have content filters now. The games on the "nice" settings still aren't very family friendly, but I will say it's nice for people who want the sex and horny prompts to be rarer and more sprinkled in. Drawful now has a way to turn off emojis, which is the only thing I didn't like about the game, so W there. Most of all, though, they actually managed to fix Let Me Finish. It has a new game mode now where you finish all your drawings in one sweep like Quiplash, and you can even add captions to your drawings. Then, it rapid-fire goes through all of them and has everyone vote on which one is better, just like Quiplash. I don't think this game is better than Quiplash now, but this combined with the ability to make the prompts cleaner, and the game is more enjoyable and is actually funny. I can't believe I'm saying this, but I like Let Me Finish now.Overall, even though I don't want this to become a habit with the company, I think this fix makes the pack worth buying, especially if you don't have a version of Drawful. The pack is on sale on their website now, so strike while the iron is hot and buy, I'd say.My old day 1 review:(I tried really hard to like this pack and keep an open mind as it got released. I played a few games with someone who got the pack early, and have played each game in the pack a few times, and I was very underwhelmed by the lineup for this one. There are only 3 games, which is already a bit of a turn-off, and even $20 is a little steep for what we have here.♥♥♥♥♥' It: All Night Long is pretty much the only game I think makes the pack worth buying at all. It adds new prompts, has a ton of QoL improvements over the original, and I had a lot of fun with it.Dirty Drawful is just regular Drawful with new prompts. It's fun, but it's also not something I couldn't have just made myself with custom prompts in the older versions. The only new things this version brings to the table is 4 colors per person and an undo button. A fun time, but I would much rather them have made a sequel to a different game, or perhaps a second new game altogether.Let Me Finish is just weird, and I really don't see it being enjoyable or funny for multiple plays. It's not very varied in its kinds of prompts, and it gets stale fast. I only see this being enjoyed by groups who are sleep-deprived or very drunk.Overall, even though it hurts to say it, I think this one was a flop. I can only hope this is a segway or breather so the team can work on something much bigger for next year's release. I'll be coming back to this pack for the better version of ♥♥♥♥♥' It, but that's about it.)

_childDocuments_.review: So let's talk about the Naughty Pack... after the 10th pack came out, many people were mad, that the quality went down, games were bad and Jackbox Games should make some changes. Many said "make less games per pack if it means, they're all good quality". I think Jackbox Games listened and tried to do that - many are mad about this decision. I am not very mad about it honestly. As long as all the games are good, I'd be fine with 3 games only. But they'd all have to be good...So about each game:LET ME FINISH is the weakest game in this pack. It isn't terrible, but needs some changes. This game needs players to make all the fun and to improvise HEAVILY. Many prompts are super random and it's quite hard to make them funny. And what I really think should be changed - the times are too little. When you have 15 seconds to explain your points you're making on the spot, it's quite hard.Still... it wasn't that terrible... so I guess for now I'd give it a (4/10) with some possible changes and additions it may get even 5 or more. DIRTY DRAWFUL is fine, pretty good. But it has an issue - it isn't original at all. We have 3 Drawful games and this is a 4th one which... yea... not ideal. In this pack we have 3 games only and 2 of them are remakes of some old concepts... well whatever. If we ignored that, it has extremely good prompts honestly, they did great job there. It's pretty funny. VERY 18+ though lol. I like the music, the emoji efects, it's just good. If it wasn't the same old Drawful, I'd give it more, rn I guess I'll give it like a solid (6,5/10)FAKING IT ALL NIGHT LONG is great tho. Like honestly... idc it's not original and a remake of an old concept, since the last FAKING IT came out so long ago and this one is finally able to play remotelly. IT'S FREAKING GREAT. While yes, some rounds are easier for the faker than others, and some prompts are almost impossible to guess fake... it's really good and really fun. We played 2,5H today and like 2 hours was only FAKING IT over and over again. It's good and doesn't get old even when repeating it multiple times. It was funny, nice animations, nice music, nice ideas... overall I'm happy. THIS is how I hoped whole pack would be, so this one game was all I wanted and this game deserves great (9,5/10)Overall:Average game score is 6,66While this may not be as much as other packs have, I think it's more than pack 10 has which... I guess it's a move in a fine direction when it comes to the quality but... rather small move, not enough.Idk... I was excited about this pack, but it didn't deliver really. As I said - I wouldn't mind having only 3 games AS LONG AS THEY'RE GOOD. But one is meh and one average. If LET ME FINISH was better, like a 8/10, I'd not mind that much, I'd be very happy. But it's really weak and has flaws. So they didn't really meet my expectations and they weren't even THAT big.Overall still - it's a FINE pack. It's fine, you may have fun with it, probably will. But will you enjoy all games? Not at all. Is it worth the money? OH COME ON... COME ON, Jackbox Games... 21 euros for three games? And one kinda sucks??? If they were all top tier I could accept that... but for an average pack of 3 games it's TOO MUCH.So while I reccomend it... for full price? DON'T BUY IT! For 10% sale? DON'T BUY IT. 30%+ sale? You may consider it. But do not waste your money people.This may be my last review of Jackbox party pack game... because if Jackbox games don't fast make their games cheaper or worth the price... I won't be buying more packs.

HOWEVER, this pack only having 3 games is very disappointing and the games honestly "suffer" by making the gimmick being "we are naughty too". One of the best parts of JackBox is the unexpected craziness of someones answer being out of pocket and dirty to create that comedic whiplash. When the game TELLS you to do it, the impact of being weird yourself is gone. Honestly should have just made a 5 game JBPP 11. This isn't to say that this game isn't presentable, but in comparison to all the other packs? Definitely needs work...
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Naughty Pack

_childDocuments_.review: Actually surprisingly bad, especially considering the price:- Let me finish is likely one of the worst presentation games, essentially being worse than Talking Points in every conceivable way. The ability to "pitch in" to a presentation is a good idea though and could be implemented in upcoming presentation games.- Drawful is just that. Drawful. But with "naughty" prompts. If you own one of the Drawful iterations that allow custom prompts, you can play this game already.- Mechanics-wise, ♥♥♥♥♥’ It All Night Long is actually a great improvement over the old one, notably adding new types of votings and improving the last round, in which you previously never got to see all of the Faker's answers, as this round was essentially unwinnable for the them. The new online mode is a good addition as well. This is the only game in the pack worth playing, which is why it's a shame that this version is locked behind largely unfunny "naughty" prompts.In summary: Save your money. Maybe wait for a Steam sale if you want to play ♥♥♥♥♥ it 2. This one ain't it, folks.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Naughty Pack

_childDocuments_.review: For a supposed "Naughty Pack", the games were rather juvenile. In a group setting, we could not finish a single game without wanting to quit immediately and move on to other Jackbox games. You would have better luck making a "spicy" game out of the other preexisting jackbox games than with this. Jackbox games are usually very good when it comes to keeping things new and engaging for groups. But when there are successful adult themed group games out there like Cards Against Humanity, this one falls terribly flat. Would not recommend this at all - save your money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Naughty Pack

_childDocuments_.review: Huge miss.  Only three titles... two of which are rehashes of older games.  I have been wanting a new ♥♥♥♥♥' It for along time, so that's welcome.  Another Drawful sequel?  Uninspired.  We have SO many of these.  I feel like for the price they could've slapped together a "dirty" Quiplash at least, but it may not have helped.  The worst offender is the new drawing game they've added.  It's just... not fun?  This game could be fixed *maybe* if the players came up with the prompts for each picture before the drawing part.  At least then when it's not funny it would be on the players instead of the game.  The baked in "dirty" prompts are just really unfunny and difficult to respond to...  I question how much this was playtested.I play Jackbox titles with friends almost weekly.  Many games do depend on you having a funny group who meshes well and gets each other's humor.  Unfortunately this pack doesn't provide a good set of tools for us to accomplish this.  I'm shocked this was released as is.
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Naughty Pack

_childDocuments_.review: My friend group and I had pretty low expectations going into this pack. The low game-count and slightly cringey trailers made the $22 price tag seem a bit steep, but we gave it a shot and honestly, the pack is actually not that bad!Let me start by saying that your mileage will definitely vary with this pack because of the nature of the topics and prompts (some may come off cringey, and some may probe a little too deep and cause awkwardness). However, we found the prompts pretty funny and enjoyable! ♥♥♥♥♥' It All Night Long is an 18+ take on the original ♥♥♥♥♥' It game from an older pack, a game which we weren't totally fond of beforehand. This new version, though, breathes a bit of fresh air into the game type with new round modes and obviously new somewhat raunchy prompts. This game was the one we played the most on this pack on our first playthrough, and if we weren't limited by time, we would've played more. The second game on the pack was Dirty Drawful, which was also enjoyable (even for someone like me who is terrible at drawing)! The prompts were funny, and the ability to request a new prompt for drawing is a nice quality of life update. I also gotta give it to the creators because they are getting very smart with the prompts/answers - they make it hard at times to decipher if the drawing description was one they made or one that your friends made. The final game on the pack was Let Me Finish and let me be honest, this was the first Jackbox game that we ever stopped playing partway through. The game concept and its prompts are really strange - the game didn't really jive with us. Definitely the "throwaway" game of this pack.Overall, I would recommend picking up this pack despite the low positive review percentage! My only caveat is that I would suggest waiting for the pack to go on sale first, because $22 for 2 good games (at best) hurts a bit. However, if money isn't a huge deal for you, I think it's worth giving this pack a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: The Jackbox Naughty Pack

_childDocuments_.review: I own every Jackbox pack but this one is just a nope for me. The prompts are so cringe and forced adolescent humor, we just couldn’t really get into it. That being said, I wish this pack was a regular non-naughty pack cuz the fact they made ♥♥♥♥♥ It so we can remote friend play (ie. Livestream play) and Drawful to have color, erase, and reactions is really freakin awesome. I hope they have this as part of the next party pack. But this naughty pack is a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: I only play online in video calls, so I never had a good opportunity to play the original ♥♥♥♥♥' It since it relied on seeing each other's actions. I'm so, SO glad they refactored it to allow for remote play, and I love the reimagined Adult prompts. ♥♥♥♥♥' It is in fact a great game but I never understood that because I didn't have the means/environment necessary to play it in its original form. As such, I feel satisfied that I got my money's worth based on ♥♥♥♥♥ It All Night Long alone. The fact that Let Me Finish is also a clever, quirky, creative new twist is just a bonus on top!Personally, I'm not a Drawful person - I didn't buy JNP with the intent of playing Drawful, and I'm not factoring it into my opinion of this pack. I feel that FIANL and LMF are both worth the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not as bad as the reviews make it seem to be. It's definitely not for everyone, but there's nothing inherently wrong with this game.♥♥♥♥♥ it All Night Long - Easily the best game in the pack. Plays pretty similar to the first game, but now it has a remote play mode to make it much easier to stream than the first game.Dirty Drawful - It's drawful. I don't have much to say on it, but it's exactly as it says on the tin. Probably my least favorite personally.Let Me Finish - Horrible for steamers, even worse if you don't have a dirty mind, but if you're in the mood and you can use your imagination, it's actually pretty fun. Plus, I appreciate that everyone in the group can share their thoughts.I recommend this game because I had a good time with it. It is a little lame that they only had 3 games, but this isn't supposed to be the Party Pack 11. If you have a dirty mind, and if you have friends with dirty minds, it's worth a go.

_childDocuments_.review: Played a little bit of each game from this pack and I'd say it was decent fun.♥♥♥♥♥ It All Night Long is basically just the original ♥♥♥♥♥ It with slightly more sensual art and questions relating to sex. While I haven't played it myself, I do enjoy the addition of a digital answer version so that the game can be played long distance over a call, which was a shortcoming that the original had. Dirty Drawful is just Drawful but the prompts can be sexual (or not, it depends) so it's definitely fun like the original Drawful but doesn't do much else gameplay wise.Let Me Finish is alright, but some prompts definitely fall short and answers can get kinda samey. Occasionally there would be one that was pretty funny though. I wish it had some sort of special final round that was worth more points or had a unique gimmick, and breaks between rounds to show point totals as opposed to just showing the score total at the end.Overall, the pack is decent, but you probably don't need it if you already have ♥♥♥♥♥ It or Drawful in other packs. Also, the price tag seems like a bit too much considering it's just three games, two of which are just reskins or two pre exisitng ones. If you really wanna get it, I'd say wait for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: To summarise, the Jackbox Naughty Pack is a great addition to the jackbox set. I rate it 8/10 overall, and will discuss below the reasoning behind my overall rating going into detail on each game. It is very fun to play with a group of friends, and I would recommend to anyone who likes playing adult spicy games with friends. I am a big Jackbox fan who has played all 10 of Jackbox's party packs and the naughty pack. I do think it is worth the money, even with three games. ♥♥♥♥♥ It All Night Long 9/10I am a very big fan of this game. I was a big fan of the original ♥♥♥♥♥ it, and this version just made it 10x better. Not just because it had naughty prompts, but it was just better in every way imaginable. Firstly, they made it more players, which of course makes it easier for the faker. Secondly, they added majority voting instead of everyone needing to vote the same person. Thirdly, they added two different ways to play the game, in person and remote play. Fourthly they added a new gamemode which is just as fun as all the other gamemodes. Fifthly (if that's even a word), they made it so that for the word game (the end round) that you vote for the faker after all three sentences are completed, rather than doing it after the first or second. This way you get to see all the questions and answers. On the original faking it me and my friends waited for the third anyway but having it this way so it forces you to do it is much better. Lastly, the questions are great. I was worried hearing about the Jackbox Naughty Pack because it primarily came from party packs which were family friendly. I thought them going from family friendly to 'Naughty' would cause them to do very mild questions. But I was wrong. The questions were funny, personal, sexual and it honestly didn't feel like they were holding anything back at all. It really felt like Jackbox listened to its community with this game which is amazing, people asked for extreme dirty questions with many added features to faking it and that's exactly what they did. The only thing stopping me from giving this game 10/10 is that I would have enjoyed a larger quantity of personal questions. There is definitely some in there, but I would prefer a bit more. But this does not stop it from being an amazing game.Dirty Drawful 7/10I gave this game 7/10 because it is good but quite honestly, it shouldn't have been one of the games in the Jackbox Naughty Pack in my opinion. We have already have three drawful games previously. The only thing they added in this drawful game was naughty prompts which you could already do by adding custom prompts in previous drawful games. The game therefore added nothing new.  It was just the same game I have played for many years just with some new emojis that you could put up on the screen. It also felt as if it was a bit of a downgrade. I absolutely love drawful animate, which of course I have played with friends with custom dirty prompts many times in the past. Going from that to a version that isn't animated just seems like a downgrade. Again, it's not a bad game, but it's just the same game as we have played before, and slightly worse because it's not animated. Faking it all night long made much more sense to be in the pack because not only was it an upgrade in every way possible but also there was never any custom prompts in the original ♥♥♥♥♥ it, making it perfect to add for a naughtier version. This is not the same case with drawful. Let Me Finish 6/10Let me Finish is the new debate style game, with the naughtiest prompts/questions of the entire pack. In terms of the questions, it is amazing. They didn't hold back which again I love to hear. But I just don't think this game has much replayability. I only played one game with 8 different prompts (8 players) and even that started feeling repetitive. It's not a bad game, I just can't say it's a great game when it felt like the same thing over and over. It is compared with Talking Points, which I absolutely love. I never get bored of Talking Points and the humour of that game is so funny hearing people trying to get through their presentation with the most absurd ideas. I guess it's this game is the same concept in terms of you have to say absurd things. But many people agree with eachother anyway. I don't know maybe for the right person or the right group of friends other people might find it more enjoyable but for me it just wasn't my type of my game personally.  ConclusionOverall I still think it's a great pack. Mostly for ♥♥♥♥♥ it all the night long, but if you haven't played much drawful in the past or you might have but not played it with diry custom prompts, then you have at least two very solid games here. Which in my view makes it worthy of its price point. I know people are dissapointed of the amount of games there are in the pack, since most normally have five. And I have to admit I was dissapointed, but at the same time i would have rather this naughty pack came out than a new party pack with five games. And that's because this is basically an entirely new genre. And when you look at the price it is currently around £17 with this new introductory offer. New party packs when they first release are around £30. So I don't think people can say it's not worth it's price point when it's almost half the price that a normal pack releases. Jackbox realised there were less games, and therefore priced it respectfully. I don't think we will see a Jackbox Naughty Pack two honeslty, which is sad, but i'm happy we got this and I will definitely be playing more of it in the future.

name: Star Trek: Resurgence
detailed_description: Star Trek™: Resurgence is a narrative-driven adventure game created by former members of Telltale Games that delivers all the excitement and wonder of the Star Trek universe. As first officer Jara Rydek and enlisted engineer Carter Diaz, you will join the crew of the U.S.S. Resolute, a science vessel on the edge of Federation space. Its mission: to prevent an ancient and powerful force from engulfing everything in its wake.
about_the_game: Star Trek™: Resurgence is a narrative-driven adventure game created by former members of Telltale Games that delivers all the excitement and wonder of the Star Trek universe. As first officer Jara Rydek and enlisted engineer Carter Diaz, you will join the crew of the U.S.S. Resolute, a science vessel on the edge of Federation space. Its mission: to prevent an ancient and powerful force from engulfing everything in its wake.
short_description: Authentic Star Trek adventure from former members of Telltale Games. Engage in diplomacy, pilot shuttlecraft, and use your tricorder and phaser to overcome challenging puzzles and deadly threats. Tough decisions will impact relationships, your story, and the fate of the galaxy. What will YOU do?

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to finally play this game, now that it was on Steam. Long-time Trekkie. I've enjoyed the other "Telltale" formula games I've played, and Star Trek was a natural fit for the strong narrative and decision based gameplay. This felt very much like returning to the era when Star Trek was still Trek (pre-2009). I liked most of the characters, and most of the story, and will be happy to revisit this for different choices from time to time.Well worth the price of admission if you're a fan of the TNG era in particular. In fact, I enjoyed myself so much it's had me wanting to go back and watch my blu rays, as well as try out many of the books I haven't read yet.Thank you to the devs who clearly poured their passion for Star Trek into this. I sincerely hope you have an opportunity to bring us more adventures with the Resolute and beyond.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: This is likely one of the best Star Trek media in decades. It feels like living through a full season of Star Trek with the best story themes from TNG, Voyager and even DS9 with a bunch of familiar and returning characters as well.It plays pretty similarly to anything from Telltale, including weird mini-games.There are however some noticeable issues, notably the hair and faces missing shadows. Most of the time, it makes the hair similar to the hair from Dragon Age Origins back in 2009. It seems there is one layer of post-processing missing.Most characters are also missing shadows in the scenes onboard the various ships, plus there are some frame rate issues even on a high-end PC, especially around the mining tractor beam scene.Overall, I still highly recommend the game to anyone who even remotely likes Star Trek.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: So far I manage to get to investigating the ion storm being directed on the ship and going covert into the mining operation. I have played this game on the steam deck and it does run the game on the deck, tho be aware that it does stutter a little but not enough to hinder the game play. This is a good love letter to any star trek fan and I would recommend giving this game a chance for both fans and new people alike.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very story-driven game and so far I've found it very engaging. Star Trek fans will love itGraphically it's good, not outstanding but good enough for the type of game.Sound is great, speech is excellent.It's like an interactive film, I've found myself closing it to play something else then deciding to start it back up again to continue my play through as I just need to continue the story
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely enjoyed this game. It truly felt like you were playing an episode of good Star Trek. Voice acting was top notch. Story was fantastic, and making choices was quite difficult. Even though the destination was roughly the same, it was the journey that made it, and the choices dictated that slightly.Sure, animations were very stiff, but they were good enough that the jank faded away behind such a great story and cast. Gameplay was basic, it is mostly a Telltale type narrative experience anyway.I really hope this is one in a series. Would love to follow this crew on more adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing story, you can tell this was made by fans of Star Trek, they understood not only the lore and mechanics of TNG/DS9/Voyager Star Trek, but they understood the spirit of this era of Star Trek. The story took me about 12 hours to beat the first time, and I am letting that story settle before I start a new run, maybe one a little less kind to certain officers on the bridge......
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: So the game is a pretty good story as a chose your adventure. _childDocuments_.review: Works great on Steamdeck!If you’re a fan of Star Trek, this is a must play. All the choices in the game make you think, the characters are great, the story is fantastic and by the end you’ll be proud of your crew and little starship.The gameplay is simple and made of a few easy puzzles, walking around, button prompts, tricorder scans, phaser shooting sections and dialogue choices, but they work to keep you involved in the story.I can’t recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: The exploration is uninteresting, the combat & stealth mechanics are clunky at best and the game did not get enough polish (which is the biggest problem with this game).  Story-wise it has some good and emotional parts and it *does* have the feel of Star Trek, which is nice. The actions/conclusions of some characters are very difficult to understand and the meaninglessness of many player choices is unfortunately a bit too easy to see through.The game mechanics and story feels like they have been made separately - one does not support the other. It's not a horrible game, but given the chance I would have chosen not to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: This Game has INFURIATED ME!!I played the Demo, then started the actual game.  I got a ways in a decided to start again, because I wanted to chose different options.   The Demo and my first (Half of a) Playthrough, the mini games seemed okay.  A fun Star Trek game that feels very faithful to the source material.However, when I started the second time, it felt like the Minigames were a little tougher.  So I get to the "Castaways" Chapter, trying to Hack into the computer in like the First Mini-Game, and I'm stuck.  I literally cannot get past this mini-game.I have watched people play online that just breeze through it, but in my game the FORCE in which the game pushes my marker our of the zone is incredibly strong, and the meter drains FASTER than it charges.  I've tried with both the Mouse and Controller, and it is literally impossible to keep the cursor in the area.  If you do manage *somehow* to keep it in the area long enough to charge the meter at all, it's almost instantly drained the moment it leaves the area.  I'm not some noob gamer either, playing Boggle and Tetris on my XBox.  Dead by Daylight, Helldivers 2, Ready or Not, and a slu of other competitive games.  I rarely if ever get "stuck", especially in Mini-games as simple (and usually fun) as this Star Trek game.  However, since there is no contingency option.  Nothing to make the game easier to try to counter it, no way to skip a game.  So, I'm quite literally stuck, and on the dumbest mini-game ever.I'm assuming my particular game is just bugged somehow.  Every once and awhile I'll load it up, try again in my controller and Mouse, get frustrated and turn it back off.   A fun game but not worth the money if it can't be finished.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: While not filled with exciting game mechanics, or puzzles like Star Trek 25th Anniversary or Final Unity, this game has a very solid story and great characters. They did a great job of capturing the spirit of Star Trek, and I'm thankful to enjoy some good quality Star Trek again after 20 years of s**t.  Would instabuy a second Trek game from Dramatic Labs.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Great story, felt like it picked up from the TV show. Full of adventure, action, and emotion. Exciting, fun, and entertaining. Multiple choices, your choices shape the narrative of the story. Lot's of new faces, and a few familiar ones as well. Only negative thing I have to say is the game is a little glitchy in certain places, but still very much playable. Graphics are beautiful as well. Did one full play through, and have started on my second for different dialog choices and to see if they impact how the story will end. Hope this helps you decide if you'd like to buy it or not. I feel it's worth what I paid, and brought back some nostalgia in the process.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: A few hours in. The story is pretty good! Amazing character development, and Trekkie flare. I'm sure the uninitiated to the franchise would still have a good time. Trekkies - this is of course, a must-buy.Edit: Played a bit more. I honestly can't stop. I can't remember the last time I've had this much fun in a game. It's one of those choose-your-own ending games. I've had pretty good system performance. Few graphical glitches. Yeah, the graphics seem dated, but the creative art design is well in alignment with Trek lore. There's some moments that are actually very immersive in its level design. Just been really excited about this game during my first playthrough and hope my review helps other people make a decision. I highly recommend this game!!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Good storytelling but held back by poor performance and graphics.I'm enjoying the story so far with its good dialogue and interesting characters. However the game just doesn't perform well. For graphics that look like just a few steps above a Flash web game of 2005, it can barely keep 30fps at 4K on my RX 6900XT. _childDocuments_.review: As a fan of telltale games and a long time fan of Star Trek, I was excited yet hesitant when I learned about this game. I have been looking for a good Trek game since finally getting into the newer series that have been coming out. And this has been the game.First the good:The characters have depth and distinctive personality. They feel like they belong in the Star Trek universe and you will find the ones that you like and don't like. This is a story first and foremost, and a good one at that. I felt pressure when making decisions because I could tell when they would have weight. And the story itself feels like it could have been taking straight from an episode of TNG. Some of the quick time events are actually very neat, . (Some did feel a little forced but it was most likely a way to make sure there were not long chunks of time were the player is doing nothing at all)And for the difficult ones there is an option to play through story mode after you fail so you never get stuck anywhere, although I wish this was stated more clearly.Then the bad:If you need to have your games with perfect frame rate and no lag or stuttering, don't get this game. Some of the animation is chunky and there are certain graphics that lag out my fairly decent computer. The base walking animation looks unnatural compared to the better scripted animations (such as in a proper cut scene where a character is doing more than just walking).Some of the quick time mechanics have widely different sensitivities when it came to joystick movement, maybe it is better on keyboard. And some of the controls throughout are just a little unrefined. Its more a minor nuisances that anything else.It also won't have a ton of replay ability, it probably be more like rewatching a movie than replaying a game and making drastically different choices. I do wish they would have chosen a slightly more stylized art style. There are sometimes where the animation of the mouth does not line up with the dialogue or the teeth look way too thick. But that is being extremely nitpicking for a studios first game.TLDRIf you liked Telltales games and Star Trek, get this game now so long as you can be forgiving to it. If you like Star Trek and are open minded about the game, get it. I am already in love with this game and its characters and am dreading finishing it because I don't know when there will be more content like it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited a very long time for a game that made me feel transported to the TNG/DS9/VOY era of Star Trek. And this is it. Rather than being a phaser combat simulator with Star Trek icing on it like so many other games, Resurgence is plot and character-driven. You'll have to set phasers to stun every now and then, but your primary weapons are your wit and your rhetoric. Resurgence asks players to consider the responsibility of leadership in Starfleet, whether on the bridge or the lower decks, and discover what choices we would make to either uphold our ideals or resort to force when under pressure. Players' decisions will shape the their relationships with other characters and the outcome of an engrossing story that builds upon one of the stranger nuggets of early TNG episode lore in a really satisfying way. I highly recommend this for anyone who loves those good old fashioned, chewy Star Trek ethical quandaries and enjoys seeing the crew of their favorite ship somehow navigate them with aplomb while avoiding catastrophe by relying on their intelligence and faith in each other. With Resurgence, you get to be a part of just such a crew and help lead them to the satisfying conclusion.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this was my very first experience with the Star Trek universe, and i have to say: I really wish it wasn't. This game, apparently, was made by a lot of the old Telltale crew who made a lot of my favourite "choose your own adventure" games back in the day, but this one does not even come close to those. But, first things first:If you want to know whether this game is worth your time or money, it hurts me to say: Unfortunately, no.And if you want to know why, let me explain:You switch between 2 characters: First Officer Jara Ridec, and Petty Officer Carter Diaz. Your ship, the Resolute, is tasked with taking an Ambassador to an alien planet to help keep the peace between 2 hostile alien races at the brink of war.As Ridec, you take an active role in the peace talks, while as Diaz you take a more "hands on" approach with whenever mechanical knowledge is needed.During the talks however, you discover a more sinister mystery that, if left alone, might change the universe as we know it.The story is well told, the characters are likeable, and during my first playthrough i was thoroughly entertained. The pacing could have been improved, at times it felt to slow, especially when i already knew what was going to happen, but it never took me out of the story.Unfortunately, this is where my praise ends.The gameplay is utterly unbearable! Every single minigame is horrendous. It goes from scanning machines, unscrewing screws, and turning levers to literally shooting ice. And you can not lose (most of them - but i'm getting to that). 90% of the minigames are time wasters, the game holds all progress until you get them right. And as I said, you can not lose. Until it gets to the QTEs.Yes, in good old Telltale fashion, Quick Time Events are back, and basically the only danger in this game. Whenever you fail one, it usually ends in your death,  but the timing is so generous, you will have to be blind, deaf and having a stroke to miss one.The bread and butter of a Telltale game however are the decisions you make in dialogues. In other TT games, your decisions feel like they have more impact than they actually do, since the group affected by them was on a smaller scale, and you knew their names and faces.Here, you are the second in command on a large spacecraft, so when you make a bad call that results in hundreds or even thousands of deaths you will feel nothing, since you never met any of them.Puzzling is also the timer during dialogue: Whenever you can choose an answer, a timer goes down, so i assumed that, in TT fashion, if you don't answer your character will remain silent. However, that is not the case: The game just stops. It waits for you to make a call. Why is there a timer?But, what bugged me the most are some decisions made in the story. A lot of you will be familiar with the concept of "chekhov's gun". For those who don't know, it is a rule in writing that says that  For example, if there is a gun in the story, there must be a reason for it, somewhere in the plot.This game has multiple such scenarios, and almost all of them lead nowhere.Ridec being a Kobliad and needing a rare element to survive? Leads nowhere. A possible love triangle with Diaz and his 2 love interests? Nowhere. Ridecs possible love interest? A possible cure for the infection? So many wasted opportunities, I am not sure why they were even brought up.Telltale used to be better that this.I am a big fan of the old Telltale games. It is save to say that without their "Walking Dead" games or "The Wolf among us" I would not be as much into story games as I am today, and "Tales from the Borderlands" is among my favourite games to this day. But this one... it just hurt.As I said, I enjoyed the story itself, but whenever the "scanner" symbol appeared on screen I groaned, because I knew the next few minutes will be agony. I am glad however to see that they still make games, I just hope they get their groove back before long.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Trek fan, this is a decent experience.  But only as a Trek fan.  As a game, it's very poorly put-together.  Dead-eyed facial features with expressions that border on cartoonish at times.  Main selling point being branching relationships, but no load/restore feature to walk back choices or view alternative responses -- quit the game entirely and resume from menu to pick up from your last checkpoint.  No dialogue skip option, no cutscene skip option.  Background music at a default level that's distracting rather than complimenting, and inappropriate to many scene tones.  Clear gaps in the porting process, such as directions to maneuver RS when playing a keyboard and mouse.  Want to back out of the pause menu, click 'Resume' -- if you hit 'Esc' you're offered to quit to main menu entirely.  People will have subjective views of the artstyle and story, but to me these things I've mentioned are the things that take away from the overall experience of the game, that distract or flat-out break the flow and curb the enjoyment of a Trek fan's experience.  If more options and fixes are patched in I will amend this, but for now I cannot recommend this without curiosity and deep discount being significant motivators.EDIT:  Having commented on the game in the mid-to-late third of the run and finished at roughly the 12-hour mark, I can tell you that very little has changed my opinion of the product as a whole.  Yes, I found myself invested in the story despite the flaws.  But I was holding out hope that completion of the experience the first time would unlock a Chapter Select or comparable feature, something to streamline a second playthrough.  It did not, and recalling my previous point of there being no dialogue or cutscene skip option, I find myself utterly unenthused at the thought slogging through the flaws again just to satisfy my curiosities regarding choice and dialogue.  For a game whose main selling point being its choices defining the story, there is very little incentive towards replay to explore those different choices.  To sum up: an experience for a Trek fan, one I don't regret, but one not worth repeating.  Holding out hope for future Quality of Life updates that may make a second helping more palatable.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great Star Trek movie. Because at the core that's what it ist. A movie that needs some input by the viewer. I had a great time with the story. If you are a fan of TNG/DS9/VOY era then you will enjoy it. That is: if you don't have the expectations of a great game.Because on the game side of things, it isnt good. The mechanics are honestly quite boring (mostly clicking stuff, quick time events and some not to well done shooting and stealth passages) and the difficulty at some points mainly results of the bad controls. You mostly walk around and click some stuff. Then sometimes in dialogues you have to chose of serveral options, most of which influence how the NPCs think of you. But the impact on the story outside of relationships seems quite small, so i don't see any reason to play it a second time. On top of that, i would really have liked some challenging puzzles. So most of the time, you're just moving on through the story and all that clicking stuff is there so you stay focused. Pro: I liked the tricorder handling passages and would have loved if they were used more in an "adventure like" game with, as already said, challenging puzzles.Regarding the technical side:  I don't care about the graphics. They aren't state of the art, but thats fine. I can deal with that easily because of the great storytelling and atmosphere. There are some glitches like animationstates changing roughly, textures not loading correctly or models popping up, but not too many to enjoy the story. So, coming back to the story and by that the main selling point: It is GREAT. I love the golden age of Star Trek, especially the later parts of DS9, since there a more... realistic version of starfleet is portraied where not everyone is perfect like in TNG. This is the case here. The characters mostly have believable thoughts and emotions and the player himself can chose to obey orders from the captain or ignore them. So you will not be able to avoid upsetting fellow crewmates, especially in the parts where you play the first officer. The storyline itself around the 2 civilations that are nearly starting a war with the federation joining in as a mediator also fits perfectly into the universe. It really felt like a Star Trek XI movie. And since i wished that they would have gone on with the TNG/DS9/VOY era movies instead of the reboot stuff i get exactly what i wanted for years here.So, TLDR:I recommend this "game" if you love the golden age of Star Trek and want to watch a great movie in that scenario.But if you're looking for a good game with interesting and well thought out mechanics you won't find that here.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I genuinely loved it. Closest any ST game has come to feeling like I was actually playing a Star Trek episode. To take a random early episode of TNG and spin it out into a full narrative like this was a genius move. Rather than the cringe fanservice fest of something like Picard this felt completely genuine. Other than a couple of unremarkable appearences by Riker I hugely appreciated this aspect of it.The story and writing were excellent and I felt like my choices were actually mattering - even if it all leads up to the same ending. I do feel like there were a bunch of unresolved plot points but you can't have everything.Visually it looks great, especially environments and effects. All of them were great, although character animations left a lot to be desired. The audio was overall wonderful, music especially was great and the voice actor performances were good, even if some of the mixing was off. (Hilariously I felt like Jonathan Frakes' performance was the weakest.)Only downsides were a handful of unforgivably bad quick-time events and relatively frequent audio bugs. The performance was also not the best. All of which could be looked past quickly enough once they'd past.I loved my time with it and really hope they get to make more, though I am not holding my breath.

_childDocuments_.review: Not releasing this on Steam from the beginning was a huge mistake, and so many people I know who are big fans of Star Trek didn't even know this existed. Epic only releases are where gems like this go to die.I wont spend a lot of time on some of the minor issues other people have mentioned, namely the fact that the animation can be, at times, not the most modern looking. However, the story and voice acting are superb and most of the set pieces are good or at the very least serviceable. My only major gripe is the responsiveness of the quick time events. Most of them are just tedious, especially when effort has been put into interactions with various computer systems or your tricorder. The PC controls for many of these QTEs are very sluggish.This entire narrative adventure blows a lot of newer Star Trek TV content out of the water and really feels like what Star Trek is supposed to be. There are a couple decisions made for the sake of story and "player choices" that are odd, specifically how Starfleet Officers behave or react to a couple situations, but they provide you with hard choices to make and some depth to the characters so its easy to look past. If you are a fan of Star Trek and are craving for a game that feels right out of the TNG era, this is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game for the Star Trekkiness of it all, and recommend it wholeheartedly as a narrative experience.When it tries to be an actual game, though, it's kind of awful. The FOV is unadjustable and the framerate and resolution are very limited unless you mod the game. This doesn't matter much when you're in conversations and decision making moments, but when the game moves into exploration mode, or, especially in a phaser fight, things are borderline unenjoyable. I am a Y-axis inverter and  because of the FOV, I think, doing that in this game feels terrible, especially in the many cases where you're not piloting a person, you're moving a cursor around a menu or controlling someone's hand directly on a console, and the inversion feels completely wrong.Some of this is made better with a mod that ups the framerate and gives you some more resolution options, but a side effect of that mod is that the QTE I think expects the low frame rate and therefore you have to move your mouse VERY FAR to get to the same place. Like picking it up off the table so you can bring it back to the far right to move it further left multiple times in the same action.This is a great Star Trek story, but kind of a terrible gameplay experience. Go in with your intentions set to "choose your own adventure" and don't be afraid to quickly fail combat missions so that you can quickly replay them in story mode, and I'd very happily recommend this game. I honestly like it very much, but it can be hard to live with.Thanks!

They were fun, yeah, but never this engaging. The first real emergency had my heart pumping. What to decide? So many options, unclear which one will keep everyone safe. Man. Most people have mentioned them, but I will go over a few. First, video controls are non-existent. Because of this there can be a lot of tearing or wonky movement from characters. I don't mind that it doesn't look photo-realistic. I'm here for an experience. If you can do that with stick figures, I'm in. That is my biggest gripe. People have mentioned that your decisions don't matter. I don't know. I would have to do a second play-through to find out. All in all, even if not a single decision matters, this game at this price is absolutely amazing and I hope that they continue with projects like this in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: ~ DIFFICULTY ~🔲 My 90 year old grandma could play it✅ Easy🔲 Normal🔲 Hard🔲 Dark Souls~ GRAPHICS ~🔲 MS Paint✅ Bad🔲 Meh🔲 Graphics dont matter in this game🔲 Good🔲 Beautiful~ MUSIC ~✅ Bad🔲 Not special🔲 Good🔲 Eargasm~ STORY ~🔲 This game has no story🔲 Like playing Temple Runners for the story🔲 It's there for the people who want it🔲 Well written✅ Epic story~ PRICE ~🔲 Free🔲 Underpriced🔲 Perfect Price✅ Could be cheaper🔲 Overpriced🔲 Complete waste of money~ REQUIREMENTS ~🔲 You can run it on a microwave✅ Average🔲 High end🔲 NASA computer~ LENGTH ~🔲 Very Short (0 - 3 hours)✅ Short (3 - 15 hours)🔲 Average (15-50 hours)🔲 Long (50-90 hours)🔲 Extremely long (90-110 hours)🔲 No ending~ FUN ~🔲 I'd rather watch paint dry🔲 Hard to enjoy🔲 Repetitive✅ Actually pretty amusing🔲 Ride of your life~ REPLAYABILITY~🔲 It's a one-time experience🔲 Only for achievements✅ If you wait a few months/years🔲 Definitely🔲 Infinitely replayable~ WORTH BUYING ~🔲 No✅ Wait for sale🔲 Yes----------------Star Trek: Resurgence delivers a compelling experience for fans of the franchise, bringing players into the rich universe of Starfleet with an engaging narrative and familiar characters. The game captures the essence of Star Trek, creating an environment that feels authentic and respectful of its source material. Attention to detail is evident, with a focus on story-driven gameplay that emphasizes the moral and ethical dilemmas that are the hallmark of the series.The story in Star Trek: Resurgence revolves around a critical mission that threatens the stability of the galaxy. Players are thrust into the role of a Starfleet officer navigating political intrigue and complex relationships. The narrative is rich with plot twists and turns, keeping players engaged and invested in the outcome. The writing is strong, and the dialogue options allow for meaningful choices that impact the storyline.Gameplay in Star Trek: Resurgence is a blend of exploration, puzzle-solving, and dialogue-driven decision-making. The mechanics are intuitive, making it accessible to both newcomers and veteran gamers. Missions are varied and often require strategic thinking, reflecting the intellectual spirit of the Star Trek franchise. However, some segments may feel a bit slow-paced for those expecting more action-oriented gameplay.The visuals of Star Trek: Resurgence, unfortunately, do not meet high expectations. Even with top-of-the-line specifications, the game struggles in some areas, indicating a lack of optimization. Additionally, players may experience dialogue cutting off mid-sentence, with subtitles continuing, and music that sometimes does not match the theme, breaking the immersion. These technical issues are a notable drawback in an otherwise engaging experience.Overall, Star Trek: Resurgence succeeds in delivering a captivating and immersive experience for Star Trek fans but is let down by technical shortcomings. Despite these flaws, the game manages to capture the spirit of exploration and moral complexity that defines Star Trek.Star Trek: Resurgence gets a 6/10.For more reviews check my Steam profileHope you enjoyed my review, god bless you

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek: Resurgence is one of the best Star Trek stories made in the last 20 years. It doesn't make a great first impression. The game has, to be blunt, some serious technical issues. For what it's worth, I think I'm at the tail end, with more technical problems than most, but there are issues. The game seems to run at an unlocked framerate, but several scenes and animations appear to be locked at 30 FPS. The mouse and keyboard controls straddle the line between functional and broken. There are numerous rendering and display issues, including Z-fighting on surfaces, improper shading, render layer issues, the soundtrack sometimes inappropriately stops and starts, and on top of all that it cooks my system far in excess of what its visuals justify. This is in spite of a simple visual style and, let's just say, very economical animation. BUT, the story. The story is excellent. It's Star Trek, down to its bones. It understands the vision of Star Trek's world. It has great characters and voice performances. It understands that questions about ethics are one of the pillars of the franchise. It understands that Star Trek isn't Military Sci-Fi. It understands the kinds of characters that Starfleet officers are. This game loves Star Trek- on a deeper level than the authentic sounds effects, LCARS interfaces everywhere, and the lovingly created interior of the U.S.S. Resolute (which it will let you tour independent of the story- be still my beating heart!). This is possibly the best Star Trek item released since Deep Space Nine. It can put up respectably in comparisons to The Undiscovered Country. Star Trek: Resurgence is the kind of storytelling that more recent entries have so often disappointingly failed to deliver.It's not perfect. But I can't recommend it strongly enough. It is, in summary, cheaply made, with ambitious ideas, unshakable belief in optimistic principles, a superb cast of characters, and its conceptual reach greatly exceeds the grasp of what the team can technically execute. In other words, it is exactly like classic Star Trek. Made me feel like a kid again. More please!

_childDocuments_.review: Updated after beating the game:For a Trek fan, this game is pretty much a must play. It's exactly what it looks like in the trailer: take control of two different protagonists with two different POVs, and make key decisions that will guide the story as the Federation encounters a threat to the known galaxy.For everyone else, this is basically telltale game. A choose your own adventure video game movie that lets you make key decisions that may or may not have drastic implications in the story down the line. You don't need to know Trek to have fun, but it certainly helps.As far as story and characters go, I thought it was excellent. I may have cried once or twice, and I want nothing worse than to return to the Resolute for Season 2. The game isn't perfect though.Specifically, this is not AAA quality: the graphics and animations get the job done, but they won't wow anyone. The specs of your hardware also matter a lot more than you'd think they would too.For such a visually unambitious game, it can slow performance down to a crawl at times, depending on how "busy" the scene is (regardless of whether you can see or interact with elements that is actually static set dressing). It's disappointing they didn't target a better Steam Deck performance, but the game is technically playable, and unfortuantely I don't anticipate a performance patch when the game has actually been out for over a year already on the Epic Store.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't even begin to express how thrilled I was with the story and characters.  Despite the flaws of the game (clunky controls and animations, slightly dated graphics), the story and choices I could make along the way was truly movie-quality programming! The story was one long movie (or a perfect 10-episode story like recent Trek) with so many choices along the way affecting your experience.  I love the ship and crew - TNG era with Galaxy Class elements remaining in a ship retrofitted with Sovereign-style technology.  It used in many places holographic displays to remain canon with modern Trek, and it honored the Discovery-era computer voice, cementing it as the stand-in for Majel.  Also like Discovery's final season, it used a TNG episode as the basis of the story - and I think it did so marverlously better than Discovery did.  Having the Titan and Captain Riker involved was cool as well.  If they made another game, the Ceritos would fit well as it's in the same era!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really write reviews on Steam that often these days, but I have to make an exception for this. As someone that has had to sit through the years of microtransaction phone games, garbage third person shooters, disgraceful ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ TV shows that go against everything Star Trek - everything that Hollywood and the AAA industry has ♥♥♥♥ out on this franchise - this is one of the best Star Trek games I've played in quite a while. The storytelling, characterization and empathy in your choices clearly comes from actual Trek fans and not some absolute hack in Hollywood like Alex Kurtzman. A lot of the mini games and mechanics - especially using your Tricorder to scan through different forms of data - truly makes you feel like you a member of Starfleet on an alien planet. Yes, there are flaws. The performance is very choppy at times, the graphics are a little dated and reek of 2010s Telltale animation, and the Mouse and Keyboard controls are weirdly wonky, but I was able to put all these aside and enjoy a great outing in a franchise that has otherwise been cooked for the last decade. Whether on sale or for its regular price, get this game immediately if you love Star Trek or a story based point-and-click adventure game. I'm feeling a STRONG 7 to a LIGHT 8.

Sure, I wasn't a fan of the game pad feel but I got use to it on a keyboard.  The story wasn't the best Star Trek story I've seen but it felt like I was in the world of Trek.  And the ending was done well.  It's worth the money, especially if you are a Trekkie.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Sure, the graphics and audio are a bit wonky, and people are gonna complain about it missing settings for pc users. But all in all, I really enjoyed it. I felt engaged by the story and characters, surprised by the twists, and (mostly) entertained by the gameplay. I'd love it if they made another and would 100% get it!Btw: I've no idea what its like for someone that wasn't previously a Star Trek fan in any capacity, but I still recommend people at least try the demo to see if they vibe with it (Its free after all!).
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: The question I'm asked is, simple;The answer, depends..... If you are a fan of the TNG/VOY/DS9/ENT-era, you will feel just at home. Lots of conversation choices and basic walking-simulator-like actions. Simple things, like moving your mouse over an item, or click and move the mouse over a screen, or press this button and click the mouse, etc... this is how you complete many little QTE mini-games. I was worried the quicktime events would be those super quick QTE's, but so far the game is very easy, very simple. I normally hate QTE-games, but this one doesn't feel like a burden or challenge.The gameplay is simple, easy and somewhat, oldschool. Some conversations you want to pay attention to, as they have subtleties and details to catch. So far, I'm finding the characters interesting and mostly well done. Nothing like the new era of ST. I haven't noticed any of that modern "wokeness" that some have posted in the STEAM forums. If anything, this is in line with TNG and VOY. So, if you're okay with those two series, you'll be just fine here!.... If you were never a fan of the slower diplomatic/ideological Star Trek (TOS up until Enterprise), then you won't like this. This doesn't feel like any of the modern Star Trek.This is also NOT for those who are looking for a highly polished AAA title. This title screams lower-budget. If you can't stand walking simulators, or older-style adventure games, stay away!A few extra comments :Voice-acting is top-notch! Very immersive and gripping.Game is not always graphically in AAA territory, most of the effort seems to have been placed on the character faces, eyes and subtle show of emotion and reaction. I think this is fitting, and the lower graphical fidelity of some scenes doesn't bother me, in light of the type of game this is.The menu is abysmal. Feels like a placeholder for an Alpha/Beta. Game also runs very poorly @ 4K, on system specs that are wildly above recommended. Game uses UE4 and some users have issues with the engine. You can turn off motion blur in the menu, because it makes the game look absolutely horrible.The game has a demo. I suggest you take advantage of it to test it out.In conclusion : For fans of TNG, VOY, DS9 & ENT!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Classic Telltale Gameplay in the Star Trek UniverseThis is a fun and engaging narrative driven story/game set in the Star Trek universe.  You join the crew of the USS Resolute as it's new first officer and also as a member of the lower decks engineering crew.  The ship is undertaking a critical diplomatic mission to broker peace between two species in conflict.The gameplay is the classic telltale style with cutscenes interspersed with quicktime events which can be disabled completely for a more story focussed experience.If you like Star Trek you will likely enjoy this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: A great idea in theory, but none of the choices you make really matter. The same basic events happen and there is barely a difference in the ending based on which characters you choose at certain points - and even then, there's just a lazy mirroring of each outcome (same dialog, movements with just your character choice replaced).That's probably the most disappointing part - this could have been such a good game.  As it stands, its a decent episode of star trek where you have occasional breaks in the episode for a faux-interactive piece to run around or push some buttons. There are so many dialog options but there isn't much flavor to them (should I pick the obvious be a ♥♥♥♥ for no reason option, or reasonable option #1 that makes one person mad, or reasonable option #2 that makes someone else mad?). They ultimately don't have an impact on anything (fire phasers or photon torpedos? evasive action or fire? polarize hull or rotate shield frequencies? Nothing matters). Most of the actions you have to take in the game are pointless timed button clicking.  The game would have been much better with actual meaningful choices and a branching storyline instead of mini games that aren't really fun and just serve to lengthen playtime. Almost no choice in the game has any consequence aside from a few places where you just die instantly if you don't push a button in the 5-second timed event which.. isn't really hard. On top of all this, there is almost no replayability because you can't skip or speed up the cut scenes at all or continue the game at arbitrary points in the story.edit: I forgot to mention that the saving system is horrible - if you close the game before a saving checkpoint, too bad. You'll have to sit through 10-15 minutes of cut scenes you've already seen. The reason why my play time is so high for this game is that I just had to leave it running 24/7 so that I didn't constantly lose progress when I had to step away. This combined with no ability to skip or speed up cut scenes combines for a really awful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Finally. We have a Star Trek game that feels like Star Trek. I've been playing Trek games since the 25th Anniversary point-and-click. Nothing since then has come close to feeling like you're actually serving on a starship as Resurgence. Years ago a tweeted at the old Telltale developers asking for them to make a game like this. I'm glad some of that original crew decided to fulfill the request!I think the game mechanics still suffer from not only the jankiness of the genre but some "press X to not die" sequences. That said, the story and moral decisions more than make up for the shortcomings in my book. Several times throughout my two playthroughs I felt like I was not only watching an episode of Star Trek, but getting to participate in it. Well worth the purchase for any die hard fan!

_childDocuments_.review: It's competent, and probably the best Trek property in a decade, but it's got serious issues and is markedly worse than any of the Telltale games.I won't get into spoilers, but the story is really good for about 75% of the playtime. The developers then ran out of budget or the writers ran out of ideas; characters die for stupid reasons or are killed off without the writers considering implications. The player is given choices related to the long term survival of entire species, but then it unceremoniously kills the only characters that can make use of the outcomes of those choices. By the time the story is over, the ship's cargo hold is absolutely packed with macguffins that are of use to nobody because the people interesting in them were dead. I'd go so far as to say that this game is a bit too bloodthirsty, the body count feels too big for a 'real' Trek property.A handful of characters in the story get the lion's share of playtime, and the game has a habit of asking you to care about characters you barely know. Once again can't be specific for spoiler reasons, but you're asked if you want to star a romantic relationship with someone who has 30 seconds of screen time, and by the end of the game you seem them for maybe 10 minutes total. Deciding who to promote? By the time that choice happens your best fleshed out candidate has something like 15 minutes of screen time.The game only has one male and one female star trek uniform model. It's very noticeable and kind of distracting that literally everyone is the exact same height and proportion. The space asian with the face that suggests a petite frame? Thick and tall like the Georgian lesbian/main character/Doctor/literally every other Starfleet female in the game.Telltale series had a reputation for 'fake' branching storylines/choices not really mattering, but this game is by far the worst.  Most decisions lead to the same place with a few dialog changes down the line. However, it's apalling just how many choices didn't lead to anything; no extra dialogue, no extra scenes, no epilogue. I feel it's worse for the 'good' choices, in the Janeway path, you at least see the corpses of your victims, in the good path you often don't get any outcome whatsoever.

_childDocuments_.review: Reading some of the reviews of this game, I felt a little dismayed at purchasing this. But I am MORE than happy I did. Just a few months before I bought Star Trek Resurgence, I was thinking about how cool it would be to have a Star Trek choices matter game. And here it is! What a great ride down nostalgic road. Resurgence brought back all those good-feels I got from watching the t.v. shows. The characters are interesting and very likable. I loved the different way of showing how each person is affected by your choices. It felt a little more detailed. There's plenty of action moments, just like the movies! Lots of ducking and rolling. Heck, I'm surprised my character didn't brush back her hair after a few rolls, this game was so in tune with the show (laugh if you know what I'm talking about). Just picture all those classic scenarios from those Star Trek episodes. Intrigue, mystery, conspiracy, being evacuated RIGHT IN THE NICK OF TIME, you name it. Star Trek Resurgence has it. Another thing is, since the developers are formerly of TellTale, how certain things were improved. Movement for starters. I cannot thank you guys enough for making character movement so much easier. No more turning awkwardly or randomly spinning in a circle or not being able to see in front of you. Camera stays behind you at all times. It's similar to that of the new Resident Evil 4. You can strafe left, right, backwards with ease. The stealth scenes. Yes, it is similar to Assassin's Creed with the specific patrol routes and guard unawareness. However, enemies tend to react a lot faster. The slightest move will get you an immediate "What was that?" followed by them heading straight for you right that second. A nice improvement I have to say. Caught me off guard. There are others, but I will let guys find out which ones. Star Trek Resurgence really is awesome game for fans of the t.v. shows and movies. Try the demo. Give it a shot, because it's definitely worth at least that. If you need any more encouragement, William T. Riker is voiced by, yep, you guessed it: Barnie the Purple Dinosaur!! Just kidding, it's Jonathan Frakes. Lol. :P

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best Star Trek games that I've played in a very long time. Amazing story. Felt like I was in the Star Trek universe. I enjoyed the ability to play both a commander and a lower decks officer. Wonderful features such as the use of the tricorder, transporter, flying the shuttle and more that give the real Star Trek experience. Animation is fantastic and the dialogue is spetacular. The one suggestion I would say is there should be more options for building relationships between character, particularly between lovers. I enjoyed after completing the game to see how my choices compared to other players. I can't wait for another Star Trek game with this crew or a completely new crew and ship.
