_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek Resurgence is perhaps the best Star Trek movie that's come out in years and it steps up the fun factor by being an interactive movie too! The writing and voice acting are excellent with the story constantly keeping me engrossed and wanting to see what happens next. But it the game has a lot of flaws to it. And don't get me started on how this version of the game on Steam doesn't have any  ACHIEVEMENTS! For a start the fact this game has been made to the old Telltale Games model is frustrating. You think the developers would have learned to do something different by now. But hey-ho. As a game, you're along for the ride and all you do is a change a few options with some breaks in the usual for some god awful combat sections and scanning. And maybe a bit of shuttle flying too. And the stealth sections are well... I won't bother describing those. Sadly all of these sections the controls are clunky and don't respond overly well - it almost feels as if there's a lag when it comes to input. As for the graphics, they are very dated looking, however that's never a bad thing. Using dated graphics with a good art style can really add to a game but also save on system hardware resources. However, that's not the case here, the game is REALLY poorly optimised. You WILL get frame drops all over the place as well as a stuttering issues and in general the frame rates not being smooth at all. This game stinks of being a rushed port. No idea what the performance is like on the PS5 but its rubbish on PC. The game really needs more time in the oven to make it run smoothly. I wouldn't be surprised if this game was rushed out before it was finished. Now on to the game itself. It titles itself as being an adventure game but it's not. Not really. As I said in the opening paragraph, it's an interactive movie where you can change some outcomes a little bit. You most definitely don't do any adventuring, you can't deviate off path, explore or anything. You're on rails for the entire show. Which isn't a bad thing at all, I just think it's misleading to label it adventuring in my opinion and it would be nice for their to be a Star Trek game one day where you can do some exploring and adventuring throughout the game. To sum it up, Star Trek Resurgence has a strong story with an excellent cast of actors, but it's let down by the game using the Telltale Games formula, a poorly-optimised and buggy game engine with a lot of poorly implemented mechanics that can feel frustrating to use. A part of me was hoping for one of those old style adventure games like Star Trek TNG Final Unity or those old OS Star Trek Judgement RIght's/25th Anniversary etc (shows my age tbh) but instead we got another Telltale game and we all know what happened to that company. I would be very surprised if we ever see a sequel to this game and if I'm honest, if we do and its done in the same vain as this, I will skip it. Honestly, I would give this game a 'Neutral' Rating is Steam has one, but I can't give it a positive. There's too many fundamental issues with the game's mechanics and build. All in all, I give this a 'Photon Torpedo up the backside out of ten'. Pick it up when it's heavily discounted.

_childDocuments_.review: Almost great. If you're already at least somewhat familiar with Trek, this game is probably going to be fun for you. If you're a real Trek nerd, you will likely appreciate the wealth of references to old shows, as well as the ability to play both a bridge officer and a lower-decks engineer to see both sides of the story.However, I have my gripes. Star Trek is ultimately a hopeful vision of our future. Resurgence, while immersing itself in existing Trek lore, tropes, and gobbledygook, in my opinion, fails to deliver on a vision of "us, but better". The resolution of the story, which is the only time that we get a glimpse of a true better future where diversity comes together, comes after 10 hours of characters being driven by petty impulses and (it feels like) causing strife for the sake of making it so not every character agrees with your choice. Several times throughout the story, you make a decision and NPCs remain upset at you, even when your decision is justified 20 minutes later based on the consequences of your actions.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek™: Resurgence feels like being in the middle of a complete new pilot episode of a series. It has what it takes to get you fully immersed into the Star Trek wold as it used to be. It's good story telling, even though a bit obvious sometimes but still it holds up to all you can expect from a typical STNG styled story.The bad parts are:- decisions do rarely matter, the game forces you back to the main track all the time, you truly only impact the relationships but not the story itself.- the graphics are a complete insult into what up to date technology normally would offer. This game looks and feels like from 15 years ago. Simply ridiculous and a completely wasted opportunity here. I can only imagine how this game must have felt with proper, up to the mark graphics and UI- The mini games and quick action stuff is way too simple and is merely a challenge. I would have liked this to be a much higher degree of complexity or challenge.Overall: This is a nicely done Star Trek story line you participate in, but I would not call this a game, as there is nothing to lose and nothing that can go sideways, with the exception that you can die and need to retry.If you like the Star Trek feeling of the 90th. and early 2000th. then you'll feel at home and will definitely enjoy the ride, nut don't expect a a real "game" here.

_childDocuments_.review: I give a guarded recommendation for STAR TREK fans only. This is a really fun Star Trek story, but it's mired in trash gameplay with boring mechanics and fiddly first-person shooter combat. The relationship-building mechanic, while interesting, doesn't actually factor nearly so much into gameplay as you would think and as a result your character has to either carry the idiot ball occasionally or flat-out violate Starfleet protocols in order to keep everybody happy.As a STAR TREK experience, I would give this an 8/10. As a game for someone who's not deeply invested in STAR TREK, I would rate it a 3 / 10. The gameplay just feels like an excuse to make what would be a fine episode into a tedious game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not very good. This sort of game really needs a very strong story and good production value, and that just wasn't there. Lots of stiff animations and poor voice acting and an overall narrative that was just sort of bland. They do try to break up the old Telltale formula with some stealth and shooting sections, but they really shouldn't have, these are always really poor and nobody was playing this because they thought it was Elite Force 3. You can't save (really), and you can't skip anything, so if something comes up or the game crashes you're at the mercy of a mostly invisible autosave, and can find yourself repeating half an hour of the monotonous clicking and bad dialogue. I like the concept, the setting is definitely ripe for this sort of game, but it just wasn't done very well. Forcing you to swap between two characters and two mostly unrelated casts probably wasn't a good decision either. The first officer's story was actually fairly decent, and it got dragged down a lot by constantly swapping over to the enlisted guy's slog of a story.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek Resurgence is an interactive movie with some choices and minigames. It's relatively faithful to the franchise and feels like just one of the 90s TV show episodes. It's also very mediocre, and some aspects of the game are just bad.First things first, the story is decent, and the choices are interesting as ethical dilemmas, which is probably the most important part about a Star Trek game. The consequences part is not great though, you'd never wonder what would happen if you chose differently, because the consequences are obvious and miniscule. All you get is an acknowledgment of your choices, as in at some point you hear "You did X and I hate/respect you for this, and I will do what you ask despite/because of my opinion on you". It's all very linear, and I don't think any of your choices affect where some later scene happens or who is present. Still, it's competently told, and the voice acting is quite good. I also liked how all the Star Trek technobabble is turned into very simple mini-games and button prompts. There are no real puzzles, just something for you to do during a conversation or a dramatic chase, making it all feel more dynamic.What is not good is the graphics. The developers are related to Telltale, and it feels like the animations are straight from Sam & Max games. This made sense in Telltale games because all of them were cartoonish, comic book-like. This one goes for a more realistic style, and it doesn't look good. Another unexpected fumble is the music, a lot of themes sound like MIDI music. I don't expect a full live orchestra score from a low-budget game, but this was distracting.It's a thumbs down, but really it's a case of 5/10 game. It's not bad and would still be entertaining for anyone who cares about Star Trek.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Your opinion of this game will probably boil down to your opinion on Star Trek in general. If you enjoy watching it, you will have a good time being part of a starfleet crew. If not, this game is not going to convince you otherwise.This one is more in the "visual novel" or "choose your own adventure" category. The game mechanics are quite simple and rarely challenging. Nevertheless, the story is well written and quite extensive (~ 10 hours of gameplay) and the game is quite good at creating an atmosphere and giving you the feeling of being part of the action, even if you are just pushing a button.Graphics are not great but sufficient. My biggest concern with it was rather the performance. I had severe frame drops multiple times on the Steam Deck, which can normally handle much better visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: A great story told from two different perspectives and characters that really makes you feel like you've been dropped into the world of Star Trek. It's broad enough that even those not familiar with the show or world would be pulled in, and full of information and throwbacks to tickle those who are die hard fans. The gameplay can be a little wonky at times for the PC port, but overall it played smooth and I was only frustrated once. It was worth it for the story, however. I highly recommend this to anyone who is a fan of choice and consequence and sci-fi games.

_childDocuments_.review: "If you like X, you'll like this!" is perhaps the worst way to recommend something to anyone, but in the case of Resurgence, it's very true. I guess in Resurgence's case it's "There's a great game here, but you need to be a fan of the shows in order to look past the utter jank and see the gem within"So whilst there are _many_ great games out there that bear the Star Trek franchise, the vast majority of those games often completely miss the mark when it comes to capturing the "feel" of a Star Trek episode, and instead often feel like a genre-game with Star Trek themeing slapped on or a mod of another more famous game. Very few of these games have managed to hit it just right and make it feel like an *actual* episode of Trek. The few that come to my mind are: 25th Anniversary, Judgement Rights, and TNG: Final Unit. And now we get to add Resurgence to that list!First, the good: It's the exact kind of Space Romp you'd expect from TNG-era trek, with your character navigating various moral dilemmas whilst trying to bring space diplomacy to a bunch of one-dimensional stereotypes. You'll be faced with classic Trek moments such as "Should I commit genocide against an entire alien species, or leave them be and maybe make a new problem for the Federation in 20 years time which another show can pick up on?", all neatly sandwiched between the occasional ship battle or landing party phaser fight. You'll get to scan things with your tricorder. You'll go to the ready room and ask for technobabble solutions to technobabble problems. You'll speak to Godlike Entities and constantly hope they don't just teleport you into the sun or something. You'll do all the kinds of thing you expect to see Picard et al do. Admittedly, it leans more towards modern Trek than 90s Trek, because it's not just "dilemma of the week", it's more like a 4 part mini series with a universe ending threat. Frankly it's better than watching Discovery or Picard. Plot wise it's solid. The pacing is done well, with the waxing and waning tension being delivered at exactly the right moments, just like on the telly. The dialogue is great too and all feels very natural. In terms of "direction" it scores a pass too, as whoever scripted the cutscenes/cinematic camera did a pretty decent job. The art and environment design is also pretty great too, even when it strays outside of what they could crib from TV.The gameplay itself is very "cinematic", with most of the action delivered in the form of quick time events. There's lots of "hold forward to advance the plot" stuff, but I felt like I could forgive it as it doesn't really pretend to do otherwise. (Also, you can't fail any of the quick time events or even run out of time in a conversation, everything just pauses! It took me a while to realise that as the game does well to keep the pace going). The game often presents you with a handful of binary choices that have _some_ sway on the flow of the plot, but they're mostly there to challenge the player and tick some boxes on an post-game website, even showing you what % of players did which choice, which is very nice thing indeed. I like the overall conversation and choice system, including keeping a record of how the other characters think about you and your decisions, even if I am just a tad upset about how inconsequential and linear this is.The bad is: everything to do with the actual running of the game. It's all a big derpy mess that feels very amateur. It's clear they spent all of their cash in the writer's room rather than on wrangling Unreal.My primary gripe is that the game is plain ugly. The environment and ship meshes are 360/ps3 era, with you being able to see the angular vertexes most of the time. The facial mesh and textures are much better and actually look *good*, but you only see those in close-up conversations. Once those faces start emoting you'll quickly be repulsed as you're thrown down the uncanny valley by Source Filmmaker level facial contortions. The walking animations are hilariously bad I saw multiple instances of float-slidey-feet syndrome in plain view.The lighting can only be described as "broken", as most of the time everything is just fullbright, with completely incorrect shadows and random speculars on shiny surfaces, including people's faces. The graphical flaws are most noticeable on the ship exteriors, as the complete lack of lighting makes the vast and empty universe look flat and like some kind of an obvious matte painting. It's worse than what you'll see on TV, even for TOS. Heck, it's worse than what you'd find the various sci-fi BBS/forums of the late 90s where everyone with a pirated copy of 3DSMax would make their own version of their favourite ship. LOWER DECKS, an actual 2d cartoon, looks better than this.And yet despite looking 2 generations old all of this seems to warm my laptop up no end, with the framerate varying wildly from 120 to 15fps depending on which way you're looking and in which scene. I'm a bit upset that I'm spending this much electricity rendering this big pile of grey, poorly-lit nonsense.Weirdly they're using Ue5, so they must have messed something up for it to perform and look this bad. They should have just rolled with the default settings or whatever?There is *one* bright side to the poor graphics: There are various moments of comic relief when the utter po-faced seriousness of the cinematic director's choices meets head on with the hilariously poor graphics. I think within the first hour of the game you're presented with two, perhaps even three, TMP-style drydock flybys and shuttle rides. Now in the movie this was done so that people could oggle the new Enterprise refit on the big screen and look at the fancy new VFX. In Resurgence it's done because it's a cool Star Trek trope that almost every show and game has done since TMP, yet no-one appears to have told the cinematic director that the ship models look like complete ass and that no-one is going to be impressed by nor swoon over a slow pan of these blocking, poorly lit, completely flat ship models floating around in an empty, space-themed skybox. The audience would be impressed if this was 2005, but it's obviously not. The flybys themselves are well composed and would look great in a movie with an actual budget, but instead we get this. Still, I think they were brave to just run with it and make the most of what they had and commit to the Star Trek style, despite the medium they had to work with.A short list of other (numerous but minor) flaws would be:* The menu font is amateur* They print a QR code and a textual link, you can't press a button or click something to launch your browser.* The keyboard and mouse controls are disgusting. Mouse acceleration, ugh.* The controller config is wild and matches no other third person game I've ever played, and the first-person action sequences have a constantly fluctuation level of stick sensitive. It's never correct, it's either warp speed or goopy.* This stuff cannot be remapped!!* Camera is frustratingly close to avatar* Spatial sound isn't camera relative, only position relative (turning head doesn't alter sound).* Lip sync sucks, very flappy, like a South Park ventriloquist* Subtitles suck and often don't match* Skip dialog is sorely needed* The choices don't matter as much as I'd like* The mandatory stealth sections are abysmal* Why does the XO (player's character) talk more than the Important Ambassador or the Captain?* Yet Another Riker / Titan cameo? Groan. Couldn't they have at least recorded Frakes in the same sound booth. * The saving system is tedious and bad.* Some of the intense drama is ruined by clunkily running about and derpy phaser fights.* I was going to pick this game up on release, but it was an Epic Exclusive. Blergh.

_childDocuments_.review: This is among the best Star Trek games out there. It is served well swapping between a senior officer character, and a lower decks character for the narrative. It also incorporates much of the existing Trek lore to make a compelling story where the choices you make matter. It is made by former Telltale developers, and story was their strongest point in the adventure games they made. This is a must have for Star Trek fans, and also a great Adventure game for anyone into Sci-Fi and haven't tried a Trek game.

_childDocuments_.review: The story was enjoyable in the way a bunch of B-tier TNG episodes are and manages to stay interesting during the time it took to finish it off but I'd never consider replaying it as you can't speed up dialogue or skip cutscenes.Rydek's side is the best part of the game, she has the best voice acting and gets to do the things you actually want to do in a Star Trek game: Fly the ship, shoot things, do diplomacy to dumb looking aliens. Diaz gets saddled with a story that doesn't work if you don't care about  but this is balanced out somewhat by him getting best girl Edsilar while Rydek is surrounded by cartoonishly evil characters who advocate for courses of action that seem like they would get you kicked out of Starfleet pretty quickly.It's very glitchy with characters floating off the ground, shadow issues on the main characters, problems with the way hair is lit, etc.  There were also times when some characters were too quiet to be heard over the music and other times the music just stopped playing only to start up again randomly later on. The minigames are mostly just tedious and repetitive but the shooting gallery segments are entirely awful to the point that I would just die deliberately to be able to switch to story mode and clear them.Overall, this game feels like it tries to do too much for whatever budget or time they had, it'd probably have been better if they'd focused on one main character and a smaller supporting cast that got more to do and more time to make you care about them. I still enjoyed it but mainly because it was cheap and reminded me of when I still enjoyed Star Trek.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re looking for some screenshots  to view all the ones I took for this game.This Star Trek adventure takes place more than a decade after the events of The Next Generation arc of the canon series, and puts you in the shoes of two protagonists: commander Jara Rydek, a Kobliad, and the human engineer Carter Diaz. Science ship Resolute is sent to a diplomatic mission to escort a high diplomat in order to stop a resource war between two civilizations; what starts like an ordinary Starfleet mission however, soon will become much more than anyone had signed up for.In good Star Trek tradition, the plot starts off mildly, only to then escalate to ever-higher stakes while putting the crew between difficult moral decisions and lethal threats to face. Mainly, other than the two main protagonists, the story is centered on the senior bridge staff and also on a couple members of the lower decks, the so-to-speak “rank and file” of the Federation. All of them are competently written, and show an evolution of character to some extent, in relation to the events that happen, although this varies in measure from one to another. Even so, they’re likable and stand out people that don’t fall flat and all have their own merits in terms of narrative. The story is articulate and varied enough to not be one-sided, it will engage you until the end, despite some turnarounds being somewhat predictable, especially if you’re a fan of the show and know the narration gimmicks Star Trek is all about.Visually and artistically, there’s a solid attention to detail and fidelity to the show’s source material. Uniforms, ship layouts, sound effects and even the technical jargon about the technology are all spot-on; the developers clearly are true fans of the show, and this has paid off. While ship interiors could be more detailed and lively, alien structures and planetside sections have excellent levels of detail and an immersive atmosphere. Too bad those low-resolution textures somewhat ruin the eye candy. You’ll explore mostly on foot through linear sections that rarely have any side areas, although numerous optional interactions exist either to reveal more about the lore and trivia, or get minor relation bonuses with other characters. From a narrative adventure, it’s not expected to have a great freedom of exploration, but even so, a better amount of meaningful optional interactions could have been better. There are no secrets, collectibles or anything of the like; what you see is what you get, without optionals.Combat sections play out as stationary third-person shooting stages where you’ll have to fight enemies coming from one or multiple sides, and in some cases switch cover to be able to hit them from different directions. Other than that, you’ll need to take cover to avoid fire and time your shots, as being hit three times will result in mission failure, and restart from the closest checkpoint. In some cases, on top of all that, you’ll also have to cover your allies, as your mission will also fail if they take too many hits. Don’t worry though, being a narrative adventure means that these action segments aren’t very demanding in terms of skill, even for those less experienced with shooters. In fact, some more challenge would have been welcome, but with this genre it’s fine as it is.Stealth sections involve staying out of enemy sight while using environmental cover, and in some cases triggerable distractions, to slip past unnoticed. A convenient indicator, with a rather generous time to fill, will show if you’re being detected, and enemy patterns are rather simple to decipher given their basic AI.There’s a variety of minigames, such as puzzles that involve operating various starfleet equipment, such as teleportation consoles or tricorders to name some, and even pilot shuttles through dangerous space anomalies. These are good and improve immersion in how you get things done organically, rather than being just cutscenes, however the control scheme made for gamepads doesn’t shine particularly well, and makes some of them cumbersome to handle properly. In many cutscenes there’s a plethora of quick time events to perform actions, such as dodging attacks, shooting people, operating machinery and more. There’s an actually excessive amount of these, and it becomes quite tiresome in the long run to deal with.The choices you’ll make as the two protagonists will not only impact the flow of the story, but also your relationship with your crewmates. This will translate into them either supporting or opposing you when the time of truly critical events is at hand, and this can make the story go one way or another in pretty major ways. It’s an incentive to replay the game, and see what would happen if you did different choices. Even so, not all of them feel meaningful in the same way, and in certain cases it feels like the relation to some crew members, important as they may be, in the end won’t count as much as stated ‘on paper’. For most of them, though, there’s a good system of action and reaction that feels plausible and works out well.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the authentic Trek experience, especially with it set in the 24th century era. The echoes of Telltale games are clear here but there's a good evolution with a nice variety of choices and interactivity, and even the brief shooting and stealth sections ended up quite fun. Ultimately there's a sense that my choices didn't matter overall, and that's common with games like these, but I'm okay with that if I like the characters and story. And I did here, especially Rydek, and felt that the writing worked for establishing strong relationships. It's a shame that visually it's disappointing for the most part, feeling like a game from the Xbox 360 era. A few crashes and stuttery frame rates at points, but not enough to make things unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge Star Trek and TellTale games fan, so this game was straight up my alley and I have no regrets.It's a heavy, narrative-based game, but there's a lot of interactive components to it. You get to fight aliens with your phaser, fly shuttle crafts, sneak around, use your tricorder, and make diplomatic choices that affect your relationships with different people in game. There's lots of awesome cinematic moments (especially during the climax) and I think they did phenomenal job making you feel like you're really a part of Starfleet.The narrative is pretty linear in a lot of ways (if you're a fan of what Telltale made, it's similar to that and those games are fantastic). It's not going to have these expansive branches of story lines like in Detroit Become Human or Until Dawn. But, instead, your decisions will help shape what your crew thinks of you and what your enemies think of you. If you've always wanted to be a character on Star Trek and feel like you're part of this universe, this is the game for you. Towards the beginning, I wasn't sure what to make of one of the main characters (Carter) and felt like there was a tiny lull in the story (for me personally), but it paid off beautifully and I found myself WAY too emotionally invested in these people's lives. I loved being able to feel like the captain of a starship and make commands to save my crew. It was epic. It was amazing. You can tell that the creators love this franchise and respect the hell out of the source material.I'd love another Star Trek game from this company. I'd pay good money to play it. This is one of my favorite games I've played this year, it was just a ton of fun. IMPORTANT: I won't dock any points off for this, but I'd highly recommend NOT using a controller for this game. It's pretty wonky and makes game play difficult. It was not a deal breaker for me, though. I was happy to switch over to keyboard.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: A good Star Trek story with a surprise return of a TNG frenemy from the first season. You alternately play the first officer and a low ranking crew man from the lower decks. The first comes with lots of ships politics and all the bridge stuff you know from the shows, the latter is the source of the much needed technobabble and hands on stuff.It is the best Star Trek game I've played in a long while, as it nails the atmosphere and most of the writing of classic episodes. The optimism in the face of insurmountable odds, believing in the inherit value of life etc., all that good stuff sets the franchise apart from other sci fi franchises is here and it's as good as ever.Luckily for the game I felt so positively about the general story and atmosphere stuff, that I can ignore the godawful gameplay. This is the first game that required me to twist my actual mouse for a quick time event. Even after switching to a controller it didn't get much better. The worst offenders are shuttle as well as shooting sections, but everything else doesn't fare much better and made me wish for more of a "walking simulator" approach.Pick it up if you are into Star Trek, but be aware that the gameplay will test your patience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is really just a series of animated episodes with some emulation of interaction inbetween, any interaction seems to be strictly linear, and no real quests are involved. i expected more. i am only a few hours into the game, but i doubt this will change much (why would the game mechanics change mid game?). If it does, i will revisit this review.Yet, these things they got right:1) The star trek lore, and its feel and vibe, which is rare nowadays (all the modern spin offs fail in this)2) The visuals are a nice blend of cartoon and CGI, i really like it.3) Only having ventured into part of the story yet, so far its well constructed.Now the things they missed:- i should have been advertised as a graphic interactive novel. As such it does very nicely capture the feel of the star trek (or more precise the star fleet) universe, and in this it has its value and is fun to play/watch, but i would not consider that to be worth more than 10-15 buck.- But still, even if they just had integrated some micro games or quests, this could have been more worthwhile. The quests that are in the game go like this: press button A, move cursor to point C before countdown is 0, or die. Talk to person A, then B, then C. - The tech aspect is at an equal or slightly less detailed level of what STNG offered. A game should offer more than a 45min show on tv though. I would have liked a bit more detailed emulation of the tech aspect for example, like when interacting with the ships computer or consoles.- The Dialogues, characters could be more "adult". They are quite polished, reasoning is kept at a simple level.If they had gotten one of these additional things right, i would give it a thumbs upStill, i see my spending the money as a vote to give to devs that understand how to get that star trek vibe right, because this is so rare nowadays.So devs, you can do much more with this. Think of mixing this with the adventure quests like the old text based space quest titles. Think of mixing AI into NPCs to make this all less linear and more to explore. And spent some time on the characters, got the commander right, but the captain and the lower rank character are a bit flat or stereotypical.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good so far. Graphics are a bit dated, but not terrible. I read some release day reviews and some fan reviews on Reddit, and many of the issues they describe appear to have been fixed (such as the lack of an "invert y-axis" option. This is obviously a console port, and obviously made by a small team in a short timeframe on a budget, but that's not the end of the world. So far the gameplay is reasonable for a choose-your-own-adventure type game. Story is good enough so far that I'm likely to enjoy it throughout.I like that there seems to be no perfect, correct choice in many interactions. You'll often make some people happy and some people annoyed with an decision you make. So just choose what you feel is right, and shape the personality of your character. The game's main story arc will take care of itself, your job is craft your character how you see fit. Jerk or kind? Strictly interprets orders, or follows the spirit of Star Fleet? By-the-book or rogue? While I'm sure there are some consequences to your actions throughout the story, your ability to shape the character into who you want them to be is the main draw. Well, that and being able to sit back and watch what amounts to a DS9/Voyager era 4-part episode:).

_childDocuments_.review: This was a tough one for me...The writing is phenomenal.  It really feels like a 10 hr Star Trek episode.  They really nail the atmosphere, and all of the writing is top notch.  I was really sweating in the face of some of the choices, and curious as to what might happen if I did things differently.Unfortunately, everything that is not the writing and voice acting is terrible.  The graphics are... dated... at best.  The animations are comically poor.  There's terrible stutter at random times, which is inexcusable on a 3060 with this level of graphics... The subtitles often don't match the spoken dialogue.  It's obvious they're based off a script, but not adjusted after the actual voice lines were recorded.But worst is the game play.  I'm not sure what the problem is, but it feels like a bad console port.  Mouse and Keyboard are almost unplayable at times.  It's like the Telltale engine got de-optimized, and that's saying something.  There's a lot of unnecessary interactions which would feel immersive, if not for feeling like crap to have to interact with.  The game is also littered with a ton of mini-games all of which feel sort of under utilized.  I would have preferred 4 improved mini-games versus the dozen of half-thought-out ones we got.  Like, imagine if the half-baked hacking mini-game from, every other sim game, but now there are 12 different ones, each used 3 or 4 times.  The stealth sections don't feel great (thankful there are only 2 of them, and they're skippable if you fail them.  The combat feels clunky and half-formed, not really impactful...  The shuttle piloting... And the one part I was hoping for, space combat, was just dialogue options?I dunno.  I want to like this, and enjoyed the story, but had to grit my teeth to get through the 10 hrs 1 play through requires.  As much as I wanted to see the other outcomes from choices, I can't bring myself to play it again to find out.The last straw that took me from a waffling positive to negative review was, there's an in-game option to see your choices, and dive in them further after you play.  I was excited for that... All it does is give you a QR code, to go to their website, to create an account before you can see...  Hard Pass...

_childDocuments_.review: Paramount should hire the developers, because this is the Star Trek we deserve. – A narrative-driven game with branching choices, great soul, and exceptional Star Trek authenticity, just shy of a masterpiece.-----------I've been a Star Trek fan since the days when you had to wait for TNG to air on one of the three channels on the only TV in the house. Star Trek has always been a big part of my life, and it's clear the creators of this game share that passion with many of us.This game is for trekkers. It's a love letter to what Star Trek represents for those who truly love it. The writing is fantastic, with engaging narrative elements and thoughtfully crafted callbacks to classic Trek lore—before some Paramount executive decided that parallel universes and time jumps were good ideas.The game uses a "branching choice" system where your dialogue options carry weight (even if the consequences aren't immediately apparent). The story promises significant shifts based on your decisions, and you'll often be put on the spot with little time to think, forcing you to go with what you believe is best. I found the pivotal moments particularly well-written, with some excellent cliffhangers along the way. It really feels like watching scenes from an episode or movie—you just can't stop because you need to know what happens next.The graphics are solid—while not cutting-edge or AAA quality, they never feel cheap or distracting from the experience. The gameplay mechanics feel secondary to the story. There are quick-time events, but they're clearly not the focal point of the game.One aspect that could improve is the music. It's not from Star Trek itself but is more of a tribute to the franchise's "feel." Unfortunately, it doesn't quite capture the grandeur of a full orchestral score, likely due to budget constraints.I got this game for around €11 on sale, and it was one of the most pleasant gaming surprises I’ve had in the past year. This studio deserves all the support they can get from the gaming Trekker community.I sincerely hope there's a sequel or a new project in the works. With a bigger budget, they could enhance the graphics and add more intricate gameplay elements. As it stands, this game offers an excellent first playthrough, and although I rarely replay RPGs or narrative games, I'm curious to see how different choices would affect the story.-----------Star Trek has been misused as a franchise in video games (Star Trek Infinite, anyone?) and even by Paramount itself, but this game truly captures the essence, hopefulness, and deeper meaning of Star Trek, all while still being a game. I think we fans deserved a treat like this, and it came from a small studio of people who clearly love their craft and Star Trek.More than just a review, this is a thank-you note to them—for giving me a little bit of that feeling I had watching Star Trek on TV, sitting between my mom and dad.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Overall 7/10This is a very fun and authentic Star Trek game done in the style of a Telltale game and the plot of the game is actually surprisingly good it really feels like you are playing through a TNG era Star Trek movie. The dialogue, characters and choices all feel authentic to Star Trek and the stakes feel very highIt is not a perfect game but you can definitely tell it has likely been done with a small team on a small budget (the studio is only 30 or so employees) and most of the employees are ex-Telltale employees and it definitely shows in the style, gameplay and storytellingOn the positive side this game is really great for one playthrough which lasts about 10 hours long and the price tag definitely reflects the shorter length of the game so no complaints thereNow choices are impactful in some aspects but less so in others. Every dialogue choice changes how other characters treat the two protagonists and it changes future dialogue and can even lead to crew members becoming permanently disfigured so you kind of have the impacts of your choices staring you in the face oftenBut on the flip side and likely because of the small budget and small dev team, there is still only one ending and just slight variations to parts of the endings and I definitely felt like there was that potential for your choices to have had more impact and for there to have been multiple different endingsSome characters die regardless of your choices which is really disappointing as there are perfect dialogue choices that could have lead up to them not dying but yet the game doesn't have those choices impact that outcome which is very oddBut as a first game for a new studio of just 30 devs on a limited budget with likely a substantial portion of said budget having had been spent on the rights to use Star Trek IP this game is definitely no small feat. Any Star Trek fan will thoroughly enjoy at least one playthrough of the game and while there aren't multiple endings your choices do still have pretty serious impacts in other regardsI would actually love it if the devs were to make a DLC expansion for this game or a sequel where your choices could be imported into and then have them have more impact or coinciding with a DLC that they go back to Resurgence and update it to add impact to certain choices so that you can save some characters from dying and possibly adding in multiple endingsWhatever the future holds though I'll definitely be buying the next project that Dramatic Labs works on and I highly recommend this game for anyone who loves Star Trek and wants to experience an authentic Star Trek story
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: This game had the great feeling of a true Star Trek story. I would love to see this edited to be a true episode that I could watch as well.****SPOILERS BELOW****....I was pleased that this wasn't only an officer's tale, but also included the lower decks as well. It was very well done and the switching between characters made me feel like I was watching and participating in an episode. I liked the tie in to one of the earliest TNG episodes that made them the main villain through the story. I had forgotten just who the Tkon were until this reminded me. Massive kudos to the voice actor for Spock. I really felt that they nailed it!The only slight (and very very slight at that) criticism that I would have is that they should have added at least a sentence in the final Captains's log about the fate of the bioformed. Also a sentence about the Tkon souls if you saved them.I would like to see the combat system and the inability to use a tricorder except when it matches the story. Starfleet officers are almost married to their tricorders so I would have liked to pull it out on demand at times.One plus for the combat system is that if you take too much damage, you can retry either in "story mode" or regular. Story mode basically gives you plot armor for the next attempt. Very helpful on some of the combats.100% would recommend to any Star Trek fan out there. I can't wait to try it again while making different choices.

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game, the story is well written and with a length of around 10 hours (I didn't interact with everything) well worth the price tag.  If you ever played a Telltale like game you will enjoy it even if you aren't a Star Trek fan. The only thing i didn't like were the repeated shuttle sections as they dragged on for a little too long.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a phenomenal Star Trek game. I have loved several Star Trek games for different reasons, but I strongly feel this is the most "Star Trek" Star Trek game I've ever played, and I've played most. I've beta tested several, been in a couple "special thanks" credits, and while they all have a special place in my heart, Resurgence was an extremely pleasant surprise.The acting is great. The lore is SPOT ON. The different choices feel like they make a difference. Dealing with crewmates, aliens, enemies and allies on a personal level is not something that's been explored much in Trek games (except maybe Elite Force), but these personal interactions at the very heart of Star Trek. Plus, being able to program a transporter lock and do engineering forensics was a wonderful treat. And the phaser fights were fun, while not being the end-all and be-all of the game.I took my sweet time picking up this title, but it was SO worth the wait. I am very much looking forward to a second and third playthrough, after a respectful hiatus to let everything sink in.Keep it up, devs! Please make more of these! Cannot say enough good things.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this game only if you're already a Star Trek fan. As a game, it's pretty bad. It's not even a walking simulator. The only real choices you can make are slightly different pieces of dialog that, at most, will swap out an NPC you didn't get to know at all with another NPC that you didn't get to know at all. That's about it. The less said about the actual game elements, the better. The build quality of the actual product are poor. Mushy, buggy, janky, terrible controls and sequences. You may have some challenge with some of the puzzles if you're suffering from severe brain damage.All that said, it was a decent Star Trek story set in the late 2300's era. Honestly, I would have preferred if it was trimmed down a bit, had the graphics polished up, and dropped as a mini-series on Paramount Plus. So, like I said, if you're really really into Star Trek, you might enjoy this purely for the story content, which isn't bad. As a game, it's terribe.

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I could recommend this since it's marginally better in terms of the writing than other new star trek stuff I've seen. At least it has some superficial similarity to some older star trek stuff. But it's well under the level of voyager in terms of the writing quality alone and as the game goes on the vibe feels less and less and less and less like trek to me. There are hundreds of old episodes of star trek of which you could just pick a random episode and it would take under an hour to experience a far better story, and you wouldn't be forced to endure the tricorder minigame or the shuttle minigame or the phaser crap. There are so many of these minigames which are absolutely immersion breaking and utterly unfun. I think the only purpose of these is to drag out the play time since I'm sure they tested these out and know that they suck. I would much rather play this as a visual novel and do away with all the minigames and unnecessary prompts. It would still not be very good, but it would be far better. Also why is spock in this. Why does spock have to be in everything. It's so pathetic.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re playing the Steam version on Steam Deck, performance is at impulse speed at best, follow this but with the following changes;  NOTE: The Appdata folder for us steam users is the compatdata folder next to your common folder in the steam install directory. Keep the ini file settings as installed but set shadows to 0. Then, in game, set the resolution to lowest setting then using Steam Deck ‘s FSR at Full.  You’ll be at 30-60fps reliably instead of 7-40fps.

_childDocuments_.review: As a devoted Star Trek fan, I was eager to immerse myself in the universe of 'Resurgence.' The game's narrative depth and strategic gameplay mechanics delivered on the promise of a true Star Trek experience. However, the disappointment came when I encountered the underwhelming graphics, minor stutters, and NO steam achivements despite having top-tier hardware. It's not quite what I was looking for in a Trek game, but this opens up possibilities for improvement in future projects."Star Trek: Resurgence" is a must-play for fans of the franchise and space exploration enthusiasts alike. With its captivating narrative, engaging gameplay, and iconic Trek-inspired music, it sets a new standard for what a Star Trek game can be. Beam aboard and prepare to boldly go where no one has gone before.In conclusion, "Star Trek: Resurgence" offers a commendable attempt at capturing the spirit of the franchise but falls short due to its subpar graphics. While dedicated fans may find enjoyment in the storytelling and gameplay mechanics, those expecting a visually stunning experience may come away disappointed. With limited Trek games available, I would still recommend getting the game to dive into the Trekverse.LIVE LONG AND PROSPER, FRIENDS!

_childDocuments_.review: At one hand there was a good (but certainly not very good story) to follow. game plays for great parts like an interactive movie. If you like games like that you may like this game. but do not expect a quality like "Detroit: Become Human".At the other hand the technical part of the game is rather poor. graphics, especially the space scenes partly look very cheap like a mobile game or a game from the 00s. Space just consists of a simple low resolution skybox, asteroids do not move or rotate, they're obviously hardbakened into the scene..At the same time the game is running very slow even on lower graphics settings. Framerate is mostly at 60 FPS but is very unstable and often drops to 20 FPS for a few moments. And always the same repeating stupid mini-puzzles which mostly feel unnecessary and unrelated. You always get the feeling they just tried to artificially stretch the game in lack of more content.The controls feel very clunky. But most of the game you cannot move freely anyway, at most you can move within one room, but in most scenes you just interact using choice dialogues or QTEs. Almost nothing in the game is or feels dynamic, everything is scripted.You always get the feeling the devs just implemented the bare minimum. If you like to explore or you like the technobabble of star trek then walk away, you won't find it here.I played it through for the ok-ish story, but likely no further time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game totally feels like Classic Star Trek (not the dreck that is the Abrams-verse). Made by people who used to be with Telltale - that's the Telltale that made Wolf Among Us and the earlier seasons of The Walking Dead - you really get a sense that you are making decisions as a senior officer, in the case of Commander Rydek, or as a member of Engineering, in the case of Petty Officer Diaz.I got sucked into the story and the decisions set up in each chapter have major impacts with the other characters you interact with. Don't let the lower-budget graphics fool you, this is definitely worth picking up, especially if you're a fan of the old Telltale Games. They very clearly did their homework by making the story continue a plot thread from an early episode of The Next Generation. Excellent work, and by the time of this review, I'm not even done with the story yet but am looking forward to seeing where it goes in my next session.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: A solid, Telltale-like Star Trek adventure. It's 2024 and the developers didn't put achievements in the game (at least on PC, the console versions have them). I don't care what excuse gets thrown out there, add achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: This was easily one of my favourite games this year!The graphics and the controls are... a little janky. The only reason I died in the game was because the controls were frustrating. BUT the story and the character development absolutely more than make up for any deficiencies. _childDocuments_.review: I have watched every star trek series/movie ever and played every trek game game in the past 45 years. This is an excellent one. It gets what star trek is all about. That is to say the storyline, game design and writing are top notch. Sadly where the game fails is that it is what I call (console snobbery). When it is showing you controls on the screen, it will often be the console controller button it shows even if you don't have one hooked up. The keyboard controls are not customizable. If you press Esc to open the menu it works but if you press escape again to return to the game, it asks if you really want to quite! *facepalm* The movement mini-games were clearly intended for a controller. This is really lazy work for an otherwise excellent game. I have seen 1 man show games that allow customizing the keys. The team lead should have had higher standards. I also hold it against them that they went for a 1 year epic exclusivity deal depriving us steamers of the chance to play. That's just excessive. 1 month would be reasonable from a business perspective. Despite all that I still recommend it to any Star Trek fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give the game a C+ or B-. I LOVED all the TNG era call-backs. This was a great way to live through a Star Trek story. The first day I attempted to play it I had a REALLY strange bug where it displayed on two monitors as a mirror image. Responded to input on one monitor but actually displayed on another.It's also a little strange that pressing "Escape" brings you into the menu but pressing it again moves you to exit the game rather than just takes you back out of the menu and back into the game (Only game I have that does this type of sequence).Fun play and great story, but the port process from console to PC felt really lazy.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write recommendations for video games, but I have to admit this game scratched every itch I have when it comes to drawing in my attention. _childDocuments_.review: This style of game isn't usually something I would enjoy but this title was highly enjoyable throughout and captured the soul of Star Trek beautifully, going into it I was worried it might be riddled with the sociopolitical propaganda that has infested Trek in recent years, I was extremely glad to find that there was no such nonsense involved, just pure, unadulterated Trek fun, while there doesn't appear to be much replayability I think it was definitely worth the money I spent on it and I would love to see more Trek games from this developer in future. 10/10 would buy again.

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are really dated looking. Not sure if it's because the game is made by a small team or if it's intentionally dated to appeal to nostalgia for late 90's early 2000's games. Your guess is as good as mine. Now that we've addressed the elephant in the room. It has the feel of Roddenberry Trek, not JJ or new trek in the story department. The rest of the game is a mixed bag, there's exploration and light puzzle solving, vehicle driving, combat, and stealth. These story interruptions are just that, interruptions that you deal with to get back to what you really want to do in this game, engage with the story. Again, not sure if this is deliberately appealing to nostalgia or small team with low budget. Like I said at the start though, it feels like Roddenberry's Star Trek. Which series is it most like, I can't decide. There's parts of it that reminded me of ST: Insurrection, ST: TNG, ST: TOS, and ST: Voyager. _childDocuments_.review: It's a 10-12 hour Star Trek miniseries, with the 'vibes' of TNG's moral quandries and TOS' fantastic sci-fi twists. The characters are all interesting and varied, the plot is a thoughtful 'deep cut' reference to a season one Star Trek: The Next Generation episode, and Johnathan Frakes' guest appearance is 100% committed. He gets extremely emotional while doing his lines!The space sequences look like a Star Trek movie, and the effects and music all sell it, along with stellar VA work. Special mention to the Spock impersonator. Doing old Spock well is hard - and he did it.In terms of presentation it's a bit janky at times. The gameplay is a lot more like Detroit: Become Human, Telltale's Walking Dead, and games from that era - warts and all. Expect QTE's, "Ensign What's-their-name will Remember This"'s, and such. If that type of game is far in your rear view mirror, you may want to pass. But I think this captures more of what made those games good, than what made them bad.Overall though, if you don't like Star Trek, I'm not sure I would even try it, but if you're here looking at a review for the game you must already like Trek and just want to convince yourself this is worth your money. It is. I love it. As a lifelong Trek fan, I can tell you, this game is The Best of Both Worlds. I love it. LLAP

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of Star Trek, have been since I was a kid and I was really looking forward to this, but the state this released on PC is absolutely abysmal.In 2024 there is really no excuse, nor has there been for decades, for a complete lack of options available. You can't change graphics settings for one, yet you can change the graphics settings manually by editing the Unreal generic INI files. The only graphical options are resolution, brightness, if you're full screen or not and motion blur. The UI looks grainy on a 4k screen, you can literally see the jagged pixels on a simple check mark on the menu. It looks like something running in 720p and upscaled with just a blur filter.The same goes for keybinds. Can't change them. Have an AZERTY or QWERTZ keyboard? Want to run ESDF instead of WASD? Too bad, not an option. The only controller rebind option is a checkbox for invert Y axis, and that it.I was really looking forward to this game a lot, as I can never get enough decent Star Trek content. Truly disappointing that it was released like this. Not just like this, but a year ago on Epic and none of these issues have been resolved despite it being out for a year technically and every single one of them being brought up before.EDIT AFTER COMPLETION: I will still leave my review as not recommended, as I believe the state of the game is poor. The framerate had consistent hits, both on Linux and Windows, with both high end Nvidia and AMD cards. Audio has strange problems, such as vocals only come out of the left speaker. Animations are unusual, the walking is so stiff it completely distracts from a scene. Controller controls to me felt clunky, but that's on me specifically. Between lack of keybind options to support the way I use my PC, and forcing a controller I didn't want to use, I found playing the game cumbersome at best.HOWEVER, the game itself is fantastic. It's a perfect homage to what Star Trek represents, with difficult moral decisions, conflict and resolution. There are lots of ties in to previous series, especially TNG, and the new races were interesting and compelling. Outside of the actual games technical issues that abound, and are unlikely to be fixed or they would have in the last year since release, the gameplay loop, story, voice acting, etc. are all absolutely top notch. It's painful to have to put this as a not recommended, but I can't even imagine how poorly this would run on a PC that doesn't have the latest generation graphics card and CPU. If a 7900 XTX on a 7800X3D can have framerate drops to sub 15 during cutscenes, that puts it up there as one of the least well optimized games I've played in years.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek is a kind of hard IP to make a fun video game for. You've got the ships and the phasers and all that, but the real value of Star Trek is the stories and characters. A Telltale style game is a n no trainer, but then you've got the problem of the writing. No chance a video game could write well enough to live to go the best of Star Trek. Heck, most of the TV shows struggle to do that. So, long story short... This game pulls it off better than any Star Trek product for years. The complex sci-fi allegories, the interesting and likable characters, the problem solving, all feel authentic. What's great is it starts off like a pretty standard episode format but soon enough it takes on cinematic stakes that are thrilling and compelling. In the end, the final climax, while it has plenty of action, winds up with a very Star Trek solution to the problem. It's so much better than "blow up the big bad enemy ship." Could it be better? Sure. There's a lot of room for improvement. Technically it still has some issues and the graphics are a generation behind, but it's more than enough to be absolutely captivating. I just really hope for more. They left a lot of things hanging that I desperately need  to know more about. Not to mention I just want to spend more time with this crew and this ship. Now I gotta go play it again and see if I can get some different results.

_childDocuments_.review: Star trek Resurgence is STAR TREK to the core.From Topical discussion of philosophical argument and perspective on an exploitation of a disadvantaged people and their impulse to seek strong leaders for their violent ability rather than ambassadors to peace, to the morality of choice weighed against the greater good.Star trek resurgence is beautiful, poignant, relevant, beautifully and expertly written and made... and truly heartbreaking.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! So well written and makes you feel like your actually apart of the story where your choices actually matter to the outcome and character development. I'm old enough to remember the  at what used to be the Las Vegas Hilton. It was appropriately named "The Experience"  because you and other people in your party are made to believe its a 3-D simulator ride like Star Tours at Disneyland, While you're waiting to be the next group to get into the simulator, you're plunged into complete darkness and after some theatrical lights, air, and sound effects you find everyone in your group standing on a transporter pad aboard the Enterprise-D where a crew member welcomes you to the 24th Century. You're then escorted out of the transporter room, down a corridor into a turbo lift that takes you to the bridge of the Enterprise-D where you can actually look around and interact with controls, survive a runaway turbo lift, and escape on a "real" shuttle craft in the middle of a space battle while the Enterprise is covering your escape. Knowing of course none of it was real, it was still enjoyable and incredibly immersive . Having gone on that ride more than a few times I was upset when it finally closed down in the mid 2000s. I feel if this game was made for VR, it would be about as close as you can get to being apart of that ride again. I have only played about 8 hours so far and even though I'm only a third of way through the story-line and I'm already hoping they plan to make a sequel!  Graphics are decent and the game runs smooth with only a few hiccups during intense cinematics its not the absolute best graphics in a game but its decent and doesn't distract from the enjoyment of the game. HIGHLY RECOMMEND if your a fan of TNG!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: This game tells a better story than a full season of Picard or Discovery.The writing feels on par with the better seasons of The Next Generation. The characters and relationships are interesting, and the visuals are well directed (if stylized).Most importantly, this truly feels like a The Next Generation game. Same Shakespearean delivery of dialogs, and Star Fleet feels like Star Fleet (not like "edgy dark Star Fleet" in Discovery or Picard). It's also much longer than I expected. It took me about 11 hours to complete. They could have easily sold this as 4 episodes for €15 each and I would have still bought it.The only negatives are that the Keyboard+Mouse controls are pretty bad, and occasionally the animations seem to bug out or rendered in a weird stutter despite a high framerate. But none of that was bad enough to sour my enjoyment. I really wish for a sequel now.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: If you're in for a Tell Tale game then I can recommend this full stop. If you're just a Trek fan I can say you're getting a great 10 hour movie/mini-series with mediocre game play. Anyone else will probably not be into it. The good: The writing is great, the story is solid (kudos to the writing team!), the voice acting is generally fantastic if a bit uneven in places. The bad: 90% of the "puzzle" interaction is not good. I'm sorry to the team, but "make the mouse move badly" cannot be a game mechanic or puzzle. Quick Time Events are pretty much a given in this type of game and that's fine. But many of these were simply frustrating and felt forced when it likely would've been better to simply continue with the pacing of the cinematic or whatever. I think this game really wants to be 90s style FMV game built in Unreal. I think that could've been fantastic (ST: Borg, what up!). I really look forward to this team's next effort and I really hope we get to hang with this crew moving forward. I think a sequel really needs more fluidity in movement, better puzzles, and fewer things thrown in just to make it more "gamey". I think a sequel building on the lessons learned while making this one would really shine. Congrats to the team, it was worth the wait for it to come to steam!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Huge Star Trek fan here,If you are a graphic hound, you will be disappointed! The overall look of the game makes it seem that you are playing a pre-2012 game. It looks really dated and that might be a huge turn of for some gamers. What this game really makes appealing to me, is that its story is written in the old stile of Star Trek right out of the franchises golden era! (NOT THE CALVIN TIMELINE!!!) To me this is a massive plus, because new Trek is…well…sh*t! A fact that hurts this second-generation Trekkie heart to the core! To have a game like this that brings back the old school of Star Trek-story telling is more than refreshing and it is just what I need these days!Also, you have to keep in mind that this is a Tell Tale-like point and click-ish story driven adventure. There is not much direct action to be expected. The focus lies in playing through a story that can be manipulated here and there, by making different dialogue choices and that is it! If this is not your cup of tea, leave this game be. Please don’t downvote. Just don’t buy! I Really wish to see this game become a success, because the Old Trek is what the Trekkies really want! I personally like the Tell Tale formular so to me this is an easy recommendation. Addition - 29.05.24:I have played through this game now and would finally like to add to my review that this was top tier Star Trek! _childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of mixed feelings about this game. I'm a huge Star Trek fan and the TNG/DS9 era (in which this game takes place during) is my absolute favorite era of Star Trek. On the surface, the character models and their animations look really poor at times for the current day but that can be easily overlooked.As far as choices go, you do get to make a few "big" decisions but most decisions you make are relatively small and have little actual impact on the storyline. Some of them depend on the dialogue you choose, and some of the big ones can have serious consequences. All-in-all, the game does what it set out to do. It feels like a long episode or movie that takes place during the Star Trek: Deep Space Nine era. The ships look beautiful and the dialogue fits well. The settings, sounds and props are very authentic to the source material.You play as two different protagonists on the same ship (First Officer and Petty Officer respectively) and it makes you feel like you get to know (at least some) of the crew... most of the bridge crew aside from 3 of the senior staff barely gets any screen-time, and only one of them gets a name. He's a Bajoran who mans the Conn and it felt like a wasted opportunity not to see or hear more from him, but I digress. Should you play this game? If you're a Star Trek fan and enjoy Telltale-type games, then yes - absolutely. If you're not really into Star Trek though, then the game will probably be very confusing and boring to you. It's a good game that would've had a lot more potential if it were to be given the right resources and I'd love to see more like it in the future, preferably in the Star Trek universe again.Also, as of right now (Sept. 30th 2024) 2 particular achievements are still bugged and are not unlocking. It's a bummer to do multiple playthroughs only to not unlock what you set out to.

_childDocuments_.review: In my time, I have reviewed a number of games for both the Star Trek franchise and from TellTale studios (many of the same team members who created this game). I have very much enjoyed the TellTale games as they had very excellent stories and were great to follow along with. In terms of a "video game", I will say this probably isn't a great one. There is not a lot of varied game play and it's very linear in how you play the game. The graphics are nothing to write home about and there is almost zero replayability (took me about 11 hours to finish the game). If you're someone who enjoys games that are FPS (Call of Duty) or 4X (anything Paradox-based), this is going to be a very different feel. It's almost more like a visual novel, where you make choices as you play through. But, moving on from the game play, there is a very excellent story which is found within this game. It is the first Star Trek product (game, film, or TV show) that actually feels like Star Trek that has come out in many, many years. It has a great and compelling story that you can invest yourself in, and allows you to choose to uphold the ideals of the Federation or to trample upon them. The characters are consistent, deep, and there are actually good people who live in the galaxy. If you're a fan of the Star Trek series as it was before 2000, then you will enjoy this game, or rather, this journey and story that unfolds.

_childDocuments_.review: Horrendous PC version. The settings menu has no options for Anti-Aliasing, FOV, Mouse Sens, Texture, Model, Shadow, Post Processing, Effects, Foliage, Shading, View Distance and Resolution quality. In order for you to modify these settings, you must turn to the config file (GameUserSettings.ini) and change the [ScalabilityGroups]. Further removal of unneeded features must be done via the (Engine.ini) all of which is located in (AppData\Local\StarTrekGame\Saved\Config\WindowsNoEditor).Frame rate wise the game targets a 60 FPS (but this can be uncapped with no change in game speed), while cut scenes target 30 FPS. That drop in the animation speed is incredibly noticeable, and takes you out of the game every time that happens.A layman shouldn't have to turn to 2010 levels of game configuration. The 7th Generation came and went, we are now in 2024, releasing competent PC versions is not that hard at all, and yet you drop this on us.Visual quality is incredibly poor.The game will do a significant resolution drop when entering certain areas of the starship (likely a 50% res drop), and they use the horrible default UE4 forced TAA to cover up the drop, which causes the image to look incredibly soft and blurry.GPU Utilization also spikes even when using the 60 FPS cap. Where does the extra utilization come from? You've already nuked half of my resolution, so why? (all of this is happening on a 3080).No fix has been posted yet for this horrible resolution drop, but you can remedy it by using "", and inputting any number above 100. (This will increase GPU utilization significantly)There is no excuse for the game running this poorly when the quality of the assets don't push any boundaries.Considering this game got only 1 patch(!), do not hold out any hope of them fixing any of the issues as described above.A shame, because the Star Trek license doesn't get used much, and I was really hoping they resolved all of the issues from the Epic release, but alas, they only came to Steam to soak up a little more cash, and are now probably off to create another half assed game.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek: Resurgence is a game that will speak directly to the hearts of Star Trek fans, particularly those who have a soft spot for the TNG era movies. From the moment you start playing, you are transported to the USS Resolute, this feels like it was plucked straight out of a Star Trek film, with a strong and engaging narrative that will keep you hooked until the end.You play as the first commander and as a lower decks petty officer, the gameplay is good but slightly limited, with a focus on decision-making that allows you to shape the story in subtle but meaningful ways. I have played through the entire story once, it feels like the current version of the game does have a broadly fixed ending with slight alterations, I would love to see even more freedom given to the player in future versions. The ability to truly shape the story and completely define the outcome would be an exciting addition to an already fantastic game.That being said, the game is still well worth playing, especially if you're a Star Trek fan. The writing is sharp, the characters are well-developed, and the attention to detail is impressive. Whether you're a seasoned Star Trek veteran or a newcomer to the franchise, there's something here for everyone to enjoy.Overall, I would highly recommend Star Trek: Resurgence to anyone looking for a narratively driven game with a strong Star Trek flavor. It's a love letter to the franchise and its fans, and a must-play for anyone who wants to experience a Star Trek adventure like never before.

With that said, this story, it's execution and the sheer enjoyment I got from playing through it were indescribable.  I haven't been this immersed in a game in a VERY long time, and I've been gaming since the Commodore 64.  I've been a deep fan of Trek going back to the syndicated re-runs of the original series and all the way through.  While this story may not be considered cannon it is one of the best Star Trek stories I've been privileged to partake of.  I would bold say that the quality of the story holds up to Wrath of Khan.  Essentially you get a 13 hour, that's how long my play through took to complete, Star Trek interactive movie.  Given the time to complete, I'd almost call it a trilogy.  I sincerely hope to get a new story for the Resolute, their crew is worth getting to know better.  My suggestion to the developers, if you do make a sequel, allow for transferring choices from the first into the next.  This is an option that has been lost for some reason over time and should be included, the players deserve to see their choices validated.  Bottom line, if you are a true Trek fan, you're money will be well spent!

_childDocuments_.review: THIS is the Star Trek I have been missing for a long while. Tough moral choices, well-written likable characters who act like adults instead of sassy know-it-all teenagers, and a focus on understanding and discovery with action coming second. If you've been unhappy with the state of overly-action heavy Trek movies and poorly-written melodrama of recent Trek streaming shows, Resurgence is the cure.Objectively, this should probably only be about a 3/5 due to its glaring limitations and flaws on a technical level. This is a Telltale-like from many of those same old developers under a new label, and technical prowess was never something at which they excelled. This game often feels just on the brink of falling apart - like it's being held together with duct tape and a few paper clips. The seams never quite fully fall apart, but it's not technically polished by any means. Still, I WAS able to finish it without any game-breaking bugs, which is more than I can say for a lot of triple-A games lately, and this did NOT have that level of budget.Personally, this feels like a 5/5 for me thanks to the writing and feeling. This IS good Star Trek. Likable characters with memorable personalities and different strengths and weaknesses make interacting with the crew so much fun. An engaging story with multiple factions and a solid number of choices with no real "correct" answer made for an incredibly engaging experience.Look, if you're a Telltale fan, you should probably play this game. If you're a Star Trek fan, you NEED to play this game. Do it!!I only hope this sells well enough now that it's no longer Epic-exclusive to warrant a number of sequels or spin-offs. I'll be there.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek Resurgence is a story-driven adventure game that delivers all the excitement and wonder of the Star Trek universe. Join the crew of the U.S.S. Resolute, as First Officer Jara Rydek and Staff Engineer Carter Diaz, on a mission to stop a powerful ancient force from devouring everything in its wake! The game takes you on an epic adventure with dialogue-heavy role-playing and beautifully crafted branching storylines. You will experience the Star Trek universe through different gameplay styles, including flying shuttles, battling with phasers, scanning with the tricorder, sneaking through ships in stealth mode, and much more.Star Trek Resurgence delivers everything you expect from a good story: surprises, twists, emotional moments and action. Although the game plays after The Next Generation, it captures the atmosphere of the first Star Trek series with Kirk and Spock very well.Development studio Dramatic Labs was founded by former Telltale employees, so it’s no surprise that Resurgence plays exactly like one of the old Telltale games. In other words: Basically, it’s Star Trek with interactive elements. You'll often see story sequences that require you to move by pressing certain buttons that appear on the screen. There are also moments where you can move around freely within a limited range, examine things and solve simple puzzles. Now and then, the tricorder has to be used, and you’ll also play stealth sequences and firefights where you have to use your phaser in a targeted manner.None of this is overly complex or demanding, but it does give Resurgence a healthy level of interactivity. And then of course there are the obligatory dialogues and decisions that you have to make. These affect your relationships and standing with crew members and other people and influence the course of the story at various points. In short: If you've played a Telltale game, you'll know how it plays out.The story is told from two perspectives, First Officer Jara Rydek and Technician Carter Diaz. The two tiers perfectly combine the different aspects of the story, and Diaz and Co. bring in the view of the lower decks.All achievements are hidden, which makes sense because we have to unlock them by our decisions. If you care for achievements, I recommend playing the game twice. First, enjoy the game spoiler free, then unlock missing achievements in your second play-through. The play time is about 11 hours.Unfortunately, you can not skip cut-scenes. On top of that, the game only supports automatic save points that sometimes are far apart.Star Trek Resurgence is not a triple A game and the graphics are not quite up to date, but it does have an incredibly good story that keeps twisting in unexpected ways and is particularly exciting in the action sequences. The game is clearly a must-have for Star Trek fans, but also recommend to everyone else.Excellent story with surprises, twists, emotional moments and actionOutstanding voice acting from all protagonistsVery good musicPerfect sound effectsAction sequences are really excitingYour decisions influence the storyForces you to make many tough decisionsNo bugs, no crashesLikeable charactersVery good camera movementGreat atmosphereExcitingNot woke, not even a littleTechnically outdated graphics, but nevertheless beautifulVery simple gameplayUsing the tricorder is a little annoyingOccasional stutters (but nothing serious)Stiff animations when walking in cut scenesPS: I fell deeply in love with First Officer Jara Rydek. In case you happen to know her email address, please share it with me.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, especially the story. Some of the animations or rigging or other things can be a little janky at times, but you get over it pretty quickly.
