_childDocuments_.review: A strong interactive story that stayed engaging and really feels like you're in an episode of TNG/ DS9 / VOY. Equal parts action, adventure, exploration and mystery, there's some real love for the franchise shining through here, and it leads to a very strong game overall. I found I was able to overlook the issues I had, and would highly recommend the game.My main gripes are slightly janky graphics, such as inconsistent animation quality, particularly in 3rd-person segments. I also feel that some of the negative character interactions and consequences are a little contrived, and it's especially noticeable in the Starfleet characters. this left me unsure how much impact my decisions had on the end of the game, at least as Carter, and whether I could have really done much to change / improve my outcome for either main character. Lastly, and this is more a note for the devs I suppose, there were quite a few bugs. Nothing game breaking, but minor things like subtitles not matching dialogue, or not appearing. At one point, a companions phaser kept firing throughout an entire cutscene.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. If you are a fan of TNG-era Star Trek, just drop everything buy Star Trek: Resurgence right now. It is the Star Trek game we always dreamed of. I can't get over how much a thrill it is to walk around just scanning stuff with a tricorder - hearing the iconic sound effects we all grew up with - investigating anomalies, working together with professional and competent colleagues, trying to negotiate peace between feuding factions... If you ever played other sci-fi games and felt frustrated at how everything always has to come back to mindless murder, this is the game for you.Which isn't to say there's no combat, or no space battles. There's definitely some of those, and they're the weakest parts of the game. In particular the cover shooting is awful, especially if you compare it to games like Mass Effect where that's a central mechanic. This game is much stronger when it embraces the classic Telltale approach of walking around mostly static scenes, examining stuff, talking to people and occasionally clicking through a QTE. As usual with Telltale-style adventures, you get put into moral quandaries where no matter what you pick it's going to annoy someone, and that may impact which character you ally with later on, but it'll never leave you locked out of completing the game, so you can relax into it and safely pick the choices that seem to make the most sense for your read on the character.Or characters - plural - because you split the game between playing a first officer on the bridge and an engineer on the lower decks. This is a key part of making the story feel personal, because instead of just seeing the captain's eye view, you get to roll up your sleeves and get your hands dirty, feeling an integral part of the crew as you tune up transporter patterns and scan miscellaneous rocks and joke around with your colleagues.The story is like a good multi-episode arc of TNG-era Trek, fully voiced, with all new characters, aliens and ships (plus a couple of cameos from old faves). Given how dark and gritty most of the new TV Treks are, it is an absolute joy to get to work on a crew where almost everyone actually believes in the principles of Starfleet. Protocol is largely observed, duty is respected and the enemy isn't some fifth column that undermines the point of the show. It's fully grounded in the optimistic and forward-looking spirit of Trek, and thankfully it's not narratively trapped in the TOS era like early season Discovery or Strange New Worlds.I loved this game. If you aren't a TNG-era Trek fan, or if you just hate Telltale-style adventures, you might not enjoy it. There is plenty of jank. Simple, almost cartoon-like graphics. Frustratingly insensitive mouse controls. Music that - while Trekkish - often overpowers the dialog. Aforementioned garbage cover shooting mechanic. But if you grew up with TNG and Voyager, if you think the best new Treks are Lower Decks and Prodigy, then this is the game for you. I really hope the developers get the chance to do more with the license. New stories, new characters, new worlds to explore - it's all right there. Excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: Engage! 100% Recommend for the Star Trek fan. I'm a couple hours in on launch day and the game plays like an interactive movie with the primary focus on dialogue options and building relationships (for better or worse). It has a solid plot line that easily could have been a series of Voyager or DS9 episodes. I can tell alot of attention has been paid to detail. However, I don't think your positive, neutral, or negative relationships actually change the plot as much as they just add some additional scripted dialogue between characters. The guard rails here are pretty big, meaning don't expect much deviation from the main scripted plot line, but that is understandable for an interactive movie type game. I would have liked the opportunity to go more off script and explore more of the ship in an open-world type game play, or even have more realistic interactions with ship computer terminals that impacted the plot or that could change entire missions. In any event, the voice acting is done well, the graphics are good, and the diverse personalities clearly come through. Yeah, its the best Star Trek game in years. Buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I dislike adventure games, they usually don't allow for novelty thinking and railroad you to boredom. I stay away from Telltale type games, because that type of gameplay doesn't engage me, the choices aren't really meaningful and the quick time events are infuriating.That being said this game has Star Trek feel written all over it. Directors really played with it and it shows. The two character story lines are ideal for telling a story. Writing is good enough, but sometimes some of the choices break immersion. You can't please everyone in this game(some of the crew are cry babies) and on one hand it's gives weight to the decision you make, on the other hand they are starfleet and it shouldn't feel like talking to a teenager who didn't get his way. The story chews off a bigger chunk than needed and I would be perfectly fine with a smaller scale story, an episode from Star Trek, but instead we got a several part movie, but it still captures the life on a starship well. In essence this game is an action packed adventure  that teaches burdain of command and tough choices.I would love to see more Star Trek games like this. _childDocuments_.review: The Telltale DNA is definitely present in Star Trek: Resurgence, for better and worse.The attention to detail is impressive; it's clear that the writers and art team did their research. From the DS9 padded uniforms to the rank insignia and starship designs, everything feels authentic. The story itself is a direct sequel to "The Last Outpost," one of the stronger episodes from TNG's first season.the downsides? Don't expect to be blown away by the animations or visuals. They're on par with what you'd find in a Telltale game from about 14 years ago, reminiscent of titles like The Walking Dead or Back to the Future. There are also a few soft-locking bugs that required me to restart the game—about two or three in the 10-hour campaign. One particularly frustrating moment involved a firefight section where no enemies spawned, leaving me to just wait out the timer. Some aspects of the game feel very dated (stealth missions with insta-fail for example)The story and writing are phenomenal, standing shoulder to shoulder with the best TNG, DS9, or even Voyager two-part episodes (think "The Best of Both Worlds" or the final episodes of DS9 Season 7). The characters are memorable and likeable, I think it's a must play for a die hard Star Trek fan.If you've never seen  star trek this might not be the game for you.  (real Star Trek = no shows or movies produced past, say, 2001)I really hope the developers get to keep telling their stories, they have really good writers.

It's not a dealbreaker, but think of this more as a holonovel than as an open-world game.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews for games, but for this one I feel compelled to.Let's get one thing out of the way first: this is not a game. Don't look at it as a game. This is a 10 hour long Star Trek movie that has game-like elements. If that's a showstopper for you then stop reading cause you're probably not going to like this game, if it isn't then please read on.I've been playing Star Trek games for a LONG time, going all the way back to the Win95 games like Starfleet Command and Away Team. Star Trek games are ALL OVER THE PLACE in terms of quality and when I first saw this game come out on the Epic launcher I brushed it off as another low effort cash grab *cough* JJ-verse games *cough*.But this game is not that. This game has heart and it has soul and within a few minutes of the opening cut scene you'll see very clearly that the devs care very much about this game and that they are huge Star Trek fans. I'm going to get the gameplay part of this review out of the way here so I can just gush about the story afterward. The gameplay is ... not great. This game is 75% quick time events and dialogue choices. The other 25% is puzzles which are only in there to give this game a game-y feel. I will say though that the puzzles don't seem like they're out of place for the universe. For instance, a common puzzle is aligning the transporter matter stream and energizing the buffer for transport. Honestly, I've never seen that before. I've never seen a game attempt to integrate that before. Usually it's just press a button and you beam down. But no, they made a mini puzzle out of it. And yeah that puzzle is pretty rudimentary, but it's engaging and it actually does feel like you're the transporter tech struggling to boost power to the annular confinement beam to stabilize the matter stream (kudos to you if you're getting all these references). And that's the great thing about this game, it feels like you're there, in uniform, on the deck, trying to save the day. All flaws aside, I couldn't really ask for anything more out of a Star Trek game. Now onto the story...This game has story. It is well crafted, it is well thought out, it is well designed, and it is chock full of Star Trek references; in some cases, very obscure Star Trek references. The game takes place in the 24th century post First Contact and Dominion War. But if you're a fan, you probably figured that out from the cover art. You play as two people: Commander Jara Rydek and Petty Officer Carter Diaz. When you're playing as Commander Rydek, you are the officer on deck. You have the information, you have the knowledge, you have the authority; but you're the one with the responsibility. You're the one who has to stand for what you believe in and make the tough calls. Everyone else has their opinion; but at the end of the day, you're the one who has to pull all those people together to make things happen. And not all your choices are going to be popular, many of them are straight up pick a side because not everyone is going to agree with what you're doing; and personally I think that's great, I think that's awesome. I think too many games shy away from the kind of deep character driven story choices that drive a good story and Resurgence isn't afraid to do that; just like all the great Star Trek episodes do. More than once I felt conflicted about the course of action I was about to take because I didn't want to let my crew down; and I think that's an amazing feeling to have in a game. On the flip side, you have Petty Officer Diaz. Before I get into him. let me just say that it is a great detail that they actually included the enlisted officer rank pip; which to my knowledge, only exists in the expanded Star Trek universe. When you're playing Diaz, you're the redshirt going at the problem in the mud. You're the one whose out in space having to repair a plasma conduit or redistribute the EPS manifolds because the warp core is going to breech. You're the one in the lower decks about to be blasted with a phaser because of some decision the brass decided to make that you have absolutely no control over. When you're playing Diaz,  you're the guy out in the field, fixing the ship to keep it from falling out of the sky.Of the two, I much preferred playing as Rydek. But the devs did a great job in not shoehorning either character into the sidelines. Both characters have impact on the story and both characters are just as important to the game. Now as for all the other characters, again the devs did a good job at fleshing them out. By the time you're through with the game, which is only like 10 or so hours, you'll know all the officers on the bridge, all the aliens, all the crew, all the hero's, all the villain's and where they all stand. It is quite an accomplishment for such a compact game. And if you're really willing to lose yourself in the story, the choices you make can feel very rewarding. And it's just awesome getting to call red alert in the heat of the moment!Lastly, I'm going to close out the review with my biggest gripes about the game. The very first one is that there are no save states. There is no revert, there is no going back, once you finish a story chapter and you've made your decision, then that's that. Like I get that for a story based game you want to have the players decisions be locked in and feel permanent; BUT, I literally got halfway through the game, made a single decision I wanted to go back on and couldn't cause the chapter had already closed (and as it turns out the vast majority of players made the same decision I did on that first go. Minor spoilers: it was the shield algorithm decision) I had to start the whole game over and play through everything AGAIN just to get back to my decision point. Which wasn't the worst because I was planning to replay the game once anyway, but it certainly felt like a waste of time to do that. Next up is the severe lack of control settings, mainly the cursor speed which is PAINFULLY slow. The UI surrounding the game is very bare bones and you'll likely find several industry standard QoL features that are missing completely from this game. Ultimately it doesn't take away from the core experience, but like how hard is it to give me a scroll bar that I can use to adjust my cursor speed? (Edit: Wait, did they patch that in? I swear it wasn't there when I wrote the review ... )And then there are the character models and animations which are ... passable at best. They look like they're 80% done and are good in most places; but they could have used a few more rounds of polish. I'll say it again, if you're here because you're expecting a slick, well polished game, then look elsewhere because this ain't it. But if you're looking for an engaging and immersive Star Trek story set in the 24th century, then this game is right for you. Seriously, don't think of it as a game. Think of it as one long Star Trek episode and you'll have a great time!Devs, if you're reading this I have two things to say to you. 1) PLEASE make a follow up. It doesn't have to be the same crew if the story of the Resolute is over; but please make another one if you can. I promise you that if you release the follow up on steam I'll buy it day 1. 2) PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE add forward facing torpedo tube launchers to the Resolute model. You have no idea how much that bothered me. Don't get me wrong, I love the Resolute and I love your decision to include such an obscure ship class in this game. I also love the choice to set the game on small science vessel like the Nova class, instead of like a Galaxy class, or something else more well known. So that's all great, but please PLEASE, my kingdom for two torpedo tubes :)

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start my review I must start by saying I like this type of game but it is not for everyone. If you ever played a game made by Tell Tell Games then you know exactly what type of game this is. If not the best way to describe this game would be it is an interactive movie. You make a choice and then you see how that choice effects everything. There is little skill involved and more like watching an entire season of Star Trek with you making all the important choices. With that out of the way, on to the review.If you are looking for a quick answer my review score would be a 7/10 and a solid buy especially if it is on sale. It does have a couple of flaws that bumped the score down that I will get into but overall this game plays smooth, good graphics, good sound and an excellent story. Thankfully this game is finished and does not have any major technical issues or at least none that I came across. It takes about 10 or so hours to beat the game but that is only one play through. You will need two or three play through if you want to get all the Achievements and see all the different options. In this game you control two different characters. One being Carter, a brilliant engineer and the other is Jara who is the 2nd in command. Being 2nd in command makes things a lot more interesting than just being the Captain. Not only do you have to make decisions and go on away missions but you also have to decide when to follow the Captains order or not. Which brings me to my first category...Story 10/10If you like Star Trek then you already know what to expect more or less. This game is a whole season of Star Trek in one game and it does not let you down. As Commander Jara you get to make all kinds of decisions some of which can and will get your crew hurt if you make the wrong decision and nothing feels worse that visiting someone in sick bay who got hurt following your orders. This is a game that requires you to get emotionally invested if you want to get the most out of it and on my first play through I played like it was real and every choice was my own. The best part is all the choices make sense and what you do can make the other people either like you or dislike you. There is even choices that make the enemy like or dislike you but I won't spoil what that can do. My point is your choices matter in the game and it will impact your life and the lives of people around you. The same goes for Carter and the things he does really effects the people around him. It hits even harder with him because they are not just crew, they are your friends and his choices can save his friends or get them hurt. The best part is Carter also does a lot of Star Trek things you always hear about which brings me to....Game Play 5/10As you see we hit the real issue of the game. The parts you actually play are either quick time events sort of (I will explain), very easy mini games or the one mini game that is so hard it makes me want to uninstall. The quick time events are not really quick. It more like press this button and you dodge or press this button to move. It is not quick, quite the opposite, you have a good 5 seconds or more which is why I hesitate to call them quick time events. The cool part is you get to do some Star Trek “Techno Babble” like re-calibrate this plasma flow or calibrate the transporter so you can get through the interference. The mini games are super easy but it is still cool to do stuff you always hear on the show. Quick side note. The people who wrote this really did their homework because even the “Techno Babble” makes sense if you are a Star Trek fan. Anyways you also get to fly a shuttle and despite issues that arise (not going to say since it is a spoiler) it is still very easy. Now what sucks is any time, except the first few, where you have to fight enemy's with phasers. I don't know who programmed this part but it is horrible. They mostly play out the same. You have to hold a room while enemies flood in. As you know a phaser is not a machine gun so when there is a lot of enemies, it is easy to get over run. Even after I got use to it and had it down where I could kill all the enemies as the came in, you would get screwed because after you kill so many you will have a short cut scene with the people you are with for what ever reason and then when it lets you continue, the room is flooded with enemies. There are things you can shoot to blow up to thin them out but it is not enough. It is a poorly balanced section and if it was not for this the game would be a solid 9/10. Other then that there is not to much else to note. Sound and Graphics 9/10Not to much to say about either which is why they are together. The game looks, sounds and feel like Star Trek. Not to much more you can really ask for. There are not any major graphical issues and while you can defiantly find better looking games, there is nothing wrong with this one and there are a few areas that look really good especially toward the end of the game. The music and sound effects all give you that Star Trek feel and it really helps immerse you in the game. Final ThoughtsOverall they did a really good job and the game is good enough to make me want a sequel. Star Trek is the perfect franchise for this type of game. I did not get into the details of the story because there is no way to do so without spoilers but just know it is really good and if they made this a TV/Streaming show, I would watch it no questions asked. If you are ready to jump into the Star Trek universe and make the difficult decisions, then this is the game for you. The only reason I recommend waiting for a sale is how short the game is. If you are a one and done type person then wait for a sale. If you like to replay games, get all the achievements or just want to see all the options, then it is worth it at full price as well. The only other thing I can think to say is...Live long and prosper.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about halfway through and I'm having a great time. Some of the actual "gameplay" parts or whatever you would call them are a little rough, and there have been a few minor glitches here and there when moving around or transitioning from "gameplay" to cutscene, but the core "choose your own adventure" part of the game is really what I'm here for and that's been solid.The voice acting is very good and the overall presentation is very solid. Characters are enjoyable and endearing for the most part. The graphics leave a bit to be desired, but there's been a lot of beautiful parts nonetheless. I feel like I'm playing a very long episode of classic Trek. I would recommend playing for any fan of these kinds of narrative games, but if you're a fan of the franchise I would say this is a must-play title.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------Additional notes after finishing my first playthrough:There are some technical issues that become more apparent as you get further into the game. Aside from some general jankiness every so often (weird animation moments, dialogue being cut off once or twice), I had one hard crash, and several moments of questionable framerate throughout the experience. Not enough of a problem to ruin the game for me, but it really cemented the fact that this game is rough around the edges. There's a lot of unrealized potential overall--held back by technical issues and questionable gameplay choices.Despite all of that, I had a lot of fun with it. The game could be a lot more than what it is, but then again, so could I. Looking forward to doing another run soon. I really hope they make more of these.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game is amazing! While gameplay is a bit basic, this games true strongpoint is the narrative and storytelling. Much like the Telltale games, this game has an insanely well developed, deep story, well-developed characters and a strong root in the Star Trek franchise, especially the era of TNG, DS9 and Voyager. Must play for any fan of the aforementioned shows. I wish they would make this a new show in the style of the 80s/90s shows now. ;)Long review:Star Trek: Resurgence is a narrative-driven adventure game developed by Dramatic Labs, bringing players into the heart of a classic Star Trek experience. Set shortly after The Next Generation era, the game offers a fresh yet familiar story filled with diplomacy, exploration, and moral dilemmas. Those who played Telltale games will know, in what moral dilemmas you can sometimes end up and how much you can occasionally doubt your own real-life principles and morals after a playthrough. ;)The game's story revolves around two perspectives: Commander Jara Rydek, a newly appointed officer aboard the USS Resolute, and Carter Diaz, a low-ranking engineer navigating life in the bowels of the ship. The dual perspective allows players to experience the grandeur of command decisions and the personal struggles of Starfleet's crew. In general, more weight on a grand scale are put on Commander Rydek's decision though, which is why I sometimes felt that Carter's decisions made less of a difference on grander scale. The sound design is a highlight of Star Trek: Resurgence. From the hum of the starship to the iconic swish of the doors, the game immerses you in its world. The voice acting is solid, with standout performances by the leads.With multiple choices and branching dialogue paths, Star Trek: Resurgence offers some replay value. Fans who enjoy exploring alternative outcomes and moral dilemmas will find it rewarding to play through again.A bit of a negative for me are the achievements. I am a bit of an achievement hunter and in order to gain all achievements, you will have to play through the entire game at least twice, potentially three times, which I find a bit frustrating. Also, unfortunately, the "Choice" feature does not seem to work anymore, which is a bummer. I always really enjoy seeing the choices I made and how many other players made the same or a different choice. All in all I would give this game solid FIVE STARS though, because I am a sucker for quality, well-written stories and well-developed characters, both of which have become rather rate these days. In essence this game can compete with some of the better episode from the old shows and in terms of Star Trek video games, this is definitely playing high at the top of the list of all ST games ever made. I hope the studio will make more Star Trek games like this!

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game so much, I binged through the entire thing in 2 days!Thank you to the development team, product owner etc for 'getting' what made the Star Trek TNG era so special. As you clearly intended, it genuinely feels like you're participating in an extended TNG episode.Pros:1. The sounds, look and 'feel' of both the internal and external of the Starfleet ships really did feel authentic2. Once you (as the player) get your head around it been a fairly 'on rails' narrative driven game, it's actually a lot of fun and very compelling3. The voice acting and story line were clearly a focus for the development team, and it shows4. Although I don't think the player's choices probably make much difference to the outcome of the game i.e. you'll still win etc, balancing the various interpersonal relationships with meeting a specific objective, adds an additional layer on interestCons:1. Clearly a console port (and still a little rough around the edges visually, although I didn't encounter any game breaking bugs)2. As per point 1, there's a startling lack of graphical settings compared to most PC games and not being able to run at higher frame rates is occasionally a little jarring but this only relates to cut scenes and not open play3. The odd error with the subtitles text but again, nothing that really causes a problem4. The mouse sensitivity for most of the mini games is shocking i.e. WAY too lowObjectively and WITHOUT the Star Trek tie in, the game feels like a game from 10+ years ago. However, WITH the Star Trek tie in (done convincingly) the experience is significantly elevated to the most fun I've had with a Star Trek game in years. Given the relative lack of development budget and the reason price of the game, I think the dev team can be very proud what they've createdHopefully they'll one day be a sequel that follows the same principles and care for the TNG era property.

_childDocuments_.review: English Version:Star Trek: Resurgence - A Tribute to the Golden Age of Star TrekAfter playing the demo, I was so thrilled that I immediately purchased the full game. It's fantastic that a demo is offered, giving players the chance to try the game before buying."Star Trek: Resurgence" is undoubtedly the best Star Trek rendition since "Star Trek: Voyager – Elite Force 1 and 2" and partially "Star Trek Online." This title feels like a lost double episode from the archives of the glorious TNG, Voyager, and DS9 era. The story is lovingly told and perfectly captures the spirit of these old series. One must remember that "The Next Generation" aired its final episode on May 25, 1994 – this game is a true gift to the fans of that era.The characters are relatable and act in the typical Starfleet manner of that period. The game immediately captivated me, and you can see the influence of Telltale Games, where the developers come from. This only adds to the game's quality.My Steam account is almost 20 years old, and I am over 40, married, and have kids. This game hits the perfect spot for my taste and is ideally targeted at my demographic and age group. I no longer have the patience for vast open-world games or massive online multiplayer and certainly don't have the time for them. Therefore, "Star Trek: Resurgence" has become my new declared favorite game.The Quick-Time Events perfectly match my gaming preference. I've been involved with Counter-Strike since Beta 0.6, but that's become too strenuous for me. I haven't even finished "The Witcher 3" to this day. "Star Trek: Resurgence" convinces me on all levels: as a Star Trek fan since the age of 7 and as a gamer. It's authentic, the characters are just as you'd expect them to be. The graphics, the lights, the colors, and LCARS look incredibly beautiful, making you want to dive into this adventure and be a part of the crew.I have written no more than five reviews in my entire time on Steam. This game is simply beautiful and makes me a happier Trekkie.

There's also a few things that should not require a button prompt to accomplish (like opening a lid) and a few of the mini game segments drag on too long.The Ugly:The game has some moderately bad audio bugs and despite the graphics being relative unimpressive, the game performs poorly even on the lowest graphics setting with frequent frame dips. On top of that I experienced several crashed to the desktop, one of which was during the story's climax.

_childDocuments_.review: ONLY RECOMMENDED FOR CLASSIC STAR TREK FANS.As is the case with the recent Telltale's The Expanse game, I don't think casuals and non fans would find this game to be appealing to them if not simply for the fact that you need preexisting knowledge of the lore from other media that span decades (and is more true of the case here than with The Expanse) to fully enjoy this game.Now this game itself have more gameplay and more variance than The Expanse but in some ways because they're implemented in just the basic way (like push combo of buttons and sticks to grab a tool) they becomes more of a chore than anything meaningful.There is more action oriented gameplay in here with basic cover shooter mechanics and stealth mechanics, but the numbers of times they appeared can be counted with one hand, and when you do them you would feel that playstation 3 generation games more often than not did them better nearly 20 years ago than this game.Then there's the visual, audio and performance aspect of this game, to sum it up I've seen better playstation 3 games than this game and this game also performs like playstation 3 PC port games from back then.Also just like The Expanse, the game doesn't support 21:9 display and also luckily there is a fix for that somewhere on the internet. IMHO all of these kind of contemporary cinematic adventure games that comes out after 2020s have no excuse for not supporting 21:9 display.All that weakness aside though, I gotta applaud the writers of this game for delivering that classic star trek story, the best I've seen since 90s era trek shows and even upstaging the season 3 of Picard show that is rated highly among trek fans. It's not without flaws, there are moments of ridiculous drama between characters that make no sense and too blatantly written just to create drama but without satisfying resolution in the end but that's the only bad things I can say from the story.As other people have stated, buy and play this if you are a long time star trek fan, and if you aren't, just stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: If you lIked Star Trek The Next Generation you will LOVE Star Trek Resurgence.This game is a love letter to TNG if ever I saw one. Fan-favorite characters like Will Riker return, with the man in question being captain of the starship Titan, and even Ambassador Spock returns from the grave, voiced with dead-on accuracy by a new VA.This game has it all. Impactful decisions that can make or break a playthrough, intrigue and mystery, returning stars, grade-A voice acting, and a solid story.Speaking of which, the immersion is total. The game goes all-out to put you in the captain's chair and make you feel that you ARE Jara Rydek. Even the quick-time events, which many may think are an outdated form of gaming, really help sell the fact that YOU are the character, as opposed to some RNG roll or just a set path.This game is a clear example of how ALL Star Trek RPGs should be made.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is janky on every level but free of major problems and ultimately a good time.- Controls cannot be remapped but there's only a few of them and it's a "low intensity" game so it doesn't matter much.- Visuals are often glitchy and animations are stiff but the game looks decent overall and characters emote well enough when it matters.- Voice acting is quite good though the quality and volume of recording can be uneven. Sometimes the subtitles don't match the voice over though the differences are minor.- Cutscenes are unskippable. This is probably the worst problem this game has. If you want to try something different or need to replay a chapter you have to sit through it all.- For the most part save checkpoints only happen between chapters so if you need to stop playing mid chapter you'll almost certainly have to replay all of it. Individual chapters are not very long so it's not a big deal, just more jank.- Story is pretty great actually as are the characters. _childDocuments_.review: As a longtime Star Trek fan, I was excited to dive into Star Trek Resurgence, and I must say, the game did not disappoint! The story is nothing short of fantastic, capturing the essence of the Star Trek universe with intricate plots, compelling characters, and the moral dilemmas we all love.One of the most surprising elements for me was the Quick Time Events (QTE). Usually, I find QTEs to be somewhat lackluster, but in Star Trek Resurgence, they are incredibly immersive and add to the overall experience. They make you feel like you're right in the middle of the action, enhancing the narrative rather than detracting from it.The only downside for me were the stealth sections. Thankfully, there are only a few, but they tend to be quite dull and repetitive. The game often forces you to repeat these stealth sequences three times, which can be frustrating and break the otherwise excellent pacing.Despite this minor flaw, Star Trek Resurgence is a must-play for any Trek fan or anyone looking for a solid story-driven game. The positives far outweigh the negatives, and I highly recommend giving it a try!Engage! 🚀

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far not the most technically masterful game ever created. But this is one hell of a solid Star Trek Experience! Especially for those TNG/DS9 era Fans. The graphics are not Unreal Engine 5 level of detail, but the graphics arn't the worst I've seen in a story driven narrative where choices matter. Especially since there are not many graphically inclined Star Trek experiences like this to compare it to as some of the most iconic experiences in Star Trek gaming are that of the late 2000s, which isn't very graphically impressive nowadays anyways. You meet some very memorable characters in the series, and develop relationships with many crew members. Though, not very easy to understand each crew members feelings and wants, the story is linear enough to make effective choices and see the repercussions based on those choices without being overly punishing, but will still cause you to regret certain choices if not balanced with other choices made prior to support certain crew members. There are some technical woes, but for the price, I think some are overly optimistic expecting too much for a reasonable price point, and doesn't reflect the true passion put into the engaging storyline. FPS is very consistent even with my 2080ti and older 9700k i7 in mid 2024. However, the animation quality is what is causing problems, as what others have mentioned. Though the FPS remains at a locked 60 fps, at least for me. The animations appear to skip or somewhat be animated in a 30-50fps environment. Making some movement jarring, and not as smooth as you would expect at times, but nothing that would take away from the story itself if really vesting time into the story and not necessarily the gameplay.The story is much longer than anticipated too. I figured, for a $20 sale price tag at the time of writing this, I would expect at least 6-8 hours of a single player experience. But in reality I'm looking at over 10 hours and still moving along the developing story. I will update this once I beat my first playthrough.The game is not just a pick and choose dialogue either, there are so many quick time events, it really keeps you engaged and needing to keep your controller or mouse and keyboard at the ready at all times. From simple tasks performing maintenance, to scanning various objects with a tricorder, to navigating various interfaces on ship consoles, flying shuttles, ground battles, and much more. It really is a engaging experience, despite them being overly used at times. Looking past this not so great PC port and some of its technical issues, the story development, choices, and overall setting hit just right for me and I would recommend this to any TNG/DS9 Era Star Trek Fan. Though if you are looking for a Call of Duty or Battlefield level of engagement, you should look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek: Resurgence has flaws. If you are an old school Trekkie, this will invoke all the feelings you had watching TNG and Deep Space 9.The story had me hooked from start to finish, the characters are mostly well written, the voice acting (outside of some background chatter) is amazing.The game gives you choices for things that are completely irrelevent to the gameplay or the story but are badass amazing moments for Trekkies. _childDocuments_.review: Big Trek fan here, but I can't justify the purchase, or really even a playthrough of Resurgence since time is also something I value. Imagine the Tell-Tale adventure game formula applied to a single episode of Star Trek and then STRETCHED out over ten hours. There are so many walking "mini-games" and what I have begun to call "Hatch Work" (Push up on left stick and right trigger to open hatch!"Most of the characters are paper-thin and the plot twists are predictable for anyone who's ever seen the show. The only real thrill I ever felt was pressing "Y" to activate my com badge, and there's a neat space battle at the end where your choices probably don't matter that much.TLDR: Watch it on youtube and save some money. There are way better Star Trek games out there. Try Star Trek Bridge Commander on GOG--it's a trip.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the most immersive Star Trek game of the last 20 years (since Bridge Commander), this game plays out like an interactive season of TNG-era episodes. I really enjoyed this format because you can either binge the whole story in one go or take it slow, playing an episode or two each evening to stretch it out over time.The graphics are... well, they're a bit janky. Some dialogue scenes will have characters slightly out of focus and the framerate is all over the place. It's clearly been developed for console first with PC as an after-thought. That being said, I didn't experience any critical issues or crashes. The game also launched into controller bindings by default despite the fact I didn't have a controller plugged in, but thankfully changing the setting in settings fixed it.I've never played this time of narrative adventure game before and it works really well for capturing the feel of the TV show. Surprisingly it isn't just QTE events for action sequences and you do actually do get to pilot a shuttle, aim/shoot your phaser, etc. it's not the most sophisticated gameplay ever but it's sufficient and doesn't really get in the way too much. The characters feel appropriate and authentic to the Star Trek universe, as if they could have been written for the original TV shows.It was a bit disappointing that the two main characters you control aren’t customizable, but their designs were well done, so I didn’t mind too much.While there are a lot of choices and decisions, the main story is mostly on rails, and I actually liked that. It encourages you to be more authentic with your choices since you won’t end the game prematurely by selecting the wrong option. I made some poor choices early in the game, which ended up being thematic and contributing to the overall character development, making the experience more engaging for me.There’s some replayability in terms of making different choices, but that’s not really for me. I’d love to see a sequel or additional stories/episodes. I was fully immersed in the story and setting, so I was a bit sad when it was all over after just 10 hours. I’m ready to dive back in with a new story or adventure.All in all if you enjoyed TNG, 100% play this game. You will likely enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it's a great experience in the Star Trek universe. If you do enjoy Telltale games and like Star Trek, this game is a good choice.Your important choices do feel impactful. As for any kind of this game, that is if you don't look to close or don't do a second playthrough. In reality, your choices don't really matter that much, it's not a branching story experience, where your choices and failues can have a heavy impact, like for example Detroit Become Human. And a design choice that is even worse... there is a timer running out on your dialog choices. In Telltale games, you character chose to stay silent, when the timer ran out and that did also count as a choice. In Star Trek Resurgance, the timer runs out and... nothing. You are still forced to make a choice and as far as I can tell, there is no negative consequence if you do let the timer run out.The story is great, it fits the Star Trek theme and overall the characters are well written. There are only a few characters that feel off and some of the conflicts do feel forced. Especially one character has a rather special development, where you really start to question how they got to be an officer in Starfleet.Gameplay wise it's nothing special and it's rather the weak spot of the game. The combat and sneaking mechanics are bad and some of the minigames are really frustrating. Especially the one where you have to hold the pointer in the middle and it completely flies away in different directions without any indication. Most of these elements could've been cut from the game completely. The graphics are okay for this kind of game, but the facial animations are a wild ride. Especially Jara seems to be stuck with a critical, raised eyebrow. Maybe she had a stroke and it froze her face...Her need to get some special treatment is only important for a short time in the game and then is completely forgotten. Why is this in the game after all?And now for the worst: In Telltale games, when you finished the story, you were able to see your choices and compare them to the choices other players made. You get this here, too. But for that you have to create an account and then use a unique ID you get at the end of the game. Not only is that a questionable choice, but that site is really bad. You get an overview of what the different characters will do after the story and how your choices impacted them. That's cool, if it would only apply for all. But for most characters it seems like they forgot to track your progress mid-game and you don't get a satisfying conclusion. While you can compare your stats to others, you can't share your results with friends to compare their playthrough with yours. Well, you can, but for every single element you have to share it seperately. This completely sucks and the only explaination I have for that is, that they wanted to force you to register an account. Or they didn't know how to implement it as a feature in the game, because their time ran out and they quickly put up that site. You can do better than that Dramatic Labs / Bruner House!Still, besides these downsides, I can recommend that game, as I mentioned in the first lines of this review.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great interactive story! I really felt immersed in the Star Trek universe. Try out the Demo, and if you like it, buy it and enjoy your life as the new first officer and as an Engineer about the USS Resoulte, switching between the two depending on the scene. I don’t recommend watching YouTube videos with spoilers, because the story is really the only good thing about this game, and if you already know it, I don’t see much point in playing afterwards.However, don’t expect to buy a good game here. If you just want a shooter and don’t care about the story, this is most definitely not the game you seek. Many scenes don’t work technically well, neither with a controller nor with keyboard and mouse. However, I found that it’s a little better with keyboard and mouse than with a controller, especially when you have to aim at something. But the gameplay aspects are not so bad that they hinder you from playing the game. And the story really makes it worthwhile. Expect a few hours of an excellent story where you make the choices about what happens, and then that’s it, afterwards you can uninstall it and have some fond memories of the USS Resolute. I didn’t see too much of a point in replaying the story even though it might change a little with different choices, because as far as I know you can’t skip anything, so would have to play the complete duration again. And since I’m mostly happy with my choices, I have seen what I liked to see.Two points of advice: If you misclicked somewhere, you can exit to the main menu and will lose all progress in the current chapter, thus are able to replay it differently without starting from the absolute beginning. And during choices, when the ‘timer’ is over, it simply waits for your interaction and doesn’t do anything bad.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fabulous narrative firmly rooted in the TNG era Star Trek universe.  The score, on/off ship camera angles (scene framing), and chapter text position and font were all pleasant reminders of the many hallmarks of Trek.  The story was well composed and moved along nicely.  The game is essentially a long form episode.  Because of that you have time to enjoy the character development and all of the aforementioned art direction and voice acting while guiding two main characters through a "choose your own adventure" type of narrative.  There were a couple of places I thought of making a different decision so I'll most likely be playing this again.  Some choices I thought every player would have made but, after the play through, found that only 20 percent of people made the same choice.  The choice analysis and percentages website makes me want to find out what other pathways are available in the story.  The music was very very very good.  Small combo orchestration for the underscore and dialog portions then scaling up to full orchestra to add weight to the action.  This game is emblematic of the TNG, DS9 and Voyager series that made me a fan of Star Trek.  If you like those series or like the pacing and nuanced decisions of Trek; you'll like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you think of ST:R as a game, it's just OK.  If you think of it as a visual novelization of season one of a new Star Trek franchise, it's outstanding.Like every first season of ST, a lot of the dialog is wooden and clunky, and especially in the first few hours has way too many info dumps. It is, however, a classically good Star Trek story, and very well told.The voice acting is good, but not great. Remember that Picard, Riker, and Data were pretty stiff in season one. If they keep the voice actors together for another game/season, I think they'll click.The QTE and timed dialog choices mainly work to keep you engaged, except for the few times when they are an epic fail and pull you out of the story. There should have been a way to bypass them.Art, costume, set design, sound, and camera are absolutely stunning, 10/10. The look and feel of Star Trek has never been captured better in a game. A few scenes gave me that jaw-drop rush that only the very best ST can bring.Technically, it ran like a dream on my mid-range Dell G16 laptop with all the eye candy maxed. I've had zero crashes or tech glitches.Most importantly, I've had a ton of fun playing this. One of my best game buys this year, and one of my best release day buys ever. If you love Star Trek, and are OK with mainly VN gameplay, Resurgence will not disappoint, despite a few clunky game and acting moments.Buy, play, and join me in hoping for a season 2!

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek, a sci-fi franchise that has spanned all aspects of media. From tv shows to cartoons to books and not to mention a few movies. I've played alot of Star Trek games and enjoyed most of them, however "Starfleet Command 3" was a bit mundane and let's not even talk about "Star Trek Infinite Stellaris". Now, with "Resurgence" we come upon another clone. What I mean by this is that if you've played either Mass Effect or Dragons Tale, you've played this game before. The creators basically took all those mechanics that made those games good and applied the Star Trek sticker too them. The story is a recycled TNG episode, they dragged some of the old actors back to give the game some relevance and the whole thing basically boils down to quick action button cues, Superman64 " Conquer the evil rings" Shuttle missions and character's so paper thin, that you can't really have a connection to them. What's with the character design, by the way ? Does everyone in the future walk like the Tin Man from the Wizard of Oz, not to mention one of the protagonists looks like he continues to shrink as the game progresses. In closing, if you're a Star Trek fan, you'll love this game. If you're new to the franchise, this isn't the right door to go through. I'd recommend watching the shows and movies first. As for the game itself, gameplay isn't very good, some parts I want to sleep, other parts I'm frantically moving my mouse so I can get it to aim my phaser properly. The story is a rehashed Star Trek TNG episode, the VA is mediorce with the exception of Piotr Michael who had me searching the cast to make sure I wasn't hearing the ghost of Leonard Nimoy. So, no, I will not recommend this game. It's a gaming gimmick that is about a decade late, with characters that feel meaningless to have any investment in with a story that is predictable.

_childDocuments_.review: It is not very often that I have to rate a game negatively especially after I played it for over 32 hours by now with two whole playthroughs...What really good about this game is the story and the voice actors. If you like Star Trek or if you are even a fan (and maybe if you remember the Tkon episode from TNG) you could easily enjoy the story line with its choices. It is a great setup, environment and you want to know what happens next.But that's already it with the positive things basically all the rest is not good up to horrible (well, maybe except the soundtrack, but at some point it gets annoying, too, and you tune it down):* Biggest upset is the game engine and connected with that the gameplay. It feels like you are in 3D game developed around 2003. For that it would be quite nice and enjoyable. But 20 years later - come on?! It looks sooo outdated, the movement of characters looks just ridiculous, the levels where you do some walking or running are just so poorly designed and rendered. It is almost a joke how bad everything looks but it is rather sad for such a Star Trek game.* You cannot skip any cutscenes or dialogues which is so annoying because also you cannot save the game as you wish. There are some autosave spots of course but they cover way too often too much of a level and if you exit early (or your game crashes) you have to repeat every single dialogue and cutscene because you can't skip any. And for achievement hunting this is also annoying since you need at least two playthroughs to get all achievements. Which is fine and totally OK for such a game...* ...if some achievement weren't broken! Until now there are several achievements which don't trigger even if you do the right thing! Since you can't save manually and can't skip anything you waste a lot of time until you find that out. The forums are full of complaints but no help yet.* Finally, it really feels strange as an "adventure from former members of Telltale Games". The interactive moments often seem so random, all the "walking freely" parts are so annoying and a mood killer because of the bad game engine, the decision making feels less "emotional" than with all previous real Telltale Games. Apparently with every choice you did that influences others in the game you can read a little about that in menu in their character sheet - but only if you pause the game every time and scroll through it! Who does that and how does that help to create an atmosphere? I discovered it by accident since you get no real explanation for that "feature" and you can only see the thoughts of the NPC regarding the last choice. You cannot even read through everything where you interacted with them before.I got the game on sale for 50% less which is kind of fine. The full-price is way too much for that and that sucks. It should have been a nice piece in the Star Trek universe.

_childDocuments_.review: The choice-oriented, dialogue-heavy adventure format popularized by TellTale Games goes like peanut butter with jelly alongside Star Trek's lore-rich exploration of ethics. You can imagine my delight and anxiety when I was offered the opportunity to play and review a standalone choose-your-own-adventure story taking place in this universe. To that end, the game’s publisher, Bruner, was kind enough to give me a key shortly after the game’s Steam release.Growing up, The Next Generation was one of my favorite TV shows. But would the writing and, indeed, voice acting do it justice, or was this to be a dud, bioforming a big-name IP like the villains in its story, all for a quick cash grab? A petty mining dispute between two civilizations, the Hotari and the Alydians, is what kicks off the story, but it’s just a smokescreen for a larger conspiracy whose stakes rise continually as you uncover more and more of the truth. The game borrows the majority of its lore from a TNG Episode (The Last Outpost), but does a great job at expanding it and providing drive and complexity to its villains. The silver screen introduced Jean-Luc Picard and his crew to the vestiges of a fallen empire, The Tkon, as they’re chasing a crew of Ferengi thieves. In the game, we’re introduced to a splinter faction of the Tkon - The Scions of the Flame - who serve as both a foil for the Federation as well as a literary device that explores a classic Star Trek moral quandary: does one species right to exist justify the sacrifice of another? On a fundamental level, the instinct to survive is something anyone can empathize with. What differentiates us is some are willing to cross the moral event horizon to achieve that goal, while others are more mindful of the consequences of their actions.Throughout the 40 chapters that comprise the story, you will alternate between two protagonists. After the game’s credits, we’re introduced to the new first officer of the U.S.S. Resolute, Jara Rydek, whose narrative explores the intricacies of command, making big decisions under pressure and the ramifications of diplomatic work. Then there’s Petty Officer Carter Diaz, a wet-behind-the-ears engineer whose challenges and trials take place in the field but are just as crucial to the plot as Jara’s efforts. Although the majority of the NPCs we meet are original characters, a few familiar faces make an appearance: Spock, Riker and Portal 63 are all integral to solving the central mystery. The voice acting is great overall - the actors playing both the heroes and villains sound convincing and shape engaging and memorable personalities for their characters. Ironically, Jonathan Frakes’ first scene in the game was probably the biggest let-down for me, as you’d expect the biggest name in the cast to deliver something more substantial than a phoned-in non-effort that has the emotional intensity of a text-to-speech conversion. It gets better the second time around, though.The cast is further extended by the crew of the ship - engineers, science and security officers - all of whom have different approaches and values that complicate your decision-making and highlight the paradoxes one encounters when trying to do the right thing. Some losses and catastrophes are unavoidable, of course, but by paying attention to everyone’s worldview and musings you might be able to figure out the most appropriate thing to say so they don’t just quit the job in disgust the first time you open your mouth.The models and animations are, sadly, not as good as the other storytelling tools employed (the voicework and writing does all the heavy lifting here), but their mediocrity isn’t jarring enough to make the experience unpalatable. You won’t have any trouble recognizing any characters or emotions, but the constant eyebrow raising and eyes popping out to show surprise or sadness feel pretty cartoonish after a few hours of robotic responses to emotional rollercoasters and Morton’s Forks.  Most choices and consequences you make are binary, but do a good job of highlighting the story’s overarching themes of sacrifice, perseverance in the face of adversity and the importance of contextual thinking. You’ll lose crewmembers along the way, friends will betray you and enemies will ambush you, but keeping a clear head and sticking to your values will pay off in the end. I was quite impressed with the causality chain in the narrative reflecting the spirit of Star Trek: if you pursue the ‘good’ ending, the story highlights the noblest features of the human spirit in both Jara and Carter. Optimism, diversity, camaraderie - every virtue that the Federation promotes is reflected in the Resolute’s senior staff. Sometimes, you have to make calls that will upset some of them - but more often than not, their sense of duty and commitment to doing the right thing won’t let that get in the way. It’s refreshing to see characters that manage to have volume and personality without becoming caricatures of themselves punish you for your choices, something that quite a few previous titles in the genre are guilty of.There are plenty of nods and references to TNG: General Order 7, the Kobayashi Maru test and Captain Jellico are all mentioned in passing. Carter’s partner in crime, Nili Edsilar, is herself a Trill, albeit one who refused the symbiote, and there is a bit of dialogue exploring the implications of this decision and what you lose by undergoing the procedure. Little nuggets of information are sometimes cleverly written in dialogue or implied (meaning casual watchers won’t feel like they’re missing out on any critical information if they don’t catch them). This also suggests that the developers - part of them former TellTale employees - really understand and resonate with the source material. As expected from the genre, quick-time events are sprinkled throughout and tricorder investigation minigames pad the runtime - not exceedingly so, but they round up the total runtime at ten hours - while the structure and pacing resembles that of a TV show episode. There are a few stealth and shooting sections in the game that don’t add much and are somewhat repetitive, but are easy and short enough to not be a dealbreaker. The narrative structure borrows the parallel narrative format - Jara’s A Story is interwoven with Carter’s B Story, tying up all loose ends and secondary plots by the end and giving definitive answers for both the inner and outer conflicts our heroes have to contend with. There are multiple endings and getting all the achievements will require multiple playthroughs, as there is no chapter select in the game at this point, but if you enjoy the story the first time around you’ll probably be curious enough to see what happens if you go a different way. In the spirit of previous TellTale yarns, these decisions are radical enough sometimes to deprive you of a character, even a senior officer, for the rest of the adventure. Resurgence’s strengths are the characters and story, at the end of the day, and there’s enough juice there to be worth a playthrough or two. While there’s nothing revolutionary or groundbreaking about the plot, it’s a competent and engaging exploration of one of Star Trek’s most popular dilemmas: how far is too far when it comes to saving your kind?

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Must buy if you are a trek fan. If you’re not a trek fan, look at the demo, try it there and then buy it on a sale if you like it.Story: 9/10I enjoyed the conflicts and choices the game presented and how they affected the game. For Jara, as a command officer, her relationships with the bridge crew were important and that made sense. For Carter, I didn't get that feeling. Despite how much I managed to piss Nili and Miranada off, it didn't seem to make a difference.Graphics/Performance: 6/10Decent graphics, but it demanded way too much resources for those graphics. I think it looks like PS3 level stuff (except some scenes with crystal vaults) and has that jank when controlling and moving around. So it amazes me that it runs this bad and has these kinds of requirements. A 5700 GPU minimum? For this quality, that just means this is very poorly optimized. I did have 1-2 crashes during my playthrough, but I guess that’s okay.Gameplay: 7/10Apart from making choices, we have quick time events, puzzles, combat, stealth and exploration. QTEs felt they were designed only for controllers, and KB/M support was an afterthought, though that does not mean it was bad. They definitely were too easy though, which felt like it eliminated the risk factor. Compare that to the easy/hard mode detroit gives, which adds some challenge when you fail QTEs.Puzzles were somewhat fun and lore related like aligning transporter beams etc.Exploration's walk/run speed is very slow and cumbersome. Though I enjoyed messing around with the tricoder and phasers to get around obstacles/puzzles.Stealth is solid, but the janky movement can sometimes be irritating.Combat is just shooting at enemies from cover for sometime while some teammate deals with something else. No real movement. It kinda gets boring after a while but it’s fine.Other thoughts:- Why does it load between scenes so much? There’s a small loading screen (<1 sec) for different cuts of the same scene! That loading screen breaks immersion.- We need a dialogue skip option. Either skipping to the next section or to the next choice. Also a history tab would be nice with records of the previous conversations/choices we have made so far.- It took me around 11-12 hours to finish my playthrough. I played one hour of the demo, bought the game and then finished it. -The demo definitely sold it for me.- Make save points clear and explicit. Give options to load from saves so that I don’t have to replay the entire game.- The facial expressions (especially the eyebrow raises) sometimes go into the uncanny valley.For a new studio’s first game, this is very well done. I definitely enjoyed 10 out of 12 hours I played, the other 2 hours felt like busy work. I’m hoping to enjoy more of their games. For potential buyers, you will enjoy this game. Now the only question you need to ask yourself is whether the current price is worth the 10-12 hours of enjoyment you will get from it. If not, wait for a sale! But you will enjoy it.For the devs, all I would say is that either focus on your brilliant writing and remove gimmicks of combat/stealth from the games (which would make it less enticing to some people) or polish those features up. And please add some quality of life features mentioned above to this or the next games that you create.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this review saying that I am a huge fan of Star Trek TNG, especially the exploration aspects and the crew interactions. I am also a big fan of space exploration in general. As far as choice-driven visual novel-type games are concerned, my review history should prove that it is one of my favourite genres in gaming. I played The Expanse's choice-driven adventure a few months ago and adored it, pretty much completing it in a single day. So in summary,  should be perfect for me. But after playing an hour and restarting twice (more on that below), I feel the amount of jank in this is intolerable.Here are my issues:- What bothered me right away was the technical subpar-ness of the game. Even though I have a strong hardware and at 4K the FPS counter says 150 (which is still quite low for what is actually shown on screen, showing that performance optimization was not a concern during development), I cannot help but feel like cutscenes are running at 20-30 fps because the character movement is so choppy.- Playing with controller, the game's menu only shows keyboard and mouse controls for its help. Not such a big deal, but the controls are also decidedly using Xbox button layouts. What is this? 2010?- Speaking of controls, the game controls so far have been exceptionally poor. RT is used for primary actions, why? Why is the cursor moving at snail's pace in those little QTE-like scenes? Why is there QTE in a 2024 story-driven game anyway?- The game does not tell you when it saves (or if it saves). In the beginning, when I tried different resolutions (to see if that fixes the choppiness, which it doesn't), I had to replay the first five minutes because the auto-save didn't save until some indeterminant point later.Overall, a disappointment. I hope there will be a number of patches to address these and possibly other issues I haven't seen yet, as I am in principle still interested in the story.

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing you have to understand about this is that it isn't a game. It's a choose your own adventure story. It simply happens to be a fairly *good* choose your own adventure story. That gets somewhat polarizing because it doesn't even really pretend to be a game; for some of you, that will of course make it worse, but in a weird way I respect that? The long and short of that is that if you're not interested in cosplaying as a Starfleet officer by occasionally pushing a button for 10-15 hours, this isn't for oyu.So first, the story: it's solid if you're a trek fan. I will say that it starts stronger than it closes, but I would also confidently say that the whole of it is better than any season of Picard (yes, including season 3 even though season 1 was actually better) or Discovery. For most of the game, I was completely able to believe these were Starfleet officers acting professionally. The game also kicks off with your ship being sent to mediate a labor dispute between two species that is threatening to break into an all-out war instead of dumping you right into Galaxy Defining Stakes, so it gets credit for that. While the stakes are, ultimately, raised, it also does a better job of making those stakes feel real than most Galaxy Defining Stakes. The last act does go somewhat overboard, but it's not so overboard that you roll your eyes at the threat, and there are several choices that remind you what Starfleet stands for sprinkled in. I think the last quarter of the game could've been condensed a little, but it's not quite dragged out. I also played this in one sitting, so it keeps you engaged.The character work is mostly solid. I think the player characters are both well-defined, and while I can't be sure, I think that's more than just me making their decisions for them because both of them, especially Diaz, have very characteristic reasoning and traits. The crew feel real most of the time. There are a couple of major exceptions to this (one major opinion drop late in the game shouldn't have the weight it does, for example, while some minor members of the crew feel like promoted extras who were given significance for little to no reason but still feel like they were meant to be important even if they aren't, while one bridge officer is just given no interactions with you at all after the very start of the game but is still treated as equal to the other two) but overall I think some of the complaints about the bridge crew that I saw during some quick googling after finishing the game (principally about ) are easily explained and not hugely atypical of characters we see in the classic franchise (). The aliens from the two cultures you mediate for are also generally well-characterized. Well, actually the species themselves are a little caricaturish, but the *representatives* of those species (each side winds up with one major character) are both great and improve their cultures by existing. I also feel like the first main character was supposed to be a Bajoran until they decided to add the deuterium plot point, but that's a small thing. I'm also skeptical, after a single playthrough, how much impact your choices *actually* have on the game, but most of them are impactful enough on the character making them that they hit for me anyway. For example, the game's opinion system for NPCs didn't seem to have...almost any effect on the actual dialogue for several characters, but the effect that it had on *me* was measurable, because the Vulcan Chief Engineer being sick of my ♥♥♥♥ and giving off red frames every time I talk to him, but then cracking and showing a sad respect with a green frame when I solemnly acknowledge my duty instead of bemoaning my circumstances? The game just generated a whole-ass character arc by changing the color of an NPC's portrait frame, and maybe that's me placing way too much importance on that but it worked.And now with the thing the "game" is doing out of the way, we can discuss the "gameplay." It's bad guys. Real bad. As I said, this is a choose-your-own-adventure with occasional minigames. The problem is that those minigames are lame, repetitive, and ported badly. For some reason almost all of them reduce your mouse sensitivity to a snail's pace, and it makes several of them incredibly frustrating. The graphics are also...not great. There are occasional random framerate drops, which I'm confident are not my machine since it's a solid gaming machine I bought less than a month ago. The camera, in its attempts to "help" you focus on your story objective or the direction you have to go, will sometimes angle weirdly and either make it oddly difficult to get to the thing it's pointing you at or just show you the nearby wall. The game's "run" function is best described as a light trot and is often not available when it would be most useful. Most importantly for the kind of game this is, your exploration is very limited, which can sometimes feel a little railroady. The only sections where this is a video game are the *very* occasional phaser fights, and even then it's a minigame from an offbrand theme park simulator that came out 15 years ago. And I guess that's to be expected. It's difficult to make good Star Trek and a good game at the same time, because many of the things that make good gameplay are the things that make bad Star Trek. As a Starfleet officer, you should be negotiating and exploring more often than you're fighting, and neither of those things has heavy replayability or a particularly engaging play pattern, especially without procedural generation. As such a game where you actually *feel* like a Starfleet officer, like this one, is probably almost always going to lean on the story to make up for the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cautious recommendation.The writing of this game does successfully feel like you are making the big decisions in a star trek two-parter. The stakes are appropriately high, and character motivations are interesting and highly varied. That said, at times choices can feel misleading. For instance  Maybe that's on me, but I feel that should be made clearer in the dialogue.That said, this game seems to be shoddily assembled, and at times frankly rushed. Be it clearly unfinished or glitched animations, random fatal errors, or an apparent lack of willingness or understanding on how to optimize shaders for a wide variety of hardware. This game absolutely chugs on a steam deck anytime there is a transparent shader on screen (a known issue with unreal engine that has well known workarounds), which is wild to me! I have pretty good hardware on my desktop pc and even there the game seems to suffer. The most impressive was when the final cutscene had a "fatal error" of an unknown variety that reloading the scene helped with, suggesting something akin to a memory leak or bad garbage collection.And on the topic of the game being rushed, it is about an hour and a half too long. There are whole scenes that do little to advance the plot and offer almost no interesting gameplay. A lot of the shooting gallery scenes come to mind. I recommend playing on Story difficulty to avoid redoing certain scenes that to me feel as if they were designed to fill time. There are some egregious examples of time-wastey level design as well, including a storage room where you can see the console you need to interact with right in front of you, but oh oops the crates have fallen in a specific way where you have to walk the entire circumference of the room to reach something right in front of you. There is nothing else to look at or do, just walk around crates for a minute or two. Additionally, there is a teleporter maze that you just have to guess on. Mazes are famously the most time-wastey and unfun kind of level design and it's kind of embarrassing for them to have included one in a game that is already _this_ long.All that said however, the game is still enjoyable. It is a strong recommend for long time star trek fans, especially if you are familiar with the common tropes of an episode and the relationship between the crew and the captain/first officer. They fumble the lore a _teensy_ bit, mostly with visual stuff (that is not a raktajino cup, dammit!) but those are easily forgivable things in the scale of the story and breadth of character interactions. If I had to pick a number for scoring, it's a 67/100. Pretty fun and engaging, with some unfortunate drawbacks.

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs some serious optimisation. It is without a doubt the worst optimised game I've played in YEARS.I was hoping this would be a great steam deck game but with lows around 10fps and highs of mid 20s it's not really playable. (720p lowest settings possible)This doesn't look like a particularly graphically intensive game and yet the frame rate, even on a decent pc is awful.Gameplay wise it looks like it would be great, but 10fps at 720p on a steamdeck is pretty abysmal.  That's IF you can call it "gameplay" there isn't really a game. The lack of performance or graphic fidelity (it looks like arse most of the time, particularly character's hair) I cannot.It feels like that was the interns first game and they hadn't yet learned how Unreal works nor anything regarding performance tuning.
