_childDocuments_.review: Do you like 90s Star Trek?  Do you like narrative, decision-RPG type games?  Buy this.If you've played Life is Strange, it's like that, only in Star Trek.  It's not really a "game", it is more like an interactive movie.  The developers have perfectly captured the look and feel of post-DS9 (post Nemesis, pre-ST:Picard) Starfleet.  The story also fits perfectly into that era of Trek.  It's honestly better than some episodes.  It's obvious the devs have a true passion for the source material.  It feels they also took some ques from Lower Decks as well.Voice acting and music are great.  Art is good--the textures and effects look more last-gen but not bad exactly, to me anyway.  The animations aren't quite so great.  They are stiff or not fluid enough to make them entirely realistic.  But that's not really important for this kind of game.  (I have the same critique about Life is Strange--except it was worse there since the lip sync...didn't.)As others have pointed out, the game does suffer from some graphical hiccups and glitches, but it didn't impact my play-through.  Your experience may vary based on your computer.The control could be better.  You will want to play this using a controller, but it feels sluggish and I don't think you can change it.  I started with keyboard and mouse for all but 2 minutes when it said I had to press number 1, 2, or 3 for picking choices.  The controls work as you'd expect, and you use various combinations of the joysticks and triggers to do quick actions that appear on the screen.  The choices have a timer bar but you don't necessarily have to select a choice within that time.  There were times I let it run down for dialog choices, but it paused the game and went to grayscale until I picked a choice.  I do not know if this is always the case.  Other times, if it's an action-based decision, I'm guessing different things happen if you miss the button press that appears on the screen in time.  That happened a couple of times to me.The weakest part of the game was the combat system.  It works, but it's a bit clumsy.  It's basically a rail-shooter.  I had to replay these segments a few times, but fortunately, they are not long segments and a failure doesn't put you back very far as even longer combat scenes are divided up into smaller parts.All-in-all, as definitely being in the target audience, I'd give this 4.5 of 5 stars.  They could expand this type of game with more open-ended levels where you can explore a bit rather than being almost entirely scripted and linear.I am not sure how consequential your decisions are.  When you make a decision, sometimes it will affect your reputation--good or bad--with another character.  So those relationships would be affected, but what impact that actually has, I'm not sure without another playthrough.  I will give them credit for given you decisions that feel they have actual weight and that you know will make one person happy and another mad so it can be a conflicting choice to make.  But as to how consequential each one is, I'm not sure.From the credits, it looks like a skeleton crew put this together, and half of that was writing staff so I'd have to say it's a good product considering that.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal! Star Trek: Resurgence for the PC is an absolute triumph in the realm of interactive storytelling. The game brilliantly captures the essence of the beloved Star Trek universe, offering an experience that feels both nostalgic and refreshingly new.From the moment you start, you are thrust into a captivating narrative that is rich with intricate plot-lines, well-developed characters, and the ethical dilemmas that have always been at the heart of Star Trek. The storytelling is nothing short of masterful, seamlessly blending action, drama, and exploration. Each decision you make feels meaningful, impacting the story in ways that keep you thoroughly engaged and eager to see what happens next.The developers have done an incredible job in creating a visually stunning game that stays true to the aesthetic of Star Trek while incorporating modern graphics that enhance the overall experience. The voice acting is top-notch, bringing each character to life in a way that feels authentic and compelling.What truly sets Star Trek: Resurgence apart is its ability to immerse you in a story that feels genuinely connected to the Star Trek universe. Whether you're a long-time fan or new to the series, the game provides a deeply satisfying experience that honors the legacy of Star Trek while pushing the boundaries of interactive storytelling.This is a must-play for any fan of narrative-driven games. It’s an exemplary showcase of how powerful storytelling can be in the gaming medium. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly and surprisingly fantastic, what more Star Trek (and a LOT of other IP-based games) should be. Let's start with the cons though but please read the pros and don't just stop at the cons.Cons: * its is not AAA art. The scenes / ships are a bit blocky like games 10 years ago, the characters look great (mostly) but hit some weird animation poses with their shoulders hunched forward and dangling arms s they walk, special effects are certainly not at what most game engines could easily produce with some love* some choices are unclear until you click them and you have to restart the section to change them* the rogue-like saves keeps you from going back which.... I get it as a design choice to keep you moving, I know why some games like that, but it just annoys me. My life keeps me busy and I don't have time to explore a game more then once - so I want to be able to re-load a bit back so that one playthrough can be my 'best' playthrough - the memory I take away from the game. Its a me thing and I don't get why its not an option* fixed characters - I like the characters, a lot. And what they were helped make the plot work. But I constantly kept feeling how I'd wished this had been 'my' character instead of 'this' characterPros:* the plot is fantastic - it really felt like playing through a movie, with interesting twists, cameos (that didn't take over from the player's story), a well-fleshed plotline... I'd happily re-watch my playthrough as a movie* actual choices - even though it plays as a movie, you do get constant regular choices, they all 'feel' meaningful, and most Are meaningful* quick-time events + real-time action - I'm not huge on quick-time event stuff but it seriously works with this game - it keeps everything feeling cinematic, while making you feel you have choices and are 'doing something', and keeping you engaged with the screen. the combat's not 'hard' either but similarly - just enough to ramp up the feel of 'action' while keeping you in a story experience. You don't go into 30 minute combats or mini-games only to completely forget what you were doing there / lose all the built up energy of the plot* dialog - it was seriously good. again, I could feel this being a regular season of below-decks or early star-trek (the great days). was it always perfect... nothing ever is, but it was very well doneIt might sound like I have a short list of pros but I think these pros pretty much cover the entire experience - the whole experience 'felt' good. Its a game I (someone who plays games of all types all the time) enjoyed, and a game I will hand off to my partner (who is totally a fluffy casual) without feeling like she'll tune it out.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very easy to grade this game on a curve and say that, for the budget it's a good game. And that's true, Dramatic Labs have done a lot with a clearly limited budget.But that does the game a disservice, I think. It's a fantastic piece of Star Trek fiction in its own right, arguably better than some of the modern TV incarnations in fact. If there isn't a sequel in the works, that would be a crime, frankly.It's not perfect though, and if you want to hear the negatives, here you go: the Telltale legacy is apparent for good and ill - you get a lot of choices that feel like they might matter, but the moment to moment gameplay can be a little restrictive and simple. It has inconsistent performance, wonkily juddering between 60 and 30fps seemingly at random. The mouse controls can be sluggish and heavy at times, and the prompts defaulted to gamepad even though I didn't have one plugged in (though it does switch on the fly after you remind me if you're on a keyboard and mouse).But honestly, this is a compelling bit of Star Trek that will appeal to anyone who has a soft spot for the TNG era, and none of those problems detract from that in any significant way.Good job, devs :)

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the story. What an ending! Some of the best recent Star Trek. Can we have more?I will start to say that this is an adventure game, it is tagged as such on the Steam page, it is also in the game description. It is not an action game, so any mention of gameplay is not really relevant. It's like saying that Detroit: Become Human is not a good lootet shooter. Completely different genres.As an adventure game, the important part is the story and the choices you make and I am pretty hooked.It has dilemmas, diplomacy, science/engineering rabbit holes to get into and so on.Anyway, if you like TNG, DS 9, Voyager or Strange New Worlds, this game is for you. Also if this were an episode from one of those series, it would be one of the better ones.I found myself caring for the characters. They are well voice acted too.It works on the Steam deck, by the way.There are some cons, although not many. Sometimes you think you are given a neutral choice but it turns out it isn't that way. You can't skip cut scenes you have already seen. A couple of times I found myself not agreeing with the solutions of the characters, and here and there you find some artificial problem that has been created to make it difficult for Starfleet's technology to operate, which, like in the TV shows, might feel a bit forced. There is one particular type of minigame that I don't like where you have to center your mouse inside a circle. The early ones are easier, but the later ones are annoying to line up (EDIT: this was a PC bug that got fixed.)Those moments aren't many though.Overall I recommend this, if you are into adventure games, like Star Trek and want to be a pivotal part of an episode in this universe.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Well...a proper, story driven Star Trek Game. So many tried, so many failed. This right here is amazing. Story wise, the setting, the sounds, the soundtrack, the characters, the decisions and all the other "little" things that immerse you in to the Star Trek universe...it's all there. Granted, there are some drawbacks, it lacks polishing, the graphics and animations sometimes feel quite clunky and rudimentary and while the idea behind the interactions is great, it isn't really optimized for gaming with a mouse and a keyboard - still, you can absolutely feel, that the priority was the story and i absolutely applaud Dramatic Labs for that decision. I hope they can make another one with a bit more budget. Some antialiasing would be great, 120 Hz and so on. Oh - and UWQHD support would be amazing. But overall, i feel like this is a very good start to a hopeful long line of Star Trek Decision making games.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game. I expected this to be a slog, something along the lines of LOTR: Gollem; a game featuring the source material but making an absolute mockery of it. What I got was the opposite. The game feels like a Star Trek episode. Real Trek. There's engineering sections, where you need to realign EPS conduits and reconfigure isolinear chips, alongside even higher stakes objectives. There's science, research, away missions. The primary focus is the bread and butter of Star Trek: diplomatic liaisons. The characters introduced are compelling and interesting, giving the opportunity to reflect real Starfleet values while maintaining the TellTale-esque dialogue options to ruin it all. Voice acting wonderful, story engaging and exciting and surprising, all in all a fantastic game. The only downside was it can get a little bit "phasery" now and again, but it's a game, so if anything all it does is sometimes become a bit more like a Trek movie than a Trek episode. But those sequences are few and far between, and really aren't so bad. I truly wish these devs make more Star Trek games. They totally, totally understand the world and machinations of Roddenberry's world, so much so that I would not be against them writing Trek for television. Nilesy

And I can say with confidence that this game captures the true Star Trek spirit! _childDocuments_.review: A must play for any Star Trek (especially TNG/DS9) fan. Yes, the graphics are quite dated (especially certain graphic effects during cutscenes, and unstable framerate, a rather unoptimsed control scheme for mouse+keyboard), there is a graphic glitch every now and then, but other than that the game really captures the Star Trek spirit quite well, and the voice acting is really on a high level (especially Spock), and a wonderful legacy guest appearance by . Also yes, there is quite a lot to nitpick, both on the technical/gameplay side as well as some of the story side, but this game gives an old Trekker like me hope...We definetely need more proper Star Trek games, and this one is definetely worth its price.PS: Now the developers have added Steam Achievements!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a hard core Star Trek fan, literally I have seen every episode for TOS, TNG, DS9, VOY, ENT & LD at least once.(Picard, still watching, and DISCO......season 1, reading summaries of the rest was enough, we don't talk of DISCO.)Played the demo for all of 30 min before I was hooked.Even in that short amount of time I felt at home. Felt like TNG-era that we know and love.Game wise....it felt like the old school Elite Force 2 mixed with Telltales, shaken up and mixed and cooled in the fridge over night for a refreshing new story that stays honest and true to the lore, no political or diversity compliance BS to push an agenda and ruin the story.So after 30 min, I pulled the trigger and bought the full game.Why?I feel the characters and can make the story mine, and I don't care what race they are Woman, Man, Hispanic, Alien. This is how you do it!And a nice surprise, and I stress this, beyond the demo, I came into this clean, so I had no idea what to expect.At one point in the game and the thing that slapped me in the face Spock.SPOCK! It sounds like him.I'm broken.If you are a Star Trek fan, and have been itching for something fresh, both for the franchise and for a game, then allow me to say this in the best way possible so you can understand how badly you need to play this."Come to Quark's! Quark's is Fun! Come right Now! Don't walk, RUN!"

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of Star Trek and of Telltale-like choice and story based games this game is a slam dunk. It feels so incredibly like a Multi-part Star Trek episode that its hard to believe that is isn't. While I do have some complaints. they are all minor, and are things that can certainly be improved on in the hopefully inevitable sequel. While I wish it didn't take this long to come to steam. the journey is worth it a hundredfold. And I can't wait to see where this team goes boldly nextMy only major complaints are that some of the graphics and setdrops feel like they just pasted a PNG graphic onto a block and called it a day. so that is one aspect that I wish they could improve upon if there is a sequelThe other major complaints is a slow of QOL (quality of life) changes. the mouse speed when doing certain actions in the QTE's is so slow that you sometimes can hardly get the mouse to where it needs to be in time. the mouse feels like its moving through mollasses. and there is absolutely no way to change that. Similarly some of the QTE actions need to be tweaked and reworked. A common QTE action that you will see is when the game will have you try to keep your mouse cursor inside a small circle while the game is trying to force the mouse outside of the circle. these would not be too bad. but the way it ultimately works out is that you have to have a very large mousepad. and space on your desk to do these as even being outside the circle for a short moment to re-adjust your mouse can sometimes completely reset your progressI also had issues with button presses not being registered. or where the game seemed to want me to react so inhumanly quickly it was just an exercise in frustrationIf these minor issues are resolved this game will easily be a solid 8/10 for me. but right now I will have to give it a 7/10

_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: To any fan of Star Trek, I couldn't recommend this more. The game feels absolutely like it was made by fans for fans, in the best of ways. Star Trek: Resurgence is far from perfect, but it has fulfilled the vision I have had since childhood of what a Star Trek game should be like, more than anything else I have seen. The story genuinely captures the feel of Star Trek, the characters and plot aren't all perfect but they're well written enough to have made it into actual Trek canon, and at times when in the intensity of the plot it all comes together and feels as though you've stepped within an actual episode of Trek. If you're not a Trek fan, but still loved the Telltale style of storytelling, I'd still recommend it, but you may not be as blown away by it, I can't say for sure- maybe wait for a sale in that case.The gameplay is similar to what one would expect from ye olde Telltale, but with some improvements. Combat was very simplistic but challenging enough to not feel like a glorified quicktime event. It won't be for everyone, the graphics are mediocre and it somehow brutalizes a pc despite not really having a lot going on (could have cooked an egg on mine), but personally I couldn't stop playing from the moment I started the demo, to the point that I bought the game within minutes of finishing said demo, and ran through the full game in a weekend like a starving man at an all you can eat buffet. And I know it won't be the last time I play either.This was a fantastic ride from start to finish and I know I'll be replaying it again soon. I really hope there's more of this in the future, ideally sequels or other trek games, but I'll be keeping my eye out for any other new projects from Dramatic Labs too!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: A genuinely enjoyable story, which managed to hold my attention through out. If you like Star Trek, you will love this. It takes everything that made the shows engaging and turns the volume up. As someone who loved the shows, I might be bias, but I believe people who aren't Star Trek fans but like shows like The Expanse would find something here too.As for the game, there's the odd glitch but nothing major and while it does support ultra wide resolutions it isn't full screen, rather a window within that screen. It didn't effect my experience though.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: If you like TNG/DS9/VOY style Star Trek and Lower Decks, you'll love this game! The story so far follows two characters, alternating between them: the ship's XO and a Lower Decks engineering geek. At the start I was having severe performance issues, but manually editing the INI to bring the graphics quality down a notch fixed that. (Note to devs: add those graphics quality controls to the interface please!)
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek: Resurgence is clearly made by a group of folks who understand and love Star Trek! It's the closest I've come to feeling like I'm "in" an actual Trek episode from the TNG/DS9/VOY era. The decisions presented in the game are great -- often you're presented with several options, all of which a real Star Trek character might plausibly make!  (And NOT just simple and obvious character archetype analogue choices, i.e. "rule follower" vs "maverick.") Highly, highly recommended for Star Trek fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Not for everybody but one of better Star Trek games. Definitely reflects spirit of the franchise which is rare and like fresh breeze for ST fans. Small cons: - reaction on controls feels forcefuly slowed down- graphics is not great (which is really not an issue, but definitely something that could be improved)
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: The game is solid - its worth experiencing at least once and it has its moments. Personally I think it has too much of key Star Trek events in it at once if something - I would probably wanted more smaller episodes that are more grounded - its sometimes thrilling too much I would say. What are problematic parts is optimalization (works on SteamDeck but its best to put on low especially if using external monitor 1920x1080 in my case else it stutters a lot which degrades visuals but I was fine with that), some options not developed enough (the core story is very much set in its path and most branching seems only temporary or not really having effect on key ending events. Some slight spoilers: , I do also not appretiate the only romance present in the game  Some other stuff is sometimes also a bit weird and sometimes it feels like devs run out of resources before doing everything they wanted with this game. Considering all the subsequent playtroughts are not that enjoyable at least for me (especially as there is no skip dialog button sadly) which is also a bit sad because you want to experience different paths in games like that usually.Hopefully we will get more one day with some of those problems learned from and fixed. Overall Im happy this exists - I would like to see remaster of that old interactive movie with Q and borgs to this format also thinking about it (it came in wrong age for me and I saw only YT videos from that).
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek written for adults is back!Yes, the graphics and the rest of the game engine is clunky, but in this genre it's the story and the script that count. It doesn't surprise me one bit that it's the former Telltale crew that put the Star Trek back into Star Trek. Neither from the latest brainless Hollywood action movies nor from the tv shows that want to shove certain political and social views down our throats. The writing is truly in the thought-provoking style of The Next Generation era that aims to show, not tell. I applaud the team's efforts and will eagerly wait for more!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from me who hasn't played a good single player Star Trek game in a long time, this was great fun to play. This is my first narrative-driven adventure game.Pros: Great story, character interactions and dilemmas to choose during conversations and critical plot points during the game. While the ending isn't really changed that much depending on your choices, it is more about the journey based on those interactions and how characters interact and perceive you based on your choices. Cons: Graphics, character models and animations feel a bit dated for today. Controls felt slow and sluggish even with sensitivity set to maximum. But these sections and quick time events were few enough and spaced out enough it didn't ruin the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: If you can look past the low budget, and honestly bad game/graphic design, it is genuinely a great experience. This game was made by people who actually care about the franchise they are adapting, so the heart and soul is there. Great story, and an even better Star Trek experience, couldn't recommend any more!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it. It's a Star Trek choose-your-own conversation with QTEs, and if you can accept that then it hits the Star Trek vibes really well. I'd happily play a (star trek) sequel to this or purchase DLC. At the start I was hoping for slightly more mission choices (this is a single long story), but it was entertaining - I played straight through over three days. Graphics and sound were fine for me. Voice-overs great. Character writing is good for most part (you'll like some and hate others). The directing/scene composition was really good.Minor bad parts: There's no choice of when to save and no skipping, so if you get interrupted you'll just have to replay a whole chapter (hey devs: we're not all 16 years old with unlimited time any more). The mouse controls suck (mostly too insensitive, occasionally very sensitive), the walking/running toggles are erratic, the rails shooter sections are painful and I'd happily get rid of them. The "choices" website no longer functions. There's a major mechanic about how people react to your choices (you're told constantly if people liked or disliked what you just said), but nothing seems to come of it?
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek is uniquely well suited for this style of "choose your own adventure" game which relies heavily on story, character building, and tough choices weighing differing morality and principles against each other. The game puts you right into a quality Star Trek episode and you decide to uphold the values of 90s trek or go a little darker. It takes its time building your attatchments to charactors so when your choices cause death or injury, it really leaves an impact.I do feel the animation budget could have been doubled, but it was incredibly enjoyable even with the 2010's quality graphics. I would buy every game in a whole series of these. I know they had origionally planned on making more but I believe plans were changed when initial sales weren't at expected numbers. I put that up to the insane 1 year epic games store exlusivity agreement limiting its reach at release hype. I really really hope they make more. This was clearly a labor of love and it shows. It filled this trekies soul with happiness enough to make me pour money into  buying episode after episode if they would only make it for me.If you like Star Trek, buy it. You wont regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: “Star Trek Resurgence” beams us into the familiar universe with a narrative that feels like a love letter to fans of the series. The game’s storytelling prowess shines like a beacon in the vastness of space, capturing the essence of what makes Star Trek so enduring. Hearing the iconic voices of Spock and Captain Riker is a treat that tugs at the heartstrings of nostalgia, providing a sense of continuity and depth to the Star Trek saga.However, the game’s technical execution doesn’t always match the grandeur of its narrative. Audio inconsistencies, such as varying background echoes, can momentarily pull players out of the immersive experience, reminding them that they are, indeed, in a game rather than on the bridge of a starship. This aspect of audio engineering and direction could have used a finer touch to maintain the illusion of the Star Trek reality.Graphically, the game doesn’t quite hit warp speed. While the character models and environments are crafted with care, there’s a sense that the graphics and interactiveness could be dialed up a notch to truly do justice to the rich and detailed Star Trek universe. Players might find themselves yearning for more engagement and a deeper connection with the world around them.In conclusion, “Star Trek Resurgence” offers an AMAZING Star Trek story that will undoubtedly resonate with fans. It’s a journey worth taking for the narrative alone, despite the hiccups in audio and visual fidelity. For those who have longed to explore strange new worlds and seek out new life and new civilizations, this game is a testament to the spirit of Star Trek and the adventures that await in the final frontier. Live Long and Prosper 🖖
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: A faithful interactive game, that adds personal choices to the well scripted, crafted and creative TV style episodes.   Gameplay and environments are simple, if not a little clumsy.   Animations are borderline 'snicker worthy' ( characters run like robby robot ).   Yet even so, the quality and style seems appropriate given how low budget some of the earlier original TV series were.   What they lacked in CGI back then, they made up for with creative, deep storylines.   The same is true here.  In short, the game has character, is engaging, and well worth the ride.   Enjoy and recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent Star Trek story for those who are interested in that kind of thing. This is more of a movie you choose the outcomes of, but its engaging enough to make you feel invested in it. Don't know how non star trek fans would enjoy this, but definitely have been having a blast as a big TNG fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: More of this! I love the Star Trek universe and this game FINALLY makes me feel like I am in an episode of Star Trek TNG. I don't need to control entire fleets and empires...just want to feel like I am in the realm of Star Trek and this game delivers that.  A bit clunky at times but solid story line and gameplay overall, especially for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Prepare to boldly go where no Star Trek game has gone before! Star Trek: Resurgence's TNG-style story features all of the Trek conventions you could possibly hope for: interpersonal conflicts, no-win scenarios, technobabble, phaser firefights, Spock, tricorders, away missions, and of course caves. Anyone who claims to be a Trekkie should put aside ~10 hours and experience this magnificent game.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: I 100% enjoyed this game, even though it is basically an interactive movie mini-series. Comparing this to other Star Trek games and I'll admit it is way better than anything out currently. A real Trekkie or even someone who enjoyed the TNG/DS9/VOL series will really appreciate and love this game. The real sense of belonging to a crew is well created here. Kudos to everyone involved. It is clunky and some sound is off but it doesn't really take away from game play. Updates should fix these issues. DLCs of different missions in the future would be great. I really miss the TV shows. There are no wrong decisions to make really.  PERSONAL WISH LIST: I wish that someone would actually make a modern version of Star Trek Bridge Commander along these lines with an open environment. While I thoroughly enjoy the shoot-em up aspect of all Star Trek games I would also like a game that allow the player to simply explore the galaxy, do supply runs, medical evacs, new alien encounters, diplomacy tasking, traditional character/species conflicts and resolutions, and of course a Borg encounter or two etc, etc. What would it actually feel like to leave Star Fleet Academy as an Ensign and work your way up to Captain and command your own vessel?   Good luck everyone.Live Long and Prosper.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: As a TNG uber fan in my formative years - this game really hit the spot for me.  Now - the gameplay is all quicktime events and occasional key presses - it's a telltale game in all but logo...BUT...but...it just feels like next generation star trek.  The plot is great and the voicework is also top notch.  It's a star trek interactive novel, really, but a bloody good one.  Recommended!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: (Steam Deck Review)Stop reading reviews and play the demo already! Quite simply this is a 10-hour interactive story. The demo covers the first hour and will give you a taste for the story and an indication of how it will run on your hardware. I found the story compelling ... like a really good book you just "can't put down" ... and played it entirely on the Steam Deck. The performance was horrible (and this is after an update in June that was to improved Deck performance specifically). Reducing the graphics settings didn't help performance much and just made it look horrible too. So, I endured the poor performance on normal settings because I was just that hooked on the story and characters. The voice acting and even facial expressions sells the story quite well.I could maybe argue some of the interactions (minigames) were repetitive ... but then again it could just be that I was sucked into the story got tired of it being "interrupted" to do things!The only reason this isn't a "10" for me is the poor performance on the Deck ... so a "buy on sale" in my opinion. All-in-all the devs nailed the story ... if they can improve the execution/performance I would dearly love to see more from them!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a pretty big Star Trek fan and had no idea this game even released. That said, the writing is SO GOOD. Dan Martin, Andrew Grant, and Kevin Bruner really nailed every single beat of a strong The Next Generation episode (think seasons 4-5, moody, practical, emotionally shifting, and FUN). I'd probably not recommend this game to too many non-ST fans, but surely anyone who has seen a few episodes or simply likes Sci-Fi would have a great experience even without knowing all of the call-backs.I'm playing M & K, so the puzzles seem even easier than other people claim. That said, Resurgence is much more akin to watching a massively entertaining, serialized TNG spin-off. Coming from a small first-game team that probably started development in the immediate post-pandemic, there are definitely some seams in character animation and scene transitions. I felt them to be jarring a few times, but not enough to dampen my enjoyment of the show. Or game. Whatever.Solid A! Thanks, Dramatic Labs, for pushing out some quality adult ST content! Can't wait to see what this dev does next!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a Star Trek fan and/or a Telltale Games fan, then this is a game for you.  It feels like a long episode of Star Trek from TNG era (technically set just after that).  It takes a one-off episode of TNG and creates a spin off that is absolutely fantastic.  The game is fairly short (I finished it in 13 hours), but it's probably good for 2 or even 3 playthroughs for those who want to see every possibility.  You get to play from two perspectives: the ship's new first officer and one of the petty officers down in Engineering.  This dual point-of-view storytelling serves the game extremely well.  And that is the strength of the game: story.  To be honest, the weaker parts of the game are the times when you have to do things.  (Walk over there and activate that console.  Phaser the dudes trying to get into the room.  Etc.)  The game truly shines with its dialogue and decision-making mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Man this was such a breath of fresh air. A game that was written the way Gene Roddenberry had always envisioned Star Trek, not like the utter garbage Alex Kurtzman has been spewing over the years.Like others already mentioned, graphics are not top notch but they are okay. The story is really great, the voice acting is outstanding (was pleasantly surprised to hear the one and only , Elias Toufexis and Liam O'brien).In terms of gameplay, it's pretty simple: choices really matter, you get directional prompts a lot to complete "action" sequences, there are scenes where you fire a phaser and where you scan with a tricorder. Can't say that there are puzzles in this game, it's more of how you handle situations and the choices you make.Overall, as a trekkie, I enjoyed the hell out of it. I can't even imagine how this game is like for someone who never watched Star Trek. I grew up with TNG so I loved every minute of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game which whizzes along keeping you engaged from one activity to the next. Set up like a TellTale game, you will perform varied easy tasks to help the story along, authentically simulating the kind of effortless techno wizardry every Starfleet crewmember displays in the course of their daily tasks.  Hold down W to push the Transport sliders forward...Press direction keys to swap isolinear chips from one slot to another, that sort of thing.The story feels like the good old Trek we remember, set somewhere around the Enterprise E era, and you will get to do all sorts of things from shootouts to repairs, piloting shuttles, aligning sensors, doing the difficult beamouts under stressful conditions, scanning with your Tricorder...All the Trek things you love.  As I say the tasks are not overly demanding, but it allows a number of crewmembers to all team up rather than have one main character be Mega-heroic and do everything themselves.Featuring a pretty fair Nimoy impersonation, the crew are otherwise all new, and well voice acted.  Occasional jerkiness or robotic character models aside, the graphics are fine and dandy, I'm having a great time.  Looks overall about the same as Star Trek online, but it is actually fun to play.  Would definitely buy a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Weak story telling with very predictable twists and tries to make you care about characters without building their character.Choices are pretty much "pepsi or coke"Jank controls.  Literally 3-4 full sweeps of my mouse pad to make cursor move to correct spot.Woke bullsh*t.  A dialog choice is "Diversity is our strength"Doesn't hold a candle to Walking Dead Season 1 by Telltale Games
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: If you can get past the quality of the graphic, this is one of the best star trek story's to come outside of STO. Pros:Impactful choices, decisions made early on affect late gameBelievable dialog- felt as though i was in star fleetEngaging environment - Especially the minigames, some of those were really difficult.Story Length, 10+ hours of pure space gallivanting. Cons:Graphic Quality- looks like a 2010 gameSome Weird Character DevelopmentOn the note of Character Development, I wanted to add that two thing really bugged me here. Carter Love interest doesn't feel believable, almost as an after thought.And there are decisions that you make as Jara that put some fo the crew members, a group of seasoned professionals, too much in their feelings. Some of the interpersonal confrontations, save for the captain, were really not necessary and took away from the story.SummaryI Gave the game a 7 out a 10 for wonderful story but low quality graphics and for the reasons above.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Need more Trek! Everyone please buy at full price and show the devs some love. We need more of these. The story is very well done. The choices feel like they matter. The characters feel real and the game sticks to canon and expands upon it. It is like choose your own adventure within a strange new worlds or next-gen season. There is a lot more I would mention but I don't want to spoil anything. Buy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very fun game. Sure, like all Star Trek Games, it has it's quirks. It has some very challenging calls to make, and you need to balance competing interests... either from the Captain, Chief Engineer, or other senior staff.It pulls in aspects of and characters from other ST series and episodes, including TOS, TNG, and Voyager, which really made playing it enjoyable. Getting to see the same story as two main characters was an interesting choice, but I think it really added something extra as you get to see the decisions being made and the result of them. There are some very tough decisions to be made, as the First Officer. In-game people will live and die by some of them, including your crew.There were a few graphical glitches I experienced and some scenes could be better optimized as they were a bit janky. The interface on the mini-games was quirky at times, and the stealth missions had a few frustrating moments. The last patch did fix a few of the issues for me, but not all of them.Overall the story, and getting to be a First Officer _and_ a Petty Officer in Engineering gave an interesting take on experiencing life in Star Trek world. And then once you complete the game, you can go to their website and see your decisions, how it compares to other real life players, and what your officers _really_ thought of you. And yes, they can very much not like you, depending on your decision.I'd suggest NOT using a walkthrough the first time you play it. Be the Star Trek officer and non-commissioned member that you want to be. If you want all the achievements you'll need to do at least two playthroughs.I'd definitely be interested if they released another game, or even a sequel, as there's lots of room to continue it.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Such a nice little Star Trek game, albeit with some problems/weaknesses. And yes, it's not Elite Force (2) or Starfleet Academy, but it's also not a full-price game with a big studio/publisher behind it. And you know when you read ex-Telltale that you're more likely to have to get involved with a story with few branches and alternatives. But if you can/want to do that, it's a nice story with some nice characters, but unfortunately also some who act strangely in context and simply needed more screen time to get involved with them. Some things seem to have been ticked off too quickly due to the short playing time, especially when it comes to the relationships between the characters. Potential was wasted there.Pros:- Decisions do have consequences that are also shown in the game. All in all, the consequences are relatively small, but still.- The game respects the good old TNG/DS/Voyager era and fits in perfectly.- The story focuses on the essentials, you are not distracted by countless side lines to waste playing time. Nevertheless, the story could have been a bit longer or expanded with more character interaction.- Finally a Star Trek game againCons:- The mouse and keyboard controls are quite suboptimal, especially the mouse is very sluggish in the mini-games when selecting points...- No free saving, only 3 save slots. Annoying, if you want to see an important decision the other way around shortly before the end of the game, you theoretically have to play again for about 9 hours (or save the game beforehand and copy it back afterwards)- Why the hell do so many developers think it's a good ideato sacrifice the main character or one of the main characters at the endso that players can't build a bond and might want to buy a follow-up game...Unfortunately, I just bought it and played it on vacation. One playthrough takes about 11 hours - and I did 2 playthroughs in 2 days. I enjoyed it and would like to see more.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great Star Trek game that really captures the essence of the prime timeline series, excluding Picard and Discovery. Making the best choices I could in my first playthrough, everything played out more or less as I'd expected it would in any series of the show. The characters were all identifiable and well acted. The choice consequences had real weight and impact to them. I hope for a second 'season' of this crew, I'd actually even want a series or at least novels of their continued adventures. It's clear the writers had a real sense of everything that makes the 'Trek Universe' feel right. However, it's not all nominally running plasma conduits and EPS relays. Some of the animations are stiff, janky, odd and out of place. While this is true of many narrative driven games, the quality in other parts makes it more jarring than usual. The marionette like stiffness makes the crew - at times - seem more like dolls than human beings. While other times, they're incredibly lifelike. I feel like more baking on this title to really sort out these animations would've served it better in the end. Furthermore, the optimization is terrible at times dropping to 15 or 20 fps from a solid (and what should remain a solid) 100fps on my system. This too causes some jarring moments that take me out of the immersiveness of the world.And some textures were rather low resolution and muddy and the point light on the main character you're playing as, is often just outright visible. Looking like Navi from Zelda. Finally, there were loose ends in the story that didn't get tied up and leave it rife for a sequel. I don't want to spoil the BIG one, but I would like to know what happened to the 'survivors' of the big event and if certain people were able to be....reconstituted as themselves.Still, these issues weren't enough to take away from the narrative experience. I will surely play the other branching paths at some point and hope to enjoy further adventures in some medium or another of these characters on this ship.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically a very long choose-your-own adventure Star Trek movie.  What's not to love?  Well, the gameplay mechanics, when you're not driving the dialog, are a little hokey at times.  In the middle of many cutscenes you'll be prompted to press a button, or move the stick in a particular direction, in order to advance... sometimes failing to do this in time can result in game over.  I'm not a fan of this.  But this is not the reason to play this game.The voice acting, writing and plot are all top tier.  It's "true" to the orginal Star Trek TNG ethos and has the technobabble, ethical quandaries and the opportunity for the characters to uphold Star Fleet morals and ideals (or not) in spades.  Wonderful.I'm 8 hours in, haven't finished yet, but loving this game so far.  It scratches my Star Trek itch in a very satisfying way.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: I love Star Trek and this game totally fits into the universe. As someone who watched the shows you never got to see how a tricorder actually worked. Thanks to this game you are actually able to use it! You do all the stuff an engineer on a starfleet ship does and it's so much fun. Some choices are very tough though. Due to all the loss and betrayal you might finish the game with some hard feelings.Don't cry, you can replay and see that your choices don't change so much after all. Just don't ever befriend Lieutenant Bedrosian. It's not worth it. Trust me!However, this game is not made for keyboard + mouse. Very frustrating at times, had to scroll for ages to reach the desired areas. I still wish this studio would publish some more games ASAP!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good entry, but needs improvements. The Ability to save in the middle of a chapter is needed, or an ability to skip ahead. Also mouse controls needs adjustment as the sensitivity is not the great. The story and setting is good, but needs to help under the hood. But you can power through it for the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Found the demo for this purely by chance while browsing, and after playing just that brief little sample, I was already hooked. My first time playing a Telltale RPG was back around 2012 when The Walking Dead came out, and I'm glad to see that type of interactive environment still exists. Granted, games like Life Is Strange and Tell Me Why had a similar mechanic where your choices impact the game and the people around you, but Resurgence has one thing Dontnod didn't have: Star Trek. I've been a huge fan of the show since the early to mid-1990s, when I got to watch TNG and eventually Voyager on the local UPN broadcast. I just want to say that this game is a perfect marriage of Telltale-style storytelling to the Trek universe, and I am absolutely loving it. The only real complaint I have is with the movement systems, as the animation seems to be slightly clunky, especially when sprinting. Other than that, I DEFINITELY recommend this game for any and all Trek fans on steam, whether you've been around since TOS, TNG, or at any point in the franchise's history.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun story with a lot of references to make Star Trek fans happy. Kept me engaged and rooting for the characters throughout and the choices I made had impact by the end of the story. Not for people that want challenging puzzles or complex mechanics but was a great choose your own adventure video game that took me a shade under 10 hours to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: As a lifelong Star Trek fan, all I'll say on this is if the team make a follow up (can easily be in a different era with a different crew - although I did love the characters in this one!) - I would buy it on day one.  It isn't perfect from a technical PoV, but it's understandable given the small team and that can be built on and improved. In terms of hitting the tone of the TNG era, it is bang on. Dramatic Labs - make another!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: If only the Star Trek on TV would be this good!Now, the game has its issues. It is a bit janky, from technical perspective not impressive at all, passable, barely. However, that´s not why you play games like this. If you ever liked any Telltale games, this is right up there with the best of them. The story is engaging, characters are well written even if at times stereotypical (but well, it is a StarTrek game). Choices are present and the minigames are fun. You can see that a lot of love went into this and I would really like to see more!Live long and prosper
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: The first time a Star Trek game has felt like real Star Trek. An amazing story and great characters, drama, action and Federation diplomacy. This game is an incredible experience as the story unfolds and some of the decisions where very difficult to make, Rarely has a video game story sparked such emotions in me, I wish I were more Vulcan for some of them. _childDocuments_.review: Review in short, for Trek fans: It's a good game, it's worth the asking price. The OST is great too, buying the Captain's edition isn't a bad idea. It's £4.50 extra only, I think that's worth it. Review at length:This is PEAK Star Trek. It's got the all-important *vibes* from the music and all the sound effects, the silly technobabble to the relatively light-hearted "both sides in the conflict are equally dubious" style of writing from TNG. When they say this was produced by Trekkies, I absolutely believe it. And the writing is good too, it's got both Trek style and substance. When fans make a game, there is often the problem of missing the forest for the trees and with ALL the focus being on just vibes and fan service, but as far as narrative quality goes that's not an issue here. Voice acting is also good, for the most part anyway. Where the forest DID get somewhat lost for the trees, though, is in the game's technical aspects. This game's performance suuuuuuucks. It looks like a PS3 game, but whenever anything more intense than a character sitting down and emoting the framerate tanks below 60, I've seen it go below 20 in graphically intense scenes. My machine isn't divine but it isn't a potato either, so this is a little disappointing for a game that reminds me of Mass Effect 2 in terms of graphics. Overall the technical faults of the game do not at all overshadow the quality of the narrative. Again, this is absolutely PEAK Star Trek. Must-buy if you're a fan of the franchise, imo. I will say that the asking price becomes a LITTLE hard to justify if you are not familiar with the Star Trek franchise, considering this is a largely linear interactive-movie style game with *very* questionable performance. But lucky you, there's a free demo for you to enjoy. I highly recommend you try it, and then decide for yourself. And if you find yourself enamoured with the franchise afterward, I recommend you go watch the Star Trek TV series The Next Generation, Deep Space 9, Strange New Worlds, and Voyager, in that order :)
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, any trek lover will enjoy the hell out of this.The passion for trek is in every design choice, its fantastic and a wonderful way to tell a story.I feel that perhaps it could have benefited from a bit more dev time as it has a wide spectrum of graphical quality and a few simple things that really let it down in the technical or QA department. _childDocuments_.review: I'll start off with some context:I love classic Star Trek up to and including the mistreated and underrated Enterprise. I've been re-watching all of TNG, DS9, VOY and ENT on a loop for many years (TOS not so much to be honest). How Trek got butchered and eroded after ENT deeply saddens me. With each iteration being worse and more insulting than the last (save for Strange New Worlds which was a glimmer of hope but nowhere near as good as the classics).That being said, I had a blast playing through Resurgence. If only for taking me back to a time when Star Trek didn't suck. This game's story and style would've fit right in between DS9 and VOY as a movie or mini series. And it also ties back into a TNG episode and features Ambassador Spock and Captain Riker, which is a nice bit of fan service. So, if you can relate to anything I've written so far, I strongly recommend giving Resurgence a try.This game isn't perfect though. It doesn't seem well optimized and there are no graphics settings other than resolution. While I had no real issues running the game on an RTX 3070, I could tell some scenes where taxing on my GPU. The visual quality is also quite uneven, ranging from really good to quite atrocious (what's wrong with some of those ugly space scenes!?).The lack of a way to skip dialog (at least on controller) may prove quite painful, especially on repeat playthroughs.You should also be aware that this game is basically an interactive movie with mini games, so don't expect the most elaborate gameplay.I also felt that the story went a little too far out there towards the end. And some characters (especially the bridge crew) weren't as fleshed out and well written as they should've been.Despite its issues, Resurgence for me represents the best, most authentic Star Trek experience since Enterprise. I'm struggling to understand how a small indie game studio manages to succeed where the big players keep failing so miserably. But if this is the only format capable of giving us fans what we want in our Star Trek, I'm onboard. Please, give us more like this!

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite a good Star Trek game.  The graphics are a little hinky, and the space for tracked choices is narrower than it first appears, but the story is excellent. Warning, however: you *could* describe this game as a series of QuickTime Events, and it wouldn't be that far wrong.  At one point in the gaming industry, that would have been a death sentence for sales.  If you still loathe QTEs, you will probably be horrified by Resurgence.   But if you don't care about QTEs or don't really know what they are, you'll probably have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Star Trek fan ever since I wasn't even a teen, I thoroughly enjoyed this game. It isn't an action shooter, it didn't have the budget that most popular games today have, and I believe it did the absolute best it could as a star trek story game for the purpose of being a story game. The story itself is the main reason to pick up the game, it's extremely unique and it pulls you in instantly. The characters feel like real people, with real motives, ambitions, and struggles (with some exceptions with out of character moments to drive the player to act immorally, but it didn't happen that much). The stakes feel real, and with every decision you make, it has a lasting outcome with the further story. It's faithful Star Trek universe and it's to the source material. I also really like that they didn't rely on big name voice actors or rely too heavily on nostalgia baiting. _childDocuments_.review: This is a great episode of star trek, or maybe a Star Trek movie even. I can't say it's a great video game. A good one, but not great.The story pretty good, very classic Star Trek IMO. No notes :)The writing is competent and engaging. Most characters feel fleshed out and like they have a backstory.Of the 2 player characters: Carter feels a bit more alive than Jara. He just has more energy and seems to have more to say about the situations he's in. It is very cool to play as a first officer as Jara, though, having to make quick, tough decisions in various degrees of danger.The gameplay is very simple, reminiscent of older Telltale Games style. Telltale Games has since evolved their mechanics beyond this, though. This game feels like it was developed 10 years ago. That's not necessarily a bad thing, it just might not meet your expectations. I did feel like my choices mattered, but not as much as I was wanting. This style is best suited for story telling. Like the telltale games, the combat is rare and simplistic. I did like There are a multitude of glitches and oddities. I got stuck several times due to bugs (I think most of them were due to using a high frame rate). At one point, I thought I'd have to completely restart because a game breaking glitch kept occurring until it randomly decided not to. They did fix one issue with an update, but the fact that it got through speaks to the QA (or lack thereof) at the game studio. And I've yet to see any additional updates addressing the other issues I faced.The graphics are weird. There are very few options and cracking open the config file gives you only a few more. The anti-aliasing is just about the worst I've seen from a modern game. I can't explain it, it just looks really bad, especially around small details. The depth-of-field effect looks okay for the most part (you have the usual issues like transparent textures looking like panes of glass, or an object having a blurry ring around it). But some scenes are just completely out of focus! Like a BOTW movie that was shot on camera in the 80s! I've never, ever seen that in a game and it completely breaks the immersion. Especially in cut scenes where a character is revealing or reacting to something.The animation is bizarre. It's as if they used 3 different game engines bodged together. Some animations run at a forced 24 fps. This would be okay as a stylistic choice (wanting to look cinematic), but it's completely inconsistent. It's not that cut scenes are 24 fps and everything else is whatever your GPU can muster (some games do this, and while it's not my preference, it is a legitimate creative choice). It's like some objects/characters were animated at a forced 24 fps, some at forced 60 fps, and some actually use tweening (allowing them to look smooth at higher frame rates). Several different objects can have these 3 different frame rates at the same time on screen! There are some action scenes with a lot going on and you can see the different rates all going at once all over the place. Sometimes a character (even the player) will suddenly switch from buttery smooth animation to a choppy 24 fps for movement and back again for the next. For example, when you're in combat, your character can do a roll from one cover to another. But this roll animation is at 24fps! So it feels like your character suddenly turns into a flip-book. Everything else in the scene is at 60 or at >120, so it sticks out and breaks one's concentration. I have never seen this, it's completely weird and distracting. There are examples of lower fps being used for stylistic choice (Spider-Man: Miles Morales, for example) or for performance (several Nintendo games), but these are done in a way that makes sense!The textures range from very good looking in some places to looking slapped together and crappy in others. There is very little consistency of quality. I prefer consistency to fidelity. I don't mind simplistic textures if I know that's what to expect throughout. Outer Wilds did this excellently. I never once thought about the textures as I was playing even though they were low fidelity because it was consistent.Another indication of poor QA: the subtitles had several typos and mismatches with the speech. It's not a big deal, but couldn't they pay someone to just play the game and check that? How much would that have cost?I bet most people won't care too much about the various issues I listed above. They basically come down to a lack of polish and incompetent QA. Which is why I am recommending this. But I would like to see those game-breaking glitches addressed...If you like Star Trek, you will probably enjoy the story & the characters. If you're not a fan you might still like it's telltale gameplay mechanics and its isolated story (you do not need to know anything about Star Trek to understand everything that's happening, you may just miss a reference here or there).
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: The story is fine, but from a technical standpoint this is another dumpster fire of a PC port.The graphical settings are almost non-existent. There are only resolution, brightness, full screen and motion blur settings. The FPS is capped at 60 and apparently there is no ultrawide support, for the people who care about those. The graphics are ridiculously low quality for a 2023 release, and there's no reasonable explanation for why they need a Geforce 1080 at minimum. I'd even argue that the non-character graphics and special effects(i.e. space ships, space stations, the skybox, etc) are actually worse than Star Trek Online, a 14 year old game. The facial animations are also ridiculous, they're all over exaggerated and feel like they came straight out of a late 2000's Dreamworks movie.The keyboard/mouse controls are also extremely clumsy, so much so that I felt pretty much forced to use my controller.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, after a year waiting for it to arrive on steam, we get a Star Trek themed Telltale game and its alright, just alright.Story was great like most of the other Telltale games but the rest of the game was just a let down, quite frequent poor performance with only sensitivity and audio not a single graphic option at all and the game is capped at 62 fps.Subtitles would often either display the wrong dialogue or just not appear at all. The graphical quality was all over the place, the game will show you a really nice shot and right next to these high resolution textures will be some incredibly low resolution assets and textures. Gameplay wasn't great just click here or press W and click there, typical adventure game stuff but when it comes round to combat its god awful, just cover based on rails where you defend allies and shoot the bad people away.As much as I'd like to say that I want more games like this, I just can't. While I did enjoy the story Its kind of disappointing how badly this game turned out visually and gameplay wise and to have waiting a year just for that really sucks.Feels like they spent 80% of their budget on the brand and big actors and then had to use a ton of unreal assets to make most of the game, saw the default unreal skybox a couple times and the game over screen looks like something you'd see in an asset flip complete with the default unreal font and it appearing so suddenly after failing.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll say this upfront, obviously I'm a Trekkie and therefore my opinion when it comes to Star Trek: Resurgence can be seen as a little biased. That being said, this game is excellent.The story is great and it proves there is still much potential and room for storytelling in the established Star Trek universe which made this old Trekkie quite happy, because I have said so for years.The game also proves that it is not necessarily required to throw in well known characters to establish a new crew and new faces, although I must admit that throwing Spock and Riker into the mix was a good idea in the context of the game as it added additional flavor to it.This brings me to the voice acting of this game which is really great and it adds a lot to bringing all the characters alive. The voice actor for Spock, Piotr Michael, in paticular did an outstanding job and can not be praised high enough for his amazing work. Other than that, the graphics do look a bit dated and the animations of the characters could have been better, but overall this did not keep me from enjoying the story for what it is. This is great Star Trek and I wish there would be more of it.And the best part of it all is, you can enjoy this game even without any prior knowledge about the Star Trek universe, because it is not required to get good entertainment out of this game.So, congrats to the devs for developing this nice piece of gaming history and...May you live long and prosper. (Hopefully to develop more games like this. ;-))

_childDocuments_.review: No spoilers.Fan of Star Trek ? That's a game for you.It's a "Telltale games" kind of game, expect spicy choices but not a lot of action. I'd even say the "action" sequences are the weakest part of the game. - Good Star Trek storywriting- Technobable through the roof- Lore-accurate, everything is canon and makes sense- Fan service with popular characters appearances- Choices are well-written, predictable and respect the  of you choice : If the option says "I'm sorry", that's pretty much what the character will say.- Choices have consequences you can feel through the whole game. Every cinematic feels important.- The "hold balance" QTEs are fun- Choices follow the ethics and lore of Star Trek: If you sound like Starfleet, you are Starfleet.- Time for choices is well-balanced: long enough to think, short enough to press the action.- Characters are internally coherent and their reaction is predictable if you get to know them well enough.- Game is stable and "plug-and-play": I did not have to fiddle with the graphics/options to have a good experience.- It takes ~10 hours to finish you first run, good runtime. - Bad "combat" sequences: too short, aim is funky and controls are very limited- Bad "flying" sequences: too long, the ship goes way too slow and they are too easy, to the point they feel like filler- Frustrating Quick Time Events: Sensitivity varies from QTE to QTE, one time you just point and click, the other time, your DPI is put at 1 and you have to flick your mouse accross the desk multiples times in order to succeed.- Graphics are all over the place: you can have a wonderful, well-lit scene followed by a close portrait shot with aliasing on the edges.- Few graphical bugs ruined my immersion: assets loading 0.25 sec late, random FPS drops.As a Trekkie that love Star Trek for the ethics, the philosophy and the rapid decisions from heroic characters, I loved this game.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Yup, that's star trek alright. Couldn't be more star trek if it tried. The good, the bad, and the ugly.First the actual game, you’ll understand why later.Didn't expect much from a telltale inspired game when it comes to mechanics, so it really didn't detract from the experience. However, I am surprised the devs haven't learned ANYTHING about how to improve the gameplay since then. If they have, I think I get where they're at. They’re stuck in a "should we add all these new mechanics and risk making the game a lot harder" type of situation. They risk alienating people who just want a casual story and game with minimal input, but that's what options menus are for. I’m not sure how to make the more tedious minigames any more fun but, the stealth sections could easily be expanded on. Add new paths, alternate routes, more aware/threatening enemies, more distractions, sudden curveballs like enemies emerging from a doorway, disguises (we have that technology guys), and for Q’s sake stop making being detected an instant reset. Do something interesting, like turning it into a combat section instead. I’m not saying make MGS or Splinter Cell, but add a little more variety, and then just add a difficulty setting. I’m not dense, I know the devs have considered stuff like this early in development. I understand how time management, cost, experience, etc, factor into making a game, but come on TWD came out 12 years ago!Same thing applies to “combat”.. This is what I mean when I say it has the bad of trek too. The combat is pretty faithful to the shows, too faithful. It consists of very silly peeking out of cover with phasers, nothing to protect yourself other than cover, and clicking a button to stun something. This is where they shoulda just said “nah we ain’t staying faithful to the shows” and gave us a true gun and armor. “But it’s a science vessel, they don’t need guns or heavy armor!” Counterpoint, VOYAGER. Counterpoint 2, Strange New Worlds.  Again, not asking for rainbow six vegas or something here, just more engaging combat. (mostly spoiler free)  Fortunately, the bulk of the game consists of story and cutscenes, NOT gameplay. In short, they took an episode of TNG that was otherwise boring, and expanded upon it so much now that I’m personally taking it as canon. Whether or not it has long reaching implications in universe is entirely based on your decisions, in my save, they do. However, decisions are honestly pretty tame most of the game. You can’t really make many “bad” decisions in this game except maybe a few. It’s really not all that surprising since you’re an experienced first officer, not fresh outta the academy for half of the game. The only unfortunate side effect is that it’s still star trek, so I had the story figured out at the literal FIRST MAJOR DECISION you make. I also tried to make decisions based not on what I would have personally chosen all the time, but what I think the characters you play as would have chosen. There’s not much more to add without spoilers. It’s just good star trek.As for the graphics and world, they’re good where it matters, bad where it doesn’t. They nailed, and I mean nailed perfectly the world of trek. It looks, no, bleeds trek in its visuals and set design, even if some of the assets look store bought. This was either created by huge fans of trek, or by people who did a LOOOOOT of research. My only gripe is those awful animations. I know animating is really really hard; I used to do it as a hobby and gave up. For most of the game, it’s not bad enough to pull you out of the story, except maybe those cover roll animations. Lol, lmao even on those. But for a game that’s mostly cutscenes and story, I expected a bit better than what we got.Idk, it’s just good trek. Less like TNG with its insanely high highs, and borderline falling asleep lows. More like voyager, consistently good, but with no true peaks or dips. Yeah I  throw that in there, I prefer voyager for that reason. Don’t fight me on that, you won’t win. Ego stroking aside, this is just a good trek game. The bar wasn’t that high to begin with, but I won’t let that detract from the passion that was put into this game. And for 12$? Hey, that ain’t too bad!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Finally got the game on steam too, though I have completed it before. The game doesn't come without its faults. Mechanically its janky, clunky, awkward. Dialogue sometimes glitches out, doesn't match subtitles or some words are left unspoken. Puzzles with a mouse and a keyboard are slightly confusing and especially a chore when you have to point somewhere in a puzzle with a mouse. The graphics and the game itself feels like anything before 2010 but I didn't put crazy expectations for a telltale-like game, because in the end it is more about the story than shiny pixels.The story, on the other hand, is phenomenal, for a trekkie at least. The characters are fleshed out, the main plot is captivating and has its unexpected turns, ship battle scenes are exciting and the whole feel of old school Star Trek is strong. I finished the game in one sitting and it felt like watching  one long good Star Trek movie with a VIP seat. Switch between the main characters was organic, the player was involved just enough to ride the flow of the story and have his moments. If you like telltale games and want to experience the original Star Trek world, this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Yea ok so... the engine is definitely first gen more than next gen. The character animations are often more than a little clunky. _childDocuments_.review: I am very happy to give this Star trek Story game the thumbs up. Keeping in mind the storytelling, lore and general quality of Star trek games we got of late, I was quite skeptical about this one, and I am glad to have been proven wrong.The GOOD:1. A unique Star trek feeling - unlike most games, you control two crew members - one from the bridge and one from the lower decks. The dichotomy of being a Commander of the Centaur-Class starship "Resolute" and a petty officer in engineering is shown perfectly.2. A genuine Star trek feeling - the story focuses on the people, just like a good star trek episode does. Unlike most surface level games, this one provides a deep-dive in almost every main character's backstory, motivations and modus operadi. This is what every Star trek fan loves to see.3. A Fan of Star Trek feeling - lots of Star trek games of late assumed that by throwing some memberberries or letting you shoot phasers, command fleets and fly starships isthe true Star trek experience. Well it is not. There needs to be some basis and motivation behind all this, and this game captures it perfectly. And yes, you will still fire phasers, give orders to fire photon torpedoes, fly shuttles, engage in firefights, be in stealth situations - all that Star trek goodness - and you will know why you are doing it and will have a clear idea in mind what your own motivations are.4. A true choices matter Star trek feeling - your choices matter and will keep biting you in the butt throughout the entire story. Crew members will point out when you mistreated or took advantage of their loyalty, you will get reprimanded if you conducted yourself poorly, and more often than not, will be in the thick of it, wondering whose feelings are going to get hurt this time, while trying to uphold the best principles of Starfleet. And yes... people under your command will live or die based on what your decisions are. If that wasn't enough - not being decisive enough and trying to wiggle your way out of situations will blow up in your face, as the developers have thought of that - don't be surprised if crewmen point out your mistakes or have a very "resolute"... pun intended I guess, opinion of your actions based on whom you supported.5. While this is a story game, it actually lends itself to multiple playthroughs - will you be a good first officer and have your crew's back to the end? Or will you have to do the most difficult part of the Commander's exam and send someone to their death? Yes that happens in the game - and this time not in the holodeck...THE BAD:1. First thing you need to get past is the stuttering at times and some janky graphics. As an old-style gamer, I couldn't care less about this - for me everything was just fine, but it may put off newer players.2. While choices matter is a good thing, I more often than not felt that I am some babysitter, having to consider everyone's fee-fees. We are in a do or die war situation dude... You can go meet the ship's Councillor later and talk how you were mistreated by your superiors, or why it wasn't your time to get a pip.3. The quick time events are kinda ok, but I wasn't sure if they were merited enough to be in the game. Quite honestly, if the story cinematic just went on I wouldn't have a problem with it.Conclusion:A game worth experiencing if you are Star Trek TNG/DS9 series type of fan. A lot of what made those series good - deep story, complex motivations, mystery, actions, tough choices - is in this game.  At over 11 hours per playthrough, I consider this story game a great success, as there is more than enough meat on the bone to sink your teeth in. As a lifelong Star trek fan, I am giving it my heartfelt recommendation. Now time to play through it again as an absolute selfish unlikable First officer and see what happens...

_childDocuments_.review: One day I want the writing crew of Tell-Tale to have the budget of, say, Skyrim.When it comes to writing characters you care about there is no one better in the business. All the little nuances of tone, the deep personalities, the body language and small expressions that sell you on a PERSON is here in spades. There are some problems on a technical level. Graphics are pretty rudimentary, there's some glitches that might take you out of the experience (wobbly backgrounds, floating characters, shadows that fail to load...etc) and there is some melodrama more akin to a soap opera than a sci-fi show at times, but that unique Tell-Tale style is back and hasn't lost the immersion factor which made me buy and love their whole catalogue back in the day.The Tell-Tale problems are still here though, although none of it eclipses such a lovingly told story tribute to classic Trek shining like Trek hasn't shown in years. The quick time events are pointless or annoying mostly. It's hard to think what could be done instead but it's jarring to go from thoughtful dialogue to THINK FAST button prompts. The choices are often pretty arbitrary or just flavor. Again the writing is so good you won't notice but usually you'll have three of roughly the same option to say, just shading your response rather than changing your destiny too much. Usually a major failure just means the game ends, not a new path, but there's a substantial story here you might get wrapped up in and it is nice to have the option to speak your mind rather than take the 'logical' option sometimes.Apart from say Cyberpunk I haven't felt this sucked into a story because I wanted to hear the next statement from the characters, I wanted to explore THEM as much as the plot or the world around me.And for classic Trek there is no finer more faithful example out there. The props, the sets, the uniforms, it's all rendered with care and full of not just in-jokes but full on accurate lore statements that make it clear the creators are fans. If you can handle some technical problems, this is still a voyage worth taking.
