_childDocuments_.review: Listen...this game has it's fair share of bugs and it would've been nice to see a system to revisit choices without needing to go through the entire campaign again......but, this is a great medium for a Star Trek game. Moral choices are at the heart of every episode of Star Trek, so putting you in the Captain's Chair truly feels like the spirit of Star Trek. I bought this game because I definitely want to see more of these, potentially episodic like TellTale.It's worth a buy if you're a fan of Star Trek or like this style of choices matter storytelling.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable experience, one of the best Star Trek experiences you'll find to date. This is much closer to an interactive movie over a traditional game (with mechanics), and while the feeling of choice is there in some situations, I would not say it's fully deterministic from my understanding at each decision moment. Having said that, there are genuinely a few branching paths which create different endings and outcomes, so an opportunity for a second or third play for those looking. All in all, I was captivated by the story, decent character development with a few twists along the way. This is a great experience, and I wish the studio and dev team can springboard off this into many more episodic experiences. With more time and money, we could start to explore an even deeper and compelling experience that the fans have been desperate for, for decades.Great release for a new studio with veteran devs, glad to see some of you were able to find your feet again after TellTale Games.

_childDocuments_.review: just finished my first play through and i gotta say i loved it! the story was fun and compelling and felt just like a TNG story arc and it blended seamlessly into the Star Trek universe. The characters were interesting (even if their facial expressions were reminiscent of Mass Effect's funny faces) and they influenced and reacted to the decisions i made in a meaningful way. Speaking of, I very much enjoyed the decision making and the "choices effect outcome" play style, it made everything more immersive as I found myself second guessing which decision was the right way to go on a couple occasions and then praising or kicking myself later when that decision was touched upon. The Bridge crew/Lower decks back and forth was different but gave the game a more well rounded feeling and made it clear that the bridge crew are not the only ones on the ship (something that is barely touched on in the shows, excluding STLD).  The graphics and mechanics, however, leave a lot to be desired as they aren't the best, and could have used a little more work. The graphics are flat, lacking dimension and almost cartoon-y, effects such as explosions and fire are poor at best and could have been much better. Mechanically the game is trash, the interaction games and how their difficulty and appearance (when they show up not how they look) are seemingly random is quite bothersome and the corridor like progression took a lot away from what the game could have had in terms of playability. Do not get me started on the how bad the Phasers and Tricorders are to use. over all... 7 out of 10. definitely a fun game to play but it could have been better, i hope someone makes another Star Trek game in the future and uses all the good things in this game and fixes all the bad. it could be a 10 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, as a massive Star Trek fan (especially TNG), I was really looking forward to this coming out. And because it's ST, I didn't need to play the demo first as I knew I'd love it, right? Wrong.This isn't a game; it's basically one huge cutscene with the odd button clicking thrown in and therefore it's frankly boring. The graphics are pretty good, especially the space scenes and the reproduction of the ship and it's systems, and the characters. However, there is a noticeable stutter (framerate drop) on most of the cutscenes (ie 90% of the game). This is annoying at first, then gets as tedious as the gameplay after half an hour or so. The gameplay is largely non-existent. Basically, watch a long and drawn out cutscene; press a button to give your opinion (don't worry, it doesn't really seem to affect anything) and if you're lucky (or unlucky depending on your point of view) you get to press some key combinations like D and Mouse Button Left to open a hatch in one of the countless ridiculous mini-games. Do you want to decide where to go, plot the course and fly to the destination yourself? Sorry, not possible. Do you want to attack some Romulans? Nope sorry. Do you want to pick your away team and transport down and solve mysteries like the old ST games? You're out of luck I'm afraid. All you're allowed to do is what the game tells you to do and you're doing little more than confirming the next cutscene with limited and simple  interactions. Finally - the characters. You play as a First Officer (there are 3 other Commanders on the bridge by the way - the phrase "too many Chiefs..." springs to mind) who is as dull as dishwater. You also randomly jump over to Engineering to play as an unknown "Petty Officer" (they used to be just crewmen in the series) who has a little more personality than the woman, but only just. The other characters are purposefully 'unique' but other than the Captain, I honestly couldn't care less about them. At one point I mis-clicked on one of the mini-games and blew the ship up, and I was actually pleased. Please try the demo before committing!

_childDocuments_.review: To preface my views, and in spite of the negative review I am about to convey, it's worth noting that due to my immense admiration of the franchise, I did find some enjoyment within certain aspects of the game.Star Trek Resurgence offers a rare opportunity to immerse oneself within a new interactive Star Trek experience, crafted by a studio that clearly respects its source material. While it's certainly fair to acknowledge this game as one of the stronger entries within the franchise's gaming history, it's worth remembering that this is an exceedingly low bar.While I don't claim to be an expert in analysing the nuances of storytelling, it's abundantly clear that the plot is one of the game's weakest elements. Given the minimal amount of tangible gameplay, one would expect the story to serve as the core of the experience. Unfortunately, the writing is often predictable, uninspired, and player choices throughout the game provide little-to-no meaningful impact upon the overall plot.Petty as it may seem, one of my most significant gripes is with the game's original score. I strongly uphold the belief that music is a fundamental component for setting the tone within a visual narrative, which is why it pains me to state that the entire soundtrack is sonically akin to YouTube's royalty-free music library. This is especially jarring since the tone and instrumentation are frequently misaligned with the narrative, creating a tonal dissonance that continuously clashes with the story's events, as opposed to enhancing them. Looping perpetually throughout the game, the incessant drone of this 'elevator music' quickly becomes grating; compelling one to feel as though they're on hold with an insurance company, rather than immersed within a space adventure.While I certainly wouldn't have expected an instrumental score that speaks a thousand words, most games possess the ability to evoke some form of nostalgia when listening to their soundtrack in retrospect. This is something sorely missing from Star Trek Resurgence.The topic of enhancing the tone guides me to my next issue: the atmosphere presented within the game, or rather, the lack thereof. Given that a significant portion of the gameplay unfolds within the confined corridors and compact rooms aboard a starship, it's somewhat disappointing that these spaces feel unfinished. There is very little depth to be found within the audible landscape, while set-dressing also tends to be rather lacklustre. There's a noticeable absence of intricate details or unique objects that might evoke visual intrigue while playing. Even small, simple additions, such as background chatter or the sound of distant footsteps would have provided a much more immersive experience.Strong voice acting performances can often be a saving grace when the music and ambience fall short of expectations. Unfortunately in this case, cast members universally present their lines as though they're reading directly from a contextless script, instilling very little emotion into their vocal segments. This issue is further compounded by dialogue that is usually rather one-dimensional. To make matters worse, the audio recordings themselves are plagued by amateur mistakes. Popping or rubbing noises against the voice actors' microphones are commonly observed, and on occasion, the audio files themselves aren't edited into cinematics correctly, resulting in voice lines being cut off marginally early. These errors give the impression of a rushed production, detracting significantly from the overall experience.Ordinarily, I would delve into my thoughts on the graphics, however a cursory glance at the promotional screenshots and gameplay videos immediately reveals their antiquity, resembling visuals that lag at least ten years behind industry standards.In conclusion, I believe that Star Trek Resurgence may be an interesting experience for die-hard fans of the franchise; however, I would struggle immensely to recommend it otherwise. The game feels like an unfinished indie project, suggesting a distinct lack of competency involved in its development.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only a few hrs in, but just wanted to say this is exactly the kind of Trek game I was hoping someone would make. if you're older fan of the franchise, love Voyager & DS9 & enjoy slow burn, character driven/choices matter type games w/solid writing, this one's for you, grab it. if you're younger, & think that era of Trek is boring & are expecting JJ Abrams type action or drama-rama, don't bother- you're gonna hate it. _childDocuments_.review: I have now completed the game once on PC and this is my opinion of what I experienced.The concept of the game is incredibly well thought out, but unfortunately this is also one of the few positive things I can say about it. Considering the game engine they use, the period of release and what is promised on the sales page, I am quite disappointed as a Star Trek fan.- The graphics are downright bad.- All models (ships, npc) are bad, lack details and are generally nothing more than standard mesh shapes. The only thing that is somewhat acceptable are the main characters.- The player camera, animations, transitions between scenes are terribly buggy.- The choice influence on the story is very limited. Regardless of which choice you choose, outside of the satisfaction of other characters, you are still forced in the direction the game is planned. The addition of this is too limited.- There is no setting whatsoever regarding graphics settings.- Mouse sensitivity (PC) in many of the minigames is terribly low and difficult to control, even at extremely high DPI.- Considering the above points, I don't understand how the game has such poor performance and consistently low FPS.There may be many more negative points to mention and a few positive ones here and there, these points stood out the most to me. I don't understand where the positive reviews come from and the reviews in their description, don't be fooled by this!I had high expectations and Star Trek fans could really use a well-executed game after all the disappointments. So I sincerely hope this game sees improvements.

A great, great Star Trek experience with fantastic characterisation, epic story, and moving moments. _childDocuments_.review: REVIEW FOR PLAYERS AND DEVELOPERS WITH PROS AND CONS:Pros:1.  Overall, the story, plot, and characters are very good.2.  The game is really a blend of single player adventure, visual novel where choices matter, and some arcade and stealth elements.3.  Star Trek: Resurgence offers about 25 hours of gameplay which is excellent in my opinion, there are far too many games over 40 hours at which point they just drag out the story with too many side missions and stories, which takes away from the main story or it just becomes boring.4.  I love that I was able to choose my first officer once I became captain, I hope they make a single-player Star Trek game someday that I can choose my entire bridge crew, head engineer, and head doctor and name, make, and choose speces, race, and gender of my own captain.5.  SPOCK, what is there not to love about him?6.  I like the diplomatic decisions too be made.7.  I was so happy that Data or Deanna Troi or characters like them where not in the story!  Thank you!Cons:1.  I made the choice I wanted too all through the game, however, I would have been upset if I had accidently pushed the wrong button as there is not a good way to replay a chapter if you wanted too.  I would not want to restart the game, especially if I was far along.  There should be a menu option to replay or start from previously played chapters.2.  Flying the shuttle craft through rings was way to arcade like for me.  Just flying through moving asteroids to a destination would have been fine and made the experience seem much more realistic. _childDocuments_.review: Despite the non-recommendation, I do want to open this review and say that ST:R is a real love letter to Star Trek, written by people who probably raced through dinner and chores so they could catch an episode of TNG or DS9 or Voyager (never Enterprise). I think ST:R does a great job hitting those high points of human drama against the backdrop of a sci-fi setting. One of the last lines in the game is about how we learn more about ourselves, and how we might surprise ourselves as we grow and adapt and I really love that as a message about Star Trek in general. Let's start with the good: * The story is actually pretty great. I think it would feel right at home alongside a classic Star Trek episode, pitting a conflicted Federation against a galaxy of minor players. For all the pomp and circumstance of the Federation, you are still so woefully alone in unknown territory, and I think the game does a great job putting you in those shoes. There's definitely a little DS-9 going on here with what I like to think of as a 'dirty federation'; where not everything about them is gleaming and shining and I think it makes everything just seem all the more human. Genuinely; the story is well written and if you're going to buy the game; it'll be for this. * The voice acting is pretty great too. Genuinely, I thought every voice actor did a great job. I think they gave a good amount of space to not only new cultures, but also old ones; and the actors did a great job embodying that. Listening to a trill talk about what a symbiote meant to her family, or about a captain's concerns for legacy were genuinely very welcome and I'm glad that space was made available for these voice actors to go out there. I'd say those are the standout positives which unfortunately can't outdo the negatives which I'd summarise as: * The worst part of this game (imo) is the 'game' itself. The little quick time events, the terrible shooting sections, the general movement around the game, me wrestling with mouse sensitivity... woof. I get that not every game is going to have the movement/ action smoothness of Uncharted or Tomb Raider, but every 'action' sequence in this game is so jarringly poor that it really kicks you out of the disbelief. The best way to describe this is that I regularly felt like I was being asked to 'eat my vegetables' and go through a shooting puzzle before I could get back to the bits I actually wanted (which was the dialogue or choices). * Some facial expressions, and some of the character models aren't... great. I think anyone with hair that gets tied up or is cropped short generally looked good, and anyone with hair that actually stood out (Miranda, I'm looking at you) didn't get well put together. I think someone had a little too much fun with the eyebrows because it felt like everyone's eyebrows were on a play of their own when they'd shoot and wiggle with an almost sims-esque energy. * And I do feel the need to mention that despite my general love of the writing and story; I thought the ending did a poor job wrapping things up. Without spoiling anything, I'll say that there's a mystery in this game that permeates through almost the entire story; and in the last ten'ish minutes you get told the answer is 'X, and there's nothing to be done about it' and that's it. You spent 7/8 hours making these connections and getting invested in the story; and then you get told there's nothing to be done about this, thxbye. * I don't think there's any replay value to this game. I could go back through and make different choices to see what the cutscenes would look like if this crewman was here instead of the other, but it never felt like any of my choices really made a difference to the story. In that funny way I think this actually played more like the television show it was based off, rather than a game since you're really just a passenger on this story that's following it's own path. So... it's still a good story, and with great voice acting right? Surely the recommendation is 'if you love Star Trek, and you're really hankering for that great 8 hour TNG episode, this is the game for you'? And I really feel like the answer is a resounding no; because that's a great episode to watch, not a great game to play. ST:R is a fantastic episode of star trek that I would've paid money to watch (it's easily better than the first two seasons of Picard, but that's like saying I'm the greatest kisser in a morgue), but it's just not a good game to play. If you want to enjoy this, go watch it on youtube. If you're really keen to buy this, I'd suggest grabbing it when it's on sale but I don't think this is a 'game' I could recommend to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally!  A Star Trek experience from people who have watched Star Trek!  If you're expecting shooty-shooty Star Trek, it isn't here.  Really, off the big screen until Discovery, it wasn't anywhere.  If you're looking for a continuation of the TV show Star Trek: The Next Generation, then you want this.  This might as well be a "lost" episode of TNG.  It is made by some of the people who have made Telltale Games before, and it very much keeps that style.  Meaning you are pretty much a participant in a story line.  You make dialog choices, you make a few moves, and occasionally, there is some clunky combat, which if it becomes too frustrating, you can make those sections GOD mode and just continue.  The emphasis here is to control the direction of the story and crew, and that is good.  This is something you can pick up and experience.  Not really play, but experience, if you want to feel as if you are part of Starfleet.Graphics are OK.  Good enough they don't distract, aside from the hair occasionally blending with the lighting.  Either way, this can be placed on a low powered machine for anyone to enjoy.  The voice acting is excellent.  The music is DEAD ON POINT for TNG - that fake orchestral synth music that was all they could afford in the original 80's show.  Its back here in its full glory.  The original TNG sound effects, equipment, and even Jonathan Frakes.  They get about everything right for the person who loves Next Generation.  I very much hope this continues.  I do love a good shooter and RPG, but every now and then, the opportunity to just sit back and live and interact here in this world with a game like this is one of the great joys of this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: PLAY WITH CONTROLLERLet me start out by saying I am a massive Trekkie, and was so happy to find another single player Star Trek game. By looking at the game in a vacuum, it's probably one of if not the best Star Trek game out right now, feeling like a proper episode of TNG or DS9. The story is fun and interesting, likable characters, true to lore (with casual racism thrown in lmao), and has some amazing beauty shots of the USS Resolute. The sound design within the ship is fantastic, and I'm glad we get another class of ship to see instead of the standard Galaxy, Constitution, Sovereign, or Excelsior classes we always see. Plus it's a nice tribute to Leonard Nimoy w/ Spock making an appearance. It even follows up on another universe altering TNG episode. Despite all the good of this game, there's a lot to be desired. I'll list my greivances:-Animations are stiff-Dated looking graphics (think PS3 era)-Jfc the facial animations. They're........ bad. -Strange interaction choices, doesn't really increase immersion or add to the story -Weird camera movements-Random micro loading screens-Texture popping in certain environments (even w/ a 13900KF + 64GB D5 + 4070TiS)-Drastic tonal shifts during conversations-Music is too loud at times-Game started off way too dark, looked like it was set in Disco's Mirrorverse (Crank Brightness to max)-Poor controls, feels like you're piloting a fridge-Shooting sucks. All combat is shooting gallery style that's just bad (slow turn speed, limited range of view)Overall though, it's clear the Devs put a ton of love into the game and spent their time where it matters. _childDocuments_.review: Resurgence is an "A" game for me with "A+" for story. This game definitely loves the recent "optimistic" series like Lower Decks and Strange New Worlds. It feels very much like a Star Trek season. Short version: It's a fun, forgiving, and fantastic romp through a surprisingly deep story that can pull on your emotions far more than any typical "point and click." It took me about 10 hours, as a completionist, so I'd recommend buying it on sale. Once you play it you'll buy it at full price for all your sci-fi loving and story-hungry friends. If they like classic Telltale-style gaming, even if they're not Trekkies, they'll love this.Similar to typical TV series with an "A" story and a "B" story you flow between two characters, an officer and engineer. The overall story fits nicely with both and the "flipping" keeps you engaged. Supporting characters work well with both and I didn't think there was a particular "preference" for one or the other. Both have tough choices to make that have truly significant consequences. I was a little skeptical when starting this game but it hooked me when the "chapter one" finished up. The people have strong personalities and react realistically to unexpected situations. The choices impressed me and they felt powerful. You'll love your "tough little ship". You also get to use your phaser like a sonic screwdriver - and there's definitely a Tardis reference. The devs have good taste!The "action" part of the game is ok - there's stealth, a tiny bit of combat, even some starship flying. Some of the sequences were extremely ackward but they seemed "reasonable" for what was going on. It also seemed like the devs realized that not everyone in gameplay enjoys the "crazy situations" of these action points so they also give you a "skip".It wrapped up with a TV-style season finale that hits all the feels and made me eager for another "season" (hopefully a sequel!!). I'm eager to "re-watch" the game to find alternate paths.Review of common features:Story: A+. I was very impressed! The right amount of optimism with personal tension and some genuinely tough choices. I think that replays will feel meaningfully different and there were enough choices that not all the "pathways" were obvious. The ending is satisfying with no cliff hangers. It feels like a nicely wrapped up TV season.Voice acting: A+ The voice acting is outstanding - both the main characters and the "celebrities" (one made me look). Even the background characters had good VA.Choices and QTE: You can tell this was made by the famous Telltale devs because they seem to improve QTE / user experience with every game. There are puzzles, some stealth scenes, and some "protect the ally" which could be annoying but, if you fail one, the game lets you use "story mode" for the event which makes it simple and reduces frustration. The few QTE are obvious and work with the story.Gameplay: A-. I use keyboard/mouse and they worked fine except for being a little clunky when using devices.Graphics: A-. Very good. Humanoids aren't perfect but there are some stunning visuals in the cinematics and touching personal moments.Sound: B+. Sound effects "make sense" while avoiding goofiness and, while the music is a bit forgetable, it's smooth enough to add to the scene. Give this one a go (on sale, the price is a bit much for 10 hours, imho).

_childDocuments_.review: As a life-long Star Trek fan, I can whole-heartedly recommend Resurgence.  My favorite Star Trek games are Starfleet Academy and Bridge Commander, and this game genuinely carries forward the excellence of those games.  Playing through the video cutscenes in Academy was so much fun back in the day, and this is a game entirely of interactive cutscenes.  While mostly on rails, there are distinct moments of choice and consequence, and the narrative seemlessly carries the player forward, sometimes on the edge of my seat.  Honestly, the narrative and acting of this story are better than most of the television episodes.  Any fan of the series is sure to enjoy.The characters and each of their motivations are genuinely compelling, as is the voice acting.  You're sure to recognize several of the voices from other games.While I still hold Game of Thrones as the pinnacle of the Telltale series, and still desperately want more of it, this is a great experience in it's own right, and definitely deserves a look, even if just the demo.  Definite replayability (at least once) to see alternative consequences despite the lack of a fast-forward button (**developers, PLEASE add a fast forward button.)

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a decent Star Trek story, this is fine! It's obvious that the creators really cared about the game and creating a compelling Star Trek story. However, as a game, this leaves a lot to be desired. The game is very poorly optimized for PC in its current state, both in how it runs as well as the core controls and mini-games. There are literally zero optimization or accessibility options.The main gameplay element of decision making is not very robust and seems to have little impact on the story progression. There are no fail states that allow you to progress, meaning you cannot fail a task and continue the story with the effects of that failure. Aside from minor changes there also doesn't seem to be any variability in how the story plays out based on your decisions. Everything will happen the way it is supposed to, with the only change being the NPC's opinion.This isn't a bad game necessarily. I like the story and most of the performances! But unless you're really itching for a Star Trek narrative, I would pass unless discounted.P.S. There is a free demo that is a good introduction to the game! Give it a try before purchase, it is a relatively good vertical slice.

_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, this game has its issues.... graphical quirks, goofy dialogue, button presses to do the most tedious tasks (walking to another room just to move to trigger a cut scene). It is still fun to play.It is basically a fully rendered 3D visual novel set in the Star Trek Universe. What I didn't know going into this game was that in the Star Trek timeline, the crew of the Resolute are very whiny. Many of the choices that you make will offend one of your crew-mates greatly. They all feel entitled to promotions or to have their opinions validated (through your choices). I tried very hard to play the Federation diplomat at the beginning of the game and tried to keep the peace. Toward the latter half of the game, I gave up on caring about their feelings and boy did they let me know (when I offended them). Ha Ha Ha. I thought panties in the future would be less likely to get twisted up (because of  lower gravity). I was wrong. If I play through again, I am going to be a big jerk the entire time just to see how they react. Will the game end? Will I end up in the brig? Before I began playing this game, I had read that this game was super "Woke", but I didn't really see it. Is it because one of the main characters was a female? Without spoiling too much, the story-line is almost a science fiction version of the replacement conspiracy theory that is going around on the internet. I am pretty sure that isn't a very woke story-line. To sum things up: This game is a decent slow paced science fiction game where your choices matter (and make people mad at you). It is fun to play even with the quirks. If nothing else, get it on discount and play it on a slow day.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Love it.  Wasn't sure when reading the reviews, but as an older Trek fan I love the cinematic presentation of this.  As others have said, it's like being in an episode (Series!) yourself and really is like being in an interactive book/film/etc.  A great way to portray the Star Trek universe and true to core.  Not a twitch or fps type affair, which isn't really how you appreciate this material anyway.  No, it's a great experience with a great story with top character interactions and dialog.  Highly recommended if you like a good Sci-Fi story and utterly unmissable if you're a fan of Star Trek.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: A bit rough around the edges, like a half-baked console port, but it doesn't significantly detract from an otherwise enjoyable experience. A few interactive prompts were broken, but thankfully you can bypass them with "Story Mode".I didn't notice any forced DEI crap, just a decent Star Trek story-line.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Space... the Ugliest Frontier.Hideous artefacting--space is one big overly zoomed-in texture--awful animations (from walking to the absurd ship movements), and facial expressions are right out of The Sims.No. Just... no.I'm sure it's lovely and interesting and has a great story, but I can't be bothered. Seems the budget was spent on making the character models whilst everything else was left to the intern.Also, no ultrawidescreen support. Not even any graphics settings--enjoy the jaggies, folks.Too many things to moan about, too little interest from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game for a Trekkie however some achievements do not work or I some how messed it up. I mean I beat the game and didn't get the "Remember Me" Achievement, I haven't explored enough into the menu to see if you can choose chapters to get achievements easier but seems you have to play through the game multiple times to get everything which is a bummer. I paid $20 for it and man it was worth the money any more than that I would pass and just watch a youtuber play but that is just me.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: The animation can be a bit stiff and the combat sections really aren't great, but it is a narrative experience above all else, and it was a *good* Star Trek story. Compare it to 10 hours of a modern trek show and it has a more coherent plot and character development than what we are usually offered. For that alone I was very pleased with the experience. I really hope it does well enough that the devs get the chance to keep telling more stories like this, because this kind of medium is perfect for Star Trek.Now to go back and play it with the rudest/worst choices possible
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through this game once already, and started a second playthrough immediately. While I'm not a big fan of some of the timed actions or other things you have to do at times, the game is still an amazing work of art to play. You truly feel like you are part of Star Trek, part of the crew. While I do wish some of the choices made had impacts for the future (although some do, but most do not), it's still a game miles above many others, and the best Trek game I have played in a long time. I sincerely hope to see more Trek games like this. It was also a nice touch to see some old faces in the game. I look forward to getting all the achievements. All in all, 10/10 game, and I was hooked from the beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely a worth while trek experience. The animations and visuals are kinda janky at times with dead eyes and weird character movements.But the actual story so far is well done.There is some performance concerns since even on a 4070ti there were several scenes that I dropped well below 30 and it felt weird.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Played it till the end once. Took me about 10h. On the tech side, the game is super unstable. Frame rate not stable, graphics are okay-ish, menu is just bad, etc... However, I kinda enjoyed it. Story is okay, choices seem to matter as far as I can tell. I some where read "It is like you play one or more episodes of a ST TV show.". And I agree. No super action combat, no hard riddles. Just a story to enjoy with some phaser shooting ;-)I would like to see a follow up, but with tech and improvements.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Star Trek, and an excellent entry in this genre (best since the Walking Dead trilogy, in my opinion). The writing and performances are great, characters are compelling, and the art style is largely well done (despite the graphics being relatively lo-fi).About the only things I can complain about are a couple minor bugs I encountered, and one of the mechanics is more annoying than interesting.I really hope this kicks off a series. I'd love to follow the adventures of the Resolute through several more games.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not far into the game, but so far, I really love it! I don't know if there's going to be different endings, but the journey to get there is what interests me the most. Not far into the game, you already have to make difficult decisions, so that's good because it's immersive and really makes you feel like you're First Officer! The animations and graphics aren't the best, but the voice acting is great which is much more important if you ask me. If you don't like these quick time events (like me): If you fail one, the game asks if you want to retry or continue in story mode. Apparently, story mode can only be accessed this way. But it does allow you to play without being able to fail. Having a physical ailment like I do which doesn't always allow me to act as quickly as my mind would want me to, I really welcome this! The game changes between playing the First Officer and a person on the Lower Decks (one female, one male). Sometimes, the change happens very quickly. I guess this was done to show that the fate of all people on the starship are intertwined and dependent on each other. It works well so far. But if you want to design and create one character to play, then this isn't the game for you. You play these two predefined characters. Since I'm giving a thumbs up, you can already tell that I am fine with all of this. I am glad to finally see a well-made Star Trek game! Thank you, Dramatic Labs! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible game. You get to try your hand at commanding a ship and will have some difficult choices to make. I often found myself allowing the personalities of previous captains dictate the choices I made - Kirk, Picard, Sisko or Janeway. Perhaps nothing will influence your judgement, however being a Star Trek fan myself meant that this was sometimes unavoidable when last minute life and death choices had to be made. Would I bend the rules slightly as Sisko used to do, or would I sometimes be brash like captain Kirk? Regardless of what you do each decision will have far-reaching consequences that will affect the fate of the entire crew, as well as the reputation of the Federation itself.Definitely one for Star Trek and science fiction fans alike. It's brilliant (and I'm only a few hours in). Music is top class too.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10 - I really hope they create more, as a fan of the Star Trek series (i rewatch them in my spare time yearly) this was a welcome game to watch and be involved with.  The major loss of points for me would be both the Phaser gameplay and the stealth scenes.. kinda felt really wierd and didn't work well with the way the game was done. Thankfully they are few and far between. I really hope they continue on to make MORE.... Easy money spent, Enjoyment worth every minute.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Story is good so far. Much more like a TNG-era story than the new shows. The game has some trouble with ultrawide monitors. I'm using a mod I found, but I'm limited to 3840x1080, instead of 5120x1440, because of severe performance issues (200 vs 15 fps). The autosave system could also be improved somewhat. I hope they make more of these, or DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Never played a Star Trek game that felt this way.  This is what Gene would have wanted in a story and game.  This is a game about decisions and how others are effected.  This is a game that will test you and see if your choices would really work in the world of Star Trek.  It is not bang bang shoot em up.  It is do whats right andbe the person original Star Trek thought we would all become.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Unplayable on AMD systems.The game is great but there are Zero Graphics Options and at least one AMD Systems the framerate goes into the single digital all the time. For Ally and Steamdeck Users: dont buy this Game (yet).The game isnt graphically impressive and a years old with No.fix so the Team hast to be incompetent in optimization. So i dont think i can recommend anyone with AMD systems to buy this horrible Port.The Story ist really great and the gameplay okay for a narrative Game so If the devs solve the technical issues, i would have 9/10 but with the Performance and Crashes and bugs 2/10 Not recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like watching a Star Trek episode. A good episode, but interaction is very limited. Yes, you get some dialogue choices, but the story is *very* firmly on rails, and most actions are the "press this one button to advance the scene" type. There are some mini games, like flying a shuttle through asteroids for a minute, or shooting some enemies with a phaser - but frankly it would be easier to just advance the action automatically without me having to press the one and only button there is.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: I have enjoyed this game. Being a Star Trek game, true to the proper timeline, without being polluted with the toilet salsa some people call Star Trek these days. The game style is enjoyable, the references are authentic. So far it has passed the test and I haven't been tempted to destroy everything around me and throw my computer into the street. I recommend this game. I would enjoy more Star Trek games built in this style, in this timeline.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: I so hoped for a good star trek adventure game, but at 1.5 hrs in, I must say, this is not it.The people who grew up on the 90's series are adults now, they are in their fourties and beyond. This game leans heavily on familiarity with the setting, and introduces us to characters both at the command and executive levels, a ship that fits the era - a refurbished pre-TNG cruiser serving as science vessel. All well conceived thus far.But. The controls are clunky, I can get over that. The graphics are relatively simple, I'm OK with that.The story and characterisation though... it is, simply put, for children. Even as an interactive story there is zero real engagement, the player is just moving the characters through their motions. The character motivations are simplistic at the very best, hitting on duty, collegiality and, for some reason from the get-go, romance, but all at a very superficial and apparent uncomplicated manner, which leads me to wonder which age group this was made for.In a single word. It's infantile.Star trek, especially 90's trek, is supposed to be about competency and grace. This is the sesame street version of those values.I'll give it another go another day, and if things improve, I'll amend this. But right now, I would suggest to keep in mind this is a mismarketed youth product. Those hoping to rekindle with TNG age trek stories as they remember them will be... frustrated, which is highly disappointing given how much longing for such stories there is in that sizeable community.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a very well optimised port. With the exception of the face models, the graphics are basically a decade old (we're talk about Mass Effect 3 era graphics) and yet it has fairly high requirements. I don't understand how a game that is fairly limited in terms of what it needs to render (this is not open world) recommends 16gb of ram.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Good voice acting, music, art, and a wonderful story that offers some hard choices among some very likable characters.  Fills the void of departing Star Trek series.  Controls are simple with enough time to think quickly about your impending choices. Piotr Michael's Spock is so convincing I had to check that this game wasn't made  ten years ago.   All I can ask is, "May I have another?"
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a Star Trek fan or just love games with a hopeful vision of the future, Star Trek: Resurgence is a must-play. This game captures everything that makes the Star Trek universe so inspiring. Set on the starship Resurgence, it showcases a future where humanity has overcome its differences to explore the galaxy and improve life for everyone. The diverse crew represents the strength that comes from embracing our differences, working together to tackle challenges and achieve great things.In a time when some people criticize "woke" ideas, Star Trek: Resurgence reminds us that diversity and inclusion are crucial for a thriving society. The game stays true to the series' core message: our differences make us stronger, and unity leads to progress and peace. If you want a game that reflects a hopeful, inclusive future, look no further. Star Trek: Resurgence is a fantastic journey into the best of what humanity can be. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed it. It felt like a long, interactive episode of TNG/DS9 era Trek which I love. Some minor issues such as some voice lines clipping, inaccurate subtitles, and some models juddering as they get into position for a cutscene, but nothing bad enough to stop me from playing. I hope they make a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Decent enough Tell-tale styled star trek game. A little janky at points, especially with the controls.  Had to switch between using a controller to using mouse and keyboard in the shooting segments because keyboard control outside of combat was painful and using a controller in combat was double painful.Though if one can get past that, it's a game that tries to give some meaningful dilemmas and its also nice to see TNG/DS9/Voyager universe stuff vs kevin timeline stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a really nice, well written Star Trek story for fans of TNG/VOY/DS9-era Trek. The choices feel consequential in most cases and there are some genuine twists and turns in the story with real ups and downs along the way. I think the ending was a little weak in that it left several loose ends, but it didn't detract from the overall execution which was good.- Graphics are decent, not excellent but about on par for a story-driven game like this.- Game time of 10hrs feels about right to me.- The whole thing feels like it's designed for a controller, though it works with a mouse and keyboard. Mouse gestures sometimes feel a bit off, like they were clearly designed for a stick.- Combat and puzzle sections a little weak, but they get a pass as this is primarily a story-driven game.- Not too much in the way of repetitive sections, the story feels fairly fresh throughout.- Voice acting and script are overall very good.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: Edit:Changing my review to yes - they seem to have fixed the D3D crashes.still hate stealth missions but beyond that, hey, I can play again lol Edit 2:Ok helluva' good ending.ALMOST want to start a new game to see how deep the twist-a-plot-goes.Old review.  No reason to delete.D3d Glitches... and worst of all "stealth" missions.  Woof.That crap kills a game faster for me than a lightning strike.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: For Star Trek fans, it was pretty cool to be IN the STORY.  You had to make decisions some at very critical times that had down-stream effects.  Overall pretty fun.Graphics weren't smooth, no way to fast-forward.  Def. recommend, just know what u are getting, a STAR TREK STORY that you are in and get/have to make choices in.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review: If one has an interest in involved story telling, you can't get much better than this. Visually it is beautiful, the voice acting excellent, an engrossing narrative, and the decision trees complex. You can take the singular aggressive response to decisions, or a more balanced approach. Your decisions, however, will not be popular with everyone you encounter, including your own crew. These decision points, while advancing the story, also teach you the burden of command. A must play for us 'trekkies' out there, it is equally enjoyable by all.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

_childDocuments_.review:
Star Trek: Resurgence is a narrative adventure game featuring dialog choices, relationship building, and exploration.

Alongside dialog-driven role playing and rich branching storylines, you will also engage with the Star Trek universe in a variety of other gameplay styles, including shuttle piloting, phaser fights, tricorder scanning, stealth, and micro-gameplay mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Resurgence

name: LOLLIPOP CHAINSAW RePOP
detailed_description: The chainsaw-wielding cheerleader Juliet Starling returns in Lollipop Chainsaw RePOP! Rip and tear through an army of the living dead like never before in this remastered version of the zany over-the-top cult classic! Boasting upgraded graphics, 4K support, improved controls, faster action, new difficulty modes, and loads of quality-of-life improvements, Lollipop Chainsaw RePOP doesn’t just bring back what fans loved – it cranks it all up to eleven! ＜STORY＞ A cheerleader takes on the undead in this zany over-the-top zombie-slaying adventure! San Romero High School has been overrun by zombies, and it’s up to cheerleader Juliet to save the day. But Juliet isn’t just any high school cheerleader: As part of a legendary family of zombie hunters, she’s more than equipped to fight the undead hordes! Using her acrobatic cheerleading skills, zombie-slaying expertise, and a seriously powerful chainsaw, she’ll face down an army of the living dead and the evil forces behind them! ＜ACTION＞ Rip and tear through hordes of zombies - with style! Lollipop Chainsaw RePOP cranks up the intensity with the all-new Chain Hit Hunting system, which lets you build up massive combo streaks, speeding up the action as you swing. The higher your combo, the faster and deadlier Juliet becomes, making each encounter a breathtaking ballet of blades and blood! And with the newly revamped Chainsaw Blaster, you can shoot your way through the chaos like never before! Rapid-fire, improved lock-ons, and auto-ammo pickup make it easier than ever to keep the pressure on. Combined with refined controls and faster action, every move feels smoother, and more fluid and satisfying. ＜BOSSES＞ Face the the Dark Purveyors - ridiculous rotting rock stars! Prepare for some of the wildest boss battles you've ever seen! The Dark Purveyors are not your average zombies — they're twisted, genre-defying bosses that bring their own brand of madness to the battlefield! Each boss has their own unique deadly styles and powers that make them formidable foes—like Mariska's psychedelic illusions or Josey’s funky grooves that warp the very battlefield around you. Every clash is more than just a fight; it’s an epic showdown against the most deranged supernatural forces ever to walk the earth. Think you’ve got what it takes to defeat these rotting rock stars? It’s time to find out! ＜MINIGAMES＞ Revamped minigames bring variety to killing zombies! Lollipop Chainsaw RePOP revises the minigame lineup with improvements to keep things fun. Whether you're launching zombie heads through a basketball hoop or trying your hand at zombie baseball, everything now feels tighter and more intuitive. More explanations and tips will help players understand the rules from the get-go, making it easy to dive in and start scoring straight away. Each minigame has been tweaked to deliver a high level of wild and wacky gameplay consistent with the rest of the game while adding variety to your zombie-slaying adventure! ＜CUSTOMIZATION＞ Juliet’s amazing new wardrobe is to die for! Juliet’s wardrobe is bursting with costumes, adding jaw-dropping new designs to the lineup alongside fan favorites from the original game. Choose from these stylish outfits to ensure that Juliet is always dressed to impress! But that’s not all—You can even give Juliet’s chainsaw a makeover! Choose from a variety of new chainsaw designs to fit your personal flair and maximize your undead-busting power. And don’t forget the new hair color options! Change Juliet’s look to match your mood and make every chainsaw swing a statement! ＜REPOPPED＞ Who ever knew that killing zombies could be so colorful? You can choose to stick with the same intense, blood-soaked spectacle from the original game if you prefer, but if you’re ready to see Juliet’s chainsaw action in a whole new light, check out the new RePOP mode! Enjoy the same thrilling gameplay, now with a splash of pop art aesthetic, where damage effects are replaced with vivid, vibrant sparkling effects. It’s a bold new look that adds extra flair to the zombie-slaying fun! Lollipop Chainsaw's music has also been revamped in RePOP, with a load of awesome new compositions from acclaimed composers known for their work in video games and anime. These new tracks, alongside the upgraded visuals, offer a refreshing, remixed twist on the game! ＜ENHANCEMENTS＞ The whole game is packed with QOL improvements! Lollipop Chainsaw RePOP is packed with quality-of-life upgrades to give you a smoother, more responsive, and better-looking zombie-slaying experience! Dive into the action with dramatically reduced load times, an improved camera, and enhanced input responsiveness. The new auto-play feature for QTEs lets you focus on the action without missing a beat, and 4K/60 FPS support means that the action will look way better too!

_childDocuments_.review: Even though RePOP is an upgrade from the OG version (outside of a few things,) Its not a $40 game.  Wait for a sale to get it because this is a very very short game. I have 4 hours currently and I'm already on the last level. What does RePOP do better compared to the OG version? RePOP+Visually much better +Has smoother gameplay +Shop is way less grindy and has two new things to buy (Chainsaws and hair dye for Juliet) and a couple new costumes+No censorshipWhats worse in RePOP?- the new soundtrack is absolutely terrible compared to the OG version. The new tracks are so unbelievably bland compared to what we had before. Songs like "Hey Mickey," "Riot rhythm," "The Way of the Fist," ect all fit the game so well and for them, and more, to not be included really sucks. I don't think the devs understand how much the soundtrack added to the OG game.- the UI is horrendous when using K&M. It would've been nice being able to use the mouse to click things instead of being forced to use your keyboard for everything. - No graphic settings outside of resolution (though the game is fairly easy to run so it wont be an issue to most)- Audio in cutscenes sounds deep fried in some levels- Collab costumes have been removed (Give me shiro back)- QTEs are a little buggy but nothing game breaking.The last two aren't that big of a deal though it would be nice to see them get fixed/readded.
_childDocuments_.name: LOLLIPOP CHAINSAW RePOP

_childDocuments_.review: Lollipop, if you didn't know, was a Warner Bros. game back in 2012 written by James freakin’ Gunn and directed by none other than Suda51, one of the most unique video game directors ever. The game also included tracks from Jimmy Urine. Maybe it got forgotten in time, but it was a beloved hit. A sought after piece of collector's item for the most even. Now, I can't tell you if WB could have released a game like this as freely today as they did in the past. However, I am very glad that DRAGAMI is back with this remaster (another Suda51 game, Shadows of the Damned, is also on the way; we are so back to the glorious 7th gen). Despite the few technical hiccups that have already been discussed (such as not being able to select resolution or some KBM-related UI issues), the game runs relatively well, and I think it would run well on most modern systems. I was unable to run it in 4K at 60, but in 2K with a 3080ti, I easily get over 80 FPS, which is fair. Though it does mean Juliet is not back in 4K, at least for me. I hope they add more options as the current director (Yoshimu Suda) is actively listening to the fans. My experience, as far as I played, was bug-free, but I might have been fortunate there. QTEs do work but feel like there's a slight input lag, and there are (even if not quite often) some issues with audio breaking down or dialogues overlapping. Your upgrades do reset after death if you didn't get to the checkpoint, and you need to rebuy them from the shop. It takes a few seconds—no biggie—but still unnecessary. There are unskippable in-game cutscenes, and you need to rewatch them if you are repeating that stage; however, they are also short, so I'll let that one slip away.It's still super over the top. As you bash zombies while rainbows, hearts, sparkles, and all that manly stuff occupy your screen, it took me a while to realize there was blood missing. That's RePOP for you. The blood is in the original mode, and well, not gonna lie, I had some fun with all those sparkles, but this being the only difference between the two game modes (as far as I was able to dig) is a bit disappointing. And being the grindhouse type of game, some blood is appreciated.I can't tell if there is zero censorship (that might not be the best word for it, as I can't tell the motivation behind it). Maybe some lines got removed; I can't recall every single one, but there are raunchy costumes (some are more than Stellar Blade) and cheesy lines such as that guy claiming to be masturbating for you tonight or Nick wishing he still had a ♥♥♥♥ when you go into Juliet's bedroom. Sexy Rider and Seashell are still there, though some licensed outfits are gone.As for the music, I agree with most. The original tracks (with the licensed ones) are a better 'complete' experience' fitting the game so damn well. Especially the loss of 'Hey Mickey' and 'You Spin Me Round' is noticeable. I don't quite hate the new list, but I don't really dig it either.The graphics are neat but lean more towards fidelity and realism. It's somewhat cartoonish but has definitely lost the (cell-shaded) comic book vibe that the original one had. I found that a bit baffling. Japanese games has this going and idk why, Lollipop is not the game to show-off tech I'd reckon.The shop is better, as you can buy most costumes for 10 to 30 platinums instead of 80-90. This means you'll be pretty much able to switch up costumes freely in one playthrough.I like the humor myself, especially the references to music groups like My Chemical Romance and Green Day, but it gets a tad bit tedious and annoying at times. Though I must admit, I have a guilty pleasure for teenagey dialogues and scripts that wouldn't make sense. This is one of the reasons I miss the 7th generation, as today's games are often more serious and pseudo-intellectual.And the price… Well, I don’t think $40 is an outrageous price, and they are also investigating better prices for different regions. There are certainly ways to play Lollipop even on PC, but legally, if you wanted to own an Xbox 360/PS3 copy, they were going for anywhere from $40 to as much as $60. So, I don’t think being able to play this properly on PC for $40 is a huge loss, even if it’s not a steal. However, you might still want to play the original. Yes, modders are working on the costumes and the music, but sometimes you grow up to appreciate the jankiness of the original.So, Lollipop, imho, isn’t exactly a game that was ahead of its time. It’s not really a hidden gem or underappreciated (as far as the fanbase goes). Although it didn’t fare well with critics and is undoubtedly underappreciated there, it has always performed well with fans and will likely continue to do so. So, what is it? It’s a super fun, ludicrous, and quirky piece of media. Sometimes, that’s all you need.ps: They say chivalry is dead. Don't do it. Don't look at the skirt.-It was a flexing material amongst trophy hunters. Many people left it at 98% for a while.★★★½☆☆

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played the PS3 version and my introduction to the game only happened now. So I don't know the smallest differences between the 2012 version and the remake. I know from discussions that the original music has been changed, most likely due to license expiry, as is often the case with games. I agree that the old music was much better and soulful, but it's not a big problem because there is already a mod that brings it back. Look for it in the guides - "Music Restoration Mod". I also installed a mod that brings back the original picture in the main menu, because I think it's more aesthetically pleasing than in RePOP.I recommend playing specifically with the restored music. Just check out these masterpieces: Let's get to the game itself. This is a very funny, colorful and dynamic "Hack and Slash" that will not let you get bored. Yes, it's not long, it takes exactly 8 hours to complete, butt each level is more interesting than the previous one.The most interesting here is the dialogues, i guess. It is the expressions and jokes of the characters that make the game so much fun. There is a lot of black and vulgar humour and it just makes the mood lift. Sometimes it's very silly, and I'm glad of that. Because they don't make games like that nowadays. I think you know what I mean, reader. But this is a remake of a 2012 game, so there's nothing wrong with the characters and their sense of humour. I remember a few jokes about Japanese, Katy Perry, Stephen Hawking, iPod, Facebook, Chip and Dale, and many others. Modern characters don't joke in that style and don't look as beautiful as the main character. That's really what we've lost. Or we've changed ourselves. This game caught my heart because it's about as good as being under the skirt of an American cheerleader. I'm serious.A nice addition is that Juliet has many different outfits, so getting through each level becomes even more varied.I have beat the game with DualSense and it was a great time, especially with the OST of the original Lollipop Chainsaw.I felt this high school vibe, and also in an American setting. It reminded me of my last high school years, those adventures and that time in general - the 2010s, which I find more interesting than the 2020s. The world was really different before 2020 and I was once again convinced of that by playing a game from that era.

_childDocuments_.review: ive always wanted to play lollipop chainsaw & i was going to buy it for my ps3 but it has been broken for a while so you can imagine my excitement when i saw it came out on steam. the pricing at $45 is reasonable to me because its the same price you would get for the original on the ps3/xbox360. the controls are very frustrating at first so i suggest going into the settings and set your own if youre not plugging in a controller. yes the controls will still be a bit funky maybe lagging a bit but its just the games mechanics and there is nothing you can do to fix it. the saves did bug me at first when i didnt understand them and it would always reset me to stage 1. i had to replay the stage at least 3 times before i understood how to save properly. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played the original the year it came out, RePOP does not do it justice. I've only just reached the end of Stage 1 and had to deal with many glitches/bugs that required restarting checkpoints in order to proceed. This game has been delayed twice yet it feels like those delays weren't enough to give it the time and quality it deserves.1. The quicktime events do not register immediately, the bar reaches halfway before it processes being pressed, when in the original, it would register your response before it even began filling up.2. The brightness takes away the atmosphere and eeriness of the stages3. Zed's new VA doesn't have the same enthusiasm and effort as his original, I understand why they had to use a new VA, but they could've had him try more. He also makes Zed appear more southern than the original. Jimmy's in-game lines also remain and actually play-over the new lines which makes things confusing and off-putting.4. The 'realistic' graphics take away the original's more stylistic charm and expressiveness. They appear more stiff/lifeless and appears cheaper instead.5. The original mode doesn't even work, I don't know if it's because classic is unavailable yet (should have clarified if that would be the case) so I'm stuck in rePOP's mode.6. The new boss music feels out of place and greatly underwhelming, what made their original themes special was due to the fact they represented their respective genres of music (punk, metal, psychedelia, funk, and rock). Replacing it with generic fighting music ruins the purpose of being the "Bosses of Zombie Rock" and another reason on what made the original more special.All in all, I feel like rePOP should've had more time spent on it. I recommend the original over RePOP not just for the original OST, but better graphics, design, less glitches and bugs, and overall more satisfying to play. What I do like with RePOP is the fact the controls aren't that difficult to get used to (keyboard wise), new outfits + letting the old outfits be purchased with the gold coins than the platinum medals like before, and it does give this gem of a game attention once more.

_childDocuments_.review: Lolipop Chainsaw was one of the PS3 Classics that was always stuck on my wishlist. Crazy, whacky, sexy and full of rainbow soft-gore. Hard not to love that aesthetic, especialy that the game was made in times were humour was unapologetic and gameplay focused on pure fun pouring out from every minute - not on micro (or rather macro) transactions, live services and creating fake engagement time by making too long but content-less titles. However 50-100$ for a used disc to a hardware that is not that often used anymore and 720p is a lot to ask, so the oportunity to play never came. It changed when I saw a youtube video saying "RePOP" and gasped thinking "Did they remastered that game and released it on PC?!" - they did. So now this review comes to say important things both on meta level and strictly game focused one. Let's start with meta level. I'm happy to pay full price of that game even though I believe it's almost always good choice to wait for sale (especialy with insanely high prices already and GTA VI planning to increase the pricing culture in the near future even further). In this case I'm happy because the studio does something that is vigorously needed in industry - it brings back the piece of art and gaming history and allows to interact with it again and not just re-live memories or dream about how it would be to experience it. I see it as a form of support and if it will encourage others to do so I think buying it even without sale is a good choice. The gaming culture is full of lost artworks and it should be one of the main missions of the industry to restore them. The second aspect that I deeply apreciate is bringing it back in unchanged, uncensored and unmodified form. Titles should be brought back exactly as they were to a T, not cut and reshaped to fit politics of times or different sensibilites of some groups - it doesn't matter if we talk about silly things like upskirt looks and horny humour or more serious aspects, we do not bastardise different works of art like DaVinci paintings or Sheakspear novels to fit wishes of some and we should NEVER do so with gaming as well as it's not in any extent lesser form of artistic expression and culture. The humour is raunchy, tastefully vulgar and full of delightfull absurdism, jokes constantly cross between those themes, but in a manner that puts a smile on your face and not weird expression of second hand embarassement. There is a lot of references to pop culture that will be most apreciated by people around 25-30 years old as it was times of their teenage years that the game refferences, but it's a nice starting point to get younger generation interested in how times looked like back then. The game is not long, it can be "finished" in around 5h, but like many other action games (Bayonetta, Metal Gear Rising, Devil May Cry) the true goal of the title is not to finish it for the first time,  but rather treat the first time as tutorial and skill-gathering run that allows to collect costumes, do insane, cool combos and unlock all secrets on subsequent runsAlso it is not a bad thing. We are overextended with fascinating, very long and open worlded games like Baldrus Gate 3, Cyberpunk or Witcher 3 and for those who do not have as much free time as they did during school or university years, getting to play a title that does not demand hundred of hours while still offering fun and excitement instead of being time killer like many for example mobile games is a blessing. Personally my game time is around 6 hours and I'm halfway through due to explaroation and learning what is what so the 5 hours of full game cycle is the low end for those who will rush from start to the end. Something that must be mentioned before we talk about negatives is a voice acting. It's A+, amazing, quality work that makes you absolutely flored with skills and delivery of actors! The lines and the way they are spoken, Julliet voice full of this silly-but-lovable energy, the sisters, Nick, enemies, voice acting in that game could be a study piece for actors in making to learn from as listening to the game alone is a pure pleasure!Now the few bad things about that title:Pop Ups with information about how to play a game are dissapearing way to quickly. I'm a fast reader yet even while focusing strictly on the information I was often able read only half or 3/4 of what was written. Can't imagine being absorbed with action or reading in a slower manner and still getting anything out of it. It's imporant because those are not basic advices like "WASD is used for movement" but actual explenations of how the game and it's mechanics works so there is a lot to figure out on your own and it takes around half of the first playthrough if you can identify mechanics quickly. Controls - the control feel stiff and unresponsive at times. While after some time you get used to how the game is played and figure out that a lot of "jankyness" is caused by lack of understanding for the "game flow" this area could be improved a little without damaging faithfullness to the original title so it's worth to mention it here. Graphic is beautifully remastered and the game looks as good as it ever looked however at certain moments or at few art pannels here and there, there is a feeling of lack of details or lower resolution as if not everything was brought to the same visual standard. It's not awfully disruptive, besides it's not about the graphics in game like that, but still, it would benefit the game a lot more if there was not an impression of gap in quality between certain parts of the game. Overall I give the game 9/10 The 1 point is reduced due to the slight issues I described, but titles like this are what made gaming fun and brought people into the hobby. We need a lot more games like that and return of the 2000-2010 ideas of what gaming should be instead treating it like a cash cow just with different paint all the time.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly forgot what it was like to be the target audience for a video game.Games nowadays have become extremely diluted in an attempt to appeal to the broadest—or fringest—audience possible. _childDocuments_.review: In its current state, I can't recommend Lollipop Chainsaw: RePOP.There was clearly an effort made to polish and refine the original cult classic for modern platforms while retaining as much of the original aesthetic and vibe as possible, but all of those admirable attempts are buried under a mountain of bugs both small and game-breaking, performance issues, and visual and audio changes that take away from the experience.In just under two hours of playing, I've encountered QTE's that won't register on-time, the coin counter displaying an incorrect total, audio desync during cutscenes, various lines from the original not playing (which the devs has acknowledged as a bug, not a conscious removal), the camera getting stuck at certain angles and refusing to move, and frequent stutters.On top of the performance issues, there are currently no graphics options beyond setting your resolution, the lighting has been made blindingly bright, the comic-style shading of the original has been removed in favor of a more realistic and cheap-looking visual style, most of the original soundtrack has been axed in favor of a far more generic one, the combat balance is strikingly off (both too stiff and too easy), and various destructable objects don't behave properly (Zed's amps in phase 2 of his fight can all be destroyed in one hit no matter how many are in a stack). The devs have stated that they plan on rolling out patches to fix many of these issues, but until they are fixed, I'd recommend staying away from this remaster, despite the clear love put into it. Perhaps this seemingly unheard-of dev team bit off more than they could chew this time.

_childDocuments_.review: Very few titles manage to seamlessly blend the absurd with genuine uninterrupted fun, and this game is definitely one of those rare gems. Reintroducing us to a universe filled with colorful chaos and audacious humor, this game is extremely fun to play, standing out as a testament to what made the original so beloved among fans while adding some refreshing tweaks that elevate the experience.At the heart of its appeal is a meticulously crafted gameplay loop that never ceases to entertain. The controls are extremely responsive, allowing players to execute moves with precision and ensuring that every combat encounter is as satisfying as it is chaotic. Whether you're slicing through hordes of zombies or exploring the whimsically dark world, the seamless control mechanics guarantee an immersive experience.A particularly commendable aspect of the game is its unapologetically uncensored approach. This decision not only preserves the original spirit of the game but also amplifies its outlandishly humorous atmosphere, providing a more authentic experience to fans who appreciate the game’s unique style. However, while the uncensored mode offers full-throttle fun, there is a slight hiccup: the subtitles occasionally don't match the dialogue. While not a deal-breaker, it can momentarily pull you out of the moment.Graphically, the game is a vivid spectacle, but it does suffer from some technical blemishes. Running on a 4070 SUPER, the framerate should soar effortlessly; however, it surprisingly falters, occasionally dipping too low for the comfort one would expect with such hardware. This inconsistency, although sporadic, is noticeable and may detract slightly from an otherwise smooth experience.Another side note, there's a lack of native support for the DualSense controller (it claims it supports it, though?). You can still use Steam Input to emulate a Xbox controllerDespite these few footnotes, this game definitely emerges triumphant as an incredibly enjoyable game that's hard not to love. Its combination of humor, style, and impeccable mechanics ensures that players will not only relish in the nostalgia but also in the fresh layers added to the classic experience. If you're ready to embrace the zany world once more, or for the first time, you're in for a remarkably fun ride.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of the OG. I was pining for a way to play it again and happened to stumble on the news that this was getting an HD remaster. I was excited. I loved the humor, the style and the way the soundtrack worked so well with the game. James Gunn's influence was clearly all over it. The combat while a bit stiff, was really fun. Graphically it was standard looking for the era, but the palette and touches made it look like a bright comic book (it directly inspired "Harley Vision, for Birds of Prey).But this port is pretty busted. There's next to no graphic options. No vsync, no frame cap, you can't pick your detail level, nothing, not even editing the settings in the ini file changes anything for me. This is a UE5 game, there's tons of options available. The frame cap is absolutely necessary because it causes the animations to look awful and cutscenes to unsync. This also affects combat. _childDocuments_.review: If you've played the original, there is nothing all that new here to gawk at. The controls are improved, there's some nice QOL fixes and the game has got a noticeable face lift (though it still looks and feels like the original). This is one of the most "just the game" remakes I've played in years. It is unapologetically Lollipop Chainsaw, down to the bad mini-bosses and janky animations. Very little was added or modified. It's not as daring as something like Mafia: Definitive Edition that changed levels and characters -- this is "the game", so don't come in expecting anything but the equivalent of an improved re-release of the original on a new engine. You'd have to be a massive Negative Nancy to find anything massively wrong with the effort done here.There's a couple bugs here that I've noticed in my short time playing that are very likely to get patched out or fixed in the coming weeks. Audio not being entirely synced with some cutscenes and some stuttering here and there (and i MEAN here and there, game runs pretty well on my rig). No graphics settings though, which is incredibly odd? The game also does not recognize my Playstation controller, showing me Xbox buttons no matter what i do. It shows Dualshock buttons in the menu, but not in the actual game. Strange.I kind of wish there were more things to say about RePOP aside from the fact that its Lollipop Chainsaw on PC, at long last! Its a good, higher definition release of the original. Not much to complain about. Funny characters, dope hack and slash gameplay... Costumes are way quicker to grind towards and are at actually reasonable prices! Wow! May actually be fun to do this time.But please, graphics settings, i beg.Bugs i've noticed:- The medal counter counts incorrectly. Your gold medals can be 250, but the game can count them as 2500 when you pick up more medals.- Some cutscenes are desynced a bit.- Shows Playstation buttons in the main menu, but only shows Xbox buttons during gameplay. Does not support PS controllers natively.- No graphics options.- Cloud saves are broken, and unfortunately do not function.- Store page claims it takes 60 GB of space, but it actually only takes 13.- It is possible to go out of bounds fighting the Killabilly by walking on his arms. Yoshimi Yasuda (the only person who marketed this release) did state very recently that these bugs would be patched very soon, so if you're very concerned about these issues, then you can just wait until said patch comes out -- which probably won't be longer than a week or two.
