_childDocuments_.review: I've waited to play this game since it first came out back in 2012 so to say I was blown away by the fact this was getting remade and re-released is an understatement.I just finished the game at the time of writing this. While I had an absolute blast this remaster is unfortunately not well optimized at all.Before I get into the problems I’d like to gush about the things I enjoyed.The game play was really fun and engaging for me personally. I always tried to learn and use any new combos I got.I thought the visuals were nicely done aside from the weird lens flare effect they had going on.The new costumes were really nice.Re pop mode with the pop art visuals instead of blood was a very cute idea.I love that they didn’t cut anything from the re-release and kept it pretty much 1 to 1 with the original release.Some of the new music tracks I thought were pretty catchy but they can never replace the originals especially in stage 3. It just isn’t the same without Dead or alive’s you spin me round.Major problems:I got off pretty lucky admittedly in that I only really had problems with stages 5 and 6 but they were damn near game breaking causing me to have to restart these stages 2 times which wasn’t great because the game penalizes you for every restart in your final ranking for the level.That makes it rather annoying when you’re trying to get the achievements for the best times on the leader board.No auto save feature. I know I’m not the only one who quit a stage thinking “I’ll be fine I’ll just pick up where I left off.” Only to then find out that I screwed myself over and had to restart the stage from the beginning.This wasn’t too big a deal in the early stages but the later ones can be over an hour if you don’t know what you’re doing and it’s frustrating.Minor problems:Some subtitles would not appear as characters spoke.Chainsaw dash wouldn’t connect with the jumping animation.Sound cut out and came back at odd times.If you buy items but don’t complete the stage you lose them.Medal counter would be wildly off at times making me think I had double the medals I actually had.No graphical settings other than resolution.With that all out of the way I would still recommend this game to those interested with some caveats:Wait for a few patches which thankfully the team is working on right now before buying. These bugs are annoying and can taint an otherwise very enjoyable gaming experience.You might want to hold off until a bigger sale comes through. While I think 40$ is pretty reasonable especially because I’ve seen OG copies go for waaay more. This game is only 5 to 7 hours depending on your skill level and willingness to get achievements. If you’ve read this far, thank you for your time. If none of this bothers you or like me you’ve been waiting 12+ years and can’t wait any longer I say get the game just know going in it’s gonna be messy but at its core this is a very fun game and I’m so beyond happy that I was finally able to play it at long last.

_childDocuments_.review: They don't make games like this anymore, which includes this remaster, you can however improve the performance by some simple config file changes , obviously still needs to be patched to work well out of the box, actually support the controllers they advertise, to run in ultrawide and fix some smaller bugs with desynced audio or missed inputs. Updated character models and animations, massively improved texture quality, unlocked framerate, optional V-Sync, and a Fidelity / Performance mode; it got everything you would expect from a proper remaster. And yes, it’s all uncensored!As with the gameplay, the story remains unchanged, written by  and . While every original Juliet costume stayed, certain licensed content from back then didn’t make it into the remaster, such as Juliet’s „“ outfit, based on Ashley J. Williams from the  franchise, or „“ outfit from . is an incredibly fun and entertaining Hack and Slash adventure, with easy-to-obtain achievements, a great soundtrack, and lots of lewd jokes and suggestive themes. The remaster embodies everything unique and fun about the original, without losing any of its glamour. I can therefore highly recommend it to anyone who loved the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Lollipop Chainsaw has that crude suggestive high-octane early 2010s vibe in the best way possible. Lots of unapologetic juvenile humor as well but done in a fun manner representative of the time this originally launched. It runs well, and seems faithful to the original aside from parts of the OST because of how much licensed stuff was in the OG release.  This has gotten a bit of a nice visual face lift with the graphics and HUD/UI elements.I played little a bit of this many moons ago on PS3 when my friend lent me his copy, but never finished it and had to return it. So I’m using this opportunity to enjoy this gem now. When I think of this game my mind immediately goes to when Jessica Nigri became a niche pop culture icon in what was the “nerd” space at the time by winning that cosplay competition portraying Juliet in 2012.There’s literally no performance settings menu and you have to mess with the .ini file (After digging around deep into your AppData folders) to do a bit of the adjustments yourself with what’s available. The only thing you can really change in-game is the display resolution as far as the visual experience is concerned. Not even options for frame caps or being able to turn on or off vsync lol. This should really be in the game menu or at minimum a dedicated settings launch config program like with some of the “passable” PC ports ala No More Heroes. Maybe consider waiting and checking the the store page for updates if they change things (If this is an absolute deal breaker for you). It seems like they're , no timeline yet of when they'll be addressing the handful of things they need to work on.Fellow Deckers you'll need to go into your AppData folder in your Home disk, and find the UserGameSettings.ini to make graphical tweaks. Stock settings makes this unplayable, but you can make it run reliably well by making some adjustments there since there's no dedicated in-game performance menu yet.Frame Limit - 60fps w/ 50fps for extra power savings, 30fps if in 720pTDP Limit - 12, off if in 720pScaling Filter - FSR, Slider MaxedIn-game, display resolution set to 1024 x 576 (for more FPS), 1200x720 (For more Fidelity)Within the 'GamerUserSettings.ini' file under the [ScaleabilityGroups] section right below 'sg.ResolutionQuality=100' change all other listed quality settings from 3 to 1 (Adjust to your liking I have Effects & Textures at 2)In some rare cases usually in transitions/QTE segments and certain cutscenes the fps can tank a bit, but it usually shoots back up immediately afterwards like at the very beginning of the prologue for example.

_childDocuments_.review: A True Return to Classic Gaming - Pure Fun, Sexy, and UncensoredRating: 8.5/10It’s rare these days to find a game that just focuses on being, well, fun. LOLLIPOP CHAINSAW RePOP brings back that feeling of playing games for the sake of adventure, without the need for forced political messages or trendy social commentary. On top of that, this game isn’t afraid to push the envelope where it matters—it’s sexy, uncensored, and completely unapologetic about it. It doesn't cater to the sanitized, over-regulated approach we often see in today's AAA titles. Instead, it embraces freedom in its design and content.As a gaming community, we have the power to send a message. The success of games like "Black Myth: Wukong" shows that there’s a massive audience for this kind of experience. We’re tired of AAA developers assuming we want to be lectured or coddled. We vote with our wallets, and games like this prove that we, the players, hold the power to shape the future of the industry. If we keep supporting bold, unapologetic games like this one, it’ll teach the big developers a lesson: give us the freedom to enjoy games the way we want, not the way they think we should.

_childDocuments_.review: This game put a grin on my face from start to finish. Fun, over the top, doesn't take itself seriously and doesn't try to send any message.The gameplay is very similar to most hack'n'slash of the time. Over the course of the game, you'll learn combos that use a combinaison of up to three button. Given the length of the game, I don't think it needs more that that.The story and characters are where the game shines for me. The voice acting is excellent and the humor and dialogs are so over the top, it's a breath of fresh air in a time where every piece of media has to further someone's agenda. I would also like to thank the man of culture who did all the camera work in the cutscenes.Sadly, some of the original sound tracks are missing. If you have never played the original, it probably won't be an issue at all. Otherwise, I would recommend modding them back in.Regarding the remaster itself, I would say that the game plays more or less exactly like the original. The graphics have been improved for 4K, though it would have been nice if the textures could have been improved a bit more. They are pretty average during close ups. The voices audio quality is another point I wish could have been improved, but this is most likely due to the original recordings not being as high quality as what we have today. In terms of performance, I did not have any issue running this at 120fps, but it will heavily depend on your hardware.I definitely recommend this game and hopefully, we'll get more like this in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to be very honest here. This game is a childhood favorite of mine, and I would have given anything to be able to play it again since I sold my Xbox 360. And I have been waiting for this game for yeaaaars. Nothing will convince me not to support this game. The art style is immaculate, the music is fun, and Juliet is back again for some kick-ass zombie-slaying fun! Plus, they kept the achievement to look up her skirt, the highlight of the game clearly. If you are a fan, and would like to support the devs, highly recommend it, I was squealing the whole time I have played it and will be booting it up to play more tomorrow. I will be getting the 100% no matter what.Edit: I have now 100% the game. Now that I have, I wanted to come back and add some finer points. As a game, I wish that it would actually have proper save points within the stages, and that you didn't need to fully just quit out of the game to be able to continue a session. Additionally, for the time attack mode, I understand the whole "dying resets you in a stage" thing. Not a problem with clearing it, but it was a pain to set aside the time to do it all in one sitting since when I closed out halfway through the first time, it made me restart entirely anyway. There are also quite a few sound bugs in the game, most notably, when the sound increases by like 100% in the stage battle with Zed. When he starts throwing a bunch of words at you right before you are about to kill him, the sound blasts hard enough to make you wince. Aside from these things, I loved that they made the achievements more streamlined, and I am still ecstatic I was able to get and play one of my favorite games from my childhood. Some great, silly fun with some kicka** fighting moves from Juliet, and cheesy, funny dialogue.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one to say I recommend. I was hopeful this would run well on Steam Deck, and it doesn't. It runs fine at locked 30FPS sub-720p. There are no Cloud Saves either, so I can't even start playing on Deck and move to my Desktop to pick up where I left off.That said, it looks AMAZING, the visuals are so much better than the original. The game play is tight and the sound design is fantastic. Everything feels super well put together. The wonky launch on Steam is a minor thing to consider, but all around, this has been a great launch for a classic hack and slash game. Yes, some things are not in the game that were there in the original, this is an issue of licences. If you're mad about licensed music being swapped out, that isn't censorship or an issue. Yes, they could have tried to get the music licensed again, but that's not always possible or easy to do.Overall, Lollipop Chainsaw RePOP is a good game. It has some issues, but they're minor on a grand scale of things. No microtransactions. No scummy DRM. There aren't any graphics options unfortunately. Some songs aren't in RePOP that were in the original. QTEs are sometimes buggy at lower FPS settings.It's an 8/10. I would advise not getting it to play on Steam Deck right now, but otherwise, it's decent.For those who are wondering, yes, the classic "I Swear! _childDocuments_.review: LOLLIPOP CHAINSAW RePOP is a delightful well made remaster that offers both a uncensored original Mode (what I recommend) and a censored new mode specifically made for weak people who can't stand blood and nudity or content creators and live streamers who are forced to censorship their playthrough.The gameplay is very fun brutal and the humor is dark, bloody, sexual and absolutely spot on. The game is not the longest but if you are a completionist it will take over 15 maybe even 20 hours for sure but if you just want to rush through the story, you can finish the game in about 8 hours.I will now list the pros and cons of LOLLIPOP CHAINSAW RePOP:Pros:Fun hack and slash gameplayUncensored (what is important for a game like this)Humor spot on (you will laugh for sure)No micro transaction (all costumes, gallery, abilities, music can be unlocked through playing the game)Cons:Maybe slightly too short for "some people" the game is around 8 hours (story mode) and 15-20 hours if you want to get everything.The performance is very bad (I hope they can fix it), look up performance on YouTube before you buy it.Overall an amazing game and in my opinion well worth even the 40$/€ asking price, this game is a 8/10 for me and if you are a men of culture who wants to have some zombie hack and slash fun, then this game is perfect for you!

_childDocuments_.review: You'll have a blast, but question your sanity along the way.Lollipop Chainsaw RePOP brings back the over-the-top, zombie-slaying action with a heavy dose of humor and style. If you played the original, this version keeps the spirit alive.What I Loved:Juliet's Array of Costumes: There were so many cute ones to choose from! I ended up wearing the OG & Samurai Costumes the most throughout the game.Fun Combat: The hack-and-slash gameplay still feels satisfying. Whether you’re using a chainsaw or unleashing combo attacks, it’s a chaotic blast, especially with the unique enemy designs.Art Style & Visuals:  The vibrant colors and comic book-inspired effects look sharper than ever.Humor & Dialogue: The game is unapologetically silly and embraces its campy vibe. Juliet’s one-liners and the absurd situations she finds herself in give the game personality.Soundtrack: It’s packed with catchy tunes that complement the action and quirky mood. It’s an excellent mix of pop, rock, and metal that keeps the energy high.What Could Be Better:Technical Issues: Unfortunately, the game had some crashes due to memory leaks. This was a bit frustrating, especially when trying to stream the game.Audio Issues: There are noticeable problems with the audio levels. Sometimes it’s far too quiet, and other times, it blasts unexpectedly.Camera Issues: There are moments where the camera can be a bit frustrating, especially during hectic combat scenes or in tight spaces.Overall Thoughts:If you're in the mood for a fast-paced, colorful hack-and-slash adventure that doesn’t take itself too seriously, Lollipop Chainsaw RePOP will deliver hours of fun. Just know that its charm lies in its absurdity, and if that’s your thing, you’re in for a wild ride!

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the original Lollipop Chainsaw, I was beyond excited to dive into Lollipop Chainsaw Repop, and let me just say, it does not disappoint! This remastered version beautifully captures everything I loved about the original while giving it a fresh coat of paint.First and foremost, all of the humor, craziness, and over-the-top fun that made the original a cult classic is still here in full force. Juliet is back and as charming and badass as ever, slicing through hordes of zombies with her trusty chainsaw while cracking jokes and delivering sass like no other. The game’s unique blend of hack-and-slash action and tongue-in-cheek humor still holds up and feels even more polished with updated visuals.Speaking of the visuals, the remastered graphics are a huge step up. Everything from the vibrant colors to the fluid character animations has been enhanced, making the game feel more modern without losing that quirky, arcade-style charm. The environments and enemies look crisper, and the iconic over-the-top zombie-slaying action pops off the screen in the best way possible.I also love how the developers kept the original's essence intact. They didn’t mess with what made Lollipop Chainsaw special: the fun combat, hilarious dialogue, and absolutely bonkers storyline. The boss battles are still as creative and fun as I remember, and it’s so satisfying to chain together combos while zombies explode into rainbows. Plus, the soundtrack, which was a standout in the original, is still just as killer!If you loved the original, Lollipop Chainsaw Repop is a nostalgic trip that nails it. And if you’re new to the game, now is the perfect time to jump in and experience one of the most uniquely fun, quirky, and downright hilarious zombie games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: So Lollipop Chainsaw. I've been waiting 12 f*cking years for this coming to pc and hell I'm glad it did. LOLLIPOP CHAINSAW RePOP is a remaster of the 2012 zombie slasher with the same name. And yeah, it's a James Gunn game. The RePOP version includes both the original (playable in resolutions up to 4K) and the remastered. You can decide which of the versions you want to play in the main menu. The following review is only about the original mode, since I've not played the RePOP mode yet. I will update the review and add another section where I will talk about the remastered version. So as you've just read, in the case you're actually able to do that, this part of the review is only talking about the original version which is basically the 2012 OG game. I've played the game with an GTX1660 Super OC and it ran without problems. So if you're like me and you don't run the newest or strongest hardware, you should be definitly able to play the OG version at least. The game is mostly unchanged from the 2012 version. I've played the game as a kid shortly after it got released together with my brother and his roommate on an XBOX360. The game blew my 10 or 11 year old mind. It was not the first violent game I've played, since my brother raised me with Quake 3, Silent Hill and other more violent video games, also I've got a couple of hours in Team Fortress 2 already. Though the violence in this game was something completely new to me. This was back then the most violent videogame I've had played before, which looking back is kinda funny, since the game really wasn't as violent as I remembered it to be. Well afterwards I did everything to get my hands on this game. There were a few problems though, first I knew the game but not the name and it took me some time to figure, just to find out that the game never got released on PC and that a physical copy of the game would be around 150€ + the cost of and outdated console, which I'm never gonna use in the first place. Well so I've tried RPCS3, which in case you don't know, is a Playsation 3 emulator. I got it to run actually but it crashed a lot, I've had like 10 FPS and the controls were ♥♥♥♥♥♥, even with controller. The experience was so bad that I quit the game before it even started, praying that the game would get a PC port. I've been writing in the comment section of the youtube trailers that they should please remake the game for computer, and now, just a couple of years later we actually finally got this. _childDocuments_.review: ❤️❤️🤍🤍🤍This is a mediocre game by any standard. Let’s keep expectations realistic. If you’re looking for a game where you can turn off your brain, put on a bikini, and slay some zombies, this game has you covered. It’s classic, dumb fun, and that’s perfectly okay. Although the game originally came out in 2012, its design philosophy feels and plays closer to something from an even earlier era.Part of the appeal for me is the combination of cute and edgy into this horror-pop style they’re aiming for. However, the art style doesn’t quite sell it as well as it could. A more cel-shaded approach might have better suited their vision, but what do I know.The game proudly wears its B-horror influence on its sleeve. The vibrant and lively cheerleader protagonist clashes against the lumbering undead zombies, reminiscent of a Strippers vs. Zombies movie. If the cheerleader outfit isn’t your style, you can opt for a more edgy alt-girl look, or something else entirely. There are many other outfits you can acquire in the game, but unfortunately, you can’t change outfits mid-stage. You must do so from the map screen, and since each level takes about an hour to beat, you’re unlikely to see most of them. A mid-game outfit switch and a randomization option would have been welcome additions.This remaster features an uncensored original mode and a stylized RePOP mode where blood is replaced by sparkles and cutesy effects. In my opinion, calling the original mode “uncensored” does the game a disservice.Because, in terms of marketing terminology, it makes it sound like RePOP was somehow censored. Without delving into the semantics of what came first—the censorship-chicken or the censorship-egg—the fact is that the original Japanese release had reduced blood and gore, and the decapitations were altered. So, I’d actually say RePOP is closer to the original Japanese version rather than censored.In RePOP mode, they haven’t altered any sexy animations, toned down any outfits, or censored any dialogue as far as I could tell. However, before you buy the game to “own the libs” or whatever (hey, it’s your money, you do you!), know that there are some glaring problems with the game. The developers have been releasing patches, which is a good sign. Unfortunately, at the time of this review, there are still some issues with the remaster. Hopefully, remaining bugs will be addressed in future updates.The game worked fine the first time I played it, but the second time, I got a black screen when I tried to launch it. I had to mess around and try different launch options to make it work, which isn’t user-friendly.During the stage 5 boss fight, I encountered a graphical glitch where the entire screen, except for HUD elements, turned white, making the fight unplayable. I had to restart the fight. The bug thankfully didn’t repeat itself, but it was still annoying since it’s a very long fight.I also noticed some zombies spawning in and floating a few feet off the ground, which looks unpolished.The release also has issues with audio. In one instance, the chainsaw sound got stuck and repeated continuously. In another instance, the dialogue that played during a cutscene repeated itself a few seconds later. There are also some leveling issues with some dialogue sounding too quiet, some too loud, and some like it’s recorded in an echoing airplane hangar. Lip syncing seems to be in Japanese if you play it in English. Oh, and they didn’t get the rights for the original soundtrack, so there’s that too. It’s all over the place, really. The camera can be a bit wonky at times, especially when using the lock-on feature, and might actually cause you to fail a few sequences because of how it’s implemented. Speaking of, the current checkpoint system is also awful. While you’re playing, it’s fine—sure, some saves are a bit rough—but the problem is that if you exit the game while playing a level, you need to replay the whole level. Each level takes about an hour to complete, so if you have to stop playing while you’re almost at the end, get ready to play the whole thing again.Then there are some mechanics that just haven’t aged well. In one of the early levels, you’re introduced to a “chainsaw dash” mechanic. You need to use it to boost yourself over ramps, but you can only do so with a running start to first build up speed, and turning feels too stiff. It just feels awkward and I didn’t find it to be as fun as it could be.Other mechanics that I disliked were present during boss fights. I didn’t like how it wasn’t possible to hurt the bosses even though I was hitting them with the chainsaw. Only being able to damage them when the game lets you, even though you clearly should be damaging them, just feels bad.The dialogue was cringeworthy to me. This game has a similar try-hard humor to games like Borderlands. It’s loud, obnoxious, over-the-top, irreverent, and juvenile. Basically, you can expect eccentric potty humor with sexual innuendos, exaggerated stereotypes, and an overall carefree, light-hearted, and satirical take on the zombie theme. That said, do keep in mind that I generally don’t vibe with “comedy” content. I’m not really the target audience when it comes to humor.One thing that surprised me was how artistically they handled some of the stereotypes. For example, the first boss is a punk rocker summoned by a goth, and the second boss is a corpse-painted black metal Viking. It shows that the developers actually put some thought and effort into learning about the various subcultures you’d find in old high school cliques, even while making fun of absolutely all of it. I can respect that.There are also some dated social media references, a product of its time for sure. It kind of reminded me of that old saying—the more things change, the more they stay the same.Regardless, I still had a fairly positive experience with the game, issues be damned. They didn’t keep me from finishing the game. This is an edgy throwback to earlier gaming eras, and I recommend it if you’re feeling burned out on safe and disingenuous modern releases. That is, if you temper your expectations. And maybe wait for a few patches and the price to come down.

_childDocuments_.review: So let me open this review by saying I'm a huge hack n slash fan, huge zombie fan, I love campy fun stuff like games like this! I played the ps3 version only a couple of years ago, the game had smooth and fun combat, everything was super responsive. I had a lot of fun and enjoyment out of that game ya know? After playing 3 hours of this game over the span of 2 days, I have.... a lot I want to say! Even more so because I think most if not all the reviews about this game on steam are BS right now.1. This game 'remaster' yes its a remaster. Sucks ass. The controls can be super unresponsive, combat feels worse and more sluggish as inputs take longer to press. Despite having a ps3 port it uses xbox buttons? The QTE's don't even ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ work as I can press the wrong button or sit there and it does it for me! 2. The graphics some how feel worse than the original. While this game has 'better graphics' the loading screens are super pixelated for some odd reason, textures in the game flicker in and out, the camera can easily be glitched out so many times. Certain items load in way too fast, or way too slow. Sometimes things don't even load in properly. This game feels like its held together by duct tape most if not all the time. 3. The voice acting is worse? I think, I don't know if they reused the same lines or not, but there's a ♥♥♥♥ ton of lines that repeat over and over again at certain sections. I chalk that up to glitches. But the audio quality is somehow worse? Like it feels like a lot of these lines were recorded on a phone or not properly ported and they just feel.... meh audio wise. Also doesn't help that most of not all the sound effects in game are delayed so much, its like im running this on below min specs with how delayed everything is....4. Glitches! Man this game has so many more glitches in it, so many in-fact that the game is nearly impossible to play (not unless you get lucky) The Hippie boss currently has a glitch that makes her well... UNKILLABLE! Yep she just freezes mid air, no bubble, can't take damage. You have to reset..... Which becomes an issues when she spawns more versions of herself.... that it can happen too. Its random too!!! Augh On-top of that I've gotten stuck on small ledges, invisible walls and other ♥♥♥♥ that I've had to glitch out of.5. Soundtrack. Okay so there was a bunch of drama when this game first got started bc people wanted the og soundtrack. Which sure is great. But.... who cares? The new music is good, anyone who says otherwise is a weird music snob. Cause the new stuff sounds fine.... Maybe instead of paying like 50% of the budget to get half of the old songs back, they could have ya know.... made a good port? Cause who cares if the music is a 8/10 or a 9/10 if the game can't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ work, run proper, or be.... enjoyable?To wrap things up this is a horrible port, and quite frankly I think the 'anti-censorship' crowd kinda played their hand in ruining this game. All that most of the reviews talk about is 'censor-ship' and how this game isn't censored or whatever. Cool we can see a barley legal girl's tits jump around and panty shots, too bad the port doesn't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ work most of the time. Maybe if the devs had stopped worrying about the whole anti-censorship thing, and the album ♥♥♥♥ and worked truly worked on it. We would have had a great port! But we don't, we have a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ half under-baked port that doesn't even work. I bet you 20 bucks a year or two from now this game will get enough updates so that it can properly work. augh why can't devs release games that are fully complete, I mean come on this game us like only 5 hours long....IMPORTANT: Do you actually wanna play this fun campy cult classic with charming characters, fun combat, and well just a good game? Buy the 360/ps3 version and play it on your ps4/xbox one. No I'm serious, not only will you have a better and more enjoyable time playing it. But you won't have to worry about glitches. Hell I'm sure there's another way to play it on pc that some how can edit the graphics and frame-rate to make it more modern without the glitches of this port! idk if there is a way, but who knows! _childDocuments_.review: The game is by all accounts very well remastered. I can't find any faults in performance or general playability. I haven't experienced any stuttering or crashes. The only bugs I've encountered have been UI related: the Options menu key remapping showing keyboard keys when I'm using a controller and have selected the "Controller" option before entering the remapping sub-menu. The game also looks good, as good as a remaster of a 12-year-old game can look.Visually I'm pleased with the game. I'm all for fan service, T&A and sexiness in video games and personally I don't require there to be some great philosophy behind showing some skin. It's absolutely okay to have skimpy clothes and revealing armors in video games without there being some sort of subverting message to justify the choices. And Lollipop Chainsaw certainly offers plenty to look at. It practically revels in it. And I'm there for all of it.On the other hand, gameplay-wise the game lacks quite a lot. The camera isn't particularly good at following the action. Many times it gets to a point where it bumps against a wall, limiting the field of view. The combat controls are "sticky", some actions feel like Juliet is stuck in completing the animations (non-cancellable animations are a pain in otherwise fast-paced action games).Sometimes attacks that seem to be meant for single targets affects multiple targets around the intended target. Other attacks that previously did damage in an arc, can suddenly phase through enemies at random, leaving Juliet open for their attacks - which then put Juliet in a stun state that can be escaped only by jumping. Enemies can also cancel Juliet's attacks stunning her while Juliet can't cancel the same attacks that the enemies use. If you have a scenario where both characters start attacking each other at the same time, Juliet will always lose and get stunned.Combos are sometimes unreliable. You can press the exact same button combinations and sometimes Juliet does the intended combo, sometimes she does another combo and sometimes she just does a set of basic attacks.Overall, I don't see Lollipop Chainsaw as a very good character action game. It is serviceable and its "score" is elevated by the visuals and the cheesecake. Without the cake, the game would be a lot less memorable and most likely would have reviewed worse during its original release and now.And as much as I like the cheesecake, I can't recommend the game. If you are here for Juliet in all of her glory, you can find footage of here all over the internet. If you are here for the gameplay, I think you can choose a better option.I would like to add, though, that none of my criticism is against the developers of the remaster. As far as I know, they excelled on all aspects and delivered a good product. The product's contents just happens to be kinda jank.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: 7/10Story: 9/10Graphics: 8/10Replay Value: 6/10Content Depth: 7/10Voice Acting: 10/10Sound Design: 9/10Mods Improvement: +0.2 to overall scoreOverall Score: 8.2/10Gameplay: The game play on normal difficulty feels balanced and nothing feels that off (though some combos feel like they should connect with more enemies than they actually do). On higher difficulties, however, the cracks in the combat system start to show. Some enemies seem to spam unavoidable and uninterruptible attacks that cause hard knockdown. Not a fan of that. I do like the re-balanced shop mode that lets you get the full move-list faster than the original game. I also like the option to auto complete quick-time events.Story: I liked the story. It is over the top and absurd with wacky characters. Is it deep? No. Is it fun? Yes. I appreciate nothing seems to be censored from the original game unlike most remasters and remakes that come out nowadays.Graphics: As far as remasters go, I have mixed opinions on it. I like being able to choose between Original and RePop modes (I have only played in Original however). The game's performance could definitely be better. I have a fairly good PC and I have had frame rate instability issues though it has gotten better since release. I also don't like some of the menu and interface changes they made to this release though I installed mods that fix this.Replay Value: This is the weakest part of this game IMO. For a game that seems to be set up to replay levels to get a better score, why can't I skip 80% of the cinematics? It gets annoying for trying to speed-run levels. The developers should really add the option to skip all cut scenes on repeat playthroughs. There are at least incentives to replay the game on higher difficulties.Content Depth: I am kind of torn on this. There is a good amount of bonus stuff to unlock and the game's campaign doesn't overstay its welcome. I appreciate they added new unlockables compared to the original game to offset some of the licensed bonus content from the original that had to be left out.Voice Acting: Top tier acting all around. Goes well with the ludicrous story.Sound Design: The unmodded game has a decent replacement soundtrack from the original but. thankfully, it is pretty easy to mod in the original game's soundtrack which really is how the game should be experienced.Mods: There are a decent number of mods out there to either add to the experience or restore the game closer to its original form.In Summary: Do I recommended this game? Yes...but unless you are a fan of the original or really want a 7th gen game experience I wouldn't pay full price. I bought this game day one and haven't regretted it but I also own and have played through the original.

No up skirt screenshots, while also making it less likely to make yourself motion sick.but they also have bikini costumes you can purchase for said character, while also having stuff like a samurai outfit that ehhhh not so sure on chief. IT is certainly a product of its time. A bit of cringe, But fun cringe. Embraces sexiness, without allowing too much objectifying As alluded to earlier It has the classic ability for you to unlock costumes/skins by purchasing them in the store with in-game currency.No micro transactions, no pre-order bonus crap, Just a game. It's a remaster/port, Not a remake. Just stuff meant to be fun, not to milk every dollar they can from you. Some of the mechanics haven't been modernized as well, while some haven't. They are trying their best to maintain a balance.I played this upon first release, definitely a bit more buggy then i care for. To the point there was some enemies missing, dialogue missing and npc’s. Nothing that is noticeable except while doing a second play through with it being more fleshed out and patched now. Still not a %100 there, but much better than it was. Except with steam overlay enabled, it breaks the game now? You have to actively click in the window after launch or it'll boot and stick to a black screen (at least using my nvidia machine). Some of the cutscenes (used to) lag a bit, This is because their rendering in real time vs pre-rendering. A LOT of loading screens and sometimes the picture for the loading screen (used to) distort. Repeating dialogue during certain moments, to the point it gets a bit annoying. This is a game that struggles a tad with its history, on one hand they really seemed to care about preserving the game as it was, a product of its time. While repop mode seems to be adjusting things to be less bloody at least, it also stands strongly on not censoring inappropriate dialogue for some reason? Considering the gore censoring it’s an odd stance, they could have at least censored that bit of hate speech in repop mode,it was an offhand remark not even in a cut scene. But there has been an outpouring of fans of the original title. Pleading them to not censor it in any way, even the original devs chiming in not wanting that to happen. Kind of surprising it'll be released on the switch with that included, I would like to see a disclaimer saying “a product of its time and does not reflect our current views and beliefs” it would hit a good middle ground i feel. It's a rock and a hard place for them to be in and I respect them for committing to preserving the game as it was. Though it is kinda sidetracked by the re-pop mode, its whole thing is to make it more stream friendly (excessive blood can cause monetization issues). But why not take the hate speech out in re-pop mode if that's the goal? I’m mixed on recommending the game, due to bugginess, the slight bit of casual hate speech (again was a product of its time,so eh) but I also understand that they want to preserve it as it was. I also understand fans didn’t want it to be bastardized like some pieces can be.  It’s weird

_childDocuments_.review: As a first-time player of Lollipop Chainsaw, I can confidently say it delivers a unique experience that few other games can match. The writing is comedic, though undeniably dated—its humor is steeped in 2000s American pop culture references, so players who are familiar with that era will get the most out of it. That said, some jokes haven't aged well, but thankfully, the solid gameplay makes up for it.Unlocking all moves and fully upgrading Juliet by the end of the game feels satisfying, and while the combat isn't as deep or layered as something like Nier Automata, it offers enough variety to keep slashing through zombies and bosses engaging and fun. The simplicity of the mechanics works in the game's favor, making it accessible without feeling too repetitive.In terms of replayability, the game doesn't offer much beyond the first playthrough, but I still think it’s worth the experience. Coming into this port, I expected a rough release, especially considering the issues seen in other remasters like Dead Rising, but I was pleasantly surprised by how smoothly it runs. However, it's disappointing that there aren't any significant graphical enhancements or the original licensed music, and for that reason, the $45 price tag feels a bit steep. It would be far more reasonable at $20, considering the game’s length and lack of upgrades. I completed it in about seven hours, including breaks, so if you’re on the fence, I’d recommend waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Back in 2012, I was very excited for the original release of this game. At the time, I was a semi-regular at Gamestop -- enough so that the staff decided to hold back several pieces of their promotional display and material for the game to give to me (and that I still have), including a large poster (that I could have even gotten signed by Jessica Nigri, Tara Strong, and Michael Rosenbaum, had I paid more attention to the guests at the local conventions). The reason I'm doing a food blog backstory is to drive home a simple fact: And while I'm giving it a thumbs up, I had to think long and hard about whether to choose it or a thumb down. Let me explain.The original game was...rough around the edges. Hardly unplayable, but neither was it polished. In 2012, the difference between this product and a higher-quality game wasn't all that far off from each other, at least not to today's standards.RePOP, sadly, feels exactly like the 2012 game. Actually, it feels  in some ways. Though it certainly looks better, it also makes you feel like you're trying to play a 12-year-old PC game on a modern computer and operating system -- it just gets.... The graphics are not 2024 graphics...they're from 2012, just a bit cleaner.On multiple occasions, voice lines are repeated over and over again, usually with the flavor lines Nick spouts. Some examples include during Zombie Baseball, he repeats his one-liners constantly, or on the farm, when he repeats the same line about the rocks getting "too close" after every single rock. But while this could just be due to poorly-programmed triggers, there are other instances too, such as the audio from a phone call playing in the background again a full minute or two after you finished the phone call. To be fair, Dragami has acknowledged some of this and said it'll be taken care of in a future patch, so by the time you play it, this paragraph may not even be a factor anymore.My biggest issue though, and also one of the lesser salient ones, has to do with the changes to the music. I get that re-licensing songs isn't always the easiest thing, but over the years when I've told people about Lollipop Chainsaw, my fondest memories of the original game were the tractor sequences, specifically due to how ridiculous it was to run over zombies in a combine to the tune of Dead or Alive's . The entire moment was forever seared in my mind with a degree of surreal ridiculousness that I've always remembered. . Other background songs, ones that I think were actually written for the original game, are also replaced for some reason. The music is NOT as memorable as it originally was, unfortunately.I'm focusing on the negatives. This is still a fun, silly little zombie-bashing romp, with cute one-liners and a ridiculous premise. Unlockables aren't hidden behind a world-ending grind or DLC paywall, and I was able to unlock everything within the span of two complete playthroughs. There are plenty of silly costumes, so it shouldn't be too hard to find a favorite.This game shouldn't be taken all that seriously. It's a pretty good time. But if I had to be completely honest, it's not a $45 good time. I don't think RePOP did enough to warrant the full asking price. So grab it on sale for $25 or less, run through it once or twice, and just plan to kick back and have a good time when you do. It's good, silly fun, and sometimes that's all we need to have a good day.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original, so I'll review this game as its own thing.The StoryThe pot of this game is straightforward and simple. Juliet is late for school on her birthday. Luckily for her, the teachers have all likely been eaten by a zombie outbreak at the school. It's up to Juliet to chainsaw them to oblivion and meet up with her boyfriend. The two of the set out on a quest to stop an even bigger threat with Juliet at the helm and Nick, Juliet's boyfriend, as her bodyless partner using all sorts of crazy movies and items. The GraphicsThe game is pure carnage! It feels like a Bayonetta game with how much there is to show... the combat I mean. The combat is pretty deep, and the animations are there to show the different ways you have available to kill zombies. It clearly looks like a PS3 game with better image quality and performance. It is not devoid of issues, however, as you may encouter some bugs. I did not find a bug that crashes the game, but when you fight the hippy boss, there is a bug that prevents you from progressing to the next stage if you attack the bubble too fast. I had to restart from last checkpoint. And let's not forget the outfits. Juliet has a whole wardrobe of outfits that she can wear once unlocked. Don't worry though, she covers herself when you try to look up her skirt. I found that out when trying to look up the sky... no, really!EnjoymentThe game is fun. It is one of those types of game you just want to turn your brain off and let things just fly in front of you. Some stuff is creative while others are just annoying. I had a lot of fun unlocking new attack combos and simply hacking away at enemies. I had forgotten how much fun this kind of simplicity was from the old days.Would I recommend?Yes, I would recommend, though keep in mind this game has got some fanservice. I mean, Juliet's neck is exposed throughout the whole game. It is a very linear game with little deviation from the main path. Both Juliet and Nick are likable characters, specially Nick who keeps an eye on Juliet's behind and is pretty much the only characters with normal common sense in the game. There is also zombies, evil wizards, and world domination plans. If you are the type who needs a serious type of game, then this is not for you. Do not take this game seriously, and you will like it a lot more.

_childDocuments_.review: Port is messy and the game in general is a licensing nightmare with missing songs and replaced voice actors. Luckily mods can address most of these issues. And personally I found locking my fps to 60 in the nvidia control panel fixed a lot of weird issues that the game was having. Given the time of release and the tendency of Japanese developers to tie game logic to framerate at the time it's fair to say some animations and mechanics are messed up as they are running too fast. Vanquish on PC had this issue when it was first ported and it was from roughly that same xbox360/ps3 era for example. So, this should either be patched or the game should just come locked at 60fps.All this said however, it is still delightful to once again control everyone's favorite bubbly blonde zombie hunter - who has been unofficially modded into more games on pc than anyone could count. Finally in her own game on PC!Like most of Suda51's games it is a little rough around the edges but contains a lot of passion, fun, good ideas, and an overall enticing aesthetic presentation that you really won't get anywhere else. In other words, don't expect the combat depth of devil may cry (it's still fun just not super deep). But do expect a fun and fully realized b-movie turned into a videogame. Lots of swearing, blood, and of course as Nick's head is latched onto the back of Juliet's skirt plenty of convenient up-skirt camera shots. And please make sure you mod the original music back in as it really helps paint the full picture of the era in american culture that this is trying to emulate.Price may be a bit steep for those who are not either existing LC or Suda fans - so if you're critical about time value to money ratio perhaps wait for a sale. This game is a ton of fun and a cult classic for a reason, it just offers a unique and memorable romp that never takes itself too seriously. Some of the culture and discourse around this game's re-release could benefit by doing the same tbh. Everyone just have fun and chill out.

I never thought anything would happen. I even tried running an emulator to play it on the computer but never got it to work. When I finally came across an article on my phone saying Lollipop Chainsaw was getting remaster I about ♥♥♥♥ my pants. I was so excited. I keep checking every day on Dragami Games and Yasuda's Twitter accounts until I finally got a Twitter account to have notifications when they post. I was here a little before the setback from 2023 until the present day when it was released.Pros:-I love the port to modern consoles. (Pc, Switch, PS5/4, Xbox One, X/S)-I love the updated graphics. (4k, 60 fps)-New and old costumes returning.-Nothing cut out or censored.*-Appreciate lower price for a "brand new game."*-Complete transparency/updates on Twitter before launch.*-Faster movement/combo mechanic.-MOVEABLE CAMERA!*Cons:-Licensed songs couldn't be ported for legal reasons.*-Buying items, upgrades, costumes, etc. felt way too easy.*-Zombies/bosses felt like they were turned up a notch.*-Can no longer "earn" family costumes by clearing Dad's score.-Marketing for the game felt lackluster.*-Glitches and bugs. (Eventually things will get fixed.)-I hate the one picture they kept for a lot of the loading screens/Only seen a couple of loading screens for a second now.**Noticed a couple of small things i.e. pilot dude in the prologue doesn't say "Jesus God!! Get off me, you bastard!! Oh ♥♥♥♥! Tell my wife I lo-." before crashing. Don't know why they cut it and why they haven't talked about any of that.*Traditional games nowadays are $60 and they could've easily put the price to that but instead set it to $44.99 (S40.99 if you bought before release or up to two weeks after release on Steam.) Eventually it will also probably get great deals months to come.*I appreciate so much for the developer Yasuda working on this project with so much love and effort and complete transparency to us die-hard fans to keep up to date with the news/updates on the progress leading up to release. Not a lot of developers/companies do this and wish they did more.*For the love of god I would hate the original version with the x over the camera because I couldn't move my camera angle pretty much the majority of the game and now being able to freely 99% of the time is a godsend. One of my favorite things they added to this game. Thank you!*I understood when they said to be able to keep Lollipop Chainsaw around for the future of the game to not renew licensed songs because of legal fees which is why the original after 5 years they said wasn't distributed after that but glad there is a thing called mods.*With the update of getting more medals it just felt way too easy to earn and spend in the shop. I upgraded Juliet on stage 3 or 4 fully when the original I beat the game and had to play the prologue again to finish the last upgrade for her. First play-through of Repop I had all costumes, upgrades, hair colors, and BGM with no problem.*I noticed playing on EASY first playthrough the zombies would slap you around constantly repeatedly like they are chained together one after the other after the other. Felt you got hit 5 to 7 times before you could get a hit in. It felt hard to leapfrog out of a group of them. The firefighters, football athletes, cops, etc. zombies felt like their abilities winded up too quickly all at the same time so I constantly went down and had to get back up. Also noticed bosses like Zed for example I would go up to him and clearly hit him with the chainsaw but it wouldn't register or he would constantly dodge my attacks until he hit me again as well as the speakers I could see the chainsaw mark on the speaker but it wouldn't get cut till I hit them again for each one till that part was done. Felt like that with a lot of the bosses where you had to get "cheap shots" on them till their health went low while waiting for them to throw their attacks or avoid being touched.*Marketing on this game was solely as far as I'm aware on their Twitter also YouTube when they announced the release date, some gameplay, and the official release. They didn't do much to show more gameplay or cutscenes on YouTube for the videos to keep it interesting just one fight or two just showing it repeatedly while showing text on screen till the video was done. There was also one video that made it seem like a scary movie from music to the screen filter choice just to show how it actually is which I thought was weird.*I love the faster loading times don't get me wrong but doing so took away more of the comic strip art style from those loading screens. The tip bar is no longer a thing, they only show maybe 4 or 5 max from the original game for a second or two then it's gone. Hate they also added this one drawing that has been advertised on the website and Twitter now it's the main picture on the loading screen and fills the remaining loading screens with instead of any new drawings or the old drawings for god sake. It is repetitive.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool simple Action Slasher where you Slay Zombies as a hot cheerleader.Cutscenes and dialogue are wacky and fun in a good way.It doesn't come off as particularly high-budget, but that's fine because it exudes its own B movie charm.You save the world from the Zombie apocalypse as Juliet Starling in her cheerleader outfit wielding a Chainsaw by beating differently themed Zombified manifestations of music genres (Punk, Metal, Psychedelic/Hippie, Disco/Funk and Rock & Roll) in 5 different stages.You unlock new Combo moves and costumes through collecting gold and silver medals by killing zombies efficiently and in style, which rewards you more and then buying them from the in-game shop.It felt like a breath of fresh air to play as a throwback to good old times of just mindless fun and dumb jokes being there just because, and I'm glad it has finally released on PC after all this time.Not all is great though, the Level design is rather linear and corridor-y. There's not much to explore in an Open World way aside from picking up limited collectibles like lollipop wrappers, or places to jump or take a detour to, like one would expect from most games nowadays. Instead you walk from set-piece to set-piece and trigger Cutscenes in-between chainsawing groups of zombies dead or fighting not very difficult bosses.It's also relatively short, if you're not the sort to look around every corner you'll finish in 5-6 hours. There are only 5 main stages (School, Stadium, Farm, Arcade, Cathedral/Construction site), but it seems replayable enough at higher difficulties. I liked the Farm the least of all of them due to pacing issues. It drags on and has odious Mini-game activities like combine harvesting zombies instead of Zombie basketball/baseball in the first two, which sounds a lot more fun as an activity than it actually ends up being.The Ending boss fight also drags on quite a bit and definitely overstays its Welcome.Another thing to note is that the Original Soundtrack and some (Optional) costumes didn't return to this version due to Licensing issues, but this seems to have been fixed if you look at the Guides section in the Community Hub.I'd say the Positives clearly outweighed the Negatives for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry for the lengthIt’s great to have this game back. I feel like I’m back in 2012 with the graphics and play style. Plus no battle pass to worry about just in game unlocking lol. With all that said though if you didn’t play during the days this game was released or before that you might get more annoyed from some of the bugs in it right now than someone who’s used to the old days (yes I didn’t grow up in the NES days but I was a PlayStation kid all the way up to PS4 lol) . Hitboxes seem to be a little more off than I remember but I could be wrong. As for other bugs I’ve stumbled across I’ll leave a listBugs 🐛  I’ve encountered:-voice lines repeating or easily overlapping with other ones.I think some got removed as well. Some zombies and one or two from Juliet. I only noticed because I remember theses lines for how funny they were. Anyway I’ll have voice lines from gameplay sometimes bleed into cutscene lines. Weirdest one is during the final level just before Sensei calls a second time. Right before the trigger for the cutscene a voice line from the starting cutscene of that level will play again from Juliet. It’s a bug that didn’t happen once but twice with one being after I restarted the game to check for any Day 1 patches or hotfixes.-some strange moments with animationsI’ve had only a small handful of zombies do a default pose. Hard to call it a T or an A pose, more like in between. More major ones involve one like during the Killabily fight where the QTE started for him to grab me as I run up his hand. The button prompt stayed (and I guess was still active just taking longer than it should’ve to complete?)  but the animation froze still. The special effects still worked as well and eventually I could continue the fight but something definitely didn’t go right there. Also I don’t remember much of it but Rosalind seemed a bit stiff in the bus more often than not. Compared to her in the crane when I did get a chance to see her she seemed a bit more stiff and lifeless in the bus and  some cutscenes in the bus.My friend encountered a really bad one making a boss fight unplayable. Marissa lost her bubble and sat in an idle animation up in the air. She couldn’t be shot or hit. My friend restarted the level and it happened again. Then they tried more rapid fire and it worked until phase 2 of the boss fight where it happened again. -the coin counter when collecting seems to be off constantly. I don’t know if I’m remembering this wrong but when you collect coins and platinum coins, it’s not always correct. I’ve had the counter say I have 1,000 for example but when I check the shop it’s only at like 207 or something. Same with the other ingame currency.-songs not playing when they should.There were 3 times I noticed this and possibly a few more I just don’t remember because I beat the game a few hours ago. But I noticed “Hey Mickey” never played as well as “You Spin Me Right Round”. Now this could just be a license thing but during the harvester mini game there’s no music playing for both of them. I know those two songs were in the game and I swear they were during those two instances of the zombie harvest. Either way no music played during zombie harvest both times as well as no music during the boss fight with Lewis Legend. Make the fight feel longer and a little underwhelming which sucks because the bugginess would’ve been more tolerable if it wasn’t just zombie and motorcycle noises playing. I need to do some reading but the game feels like a rip and port into newer hardware thanA remastering. Kinda looks it too. I could be wrong though but seeing a cutscene of Juliet holding the phone and her fingers looking (somewhat noticeably) off with or Lewis Legend having a broken looking hand when it should be on a handle bar or his guitar (if it doesn’t go invisible) are not something that should be in a remastering. Look at Crash and Spyro. (Still waiting on Spyro 4 btw). Great remasters, few changes, bug fixes like any other game, but in return such an update for all generations young and old to enjoy. It’s still fun don’t get me wrong but if the second phase 2 different bosses is unplayable because of broken animation or the whole screen going white besides hud elements (which happened to me twice. I don’t know if it was because I restarted and verified files but it did eventually fix just not the music for that battle). All in all it’s great to have this game back and I’d love to see a series even. But I do want them to fix this one first. They said they wanted it to feel a bit more modern so they got a good amount of fixing to do to get it there. Right now it just feels like it was straight up ripped from PS3 and made compatible with newer consoles. Still playable but some big yikes along the way. I’m fine with graphics but the lack of options is annoying. I’m fine with them looking like PS3 to a degree but some finer lighting, outlining, and post effects would would really help this game not feel like a rip.By the way if you try to pick full screen or borderless the words don’t appear. Just windowed mode but I still can select the other 2 options I just have to figure out which blank is which. It’s still a great game I’d say to go play if you have a sense of humor especially but they got some fixing to do. Quite a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite 2012 classics! I love this game, and played it over and over. I missed this game and glad it's finally been implemented to Steam. It's imperfect, however. Riddled with bugs, QTE's breaking and having to start over an entire stage just to come across the same problems, No Playstation input controls (I use a Dualshock 4 controller), sound breaking/impaired + Juliet can't count. Voice lines spams revolve around boss battles or mini-games. The gameplay feels more... clunky when the original had minor issues though, and the camera/aim still feels bad despite the remaster claimed they "fixed" it. I've always enjoyed the trashy writing and how chintzy it is. I do look back at some jokes that I missed. Some are funny, some aren't. I am happy Lollipop Chainsaw is back in my library (even though I own the Xbox 360 copy) and I can play it again. I'm hoping to see bug fixes and patches so it can be stable at least. The price tag is too high and I would wait FOR ITS sales or use RPCS3, I was gifted my copy. However, I'm not against anybody who decides to buy it but consider my review if you see it. Editing my review, and it seems like they had QTE's set to Auto when you start the game. I turned to manual, restarting my game multiple times because my QTE's were stuck and I couldn't advance on boss levels. Please fix this, it's boring to have QTE's set automatically, but what's worse is to not have them working properly when the assist is turned off. It's likely the devs had it preset as Auto knowing QTE's were broken so they can hit release day with a bandaid and patch it later. It should be patched asap imo along with everything else that's been mentioned. There are A LOT of game-breaking bugs in the Remastered version than the Original version. Lollipop Chainsaw in 2012 was anything else, but infested with major bugs.I will update it if fixes are implemented, but I don't know if that'd happen anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Lollipop Chainsaw RePOP is the ultimate blast from the past. As someone who played the original in my teen years, diving back into Juliet Starling's over-the-top zombie-slaying adventures feels like reliving those wild, carefree days. The revamped visuals and smoother gameplay bring it up to modern standards, but it still has that same punk-rock energy and humor that made the original so iconic.It's more than just a remaster—it's a time machine. From the killer soundtrack to the campy B-movie vibe, RePOP captures the joy of youthful chaos and lets you experience it all over again. Whether you're shredding zombies or laughing at the cheeky dialogue, it's a perfect, nostalgic thrill ride.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial Impression:Had no issues running the game but some more options to tweak the experience would be nice. Enjoyed the Prologue Chapter so this is a definite play. Its fun.After Completing the game:This game is fun. Its not a perfectly crafted action game by any means but the different scenarios and elements never tire you of something to go back to and try differently. I started to get worried, thinking the game was going to drown me in saving classmates but it changed swiftly when things started to get monotonous to challenging me with the few encounters with Alive people through treacherous zombie odds. Different kinds of zombies, all with relative weaknesses and advantages they exploit quite a bit. The boss fights are fun and memorable. Getting to the boss fights, you encounter the one major detractor on the game, and that's player agency. You feel as though you're open to select any which way you want to attack to defeat a boss but the intention of what to do shows up quite a bit to guide you through fights instead of letting you solve it yourself. I'm pretty good at turning my ears off but the disembodied head yells at you what to do to defeat certain boss segments. I felt like that ruined a lot of the surprise of what to do in the game. I'd prefer to repeatedly fail instead of being prompted to shoot or cut with a chainsaw. Its hard to think of other poor qualities of the game. Most of what else I experienced was plain fun. My favorite segments were all the ones where the game goes out of its element to deliver completely different game play scenarios. I had a lot of fun just shooting things but I got deeply annoyed whenever the 3 Kill Combo would pop on the screen. If anything needs to be fixed in a sequel, its probably removing that cutscene.

_childDocuments_.review: some of my fav things about repop:1: the speed modifier from chain hits feels great and balanced2: the combat itself is a lot less clunky than the original3: the reduction of shop prices makes it a lot less grindy than the original4: graphically it looks amazing, i know some other people are having issues running the game but for me i havent had any at all5: the new music and theme songs are really good6: the fact that the original loading screens are in is such a cute detail, plus the new loading screen is so cute7: overall the game feels a lot smoother to play things i dont like about repop:1: if you have fullscreen on and you alt tab the sound will desync, just turn on windowed and ur fine :3 (it has borderless so why wouldnt you)2: lack of graphic settingsthese could easily be fixed with an update, i just beat the story and those are my only issues so far, i definitely recommend playing this game!

_childDocuments_.review:
Various factors resulted in things making it so that fans can no longer easily play Lollipop Chainsaw, and it has been some time since players have not been able to access the game on current consoles.

We, the original development staff on Lollipop Chainsaw, think of the game as very precious to us, and did not want to leave it in limbo, where players who want to play it cannot. As such, we purchased the Lollipop Chainsaw intellectual property from Kadokawa Games, and decided to develop a remake.

One thing that we have to tell fans of the original game is that even though the original staff are working on the remake, there will be elements that are different from the original. Additionally, since we have access to consoles with higher specifications, we will be taking a more realistic approach to the graphics this time.

In any case, our goal is to make it easier for gamers who want to play Lollipop Chainsaw to do so.

name: CORRUPTION 2029
detailed_description: Set in a dystopian America in the not-so distant future. CORRUPTION 2029 is a turn based tactical combat game from The Bearded Ladies, creators of ‘Mutant Year Zero: Road to Eden’ and Miasma Chronicles. Using your supreme tactical abilities, command a squad of heavily augmented ‘units’ deep into enemy territory to discover the cause of the CORRUPTION. CORRUPTION 2029 is a hardcore tactical game that should test the mettle of even the most experienced tactical gamers. FIERCE TURN BASED COMBAT Engaging in tactical combat is a formidable challenge that requires exceptional strategic planning for victory. You must lead your squad of four units across the battlefield, mastering the art of tactical positioning, effective cover utilisation, and maintaining a clear Line of Sight. Employ a range of explosives or specialised weaponry to obliterate enemy defences, and leverage powerful tactical implants to gain a decisive advantage. SILENT STEALTH OR LOUD AND DESTRUCTIVE Approach stealthily, devise a flawless trap, and take out unsuspecting enemy forces with your silent armaments, shifting the odds in your favour. Alternatively, grab your most powerful Gatling guns and grenades, unleashing a storm of firepower—it's entirely up to you. EXPLORE A NEW AMERICA The United States is fractured by civil war, split between the Free Alliance and the oppressive New American Council, who have been engaged in a brutal struggle for dominance for years. As the balance of power shifts, the NAC faces catastrophic defeats, and intelligence suggests they are on the verge of creating a desperate weapon of terror. What exactly are they constructing? What lies behind the CORRUPTION?

detailed_description: WHICH EDITION IS RIGHT FOR ME? The Elder Scrolls Online Collection: Gold Road and The Elder Scrolls Online Deluxe Collection: Gold Road includes the base game, Gold Road and all previous Chapters. Those who purchase the Deluxe Collection: Gold Road will also receive the Deluxe in-game items. Players purchasing the Collection editions can jump into the base game, Gold Road or any previous Chapter right away. The Elder Scrolls Online Upgrade: Gold Road and The Elder Scrolls Online Deluxe Upgrade: Gold Road includes Gold Road only, plus Deluxe in-game items for those who purchase the Deluxe Upgrade: Gold Road . Digital Deluxe Edition DELUXE Those who purchase The Elder Scrolls Online Deluxe Upgrade: Gold Road or The Elder Scrolls Online Deluxe Collection: Gold Road will receive the Deluxe in-game items, including: All past Chapter Collector's Edition / Deluxe items** (only included in The Elder Scrolls Online Deluxe Collection: Gold Road ) Mount: West Weald Tharriker Pet: Skingrad Guard Mastiff Outfit Style: Skingrad Vedette Armor Pack Memento: Ulfsild's Tome of Legends Colovian Emote Pack (3 emotes) **Does not include past Chapter pre-order / pre-purchase in-game items. About the Game Begin your journey and experience the unparalleled storytelling and lore of The Elder Scrolls . Explore Tamriel—a massive living universe where your choices shape your adventure. Go it solo or with friends and allies as you explore, quest, craft, and roleplay in a world where you can customize your abilities and gear to suit any playstyle. No game subscription required—buy once, play anytime. GOLD ROAD BRAND-NEW ELDER SCROLLS STORY - For the first time in The Elder Scrolls Online , a new Daedric Prince walks Tamriel. Forgotten to even her most devout followers, Ithelia has returned. Why has she returned now? And what are her followers' plans for West Weald? Embark on an adventure to preserve reality before the threads of fate unravel in Ithelia’s wake. EXPLORE A NEW ZONE - Venture into West Weald, an Imperial region last seen in TES IV: Oblivion, now threatened by the encroaching Valenwood jungle and Daedric incursions. Defend the Colovian capital city of Skingrad, investigate the wilds of the Dawnwood, and explore ancient Ayleid ruins and the mountainous Colovian Highlands, all endangered by the chaos of Ithelia’s return. SCRIBING - Delve into the heart of magic itself with Scribing, a unique system that allows you to customize your playstyle in new and exciting ways. Collect special skills and modify their effects and functionality to make them yours. With Scribing, you truly have the freedom and power to play your way. DISCOVER GREATER ADVENTURE! - Dive into a challenging new 12-person trial called the Lucent Citadel, contend with dangerous world events and bosses, immerse yourself in captivating new delves and public dungeons, earn unique in-game rewards, and much more. The Collection: Gold Road and Deluxe Collection: Gold Road includes the base game, Gold Road and all previous Chapters, as below (plus Deluxe items for those who get the Deluxe Collection: Gold Road ). name: Rusty's Retirement
detailed_description: Rusty's Retirement is an idle-farming simulator designed to sit at the bottom of your screen allowing you to work on other tasks while caring for your farm! Grow crops: Plant crops and watch Rusty get to work as he waters, nurtures, and harvests. Unlock new crops as you progress, from crispy carrots to ripe tomatoes. Produce biofuel: Use crops to produce clean and energy-efficient biofuel, a vital robot power source. Sell biofuel to other machine inhabitants and reinvest the money into expanding your farm. Automate with robots: Deploy a team of cute little robots to assist with planting, watering, and harvesting. Customize and upgrade your helper bots to increase efficiency. Multitasking: Rusty's Retirement is built to sit comfortably at the bottom of your screen allowing you to do other tasks while caring for your farm. Zoom in or out for a less distracting view, or alternatively turn on 'Focus Mode' which slows down crop production. Vertical mode: You can also create a new vertical farm that sits comfortably at the side of your screen. Twitch Integration available: Streamers and viewers can build a farm together. Viewers can control what task their robot should focus on through chat commands like !plant !water !harvest.

_childDocuments_.review: I am absolutely in love with this game.Honestly my only real complaint is that I wish there was a full-screen mode. Or larger window mode.I know the whole "twist" is supposed to be idle-farming while doing other things. But, why not in the world of multiple screens? Or when doing off-computer work?There are some minor bugs, but I haven't encountered anything gamebreaking. (And, in the two days the game has been out there has already been two tiny hot fixes released)And there is an active and helpful discord.
_childDocuments_.name: Rusty's Retirement

_childDocuments_.review: Now this is ADHD-GAMING.It's actually very cute and as someone with ADHD who spends a lot of time studying/working from home, it's pleasant and unobtrusive enough to be a nice little dopamine hit between tasks. I prefer to keep it on "focus mode" (doubles time to grow crops) and leave it on my second screen. It doesn't call my attention away from more important things, and helps keep me from getting too frustrated at my work. Unlike other games I've tried to play in my short breaks, I don't feel at risk of spending more time than I expect to here. The visuals are cute, the progression is simple but engaging, and I like the music. Plenty of options to run it vertically, horizontally, smaller, larger, etc. It's all smartly made and does what it says on the tin.It's just nice. I like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rusty's Retirement

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun for ~20 hours or so. The pixel art is charming, and it's nice to see the bots running around doing stuffs while you keep unlocking new stuffs. Not a fan of the lack of meta-progressions between maps though. Once you're done with a map, you just redo all the progressions on a new map. And from what I see (only unlocked the same map), the items you unlock are exactly the same. So it's just a bit dull to me.

Featuring the complete single-player experiences of both games, including bonus content from the Game of the Year Edition. Red Dead Redemption does not feature multiplayer content. Experience the story of former outlaw John Marston as he tracks down the last remaining members of the notorious Van der Linde Gang in the PC debut of the critically acclaimed predecessor to Red Dead Redemption 2. Red Dead Redemption and its iconic zombie-horror companion story, Undead Nightmare, can now be enjoyed on PC in stunning detail together in one stellar package. Red Dead Redemption includes new features to bring the game to life on PC, with HDR lighting, native 4K resolution at up to 144hz on supported hardware, monitor support for Ultrawide (21:9) and Super Ultrawide (32:9), adjustable draw distances, shadow quality settings, and more.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine making frame generation an NVIDIA GPU exclusive feature when FSR 3 support (only upscaling unfortunately) is technically already in the game. RTX 40 series GPU owners aren't even the majority and the game in theory should already run well on those cards.There's a weird issue during cutscenes where the framerate tanks below 60FPS, but actual gameplay seems to run fine. This game seems to have really strange framerate issues at the moment.You have to switch the display manually in the graphics settings because using the shortcut to move a window to a different display results in stretching if they aren't the same resolution.HDR support in the game is half-baked, for some reason it looks washed out and reds look like browns.DualShock and DualSense support is not in this port, there's only Xbox prompts.The most positive thing I can say at the moment is that most of the features they advertised are there (setting aside cutscene pillarboxing on ultrawide, which is understandable since they likely don't want to go and touch these up to fix issues), and the game doesn't seem to play terribly on a mouse and keyboard. It also runs mostly at a locked 60FPS on the Steam Deck with everything maxed out but shadow quality set to medium, and shadow blending set to smooth.EDIT: Before anyone says "Just use the Nukem9 DLSS to FSR mod, Uniscaler, or DLSS Enabler", trust me, I've tried both of these and yet while frame generation works fine before you enable it on startup, it causes the game to not even boot up if you have it enabled from the get-go. The fact that I've spent nearly 2 hours trying to troubleshoot this game (much in the same way with Red Dead Redemption 2 and how it crashed with my USB headset at launch) should already be a massive UX failure. People can spam the jester award at me all they want, I'm dead serious, cope about people not being mindless consoomers for a change. Modern western/eastern game studios can't even get a port of a 14 year old game correct nowadays.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Dead Redemption

_childDocuments_.review: Hopefully this is a step in the right direction for Rockstar. They got a competent studio to make a stellar port and listened to what the fans want. Game runs extremely well, I've found zero bugs/issues so far. Only small note is the price, 50 Euros for a game from 2009 is borderline comical (especially with no multiplayer, meaning it has less features than the original). Unless you're dying to play, wait for a sale.That being said at least your money won't be wasted, as the game is stellar.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Dead Redemption

_childDocuments_.review: Should Rockstar still be charging $50 for a game over a dozen years old? NoIs it higher quality/value than 95% of games being sold for $50 on Steam right now? YesWait for a sale if you want to save 15-20 bucks but still is a better game/value than most games you'll find on steam especially when you consider mods.
