_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those times I wish steam had a third option between recommend or not, like a maybe. I leaned towards not recommend for mainly two reasons. First, Atlus has a tendency to make definitive editions with big additions to story and gameplay. Second, the story was on rails with no real diverging paths or choices for replayability and I personally did not enjoy it as much as I hoped.In terms of gameplay I'm leaning positive overall. This is the most QoL heavy Atlus game thus far and for turn based RPGs in general. You have the tools to essentially breeze through the whole game with minimal turn based combat outside boss fights and making even them easier with the rewind option. I liked the QoL and the only thing I could see missing was a loadout option for specific team/archetype set ups. Other than that, while I enjoyed the smaller main story dungeons that you could easily finish in a in-game day and addition of smaller optional dungeons for side quests there was a lot of re-used areas. I have similar feelings to Archetypes and enemy variety, while I didn't mind not having the roster of Persona/SMT and liked Archetypes in general, the enemy variety was an issue for me, a lot of re-used enemies and bosses. The social/bond aspect was also easier, no filler time needed to spend between bond level ups, no hidden bonds unlocked from side activities or other bond progression, less levels to max out, easy to track and travel to. I just wish they had voice acting other than the first and last bond level. UI looked great in general other than sprinting, I did not like the blurred screen, speed lines and yelling from the MC, ended up avoiding using it.Now in terms of the setting, story and characters. This is subjective but also the most important part in a big narrative RPG for my tastes. Unfortunately this game was mediocre at best for me. Setting was fantasy but more of a steampunk with magic than a medieval fantasy setting I was hoping. I liked the art style in general  but the main party designs didn't click with me, moving away from a school setting and saying they are adults was not enough with how young most of them looked. Fighting with greatswords, spears, axes etc I wish we had options to customize the party outfits with actual armor, wouldn't even mind if it was paid DLC.  Music was interesting, very subjective, I liked it a lot initially but I felt it got repetitive too fast, especially the monk chanting in the background but I liked how they connected it with feelings/magic.Now the most important part, a good and immersive story for me is like a well told lie, something that hooks me and keeps me believing it til the end. This game was not immersive for me, the lie it was telling didn't hold, I caught myself disagreeing with and questioning the messages it was trying to pass. That lead me to unintentionally nitpicking and overanalyzing. The overall messages ended up as unimpactful and a lot of characters simple and one-dimensional. I wouldn't call it bad, it had high points and as I said it's subjective. I'm sure it will resonate with some people, it just didn't for me and I really wish it did.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible game, it changed my view on a lot of things.if you are on the fence about buying it, play the demo, if you like the RPG-esque VisualNovel-y gameplay, come try it out, you can import the demo's save data too!SPOILER FREETHE GAMEPLAYPROS;It feels very satisfying, and coming from other great turn-based games, takes kind of a different twist, inspired on the Shin Megami Tensei Series it makes their gameplay more accessible for a wide audience, while not taking away from loving fans.The Followers in this game are beautiful, every character is full of charm in their own way, and every single one is lovable, even the worst ones.The main dungeons are beautiful, the worst ones still reach some other game's peaks, even though it isn't everyone's cup of tea, it's definitely mine.The soundtrack is absolutely gorgeous, from beginning to end the music is just wonderful, just perfect for this game.The game gives you time to do pretty much everything, if you don't waste time around training for HP and SP or restart dungeons, you should be good, just do something every day.CONS;The secondary Dungeons are very underwhelming, coming from Persona 3 Tartarus and Persona 5 Palaces, this just feels like the odd one out, they feel like Persona 4 dungeons with a bit more exploration and a lot longer, some people may find them not as bad, but if i replay this game i'll do everything in my power to go in as little secondary dungeons as possible, reused assets, very weird gamedesign, overall a mechanic which could've been great, but barely scratched being decent.The difficulty curve feels weird, initially there is a couple of secondary bosses which are weirdly hard even following the advice the game gives you, while late game there's some incredibly easy and incredibly hard bosses, close to one another, the difficulty curve feels like a roller coaster, the highs are as uncomfortable as the lows.OVERALL VOTE9/10May be my favourite JRPG of all time, even after thinking about it for a couple days, my idea remains the same.i think this should win the GOTY and every other award you can throw at it, incredible.

_childDocuments_.review: Atlus really put forth their best here, Metaphor is one of the greatest games I've ever played. Metaphor is truly like playing your way through a provocative scyfy/fantasy novel. This game checks every box. If you are a fan of this genre, if you love the Persona titles, including games like FE Tokyo Sessions, then you will absolutely love metaphor.  It plucks all the best elements out of their previous titles, pays homage to some other great games out there like Fire Emblem Three Houses.  The issue of racism is an important theme, but it's not forced. If you play the game simply to enjoy it it's truly remarkable. Some maybe determined to dislike it because of the way it addresses social issues, but it is done tastefully. In a less divisive era it's not even something I would mention.  Euchronia is an amazing world! I hope the game wins game of the year plus more.  The soundtrack is beautiful, it's just top shelf in terms of RPG games in recent history.

_childDocuments_.review: Metaphor is at it's core a high fantasy take on the tried and true Persona formula.  I think it works very well in this setting and I may even actually prefer it to the usual high school theme.  Once again Atlus knocks the  writing and characters out of the park and this game even tackles more mature themes than it's Persona counter parts.  Visuals are nice and are very similar to both Persona 3 Reload and Persona 5's.  The stylized UI is in the same vane as those two games as well and I really loved the way it looked.   Music is also very good as well,  but VERY different from the modern pop soundtracks that the Persona games use.  It fits very well with the setting and theme however.This game has a new take on the Persona turned based system as well.  For the most part, I really liked the changes.  Instead of using weaknesses to knock enemies down and then doing All-Out-Attacks,  you will attack enemy weaknesses in order to essentially get more actions on your teams' turn.  Also when activating any attack,  you can simply press the button again in order to skip straight to the resulting damage etc....  This is actually a great quality of life addition that helps to keep the turned-based mode fast and engaging.  And speaking of quality of life,  you can now use the games new action combat system (very basic with just a simple combo and dodge) to kill enemies in the over world instantly if they are too low a level,  instead of having to fight them in turns.  This is probably my favorite change, as it really helps speed up dungeons and grinding if you are into that.   The only real gripes I had were mostly minor annoyances.  For one, the game occasionally has different weather effects that would basically make it so that when you were fighting in Turned-based mode.... when you hit an enemy weakness,  you would NOT get any extra actions.  They would simply just take the improved damage.  I thought this took the only new and fun mechanic and just removed it.  True you get more exp etc.. when killing this way, but I thought it just made the combat a lot less enjoyable.  The other problem I had was that, in this game,  the main protagonist can no longer swap Archetypes (Persona's) mid combat.  This made it a little more annoying when you were fighting enemies for the first time.  There was a nice rumor system that would give you hints on enemy weaknesses and strategies,  but this didn't help on other mobs that were not apart of this rumor system.  This made it so that sometimes you would go into a fight and realize that you did not have the correct skill etc equipped that would make the fight much easier and you will end up wasting a lot of MP resources instead.    In addtion, you do not gain the ability to "scan" enemies until you are like 80% of the way through the game.  So the trial and error is real sometimes.  Also, why is it, that in every Atlus Persona type game... you cannot access the main menu during combat?  Sometimes I would like to just reload a save instead of having to Alt-F4 out and restart just to do that.  Other than those small gripes, I really thought this was an amazing game with great mechanics and a great story.  Well worth your time if are into JRPG's at all and a no brainer if you like Persona games.

_childDocuments_.review: My journey to becomming King has finally concluded. Thoughts/Opinion(s):I loved the world setting, music, and its flat back red haired knight enough to continue to the end of its stretched out pages. What I disliked is how stretched out the ending felt and the lack of NG+ features it gives you. Sure, once you beat the game you gain access to a new dragon fight, keep your powers but have to find them again, and you keep your Money/MAG currencies as well as items. But honestly, that's just not enough for me. I want my Prince at the start instead of the end for NG+. I want to feel over powered instead of having to go through the journey again with enemies having a +1 turn. I wouldn't mind grinding out the party's love system all over again, that's just my take.Perhaps modders will create a better NG+ for the longevity/replayability of the game. Until then, I can finally close this fantasy book and move on to better stories.

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the game on hard after ~80 hours. Really liked the game over all. The beginning is stronger than the ending as the game kind of gets bogged down under the weight of its own ideals.Pros - 1. Companions are good/great. Almost every character is well fleshed out.2. Archetype/Job system is well done. Progression feels good.3. Deciding on what you need to do first within the time limit is engaging. (Virtues/followers/dungeons)4. Music is nothing short of iconic.Cons - 1. Story falls off. Anxiety/magic lore didn't really hit for me (though I did like the music idea). Just really did not vibe with the plot of story/fantasy nor did I appreciate the philosophical questions posed therein. 2. Gear was kind of whatever. Just stat type gear that is not well explained until you get to end game. Even then, gear is mostly just stat sticks and not something that noticeably changes your character.3. No big end game side dungeon type thing. There are SOME quests at endgame, but not like you would expect for an 80 hour RPG.4. The game visuals are repetitive. Every tower looks the same. There are 2 types of dungeon: dirt or castle. Their visuals are reused over and over. (Nature set pieces you take drawings of are great though!)Overall - Job system and companions carried by desire to keep chugging through this 80+ hour rpg. You will not be disappointed in Metaphor if you are looking for a massive RPG to lose yourself in.

_childDocuments_.review: This has quickly become my favorite game Atlus has ever done. I like the setting and vibe a lot more than the other games, and while their other games are great experiences I think this one really stands out among all of them. The way it plays and feels is great. The turn-based combat feels the most visually appealing to me compared to others, you have a row mechanic where you can position the party member in the front or back row when controlling their turn. Being in the front row yields more physical damage, but you also take slightly more damage, while being in the back lowers physical damage but raises defense, certain ranged skills like for the Gunner Archetype tree can only be used in the back row. There's also a small element of real-time combat as well, being able to attack enemies to stun them then initiating Squad battle {turn-based combat) to get the upper hand while they're stunned for a couple turns as well as in introductory attack dealing significant damage. Enemies lower level than you can just be struck down with a hit or two to defeat them without going into turn-based mode, if you are attacked while trying to take down or stun and enemy this way you will be ambushed, you can dodge roll to avoid them if needed. The mechanics for this are essentially the same as most of their other games. But I really enjoy this extra little addition to the gameplay.The music is absolutely wonderful, it really fits with the setting and I find myself listening to the entire Main Menu song each time I start up the game before loading into my save lol. Time management is the same as Persona 5 and others. The story is quite engaging and interesting too with having a voiced protagonist this time around, I've been on the edge of my seat the entire way through. All in all, this game is absolutely amazing and I personally believe this is Atlus' best game to date and is a MUST PLAY!

_childDocuments_.review: Start with the cons:I certainly didn't miss this game-play loop, Game starts off great with loads of detail and engaging storytelling, then you get to the part where the voice acting disappears and now you're reading hours and hours worth of exposition, and fighting in dungeons that can go on for upwards of 10 whole hours. These Graphics are outdated, it isn't an "art style" its a lack of innovation, Honkai Star Rail is a year old now, its a free 'Mobile' Game and its nothing short of Stunning. it isn't wrong to nudge the development team into thinking about graphical improvements for future games.Pros:Game has a great set up with an enticing opening sequence, you are not eased into the story, you are thrown into it head first with your crew quite confidently planning on achieving what I assume to be your end goal is in the first hour of the game, very bold.The voice acting has been great so far, I did go for English voices in the end as immersion is key so naturally British Accents are the go to for that but.... the MC has an American Accent? so yeah that's a thing maybe there's a reason for it who knows. I like the voiced protagonist, Atlus looks like they might be stepping away from self insert characters but I have been given some sarcastic options so far which is nice.the first few hours of combat was very fun and satisfying, if you are playing the game casually you could have a lot of enjoyment with the dungeons. In Conclusion: This game doesn't have the comedic brilliance of a Persona 4, It doesn't have the stunning visuals of a Persona 3 (Reload), It may actually be on par with the movement of Persona 5 though.But what it is, is something new, something unique and something that NEEDS to be successful if the industry of gaming is ever going to innovate away from the souls like copy and paste games that keep being churned out.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as I'm concerned, this is a decade-defining RPG.ReFantazio is gorgeously written. The world, the plot, the characters, the real-world commentary, and everything in between kept me coming back throughout my 100+ hour playthrough. There was never a point where I felt bored-- the I could not wait to see where the story went, how the characters developed, and new things I unlocked. There are a few stretches that felt like a slog, but never so bad that I'd put the game down and never come back.I will say, some of the story beats and twists are extremely predictable and I was initially disappointed by these. However, the writing does not treat these twists and turns as groundbreaking plot points, and feels like it expects the player to see where things are going. After encountering this a couple times, I feel like the game is better off this way, than say, building an entire plot around a twist that will turn everything on its head.My only criticisms of this game involve the combat and some opinions around the way the world is written. For combat, there are a couple enemies that are atrocious to fight (can I get a Fishy Fandango, anyone?) and the game essentially traps you in animations and combat. Especially if you die, you're forced to watch an end game screen for a bit before you're able to hop back in. If you're losing a boss fight, you're unable to 'give up' to boot a save, which can feel pretty bad.As far as world building critiques-- one of this game's themes is racism. They never _show_ the societal structures that keep 'lesser' races oppressed. The prejudice often feels like people saying mean things to/about 'lesser' races, as opposed to how, in reality, racial prejudice creates and upholds systems that limit how a person lives their life. There are moments in this game, like in the Opera House, where there doesn't even appear to be any prejudice, outside of exclusion of Eugiefs and Elda. I only played this game once, so it's possible I just missed these moments, but it genuinely feels like we're told 'the Nidia experience a lot of racism', but without those dialogue moments, there's no reason to believe this-- Nidia are shopkeepers and singers, but never beggars or thieves. I'd say most of the tribes don't seem to experience any kind of life-defining racism.Finally, the game lacks opportunities to learn more about the different tribes, probably because in reality they aren't very different outside of appearance, excluding the Mustari, who have significantly different cultural practices. This is disappointing to me, because the the races are honestly super neat, and while I learned a bit about the Mustari, I would have liked to learn more about cultural practices of other races. In retrospect though, maybe that's the point, huh?

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: it's breathtakingly refreshing to play something new, instead of the usual cash-grab remake, the censored demasters, and the soulless "AAA" slops we've been getting every month. Now allow me to dive deeper into this game's positives and negatives based on my 130 hours of playtime. +Not a huge fan of turn-based combat games in general, but it's amazing here. It's fun to buff your party, while debuffing enemies to obliterate them. The synthesis abilities are wonderfully animated and it's immensely satisfying to kill bosses with it. The fact that you have full freedom to use whichever archetypes and abilities you want is an immense improvement over Persona 5. The overworld combat where you can stun enemies to gain advantage is cool as well.Yeah...I love the art style of all Atlus' games. They always bring something cool to the table, and my god the UI design is eye popping . Characters are beautifully designed and distinguishable. The gauntlet runner is a very creative idea. Extra points for the monster designs, Not a single reused monster from any of the Persona games. Kudos!Played it in Japanese audio  and it's almost perfect. The only problem is, there are still instances where the player reads the lines and characters aren't voiced/wouldn't have audio.Just like the Persona games, you can make friends along the way. Spending time with them unlocks perks and new archetypes, and this is one the ways to level up and increase your power plus fame. There is also a popularity ranking that increases the more you help people. You can even debate people and destroy their popularity, while increasing your own.Except for one, all the other main dungeons were fun to explore and well-designed. Don't know about the others, but I had zero problems with the port. In my entire playthrough, I didn't encounter a single bug or crash, which is astoundingly crazy in 2024, lol!This might be controversial, but the music just didn't do it for me, except for maybe 2 tracks and that is a shock. This is because Persona 5 has some of the greatest tracks in video game history! Maybe Meguro-San was busy with Persona 6 and didn't have the time? There are a lot of reused tracks as well :(While the story starts off great and it has some wild twists, it fizzles out by the end. Maybe it needed more bad guys than just Louis. The game is also heavy on exposition, I get that all of Atlus' games are, but it's way too much here. Not all is bad, the 2nd main dungeons' story arc caught me off guard and pulled my heartstrings.Also... Compared to the main ones, the side dungeons were not so hot. They were less inspiring and repetitive. Some of them were really short too. Maybe cutting out a few of these would've helped the overall pacing of the game?--The game can feel grindy at times, especially if you want to level up a certain archetype's combat ability.--I wanna change costumes man! Even if you change into your DLC costumes, they revert back during cutscenes and dialogue...ugh.Overall, it's definitely a solid game I'd recommend to JRPG vets and newcomers! If I were to give a rating, it would be:

_childDocuments_.review: Metaphor: ReFantazio is a fantastic game that follows the Persona formula very closely while still being it's own game.  I really like how they gave the main protagonist some voice lines, as to not just be in dialogue with other characters and respond with nods and grunts.  I have only played over 25 hours of the game, and in that time, I have a pretty fleshed out party, but they don't feel as engaging or lovable as characters in past ATLUS titles.  There have been characters who have entered my party and I assumed they'd be the difference maker but they just end up on the back burner not really catching my interest at all.  The most exciting part of the game for me is the enemies.  There are some unique monsters that are very refreshing from battling the shadow themed monsters in persona titles.  The enemies and bosses are unique and created with great detail and always offer something new to admire as you take them on through the various quest and battles.That comes to my point of the weakest aspect of the game.  The questing.  I am following the story, but the questing in this title seems so disjointed and uninspiring.  There are the typical fetch quest and giant monster  bounties, but I never went into any one quest feeling like I had much to gain.  Once quest was so annoying that I just backed out of it and went with something else.  It just wasn't fun.  I think the other thing that is bothersome is the difficulty is hard to gauge.  I initially had this game on hard, which just means to me that I have to pay more attention to strengths and weaknesses, but when you have enemies, that on their turn can take multiple turns and wipe your entire party, it just comes off as a bit unfair.  I have adjusted the difficulty to normal, but at this point, I just might go on easy mode just to experience the story in it's entirety.  The battles don't feel challenging, they feel like luck is the largest factor and if you don't have luck, you're going to get beaten pretty badly.  I guess the lesson would be to grind away, but if grinding isn't your thing, then what are you left to do?  This is all coming from someone who's beaten Persona 4 in double digits and has seen the best parts of the entire series.  The execution of combat is pretty awesome though.  When you are in battles with a slight edge to them, you feel really good when you pull them out.  The game rewards you with extra points for not being touched in a battle, but I feel they could have done more with this.  Character growth is substantial and the combination of specials combined by our heroes are fun to pull off and even better to look at.  Overall, I think this is a fun game.  While at times, I feel it comes across a bit unbalanced, that's not to say that there isn't something there for fans of ATLUS games.  If you love ATLUS RPGs, you'll love this.  If you enjoy the Persona  or SMT series, then you'll feel right at home.  Metaphor: ReFantazio is far from a perfect game, but it's a fun title that is worth all of the attention and hype that it has received.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy Persona games and fantasy RPGs, you will enjoy this.Just, beware the extreme issues with performance. I usually do not give a damn about FPS drops, but here, the game turns into a Powerpoint slideshow with 0.2 FPS whenever there's more than a couple enemies on screen - that is to say, the entire game freezes, and every 5 seconds you get to see the next frame. It'd be annoying with turn-based combat, but there is action RPG elements with real-time fighting on the overworld, and good luck rolling to dodge enemy attacks when it takes 50 seconds to complete one single roll due to extreme stuttering. There's been a lot of issues with cloud saving too, save files straight up vanishing into smoke, so just because you saved, the game told you the save was successful and you can see the new save was successfully updated, don't you dare think that your data is actually safe; it can and does revert to previous save files at random. My computer is a gaming war machine, and even it struggles when Metaphor is running: if I tab out while the game is on, my mouse rubberbands. All that is with low-qualify graphics, no antialisaing and capped 30 FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: Every bit of this game is soaked in Atlus DNA and I must preface this by saying that this heavily affected my enjoyment, for better or for worse.The gameplay is extremely reminiscent of SMT and Persona (Social Links, dungeon crawling, and combat) and carries some details from Etrian Odyssey (Team building and positioning).  The Press-turn system makes a return, but I felt it was pretty one dimensional compared to its predecessors.  The difficulty on Normal strikes a nice balance.  Bosses range from straightforward and easy to meticulously difficult at times.  Followers (aka Social Links) return as well and focus more on telling a story.  Time management in the game is flexible enough that players shouldn't feel the need to reload their game as long as they try to optimize to the best they can.  Archetypes is the bread and butter of the game.  It is a combination of standard class systems mixed with Altus' classic demon/persona formula.  It is comparable to Etrian Odyssey's Grimoire mechanic which allows for great customizability and variety.The story is somewhat standard, and excels with likable and fairly unique characters.  Some leaps of logic were made in the story (especially towards the end).  The game's extreme stylized visuals and distinct soundtrack betters the otherwise mediocre gameplay and enhances the story.Though I personally felt the game was lacking due to my own personal expectations, this is still a solid game for any RPG fan and for anyone who has yet to experience an Atlus title.  I would not recommend the game for those familiar with Atlus' works.  7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a high fantasy Persona filled with interesting political conflict. Great story, deep characters, and pleasant art and music. And in that sense its great!But then the combat. Ugh. Its not even hard its just exhausting. Every battle consists of some enemy that will spam you with full AOE attacks that at least one of your characters is weak against and then, guess what, they get to attack again. And the computer KNOWS your weaknesses. They will target your weak characters almost every single time. So, you're either waiting for the game to spend 8 turns attacking you every round, or you're strong enough to kill the enemy in one turn, yourself. There is rarely an inbetween, and when there is, you're SLOWLY chipping away at a fight for 15 minutes.I'm around 80-90% done with the main game and it feels like such a slog whenever I enter a dungeon.Its really not fun to me to run into a fight, die because a boss has some niche mechanic that my party isn't setup for, and then go into menus to figure out how to cheese it. I'd much rather adapt on the fly during a battle, but that's all just preference. I find it odd that they give you a retry mechanic in mid-combat. To me, that tells me that the intention is for you to go in and get your party wiped just to figure out an enemy's weakness and then restart with your new knowledge and annihilate the enemy without any risk to yourself at all. I'm just not on board with that. The stakes are gone, it just becomes a "craft the perfect party for every separate encounter" type of game which requires way too much class swapping for me to have fun.Idk, there are clearly a lot of players that don't mind the combat, but it was the lowest point for me. Despite that, I'm still finishing the game if that says anything about the other good parts like the story and social gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely recommend this game. Just finished it, and I enjoyed every second of it. What I liked:- The combat is fast and fluid. There are a lot of tools you can play around with (ex. formations, synthesis) and it can make the overall experience even better. There is also a retry function, which can be helpful at times when you're unlucky (ex. Strohl missing that last hit :) ) . There is also an overworld combat which makes grinding for money/items much faster, and it is more than welcome to not have to take down low level mobs. - The daily life is simpler than in Persona, there aren't that many functions that you can use. You either develop Royal Virtue, do dungeons or spend time with followers. However it's streamlined in many ways. You can see how many points you get from developing stats, and no need to sweet-talk followers since all follower talks are a level up. - I really enjoyed the story. it had it's fair share of plot twists, a good pace. The antagonists throughout the story were all amazing especially the main villain who always had presence during his cutscenes. The allies you meet during the journey were also all had great backstories, personality quirks and they all get even more fleshed out during the follower talks. - Music is 10/10. I still hum Ode to heroes :D There are a couple of improvements though that could've been made:- Graphics can be grating at times. The main characters and everything front and center look good, but backgrounds or some specific parts can be low poly at times (ex. Bardon's igniter or necklace thingy)- The overworld combat is very simple, and janky. I think there could've been some extra additions, like using spells to hit enemies or inflict status ailments before a fight. The idea was there, since there are some items that can help for example a food that makes attacks a 1 hit stun/kill, but this could've been extended a bit furtherThere is a free demo which has the entire prologue + 3 days from Chapter 1, which is around 5-10 hours depending on your speed and selection of difficulty. Moreover, the save can be carried over to the full game so no progress is lost.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give the game around 6/10. In my opinion, it's not a must buy/play, but overall an OK JRPG.My playtime is around 75hrs, about 10 hrs of spent on grinding. Personally, I felt like the Sanctism should play a bigger role in the plot due to how big their influence are in the game. But alas, nothing interesting happened about them. I have high expectation that the 4 Sanctifex Forden cronies would do something crazy in the game but nope, they serve no purpose to the game. Plus not much mindblowing moments in the game.~ The graphic is looks good and ugly at the same time. There's a lot of clipping in the animations making cutscenes look wacky.Cons:- I felt the dialogue is SUPER repetitive, in both story and followers dialogues. After some point, I did not even bother to read them (which I rarely do in other story centric games)- A lot of the optional dungeons design looks the same, there are like 3 tower dungeons that has almost exactly the same layout.- Most disappointing part for me is there is none/barely any memorable OSTs in the game considering this is sort of an ATLUS game. _childDocuments_.review: Quite honestly among the best and greatest fantasy games of all-time. Absolutely stellar Worldbuilding, Characters and Story. All 3 weaved in effortlessly and extremely consistent throughout the entire game. The fantastic Music and Combat adds even more to the world.Have played many fantasy games in my life, but never seen one this consistent and bold in its persistence. A game despite being over 80-100 hours long, leaves little room for flaws. It feels meticulously crafted from bottom to top. You can feel the love and effort poured from the developers as you journey through it.Pretty much everything has great nuance to it. Fantasy stories are not something new. They are quite common. But they tend to always fall  my experience.  Yet...Metaphor ReFantazio is one of those extremely rare cases where it does feel real and genuine. Because of the high level consistent worldbuilding, characters and story...it takes the fantasy concept to a level rarely seen. It's got arguebly the best worldbuilding ive seen of any fantasy game. Its among the best written videogame stories Ive experienced. And its characters are written amazingly well, to a consistency I honestly have never seen. With alot of nuance and emotional value that makes you resonate with pretty much most of them, if not all of them. The music is really fantastic. Memorable tracks and something that has its own little story within the game aswell. On top of the fantastic combat. I would consider it a masterpiece. Thats how meticulously well crafted it is. I think it sets the benchmarks of what RPGs can achieve, especially JRPGs. Just like how BG3 set that benchmark last year.  I can see now why this game took so long to make. You cannot achieve something this remarkable and bold without a big passionate team and clear vision behind it. If youre into Fantasy or RPGs, I definetely would not miss out on this one. You'll most likely be blown away.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not Persona nor SMT. It's Tokyo Mirage sessions SE# encore, without the Nintendo licensed characters and it's excellent.additional note: The game has a horrible endgame. They add not one, but three party members at the last possible moment and then send you on a roller coaster of cut-scenes and boss fights without letting you prepare for any of them. If you don't have a old save and need revives or something, your stuck beating your head against the encounters until the AI breaks. It's not fun nor like anything else in the entire game. Also, upon coming to this point a bunch of side story content just vanishes and your stuck with what you have. What's horrible about this is if you pursued the wrong thing for the whole game you can get locked out of the strongest forms for that playthrough making the final fight a drag. They also only give you 10 in-game days to prepare for this fight, which isn't enough time. It turns into trial and error real quick. I suspect a expansion in the future that will fix this because it's probably just rushed development and wouldn't hurt from being longer.

_childDocuments_.review: Game mixes the Persona formula with the Fantasy genre well. It seems they also made improvements to the time management loop that makes it feel less repetitive compared to persona games (the traveling mechanics, more in between dialogues, side dungeons etc...). It will feel repetitive eventually, that's natural, but it holds up more. The story is good enough, not amazing (I'm at the last 15% give or take) but has its highs and the characters are fun.Unfortunately, it also has some of the Persona flaws. It's generally an opinion, but it feels like they were afraid to take the full dive in some story and writing aspects, and some of the side stories writing (especially followers/slink) is still quite bland and bad IMO.Overall, an extremely fun and addictive game and I highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game. Story was alright. Combat was as difficult as you made it out to be. Bring the right ability/damage type and it was pretty easy. Protagonist could have used a little more personality as it really seemed like the main character should have been Strohl. You don't really get enough spare days when everything opens up. You can finish everything but it's pretty tight.Really feels like you are punished if you ever stop to grind out some archetype exp as it ends up overleveling you and trivializing combat by taking away the forced combat encounters. Not having to do all the random encounter combat saves a ton of MP which seems to be the only real challenge. If you dont stop at all to grind, you are starved for money and magla. Really seems like some numbers tweaking would have done wonders.Seems like they realized very late in the games design that there wasn't a good way to farm archetype or catch up your later party members in levels You get your magic stat based party members and archetypes far too late into the game. The summoner outclasses the other caster so hard it's not even close and you get the final Berserker/Destroyer so late that you most likely have already unlocked Royal Berserker, making all the others pointless compared to Wanton Destruction and the other attack that ignores all resists and still benefits from all strike bonus damage. You never really get a chance to make much use of Martial Artist/Destroyer, outside of bringing over abilities to save MP clearing trash using HP costs.

_childDocuments_.review: Metaphor is an interesting experience. Atlus takes all their past learnings from decades of SMT and Persona, and with it, creates one of the best turn based RPG systems i've seen in decades.The gameplay is really tight and addictive, made even harder to put down by the high quality, soaring orchestral score of the battle themes. Character progression is far simpler than SMT and Persona, which I found to be a good thing; the class-based system reminds me of final fantasy tactics, where you could mix and match elements of jobs you had mastered to enhance your characters to fill whatever role you wished them to fill. There's also QOL features such as a "retry this battle from the start" button in case you make a really big mistake during a fight. Really good stuff.Where the game falls off a bit, however, is in its story and characters. It's not good, but it certainly isn't bad either; however, after having played many of ATLUS's other games, it does seem like a marked step down from their usual seal of quality. To me, most major characters felt bland and uninteresting, like generic good guys with one or two quirks thrown in to count as personality. The party felt like characters, not people, and often have no flaws, or cartoonish ones. The follower NPCs are a bit better with this but nothing to write home about; and most of the visual character designs were distractingly bad IMHO (looking at Strohl and his silly banana Timbs coat, or Catherina in general). English voice acting also left a lot to be desired for me personally; everyone talks the same generic, old english way, with the very jarring exception of the protagonist. On the story side, it's.. really standard RPG fare, although slightly darker than usual for the sake of shock value. The game can't help itself from brutally killing people to reinforce its messages that it uses to beat you over the head with. "These guys are evil, and racism sucks!" is all it ever really amounts to. The ending wasn't terribly satisfying either, as it was certainly one of ATLUS's weakest final boss fights in terms of spectacle and quality.All that aside, the game is an easy 9/10 as the good handily overshadows the "bad", which I only say is bad when compared to the company's other works, and through the lends of decades of RPG experience. Drspite my nitpicking, the best TBRPG combat of the decade is ultimately wrapped up in a tidy and functional package, even if it feels a tidbit 'sterilized' for mass appeal.
_childDocuments_.name: Metaphor: ReFantazio

_childDocuments_.review: Atlus really just gave us Persona 3 Reload, Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance, and now this. Great RPG and definitely Atlus at their best. The game uses Persona 5's or Catherine's engine so if you like that look, its here as well. I am pretty sure this game got announced around the same time as p5. I've been waiting FOREVER for this.I personally think it handled a lot of topics FF16 tried to dabble on so much better. Shows actual oppression and injustice, classism, racism, sexism, and prejudice against cultures and religion. Really surprised Japan discussed these topics pretty unbiased with so many cool designs for their POC and non human-like designs. Combat is the usual SMT/Persona/DDS style with a mix of the Final Fantasy Job System and Trails as well.OST is FANTASTIC. They use the normal fantasy style of music but incorporate the many motifs to represent the different cultures. Best track imo is the Island's Theme. The game is relatively easy, if you grind I am sure it's even easier. The beginning can be a bit tough though but I highly recommend playing on hard. A lot of my achievements were not unlocking and I am sure its due to the connection from the demo not translating those achievements. _childDocuments_.review: The Kingdom of Euchronia is teetering on the brink of collapse. Years of strife have drained its people, breeding mistrust and deepening societal divisions. A rigid, oppressive hierarchy governs the land, with racial prejudice and fear ruling daily life. As whispers of monstrous abominations spread, threatening the safety of both city dwellers and rural folk, the nation’s leadership lies in ruins. The prince, cursed into a perpetual slumber, is presumed lost. The king, assassinated in his chambers, leaves a fractured nation behind. Two dominant factions vie for control:The Sanctist Church, a powerful religious order, clings to its reign by sowing fear and marginalizing those deemed “lesser.” Meanwhile, the formidable Louis Guiabern rallies an army that prizes strength and merit above all else, discarding the weak in the pursuit of dominance.Metaphor: Re Fantazio plunges you into this tumultuous world just days before the late king’s funeral. You step into the shoes of a young Elda—a race despised by society and reviled as unholy abominations. Scorned by the populace, shunned by the powerful, and forced to endure the worst the kingdom has to offer, your journey begins with only a loyal fairy companion, Gallica, by your side. Together, you embark on a desperate mission: uncover the secrets behind the prince’s curse by seeking an unknown ally in the Euchronian army.But in a land where your kind is seen as expendable, the army has no qualms about sending you straight to the front lines. Here begin’s the trademark Atlus tutorial, an exposition-heavy dive to explain and set-up it’s richly built high fantasy world that fuses biomechanical marvels with knights, elves, and magic.After five hours of setup, the stakes skyrocket as the late king’s magic triggers a kingdom-wide democratic race. In a bold twist, the next ruler will be decided not by birthright but by earning the favor of Euchronia’s divided populace. From here, the game fully opens up, propelling you into an epic 60-hour adventure filled with political intrigue, harrowing dungeon crawls, and battles that span the kingdom’s breathtaking landscapes.At the heart of your journey lies the aforementioned biomechanical marvel: the **Gauntlet Runner**. This cutting-edge blend of technology and magic serves as your mobile base of operations, an indispensable companion as you traverse the sprawling landscapes of Euchronia. With cities, settlements, and dungeons spread far and wide, travel isn’t instant—it’s a journey. Fortunately, the Runner is more than just a vehicle; it’s a home.Outfitted with an array of amenities, the Runner becomes a hub for both survival and strategy. A bath provides temporary stat boosts, essential for tougher battles ahead, while the kitchen lets you prepare meals to carry into combat. A small onboard library offers more than just lore; reading its books builds Virtues, a unique mechanic acting as skill checks for unlocking quest opportunities and furthering side narratives.Life aboard the Runner isn’t just about preparation—it’s about building a connection with your party. Whether sparring to hone combat skills, helping keep watch from the crow’s nest, or gathering around the fire for heartfelt conversations, these moments strengthen your bond with each companion. These relationships grow naturally, making each interaction feel meaningful as you uncover their struggles and triumphs, only compounded by how different each companion is in terms of design and personality. From the stalwart Roussainte Heisenberg to the contemplative Eugief Heismay, each member is as colorful as they are unique - creating one of the most engaging and interesting party compositions in an Atlus game yet. The world of Metaphor is absolutely captivating to explore, with every location offering a unique blend of visual splendor and narrative depth. From bustling cities to serene villages, the places you visit are living, breathing reflections of Euchronia’s fractured culture.Take Port Brilehaven, a coastal city where massive floating spheres of water dominate the skyline, creating a surreal, otherworldly atmosphere. Or venture to Eht Ria, a small tribal town scattered across the islands of the Prismatic Sea, where coral reefs can be barely glimpsed above the waves, glowing under the golden sunlight in a breathtaking display. Then there’s the holy city of Altabury Heights, nestled high in the mountains. Its red and yellow, autumn-like foliage glistens beneath a gentle snowfall, blending tranquility with divine reverence.Each location pulses with life, its culture, politics, and architecture interwoven into the fabric of its design. The struggles of the citizens, the structures of power, and the natural surroundings combine to create dynamic microcosms of a world in turmoil. Every city offers a new layer of understanding, further immersing you in the kingdom’s plight and providing reasons to inspire change.But exploration comes with challenges. Lurking threats and political unrest abound, and it’s here that Metaphor shines brightest with its masterfully crafted combat system.Whether you're fending off monsters spawned from the kingdom’s darkest nightmares or clashing with rival factions, combat is more than a test of skill—it’s a reflection of your journey. Early on, you unlock your first Archetype, a manifestation of a legendary hero from ages past. Archetypes grant unique skills, allowing you to tailor each character’s abilities to your playstyle. Over time, you’ll unlock additional Archetypes and the ability to carry over skills, crafting a personalized vision for each party member.Combat itself is a finely tuned chess match. Positioning matters—characters in the front row deal and take more damage, while the back row offers reduced offense in exchange for some brief defensive safety. These decisions cost Press Turn Icons, a finite resource dictating your turn’s actions. Striking weaknesses or executing special abilities earns extra icons, while missteps can quickly deplete them. Every battle demands strategy, whether balancing buffs and debuffs, managing status ailments, or repositioning teammates to avoid enemy attacks targeting specific rows.Mastering these intricacies is no small feat, but the payoff is immense. By the endgame, you’ll face some of the most challenging yet fair encounters in the JRPG genre, where the stakes are higher than ever. These battles elevate the narrative without a single wasted line of dialogue, showcasing the escalating tension and gravity of your journey through sheer gameplay.  The game demands—and rewards—your full engagement, offering a combat system that feels as alive and dynamic as the world it inhabits.Metaphor: Re Fantazio is a triumph of storytelling, world-building, and gameplay—a rare blend where every piece feels meticulously crafted to serve the greater whole. From its sprawling, politically charged landscapes to its deeply personal character arcs and intricate combat systems, the game offers an experience that is as emotionally resonant as it is mechanically rewarding.What sets it apart from others in the genre is how effortlessly it balances its many elements. It doesn’t just ask you to engage with its systems—it invites you to live in its world, to feel the weight of its conflicts, and to reflect on the choices you make as you guide your party through their trials. Each step of the journey feels meaningful, from exploring breathtaking cities steeped in culture and conflict to honing your strategy in battles that test your wit and resolve.By the time the credits roll, you won’t just have completed an adventure—you’ll have truly experienced one, full of growth, hardship, and triumph. This isn’t just a game; it’s an unforgettable odyssey that reminds us of the power that one person has in the face of overwhelming odds.

_childDocuments_.review: I have some mixed feelings about this one. On one hand, I love the setting and the vibe of the game. On the other hand, I was so frustrated by the game mechanics that by the end of the game I turned the difficulty down from hard to story just because…I was kind of exhausted with the combat and class system after 130 hours or so. I just wanted to see the ending and GTFO.I have played Persona 3 reload, 4 Golden, and 5 Royal as well as Tokyo Mirage Sessions and SMTV. I am going to make parallels to these games because if I am being real they are all the same game wrapped in a different story. Otherwise it’s really the same turn based rpg mechanic with the same elements and similar moves in all 3.Here’s what I liked:- The story and the characters. But if I am being honest, I prefer the stories fromPersona 3-5. I felt a little distance from the characters in this one, but I still maxed out all of their bonds. Some stories I liked more than others. But there were no characters I didn’t like. So there’s that. The overall story was also really good. Had a lot of touching moments. So if you enjoy Atlus stories, you’ll probably love this one too. It was my favorite part of the game.- Combat and archetype system. I am going to put this in things I didn’t like as well for different reasons, but for a good while I enjoyed the combat. It’s basically the same Atlus turn based rpg system with the same usual moves for the most part, but all of your characters get to turn into a variety of different…uhm…transformers basically. Robot fighters. It’s what you expect from Atlus for the most part. It’s the same thing as always I don’t know what else to say. - Art & Music. As always, beautiful. Why I bought the game for real. I knew I would love the art and music. What I didn’t like:- After a while, combat got really old and boring. Toward the end of the game there was nothing keeping it super fresh. Unlocking new archetypes started to become a game of resource management. And I think I really have played too many games from Atlus using the same systems which brings me to my next point. It’s a “new game” but they could have made it more original but instead the combat is the same as every other game they make. And I am kinda bored of it by now. They need some innovation desperately. Because I have high expectations for Persona 6. - The amount of enemies and bosses they recycle in this one is too many. I felt like I was fighting the same enemies the entire game. Dungeons all looked the same for the most part. And exploration because of all this was very stale. - Some things people keep asking for, some don’t agree with it, but I feel like they are things they have to address and tell everyone ‘no’ with every release. 1.There’s no female protagonist option. I wanna see it. 2. No romance. Not even just no romance options for the protagonist, I can’t think of any npc characters in the entire 150 hours I played that were in a stable relationship. The game I would say is completely asexual. So I liked it…not my favorite release of theirs. If you like their other games you will probably like it. Not my personal favorite.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to talk about the pros and cons of the game as there are enough people who have already done that. Instead I'm going to talk about how I actually felt playing it.My first jrpg was Chrono Trigger back in 1997. At the time, games were just a past time for me but Chrono Trigger changed that. It gave me a completely new perspective on video games, how the can be more than just a past time but an interactive experience unlike anything else at the time. However over the decades the genre has pretty much faded into obscurity due to how derivative every new jrpg felt.Metaphor: ReFantazio on the hand changed that. It is the first jrpg in more than a decade to rekindle that excitement that I had playing classics like Chrono Triggerr, FF6, FF7 and the likes. It reminded me about what was so amazing about this genre and most importantly, why I fell in love with video games back in 1997.This game is just oozing with passion and creativity. It's a testament to the decades of experience that the Persona team had gained developing their unique brand of jrpgs. To put this into perspective, I had played FF16 just a week before Metaphor and it felt like a game made by a team who was unfamiliar with jrpgs. This to me was mind boggling given the fact that some of my all time favourite games were made by Square Enix. There was so much of thought put into every aspect of the game that I couldn't help but admire what I believe was the team's determination to create the ultimate jrpg experience. For instance, I cannot recall any pther jrpg that had a chat log that you could access instantly with a single button input in case you went through a conversation too quickly or if you felt like reading again some dialogue that is of particular interest to you. The game also allows you to instantly teleport to key locations like item vendors, right up to the doorstep of said location regardless of how far away they are. Combat feels is incredibly fluid because you can just skip the casting animations if you're tired of watching through it. In fact, it's this respect that the devs have for the player's time that prevented the game from being a chore after 70 hours of playtime. Yes, this is a very big game if you intend to complete all of the side quests and no, it does not get boring thanks to how incredibly well designed the combat mechanic and dungeons are and how well paced the main story is.If you have any love for this genre then do yourself the favor of at least trying out the demo. It's truly an amazing game that I'm certain will be heralded as one of the greatest jrpgs ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: Games long so I will keep the review short.The good:+Short side compared to any Persona game so it doesn't overstay its welcome+All the characters are written fairly well and are interesting.+Combat system is good. Progressing classes also had a lot of thought put into it for both casuals and more hardcore players.+Music slaps+Performance is good (sort of)+Story is good, even with the very "slap you over the head" messaging it tries to send about IRL stuff.+Bonds and pacing is good. You don't need a guide to max anything unlike with some of the Persona games.The Cons:-Graphical fidelity issues. Looks like a PS2 game. Some textures have like some ugly 180p resolution and it stands out so hard idk what that s**t is.-Your Fantasy can die from your character not rolling the overworld attack and you get ambushed.-Some dungeons are really samey-Some bosses have annoying gimmicks that aren't hinted at in dialogue before the fight (ya'll know who i'm talking about).-From my understanding if you buy any of the DLC with the different game OSTs it doesn't work unless you actually get in a squad battle. -If you aren't that into dialogue there is a TON of it. To be fair though if you don't like dialogue you shouldn't be playing an Atlus RPG lol.Overall:If you tried any of the Persona games and thought they were too long this game might be for you as it isn't as long as those. This is overall a great game that is carried by its characters and combat. I think the locales and graphics in the game are a weakpoint but not enough to bring the game down. Overall its a recommend from me if you are an Atlus fan or someone wanting to try something new.

_childDocuments_.review: actually fell in love with this game. I wasn't so sure about it at the start, it took a while to get into the groove of combat for me and it did take me a bit to warm up to the story, but at a certain point it all clicked together. I adored every single character in the game and I think the english voice cast did a crazy good job at bringing them all to life. I also appreciate that unlike persona, you can absolutely max your relationships and finish everything in one playthrough - despite that, I still have the urge to play through it a second time. For the record, maxing out everything on a first playthrough won't even require you to follow a strict guide so long as you're paying attention to your actions, which is a bonus.The character designs are all great and I ended up looking forward to each characters appearance, the humans as well all had a really cool look to them. Not sure I super loved the fourth wall stuff, but I got what they were going for. Anyway, basilio and fidelio are my favourites. Play the demo first, but definitely give this game a go :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game features a compelling and charismatic ensemble cast that tells many inspiring and relatable stories. There is not one party character that I don't like and even the secondary archetype characters are very fun and engaging. In my opinion, this game's greatest strength is its cast. The score is amazing, the artstyle is very fresh and unique, the storyline is very ambitious and it delivers a socially important allegory, the gameplay is familiar but adds in some mechanics that set it apart as being distinctly  For me, it is my GOTY. The only gripe I have with this game is the difficulty of the final battle. I think it didn't feel rewarding, by the time I finally beat it I really was just ready for it to be over. _childDocuments_.review: Beaten the game on hard, all quests completed and obtained true ending.The quality of the voice acting is fantastic, however the coverage of dialogue actually voice acted is spotty, quite often you'll hear a generic placeholder like "What?" in place of several sentences which can derail immersion in a given quest / story segment when there's little emotion to back it up.As for the story itself, whilst I won't spoil the turning point in which I came to dislike it - this story felt incoherent and rushed towards the end. Several locations with moderate relevance and intrigue are never mentioned again or explored, one of which is even on the navigational map and implies "not yet" whenever you try to travel to it. The story started with ample intrigue and world building just to fizzle out by the end as a persona-esque ending of unresolved nonsense.The combat is basically persona with a mask on, the archetypes being limited sets of persona abilities with minimal inheritence or overlap. It did take away some of the fatigue of persona's fusions and other such gimmicks at the cost of build variety, and the world combat would often make your build redundant by slaughtering once intimidating enemies with a couple of swings of a blade.Ultimately I don't think the full price reflects the quality of the game, it felt incomplete and the story despite being presented as a fantasy setting of a different name is basically still a persona setting, if not for the nostalgic support of being persona-adjacent I don't think this game would've been well recieved.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a fan of the Persona Series (and then the SMT series as a whole) since Persona 3. This is the best iteration of the formula to date. The combat benefits extremely well from the over world attacking system. The Archetypes also provides a lot of potential for build paths strategic team switches. The travel system is super unique and benefits the pacing and the story progression very well. Changing up to a fantasy setting is also very refreshing (no more living the high school life for the umpteenth time!). The characters all feel very vibrant and different while still complimenting each other. I recommend strongly to anyone who enjoys jrpgs and can deal with the story often taking center stage over gameplay, even if you've never touched an SMT game. Here's hoping they decide to continue this as an off series to Persona! (or similar style!)

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10Really nice change of pace from traditional turnbased combat, tho if you're grinding for archetype xp, chances are in late game, you would barely get to fight mobs in turnbased mode (can be considered a down factor since the regular battle theme is fire)Main dungeons are pretty well made, optional/side quest ones get boring pretty easily as they are more or less the same. Moderate enemy variety, since most enemies are reused every arc, with a different color coatingSome soundtracks are fire, other are pretty forgettableOne of the problems with the job(archetype in this game) system i found is every character from mc to last character which you unlock near the very end starts with an empty archetype mastery, so the characters you have from the start of the game will have more archetypes unlocked than the last, which kinda sucks since the last character you unlock is the second best phys user (or first if mc isn't phys focused) and the only way to utilize that character is to grind, a lotOverall, still an enjoyable game

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game today and this is without a doubt the best game i have played since BG3 came out. They took all the best elements from Persona, mixed it with the best from SMT's combat system and made a story that actually got me choking up at some points. Combined with the Archetype system allowing for an insane amount of battle formations, the overworld combat making you not waste time on low level enemies while still not making it completely safe (yes i died once because i got swarmed by skellies in a tower) yet still rewarding enough to actually interact with it. add to that some of my new favorite party members (i absolutely love my homies Strohl, The Eugief and the Paripus that join later, no names for potential spoiler reasons) and its my GOTY by a landslide.

_childDocuments_.review: Before this game came out, I remember reviewers saying that this is Studio Zero's and Hashino's Magnum Opus. I kinda doubted this considering how incredible the Persona series is, now after finally beating the game and doing as much side content as I possible can I am inclined to agree with that sentiment.This game feels like it takes all of lessons the studio has learned about writing, gameplay, and visual design and puts it all into a brand new IP. Even with the similarities to Persona and SMT are there, they are fresh enough to stand alongside both series. If you even remotely enjoy turn-based RPG's, you owe it to yourself to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: 11/10. After finally finishing in the game, I can very happily say it's an absolute masterpiece. It's rare for a game to absorb my attention and immerse me in such a way that I play for over 100 hours and still don't want the adventure to end. I feel like I blinked and two weeks passed (wtf it's already October 27th???)...Everything is absolutely top tier. Music, sound, world, characters, story, combat, you name it. I really can't think of any complaints outside of maybe the anti-aliasing being kind of weird but at the same time it made the background environment feel alive at times so it didn't bother me. The art style and vibes definitely make up for it. Plus, being able to kill low level enemies without having to engage in turn based combat really spices things up. Each class has different overworld passives and some even allow for mana regen or incredible amounts of money so it gets very addicting to just run around slaying everything. I wish this game had a kill count, I easily mowed down thousands of enemies just to prevent myself from using mana items because "what if I need them later". I never used them LOL, classic If you have any interest at all in this game, you should give the demo a try. I wasn't really sure if I wanted to dedicate time to a JRPG right now since it's spooky month and there's been so many other good game releases lately, but after finishing the demo when it first came out I was incredibly hooked and could not stop thinking about this game. It's worth.The demo haunted my brain for weeks before the final release and it even haunts me now that I've finished the entire game, but in all the best ways. ok done yapping bye

_childDocuments_.review: Metaphor: ReFantazio should win Game of the Year because the swordfish in the sky clearly knows how to juggle flaming marshmallows while reciting poetry in Morse code. Also, the map smells faintly of lavender, which is an undeniable advantage over any other game.And honestly, I prefer waffles over pancakes because they have built-in syrup pockets. Who wouldn’t want that level of breakfast engineering?

_childDocuments_.review: With a stunning art style, charming characters, and an immersive story, this game is a must-play for fans of the genre.The attention to detail in the game's art style is second to none, and the characters are all brimming with personality.The game's combat system is both engaging and intuitive, with a variety of skills and abilities that allow players to customize their playstyle. The enemies you face are challenging, but never feel unfair, making for a well-balanced and satisfying experience.In comparison, Metaphor: ReFantazio's story, while engaging, doesn't quite reach the same heights as Persona 5. It's a well-told tale, but it lacks the same level of complexity and nuance that Persona 5 brings to the table.At the end of the day, both games offer fantastic gaming experiences, but Persona 5's story is truly in a league of its own.In conclusion, Metaphor: ReFantazio is a must-play RPG that stands out from the crowd.

_childDocuments_.review: Any fan of modern JRPGs should give this some time. An expertly presented adventure with attention given to vivid aesthetics at every point.  The unique world is fun to explore and the characters are engaging, though borrowing from well tread tropes.  Combat hits a good balance of punchy and tactical, with options to breeze through low level mobs without slowing down later gameplay.   The time mechanic and forced opportunity costs, familiar to SMT/Persona, may not appeal to everyone but is a core component with increasing complexity that builds as you progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Metaphor: ReFantazio

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't bad, but this many years in the Atlus format isn't cutting it anymore.To be blunt and short; it's Persona with an unimaginative fantasy skin, reiterating the tropes of the genre we've seen so many times before.The story proceeds with slow pacing and, with one or two exceptions, the characters are stereotypical and one-note.The combat mechanics have welcome changes, but those changes come with more boring grind and lacks the experimentation and variety of fusion.The score has a few standout tracks, but overall lacks the impact of Meguro's previous work.The game is about traveling, not about seeing sights and visiting places, but specifically the act of traveling itself. For much of the game you're selecting destinations from preset locations on a map and spending time inside your Gauntlet Runner. Fantastical locations and vistas are reduced to a single JPEG with dialogue on top and large cities consist of a few small screens with a couple of NPCs and small indoor enviroments.Dungeon design is samey with most side locations being little more than a copy-paste job.With all of this said, being a game produced by a AAA developer with years of experience in the genre, Metaphor is still not a  game. It's a perfectly cromulent 7/10 or  even 8/10 JRPG, but Atlus has to expand and innovate if they want to stay relevant in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. _childDocuments_.review: Fun game.+ Good soundtrack+ Rollercoaster story--last third is a crazy stream of plot twists that keep coming at you right up until the end of the game+ Well-written characters+ Japanese voice acting was good+ Forgiving calendar system that allowed an idiot like me to get most of the achievements in one playthrough+ Long game with lots of content- Simple action overworld combat is nice to have, but doesn't feel the greatest- Can't romance anyone (removing romance helps focus the story, so this could also be a pro)- Side dungeons start getting repetitive towards the end of the game- Long game with lots of contentI never thought I would like a game about the campaign trail to become El Presidente of Fantasy Land, but here we are. If you have a spare 60-100 hours to flush down the toilet, consider playing this.

_childDocuments_.review: absolutly fantastic game, the next generation of persona games and if this is the future we can expect from Atlus then i'm very excited.   The Combat itself feels familiar but great, with the ability to streamline combat into a simplified ARPG if you over level enough.  Saves time on grinding and just gives the game a whole new feel.  Each archtype has their own attack in the overworld, as well as passives that actually incentivise this overworld combat rather than the squad based combat, like regening MP or HP when you stun or kill an overworld target. On top of that the story is top tier atlus content.  The twists and turns really do keep you on your toes, and this is the first game in a long time that the ending left me with a feeling of hope, rather than the emptyness and loss of completing a game that's been your constant companion over 200 hours. (looking at you persona 5R)a completely enjoyable game, that i look forward to revisiting when the inevitable expansion hits.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.I see a lot of people compare this to Persona, and it does draw a lot of inspiration from the Persona games. It also draws a lot of inspiration from Atlus' other games as well, mainly SMT. I would say the narrative and story telling is more reminiscent of Persona while most of the game play elements are drawn from SMT, so comparing this game to Persona and SMT both seems fair. The story Metaphor tells, while good, is not on the same level as Persona, and the game play, while good, is not on the same level as SMT, but rather Metaphor strikes a good balance here and doesn't skimp on one element in favor of the other. This game is clearly meant to be a culmination of all Atlus has done over the years. I'm not sure it really offers any new ideas though, it mostly refines and polishes old ideas to create a very familiar experience. It's a great game, but it does feel a little bit dull at times. It suffers from the same mid game drag that the Persona games do, and the  Story is a little predictable. The twists the story throws at you aren't as impactful as it feels like they should be. I played the game with English voice acting and dialogue, so I can't speak for other languages, but I found the dialogue to be poorly written and the voice acting is pretty bad for some characters. I've heard that the bad dialogue is the fault of localization, though. I know I laid out a lot of criticisms here but I really did enjoy the game, Atlus has a good formula here and it shows, the fights are fun, the archetype system makes for good strategic decision making, and the characters are fun and (mostly) interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Review post demo with an optional dungeon/1st main dungeon complete (I am going to leave this as minimal as possible and is directed mainly at seasoned Atlas fans for a quick review no MAJOR spoilers here)Metaphor: ReFantazio is the newest IP from the Persona team! Metaphor takes place in a high fantasy setting that has been very reminiscent of Ivalice for me (FFT, FF12) The heavy use of magic/magical items, general location vibes, and various tribes of people all come together perfectly and has been very immersive/refreshing.Persona mechanics: social links, calendar + deadlines, 1 day/night activity cycle ex. All these systems are polished/tweaked a bit but any returning Persona fan will feel right at home. Combat: SMT Press Turns! Hit a weakness - get that half turn! I am very happy they decided to use the SMT press turn system as it feels right at home in Metaphors setting. Prepare for an old fashion miss your attack, lose your last two press turns, and then get wiped by the boss like I did lol.Music: Slaps hard. Hard asf. Meguro literally can't disappoint me at this point. Shout out too the couple tracks that sound straight outta Strange Journey. That music during the intro waste section was so goooood.Difficulty: Balanced and fun on normal like any persona title should be. The addition of the press turn system definitely helps normal difficulty combat feel a bit better than usual imo. Hard didn't feel much different for me besides my numbers going down and the enemies going up. You can switch difficulties as long as you aren't in combat so you can adjust to whatever suits you. A warning too long time SMT fans - even hard will be easy for you but it should still be fun.That's it! Thanks for reading. This is definitely a must buy for any Atlas/JRPG fan. I'll be back to leave a story review in a week or two.

_childDocuments_.review: About 8.5/10. Good but not great. Can't help but compare it to how memorable P5 and P4 was and how Metaphor did not have that impact after finishing the game. I feel this way mainly because there are so many factors preventing better immersion. And when it comes to fantasy stories, immersion is so important for me.Firstly, the calendar and the social sim does not fit quite well as it did with Persona's high school setting where it made perfect sense. There were some ridiculous writing in the story and dialogues to accommodate the calendar system. As for the social sim, sometimes they don't feel realistic since the npc's in question are disjointed to what's currently happening within the game world (without spoiling anything).Second is the writing itself. I'm not sure how to explain it but the game feels like a children's book where the characters basically keep reminding me about how important it is to face 'my' fears for hours on end in a straight up manner and not in a metaphorical way. And this is obviously intentional. I'd hope Atlus just told a fantasy story and let the player translate what the story means for him. This absolutely breaks immersion turning a good game into 100 hour lecture. Third are the locations themselves. The cities and dungeons are large but somehow they just look dead. I think it's because of the colors.Fourth is the music. They're not bad at. at all. But Persona's is just way better and sticks with you.So yeah. good, forgettable game. Still worth playing and paying for at it's price. Atlus, please make Persona 7.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this review, I am currently in the first 8.3 hours of the game. Would I recommend it? After playing the first 8 hours, no. But I will continue playing and hope that my thoughts towards it will change.Concept: 8/10 - It is a breath of fresh air for having a story that wants to tackle the impact of politics and government to the people that it governs. So far, at its first 8 hours, it talks about how in an utopia, democracy is the way to form a government. Although it is not entirely true, I am interested with how it will hold up as the story unfolds given how Atlus games are brilliant in terms of making twists that are thought-provoking and usually challenges the set tone or idea.Story & Characters: 9/10 - This is where Atlus really excel. All characters have realistic motivations that conspires to a grand quest. They are fun but serious characters that transcend the game. The story is highly interesting and intriguing as it reflects our real world while also referencing an utopia that seems to be the perfect version of our world.Gameplay: 5.5/10 - Although the Archetype system is interesting, it is undoubtedly unoriginal for the sole reason that those are just job classes that you can equip on all characters. Quick fighting is good but not so good that it is revolutionary. If I would compare this with another Atlus game, specifically P3R, P3R's gameplay is much better just because it offers the One More mechanic which makes hitting the enemy's weakness worth it. In Metaphor, hitting enemy's weakness means nothing really aside from having a slightly stronger attack. Also, the thing that I hate about it so far is how the game gives you options with the dialogue but do not actually give you any. Most lines are just saying the same thing so choosing either would not really impact how the story will unfold or how the characters would develop. Lastly, freedom is highly limited within the first 8 hours of the game. The moment you set foot to getting a vessel to travel the map, you will automatically go into the journey and there's no turning back and you can say goodbye to finishing the quests in the city before actually leaving.Design: 7/10 - I love how the characters were visually designed as well as the cities. However, if we'll talk about the dungeons, it's a different story as most dungeons (in the first 8hrs of the game) are bland and uninteresting. In comparison with other games, it is redundant and boring at worst.Music: 8/10 - IT IS GOOD. It sets the tone very well. Nothing more to be said here.
