_childDocuments_.review: Basically Persona, but in a unique fantasy setting. It’s very philosophical and questions the importance of fantasy itself and how it can inspire hope and change—often in political contexts. The narrative tackles various societal issues (like discrimination based on race or societal class) in a profound way. The story is interesting and often quite moving, with characters who are relatable, funny, and memorable. Overall, the game is well-written. Its vibe reminds me a bit of Berserk. There are quality-of-life improvements here that I’d love to see in future games, maybe even in Persona 6. For example, you can dodge and attack with a button press, like in an action game, allowing you to defeat weaker enemies or weaken tougher ones (though you still need to enter turn-based combat for them). You can also restart the entire battle with the press of a button during your turn. While some might see this as a drawback, as it reduces the challenge, I appreciate that it saves me the time of running all the way back to the same spot.SMT demons are absent, and instead, we have an entirely new collection of monsters that you can't capture or use. The main cast uses Persona-like entities called Archetypes, which represent various fantasy roles—like warrior, mage, healer, and more. This time, not only can the MC switch between these "Personas," but all characters can use every Archetype, and the game often encourages you to do so. I often found that switching Archetypes in response to difficulties led to significant improvements in my strategy.It also feels more mature to me because it explores deeper themes than just local injustices in a school or a town; it delves into the very core of human behavior and how rotten desires lead to the biggest mistakes humanity can face. Actually, the bosses in the game are called Humans, which is quite fitting. If you’re tired of high school settings but enjoy the Atlus formula, then this game is for you. Some players may miss the dating mechanics, so keep that in mind if it’s important to you.The art is absolutely best in class; the famous Atlus UI is very much present here. The sounds, the music, and the character portraits—it's all top-notch. If you’re into artsy stuff like that, then there is honestly no better place. The stunning visuals and audio not only enhance the experience but also serve to immerse you further in this world.The demo is pretty lengthy and lets you continue where you left off if you decide to buy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Metaphor: ReFantazio

_childDocuments_.review: Juxtaposing the idealistic and the horrific this game brings a lot of what I like in the Persona games and cuts off some of the extra fat that burdens that series. Menus, combat, screen transitions, everything has a very stylish quality to it that is very enjoyable if it fits your aesthetics. Graphics are more style than polish but play very well into the setting of the game. Combat is challenging and at times unforgiving, you need to be on your toes to not be caught off guard or defeated due a moment of carelessness, fortunately there is a battle reset option to begin again at the start of a battle. The day to day choices are for the most part more forgiving than Persona 5, as are the bonding events, but criteria is not always as clear as you might want.I haven't finished this yet so hesitate to say more but I will simply say that I find the game hard to put down once I pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Metaphor: ReFantazio

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game all around. I have never player an Atlus game before and this was a stunning introduction.It just takes everything about a standard JRPG and just nudges it to be better. The music, visual, story, and gameplay are all just a cut above.It feels like it is very respectfully inserting itself into the tradition of JRPGs and putting its own twist to it. It is very satisfying.I had no serious issues with this game. The only thing I had any negative feelings toward is the time-limited aspect, which is generally generous and allows you to get what you need to do done with time to spare. However, as a newbie to this style of gameplay (who always finds time limits in RPGs mildly stressful) it can be a bit difficult to understand precisely what is most important to do. This was not really an issue for me until the very last deadline, in which because I was trying to complete everything with every follower and side quest I ended up with zero days to spare. This, however, was a minor issue more particular to me than the game itself. I anticipate very few players having serious issues with this mechanic.
_childDocuments_.name: Metaphor: ReFantazio

_childDocuments_.review: I'm "only" 24h in, so I haven't finished the game. But considering all I've seen, together with my history of playing Persona 3 and 4 on OG Playstation 2, and then more recently P5 and P5 Royal, I can already tell this is the crystallization of everything from the best the studio has had to offer from those titles, AND then some. Also in a completely different setting from before, since Persona games star high-school students.It's a jRPG with flawless artistic presentation, it's turn-based combat that manages to improve and be more engaging and complex even compared to P5R, you can be sure to have space to optimize your squad composition and development to exploit the enemies. And all this with  characters and story beats that feel just so engaging and inspiring.It unabashedly pokes at you comparing the so-called "fantasy" world of the game to that of the real world we live in, and asks you to consider what you truly believe in.I usually play this kind of game with the OG Japanese VO, but given the specific setting of this game (a "medieval"-esque fantasy land with so many echoes of other fantasy-like and traditional folk-tale stories from the "european"-centered culture) I took a chance on the English VO. Boy, I am very happy with that choice - they did a phenomenal job with different voice actors with different origins in the English-speaking universe. I can recognize Irish and Scottish and English and so many other accents and vocabulary, even like Hulkenberg has clear German or thereabouts tones in her accent. All this is pretty cool since it really lends to an important aspect of the game which is about the different races and locations from the world. I'm from Portugal, I learned a bit of Japanese, but of course I'm so much more familiar with closer to home accents in the English language, this is very cool. And for native English speakers I can only imagine how rewarding it is.Even if I'm "only" 24h in, I can tell this is the epitome of everything the Persona games have realized, and it's very impressive. Everything is just so sleek and optimised you can feel all of it, between the challenges of combat, the interesting unique moments with characters, and optimizing your development.And yet there is more - I feel strong hints all around about the "message" the game purports to convey to the player, and I'm feeling it building as I play.I couldn't hold myself any longer writing this review, since I know I'll have at least 100h total before I finished, but people need to know how great this is.I haven't even mentioned the lovely soundtrack that pretty much creates a world of its own :)Truly this feels like an instant classic surpassing so many jRPG classics from before, and this launched in 2024. It also runs beautifully on PC - anti-aliasing could be smoother but there are no bugs whatsoever and high FPS are sure to be achieved.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is amazing. They fixed some of the biggest problems in Persona 5 and improved upon the formula while incorporating the press turn combat system. _childDocuments_.review: Metaphor: ReFantazio, what a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. Despite both Persona 3 Reload and Episode Aigis coming out this year, this game is my game of the year. Truly, this is one of the best games I've played in recent years, with a story and cast of characters that will surely stick with me and impact my life just as strongly as Persona has. Each character you meet throughout your journey within the Kingdom of Euchronia feel alive, having their own beliefs and goals to fight with all their life for. A father who has lost his child, trying to find closure and peace. A royal guard who has failed the ultimate duty, protecting the prince, thus loosing all motivation to upkeep her title. A noblemen who's village was razed to the ground, trying to seek revenge and his true purpose, and so many more. Both party members and enemies alike, all felt real and written in such a way that you could understand what they fought for, and see the passion for said goals through both words and action. The main antagonist, Louis Guiabern, will go down as one of the best villains in media (in my opinion). At first, his goals and aspirations seem ludicrous, striving for the throne of the kingdom to change the world so that only the strongest shall prevail. But as you persist throughout the story and get to know him more and more, the more you come to understand him and what he was truly fighting for, even sometimes agreeing with what he had to say. Ultimately, however, the way he approaches such change is against how you, the player and protagonist, wish to go forward and thus, are forced to fight him. He's a villain that is both unlikeable, yet understandable to a point that you don't hate him, and only wish he could see things how they should truly be laid out, without conflict and bloodshed. OH and don't even get me started on the reoccurring plot beats of magic and magla, and how this game is just one big "Anxiety sucks but if you learn to live with it, it can become a strength and not weakness" message and I LOVE IT. The story as a whole is amazing, and the team over at Studio Zero should be proud of the new world they created, following their success with the Persona series. The music is phenomenal, with Shoji Meguro behind its creation it's no surprise the music was gonna slap. With his works including all of the Persona games, the mid-era of Shin Megami Tensei, Trauma Center, Catherine, and now Metaphor, the man knows his way around music and bringing an energy to any moment, whether it be a bombastic and epic moment, or those of sadness and grief. It's spectacular. The gameplay is perfect, being a full combination of SMT, Etrian Odyssey, Digital Devil Saga, and Persona. The turn based combat feels super rewarding, and having the ability to swap classes on any characters means you can have a party tuned to how you want it, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ required. Want a full physical party? Done. Full Magic? Done. A hybrid party focused on both? Easy. A party comprised of buff, debuffs, healing, and a single hard-hitting damage dealer? Might take awhile, but it can be done. The only limit to your party is the effort you want to put into it, and I think that's the best way of implementing player expression. It's leagues beyond that of Persona in that regard. Overall, this is not only an amazing Fantasy JRPG, it's just a fantastic game with so much that can be pulled from it, I could keep talking for hours about it. This game is a love letter for ATLUS fans and RPG fans alike. If you have even the slightest bit interest in this game, please, I implore you, get it. The 80 or so hours it'll suck you into will be well worth it. Now then, times marches on, and the age of a new king draws nearer...
_childDocuments_.name: Metaphor: ReFantazio

_childDocuments_.review: 100% Yes, you should buy this game. Whether it is the collectors or base is up to you, however this is a game that needs your support. Your effort, a series starter. A start to something more and only by you buying it and playing it can we make that happen. Simply put, this is Persona with an American world view. Some may disagree, but if you have played Persona or any SMT game you will see there are overarching themes within the game. Relationships to build, constant growth and development with your characters. A sliding difficulty, dependent on your ability to grind. This is an example of what JRPG is and should strive for, the characters are engaging. Although typical, they face struggles some more than others. You have choices on how you interact with them as well as benefits in doing so. Every effort rewards you in some way or another. Fighting is turn-based, simple like most of its kind but with just enough variety to give the first few fights novelty. Yet as you get too powerful for an enemy or in my case as it is about to get boring, you can find ways to deal with them in only a swipe. To make the battles less tedious but still fruitful.I was waiting for this game for months, I am pleasantly surprised and it is the only game I am playing till I finish it or get deep enough to take a break. I do not regret waiting for it and it has rekindled my hope in the games industry that we have not forgotten what makes RPGS be so enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Metaphor: ReFantazio

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game. I started like most on the prologue, mind you I started it on hard mode. This gave them enemy an extra turn. I personally recommend you start or normal for a challenge that is fair, and any lower difficulties for a "Blitz Creeg" or "Speed Run" of the game.The game plays well, similar to Persona 5 Royal but with some reworking of certain mechanics. Fighting is a rewarding but hard battle but ultimately boils down to Survive, find their weakness, hit weakness to exploit turn gaining if you can, and buff or do more damage. The Social Links of this game, or Followers as they are called, are all pretty great. Each time you visit them you rank up now, no more of that needing enough affinity points to get them to even want to visit or rank up. This leads to saving much more time to rank them up. Time which than spent leveling up your Social Stats, now called Royal Virtues for this game. Why? Because now you will get essentially stat gated. This means until your Virtues are high enough you cant rank them up yet. I think is a fair trade for not having to waste a time slot on a repeated event or something I have already seen. Social Stat grinding is not as bad, you can see exactly how many you get when you get them, and can pretty easily grind them out by using your time during travel to gain stats.Now lets talk money. The game runs on two currencies : Money and Mag. Mag is all that is important really, as grinding it up is a bit harder than money once you unlock certain classes. Mag can be spent to do stuff with Archetypes, the replacement for personas or demons if your from Soul Hacker or SMT. They are basically your standard RPG classes and work really well to teach you how to combine different ideals into one strong fighting force.As for the story? Its good go play the game! Stop reading reviews and treat yourself! ITS A GOOD GAME!

_childDocuments_.review: I heard someone on the internet say that this game is the Elden Ring of Atlus games. And after playing through it completely, I could not agree more. _childDocuments_.review: Basically persona but with SMT press turns and a very well made DDS style job system along with a new fantasy setting. _childDocuments_.review: Johnny Metaphor brings you the GOTY of 2024It is indeed similar to Persona but it isn't a copy paste with a fantasy setting. Everything is crafted specifically for Metaphor, with new mechanics, mainly the job system via archetypes. Without spoiling too much, the game feels like old school final fantasy games where you had to think before going into an important battle (not grind, think and prepare your team accordingly)It's really fun and challenging, it also doesn't fell as repitive as Persona games can get when you're grinding dungeons - it flows smoother.If you like Persona games this is a must play, so far I like every aspect as much or more than persona, with the only exception being the music doesn't leave an impression as strong as the Persona gsmes did (it's good though, just not as remarkable)If you have no idea how Persona games are, you basically have s turn based JRPG dungeon crawler mixed in with "real life" elements that help your combat stats, unlocks, etc.If you like turn based games I think you should try metaphor.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Fantasy Persona. Get it.I'm maybe almost halfway through the game now and its just as good as Persona 5 but with a better combat and RPG progression system. I would go in as blind as possible. Game loop is super addicting, UI and Art is beautiful. Combat is great. I only have minor gripes.The only obvious flaw is that some of the areas and cutscenes feel a bit lackluster in terms of visual polish. I'm not really someone who cares about graphics much but it is noticeable how unpolished some of the cutscenes/areas are. The reason for this is that it's a fantasy setting with large environments, and some of those environments are only shown briefly, so they spent less time on them. In Persona the lower polish urban seems look better because they are "realistic" but the fantasy environments end up looking last gen when they are unpolished. It makes me think they are saving those areas to be retouched in a potential future remastered edition.I have some minor gameplay complaints as well:- Level balancing feels all over the place for some side quests, I think dungeons/quests need clearly stated level ranges. Especially when you have to plan out multi day trips to reach an area only to find out you are underleveled when you arrive.- Weather really only serves to annoy you and delay plans. Needs to be nerfed or removed.- Planting seeds should not take time, it makes no sense.- All of the story bosses I have encountered are a bit underwhelming so far and I first tried them with few issues. Still ok fights but none have surprised me like P5R fights did.Overall I think there is a good chance Atlus will make a P5R or SMTV:Vengance version of this game and fix all of these issues. Even if they do that I do not regret my purchase, the game is insanely fun. If they do make a remastered version I hope there is some sort of a new game plus to transfer previous version saves, as this is the only Persona/SMT game I would actually like to NG+.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep it short and sweet: I've played P4G and P5, and I like this game more than both. The archetype system works better than the Persona system. _childDocuments_.review: Metaphor ReFantazio is peak Atlus fanservice.This game feels like a love letter to everything Atlus has ever done. It’s full of nods, winks, and callbacks that longtime fans will pick up on right away. Weapon names are straight out of past titles, character names are clever anagrams of older ones, and the dungeons, towns, and traveling all carry little echoes of previous OSTs.Instead of getting bogged down by their history, Atlus turned inward for inspiration and, rather than facing a creative collapse, they wove everything they’ve done into an amazing tapestry of their old works. It’s a celebration of their past that somehow feels completely new. And this doesn’t even get into the layers of meta in the narrative itself.It’s clear that Atlus hasn’t lost their creativity or unique voice, and I’m so glad they took this risk. This game is packed with style and inspiration, and it really stands out.In a time when the world feels so uncertain, the game’s optimism is such a welcome change. For some I'm sure its hopeful tone and fresh perspective couldn’t have come at a better time.Looking forward to any upcoming DLCs and can only hope that this does well enough to lead to a sequel.

_childDocuments_.name: Metaphor: ReFantazio

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a Persona / SMT Junkie this game is a MUST. This is the very first time ATLUS break free from their mold. Gone all the devil summons (Jack Frost we miss you) Gone all the weird but beloved spells (agi? not Fire? Hama?? Zio???). The setting is pure Fantasy not modern world Japan. I won't spoil the story but as usual the story is weird but very interesting; this is not the usual hero/orphan fighting the bad guy/devil king (the main monsters/boss is HUMAN for once)The usual JRPG "Drag" is here expect 1-2 hours of dialog, tutorial and cutscenes to move the story along but when you finally get through it Voila! you can feel the magic immediately and also the incoming dread of 70-100 hours of your life that you WILL DEFINITELY SPEND to finish this masterpiece (Family guy/gal be prepare for the scorn and leering eyes from your spouse)I play this in Steam Deck OLED and it work beautifully; there was a hiccup in the demo version where the FPS can dip to the 10's but ATLUS manage to patch it before launch. Now it can hold 30-60 FPS depending on the scene. the open area is still a challenge for the Deck, It can sometimes dip to below 30 (Update: Steam Deck got some firmware update and improved the performance dramatically, for best performance set the texture to low)Just Finished this masterpiece; the ending is very satisfying without any loose ends and it keep it open enough to warrant further sequel / expansion.I believe this JRPG will be more acceptable for the common gamer especially for those that haven't played the Persona series. Atlus use the engine and framework of Persona 5 and reformulate/rework it to something distinct enough to be its own thing.This title is the first time Atlus dwell into fantasy RPG so there will be some shortcomings:- The Archtype system is unbalanced, some are very very useful, but the rest is so so bordering useless/nice to have. at end game you will stick to a single Arch for every character no need to change/swap.- Setting up the Archtype is also a chore, so much stuff to be inherited but you will be using only a couple of skill, I usually end up just choose whatever skill available not thinking too much.- The bonus/benefits of max level an Arch is not good enough, the bonus is minimal at best. there is no broken stats/skill inheritance to abuse (example FF V job system where you can inherit permanently a job trait; creating the ultimate character)- Items are so various and effective, you can just use them for all the healing and support making a lot of class useless.-There is no major difference between character, only the stats distribution and the exclusive Archtype; but this is a common problem of implementing job system in a JRPG; at the end every character is a blank slate, with effort you can clone/reproduce any character function.- The Archtype still feels too safe there is no wacky or out of the box unique Arch; all the Arch here are very generic you can guess 90 percent of them by using just a little imagination. I think this is FF tactic fault; that game set a very high bar for a job system; the variety, creativity and quantity of jobs is amazing.- Dungeon design is so so; only some are interesting the rest are the usual fantasy dungeon design that you have seen thousand of times in other games (compared to Persona 5 where every dungeon is unique)But for the rest of the game is just perfect the story is not predictable as other JRPG tropes, there is still more to the story til the end game.The character story and background are interesting and distinct enough so you care about them.The story is though provoking enough going quite grim in some places but not as dark/heavy as persona 5 which I considered just right for a lot of people.The music is LIT as usual Shoji Meguro never fails to deilver, example here they use a real monk chanting Sutra as the background music. With all that shortcoming I listed above the game still shines and still a MUST PLAY for fans of Atlus and JRPG in general, it is that good and unique. _childDocuments_.review: It's a breath of fresh air that we’re no longer students wandering Tokyo, starting with finding a lost cat and ending up battling gods. Metaphor: ReFantazio isn’t just another run-of-the-mill JRPG; it truly feels like a next-gen experience. The game blends action gameplay in the overworld with the ability to initiate turn-based combat at will. This dynamic combination is wrapped up in an incredible UI design that is an absolute joy to look at (though it can sometimes be a bit overwhelming when there’s too much things to look at, leading to the occasional wrong button press.) While the music isn't entirely to my liking, it carries an unique charm. The bond themes, town tunes, and combat tracks remind me of Fire Emblem: Three Houses. Known primarily for pop and jazz, Meguro has truly outdone himself this time.Graphic talk. Metaphor: ReFantazio maintains the familiar style seen in Persona 5 and the Persona 3 remake. Although it may not meet modern graphical standards, its art direction shines brilliantly. The vibrant fantasy world is brought to life with stunning anime cutscenes sprinkled throughout. While we don’t turn to Atlus for cutting-edge graphics, it’s worth noting the visual charm the game offers.If you've ever played an Atlus game, you know this is something you simply can't miss. For newcomers who haven't delved much into JRPGs, I'd highly recommend giving this game a try first before anything else. It's the kind of experience that can genuinely change your life and I'm not joking about it. By far the one of the raregame that caught my attention this year, and I think this game should at least be nominated for GOTY.Also Hulkenberg is best girl.

_childDocuments_.review: Metaphor felt like a nostalgic journey. While the game isn’t perfect, all its systems work perfectly together, giving the experience of playing a classic RPG from the good ol' days.The story is linear but highly engaging, keeping me interested from start to finish. Between main story missions, you manage your party, strengthen bonds with key characters, and complete side missions. These elements blend smoothly into the narrative, so I never felt like I was wasting time. Most side quests tie directly into the main story, and the characters you can bond with have their own compelling storylines, unlocking unique classes throughout the game. New characters are introduced well before they officially join your party, allowing you to connect with them early on.Visually, the game isn’t groundbreaking. While the graphics are decent, there’s room for improvement. The menu screen, however,  looks absolutely phenomenal.The biggest downside was the dungeon design. They all felt similar in both structure and appearance, especially the tomb dungeons, because there are a lot of them.Monster designs were solid, but there wasn’t much variety. While it’s understandable given the story’s focus, I still wished for more diversity.The turn-based combat system had just enough depth to keep me engaged. Since the game is primarily story-driven, those looking for a deeply strategic RPG may need to look elsewhere.In summary:The game delivers excellent storytelling, a charming and well-developed cast, intuitive menus, and enough strategic elements to stay interesting. It was a well-rounded experience, and I can’t remember the last time I felt this satisfied after finishing a game.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best JRPGs I've had the opportunity to play. Similar to the Persona series, it incorporates a calendar system along with the life-simulator/dungeon-crawler gameplay loop, but manages to add its own twists to make it stand out as it's own game.The characters are all lovable, the awakening cutscenes are hype, and the soundtrack is phenomenal (monk rap goes insanely hard).The story is very engaging, you really feel as if you're on the path to kingship with all the trials and tribulation that you face as the story progresses. The political strife and social discrimination presented in the game is very believable.In terms of the follower system (Metaphor's way of social links), it is done very well. Normally in Persona games, you must plan your time very carefully if you want to max all social links, however you are given more leeway in Metaphor so that you are able to experience all the follower's storyline to the very end. Understandably to some extent, there is no romance route for the follower system. However, it is heavily implied for a few of them albeit not explicitly told.Overall, an exemplary game! High recommended to anyone interested in JRPGs or the Persona series.

_childDocuments_.review: Best jrpg I've played in a while.  Every game is subjective, but this game scratches all my itches.  The game does a great job of balancing game play, so I do not feel like the game is too easy or too hard.  I can grind/farm if I want, but the game balances power really well.  If you get a little to high in level, then you can simply one shot mobs while exploring without having to load into turn based combat and get less xp for doing so.  If you over farm xp, then you'll quickly get caught back up in power level while progressing, so you'll be back to regular turned based combat.  The game encourages you to try out different combinations of classes (archetypes) to counter the mobs in each dungeon.  If you do not change things out then combat  can be very difficult.  The story is a bit heavy handed for my tastes at times, but I still like the characters and story.  The art/graphics are great and this game runs extremely smoothly on my computer with full graphics (this games demands much less on my computer that other modern games).  I'm probably 1/3 of the way through the game and I am really enjoying it.  Also the game has a unique timing element that encourages you to continue with the main progression which I like compared to open ended games where I find myself getting bored and side tracked trying to finish all the side quests/objectives.  This game gives you enough time to do some side stuff, but then you'll be basically forced to get back on the main story path for a bit which I think is a really creative game design element. While this game has some skin DLC's (which I have not purchased), there is no obvious advertisement in the game (thank god).  This game is worth every $$$ I spent on it so far, and I do not anticipate that changing.Update;  I beat the game around 125 hours.  I really enjoyed the game.  The timing mechanism made it impossible to complete all the things I wanted to before the end which frustrated me a little bit.  Two things I wished I had known early when playing the game:   Use all the days to do stuff even 1 day left.  Play whatever archetype you like and when it is level capped, you will get plenty of points to level others you do not like so you can unlock everything.  I spent way too much time playing archetypes I did not enjoy to unlock everything.  On new game plus, you get to keep all your items, money and mag points.  Wished I had farmed more mag points at the end if I had known they would carry over.  I unlocked all archetypes on main character, but did not level all of them nor did I unlock all skills which I'm OK with..gives me something to do on new game plus.  I'm glad I unlocked enough to receive the badass 500 damage sword, and unlocked the ultimate ability by maxing out all royal archetypes.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, very comparable to the Persona series, and if you like 3/4/5 this should scratch a similar itch. Since most people know 5 the best I'll compare it to that, then you can use 5 as a proxy if you really care that much. Overall I'd say Persona 5 was better, but Metaphor can still stand with it as a similar quality.This review is going to seem pretty mean, but don't let that fool you. Being 95% as good as Persona 5 and even better a few aspects is still pretty good.Oh, and spoilers.ENDING SPOILERSPersona 5's characters were great. They had all sorts of opportunities to express themselves. The fact they were basically leading double lives and had lifestyles that clashed with each other gave them a ton to work with. Metaphor doesn't have that luxury. The characters don't lead double lives and they're given very little outside of the main quest and social links. This is at it's worst when it comes to dungeon chatter. Going through Mementos in Persona 5/Royal and having the party chat about random stuff was memorable and endearing, but in Metaphor they just talk about being in the dungeon and near enemies. What we have in Metaphor isn't bad though, what we do get is some pretty good writing (much less horny, thankfully) but it left me wanting more. The party members don't interact with each other nearly as much as they should have.I will say that the Social Link MECHANICS are a lot better. I don't need a guide on min/maxing each and every social event just to save a few days, or spend days raising an arbitrary hidden friendship integer. Getting an answer "wrong" just gives you a little less MAG, so I just answer how I feel like. This is how it always should have been.Some gameplay though. I actually REALLY prefer Archetypes to Persona. First off, they give you full freedom. It's not just the protagonist, all party members get full access to all the mechanics. Along with not instantly getting a game over if the Protagonist falls in battle, this makes for a much more interesting combat system where it doesn't pull it's punches. While I do like the Fusion mechanics of Persona and SMT, just being able to get the abilities and Archetypes I want instead of needing an online guide was nice. The actual combat is about the same, so it's not like the challenge is ruined. It's harder from what I've experienced, or at least has bigger difficulty spikes, but that's not a bad thing.Oof, Metaphor loses this comparison hands down. Persona 5 gave you dungeons in a theme of "places to steal from" going from Art Museums and Casinos and ending cleverly on a prison break. In Metaphor you go to a castle, a cave, another castle, a tower, a tomb, a cave, a castle, an airship, etc. "An airship sounds fun!" you may think. It's the worst dungeon. Forced stealth sections and bosses on 3 turn timers or you get a game over, making you restart the entire stealth section. There's also one point where you choose between two paths and just don't get to see the other one, not sure what that's about. Just a terrible time all around. The rest of the dungeons are just linear hallways with occasional splits for loot or some basic mazes where you can't see the map so it plays like a linear hallway with occasional splits. Sometimes the walls all look the same and you're looking at the minimap instead of the actual game, which is never a good thing.MID-GAME SPOILERSAs an RPG it's not just RP, there is a little G in here. Combat is a mix between SMT turn management and Persona party management while doing it's own thing with Archetypes and it comes together to actually feel satisfying to take some big enemy down.Overworld combat is a thing now though. You can move, dodge, attack, and that's about it. It's no Dark Souls or Kingdom Hearts, but as a way to skip easy turn-based combat it's a pretty good modern attempt. The game doesn't put too much faith in it, there's no boss that makes you switch between overworld and turn-based combat.It leaves a bit to be desired though. For example, the protagonist's Archetype changes the weapon they use, but since you only every use a few because that's usually the best strategy most players just won't see more than the default and one or two others. I also don't see why overworld combat and turn-based combat need to be in different "spaces", could have just had everyone run into position when combat starts like in Modern Pokemon. That's mostly a nitpick though, if that even, how it is now is fine.Gameplay, yes. Story, hard pass, do something else.If you see this as a "Persona 6" of sorts it's a satisfying enough sequel, but it left me wanting something deeper.

_childDocuments_.review: I was never that into Persona but always made an attempt to get into the series playing about a 3rd of Persona 4 Golden and Persona 5 on Playstation. The general vibes and highschooler living a double-life thing just never appealed to me and I was never a fan of the time-based choices mechanic. I gotta say though this game is everything I thought Persona was going to be from the way others talked about it. I haven't beaten it yet but at 33 hours in I'm loving everything about it. This game has me heavily engaged in it's narrative taking a much more mature and serious approach to it's world, opposed to the whimsical teenage angst and often comic-book-like tones of the Persona games (albeit Persona does still tend to tackle heavy "modern" themes). The biggest factor that I believe elevates this to a place more people can enjoy is the setting, which will submerge you in a world-spanning odyssey-like political campaign for the throne through an engaging tale of political intrigue, moral debates and occasionally delving into straight-up horrific dark fantasy. The many companions along the way are also a joy to befriend, each having deep character motivations and backstories that you'll learn more about as you venture through the fantastic world ATLUS cooked up. The time-constraints that I wasn't a fan of before I now see as valuable decisions both affecting the RPG mechanics unlocking skills you need to survive as well as upgrading many quality of life features that the Persona games lacked in. It no longer feels like an annoyance of not knowing exactly what may be a waste of time because nearly everything you do is now valuable and feels important. Point is if you're a fan of the Fantasy Genre as a whole or perhaps didn't always like the Persona games like myself but still enjoy a traditional RPG then you owe it to yourself to play Metaphor. Might even be my game of the year but I'll wait till I complete it to make that declaration.Update: This is 100% my game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: As I haven't finished the game till it's conclusion, I cannot tell you anything about late-game to end-game content. I can however give  a good opinion on what I have seen and how it makes me very excited to get to the rest of the game.I -  Overview and Story (No spoilers)      So far the story has me hooked. Granted, this is a type of game that will hook you completely or you just can't get into the flow of it all. The game is somewhat linear but gives you a certain amount of freedom to do your own stuff. The things you can do are probably one of my favorite pro's of the game. Everything you do is related to the world and, until now at 25 hours into the game, I haven't had a fetch quest in sight. There are no trivial side quests at all and everything you do ties into the overarching story and world.The characters I have met so far are fantastic with one obvious standout. But you will probably think the same. They all have their own backstory, quirks and reasons for being where they are. They are, compared to most current day AAA games, explained with logical stories. If there is one thing I often hate in games, it is the inclusion of character with weak reasons for being there in the first place. This game has none of that, so far.Overal the story so far is really good. It is not just the story that makes a game amazing though. The story, great as it may be up till now, really has some moments where I feel the reasons some characters do certain things in certain situations.... Let's say, it was not the best writing in my opinion. BUT it wasn't so bad that it pulled me out of the story. Just questionable and move on. Eventually things come back together with other parts of the story which makes it all seem like normal. This sounds harsh maybe, but it is nitpicking at this point.II - Gameplay and Mechanics     The gameplay is fantastic. To those that played Persona before (I only played 5) it is more of the same. You get your archetypes (persona's) and you have to work with weaknesses to gain extra turns. The combat is nearly the same but there are some things Atlas has really improved. To say they added some QOL changes to the mechanics is an understatement. The way the UI works, the overworld battles again weaker enemies, front and back line during combat, just a few things that enhance the experience.The way you navigate the world is just open areas like a city or town with multiple locations that you can visit. It all looks really nice. It is more skill issue then anything else, but the way you go about using MP is very hard for me. MP restoration potions are hardly available, at least where I am right now and earlier. I can't finish dungeons in one go, as I seem to bump into the wrong dungeons that are always a tad to difficult, making me waist another 2 days. (granted I do level up a lot in those places. So it's not all bad.)There is one thing that annoys me a bit about the game though. There is a layer of unfairness to it all. En example of this, for instance, is that I spoke to a guy that send me on a quest to a dungeon. I ran in, checked the enemies, found their weaknesses and prepped my team to blast through all the mobs.I reached the boss and..... my team was useless. I died in the first couple of turns because my party was half weak against an element and the other weak against it's normal attacks.....I don't have an issue with something like this normally but you can hardly prepare for it and you will have to be sure you either opened a chest somewhere for a quicksave or have saved before going in. Which is also not always a sure fire way. Some enemies you meet in a dungeon can suddenly turn your whole dungeon run on its head.  You could go in to enemies that are weak to fire, then bump in to one of the rare enemies in there that attacks you and pulls you into the battle. You then find out it is resistant to all the elements you have equipt and your party is weak against his. Tough luck trying to get this guy down. I have died multiple times this way or ran out of MP while trying to survive. Meaning you can go home for the day, as you don't have enough or any mp potions.III - Visuals and PresentationCan't say anything else then that it is artistic as hell. The style of the game is fantastic and every button, text balloon, basically everything on screen, looks amazing. Graphics are not that amazing, but the style in which it is presented doesn't need that. It's an anime styled game in the end and who wants realistic graphics in such a game. IV - Sound and Music      Music is also a massive pro. It really shows the attention to detail. The music fits will with the theme presented and the situations you find yourself in. Sounds are what you can expect from a AAA JPRG. That is not a bad thing though, its just that you can only go so far in sound design and effects. This game is great with that.Something to note for me is the really good voice acting from the English cast. I have not had any complaints about them at all and one of the characters had me look op Sneep from Harry Potter..... Hope I'm not the only one haha.VI -  Replayability and Longevity       As stated earlier, I am nowhere near end-game and maybe just approaching the base of the game. But as far as I can see right now, it really feels like playing more of this. The mechanics and gameplay in general feels really well fleshed out. It is fun to do battles, though some enemies are annoying as hell. Ok I know most is skill issue. I never really played a game that had me switching up my classes this much. So it is taking some getting used to. But the game can border 'unfair' at some points. But apart from that, the gameplay loop is good, you get everything unlocked at a steady pace and there is always something to do next. That next thing will always do something interesting, push your relation with a character to the next rank, a sidequest dungeon, a new character to bond with, or trying to increase your stats like 'imagination' or 'courage'.VII - Overall Impression and Final Score       Let's close off with just a this. The game is amazing. Yes there are some annoyances, but they are mostly skill issues or just a little unfair on the player. On the other hand, just imagine this was a real world... In the real world things also don't go according to plan all the time. So I will definitely not take that from it's score.The story is really fun, the side characters in your party are awesome and the characters you bond with all have their own quirks or serious background. It's not all super creative but it works well in the setting and it binds it all together nicely. Overall I would say there is little to fault the game for. Everything works and haven't seen any bugs yet.That is something unique these days.....I would give this game a 9.5 overall, for as far as I have played it ^_^

_childDocuments_.review: Metaphor is an excellent RPG from start to finish. It put its own twists on what might seem at first like a normal fantasy setting, establishing an interesting premise from the get-go with various elements and then executing well on its narrative elements throughout, keeping me interested in both the character stories and overarching story from start to finish. It kept me guessing and still managed to surprise me. The cast is excellent, with one of the best RPG parties I've ever had the pleasure of using, and the freeform Archetype system feels like a highly refined evolution of similar games that came before. Everything from the visuals to the voice acting blends together into a massive but complete experience that never felt tedious or grindy, with a highly satisfactory pay-off and a lot to say with its various metaphors, and it left me missing its fantastical world and people.

_childDocuments_.review: Metaphor is just a Persona game with some light differences that ultimately don't matter. If you've played any of the modern Persona games, you've played this. Not just the game play, but down to the plot. Following the Persona structure completely hamstrings Metaphor from finding its own identity and renders its plot a lifeless husk of rushing from one big moment to the next.Some notes: -Things start off alright: the pacing is okay, there are some intriguing ideas here and there. Characters get their moments and time to establish who they are. There are a lot of heavy themes being tackled here, and every so often you'll get the hint of a good line or an interesting train of thought. Don't let any of that fool you: this game has nothing to say, and the pacing quickly nosedives. All of the themes in the game are grossly oversimplified, with nary any of the characters set up as rivals having any sort of contrasting point of view that would make the party, or the player, consider their actions. Instead, they're comedic relief characters. The Actual Bad Guys are just bad guys who have bad ideas. Past a certain point, things simply start HAPPENING, and as you barrel toward the late game, even MORE things just start HAPPENING. It's jarring, rushed and nonsensical. There is no tension in the narrative, no burning to desire to know what's going to happen next. As of my writing this review, I am close to the end of the game, but I don't see a reason to bother finishing it. If the game hasn't had anything to say or present any interesting conundrums in the first 50 hours, I doubt the last 10-20 are going to change that.-The job system is a fine idea, and I appreciate the greater control over what every member of your party can do. But the job system is also a massive, boring grind and all of your progression is locked behind social links, which in-turn have progress locked behind the completely arbitrary personality stats system. The personality stats have never been interesting in Persona, and it's not interesting here. Social link stories here are also oversimplified and quite dull, but you basically don't have a choice but to do them if you want even slightly more insight into half of the cast who joins you.-Combat is the press-turn system. You'll know it very well by now if you play Atlus games. The bones of it are fine, but the execution is terrible. Many battles are all the same format: big enemy uses a skill that gives them additional turns, they buff themselves, debuff you, then do some big move. That's literally 90% of the encounters in the game. I struggle to recall one encounter in the game that was interesting, or that required me to change my tactics up much. The press-turn system, while fun, has been in use now for close to something like 20+ years, and I think it's fair to say it's time for something new to take its place.-There are four side dungeon tile sets in the game. One of them (a tower) is literally the exact same layout every time you do one. The main dungeons you go through aren't much more interesting, with one of them in particular being what I'd consider the absolute worst dungeon I've ever played in an Atlus game.Having written this far, I strongly believe the Persona-style calendar system is solely to blame on these shortcomings. This game could have had a grander narrative if it weren't hamstrung by how much the structure of a Persona game dictates how plots must play out. If this were a more linear game, it could actually take its time to develop out its ideas, character and world or give the player more agency over the job system. You can see glimmers of greatness behind the mediocrity. As things are, Metaphor is the worst kind of game: boring, bloated and lacking an identity of its own.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based off my time with the demo (about 7 hours) and the small amount of time I've logged into the actual game. I may update this review once I've beaten the game but that will be at least a hundred hours from now. Atlus games are a marathon, not a sprint.Luckily, the game is fantastic. The world building, the art and character design, the music, and the story have all been top notch so far. Pacing wise the game is much faster than the Persona games. For instance, you're actively running through dungeons and fighting enemies proper within the first 30 minutes compared to Persona 4 or 5 where it can take upwards of two hours to get through the "prologue."The actual combat and gameplay loop is the most refined version of some of Atlus' other games and it's great. The combat is quick so you're not sitting around waiting a lot in this turn based RPG. Plus the difficulty is just right even on Normal. Battles have a tendency of snowballing in your favor or spiraling out of control due to how the devs have implemented the weakness system. If you've played a Shin Megami Tensei game you'll be right at home. Plus there are new changes like the overworld combat which allow you to do dodge rolls, and combos on enemies in order to stun them and get a free round of combat. However, if the enemy hits you, then they get a free round of combat on you. It's a high risk, high reward kind of deal.Overall, if you're on the fence, I heavily recommend downloading the demo, giving it a try for an afternoon and if you like what you're playing, then pick it up. For a huge JRPG and specifically Persona fan like myself, this is an easy recommendation.The only gripe I have with the game so far is that the performance is kind of spotty. I personally haven't encountered any major issues albeit the occasional framerate dip, but I know other people are more sensitive to that sort of thing and it's dependent on your hardware. It's worth bringing up, but I don't think it ruins the experience by any means. Fingers crossed it gets patched though because it's a blemish on an otherwise amazing game.Lastly, for everyone that's already an Atlus RPG fan, they've already gone on the record saying that they won't be making a "Royal" or "Golden" version a year from now. We won't have to rebuy the base game again or anything like that which is fantastic to hear.

_childDocuments_.review: I would say Metaphor is a pretty good game. It is a political game to an extent, and I was scared that it will be another "idealistic teen utopia" story where the main characters stand for everything good against everything evil. I was surprised that it was not fully the case. Characters sometimes actually discuss political topics, which is a progress from the persona games, which were fully teen-oriented. The social links, on the other hand, are kind of shalow for the most of the time. Personal stories are not that interesting and, as usual, don't affect the story in any way. It only affects the mechanics of the game. And the political social links resolve their conflicts in one day, which is not how people work.On the other hand, the villains are the highlight of the game. This game probably has the best main villain of all Persona games (this game is basically Persona 6).Combat wise I don't like how ambushing enemies will not guarantee you two turns. Ambushed enemies will be stunned for two turns, but your attacks can sometimes wake them up, which loses its value. But don't worry, because now you can restart your battle during the combat, which resolves this issue. The question is, why create a problem and try to fix it when there was no problem to begin with? Just make enemies lose two turns and the restart battle button will not be necessary.Similar issue with statul ailments. This is a constant problem with most SMT games. They are applied randomly, you kill enemies faster with normal attack than with ailments, and the only enemies that you can potentially use it on are bosses. Bosses are immune to ailments, so 99% of the time you just don't use them. Make them at least somewhat useful by affecting bosses or maybe make ailments application guaranteed on the first turn or something. Because if you actually want to apply an ailment, you would just restart the battle thousands of times to do it, why not make it guaranteed?Anyway, other than that, a new turn mechanic is a fresh addition that makes combat more thoughtful.The other thing that was weird was the anime cutscenes. They have pretty bad CG and the overall animation was not great. In-engine cutscenes looked beautiful, but anime cutscenes ruined some moments because of some ugly CG and bad direction. Get this anime out of my anime game.Music was okay, expected more bangers.So yeah, the game is pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: Very ambitious celebration of the Atlus RPG formula combining the press-turn system, persona social sim and archetype(class) system. For the most part, sticks the landing gameplay-wise. The plot had nice emotional beats and does what it sets out to do well enough. Biggest issue is the late-game sequence reads a bit rushed but that's honestly expected with long games. Characters are very charming and the follower bonds(social links) are well-written. No egregiously bad SL you'd see in persona. Biggest issue is pretty steep A-exp curve making it hard to experiment without a lot of grinding. Fortunately the game as an on-field battle system for clearing weaker mobs that can mitigate but hopefully in a future installment studio zero lowers the curve or adds more ways to get a-exp. If you're unfamiliar with abusing the press turn system used in SMT prepare to have a hard time especially at the end. Despite some tracks being absolute bangers(the battle music in particular), a lot of tracks are just there and forgettable. Strong recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically Persona but in a fantasy world with magic and different races besides humans. Also, there's no romancing and you're not playing as high school kids in this game. Your party is pretty diverse with a knight, a nobleman, etc. And you get a nice in game record book (called the Memorandum) that lets you view lore and history about any characters, events, or places you come across. There's a lot of great worldbuilding here and the game tackles serious and mature issues like racism in well done way (so far, at least).The combat system is turn based. However, unlike the Persona games which *only* offer turn-based for every fight and only let you attack once in the dungeon to get an advantage once the battle starts, Metaphor actually lets you fight enemies in real time. It's meant for breaking an enemy's guard (a separate meter next to their HP bar) and then choosing to go into turn based combat where you do a ton of damage to them at the start of the battle and the enemies start the fight stunned. But it's not limited to that. Small, weak enemies will die in one hit and if you really wanted to, you could fight strong enemies this way never going into the turn based combat. The equivalent of personas in this game are the archetypes. Though, these honestly feel more like RPG classes or jobs. You can't switch between them during battle like you can in the Persona games and unlike in those games, you can learn and equip them on other members, not just the main character. Each one also provides extra abilities - often for helping you outside of combat, too.The world, characters, voice acting, animation, music, UI, and everything is just great so far. It's the culmination of everything Atlus has learned making SMT and Persona games for the past 20+ years. This game is fantastic so far.(Side note: I know my play time is pretty low at the time of this review, but I also put over 10 hours into the demo, which isn't counted as play time for the full game. I've played the prologue twice and made it past the first dungeon, a side dungeon, multiple bosses, and have leveled up half a dozen archetypes above level 15).

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best Atlus game I have played, and one of my favorite games of all time.There are a few things I had problems with, one big (#1), and the others small issues:1. The story is great, but it feels like each character says every little thing about the plot. Like, I figure something out right before the twist, it feels great, story moment happens, and then the two people involved spend ten minutes talking about each individual detail of the twist in the middle of a tense scenario. Then, ten minutes later, the characters act like the plot point wasn't explained and then have to deduce it again. Like I'm not 5, and this isn't Persona, your target audience can piece this together. Honestly, this kind of drags down the story a little bit, but the story besides this is really good. 2. Dungeon variety needs changing. There are so many cool locations they show on the map when traveling and some of the boss setpieces are great, but the regular dungeons just seem like corridors. Persona 5 I believe has had the best dungeons of the Atlas games. 3. Feels like the last third of the game suffered from cut content. Don't want to put spoilers here, but there is a boss you just end up fighting, where it feels like there should have been a dungeon. Again, not a major problem, but you can kind of feel the story beginning to run out of steam.4. Plot holes - people pop up randomly when they should take days/weeks to cover the distance we can with our flying runner and teleportation. It is very annoying sometimes.Those being said, there is so much more to enjoy about the game. 1. The Combat is probably the most amazing version of  turn based combat I have ever played. It took the Persona games and opened up the already deep system of weaknesses by allowing every party member to be every class. The turn system is brilliant as well, and I loved managing turn crystals much more than the "One More" system in Persona.2. The Companion stories were amazing! In other Atlus games and even most other RPGs, there is always the one companion storyline that I don't like. I hated the Gourmet King's Social Link in Persona 3. In this game, I appreciated every single companion story, and  felt like all of them were well written. The main cast of party members are well written and fantastically voiced, and I loved spending time with them more than almost any other cast of characters.3. The Difficulty in this game is just right on Hard Mode, and I would recommend it for any fans of turn-based games. As long as you don't deliberately overlevel, fights come down to setting up proper formations, and remembering the capabilities of each of your party members. The boss fights felt fantastic to finish after "solving" the mechanics, and it was very rewarding.4. The main story of this game is very good, and I loved the themes it explored. Even if it did treat me like I am five sometimes, overall I was left with a very good impression of what it was trying to say. 5. The aesthetic of this game, the world design, and the overall presentation were fantastically well made - a great combination of tropes with just enough new to feel unique.6. The Music in this game was fantastic. There were no obvious earworms like in other RPGs, but it fully elevated the scenes it was meant to and perfectly suited the fantasy setting.I am not sure if this will turn into a franchise: no idea where they could take things from here. However, I am really happy with this new team within Atlas, and am looking forward to what they do next!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fine game.But truth be told, it doesn't live up to the absurd amount of hype the game had at release.As the steam review system is not about being good or bad, but recommended or not, I have to decline recommending this game.More passionate people than I am on the topic have written extended reviews, but here are my two cents : CONS- Dungeons are uninspired, and sidequest dungeons are copy-pasted. Same goes for cities. They mostly feels like lifeless hubs rather than immersive role play areas.- There are very few things to actually do in the game, except raising your virtues and working on your "social links". Most are so uninteresting that you'll just skip the dialogues.- The writing is simplistic, on a topic that should be more nuanced and complicated to handle.- The class system is clunky and poorly designed. Also, it doesn't mesh well with having to handle 7 characters.- The calendar system feels out of place. The game would have worked better as an old-school open world game.- Combat is painfully boring and easy to abuse.PROS : - Music is a matter of taste, but I find it fantastic.- Despite the story's quality, the setting shows great promise for a franchise.- The world's aesthetic is compeling and intriguing. Special mention for the human's design.- As always with Atlus, the UI and overall presentation of the game is excellent and over the top.So, yeah. I don't get the hype. I'm a bit baffled by it to be honest. I play less and less each week, I'm not sure I'll finish it.Time is a precious thing, and should not be wasted on mediocre products.

_childDocuments_.review: Metaphor: ReFantazio feels and plays like a natural evolution of Persona, almost as if it were a Persona 6 set in an original fantasy universe. Atlus has outdone itself with a stunning art style, a mesmerizing soundtrack, and gameplay that flows beautifully, seamlessly merging exploration, social interactions, and strategic battles. Each character and setting bursts with personality, and the vivid, magical landscapes pull you deeper into this rich world.While the game has so many strengths, my main criticism is that the story can drag at times, lacking the same gripping, edge-of-your-seat momentum that Persona fans may be used to. It doesn’t quite have the same immersive pull, especially in its early chapters. However, the excellent voice acting and well-developed characters deliver emotional depth that keeps you invested. I also must appluad them for managing to make the games difficulty feels really fair and challenging without requiring too much grinding.

_childDocuments_.review: A refreshing take on the Persona and Shin Megami Tensei formula. The characters are also really well written and charismatic (I love how intimidating and cool the main villain is). It lacks a bit on the technical side, and it can get a bit repetitive (the side dungeons almost look identical to each other, too), but if you like the genre and the series the creators of this game made in the past, you'll probably really love this. I loved Persona 3 Reload, but I'm giving my personal GOTY to this because it's a new game and I want to encourage ATLUS to make more of them, instead of constantly remaking/porting old games with new features. Those are welcome too, but I prefer new and original games over them

_childDocuments_.review: ( full review with screenshots:  )This is really a neutral review, but Steam doesn't allow those. You know the drill. Persona 3 through 5 are all 10 out of 10 games for me and are some of the only games I've ever come back to more than once. Metaphor isn't technically part of that series, but it's impossible not to compare them when it comes from the same team and has so much of its DNA in common. Unfortunately, the comparison is rarely favorable. This isn't by any means a bad game, but it's nonetheless a step down from its precursors in just about every important way. Even though I don't regret playing it, it's just about guaranteed to be the most disappointing game I play this year. How did it get there? The biggest problem is, by far, the cast. Persona is made by the strength of the core party and the chemistry between the characters, but Metaphor hardly has any of that. I spent 60 hours on my playthrough and would struggle to describe the relationship between any pair of the main party members. Some of them are just underdeveloped overall, but the bigger issue is that they hardly ever interact in any meaningful way. There are interesting dynamics between just about every pair of characters in any given Persona game, but Metaphor's cast barely even speaks to each other unless it's through or about the protagonist. This all caps off in what is supposed to be a touching moment of one character overcoming his prejudices in regard to another in the final 30 minutes of the game, but it's rendered flat by the fact that conflict hadn't been brought up at all since the pair were introduced. Sadly, the characters in the equivalent of social links are hardly any better. Even the weakest Persona SLs give the character a personal conflict to overcome and grow from, but Metaphor forgets that basic element of writing half the time. The party member SLs are particularly bad because any character growth, assuming there was any at all, happened in the main plot, so their stories start with them already being perfect and usually end with them solving a problem in a tremendously predictable way. Non-party characters do a little better since they're allowed to have flaws and improve themselves, but even these are generally too trite to be memorable with morals like "stealing is bad" and "don't build dangerous weapons just because". I do like that they've made links guaranteed to advance every time you hang out with a character, though. It removes some of the guide-bait from previous games where choosing the wrong option a couple of times could lock you out of seeing the end of a character's story. The plot at large is at least written better than the characters. The core idea of a medieval magical popularity contest to elect a new king is interesting and there are some scattered moments of clever worldbuilding. It's all pretty serviceable, if about as subtle as a freight train. The theme of this game is "anxiety" according to the developers, and you will know that because every other word is "anxiety" in the last quarter of the game. The opening cutscene shows a man bribing a church official and then cuts to another man cursing out a beggar, and that's about the level of subtlety that you can expect from the whole game. It's supposed to be a fairy tale, so absolutely smashing you over the head with the message is certainly on-brand, but even then it might go too far. It also tries to cram far too many plot twists into the last 10 hours, so it turns into a soap opera with everyone betraying everyone and many fake deaths. Gameplay fares the best of all the parts of the game, although it's still somewhat of a mixed bag for me. I really like the idea they're going for by having a job system instead of personas, but locking both class progression and skill inheritance slots behind social links that are themselves locked behind the plot was a huge mistake. Say you want to have a Merchant in your party - you'll unlock the basic class fairly early on, but you won't get access to its upgraded version until the last month of the game, and even progressing it enough to unlock additional skill slots will take until the next chapter. There's no way to know where these gates are in advance and most classes have access to a very narrow pool of skills by default, so it's pretty disappointing if you've wasted your time on one that turns out to be locked for who knows how long. This would have worked much better if social links only unlocked the initial class and all further progression happened through leveling up or items. As it stands, some classes are clearly better than others for much of the game simply because you're actually allowed to progress the relevant link. Beyond swapping personas out for a job system, the flow of battle is also radically different. You now have a dodge skill in the overworld and only enter turn based battle after attacking if the enemy is near your level. Once in battle, you have turn icons that control how many actions you get. Everything takes one icon except for special combo actions, which take two, and passing, which takes half, but the cost is reduced by half if you hit an enemy weakness or get a critical hit. The icons are really close to being a good idea. On the player side, it's held back by the fact that you can lose 2-4 icons if you happen to hit an enemy resistance or reflect, which is absurdly punishing considering you've already done no damage and likely had a character KO'ed if damage was reflecting. More problematically, later bosses like to spam moves that give them a ton of extra icons. This isn't much different than the boss just using a super attack in terms of difficulty, but it means you have to sit through a boss attacking up to 8 times in a row. Even with sped up animations it takes far too long and the movepools are so small that the boss is often using the same move multiple times anyway. It seems like they wanted to go for something like the Octopath Traveler battle system where actions are a currency that you need to spend carefully, but it's just not very interesting because of how much better it is to hit a weakness than do anything else. Lastly, music and graphics. They're fine. The game broadly looks pretty good and actually has some really excellently drawn optional viewpoints, but an overeliance on recolored enemies and narrow corridors means that a lot of the game can't take advantage of the game's graphical prowess. The music is a lot of chanting. Some of it is pretty catchy, but there's nothing here that can match the masterpieces in the Persona soundtracks. This is probably the part of the game that's most held back by weight of expectations. If this soundtrack had come from some random guy, I'd probably be pretty happy with it. Instead, it's hard not to be a little disappointed with it in comparison to Meguro's previous work.

_childDocuments_.review: If you somehow aren't already aware, in terms of the people behind it - this is basically Persona 6 (but it's way more interesting than just that). The best battle system a JRPG has ever had, and probably my favourite game ever in terms of pure gameplay. The job system and SMT3 styled press-turn mechanics lead to an extremely satisfying and rewarding evolution of the strong parts of Persona 5's excellent combat. Metaphor takes the perfect-strategy idea seen in Persona (how can I get through this encounter without getting hit?) and runs with it, allowing a huge amount of freedom with player expression with how they tackle each fight. With said freedom, the game is free to throw tons of challenges at you that make you rethink your builds and how you'll play, where switching your setup can lead from an encounter going from impossible to trivial. The lategame is too easy but oh well... lol The story and setting are excellent, probably their best apart from Persona 3, with a profoundly unique take on the fantasy aesthetic that doesn't feel like anything else. Parts of the narrative can feel predictable but the cast and especially the villain are some of Atlus' strongest. Shoji Meguro's soundtrack is great as usual and while I do prefer his typical pop and rock music style seen in the Persona and SMT series, the use of grand orchestral themes here is excellent. Lots of great quality of life too! Quick battle transitions, restarting a fight if you mess-up, etc. It doesn't waste your time (in fights at least). If you like JRPGs you should play this game!!! It's one of the best. Hashino and his team are consistently delivering the best stuff out there at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: I've longed for a fantasy story in a games which is not based on humans, dwarves and elves. This gave me that. I'ts a unique and interesting lore which paints a new touch on fantasy that is uncommon in game media today. It still touches politics and society but to me it becomes much more interesting when the world it occurs in  is unfamiliar to me, a fantasy that is allowed to be just that, a fantasy. I loved the from zero-to-hero format this game adapts in it's own unique way, and how it's not afraid of depicting subjects like racism but in another world.The gameplay itself it very similar to the Persona or Shin Megami Tensei series. Turn based, weakness-exploit focused. Class variety is great and there are LOTS, and some that are quite unique. However I grew up with the Final Fantasy series and know most "spells" by heart. I find the naming of skills/spells in these games super confusing, but I guess it's just a matter of familiarity.Game length is fine, if anything I think it dragged on for a bit long in the end, even though the ending was very satisfying. My current playtime of this review is from start to finish, doing almost everything except a bunch of very late game quests and one that bugged out in the beginning, which has now been fixed by a patch. Played the game 100% on steam deck where it ran very well.I recommend this game if you want an RPG with a unique and well written fantasy story, which diverges from the usual set of races and social constructs that are depicted today in media.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying if you expected this to be an evolution of Persona 5 this is not it. Not to say it was not a good game but if Persona 5 was a 10 this would be a 9.The reason for that is that this is a simplified version of everything persona. For example character development is straighforward, you don't need to develop the relationship to gain a level, you just get a notification when it's time and go talk to a characters. Romance is missing and while the archetype system is more fluid since all your party members use it it's also more restrictive in experimentation and individual strength than Personas.The game can be as difficult or easy as you want it to be. Since you can always get info on the monsters in a dungeon all you need to do is switch all your party to archetypes that counter everything.Overall i enjoyed the game a lot. The characters were great, the story was enjoyable and unlike a lot of other games had an Epilogue not making you wonder what happens to the characters you spend days with.Some minor things to keep in mind - ultra wide screen is not supported and while it has some FPS issues the game overall runs ok on the Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: As most, I compare Metaphor: ReFantazio with Persona 5, since the games share many similarities and most PC players found their entry to the Megami Tensei series and spin-offs via Persona 5.+ Fantasy setting = no high schoolers for a change, overall tone is slightly more mature too+ no romances = wouldn't fit to the story and would be superficial and cheesy anyway+ Rock/Paper/Scissors turn-based combat where you try to exploit enemy weaknesses as good as you can+ added hybrid combat system: you can fight mundane enemies with simple real time attacks or prep harder enemies for an advanced ambush with more early combat advantages (more damage/stun)+ revamped class system. Instead of a myriad of Personas/Demons you can unlock 44 classes for every character and up to 4 skills from other classes you've learned+ far more flexible schedule system (Persona 5 had a horrible system where you had to follow walkthroughs to max out bindings with other characters+ 80-90h playtime+ fantastic soundtrack+ great English voice actors+ more varied dungeons and locations- no technical improvements, still no TAA anti-aliasing, nor Upscaler supportMetaphor was very enjoyable. It's a story-rich fantasy RPG. That you don't have to play as another high-schooler was a very welcome change. The hybrid system to fast-kill mundane enemies increases the gameplay pace is a nice addition. The Schedule and NPC affinity system is far more relaxed than Persona now. No need to meticulously workout who to hangout with or follow a walkthrough to optimize your playthrough.Same goes for the dialogues with your team mates. Affinity is no longer bound to the "right" answer, which makes conversations far more enjoyable. The persona/demon system makes place for a class or job system which allows for a very high freedom of party constellation if you prefer to play along certain teammates. While you no longer can "breed" the ultimate Persona, your teammates are no longer bound to their starting class, everyone can learn anything (though some are bit better as others at certain jobs, depending on their base stats). You no longer need to adapt your protagonist to your teammates but pick what you like. To keep up flexibilty, every class can learn up to four skills they unlocked from other classes they learned.The overall presentation is on level with Persona 5, locations and dungeons have improved over that and have become slightly more sophisticated. Technically, it hasn't improved, the engine seems to be the same. That means no TAA or upscalers and if you want to have a smooth looking picture without aliasing and nervous textures, you need to set resolution/resolution scale high. Since the overall layout of locations is more complex now, it means the game is less performant than Persona 5.I played the game in 4K (2K native with DLDSR 2.25x) and 150% resolution scale (had 200% in P5 for 60FPS), FPS were between 45-85 depending on the location. 125% might have given 60+ FPS, but I prefered the better image quality.i9 13900k, Gigabyte Aorus Z790 Master, 2x16 GB DDR5 GSkill Trident Z5 (no RGB crap) 6Ghz, MSI RTX3080ti Gaming Trio X, Soundblaster Z, WD Black SN 850X 4TB M2, Corsair HX850 Platinum PSU (850W)

_childDocuments_.review: I usually enjoy ATLUS games, and still didn't expect to thoroughly enjoy most every aspect of this game.
