_childDocuments_.review: There seems to be two distinct reviewers for this game: Those that want themed, premade things and those that appreciate the modernized customization and freedom. Building is fine -tuned here, especially with environmental things like water, terrain, rocks and vegetation. Pathing of everything, even water, is significantly better than the first game. If you are new or played the first game, I would recommend looking at the controls as they are a little different, but I think it's for the better. If you think about the controls like your playing on a tablet with touch controls it kinda makes it more intuitive.For instance, right clicking is a big part of your controls. How would you exit something on touchscreen? Click off of it. You don't HAVE to use the "x" to close a screen, for instance. Another way right clicking is used is for undoing when a tool is equipped, like water. With the water tool selected, right-clicking over a body of water removes it. Left clicking reapplies it without having to move to a select and delete tool. Another way is you must hold down on some tools (tends to be ones that will cause drastic change like terrain or bulk-placement of environmental items) to initiate it. About quarter of a second.It's like some people are you're used to a console controller and are using a mouse and keyboard for the first time. I think some reviewers are left with a bad taste when they think the team is focusing on customization in one thing, but it was actually targeted towards another. The simple things are there but you can dig a little deeper to customize how the game responds to things by default instead of just not allowing it whatsoever. I particularly like that it does not feel like I have to look up a video for anything. Like how silly it was that the pathing in the first game required multiple, odd or well-placed guesses to get it to do what it wasn't programmed to do.  I think the negatives are harsh, save for ones regarding persistent glitches or bugs. I have not encountered any bugs yet, but I haven't play too long yet either.

It offers a wide range of customization options, allowing you to create unique and thrilling rides, immersive themed lands, and stunning water parks. _childDocuments_.review: Planet Coaster 2 introduces some  that add meaningful depth to park operations, enhanced with , dynamic lighting, and weather effects. The visual upgrades really draw you in, and the  allow for intricate, creative design of rides and attractions—truly a playground for anyone who loves building and tweaking their park’s layout.However, it’s hard not to wonder if Planet Coaster 2’s developers brought in any UX experts or did any user testing at all. So many flows in this game are flawed, making management feel like a chore rather than a joy. For example, the  is a bit of a letdown. Chapter 2’s challenges are already frustrating, with requirements like the "" advertising campaign inaccurately described, making you think you need only one of each shop when you actually need three. This type of oversight makes the experience feel tedious rather than challenging.Adding to the frustration is the process of , which, while intended as a learning exercise, often feels overly complex—borderline impossible. It detracts from the sense of achievement and immersion.The game’s  and frustratingly inefficient, making me wonder if this is one of the worst-designed interfaces I’ve seen in years in the PC gaming industry. For instance, setting custom prices in shops like *Just A Momento* is a nightmare. With 26 different product types, you have to manually change each price one at a time, requiring multiple clicks for each item. You’d think you could simply click on a product price and edit it, but no—a pop-up opens, you have to click again, and then click confirm. A simple bulk-edit or apply-to-all option would make a world of difference.Pathing tools also feel clunky. While queues can be created, there’s no simple “” option, making path layout and alignment unnecessarily difficult. Even worse, the game fails to save basic settings—if you sort your attractions table in a specific way, it reverts back to default the moment you leave the menu. It’s as if the game wasn’t designed with player efficiency in mind.Even the  is a mystery. The game provides no guidance on what drives this rating or how to improve it, leaving players to guess through frustrating trial and error. And when editing scenery groups, sometimes the browsing feature below is accessible, and sometimes it’s inexplicably missing, adding to the inconsistency and frustration of using the interface.Overall, while Planet Coaster 2 has some , the lack of UX attention, frustrating UI, and flawed core mechanics hold it back from reaching its potential. The game could benefit greatly from serious user testing and UI improvements to make the experience smoother, more intuitive, and ultimately more enjoyable for park management enthusiasts.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Coaster 2 is more of a dlc to the original Planet Coaster more than it is a new game. The only new additions are water features (pools and fumes), electrical/water management, and career parks voice acting. Even with these additions and "Norse/Mythology/aquatic/Resort" themeing the game truly feels no different from the first other than the fact many features were removed or to simplicity to care about. One of the first features that has been scaled down dramatically is park management which was such a staple in the first game where you had a 2 career parks to learn about managing parks and managing employees. management features like promotions, managing payroll, and individual prices for rides, shops, and ticket have all been scaled down or removed to the point where it never matter to even look at these things in the new park management tab. Another somewhat unnecessary change was the career parks having voice acting. In the original planet coaster all you needed was a short paragraph about the park and why there were issues so you can go and fix them. Now you have voice acting (Mostly average) to say the obvious or basic level knowledge for every single 'objective' in each park.Ultimately Planet Coaster 2 could be a very reasonable sequel if the water and quality of life features were hailed in with updating and increasing the management systems of the previous game. I can definitely see the devs bringing in dlc of upscaled items from the previous game to match the bare content at launch since so little 'new' things are present

_childDocuments_.review: Hi everyone.To start, I have 2000 hours in Planet Coaster 1 so I am familiarized with the original Planet Coaster 1 controls, as well as the original path making system and coaster building system. For this game, I have only put in 1% of the amount of hours into this game compared to the original. However, I have a lot of comments about the game in its current state.Positives+GraphicsThe game looks cleaner and presents better visually compared to the first game. +PathingThe pathing system improves upon Planet Zoo's pathing system (which was a huge upgrade from the initial Planet Coaster pathing system). The ability to create plazas and winding paths with ease was missing from the original game. Also a big fan of the stamp option when creating paths.+CoastersAside from the pains that came from pathing in the original Planet Coaster, one of my other major issues with the game was the difficulty in obtaining smooth coasters. Smoothing tracks is easier with the updated smoothing tool and provides better riding experiences (and a lot less time to obtain smooth tracks).+PlantsThe inclusion of the scenery brush (brought over from Planet Zoo) is a very welcome addition to the game. Filling up empty areas with trees takes seconds now (instead of painstakingly adding in individual trees for an entire park). There is also a larger selection of plants to choose from, which helps to spice up a park's look.+Pools/SlidesThe inclusion of various slide types and the ability to create any shape pool is a very fun feature.+ManagementThere is more challenge to maintaining and keeping the park running compared to the original Planet Coaster. Ride attendants have to be managed, and money plays a more important role in franchise mode.Neutrals/The GridBuilding on the grid can be a challenge, especially when it comes to building shapes of certain game assets, such as circular flat rides. Trying to make a circular base/structure for a flat ride out of rectangles takes a lot of effort./Current ThemesI like the six themes available (5 + 1 generic) as they are cohesive and mesh well artistically.Negatives-The UISearching for various items seems more of a hassle than before. The screen gets cluttered easily when building. The ability to increase/decrease the size of various images of items is missing. I dislike that there are two staff buttons (one to purchase at the bottom of the screen normally and the staff button in the park management button). -Scenery contentAfter playing so many hours of the original Planet Coaster, one becomes acquainted with the various scenery assets available (props, building sets, misc.) of Planet Coaster, Planet Zoo, and the many DLC released, the content provided for the release of this game feels inadequate/lackluster. Only 10 animatronics available, no glass ceilings or walls, very few shops/food and drink options, no additional guest interaction in the park outside of coasters/flat and tracked rides/pools/slides, tons of assets from PC1 and PZ were not included.Hopes for Future Updates*Slide physicsI believe this should be released sometime soon but currently not present.*More assets per theme / different DLC contentAs mentioned in the negatives, a lot of previously included assets are not in the game currently. The game offers pieces to *build* your own, but the final look is often different than that of a crafted asset. And look. I know a ton of DLC will be released for this game (as evidence of PC1 and PZ). I believe it will be mainly touting themes (how many more coasters/flat rides are out there?) and assets. My hope is that previously included assets are released for free, and each DLC is well rounded in its assets. I played PC1 for 8 years and I will do the same with this one. Help us create more for longer. Additionally, for DLC content, I am hoping that there will be more for guests to do while in the park. Yes, they walk around the park to the various rides or shops present, or to swim, but that is about all they do while in the park. I think a 'games' pack would be fun to include, whether it be games like coin toss to win stuffed animals to carry around the park or minigolf type games that can be crafted/played. **Planet Coaster 2 / Planet Zoo Cross PlayThis is a crazy request and would probably require a lot of effort/time/planning/signatures, but I think it would be amazing to enable the inclusion of Planet Zoo alongside Planet Coaster 2. Managing a roller coaster zoo would be intriguing. It would also enable weather to play a bigger role in the game (managing guests and animals in regards to being outdoors). Overall CommentsI love both Planet Coaster 1 and Planet Zoo. Having put a lot of hours into both games, I can compare them to Planet Coaster 2 and I am very happy with the state in which Planet Coaster 2 was released. The game looks amazing. Creating coasters is a lot easier with the updated smoothing tool. The scenery brush (and lots of plants) is a very nice inclusion for the game. I also am really enjoying the slides/pools addition to the game.In future updates, there are several areas of the game that need to be addressed for PC2 to match its predecessors. As more features are added into a game, managing the UI gets trickier. The ability to customize more aspects of the game would help, such as increasing image size or removing the pop-up screen when purchasing rides. Additionally, more content is needed in the game for it to be playable long-term. DLC will be released that is hopefully fulfilling, but more content for the base game is needed to make the game complete.Rating: 9/10Can be improved to 10/10 with more assets, good DLC, UI customization. Could be a 15/10 if Planet Coaster 2 and Planet Zoo crossover and are able to be played as one game.

_childDocuments_.review: Never knew a legend could degenerate so badly. This is why:- A blurry screen due to excessive graphic settings, which makes all the innovative settings only decrease the quality and performance in the end- A third-party account (Frontier) is needed in order to download items from the workshop, which also has a limited download amount... Do developers care about privacy as they claim to be, as the more accounts you have the more easily you can become a victim of a data leak? - Limited workshop downloads due to disk space storage and/or the third party application, see above (of course the downloads may increase in the future and can this be seen as a momentarily take on the situation)- A whole new HUD invention only Planet Zoo players are familar with, meaning PC1 players will have to get used to it and first need to work their way around everything (no tutorial whatsoever, maybe in the career mode which I haven't played yet)- No PC1 integration, meaning if you thought you could recreate your awesome PC1 parks/blueprints you'll have to start from scratch...Not recommended at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a "maybe" or "wait and see" for now. Not worth the price as it stands. There's a total of 5 ride themes. Aquatic, Resort, Mythology, Planet and Viking. These are not exactly a large variety. Frontier is seemingly paving the way for future DLC to fill these gaps, which in my opinion isn't really acceptable. I'm just going to assume Frontier has seen the success Planet Zoo has had with it's plethora of DLC and applied the same business model to PC2, which would be fine if the starting themes weren't so bad. For £55 (deluxe edition) this game is not worth it, even the standard edition is pushing it. I would wait for a big sale to purchase if you're interested in park builder games. The UI is also pretty bad. Visually it looks good, and it's fun making coasters and trying out slides on the pools but it all feels rather hollow and beta test-y at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is borderline completely broken in it's current state. Path tool is a nightmare to use, sometimes paths that worked fine previously completely stop functioning and guests get stuck on nothing. Slides with zero guests will register as having abysmal wait times, and therefore nobody rides them. Build tool is barely usable, some walls/pieces simply won't snap to the rest of the building. Slide platforms are a disaster and impossible to remove pieces without deleting everything, and sometimes flume starts will show up as colliding with non existent terrain and render the platform useless. Things across the board won't register that they are connected to a power or water source. UI and Workshop are also a mess but enough people have mentioned that already. Slide physics are incredibly disappointing... as in there are essentially none, why even bother including banked tracked pieces if rafts are going to ride it like they are glued to the ground The slides experience next to zero slowdown in flat sections. RCT3 was dramatically better almost two decades ago.You're going to have to abandon parks because they simply stop functioning. Also can't continue the campaign because the game won't recognize that objectives are completed.I hope we will get a functional version of this game eventually; but in it's current state calling it an alpha would be generous. Definitely disappointing coming from hundred of hours in Planco 1, and I remember that being actually acceptably usable at launch. I believe there is definitely a worthwhile sequel under the hood here, but I can't fathom how they thought releasing it like this was okay.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating 2/5  Graphics - 2 (Not as good as Planet Zoo or even Planet Coaster 1.  At first launch, the game looks incredible.  But, as soon as you start placing wall/roof/floor pieces together, you'll notice how they don't blend together and the lines of their edges are very distinct which looks horrible)Controls - 2  (Camera freaks out worse than it did in Planet Coaster 1 when placing pieces near already placed objects or in tight spaces.)Pathing - 2  (This is a weird one.  There are options that make pathing easier while at the same time, removing the ability to path on an already established grid is confusing.)Building Pieces - 1  (Minimal building pieces at launch.  Minimal theme options as well.  Planet Coaster 2 is definitely set up to be a pay for DLC fest in the near future.  There wasn't even an "Ultimate Edition" available at launch that will include ANY future piece packs. There aren't even glass pieces available for windows!)New Features - 1  (The new resize feature is a good idea but poorly implemented.  You can only resize the whole piece rather than being given the ability to only make a piece taller without making it wider, etc.  Even a game in Early Release (Prehistoric Kingdom) offers much better resizing options. The new scenery paint brush is a cool idea but is quite useless most of the time as even the lowest setting on the brush creates way too dense swaths of whatever trees, bushes, rocks you have set to use.  Again, (Prehistoric Kingdom) handles this much, much better.The best way I can describe Planet Coaster 2 is a game that has been released at full price even though it feels like it's a game barely out of Alpha stage.  Many features do not work.  Everything from guests not riding water slides to triggered effects on rides and coasters not working.  I also find building much more frustrating than it is in Planet Coaster 1 which is years old now.For me, this is a "I wish I hadn't purchased" product.

_childDocuments_.review: I've just started with the game and messed around with the 1st level just to get an idea of how it compares to PC1. I've been finishing up parks I never got to in PC1 in anticipation of the sequel so I can quite strongly compare the differences spotted so far which I will cover just from 40 min of play time I have.PC2 is super new and performance is great off the bat, especially compared to PC1's release. It looks overall similar but if you stop and pay attention you can see the visual improved in various aspects that overall come together quite nicely.The main issue is the bugs so far. For the first mission, I have to save and reload my park twice because it wasn't registering the actions I was doing towards the compulsory tutorial tasks. Eventually I had to just restart the scenario but it was like 5 min lost since it was early on. I just hope this doesn't become an issue on a park you have spent hours on.However I will say Frontier have been super quick to release an update to address feedback on the game and seem to listen to the players and will keep them coming which I can really appreciate.So far I have mostly seen much of the same content with some new rides and coasters but the main new content so far is the water parks which I am yet to experiment with.Some scenery themes have been traded out so we don't have Western and I think Space, at least from other reviews but the Greek Mythology theme added is even better imo. I'm sure we will get the older themes back in either later updates, or more realistically paid DLC. I wouldn't have a problem with the later tbh because it will content they worked on after release so having a price on it is understandable but they should have at least given us the PC1 scenery as well.The day 1 DLC they included SHOULD have been free with the base game as they did have this content ready with the release and it's mostly stuff from PC that was included for free. PC1 added some free content in updates so I hope with new content we do get, there's at least some free stuff as the game expands.The Steam workshop feature has been removed and instead you use the Frontier workshop. A tad annoying to create another account type if you don't have one already but it's easy to use and used in game where you can find and add content that's ready to go. The size limit isn't great but they already heard the fans and increased the limit from 1GB to 4GB with apparent plans to increase it more (hopefully we eventually get no limit or limit that's really hard to reach for the average player at least).They have added more and new ways to build things from paths to scenery onto rides directly. I think it's something that seems over complex at first compared to PC1's systems but I think once mastered will allow even more customizability and flexibility. They still have many of the older systems in as well like putting things onto a grid.If you really have an attention for detail and see how amazing the career parks are to start with and want to try maintain that level of detail and professional set up, I think the new mechanics will make that better. If you are more casual and just like to throw down rides and not go that all-out with matching the rest of the park in terms of quality and level of detail, it's probably more complex than it needs to be.Will update my review later but I'd say this is something to keep wishlisted and keep checking back in on the state of the game, and future updates and content. It's great as is for me personally but I'm sure it will get better and better.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, not great.I definitely had fun playing PC2. The game is absolutely beautiful and has infinite possibilities. For me the UI and editing was much more easy than that of PC1. Planet Coaster 2 offers 4 completely new themes. Viking: I love, the rides are great, the scenery is great, couldn't have nailed it better! Mythology: One word, WOW, every single scenery part, ride is beautifully worked outed and designed, Mythology offers a plethora scenery pieces to have fun with. Resort: To be honest, I don't quite get the idea of having "Resort" as a theme, scenery is just meh and feels kind of rushed. Aquatic: It's fun, sadly it really only fits the water park aspect of PC2, and in no way the theme park aspect, overall another "fun" theme but sadly only for the water slides.Based on the advertising the game heavily relies on the water park aesthetic and yet fails to do so. The content is just not enough to justify a 50 USD game when the original is still cheaper and has better overall content! But looking away from the bad, the water parks are just amazing, the pools are beautiful, the flume building is the stuff of my dreams, and just a fun time. I was let down by the fact that there are only 2 other themes you could use for the theme park part of this game. Don't get me wrong, they're both great, it just pails in comparison to the amount of possibilities we had in PC1. Summarizing everything said above, the game is fun just not "complete yet". The game is worth the price you pay for, regarding if frontier add DLC's and more content overtime. I would still definitely recommend this game! 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: The experience of *Planet Coaster* really depends on what type of player you are. Personally, I play it as a sandbox builder, spending hours perfecting the smallest details. I absolutely love this game, and the sequel brings some fantastic upgrades: scaling, a better path system, enhanced graphics, and an overall more flexible building experience. The water effects are stunning, and the ability to customize coasters and flat rides opens up a whole new world of creativity.That said, there are still a few issues and bugs that hold it back (though not enough for me to stop recommending it):- Customization on coasters and flat rides is limited; strangely, transport rides can’t be customized at all.- Limited color options for scenery items like rocks and props.- No weather control yet, though it’s slated for a future update—something that should’ve been there from the start.- While the path system is more flexible, there’s a learning curve to achieve specific results.- The UI feels clunky and unrefined, with more clicks needed to accomplish tasks.- Benches and trash cans still snap only to path edges, limiting placement flexibility.- Waterpark elements are sparse; where’s the kid-friendly stuff?- Slide physics are awkward, though they’re reportedly working on this.- The workshop is disappointing; they should revert to using the Steam Workshop or significantly improve the current one.If you are playing more franchise and actually play it as a simulator -> please look into the many other reviews, as this is something i do not do.

_childDocuments_.review: Not got massively into building yet but i've explored all the new features.Firstly theres alot of complaining about blurriness, i easily fixed mine by just putting the game in fullscreen and to my monitor native resolution but apparently it can happen due to depth of field so not sure there. The game is incredibly optimised which is a breath of fresh air these days on launch, DLSS is supported along with frame generation AI which makes the games perform 100 times better than the original while also looking fantastic.Dark rides are now way easier due to dynamic lightening so you dont need to use a time machine for that anymore.The new pathing tool is insane, its what i wanted as a kid from RCT3 and one thing that bugged me in PC1, its literally perfect imo.The huge amount of customisation is crazy also, like even things as simple as making signs allows you to make them bigger and add your own text on top of that as separate things.I dont think we'll get a steam workshop as frontier has their own built in now so thats pretty cool.I did encounter a few small bugs, like i placed a flatride down and it softlocked the game, this is the only time it happened and diddnt do it again so not sure what happened there.Honestly the "mixed" reviews are astonishing to me, should be at least very positive

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure like many of you, I've been burned by poor releases quite a lot in recent memory, so when PC2 dropped to mixed reviews, my heart sank thinking it was going to be yet another addition to my list of despair (*cough* Cities Skylines 2) but took a chance and purchased the game anyway. After getting a good 45 hours of playtime under my belt (in barely a week) I was expecting to find something to dislike... still looking btw. Is it perfect? Lol no, the UI is kinda garbage for PC users, the amount of menus I have to go through to find the tree I like is going to give me carpal tunnel, and the path finding logic of some of my guests is nonsensical, IE I'll see a huge group of guests all beeline to a ride, stare at its queue, then turn around with 0 thought as to why they wen that way (kinda relatable but..), also nobody seemed to have any interest in my waterpark after the first day, I built a really cool wave pool :( Beyond this? Just as fun as planet coaster 1 if not more, hoping for more themes as my artisic talent is lacking but the new path building is great, game looks great and runs great (for me at least), and overall I'm having a good time with it. Could use a little work, but overall a great park management game.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet Coaster 2

_childDocuments_.review: So far I am enjoying this a damn site more than the first game! It runs really well, the gameplay is engaging and the presentation is great! I don't understand everyone's complaints with the UI, I barely played PC1 and this seems fine to me as a PC user. The paths are much improved, although still a little bit tricky at times (nowhere near as bad as PC1). Custom shaped pools are tricky and could do with some work, along with some balancing needed for campaign goals. All in all I think it's the best park sim since RCT3 and has loads of potential!

Overall I have a hard time recommending this to anyone, but since there isn't a maybe option, I selected yes. Give it a chance but just know that it is very different.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just not ready. They should have just bit the bullet and launched as a "Early Release".Biggest Gripes:- Pathing is great when it works but super jank. It is not as clean as PC1 or PZoo. Even with the new tools. The Draw Tool can be helpful but is super limited by the angles it allows you to choose.- UI , annoying to navigate. Things in odd places. Massive full screen menus.- The new "Upkeep" or "Maintenance" system feels tedious. You're not going to stop things from degrading, which IMO is a step back from the system in Planet Zoo. You can't maximize your Mechanics in the park, you can flood it with them but things will still degrade.- Staff as a whole feels terrible. We didn't get fully modeled Staff Rooms like in PZoo and managing them is even worse. The Staff Zones are Drawn but move with Camera angle so it feels like you don't know the definitive border. Assigning those Work-Zones are a massive headache. No drop-down menu to quickly assign and manage like in PZoo. Park Info > Staff > Schedule > Click Schedule Slot> >Advanced Settings > Work Zone Box > Apply Setting. FOR EVERY EMPLOYEE ONE BY ONE. Janitors also seem to just be worse than ever before, even when I assign "only take out trash-cans" to 8 of them, they still just walk by full, overspilling cans. Vendors have their bugs too.- Frontier Workshop: Besides the long load times and download limit, searching for something specific just can't be done. You can type the name of a Blueprint in Word for Word and not have it show on the first page. Something is severely underdeveloped with the Search Tool.- We hyped WaterParks but didn't launch with Waterslide Physics. Also placing Pools on the map will Slow down the game Significantly. We're talking 6 Second Delay to place things or higher (Deleted all my pools around that mark and Friends did the same while testing it), even if the pools aren't being used/populated. To build a Massive full map Waterpark will slowly just wreck your game.- We dropped Coasters without the ability to have Two Stations (It's coming in Update in December) and at least on Junior Coasters the Lapping Mode doesn't work. Laps will not save and will revert back to 1. Basic functions that worked in PC1.All in all just a huge step-back. More issues others have covered but a lot of it can be polished but you can't Polish Day 1 DLC that was in PC1. I expected them to really launch off the Improvements they made from PC1 to PZoo and make another big leap. Instead it feels like a brand-new team Porting PC1 to an upgraded Engine. I'm just gonna blame the move to integrate Consoles so heavily setting it back so hard.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated Review: The game crashes randomly, the color I select can't be remembered when I click into a new building piece, you can't toggle the weather or turn off the rain in sandbox, bottoms of the pools connect terribly making it incredibly hard to make a gradual pool entrance (They should add a proper staircase for pools), you have to confirm selection every time you want to use the selection tool, and in the Frontier Workshop you have flat rides and coasters under the same category "Coasters", when half the uploads under that category are flat rides.....This game is obviously rushed and has a lot of polishing and fixing up to do. Would NOT recommend you buy this game until its fixed. This game is a hot mess, and the community had to tear Frontier apart to get real water slide physics, something that should've been in this game on its release.... This game should've released for beta testing, but Frontier opted to instead get feedback with your money already in their hands.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Coaster with a better pathing system, updated graphics, more customization options in every aspect, plus the ability to now create waterparks. Some people are complaining that it feels like a massive DLC, but this is exactly what I think a sequel is supposed to be. It didn't reinvent the wheel, it's still the game I know/love/expect, but with significantly more content, QoL updates, and better graphics. I can understand being dissapointed by certain things, like the "multiplayer" mode just being a built in file share, or your favorite themes not being present in the base game, but overall I think it's a great sequel. I also like to believe Frontier will address some of the more glaring issues, like bugged out physics or the built-in mod workshop being so lackluster, as Frontier has a pretty good track record of fixing community concerns as much as they can. Worth the $50.

_childDocuments_.review: I looooved PC1. I don't think PC2 is good yet. I hope with updates and scenery pack releases I'll be able to change my review to a recommendation. I wish they hadn't tried to add water park elements and instead improved and expanded upon track rides, roller coasters, and theme park functionality that already had a foundation in PC1. Since they went to the trouble of adding water park features, I tried building pools and lazy rivers, but I didn't enjoy it because the guests don't interact with them in a satisfying or realistic way. They don't float in the lazy rivers, the best I've seen is sometimes they walk slowly along the bottom of the pool. I've never seen a sadder lazy river. I hope they release updates to improve the game later, because I've been SO looking forward to this sequel and really want to enjoy it the way I imagined!Negatives:1. Water park elements are thin. The game went to the trouble of adding water park elements, but it doesn't feel like they finished implementing them.2. Pool and path building is very finicky - If you're adding paths to the pool edge yourself, the starting shape of the pool will be changed by the paths. Doing fully custom pools take a lot of trial and error. The draw path and pool tool is a nice idea, but it's super clunky to use.3. Controls and menu navigation feels inefficient and strange. I often use ctrl+z because of the finicky building controls, but I wish ctrl+z didn't undo the entire draw path I just did. Sometimes it also takes a chunk out of the pool. Menus will stay open sometimes, but sometimes close and I lose my spot in the browser. It doesn't feel intuitive. 4. Customization seems shallow right now. For example, pool light colors aren't customizable, you can't add custom park music, no customizable water colors and there's no terrain stamp tool like in Planet Zoo.5. Scenery items aren't very useful. They're either way too specific or too generic. I can add a fantastical angler fish type animatronic, but there's not basic sharks, fish, or any animals. They have lots of specific viking and greek themed items, but nothing like generic adventure, haunted or medieval. I get they'll probably be releasing scenery packs later, but the starting items make it very hard to theme areas to my liking without a ton of layering. 6. I don't understand why they added power and water management. Granted, it's something you can toggle off in the sandbox mode, but I don't understand why they added this when there is much more basic theme park stuff that needs attention.Positives:1. Graphics look nice - the water especially looks great.2. Paths - I listed this as a negative as well because it's kind of both. While we have better flexibility to add large courtyards and curved path shapes, the tools to build them are clunky and frustrating to use. 3. I like the added weather. However it doesn't look as good as in Planet Zoo, and rain doesn't affect pool surfaces.

_childDocuments_.review: I am deeply saddened to be writing this.As an avid fan of Planet Coaster 1, the release of PC2 left me feeling sad. You would expect a sequel to have the base features the first game had, but Planet Coaster 2 leaves a lot to be desired. Where are the hotels, restaurants, security guards, security cameras, vista points, vandals, video billboards (and custom billboards), all of the different brands like Street Fox Coffee?Why were so many management features removed? We used to be able to customize our shops pretty in-depth. Money is seemingly infinite. I can continuously keep placing coasters down and still have millions. Shops used to have to be tinkered with and placed in the proper spots for effective sales, now peeps just swarm no matter what.You would think they would play a simple play before launching... Play for more than 20 minutes and you'll start to see all of the glaring issues. Why do peeps all take the exact same path? Why do the peeps all randomly decide to leave the park at the exact same time, while new ones are pouring in to replace them; causing massive path congestion constantly. The staff rarely do their jobs. They frequently get stuck in position, requiring you to move them to get them to walk again. Guests use your pools and flumes on day one, and then after that nobody uses them. Guests refuse to queue for rides saying they don't want to wait for 0 minutes.This game has a lot of potential, but for them to release it in this state makes me really worried. I recommend against buying this until they smooth it out, until then keep enjoying PC1!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this was a huge disappointment. They added two new really cool ideas. One the franchise mode. And two is they improved the visuals. The positives kind of end at that. There is so much backwards progress from Planet Coaster 1 and Planet Zoo to this, it is insane. Some of the best features that made PC1 and PZ fun are just gone. _childDocuments_.review: Using a console-style UI and navigation on a PC title is frustrating. I understand that console players often have to wait after an initial release, but PC players shouldn't have to deal with a poorly optimized interface because developers didn’t adapt it to PC. There are no tooltips, and hovering over an item often doesn’t show what it is—you have to click it to find out. Selecting a ride, for instance, requires navigating through three menus. When adjusting settings, like path options, the UI feels very console-centric. Instead of dropdowns, you’re forced to cycle through settings with left and right arrows, which is unintuitive on PC. The game looks fantastic, but the clunky navigation and tedious interactions make it frustrating to play.Edit: after 10+ hours it's getting easier to know how to navigate but it should still not be so difficult. I'm deciding to change the review. The game itself is great and once over the UI hump I'm quite enjoying it whereas before I was just getting frustrated.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet Coaster 2

_childDocuments_.review: The bones of a great squeal are there. There are many improvements that need to be made and I hope many of these changes are not locked behind a DLC paywall. For now I would recommend sticking to PC1. The game is by no means unplayable, but there are several details that annoy me enough to recommend PC1 until they are addressed. First and foremost the game wanted to run in 720p with 15fps on my fairly modern machine. It took a few reddit posts and fiddling in settings to get it to run and look its best. From my understanding this will be fixed in hotfix 1. I'm disappointed by the lack of swing launches on the roller coasters. It's clear why they did not advertise it leading up to launch because they knew they would get push back from the community. They just showed switch tracks and let the community infer that meant swing launches. They knew that was a highly anticipated feature. They knew very well what they were doing and that is shameful on the devs part. If I purchase a roller coaster simulation game in 2024 I expect it to be able to emulate the types of rides being built today.What annoys me the most about the game is how different navigating menus are. It was clearly designed with console in mind as everything is put behind a couple sub menus that you need to navigate. There are zero tutorials or help that I have found to make navigating the menus easier. All they needed to do was continue the system from PC1 and I would have been happy. Coaster track and rides clip into itself or the terrain.The pools are fun, but they did the same thing from RCT3 where guests can swim around in splash down pools for slides. This severely limits the realism from a water park. The lifeguards will attempt to save guests that need it, but they just swim up and blow their whistle at the drowning guest. Not realistic, but funny af.Career mode now has cut scenes. My tic tok zoomer brain can't handle two minutes of pointless dialogue about a silly story leading to me managing the park.You still need to wait for guests to unload and get off the platform before new guests will board a coaster instead of both being done simultaneously.To partake in franchise mode you need a Frontier account. I don't want another account I need to sign into so I guess that feature is useless for me. I would wait a few years until the inevitable fixes are released and keep playing PC1.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet Coaster 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't own Planet Coaster 1, PC2 will be a fun romp into building amusement parks. It's fun, it runs pretty cleanly, and it does have some features PC2 has that PC1 does not. Go in expecting a fun build-heavy game.If you have Planet Coaster 1, your fond memories of the first may get in the way of fully enjoying the title. I've never liked any of this developer's UI layouts, and this one is no different. It's not better or worse than PC1 or Planet Zoo, just different and not what I would call 'good'. Many tools are buried in menus and it seems to be neither well-optimized for keyboard or for controller, but a mediocre mishmash of the two. The pathing tool is MUCH better than in PS1, as is terraforming. Graphics look...fine. Very close to PC1 and I'm torn on whether or not it's good enough of a jump to warrant a whole other title, but it doesn't look bad at all. Less clipping than PC1 with building, and the water tools and rides are a fun addition. Some of my people occasionally have pathing issues, but at least in PC2 I can drop them in a pool and let out some frustrations. The single/multiplayer franchise mode is neat. Overall a good time. I'm a little disappointed that there's not more of a distinction between the two releases visually and UI-wise. If you have PC1, wait a bit til a few more patches have dropped.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet Coaster 2

_childDocuments_.review: So far, Planet Coaster 2 is a gorgeous disappointment that threw out a decent PC UI for a very console friendly UI that results in the game taking 3-5 extra clicks to do what took 1 in PC1… at least on my PC. As of now, I’d rate the original much higher in terms of being user, creative friendly. Good news is that Frontier seems to be super open to feedback and with this being the #1 complaint, Frontier will update this for PC if they’re smart and make the PC UI as decent as the first game. Until then, this game just takes too long to do what’s fun and easier in PC1. Graphics are gorgeous though. New coasters lack some of the latest and greatest in the industry (xtreme spinners, swing launches, modern track styles), but plenty of cool new stuff to enjoy. Water park physics are very RCT3 - wonky and goofy. No interest in the water park stuff yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I eagerly anticipated Planet Coaster 2 after viewing early access gameplay on YouTube. As a seasoned player of similar games, I appreciate both creativity and challenge in gaming.However, Planet Coaster 2 did not meet my expectations. Reflect on your school days; completing a project successfully felt rewarding, didn't it? Conversely, an incomplete or poorly done project brought disappointment. It seems that game developers might be overlooking these core emotional responses. They conceptualize an exciting game, but often deliver it only partially completed, expecting players to be content with a product that feels like an unfinished school project, impacting the overall experience negatively.Currently, Planet Coaster 2 falls short:- Conceptual Design: The concept is promising. Designing and creating elaborate parks is engaging. - Gameplay Mechanics: Managing the park lacks depth. There's an absence of challenge or hardship, which is crucial for maintaining player engagement.- Technical Issues: The game is plagued by numerous bugs. Logical inconsistencies are common, and neither the in-game guides nor tutorials offer sufficient help, often necessitating community collaboration to resolve issues.Recommendation:- Current Purchase:  I would not recommend buying Planet Coaster 2 at this juncture. - Additional Content: While it's ultimately your decision, I would advise against investing in extra content until the core game is polished.I am hopeful for future updates. Once improvements are made, I will reconsider and update my review accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been an avid fan of Planet Coaster 1 and Planet Zoo. Although I love the better graphics, the new water and build features, and the updated coaster, I'm finding it hard to enjoy the game. The paths are a major problem. I feel like Planet Zoo had great pathing, it seems like they brought some of the features into this game. However, it seems like the guests pathfinding is bugged like crazy. On top of that, the paths cross and merge in weird ways causing invisible barriers for the guests.  I have had to destroy whole path sections to fix this, and they still keep appearing. Pathways seem to either be square or round, its hard to find a good balance between them especially in ride ques. Barriers and fence blocks were a great help in Planet coaster 1 and Planet Zoo stopping guests from entering zones or forcing their direction, but it didn't carry over to this game. You use to be able to sink them into the ground forcing guests to walk around them. Building grand fountains and structures on the pathways seem obscure when the guests just walk right through it. Although using creativity to design your own buildings and scenes with the given scenerio items is nice and can feel accomplishing. I do feel like the game was released with half of the usual stuff. I remember having so many options in Planet Coaster and Planet Zoo without needing  a DLC pack. It feels like we should have had a lot more scenery items and roofing options. The game isn't bad, there are some great additions and features and the devs are clearly working hard. Its just hard for me to enjoy the game currently when I'm constantly running into bugs and feeling like more is missing from the current game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for a little while now and overall I'd like to think that if you enjoyed previous titles from Frontier or are into coaster builders/sim games you'll like this and should give it a try. After all, it 's still Planet Coaster and one of the best coaster sims available, IMO. I'll break it down below if you want a more in-depth assessment, Some honest thoughts about the game in it's current state:It's good and bad. The game hits a lot of highs, but has some pretty steep lows as well. Anyone who played the first title will immediately notice some pretty large things missing including:-Security Guards and cameras/any security feature at all-The ability to change weather/user friendly time of day UI -Snow-Simplistic pathing system to go along with the new pathing system + tools. The "classic" pathing is still not the same as the original pathing from PC1. The stamp tool is a great addition but for some odd reason lacks a "circle" stamp. The only easy way around this is to stamp an octogon and then use the rounding tool to smoothe it into a circle. However, you can only round the smallest size stamped octogon. Any larger and the tool will not create a circle. Very frustrating, a simple circle stamp is all that's necessary. -Many of the Planet Coaster branded shops are no longer available such as Mexilente, Street Fox Coffee, etc. There are like 3 new shops/brands but most of the ones we've had from PC1 and Planet Zoo are gone. Gulpee and Pipshot have been reduced to 1 shop a piece instead of Gulpee Soda, Slush, and Energy, etc. -Restaraunts are gone-Hotels are gone-No edge scrolling -Guests limited to 6000 max-Finance tab is limited and only displays your park's finances with a line graph rather than a detailed breakdown with numbers & categories-UI is generally not friendly for PC players and is weirdly merged to be fully compatible for both PC and console. Why? Just give us the original PC UI, and if we plug a controller in have it switch to controller compat. The needless clicking of so many menus and buttons is exhausting to the consumer and dampens a game that already requires a lot of patience. -Some issues right now with mechanics and staff getting stuck in random places forever, or getting stuck while trying to complete tasks/enter ride areas. Hopefully this is addressed and fixed by Frontier soon, confident that it will be as they've already done a hot fix on day 3 of release. -No Steam Workshop (for now?). Right now we have the Frontier Workshop and it's okay, but Steam is much better. Hopefully Frontier takes that to heart and returns the Steam Workshop.Now that my main grievances are out of the way, here's my positives:-PC2 generally stands up against the first title/other coaster builders. The creativity, freedom and feel of this game is top-notch-New pathing system + more path freedom. New shapes and ways to experiment with paths and plazas. Absolute bonus is the amazing amount of path styles + the ABILTY TO RECOLOR THEM! No longer are we doomed to have path colors we don't like. Not to mention the new ability to mix and match rails and auto-place bins and benches along the path as you build. Amazing feature and I hope they expand on it soon as right now you can't auto-place both bins and benches, only one or the other.-The ability to create flat rides from scratch. Flat rides only ever came in the variant that Frontier gave us, but now we can start with a completely bare flat ride and attach any piece you want to it that will spin, move and trigger along with the ride-Ability to scale objects now. Need I say more?-Pools! Finally, the ability to have a WATERPARK with my theme park! The pieces are fun and Frontier is already ironing out the pool/slide physics people are having issues with. -So much new foliage, it's almost on par with Planet Zoo (base game). Huge upgrade from PC1.-The physics and graphics are 10/10, for the most part.-Way more mascots/entertainers available to hire in base game.-Way more/better terrain paints. You can finally ACTUALLY "garden" and make dirt paths/rocks/stone that look attractive instead of using dry grass to signify where a garden is. -Great scenery pieces available base game. Overall, there's a lot of good and bad about this game. Some say it should've been a bit more polished before release which may be true, but don't think this isn't still a great game. Frontier has shown to be pretty responsive so far about everyone's issues & opinions so I've got a lot of hope for the future of this game, whether it's free updates or much anticipated DLCs. If you're into coaster builders, sim games, or a fan of any of the previous titles, I'd buy this. If you're a little more picky and want things to be more smoothed out, wait a couple months or until a sale to grab this. Here's to hoping we all waste 1000s of hours on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high expectations for this game after spending many hours on the first Planet Coaster and also on Roller Coaster Tycoon 3. However, this feels like a big step back. While it’s true that there’s a significant improvement in graphics, path creation, and roller coaster building, there are many areas where it falls short.Bugs aside, the interface is terrible—clearly designed more for controllers than for keyboard and mouse. The menus for viewing simple stats, like the profit/loss balance, which you could easily see in the first game just by hovering over the button, now require you to go to a separate menu that pauses the game, and you're forced to read a terrible chart that makes everything cumbersome. The passage of days in the campaign mode scenarios makes no sense at all. After playing over two hours in the same scenario, only six hours have passed on day one of the park’s opening. This is confusing given the previous time system we were used to.Customization of attractions is one of its strong points, allowing for more customization options and a big quality improvement over the previous game. But visitor management is terrible. When you open a new flat, all visitors abruptly change direction and head toward it, as if every single visitor is moving in sync with the same thought.The lack of themes is another downside. Although there’s now much more creative freedom to build what you want, many elements that could have enriched the experience are missing, such as lasers, robots, spaceships, pirate-style boats, treasure chests, etc. The physics of the slides, the game’s big new feature, are absurd, looking like they’re in fast motion and not following any logical physics.I’d like to think that Frontier will make improvements in this regard, but it seems to me that the issues run so deep that the game needed another six months of development and polishing to be decent. I don’t think this will change much in the short term.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing 300+ hours in PC1, I have anticipated the release of this game for months. I am excited to get into some of the new mechanics, customization options, graphical improvements, and quality of life fixes... BUT! I cannot get over the clunky and unintuitive user interface.Navigating menus using escape or even the left mouse button doesn't close menus in the way it feels like it should. The menus are also fairly confusing in terms of layout. Not that I don't expect some changes, but the taxonomy isn't very sensible. Good for release day! but needs some fine tuning to become a classic like the first.Also the guests seem to be incredibly picky about the most simple aspects of the park? Like I'll have a coaster with >8 excitement, <3 fear and nausea, at $3 with like 10 people in line and practically EVERY guest says the line is "massive" and the coaster is "way too expensive". Maybe I'm just bad, but the balancing is wayyyyyy different than PC1. Maybe it's a learning curve, but it makes me feel like I have no idea what I'm doing.

_childDocuments_.review: the only reason i keep playing this atm is because its the only new game in this genre available. _childDocuments_.review: As many, many others have already said, this game is currently unfit for release. Riddled with bugs, poorly optimized and completely unintuitive for anyone unfamiliar with Frontier games, it even has a spelling mistake on one of the menus. A huge amount of content is missing in comparison with Planet Coaster 1 which makes this a very bare-bones base game. Frontier have already released DLC which is nearly half the cost of the base game so it looks like we're going to be paying for stuff that should have already been in the game. They have an update planned which may or may not fix at least some of the issues, but that's not due until December, which makes me suspect that this is when this game should have released (AND as early access!)The disappointment with this game is huge for fans of the franchise. I'd give it at least a year, and even then, see what other people are saying because buying it now, you're paying to be a beta tester.

_childDocuments_.review: I brought the Pre-ordered deluxe edition as I am huge fan of Frontiers Planet Coaster 1 and Planet Zoo, so of course had to buy it. First of all they listened to the players of wanting a Water Park (as sadly didn't get one in PC 1) Which is a dream come true! You can build your own pool with different depths, add your own flumes and Lazy River. Lots of scenery pieces ( and blueprints to place) to choose from with themes of PC, Mythology, Resort, Viking and Aquatic, with 5 new Mascot Entertainers.  You can now add scenery pieces onto the rides whether it be flat rides or coasters. Also you can now share your saved park to other people let them add things in and send back to you. They have a dedicated workshop in game now to upload, download. They have also added electric requirement and Water filtration too (you can turn it off on sandbox mode)Visually the graphics are beautifully improved the PC 1, navigation is slightly different but once you know how its a lot easier I think. The only problem i'm having is the management with staff i'm finding difficult never was great at it on the first game so i'm finding it more challenging. As so far not found a tutorial on it. There are some bugs at present (20/11/24) which is a little frustrating, but I've seen from the patches some are being fixed or onto fixing. (However didn't expect this many, as there are more than PC 1)Is it worth the full price plus Pre-order at the moment no but i'm in trust of frontier to fixing the bugs which is letting it down. Once the major bugs have gone then deffo worth full price. However, I recommend it 100% if your a fan of the previous game, want improve graphics more customisation, and detail management and want pools (as it is focused a fair bit) and a overall fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: I still would recommend the game, but not now. Whilst they did change a lot for the good, like paths, coaster smoothing and stuff like the pieces to make static props animate. It does leave a bit of disappointment that there are some things like guest AI, game exclusions and an overall feeling that it needed to be in the oven.___________From this point I'll be breaking down my points:Things Frontier Confirmed:*No legit custom pieces for custom Coaster support ( Will be Addressed in Update 1 )*Custom Coaster trains and flat rides, but not on water, dark or transportation rides for some reason ( Soon to be Addressed in Update 1 )*The exclusion of billboard and speaker customization at launch ( Will be rectified soon )*Loading/Unloading Stations not bring a separate station ( Addressing soon in Update 1 )*Slide Physics ( Addressing soon in Update 1 )Good:*Pathing system is more liberating than in Planco 1 and Planet Zoo*Scaling*Scenery Pieces are neat*Addition of track pieces like switch track and drop tracks for example*Customization on Flat rides*Custom Coaster Cars*Campaign is refreshing a bit*Guest Spawn-points are semi-modular*Game's score is very awesome* VA's from campaign are really charming, each personality on full display.Cons:*Pathing system can be very janky, rounding too for example doesn't always leave a natural curve*Guest AI are stupid, they can't figure out how to get in line for a bus to reach a separate section of my park, then I placed a bridged section to what was supposed to be a separate part of my park and then they use the buses there.*Guests complaining that the queue is too long when it's only nearby the entrance gate to the station that is filled*No round pieces to animate static props*No round stamp tool*Lack of detail in break rooms, especially disappointed given the attention to detail in Planet Zoo*Rather than expanding on the Restaurant concept like what they did in Planet Zoo, it's been gutted*Rather than expanding upon the Hotels, especially to capitalize on the Resort theme, instead we just build hotels that aren't functional.*Personal Nitpick and may be addressed soon, but I would have loved for the Planco 1 themes to come back.*Guest spawn point is bizarre, just three busses and the paths, not even like a road and sidewalk or a parking lot or something, just on the dirt.*Scenery brush is cool, and I love the toggle to avoid paths, but I need it to also avoid pools and attractions.*Either because of the Cobra Engine or not, I wish you can toggle whether a Scenery piece had collision or not so that guests don't clip through*Speaking of, the fence in Planco 1 and the Guest kerb in Planet Zoo that made guests avoid stepping beyond that, no longer function as guest barriers.*MUPLAYER IS NOT YOUR TYPICAL MULTIPLAYER, IT IS NOT PARKITECT WHERE YOU BUILD TOGETHER, AND I FEEL THAT THEIR MARKETING IS SOMEWHAT MISLEADING WHEN IT COMES TO THAT IF YOU DON'T DO YOUR RESEARCH.*Clunky UI made for Console/Controller users, whilst removing shortcuts and changing position of them for those on keyboard and mouse.*Copying an object with CTRL+D/X seems to not copy the item property, has been noted with music speakers.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic sequel! There have been so many small, Quality Of Life additions for this game compared to the first, including the ease with which we can build plazas in our parks, separate priority queues, custom animatronics  and the ability to build water parks, among others.The new themes are beautiful and suit both water parks and coaster parks really beautifully. The graphics are stunning. I also like the fact we've been given 4 different types of sandbox mode, to allow you to decide how much challenge you want. It really feels like there's something for everyone.I can't honestly say I've had the issues with the UI that many have had - I found items in the menu easy to find (it feels similar to Planet Zoo, so if you've played that, you'll probably find it a bit easier) and building has been nice and easy. _childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of Roller Coaster Tycoon, the 1st Planet Coaster, and also Planet Zoo. Love them all and have a huge amount of play time. You can imagine my excitement when I realised that Planet Coaster 2 was being released. I pre-purchased and immediately downloaded it once it was available. I like sandbox mode so I can build beautiful parks so set about trying to build my first structure. I will start with the negatives. Immediately, it was apparent that the interface was awful. Then, I found that the colouring system does not work well i.e. I extended a 4m column with a 2m piece. What I found was that the game did not remember and translate the colour from the 4m to 2m piece. And, when using the x keyboard key, it still did not seem to line up with the 4m piece correctly. And, I later logged out and returned. It did not seem to remember my last colour choices. I could go on. It was all very dispiriting and prompted me to come here and see if others were happy, or whether I was just being negative. The first point of note is that, as others commented, the interface seems designed for consoles. Perhaps it works there but at the cost of a downgrade in the interface for the PC. And the limitation on guest numbers to 6000 is a joke, and presumably for consoles. And I am guessing another problem, the lack of glass pieces, is also driven by limitations of the console. And the workshop is horrible - the Steam workshop was great. The positive I have seen so far is that the paths are absolutely outstanding. It is also great that they have added water rides as I loved that feature in Roller Coaster Tycoon. However, I have read here that they are not using physics, for the water slides, and (if true) would be a major disappointment. The okay are the building pieces that come with the base game. But, as others point out, there is no sci-fi or Western themes which is a little disappointing. Whereas I should be playing the game right now, I am writing this review instead and wondering whether my disappointment is enough for a refund. Instead of being excited, I felt let down. I am not sure which way I will go on the refund yet, as I kind of hope Frontier will listen to the feedback and start sorting out the problems. Here is the bottom line; I really don't care about the limitations of consoles, I want a game for a PC that matches the great work Frontier has done on the original game and Planet Zoo. I will post updates if my views change with more time in game. In the meantime, I cannot recommend this game. You would be far better off buying the original Planet Coaster and wait and see if Frontier responds to the negative feedback.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played Planet Coaster 1 and Planet Zoo for well over a thousand combined hours, I would highly recommend this game, even in its early state, to anyone who has an ounce of creativity in their brains.Lots of people have shared concerns that not enough deviated and improved from the first game, but the creative opportunities offered in this game far outnumber those ever given in the first. For example, smooth coasters, true darkrides, custom animatronics, scenery scaling, waterparks (including wave pools and lazy rivers) and a far more flexible pathing system make up a better basegame than Planet Coaster 1 ever had.Frontier has also actively adressed concerns about the game, and been generally open with the community. They have already implemented most of the highest requested features, and have taken the feedback to create seperate load/offload stations, custom audio/visuals, and water slide physics.Overall, I am extremely happy with the state of this game, and the problems it does have I am confident will be ironed out (It seems many people in the community have forgotten the problems the other planet games had on launch. Rose tinted glasses and all). I am also somewhat ashamed of the community, who have completely overblown problems and overlooked everything we have been provided thus far. The only problems I have had are negligible, like too many guests entering the park when I have just started, or objects reverting colors when I press ctrl z, nothing that has really impacted my enjoyment of the game.In short, I believe Frontier has delivered another great addition to the planet family, and I am way more excited to see where this game goes than I ever was for Planet Coaster 1 (which I still loved). If you are a creative person at all, PLEASE play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Planet Coaster 2 hyped and ready for all the theme park magic—only to find myself slogging through a mess of design decisions that make you feel like you’re stuck in a broken-down ride. First, I tried Career Mode, thinking I’d learn the ropes. Instead, I got an obstacle course of frustration.Let’s start with editing coasters. So, as a "Coastorian" or whatever, my first task is to renovate an old coaster. Easy enough, right? But unlike every other building game where you just hit space or enter to snap the next track piece in place, here those keys do nothing. Instead, they throw you into a different editing mode, forcing you to manually select "Place Track" every single time. Who thought this was a good idea?Fine, I finally get through that, and then it demands I place *eight* flat rides. Eight? Why? But I press on, only to discover another headache. In the original Planet Coaster, you’d place a flat ride, drop a queue, and the exit path would follow naturally. Planet Coaster 2 decided, “Nah, let’s complicate that.” Now, you have to select the path tool yourself to make the queue and then re-select it for the exit path. Why make this so clunky?And the final straw—the thing that actually made me hit "refund"? An advertisement campaign. Simple enough, I thought, after handling one in the first park. But this time, it won’t let me start a campaign because I “need a gift shop, soda shop, and restroom.” Sure, I place them, power them up, assign staff, the works. But still… “Requirements Not Met.” I literally dropped 100 shops and facilities, all to no avail. And if I can’t even get through Career Mode, how am I supposed to tackle Creative Mode?This isn’t just a learning curve—it’s a learning wall, with bugs stacked on top. I paid for a complete game, not to be a beta tester for Frontier’s inevitable DLC cash-grab.TL;DR: Avoid the hype train. Planet Coaster 2 is a buggy, frustrating mess that’s not worth the price. Don’t make the same mistake I did.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE:After playing the game more and getting over the initial hurdles described in my original review, I have enjoyed it for the most part and recommend getting it for those who can look past the initial bugs. The devs have already confirmed they are working on a december patch to fix some of the issues described which will dramatically help the game. Still disappointing as a full release and I would treat this game as early access at the moment.Additional Issues I've Encountered:-Lots of crashing, specifically when trying to undo something-Pool physics are abysmal at the moment-Weather doesn't seem to have much impact at the moment, and on the tropical map it rains way too much-Half pipes do not work on any flumes (at least for me)-The water jet conveyor belt on the raft type slide has a bug that causes it to go at an immense speed no matter what you choose-A bug that causes guests to not queue up for rides-Guests do not attempt to avoid sceneryORIGINAL REVIEW:I cannot in good faith recommend this game at this point in time. It's clearly an unfinished product with removed features from PC1. Despite it's upgrades in certain categories, the missing/broken features overshadow the good aspects of the game.In my limited playtime, here are some examples:-Coaster editing is very sensitive. Constantly placing track pieces when I don't mean to.-Terrain sculpting has a delay before beginning. Meaning you have to hold down the mouse button for a couple of seconds before the terrain starts to change.-Building pieces do not retain color change. When undoing a placed building piece, the piece then reverts back to its original colors so you must then deselect and duplicate another piece that has the color change or manually change the colors again-UI is very laggy and unintuitive. Constantly switching between tabs to find the correct setting, a clear step back from PC1-Scenery brush also lags and doesn't contain the scenery within the brush circle, constantly placing them on the outside-The display is very blurry (which fortunately can be helped a bit by tweaking your settings)-Limited biome types in sandbox, only four at the moment which is less than PC1 launched with-Remove scenery themes such as fairytale and pirate, a move that makes it seem like they just want to sell it back to us in the futureDespite the improvements including new coaster types, coaster smoothing, graphics, and pools, this game is another clear example of the industry shipping a product not ready to be released. I only hope they will provide free updates to add/fix these issues in the future instead of penny pinching their fans for all they're worth

Completely separate priority pass queues.+ Nice range of coaster types, and visual upgrades to those persisting from PC1.+ Assets are generally quicker to place, when not contending with the UI.- No ability to add custom signs/assets/music.- Weird workshop limitations on downloads/uploads.- Many assets and theme options seem to be suspiciously lacking, especially compared to PC1, seeming to pave the way for a plethora of DLC cosmetic packs. _childDocuments_.review: To start, I loved the first Planet Coaster and spent hundreds of hours working on a custom theme park. So I was really excited when I heard about Planet Coaster 2. The whole waterpark aspect wasn't the most exciting thing to me, but I was looking forward to upgrading from PC1 regardless.There are a lot of pros and cons to PC2 so lets get into it.PROS:- Performance is great and runs super smooth, even with a packed park and a ton going on. I remember PC1 would be struggling when I had a full park in sandbox, but so far PC2 is looking like a large improvement. (There is a weird motion blur/ambient occlusion thing going on that makes everything look super out of focus and soft, but so I recommend toggling that off)- There were a lot of good quality of life improvements from PC1. The pathing system is much better than before and im glad they kept the option to use the original system as well. - The management side of things feels much more detailed (for better and for worse which ill get into). But creating work zones works really well and feels like an improvement from the last game, also its cool how guests have dietary restrictions and other more in-depth characteristics. - The campaign feels much more polished this time around. There is voice acted narration which was a nice surprise.- Ride customization is fantastic! Being able to edit directly on to your ride and not have to worry about tracks or anything overlapping gives you so much freedom to do some cool stuff.- Generally most gameplay aspects feel like an improvement from PC1 overall.CONS:I am going to have a lot more cons than pros and I want to preface this by saying none of these are deal breakers for me, but definitely things I found a bit disappointing. Im going to try and mention some things other people havent mentioned as much in their reviews.- Energy management and refurbishment is first up. I dont mind having to manage the parks energy and power and its a fun challenge trying to hide generators. But from the one campaign chapter I played, I spent an insane amount of time just managing my mechanics and making sure that my rides were in good shape. Between that and my army of janitors it felt a bit oppressive. This could just be I still suck at the park management side of things though. - Lack of customisation. PC1 had a TON of fun themes and assets that most people would use in a theme park. PC2 has some stellar themes that all look great, but two of the four feel very specific to water parks and it feels like there is less overlap between them, which limits you a bit with what you can do with the pre-made assets without going really in depth and making your own blueprints. - Limited Biomes. This might just be a me thing, but in the sandbox mode there are only 4 biomes you can choose from and all of them are just Green, Tropical Green, Mountain Green, and I honestly cant remember the difference from the last one but its another green map. I loved having the option to have a more arid or a park with some snow in the first game, so it was a let down to see that was gone.- This is a small one, but you can no longer build terrain around your coasters after you have placed them. If you do the terrain first, you can have your coasters tunnel through when building. But if you try and do the terrain after, then your coaster just clips through the terrain. This is one of the most frustrating things for me because it was so nice in PC1 to just be able to step up your coasters design after by building some terrain around it. But im hoping this is just a setting I havent come across yet. Overall, im enjoying the game and im excited to play more, but I really wish they hadnt taken out some of the older features and also had some more premade assets that covered wider genres. There is a good selection, but like others have been saying, it does feel like they are waiting to release other stuff as DLC (the day 1 DLC for the vintage pack also annoys me a little bit)Despite having a long list of cons, I still recommend this game and like it. I only have 5 or so hours in it while writing this review, so im sure some of the cons might just come from me not fully understanding how everything works yet...So if you are new to Planet Coaster, I would say you will probably enjoy this game a lot. If you are a fan of the original, you will still enjoy this, but there will definitely be some things that you will be missing and it will take at least an hour to get familiar with all the new controls and UIEDIT: Forgot to mention but the music slaps!

_childDocuments_.review: The game has more bugs than the first one. This is a console game that was poorly optimized for PC. At least make decent controls. This is just an insult to anyone who has played PC1.The Frontier workshop is unusable. You can only search for tags and each item can have just one low res picture.Mechanics get stuck and rides won't get repaired. Guests pile up on paths in the campaign map (didn't they test this!?). Guests won't use the pools, even if the prices are set to 0 and everything that's required is built. The campaign is either poorly explained or buggy. Several times I did exactly what's requested in the mission, but I didn't pass it. For example it said "build a guest facility". I built every single one of them and couldn't progress the level.The turntables are interesting, but only boring rides support them, which means they'll sell DLCs with more interesting coasters supporting these in the future.There is only two main themes: Mythic Greek and Viking. The original game had far more and iconic themes, such as the Western, Pirate and Fantasy theme. In this game you are far more restricted, when it comes to what you can build.The game has been created to reach a broader audience, through console and gameplay. The challenge in this game is to build 2-3 rides at the beginning, then let it run in fast mode for a few minutes and you have enough money to finish every campaign level (note that a bug causes guests not to use flat rides, so you are better off by just building 1-2 coasters with a loan).It is way too frustrating to finish the campaign, when the only sense of challenge the game has is its bugs and issues.They learned nothing from the mistakes Skylines 2 made, it's pathetic at this point.

Until I opened it and my heart sank. There is so many teething problems that need sorted and I’m sure frontier will get around to it. But for now. _childDocuments_.review: Planet Coaster 2 is the best successor we could get to Planet Coaster 1 and RCT.The game is gorgeous, well crafted, with a lot of personality, vibrant style, amazing guest animations, lovely music, and lots of fun and dynamic energy.Some people complain about the lack of that specific feature they want, like load/unload stations, special track pieces, more themes.. Don't get fooled by them. This game is outstanding and has many amazing things to offer. If you like the idea, or the genre, you'll be amazed by it and enjoy for sure.Are there some minor problems the day after release? Sure. Like any other game. Will they be solved? For sure.Will the game continue expanding and bringing mostly everything people demand? I'm pretty positive. Frontier has already stated new stations are coming.This is a great game, that, as any other in this genre, needs time to get hold of. But once you do, you'll be in for a great ride!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this so badly. Everything takes twice as long to do with so many clicks to get anywhere in the menu.
