_childDocuments_.name: Planet Coaster 2

_childDocuments_.review: Only four problems I have encountered thus far.1. Lag is here and there, causing some inconsistencies when making rides and paths.2. The builder for the pathways are touchy; you have to literally touch the other pathway to connect, and they tend to co in all kinds of wacky directions3. maintaining the power utilities is a bit of a challenge, as the option to manually connect generators, distributors and the like are not as straightforward as I was hoping.4. The only current themes I have available are Viking, PlanCo, Aquatic and Mythological Greek. I'm hoping more historical theming elements will be included soon, as I'm looking forward to making a Roman Empire themed park soon.But as far as these issues go, they aren't really that game-breaking or detrimental. There are a lot of creations curently available to make your park something absolutely astonishing. So if anything, these issues I have are ones that can be swiftly and decisively fixed by the developers.Getting past these issues, the game is far easier to handle, and I was able to make my gate, facilities and rides far faster than i was in the predecessor. My "Northern Wonderland" park is doing incredibly well, especially with all of the new features and mechanics introduced.I definitely recommend this game for anyone that wants to put their ideas to the test, and while there isn't very much content right now, that is set to change very soon.8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a cash grab, I really was looking forward to the new things in the game, but especially the switch tracks, drop tracks, elevators, etc. are only for a couple coaster/water ride. I'm very disappointed in Frontier and unless they do a lot of FREE updates, this game is not worth your money.For realism I would've also liked some more changes for lifeguards and pools. the pools are the main one, in most waterpark there are exit only catch pools for slides, this game has no option for that. Along with this, adding shows or theaters would be nice, but that would be a hard one.I also need to add that it feels as if the developers said screw PC players, bc everything is optimized for console and are leaving out thing that would work amazingly in pc1 for PC players (custom sound and images). _childDocuments_.review: New lightning and slightly updated graphics help create an immersive game. It looks good! _childDocuments_.review: This game has good bones but needs an incredible amount of polish. Unlike Cities Skylines 2 which is broken at its core, Frontier could eventually make an enjoyable sequel with some time and attention.To start with, there's just way too many stupid bugs in the every-second-of-every-game stuff:- The "improved pathing" results in swarms of guests that get stuck on each other and raises things like hunger, thirst, and litter because these people can't get detached.- The food restriction stuff is incredibly overdone - people won't eat at a shop unless every single person in their group can eat there. Some people literally can't eat anywhere because of the randomness.- I get a ton of "the queue for Ride X is too long" and I look and the queue is 2 minutes.- The game has almost no "ready made" scenery. Some of the themes don't have any ride skins or building skins. An incredible shortage of animatronics.- 90% of my time is spent managing when employees take breaks, or relocating them to where they should be because they don't ever really respond to stuff. They seem to just wander until they chance upon something they feel like doing. They often stand and just stare at garbage or broken rides.- This is the inverse of guests, who literally only walk to their next destination. There's no wandering at all. Build a cool section of the park with neat scenery? Better have a ride or shop in there, because no one's going there. Huge path promenade type areas? All your guests will just bee-line directly to the entrance and exits.Finally, the workshop. The workshop is the most broken part of the experience. To get any variety of anything in the game you'll either have to make it yourself or get it from the workshop because there's a huge lack of built-in assets. Only problem is the filters don't work. As soon as you find an item you like, your filters are wiped clean. Anyone can apply any filter to any item so even using the filters is a waste of time. The #3 item in the workshop is a parking lot tagged with 5 themes, of which only 1 applies at all. The #4 item is a Viking tavern with every theme tagged. There's zero moderation, and because you can only see 8 items at a time, you won't want to browse past the first 2 or 3 pages.This review took me more time to write than anyone at Frontier spent on playtesting.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I've mainly been building a water park, but overall the game seems to be an improvement over the first. There are a lot of nitpicks but the majority of them seem to be issues that can be easily fixed through updates. This happened with Planet Coaster 1, the game did not release perfectly but this is a game that Frontier actively updates with DLC and large free updates.The main improvements in this game will probably make it difficult to go back to Planet Coaster 1 and definitely outweigh the things that need to be fixed in this sequel.- The pathing is just so nice, it makes the game instantly feel way better. If there is any one thing that makes this game better, it's this- The addition of pools, even with the lack of good physics and some other nitpicks, is just super fun. They have also already announced they will be adding proper slide physics, so this is being worked on.- Scenery brush. It just saves a ton of time, probably many hours by the end of a park buildThere's some jank and nitpicks, so I will only mention the more noticeable stuff I've experienced so far. I don't think any of these are big issues, and they all seem fixable. They have also already announced, just today, that a lot of these issues are directly being worked on and fixed- The pathing sometimes creates weird spikes, but these are easy to fix if it happens. There's a lack of customization for the actual path deletion. The stamp tool doesn't have many sizes- The peeps in the park sometimes group up and move in weird ways, but it only seems like this when there is reason for a crowd (something closes, something new opens, so on). They seem to spread out after a while but it happens occasionally- The peeps in the pools also seem to weirdly group up around lifeguard chairs, it just seems oddly crowded in big clusters while other areas have no one- The UI is a bit of a mess, it's not that annoying to work with but it is definitely more messy than Planet Coaster 1- 6k park guest limit for PC doesn't make sense, but they announced today they will remove this limit for PCAs for performance I haven't noticed any issues but this PC is also above recommended specs. Seems to run fine so far with a water park at around 2k guestsOverall very fun so far, just a bunch of different small bugs and weird decisions, but again, they all seem fixable and Frontier is a company that does continuously update their games over time
_childDocuments_.name: Planet Coaster 2

_childDocuments_.review: Frontier were always going to prioritize content creation, but they've deprioritized management to the point it feels like a powerful creative game engine, with little meaningful gameplay.Management is lacking and buggy, it's difficult to tell what's your fault or the game. Don't be too concerned with mismanagement holding you back, there's so little optimization needed you can mostly ignore everything and be profitable. Your rides will constantly break down because mechanics don't work, there will be dozens of extra staff doing nothing because they are auto hired but not auto fired. Ride staff glitch off the map and then take an age to walk back in mid-air. Vendor staff stand outside closed shops "looking for work". After a while it just feels like such a mess it's not worth the effort.On the content side, some genuinely great improvements (swimmable water, track building, ride decoration, pathing, object-scaling, scenery brushes, lighting) are overshadowed by needing to constantly battle a cumbersome UI.The choice to go with a single PC/console ecosystem needs addressing. People are well attuned to when something "feels off" when interacting with the UI and here that's most of the game. I've put in enough hours that it should feel intuitive but it never does, and actively prevents me wanting to play.You can put enough hours into content creation to make the purchase worthwhile, but as a game it's lackluster and frustrating to interact with.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to the follow-up to Planet Coaster after I've enjoyed it but especially Planet Zoo a lot. Both of these games had fundamental flaws, like the really fiddly and hard to control path building system. When seeing in advance, that issues like this were finally addressed in this installment, I was very happy. (Spoiler warning: The path system is very promising with many improvements, yet still so many (old and new) issues which still makes it a rather tedious job to build paths in all but completely flat environments)Once I started playing the game the day of its launch, one of the first things that I noticed was the terrible UI. It looks clean on first glance, but using it is a nightmare. Everything requires about 3 clicks too much, navigating menus is tedious. Oh and menu translations are worse than 2010s Google Translate, tooltips and sliders often have text overflowing to the sides. Speaking of tooltips: They aren't even shown when another item is selected. The menu also doesn't even highlight what item is currently selected. Most of the UI is even hidden when another window (like an item's properties) is on screen. The multi-selection is unbelievably tedious to use (Who even made all of those decisions around this?!) and not even consistent across modes.And for some absolutely unexplicable reason, there is no option to turn on edge scrolling for moving on the map using the mouse. The only way is using the keyboard or right-click-dragging the map, which is just awful to use. The decision not to include this extremely basic feature is absolutly mind-boggling to me.After many hours of playing, I've encountered so many crashes from literally just placing an item in the world. I had to set auto-saving to the smallest setting of one minute in order not to waste too much time rebuilding what had already been done before the crash.All in all, this game feels like it's in a late alpha, maybe early beta stage. It is nowhere near ready to launch and I sincerely hope there will be extensive work on Frontier's side to fix those issues in a timely manner. This game has great potential, but all of it is overshadowed by terrible user experience, unreliable stability, missing balancing in so many aspects and useless "features" like the electricity grid, just to mention one. At least it can be easily disabled.One could imagine that the customer can expect to get a finished product when buying a fully released game at full price, but this is sadly no longer how it works these days. Last year's release of Cities: II was another such game with great potential and promise that was released prematurely in what was at best an alpha build. One year and a lot of negative reactions later, devs are still struggling to get it to anything near what had been promised, while players, rightfully annoyed and disappointed, have long since moved on, making a promising sequel to a beloved predecessor basically irrelevant. Overall, I have more hope in this game than in Cities: II after its terrible launch, but a lot needs to happen soon, otherwise I fear that this game might join the likes of Cities: II.So please, Frontier, fix this game before it is too late!As for my part, I'll continue playing for now and hope that improvements are coming. At the same time, I'm glad I only bought the base game and not the Deluxe Edition, an additional 15 € for not much more content. As it currently is, the value for money of this game at the time of release is... a bit of a stretch - sadly.

_childDocuments_.review: At present I wouldn't recommend this game if you already own Planet Coaster. Yes, this game looks good, runs well. But there are some critical issues that just make it frustrating at the moment. Namely the UI and the maintenance + staff management system.The UI is okay, but some menus are only available as a fullscreen menus - and they reset every time you exit them and come back in. Example: To schedule staff tasks, you have to locate them and pick a time slot in a list of all park staff. You can filter to roles and zones, but every time you assign a task the menu resets to all park staff. Needless tedium.Maintenance  is a whole other can of worms. At present, my generators are going from 100% condition to critical condition in a few hours. I have a mechanic assigned to perform maintenance on each generator two times per day. Yet they cannot survive this maintenance interval. Rides aren't as bad but also cannot survive a full day. I am all for ride maintenance being a part of the gameplay loop, but right now everything breaks so fast that it is nonstop maintenance alerts. I'm convinced this is a bug but who knows.Don't buy it yet - if you are getting the PlanCo itch seeing videos pop up and whatnot - just play PlanCo 1 for now. Wait this one out. some of the systems just aren't fully baked yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I had to rewrite my review after getting some more time into this game. I have changed it to not recommended. Unfortunately, a select few bugs are making the game unplayable for me in a way that is extremely frustrating, since none of these issues were present in Planet Coaster 1. The main game-breaking bug is that guests and queues don't work at all right now. Queue lines are completely broken for all ride types, especially pools/flumes. I'm not sure how this made it past testing to be honest, as it was immediately apparent to me (I have 1000+ hours in Plan Co 1 not all on this account) that queue lines and pricing of rides were broken.The new pathing tool is somehow better and worse than other Planet games at the same time. The *concept* is great, but I find myself fighting the free draw tool more than I find it being helpful. I end up reverting back to the classic path tool frequently because trying to get the draw tool to work is difficult. Why not just let me literally draw? I could hold down the click and just physically draw the path I want -OR- loosen up on the auto-snap in the draw tool because it is not helpful in its current state. Also, how am I supposed to tell what height the paths are at? It makes it almost impossible to create good stairways or ramps.The silver-lining with all of this is that the coaster builder is great and has much better smoothness than the first game, so that is promising. I also enjoy the plazas as a concept but they are only semi-functional right now. Barriers don't do anything and the guest logic makes traffic-jams too common.The new UIs have become more frustrating over time, as I find myself spamming the escape key to get out of the web of 8 menus I had to open to accomplish a simple task. This seems like it was not tested on PC, or internal testing didn't notice it because they got used to it over time. I could overlook the UI issues if that were the only issue though, and it is a relatively minor problem.I wish Frontier would have done a beta test with some of the more popular creators, because I would think these issues would all be obvious to someone who played Planet Coaster 1 or Planet Zoo.Overall, I would wait for a patch or too before buying this game. Frontier is known for being receptive to community feedback but I wouldn't rely on that. Luckily, everything I've brought up is already acknowledged on Frontier's issue tracker.

_childDocuments_.review: It's tough to see such a great IP with mixed reviews within the first week of release. I believe this is game deserves better, HERE'S WHY:The game runs great. It auto-adjusts quality according to your system strength (like most modern games). People who complain of poor performance are using bad hardware. I have tested this game on a PC under requirements, at requirements, and above requirements. Runs great. No glitches.PC1 was already a visually stunning game when it came out, but PC2 is even better. Cinematic/first person mode really showcases the raytracing upgrade this game got. I was very surprised to find that PC2 is still on the Cobra Engine, when it looks like UE5.I've seen A LOT of complaints about the UI, and that it's console-focused. I'd agree it's console focused. I think whenever you make a change to the UI to any game, people will complain simply because it's a change. While I do prefer M&K, controller doesn't feel bad. Like anything, you just got to get used to it. They removed A LOT - I mean A LOT. Security is gone, hotels are gone, and restaurants are gone.. And honestly, not mad at those changes. Security sucked regardless if you had cameras and guard everywhere. Monorails made travel more difficult for little payout. Hotels and restaurants were pointless.They added waterparks, which was a great update. They added scenery brushes so it takes a fraction of the time to decorate your areas. They added water/electricity, which is a great addition but so far poorly executed. It's surprisingly confusing, considering that PC1 did a great job at making things simple.Yes, there are bugs. The biggest bug I've encountered is a 0% scenery rating for custom built flat tracks. It is pretty annoying, but I'm sure they'll fix it soon. Also, I feel like the guests get stuck/bunch up more in PC2 compared to PC1? Regardless, Frontier is an excellent studio and I'm sure patches will roll along quickly.Overall, the bones are there. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic update to the original game. It's quick snappy stable performance even on my laptop is the first thing that stands out. The original game seems like a horse and buggy in comparison. Next is the lighting...it is incredible. We can finally make completely dark rides and tunnels without resorting to tricks like the original game. Just completely enclose a building. Partially enclosed will look shady and half dark and half light like the real world. The transitions in and out of tunnels is just perfect. The resolutions of textures and characters has been improved as well from the original game. So much nicer. The next improvement is sound, something often overlooked in games but wow, it is just SO much better and more true to real life coasters and flat rides. Also the menu has little drops of sound here and there matched to the the item that you are selecting. Really impressed that they did something like that and it just makes the game that much more charming. Pathing, the absolute bane of the original game's existence has been MASSIVELY improved. That's not to say it's perfect, and there WILL be times when you have to play around with it but nothing like what you had to do in the first game. Also your paths will now get saved with your ride blueprints unlike the first game which is super awesome. Another awesome thing is that you can add scenery to rides and coasters and make them look how you want. There are also animatronic rods that you can attach stuff to..basically almost anything can now be brought to life and move bu attaching stuff to them. The new Viking theme is absolutely beautiful as are the maps themselves. The coaster builder is much the same, but the coasters themselves are smooth and not all janky like the first game. No 4 meter method needed here! There's a button right on the builder to smooth them!The negatives would be that there are some rides and features currently missing that the original game had like fireworks and some flats and coasters, but that is MORE than offset by all the new things in this game that were not in the old one. New flat rides, Switch Tracks, Drop Tracks, Haunted Mansion omnimover ride with continuous loading, Tilt Rack coaster, soon separate load and unload stations will be included. Frontier is VERY good about fixing and adding things, and adding what people want, so I am not worried that some things are missing now. I do find the laying of electrical lines to be a little pointless in this game, though it does add a wee bit more realism aesthetically that encourages you to want to make backstage areas. But it seems half baked. Employee staffing and scheduling is another feature that seems half baked as well. But perhaps they have more plans for this in the future. I'd also like some of the missing themes from the old game like Western and Spooky, but here again, I strongly suspect those are on the roadmap for the future. The future looks VERY bright for this game. Even in this somewhat unfinished state, it gets a 9 out of 10 from me.

_childDocuments_.review: PLEASE READ BEFORE  COMMENTING OR HATING When I got this game day one, I played 15 hours straight, and I had a lot of fun and finally got to have a better experience than the first game. But those last 5 hours ruined it for me, I started realizing when going Career mode staff even in other mode staff wasn't doing anything but walk back and forth saying LOOKING FOR WORK. I gave them high pay, work  rotation, and a break room with staff area all together. But they would just leave their post, leaving my ride broken or not run and leave my floors looking worse than thrillville trash picking up mini game, It's so bad that my park is destroying itself.I even made a test with four lifeguards to find out they will mostly leave you gusts to drown rather than helping them, I even have one Mechanic to do one generation and never fix half the time and a dozen janitor walk past soooo much trash to maybe clean one thing at best. I pretty much left here waiting for frontier to acknowledge the bug on frontier tracker so I can play again in which sucks. Are there other problems with the game? _childDocuments_.review: ---Good At First Glance...--- --First Impressions..At this point I have only played around with it for about 60 minuets trying out the new tools yes they are an improvement but they could do with a little more tweaking.  Yes I should have done a Scenario or a tutorial first but I wanted to test out the new tools.--Tools.I like the path tool it is a much need improvement it seems hard when drawing a path to make them re align to a snapping point. the scale tool is amazing but you can only go so far and maybe I was doing something wrong but with a group of objects when it scales up or down they scale individually and are moved in relation to the other objects. The  Terrain tool seems good so far but I don't think it is a better improvement over Planet Zoo as I could seem to get a hard edge lowered or raised I may need to keep using the tool it seems like it has a lot more features then Planet Zoo but I look at it and I think me to much effort there is still no asphalt or concrete terrain paint that is much needed for individuals who like to add car parks and roads to their Parks/Zoos.--Menu...I have found that the seems why to over complicated and there seems to be just to much going on with it, and when going to the scenery tab it is by default blueprints that is very annoying that you have to go to another tab called create custom I do like the workshop tab. The  staff tab is very good and very in depth but at times I think it is too in depth and seems daunting to use at times. the power and water aspect are very cool with power lines and pipes but it is again maybe to much it would be nice to have power generators hidden away with power lines going to the rides but you have to set up a substation in a small radius around your rides. and I still had to do this even when in sandbox with no power.--Graphics...The game for some reason when I first started the menu was fine but when loading a park everything was so blurry I had to spend about 10 minutes fiddling around in the settings before it was a somewhat of a improvement there are some parts that are still blurry. I need to investigate this further to see if anyone else has had this issue and what the fix is I was a little let down by this as the game determined that the correct setting should be Ultra so I was expecting that it would be fine and I wouldn't have to mess around to much with the settings.--Profile...this is not a big issue but for someone who likes to edit their in game avatar it was a little disappointing that this feature for some reason was not working and would just say disconnected I tried to find in the vastly overwhelming Settings menu if there was some profile login page but I would not find it.--Overall Conclusion...I will give this game another go after the first major patch but I do not see myself at this stage coming back to playing this game until there is a major improvement in the game or a dulled down version sadly I do not see myself putting to many more hours into this game unlike with Planet Zoo. With that aside it doesn't seem the right fit for me I really liked Planet Coaster and Planet Zoo but this one seems like something different much like when RollerCoaster Tycoon 3 came out it didn't feel like RollerCoaster Tycoon 1 or 2 but this doesn't mean its not someones cup of tea other people may enjoy these things so I do recommend people to try this game.--Pros & Cons So Far...Pros-Improved Pathing Tool-Scaling Tool-Improved Graphics And Look-Water ParksCons-Confusing Menus-Convoluted UI -Blurry Graphics-Over Complicated Settings Menu-Camera Movement Feels Off-Draw Path Doesn't Seem As Good As It Was Made Out To BeI will revise this review in the future if I can.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent follow up to Planet Coaster. Brilliant additions such as special track elements, and of course water parks. The new pathing tool is great too, but at first, being used to the original PC pathing system, changing the heights of queue lines was a bit fiddly, but easily got around once figured out.The coasters are now so smooth in comparison to the original game, and there are loads of options to suit everyone. The scenery brush is also great.However, this is clearly not made for PC gamers. The UI compared to the first game is horrendous, and clearly designed for console users. I really hope Frontier fix this, and have every faith they will listen to the issues about this. Even when I went in to change the key binding to add a track piece on coasters, some of the keys can't even be changed. This really needs fixing.In addition, there are way less themes, and the sandbox parks are extremely small compared to the original game. The download limit from the Workshop is also frustrating.I have given this an overall recommended review as there are some great features, and with the above fixes, the game will be great. Please Frontier make the PC version work for PC gamers, and not be what looks like a console port! In it's present state, I would say I'm in the middle of recommending and not though (sadly Steam doesn't have an option for that).

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give this sequel, as of release, a B+. If you've played PC1 religiously like I have, it's not the most seamless transition from the first game to the second. Lots of new features that I truly appreciate are here, like expanded pathing system and scenery brush tools, the lighting improvements, and customizing coaster cars. On the other hand, some new UI/UX choices for this game aren't as polished, so in some aspects I felt like I had to start learning and getting used to a slightly different game. There are a ton of great scenic additions to this game, but I couldn't help but hit creative blocks early on due to the scaled-back amount of props and decor to play with. It's hard to contend with, being a faithful PC1 player with access to 8 years worth of added content and DLC's to have a truly full sandbox. I have faith Frontier will bring back the classic themes to this game, like sci-fi, western, spooky, etc., and that they have some great DLC's planned... _childDocuments_.review: I want to like this, but there's a ton of QoL issues in the way of making this a great game. I'm in the middle of a Factorio run and I played Satisfactory before, so I expect a decent amount of QoL from my top down management games and this ain't it. Here's a few of my biggest pain points:- No seemingly fast way to copy and paste items. I'm constantly going through menus that, for some reason, have to load. I suspect they decided to make this always online, so it has to load the available assets each time you open the menu.- After placing a building you have to typically open it for business. This is so tedious because you're going through a couple menus to hit open. I don't know why.- Staff randomly just runs off. I can open a new stand, have a new staff member hired to fill the position and he immediately walks away. - There's *so many* steps in the way of having fun and just managing the park. I can disable a lot of this in settings but I feel like if the devs put something in the game, I want to try out the systems to see if they add depth to the game. Again, coming from Factorio, the electrical system and plumbing is just bizarre. I started designing my park and by the time I placed a pool and some decorations/facilities, my first generator was almost broken. Why is a practically new unit breaking down in 15 minutes without maintenance? Seems like an after thought.- The rate at which people come to your park is overwhelming. Within 20-30 minutes you've got over 1,000 visitors. You might only have 2-3 rides/pools and you have 1,000 people. No ramp up, no time to gradually prepare the park for so many people.- There's a few tools for placing paths which makes it extremely customizable, however it also makes it hell for you to bring your vision to life in many cases. Need exact measurements, exact placing and exact distances? I wish you the best. The pathing tool by default is dreadful for aligning tiles, making symmetrical paths and bringing paths together. Awful.- The search function within categories repeatedly doesn't turn up anything, so I'm hunting through menus to find certain items. I actually ended up quitting tonight because I couldn't find a trash bin anywhere. You can add it as part of a path when placing it, however after the fact it seems impossible to place trash cans. I did the tutorial and I still didn't find it within the menu I was told it would be in. This goes back to my previous complaint--this game is a menu nightmare.I hope the devs take some of the feedback to heart and work on the game a bit more. I think it can be great, but the main gripes around the UI/UX are just not keeping me engaged. I can't refund, although I can't say at the moment I'll play much more of this when I have other more fluid games to get through.

Also concave sections of the pool can result in glitched railings around the edge.My main issue is with the flumes. I was so excited to get this game. Since RCT3: Soaked! I've been dying for another waterpark game, and was feeling this was it. This game really doesn't live up to even my lowest expectations. The flume physics are WORSE than RCT3 - the expansion of which came out in 2006. Just completely unrealistic, especially the bowls, and it completely ruins any sort of immersion or desire to create a realistic park. The flumes themselves are also unrealistic. Waaaay too many bolting points, plus the inner tube flumes having flat bottoms which the riders seem to "stick" to? No thanks.Other than that, the new UI is nice in some areas but feels unpolished in others (settings mainly). _childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I find myself becoming frustrated with Planet Coaster 2 more often than not.Peeps wander aimlessly and don't ride rides, they'll jam up paths running into each other back and forth, they'll complain a ride is too expensive even when the price is rock bottom (and forget about using the new price setting, it's straight-up broken,) they simply won't queue on rides even when the line is super short (tho still complain it's too long,) they'll bug out in queue or getting off a ride causing everyone to become stuck (riders and peeps in line alike.)Mechanics wander aimlessly and don't fix rides unless they're broken (sometimes not fixing them at all,) you'll hire a half-dozen mechanics for your small park but still get constant messages about "service badges" expiring because they just don't fix things, you'll try and place them next to things that are broken down but they'll just walk away.Speaking of staffing, the staff management is awful. The schedule system is awful. Ride attendants will just walk away from a ride because they're on break, leaving guests standing there and the ride non-functioning. Maybe another staff member will show up, maybe they won't (even if you've hired extra.)Building a fun park becomes bogged down by weird guest and staff behaviour and  pop ups that something is going wrong. You'll be micro-managing / fighting your way through poor UI/UX and bugs when you should be having a good time strategizing and designing your park.Will Frontier fix this mess? _childDocuments_.review: So far I have only messed about with building coasters and a little bit of scenery, but so far the game is incredible! The people complaining about minor issues with the game are overlooking the plethora of new content in PC2 that wasn't in the original PlanCo, for example:- Waterparks, which I won't use much because I'm more of a theme park guy, but I appreciate them being there- Attachable scenery, which is a game changer. There are a few trains that are a little too themed at the moment, but frontier have promised to rectify this in the future.- Pathing - While it can be finicky at times, PlanCo 2's pathing is miles better than PlanCo 1's. And if you disagree, then you can still use 'classic' paths,; they're still in the game too!- Graphics, which are beautiful. Ray tracing, lighting, details, it's amazing. Although I think I'd prefer it if the saturation was a little lower like the original game.- New coaster types - Drop tracks, switch tracks, turntables, the list goes on. There are still some coaster types left to be added (Intamin Blitz, I'm looking at you...) but these will surely be added in either updates or DLC.- Management features - While I'm not much of a management guy, I can appreciate the effort put in to expanding what you can do with management that you couldn't before.- Scenery - The current themes are versatile and can be altered to fit whatever theme you want, especially with most items being recolourable AND scalable. Also, making your own animatronics is really cool, and I cant wait to use this for dark rides.- Coaster smoothing - coasters are now so much easier to smooth.- Scenery brush, an absolute life-saver. I can't believe how much easier foliage will be to make!- There's probably more that I can't remember as well!However, there are some negatives that need to be addressed, like:- The UI. While I haven't had much problems so far, judging by what others have said, when I start building a detailed park it might start to annoy me.- Guest AI - I haven't heard many people talk about this yet but the guest AI is... weird at times. They stand doing nothing for long periods of time and as of 8/11/24, don't seem to use food and drink stalls at all. These are probably just bugs that can be ironed out in the following weeks though.- No glass. Pretty self-explanatory- And then there are the things Frontier has promised to change in the future: guest limit, themed trains, video billboards, and most importantly, the slide physics!Overall, the positives of Planet Coaster 2 vastly outweigh the negatives. This game is an absolute blast and I cannot wait to get stuck in with more intricate builds! I highly recommend it for theme park nerds like me!

_childDocuments_.review: After several hours with Planet Coaster 2, it’s hard not to feel like this sequel took inspiration from Cities: Skylines 2 by stripping down the original game’s strengths, resulting in a sequel that’s ultimately a downgrade for PC players. Despite some new features and improvements, Planet Coaster 2 struggles with a range of frustrating limitations and design choices that have taken the fun out of the experience for seasoned players.The most immediate disappointment is the interface. Clearly designed with consoles in mind, the UI has become a cluttered, menu-heavy obstacle course, sacrificing PC-friendly intuitiveness. Menus that once felt smooth now require several clicks to get to basic toolsOne of the most glaring issues is the hard guest cap of 6,000. For a game all about building sprawling, bustling parks, this cap is stifling. Paired with the inexplicable removal of hotels and security guards, the park management experience feels stripped-down and hollow compared to the original. These “small” omissions add up to a park environment that feels a lot less lively and complex, impacting both immersion and long-term playability.The coaster-building system does introduce some additional options, but the process feels far more cumbersome and clunky than before. What should be an improved feature ends up being a tedious exercise in frustration, slowing down what should be one of the game’s most exciting aspects. The same goes for ride station construction, which feels unpolished and awkward to navigate. Even the little things add to the disappointment: the removal of fireworks may seem minor, but it’s a feature I genuinely miss for park atmosphere and special events.Adding to the list of letdowns is the lack of Steam Workshop support. Frontier has opted for an in-game asset sharing platform to cater to consoles, but PC players are left with fewer options for sharing and finding custom content. The themes provided feel uninspired, and the removal of user-generated media really limits creativity.Not everything about Planet Coaster 2 is a step back, though. The addition of water parks is a standout feature, and it’s implemented beautifully. The graphical upgrade also brings an impressive level of detail to the parks, and the new scaling tool is a lifesaver for detailed customisation. However, these positives are too often overshadowed by frustrating design choices that feel aimed at consoles rather than PC.In the end, Planet Coaster 2 feels like a missed opportunity to build on the original game’s strengths. For PC players hoping for an upgraded experience, it’s difficult not to see this as a sequel that compromised on what made the first game great. Instead of being an exhilarating next chapter, Planet Coaster 2 feels like a stunted, watered-down version of what it could have been.I really want to be able to change this review to a positive recommendation, but until these issues are addressed - I'd wait before pulling the trigger on this one.EDIT - Some of these have been addressed ad future hotfixes, I will re-review when all of these eventually go live.

_childDocuments_.review: I read the negative reviews and bought the game anyway. Glad I did because the 'issues' are blown out of proportion. Other Negative Reviews:6,000 Guest limit. True. I looked back at my PC1 parks and barely had 4k on some of my biggest ones so not an issue for me AND they've said they will make it bigger later but wanted it 6k for launch to ensure consoles can play the game. UI is weird. Maybe... I don't have any issues with it. It looks JUST LIKE PC1.No Night. False. The days are MUCH longer in general so you can't sprint through a couple days in a few minutes. Each day, even at times 3 speed, takes a long time to get through so the days AND nights are much longer.No security. True. Couldn't find any cameras or security staff to put in the game. Not game breaking to not have security yet....My Issues:The main issues that I've seen in my time is NPC pathing and textures. My mechanics glitch/freeze and can't find the path to fix rides even though they're standing on it. Crowds bunch up and stay in packs of seemingly a hundred / hundreds while only a few are able to separate from the herd.Textures go in and out when close to the map and at an angle. Can see through the grass to the void down below. What I like:I'm not an expert at PC1 so some of these might be in the game but it feels like there's so much more that can be done to customize in PC2. I've been layering paths on other paths to give certain aesthetics. Can group things together and delete all at once even though negative comments say this is harder to do...Literally group and press delete.Can just double click on things to select them and then build again. IE double click on laid path and can now lay more of THAT path. Can copy and paste sections of path to fix areas that may have gotten screwed up when dropping a ride. Deleted a ride and it ate a chunk out of my path. Used the selection tool to copy a finished section and just pasted it in to the piece that was missing. Can make custom pool shapes and then add them to existing pools by duplicating the shape. I made a big pool with an island in the middle and then a smaller pool on that island lol Maybe I'm just a nerd but I think that's rad. It's tough to put more into words where, it's PC1 but better. Is it complete? No. Is it playable? Yes. Is it ENJOYABLE? Yes.I'm hyped playing it right now so I guess it just is what it is for the negative reviewers. As a lot of youtubers have said, if you like PC1, you'll like PC2.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game has some great potential.. it was really released in a bad state that should have been more thorough played and tested. Almost about every feature, new or in the previous planet coaster has some kind of bug or issue with it. I have over 2000 hours in the first game and looking forward to this game, this is incredibly disappointing. This game is littered with bugs and limitations for PC users whilst the game was clearly designed towards a Console platform that does not mix in translation, making the game feel very clunky and empty.On the management side, current caps and guest AI severely hinder this game. Ride wait times are very messed up, guests will consider a 2 minute wait for a ride too long whilst water park slides also have an issue with calculating their wait times, leaving most guests just walking around on paths, combined with the current guest limit makes it very hard to earn money in a larger scale park. The UI is very clunky, for example, all staff options for some reason are under two different spots, some options may be found under the staff tab at the bottom of the screen whilst the rest you must click Park Management in the top left and then select staff. Things like this add unnecessary complexity to the game.The coaster builder lacks shortcut keys and the it takes multiple clicks to do switch tabs to get to options that would've taken a single click in Planet Coaster 1, including a massive difference in having a Construction Mode and Edit Mode, still I do not understand the difference between these two and it is unnecessary while in PC1 they were all mixed together. The UI is a massive downgrade in both the coaster and ride tabs from Planet Coaster 1.There are many issues in this game with the UI that will cause mass frame drops. Some can be figured out, such as sliding your mouse to hover some items that display a text description will lag the game, others are unexpected. A lot of these are frustrating from the sheer quantity and it feels like they have not been ironed out at all before release.I would love to see this game fixed but honestly I am finding myself more frustrated every time I launch this game. The lack of simplicity and the amount issues that should have been fixed before launch are really hindering this game, especially at the price tag it holds itself to. _childDocuments_.review: The game is... okay. Not bad, not good, just okay. Although I like the game itself, and think it's a leg up from the first game; there are some stuff that left me disappointed and even a little disgusted. I'm remaining fairly neutral in this review, because I think Frontier did great (although others may think otherwise).I'm going to start by listing some of the things that disappointed/disgusted me. Now I am writing this with optimism, because I know many of the things on the list could be fixed later on down the line.- For some reason, the lack of themed items in the game puts a damper on my creative spirit. Sure, the Resort, Mythology, Viking, and Aquatic themes are all fairly interesting, there's not much else in terms of other themes in the game; and that makes me; a complete novice at decorating, more than a little nervous and restricted.- The fact that we have a limit on guests in the park doesn't make sense to me. Sure it may help reduce lag, but so? Why put a limit on something easily managed?- I think the flumes need work, and I know I'm not alone with this one.But enough of the bad stuff, what about the stuff I liked? I'm not being overly enthusiastic about these because I might cause controversy with the list.+ Completely dark interiors have finally made it! Now we don't have to use the time settings to make dark rides.+ The ability to put scenery on rides and even coaster trains opens up a massive can of worms when it comes to creativity, and I like it! That said, I'm still a decoration novice so I'm still waiting for something to scratch that creative itch of mine.+ Separate priority lines are a cool feature.+ The pathing tool got a major rework, and I like it's ease of use now.And now here's a list I'm mixed about. Now, when I say I'm mixed about these, I'm neither positive nor negative about these.> I'm mixed about the Frontier Workshop as a whole. Sure it's cool, but it's a far cry from the Steam Workshop we've come to expect. > The coaster/tracked ride stations still need a bit of an upgrade. We will eventually see Omnimover Stations (for coasters), rotating stations (for water rides) and Dual Stations, right?> I'm a bit bummed out by the lack of custom media at present, but they will add it eventually. I mean, PlanCo 1 didn't have those features when it launched back in 2016, so...I really need to wrap this review up since I only have so long to do this, but tying it all together, Frontier definitely put all of their hard work and dedication into making something fun (yeah, I know it's flawed slightly, but that's what updates and hotfixes are for, right?). I should probably add that I am writing this review because I think there's room for improvement, and just giving my honest and humble opinion (since I was one of the people who preordered the game. $65 well spent). I should also add that I will update my score and review later on down the line because updates are coming around the corner (by the way, Frontier's 30th Anniversary is coming up, so I think there's going to be an update for that like how Frontier gave PlanCo 1 an update for their 25th anniversary. Just saying).Gameplay - 7/10Quality - 10/10Performance - 9/10Fun - 8/10 Overall Score81% (out of 100).

_childDocuments_.review: Right now the game takes much longer to do things vs. the first Planet Coaster; if you are trying to build a theme park with custom buildings and realism, you'll find it takes sometimes 5 times as long to do something like build a simple bathroom. The game and menus are not user friendly on a computer. Some examples: When building pathways or queues, it's extremely hard to edit an existing pathway or queue, the right click is no longer deleting a path for you that you can then quickly right click to re-shape; it is all taking extra steps now, switching multiple menus, and re-building. A simple two-click, two-second process before can take minutes now instead. When using building pieces, it was nice to quickly find the object elsewhere in my park (Say, a wall lamp) and add that to another building. I don't think this is possible any more, you'll need to find every piece in the menu, every time. A 5-second process turns into a minute-long process. Every part of the game stems from these issues.In just 30-minutes of playing you'll find yourself frustrated with how long things take if you are trying for realism.I was hoping this would be a game that was similar to an RCT1 to RCT2-like modification, where everything is familiar and issues that were brought up were fixed (like paths, or the massive ride footprints that don't need to be so big), and then rides were added/evolved, but unfortunately its like an RCT3-like advancement, which may make a lot of people upset if you enjoyed the earlier versions of RCT more.This game is for people who want to quickly plop down some pathways and make some roller coasters. It's not what a sim-game/builder-game player wants in a game. I will continue to use Planet Coaster 1 for now and do not recommend this game, I'm upset I purchased it.

_childDocuments_.review: This took a little while before I was really ready to write a review because I am really torn on this one.  There are a few great new things and several negative things that make me question whether paying full price was worth it.  First like most I did play PC1 for many hours and did thoroughly enjoy it.  At the end the only reason I stopped was maxing my PC out with a massive park with a couple hotels and thousands of guests.  Just felt like I hit the end.  Personally I'm not into it for the creative side so much.  I loathe spending hours designing the perfect building or scenery around each thing you place.  Not my cup of tea.  So with that in mind...The good:Better graphics of course.  Clear as day and on a decent PC with some tweaking it looks great and plays ok.  I'm not here to flex about my rig but can maintain above 100fps in 1440p in most scenarios.  When the weather changes especially with 4000 plus in the park it can dip down to 60ish.  Personally I couldn't care less about fps in these types of games anyway.  Just give me a stable 60.   Even at high numbers the fps dumps from 140+ down to 60 are noticeable.  The game is brighter and more vibrant which is pleasant to watch.Park management for the most part. (Negatives later on this)  Little clunky at first to set up zones and then fill them but it works.  Also being able to look at each individual zone get a rating and use the overlays for info to make adjustments where needed is nice and gives me more to do besides scouring the workshop for scenery skins...Career is actually decent I think.  I haven't completed it yet but on hard you are forced to spend quite a bit of time on each park to get platinum all while learning how each of the tools works now vs then.  Coaster creation is easier at least for me. Again as someone who doesn't really like to spend a ton of time creating fake things in a video game and would rather just focus on management it does seem to be simpler to pick up and work with.  I've made a few so far and getting the track to go where you want it to is pretty intuitive.  Can we just get rid of the stupid smooth button?  I mean do we not just do it with every creation to make sure they aren't puking the second they step off the ride? I mean it works as I've had a coaster go from above 6 on nausea to under 3 just by smoothing but seems tedious. And finally water parks...I guess kindaOk so the negative...Let's start with water parks.  Yes we wanted them and yes they are there but like most complaints the physics leave quite a bit to be desired.  I have found myself enjoying building flumes that intentionally launch the rider right into the flume on another one in the pool....I was hoping for a nope you cant do this or that annoying sound the game makes when you can place something but it just lets you do it.  Or IDK have medic stations and have people go there when they get sick/injured.  I wanted to see some water carnage but guess that would've required a mature rating or something.  Hotels and security....umm who what when where and why did they disappear?  Were those not simple enough to implement in this NEWER version?  Where are all those little vandals tipping over my trash cans that the janitors refuse to empty even while standing right in front of them complaining of nothing to do? Why can I not treat my customers more like prisoners with security cameras every five ft? How am I supposed to keep people in my park for months and bleed them dry of all of their financial wealth for the betterment of Coaster Coast or whatever they are calling the company?  Back to park management...It's there and once you can finally figure out how it works its ok.  On hard you really have to setup multiple zones for your staff, build a couple break rooms in each and make sure they have enough of each type of staff to cover the area.  Make the areas too big and staff will complain that it takes too long to get anywhere/may miss their break.  (Illegal for hourly employees in most places I believe lol)  My gripe is with how tedious it is to get set up.  Just a big ol list with a few filters sure but you have to go through them one by one to set their zones and what not.  Can this not be easier?  Can the staff just automatically join the zone you place them in to begin with and then you decide if you want to move them? Am I missing something in the convoluted staff menu?  And why do you have to go the hire screen to make a zone and not in the park management screen? I'm not hiring a zone I'm managing it...And although many tout about the new path  making tools I beg to differ on that...The park that really annoyed me was the solar energy park with natural paths...what a nightmare to create anything.  That stupid intersecting terrain error became the bane of my existence for 3 hours while I just fought to move on. "It looks like it will connect, its at the right height not too sloped and nothing in the way but.....nah try again. All I think about every time I hear that buzzer sound is the part in dumb and dumber with the most annoying sound in the world. In the end I feel like it is a nice graphics leap forward and attempt at a new mechanic but maybe took it a bit too far when they removed features to make room for the coding of the debacle that is water parks.  If you're new to this game then maybe when it's on sale.  If you're a vet...think long and hard about it lol maybe you'll get lucky unlike me and watching several hours worth of youtube footage would satisfy your curiosity on the water park thing.

_childDocuments_.review: When I originally played this game, it was unplayable from Nov 6th right up until the first hot fix on Nov 21st.  Below, I have crossed off all the bugs I am no longer experiencing, however, there are still a lot of issues to be addressed.- When guests are holding food, the food is invisible in the first person- - Drop down flumes ending in a straight-down drop cause the flow of water to ramp perpendicularly flinging guests forwards 90 degrees instead of down- - Staff get stuck in bathrooms- - The finances are two easy, I made 1 pool and waited 1 in-game day and the $100,000 I started with in franchise mode became $100,000,000. In Planet Zoo, I struggled for money big time and the challenge was rewarding.- The profanity filter won't let me name parks or blueprints things such as "The Logging Grounds" & "The Soaring Groves" because of the middle four letters being a slur. I've seen blueprints like "Pool pass Hut" showing "Pool p*** Hut" because of profanity which is a bit silly. If you add "at night" to a description, it reads "at ***ht".- - The advertising section of the game is redundant because it is too easy to make money- Guests do not use priority queues no matter what- Scenery placement do not remember their colors and scale as you place them unless you duplicate the original item you placed- Why is there no temperature water facility when you have one in Planet Zoo? Would be nice to make a winter-y hot pool. Especially since all the other facilities are a copy and paste from Planet Zoo.Overall, there is a lot of work to be done. I wouldn't quite recommend this game yet to new players, however as a someone that exclusively plays building games, I will keep playing it. I will change my review to recommended once I am not constantly being reminded of the remaining bugs every time I play.

_childDocuments_.review: So a few things to start with I rate the game 7.5/10 a few things could be improved but half the reviews expect the game to be as “full” as planet coaster on release without any dlc.The pros:Performance has been improved a lot I loaded into the old game with a large park and limited to 6k guests. Pathing improvements but still janky if you’re literally .25 meters off they won’t connect using stamp tool. Why? Rides are a lot more smoother.The entire day cycle rather than years is much nicer. More customisation is always great for rides.The cons:Some times the snapping isn’t intuitive and takes a bit of fiddling.As I said the pathing stamp won’t just auto connect if it’s slightly off height.The new priority queue is silly instead of skipping a portion of the line it’s now a separate enterance. The really bad:The game is absolutely easy to make money even on hard in sandbox it’s meant to be a management game why’s hard so easy to make large amounts of money with 2 rides and a 50k start.The money makes no sense. I’d rather have inflated numbers a rollercoaster might cost 2/4 million not 7-14 thousand and when you compare that to the 50k start can easily have multiple to start.The management is still dog poop. Too many menus too much faffing around. Also power you’ve just added an extra step for distributing it but guests no longer have the bad radius for staff buildings so don’t even have to hide them away now.The entire waterpark thing every guest will use no matter the weather and just crowd into a small pool or stand next to it. Guests will complain about a 2 minute queue, guessing it’s irl time but why since you have the ingame days now why not 38 minutes ingame. Like come on I want my queue to be used up not 12 people stood there. And the queue end is just an end no pre built end to the queue any more so unless if you manually add fences it looks stupid. The biggest downside. A PC game that’s built for consoles which is evident. Guest cap the stupid workshop and menus I can’t even use the work shop without loading it going for a poop and coming back it takes that long to load. _childDocuments_.review: Currently I can not recommend this game, when better versions of a park management sim exist. The aspect that PC boast so well is it's customization when it comes to structures and placement and truly allowing your imagination to run free. As many other reviews have noted. this game is severely lacking in the building items department. My full time with the game has been in Sandbox mode fighting with creating buildings, but then needing to patchwork specific items to incorporate into my designs. I had to make my own column because the selection can be counted on one hand and even those are variations of each other. Where's the vast array?Then building feels extremely clumsy as nothing seems to line up perfectly because everything is just so ever askew, so then this line of wall you have is actually drifting just ever so slight to the side and so now a pathway is poking out at one end but not at another. All you did was perfectly place a wall that then turned into "Building Editor" which strips away free movement from you to force you to move on the grid, but wait, are you moving relative to the piece or on the world grid? Well if you need to change it to world, watch out it might make a jump, and then the pieces won't line up anymore. There needs to be a way to put the world grid up permanently, or to show the relative grid of a piece that you are duplicating off of. Let's talk lack of building pieces, or better yet, lack of control, Why do some building types have some variations of walls, while others do not? Some, you can get a half arch, others, you are forced to a full arch wall piece. Why do some pieces have properly inverted wall pieces for roofs while others don't? It wouldn't be a problem if you could rotate on the y axis to turn pieces around, but why aren't these in game. There are no pieces that meet with angled roof pieces so you can't have a clean on the inside. Again, if all pieces had full movement control then this wouldn't be an issue. Lastly, bugs and general gripes. I have encountered a few bugs dealing with building in general. When selecting a piece to copy and advance move, when attempting to change to the other piece modifier options, it just gets stuck on one and it won't translate and longer, or it won't spin unless you free move it or start the process over again. Which brings me to a gripe, with the multi select tool, which will select EVERYTHING period, there needs to be a way that it saves the original multi selected items after you are done with whatever you needed to do with it to begin with. To select a large number of items, which is already a painful process in and of itself, that then encounters this movement bug to exit out of moving just to have to re-select everything is not intuitive nor a good time. I selected this many items, please return me to those items when I am done just in case I need to do something else with it. Another bug that I have encountered is within the UI where some building pieces can have their scale altered, while others can not, if you select, let's say a wall item that can scale, then select another wall that can not scale, the UI will hold onto the scale slider but obviously not do anything. Again, If all items had all range of motion, it could cut down on a lot of item clutter, as well as make building a much better experience. I want to play this game, but I have been waiting for so long to build what I have been attempting to build in other park sims for a while and I have just been fighting with the systems every step of the way. Play the first one, play Parkitect, thus far they are a better bang for your buck in the creativity and freedom department as the amount of assets they have really make for creative unique builds. One last note/suggestion, please update how sandbox is done. Look to Parkitech for how a proper sandbox level designer could/should be done. Allow us to generate our map, allow us to chose the park's initial scale and how it can be bough later on. Please allow the immediate mad outside of the boundaries be editable so that if I raise land next to it, it follows suite. All in all, this is more of the same, and pick it up if you want to, but know that they have quite the few update's to push out that NEED to be free, that isn't entitlement talking either, before this game actually reach true sequel status rather than general DLC update status.Oh, and while they've announced it, real quick edit to this, how do you launch this type of game without proper glass pieces?? It's good the team got push back on this, like... what theme park have they gone to where glass doesn't exist???

_childDocuments_.review: Still an early review, but let me extend it a bit.Game is overall at a good start, if you don't expect all Planet Coaster 1 contents + DLC for just 50 bucks (new game in new Engine version means, they can't even just take them over. But I'm sure most things will come back in updates but also paid DLC).Right now there are many smaller problems and bugs, as to expect from a new game. That said, I agree that this game is maybe published a bit rushed, personal guess, cos the didn't want to move from their usual November release date (all Planet games released on November).- Pathfinding looks pretty flimsy, guests don't queue properly, guests and staff collection in a blob and things alike- Maintenance is not always working, something isn't right there also- Safeguards also fail sometimes.- The UI is unintuitive and overcomplex. And no, I'm not sure it's cos of console players, cos they are whining as much as we do about it.- Some graphic glitches, for example on water rides or some ground textures- I think the ingame notifications are a bit oversensible and also, don't disappear on timeBut there already was one Hotfix, more things are announced, including the removal of workshop download limit on PC (4gb now since last patch for now), raise of Guest limit on PC (6000 right now) and they are looking into waterslide physics. All in all I'm positive Frontier will soon have fixed most of the problems.From a technical view, it runs fine for me, no crash until now and at least in my experiments and smaller parks (up to around 2k guests for now) I hold most of the time over 120fps (RTX 4080) on very high / ultra settings.All in all it's - like said - fun and I think a good base for what will become of it with more contents and DLC.Would I recommend? Honestly, if there was a neutral choice, this review would right now be neutral, but there isn't, so I say, recommend, if you don't have unrealistic expactations, it's a new game in a new engine, neither are there all the contents PC1 has right now, nor is it completely free of bugs and problems right now.Oh, and some are whining, cos there is a day 1 DLC, but honestly, that's the rides from the Deluxe Edition, it was to be expected to be available from day 1. You may not like it, but then you're not liking surly 80% of nowadays A+ titles.

_childDocuments_.review: Crash, Crash, CrashI got the infamous 13th/14th gen Intel crashes but why ONLY on THIS game and no others? And why is it the graphics driver crashing in the logs if it is CPU related?Regarding crashes, I did a fresh install of Windows for this game. Latest Windows11 drivers, updated BIOS, every driver is the latest driver. I CRUSH the recommended PC specs:13700K, 64GB DDR5 RAM, 3080ti, 2TB NVMEMy solution (finally found it) for crashing to desktop was to underclock all cores to no higher than 54 multiplier (5.4 Ghz) and bump up voltage a little. There are good UNDERclocking guides online for unstable 13th gen / 14th gen intel CPUs. ALSO: turn down graphics settings to LOW. It takes BOTH those things to alleviate crashing for me.The game is not ready for release, as others have said. My favorite, most-played game of all time was the original Planet Coaster. This game has LESS than just the vanilla PC1 launch in terms of scenery and games.The game is MOSTLY stable on a laptop I tried on low settings. Ryzen 7000 series and RTX 4060 laptop GPU... So your mileage will vary based on system, but the point is I have 2/3 systems just crashing on this game. Not a good place for a launch.Aside from crashing, gameplay is a mixed bag:First and foremost, PC is supposed to be a rollercoaster / theme park game. It feels like they made "Planet Waterpark". The core themepark game feels "early access" or like a "demo" of the game (in Beta). As of now, there are basically 2 themes: Waterpark and "Viking"... and both themes feel kind of like they are meant to work for a waterpark. User interface is what everyone says it is: "designed for console players" (not PC creators). The clunky cumbersome UI makes playing the game mildly frustrating"...  This is especially true for those of us used to Planet Coaster and Planet Zoo where we actually had a nice experience. The excellent building mechanics of Planet Zoo where you could really build just about any shaped structure are lacking in this title.Here were my expectations:Improved graphics of latest Cobra engine (think Planet Zoo) - CHECK (we got it)Improved performance on large Parks with lots of guests - They limit our guests so I assume NO.Planet Zoo style restaurants where you can see your guests sitting at tables and build realistic restaurants (NOPE. I ASSUME they will give us this as another paid expansion)PC1 level base game assets/theming - NOPE, not even close. It is missing nearly EVERY basic theme. -NO Castles theming-NO Western theming-NO Sci-Fi theming-NO really generic "Vanilla" PC1 windows and doors (seriously?!)... You don't even get basic asphalt or wood tile roofs as a building option.They basically gave us 1 expansion pack theme which is "underwater/little mermaid" and "Viking" - both geared towards a waterpark, and then gave a very barebones and eclectic mesh of some basic brick walls and assets they imported from the "aquatic" expansion in Planet Zoo.What I want:Fix the crashing. Give us back more theming options, like castles, western and fairytale themes, like in PC1 base-game. These are STAPLES of the genre, and you omitted ALL of it. Give us Planet Zoo restaurants as a free update, or at least as part of an expansion that includes the western, castles, and fairytale land stuff you should have included in the base game.This is already feeling like a broken demo where they are going to cash grab 100 expansions instead of giving us something no better than early access.This game under-performs and under-delivers in its current state.CRASH (literally) and burnThis game needs to come a LONG way to be as good as PC1 was. It's currently not worth $50. I just wish they would have sold it honestly (with an early access label on it) and then given us the vanilla PC1 themes as free development updates. The water park thing should have been their first $29.99 expansion for those who wanted it.That being said, I am giving a recommend only because I WANT this to get fixed. Good things:-Pathing is improved (even if it is hard to really master the "imprecision" of paths that you can't just drag and paint on where you want the way they made it look in the demo videos.) That being said, putting paths within paths (different textures) is a massive realism improvement and the custom stamping and drawing tools do allow massive improvements in creating/filling in pathing. You just have to take the time to master the tricks/quirks to make it work for you.-Graphics are a major step forward. Basically planet zoo level.-Roller coasters are much easier to manipulate/smooth/adjust AFTER construction (though they are harder to build through the clunky UI)The core game with Planet Zoo restaurants and BASIC theming that SHOULD have existed at launch would make this a very GOOD game, and a few UI fixes would make it GREAT.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Coaster 2 feels like a thrill ride that was rushed to open before it was ready—and it's taking players on a frustrating loop-de-loop. As fun as it is to build your dream park, the water slides, which should be a major highlight, look surprisingly clunky and poorly animated. It’s like they’re crafted from cardboard, which feels like a big letdown, especially when they’ve been advertised as a big feature.Then there's the performance: the game's system requirements are jaw-droppingly high, making you wonder why a theme park builder needs such hardcore specs to look decent. And speaking of themes, where are they? For a ‘theme park game,’ it’s surprisingly void of actual themes. It feels like someone handed you a cake, but forgot the frosting.Worst of all, the user interface is a huge step back from the original. It's cluttered, confusing, and clearly designed with consoles in mind—meaning PC gamers are left navigating a messy, console-first interface that feels downright hostile at times. It’s baffling why they couldn’t build on the simplicity of the first game’s UI.All in all, Planet Coaster 2 feels like a game pushed out too soon to cash in quickly, leaving players to wonder what pricey DLCs might be lurking around the corner to ‘complete’ the experience. Fun to play? Sometimes. But ready for release? Not so much.

One of the biggest features of PC2 compared to PC1 is that there are water parks. How this got through QA is completely beyond me.100% not ready for release. Do not buy. Wait.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Coaster 2 takes the magic of its predecessor and elevates it to a whole new level, delivering an exceptional theme park management experience that is as captivating as it is creative. Frontier Developments has clearly listened to fan feedback and invested in making this sequel a worthy successor.The visuals in Planet Coaster 2 are great. From hyper-realistic coaster physics to intricate environmental details like weather effects and crowd behavior, the game is a visual delight. Watching the crowds respond dynamically to your park’s attractions adds an immersive layer, making your park feel alive.The sequel introduces a deeper management system, offering more control over park operations, staff, and guest experiences. Customization options have been greatly expanded, enabling players to create highly personalized parks. The game introduces modular building systems and more nuanced terrain editing, giving players unparalleled freedom to shape their creations. The ability to share designs via the community workshop ensures endless replayability and inspiration.Despite its complex systems and stunning visuals, Planet Coaster 2 runs smoothly on modern hardware. It also caters to a wide audience, with tutorials and difficulty options that make it welcoming for newcomers while still providing a challenge for seasoned players.Frontier Developments has outdone themselves, creating a sequel that not only honors the legacy of the original Planet Coaster but sets a new gold standard for theme park simulation games. This is a must-play for anyone who loves creativity, strategy, and the thrill of roller coasters.

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this one with all my heart and soul. I really was. I've poured hundreds of hours into Planet Coaster 1. But now after only playing this game for 8 hours I already feel my motivation waning and my frustrations only growing. I don't know about anyone else, but all I really wanted was a Planet Coaster game with better graphics than PC1. PC1 was amazing. It still is amazing. It has a huge fan base and an enormous community workshop full of the most incredible blueprints. It really is a sandbox game that is made for fans, by fans. The game only provides the elements - the people, the community actually make the content. And that's why it works and is awesome. All my parks in PC1 are made up of 95% workshop blueprints. It's like the makers of this game forgot why we love to design rollercoaster parks in the first place. Hint? Because it's FUN. PC2 is not fun. Planet Coaster 2 has borrowed elements from Planet Zoo, like introducing electricity generators and power units. Guess what? It's boring and it feels like a bloody chore. Why do I care about placing generators all over the place or water filters? I just want to build awesome stuff and see my peeps having the best time. The user interface is incredibly clunky. Did you do any user testing at all? Compared to PC1, the interface is a nightmare. It's over-engineered, complicated and it takes forever to find anything. I've spent so much time already being frustrated and having to look up tutorials on day one because I just can't figure out how to do things. And everything just takes so much longer. In PC1, if you wanted to make a shop, you just selected your shop and placed it near a road. There would be an automatic pathway created and the shop would be automatically open. Aaaand done. Simples. Now in PC2? You have to place it near a road. You have to create the road pathway yourself. Then you have to click on the building. Which will require another click to select the shop itself. And then you have to click to open it. Seriously?! Who does not want their shop to be open by default?! And why make us do all these extra steps? It might sound like a minor thing, but just consider how many shops you have to create in a park. It's just not fun to do all these extra steps. You are literally draining away my motivation to play this game with every extra action that you're forcing me to take. What was wrong with the super easy way things worked in PC1? Did you really not learn anything from what made that game awesome?It really feels like this game just has no soul and is just a weird mash up of Planet Coaster and Planet Zoo. I was looking forward to the water parks which I loved in the Rollercoaster Tycoon games but even that isn't as fun as I was hoping it would be. Plus the graphics themselves? Really not that great. I don't know why, but everything just looks somehow blurrier than in PC1. I feel like my glasses aren't working properly when I play this game. Not to mention the numerous bugs that I have already found in the first three scenarios. I also don't see a way to import any of the amazing blueprints that people have created from PC1, which I think is at the very heart of this franchise. I really hope that there is a way, because if there isn't, you guys are making a terrible mistake. All in all, this feels like a big letdown from a huge PC1 fan. If you need me, I'll be playing the original Planet Coaster and actually having fun with it.
