_childDocuments_.review: Planet Coaster can be used to make a lot of different kinds of parks, and it facilitates many different styles of play,  So I can't say everyone will have the same experience as me, but I'm really enjoying this game.At first I was super annoyed at the pathing tools, and the fact my rides were always breaking down even though i had a ton of idle mechanics.  But once i figured out that I could make hybrid spline+grid based paths that merged cleanly by using a combination of the path stamping tool and splines with the straight and curved  settings I was really happy.  Paths can still be fiddly but I also feel like I have more control over the layout now.  And making switchbacked queue pathing is a dream.It still feels like mechanics do a really bad job of finding work on their own, but I mostly solved that issue by creating work zones, assigning mechanics to a zone and changing their schedule to work that zone all day.  I think a lot of negative feeling on this subject is that the condition system seems to work differently from PC1.  In PC1 breakdowns were a roll of the dice, with higher probabilities if the condition was low.  But in PC2 it appears breadowns only occur once the condition reaches zero and mechanics just need to service the ride before the service timer expires (which seems to be around a 1 or 2 hour game-time interval) to prevent the condition from decreasing.One issue that I still have is that guests tend to walk to rides they want to go on then turn around and leave for seemingly no reason.  After some fiddling I discovered that the ride price was too high (despite setting the price to 'bargain').  Folks were walking up, deciding it was too expensive and leaving.  But there was no feedback, no thought bubble saying 'ride x is too much money' or the like.  So the system may be working as intended, but the feedback to the player could use a pass.  UPDATE:  after spending more time with this I'm not sure the price was the fix.  What I'm seeing now is that people are leaving because they don't want to wait in the line, despite the line having a considerably lower wait time than their tolerance (in some cases the ride has a wait time of zero and they're still leaving).  So yeah this definitely seems broken beyond what I noted in my original review.  Crossing my fingers for a fix in the upcoming patch!I've seen some funny stuff as well.  After several hours of downpour all my guests were heading to the gates.  On a whim I slapped down a Body Dryer and literally every single guest was drawn to that one point in the park in order to get dry.  Was also amusing to see all the trash they dropped in that one corner of the park.On the visuals front this game is GORGEOUS.  The light filtering through the tree branches is really nice, and adding lights to your coasters at night is something to behold.  I'm running in 4k on a 4070Ti with max settings and DLSS balanced.  Not quite hitting solid 60 but likely close.  I'd kill for VR support, even if it was only for walking around the park and riding the rides.Lastly, one other reviewer stated there was no random rotation of objects.  This is not true.  Not only is there random rotation but random scaling (and more!)  the trick is that you just need to make a scenery brush, add some scenery to the brush, enable the random rotation settings and set the min/max scale and now you can paint with trees.  I spent a good 30 minutes dialing in the perfect Black Spruce forest brush and now my viking village is looking fantastic.  Hundreds if not thousands of trees placed with no more than a click and drag.  Honestly, the new scenery brush is fantastic (its the small tree button in the lower right corner if you missed it).Anyway, I'm having a great time with PC2.  Its got a few rough edges right now for sure, but I suspect they'll be knocked off with a few patches and hotfixes.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying my time in this game, I had Planet Coaster on console and enjoyed it but the building, terrain sculpting, roller coaster building and path placing is much better on this game and feels more natural on PC. The workshop has so many amazing blueprints already made by the community so its got a great community aspect to it and its been out for just over a week. The water parks are lots of fun, welcome addition to the game. Guests feel not as stupid as the first game, and have more natural behaviours. The heat map feature in this game is really helpful and in depth so it gives me a nod on what to work on next to improve guest satisfaction, and staff morale as well as scenery improvements, power and water management. This was definitely a yoink from Cities Skylines, but works really well. I found myself spending a lot of time getting the hang of the advanced movement and scaling of building pieces and still not 100% but that will come with time and experience in the game. I understand the mixed reviews as there are a few teething problems, I've noticed mechanic's behaviour where they don't service the rides on time and when you emergency call them they sometimes don't fix what needs fixing.The paths are also a bit janky sometimes, you can work around this with a bit of playing about, but takes a lot of time to sort out. The item you have selected is highlighted blue so seeing the colours as you imagined can be difficult when colouring the selected item. THERE IS NO GLASS!! This is confirmed to be coming in a December update. Overall it's really fun with a learning curve for building your own custom rides and scenery items. It really opens your imagination and is nice to chill out to. The developers are working on fixes ASAP with an update in December addressing some of my concerns. It's nice to have a game developer that actually works on their games once released. I look forward to seeing how this game improves over time. I would recommend in its current state for new players, experienced players of Planet Zoo/Planet Coaster 1 may want to wait for fixes and improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm actually shocked at these reviews. This game is nothing short of outstanding, and I sincerely can't believe how entitled, misinformed and/or ungrateful people are these days.This game is a LOVE LETTER to Theme Parks and Theme Park games. The fine folks that worked on this clearly did so with love and passion! It's a damn shame that they went home today to a 55% score. Just think about that.Here is an actual review of this game and it's contents.PC2 is better in literally every single way than PC1. It looks a million bucks, truly, it runs fantastically if you are prepared to spend some time with the settings.  It has more parts than PC1 at launch with well over 3k pieces. It brings to the table Global Illumination, which finally enables indoor dark rides without having to build underground. The engine now empowers us to attach SCENERY to RIDES. Yes, to the moving parts to now, it's actually mind-blowing to anybody who has enough brain cells to figure out what a technical achievement that is for Frontier.It's AWE-INSPIRING to behold this game in action, the vibes, the looks, the simulation aspects, but most of all the straigh-up God-tier lighting. It's just magnificent. Truly spectacular for anybody with the system to run it at decent settings.The amount of stuff we can do now is just off the charts. The waterpark stuff is great, it's all just really fun to build with and look at.It's a pretty heavy game to run, it has to be said, but it delivers on the performance it demands, and it scales really well. Adjust settings for optimal results as always, the game is very well optimized and we can see GPU temps and loads performing as expected based on on-screen renderload.As for "removed" features. They never were in this game. Accept that this is a completely new game, and that certain things will come later, as they were not a main priority during the 1.0 Devcycle.Frontier has communicated their intention to update the game with various requested features. Fantastic, and let's have some faith in this team.Please buy this game. If you love RCT, you will love this, if you love PC1, you will love this. If you enjoy Theme Parks and would love to get into something like this...BUY IT. IT's absolutely FANTASTIC, and will only get better from here.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a decent PC with a 4070 and 12th Gen CPU with 12GB Vram and the game just lags and stalls/freezes every few seconds. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Mostly good stability and by this I mean I had a few moments of lag when doing the first person camera on specific rides and it was like a few frames dropped nothing crazy definitely runs better then other games I have played day 1-It knew what made it's experience and improved on that-Pathing is so much better my parks look like real parks-Energy mechanic is something else to manage and I appreciate that-Creative allowed me to make custom game modes that allowed me to decide what I wanted to deal with and I was a big fan of that-Attaching items to rides is a massive improvement even if the system is confusing to learn-Building is a little more intuitive sometimesCons:-This is just personal and not the popular opinion but I do not like the fear system and was disappointed to see I could not turn it off this drastically restricts the rides you can create. For water slides I found this annoying more then regular rides and couldn't figure out how to use the loops provided-While I eventually figured out how to work the system the attach stuff to rides mechanic is a little awkward because you can't control what attaches where directly and sometimes it just randomly decides it's attaching everything to a random component and that's a glitch I can see that's a glitch because sometimes it's extremely intuitive and just goes where I click.-I genuinely could not find out how to build pool paths-Moving into and out of precision object movement was frequently frustrating to the point I started only using precision. I don't remember 1 doing this but either way if I went to change to precision mode I would drag my mouse causing the object to just be in a completely different location.-I found themes and objects where incredibly restrictive and something as simple as I want to build a kid zone with fantasy things become a challenge and I ended up just doing vaguely scary viking themed stuff.All and all it's an experience that is better then 1 so great job on hitting that goal and of course it's still a good game just because I have more cons then pros doesn't mean those cons are worse then the pros just that I had more to list and most of these cons feel like something I would expect to be updated or frankly could just live with. The game is worth it's price and does feel like a real improvement on an existing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen alot of people hating on this game, and I understand why, as it's very buggy and a bit clunky. _childDocuments_.review: There are two types of players of PlanCo: those who emphasize and enjoy the management aspect more and those who emphasize and enjoy the artistic creation aspect more. I am more of the first type of player. In PlanCo1, there was lots for both types of players. I enjoyed making the occasional coaster from scratch, but was more thrilled by making my park a lean, mean money-making machine. In the sequel, they have completely GUTTED what made PlanCo1 a great theme-park sim. Hard cap of 6000 guests, no security, no hotels, no large restaurants, tech tree that is a joke, staff AI that acts ridiculously, etc. About the only system added is the power and water from Zoo, but other than that they just flat out removed most of the systems and features which made the first one interesting and complex from a management perspective. It looks amazing, sure, and those that seem to be giving it positive reviews seem to really like the features they added to the artistic side of things. But as a theme-park management sim, PlanCo1 is just the vastly superior product at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Coaster 2 means a lot to me, and to many others too! not only will fans of the simulation genre love it, but theme park fans will definetly love it. It's a wonderful game, full of charm and wonder, however, it's not without it's issues, tho Frontier have acknowledged certain things and have stated they will fix • Visually, Planet Coaster 2 looks so much better than Planet Coaster 1, the lighting system is better, the detailing on guests, coasters, and especially restraints all have more polygons, It's deffo an upgrade! • Path System, It's great to be able to plop a ride straight onto a piece of path and it feels like things are easier to space out. • The Water Coaster, with the 4 in a row seat setup, it has a great splashdown piece that at first, I made a drop rather steep and it looked fine, but then I made it less steep and the transition still looked great! • The Passion, you can really see it in guest animation, ride animations, it all has it's charm. • Water Rides, other than the new water coaster in my pros, the log flume in Planco 1 had a very small splashdown transition that seemed too small/abrupt, this is still an issue and looks very silly if you make anything a bit high. To make things worse, the Antique Log Flume has a smaller, more silly looking splashdown piece, also the chainlift ending seems odd, and for whatever reason, the antique log flume has a track piece you can twist, but not turn. • Boomrang Coasters, the normal one still has this awkward straight piece as part of it's lift hill, meaning you cannot do a smooth transition between the loop and the second lift hill. The inverted boomerang in Planet Coaster 1 made you place a 12M long straight piece before each lift hill, I think it's smaller this time around but again, transitions. • Path System, which is in my pros and it's wonderful, but we were told by the team that the old pathing system is still there, however we're unable to make cattlepens like we could in Planet Coaster 1 by selecting the grid when placing queues. • Textures, some textures are very odd. The log flume use to have this lovely looking water in Planco 1 that looked like it was moving with the track and swaying at the edges, Planet Coaster 2's in flat and this weird VERY blue texture, and you can see texture tearing between track pieces. Also unsure if it's a texture thing but the Pirate Ship has this weird texture or ... glass? the wheels that push the ship seem to be clipping through it, it looks weird. • The UI, people have mentioned this already and it feels like a no brainer for us to be able to pop menu's off the side, keep them open and move them about around the screen like RCT1, but instead we have them stuck in places we don't want and some awkwardly close when we need them open.

_childDocuments_.review: The potential for this to be the earth shattering sequel to Planet Coaster is definitely there. However at this time (2 days after launch), the game feels like it was released too early. There's a lot of bugs and glitches that should not be in a released game. Certain aspects of the game have been exponentially improved on from the first game, like the coaster editor.  It is a lot easier to create smooth coasters with correct element shaping than the first game. The lighting is incredible. The way you can attach stuff to coaster cars and moving bases is great. The graphics have really been improved. However, it feels like there was a lot of attention put into certain aspects of the game and others were neglected. The water slides are terrible, which is odd because it was the big new feature for launch. There are no physics in them and the end result feels like a half attempted thing. The sides of the slide on any tube slide are straight and the bottom is flat. Meaning the rafts cannot go up on the side of the walls like an actual water slide does.  And the animations for the special pieces on the slides desperately need help. The slides look great when you are visually looking at them, but when you watch guests use them its too unrealistic to enjoy. However, Frontier has already publicly said they are working on a fix for this, so I am super excited to see this. Some of the coasters have the wrong restraints on them from their real life counter parts and some even use the wrong track/train combo. The Gravity Group Timberliner trains do not belong on RMC track. Also, the physics for the tilt coaster (in game tipper coaster) are wrong on the tilt track. When the track is in the vertical position and releases the train, it does not fall under the physics of gravity. It launches off the track piece and results in an unrealistic looking segment that would be such a cool feature if animated correctly. The coaster also moves through the layout too quickly due to this launch. It was touches of realism combined with the endless creativity that made the first game so great. This sequel seems to be more focused on creativity with not as much realism. It would be nice if  they brought back the ability to swap coaster trains on different tracks so I could put the Gravity Group trains on an actual wood track. The game would also benefit from having more animatronics. I find those to be key pieces in building a dark ride, but the game only has a few. It would also be nice to get the pieces back from the original game.It would be fantastic to see those pieces with the better graphics and lighting. It may be worth getting this game after some updates if you want a fantastic game right from the start. The potential for where this game is going is great, but the launch version just feels like a lot got rushed  and cut back to have the game out by Christmas and really could have benefited from a later release. I think people loved the original game so much that they were expecting a 10/10 game from the start. But in reality, it is a new game that is going to have to work out issues. The launch version of the game is a 7/10 with the potential to be a 20/10 in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unfinished. I love Planet Coaster 1 and Planet Zoo. My expectation for Planet Coaster 2 was PC1 with Zoo's QOL improvements, with an improved path system and water parks at least at RCT3 level. What we have is a UX nightmare of what feels like a game that wasn't even play-tested outside the team that built it. The attention to detail and care that we saw in the first two Planet games is simply missing. This missing care - not to mention lack of dignity to release it in such a state - leaves me pessimistic for the future of the game. If updates fix the issues, they'll be substantial enough that we'd nearly call it "Planet Coaster 3."p.s. A complaint I haven't seen elsewhere - PC1 had 4 options of coaster stations (pass through or same-side, left or right.) PC2 has only the worst one - same-side, and only to the left as far as I found. It still requires every single guest to step off the station (not just get past the gate) before letting new guests on. This is same exact behavior as the original - except they REMOVED the option that bypassed this silly quirk!

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of a first impressions review so far TBH. I'm enjoying the game overall. I LOVED Planet Coaster 1 and there are some definite quality of life and visual improvements. If you're a fan of the first one this feels the same with some added extras to make things a little more dynamic. However, I find the path creation system good and bad in equal measure. You can create wide open spaces a lot easier and create more complex designs but the UI doesn't seem as smooth or as straight forward as the first game. I've not really had too much time to play with it though so this could and probably is a ME problem but in PC1 you could lay a path in one material and simply drag another over it to change it. I cant seem to do that here, which is a pain if you want to change a complex layout mid design. Again that could be user error on my part although I've got around 250hr in PC1 so I'm familiar with the UI.There also seems to be fewer flat rides available, or rather fewer generic flat rides. By that I mean which ones there are are very much tailored to a specific theme so you can only really use them in that area. I.E Viking, Mythology, Resort etc. Its a shame as the ability to use rides in any zone to fill gaps etc in PC1 was great. It would have been great to let current PC1 owners have access to the content from PC1 too like the Wild-west themes etc. Similar to how the Warhammer Total war games are more larger expansions on the previous game but no doubt we will see "classic" packages come in as DLC down the line. The choices of themes seem too different to easily create different styles like in PC1 you could use elements from wild west, fantasy and the generic theme to make Disney like Main Street USA or compliment the futuristic design with elements from the generic stuff. The power system seems a bit of a chore but tbh I play this purely sandbox as a chill-out game so I turn that off.All in so far its good, but there's a few minor areas, but again that could be me and not the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a clear evolution of Planet Coaster 1, and the inclusion of water parks is great. Unfortunetly at the current stage this game is infurrating to play. The controls and the UI are enraging in PC, I´m amazed how this hasn´t been raised during development. There is an insane lack of hover tooltips, the staff schedule lacks basic Ui affordances to make it a proper managment tool, having to make so many clicks is insane. Information on the blueprint stock rides should be visible before purchasing, testing, etc. If the game career asks me to build a coaster with X meters or drop, show me that data on the blueprints. But the most rage quiting part is the path system. From the videos it looked amazing, but I don´t know what it is that makes it so so bad. The PC1 system was limited and clunky but worked, here if we have more flexible and powerful system that is still clunky and ends up not working. Paths don´t connectto each other half the tame and the minimum height different breaks them, and because there is no clear UI telling you if pathfinding works you just need to guess. I´m not happy giving this feedback because I see where the devs were going, and maybe with some tweaking they can get there.And ultimetly i dunno if bugs or inteeded, managing the staff is such a waste of time. Bins are not cleaned and rides not fixed even though staff is ¨looking for work¨and walking by the side. Overall I would say right now people should wait a bit to see if they make a proper UI and control scheme for PC and fix the few bugs with the path system and staff that are so annoying. I really wish to change this review soon!

_childDocuments_.review: First impression: It's like the Franchise go's 10 step forward, and 10 backwards at the same time.PROS:- It can look very nice- Sound effects are perfect- Atmosphere is great- Pools are nice, eventhough i am not really into waterparks.- ALOT of Coasters- Lighting is very goodNeutral:- Peformance, no big issues runs okay RTX4090, 2k. but i did not have had any big guest counts.Cons:- Atrocious UI. Worst i ever seen. everything is hidden in a tab or you have to scroll down.- To much Micromanagement. (It would not be that bad if the UI was better)- DEI Guests & Staff- Tiny maps- Max guest count 6000- Not alot of themes. Can't believe there are no western, SF, fairytale themeing...etc...- Stations are pretty much the same if not worse- Colours are to warm for me- They tried to add more management in the game. with electricity, pools, maintance, Ride operators that leave without notice. But it's so poorly done. (go back to the UI)- It's a console game (hence most issues)- No benches with back lean.- Remove the heatmap button when you hide UI (camera mode)- Where is Edge scrolling?- Picnic seat does not work as a bench- No Hotels, restaurants, ATM's, and limited bins, benches, and stuff- Always Sunny, even when it rains.- Can't sync toilet prices- No guards- No Management- To easy money- Sometimes no guests for rides. Even if there is a operator/good price/electricity- Ride often gives 0.00 as price- Nobody go's on ride anymore > Check price 245€ for a Bargain. 450 on premium. Change it to custom and back on Bargain = 45€- In Planco 1 you had a idea what the pricing should be. Now its a random number.- Guest got stuck on the queue line all the time- Ride operators are bugged. sometimes they 5 seconds and they decide to leave. Guest stuck on track.- No car or trains when pressing TEST- No car/train moves when pressing TEST ride. - Pre-build rides on maps or bluprints are place oddly. Tree on track, floating, chest, train clips other track piece. Like they finished in a hurry- DLC absent- Very Bad flatrides (were are all the classics that are like in every theme park)- No supports under Paths, and even when you are not close they can disappear.- Log Flume, Metal piece between sections...- During Dawn the weather is becoming very red- Synchronise flatride operation is bad. Guest teleport to seats in air. IRL guest take place at ground level. When the rides stops the other seats are at ground. Similar issue with other rides like Tiny Eye.- FD Vision ride, Normally moves constantly. yet it stops if there are no guests. Other guests are sitting on the ride for houres.- And more bugs....I will review this properly within a month or so. But Frontier needs to turn this Console Port into a proper PC game, ASAP.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love it, like I did with the first one.Spent a couple of hours in the game and encountered some very frustrating bugs.First day, the game just randomly crashed like every 20-30 min.After the Hotfix, I often having a major bug with the controls.If i hover over the park with "wasd" and trying to click like path editing, the game often gets stuck at one direction i moved into like camera drifting continuously to the left till i press the "a" button again.Than the guest crowds are driving me crazy.Like 50% of my paths are full of huge guest crowds while some paths are not being used.The problem here is, the guest get hungry and thirsty or want to leave the park, but can´t reach it cause of the crowds.Next Problem I encounter very often is, that Coasters and Slowrides are often stuck with guest in it.For example, I have a dark Ride themed Slowride and often i get the Message "your guests think that the ride takes to long"So I look into it and well.....the Ride isn´t even moving at all but Guests are standing in line and sitting inside.So i thought something needs to be repaired, but no the ride is fine.Same happens with a Coaster of mine.I rly hope they will fix this whole stuff, cause I´m having fun with the game but in this state, I can´t play any further.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a massive lover of theme park tycoon games since RCT1, but while I recommend this, there is so so so so soooooo much that's iffy.- Waterparks! Who doesn't love getting wet, and the detail does enable something absolutely fabulous.- The optimisation efforts. Generally I've actually had better performance with so much on the map than Planet Coaster 1, somehow...- The slight increase in graphical fidelity. Better graphics = Better game, obviously... Right?- Paths... What was someone smoking here? just having a 'fill' function, the ability for there not to be constant unnecessary snapping, and so many QOL details have simply been missing here. In some ways it upgrades the abilities of before, but in others it just makes life imperviously difficult still. Literally copy Cities:Skylines on this, simples.- Ride scenery. The rating seems to barely work and so much has been omitted from the first game. They could have easily ported over the assets from PC1 to PC2, surely? As someone who works in the gaming industry, it just doesn't make sense and if it becomes DLC I'll be a very grumpy man...- UI????? If there was a mouse/keyboard mode compared to a controller mode with condensed UI in a smaller scale, there would be 0 complaints. The amount of detail is amazing for those who enjoy getting into the nitty-gritty of things, but that it whams on my screen is beyond comprehension. Truly a silly sausage decision.- So many QOL systems from PC1 has just disappeared entirely from PC2, from the detailing options, to how snapping works, to the UI as mentioned above, etc. I literally notice something new that bugs me every time I play.----Overall, PC2 isn't a bad game. Far from it. If you enjoy the wet side of theme parks with further graphical options than before, then buy it, but if you already have every DLC from PC1 and you don't care about waterparks... Wait until a year has passed, get on sale, and you're golden.But for the love of Chris Sawyer... Frontier, plz fix.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Coaster 2 delivers beautiful, upgraded visuals that feel fresher and crisper than the original game, and there’s no denying the graphics are a treat. However, while the improved visuals are nice, the game feels like it's missing some of the core elements that made the original so memorable. Gone are the Pirate and Space themes, among others, which means you’re limited in creating the themed parks that gave Planet Coaster 1 its unique charm and creativity.Gameplay-wise, it lacks depth. The variety of rides feels noticeably limited, which quickly leads to repetitive game play, and the mechanics don’t introduce anything particularly new to keep you engaged. Planet Coaster 2 has potential, but it feels bare bones compared to the original. It's playable and could be a fun experience, but it’s hard to justify at full price. If you can get it on sale, it’s worth a look, but don’t expect the same depth or variety as the first game.Overall, I'd review it neutrally if Steam allowed; it’s an okay game, but it doesn't live up to the legacy of the first Planet Coaster.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Planet Coaster 1 for more than 5000 hours and I can see myself playing this sequel for another 5000 hours. I really love this game so far and it's true to the original while refreshing the same moment. And yes, not everything is perfect. Far from it. There are (mostly small) bugs, issues and certain other things Frontier needs to iron out. But the pros outnumber the cons.The abillity to scale your scenery is fantastic. The waterpark-feature just is amazing. Then there is the new pathing tool, which is amazing too, once you're past the first stages of getting used to the tool. Add the refreshing themes, the improved graphics and optimization and you have a potentially great game - and it's fairly decent already! Building smooth coasters was never so easy.Some people are/were disappointed. We all have different expectations and demands, which is natural. I'd recommend this game to anyone who loves to have fun with making amusement parks. And have a look at YouTube, people have been making amazing stuff already. _childDocuments_.review: An all-around upgrade from base Planet Coaster 1. _childDocuments_.review: I had to leave this review because I simply don't think the negativity it's getting is fair.It's been given countless bad reviews regarding "corporate greed" or fundamentally broken mechanics where people make out the game to be unplayable. This simply isn't true, its not as polished as PC1, but that's understandable, it hasn't had years of bug fixes and QOL updates. There is the making of a fantastic game in here, sure you might run into a problem now and again but Frontier are actively stamping these issues out with 2 patches already and a huge update in December.This is a really fun game. I've put 25 hours in so far and I'm having a blast. I've ran into a bug once or twice, but it's little things, nothing game breaking. I've had 2 crashes, but the game is so efficient it takes no more than 60 seconds to get back into it and the autosave runs extremely regularly, I've not lost any work.The game is great fun, it's a massive advance on PC1 and there's so many new features.To the people claiming this game is to sell DLC only, you're simply wrong. The base game is more than enough for 99.9% of people to never need to buy any DLC, I doubt I will. There's more than enough coasters and rides to fill your park, the only gripe is too few assets like bins and benches and what not, which is being resolved with the massive catalogue in the workshop.If this game was just a cash cow, you'd be paying extra for the waterparks, they're not stupid. These are the same people who made RCT3 which incidentally had a payable DLC for waterparks... "Soaked!"They need to make money, so of course DLC will come, but you're under no obligation to buy it! The game is fine as is.Summary: Great game, good fun, some work to do, but it's being done. Looking forward to the new free features and no, it's not just a DLC selling tool.

The new paths and pools features have massive potential but the game does a bad job explaining it and it feels underdeveloped. The campaign mode is mostly the same tasks over and over again (which isn't unusual to this genre of game) with some of the worst "characters" and dialog ever. The game also itself doesn't run that great and stutters a lot more that it should considering how good the first game runs. The franchise mode is really cool but it also requires the making of a Frontier games account which is annoying. It's a game I will stick with because a good game is there but it's currently buried beneath a clunky UI, half finished new features, and an overall un-optimized experience. 6/10 - InfiniteUpdate: Recent hot fixes have fixed many things relating to guest behavior making the game much more playable. _childDocuments_.review: I can't remember the last time I left a review on Steam for a game it's been years....Planet Coaster 2 is stunning! Stunningly pathetic. I've been with the Planet games since Planet Coaster 1 was released and let me say I don't have words for how horrible this game is in its current state. It like it been developed by a totally different studio and they released the Pre-Alpha version because this certainly couldn't be called a beta or alpha version. The Sim for the people in the park is basically non-existent. They won't ride rides, they get clumped up and stuck even on the widest paths and then the staff AI..... Your rides and shops will randomly close because no staff are present even though you have a staff member scheduled for that ride. People will say your rides are too expensive at get this.... $0 for the ticket. They won't ride your water slides even if they are free. The whole point of the game is broken...Then the amount of included rides, shops, and themes is simply insulting. Then they offer a paid DLC at launch.. If you played through the Cities Skylines 2 launch and flop this is strikingly similar...They say they are fixing a lot of it in December, but that will have to be a massive update to get the simulation working even the slightest bit like Planet Zoo or Planet Coaster 1. From a company that developed and then supported two massively popular and successful games and then put of this garbage.. I have no words...

_childDocuments_.review: Really just an expansion for the first game, but not as good. Park sizes are incredibly small, absolute joke, its not even as big as the small size on the prior game. Avoid this game at all costs. In sandbox you can no longer pick your terrain textures, which is a a massive step back since the last one, they needed to expand the selection. Pools are very weak, you don't seem to be able to stop guests from walking through them in normal clothes. The waves don't seem to be mesh deformation or anything like that. Just a texture. RCT3 Soaked expansion was better than this.Overall it's a massive letdown. I've gone past the refund window, but if I could refund it I would.The sound it plays when favoriting a item is gross, get it out of my ears.There is a huge lack of themes in the base game, even less than the first. _childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Planet Coaster 1 and Planet Zoo, I will say that there's a lot of really great new changes made to this game. Unfortunately there are also a bunch of negative changes, steps backward in really basic ways. The UI and controls are worse than Planet Zoo in many case and in some ways things are even worse than Planet Coaster 1. 1 step forward, 2 steps back. It looks like Frontier is aware of many of the issues and working on them and I will change my review if and when these issues are addressed. Sadly this is yet another game released in a very unfinished state.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend the game at this state and I'd like Frontier to feel that. With hundreds of hours in PC1 I can confidently say this game feels bad, clunky and most of all unfinished. Many items, some itemtypes even are flat out missing, probably to be bundled into dlcs in the future (for example no fireworks whatsoever). There are like ten total animatronics in PC2. What?The menus are awful. Like really, rage inducing awful. Player time is not respected at all here. Press ESC ten times to close a menu, you can't scroll in first menu anymore when anover opens, that can also scroll. Menus close themselves all the time. Bugs, bugs, bugs. Still no dark mode.I had a technician drop under the map, basically bricking my small park due to power being out and the technician being unable to fix it. Sometime after, the technician reentered the park like a guest would. The generator I had to replace manually, then I had to replace all power distribution stations, because the old power lines stay in the ground. At this point, the park was empty and my mood gone.When you have multiple scenery pieces selected you MUST use right click, then left click together to turn the camera, if you press left first, your selection gets deleted lol. Track pieces place themselves randomly. Some buttons are unclickable if they are only near other UI elements. Creating a coaster is lots more work, just because you have to swap between build and test menu all the time, and none of that can be done with keybinds.Core technical features were removed. You are unable to rebind free look camera. The advanced camera that would rotate around your mouse instead of the magically determined focus point was just... removed. The camera flies all over the place often. I can't even set an audio output device anymore.Honestly, I'm going back to PC1 for now.

name: Edge Of Eternity
detailed_description: WISHLIST OUR NEW DEAR VILLAGERS GAME About the Game The world of Heryon is torn apart. Years ago, the arrival of a mysterious alien force ultimately plunged the planet into an endless cataclysmic war where both magic and technology were unleashed to their worst and darkest extremes. Now an even greater threat has emerged : in a despicable act of war, the invaders released the Corrosion, a fatal disease turning living forms of all kinds into misshapen abominations. In these desperate times, a young soldier will have to face his destiny and embark on an epic journey that will change the fate of Heryon forever… Key features: An enthralling story filled with plot twists and heart-wrenching moments A gorgeous fantasy world to explore Epic battles with a unique and strategic turn-based combat system Charismatic and unforgettable characters Stunning soundtrack featuring Yasunori Mitsuda (Chrono Trigger & Xenoblade Chronicles) A crafting system A fearless yet adorable beast to befriend 50+ hours of gameplay About Midgar Studio Midgar Studio is a small French independent development studio created in 2008 and composed of thirteen video game enthusiasts. The studio is located in Nîmes in the south of France and specializes in hardcore games especially on PC and consoles. More from Dear Villagers

_childDocuments_.review: The base game has some very interesting mechanics, a little bit janky how its put together, but I like the battle map mode and somewhat snappy turn based combat. Some really cool ideas go into the functionality of the game. Tons of save points and fast travel points just from the first two hours of gameplay. Tons of thought went into how the combat plays out and even does a good job explaining the functionality of the options you have at your disposal. Escape skips the cutscenes which is welcome to me with these kinds of games. There are a lot of cutscenes but once you get through the "prologue" it does seem to let you explore. Honestly the way the game is set up it reminds me a lot about how older mmorpgs are set up. which is welcome because it does not force you to do a lot of the kill x creatures and gather x plants quests.  Some of the tutorials are busted and caused a reset or two, but I am confident if/when reported this developer would take the time to fix it I can tell how much effort went into this game. Now the real crux of my issue with this game. The story and dialogue is VERY cringe worthy, a lot of it seems to be inspired by low effort jrpgs and not in a good way. Most of the interactions i have seen so far are half baked or completely forced and the story so far seems to be going in a direction that really just does not interest me. It took a lot of personal will to push past the first hour based on the fact alone which is a shame because their is a diamond underneath all of the boring basement dweller filler. I will be keeping an eye on this developers future work as this could have been a game that blows games like final fantasy out of the water but to me the story and diaglouge is THAT bad. So that coupled with the jank this game does have I can not recommend this game at full price unfortunately. I want to love this game, and I hope the developers keep polishing this game up because I can see myself sinking 100+ hours into a game like this especially because you can skip most of the story, but I should not want to skip the entire story just to play a good game loop.TLDR;Good mechanicsfun combatlots of minor glitches and forced restartsCRINGE story and dialogue5/10

Writing is a bit corny and uninspired. There was way too much moaning and melodrama. _childDocuments_.review: Good game. Slow start, but ramps up as the game progresses. There are some things at the start that just don't make sense (cutting the chain on a down drawbridge isn't going to make it go up, it works the other way), but beyond some of those small issues, its pretty straightforward. The artwork and graphics are great. The developers really made a world that looks and feels like you're on a different planet. The storyline starts off pretty basic, but gets better as you go. The one things that I don't care for is that the world doesn't respond well to the storyline itself. No one is running in fear about an invasion of robots. For all NPCs, they're just living normally.Fights are good, along with the AI. The crystal setup for your weapons is pretty basic and probably needs some work. Essentially all the crystal slots just give a + percentage to things like physical defense, or magic damage. Some of them give spells or special abilities which vary from character to character. The recipe system needs some serious re-balancing, since all of the weapon recipes are random drops. Either you get lucky, or you don't. That's a problem, since there doesn't seem any reliable way to farm for these recipes, and they're not purchasable anywhere. As far as all other recipes, they are purchasable from vendors at various points in the storyline, including the recipes for some of the components needed for the weapon recipes you may receive. It is very frustrating to have a top tier weapon recipe and not be able to create it. Speaking of components, there is no bestiary in game to let you know what items drop from which enemies. Not only that, but the drops that you receive can be not only on the enemy, but the enemies level, which is linked to your level and/or your location. As far as enemy variety, there is not much here. There are less than 10 different enemies in the game, with each one coming in normal, corroded, spectral, or (sometimes) big versions. Based on the size of the world and scope of the game, that number should be tripled. On the plus side, nearly all the enemies make perfect sense in a normal world. Mostly animals. But there needs to be more.Looking forward to seeing what the last two chapters bring later in June. I think the developers are great, and will resolve much of the above in future patches.

_childDocuments_.review: Very Rough around the edges, in ways that I'm really not sure are fixable, but there's a lot here that's worth exploring.But enjoying this game seems like it's going to rely a lot on if you can look past the issues, janky setup, and awkward delivery to enjoy it for what it's  to be. And I'm not saying that you ought to be able to- I genuinely can't assess the quality of this game without tackling the fact that it's a bit of a mess, and you're going to be playing a lot more of the mess than the parts that shine.... but because the core mechanical engagement with the game seems to be a solid foundation of turn-based RPG combat, and the storytelling, while somewhat awkward was in need of an extra draft or two in the script, is also building on solid foundations beneath some clunky dialogue- The two primary characters actually have a great sibling relationship, even if I roll my eyes at the details of most of their conversations. The details are rough, but you can see through them to a strong core underneath often enough that they work.If you asked yourself what a game would look like with solid fundamentals, interesting ambition, but just not enough polish, Edge of Eternity is the game you get. It looks beautiful, but you need to turn the settings down or the frame rate goes wonky when you move. It has an interesting and emotional story at its heart, but the dialogue that tells you that story is inconsistent at best. It has solid turn-based combat, but the ways you interact with it are about as janky as they come. I haven't yet felt like I was  with the game to get through its awkwardness, but the awkwardness is there, and if you think that will sabotage your ability to enjoy the game, this one might not be for you.I'm definitely curious to see where this one goes, but I can't recommend it without serious conditions. You gotta accept its clear problems and be able to love it anyways. And if you manage that, you might just be golden.Edit: Yeah..... I tried, alright? But there's only so much watching solid ideas fall flat and lifeless that I can take and want to see more, alright? The game tries, it really does, and I respect the effort from such a small number of people, but that doesn't actually make me want to keep playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Edge Of Eternity - $34TLDR at bottom.Game type: Semi-Open/Open World ‘Japanese Style’ RPGNumber & type of player interactions: Single Player; No Player InteractionsDescription: Edge Of Eternity is a semi-open to open world Japanese styled party & turn based RPG. It sports a combat grid, free moving camera, skill customization & predicted encounters.Operating System & Control Options: Windows 10, with Linux & possible others in the works. Currently supports DirectX 11 & there’s OpenGL support spoken of. Controls are a non-customizable keyboard/mouse interface or Xbox & Playstation style controller support. Supports AZERTY & QWERTY layouts for keyboards. Fans note that the product’s roadmap claims to be allowing more in the future.Game Mechanics: The game’s mechanics are a semi-open to open world with free character movement in zones. Actors are interacted with in the 3D environment that that the game’s world is composed of. Combat takes place after encountering a hostile actor’s field model which is then, almost directly, taken to a grid based arena that is almost exactly the area where the encounter took place. The combat is turn based using an active meter to display cool down of actions for any character on the field. With no action points to account for each action a character takes is a turn which is then followed by the cool down.The game makes use of elemental rock/paper/scissors & physical attacks that the player chooses via the equipment menu while not in combat. The governing of the skills is done by a health bar, a mana bar & the previously mentioned active meter.Skills so far, having achieved approximately half way through the second city’s zone, are basic but well balanced with the only thing taking notice being an omega/uber/champion enemy creature’s version of a dividing/illusion skill that the enemy did not last long enough to actually use.Character levels are automatic but stats can be influenced by equipping various armours, arms & accessories. Town inventories are basic with the player strongly encouraged to use the crafting system.The crafting system uses a simple collection scheme that many games have previously, with, so far, customization of the items being done via two or three-way branching upgrade paths.The player’s party is based of up to four characters who are predefined in their rolls. For example the starting two characters are a standard fighter character with middling defense, enhanced to high attack power & speed. The other character is a glass canon character who has low health & defense but hits like a nuclear missle.Story: The story, as presented so far, appears to draw on standard (J)RPG tropes with a hero rising from the random collection of people to be the hero that saves the world from an unfathomable force or entity.There are indications that a Face-Heel turn may occur at some point in the story so a twist that helps the story break away from normal tropes may occur & would actually be quite welcome.Characters in the game are represented to perish/die however the deaths lack impact due to the player’s ability to sympathize with characters not being given a chance to develop.Characters are presented as having a past before the game starts instead of being cast into the world as a new born when the game started. This is honestly a refreshing from a lot of games where the developers seem to think players will identify/sympathize with actors who have no back story better.Art Style/Graphics: The art style is generally consistent with fresh takes on many things that make the game’s world feel unique & not a copy/paste of previous worlds/ideas that are ubiquitous in the fantasy settings used by many authors. Of course some such things feed into all works so while some are encountered it doesn’t make the game’s world feel homogeneous.There is good colour usage with a wide variety in use & not unexpected combinations.World physics are done decently however there is a minimum in use with basically only trees & grass simulating wind blowing & taller grass reacting to the player’s movement a tad.Very few particle effects or light tricks appear to be in use & could go a long way to make the game more immersive.The graphics do, sometimes, lack some depth or filter & lead to too ‘smooth’ of a look. While the art style is generally consistent some times the chosen style can still lead to a ‘why?’ experience on the part of the player. This will tend to be a personal engagement factor with players.Sound/Music: Sound is of a decent quality with little clipping or imbalances. Music generally does not interfere with hearing aspects of the game’s world that are important.While there is voice acting it does not generally line up with actor’s movements. The voice actors chose do a decent job of presenting character’s states but sadly it is limited to major actors & scenes. The developer has indicated this is a funding issue & is unlikely to expand unless the game experiences a massive increase in popularity.One of the very few problems with the audio is that the microphone seems to be misplaced in some areas/conversations leading to troubles hearing actors.Target/Suggested Audience: The target audience appears to be the current mean RPG player on Steam in Western countries. The audience I personally would suggest is anyone seeking a fresh IP for an RPG insetad of the status quo.Summary of Pros: The pros of the game are pretty good: the game appears to be mostly balanced, the game’s world appears to be well thought out, developer is currently active in patching & supporting the product. Contains enough content to leave it interesting for dozens of hours & is an IP that has the ability to expand if the developer doesn’t let it wither away.Summary of Cons: While the cons of the game are not horrible/game breaking there tends to be lots of them. This, in the end, is what may cause players to deviate away; it will come down to personal engagement & participation of players.The biggest two problem the game seems to have are: clipping issues & glitchiness where the game has not received personal attention from the developer.The clipping issues are small & plentiful. While it does not break the game or even cause a massive problem, it is, however, very noticeable. This can cause players to feel the product is unpolished or not main stream.Examples are plants & actors that the player character can run through, plants with bounding boxes that are too big, clothing & weapon physics errors & environmental roughness.The developer has used a lot of random placements & other tricks to lower filling times in exchange for a larger world. This has lead to a game world that doesn’t always feel ‘right’.One example is the crowds in the second city;  actors are repeated many times & don’t ‘feel’ in the right spots. When queried about it the developer indicated that some optimizations to such things would occur in future patches.While these are two of the most noticeable problems there are others that can be noticed from time to time. A few examples of more minor ones are stiff animations, lack of landmark navigation items, no map, mini-map customization or zooming.Reviewed copy obtained via: Steam store front purchase – Early access; review hours done in ‘release’ build + post patches.Recommendation Level/Over all opinion: The over all recommendation used to be a positive one; however with recent forced addition of Japanese voices to please a small subset of customers the over all recommendation is a negative one.Forced, on a quota, to download 8 GB of data I cannot use as I am not Jpanese, it feels like one of the crappy moves Square Enix would pull on Final Fantasy customers.However... it's not a mega corporation but a small time studio & speaks ill for the future of the company.The recommendation is to find other products, in the same price range, that are more polished.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: pretty world.Cons: Everything else. Combat, story writing, voice acting, animations, crafting, cooking, ALL of it is D-tier or C-tier at best.This game is very clearly made by a small team of indie devs who are trying to make their magnum opus. They've put a ton of effort into creating a beautiful, large world. They've certainly done that - I don't think I've ever seen such a Unity game with an environment like this one.Everything else though, just stinks. Yes, I've put 60 hours into this game (because I'm trying to go through the unplayed games in my library) but I've been bored for most of that time. The writing is barely good enough to keep you mildly interested, but by the fun long stops after 10-20 hours.That large world? Its empty. It turns quests into walking simulators. Running, and running, and running, and running from waypoint to waypoint. There's nothing to do in this big world.Enemies get tiresome real quick. Combat is slow and turn-based. Other JRPGs with similar turn-based battles have options to speed up battles since grinding is BORING. This game has an auto-battle feature, but its cumbersome, slow, and dumb. Auto-battle just uses random skills. Unless you have a significant power advantage, auto-battle will lose. I've literally seen characters cast healing spells on enemies. With the slow combat pace and the usage of random skills, auto-battles take forever and will quickly have you ignoring the game in favor of a podcast or whatever you're watching on the side.Crafting is a hot mess. Most of the weapon recipes will be inferior to your current weapon by the time you unlock them. Why are there so many weapons in the tech tree then? You craft weapon #1 since it is needed as a material to craft weapon #2, which is needed as a material to craft weapon #3.... Crafting materials is the biggest chore I have ever seen. Some resources drop from enemies. Those are easiest to buy since going out and grinding enemies is BORING and ANNOYING. But then, you've also got to craft certain crafting materials. Those are tiered as well. You must craft resource tier #1 which then is a crafting material to craft tier #2 and so on. And to craft each tier, you'll have to go and run to one of several shops to buy crafting materials for each material tier. As it sounds like, its an absolute chore.Cooking is just selecting a meal at an Inn when you rest. They just give passive bonuses.There's too many actually good games out there. Don't waste your time/money on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: So I hate to write this because I genuinely wanted to like the game. The game looks beautiful, you get to ride a nekaroo, the combat is decent, and the brother/sister dynamic is really good. Yet the bad animations, subpar voice acting, and predictable story makes me want to ditch this game. The side quests are pretty much the same except for a few that I actually enjoyed including the one where you figure out you have a treasure chest problem. I also feel as if the companions are shallow and uninteresting. The combat is either over in one turn or becomes a pain in the ass as time goes on, but in the end the animation is what killed it for me. The characters barely show any emotion besides through text and its hard to take seriously when the character is trying to cry and it is the same face they make all the time. Overall Edge of Eternity gets a 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried my hardest to like this game. But as I'm getting less and less time to play games, I have to be able to cut off the ones I don't like once I make the realization they aren't going to get better. - Edge of Eternity has a lot of promise, and it's a great attempt by a small team to make a new RPG series. If they take feedback earnestly and try to improve for a sequel, I'll definitely check it out. But as it stands for this game, there are too many annoyances for me to be able to give it a recommendation, and I quit after 15 hours. More in depth, here are a list of problems I personally had with this game (that even as a small team they should have been able to address)...* After 15 hours in, I still have the same 2 party members. I had a 3rd temporarily, but they yanked them away fast.* Combat is laboriously slow. Which is a shame, because the combat isn't half-bad. A "skip animations" option would have been a great fix.* It's hard to make a build when each new weapon completely reorganizes your crystal tree, rather than growing it.* The open world is stale and empty, other than the same monsters respawning. It's very pretty, but most of the locations have no actual point to them.* The story is... inconsistent to say the least. Spoilers: * Side-quests are pointless, but without them you don't get enough EXP on normal, even with the EXP patch.* Crafting is useless and gathering materials is completely RNG. Not every game needs crafting, please. If it was completely removed it would actually be an improvement.Edit: The developer has pointed out that there is a button you can bind to toggle the battle speeds. Wanted to be completely transparent since my goal was not to tear this game apart mercilessly.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, it looks kinda cool, feels good in many ways, but it ultimately lacks many basic features  and feels like a shallow concept stretched way too thin.----Art----The environments look pretty nice. Characters models are alright.The animations mostly look terrible, I understand that it is a small indie team and I didn't expect them to be great, but they're still pretty bad for my low expectations.Same goes for the voice acting which is most of the times hilariously bad.The dialogs are about as good as the voice acting itself.----Combat/Crafting----The combat camera is janky as hellAnimations often glitch out when moving to different spots (happens pretty often in puzzles)Not much depth to the abilities that are available, only basic elemental attacks with a really low chance for an effect to proc (at least till the game bore me enough to stop playing it)The crystals system to upgrade stats/grant new skills feels like a good idea but is really underdevelopped.I tried to grind a bit to make new weapons, abandonned pretty fast because the drop rates are ABYSMAL.Killing over and over the same monsters (easily 50 times+) to craft one basic item is not fun imo, especially when most of the time you don't get rewarded anything and have to do the entire process again for the next upgrade.----Conclusion----This feels like a game where too many things tried to be done at once, on one side you have a gorgeous world you want to explore, but on the other side everything else about the game feels like a rushed out concept that was poorly implemented.This could be great, but isn't, and I feel like there are way too many problems with the game now for it to be good before a long time.Seeing that the developpers plan to get out of early access by june, I hope that they'll take a good look at their own game, and go over everything that is currently wrong about it, before trying to add more story content.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game could be fun, it's just dealing with some issues I see as major.Gameplay :Animations are often unrealistic, unnaturally fast, and repetitive.Traveling around is far too common, became tired of running around without my motivations established.Fighting is slow, and when offered a mechanic to speed up, it doesn't always work, and doesn't say why. (Just speed fights up permanently?)Looting/Crafting feels empty, no changes visually, or skills learned, ect.Looting takes two key presses to complete, considering the amount of loot, one would be fine, just have the menu close itself as the player leaves.Using Weapons/Equipping Armor feels empty as well, no visual changes. (Just have the players find different ways to improve the characters ALREADY EXISTING armor/weapons.)Battles can take up to 10 minutes, with almost no rewards. Virtually no high-end strategy other than healing at proper times, moving, and knowing how much damage attacks will do.Visuals :Running animation looks like someone hardly jogging.Attacks/Mob animations hardly have any variance.Battle win cut scene seems unnatural, and quickly takes you out of the game.Constant distance rendering issues.Lighting in initial levels is overwhelming.Long landscapes with repetitive flora/fauna made for bland traveling experiences.Audio :The voice acting is consistent, but it is consistently bad acting. Reminded me heavily of The Legend Of Zelda TV Series, "Excuuuse me, Princess." could have been said by the characters and it wouldn't have felt out of place.Hardly any "attacking" or "getting hit" sounds, also felt empty.No audible queues when player turns change, time speeds up, or a character is about to be hit by a charged attack/spell.The soundtrack is quite nice.As of writing this review I cannot personally recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Holy, I forgot that this game was made by 9 persons, so yeah... the game is looking pretty good for a 9 person team. Even through the game's is in an Alpha state and there's a bunch of bugs, inconsistencies, overall a 2/3 optimization and things that I would love to change about the game right now like : Enemy encounters, all the stiff/ugly animations, certain movement mechanics and so on...I got to say, I LOVE this game, is far far far from being finished (2020 I'm waiting) but what we have here has a lot and I mean a LOT of potential to become one of the best RPG's on PC, and I'm not kidding. I am going to sum up, all the things a Like right now about the game and also my own personal suggestions about what needs to be fixing/changed or added into the game.(+) PROS:+The visual section and graphics are great, while theres room for improvement theres no denying that the game looks great for an alpha state.+The combat is turn based but with a twist, the arena where you fight is determined by where You encountered an enemy and this arena is divided by zones, these zones can be affected by You and the enemies with attacks and debuffs so repositioning yourself is the only way you're not going to get killed. That is why when you enter a combat the place where you started is really important and will make a big difference when fighting foes, if You just happen to be in the area of a Healing crystal You will get heal every certain number of turns... and this can turn the tables between You and your enemies, keep in mind these affect enemies as well, so repositioning and zoning your enemies is important.+The map is beautiful and big, not only that but theres a lot of resources that you can gather across your adventure, the map is fullied with enemies, quests and events that reward You.+Everything about the gem mechanic feels amazing, while exploring or killing enemies you will get "Gems" these will unlock abilities and will grant you stats, and each character has its own "Gem tree" where you put the gems and basically make your own build. I would love to have multiple trees to choose and upgrade my character but I'l guess well have to wait for that in the final release.+This game has a lot of content for an alpha, all the equipment and gems are functional and is pretty damn fun to mess around with builds.+The game has a very interesting lore that I'm excited to fully discover.+Most parts of the Interface look insanely good for an alpha state game.+Currently while the soundtrack is nothing super stunning is not bad and I belive they are saving the best for later on in the game.(-) CONS and (*) SUGGESTIONS:-The voice acting in general could be a little bit better but hey, overall is not bad. Also I would say that the dialogue between characters  sometimes feels off due to the voice acting.-The world is vast and big, I would love to have either a mount or a sprint/run mechanic to get to places faster EVEN if this mechanic tires Your party. -Also because you can't Jump, some places are odd to get into, for example you just happened to found iron, but the iron is behind a fence, you can't just jump over the fence, you have to rotate the hole fence just to get to the iron, is just odd. -Pretty much any living form wants you dead for some reason, even the most harmless looking piggie (Okko) wants to fight you and its kinda Annoying when all You wanna do is farm some resources. This could be fixed easily by making some enemies harmless or unninterested in fighting unless you attack them. But this would also imply adding an "Attack Button"-The game is in an alpha state and so does the optimization, the game runs sometimes at 60 FPS and sometimes at 30-25FPS... also my CPU and GPU temps are going crazy when playing in High Settings (I have a GTX 1060 6GB, Ryzen 2600X, 16 GB Ram) My cpu hitted 59° Celsius while my GPU got to 68° Celsius, this doesn't happen with other games at all, the CPU never ever goes up 50° C, and the GPU 60° C. So this game needs a lot of work with the optimization.*Just like in Persona games add an "Attack Button/Attack Mechanic" When nearby an enemy, attack them to guaranteed the starting turn in a combat, not only that but this would fix the "Attack the harmless creatures to fight them". This would be needed to make the combat a little more strategic and as I said before would fix the Issue that needs to be adressed.*Make items usable out of combat (Idk If I'm pressing the wrong keys or those don't work out of combat).*Inn's are a main mechanic of the game, so having "Camps" as a secondary tool to recover Party energy would help with long traveling.*BUFF the selling cost of Iron, you're telling me I'm selling a piece of Iron for 5 Gold? PLS BUFF, at least 8-10 gold?.Overall the game's looking pretty good, let's wait until 2020 to get the full game and lets hope most of the bad parts of the game are fixed, best of luck for the devs and keep up the great work guys!

The story seems interesting, the world seems unique and the graphics do the world justice. What turns me right off are the characters. The characters in the cut scenes are animated extremely poorly. Characters looking around trying to be moody come off absolutely robotic and it completely undermines what would otherwise be a powerful moment. This happens in every single cut scene. The story has unbelievable potential but, in its current state on August 18th, 2020, it throws it all away with absolutely amateur cut scenes. Did you think Mass Effect Andromeda had poorly animated cut scenes? This is significantly worse. That, among the overwhelming bugs. Graphical bugs hindered my short time in the game. All sorts of pop in, characters hair flashing in and out, it just takes you out of the experience.This game has the bones to be an absolute banger of a JRPG. As of the writing of this review, it needs more time in the oven to cook but it will definitely stay on my radar as it develops.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun. It reminds me of Final Fantasy Tactics and Ni no Kuni. The environments and music are great for an indie RPG company. The dialogue can be good at times and made me laugh at a few moments. The characters and story are also well developed with only a few moments in Chapter 1 where the story dragged a little. The only issue I have with the game in Early Access is the character models. Some of the character models need to have some small details changed like the hair, speaking animations, and arm movements that models use. I also had some problems with clipping outside of the map in some areas (mostly in the cave areas). Overall, I recommend this game. I think people should buy this if they like turn-based RPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game so far is excellent. I am really enjoying this for an indie title. I just bought it, so my opinion could change, but first impression was WOW for an indie game!! Best indie RPG I have played that is this quality. Very similar to Old Final Fantasy titles, this game is what new Final Fantasy games should be like.However, as much as I like it, I find one thing that truly holds it back, IN MY OPINION, and that is "Team Energy" that mechanic needs to go or at least be fixed. I feel it limits exploration and being able to constantly sprint which I tend to ALWAYS do. I have played so many RPGS and this game could be a AAA title, the fact its from a small developer is downright amazing. SO I am hoping, unlike big developers, that this small team will listen to what we say and continue to develop it to how the fans and the people who are playing suggest. I am not alone when complaining about "Team Energy" the majority of "bad" reviews are based around this mechanic. This is not a survival game, it is an outstanding RPG, so if the developers eliminated this mechanic from the game entirely I feel it would open up a new sense of freedom, because running out of energy when out exploring will bring you closer to a "game over screen" and why even explore if we constantly have to sleep at an Inn to replenish our energy. TO be fair I have not hit 0 energy yet so I do not know what happens, however, the first inn I had to stop fighting and I am not sure if I missed any events because I rushed just to replenish a stupid meter that was falling. It is a Gimmick and needs to go. Team Energy so far is my only real complaint.The Combat is excellent, turn based, with really using the environment to your advantage and disadvantage. I enjoyed the first few puzzles the game offered as well. Being able to move in hexagon tiles while utilizing turn based actions added a lot to the true and tried old system of turn based RPGS of old. Added a new layer of a system that has been done so many times.The graphics are beautiful and better than most AAA worlds (tales series comes to mind), with very bland worlds and environments, this world is not like the Tales Series its more like Xenoblade Chronicles  with live weather, day and night, rain, snow, and blue skies!! I love how intricate the world feels, I just wish I could get LOST in it without having to worry about sleeping at an Inn just to refill the team energy meter. Instead of looking at other things on screen my eyes are fixated on a meter..... Please eliminate "team energy" and this game would be 9/10 in my opinion. With Team Energy limiting the freedom and scope of exploration and side questing I have to deduct points 7/10 Hopefully the developers are reading these reviews because I want it gone tonight. LoL Patch that kills it, Keep the FOOD Bonuses or have the meter only affect Food Bonuses AND NOTHING ELSE, Really there is no point for it, so best thing would be to eliminate the team energy mechanic entirely!!!!But do not be discouraged, this game is worth it, early access is fantastic and I am really enjoying it except for that one minor issue. To the Developers: Please rethink the Team Energy mechanic or alter it in a way that does not limit freedom. Thank you!!!! Overall, excellent game, lots of fun, buy it, support the developer so we can have more games like this!!!!!Because this game is in early access I really hope the developers remove Team Energy entirely from the experience, if they do, then I feel this game will be a HUGE success and could be Indy game of the Year. We do not want to feel controlled and limited when we play RPGs we want to explore at our hearts content and never worry about a stupid meter ruining our adventure.Thank You for making this game, please consider removing the team energy mechanic from the game and I know this will be a huge HIT!!!!All bad reviews seem to centered on one game mechanic (not all but the majority) I hope the developers are paying attention!!!

_childDocuments_.review: So this game DEFINITELY needs some explaining….You probably have seen multiple reviews about how either good or bad this game is. To be perfectly honest, this game has an extravagant number of issues that should have been caught by a solid QA group. However, this is not a bad game. (Yeah, I know that does not make much sense)Playing through the game I did not experience anything game breaking. What I did see is a large amount of characters disappearing, slowdown in the final area, slow environment filling, and slight stuttering when traveling fast. Mind you I was playing this in 4K. This is the first game I have ever had issues with in 4K and I was playing God of War on the highest setting prior to this game.Pushing past those issues we have the game-play issues. First off, the game tries to innovate itself with a gimmick system for everything. You get a new weapon! well you need to level up that weapon to open gem slots for special abilities. You can only go one way so look before you fill in. Second, the combat is based on the directional and buttons. So, pick the left side for magic and such and the right for combat/movement/items/etc. The list goes on and on. Every feature of this game has some form of system to it to include weather and what you are standing next to. Item creation is a royal mess as well. You do not know how many you have while making them or you run into the bigger issue of having to wait on the story to be able to make items. There are times you will have to wait an entire chapter before upgrading you gear even though you have the recipe. One of my biggest issues is the camera. You will be fighting this thing just to see what is on the field. Couple that with vegetation and enemies being dark. The experience screens take too long and you have to wait a few moments before being able to close them. There are a lot more things like NPCs do not move around making the locations feel a bit lifeless, but I will not spoil the ‘fun” for you.Now at this point you probably asking why am I bothering to recommend a game that has so many issues. Well, they do get some of the most important features good. The combat once you get used to the gimmicky controls is well done. You can setup different types of attacks on an open field. The combat has many issues that need to be taken into account from extra weapons on screen to traps that can hurt of help you or the enemy. The story is also good (decent). They give you the initial goal and keep building from there. Unfortunately, they never really explain anything until the second to last chapter. The music to the game is pretty good as well, I ended constantly going back to two locations just because of the music. Voice acting is also pretty decent. Nothing AAA but considering a really really small team made this, I would not expect it to have that. Additionally, most the game is not voiced.  Lastly, we get to the graphics. They look AWESOME. This is probably where they spent the majority of time. When everything is fully loaded the ground looks beautiful. The detail with various types of plants is outstanding. The backgrounds also look great. Again, it is a shame that it does not load as quickly as it should.If this was a game produced by a large well-known studio, I would definitely say this was a hot mess and definitely not worth the money.Considering this was created by a really small group with lots of innovative ideas for trying to improve game-play. I definitely say they did a great job. The game is fully playable and you will definitely get about 40+ hours on a standard run. I enjoyed my time while playing and would probably by another RPG if they made one provided, they taper their concepts to what they can reasonably accomplish. -  They definitely bit off more than they were capable of. But at least they are nowhere like Cyberpunk 2077

_childDocuments_.review: Edge of Eternity is an ambitious game, but it doesn't quite live up to its scope. The game feels like a homage to the classic Final Fantasy games of old, but its enchanting world is let down by the lackluster events happening on its surface. The combat system and character customization are well-done, but they don't matter if there isn't a good reason to keep moving forward. While JRPG fans will likely find enough to like that its worth giving Edge of Eternity a shot, other players should seek more engaging options within the same genre.
