_childDocuments_.review: Abandonware - Do NOT buyThis game has been sitting in my library for some time, so unfortunately a return was not possible anymore.As of the time of writing this review the last patch was applied almost a year ago!!! And this game needs updates.It is riddled with bugs. And a lot of them can only be fixed by restarting the game. Not the least of which is when the game decides to not load the main menu and you have to Alt + F4 out to try again.One longer fight froze and crashed the game while another one could be called game breaking. No fixing that one except for holding the forward fight time button.Visuals - The game looks pretty in a kind of 2010 kind of fidelity and the world is beautifully crafted alas a bit empty.Except for the random little rock you get stuck on while traversing. And when i say random i mean they are everywhere.Audio - The volume/levels of the audio files differ a lot in certain scenes. In the same conversation with 3 different characters it can differ a lot for no apparent reason. None of them is screaming. Also the bg music changes in volume in the same region a lot between restarts of the game.Quality is not that good either. At least for the English dub. Some soundbites feel like they were recorded in a living room.And there is almost an entire chapter without the dub altogether. The files seem to be missing. Verifying game files did nothing there.Story - is entirely forgettable and i regret that this is so. It starts out strong but gets bland fast until it gets rushed all of a sudden. Some story lines don't get resolved properly and just stop. And that is not just the side quest. This applies to the main story line.It felt stitched together at the last minute and some research shows that in the last major update it got changed. The original Prologue was replaced, cut up and reused as flashbacks. It does not work one bit this way. (most likely not even before)But it gives you a nice bug where you are not shown in the appropriate clothes and weapon and keep your current equipment skills and level. It makes your one character way overpowered and breaks the story.Crafting - is a mess. Craft able weapons are way to overpowered. You get recipes for weapons and some armor way before you have any chance of getting the materials. The crafting menu just does not work with controller. m&k works flawless but only when applied in the settings. Button prompts do not change when seamless swapping between mouse and controller.Combat - wants you to think it is more tactical than it is. You fight in a hex grid, can only use predetermined items with the characters, can setup starting positions of the tanks and casters, you can interrupt casts and get interrupted. But at the end of the day you can just brute force the fights even on nightmare without ever using a single item.If this review has not determined you yet: have at it. Easy game to get 100% of the achievements in and there is rly no other reason to touch this mess. I hope I could help. GL & HF

_childDocuments_.review: is an underrated turn-based JRPG with gorgeous environments, enjoyable battle system, on point voice acting, intriguing story and MMO-style crafting system. Combat takes place on honeycomb-style grids with ancient artifacts on spaces that passively boost stats or deliver devastating attacks that damage multiple spaces. The battles are turn-based and actions have a casting time before they can be used. Character abilities and stat enhancements are tied to their weapons by attaching crystals to them. Each weapon has its own crystal grid which unlocks as the weapon levels up similar to the Sphere Grid system from Final Fantasy X. New weapons, potions and armor can be crafted by gathering items from the environments or from monster drops. The story starts off slow with only two playable characters for the first few hours but other characters eventually join. The dialogue and interaction between the characters are often humorous which makes the story more enjoyable. Puzzles utilizing the same honeycomb-style grid mechanic are used at some locations to change up the gameplay. There are many side quest, optional puzzles that are challenging and collectibles scattered throughout the world which greatly extends the play time. Similarly to the Chocobo in final fantasy, you can ride an adorable cat creature (nekaroo) at any time by pressing "T" on the keyboard. For most of the game I did not know this as there were no clear indication (unless it was mention during the tutorial). It is obvious this game is inspired by the best entries in the Final Fantasy series and other popular JRPG.  This is my favorite indie JRPG that I have played thus far and impressed that only a 9 person team built such a beautiful world. If only there was a photo-mode to compliment the stunning vistas. [9/10]

_childDocuments_.review: Two words: Aggressively mediocreIt's as if the devs, lacking any idea of what they wanted to create, what they wanted the player to experience, just looked at what other games were doing and threw that stuff in the their game because "that's what games have".  Then, lacking any ideas for characters, or plot, or setting, borrowed heavily from every boring, overplayed, predictable, stale trope they could think of.The game doesn't have any glaring flaws, or massive game-breaking bugs or anything; it's not even close to the worst game I've ever played, for sure.  It's the JRPG equivalent of a big bowl of plain oatmeal - it's fine, I guess, but I wouldn't recommend it to anyone, unless they outright asked for something "boring, but serviceable".

_childDocuments_.review: 10APR2019 early alpha reviewI bought this game on kickstarter 2-3 years ago so I was ecstatic when the beginning of the product was finally released. The game currently includes the first two chapters of the story. I played for 7 hours and I estimate that I'm around 75% done with the story. Doing all of the current content probably takes 15-25 hours (this is an estimate. I have not done it yet.)Story: Decent setup for a story so far. The game has an overarching advanced civilization vs humans theme. The problem right now is that you don't see any of the war or advanced civilization in the first two chapters. This makes it difficult to rate.Characters: I really like the interactions between Daryon and Myrra. The characters have depth and are interesting but time will tell if they are dynamic or static as more content gets released.World: The game is open world and the level design is really nice. One gripe that I have here is that there is an overabundance of resources to gather on the map. It ends up degenerating into you only gathering the things that you happen to walk by and still have plenty of materials unless you are crafting several times to get equipment with the stats that you want. On the overworld, all enemies are very easily avoided by sprinting around them. This is good and bad. For one, you can just run into areas much higher level than you later in the game if it stays the same but on the other hand running around the world map isn't a huge grind.Combat: This is where the game shines. The combat is fresh and done on a hexagon grid system. This allows you to strategically move characters around (at the cost of not attacking) to outrange certain enemy attacks. There are also several things that help on the battle field like crystals (that give various buffs if you stand near them) or weapons that you can launch attacks from if you happen to be near them. Enemies have a pokemon style set of weaknesses and resistances to various elements (I think there are 8 but I have only discovered 6 so far. Thunder, water, ice, fire, earth, poison). These resistances and weaknesses are discovered as you use elemental attacks against them and displayed nicely over there head so you can reference it in later battles. Enemies have unique skills that they use to their advantage (such as copying spells that you cast or doing a directional AOE attack and then moving 2 tiles in that direction). One thing that I don't like is that spells are expensive to cast and the party full heals after each combat. This turns short battles into nuking opponents with spells and long battles into battles of attrition.  Quests: The game has a hunt system that contains more of the generic quests (kill x enemies, kill this big enemy, collect x things) and there are also events that are fairly generic (help injured traveler with item, save person from animal attack) but the side quests usually have a good story and depth. Some quests also have decisions that you can make that affect the outcome of the quest. Bugs: In 7 hours, the game has not crashed and there have been no gamebreaking bugs so it is already better than fallout 3. That being said, the game still has numerous bugs. If you want a good feel of what they are, visit the technical part of the steam forum. Ones that I have frequently are audio and sprites in the overworld appearing when they should or disappearing (never enemies thankfully). Some people have experienced significant bugs such as characters disappearing from your party or the game being uncompletable. The game has a bug reporting system that I like to use for easily explained bugs but ones that require a screenshot or video I prefer to post on the steam forum. I expect this to get better over time but as more content is released there will likely be setbacks.All in all I am extremely excited for the rest of the game to come out.

_childDocuments_.review: Game overall is easy enough to complete and I loved the fact that if you somehow loose a fight the game doesn't put you back to the menu making you lost progress because you were overzealous or lost against a boss etc... you just get back before initiating the fight.Tutorial level is slow especially when you don't know you can change the speed. you just spam attack against a target dummy. It also makes you experiences what a full party feels like which is great but the game makes you go through HALF of it with only 2 characters and you get a full party 75% into it.Now for the story I have a lot of mixed feelings, there are strong moments but to me none were because of the main villain in fact I would say he is the weakest part of the story overall. I loved the interactions between the siblings and it is sad the future party members don't get as much in terms of developments and bonding especially when it comes to the 4th party member who don't get much to do and now that I think about it, the reason we came to said party member has yet to be done which is funny as the game is over before that.Game really is focused on the siblings and what their initial goal is, if its not related then it is explained at surface level leaving you not caring about it.That being said, this game is a love letter to the genre with interesting design and is a huge accomplishment to be proud of as a small team developper. I would love to see a sequel or just the storyboard for what is supposed to happen next.Curses the red widow...

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of turn-based combat games, this one is very lackluster.+Graphics are nice along with the environments+Story isn't bad+Not a bad variety of enemies.~I didn't run into a ton, but there was definitely a non-negligible amount of bugs. I ran into one where a character disappeared for multiple fights including a boss fight that's apparently a common bug. If i was playing on anything other than easy I don't think I could've completed it.-World is pretty empty even though it looks nice-Crafting is skin deep, components are way too hard to find, and by the time you find them the item is usually useless-Lots of running around to get from place to place and the fast travel system isnt great.-Limited amount of spells/attacks and the way to get them is awkward at best.-The crystal system sucks.-Leveling up, everything is automatic. _childDocuments_.review: I'll give this game a gentle recommendation, but only if you like somewhat "mixed reception" PS3 era RPG games like White Knight Chronicles, Folklore, Drakengard 3, Resonance of Fate and Star Ocean Last Hope.  If you still enjoyed those kinds of games despite certain iffy aspects of them, you'll probably really like Edge of Eternity too.It's a very fun turn based JRPG, which feels in the spirit of those kinds of PS3 era JRPGs.  It definitely feels mid budget, and not an AAA experience, but it also feels like the devs did the most they could with what resources they had available to them.  Certain aspects like the fluidity of combat and the overall look and feel of the world come across as very highly polished and well-done, while other aspects like animations and the battle camera feel a little janky or unfinished.  There are also some typos and grammatical errors, not enough to take you out of the game, but enough to make it feel hastily written and not edited.  That said, the writing and story quality itself is actually pretty good, the characters are likeable.So, if you like turn based combat, anime style character design, and some or most of the games I initially listed, I almost guarantee you'll like this game.  If you looked at that game list and said "ew, no" then this probably will elicit the same reaction.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game. Not perfect, but certainly worthwhile. The story is great and I hope it gets enough love for us to see a sequel in the future.The developers were clearly inspired by other games, but I also noticed that they had actively worked to solve problems common in other games (like accidentally selecting a dialogue option when going through dialogue a little too quick). The gameplay is smooth and fun, and the dialogue is cheeky and sarcastic as it dances along the line of breaking willing suspension of disbelief without ever quite crossing.The script could use a proofread, and there are a couple minor points where I felt like a change had been made in the game and it was missed in some of the dialogue. My one mechanical complaint is that a few of the menu systems were a bit clunky in their operation. There was nothing that couldn't be fixed by backing out and going back in, but there were times I got a little frustrated that I had to go through extra steps to do what I wanted. My one gameplay complaint is that the crafting system felt time consuming and pointless because you could simply buy all the ingredients you needed - so, I spent a bunch of time running between crafting tables and stores when I feel like I could have just bought the completed object (or had a much simpler system).

_childDocuments_.review: Back in December 2018, I posted one of the very first reviews for the Early Access of the game.  I don't know what the developers were feeling, but it's a completely different game than it was.  Some of this is for the good and some isn't.  However, I still can't recommend this game, because I ran into a game-breaking glitch right in the first town.I mean I'm talking Xbox 360 Enchanted Arms type graphics.  Nowhere near as picture perfect as the environments.  Which is bizarre.  I haven't even mentioned yet the horrible lip sync, which I could live with if the graphics and the movements of the characters weren't so bad.  It's like watching mannequins held up by strings like puppets trying to talk.  So the faces are improved, yes.  But now animation is jacked up.  No emotions, no sync with voice acting, nothing.  This has been almost 4 years and they still haven't perfected this.  I'll give them at least partial credit for the fact that the faces no longer look blatantly like mannequins, but I was left dissatisfied at the general appearance of everyone still.There's potential here but it feels like they tried to do too much.  Fonts are way too small - like Shadowrun Returns small - and the menu is just way too busy and confusing.  Definitely need to go back to the drawing board on that angular design because it's not appealing on a TV unless you drop the res down to 720p.  Significantly improved, much better, scaling options to be able to read fonts, etc.  Still not a fan of the battle grid but it's not a detriment.Then there's the battle engine.  Someone didn't get the memo, but the first boss battle, you're limited in what you can do.  It tells you to do something but doesn't give you the command.  The whole "get hit and lose your casting" got annoying REAL fast.  But then you go to the basic enemy after and all of a sudden there's a MOVE command that allows you to move your caster behind your main character, keeping them largely safe from this attack.  Would have been nice to have that command against the boss!Unfortunately I've got none, because this is where I ran into the game-breaking bug: in the first town, I got the bag from the girl waiting, then I was told to access the menu to equip a crystal.  I remember this; so I went ahead and did so.  It then told me to LB/RB to switch to Selene.  Problem is, Selene hadn't joined yet.  This definitely didn't happen the first time I played or the second; and I have no idea why the game wasn't checking for sequences, but I basically couldn't get past this because you can't back out of the menu (It's locked into tutorial mode - and BTW, not a fan of games that don't let you skip tutorials as that would have let me solve the issue).The game is also on rails, and without a map you're not really getting lost, but running into walls got old fast.At least for as far as I got, I never got the feeling of being on rails that much.  Certainly had corridors but nowhere near as much as I remembered.I bought the game to support the developer as they work through this process.  You could have a sleeper hit on your hands.  Just don't overthink it.It's obvious they care about the game as they've been patching it for years.  My concern is, at some point the wrong things are getting tweaked. The core gameplay is completely different, so people from EA basically have to start over,and certain things feel like a step back (i.e. the game-breaking bug I mentioned).  But I still recognize they care about the game, and that's worth something; simply that I cannot recommend this when you encounter game-breaking bugs right off the jump.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a ripped off autistic cousin of a final fantasy game. If you are wondering if this is some hidden gem because it's made by indie developer, you're in for a terrible disappointment.Writing and dialogue are laughably bad, animations are stiff, music couldn't be more generic. The battle system and environments aren't too shabby. Open world is a bit bare bones but you can harvest items and find enemies roaming around to battle instead of random encounters. The story and immersion is so chaotic that you'll have no idea what is going on in the world around you. Youll be coming out of a huge battle but none of the townsfolk seem to be affected by the war. Everyone you talk to feels droll and uninspired. Hell even the conversation between Selene and her dying mother feels about as convincing as a conversation about coming out gay to your catholic parents.If you really do feel like trying this game out then either buy it on a sale for 10$ or less, or watch someone play the first 2 hours of it to get a feel for the quality youll be working with. Better yet, buy final fantasy 12 on steam. It's the same type of game but 100x better.

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry guys (Midgar Studio), the game looks beautiful and it feels like you put a lot of effort into it. I feel bad having to give this game a thumbs down. But, well...I originally played your game when you released it in early access a few years ago. I got up to (or close to) the end of the playable area at that time. I have since been looking forward to continuing the story and seeing the game improve. And maybe it has, in some ways that i'm missing.The biggest problem with the game is the pacing of exploration and the generic battles the player engages in during that exploration: It is too slow! I loved FF7 back when it was originally released on CD for the PC back in 1997. I'm talking about the rewards screen that shows up after every battle. Sometimes it takes me longer to get through that after-battle rewards screen than it did to fight the monsters. The game would be better if it could seamlessly transition from the exploration map to the combat grid, and then back to the exploration map, and present the rewards as scroll-away notifications on the side of the screen. If the battle was particularly epic, and/or the loot was particularly epic,  maybe show the after-battle screen.Disclaimer: This is personal preference.1. Exploration. What is the point of sprint energy and team energy and sleeping? There's no risk vs. reward to sleeping. If i want to conserve team energy then i just have to sprint intermittently. Yeah, i get it. But what is the  of forcing me to travel slower. There's no risk vs. reward for sprinting or not sprinting. And, if you're going to have this kind of give-and-take mechanic in your game, there should be. Maybe this is something that becomes apparent much later in the game?2. Exploration. "Squirrel! Squirrel! Squirrel! Bark bark! Shiny!" I'm talking about the harvesting mechanics. I don't blame you for copying this from every other game out there, because if it works why fix it, right. Thing is, this ain't that type of game. This isn't an MMO. In an MMO, if you go out harvesting a bunch of different resources in the wilderness, the risk is that you could get jumped at any time by a monster or hostile player. This game is too linear and too safe for that. Far more significantly: The heroes are on a grand quest. So why do you have them stopping to harvest as if they have all the time in the world? It makes no sense.3. Exploration. The mounts. I'm not going to talk about this. Just... again, why?4. Loot. This is another thing that may make more sense later in the game. But, the loot from the monsters the heroes encounter seems lackluster and grindy. It feels like it lacks significance to the quest and purpose for picking it up. This is a criticism i have of most RPGs theses days, so you all aren't unique in this, but it still applies.5. Side quests / Jobs Board. Again, we're on a grand quest. Why does the game have me (figuratively) out walking the dog, picking up groceries, and collecting 10 boffins to give to farmer Bob? A good way to do side quests is to tie them closely to the character's journey. I'm not asking you to one-up the Dragon Age series or SW Jedi: Fallen Order, yet. I'm just asking for things to make sense in the context of your story.6. Crafting. This one... (exasperated sigh). I  to give feedback that you all can actually use. Maybe in this game. Maybe in your next one. It's just that there's too much to cover. There's too much that's wrong with it. Again, these aren't problems unique to this game, but they're still problems, in my opinion.For example: Crafting new weapons shouldn't be as easy as finding random plans in random boxes out in a field and throwing a few components together. (Why are so many artisans just leaving their boxes all over the place for my heroes to find?!) There's more i could say about the folly of crafting in games like this, but i won't bother unless someone asks me.AND FINALLY:7. The Leveling System. (Again, not just you, but now i'm gonna get on a soapbox.) So, you're telling me that my hero has (or heroes have) been in the military for years, but it wasn't until they left the military and started wandering around the wilderness that they started to gain some levels and do cool stuff?! Really?! Come on. Almost every RPG centers character advancement around this trope. In some rare cases it works really well because there's a solid reason. In most other cases, it is just something the player looks past because its fun to have a power fantasy. No harm there. But many times it doesn't make sense, because it doesn't understand the trope of the Hero's Journey.A couple of easy ways to fix this upfront (that are incredibly difficult if not impossible to implement after the fact) is to either explain the character's suddenly increasing power as being unlocked by a massively traumatic event, or to facilitate it by having the character become aware of places in the world where they can travel to perform a sacred rite. And only when they perform that sacred rite at the designated location do they unlock level 2; and then level 3; and so on, each time in a different place. Maybe something like this happens in this game?I'll probably never know.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a terrible game, it's not bad. I do agree with a lot of the other reviews in the negatives, though. I'm not that far in.This game seems to borrow a lot of elements from Final Fantasy, that's the only JRPG I've really played, so there are some big similarities.It's almost like it's a fan-made Final Fantasy XV, made by a FF fan who didn't like the direction of the game. It seems to borrow some elements from XV, borrow a lot from FF XIV (the MMO) and borrow a lot from FF7. It plays a lot like FFXIV, especially the equipment, crafting, dialogue-heavy story and side questions, the "kill X enemies, bring X to Y" type quests. It's also got a heavy dose of FF7, with the crystal system and combat, the general style and setting of the game also. There's also a bit of FFXV, with the hunt boards, the item collecting, and a bit of the aesthetics as well. One complaint I have, is that the combat is somewhat similar to FFXIII in the recovery. After a fight, you are 100% recovered. This really makes dungeons, etc, kind of a grind. If you can kill 1 group of enemies, the next dozen groups of the same enemy at the same level pose no threat either. You never really wear down from combat over time, so combat is super low risk/low reward. You get a lot more EXP from side quests, and random enemy fights are not really worth the effort. Trying to fight a harder enemy or grinding doesn't really seem to be an effective strategy, the game pace is dictated more by the side quest EXP gains than just random encounters. This is also similar to FFXIV (and probably other MMO's). Field enemies are just decoration or crafting items primarily, the side quests are the main component. Another complaint I saw in the reviews was the lengthy dialogue, and I agree with this one as well. It tends to talk in circles or talk about a situation vaguely, without really describing it. Some times, it would be better just to show a flash back of the situation. The side quests are also a bit wordy, the dialogue is very MMO in that it's trying to be funny or entertaining, but just drags on. I'll probably update this once I'm done the main game, but it's not terrible. It's a decent value if you want a JRPG with modern graphics.

They just basically have two simultaneous storylines that one, don't make any sense, and two, can't even connect. Leveling is just horrible, it takes a while to level up. (Without doing many side quests, you can get to level 35-45 at the end.)Crafting is a bit of a grind, and can take up to several hours to make one item, but I haven't played since before the bestiary update, so things may have changed.As for the price, if you get it, get it on a sale. _childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is about a 6/10 for me. I'm approximately 12 hours in so will review what i have so far.The good:- Crafting system is expansive and unique- the world really is beautifully done, and the areas so far are interesting to look at- the combat system is really well done (FFxFE crossover which i love)- leveling up weapons is a neat concept, and the crystal concept is also fresh- the story is unique and not another beaten dead horse. It feels familiar but not repeated- the resting mechanic is a unique concept. It feels tedious at times but also new and fair- the door puzzles are fun little asides to do and uniquely madeThe bad:- the voice acting and writing at times are extremely horrendous at times. Specifically the prologue, it was such a turn off I considered just dropping the game altogether- the world feels fairly empty, and towns feel overcrowded but with no one to talk to besides merchants- loot has little to no descriptions so it's hard to tell what does what or if things matter- the characters are flat, and seemingly one-dimensional (this may change with story progress). The MC basically looking like a Noctis clone also doesn't help. - leveling up weapons, while fun to see the exp go up, feels pointless and having SUCH a dps drop after obtaining a MORE rare weapon is frustrating- stats are hard to identify. A mechanic where upon leveling up it shows before/after of stats would be great to compare characters as well as actually VIEW progress (thinking of a Fire Emblem type thing).- parts of the world are so massive that i feel like of my 12 hours played, 4 of them have just been running from quest to quest all within the same area, even on a neckaroothe bugs: (it's still early access, so some of these can be forgiven. But some of the bugs were so horrendous it appeared more alpha stage than anything).- characters randomly floating in town for no real reason- the entire floor bugging out, would have to sit afk for a solid 2 minutes before it would eventually render in- the AUDIO bugs, GOD the audio bugs were SO bad. After winning a fight and before the world would load in the audio stutters and goes from 0-100 SO fast. During some puzzles the audio would stutter so badly i muted the game altogether. Playing this game with headphones was impossible and this REALLY needs to be addressed. This game quite genuinely has SO much potential. I really do love the scenery, combat, and story. But there are a lot of issues that people should be aware of before purchasing such as the sometimes gamebreaking bugs, the laughable voice acting, and how meaningless weapons and leveling up can FEEL (even though it isn't).

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME ISN'T WORTH IT!TLDR the plot is underdeveloped and most mysteries remain unexplained at the end, the mechanics are underdeveloped and the final boss has multiple instant death attacks that it uses without proper warning or ways to avoid. All of the mechanics are fine individually, but don't come together properly. Crafted weapons stay viable for 10-15hrs of gameplay until you can unlock the final crafting recipe for a given tree and then you will use that weapon for a similar length of time. The gems attached to these weapons give so many stats that armour choice is meaningless. Upgrading crystals is literally random or at least I couldn't figure out the pattern-you can shuffle stats around before you finish and they are completely different each time.Keyboard and mouse controls feel clunky.The UI for crystals has no sort function whatsoever so finding the right crystal is needlessly painful.The random encounters are okay but can drag on for a bit. The plot sort of improves after the first few chapters but completly nosedives at the end.However the main problem concerns plot, pacing and boss fights. The game introduces you to the archilites at the beginning as an alien race that attacked your planet and spreading a nasty disease called corrosion. Your main characters stated goal is to cure this disease. This is a great hook but the game ends before you even find out what this disease or why it is happening, let alone cure it. All that happens with this plot point is to add to the mystery (it probably isn't the archelites doing). You never find anything out about the archelites at all! Nothing. The main conflict concerns a Saturday morning cartoon villain with no compelling motive for doing anything. It is symptomatic of the plot that a character is introduced in early on, acts as your first companion and then disappears from the game until the end of the plot, you would probably forget about her if it wasn't for the fact that she is the best companion from a mechanical point of view. Boss fights are bad. The best ones merely take a long time to kill, whilst the last two straight up suck. The penultimate boss has an instant death area denial attack-step on the hexes and you die, not take a lot of damage, but just die. This takes up 90% of the map and means that the boss fight is a waiting game until this effect goes away. The final boss fight is worse. The first form (of 3) is simple enough boss fight-high health and defence okay attacks. it's tedious but there are worse fights. Form 2 is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! it has an instant death party wipe spell that can only be avoided by hiding in the shield created when you destroy a crystal. The problem is that shield doesn't last so you have to time killing the crystal-and moving your party into the protected hex with the boss casting this spell. This timing isn't obvious by the way. The 3rd form also has instant death moves and the game gives no warning of this until very late in the piece. This would be okay if the fight had any narrative weight and theaming but it doesn't.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never leaved a review for any game before but this game is made by a small studio and playing it, I could see that they have poured their heart into it.The story of the game was very intriguing, had me asking myself many questions cause I always wanted to see more of it, and couldn't wait to see more of the story. I think they didn't dive much into the background of the archelytes and the silver haired women, but it might be for *SPOILER*, a sequel to the game because of the ending scene after the credits, which I really hope to see. I give it a 8.5/10 (just because of what I mentionned. if a sequel ever arrives with these, I will change that.)The soundtrack was Great, really following the game, environment, emotions, etc. It was really beautiful. I give it a 7.5/10 because there wasn't any songs in the game that hooked me like some soundtracks like Chrono trigger.Characters were very interesting each their own way. They each brought something different to the party and to the story which made everything even more enjoyable. I really got attached to the characters, and the bonds they form between each other as you can see the progression in them throughout the game. I give a 8.5/10Visulay the game is really nice. For a game of a small studio, and not a AAA game, it was really beautiful. Everytime I got somewhere new to explore I would go like "wow.. Its really pretty." And would always try to go around the whole map searching for chests, but also seeing everything of it. I give a 8/10 for the visuals.Battles are freaking amazing. A mix of tactical with turn base. What can we ask for more. They were well polished and I never even found one fight through the game boring or long. Everything was smooth and always fun, even some fights having special mechanics and all. a 9/10The other features of the game like crafting, puzzles, and crystal nodes on weapons are all great. There is only with the weapon nodes that I find the devs should recheck and maybe do some special stuff with nodes, or at least change them a bit so you can have different ways of building your characters. I give a 7.5/10In all I give the game a 8.5/10The game is a hidden gem that I would tell any jrpg fan to buy and play right now. It is truly worth the price. I have 45 hours to beat the game and I havent even done all sidequests. This game is above many AAA titles I played. Just give it a chance and let yourself be charmed by this gem.

If you want to buy an RPG for the tactical combat and monster grind, this game is for you. But if you're interested in a well developed story, this game will piss you off.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. So I've decided to give this a positive recommendation despite it's many faults because the game had a decent, if not all put together, story and it wasn't unenjoyable or overly grindy. Keep in mind, I played my first run on the highest difficulty, so my opinions here are based on *that*. Playing on easier difficulties may result in less busy work.First things first, congrats to any dev team that can put together a game that isn't bad on it's face. That said:The battle system: It's a fun way to pokemon your fights, however the hex movement and placement system is a hinderance and, at times, something that breaks the game. Terrain features prevent hexes from appearing and on certain terrains might fights impossive. Another fact, and this goes along with the other critiques here, it eventually becomes a chore. End game trash mobs have too much HP and not enough weaknesses to exploit making them drawn out and unfun. At this stage of the game, we're looking to clean up and get through to end.Items: Restriction on battle items is only useful if the items *remain useful*. Which they don't By the time you get potion+ or ether+ they are already woefully underpowered. There are no "max" potions for restoratives, so it basically becomes a waste of a turn to get MP for a single spell back, and depending on what you cast, maybe not even that.Weapons and equipment: This system was a nice idea, but executed poorly. By the time you find the top Tier 2 recipes and make those items (which can be done very early) you won't find a weapon ever worth you time via chests or rewards. Armor had almost no variety and you could construct the best of a certain type than you ever could find in a chest or get as a quest reward (except unique armor, which were on the whole not much better) .Gem System: God. I spent more time rolling gems than I did playing the rest of the game. Because I am both a  stubborn bastard and greedy it took me ages to constantly roll for both the stat types I wanted (of which there were only several useful, see Stats). They are 100% RNG with no way to lock a "stat" to be in place for a reroll. On top of that, the stats are rest every time you combine gems, so you'll have to reroll all over if you want to make you gems any strongerStats: There were only several useful stats, and not all could even be boosted either by equipment, gems, or weapon slots. Resolve was absolutely useless to have. There were zero ways to improve this. Additionally, only four stats really mattered in the end: Attack, Magic, Incantation Speed, Speed. Haste was useful if you had sunk enough speed into a character already. Defense was a bit poinltess except on Ysaris, who was the tank and even then his equipment and natural stats already put enough into those that adding more just wasn't necessary. it made mroe sense to build him similarly to Daryon with attack, speed and haste. Magic Defense, well, there wasn't enough magic to worry about. Most spells were easily interrupted by physical attacks. There was enough HP on the characters that mattered that adding it wasn't necessary. There was almost no way to boost MP (except a few trinkets that you could only get through the Lighthouse missions). All-in-all, not alot was done to balance the necessity or usefulness of the stats. But it made it easier to min-max, if you spent enough time rerolling your gems.The story and narrative needed more fleshing out, and less woe-be-me's. If this studio makes a sequel, they'll need to put a lot more though into their mechanics and how they translate to "fun" and engagement. A lot here seems slapshod, but it was still a decently enough entertaining ride despite the criticisms.If you want a relatively simple RPG, go ahead and pick this up on a sale. I can't really recommend paying full price for it.

I do enjoy the relationship between the brother and sister, but the turn base combat system kind of kills the narrative of the story. Although the turn base combat system looks clean, it does not feel necessary. The combat pauses the story and takes a few minuets to finish a battle. I would prefer a live combat system combat system (similar to kingdom hearts) to really have a good flow between story and combat. _childDocuments_.review: I was fairly skeptical buying this game, even with it being $19.99. They advertise being a small team (Currently of 9, project started with a team of 4.) That being said, I was more than pleasantly surprised. First off, just to put this out there, this game (As of the time of writing this review) is currently in Alpha, and has 2 of the chapters released. It's not the final product, and does have much less content than they do plan on releasing. There are still some bugs that they're ironing out, which isn't an issue for me, but it might turn some people away.The combat system is fairly unique, even though it's turn based. The game's cutscenes use in game models, as opposed to being pre-rendered, so they're not as good as some of the AAA title scenes; That being said, they're not bad either.Honestly, this game isn't complete yet, and is still a work in progress. Even so, it's the most fun I've had playing a JRPG in a long time. JRPG's have been a long dead genre to me, as I haven't found the spark of enjoyment I used to have playing them, and this game has something special about it.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate rating this game down because I genuinely enjoyed it but it's been abandoned by the developers / studio leaving a lot of issues. Especially with the New Game + mode. For context...The game has a wide variety of weapons, armour, gem mods and combat layouts.Each character has a specific weapon type and ability list fuelled by a gem functioning system.If you've ever played FFVIII then you know what that means.Armour can be hot swapped among characters but pay attention to the stats.Your biggest grind will be fruits, materials and money.Do NOT start New Game + until you've bought at least 10 of every end game material from the vendors.You will lose access to those materials on a restart and will only be able to use what you've got.The biggest pain you will ever know will be audio and display glitches.However, be mindful that at a "certain point" in the game, you will be faced with some "junky" puzzles where you can only forefit to get past them as that's 1 of several on-going bugs that belongs in the "scrap yard"...You'll figure it out.For all those achievement hunting thrill seekers out there, after completing the main game and switching to NG+ you'll have a challenge for sure but it'll still be doable. Right until The Neckaroo Farm Flashback Fight. That's where your dreams, and mine go to die.You can't skip it. You can't beat it. It's Mandatory. And, It's, TORTURE.The boss fight at current cannot be beaten simply because the scaling is off where the bosses movement speed and damage hasn't been balanced, they're just set to max. Literally. This is a recent glitch in terms of development updates. This fight was possible once upon a time but 1 of the patches broke the encounter and with development abandon this is unlikely to be fixed going forwards.It's sad news for all Edge Hunters out there but alas, it is what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: As with any precious and roughly hewn stone:  With careful study and adjustment, the light can shine through in a truly astounding way.There are some small arenas of discomfort:-Minor visual effects linked to specific spells that (depending on weather) just don't look right.-Certain NPCs are comically under-animated.  Add to this that many are simply not visually appealing.-I played using the Japanese voice over pack; animations often didn't match the dialogue during cutscenes.-Certain fights cause action time to hang.  *This doesn't soft-lock the game*, you always have a button that moves time forward manually.-Certain puzzle fights *do* soft-lock the game when they start, but the devs added a "restart" button to refresh the encounter.  This fixed it every time.-Given that you're working with an ATB-like (Action Time Battle) system, and there's a stat you can stack that's linked to how often a character gets a turn...  Take the time to tweak your stats so you can go faster.  It's pretty much required by the end.With that out of the way, Edge of Eternity is a work of great beauty:The land is extremely detailed and vibrant at all times of day.  There are a wide variety of environments and despite the opening stating outright that advanced technology is part and parcel of the story being told, I was thoroughly lost (and invested) in the authentic fantasy feel of the game.  I found the story fascinating to follow, and I thoroughly enjoyed the ride.Cedric Menendez is to be commended for his splendid orchestral composition.  I had to go looking for which tracks Yasunori Mitsuda contributed to the OST because I simply couldn't tell offhand.The character writing is wonderful, though it is limited initially.  You're stuck with the first two characters for quite a long time; the story has a very long and steady introductory arc through... I want to say chapter III.  Everything beyond that point is an absolute joy.  The ceiling for spectacle was already quite high, but they continually raise it.  There's always something new they want to show you.  Sometimes it's genuinely horrifying; more often, it's breathtaking.  In combat, it's curveball after curveball; testing the limits of their own combat system in innumerable ways.I found the voice work (again, I used the Japanese voice overs) to be excellent.  I can't speak to any others.  Tone and expression was very well chosen, and I found every member of the main cast likeable.Before I forget:  You also get to ride a giant cat.For anyone who enjoys turn-based combat and has a love for reading, strong recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, this game seriously needs an epilepsy warning. There is a segment of the game with an excessive amount of flashing lights, and that segment goes on for a very long time - lasts the entire time you progress a zone in the world map, in fact. I don't have a problem with bright flashes, but this was enough to give even me a headache. If you are susceptible to that sort of thing, then for the sake of your health, stay away from this game.My main gripe with Edge of Eternity is its story. Edge of Eternity's story is an unfocused mess that picks up and then abandons major plot points and plot devices seemingly at random. You go through the entire game being introduced to more and more questions only for all of those questions to be sidelined without so much as a comment from the cast or any of the NPCs in the world - practically none of which change their dialogue from the first time you meet them regardless of how much the world itself changes. To top it all off, absolutely nothing is explained or resolved in the end. Not a single thing. You know almost as much at the end of the game as you did at the beginning. The characters' motivations, goals, and personalities at the end of the game are basically the same as what they were at the beginning/when they join your party. Nothing is achieved. Nothing changes. The entire exercise feels like a waste of time. The game's ending practically screams sequel bait, but not only is a sequel unlikely to ever be made, a sequel would not fix the narrative issues of this game.You can patch out bugs, add in features, and polish gameplay - all of which the devs appear to have plans to do - but you can't fix a story that is inherently broken, and in a JRPG, the story is crucial. For that reason, no matter how much potential this game has, I cannot recommend it.If you don't care about the story or don't mind a story with poor pacing and no resolution, then go for it. The gameplay is decent, if somewhat rough around the edges. The voice acting is superb. There are moments of genuinely well-written dialogue. And the world is pretty to look at, if a little stiff and empty. As my hours played proves, you can also milk a lot of content out of this game if you really try, although most of that was me trying to make heads or tails of the completely unexplained crystal crafting system and grinding to try and min-max my characters to make each of them useful in battle, which is harder than it sounds due to RNG battle missions for RNG crystals with RNG stats that can be crafted and upgraded with RNG skills. Yeah, there's a lot of RNG here.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game's concept.  The battle system is new and different, the character writing is fun, and I don't mind the overall story so far.  But the game is plagued by so many noticeable, one-off bugs that should have been polished out during the lengthy early access period.  I can forgive a lack of polish (and honestly I don't feel that's much of an issue here), but it's a lot more frustrating when you encounter functional bugs that directly impact gameplay.Thankfully so far, these issues can almost always be resolved by restarting the game, and many can be addressed with work-arounds like backing out of a menu and re-entering.  At the end of the day I really appreciate what the devs tried to accomplish, and given that the studio is less than 20 people, they did a great job.  Despite the bugs I still definitely recommend this game.  Just please don't go into this title expecting a flawless experience.I do want to note that the developers are continuing to put out lots of bug fixes post-release, and even though the game is now out of early access they aren't treating the game as done; instead they're continuing to work on improving and polishing the game.  The game also gets bonus points for Ultrawide support and unlocked framerates, which are recurring complaints I've had with other JRPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure this game is for someone but it sure wasn't for me. Gameplay is kinda wonky.  The foundation is there but you spend so much time with only two party members that there's no tactical depth.  Dayron is going to run in, draw aggro, and otherwise hit things with his big sword (sidenote, no idea why people give him so much ♥♥♥♥ about the sword, he is very obviously effective with it.  He's also QUITE FAST for some reason) and he'll pretty much win most encounters on his own because Selene is slow as HECK and has to deal with casting times on top of that.Game's got some secondary systems but they're not really fun to interact with.  Crafting in general was just a pain in the butt.  Despite picking up basically everything shiny off of the ground as I explored the world, I still had to go to the vendor for crafting materials to make equipment (which were generally not really worth the effort for the minor stat upgrades).  Intermediate crafting mats do not need to exist.  Things you pick up should feed directly into useful items. Did not like having to reroll gems for the stats/abilities I wanted (caveat, being able to reroll is better than not being able to re-roll gems but a point buy system or something more predictable would have been better).  Gems are also very impactful on your character's stats.  At the point in the game where I quit, focusing on speed gave Daryon about a 40-50% boost to the attribute just from Gems.  That's kinda ridic(ulous).Leveling up weapons is something that seems interesting but it's just something you kinda work around and deal with until it stops being a problem.I like the idea for the main story.  Two kids going on a real personal quest (that would also coincidentally help most of the world) while some REAL ♥♥♥♥ is going on in the background is very interesting to me.  Unfortunately, it just wasn't enough to hook me.  I've probably got ADHD.  Help me out.Setting's cool.  I like the cat mounts.  You can pet them.  That's good!Graphics are... serviceable.  I will only complain about the shadows.  Did not like them.  Not a big deal, just sort of distracting.I liked the Voice acting.  I keep hearing this is a small studio (I just looked it up, they have 8 people, one of whom is the CEO so really they just have 7 people haha jk (or am I? (I'm not, he's also the lead programmer))) and I understand the challenges that brings.  That doesn't change that the game was really ambitious, included too many extraneous systems (but they're stuck with them now), and just barely fell short of the mark.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like about this game: graphics, sound, combat, semi-open world, character development, voice acting.The negatives are mostly forgivable: long load times, stuttering, clipping, a few crashes, and a horrible crafting system.However, there is one big negative: the central issues in the story are only partly explained, if at all, and some of the explanation given is hard to accept.Although I disliked the final battle and ending a lot, I'm giving it a reluctant thumbs-up, on the strength of the enjoyment I had during the rest of the game.Update 2023-01-18: A recent patch notice said that the final battles boss was made easier to defeat, so I applied the patch and tried again. No soap, even on Easy difficulty. Part of the problem was that I had forgotten a lot of the combat mechanics, and there is no Help to explain them. For example, one of my characters ran out of EP, and nothing I could think of to try replenished it. I looked online and could find nothing either about this, or about how to succeed on the final battle (the only ones I found were all failures). The fact that there is so little helpful material online that players have contributed about this game says something about the game, I think, and it's not good. For these reasons, I debated changing my rating to negative, but in the end decided to leave it.

_childDocuments_.review: I said i'd update my review after putting more hours in, so here you are.The game is quite lovely in fact. The combat is very reminiscent of FFXIII, but still stays unique enough to set itself apart. The advent of crystals that not only change your stats, but also what spells you can use is a fantastic idea, great for allowing customization/optimization of how you play the game. The main character, aesthetically, is a fairly generic JRPG protagonist. Make of that what you will. Personally i see no issue with it. The Protagonist is traveling with his sister, who is a QT spellcaster. the combat in my experience seems to be very well balanced. What with spells that take 1-2 turns having dmg outputs that puts the immediate attacks to shame. Enemies have strengths and weaknesses to certain damage types too. The way the combat and battle system works is also so refreshing. it doesn't just port you over to a themed battlefield for the area you're in, wherever you're engaged BECOMES the battlefield. Speaking of, another unique addition which i found fantastic, was the crystals. Occasionally you can enter a battle on the same hex, or near the same hex, as a crystal of various colors, each with a different benefit (heals you each turn, higher attk, higher def, etc) This is great for tactics and you can lure an enemy to a crystal to tip a battle in your favor. For an alpha that's only a month old (as of this writing) this game feels incredibly polished. I daresay it feels even more polished than plenty of fully released AAA games these days. In fact, you can feel the love and passion the devs put into making this game. Something that i enjoy is supporting a passionate indie dev that knows how to make a good game. I can proudly say this is one such dev. The story, it's there, it's solid, it feels real, it pulls you in. The characters breathe life into it, they feel real, like you could reach out and touch them. Their behaviors and dialogue feel so natural and lifelike, it boosts immersion to an incredible degree. The game isn't perfect, naturally. The animation for your sister, who follows you around, is choppy at best. during one of the cutscenes where they showed a large landscape view, there was a blacked out area as well. These are both very minor bugs though, and for a game still in alpha, this is by far the least severe bugs you can have. If i had to rate this game out of 100, i wouldn't even take points away for that. The game gets regular updates, patches i assume, i just know it updates a lot, which shows the dev's commitment. All small updates though, nothing annoying. This game, all things considered, as in the fact that it's a 9 man dev team, still in alpha and only a month in EA, i'd give this game a solid 100/100 for it's current state given those criteria in mind. Do i recommend this game? Absolutely. Even if you've never like an EA game in your life, this one is so stable and polished for an alpha, i think it'd be the berst starting point for an Early Access noob. If you're a fan of JRPGs this is a must buy, even if it only has i believe the first chapter out rn. More will come, just be patient. Thank you to the devs for putting so much work into a fantastic game and i can't wait to see how it progresses, keep at it!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being one of the 0.5% of players that have gotten all the achievements and generally enjoying the game, I still hesitate to recommend it.  There's a good game buried underneath a ridiculous amount of bugs, glitches, graphical issues, and some questionable design choices, so if you can look past some minor interference it might be worth checking out.  In its current state, which seems like the developers have given up on now as "good enough," I'd probably give it a 6/10.The game is an homage to, and a little bit of a spoof on, the Final Fantasy series and games similar.  As someone that has given up on FF as it's moved away from turn-based combat, fantasy-centric setting, and then party-based combat (last main entry I played was XII), I was happy to see this game go back to how FF used to be.  The story was pretty good and the music was great - nothing innovative, but certainly enjoyable.  I liked most of the characters, they grew on me as the game progressed, and the voice acting was for the most part pretty good.  I think the story pacing and quests were good, but it fell into the usual trap of "unlock new area, do same tasks again."The combat is standard turn-based on hex grid with elemental strength/weakness and buff/debuff.  You activate skills and increase stats by augmenting your weapons with crystals.  I started with Normal mode and after a few hours found it to be ridiculously easy to the point of boredom, so started over on Nightmare mode and it was a little more challenging, but still not that hard.  It's an easy game to learn, there aren't many tricks.  General enemy type is limited and reused a lot, typical for small developers, but the bosses were pretty good.  There wasn't much grinding, which was nice.  It was mostly balanced, but I found myself stacking as much Speed/Haste stat as possible so the enemies wouldn't keep lapping me on turns.Crafting is poorly implemented and rather boring.  Resources aren't balanced well, with the ones you find being too numerous and the ones dropped by enemies being too few.  They throw money at you the whole game, so I ended up buying most materials.  The weapon recipes are crazy slow to start and then they dump like half of them on you at the very end and you get some recipes long before some of mats are unlocked, just pure frustration.  Most crafted weapons are completely useless and a waste of time, it's a really weird progression.  You are able to craft/combine crystals into hybrids, but it takes a lot and is somewhat random, so I never even bothered with it, the ones you get from drops/chests are good enough to get the job done and you change weapons so often you can't really plan out the crystals.The most egregious fault of the game is all the bugs.  Even the opening cut scene has glitched graphics!  For the most part they are minor annoyances.  In my play through I had three bugs that caused me to Alt-F4, one tutorial chest made me force-run into a wall and I couldn't click on anything, the other two were during boss battles where the enemy moved and everything locked up.  The save points and auto-save are pretty robust, so I never lost any real progress, but definitely anger-inducing.  Other than that, numerous graphic issues, so many typos and subtitles not matching voice acting, sound not at the source or crapping out, and your mount gets STUCK ON EVERYTHING.I try to cut indie developers some slack, but it's pretty obvious they took on more than they could handle with this ambitious game.  At the core it's good, but they just didn't finish it.  I don't expect the quality or polish of a AAA game, but geez, at least fix the typos!  Despite the flaws, at least I still enjoyed it, so kudos to them for making it!

_childDocuments_.review: While I'd like to give this game a fairer shake, the realities of the steam refund policy make it impossible to do so, as this game's opening hour or so left such a bad impression that I'd really rather not risk not getting my money back. There doesn't appear to be any particular depth to the combat, less than you'd find in many games decades its senior, certainly. It's turn-based with an overly simplified positioning minigame. Controlling the camera during the zoomed out view of combat is obnoxious, because you have to click and drag to move the camera, but you must go to the edge of the screen and push the camera out instead of having it just move the camera to keep your "anchor point" centered as you'd expect from any other similar panning system. The camera is also reset by basically anything you do, which makes it difficult to actually take in the field in its entirety. The camera bit is mostly a nitpick, there's just nothing to talk about with regards to the combat, because there's nothing there.While the writing in the opening segment feels as though it probably isn't representative of the rest of the game (and to be clear, it would be awful if it did stay that cliched for the rest of its runtime,) the direction of the cutscenes was bad enough to immediately be noticeable, even to someone like me without any knowledge of the subject. It is awkward, often to comical extremes, and makes caring about the initial characters or relating to the main character impossible.To say the character models were jarringly bad would be an understatement. Character proportions look terrible, like characters with entirely different physiques were squished onto identical skeletons. The hands in particular are distracting in how oversized and generally gross they are. The hairstyles are very anime and clash with the rest of the game's visual identity, though it doesn't actually have one. It would not be an exaggeration to say that, at least in the game's opening hour, its presentation is many times worse than it would have been had it been using the kind of graphics you'd expect from a handheld game 20 years ago.I don't want to rag on the graphics too much, because the environments did look good, but the environments are also probably the least important part of this style of game, and it only serves to draw attention to how awful the characters look by comparison. The NPCs in the second area you're introduced to are essentially comedy territory. Most are static, which would be fine, except some of them have talking idle animations sped up at least two times too fast, and one of them had literally nobody in front of her. A town of caffeinated mimes and statues, I suppose. If the game was going to go for this level of realism in its graphics, it needs the animations to match, but it most certainly does not achieve that. I'll say that I think the voice actors seem pretty talented, and I'm sure they'd sound even better further into the story, though I don't know how much of this game is actually voiced. Anywho, this game has shown literally nothing even vaguely attractive in its opening hook, so I'm just gonna refund. If you get this game for free, give it a try, maybe it gets better. Hopefully it gets better.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this yesterday, and have put in nineteen hours already. The game is hard to put down, and for being in an ALPHA state, it feels and plays better than many finished products I've played. Far better, in fact; I've come to realize that labors of love from small dev teams have been the stars of my Steam library; CrossCode, Edge of Eternity, Troubleshooter, et cetera.The brother and sister main characters have quite a bit of banter that I do enjoy hearing, as it reminds you that they are rather close and enjoy ribbing each other from time to time; the characters have character, and aren't afraid to show it, and it's refreshing. The player may forget the grand quest of "go save your mother from the disease that's killing her" - but the characters do not - and I only say the player may forget because there's a very large world to explore.The game is rather polished in a number of areas, and the few bugs I've encountered have been easily forgivable due to... you know, the fact the game is in an early access alpha state. The only times I've gotten frustrated with the game's state are when I came across two unbeatable puzzles due to the kill tiles not letting you move two different characters at the same time, and when there were enemies spawning inside walls. That's precious EXP gone to waste!The game runs fairly smoothly on my slightly older machine. I just entered Chapter 3, and the sequence at the beginning was absolutely amazing, filled with tension - the turrets and environment made for some very satisfying battles! - and paced perfectly - which is a theme I've noticed. The pacing of everything is set just so that right before you start to want something to end, you conclude a section that might otherwise grate on your nerves if it persisted any longer. In short, you will never come to a point where you have complaints about the length of dungeons or story sequences, because they're just long enough that you won't start to dislike an area, but not so short you are left wanting.In short, the quality and polish of this game, for the state it is in, is absolutely superb, and I look forward to playing it more. It's clear from the get-go that much love and care has been put into the game, and I can't help but get sucked into this world-in-progress.I would rate it 10/10 - everything the game has thrown at me has felt *right,* and I'm eager to see where the story goes.

_childDocuments_.review: - The game tries to put together mechanics coming from every RPG in the last decade but fails to make them interesting (that gem system... +10 HP when my guys have 400 each ? +1 speed ? Why ?).- Fights quickly become boring and repetitive.- The dialogs are as cringeworthy as any old JRPG (the voice acting is good though). - WTH with that smartphone-like UI ?- The graphics are a hit and miss : the landscapes are competent/good but the characters are poorly made and awkardly animated.- The world feels dead : you pass trough camps and villages full of standing NPCs doing their generic actions. Soundwise, Baldur's Gate 1 villages seemed more lively... And Yeah, I know, it's a JRPG thing, but do you really feel obligated to copy them in their worst designs ?- And finally, the world building makes very little sense : a super advanced civilization is attacking a world they were uplifting (OK, sounds like an impressive waste of resources but perhaps the last election led to a drastic change in the political landscape of our dear overlord...). The intro clearly states that the war has been going for some time, the world has greatly suffered from the fights and the ennemy is using a bioweapon to genocide the local population.... And in the first 3 hours, I have stumbled on a medieval city standing entirely unprotected, like if nothing happened. How is this even possible ? They have freaking spaceships on the other side, what's stopping them... THE WINDMILLS ?Nope, it's a hard pass for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The expected graphical/optimisation issues that come with early access games is definitely there, the most notable probably being the very rough camera movements - that said, this has not affected the bit I have played so far and unless I run into something game breaking (which doesn't seem to be the case for most people) it is not likely to.The combat feels very classical with a very clean UI and control system. The sector based movement they've added to the traditional ATB turn based is interesting and I look forward to see how they utilize it - and ATBs stop filling when you are choosing actions; thank you Midgar for this.The world is beautiful and I look forward to seeing more of it.The story has an interesting premise, though I would really like to see the exposition dump at the beginning turned into a playable epilogue (or at least the portion where to desert and find your sister)The music by Mitsuda is of coarse fantastic.The weapon gem socket system feels fun and interesting, reminiscent of a combination of the Sphere grid and weapon based skills in FF10.Typically I have little interest in indie rpgs, but I greatly look forward to seeing this game, world and story get fleshed outEnding notes: If you're interested in a final product, I'd definitely hold off as it is still in Alpha and will be awhile - But if you like JRPs best to put this game on your wish list and keep an eye on it. If your interested in playing a great alpha stage JRPG and see how it develops and grows, the product, even in alpha, absolutely feels worth the $20

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for March 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before April 4th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.It is an Indie Final Fantasy which sounds strange.Edge of Eternity is made by Midgar Studios, it was kickstarted in 2015, put into Early Access in 2018, and fully released in 2021, with continued post-release support up until the end of 2022, so far.  This is done by a team that lists only 13 developers in the credits and this game is supposed to have 50 hours of gameplay.  This is essentially a major title, done by a tiny team that tried to aim for the lofty goal of something like Final Fantasy. For the size of the team, this is a massive accomplishment.  This is a huge undertaking, and it seems like they delivered an enormous game.  The combat feels interesting and there are a lot of different systems in the game.  The world has a great feeling you can explore it for quite a bit.  The story feels epically large at times, and it’s pretty obvious there’s going to be a lot to unpack. But that’s also a problem.  The opening has been modified from the original release, and it can be a little inconsistent at times, like the party feeling bad about one person who dies in a cutscene and ignoring the next character who dies in a battle.  The initial release had a cutscene of their reactions, which was probably cut for pacing but it’s so jarring and calous.   This is a game that took 7 years to fully realize and there’s varying quality over that time, but that’s to be expected. Pick this up if you want a JRPG, especially if you want to see one from a smaller studio.  When the writing grabs you this has an interesting premise, but you also will hear odd lines at times.   Combat is going to be the star here, and the world feels like a place I want to explore.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth your time but manage your expectations first. This is an  game so there will be plenty of flaws. Edge of Eternity is a good game but could be better. Good luck in your next game, developer!I bought this game just before they released it out of EA so I had set my expectations appropriately. This game has a lot of potential but is limited by several circumstances that I understand. 1) The game has lots of lore and interesting concepts but the way the narrative represents it is kinda poor. World-building barely exists, then they throw you tons of jargons that they expect you to understand. As a result, I don't even care about the world's history. Comet? Church? The war? Nahhh I just care about my cat.2) The characters are okay. Their interactions are well defined and each have their own traits. But, sometimes it was shown awkwardly in some cutscenes. Ehh minor issues.3) The audio transition between scenes are jarring and sometimes there is no audio at all after teleporting. Very immersion breaking for me.4) The music in the overworld and final boss theme are my favorites. The song in the loading screen would probably be good as well if I could only listen to it before it is abruptly cut out.5) Then the UI/UX. This is what brings the score down the most. The first hour was painful. I missed several treasures because I didn't notice the interaction prompt. Put some background on it please. White color UI does not mesh well with snowy white environment. Then, when you walk to a NPC, you'll see the interaction prompt every time but not sure which NPC is being talked to. So confusing. Next, the map. I need to press every button to know which button to open it. Then, it also does not specify which area is walkable, it just shows everything. Finally, please improve the shop UI. I accidentally sold my gems when I thought I was in the buying section. This caused me to grieve an hour in my bathroom. There are more but it's better to experience it yourself.6) The open-world area is huge, filled with lots of collectibles and monsters. The environment is very pretty but felt too large for nothing. The game does not use the space well and the narrative also just ignores it. They just depend on some quests to use it.7) The combat is interesting at least. The most fun out of this game minus the camera and UI issues. 8) The character animations are as expected. Ehhh it's acceptable.9) I like the character designs and their portraits. Overall, it is a good game but could be better.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hit and miss, but more hit than miss.Remember, this game is made by a small but very passionate and dedicated studio.As the time of writing (10 hours in), the game feels good. I've yet to encounter any bugs actually, there was nothing game breaking or similar happening The Prologue/Intro of the game was actually really well made, I quickly connected with the characters and their witty dialogues.The Open World is really beautiful, but there isn't much to do. Here and there is your odd glowing chest or item you can loot with a few monsters etc. - nothing special there. Traveling this open world tho is ... sorta funny. Let me explain: The way the character runs is odd. Like really odd. Usually the camera is behind the character, but of course while you run around you can pan the camera around. When you do so, pan to either side of the character and you will see what I mean. The characters run like they stubbed their toes, but all 10 of them, consecutively, oh yeah and the floor is made out of sandpaper. It's really odd and makes me laugh. I wish tho there'd be a dedicated jump button. Sometimes you stand in front of small rocks or tiny fences and instead of jumping over them, you have to run around them. Also, while traveling, it would be nice if the characters banter more with each other to lighten the mood a little, that's almost completely not present in the game.Graphical:Like mentioned earlier, it's a beautful game with lots to look at, the foliage is lush, the weather believable and textures look quite sharp ( I play 1080p with all settings to max ).NPC look a bit boring, but that's no surprise tho, why waste time and ressources on NPC you barely look at.Audio:This is a miss for me. I really don't dig it... the fanfare at every end of a battle is kinda lame imo.The music while traveling sets the mood alright, but it just misses that certain catchiness if you know what I mean.The voice-acting is surprisingly well done and sometimes so on point, it really gets to me.Story:Can't say much right now, I think I'm in the middle of finding out what's really happpening.Gameplay:Traveling is mentioned above, TL;DR - World is beautiful, but not much happening at all.The fights are fun, I play on normal difficulty and for me it's just right. The tatical aspect in this genre of video games is refreshing, reminds me a bit of South Park The Fractured But Whole.The companions... well I don't really know. I'm 10 hours in and only now the third character joined the party, but by the looks of it, they will leave rather soon again I guess. The developer stated that there will be around 6 party members in total, I guess they just take their sweet time.So all in all: Yes, I would recommened you this game. Graphics beautiful, Cutscenes and dialogue are well told, combat is fun if you make it challenging and much more. If you're a fan of the old turn based Final Fantasy games and their World settings, this is for you.
