_childDocuments_.review: If I had to use one word to describe Edge of Eternity, it would be Immature. Not in the sense it is "childish," but rather this was very clearly built by amateurs, and it shows at every level. On the surface, this game is pretty neat, but as soon as you wade into the pool, it never goes lower than waist deep at the at the furthest depths you can achieve. Most of it is ankle deep at best. I can't give this game a hard "No," and since Steam has yet to offer a middle ground rating, I do begrudgingly give it a thumbs up. The only reason I'm giving it it a thumbs up is because I would like to see the team behind this game continue to grow and mature their story that they've clearly sequel baited at the end of Edge of Eternity. Frankly, I'm mostly just going to go over my problems with this game, primarily its story. It's a decent looking game with fun enough combat mechanics to keep you engaged, and the banter between the characters is enjoyable. Daryon and Selene interact like siblings and constantly throw playful jabs at each other and genuinely care about their bond with each other. There's nothing either of the wouldn't do for the other and that's a dynamic that's maintained throughout the story. That's really the only positive thing I can say about the story. There will be very minor spoilers beyond this point. The narrative for this game is a mess. It's littered with so many threads that are strung out very early (in the first 10 hours), never fleshed out, then suddenly pop up 45-50 hours later when you're already at the end of the game as if the writing team went "Oh yeah, we need to address that thing we brought up at the start of the game" at the 11th hour. Or they flat out never address threads and just leave it to the implied sequel. Why did the Aliens attack Heryon? Don't know. They came in peace at first, then they went to war. For some reason. And it's been an untold amount of years since the start of the war. And uh, for some reason the Aliens didn't just rolfstomp Heryon's armies with orbital bombardments if they ever tried to build up forces to challenge the aliens. Was there some sort of magic that prevented orbital bombardments from happening? Don't know. It's never mentioned. Hell, the Aliens apparently bombarded one of the continents on the planet at the start of the war, but then suddenly never again? Well, actually an orbital bombardment with nukes becomes a last minute plot point towards the end of the game instead of so, yay I guess?The aliens clearly outclass them on the battlefield even with the people of Heryon having access to magic, but uh, the aliens never seem to do anything to achieve a strategic success? They just seem to fight in some spot on the planet and never use their overwhelming military superiority to do anything meaningful and instead just waste resources and not playing off any of their advantages. And this is pretty much the problem with the narratives throughout this game. This is just one of many. The writing team desperately needed an editor at the start of their story process to go "This story beat isn't structured very well, and here's why" in order to fix the problems before they actually started trying to flesh out the story. Instead, they start off with a story beat, it's not fleshed out very well, and then it doesn't come up through most of the game. Well, it eventually comes up anyways, usually at the most inopportune time or causes a tonal whiplash to what they were going for and it just leaves you scratching your head to wonder why the narrative/story beat was created in the first place. But at least Daryon and Selene's banter is fun. Throughout the game, you gradually pick up more party members, but you don't really get your first permanent addition to your party until 25-30 hours in, and you're practically already halfway through the game by that point so you don't get a whole lot of time to really care about them. There were sidequest characters that got better character arcs than your party members that felt mostly shoehorned in because the game needed to have a party system due to being an attempt to emulate a JRPG. One of your party members was meant to be used as a vehicle to get you from one area of Heryon to another, but the game ends before that ever happens. So uh, hopefully it comes up in the sequel? The story feels like they took an outline, sprinkled some banter between the characters between the outline bullet points, then hoped that was good enough to write a story. If you're here for a well written and fleshed out story, you will be left wanting. There's charming moments, but they're not good enough alone to prop up all the other problems. Also, this game is littered with bugs. All kinds of UI, visual, and audio bugs. It's really jarring when you're supposed to be hearing character voice lines, but for some reason the character audio goes dead except for the sound effects and music, then you maybe hear one word or two from a couple of sentences they're supposed to read off their script. You only know what they're saying because there's captions. I mostly just considered them part of a janky experience given this was made by a small team, but you definitely notice them when they do pop up and it does detract from the overall experience. Overall, this game is was okay. I would give it a barely passing grade because it has an okay enough foundation, but there's not a lot of substance here. The narrative emotional pay offs towards the end of the game aren't super impactful the way the writers hoped it would be because they didn't give the player much of an opportunity to build a rapport with the characters involved nor the story beats. I hope these are criticisms the development team has taken in and learned about so that their next game/installment in this series will be fantastic. I do applaud them at giving it a shot because this kind of stuff is hard and very easy to mess up, and I hope they've learned from the mistakes they've made with this game to improve upon their future endeavours.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is terrible on every level. There is literally nothing good about this steaming turd. The graphics and animations are a pathetic joke. The battle system would be laughable if I didn't pay money for this horrible game. Seriously, one of the worst battle systems ever. I'm at level 20 and I still only have the one melee attack for each character. WTF!? The magic is beyond useless as every spell has a wait time to activate, so you'll always get attacked while waiting for the spell and if it gets a chance to activate it's totally underwhelming. The only way to get spells for anyone is to attach crystals to your weapon. Even the useless magic user has to follow the same rules as the melee character. There is no penalty for not being a magic user, but the penalty is permanent for the magic user because she's less than useless at melee attacks. She's basically a completely useless character unless you like having someone around as fodder. Fast travel is necessary because of the over-sized "open" world. The game is a running simulator. Even with the teleport feature, have fun watching your character running forever to your required location. Have fun finding the teleporters because they're not on the map. If your lucky enough to be close to one, you can see them only on the mini-map. Leveling up seems to have little to no effect on your character. Again, level 20 and it still takes the same effort to kill everything I've been killing up to this point. And only killing them with one basic melee attack over and over and over till you puke. The crystal system is also super useless as you won't be using any of the pointless spells and they also seem to do nothing to your character. They state the added stats to your character but again you can't feel or notice them in any way through battles. It's as if they're telling you how much you're improving without anything actually improving. The mouse pointer is just the regular tiny PC mouse pointer and it gets lost on the screen in every turn for every character for every battle. I enter a battle and have to circle the mouse for about 5-10 seconds to try and find the pointer. Then I can click on the thing I want to attack. This game had to be made by people who never played a game a day in their lives, or it was made by people who wanted revenge on gamers. This is one of the most frustrating and idiotic part of the game. Every fu cking turn for every fu cking character for every fu cking battle, you'll spend more time looking for your mouse pointer. They couldn't even change it to something of their making, maybe something large, colourful, and bloody noticeable, no, just use the computer pointer, a little white arrow lost in a sea of particles. Right, I hope you love particles everywhere. Is this supposed to cover up the horrendous graphics and stiff, unnatural animations? It doesn't, it only camouflages the mouse pointer. It's also a looting simulator. For the OCDer's, every item will set a notification alert on one of the many menu items. It doesn't matter that you have 100 of the items, it'll let you know you picked up another one. I hate these fu cking constant notifications. You'll remove them, which isn't simple either as you have to go into numerous sub-menus to make them disappear, only to have them reappear seconds later because you're picking ♥♥♥♥♥ up constantly. What a fu cking joke. Sometimes there are voluntary bonuses added to a battle, but they don't give you enough time to read them before they disappear and there's no way to see them again. I stopped playing this game and have uninstalled it because it not only one of the worst games ever made it also has zero potential to become anything better.

_childDocuments_.review: So, now that I have finished the game I am updating my review to a recommend, but it's tough to do so. It's pretty rough around the edges but it's charming, the world is beautiful, and I did enjoy the game overall.For the games problems:I didn't find any that kept me from completing the main story but there is one that prevents a side quest from being completed and that is with the crystal fruit collectibles. There's a bug where it makes it impossible get all 100 of them. Fortunately there is a way to be able to console command in the missing fruit so at least I didn't need to start over the whole game to do it. I was around 50 hours in when I found out I had this bug so restarting was not an option for me.There are some graphical glitches, some glitches with the hex grid not working properly, and the special attack animations are pretty bad (the main character's special animation is just awful).On the final phase of the final boss, I did have an issue where one of my ranged party members could not target the adds. I had to run this party member up to the enemies and use an AoE ability that targets the hex instead of the enemy in order to attack them. There is an issue when you replace armor, and sometimes weapons, with a new piece that armor or weapon can just disappear. The cost of crafting endgame armors and weapons is really high if you don't want to grind mobs over and over for the mats and not having those old armors and swords to sell really hurts the in game wallet. Fortunately this seems fixable with a reload of a save file. It doesn't give the armor or weapon back if you save and reload after it disappeared so you need to reload a save file before you lost it if you want it back.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this at about 10 hours in to the game so here you go.This game is amazing for such a small team, there are so many other games i have bought and played but not been immersed in as fully as i have with this one, i have had to drag myself off of this as i have completed the first chapter and i don't want to burn through the game to quickly. The pricing i feel is spot on and well worth every penny for an early access game that is this good, of course it isn't going to be perfectly smooth just yet but i personally haven't experienced any bugs yet and i haven't had to use the unstuck tool either which i though was a great addition.At first i didn't think i was going to like the battle system but now i love it, you can see why its the way it is and adds variety to the attacks and the ability to form some sort of strategy. The loot system is pretty good but they don't shower you in shiny golden armour pieces or the spear of destiny which i think is to get you to use the crafting system and find other ways to get powerful equipment.overall 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on the day it went EA. However, I waited until the finished product to play it. I just finished with 91% of the achievements completed. The last few I couldn't be bothered with.  Onto the review itself.The best way to sum it up: This is a game of unrealized potential.All elements to make a great RPG are there, but most of them are unfinished. The battle system is the perfect example. It has many elements that could be great such as back stabs, positioning, elemental magic resistances, and etc. But ultimately none of them matter. The difficult is too easy to make any of this matter, even with everything cranked to the max, by the end of the game Daryon is only going to use Armor Breaker and Shadowstep. The grid system itself was underutilized. Other than a few boss fights, positioning never matter. Equipment progression is partially left up to RNG (depending on what the cat finds). And I only upgraded armor once... I played mostly on the 'hard' difficulty. The crystal system is neat, but seems unfinished. It never seems to make a huge different as no matter what path you pick you're just gonna min/max anyways.The story is largely unfinished. It quite literally end on a cliff hanger with the last words of the game being, "The war isn't over yet." A lot of character development is forced. For example, most of Selene's development is in the last few hours of the game and still leaves a lot to imagination. But I  must say Yosirius was a great character in terms of development, albeit a bit fast.The music, most of the music is great. Then... for some reason halfway through the game the battle theme changes to this annoying track.The environment was annoying at best. Nothing stood out as neat or imaginative, rather a bit of seemed misplaced. The worst was running through the lava area and the jungle and it randomly starts snowing in these environments. The side quests in this game are terrible and boring. "Find this," "Beat this," and "Gather this" with very little else.Was my time investment worth it? Sometimes. My enjoyment declined as the game progressed.Can I recommend Edge of Eternity? No, not currently. I think Midgar Studios needs to take a step back and decide what they want this game to be. The ending says there will be more free content and that might address many of the concerns I have.It should be noted that Midgar Studio is an extremely small studio and they accomplished a lot. They should be proud of what they made, but ultimately studio size and merit are irrelevant to player joy.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid, tactical, turn-based combat; immersive world-building; well-written and will-acted characters; expansive overworld; multiple sidequests; customizable abilities: this game has a LOT going for it. Yes, there are some rough edges. The shopping, crafting, and weapon customizing UI could be cleaner, for example, and there are some clipping and camera glitches. The game's pace is also surprisingly slow, though I found this to be a positive as I could really immerse myself in the game's world. Ultimately, this is a solid RPG whose strengths FAR outweigh its flaws. If the game's description sounds at all interesting to you, definitely check it out!

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, just know you won't get much of an ending. The turn-based grid combat system is fun for the most part, although a bit easy (might want to play on hard right off). The crystal/weapon system seems off. _childDocuments_.review: I don’t write reviews very often because I barely have enough time to play the games I want to play, much less write about them. After spending a solid nine hours in the game so far, completing the first chapter and checking out the second major city you come upon in the main story, I felt compelled to give these developers a positive review. I am quite impressed by what a team of nine people have put together here. The level of quality on display is what you would expect from a big studio. Sure, there are a few rough edges here and there, but it’s nine people and the game is in the beta phase of early access.The bottom line is, if you love JRPGs and Final Fantasy games in particular, then you will enjoy this game. The developer team clearly draws inspiration from Final Fantasy. They named themselves Midgar studio after all. And this game oozes the Final Fantasy vibe from the visuals, which are beautiful, to the soundtrack, which is outstanding. Using a modified version of the active battle system, they have incorporated hex-based movement into the combat which adds a level of tactical decision making into the mix.The dialog writing is a level above the standard minimum exposition required to move the story along. Touching on serious themes in ways that are sometimes deep and profound while injecting humor from time to time so as not to become too heavy. The brother/sister main character’s relationship is handled well and draws the player in, as does their main quest. Overall, the writing is consistently intelligent and the voice acted parts are professional level.Basically, Square-Enix should hire this group right away as this game feels more like a Final Fantasy game than some actual Final Fantasy games and from what I have seen they continue to work hard on what is obviously a labor of love. This is one early access game I do not feel bad about spending money on and I look forward to what these developers have yet to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Here I was thinking I was losing my love for games... I've searched for game after game trying to find something to peak my interest and game after game I was disappointed... That is until I played Edge of Eternity.Don't get me wrong, with this great game comes more cons than pros however, unless these cons really bug you, I say purchase the game and fall in love with it as I did.PROS:- Visually stunning: I can't stop taking screen shots!-Combat system is easy: Games are getting too intense in adding 700 different options, this is pretty simple and straight to the point-No tutorial needed: If you're a gamer you can just jump right in and you get the hang of things pretty quick-Harvesting is fun and materials aren't hard to come by: Simple as thatCONS:-Cross eyed characters: Literally every characters eyes are like chameleons in this game, they all need a good eye re-work as it's super quick robotic movement and most of the time their eyes are crossed-Items need explanations: Most items you have to look up online as there aren't many explanations, and this can get tedious as it's a newer game and there aren't many answers out there-Still confused with MP on Daryon: After a few moves he loses all MP and can't attack anymore. Ether can't refill it, and he just sits there. Not sure how to fix that.- Unnecessary running, there's a lot of it: once you finish a quest you need to run back to the person or board you grabbed it from. There are teleport stations which are helpful however, a quick fix would to just have a "quest complete" pop up. -Voice acting It's pretty bad: I understand it's not a AAA title, but it really makes the game feel corny at times just listening to the characters talk.-Combat: Sometimes enemies get about 7 attacks in a row while I only get 1, still very confused on how that happens.I know it's still a work in progress and I haven't even come close to beating the game yet. I will add more as I progress, so far I am enjoying it, it's just some of the little things that would need a good fix before sending it out of alpha!

_childDocuments_.review: The best words to describe this game are "comforting" and "relaxing". It doesn't do anything too crazy within the JRPG genre, but that's ok...8/10I think the unfortunate problem this game has is that it looks . I think people see the gorgeous graphics and the beautiful world and they assume it's an AAA game made by a studio with tens of millions of dollars behind them. This is an INDIE game made by a SMALL studio. Another unfortunate problem is that during Early Access it had a ton of bugs and people had difficulty running the game well or at all and got hurt by bad reviews early on. Then for some reason, it was pushed into full release probably before it was ready. This led to a whole host of more problems with complaints about the game not having enough depth as well as persistent bugs. If you look at their 2021 and 2022 ,  the truth is this game probably shouldn't have come out until 2023. However, someone has to pay to keep the lights of the studio on and they probably needed to make sure they made some sales. Additionally, I think whenever people see a game that was a funded Kickstarter they are worried it will never actually be released.As for me, since I picked up the game relatively late and didn't even start until Jan 2022, I think I missed all these annoying problems the game originally had. I was able to enjoy a mostly bug-free experience without any optimization issues. I am a little sad that I will miss out on some of the 2022 roadmap things since I don't usually come back to a game after I beat it, but we'll see.Here's the real deal. This is a good JRPG. It has an ok story, a beautiful world, and good enough characters. However, this is definitely not Final Fantasy XVI --- and shouldn't be compared to that. The gameplay is much better than Tales of Arise --- which I still contend is a bad game that is just pretty. However, it does start -very- slow with the inability to move around very quickly for the first few hours of the game. This makes it feel very drawn out early game. Once you get access to a more permanent mount early-mid game, the world opens up more for you. Honestly, I think this was done on purpose. This isn't a game that is made to "sprint to the finish". It's obvious to me that the devs want you to enjoy the world. It's ok to get lost and backtrack and do some side quests and some bounties and other stuff. You are expected to want to craft things when you can, which can take up some time as well.I spent ~52 hours on this game according to Steam. My save game file says 56 hours though, so 56 hours is probably my true playtime.  I got the majority of the accomplishments just playing the game through casually in my "Main + Extras" style. I enjoyed it a lot. If you are like me and felt Tales of Arise was "missing something" and don't understand how it almost won game of the year --- then Edge of Eternity may be for you. You just need to go into it with these things in mind.Take your time, enjoy the world. You can save anywhere so play a few hours here and there. If you try to do 10 hours in your first sitting or something, you won't like it.This isn't a huge studio that is pumping out AAA games with millions of dollars behind them and 100 different teams working on it. This is a small studio that is trying to make its own love letter to JRPGs -- and I think they've succeeded. You will notice some clipping of hair through clothes. Sometimes expressions may seem weird. The camera may do weird stuff at some times. Give them a break. Enjoy the experience.This isn't quite as deep as something like Trails in the Sky First Chapter where it takes 20 hours to build the world. However, the beginning is very slow and you may feel like nothing is happening. You just need to give it time, don't trash it too early. I consider myself pretty patient, but I almost quit the game in the first 10 hours or so from a perceived lack of progress.Edge of Eternity is a good JRPG, which falls just short of being great. That said, it is still worth a play and you can really see the potential this studio has to make another JRPG taking the experiences they learned from this one. I think this game should be considered a success and hope that this studio is given the opportunity to make more games like Edge of Eternity and/or give it a sequel or trilogy or however many continuations it needs. I hate the word "polish", but that was probably what the game needed more of before release... however, that is sometimes only reserved for big studios with the deep pockets to make that happen.

_childDocuments_.review: It went a long way from EA to full release. It definitely has it's quirks and issues, like most games have, but for what little budget was available and for such a small developer team, it's a really good game. The story is intriguing, yet it might not be for everyone (That's true for most stories. There's no book with a common consensus of "I like".) and as far as we know, it's just the beginning. The characters are pretty likeable in their own ways, especially a certain guy you meet in the second 'major' city, and while the setting is rather dark, there are many light-hearted moments, fun conversations and quests. The devs heed the community and are very communicative, which can't be said from many devs these days and later on there will be mod support too, which will help the game tremendously in regards of longevity and perhaps replayability, depending on how the modders are able to add their own stuff to the game. Given the rather constant updates, it's well worth the price and you are sure to get enough bang out of your buck. If you like the game and want to support the devs even more, so this game and it's maybe/probably-sequel become even better with more funds, consider to also buy the cute Nekaroo skin for under 1€ ^^ A bit patience is advised. Don't get too hung up on little issues that are likely to be resolved in the future, else you won't be able to enjoy the game for what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: The first hour of the game is a pain, but it gains momentum after the "exposition" is over. They did a great job on the characters. Although most are leaning into rather annoying stereotypes, they have so much individual features and realism to them that they all are charming in their own way and overgrow those stereotypes. I haven't seen this so well done since the Persona-franchise. Same for sidecharacters and sidequests. Those are really interesting and get you invested. I'm stuck at chapter 5 at the moment and up to this point there is not really a story to talk about. You go with the initiate goal  and that's that. The fact that  is constantly beaten over your head, which is REALLY annoying and a sign of superbad pacing as they clearly have something to tell but are not sure when to reveal what clue. Worldbuilding and design are super interesting even if it's not my cup of tea most of the time. That's perfectly fine. It's original. 10/10 for that alone. What killed this game for me is the technical implementation. Nothing works. Many of the menu-points don't work properly, there are HEAVY loading issues, glitches, bugs etc. It's ignorable at first and you learn to manoeuvre in the menu and make notes for the missing information but the issues grow with your progress. For me personally, it started to frustrate me to much when I got to chapter 4. The game stopped at random to load parts of the environment, NPCs etc, savepoints glitched out and the loading times just ran amok. My PC is surely an over-average build and I have no problems with other games (Detroit become Human, FF15). I'm currently in chapter 5 and the game needs 1-2 Minutes loading time per 5 steps. Every time it is a gamble that something glitches out. I'm currently 73 hours in and played to chapter 5 ONCE. It is a shame that this game ended up as just an other cashgrab Early-Access that was pushed into full release despite being a mess. I highly recommend against buying it until the developers dealt with at least the major issues. (Yes I know that they are a small team and I, like basically everyone who reviewed, think that they had an amazing vision. Unfortunately without an accessable endproduct this vision becomes just waste. The size and origin of the team does not change this.) Please devs, deal with the technical issues. Your game deserves it!

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game and the closest thing to Xenoblade Chronicles on PC except it's less action packed as it's Turn Based. The world and graphics remind me of that and some of the enemies. That's the end of the similarity though. The game is great but damn that ending...I hope the game continues in a second game but I am not so sure as its already been a long time since the game came out and I understand I have finished this in 2024, very late to the party! The game is extremely buggy though, I read online from many people this is the case but I didn't know what they meant as the first half of the game seems to not have many then all of a sudden you reach a certain point and then many bugs happen. A few bugs I can remember: A party member disappeared. I wasn't sure if intentional or not but it felt way too wrong and slow and I could still hear them talking and they had dialogue when we were getting chased by enemies. At the end of this a boss fight which you could tell was set up for 3 party members. I only had 2 and the fight then took me way too long. I did manage to do the fight but it was ridiculously slow. I went on YouTube after to check this fight and sure enough that player had all 3 party members in the fight! Another minor bug in a story cut scene one of my characters had duplicated themselves LOL! Wait, just typing this I am now wondering if this was a bug! HA!! If you play the game you will understand why I am now questioning that, however I 100% think that was a bug but damn that would be clever if it wasn't. In the cut scene my character was there twice. It looked like they were watching themselves. I think it was definitely a bug but this actually makes me question things now knowing what I know of the story lol. Another combat bug I had an enemy on a grid but they were not actually there. They were on another grid but visually they were somewhere else. I had to go around the battle field randomly attacking grids until I found the bugged enemy. That was a little annoying. There's quite often camera and control issues in combat too when it bugs out. Sometimes the game just looked like it was doing nothing for a while and I had to press a lot of buttons, mainly switching the camera view or setting auto battle on for a moment in order to get the game to come back to normal. Very annoying and this one happened quite a lot in the second half of the game.That being said, I forgave the bugs because I really enjoyed the game, characters and story. I still recommend it despite all the bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally came back an want to update  review. It has improved a great deal. I had no issue getting the game to start and run. Gameplay also worked well enough. Things are explained well enough as well. Sadly I still can't recommend the game yet as the sound design and writing at the moment is truly amazingly levels of bad. The first few mins you will be treated with. Exposition. Hi this is my character trait. Final fantasy reference.How odd that trait is nothing like my trait! What is your trait friend? I'm just here to spew exposition and die! *proceeds to die* DON'T WORRY GUYS I'M HERO.So writing not exactly top tier. And it is worse with rather terrible voice acting. Voice cracking, odd moments of enunciation, Sometimes it sounds like they are moving away from the mic so the volume of lines change. Just almost as a whole feel sounds like they all recorded in their closets and I am certain they did not record with each other so it really feels and sounds like they are talking out loud but not really with each other. I did have fun with the gameplay and muting the entire thing helped a great deal. I think the team is clearly working hard and I look forward to updating this review again in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: is bad. It's 3 out of 10, which is the worst kind of bad. 1 out of 10 is bad, but it's obviously and immediately bad. You know within an hour of pressing start that this will not be a good time and can grab a refund immediately. (Or continue, either for laughs or for something to complain about on the internet.) But a 3 out of 10 is constantly on the verge of being good, constantly convincing you that if you give it just one more chance, the devs will surely be able to pull it together. Then the credits roll and you realize you've wasted 70 hours of your life on something that never lived up to it's potential. This is .It starts out okay. The high-quality graphics and sound speak for themselves, and the plot is definitely intriguing at first. The gameplay is standard JPRG fare, heavily influenced by , but with a few new wrinkles. It's nothing revolutionary, but serviceable enough at first. Soon, however, it becomes apparent that the devs have bitten off way more than they can chew.The first problem is the combat system. It uses a version of Active-Time Battle popularized by SNES/PS1 era Squaresoft (now Square-Enix), but on a hex grid with additional considerations. It's supposed to be highly tactical, requiring you to managing formations, positions, elements, the battlefield, and so forth. In reality, the Haste stat is so imbalanced that all other considerations can be ignored. Haste controls how much time there is between a character's turns, so by pumping it up as much as you can, you can throw out a half-dozen attacks in the time it takes an enemy to wind up one. Add in drastically overpowered crafted weapons and a few key buffing spells, and you can faceroll the entire game, turning the battles into a trudge. It got so bad I was at the final boss before I realized that the second-level healing spell was actually really good; I had never needed it due to being able to easily win every fight with a straight-up damage race.The game still could have worked if it served up a good plot, but there, too, the devs had too much ambition for their own good. The initial plot hook and worldbuilding are interesting, but before long subplots start multiplying like rabbits, and most of them are not very interesting. I finished just yesterday, and literally cannot remember what was up with those two bounty hunters that follow you around, or why that loopy priest was out to kill Selene. Several interesting sidequests end anticlimactically. One about empty graves ends abruptly in the middle, with no resolution. Another, regarding a  Nekaroo ranch and Nekaroo races, never actually gets started- an NPC mentions improving the ranch once you've bought it, and a single race is available, but it's never developed beyond that. A whole chapter is spent trying to make friends with a sky pirate so you can fly to a otherwise-unreachable city on her airship, but after the sky pirate joins your party you wind up forgetting about the airship and the plot goes in a completely different direction.Well okay, that last point is actually explainable. Right about the time the sky pirate joins, is the point where Something Ran Out. Maybe money, maybe developer morale, maybe both. Whichever the case, it's fairly obvious that right about then, the developers decided they weren't willing and/or able to work on this game anymore. So the current arc villain is upgraded to Final Boss and the game rushes you through one more chapter, resolving as much as possible through infodumps and perfunctory boss fights, and then rolling credits and throwing in a sequel hook post-credits, just in case. Yeah, I'm thinking no.Is it presumptuous of me to theorize as such? Perhaps. But I've played enough games to know the signs. I didn't even mention some of the lesser problems: the bugs ranging in severity from annoying to hilarious, the characters spotlighted in Kickstarter updates or Steam Trading Cards that never appear in game. And the decay is obvious just in basic level design. The first two chapters throw out interesting little quirks like puzzle shrines, and pseudo-random tabernacle quests. But all these things eventually fall by the wayside, and later levels are primarily large empty spaces filled with optional mobs. All signs point to a game that was far more ambitious than the devs could realize. Too bad, too, because there was a lot of potential. But the bottom line is that  is just not fun. Pity.

_childDocuments_.review: the most important thing to know (especialy looking at steam's 2 hour refund policy)Act 1 and thus the beginng of the game (which takes quite a while depending on your playstyle) is not indicative of the rest of the game and actualy pretty bad. it's hard to put into words how much the general feeling of the game changes once you get past that frist act and hit Jagholm. now, let's pretend act1 doesn't exista) the game looks (still) pretty good for such a small devyes, animations aren't the best and it's no Cyberpunk, but for the genre this is actualy pretty nice looking.the art-design is a tad hit and miss, but there are quite a plenty very nice to look at areas. there's a lot of charm in many areas and weather effects, attack effects, etc. are just the icing on the topb) the plot is not FF7, but again: even not keeping the size of the project in mind; it's good. the writing a tad hit and miss (and the start of the game is just plain bad); but there were quite some moments were i had to smile, and i often enough found myself wanting to know how the plot progresses. many characters and their interactions work quite well.the voice work of the main cast is pretty good, side chars and random voiced actors are downright horrific. there's also a lot, and i do mean a lot of voiced lines, ingame cutscenes including.c) combat starts of downright nausiating boring, but again: after Act 1 it's actualy quite outstanding. you get not just ATB-turnbased combat, but also a hex-board, which increasingly takes placing and zoning into account: moves that kick melee enemies away, planning for attacks hitting multiple hexes, blocking special zones, etc. . the combat maps are also often enough filled with special objects (like healing crystals, or ballistas that hit for tons of damage) which gets often used especialy in boss battles. also every fight got "special rewards" which means you need to do specific tasks to earn special rewards (more cash, specific crafting mats, etc.) which also transitions into the boss battles and while certainly not beeing forced (you can ignore the system) but a nice to have addition.now ad ontop weather conditions which will influence elemental attacks and spells. weather effects that are actualy present in the real game world (for example: it snows, your ice attacks/spells are buffed, while fire-damage is somewhat reduced)i'd defintily rank the combat system as one of the better (even best?) ones in the genre (modern day).d) progression is where the game falls a bit flat to me. you level as you do, but that's about all the progression you get when it comes to character development (no skills, no skill tree, or attributes you chose, old school +1 level). on the other hand weapons you find level aswell, and not just increase in stats, but also unlock more crystal slots. crystals is where much of the progression is at. crystals (miniversion of materia) offer everything from simpel attribute boosts to the actual skills your character use.there's a whole merging-system for crystals, which offers motivation to get more, combine em and get better versions. the difference between plain crystals and crystals you actualy care for is monumental.which leads me to the good about progression in general: attributes matter. speed (atb), incantation speed (how fast you cast), aswell as all other attributes (strength, magic, etc.) can be found everywhere from level ups, to every piece of armor you wear, to crystals and building feels rewarding. often in jrpgs 1 more str doesn't feel like anything, but in EoE you "feel" every attribute increase. e) there's a full fletched crafting system. from the merging and crafting of crystals to pretty much every piece of gear you can carry, usable items and quest related stuff. you get mats from fights (certain enemies drop specific parts), in chests, but also all over the map. close to rocks will be "rockish" materials, find roots near trees, etc. all in all after a very rough start (i found myself more than once close to uninstalling during Act1) i realy like the game. it's a slow starter if there ever has been one, but once i hit Act 2 the game became very entertaining, very charming and just a very enjoyable jrpg in general. is it the best jrpg ever created? no, is at a trashfire like many jrpgs comming out recenetly from bigger publishers (S....)?nope. do i recommend the game: most definitly, but get ready for a rough ride until you hit Jagholm.

_childDocuments_.review: I see a lot of ridiculous people throwing comments like this is a AAA game or better than AAA, which is misleading. For an Indie game with a small team, they have done an impressive work, but no this is nowhere near AAA, yet. Falsely over-complimenting it is not going to help them improve, which is what a game in Alpha needs to do. If this is already AAA, then 50% of the games out there are AAA. The game has good concept in terms of mechanics, but could do with better polishing in execution. The graphic interface is not exactly comfortable, like the symbols above the enemies are pretty small, so you need to focus a little to see them properly. Save point can also be improved by making the save file selected being more obvious, like using an arrow or highlighting a greater portion of it to make it clearer. The tutorial explanation can also be broken down into several steps or pages instead of throwing everything into a picture, which makes it look crowded and messy. The sister AI also gets stuck a little too much when moving around the map.All these may sound like nitpicking, but are what differentiate between professional and amateur execution, when it comes to overall user experience. I can't say much about the story writing as I am not very far into the game yet, but so far the backdrop seems to hold good potential.That being said, it is still very impressive for a game in alpha and I look forward to it being developed fully! You can tell a lot of thoughts have been put into the game mechanics and I like it. Hopefully the developers can keep it up and we can see more good RPG developers from European countries in near future :)

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr most of the thumbs downs are on Early Access with less than an hour of game time in the 1.0+ release.  Ignore them, this game is great, and keeps getting better.This is an incredible feat by a small crew of passionate developers who have listened to their backers every step of the way.  This game shoots for AAA, and comes close but misses by barely an inch.  But for $20-30?  100% worth it!  And they have tons of free content loaded in the pipeline.This game is unique in that it does a good job scratching the MMO Grind itch, and also modernizes the JRPG turn-based  battle system (granted I loved what Square did with FFVII-R, but this is more classical than that).  Seriously, give it a shot.One MAJOR warning I have is don't get stuck picking up all the side quests.  Just progress down the main story (which is REALLY good) and if you need to power level, there are tons of fun opportunities available.  As a completionist myself, I fell prey to this trap, but you'll soon find that there is a near-infinite amount of side quests available at any point to grind out if you want, but you really, REALLY don't need to!  You'll come across them all eventually.  Just pick up the hunting quests from the boards and grab a quest here-and-there, but the Purple Diamond quests aren't needed to be 100% completed.This game is really, really fun!  I'm loving it, and have enjoyed a couple playthroughs already.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very much a throw back to the PS2 and early PS3/Xbox360 era of JRPGs with a twist. First and foremost it is important to note that this game is developed by a small team, I believe the team is only 8 people, so temper your expectations on quality, and expect indie or small AA studio quality, which is fine, the game is great. The world is very vibrate, and unique, it is set in a medieval fantasy world mixed with a scify/cyberpunk theme. You follow two siblings as they look for a cure for their mother, during which you get involved in religious and military politics. Pros: -Beautiful and unique world.-Rich lore, and engaging story lines-Unique Premise - Fantasy world, with technological invaders. Even has Al Bhed like people. -Engaging Combat JRPG with a tactical overlay-Good Performance, had zero crashes and only two areas where my FPS dropped from a stable 100 FPS.-DLSS support-Great music-Rich character creation system-Crafting system-Interesting Side Quests, specifically the later half of the game-Interesting VillainsNegatives-Writing at times can be a bit amateurish-Lots of grinding if you want to stay up to date on crafting-Gem system could've been streamlined a bit so that colors of gems had more meaning-Theia is a rather useless character in combat-Animations can be all over the place-Combat doesn't start really taking advantage of the tactical layer until later in the gameOverall I am really excited and hope the team makes a second game as I think given more time, and resources for a second game, they can improve upon this formula and fix a lot of their issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler alert. If you didn't finish this game or play it yet, don't look at this review. I have mixed feelings about this game. I love RPGs and the trailer to this sounded really awesome. The initial story in the trailer pulled me in, and the prologue (despite its bugs) proved to be a great introduction into the story and world. Unfortunately, the strength of the story does not maintain the momentum we experience in the prologue. Worse, the animation is horrendous. The characters barely move their mouths and it is totally off from what they are saying. Their body language is almost always disconnected from the situation, especially when things get intense. Going back, the story suffers a bit after the prologue. I didn't see an archelites until the end, only for us to find out they are human just like the people who live on this planet. There is no explanation as to why the "space humans" are destroying the "land humans" and then we learn the Corosion never came from the alien humans, so then where did it come from? Who are the gods and why are they dying? Is there some kind of scientific explanation for those gods? If the archelites have an entire armada of spaceships, realistically, they could have enslaved the planet within a couple of days. They are just floating doing nothing and we don't see a single ship until you fight the final boss in space where you see the ships, and then a single beam comes out of the protagonist that just so happens to destroy the entire fleet? I didn't buy that. Also, characters are just as important as the story. You always need to have interesting characters, and I felt most of them were flat and the dialogue between them was mostly stale rather than dynamic. Only once did I laugh, which was when Ysoris heard "hydrogen bombs" and repeated it as "hydrojam" because he like all land humans have no idea what that is. Hopefully they never find out. The story also gets bogged down by a weird mix of archaic English that fits the genre and then we hear slang from our day and age. This is by no means a deal breaker, but too many times I felt the story would get impeded by unnecessary conversations that did nothing for the story. Maybe they were meant to be moments to sprinkle humor, but anytime Derek and Gavin appeared on screen, I just wanted to skip it. Some of the music was good while other tracks were annoying. The world is well designed, beautiful and colorful. This is one of its strengths. However, it also felt a bit hollow at times because we get the sense there is so much more to this world especially since one of your characters is supposedly a sky pirate and yet we never see any airships. We see spaceships in outer space and not once do we see one descend. No sky pirates, no airship to command and explore the world. No boat to sail between continents. There is a lot of potential here, and I did like a bit of the ending. After the credits, there is a hint that there is much more to come. But if the developers by any chance see this review, I implore you to fix all the animations ranging from dialogue, how enemies are defeated, and the stances of the characters. In the end, I do recommend it because I can see they are trying but the developers need to keep improving it.

_childDocuments_.review: Edge of EternityEdge of Eternity is that game where it does a lot of things in a unique and interesting way but falls short on things that are supposed to be basic. The game has a lot of tediousness tied to it. From combat, to roaming the world, from the quest to the progression itself.The graphics looks nice and art reminds me so much of Final Fantasy which I'm guessing where this game is inspired from. You're able to get a Nekaroo (this game's version of Chocobo) later on which makes exploration more fun. The loots and in-game challenges that gives rewards are totally randomized which makes every encounter have something to look forward to.To clear some misconceptions, the game is an open-world but it might not be what you think. It is a linear one with huge open space in each region. The free roam goes into that huge open space where it contains its own rotation of regional events, NPCs that offer quests, and bosses you can test how effective your characters are. It could be a deal breaker to some but, I find roaming in it feels as good as roaming in games that are actually open world.Although the game has levels, Edge of Eternity does it differently. You get crystals with randomized stats and abilities which will build the core gameplay of your character. Each weapon offers a "map" with different colors each corresponding to which crystal you can socket and gain stats or new skills from it. As you level your weapon more by using it in combat some longer nodes are unlocked making space for more crystals to be put in.The "Queue" system is tolerable in first few hours of gameplay but later on it becomes a chore. Moving takes an entire turn in a game that feels like it should've been just a flat out turn-based not tactical. Moving feels cheap when you can just kill them immediately with melee or range attacks depending on the situation. There are fields that give certain amount of bonuses or a new skill to give you an advantage in the fight but those felt unnecessary too as your character abilities will be enough to finish all the fight.Bugs exists here and there. They are not game-breaking nor hinders your progression but it does irk you sometimes. Dying in battle makes some of your quests (including finished ones) disappear. Camera behaving weirdly in such a way that it doesnt give you any information on the battlefield. It also lacks a lot of quality of life improvements such as the interface not being easily understandable at a glance. 12 hours into the game and I still get confuse. You also can only save in specific locations where there are save checkpoints but the game has a feature where you are able to save anywhere. While that removes the inconvenience of running into one, it will still spawn you in the nearest check point from where you saved. This annoys me a lot when I'm inside dungeons or doing something in a specific area and I have to go back there and fight all the spawned monster  for the second time. Overall, the game shows promise and it delivered in a lot of things. I would say it's not for everybody. You can buy the game and if it doesn't click with you for the first few minutes then it's probably not the game that will scratch your JRPG itch.

Because of that, and because of the clear dedication shown by the team, I am updating the review to a good one. I am still not sure if this game should be out of early access (there are bound to be more bugs), but now I get to actually enjoy it and have not run into any other bugs since. Good work, guys!Original Review:I was pretty excited for this one. Followed development for years but decided not to play it until it's actually finished. Now that it's out of early access, I thought it's finally time to play. Yeah... no. Just no.Guys, just because you have finished the story content, that doesn't mean the game deserves to be out of early access. Don't get me wrong, I appreciate what you are doing, and given the fact that you are only a team of 14 people, what you have accomplished is impressive.But that doesn't mean the game is ready for release. In its current state, it's honestly a mess.The prologue was fine. You could tell it's a little rough around the edges (especially the facial animations), but perfectly fine for an Indie game. The only thing that bothered me was that cutscenes would often be overly blurry for no reason at all.But then I got to the intro town, and that's where things started falling apart. NPCs that randomly appear and disappear (all of them, including the one who gives you the letter from Selene), animals that I can walk into, and road textures that are just floating around in the air, following me around. It's a buggy mess, and definitely not finished in any way. I mean honestly, I'm sure you've witnessed the fiasco with the Cyberpunk release, and how it tarnished CDPR's reputation. Do you want that to happen to you?If you ask me, you should put the game back into early access (if Steam allows that) and work to fix it. I see a lot of potential here, but at the moment, this game is simply not finished. Honestly, from what I have played, I wouldn't even call it playable at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has come a long ways in a relatively short time. It definitely has a strong JRPG feel to it. The environments are beautiful and the game play is entertaining. There are tons of resources that you can choose to collect while you're roaming from destination to destination. There are even random events that you can choose to engage in. It almost feels like a single player game with some limited MMO features implemented. At present, it only has the first four chapters available for play. The devs are working to add more content as they go.  I've found that it has minimal obvious glitches which is also a plus.  The encounters have a tactical element to them. You fight on a simple grid and there are even objects that you can position yourself by before engaging in combat. These objects provide various tactical uses during battle. The equipment and especially the crystal system is complex enough to make the game stand out a little bit. It definitely has a little bit of a learning curve to it. Once you've mastered it, you'll be fine though.The maps are large and filled with resources. At times it feels like the encounters are a little sparse though. You can also opt to avoid encounters since you can see them roaming the fields. Now, at times it feels like the combat can get a little easy. It might just be a factor of lucky equipment and crystal drops making it easy at the current point that I'm at. I will admit that it easily tempts you towards stopping and just exploring the maps for resources and battle loot. You can occasionally get conditions that, if you succeed, will grant you bonus loot. In this respect it feels a lot like an Elder Scrolls game with the random wandering.The minor glitches that I've encountered are the occasional graphics hiccup and the sound cutting out in certain spots. You can correct both of these issues by relaunching the game though. I'd certainly like to reserve my final review for when they release the completed product. It is a solid experience though as it stands presently. You almost wouldn't believe that this was an Indy title.

_childDocuments_.review: I’d spent a long time picking my way through the innards of an alien forest on the back of my giant feline steed before I found myself near the ocean. The purple grassy fields and the twisting treelines slowly receded into white sandy shores and tide-carved rock formations. I was glad for the alteration; the unfamiliar forest, like the majority of Edge of Eternity’s locations, are beautiful in their unusualness, resplendent in vibrant, out-of-place colours, but the change in locale meant I was near a fishing village. Here, I could restock on supplies, visit a bounty board, or even craft some new equipment if I’d managed to forage the correct items. The plan was to avoid the new collection of roaming hostile wildlife and head straight there. To establish a new hub; to visit an inn and regain flagging stamina; to see what new plot strokes I could discover. It was a good plan. I didn’t quite see it through.On the shoreline, before the village, stands a solitary jetty sneaking out into the endless ocean. Guarded by a weary fisherman, a girl sits right on the edge, as close to the water as she can get. She hears voices, she tells you, they spoke to her in her dreams. Only the voices belong to the god of the ocean, the purveyor of forgotten thoughts. As such, it’s in their nature to be forgotten, and the girl fears that the fleeting recognition will leave her should she dare dream again. If she forgets, she’s certain the god will cease to be. She’s deathly afraid of what might be lost if she sleeps. She hasn’t slept in days.This isn’t my first JRPG, so I knew where this was heading. There's a small collection of fetch quests littered around the newly discovered area where you’d have to kill X amount of local wildlife, or collect Y from some corner of the beach. And, despite the urgency she placed on how she was struggling to starve off exhaustion, I knew I could wander back late game and pick the side quest back up without any penalty. Despite that, I didn’t. I dropped everything there and then and did all the finicky busywork that was asked of me, including a really painful task about searching down scattered tombstones and memorising their engravings so I could be tested upon them later. But I powered through nonetheless, and I did so because I was captivated by the girl, by the sheer terror in her words and the magnitude of loss should her god be condemned to oblivion.I’m making a point here in case it wasn’t clear. Sometimes, you ride through the turbulence of Eternity’s oft-roughshod gameplay because you’re captivated by the world, the characters, the setting. The effervescent realm of Heryon is not unlike Earth, but has developed a completely different ecosphere, encouraging life we’d otherwise deem impossible. It’s explored by dual protagonists, Daryon and Selene, whose sibling relationship is often the hard focus of many of Eternity’s varied highlights. They bicker about past slights long worn down, or share irrelevant little inside jokes incomprehensible to the rest of the world. Like many other siblings, at their core, they’re very different people who perhaps wouldn’t get on in normal circumstances, but are bonded together because they’re family. Selene’s self-righteous and overbearing, used to getting her own way through weight of intellect and cult of personality. Daryon’s more cynical, more guarded. He’s the prototypical angsty teen in many regards. Only, for a change, he has every reason to be.Rather than gift you a jerky protagonist and then dole out hints as to why they’re such an unlikable prick littered throughout, Edge of Eternity leads with it. Like many young adults, Daryon is conscripted to join the Heryon front line in a war against interstellar invaders. It’s not particularly well matched; the invaders have starships, battle mechs and laser cannons while Team Daryon have melee weapons, giant cat steeds and magic. The odds were already stacked, and then the corrosion came; a rampaging virus that infected any living being. It warped docile wildlife into rampaging monsters, and perverted once picturesque landscapes into gothic nightmare fuel. It took people and it turned them into something… less. Something violent, unthinking and hungry. The opening stages of the game throw all of this and more at Daryon - the desperation and hopelessness on the frontline; the gulf of power between the invaders and the natives; the sweeping undiscriminating cruelty of the corrosion. It changes him. It would change anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 6/1/21 - Added in a few things, also some vague spoilers for the start of the game.Edge of Eternity is a game I've had on my wishlist for a while and kept my eye on as it seemed promising. I obtained it recently and played just over an hour of it. I'm sad to say that it, in my opinion, still only seems promising.The design is quite nice, the team has done a good job on the art and sound. Voice acting is quite nice as well, the added banter to make the characters seem more alive is a welcome addition however there seems to be some varying delay between characters talking (some are slower whilst others sound faster). There's also delay between the what is being said and what the subtitles are saying.However upon starting the game you are thrust into the world and a situation that you (the player) have no time to really react or respond to. Who are these people? What is this place? What is going on? Even as it progresses I was still left wondering what was actually happening, other than the obvious of course. The tutorials could use a little cleaning up, the info boxes take up a large portion of the screen. Combat is a nice change from the usual turn-based however I do hope they adjust how the camera works, being able to use my mousewheel to zoom in and out would be great as well as  the controls of moving the camera felt a little sluggish.Somehow the main character gets himself a new set of armour which I wasn't entirely sure how that happened - one moment he has this uniform and then somehow he's obtained an entirely different set of armour. This isn't really a huge issue, it's just not explained and so is kind of strange.I couldn't find myself becoming interested in the story, the premise is interesting but nothing particularly drew me in to want to keep going. The opening trailer tells you of this sickness/disease(?) and it occurs at the start of the game but doesn't make sense as to how it just appeared and did not effect everyone.Hopefully with some more polish and cleaning of both the gameplay, story and UI and the full release, this game will be fun to play. _childDocuments_.review: Edge of Eternity is a turn-based jrpg set in a world close to being post-apocalyptic.Gameplay:OPEN WORLD: There are two main parts to this game, similar to Pokemon. The main part is the exploration phase, you explore the massive 3D open-world the game has to offer, interacting with npcs, accepting quests, mining or harvesting resources and encountering monsters. BATTLE PHASE: The second phase takes place when the battle scenario starts. The ground is split into hexagons and your characters can stand on the same or different hexagons. it's similar to other turn based games as the characters take turns moving, spamming items, attacking each other, spamming items, using magic and spamming items. So far, only the player can use items, but the opponents also have their own unique set of attacks, magic and skills. They don't simply just mindlessly charge at you and attack. What makes this game unique is the way the turns are split up. Rather than having each character make one action every turn, each person can make one action based on their "speed". A character could attack twice before his friend or his enemy if he/she's turn comes before theirs. It adds a whole new element of strategy for players. Aside from turns, the battlefield also affects the way people fight. Remember the phases I was talking about? During the exploration phase, there's plenty of props and land forms around the map. Initiating battle with a monster near one also adjusts your surroundings to be part of the battlefield in the battle phase. Uselessly pretty crystals on the map suddenly become hexagon spaces that can give buffs or become harmful traps. "Siege weapons" props become controllable weapons of AOE destruction. Incorporating the ever changing map into the battle as a controllable element makes the game a lot more fun and exciting. BOSSES: Most bosses aren't too hard if you know what you're doing. As long as you don't have Selena THE MAGE, tanking the damage and Darion THE TANKY SWORDSMAN hiding behind her you shouldn't have too much trouble. Normal fights and early boss fights usually don't even require the use of items. Every once in a while you might come across an annoying boss that seems hard to beat. Most likely you have to rely on a different strategy to beat them. For example, rather than directly fighting the boss head on, you might have to have the Darion block and spam heal on every turn in order to hold back the minions while Selena spams magic at the boss.....completely ignoring Darion's plight. Yeah I'm a monster.PUZZLES: Throughout the game, there are also simple little puzzles for players to solve. So far, most are optional and the few that are required to progress aren't very difficult or dangerous. Even if you really have a problem with those, the friendly wiki should offer some help. Art: The open world is breathtakingly beautiful, contrasting with heart-achingly tragic background story. The cities/towns are surprisingly large and detailed and natural environment is exotic and dynamic. First, you'll be moving through a large blizzard, next thing you know you end up in a snowy cave. After that, you find yourself on green grasslands below the blazing sun.  Aside from nature, there's also the characters and....... the monsters. The characters are relatively realistic and pretty- and no they don't have massive eyes like anime characters. While I enjoy the anime style art, that doesn't mean EVERYTHING has to be like anime. The monsters are also.....realistic....to a horrifying degree. Lots of people and animals have been infected and are slowly eroding away, in painstaking detail. Some monsters come off as pitiful victims, others come off as horrifying and gross abominations. It goes to show just how scary the Corrosion really is.Story: Most of the story is still in development, but what they have so far is already amazing. Some might call the story cliche, but most of their ideas carry some sort of tragic symbolism to our society. Being assigned to kill a dangerous, yet noble ancient creatures on the brink of extinction, the heart-wrenching duty of soldiers to put down infected/(in modern terms, zombies) who were once their friends and comrades in arms and the never-ending feud in politics even during times of crisis. I recommend doing most or all of the side quests as you advance the main storyline. It's not needed to get to the end, but most of them provide more outlook on the citizens of their world. One quest could be to indirectly discourage a reckless and new kid from joining the army, whereas the kid wants to enlist with his friends in order to avoid the random draft and end up with people he don't know and possibly can't trust. Another quest could be the revival of a forgotten goddess who protects the sweet memories people hold dear from being forgotten. Many quests contain either a sense of longing and solemnity or a note of heartwarming hope.Overall, what makes this game great is the unique battle system and the wonderful storyline. If you enjoy playing a DnD style battle or enjoy a fulfilling plot, this game is definitely for you. I personally believe this game to be 10/10. I'd rate it a 8/10 right now due to certain bugs and flaws, but most of them have been fixed by the developers and lots of new content is being added every few weeks or so. If the full price is too much, then you can wait for the discount, but I personally believe this game is easily worth the full price. Devs, keep up the good work!

I'm not sure how to characterise this and that's really frustrating but I wish it was more...interactive or intuitive I guess. Its serviceable but not great.I liked playing this game but damn I hate the things about it. Maybe in the future it will be great but as it is now, NO.
_childDocuments_.name: Edge Of Eternity

_childDocuments_.review: So on the one hand this game is visually stunning, has a unique and engaging plot, with clever and enjoyable characters.On the other it has some of the worst boss design, useless or worse mechanics, a cliche protagonist at best, nonsensical plot twists, and absolutely cringey dialogue.This game is Jeckle and Hyde.  While the overall effect is positive there are stretches of the game (particularly the survival section of finding Alpharius) that will have you tearing your hair out with how tedious the bosses are, how dumb the characters are, and how poorly paced everything is.  It's like the normal, competent developers just take a break and the z team takes over.That said the overall impact is still positive.  Selene is one of my favorite RPG characters (Darryon is...not, to say the least), a combination of brilliant and arrogant that you almost never see in a priestess character.The storyline is very good and unique where it's good, but it has an amateurish feel to parts where it seems as though plot twists exist solely for the sake of including twists.  Some of the "betrayals"  made me laugh outright at how it was presented.  The dialogue and character development is similarly a mixed bag.  There are some sections of dialogue that sound like they were written by a high school fanfic writer, downright cringey.  Most of it is passable enough though.  The voice acting on the other hand is almost universally very good.So far overall, for all my complaining, it's a good game.  I think the generally quality throughout actually highlights the awful sections and weak points because you see what this game could be.  That said it's easily worth the price and generally quite solid.  Just go in prepared to slog through certain sections.Hopefully they continue to work on boss and quest design as this progresses.  Overall it does feel close but it's going to need some love to reach the next level that it absolutely can be.
_childDocuments_.name: Edge Of Eternity

_childDocuments_.review: I am not sure how to put this game in words. I do like this game a lot despite the numerous BUGS in this game.. Playing this game made me realise how much the DEVS had put their heart and soul into this game but why didnt they clear out the bugs. It would made the game from good to great.  The STORY, the graphics, the environment is surprisingly good and each character does not play the same way which is what i like about this game.  The character dialogue are interesting and wonderfully crafted to make me feel attached to the characters.  Give this game a try and push past the initial parts. It gets better. I would give a 7 / 10 rating.

_childDocuments_.review: 81 hours spent, just finishing msq and all side quests (as much as I can get). RPG and JRPG lover and actively working with game development especially on music and audio (Composing Mixing and Editing)First of all, I can say that I like this game, the concept and fundamental lore is quite interesting.I am really looking forward to what will happen next, and I'll be happy to purchase the Edge of Eternity Part II.BUT, I have to be honest, I can't blindly recommend this game NOW, not like this version 1.2.If you are a RPG and JRPG lover, this project is worth to be supported.If you are a Gamer or Consumer purchasing for experience, you should purchase this game later.Roughly rating:Perspective A - for acknowledging that this is an Indie game with a tiny development crewBasic Lore and Story - 8/10Experience of Storytelling - 5/10Character - 6.5/10Graphics - 8.5/10Music - 8/10Audio - 6/10Battle and Gameplay - 8(concept)/10   6(experience)/10Perspective B - for rating an ordinary commercial RPG gameBasic Lore and Story - 7/10Experience of Storytelling - 3/10Character - 5/10Graphics - 7/10Music - 5/10Audio - 3/10Battle and Gameplay - 6(concept)/10   4(experience)/10I think that the developers should known better than any other that the lack of polishing and so many critical bugs.anyway I'll leave it here while the memory is fresh just in case the developers didn't recognize the problems exists.---POSSIBLE SPOILERS---1 Lore, Storytelling and ExperienceThe Concept of the world is interesting, it's really something, but through out the game there's so many problem that brought down this good start of this fantasy world. The areas and the cities, the organizations, the forces and powers, all of them have to some extent not extraordinary intriguing, but at least worth your notice kind of design and concept, but later on it is neither untold, not extended to what they deserved. The cities are interesting but they are so hollow, like a set of a CM stage and nothing more. It's a pity that they don't have the resources or simply decided not to work on the building of the world lore more. I noticed they have tried to implant some details of the culture the geography though some dialogues, but the execution is really not good. And the poor performance of characters just make it worse.2 Characters and Characters developmentIt is clear that they just don't have the resource of time to make it better.Main Characters are fine, the designs are fine enough. But the cutscenes are just horrible.If I was reading a comic or a vocalized novel, rather than watching those cutscenes, I‘m sure I could have at least 100% much better experience, especially the last chapter. The cutscenes there were so bad there they made me feel so hilarious that completely ruins the story climax for me, such a pity. The lost of some characters was a nice plot, but thanks those hilarious cutscenes, when I should be touched and sad, I was just feeling embarrassed and it leads to unsatisfied.Some behavior of Daryon, the rages through some of the lines, is really annoying and confusing.It seems to be directly caused by the lack of foreshadowing, either there was more happened before or between but no time to make it, or simply that the writing is what it is. The similar experience goes with Alpharius too.NPCs are bad, just hollow, I'd prefer that by cutting down plenty amount of meaningless unnecessary dozens of dialog bubbles NPCs and just focus on a selected few of important NPCs for each area and city, through them goes the side quests, and through those interaction you know the lore the world the culture better, little work much better experience. 3 GraphicsGraphics is good, pretty good, despite of some weird lighting effects, reflections and bugs.The Art design is really doing a good job, better than commercial average good job.Some Japanese commercial RPG developing company should be ashamed of themselves, with their resources and budgets and what they achieved.The only point to be criticized is the lack of systematic or open world designing experience I suppose. or rather insufficient resource or time. For example the world map, It's easy to tell how it was done by "finish area A, draw a path, glue them to area B", But I'm quite sure they can do much better job in the next part.4 Music and AudioMusic is decent and some tracks are just masterpiece, the reason I think we all know, there's no need to discuss the details. I rated 5/10 via commercial game perspective is because the insufficient amount of total track numbers, could use at least 10 to 20 more tracks. SFX is good enough, but still with plenty of polishing to be made.For example the whole set SFX of Fallon’s gunshots, it's unacceptable that they couldn't have done better. VA (I've been constantly switching between JPN and ENG) is fine, though I consider in some cases the problems is due to the game itself rather than the performance miss of VAs, I'm pretty sure the VAs know what they're doing, but they wouldn't know how the game would actually present it. So when it was actually implanted into the game and played as what the game can offer or meant to be, as mentioned above (Story progress and Cutscenes problems), the combined experience is somehow damaged, really a pity.There's also some problem is with the mixing, unnecessary reverb for UI SFXs in caves and cathedrals (I think they've been using Wwise for interactive audio, if so the cleanup and doublechecking work needed will not be that much tiresome as far as I can tell)The DB or volume balancing is not fully standardized. I can tell they did pay attention to this in the early chapters, you can feel that everything is balanced or at least adjusted. I can only suppose that it was the lack of resource and time that they cant afford to keep up to the end. ENG VA balance is not perfect but will do as I can tell.But the JPN VA volume balance is obviously worse than ENG, can use some work here (simply checking the files will do).5 Battle and GameplayATB turn based is good. UI needs much more polishing.Puzzle solving via battle movement is quite refreshing, pity there's just that much and mainly in the first half of the game.I played with gamepad, the most annoying thing is when I'm riding my nekaroo exploring, and fetching resources by the way, since button X determines both Interact and Sprint, it's really just tiring and bad experience. Try it once I think the developers would understand what I mean.  Powerstone? Crystals?  merging is fine, not bad, I think I've spent at least 5/80 hours merging and rerolling perhaps.Crafting is a pain, I really hope I can check my crafting recipe in my menu, it means if I get a new recipe in someplace halfway in a mainstory quest, I dont need to run all the way back and teleport to a crafting desk so I can check that do I need or is it worth it to craft this for the coming boss right now.And I really need to sort the recipes while Armor Crafting, sort by power and sort by body parts, it's a mess now, too messy that I'd rather not bother crafting armor even before final boss fight.6 OverallPlease do better and I know you can and I believe many are looking forward to.
