_childDocuments_.review: After 10 hours some little things just took me out of the game. I get games having weather changes, but this one had it for the sake of having it. Take the starting area for example, a lush beach setting. Sun, sand...then in .5 seconds the entire place is covered in snow..instantly blanketed and the snow is coming down like bullets shot from a gun. It was jarring and unpleasant. Environment is also ticky tacky. In one open sprawling area I was heading to the main gate of a city and I was blocked by a 6" tall fence. It didn't pass my knees. There is no jump in the game so I had to navigate around it. Moving forward a few hundred paces the fence ended at a small...very small rock on the edge of a pillar that was the entrance to where I needed to go. Again-no jump. Backtracking was what I had to do and this small fence took me, and I'm not kidding, 1/3 of the way back across this huge map till I found a break in it.  I get making your game "feel" big, but me having to walk for over 15 minutes to navigate a knee high fence is what just ended it for me. The combat is decent for a turn based RPG. The pacing in it is fine with the small grid based movement for some strategic elements.The music...it was sooo damn quiet I had to go into the settings and turn everything else to 20% and have the music at 100% to even hear it.It's early access and I get there are some bugs, but the environmental navigation, if that fence is any indication, is game breaking and I won't continue knowing things like that await me. They're not challenging, just irritating.
_childDocuments_.name: Edge Of Eternity

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game to give it a try and despite the negative review there's a lot of good in it. The main reason for the negative review is it feels incomplete and a bit shallow for now.Some details below.For me the first thing I noted was voice acting. Now this is a small developer and as far as small developers for sub 30 euro games go the actual quality of the English VA was fine, perfectly acceptable. It could have been better but hey, I've seen 60 euro games with worse. The problem is how little voice acting there is. All the cut scenes have it, great. But then none of the character scenes in inns had it? Why? Those scenes are supposed to be some of the most important for building out your characters and their relationships. This extends to the text boxes you see during gameplay, on occassion they are voiced, most times not. I don't expect voicing for every random NPC or even for the main characters on side quests but I would have at least liked to see all mandatory text boxes have voice over. Another minor ♥♥♥♥♥♥ is that the lip syncing is somewhat off sometimes, but that can be forgiven and is more just worth a mention as a slight detractor.Next is the animation. The biggest thing I hate about it is something so minor it may not even be noticed by all but the eyes. THE EYES! Why do they snap to and frow during cutscenes. One frame they are looking in one place, the next they snap immediately to their next target. It is just a bit jarring. I can forgive the average animation because of all the good points and it's impressive for the size of the development team, but the eyes and by extension the head snapping in cutscenes was one of my biggest pet peeves.Other points are mentioned by many others like the rather cumbersome exploration/sprint system and the harvesting nodes everywhere, the combat results screen being slow and a few glitches with inventory screen (e.g. swapping characters on the equipment screen stops you selecting anything in the next characters screen. You need to leave the screen and go in for each character.)There's many good things like beautiful graphics and seems like a decent story but I am going to wait until the game is more updated and completed to finish it out. I think it may have released out of early access a bit too soon since the roadmap discusses new content and new characters. If I finish it now I'd miss that content so it should not be called a finished game with more story content still to be added.Great potential though
_childDocuments_.name: Edge Of Eternity

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so up to this point I've only finished the opening cave sequence of the game and I have some general feedback on how the game progresses. The entire sequence in the cave leaves me with an overwhelming sense of boredom through exposition. They keep talking about how the sister saved the brother's butt in the caves when they were children which seems like a much more interesting sequence of events than the one we're currently experiencing. This can easily be solved with a playable tutorial/prologue with them as kids going through the cave and the player experiencing what the brother and sister went through for themselves instead of just telling rather than showing. I kept feeling like you were referencing something more interesting and I wanted to see that rather than hear about it happening from the siblings memories. The crystal system is very interesting and I like the way that it makes your characters progress but the tutorial showing how it works isn't clear enough. The first big issue is that the first crystal you get is the wrong color for the first character that pops up on your screen. I understand that the purpose of this is to get the sister to learn the fire spell that opens the rune door to the first mini boss (which because the tutorial was unclear I didn't even understand how I got the fire spell in the first place or why I was able to use it to open the door), but I felt like I was doing something wrong when I tried to give the crystal to the main character and I couldn't put it anywhere. Maybe instead of showing a big wall of text that you expect the player to read in order to understand what the tutorial is showing; you let the sister take over the menu and SHOW you what you need to do and give an explanation as to why you need to do it, because clearly she knows more about what's going on in this world than the person playing this for the first time. This would also clearly explain why she got the fire spell you use to get past the rune door and in the following battle which I didn't even know I had until a few turns in when I pressed the wrong menu button. You could even add in a bit of snarky dialogue like:Brother - "Hey why do you get to use the crystal?"Sister - "Because clearly I'm the only one who knows how to use it :P"On a positive note though the game feels nice to play. The character movement is smooth and responsive and feels good, although the sister did get stuck at the entrance of the cave until the first cutscene started. The combat is really interesting and I enjoy the menu system use on controller, although what pops up on the menu should be changed Eg: Having all attacks show up on the right trigger and the other show a menu of items you can use instead of one trigger showing magic and the other showing physical attacks. The way it is now leaves a lot of accidentally pressing the wrong menu while trying to figure out what to do. I also agree with one of the other reviews here in that the character's should be color coated on the battle screen so they know who they're attacking with instead of accidentally using a physical attack with a caster. From what I've seen so far I'm really impressed with what you guys have here, it looks really pretty and the character designs are very unique. The voice acting isn't half bad and the world feels and looks interesting, at least from what I saw in the first half hour or so of the game. I look forward to seeing how this game progresses. I think it could be a really solid game and I want to see how the story plays out.

_childDocuments_.review: While currently unfinished it gives off a mix of Golden sun and the Final Fantasy series, not bad at all. _childDocuments_.review: If you want to give this game a try because you are to a rpg lover and you know that it have been developed by a small team; go for it, but be prepared for some deceptions.After so much time on it here are the positive points : great landscape variety, voice, some funnies png, some good music tracks, the nekaroos, some battle mecanism (gems, moving on the battlefield), voices, the story backgroundand the negatives points i have noticed : still some non blocking bugs (started to play on 1.0 and then continue on 1.1 until the final boss), the menus (craft weapons or stuff what a pain! ), ennemy focus is sometine not memorized, all the game is not so hard even in normal mode but some fight are harder (protect the jungle village, all fights with waves of ennemies, the last dungeon) and another impossible : the final fight, two evenings i am trying but cannot beat the third transformation of him even in easy mode (should do before the last update which made this battle much much harder) i am level 57 and got the best stuff i can craft and have done all the side quests.It is sad but i will left this game with unanswered questions :(.So in conclusion i had some good times but the end of the game left me not a so good taste,I think the next game of this game studio will be better and i will wait for it :)

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I think this is a solid JRPG from an indie studio and the price is spot on. Its got a decent story and a turn based concept that is fun. I only put 27 hours into the game and probably wont return, I have a lot of other games to play and this one just didnt catch my attention enough.I think the main character is just too strong, maybe im building wrong, but I can usually get 3 attacks off before anyone else in my team. By the end of the boss fight, attacks by my main character will be like 30 to 6. So the combat got a little tedious for me.The Voice Acting isnt the best but it isnt terrible, the story does enough to make me wonder what is going to happen but in the end it wasnt strong enough to make me want to grind through the combat. I dont think the game warrants a negative review, and I believe most people looking for a JRPG will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game and it's developers have done an outstanding job working on this game. I had to stop playing for a while because I kept having to close the game due to bugs. I payed attention, and I was happy, and surprised, to see how often the small team of indie developers updated. I recently started playing again and had a lot better experience. The graphics are definitely a big plus.

_childDocuments_.review: Words alone can not make you understand how good this game is. If you enjoyed the days of turn based tactical RPGs, you will just have to shell out the cash and try this out for yourself. There are some systems that need a good deal of polish, but the pro's greatly out number the cons. The drive to find out what turn the story takes next, kept me awake well after 2 am. I just wanted to know what was going to happen next, and then after that,,,, and more. The world is beautiful. It is not open world exploration and that made me a little sad, but it's not bad either by any means. The game at least in it's current stage is only single player and will probably stay that way, but it's still a very enjoyable  experience.  Combat is very similar to FF12 with a little Suikoden Tactics flavor mixed in.  Just go buy it, you will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game. I recommend it. Nice RPG. Fighting is tactical in a different way. Fun game. Cool characters and story. I like it. Game controls are good. _childDocuments_.review: It is probably the best new game I played in a while. I only dipped my nose into it but that first hour was very eventful. The opening scene to the ending one was all spectacular watching, voice actors are so good to display emotions and meaning. Finally, the story that does not bore me, even though I have seen the likes of this and when I finally entered the world on my own into the first location I had these Fable vibes. It looks nice but is not top notch graphics, I play on maximum settings and my game froze once just before I encountered my first saving portal, luckily game kept an autosave just few minutes before that moment. I just needed to loot all chests again and pick up quests. The combat here is a tactical turn-based, it looks like a solid RPG too with gear I can equip.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought during EA, waited for the release but couldn't get into it.As I have very little game time take it with a pinch of salt. But to me this game illustrate the saying : .You can really tell that the studio lacked the funds (and to a lesser extent the experience) to successfully release such an ambitious project.......nullSorry :-/-Poorly designed, balanced and shallow features (crafting, "skill" crystal).-Poor writing : very cliche and cringy.-Good design for the battles (using t-rpg grid), poor execution resulting in boring samey battles.-Empty world.-Characters models and animation are pretty bad.-Uninspired side missions.I wished the studio would have been a lot more realistic with the project by not going full 3D and trying to make a final fantasy clone game without the budget nor the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to be able to play this game. I feel like if I was able to it would be the kind of game I could easily recommend. But as is even on the absolute lowest settings to the point the game is just a hazy pixely blur the FPS is just beyond unplayable. Maybe a couple frames a second. I5 cpu second gen, gtx 760. I realize its not a powerful computer but I  play far more graphically impressive games are medium to high settings absolutely fine. Which leads me to assume this is an optimization issue or an over reliance on overly complex graphical effects.  Or maybe too many things are trying to load in at once?The cave area works okay enough but when I leave that area the fps just died and it becomes unplayable. _childDocuments_.review: Bought this on sale for 16$, and definitely don't regret it.  Considering this was made by a very small studio, the environments are very impressive. _childDocuments_.review: After playing the first chapter i have to say it realy has potential to be one of the best rpg's of these last couple of years in my opinion. _childDocuments_.name: Edge Of Eternity

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of reviews saying this is the quality of a AAA game. I disagree with those but not by much. The game looks beautiful, the combat animations are phenomenal, the environments look fantastic, combat and UI are intuitive, the tutorial is actually helpful, and all that makes this game incredible impressive for a 9 person team. The only things that make it evident that it isn't a AAA game is that the voice acting isn't great, it's not bad just not always on point, and that the models, as intricate as they are, during cutscenes can be a bit wonky (pupils disappearing, necks stretching weirdly when looking around, just little things like that that wouldn't pass AAA QA).I do highly recommend this game and it's unbelievable  that a 9 person team made this. It's a fantastic game that any fan of Final Fantasy would enjoy and should play.
_childDocuments_.name: Edge Of Eternity

_childDocuments_.review: Couldn't continue playing after the first zone with how bad it is - bad optimization, bad intro, bad options in main screen, bad combat, no tutorial, janky movement and other issues. It might become good later on as it's seems the game has potential, but i doubt it as its a fully released game; if they developed it for one-2 more years, it might have become a good game.for the bad combat, its mainly a problem with camera control issues for me. i like the idea of having sidequests per combat to increase rewards - but at least early on some of the sidequests are impossible to complete. bad options menu - if you're in the main screen and press options, its generating a cursor that isn't in the position of your real cursor, so your real one is invisible, with the only identification is buttons being hoverable.bad intro - the problem is not the first cutscene, but when you're loaded on the ship - everything constantly freezes, stutters and visual skips.early bad exploration - some of the rewards from chests are so bad that you think never to explore and pick up chests; the resources aren't explained and you can't do anything with them.If the developers are watching the reviews, you need serious work on first section, as this is where you're trying to hook your players into the gameI could go on further on the issues I've encountered, but i only played less than 1 hour, and i got this game as part of a bundle i bought - so i won't delve even further.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this by saying I enjoyed the game, but I can not recommend it to anyone. The game's main story is complete, but other content is very clearly unfinished (and it even says as much when you beat the game). The ending does feel very rushed, with a lot of abandoned plot threads that were critical to the story up until the chapter before last - whether that was meant to be sequel bait or the story was rushed to a finish so they could have a "complete" game, I do not know.The developers have not been heard from for roughly a year, since mid 2023, and seem to have abandoned the title. If this game were actively being updated and its content would be finished and its bugs fixed, I would have recommended it as a very ambitious indie JRPG. But as it stands, I cannot.
_childDocuments_.name: Edge Of Eternity

_childDocuments_.review: Great RPG.A remarkable achievement for the number of people working on it (4, recently upped to 9).Note that, as it a very early access, only a small portion of what should be the full game is available right now (although it did take me more than 10 hours to run out of content). It can be argued that it is a bit overpriced for this reason. However, I decided to buy in nonetheless to support the devs, who are very responsive to feedback, and have fixed certain bugs within hours of those bugs being pointed out to them on the forums. They are also very welcoming of suggestions, so you should buy in if you would like to help shape the final game.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally talked about a bug that kept me from progressing for two weeks in my December 2019 review.  It was over a month before it was patched.  I had given up on the game until I decided to try again about a year later.December 2020 Review:I ended up finishing all of the available chapters as of 31December2020.  If you are like me and continued the game from previous save, make sure to play the prologue first.  The game is still buggy, but the performance is improved from a year ago.  I had one major bug that I encountered in Chapter 6.  At one point the party splits after a fight.  You start with two individuals and complete their given task.  Afterward you shift to a cutscene for the other two party members.  The game stalled in the cutscene and crashed.  I thought no big deal, I should be able to use the autosave.  When I loaded the autosave, I started with only the character you get in Chapter 4.  They were trying to do a quest of getting through the mountain with Level 16 enemies.  It was completely wrong.  I had to watch a youtube let's play to figure out that I needed to start from an earlier save.The battle camera is not good when you have enemies on both sides of your party.  During Chapter 5, there is an enclosed area where I struggled with the camera to see the part I had to defeat.  I don't remember having this issue with the camera when I played in December of 2019.  The mini-map doesn't always seem to load and the way markers don't always advance.  Sometimes if you exit and reload the game, the way markers will advance, but not always.The voice acting is good.  I was impressed.  I like the music and the cutscenes as well.  The story is picking up by the end of Chapter 6 and I do want to see what will happen over the last part of the game.  It's impressive that this game is made by a small team.  Hopefully they can make additional improvements before the final release.  I still don't recommend this game because of the different bugs and issues I have encountered.  However, the team has been working on this for almost 6 years (if you count the original kickstarter) and they keep making progress.  I am hopeful and optimistic.December 2019 Review:This is my first time playing an Early Access title.  The concept of the story unfolding over time like a television show seemed like a good idea at first.  I ultimately have not liked it because you keep forgetting the various nuances of the battle system as you stop and start the game.  I wished I would have played it after it was done and optimized.  It does seem like it will be a good game if it gets finished.The developer was upfront about it being buggy and not optimized.  I won't list all of the various crashes or game glitches I have noticed.  They distract but don't ruin the experience.  However, I have run into two different occasions where I couldn't continue due to a bug.  The first occasion was a soft lock where you would win the battle, but it wouldn't progress.  I was lucky that a patch was issued after about two days.  The next occasion I have not been as lucky.  I am in Chapter 4 and can't finish a puzzle due to not having enough turns.  It has been over two weeks and I can't progress.  The developer explained the delay, but still it's been over two weeks.  For 15 - 20 dollars you can purchase other RPGs that are more complete and polished."

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to write a review for this game after reading some negative reviews and the devs' reactions to those.I've been following this game for quite a while, playing Early Access and beta builds. Most of the things in the recent negative reviews are (or used to be) true, even though they mostly depend on personal taste and subjective expectation. Parts of the game  get grindy, the story  Shakespeare, the music  composed by Hans Zimmer, the facial animations  on Square Enix level.But I think that's the point: this game was made by a small studio, not Square Enix, but I've had so much more fun than in several Final Fantasy games or other (J)RPGs. I think the visual quality, the size of the game, the offline-MMO feeling that you get while playing: that's AMAZING for a game from a small studio.The visuals are great, the voice acting in on point, I even liked the humor and sarcasm of certain party members (which I very rarely do in these games). The game shows lots of ideas and ambitions to be beautiful to look at, to do something new and unique that isn't your cookie-cutter JRPG (combat system, equipment, gems, skills) and to include MMO-style aspects like a crafting system, for which you gather ores, herbs, lumber from the environment as well as monster drops.What's most important to me is that you can literally see how much the devs love their game and how much effort they put into it. How very much they appreciate and value community feedback.Shortly after release, they launched a patch to address exactly those issues that were predominantly mentioned in negative reviews, like animation quality and nightmare difficulty scaling.During early access, I submitted feedback on the community page to express some suggestions that would improve the game in my opinion, for example I thought that weapons had some pretty bad scaling, because they lacked a main stat that would reflect the weapon level. Shortly after, I got a dev reply and an update to the beta branch that would include a reworked power stat on weapons. Honestly, I find it awesome to see a dev team looking into community feedback that much and to witness them constantly trying their best to improve the game. Someone complained that special attack animations aren't skippable and I agree, but heck, I can see QoL stuff like that changed within a couple of days, just because the devs read those feedbacks.I love that and think that the devs deserve a lot of praise and support for what they have to offer.Even though I can absolutely see the point in most negative feedbacks here (and upvoted them, because they do indeed point out weaknesses), I believe that the game currently appears underrated and I can only tell you that the fun and appreciation I already had playing the game was totally worth the price tag - and I can't wait to re-play and complete it now that it's released. If you can see the game for what it is and not confuse your expectations with an AAA Final Fantasy that sells for double the price (and then turns out to be FF-XIII-2), you'll find the game amazing, too. If you really dislike certain aspects of the game, I can only suggest to leave some constructive feedback and let the game rest for a while - but do return at a later point. You might be surprised.

The devs have told us to think of this game as an anime with upcoming seasons releasing. Pros:Good character development thus farGreat musicGood voice actingAwesome ambiance and zone designCompelling story hook with a nice blend of fantasy and sci fiHas some unique puzzle solving for lootCons: (take these with a grain of salt...the game is early access)A bit too MMO-like with gathering quests/real time events (but aren't too grindy)Battle is exciting until it isn't. You will be killing a lot of the same or re-skinned woodland creaturesCrystal system is not really a new idea...basically same as materia system from FFVIIA few minor bugs exist: music continuity issues, falling through architecture (game has an unstuck feature luckily), and interactivity with NPCs/objects can be sometimes be wonkytl;dr the game scratches a JRPG itch quite nicely. _childDocuments_.review: In a lot of ways I really miss the older entries of Final Fantasy. Things really haven’t been the same since X. While I do enjoy some of the new entries, there has been such a huge divergence in its formula over the past several entries, it has left a gap which feels like developers are a bit worried about going back. Edge of Eternity really reminds me of those older days, and although it has a few rough edges it definitely scratches the itch.Edge of Eternity starts out like most RPGs. A war is raging between two factions, the inhabitants of the planet Heryon and an “alien” species called the Archelites. The Archelites were friendly at first and even shared their technology with the people of Heryon. Suddenly, for some unknown reason, they decided that they were no longer worthy of the technology and started to attack the people of Heryon. They wiped out entire cities quickly with their advanced technology, and it wasn’t long until they unleashed the worst weapon, the Corrosion. This sounds like a fairly typical story, and it is, but as the story goes on you find out more about the Corrosion, the Archelites, and the military, political, and religious factions on Heryon that adds a bit of spice to the story.You start the game as a soldier name Daryon. He is a member of a squad in Heryon’s army, The Consort. These are the front line troops fighting against the Archelites. You receive a letter from your sister, Selene, who is a priestess of the Sanctorum which is the religious faction on Heryon. Her letter was sent to inform you that your mother has caught the Corrosion and that Selene needs your help in finding a cure before it is too late.Of course, everything goes to hell and there is a surprise attack by the Archelites. This attack nearly kills everyone at the outpost you are stationed at. However, you manage to make your way to a bunker where another Sanctorum priest is trying to perform a ritual called “The Ascendance.” This ritual basically absorbs people and turns them into a giant energy weapon that will destory the Archelites. Your character, Daryon, is then targeted by the ritual but you manage to destroy the crystal that is used to absorb people just in time to save your life. You are the sole survivor of this attack and decide to desert the rest of the Consort to go help your sister and mother.Most of the game you spend as a party of two, Daryon and Selene, but along the way you do meeting other party members to help form a party of four in total. I believe the max amount of characters at any time was 5, but only 4 members could be in the battle. The story has the usual elements of betrayal and politics along the way that do manage to keep the story interesting over its 40 hour run time.The main issue I have with the story is the ending. It just kind of drops off, in a way it feels like we just hit the halfway point. There is obviously a push to provide a sequel or at least expand the game with future content. There are free updates coming soon, but I’m not sure they are expanding the story from this point. So it is possible for this issue to be remedied in a future update.Outside of the main story line, you will come across characters and bounty boards around the world that will provide you with additional side quests. The bounty board quests are the standard fair, kill X amount of X enemy. I took my time and finished every quest from these boards and would say that 99% of them are not worth the time. They give very limited experience and rewards in most cases, but I would use them to level up my weapons. The NPC side quests though are a bit more involved and have minor side stories attached to them which were overall decent. I do wish there were more of a focus on these types of quests outside of the bounty boards, but you usually would complete them while doing the side quests as well.The battle system is one of the highlights for me in the game. As you come across enemies in the world, if you touch them a battle will start. If you can get a pre-emptive strike on the enemy by performing an attack outside you will start the battle with a speed advantage. Once you begin the battle, the map is then divided into a bunch of hexagons. Your characters and the enemies can move around the battlefield and postition themselves to get back attacks and protect other weaker characters with stronger ones. Some characters have abilities and spells that can reach enemies further away and you must position your party to get the most advantage of the map.The battle field also has crystals which can boost the stats of both enemies and your party if you share the space on the field. The battles themselves are turn based, and based on the characters Speed stat they act faster. There are also other stats such as Incantation Speed and Haste which can augment how fast your characters behave such as lowering the time it takes to cast a spells. Spells and abilities also have elemental attributes, buffing, and debuffing effects. You can use these different elements to take advantage of enemies weakness to increase your damage. Finally, when you spells are being cast, normal attacks can interrupt both your or your enemies spells. There is a nice balance to the strength of those abilities and being able to interrupt them.Each character has different pros and cons. Daryon is the agile melee attacker, who has limited access to time spells but has a mix of elemental sword attacks. Selene is your caster, she is weak but can cast powerful spells and provide healing effects to your party. You also meet a few ranged attackers, using either guns or throwing knives. A defensive character that is slow but can attack all enemies in a space and taunt enemies to protect the party from attacks. Lastly, a support character who can help provide healing and ranged attacks. The downside is once you finally get access to the full party the game is almost over. This gives an akward pacing feeling to the game and I was more surprised that the game was actually over so soon after finally having a choice of my party composition.Customizing your character’s abilities are done by equipping your weapons with Crystals. Each weapon has a tree of nodes that you can equip matching crystals into those slots. There are often many different paths that each weapon has that can focus on defensive or offensive abilities. This reminded me of the Final Fantasy VII’s materia system, mixed with the sphere grid of X. The crystals themselves have varying stats and abilities that come with each one and can allow you to customize your character’s abilities. I found that often times the best crystals to equip are ones that augment your speed and incantation speed stats. Speed is key to acting faster, which can allow you to interrupt enemy spells before they cast them. Incantation speed allows you to make sure your spells can be cast without worry about being interrupted themselves.There is a crafting system for both weapons and armor, however I can say I didn’t craft a single piece of armor but I tried to craft a few different weapons. I found that most of the time, you will get weapons often enough that are strong enough to beat the game without crafting. One issue with the crafting is that it is a bit rough to keeping track of where materials drop and how exactly to farm those materials so you can craft weapons that are worth the effort. I think it is definitely possible to skip the entire crafting system and not miss anything important. I feel like the weapons can definitely use some scaling, or at least make it easier to find and buy crafting materials to make the crafting system worth investing time into.Graphically, I was quite surprised by how well the game looks for such a small development team. The rest of the review is posted on Rectify Gaming due to character limitations here I can't post the full review.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very aesthetically pleasing and promising, it has fast growing community of fans and kind and responsive small team of developers who are constantly polishing bugs and details and look dedicated to the game of their dream.I'll still leave a positive review, even though at the current state the game is very short, it takes like 8 hours to complete the main story without grinding too much, and maybe 4 more hours to get all the achievements, side quests and collectibles. Feel free to invest more time if you are like me willing to help the devs by finding bugs and reporting them via awesome ingame bugreporting console.The main cons, in the priority order, are:- Repetiteveness of minor regular battles (which can be avoided most of the time, but will annoy you to death when you wish to simply go exploring). - Controversial battle system, which is turn-based on a hexagonal grid, and looks too much like Disciples 3 at the moment. There is a backstabbing damage, and some hexes which can provide certain benefits, like free healing each turn, bonus to damage or even a mountable ballista. But otherwise there's really little use of moving your characters on a grid. Static system like Disciples 1-2 could really make this game better. Also there's no chance to miss at the moment, everyone always hits which makes battles too predictable. You know, battles were one of the main reasons why Disciples 3 failed. Please don't make the same mistakes- Technical issues: memory leaks, random lag, stuttering, etc. This will most likely be fixed in future patches I suppose, so I won't insist on this point.- A little bit boring level design for initial level of the game (dark forest). It is too dark and foggy, and may dismoral any player who is not patient enough.- Unresponsive menu which takes some time to react and has some unnecessary actions and clicks (especially save system and targeting in combat which can be only done with the mouse unfortunately)- Very few items and loot, and except potions that restore HP and MP, I haven't found any useful tools which may be used tactically on the battlefield. Like poisons, traps, gas bombs and such. There are none at the moment.The things I liked though:- Beautiful character design, both 3D and 2D. Really beautiful, and animations are mostly smooth too- Charming main world (surroundings of the town of Herelsor where you are exploring 80% of the game). Design is lovely.- Very good voice acting which keeps you with the story- Interesting crystal system, weapon levelling and character progressionI hope the game will be improved with time, but even now it leaves a good impression and you feel the soul in it. It is not a passing by common product focusing only on money, you feel like the devs are trying to make the game of their dream so it's very inspiring to be involved in the process playing Early Access. It is funny that at first I asked for refund after 1.3 hours playing, but soon after refund I re-bought the game again because I missed it so much that I even had a dream about it. Keep up the good work!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game so much. I have it every chance I could. Unfortunately its filled with good ideas, and interesting concepts, with a pretty compelling story.... And implemented terribly. The cutscenes are uninspiring. Drama feels forced and those moments of pain and loss they try to share with the player completely miss their marks. The combat is monotonous and tedious. Monster one level above you is a god, monsters one level below are cake. There are literally 12 total spells for the mage. and every combat, even bosses, is just a game of rock paper scissors until you find their weakness IF you even have that element equipped. Not to mention this game notes itself as a JRPG and yet your party is 2 people -.-* . To compound on this, the game becomes grindy in the worst of ways. Every weapon starts at level one, and it takes a lot of combat to increase it, the crystals (reminiscent of the grid from final fantasy x-2 but tiny and attatched to the weapon you keep replacing) are lack luster, and the improvement system is god awful. The last thing I want to do is rack up pages and pages of crystals just to gamble 5 in hope for a better one for this particular weapon, replace the weapon 10 minutes later and start all over again. The final 'come on guys, are you even trying?; for me was the prison break. "I wont kill the soldiers cuz I was one too. So lets get a 40 ft tall boar with tusks longer than spears and a bad temper to wreck the place as a 'distraction'". Yea... Those soldiers are definitely still alive... And the 'oooh, its so big it makes the screen shake when it runs' was more like a first person epilepsy simulator, is it just makes the terrain go up and down real fast like its glitching. Gave me a damn headache. ----TLDR: game feels like a combo of other video games good ideas but half done and cobbled together lazily until nothing feels unique or inspiring, sad to say but with 17 hours of gameplay its just one ' *groan* "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ really?" ' after another until eventually you quit.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty decent ATB RPG for those looking to scratch that itch with something new(ish). The graphics definitely show their age but if you can look past that, the game play is fun. The combat has some tactical elements to it, having you position your characters on different hex spaces to flank enemies or keep mages as a distant to avoid major damage. Enemies hit hard but all HP and MP is healed after every battle so it really pushes you to go all out with every fight. There are reward conditions every fight that grant items if you hit it. Some are just not possible for specific fights but it's not a huge loss if you don't get it. Boss conditions are worth it though as they can award higher quality gear than what you may have access to at the time. The skill system isn't the greatest. You gain buffs and skills by equipping gems on a grid. Each weapon has it's own grid and levels up independently unlocking more slots in the grid to equip. Some gems have skills and some don't. You have to fuse gem together to create gems with better skills and stats boosts. You can only follow one path in the grid (from what I've seen) which feels limiting. There are light puzzle elements that offer rewards for completing. The story is good, not award winning but your traditional RPG story. Over all, the good outweighs the bad here so it's worth a shot if you can get it on the cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: Longtime JRPG fan, as well as an independent artist. So I admit up front I am extra inclined to support projects like this. Audio levels are wacky, dialogue is incomplete, and there are a ton of performance hitches in what is otherwise a visually unique and beautiful game. However! This game has so much heart and creativity. The music is great, and the battles are tactical and flashy (if JUST a bit too long). The main characters are brother and sister, and their relationship gets off to an interesting start (UPDATE: I initially did not believe the game let you play as the sister, but the devs pointed out how to do it. Thanks!!).  To me, this kind of game is the reason Early Access exists, and I'm happy to support the team making it.TL;DR - If you have a soft spot for JRPGs as well as some patience and empathy for talented people doing good, ambitious work, give this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Edge of Eternity is what I would describe as cracked gem. The flaws are visible even on the surface, but despite that it still gleams and I think it's worthy of attention. First I want to get to some of the flaws, however.The story's pacing can at times be a bit all over the place. It's generally fine-ish, but at times it feels like too much happens in too little time. This issue reaches a crescendo in chapter 6 in particular but I'll get back to that a bit later as I particularly have issues with this chapter of the game.Balancing can be an issue as well. For a point of reference, I did my playthrough on hard difficulty and it wasn't particularly difficult throughout. Which is fine, I think. There's still a difficulty setting above hard but it's not simply the difficulty that is the issue. Certain fights in the game simply don't feel that fleshed out.  is a complete joke that comes to the top of my mind almost instantly.  also felt excessively simple, which is a fair bit less defensible given the stakes of that battle in particular. In short, the game has balancing issues at certain parts of the game.Yes, there is a bit of grind but I think it's perhaps a bit over exaggerated. Maybe I'm biased since I'm a big fan of open world RPGs, but I didn't really feel the need to grind outside of doing side quests and bounty quests. Most bounty quests ask you to generally kill around ~4-7 of a certain enemy so it's not even a significant amount.I also did not like the gem crafting system. It is an RNG-based system where you take two gems and you re-roll until you get the stats and abilities you want. It doesn't present itself as much of an issue early on when you only have a few characters and relatively few gem slots to juggle. By the end of the game, however, you have 5 different characters to juggle, with end-game weapons with way more gem slots than early game. It simply feels like the system doesn't respect your time by asking you to essentially slot-machine to what you need for any given character.Finally what I believe are the most serious issues of the game. Chapter 6 is, perhaps, the  time I did not really enjoy my time playing Edge of Eternity. In short, the balance and pacing issues I mentioned earlier come out in full force. So much happens in so little time that doesn't get explained that thoroughly that I simply felt dizzy by the time that chapter 6 completion achievement popped up. I had to put the game down for a bit and I was worried it would mean the final parts of the game are simply bad. Thankfully, chapter 7 rebounds  but it's not completely in the clear. The game commits what I believe to be one of the greatest sins in storytelling.  That's right, it gets sequel baited.Regardless of all that, I still give this game a recommendation. So, why?Well, this point might seem a bit shallow but the game genuinely looks very good. Yes, on the micro scale the lighting can look a bit off at times and even occasionally bug out, many textures are smudgy, character models not related to the main cast are notably lower quality and are very often copy-pasted. On the macro scale, however? The world? The environment?It's gorgeous. No, like, genuinely one of the best looking games I've played in that regard, and this is an indie title! I felt like I could get lost moving around the world for hours.As well, despite fudging up certain bigger plot elements, I found the smaller interactions of the characters to be genuinely compelling. Don't get me wrong the game is very trope-y, but that's not necessarily a bad thing in itself and I found some of the main cast in particular to be compelling. Unfortunately the final two party members, , are introduced far too late into the game to get any sort of serious development. Besides that, though, it's quite good.Despite the balancing issues I found the combat system to be pretty interesting as well. I don't think it's been as fleshed out as it has the potential of being, but regardless I found the combat to be interesting enough to keep my attention throughout the game with some lulls when the challenge occasionally falls off a rock.With all that said, I really enjoyed my time playing this game. Sure, the flaws are very apparent, but I don't think the flaws are necessarily bad enough to write off the game completely. If you enjoy this type of game I'd recommend it, particularly if you find it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. Sure it's in early access and you can expect the typical bugs and glitches but this is one game I'm glad I purchased. Despite the bugs that are obvious with these early release games, I find myself addicted. I look forward to seeing how the game grows up to release.Now, as most people have pointed out already, the battle camera is an absolute nightmare. It moves around on its own like rotating around to show you who is making an action and in which direction, or just trying to create a cinematic battling experience. However, you can also control the camera yourself BUT the camera animations mentioned before still play even if you're controlling it. This just throws the camera in all directions all at the same time. In some cases the camera is so zoomed in that when I try to pick a target to attack, I can't see them and have to try and spin around (or zoom out) to select the damn thing I want to hit! I'm not even going to mention when the camera clips through geometry! The camera is my biggest dislike and I really would like to see a generic static battle camera. The dialogue/interactions are....there(?). Enough said on that. It's one of those things that I just want you to experience on your own. Some people don't mind it (like me) but others have been quite vocal about it. I'm not bothered really as it is in alpha, and I assume that this is the least of the devs worries. I'll just say this though, it can't get worse. It is a linear game, however the areas you visit are quite large. Lots of stuff to harvest and plenty of enemies to kill. Nothing too exciting really but I enjoy it.It's a game for the future, not the present. We are testing it after all and I like what I see. 10 hours might not be much but it hooks me in and keeps me going. The crystal system for weapons are neat and there is a crafting element too, although I don't really see the point of it in it's current version but we will see if anything happens to it over the course of time. Looks good (at times) and the weather effects are cool too. I have more negatives than positives but I would still recommend it. The 'report bug' feature (as well as the unstuck feature - which is something that most games should have outside of alphas/betas anyway. Seriously why isn't this added it's a god send!) is there for a reason and I hope they actually get read! The negatives are small and easily ignored (except for that damn battle camera) in contrast to everything else. Its a nice game. Worth getting involved in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning graphics, well designed areas and nice voice acting combined with a good storyline, a good amount of content and characters, which can be a bit too much of a "stereotype" sometimes. Well, that's not really a big deal. The two major problems (from my point of view) are: the camera-movement during combat (to be clear: the camera is rarely where you really need it, it switches around and sometimes focus completely empty areas) and the volume of sound effects during cutscenes and during quest-dialogues. Sometimes it raises up so loud for no reason, that my headset explodes (can be a simple "pull the sword" and you think he stabbed you in your ear) and it can't be ajusted correctly in the options menu. But to be fair: the game is still in progress and the devs made huge steps from the release up to now based on the story, the combat-system in general and the amount of items and gear. So yes, I definitely recommend the game to you, if you are able to accept some smaller issues.

_childDocuments_.review: From time to time I get an itch to play a really good RPG. That last itch was scratched with The Witcher 3. Of course, that was a fully fleshed out and developed game so I can't really compare The Witcher 3 to this game. To keep things short, the game has potential to be a great RPG but it has a long way to come before even coming close to being a finished game.Overall, the game has a lot of things that needs to be worked on. When I play an RPG, I want to be immersed into its world. I want to be able to experience the story as if i was there. It's a far ways from that sort of experience, but it certainly has the potential to reach it. So is it worth $20. Eh... right now, not really in my opinion. It's a bit too rough for me at the least. If it goes on sale, definitely buy it to support the devs. I wish there was a middle thumbs because the game isn't bad. It's just not finished. I can't wait to see the finished product.

_childDocuments_.review: Get it on a 40% sale or there about, mostly because it needs a lot of polishing.Sure, the game is released, doesn't mean they're done with it however, more stuff is still on the way.My main issues are the following:"Jank": There was a lot of minor things, such as voicelines not corresponding with whats written, typos, player placement not even close to where the cutscene ends them (constant, just felt weird to me) and even a quest that put me in a different place on the map for no reason.Selene: Painful character, just.. no.Animations: Compared to the standards nowadays, the average animation work is fine, but often goes stiff, such as the Ultimate Attacks for each character, especially Daryon.Facial animation barely exists but that's fine with me, as that's probably one of the hardest things to do right.Combat: The combat tries something unusual, with a grid based system.That in itself is not a problem, but when moving uses a full turn, and some characters are ungodly slow as charging their ATB (Ysoris and Theia, even Selene towards the end of my game), it caused me to never use some abilities.I barely even used Ysoris because of how slow he is by default, so whenever it was his turn and he was out of reach, I would sometimes just skip the turn.Theia is just the odd one out considering they need a buildup of energy, which again is a lot of turns of nothing.For the rest: the story is pretty good, the Corrosion design is great, the music is extremely forgettable and dialogue quite often quite annoying in the way its written.

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminded me a lot of Star Ocean. The visuals are not as animated however the game overall is a 9/10. The combat started out kinda slow but as you unlock more weapons and begin crafting the customization blooms into something fun and rewarding to explore. I only died two times throughout the game so the boss mechanics in combat were not difficult however not always explained. I enjoyed the story up till chapter V. In chapter V i felt it got kinda dry but still had a good ending. The bugs/glitches/crashes i ran into total around 7. I had 2 hard crashes where the game closed for seemingly no reason. I experienced a inventory glitched where some of my resources and at one point i had a weapon disappear. The voice acting had 3-4 times where it did not match the subtitles and maybe didn't make much since. Most of the puzzles were just somewhat fun. No puzzle really felt to easy but I never felt challenged in solving them either. A fun single player RPG. I beat the game in around 50 hours and only unlocked one of the Ult. weapons.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game! It took me around 60 hours. I completed most of the content that came up with only a few side quests left unresolved. Reminded me of Star Ocean given the sci-fi elements that are incorporated into an otherwise high fantasy setting. The dungeons (particularly The Vanguard and the final dungeon) really surprised me at how well done they were with different mechanics needed to progress, and the story telling that was happening. The world design was gorgeous.The first half of the game was a bit slow in terms of pacing as it took a long time to fill out the party, and also it felt like a lot of the story beats were deliberately being held back. Things didn't really start coming together until the end but unfortunately a lot of the plot threads were left unfulfilled. There were some typos, and I did have a crashing issue at launch that was resolved promptly by the last big update and I have had no such issue like that since. To the developers credit, as of writing this review, they have continued to update and support the game so it is only going to get better.I wanted to comment on some of the negative feedback people have been leaving on this game. Some of it is fair, at the end of the day this was a small team doing their best and certain aspects of the game are not as refined as what one might expect from a $60 game (so good thing it's only $30). However most of the reviews are coming from people who haven't played through the game and to some extent they don't know what they are talking about. For example someone mentioned the soundtrack as bland however they have only played for 7 hours and so there are multiple stand out tracks that they haven't heard yet. We have to remember this is a 50+ hour game so while some of the music is run of the mill, there are definitely gems in there that are on par with any top tier soundtrack. Someone commented that Daryon just seems to get over the horrible event that happens in Chapter 0 too quickly but as they haven't played the entire game they don't understand why that criticism is flat out untrue. Overall, this is the most fun and ambitious JRPG that I've played in years. It punches well above its weight class. It feels like it is supposed to be AAA quality based on the length, gameplay, and even graphics and by AAA standards it doesn't quite deliver (although to be fair AAA games launch with bugs all of the time and most of them aren't nearly as good on the whole as this one is). Compared to games actually on this level, this one blows them out of the water.I had a lot of fun and look forward to seeing what this studio does next.

_childDocuments_.review: While very much an indie production, and marred by the expected issues, Edge of Eternity drips passion, love and care from it's every moments, and even in these early hours I've been very impressed by it's systems. Combat is a really fun blend of tactical and turn based, the crafting systems are implemented so they can be used if you so desire, or completely ignored, which is fine by me. I've really enjoyed the voice performances so far - they all have this theatrical nature to it that lends a sense of drama to everything. The two leads are well written and interesting and interact with each other in surprisingly believable ways. The story has already taken many interesting turns and I look forward to seeing where it goes. I will update this review as I go along, just wanted to leave my thoughts as I have thoroughly enjoyed the 13 hours or so I've put in.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty decent game overall. Could use a lot of work though. Tons of screen tears from the graphics not loading properly. Tons of wrong subtitles that don't match what is said on screen (even had one french subtitle during a cutscene). Characters/enemies getting stuck in the environment and become untargetable or unable to move/act. Equipment disappearing after unequipping them. Bonus missions that are impossible to complete appearing consistently, i.e., "kill the enemy in 1 hit" when it's a high end mid-boss type enemy like the Big Orokko or enemies with high physical/magical defense. Music disappearing after teleporting. The list goes on.Apart from the bugs and glitches, the main cast seem poorly animated, and the moves are poorly animated (Darion's arm clipping/freaking out during his ultimate move). Very few NPC variety (Kora's army all had the same NPC design. Literally 0 difference). The crafting/merge system is interesting, but either pointless or tedious. There is 0 reason to use any other weapon in the game other than the highest tiered weapon you can craft at the moment. The orange tier weapons last you for a few chapters even on high difficulties, making the whole progression of a weapon pointless and also makes found weapons pointless. The merging of the gems is a neat way to customize and upgrade your characters, but the whole randomization of a set stat range and range of abilities is very tedious. Can spend hours cycling through stats just to try and find the right combination you need for the build you want, and I'm not counting trying to get absolute max stat for the tier of gem either, which takes significantly longer.The collection of the crystal flowers is pretty annoying to say the least. Even though they glow and can be seen from quite a distance away, it's still annoying running all over the map several times over just to make sure you got each one for each area you visit.Another thing, placing new characters items/crafting schematics in older areas is absolutely a slap in the face. Even if the main quest takes you back there, the enemies are usually still pretty under leveled despite being upgraded from progression and don't warrant a re-exploration of the area, especially when there is only 1 chest or two added for the new character, and maybe a Nekaroo dig site for the schematics. Preferably, just get rid of the crafting system and make it similar to most other JRPGs and either have the weapon come from a chest or you can buy it. That way the chest weapons can actually become relevant and necessary. Another suggestion, give chest items abilities like the crafted weapons or take them out completely.Overall, I'd give this game a 2/10. Great story, good sound track, great character design and development. Sucky everything else. If there weren't as many bugs that happened frequently to the point it broke the game, I might rate this a 7/10 tops. These bugs need to be fixed ASAP for the game to be enjoyable. In a single 8 hour session of playing this game, I'm submitting at least 5 or 6 bug reports, all of which are unique enough from each other to warrant a separate bug report. It honestly seems like this game was released without having a testing or beta session for quality assurance. I would not recommend buying this game at full price. Wait until it goes on a large sale before purchasing.

_childDocuments_.review: I helped Kickstart this game 5 years ago, and the best thing I can say is that they haven't given up on working on it. Kudos on never giving up.In reality, the game works (mostly) but isn't very good. Nothing is specifically bad, but there are rough edges everywhere not least of which is the dialogue, camera, and environmental objects as set dressing. Maybe in 5 years if progress remains steady it will be a finished project. If you want to jump in for an alpha-like experience go for it, but as it stands it's not worth the money.I'm conflicted about the recent update - as an 'Anniversary' update feels like something you would release for a game that was done a year ago. As it is, it's mostly a reminder about how progress is so slow. Still glad this small team is working on it - and again - good on you for doing it - but in my mind it's time to move on.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to agree with most thumbs down comments here.  I barely started the game in EA when I just knew there was a ways to go.  The storytelling was clearly the work of amateur writers, of the quality you might get from a somewhat gifted 8th grader (basically the passion is there and it has some elements, but they are raw and not at all refined).  Characters are bland, narratives are ham-handedly forced through exposition, the character archetypes are so cliche, I was groaning within minutes.The bugs I encountered in EA were pretty crippling as well as the entire user experience.  I filed a nice, detailed bug report, but apparently it wasn't even consumed at all, because now I see this game went to full release a mere month after my report.  From what I had seen when I played, I assumed there was at least another 9-12 months left in development, that's how unpolished and unfinished this game was.  As someone with a long career in software development myself, I can't even imagine having any pride in releasing a game in that condition, so I guess they may have had their hand forced by economics or business politics.Long story short, this is a very unpolished work with quite a few bugs, many frustrating UX elements, very cliched characters, and the kind of story a 12-year-old might write in their idle hours.  Not the worst game in existence for sure, but unless you're into these kinds of naive, amateurish types of games, I'd steer clear of this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This will be a living post that I will edit as I progress.Day 1: Not RecommendedGood Points:- The world looks nice- The combat system is neat- I think the world has potential (otherwise I wouldn't enact the labor of all this).- I like the animal designs. The cat mount, and the chicken... things. A nice nod to, but not blatant ripoff of, FF.- The protag, is likable enough, if not a tad too tame.- It has all the fixins, but it is death from a million cuts.- Music is nice- I like looking into the distance of this game.Bad Points:- The combat system is slick on a keyboard, but on a controller it's just cumbersome.     -- Maybe you could keep the current set-up but color code each character. I often don't know who I am attacking with right away and I will melee with the caster or just get in other general L2/R2 button battles.- Music skips, dampening, and awkward looping mid-track. Often when pressing buttons.- The game feels abysmally lifeless- Going in & out of combat makes the camera go nuts     -- When in battle mode the camera sometimes starts underground or inside a wall or mountain- Inputs (mainly in combat) are dropped. Casting spells and Grid Movement is the main occurrence.     -- Selecting a grid will either not do anything and return to the previous menu, confirm but go to/attack a grid I didn't choose, or work fine. Roll the dice.     -- Same with attacks, I will clearly be selecting my desired target only to have the character attack something else.     -- My theory on this is that there is moment after you select an enemy/grid and the battle grid disappears, but there is still a small moment that any joystick movement will still be registered and select something new without your knowledge.- If its possible to fix the whole "camera too close to the wall revealing a characters horrifying underskin" business. Please do so. To me, its the hallmark of bad design.- The overworld is a damn mess. There is so much crap everywhere its painful to look at.     -- For some reason I can barely even see the monsters     -- Collectibles all look the same but are always different. It's kinda, idk...     -- It's impossible to tell how many monsters I will pull. Sometimes one is chasing but I fight five and, other times, the reverse.- The quality of the character models is inconsistent.     -- They actually look better in the over world than in cut scenes.     -- In cutscenes many times the textures don't load right and they look like PS2 graphics.- Cutscenes disobey the law of thirds.     -- NPC dialogues have the character animations reset every time you press the button to advance.     -- The cutscenes are not voiced, which I understand, but it exacerbates the lifelessness problem. At least have a Zelda/Peanuts like "ma ma maa" or NPC music.     -- Having a picture of the person talking would be helpful. Doesn't have to be fancy with many reaction pics. Static would be a tremendous improvement.- Running combatants, such as the Tinkertoy (er whatever) Bandits will often run (clipping) into buildings and mountain walls. You can still pursue and attack (ending up inside walls, too).- I already wrote a long diatribe about the writing style, but deleted it because it was excessively harsh...     -- The dialogue between Salene and Da... S&D in the beginning is excessive.     -- Five minutes in and I already hated the both of them.     -- The tone is inconsistent. One moment, we're in a dire situation with a heavy blizzard talking about our dying mother and the next we are in a cave that randomly has some significance to our childhood. We proceed to be reminded, at length, 3-4 times that our sister one time bailed us out of a sticky situation. Every time the brother is just like "gee golly shucks." After the 4th time upon beating the mini-boss, I cried "Shut the ♥♥♥♥ up, ya ♥♥♥♥!" and started spamming buttons to skip. This whole cave sequence took all of five minutes, three minutes of it being cringey dialogue JUST for the sole purpose of pointing out the sister got sent to Hogwarts er something for your goof. If this is a JRPG homage, and the dialogue makes me want to spam-to-skip in the first five minutes, we are in for a bad time.     -- The writing assumes that the audience is braindead. **Points to the Crystal Fruits quest giver convo.     -- NPC convos are way too long. ^^^     -- The writing tries too hard to be funny and falls flat. WHICH IS FINE, being funny is extremely difficult. People get paid millions for it. I would rather have stoic and rigid characters (that anyone can write) than a bunch of unfunny catastrophes.     -- I can see liking the protagonist, but the sister is a boring, one-dimensional, know-it-all, glorified NPC. She even sounds robotic. Maybe that's a spoiler, I don't know. Something about life and machines...- The gem's in the weapon's business is confusing and needless complicated. It makes getting a new weapon a groan instead of exciting.- The sprint is broken. When you hold the sprint you burn stamina. After you let go, you continue to sprint for a few seconds but your stamina heals. If you burn it to zero and let go, your stamina is healed before you stop sprinting. Making the whole energy system useless as you can just lightly tap the sprint and it you'll run forever at no penalty. I think the stamina business isn't necessary to be honest.- The group energy system also leaves me scratching my head. To me, it'd make more sense to have battle damage be persistent and just have that be the groups limiting factor.- Time skips to day anytime the game wants to show me something. I come to the first Inn or the Helistra towny, I go from midnight to 2pm.- There are just a million little graphical this-and-that's that are indefinable that the game actually makes me feel sick and physically makes my eyes hurt. I really hate saying that, because so many people say that if they are getting 59.99 FPS, but it's the truth. :-/- Finally, I just wanted to point out the meta-irony of the protag saying "This feels like Deja Vu" just about every single fight. It's supposed to be funny, because you get in a lot of similar fights. Yet, when you say it every other fight then it's commenting on the in & out game.     -- It wouldn't hurt to have our hero's have a closing victory quip and flourish at the end of fights.Ultimately, I'm interested. Please, keep going and working on it. I will say I think this is a pretty sloppy Alpha. If it was a Beta, I'd be a lot more nice and forgiving. It's tough love. If you plan to release this game at anywhere near it's current state it will not be successful. Not even like a "dedicated following" successful. The one's that are saying as good as/better than AAA, I think are letting the AAA fall from grace pollute their opinions. I hate AAA, too, but they at least, typically, make something stable. The best way I can think to put it is: it feels like someone hand drew a picture of the Sistine Chapel's artwork. All the shapes are there, it's even a damn good take, but it lacks the finesse and completeness of the original. In closing, I am just one dude, what do I know.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game so badly.  It ticks all the right boxes for a JRPG: intersting battle system, strong story, and strong characters,  How could this possibly go wrong?  Well, for starters, and by far the worst part, is that in chapter 3 and chapter 4, the battles become annoying, not interesting.  The key problem is that the battles all require a high degree of movement, but movement takes an entire turn.  In many cases, you end up spending 70% of the battle just running.  Presumably the developers are going to add yakety sax to the sound track to help.Beyond just the movement, the timing for attacks and reaction is just too tight.  It happened way too often that I'd start a basic attack spell with Selene, and seconds later the boss would start their super ultimate death spell, targeted at Selene's location.  Selene would finish her cast, but then die horribly before getting another chance to move.The locales are beautiful and very well done.  Unfortunately, there's nothing to do in all that vast expanse.  You've basically got a quest hub model here...without any quests.  Good thing you level up so fast so you're not missing anything anyway.  The towns, while beautiful, all feel generic and soulless (except for that one with the mine that you save in chapter 2).Also worth noting are the puzzles. which are horrible.  They make no logical sense, and are required for progression in chapter 4.  On the plus side, skill progression is another key aspect of JRPGs, and one that Edge of Eternity does well.  Leveling makes you stronger, but skills come from crystals that you slot into weapons.  The crystals also give you stats, and so getting the right combination of skills and stats is a constant challenge.  It also helps that crystals are frequent loot.  I found myself compulsively optimizing for +1 speed (to avoid the ultimate death attack), and had a lot of fun doing so.Finally, the story.  Despite the hubs, this is still just the same old hallway quest you know and love.  Fortunately, the story is halfway decent (so far).  The characters, despite being the chosen of God and/or Satan, are interesting and have good chemistry.  The quest itself has enough turns to be interesting, although by chapter 4, feels nowhere near over half completed.Ultimately, the flaws are superficial, not structural.  If the developers can stop tripping over themselves by trying to be clever, there's an awesome game potentially here.  Make movement cost only 75% of the action bar and eliminate the puzzles, and all of a sudden the game becomes fun again.  There's other stuff (like the empty open world) that will presumably be fixed in time as well.If these things are fixed, the game is an easy recommend.  For now...the problems remain and destroy what is otherwise a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to give this game a chance by playing from start to finish, but I run into a game breaking bug when I reached a certain battle to protect the gates of a city (wont say more to avoid spoilers). So the battle was utterly impossible, the characters cannot move after 1 turn, auto battle does not help either and its impossible to win it.That’s the thing about this game, it was released in 2022 and I played it in 2024… 2 full years… by this point I would have expected at least game breaking bugs to be fixed.This has gotta be one of the most bugged games I played, period. But let me give a few more examples.When I started playing the game, for some reason, was even more bugged. Up until chapter 4 I encountered all kind of issues. From audio cuts, resources or quest items not showing up, the lighting being all over the place having seizures, NPC stuck in a T-Pose, teleporters blocked even if they were in the same region, even more bugged battles from the one I mentioned. So, how this was fixed? Well after verifying integrity of game files about 3 times and after a re-install most issues were finally fixed, and I could play the game.Don’t get me wrong, I still had f-ed up lighting, teleporters red-out (even if I could reach those on foot, they were still blocked), I didn’t got anymore audio cuts but wish I had considering how bad the voice acting is… Regarding that, don’t bother switching to ♥♥♥, stick to En, they are both bad, but at least you will understand one of them.How did some ppl reached the end and did not mentioned all those issue is beyond me, maybe my PC decided to hate this game and broke it. But I will stop here mentioning the bugs, cuz I will be here all day talking about them, let me bring out other points. The dialogue, what can I say about this, no wonder its call Edge of Eternity, the way characters speak makes them Edgy for Eternity. Simple word to describe the dialogues is cringe.Auto battle… OMFG! I have played SNES/Sega with better programed battles. This feature annoyed me the most, the main reason is the characters are f-king brain dead, and I mean more braindead that your average TikTok influencer, if you plan to use that feature to farm lower level enemies, you better pick 1 or 2 enemies to fight or else you might lose. As an example, you will see your char using debuff skills when the enemy is at 1 HP! You will see them use completely the element which the enemy resist to, and will use any skill at random. Funny thing is that the enemy is doing ok for themselves, but your chars with auto ON are just lobotomized.Huge but barren world, if you see screenshots of this game it looks gorgeous, you might mistake it for a Square Enix game, but ohh boy, getting into that world is so damn lifeless. Even the cities, filled with NPCs, they hardly have any animation, most dialogues are just 1 sentence long, they feel so dead.Puzzles, there are a few puzzles around and all of them put you in the combat grid map, you do not fight anything, but you race against the time to solve it in as few turns as possible, why is this needed all the time, I dunno, they could have been placed in the world without getting you in combat. Also, ofc, some are bugged and require a restart to de-bug it.The main story it actually started off nicely, it was not the generic evil guy does something evil and it’s up to you to save the world. You just want to cure someone from the space AIDS which turns people black, and we cant have that. The thing is, it becomes convoluted by shoving new elements with every chapter despite the characters always knowing about them but never mentioning them; and also forgetting about some of the things which just happened.So TL;DR: I know the dev team is very small, but took on more that they can chew with this game. Way too many elements which barely add anything, way too many bugs, way to big of a world, and a letdown narrative. They should have made a 2D JRPG like the old school FFs or make this 1 smaller, way smaller.

_childDocuments_.review: I dont wish to be cruel , but this game needs a ton of polish , still I can see the love that went into it , but from poorly explained systems (for example they never tell you how or when you learn skills permanently) , to bad editing in cutscenes and transitions , weird sound levels (there is a lot of anoying ambient sounds that disctract instead of adding to the ambience) ,  a lot of work is still needed for this gem to shine. Battles can get a bit slow due to the reliance on speed and haste stats , also add that it has a grid based system , they become very slow , now Im a patient person but I can see many players getting tired of combat. Another huge mistake is that you get your third permanent party member after 40 hours of play , then in the last third of the game your forth and fifth , so there is a lot of pacing issues. The story beats have logic behind them but a lot of things are left unexplained with no way to know them  , so no this isnt a case of hidden/obfuscated lore or story , it just isnt there , also there was 1 mayor plot hole that I was screaming or rather waiting for a character to use something that was supposed to be used , yet they never do.I only had 1 crash to desktop , so you can pretty much play the entire game from start to finish. But still despite all this there are some really good scenes that made like the game , and I do like the characters in the main party ... so again if the developers managed to really polish the game it would have been a really fantastic game. Do I recommend ? well yeah , but as you can see you have to put up with a lot of things to enjoy the game.
