_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - I recommend this game as it shows amazing promise from an Alpha test version that feels like a mid-beta.After quite a few hours on this game, I still haven't ran out of things to do. This is only the alpha, and it appears that the whole storyline isn't even in the game yet but what they already have in the game shows great potential. There are relatively few bugs for a game in its infancy.Pro:1. Looks fairly polished - a little more touch ups here and there and the game will look near perfect.2. Very few Bugs - For a game in Alpha, its amazing how few bugs there are. Only noticed one or two so far, and they are not game breaking. For an alpha, Midgar Studios has already put out a more finished product than Bethesda did with FO76.3. Great Tutorial - Most games either give you a horrible tutorial, are extremly intrusive and flood you with information, or put you in a fake training scenario which doesnt fit the story line. This game fits it into the story line and presents just enough information to ensure you can play effectively.4. Nostalgia - It feels much like an earlier Final Fantasy game with the battle system and encounters. Similar to a FF-X style of system. Brings back that feeling with the graphics of a new game.5. Content - There appears to be a large amount of content in this game already, even though its pretty clear the alpha of this game hasnt released all the content it has.6. Weapons - Each weapon has the ability to add/change stats and abilities for your character. You can have multiple weaons with different stats. I have two swords, one is focused mainly on damage while the other turns him into a tank. I can see this being a huge benefit in later stages of the game.7. Brother/Sister Dynamic - The writing for this is pretty much spot on. It feels like just the right amount of antagonizing eachother while still being supportive.Cons:1. Camera in Battles - You control the battle from 3rd person, which is normally a great thing but in this case It seems as if i always get my camera behind a tree, a rock, or some kind of flora. We really should be able to reposition the camera in battle or not have plants in the way and/or translucent.2. AOE/Grid Spells - When you cast these spells, the grid attempts to show everywhere the spell can be cast, but the camera is at a low angle and moves while you are moving your mouse. This makes grids that are at a far distance very difficult to click on.3. No markers for Quest Boards/No mini-map - When you have to turn in quests to a quest board, there is no markers or compass guidance on how to get there. While I have a decent memory, finding the nearest one can still be difficult without a mini-map showing them or any compass markers.4. No Fast Travel - (No longer a Con, you can now fast travel between save points)5. Extra Members in Party - So far, it seems like they throw a random, completely useless character into the party for one or two fights and then you dont ever see them again. I'm guessing this is just because its Alpha and they havent developed the other potential characters very much.With all the Pro's/Cons, this game still feels very promising. It already provided me more hours of entertainment than some "finished" AAA games do. For $20 or less, this game is a steal. I sure hope that they continue to develop the game and I get to see the full release. It would be a disappointment if this game stayed in perpetual "Early Access" like many other games on steam have.

_childDocuments_.review: I understand my playtime given the usual length of JRPGs could be considered not nearly enough to warrant abandoning this game and giving it a negative review but quite frankly, I can see all the signs of a bad game. Or perhaps a bad - mediocre game, one that is esentially playable but you'll forget soon after. My initial impression of the game was 'Xenoblade Chronicles' whereas upon playing it for close to an hour the conclusion really is 'turn based White Knight Chronicles'. A servicable game in its own right but not a game anyone really raves about except a few weirdos. If you're one of those weirdos, enjoy this game. Another comparison might be Kingdoms of Amalur but with worse writing.Anyone else is probably not looking for an empty world filled with boring combat and mmorpg style presentation (the game really looks like the most generic Korea grind RPG from 2012) and quest design (go here, kill that, speak to this guy, track only a single quest at a time for no reason other than being annoying). There are too many pointless systems tacked on the game which serve no real püurpose other than just making the game appear bigger than it is. The devs should've streamlined more, focused on stuff that matters and not run out of money apparently and just nosedive the ending and leave a bunch of stuff unresolved which most of the playthroughs here - even the positive ones- bemoan.The game is supposed to take about 28 hours to beat doing zero side content and I simply can think of quite a few better things to do than play this game. If you don't have a backlog of 50+ games and really want a bland JRPG, I guess you can give this a whirl.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally this was a positive reviews, for the effort. This game makes me really angry. Devs are a small team, this is, basically, an indie game. This is a jrpg based game made from a French team and this is their first big project.The game is an improvement on every classic jrpg trope (design and gameplay wise). It has very good graphics, the places are big, full of details instead of the usual corridor with some grass around. The monster design is interesting as the characters’, there are no anime tropes, no anime character design, even the size of the conflict is more appropriate for a wrpg then a jrpg.But this game completely fails on the plot, the world building and it doesn’t respect the player  time. I can’t even put a “it’s a mmorpg changed in a single player so it sucks” (like DAI) cause it’s not. I played seven hours, which is not an high number in a totality of a standard jrpg but in those six hours the plot didn’t advanced by an inch, every quest (even the mainline) was uninspired mmo tier fetch quests. There is NOTHING interesting in the big world, you just keep following a continuous “go here to find hints, to find another hint, to find another hint, to find another hint for a guy that (maybe) will explain something”. Spoiler: it doesn’t. This is the tendency of the entire game. The party doesn’t even expand, there is no long cinematic, nothing except two or three inn scenes, it’s just boring grinding and going around the world by foot hour after hour.The game sabotages itself, it’s useless to have a pretty game where plot, character stories and everything around the world go absolutely NOWHERE, they are bland, uninspired and it’s a slog to play cause you stop caring on the half of the game. Motivation and character building fails apart everywhere and you are working on a plotline “we have to save mom from a sickness”. I mean how do you screw a thing simple as this. If you have played the tutorial and puzzled your head around the immediately 360° of Daryon motivation about the war or the awful tryhard to make me care about characters who die exactly 2 minutes after the first combat the rest of the game is on the same wavelength and even worse than that. Why put the effort on having tracks on snow, different biomes, night\day cycle, weather effects, season effect which impact in the game and are not only aesthetics, a good skill system and an interesting battle system when you kill the entire game making the most boring thing to play ever?This is why I’m mad with those people. A jrpg is not a game where you can say “just ignore the plot for the gameplay” I’m not playing quake I’m playing a (maybe) 60 hours game where I can do the same thing every 2 minutes. A terrible grindy game can be saved by the plot or the characters, but you can never do the opposite, not in this genre of a gameSo, sorry, I really appreciate the effort but the devs have screwed up literally in everything except the presentation and the gameplay. I hope there will be improvements in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Finished the game. Basically everything I said below I affirm. Combat camera is most annoying part of the game, but it's not that big of a deal.I did all side quests but 2, min/maxed my gear and got the best weapons, crafted best armor, etc. - about 45 hours total.Overall, definitely recommend if you're looking for a Final Fantasy-esque TRPG and can deal with an indie budget.________________I'm 10 hours in; think I have at least 20 or 30 left as I'm doing basically all of the side content.Overall, I'm pretty impressed.Writing quality varies, but it's leagues better than Forspoken's! I think the VA for Daryon is great... Selene, I'm mixed on. Some of the side characters have good VAs, some don't. Overall, it's not terrible, but acting would definitely not be one of this game's strong points.The lighting and weather model is FAR more varied than I expected (heck, I didn't even expect an actual dynamic model to begin with!).As a fan of most of the Fire Emblem and Final Fantasy games, I think EoE successfully replicates the fundamentals from those games' systems. The animations and VFX are pretty good; though the battle camera is a bit annoying to navigate/use.As far as graphics go, the game looks fine for what it is. They're good enough that I don't feel they are distracting from the experience - the uber-fantasy art direction is employed very well, which along with the lighting/weather stuff, makes the game a pretty satisfying visual experience despite a lack of fidelity.Technical stability has been pretty good. There are a few minor things like the subtitle not being correct for the spoken line, a possible bug with crafting a weapon, etc - nothing major.And lastly, what initially caught my attention when I watched trailers: music. Game has a fantastic soundtrack. Pretty sure the composer "borrowed" a bit of Star Wars for one of the themes - it's well-implemented into the score.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Graphics are excellent.  World is very pretty.Creature/NPC design is good and has lots of variety, while still maintaining staple types.Music is ok, but there isn't much of it.  Uses ambiance to great effect in some areas.Cons:Story starts off well, but drops off fast.  There is no moment where I felt invested in the cause.Gameplay is incredibly boring.  It's tactical, but it doesn't feel rewarding for actually using tactics.Abilities that require activation time or have long animation sequences feel very underwhelming.During battle there are tactical' objectives you can complete to get items, which are not very rewarding.Core Progression is....unremarkable, wear any equipment and gems and your good to go.Removing equipment and gems seems better to bring out the games tactical elements.I mentioned world looks good, but nothing stands out as 'lets go explore'.There is lots of loot, but instead of at the ends of interesting 'lets go explore' locations, they are just scattered along the edge of the world map.Exploration involves 'follow the right/left walls and you'll get all the loot'.Buying items in bulk is a chore, you have to buy one thing at a time.Crafting items in bulk is a chore, you have to craft one thing at a time.Crafting benches are almost never in convenient reach of other crafting benches or shops.All gems share the same stats.  Different color gems grant different abilities.  No real depth.Crafted items don't really give a significant boost over bought items and require way too much time.NPC's that join your group have no indication if they are temp or perm, and take your items when they leave.Ugly:The game features a decently sized world space to explore.  Unfortunately, instead of using the terrain and story elements to block progression, they use roadblocks and invisible walls in some of the later sections.  It doesn't really feel right when an area that was previously blocked suddenly opens up without explanation.  In one case, the area is blocked off from one direction, but when you arrive from the other side it's cleared - but the underlying cause for why it was blocked in the first place still exists and there's no mention as to why it has changed.Another thing to note, is that there is no jumping in the game and minor things will get in your way often.  This leads to your character getting stuck on small rocks, fences, even the decorative elements on road on bridges and cities.  This makes no sense, as you can climb on other terrain elements like boulders and tree roots and other large objects.  If this isn't crazy enough, in combat, it's the opposite - you can walk thru things except large objects.Earlier I mentioned that the way to obtain almost all the loot is to follow the 'left/right wall', but you must be careful not to get stuck in terrain and the invisible walls when doing this though.  There are a few locations in the game that looks like there might be a way to get behind something, but just past it is an invisible wall - even if there is a legitimate wall behind it that would block your path anyways.  In some instances, I would get stuck between this obstacle and the invisible wall, and could not escape.  The only recourse is to load your last save.  This has happened multiple times.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Version: Overall I had fun with this game once I got it to run without overheating my PC (lowering settings to the lowest possible, turning off AA and setting resolution to 1280 x 720 x 60 did the trick). There are issues, but the devs are working to fix them.Longer version:Edge of Eternity is a new RPG by a new studio with a small team. It tells the story of a brother and sister and their journey through out the land. The game has some issues, but most of them are now nitpicks, though a couple are more critical in my opinion. Here is the summary:Good:-Once you get the settings set for your PC, it runs well.-Very customizable. You can set anything you wish. Want level scaling? Turn it on. Want a lower resolution? You can have that too.-Lots to do if you like side content.-The devs are very active in fixing this game too. If the stuff below is too much for you, give it 3 - 6 months and try again as it will probably be improved even more.Neutral:-The plot ends on a cliffhanger. That may annoy some people.Bad (but might be fixed with time):-Battle camera still needs some work. I had a fight in Chapters 5 6 and 8 where the camera went point blank on my characters and no setting would fix it. The camera was so close you couldn't even see what was in the other tiles (again that was with any setting, nothing fixed it). Seems to be an issue in small spaces like the last dungeon of Chapter 5 mainly.-Crafting. I'm not a fan of crafting in the first place, and here there is one stone that is rarer than diamonds and you need it to craft even a first tier weapon. I think I found 8 of them all game in the end, maybe. Suggestion to dev: Sell some weapons please. I went chapter 3 - 8 with Selene on the same staff as I was stuck due to not ever finding that stone. As it is most games with crafting at least sell *some* weapons to the player.-EXP rewards are unbalanced late chapters. I never want to fight another Honey or Ambrosia ever again as the EXP I got for the time it took to defeat even one of them was just not worth it, even if I was fighting one listed as 2 - 3 levels above my parties level. Also quest EXP was too low to care about once I got above level 25 as it never seemed to matter or advance my EXP gauge any.Overall I'd say its a solid 7/10 in the end. It has some issues, but the devs are actively fixing it too. If the issues are too much for you wait 6 months then try it again.

_childDocuments_.review: The story in the this game is amazing. I love the characters and the setting and the worldbuilding. It hooked me early and kept me hooked. The one thing I don't like is it's more like part 1 of 3 than a whole, complete story. And the one major plot point that got completely resolved was the one I was least interested in. That I couldn't wait to finish so I could get back to the rest of the story. And then there was no rest of the story (yet?). I really hope there will be a sequel or two forthcoming. I'd be willing to buy them at full price, and I don't usually buy games for more than $10-$15 on steam.Overall, I'm really impressed that a small indie studio managed to pull off a game like this. It has got some rough edges, though. I ran into a few minor bugs, but nothing game-breaking.The system for moving the camera in battles works well most of the time, but it gets awkward in tight spaces, of which there aren't very many in the game. I had to zoom in more than I wanted to in such spaces. In the more zoomed in camera mode, the battles frequently start with the camera looking off in some random direction instead of at the enemies, and then you have to repeatedly start battles by fixing the camera angle.In the final boss fight, the camera worked a bit differently and wouldn't let me use the sort of camera angle I'd come to like and get used to throughout the game, because it wanted to focus on the impressive looking final boss. I found this very annoying, and one enemy managed to sneak up right next to my party without me realizing there was even anything there because I couldn't look in that direction without spinning the camera all the way around.The interface was good, but I had a few annoyances with it. It's way too easy to accidentally turn on auto-battle (at least when using a controller, I can't speak to the mouse/keyboard interface), as the button which turns on auto-battle in one mode is the same for using certain attacks in a different mode. It's also too easy to accidentally use a character's special attack, for the same reason. Also, the run button is the same as the one for interacting with things in the world, so if you change the setting to make run be toggled rather than having to hold the button down, then every time you interact with something, you'll stop running. These issues could be solved by allowing the player to re-map the buttons, but I couldn't find anything like that anywhere in the menu.

_childDocuments_.review: Tragic as it is for a small studio to not quite meet expectations, there is too much wrong with this game to ignore. I simply didn't have fun playing this game, even though I love turn based fantasy RPG's. It's very clear from playing this game that the graphics (specifically the environments) were prioritized over all else. What I liked:The Graphics (mostly)- The environments are beautiful, bordering on gorgeous. The land is dotted with crystals and glowing plants, which while not unique to this game, certainly liven up the quest commute. The character portraits are nice. The combat animations are serviceable. The character models, aside from perhaps Daryon, Kora, and Myrna look awkward and robotic.The Setting- Magic and the gods, technologically advanced alien raining death upon the land, a religious cult, a theocratic society, cat-like mounts!? I'm sucked in, I want to know more. Even the absolutely done to death Corrosion concept (read: The Darkness, Blight, The Infection, etc etc) doesn't irk much because the the great environments make corroded landscapes look so striking.Daryon- I liked the main character, so sue me. His voice acting and character model are probably the best and I liked him as a put-upon big brother. Though he is rather passive, which can annoy at times.What I disliked:Sound Mixing- No one cares about sound mixing. I certainly don't, so imagine how bad it must be for me to not only bring it up, but list it first. Dialogue is often layered under the music track, making it difficult to hear, dialogue that plays during fights cuts off before finishing, sometimes audio cues like purring or lightning crackles will play continuously. The worst was a persistent insect sound effect that made me think my headphones were dying and, frankly, almost quit in frustration.Combat Mechanics- Sorry to say, but I didn't like it. Daryon and Selene have very boring skill sets based on attacking with elemental damage and you're stuck with just them for half the game. Setting crystals to weapons to increase stats and gain skills was a neat idea, but since forging crystals is so important, maybe there should be a tutorial or some rhyme and reason to what skills and stats get retained when you combine crystals? Leveling up feels pointless since huge chunks of your stats and most all of your skills are tied to weapons/crystals, which feels off message for an RPG. The hexagonal grid gameplay was fun, if a little underutilized and could make boss fights feel strategic when all the pieces came together. Choosing which skills to use in combat was a nightmare. I chose the wrong skill many times or accidentally activated auto battle at key moments. Very frustrating.Story- Yeah, huge chunks of the plot got sacrificed on the altar of high quality graphics. This story is a barely coherent mess. Almost nothing gets explained as the protagonists contend with multiple world ending disasters. What's the Ascension? It's a ritual that makes a big hand appear in the sky and requires human sacrifices to work. No more detail needed. The Corrosion is an unexplained illness that strikes at random and is related to a silver haired goddess we never meet and is destroying the land. Our whole quest is to find a cure for it, so might be nice to have its origin explained. The Seed of Destruction is something that when activated will... ? Do something bad. Kill the protagonist, maybe. The alien Archelites are planning to rain fiery death upon the land, but for what exact purpose goes unexplained. The main villain is trying to initiate a FIFTH nonspecific catastrophe. Like, this isn't fun background worldbuilding, this is what the whole plot is about!Bugs- Didn't happen very often, but the game froze twice for me and crashed to desktop once. For some reason the mouse cursor always set itself in the dead center of my screen whenever I opened a menu (and went away during proper gameplay), despite the fact that I was using a controller. Personally, I could feel my immersion being ripped apart every time I paused, though I think many people could overlook it.I won't go on, but the 'didn't like' list could be a lot longer. I think this game is a technical achievement for what appears to be a small kickstarter backed development team, but a key aspect of game development (or any creative work) is to take a realistic view of what you can accomplish with your skills and within the timeframe you've set for yourself. This game missed the mark.

_childDocuments_.review: Edge of Eternity offers a very interesting story, which unfolds bit by bit, but provides a nice framework for a fantasy roleplaying game. The animals and humans mutated by the corrosion disease, and at the same time, the world threatened by war with aliens, provide a lot of opportunities to behave truly heroic and help everywhere.The world design is very good. Both visually and in terms of variety and scope, there is a lot on offer here. What I really miss in the game is that the characters can’t jump and sometimes can’t even get past small fences or stones, so that you often have to take unnecessary detours here.But there are also some construction sites. Besides the sometimes appearing camera problems, now and then performance drops or flickering textures, there are also some things in the gameplay, which are not top. For example, you can find equipment items again and again, which have completely different values, but all have the same name. This not only makes it unnecessarily complicated to sort the equipment, but the items look so very monotonous and boring. Some creativity would be needed in the naming of the equipment here.The fights are sometimes somewhat repetitive, but mostly entertaining, and there is always some tactical extra depth due to special opponents. I also like the bonus challenges in the fights, that’s a great idea. But it happens every few fights that you get a task that is not solvable or not reasonable in combat. So you have to kill a certain opponent last, but there’s only one anyway. Or you fight against a single weak animal, and then there is a “Suffer XYZ Damage” task, which would require you to do nothing for about 50 turns so that the weak animal would have the chance to do that amount of damage at all.Edge of Eternity has small weaknesses, rough edges, and problems. But for a small price, you get a game from an indie developer that can do much more than almost any other indie game I’ve seen so far. The game is not finished yet but is slowly approaching this state. Since the price will be increased soon, and it is even on offer at the moment, I would recommend to buy it now, if you are interested and minor problems and bugs don’t scare you off.But in general, I think that almost every roleplaying game lover can get a lot of fun out of this title. And if you also have a preference for Japanese roleplaying games and the style of the Final Fantasy series, you can’t go wrong with Edge of Eternity.But if you can’t stand bugs, camera irritations, a jumble of high-res and low-res models and textures, as well as other flaws and construction sites, then you better avoid the game for now and maybe check back in a few months.All in all Edge of Eternity is a great game, in unexpectedly good quality for an indie title. For a relatively small price, you get a great adventure with lots of rough edges. Game fun for RPG fans is definitely possible in large quantities. The game is unfinished but should be enjoyable and playable for most players even in its current state.That’s why I would like to give a base score of 85% for this enormously good price-performance ratio. For unfinished design, small technical failures, and the prospect of a future price increase, I would like to deduct a total of 7% from this. This brings Edge of Eternity to a final score of 78 % as of August 2020.EN DE

_childDocuments_.review: ***THIS GAME POSES MASSIVE HEALTH RISKS THAT NEED TO BE FIXED IMMEDIATELY***I have completed this game so first, let me start with a positives and negatives list and then I'll jump into the serious problems with this game:Positives-Beautiful open world-Japanese VA (Not sure about Eng)-Story-Music-Occasionally interesting side quests-Character Building-AmbienceNegatives-Graphical glitches far too frequently and everywhere-Camera is horrendous-Mount feels bad to control-Giant cat mount gets stuck on every small rock bigger than its toenail-Music/sound design cuts in and out very frequently between interactions-No VA outside of main characters-Questing is horrendous: Nothing but fetch quests/kill x amount of this from start to finish of the game-Save points throughout the world are sometimes put in stupid places because cut scenes start and you are locked out of going back to the specific save point due to invisible walls-Combat is subpar at best and feels completely unfinished.-Grid system is janky and feels unfinished most of the time and causes the whole game to feel sluggishSERIES NEGATIVES AND PROBLEMS-Game at key points show ultimate attacks, but then change the design of them from the initial introduction. What is the point of having this really cool first look at an ultimate ability when right after that, that same ability is completely different for the rest of the game!?-Crafting system makes absolutely no sense. Combing attack and defense crystals gives you Speed and haste and magic crystal give you defense??? What? There is no incentive to save any specific type of crystal as none of them correlate to what they actually give you when combined-Bad mechanics in some parts of the game. In a certain area, that is not very large, you have to solve 7 of the same puzzles before getting to a boss fight. The whole thing is unnecessarily tedious-Multiple save files are permitted and that is nice. However, in my experience, I had the games autosave mechanic overwrite my manual save in favor of the auto save numerous times which led to absolute frustration to near points of uninstalling-Bugs everywhere. Abilities phasing through the ground, monsters floating 60 feet in the air and not coming down, random things disappearing, enemies AI messing up in fights, abilities not working properly and the list goes on-Said auto saves are randomized to hell and back. They are not consistent. You can get an auto save somewhere, get one again 8 minutes later and then not another one for another 20 minutes.-Certain quests are undoable until later on because your character is under leveled under normal progression circumstances. Serious grinding is needed if you encounter these SIDE QUESTS and it really feels like it shouldn't be.-Boss fights are unfair to varying degrees throughout the story-Game mechanics are introduced at specified points in the story that are half assed out of that specified point. I.E. hacking doesnt work when in other fights it does, regeneration works in a specified story point and never again so that mechanic should never even be introduced because it causes confusion with that character in your party later on thinking it still applies-No directive on what mechanics are and are not apart of the game outside their introduction which lead to annoyance and misunderstandings*****MASSIVE HEALTH RISK!!! PLEASE READ!!!*****This game has a serious problem with its cutscenes that were never fixed. I experienced throughout my playthrough several times of lights in many areas flickering and flashing constantly and being oddly too contrasted over what they should've been. Said lights also flickered and flashed in these areas but not all that badly. Still needs to be said for photosensitive people. During a main story sequence, had the entire screen freak out with half of the screen being covering in a bright white wall that kept flashing abruptly when the camera kept panning over the main character. I am not prone to epilepsy or am not photosensitive but this constant flashing sequence caused me a bad headache to the point of needing to block the screen until it was over. The main guys ultimate ability has overly bright flashing lights that need to be seriously toned down because every time I use it, I have to block my eyes, EVEN DURING MID DAY because the flashes are just far too intense. This game has been out for over a year and none of this was fixed. Too many flashing lights that are far to bright and far too intense for that they are and how they should be. I got several fairly moderate headaches from these flashes throughout the 40 some odd hours I put into this game.I really wanted to like this game because my girlfriend bought it for me on my birthday which is the day this game came out. This game is nowhere near finished and has been abandoned for over a year. At its core, it held a lot of promise, but its overbearing problems and negligent devs not fixing the main issues and serious technical problems with this game means you need to stay far away from it, even on sales. If you suffer from any photo-sensitivity, please, stay away from this game. I cannot warn you enough.

_childDocuments_.review: The devs attempted an ambitious project, but it’s clear they could not execute it properly. Grand ideas, without an accurate distribution of resources and manpower, ended up underdeveloped or done on an amateur level. Edge of Eternity is a game that promises much but delivers little.What ruins the game is storytelling. It’s done without a real understanding of character development or plot progression. Overwhelmed with cliché, overfilled with unoriginal ideas and predictable twists. As if in a cheap drama we beat an enemy girl nearly to death, because she attacked our heroine, only to have her miraculously recover and try the same ♥♥♥♥ — now with the other protagonist — in less than ten minutes.Oh, who needs realistic consequences for their actions in a video game, right? We aren’t playing an RPG, where character development and story progression are supposed to matter. Pathos and childish whims — that’s what replaces them. And don’t forget pointless cut-scenes that serve as nothing more than fillers.Sadly, even ignoring the story won’t help you much. Fighting becomes frustrating and repetitive in no time, taking away from any actual sense of accomplishment. Especially when you do nothing but run on an empty open arenas or gut-like corridors connecting them. Overall, Edge of Eternity is a mediocre waste of money worth of your attention only if you have zero other JRPG’s to play. And even then, better try some other genre.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all this game is about a 7.5 / 10On a true weighted scale...  Almost nothing reaches a 10, almost nothing is a 3 or below (that is actually released anyway) and the average game is... well a 5.Had this since it did its EA initial launchThe game was promising, along the way they abandoned a lot of ideas (you can see them briefly used in game then never again from time to time)It has improved in a number of ways since then, I don't plan to do a fresh fresh run on the game so what I have is from a mixed playthrough.The story was always mediocre 6/10Graphically its a 7/10Gameplay battles are a 5/10 - 8/10 depending on where you are in the storyEndurance in battles is quite limiting, you either overwhelm your enemy or you run out of mana to cast spellsAlso the mix mash of characters is inconsistent with how powerful / weak they are.  No thoughts of balance went into having party members that fill roles or don't just dominate the battle fieldVariety in spells is a 3/10 - They are mostly level 1 spells, you only come across level 2 on occasion (and again I haven't delved into crafting and won't its possible that they have level 2 or even level 3 spells for everything just tucked away behind crafting chains... they don't, but I like to imagine they might)... in addition a lot of the elemental types are still simply missing.  Lot of opportunity wasted to even have different tiers al la final fantasy to make them betterPuzzle mechanics are a 5/10, puzzle mechanic bosses with no rhyme or reason of how they work a 2/10 (which might have been fixed since I was there)Loot wise its a 6/10, you still get potions in the final dungeon... shame.  Chests shouldn't be worthless garbage.  Otherwise you are flooded with spell gems, flooded with cash, and flooded with useless weapons (which i again haven't looked into since launch, but weapons and armour pre going live were atrotiously bad)Lastly what you all come here for that NO other steam reviewer does... Mouth feelit gets an 8/10 on the mouth feel bringing its overall score up to 7.5/10This being said I'm wavering on throwing it to a no, multiple additional bugs in the end game part that lead to CTD and having to back to your saves.  More bosses with instant party wipe moves which is extremely poor gameplay.  A boss that you can't defeat (must lose to win and progress) and then the final boss who stops taking damage at 0 hp, nothing in the field you can interact with, additional damage doesn't end him, and then oh look a kill all party move again...The additional bugs knock 2 points off my mouthfeel score bringing the total to a 5.5/10, the meta score is higher can't recommend The really stumbled in their haste to make it over the finish line and it shows.

_childDocuments_.review: It's kind of mediocre. Pretty graphics but the gameplay feels wasted here. Edge of Eternity is a mix between a tactical cRPG and a Xbox360-era JRPG. The grid movement system is interesting, but the game rarely takes advantage of it in the first 13 hours. Most of the side quests I've encountered are simple "go here and kill a number of this thing" type quests. The side quests' stories are dull. The main quest is relatively dull and meandering too. There are also a lot of systems that don't really matter and just add busy-work. Overall, this game feels like a chore to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I had been eyeing this game for years already when it was in EA and was planning to wait for it to be finished. However, the game feels like it should still be in EA what with the amount of bugs and glitches happening. It isn't all bad, I did truly enjoy the first good half of the game. I didn't understand the negative feedback and felt people were being too harsh. I initially wasn't too bothered by the fact it lacked the quality a triple A game would have yet. I knew I was signing up for playing an indie title made by a small team, after all. I enjoyed what is there.But then, the game breaking glitches started to happen and slowly, it all started to crumble apart in every possible way. The last part of the game just... was a slogfest. Too much dialogue, too much stuff happening in one go. Too many loose ends and confusion. Too many dragged out moments and slow talking. Oh god, the slow talking and dragged out scenes of characters sobbing and other characters staring at sobbing character for seconds, it was agony, I just wanted the game to get to the point and be done with it by then. Too much walking down 'hallways' and fighting enemies over and over. Forced puzzles as well. Not a fan. And, while I did continue to consistently enjoy most the environments, music, and characters (most of the time, I didn't really like them all that much near the end any longer and agreed with the bad guy's spiel) and some of the main story moments and side-quests made me chuckle, half them also did the opposite. And more and more, the poor animations, namely the cutscenes, started to also grate on me more and more. It's one thing to not be able to make elaborate animations, but I felt what was within the devs ability was not utilized as well as it could have for cutscenes. Something 'happens' in a cutscene, for example. But it's very out of the blue and abrupt, and there for a split second, without any build up or explanation, and it goes by so fast, I was left wondering if it was a glitch at times, since... well, this game is glitch-city so it could have been but there was a certain consistency in this happening in cutscenes that I don't think it was a glitch. There's visual glitches where the sky keeps spazzing, sound glitches where you hear random loud galloping, voice lines cutting in and out, three different songs being played at once, quest items not showing up, you name it. This game's got it.Then, the combat is terrible for a multitude of reasons.  It's grid based turn based combat. Already not a fan of that because that kind of set up tends to be incredibly slow, waiting turns for each enemy to take one single step forward is tedious and boring. This is a matter of taste though. But even then, the way this game does it, doesn't help. For one, it is often impossible to get a good overview of the battlefield. It's also hard to see what is being selected most of the time. Then, the sounds are often not aligned with what is happening. Combat lacks a sense of impact. The skills look very mediocre too. It's very underwhelming.And the glitches and bugs are the most prominent and the worst in combat. Enemies are locked out of the battlefield grid and you can't get to them. You can often bypass this by hitting auto battle most of the time, as characters then attack through walls or what have you. But it's just... not good that one needs to resort to that. There will also be certain fights that have mechanics unique to that particular fights. Which is cool, I like the creativity of the devs to try and add variety to the fray. But, it's hardly ever explained. Then, the ultimate bug; some fights just completely stop working where your commands don't do anything, and you can wind up being softlocked. The only way I could get past it was through using the dev console. Why did I finish and play this game for the amount of time I have then? Well, like I said, I initially had a good time, so I decided to see the game through the end despite all these flaws because I had invested so much already and wanted to see how it'd end. This may be a bit spoilery so beware, but... I dunno if I feel it was worth doing that. The final portions of the game were bad, and the ending was.. anti-climatic. I am honestly confused what even was going on anymore with the protagonist. What was he even doing? How did he know how to do it? What was actually happening? How? As it stands, I can't in good conscience recommend the game, whereas during the first half I felt I was going to wind up giving a positive review. But I can't. Still, I do appreciate the devs for clearly handling feedback well and so I have faith that they have learned a lot from their mistakes, and that they will improve.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has no real identity.  The story is bland with very poor voice acting.  I'm 10 hours in and the main story is nothing but fetch quests that that never really feel like they're pushing along the story or towards your character's goals. I'm sure you've seen this before "Hey, I need item to get to place A", so you go to take a boat but you can't set sail because there's a sea monster, so you have to go kill the seam monster, then the sails of the ship are torn so you have to go kill 10 creatures for the materials to make a sail, oh then because the ship was delayed all the food spoiled so you have to go help them get more food, you go to the farmer but he lost his dog that protects the farm from predators so you need to get bait to lure back the dog...those aren't the exact details of this game but I didn't want to spoil anything.  The point is, everywhere you go you have to do so many sub tasks that you honestly forget what it is you're actually supposed to be doing.  It's just padding out the game.  Unfortunately the game itself isn't fun so it just makes the whole experience boring.The game isn't fun because instead of having a few core mechanic that are really well developed that just took too many ideas from other games and tried to cram them in one system and it all feels shallow:Crystals - This seems like it was taken from FFVII's materia system but has none of the flexibility.  Each character in this game has a set "type" of skill so you can't really use crystals to customize the characters.  Put a red crystal on the sword character and he gets a skill where he swings his sword and it's fire damage.  Put a yellow crystal on the sword character and he swings his sword  and it's lighting damage.  Put the same crystals on the mage and they'll cast magic that deals fire and thunder respectively.  You can't use these crystals to really customize the characters in even a fraction of other systems it borrows from.  Crafting - You find so many different types of materials in the open world and there are so many different types of materials that it's overwhelming to try and craft.  The number of items and materials in this game for how little they seem to be used makes crafting seem like you should just skip it, it's not worth the effort of figuring out what you need, where to find it, and then craft it as almost all of it can be purchased and it's just so much faster to do a few random battles to get the money to purchase what you need then the hassle of crafting.  Also when you're going to buy a recipe, I found no way to see the stats of what you'd craft.  So you'll see a sword recipe or armor recipe and have no way of knowing if it will be an improvement or not before you buy the recipe.Battle system - Tries to incorporate FFVII's ATB system while also trying to mix in an SRPG's grid and movement system.  It could have been fun if well implemented but there's not really any strategy to it.  It really just ends up being you have to waste extra turns for melee characters to keep moving into range of enemies that like to run away.  It's not like an SRPG where you have 8-12 units on a large map and can take tactical positions.  Sure there might be a buff on a certain square, or a turret you can activate but that's not strategy, it's just a no brain'er to use.  All in all, it just makes the battles take longer as you chase enemies that started the battle further away.All in all this game can be summed up as quantity over quality.  Extended fetch quests, too many shallow battle mechanics, and a cumbersome crafting system.  I can usually forgive a game if it has a bad story but fun game play or bad game play but a good story.  This game unfortunately has a boring story with boring game play.

_childDocuments_.review: Went in expecting a mediocre experience because that's what everybody was saying. Early combat is rough, feels sluggish and boring, and the combat camera sometime clips through terrain or trees, but once you get into customizing your crystals and gear, and the map opens up it's definitely better than mediocre. There's some jank to be sure but I find the gameplay loop addictive, environment fun to explore, story engaging, characters charming. I wound up doing most of the sidequests so far because I was having fun with them. NPCs have dialogue with worldbuilding and side content teaches you something about the world most of the time. 8/10 so far. Pacing has been good and the game has made me laugh out loud a few times. There's an option to enable saving from anywhere so the game is respectful of your time. Quest rewards matter so quests feel rewarding.So, a little rough around the edges but with a solid, shining core.

_childDocuments_.review: Game feels unfinished and needs a lot of work. I experienced plenty of gameplay bugs, game breaking bugs that required force shut down, crashes (Both random and frequent crashes in the same area). Lots of UI issues such as crafting tree navigation, no armour craft sort, no skill tracking when inserting crystals, can only track 1 quest at a time, no save point icons on world map, world map needs faster navigation, no explanation of stats (for example, what's the difference between haste and speed? What does resolve do?), etc. Biggest issue is more balance and progression feel. Despite having a party system, you spend so much of the game with just 2 characters. Then when you finally get your 3rd character, they leave you shortly afterwards and then you spend another huge chunk of time with just 2 characters again before getting your 3rd character back. Just doesn't feel that enjoyable.--Gearing progression could use workItem progression just feels off. 25 hours in and I'm still using the same weapon I crafted 2-3 chapters earlier...all the crafting mats, quest drops, boss drops are worst weapons than the weapon I crafted 10 hours earlier. Should not be like this. I did get a recipe for a stronger weapon but it requires higher tier items that I can't attain. This is fine but when combined with how little crafting trees there are, there shouldn't be that much useless crafts.--Autoplay AI can be unusable in certain conditionsAutoplay is nice to have in a game with a somewhat slow and tedious gameplay. Except the AI is terrible. Even when grinding battles that should be a easy win just spamming autoattacks, the AI will spam all their mana on the same debuffs over and over. They'll walk out of an AoE just to walk back into it. Environment effects just break AI to dumb levels where easy wins could be a game over.--A fair amount of bugs and crashesGame breaking bugs like sometimes the game will give you control of a NPC (turrets, puzzle npcs, etc.). You aren't suppose to have control of these characters. Problem is if the bug occurs and gives you control, you can't do anything. You can't take any action, skip your turn, or change to another character. The only solution is to restart. If it's a puzzle, you can restart no issue but if it was a battle it's gameover and you lose all your save progression. Super frustrating when this happens.There were a lot of gameplay bugs as well. For example, there is a quest where you have to fight waves of enemies. My first time, I lost really badly and on re-try I realized the quest bugged and spawned all waves at once. Another boss battle that had a mechanic to give you a X amount of turns to get to a safe spot, except the boss bugged and immediately did the mechanic without giving you the turns. Probably half, and I'm being generous with half, had issues.Nearing the end of the game now and it is buggier than ever. I've experienced several crashes so far causing me to lose progress and time. Some from cutscenes, some from battle. They are consistent, so I have to skip the problem cutscene or try to rush the mandatory fight before a crash happens. I've crashed over 7 times in one area alone, super frustrating for a game that no longer in early access and should not be happening. When I researched how to prevent these crashes, I found several topics saying you can't and these crashes happen on console ports too! If I had known the amount of crashes there are near the end of the ganme, I honestly would not have played this. It is clear there was insufficient QA in general and the later sections of the game was rushed.--Balance issues with useless charactersThere is also some balance issues. Some characters speed is so far ahead of the other characters it makes them feel like deadweight. If you're fighting a boss and there is a mechanic such as a area wipe, if you're unlucky and this occurs when you're sub characters have low turn bars, they might die without getting a turn. Meanwhile your speed characters are not only out safely but you have to keep skipping their turn waiting for the mechanic to be over.Many characters such as tanks and supports are just dead weight due to how low their innate speed and gears are. By the time they set anything up, your DPS characters have had multiple turns and have done many times their possible damage.--Mediocre and generic JRPG storyLastly, the story is stereotypical JRPG, nothing to write home about. Character personalities are VERY cliche and pretty bland. The main character is so edgy it makes me cringe. World lore is okay.Gameplay is a hate it or love it thing, it is turn based and can be very slow. I say most people will get bored of the gameplay in a few hours and will settle with autoplay. I only managed to not lose my mind as I had a huge backlog of youtube videos I had playing on the side. This is actually a great game if you have something to watch on the side.Overall game is not bad but at its current state I can't say I recommend it. RPGs take a fair amount of time to complete and there are a lot more polished RPGs than this. If steam had a neutral option, I would pick that instead.

_childDocuments_.review: So I wouldn't over hype this game.   The game isn't going to on par with tales of or final fantasy.  The game is graphically sound but I think they spent too much time wanting to make a game that looked like a modern AAA game and I don't think they're going to make that time back if they're planning to release the finished game next year.  The first thing I looked at when I opened the game was the settings just like any other game.  First impressions come significantly from the settings.  There's no key mapping.  There's a confusing slider for mapping between preset options but there's actually only one option but you can slide it between option A and option A.  A lot of the times key mapping lets you get a gist of what the controls are, how you're expected to interact with the world, and fixing poor mapping choices so that E is your interaction key just like in every other game.  Beyond that the graphics settings are very confusing.  The resolution is up there at the top and you have to scroll down a very small very slow moving bar and your stuck wondering why they didn't just do it like every other game.  There are a million settings with their own scroll bars with little information about what the option does or how resource intensive it is.  The biggest problem is really that there's too much going on in the menu and each of the options take up way too much space while the important options like resolution, fps, v-sync, gamma, full or windowed screen, and what not are either relegated to the peripheral or not included.  Menus and options are very important to a game.  I don't think we really appreciate how much a games various menus, its level of direct communication and interaction with the player, quantifies the overall quality of a game.  This game has very bad menus.  They are confusing and offer very little explanation, guidance, or choice to the player.  The tab menu for the game doesn't economize it's space at all.  It doesn't look good.  Important information doesn't pop out at you.  Very basic options and navigation aren't emphasized at all.  It's not quickly apparent on how to change characters in specific lists like equipment or crystals.  The menus are very difficult to work in as you'll be using the mouse to navigate  with very little keyboard navigation.  In general this game uses the mouse way too often to the point where I'm pretty sure the developers do not use the mouse and keyboard and have never used the mouse and keyboard set-up.  I haven't tried the game with a controller.  A young relative broke my steam controller I'd be curious if they have a decent preset for that or if they support playstation controllers since why would anyone have an xbox. That's not a criticism of them.  It's just that the full controller support tag is given out far too often and Steam should specify exactly what hardware is supported.  I'm off topic.  I'm coming at the game from the mouse and keyboard set up.  In that set-up navigating the menus is not very satisfying.  The next major issue I have with the game is the big yellow dot.   Having objective markings is actually very bad and lazy feature of a game when it's just on a mini map.  I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hate objective markers in games.  The game becomes following the big yellow dot.  This big yellow dot isn't on a map.  it's right there at the start of the game laid over the environment.  Like you're looking around at the world and theres a big yellow dot.  That's actually enough to ruin the entire game.  I didn't have any fun because I was just following the big yellow dot. I was just stupidly, brainlessly following the big ass dot.  It usually indicates poor level design to have a big dot on the screen.  It means the level designer didn't make the map noticeable enough to navigate it without being directly told.   The bits that I've played through were fairly simple to figure out where to go since they were generally straight forward.  Maybe the level designer thinks the user is too stupid to navigate a straight forward path without a big ass yellow dot to follow.  I don't know.  Really there isn't anything else to say as long as that dot remains whatever potential the game had is ruined.  Speaking of annoying ♥♥♥♥ on the display, your mouse pointer is visible through game play.  Speaking of the mouse pointer you use your mouse way too much in this game.  Let's look at combat.  You have hot keys for combat actions.  Maybe xcom has the whole idea of hitting the key twice to confirm action or tabing between enemies patented or something, but the fact that you have to use your mouse so much in combat is a serious issue that slows down combat to a grinding halt.  It's not fun.  I'm playing it thinking that the developers didn't both playing the games similar to the genre their attempting to emulate. It's that simple ♥♥♥♥ at the core a game that will break it.  The game mechanics suck.  If the game looked like minecraft but it had really nice menus and really good controls it would be a better game.  People feel like what they want is a visually appealing game.  The developers feel like what they want to do is make a visually appealing game.  What people actually want is a mechanically sound game that's satisfying to play and they'll play a game that looks like final fantasy 7 if it plays well.  I don't know what the game is going to look like in it's finished state but I can tell you what the developers value and what they'll probably continue to focus on and ignore.  They want to make a visually appealing game.  That's what they care about and they're going to fail because the amount of time and effort it takes to make all of the assets and get all of the details right is too much.  They should have made a game with lower graphics.  I really don't think that these core quality of life features are going to be addressed.  It's too much and it should have been their focus a long time ago.  Let's talk about combat again.  I lacks crunch.  It doesn't feel satisfying.  There are a lot of other games to figure this out and I don't think they really bothered.   This probably has to do with cluttered screen space and no audio art designed to identify important situations .  Again they could have spend a lot less time on the graphics and a lot more time on the audio of the game.  Any those are the problems I took issue with in the game.  Should you get the game right now?  That's up to you.  If you like this particular genre.  I you like the charm of small studios getting over their heads.  If you don't mind the risk of early access then buy the game.  The game isn't broken.   It is severely unfinished.  There's quality and attention put into the game that you can really see.  I don't feel as though it was placed where it should have been.  I think they really should have been game mechanics in place rather than pretty graphics.  I think they should have better level designs rather than big yellow dots and pretty graphics.  The game running at 60 fps is more important to essentially all of us than that the game look competitive to AAA games and It's not going to look competitive at any frame rate.  They don't have the budget and the only thing almost good enough graphics gets you is very ugly character models.  The game seems to fail to understand what makes a game compelling.  It doens't Ask what makes other games work.  I don't feel like they're going to fix this more tedious issues. The don't consider it important.

_childDocuments_.review: i bought this in Early Access and didn't really play it until about a week ago.  After one go around on normal, I'm kinda split on whether I'd recommend.  The games graphics and visuals are just gorgeous.  They really built up a beautiful world with multiple biomes, the characters are well drawn and the animations are smooth.  That said, there is a distinct lack of any of this really being brought to life.  There are about 10 different mobs, reskinned and scaled as you progress through the world.  The people in towns are inconsequential, static and for lack of a better word, generic. The story, is meandering, full of tropes and never actually fleshed out.  Characters are introduced and dismissed without actually progressing the story and in the end, nothing is actually explained.  It left me with the feeling that the authors had vague ideas of concepts they wanted to incorporate but settled for simple mentions of the concept without ever touching on it again, or tying it into the plot.  The whole war is never really explained which was irksome.  At times there is little direction on where to find things (I finished the game, and I have no idea if the top craft-able weapons recipes exist or where to find them).  I swear I picked up recipes for end game craftable leather and other items but there is no workbench that I can assemble them on.  Some weapon craft tiers I picked up the top recipe but have no clue where to get the prerequisite weapon recipe to craft the damn thing.  Combat is at first fluid and fun, as you learn the system, but after about 10 hours you'll end up playing on 4x speed wishing there were an even faster option or even an auto function.  Enemies will glitch spawn out of range, entire maps will place your characters in places they cant move out of with enemies that will never close range.  Stats aren't very well explained, for example there is a Speed trait, a Haste trait and an Incantation Speed trait.  For the life of me, i still have no idea what the difference between Haste and Speed are.  The camera becomes endlessly frustrating when trying to select a target (i played through on a gamepad), and I would often thing i was aiming at one mob and strike another.Hardware-wise I played through on a 5900x and a RTX 3070 and scenes would bog down in certain places (Towns would load in piecemeal, animations would stutter in combat, etc).  Overall the game was enjoyable but left me feeling like it was going nowhere.  I'd pay the current sale price of 25 bucks US but not sure i could recommend it for any more.  It still feels unfinished despite being out of early access.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's a shame but the animations are jarring.It's pretty noticeable because the rest of the game is wonderful. The music, the battles,the UI, the sounds, the graphics. All of that is amazing  for an indie title. The voices are "meh" in my opinion, never could listen to anime styled characters talking in american english. It looks weird.I don't understand why every indie team is so ambitious. If the mayority of the cutscenes were made with dialogue balloons, the size of the maps were smaller and the graphics a little less cinematic there would be more money to use on animations. And animations should be important if the characters have voices and move around a big world  full of wooden people.  If animations aren't polished why do cinematic cutscenes? Maybe a visual novel style for the dialogues was a better choice. Who knows.The way the game is now it looks they've sacrificed animations to focus on the rest of the game. It must've been a difficult choice. The thing is that the difference between animations and the rest of the polished game is just too much. Try to walk slowly with your character and look how he moves. Same for running and when they move from one hex to another in battle. Same for cutscenes. It's terrible.The problem is that they are pretty detailed and high resolution so if they move like puppets it's uncanny. If you are aiming for so much details animations must be on par.If animations are fixed or if the game reaches some kind of balance with this issues I will definitely play this game. As it is now it takes me out of the game and the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick and simple review. Decent-playing JRPG style with an impressive attempt at world-scale and building, creature design, and storytelling. I've just entered an environment that is wonderfully glowy and blue. Pretty!What I'm enjoying most, is the crystal-based weapon socket system that determines the party members' skills. Though so far, the characters are tied to specific jobs, there is plenty of room for experimentation. Casting speed over spell damage? Damage over protection? Try to get  close to balance? - Working out what suits the grander encounters  best is an engaging process of trial/error and learned application of strengths.Limitations on items brought into combat encourages using your party members' inventory uniquely as well. There's a greater demand on strategy in this way; you aren't taking 99 potions into battle that any character can access. I'm enjoying the early chapters of Edge of Eternity, and look forward to moving ever closer to that.... edge.

_childDocuments_.review: Edge of Eternity is an ambitious turn-based RPG that manages to strike a delicate balance between classic and modern elements. Developed by Midgar Studio, this visually stunning game captures the essence of traditional JRPGs while infusing it with a fresh and engaging world.The standout feature of Edge of Eternity is its captivating storyline. Set in a vast fantasy universe on the brink of destruction, players embark on an epic journey to save their homeland from an otherworldly threat. The narrative is filled with compelling characters, intricate plot twists, and emotional moments that keep you invested throughout the game.The gameplay mechanics in Edge of Eternity are solid, offering a blend of strategic combat and exploration. The turn-based battles are challenging yet rewarding, allowing players to customize their characters with a wide range of skills and abilities. The world is beautifully crafted, featuring diverse landscapes, ancient ruins, and breathtaking vistas to discover.One of the game's most striking aspects is its stunning visuals. The art direction is top-notch, with vibrant colors and meticulous attention to detail bringing the world to life. From the towering cityscapes to the ethereal magical realms, Edge of Eternity is a visual feast that never fails to impress.However, the game does suffer from some technical issues and occasional pacing problems. While these hiccups are minor and do not detract significantly from the overall experience, they are worth mentioning.In conclusion, Edge of Eternity is a commendable RPG that successfully combines the best elements of traditional and modern gaming. With its captivating storyline, engaging gameplay, and breathtaking visuals, it offers an immersive experience that will leave fans of the genre satisfied. Despite a few minor flaws, it is a solid addition to any RPG enthusiast's collection.

_childDocuments_.review: I have waited years for the "final release" to play something that's out of early access, but sadly, it still feels like it is. The game is riddled with small bugs/annoyances and coppy transitions, and overall still feels very amateurish. There are also very weird design choices (bought new equipment, they all have the EXACT SAME STATS as a different set, can craft 2 different weapons with the exact same stats...why) and lack of QOL elements most RPGs had since two decades (being able to buy/sell more than one item at once or seeing stats comparison on gear for example.The environments look stunning but are held back by the characters who look awful. Overall, it feels like they bit more than they could chew, it was a very ambitious project with low budget, took years and they just had to put the final stamp on it at this point

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly rate this game A, at least for effort. There is very little I find myself complaining about. The voice acting seems to be a small crew but despite seeming amateur I really enjoyed the dialogue and many character interactions. Combat doesn't require tactical levels of concentration but if you don't pay attention you can end up in a really bad spot fast.The biggest complaint is bugs and glitches. They are going to happen probably every other time you boot up, as of this review. Some animation issues will occur, sometimes you will have to reset the game, as long as you save at every save point you shouldn't lose progress unless you really unlucky. That being said they are VERY open to receiving notices of any issues to the extent of there being a bug report tool in the pause menu. TL;DR They know the game isn't perfect but they want to make it as great as they can so if you like RPGs and are patient this game is a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily understandable mechanics that nonetheless require a bit of attention in every fight, good music, non-standard characters who deliver at least decent banter, a unique design and pretty surroundings. Good tutorial for its systems.BUTThis is a slow burner. I'm over an hour in and am still just running into a singular direction towards the first town. The only things happening so far are a few tutorial areas and two tutorial mini bosses. I feel the need to add that those tutorial bosses were decently well designed and taught the importance of movement in combat, with the second one being fully capable of killing the party if the player decided to just stand around and knock it on the head round after round.The problem with this game is its ability, or rather inability, to hold the player's attention:I have progressed through three areas so far and nothing noteworthy has happened. Which can be fine, if the things that aren't noteworthy are done well. Sadly, they are merely okay to good~ish.Furthermore, the maps are pretty and big. Pretty in the sense that they really sell the world that this plays in and are nice to look at. Big in the sense that distances actually feel somewhat realistic. I've walked a few kilometers in this game by now. And while this does indeed give the player a sense of scale, it also is rather boring. These treks from A to B feel slow. There doesn't appear to be a sprint option beyond a minor speed increase that is also linked to a rapidly depleting stamina meter, meaning that movement feels somewhat inhibited. While big, stretching environments are nice to look at, moving at a "normal" pace just stretches parts of the game that are unintersting to begin with. Imagine walking similar distances as in FFX but without the neat bends in the road and with little to explore. This really becomes apparent in the area before the first town.Overall, I recommend the game in its current state and at its current price of 19.99€.It gives a nice feeling that, so far, only the old RPGs from the mid 2000s really held.However, it requires a massive amount of patience. A kind of patience that I severely lack.

_childDocuments_.review: The music is good............that's all I can say (it IS Yasunori Mitsuda, soooo...)I played 2 hours. That's all I could stomach. Unlikeable characters and a storyline/conflict I just did not care about even as far as 2 hours in (if we aren't connecting with the characters after 2 hours with them, something is very wrong with the character writing), very cut-and-paste fantasy style story (oh no big bad disease petrifying people! ...I'd have been so mad if later there was a "let's fix it with FUTURE TECHNOLOGY!" - if I wanted that, but in a GOOD game, I'd fire up Star Ocean The Last Hope...seriously this game is THAT uninspired). Oh and I haven't got to the battle system yet. I love turn based and have been hurting for new games with it, I'm a very traditional JRPG player..and there were some good concepts here, but the execution was awful. For a game released in 2021, there are some pretty egregious graphics style choices (was this made for a Switch...?) and glitches (was this tested...? oh, yes, it was, by us, the customer) - I counted at least two instances of the global shadows/day night cycle glitching horrendously, on the SAME world map.Overall, I regret having purchased. Your money is better spent elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: A game with plenty of passion but no concise vision in mind. A bunch of ideas and mechanics thrown together aimlessly which leaves you with an over designed bloated mess.I guess I'll start with the positives. It's got pretty scenery and somewhat interesting lore... they made a decent effort for the writing and voice acting. The combat is certainly an attempt at changing up the JRPG formula. So for the gameplay, it feels like basically any open world game you've played in recent years but with some really bizarre design choices that I'm shocked made it through early access. A lot of design choices taken from MMOs, running around finding all the ! marks above peoples heads to cross off the list. The bland board hunt quests of just kill X number of Y enemy. A needless amount of work benches/vendors/items. It also has some of the most intrusive and handholdy tutorials I've ever seen in a game. The game will stop you to tell you how to do things you've already done 4 or 5 times. Lets start with the map. They have every vendor on the map. They have rest spots and inns. Not save/fast travel points which you use the most so you just have to remember where they are. Even the quest boards aren't on the map so if you missed a quest for that area have fun going back when you finally notice. How no one pointed this out in the years it was in early access is beyond me or maybe it was just ignored. This might be why they included the option to save anywhere because finding a save point can be so difficult. This has been a feature in games (JRPGs in particular) since the PS2 but I guess they just forgot here. Also why does fast travelling cost money, more MMO ideas for you.While exploring everything looks pretty with nice blue glowing effects everywhere. It's nice... until you realise that most pick ups use a blue glowing effect to show they're pickupable. So everything looks like it can be picked up, if you're a completionist hoarder may the dead gods help you. There's a lot of shin high fences that block your path, unfortunately there isn't a jump button. So get ready to walk round a lot of pointless walls. A sprint stamina metre that if you use too much weakens your party in combat. It's a push that your combat trained character can only run for 10 seconds before getting tried but mounts as well? Really?!The gear/crystals/upgrades. The best way to describe the crystal system would be imagine materia from FF7 but make it mostly random stat boosts that sometimes have random abilities and they're found everywhere. So imagine materia but without that discovering a new spell feeling, just the 100th attack +1 defence +2 red crystal. It's all needless RNG; all of it. Crystals with random abilities/stats, random drops/random selection at vendors. Craft gear, it's stats are random. There's no compare option for crafted gear to see if it's worth crafting something because you don't know what you're getting. There are (at least) 4 different work benches all with different things that are needed to craft on other workbenches. It's all so MMO. It feels like if you played FF14 and levelled up every crafting class, just running back and forth to check what you need for one item every time you want to make anything. You can also fuse crystals with a random chance to get a better one. When I put 5 in for a "100% chance of a better gem" and it still came out as the "same" level I knew the RNG was just wasting my time. Again it feels so much like an MMO just trying to pad out the run time by making you roll the dice to get anything worth while. The combat. The UI is either pointless or broken. Enemies are strong or weak to certain elements and it's meant to mark which above the enemy after you've used that element on it. Very SMT/Persona. But it doesn't give you enough information. Say you're fighting an enemy, the game says it's resistant to fire/ice/lighting but fire does 100 damage, ice 120, lighting 600. This happened for the vast majority of battles. So you were better off trying to remember each enemy for their weaknesses rather than using the UI which is meant to tell you. Luckily by the time you finish chapter one you'll notice you've basically only been fighting the same 4 enemies with slightly different names over and over so you'll have a good idea what works the first time you meet a "new" enemy. They really mix it up when they start throwing "corrupt" or "ethereal" versions of the same monsters, usually with the same weaknesses. It can also be really difficult to work out what you're targeting, more so when you're trying to heal. The "highlight" for your target is the same as it's a target with a slight intensity change. So when you're trying to heal are you aiming at the guy with the white flashing circle or the guy with with the slightly bigger white flashing circle. The skip button at the end of combat is more of a suggestion than a working button. You can mash skip or wait for the exp bar slowly fill up, it takes the same amount of time. The story and the characters. Not much to say really. Feels like a typical JRPG. Though at the 13 hour mark only having two party members gets stale. A lot of it feels overwritten and it can drag out some scenes but you could argue that's a trope of the genre. Then the bugs. Enemies getting stuck off the battle map but it's still hitting you but you can't hit it. Menus stop working so you have to exit out and hope it works next time. I had a hard time getting a DS4 controller to work. It worked on the main menu but not in game. Setting the resolution to 59 hz, locking the frame rate to 60, turned off v-sync, the game wouldn't stay below 100 fps. So it was a weirdly high demanding game performance wise. Might need a 3rd party program for both controller and framerate. Honestly when I finished the prologue I was contemplating refunding the game but I thought I'd have some faith and keep pushing on. That was my mistake. By the end of the first chapter my patience ran out.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is weird. It strikes me as a game made by a small team that got themselves way out of their league. The whole game seems like good ideas executed poorly. I think that if you're going to do a game with a team of this size, it would make more sense to go with a more stylistic art style to hide the jank, because when you go for a more serious realistic look like this game does, the cracks show very easily and you can't as easily ignore it as part of the style.I want to like it, but it's about the most average, unremarkable thing I've played in a while. It's not bad... it just doesn't give me a reason to play it instead of something else, and when there are as many games out as there are these days, you need to do better to compete for people's limited time.
