_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking through reviews wondering why there are so many negative ones recently, know this: People can't read, don't want to understand that this is Early Access or even spend the time playing the game. Your best choice is to ignore said reviews massively as they do not represent the actual quality of this Early Access and the game itself. Furthermore the team has only 9 people as of writing this review. There were less at the start.Now to the actual review itself. I'll start with the performance aspect of the game.I've bought into this Early Access from the first day it launched on Steam. At the start I had the game running on an i5-3570k @4.2GHz with a GTX670 2GB and 8GB DDR3 RAM. At first the game was running very poorly, couldn't reach 30FPS outside of the first two zones regardless the settings (resolution always was 1080p). HOWEVER...On the game's Discord, the developers are very active, open and helpful. They immediately acknowledged the issues, informed about why there are issues and their plan for how to deal with it in time. And indeed, in time with updates, the performance was steadily improving. From a relatively unplayable experience I got to a relatively stable 30FPS at medium settings. While there were still issues and in places the framerate dropped massively, it was still not final and optimisations were still to happen.Again, most importantly, developers were always open about it and they constantly try their best.Later on I moved to a 1060 6GB, and I was able to play at stable 60FPS at max settings at 1080p. With the latest optimisations that only improved. Moreover the stuttering that was quite noticeable and jarring at the start was steadily reduced and the frame timing as of now is incredibly good. Gameplay is very smooth even if you run at lower FPS (I tried running at 4K for lols).Bottom line? As long as you meet the minimum requirements and adjust the settings accordingly, you should have a playable experience that will most likely still improve in time.Now onto the gameplay:It's a turn based jRPG, therefore those familiar with Final Fantasy games will most likely feel at home due to the "ATB" gauge. You have normal attack, ability to move on the field, spells and skills that cost mana (HP and MP regenerate between battles, similar to FFXIII) along with some static objects that can be used to damage enemies, heal yourself etc. With the latest chapter also "limit break" ability dropped in for one of the characters. Basically all the good stuff that you'd expect from jRPG are present... bar one.Gear. This is the one and only gripe I have with the game so far. The equipment system is akin to the RNG loot based system from games like Diablo or Nioh. Every piece of gear has different rarity levels, that can roll different stats with different values on them. While this adds to replayability, I feel like it goes against the jRPG spirit and adds only unnecessary grind that isn't very enjoyable, at least for me personally. Developers have stated there is some unique gear planned that will have fixed stats on it, so that possibly will help, but regardless I feel like the gearing is the weakest point of the game so far.Audio and visuals:Game has a specific art style to itself. It's neither photo realistic or full anime style. More of a blend of the two. You may like it or not but the game overall has a rather charming look to it even if it's arguably not among the prettiest games out there. This is probably also where people may feel like the game "doesn't perform well" when compared to the visuals at display, however that confusion is purely due to the art style used (maybe also the weird vegetation system that at lower settings changes lush forest into a barren wasteland). Just because something doesn't look photorealistic doesn't mean it's easier to render in any way.Sound wise though... it's a much more consistent experience so to speak. If you've played through many jRPGs it's almost guaranteed that many of the songs will "hit you in dem feels" hard, as some of them have strong nostalgic feeling. The rest while not being as good, still presents a good level that matches surroundings where you can easily enjoy exploring without feeling boring or generic.Early Access experience:This is by far the best thing about this game. Developers are open, they engage in discussions on the games official Discord server, if you have issues they or community will try to help with it. Also currently they are trying to cycle between a content and optimisation phases, so one month there are optimisations, other there's a content drop.Most importantly though you can see that said developers are just jRPG fans. They are passionate about their work and the games in general. Feels like the Razer motto here would describe it well: "By gamers for gamers".Naturally Discord is also the place where the new information usually drops first. It's not uncommon for someone's suggestion to be added later into the game. In fact depending on what it is, it can happen within hours. I've been a part of 4... no, 5 Early Access games so far. This is by far and wide the best, especially if they keep it up. I'm saying that since I was in another Early Access where at the start the devs were open and friendly but later on they just jumped on nostalgia hype and instead of making the game they proclaimed, they ignored community, threw features and just called it a day. Hopefully that will not be the case here.Summary:Game is a solid base. There's still a lot to be done but everything is moving in the right direction. Optimisation passes happen after every bigger content update and developers are extremely active and open. There are few things that some may not like but in overall the game is more likely to attract you and keep you playing than otherwise. Also some butthurt people who haven't played more than 1h are bombing with negative reviews. Ehh...

_childDocuments_.review: This will be my first review on Steam.First impressions of this Alpha rease are extremely posotive.  The graphics are very nice and the open world concept showcases it very well.  The turn based combat is well done.  Questing is straight forward, pick it up, go to way point, finish the objective, turn in.  Currently 8-10 hours of actual storyline/side quest content in game as this is only the first installment of Alpha.  Expect to get to level 15 or so as a soft cap.  After you finish with the main story line you have access to free roam in the current content.  Gather your mats and try your hand at crafting some gear.  4 levels of gear, White/Green/Blue/Purple.  There is currently 3 Legendary free roaming Beasts in the content as well.  Weapons are enhanced with a tree augment system.  Crystals are equipped in slots to gain not only the crystal benefit but also the slots contain a buff as well.  You gain your spells and special abilities through this system as well.  Other good things to note.  The devs are on Discord and Steam contantly checking messages on issues that need to be addressed.  They are a pleasure to talk to.  Hotfixes are being implemented as they get the kinks worked out.  Are there bugs?  Yes.  It is Alpha.  But so far when the bugs get reported the devs are quick to fix them.  I am currently free roaming just to find them so the game can be that much smoother for the launch.  Cons:  Well there are bugs.  Also some people are experiencing framerate and lag issues which the devs are working on fixing as I type this review.  I run a 1080ti slightly overclocked and have minimall to no frame issues.  If you are looking for a classic RPG with the potential for 100+ hours of game play when it is completed, give this game a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally reviewed this back when it was in Early Access, and had good things to say about it. I've tried picking it back up again now that it's live, and while I'm enjoying it... I also find myself incredibly bored with it at the same time.Turn-based RPGs are pretty much all I play with RPGs, but the combat is clunky, the crafting and item system make 0 sense (and is clunky), and while the story is good the dialogue really could use some full localized writers on it. It's not great and I find myself skipping through it.Combat: The grid based system is neat, but very bland and kinda pointless. Moving feels terrible in this game, and sometimes you're forced to move multiple times even with characters who are very slow. The combat is easy very easy or very hard, with no in between. You're either desperately trying to heal yourself, or maybe you throw out a single healing spell in a boss fight. Honestly, it'd just feel better to have a typical "front line, back line" and call it a day at this point.Crafting/Items: The crystal system is a cool take on a (very simple) license board, but in practice is done badly. It's not intuitive at all, and it's incredibly bland. "2% magic defense" "3% physical damage". And then the damage types themselves make no sense -- Apparently according to what I've found on the internet, the main character does *only* physical damage even with his "abilities" that do elemental damage which is information you CANNOT find anywhere. There's like 3 different haste stats that are not explained at all, and some of them don't even work for certain characters so it's wasted.The crystal system itself with the spells is a bit of a mess -- they're constantly changing spells, and every time you adjust one, it changes position on your hotbar, so your buttons are always in different places..The crafting is incredibly not-user friendly either. There's a list of materials that you need. Can you figure out at ALL how you get them? Nope. Look that up online. But then this game is, currently, so small that you can't even find info for it like you can for bigger games of course. That's not the fault of the creators, but I do fault them currently for just the absolute lack of information. Problem being, 99% of your stat upgrades come from crafting weapons/armor and good luck finding things unless you kill EVERYTHING you come across and explore 100% of the map to do so. Which, I like exploring, but even then you miss things, and fighting every 5 seconds with random, boring encounters.. Pass. this game still feels like it's in beta. It's definetly come past alpha, but it feels like it's in beta and still needs a lot of polishing and QOL before it would be a release game. Except, it is released now. I would NOT recommend buying this yet, but check back in a year. I do have hope for the developers.

name: KILL KNIGHT
detailed_description: Once a loyal knight, betrayed, and banished to the Abyss. A desecrated corpse inside reanimated armor. You rise to an eternal death. Branded KILL KNIGHT, you have one purpose - KILL THE LAST ANGEL. FIVE ELDRITCH LAYERS KILL, OR BE KILLED Dance with death in the Abyss, and unveil intricate layers of gameplay lurking beneath the surface. Exploit enemy weaknesses, enact brutal executions, weave through your arsenal to tactically manage resources, and unleash destructive wrath blasts to turn the tide. Every encounter is testament to your mastery. KILL KNIGHT’s polished, minimalist aesthetic, and retro visuals pay homage to the neon-soaked arcades and shooters of the 90’s. Set across five relentless, hand-crafted eldritch arenas, KILL KNIGHT embraces lo-fi brutalism and revels in the dread and dream-like ruins that surround your descent into the Abyss. Survive the otherworldly onslaught and complete challenges to unlock powerful new equipment for your Knight’s Arsenal, and evolve your unique playstyle. Learn to harness the special abilities and fire-modes of KILL KNIGHT’s array of pistols, heavy weapons, swords, and armor. Take your fight to the global leaderboards against friends and foes alike. Enter if you dare, Knight, and revel in the carnage. Fast and visceral top-down, push forward combat that rewards aggression and precision An immersive otherworld dripping in corrosive atmosphere with a retro-inspired aesthetic Descend through five fatal layers , each more deadly than the last Choose your challenge, with four distinct difficulty settings to overcome Survive long enough to raise your Kill Power , increasing speed and damage Complete challenges to unlock your Knight’s Arsenal, and evolve your playstyle Dive into Sever Mode , combining all five layers into one extended arena challenge Ascend the global leaderboards , and compete with friends for high-score supremacy Join the community on Discord!

_childDocuments_.review: Kill Knight is finally here! After 6 months and dying to play the game after heavily enjoying the demo, was it worth the wait? I’d say so. Does it set the twin stick genre on fire and take it to a new realm of game design and arcade action?  Not exactly, but it does offer a lot to fans of the genre. ———————It’s sad that this needs a disclaimer, but first it should be mentioned this is NOT a vampire survivors type game or a roguelite, and NO, that does not make it worse.  This is an arcade game and arcade games live and breathe via their gameplay systems, score-chasing potential, tight and polished gameplay and level design, and a deemphasizing of fluff, including hundreds of useless guns/upgrades and randomized/procedurally generated levels.  This is a skill based genre that rewards mastery, not getting lucky via the right perks. Now onto the actual review.———————————At its core, Kill Knight like all twin stick arcade games share DNA with games like robotron and smash TV.  The first thing that sets it apart is its loadout system. Your knight is compromised of several aspects to their kit such as primary and secondary weapon, sword, armor, cape etc. each category has different gear that you must unlock, and you can mix and match the gear to make a build that suits you.  There are no other alternate characters, but the loadout system lets you make many combinations.  The first critique is some gear seems to invalidate others and sometimes feel like direct  improvements of previous gear.  Some of the weapons don’t seem to change playstyle too much either. It’s solid but could have been better. The next thing that sets kill knight apart is its mechanical depth. There are a lot of options and attacks available compared to a typical twin stick shooter. There’s a gears of war active reload system with a 3 forked choice of what attack to do during the reload. You have a primary and secondary fire with a doom eternal style ammo system for secondary weapons. You can absorb enemy orbs at any time with a button to pull them towards you magnetically. Your secondary weapon also has a special shot once you absorb enough enemy orbs. You also have a sword that can be used any time. Your sword can also parry certain attacks and do execution style kills on staggered enemies. There’s also bayonetta style witch time that can be activated after a parry as well as a hyper attack once your sword meter is fully filled. While at first it seems a lot to keep track of (and it is), it doesn’t really take long to get a grasp of the gameplay loop. It essentially boils down to knowing what active attack to do to keep your resources in equilibrium and also to maximize damage per second.  The positive of the gameplay systems is in giving the player more options, there’s more opportunity for meaningful player decisions and there’s a constant resource and weapon management aspect while also fighting the enemies. This requires the player to develop situational awareness in order to help inform their decisions. The downside is while the breadth of mechanics does add to the strategy, at times it can feel like the actual depth of the game isn’t quite parallel to the breadth of attacks, sometimes making the game feel mechanically bloated without adding much. Again, there’s a lot of good here, but the game doesn’t quite take full advantage of its mechanics. The level design follows a similar trend, and by now you may be noticing the overarching pattern. The level design is pretty good, but can feel like a bit of a one-trick-pony in that the game relies too heavily on a single aspect of the level design for being a condensed arcade game; that aspect is the arena lasers.  Basically, the arena sizes and shapes are constantly changing, and eventually the game starts adding in these lasers that you must dodge through while fighting enemies. It seems like a mechanic that you’d expect occur in a part of the run then move onto something else, but this laser system once it is introduced in level 1 becomes the bread and butter for basically the rest of the entire run. The laser patterns do change constantly, and each level does introduce new enemy types and some level specific mechanics. It just feels at times that these new introductions from level to level take a back seat to the arena lasers and I feel the game was too heavy handed with this system as a way to try to force difficulty rather than through more fundamental bullet-hell aspects like complex bullet patterns or enemy types. Speaking of enemy types.  Again there’s a lot of good here but don’t quite live up to their potential for me, and that is mainly because many of the enemy types have very direct and easy solutions, such as just waiting for the chance to parry and kill them, or another example is the game basically wants you to always use special shot on armored enemies (armored enemies are purple and your special shot is purple and causes explosions when shot into armored enemies).  Essentially, what  could otherwise have been great ways to pressure the player into scary situations via enemies at times can feel like the game gives you too easy methods to dispatch even what are supposed to be the most tanky and threatening enemies instantly. I’ll begin to wrap up my review with a collection of assorted thoughts. -I personally think the health system is too generous. You can go from basically on the brink of death to back to full health pretty quickly in some scenarios, undermining the typical arcade aspect of your mistakes having long term consequences (often the main consequence of getting hit is lowering your score).  -The bosses (or lack thereof).  Not to spoil anything, but the game was underwhelming with its boss design, however this is basically a staple with twin stick shooters as really none of them have great bosses and they all generally use the same general bullet patterns with straight shooting bullets that fan out in circular shapes. - the game feel of kill knight is excellent and perhaps its defining feature. It just “feels” good. Very smooth, you move fast but not too fast. Weapons feel fun. Killing enemies is fun. You’re a knight. You kill. What’s not to like?  -circle strafing seems too powerful in the game. To those who don’t know, circle strafing is where you run in a circle around enemies while also shooting enemies by rotating your aim as you strafe.  Because the game relies heavily on fodder type enemies and enemies that chase you, you can at times breeze through certain arenas with almost no challenge or strategy circle strafing. The game could have done a better job at times to force the player into more complex movement patterns via enemy and level design/hazards. -the game also has a kind of issue where harder difficulties don’t feel particularly much harder, due to the overall setup of the game design.  The game essentially rewards the player as much as punishes the player when you introduce more enemies, because more enemies = more orbs = lets you do your special attack more often = more health.  It also means you can restock your secondary weapon easier because sword attacks will kill more enemies with each sword swing, and secondary weapon is designed to be able to clear a ton of enemies quickly. Basically there’s a kind of positive feedback loop within its game design that somewhat nullifies how much the difficulty can be increased simply through introducing denser enemies, because sometimes it can actually help you rather than pressure you more. ————————In conclusion, Kill Knight is an impressive game that adds a hot new title for fans of the genre to pick up that boasts great and intense game feel, visceral aesthetics, and a nice blend of enemies and weapons.  It falls short of its potential in some areas, sometimes trading depth for breadth.  While it doesn’t take the genre to new heights in my opinion, I’d still say give it a try, especially if a more casual player.

_childDocuments_.review: Fast paced twin-stick shooter mixing shooting with melee and heavy resource management. Seemingly inspired by Devil Daggers & Hyper Demon it leans more into endurance-based challenges rather than bite-sized levels with large enemy or boss fight variety. On top of a high level of challenge the game has a focus on score attacking with a polished system to match.If you like challenging twin-stick shooters and also pushing for high scores this should be an especially easy sell. If not, you might like it simply because it's a hectic top-down action game that does a solid job mixing up ranged and melee attacks.The game is mechanically dense right from the get-go which can be the first turnoff to some. You have many resources to manage. With the caveat that some mechanics can be ignored while still performing well: perfectly timed pistol reloads or walking over small items for speed ups may look central at first but you don't need to worry about them much. Ammo gauges encourage a varied usage of tools similar to Doom Eternal to keep each ability available. Core reloads being tied to meleeing enemies or aggressively collecting dropped items.For movement you have access to an invincible dash/roll like many similar top-down games. The dash is much less overpowered than say in Nex Machina. It's something you should think of as another resource to manage rather than autopiloted: especially on more challenging modes.You might also use up dash stocks to cancel the recovery of a melee slash or to get in for one, making your defense weaker for a moment. You can totally get cornered and take a bunch of damage for poor positioning. On the highest difficulty the most basic melee-type enemies move a little faster than your walk speed which should be telling.Kill Knight is somewhat lacking in level variety. You mostly fight the same enemies again but with different environmental hazards or a longer endurance stage. Rather than unique enemies or bosses popping up often. The environmental hazards can be cool though, as the stages transform over time and often restrict your movement.There is a gear system to change your weapons (two ranged, one melee) on top of an armor piece and accessory. If you change all three weapons it can feel like playing an entirely different character. The different 'heavy' weapons range from high power single shot shotguns to long range machineguns and have completely different matching Wrath Burst attacks (which are the only way to spawn health items). These can really change your methods of healing or taking down heavy targets. Some of the armors give you a new attack tied to the dash which can add a whole new layer to things. Generally playstyle variety isn't massive but the synergies between equipment can be fun to play with.Kill Knight has a very solid scoring system up there with things like Assault Android Cactus. Scoring seems like a major focus of the design of the game instead of an afterthought.Picking up health items at max health gives you bonus points making them double as score items. You spawn these at a more rapid pace the better you use your Wrath Burst weapon. This spawning of crystals / score items by precisely destroying groups of enemies can be really satisfying and reminds me more of the scoring systems in arcade scrolling shooters rather than your average twin-stick. The nice part here being this skill for score attack is also the best for survival: more healing items are spawned. But do you want to risk moving all around the stage to collect them?On top of other score bonuses the time bonus in each stage is very significant so optimizing your clear times to be faster is always relevant (again similar to AAC).Nailing all the scoring tricks, using melee efficiently, not taking hits and beating the stage quickly is an impossible task to pull off perfectly. But the closer your gameplay gets to that it certainly feels and looks cool. When you first boot up the game and if it clicks at all it's clear that the skill ceiling is high and there's cool stuff to do: the scoring system matches this very well.Using normal sword swings may seem like pointless strategy at first as melee is somewhat risky. But melee becomes more relevant the further you optimize stages (or complete the matching Carnage challenges). The sword gauge built up by melee kills is used for full screen bomb type attacks which award you the more enemies you clear out at once. In a way this increased focus on melee makes the game more difficult (even after beating the highest difficulty!) but also gives you constant reloads on your heavy weapon, making the playstyle efficient if done right.At the time of review many gear loadouts & playstyles are valid for high scores: someone using Sword 2 to absorb bullets for extra meter gain, some pushing the time bonus to its limits with Heavy 3, another using perfect reloads more than others and so on.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, this game is seriously fun! The mechanics are insanely good. Although there are a few things I don't really like (I'll get to that in a bit), this game really brought bullet hell games back to life for me. The difficulty at the start is real, though—because the mechanics are a bit complex, especially when you're trying to learn everything at once. But once you're used to it and your muscle memory kicks in, it's like you’re on auto-pilot just watching monsters get wrecked while still feeling the challenge and pressure.The DownsidesBuying Equipment: Collecting points is a grind. To get all the equipment, you’ll need to put in a ton of hours. For example, a weapon might cost 2500 points, but one run might only get you 100 points or even less. Sure, clearing a stage gets you more, but it's tough, you know. If it were that easy, the game would be over in an hour. And there are like 20+ items to collect, some even more expensive. Each run is also pretty exhausting, so grinding for long periods can get a bit much.Art Style: I like the art style overall, but there’s just one thing I’m not a fan of: the design of the equipment, like weapons and armor. I was hoping for something more epic-looking, Cool weapon shapes, badass armor. Some weapons I don't even know what they are by just looking at them! You’ve got to buy them and try them in-game to figure out their abilities. Everything is too pixelated. Sure, you can kind of tell what’s what, but I feel like the design could’ve been better.Music and Sound Effects: This isn't exactly a downside, more like a wishlist. I liked everything—the music and effects are solid and meet the standard—but the game’s way more fun than the music. I feel like if the tracks were more diverse or more intense, it’d be perfect. Another thing I’d love to see is voiceovers for the characters. It feels like something’s missing without it. Or even some combo sounds, like in Devil May Cry when you're chaining combos and you see that combo meter go up. It’d be awesome to hear something other than just the number ticking higher.If you've made it this far, I know I’ve complained quite a bit, but trust me everything this game does, it does exceptionally well. It really raises the bar for bullet hell games, and you should definitely grab it.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun.It's a fast paced game where your hands do the most of the work, and you have to focus and react quickly. (and learn how to auto-pilot it once you gain the muscle memory)It's also made of  arena levels, basically 5-8 minute endurance fights where you have to start over if you die, and it will take you a few retries until you get a grip on the level and have a general plan for every stage of it. Levels are cool, as you progress they change shape to catch you off guard, and you start to learn and memorize what's next.So unless you hate constant action, you'll like this game.The only real problem I've encountered is that swords are usually too risky to swing, and miss a lot if the enemy is too close, and the only way to optimally use them is to use them for their special skill.Which brings me to another gripe I have with the game. There are too many skill metres in this game. You have one for the pistol, one for the secondary, one for the sword, and they're all kinda connected to the single  quick reload mechanic. The most optimal way to play suddenly becomes hitting the quick reload to fill the metres faster and juggle between weapons. The game never literally forces you to use anything, but -like execution based design rewards you health and ammo for playing this way. I just wish it had more freedom to it, so we could have sword-only, pistol-only playstyles and other ways to play free from the quick reload.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, I like it, but I was assuming I'd love it based on some friends' thoughts and I'm just not there yet. I'm hoping I will be at some point.My main problem is there's just too much going on. This has been a debate for decades in arcade styled games (especially in shmups) -- limit the mechanics to a few and have the intense action and hand-eye coordination be the focus, or try for something new and add some complexity to the systems and weapons. Kill Knight goes pretty heavily towards the latter with several different gems to collect, all of which power different weapons (or health), and these different weapons involve a lot of different button presses. Standard shot, heavy shot, "bomb" shot, slash, heavy slash, dash, absorb gems, and possibly more I'm forgetting.While that may sound manageable, this is a lightning paced twin stick shooter and all of these moves require different buttons and often combo button presses... while at the same time you *also* need to keep an eye on your reload meter so you reload in the zone and keep your score multiplier going, not to mention all the other meters (four?) you need to glance at to see if you're filling up those special weapons, and also somehow find the time to glance at the list of achievement-like objectives you need to complete to unlock other weapons, and, and... it's a lot. Too much for my preferences.Also, while I get the grim, hell-like look they're going for, Kill Knight is pretty bland for the arcade shooter genre which usually sees screens crackling with many bright colors and shapes and interesting backgrounds. This game is grey and red with really bland arenas.Sounds like I dislike it but I don't. There's a super intense, tightly controlled twin-stick in here with great (and useful) sound effects and some interesting ideas, but there's just too much unnecessary stuff surrounding that core for my taste. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Talk about a nice surprise. KILL KNIGHT is a fantastic twin-stick shooter up there with Assault Android Cactus, which I still consider the best game of this style. KILL KNIGHT is a little different though; rather than working your way through dozens of short levels and some boss fights, the essence here is surviving unrelenting 5-15 minute gauntlets. There's only 5 stages, but they're designed to near-perfection. Every level is a choreographed nightmare with constantly shifting terrain and hazards, and a few mistakes can spell your end due to the meagre health bar. It isn't rare to die within literal seconds when you first start playing. Not moving equals instant death. The game doesn't pull its punches even on the easiest difficulty; The beauty of KILL KNIGHT lies in its complex yet elegant central design: two main shot types, a special shot, a close-range sword attack, a dodge, and an absorption mechanic. You need to juggle these five actions constantly (alongside moving and aiming, of course). One of your guns is your regular shot and it's your go-to. Your other gun serves as a stronger, special shot with depleting ammo. The sword is for close-range strikes and leaves you vulnerable. Finally, you have a special shot that runs on a long meter that is filled by absorbing red gems. It may sound simple on paper, but in the heat of the moment you'll come to realize how mentally taxing it is compared to other games of this kind. Rarely do games this intense require the CONSTANT use of so many mechanics, mostly tied to the 4 shoulder buttons on the controller. It can be both mentally and physically exhausting... In a fun way, of course. :-) In order to improve at the game you need to master its mechanics and learn the patterns of the small yet thoughtful enemy selection. Firing your main shot alone won't cut it, especially once the larger enemies start appearing, so you'll need to rely on your secondary and special shots, along with clever uses of the sword when you find openings. See, in order to refill the secondary's ammo meter you need to get melee kills. And in order to to refill your special you need to absorb gems like mentioned before.  There's also a reload mechanic, where a meter appears after your main gun's ammo depletes, and then a bar will appear on-screen, Gears of War-style, and depending on which of the 3 possible buttons you press, you'll be rewarded with either temporarily enhanced regular shots, an instant absorption of every fallen gem on screen, or a huge sword strike if timed correctly. You aren't greatly penalised for missing a timed reload, but in later stages these can prove crucial in a pinch.Another great aspect of KILL KNIGHT (I like repeatedly writing it in all caps) is the amount of options. There's 5 types of every weapon and armor set, and 10 passive items with different effects. One look at the in-game leaderboard for any stage will show you that almost any combination can be viable, which is extremely refreshing. Admittedly, the game's title is a little silly, but the artistic direction is phenomenal. This one is all about gameplay and style, and it succeeds at both beautifully. It almost reminds me of something like Devil Daggers, and apparently Sorath's games served as inspirations alongside arcade games generally. It also should be mentioned that all unlockable items are obtained by completing in-game challenges, but they can also be unlocked by means of an in-game currency that takes longer to accumulate. I think this is a great system.After finishing a round, you're given a score, along with a multiplier bonus depending on the chosen difficulty. It's nice and elegant, and I appreciate how the leaderboards aren't separated, so theoretically even people playing on lower difficulties can score big. The scoring itself is actually surprisingly deep, since the game has a kill streak, and obviously aiming to maintain that in order to get the largest score is ideal, so that adds another layer. Finally, there are blue health gems that will drop from enemies defeated by your special shot, and these reward more points if collected at full health.This is a fantastic game, and I hope to see more from these developers. Let it be known that there are people out there that appreciate this uncompromisingly focused design and challenge, especially in this day and age. It's great to see new titles with an appreciation of finer arcade mechanics, but with innovative gameplay and interesting aesthetics. Especially because many smaller titles that claim to be arcade-inspired are actually pretty stress-free, and more predatory in their design than some would like to admit. Also, is it a coincidence that both of the best twin-stick shooters are developed in Australia? Wait, Sorath (developers of Devil Daggers and Hyper Demon) is also Australian? Well, keep it up with these fun and unique games, please.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap, this game is great. I have a soft spot for twin-sticks and have been itching for a game similar to nex machina and well damn this is it. It’s Gorey, flashy and downright intense.The game has about 5 stages but each stage is relatively long (about 10 to 20 minutes or so) and just throws everything at you. You can customize your shot type and armor. Unlocking it all afterwards is similar to a rogue-lite. Most of the load outs come down to personal preference which can make someone else's run seem unique and fresh. You have to actively reload at the correct time to get a better shot, you can also melee to reset the ammo while simultaneously gaining meter for your second shot and lastly you collect blood gems to get your special shot out. The game will throw countless waves and everything fits so well.I legit got a blister on my thumb the first day because I was playing for such a long time.Another cool thing is when stunning enemies with your special shot you can just straight up melee their back dark souls style creating this cool animation. The game has a variety of difficulties but make no mistake even the first difficulty can get intense on stage 5. The main appeal of the game is speed and how fast you can kill an enemy. Always encouraging to challenge you and your friends on the leaderboards for fun. I love this game. Please try it!

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely ferocious piece of hyper-focused game design that somehow feels like a completely stripped down cross between Robotron 2084, Devil May Cry, and Vampire Survivors. It's an intoxicating blend of maximalism and minimalism, with a level of intensity that feels like the whole thing is just going to self destruct at any given moment.  It also looks amazing- if the characters in the Panos Cosmatos film Mandy were to play a video game, this would be it. A stunning, challenging skill-focused game I expect to be playing for years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't believe more people aren't playing this.  It's so good.  The combat is surprisingly deep.  Everytime I get stuck at a level I decide to learn another one of the mechanics I'd been ignoring until then.  You can happily ignore the majority of them for the early levels, but the later levels are no joke.  Then you have the option of either Getting Good, turning down the difficulty, learning more mechanics or maybe unlocking a new weapon.   One of the mechanics I still haven't fully grasped is the parry kill.  Many of the enemies have a moment just before they attack that you can launch a sword swing at them during.  If you time it just right, you insta-kill them.  Some enemies have a very obvious window, some have such a small window you only know it exists because you accidentally hit it once.  I usually play after work and I'm sleep deprived.  Anything I do normally has me dozing off at my computer table.  Not this game.  I'm wide awake when playing this thing.  It's extremely engaging.  And there is a good range of enemies.  There is a fair bit of model reuse, but they'll reskin one of the enemies, upsize the model, then change it's attack pattern.  And I don't have a problem with that at all really.

_childDocuments_.review: I changed my review from Yes to No (old review below).The reason after 6 hours of playing, I only beat 2 (two) levels. This is frustrating and doesn't give me any feeling of progress. The 1st and 2nd level can be beaten in like 5 minutes, but it took me like 2 hours of retrying. During that time, the game felt satisfying and I learned many smaller things which made me better.However, my best attempt in level 3 is at 13 minutes game time and I'm trying to beat that level in what feels like 4 hours with breaks in between, because the game is draining and I can't do more than 3 runs in a row. I wish the game would acknowledge my smaller improvements, but the 3rd level just adds more and more moving objects on the screen until there is no pixel left and I eventually get hit by something. I wish the game would have like 20 instead of 5 levels with a more gentle difficulty curve, but I guess that would need more enemy and level variety.Now you might want to drop a "git gud" comment, but I'm not a player that gives up fast (I beat the Elden Ring DLC endboss on level 150 after 12 hours). In my opinion, this game is not doing enough to make the player feel like they are improving.old review:This game needs 100% focus every single second. The 1-2 seconds level transitions and 6-7 seconds slowmotion after deflecting certain enemies are the only time you are allowed to breathe in. You have the perfect amount of abilities to constantly think about the next good move and not be too overwhelmed. The game is challenging, but feels fair and balanced all the time. _childDocuments_.review: This game feels a breath of fresh air due to its great sophisticated yet accessible attack and defense mechanics. This makes the gameplay loop fun and not repetitive. Each new unlock allows you to create different builds that might be better for certain levels.The game is very challenging and takes a bit to learn the mechanics, which are essential to master for successful runs. There is a global leaderboard for each level and each difficulty. Each run last several minutes. The play session is spot on and it's a game that you go straight to the action and it doesn't feel slow or tedious.  You can dash, parry, use melee and range weapons. I highly recommend playing with a controller of course.The game has great art style as well.Negative: frame drops when I clear lots of enemies at once.UPDATE: Playing more, I found it a bit annoying that I need to replay a lot of previous levels to get objectives or currency to upgrade. _childDocuments_.review: Game is freakin' RAD! Awesome artstyle, addictive action, etc etc Main thing I love about this game compared to some of it's contemporaries is it feels like it has more to do, plus runs actually end.... I've gotten tired of games like this that go on forever and feel like they are randomly generated. You can get to a point where you memorize every new wave to better predict your next move. The overall gameplay, clearing a stage, isn't too difficult. Where the game shines is the bonus objectives that also unlock new equipment that can vastly change how you play,
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: I sunk an insane number of hours into the demo. I cracked the top 50 and managed to stay there until the demo closed. If they said that was all the content I would get for $15, I would have been happy with it. I was expecting to pay ~$30 for the expanded content at launch and would have happily paid it. Smash TV and Super Smash TV got me hooked on games like this. Not many in the genre do it this well. This is one of the best, most addicting games I have played in a while. I also haven't been this interested in challenging the leader boards since I went high score hunting at GameWorks in Seattle, WA two decades ago. Be prepared to actually learn to play a game. The mechanics are tricky to get the hang of and time, but super rewarding when you figure it out. The mechanics also feel familiar so it's not necessarily a steep learning curve. Few can jump right in and feel at home. That's what makes it fun and re-playable. The kit combos are fun to put together to fit your play style too. It's all around a great experience. _childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: It was the best game I played this year, and I didn't even know about its existence until its release.It's extremely challenging, probably the hardest game I played in 33 years, with great aesthetics, gunplay, bladeplay, and movement to all make it worth it in the end. It's a game that requires you to use every single mechanic in the game effectively to complete it on the lowest difficulty.I also loved the lore behind the levels that developers posted in a blog format.The very best thing though, despite the difficulty, is that I had zero fatigue from playing and completing it, immediately wanting to continue pushing myself on harder difficulty, which I plan to do as soon as I shrug off the busy schedule of games lined up in October.I cannot recommend this game enough, especially for its asking price.Remember to blink and don't bring the short-ranged pistols into the very last layer and the final boss fight. I learned that the hard way.Played on Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: KILL KNIGHT is without question the best twin stick shooter ever made. Yes, I've played Housemarque's games. They're all great. But they're not KILL KNIGHT.KILL KNIGHT ushers the genre into the modern era with a stylish and over the top combat system layered with countless opportunities for skill expression while you compete for high scores. I put a little over 40 hours into the demo which only contained the first level - and the full game is better in nearly every way. The $14.99 base price is a steal.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Considering how fast this game is, it needs some system that warns you about projectiles and exploding enemies that come towards you from outside of your view zone. I've died countless times to an unreactable explosive enemy that just rammed into me at max speed from a blind spot, leaving me no chance to react and dodge. Maybe add a small bright flash at the edge of the screen if something is rapidly approaching you from that direction? Or a unique and noticeable audio cue? This would prevent a lot of frustrating and unfun deaths. Great and somewhat difficult game, kind of similar to Devil Daggers and Hyper Demon. Requires fast decision-making skills and reaction time, there is a sizeable arsenal of different abilities that you NEED to know how to effectively use.Visuals and overall style are just 10/10, it is very simple but still epic and brutal.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. I've played a handful of games like this in the past and this exceeds all of them. It's really arcadey and you will very likely die a lot so if replaying levels to learn how to perfect them isn't your thing than this game won't be for you. But for everyone else no game has done it better.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: You see the blue thumb, you know it's a recommend - and I want it to count towards the "Overwhelmingly Positive" score this game deserves.do wanna say it's weak that Vampire Survivors - a great game - has become the new mould we compare new Isometric Action games to. because as awesome and fresh as that game was when it released, KILL KNIGHT'S nothing like it. to do really well in Vampire Survivors, you really just needed two inputs: Left Stick / D-Pad and Confirm Button. to do well in Kill Knight you need both sticks and even all buttons, too. Vampire Survivors was killer, but this is just a different level of intensity altogether. it happens to be isometric. lots of games were before Vampire Survivors.KILL KNIGHT I'd compare more to DEVIL DAGGERS. you start a run and kill demon creatures until you die by the increasingly difficult enemy types and numbers that keep coming at you. then you're scored and ranked by how well you did on a giant scoreboard made up of weirdo insane people calling themselves ridiculous things like 'Maga-Man', 'Dopioid' or 'Elon Musk'.Devil Daggers scored you on your time, Kill Knight scores you on your time but also combos, kills, stuff like that. it's a very focused and uncomplicated game, and it's absolutely what the doctor ordered for Twin Stick Shooters. best new Twin Stick I've played since the good 'Android Assault Cactus' and even the great, great NEX MACHINA. it might actually have the potential to be on the Mount Runmore of Twin Stick Shooters along with Nex Machina and I'd say the GOAT, Geometry Wars 3. we'll see. it's really early to call, but it seems to be the real deal, now we'll just have to wait and see whether or not the Honeymoon Phase turns into something sustainably replayable. if you love difficult, high-intensity Twin Stick Shooters like Nex Machina or Geometry Wars, get it.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: KILL KNIGHT is stylish, tight, and tough as nails. I am stuck on the fifth floor with 10 hours played, but hey, that's OK. _childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Want to chase high scores with an arcade game with tight combat mechanics? Buy. This. Game! Going through the tutorial, you think "whoa, there's so many ways to kill! This is going to be complicated!" But when you play for a bit, all the mechanics just flow so well together. Gameplay is really elegantly designed.As for content, there are 4 difficulties (you have to unlock the 4th one) and 5 different levels, which each level being noticeably longer AND harder than the previous, and a 6th level which is basically a gauntlet of all the levels combined with added difficulty. Levels are dynamic with environmental hazards and there are many different enemy types.In terms of progression, you start off with one loadout, but each gear has at least 5 different unlocks obtained by completing certain challenges or spending tokens you obtain from just playing.Played the demo of this during Steam Next Fest and it was by far the best demo out of the ones I played. Full game did not disappoint. I wish there were more levels, but I think even with just 5 levels, it's totally worth the purchase. I also played keyboard and mouse through the whole game, which is fine, but controller is probably better for maneuvering with the analog stick.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Kill Knight is a pure arcade experience: very fun and very addictive. The audio is punchy, the Knight's controls are responsive, and there's loads of unlocks to drive replayability. My only criticism is that you're loaded up on complex tools right at the start with a menu-based tutorial which introduces all the mechanics in piecemeal instances; there's a lot to learn to play Kill Knight well. Once you're over that hump, there's a bunch of fun to be had.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: If you like twin-stick shooters, this game is IT. A word to the wise, don't skip the lower difficulties. You're meant to play on the easier ones to unlock gear to better take on the harder ones. But, if you're just built different, you can still beat the entire game with the standard gear. The game recommends a controller, but it still plays incredibly well with a keyboard and mouse.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Fast, intelligently designed and perfect on Deck; 15 hours in a weekend speaks volumes.There’s a learning curve behind the initially overwhelming Hades-meets-Housemarque intensity; the designers have clearly considered how unlocks - abilities, guns, swords, buffs - scale across the grind. Kill Knight is the surprise of my 2024 so far; relentless, clever, it takes ingredients from a range of schmups and slashers and manages to deliver an original flavour.

_childDocuments_.review: I've put 72 hours into this game since its release a week ago. You do the math. Its addicting, aggravating, insulting but extremely satisfying when you conquer something you've been slamming your head against for hours at a time. I don't even like bullet hell games, but the art direction stuck out to me and I thought "what the hell, its cheap, why not?" and the last week has been a blur. Progression is slow, but there overall I think the game is balanced enough that if you look at the "builds" for the highest leaderboards, there isn't a particular weapon or armor or sword that outclasses something else. You will find what you like, and find success in what you find enjoyable. I've beaten the game, and am now in the process of grinding out the final trophies, which seem to be sadistic in nature. _childDocuments_.review: Hear me out. I like this game. I just defeated the endboss prior to writing this review.Kill Knight has really solid, fast-paced top-down combat with a blend of ranged and melee attacks. You will be constantly managing ammo, wrath energy and blood energy killing enemies swiftly and with the right tool to replenish the resource you are in need of the most. There is little for me to criticize about the combat, I might have some minor nitpics but this combat is easily S- or A+ very polished and satisfying. BUT, there is one big but:This game is HARD. I only completed the 5 levels on the easiest difficulty, I was pretty much stuck playing some of the levels for 1-2 hours, in particular the last level. Expect trial and error.This also applies to special challenges you need to complete in order to unlock new weapons - think, completing a level without losing your killcombo, or without missing a single fast reload.I do think that this game's greatest weakness is that the baseline difficult is TOO HIGH, and it does not ease you into getting accustomed to the base mechanics by playing progressively harder levels. You know, developing muscle memory and that kinda stuff. Instead, you'll be beating your head against a wall when trying a new level, if that's not your thing, this game likely isn't for you.Still reading? Not gonna spoil anything, just get the f'kin geme
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I changed my review from "not recommended" to "recommended".It's a well crafted game and not expensive, so give it a go to see for yourself. You won't regret it. The missing early progression is causing more frustration than the game might want to. It starts barren but opens up if you can beat it. The difficulty modes are an important tool to use - the game feels different. Use it to memorize levels and progress upwards.I still think it needs more levels (layers) to choose from. Especially some shorter ones to ease players into the game. Let people have at least a small accomplishment before feeding them to the dogs.---Kill Knight doesn't shine in content variety and gets repetetive extremely fast. With only a handful of different enemies to show, the game places you in a reshaping environment. That creates various "situations" but doesn't change gameplay much.You're honing your muscle memory to correctly press all the buttons on your gamepad at the right time. It's a good chug of stress for this mundane, uneventful life. But I'm really not sure why "you need to use all your abilities with perfect timing without getting hit" was mistakenly used as the starting point for difficulty progression here. If you're not winning, the game let's you rot in boredom hell. Losing means repeating the same content loop, over and over. Nothing changes, you're only getting faster at it. Not super fast! Only slightly faster. Loadouts are seemingly meant to add variety after beating the game in boredom & frustration mode first.I kinda like the game and first time playing feels exciting, addictive even. But it doesn't want me to have a good time. I think it appears a bit rushed and unfinished, but upside down. The early game is just missing completely. It's disappointing, looking at how promising it can be.---Update 1 after 3 hours: I can beat the first level on lowest difficulty, if I manage to stay focused all the way through. I unexpectedly unlocked a second heavy weapon, which was easier for me to navigate. A good example for how choices impact potential enjoyment. My current take: The game feels easier once you find your flow. You'll have to find that on your own though. I went for a melee/heavy/melee/heavy rotation because I desperately wanted things to go faster. It helped a bit.---Update 2 after 5 hours: I beat the second level on lowest difficulty. Went back and beat the first level on medium difficulty. It gets better and I have more things to choose from. Everything that gives me a choice is nice. However, I wish I had more digestable chunks of content to play now. Every level is an endurance test.---Update 3 after 6 hours: I think I have so many complaints because I can't put this game down. It's too much fun to play, so I want all the things. I think I can easily recommend this, despite any shortcomings it might have.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: I very much live in this genre space. From my first love, Smash TV (1990 arcade game), to Enter the Gungeon, to the twin stick revival thanks to Vampire Survivors, to Brotato, to isometric top-down games in general (look at my Path of Exile playtime). This is my kind of game.Except it's not. I think the devs were a little confused about what they wanted to create. It's got the twin stick shooting zerg fest of like any one of these games (e.g. soulstone survivors), but the active reload mechanic of Gears of War, combined with multiple active reload mechanics, and sword play with a parry system, and a consumable secondary weapon system, and super weapon system, and traps... and... and........So you have to figure out how to control both sticks with both thumbs, while shooting with the right trigger and dashing with the left bumper. That's easy. Then you need to time your active reloads. OK. But what if your super is depleted? Then you have to use a different button to active reload. Fine... Oh, but you can active reload with a sword attack in order to replenish your secondary weapon... which is the X button. So, you have to run using the right stick (one thumb), aim using the left stick (second thumb), and press X (third thumb).Maybe if the monsters were bigger and slower, there would be more thoughtful combat, but on top of this entire mess, I'm not going to stand next to a monster and wait to parry it at the appropriate time, all while moving, shooting, dashing, active reloading, blah blah blah.But really, just don't buy it for the damned forced CRT filter (grainy, scan lines, curved corners) on the menu screens with no ability to turn them off. It looks absolutely stupid on a 4K HDR display. I had a CRT. I'm not ****ing nostalgic for it.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: takes to long to unlock anything very grindy kinda boring not much to the game load into deathpit pew pew which i thought might be fun but it gets very old very fast especially when you aren't unlocking anything new even after a successful mission.  i do like the combat mechanics of the game i didn't find them overwhelming.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good! At its core it is very simple - you have a dash, a fast attack, a heavy attack, a melee attack and a special attack that can be charged up. What makes this special is the way that these all compliment each other and synergise. The heavy attacks are recharged by melee attacks and health is restored by the special attack and the fast attack combos into any of the others with a well timed ability press to get a powered attack with variations depending on your input. It is just so satisfying and as the dev description states it truly does reward you for aggression and precision.It is quite challenging. I have beaten the first level on acolyte difficult but there are still 4 more to go and 2 difficulty levels higher after that too! All in all I highly recommend this for anyone looking for a challenging fast paced precise and aggressive combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so I just beat the 3rd layer out of 5 on the Medium difficulty and WOW, game is hard. I played the demo back in NEXT FEST a lot and loved it. I've had the active reload sound seared into my brain ever since. I think at its core, if you enjoyed the loop of DOOM ETERNAL where you had to manage and juggle a bunch of things at once you will enjoy KILL KNIGHT. I've only unlocked a few of the different equipment, but they seem to provide a lot of build variety. Like I said at the start, it is hard, but it's one of those types of game where you just keep telling yourself "one more." And it has a parry, which is always a sick thing in my book. Really, really love the sound design too. And a tip!!! You can parry the enemies that shoot the lasers! I do recommend it, but I'm kind of back and forth on the fact that the levels are NOT random. They are sequenced in a way that as you play you learn the spawn of enemies, arena changes, etc. I do think this is great in getting into the flow state of the game, and where it excels. However I've found myself restarting layers if I botch something on a specific wave that either hinders me or removes my kill stream (your kill streak). I don't think it is bad, but it's something I've been thinking about. Another nit pick I have is the kill stream. Sometimes when the platform changes there is no way to keep the streak going because the enemies have yet to spawn in, or they spawn in just outside of your screen. I think this goes back to learning the layers and spawns, but I have gotten frustrated when I lose my kill stream due to an enemy spawning in .1 second too late for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Kill Knight delivers solid gameplay mechanics and fast-paced bullet hell action that can be genuinely fun for fans of the genre. Unlocking new items is locked behind skill-based challenges, which can detract from the overall enjoyment. If you’re a fan of bullet hell games, you’ll probably enjoy Kill Knight, but I’d recommend waiting for a sale with a significant discount, as there are better bullet hell games on the market for less than half the cost. That said, I’d highly recommend Kill Knight if you enjoy other bullet hell games.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a oke twin stick shooter, it has it's fun moments with decent challenge, but doesn't really stand out and certain aspects of the game aren't that polished enough to make it a worthy addition amongst the greats of the genre, with * visibility sometimes being an issue, * off screen bullets being a thing, and * 1 frame instant kill moves with *no visual cues while other times they do have the visual cues(creates unnecessary inconsistencies),* dropping the very little iframes you have already mid dash if you go for a melee attack isn't the best idea for a game like this (it overly limits a very offensive play style), because the cooldown and amount of dashes available to use is already a sufficient enough restriction,* not a really engaging score mechanic, * the combat UI could've been done better with regards to displaying information to the player, just to name a few things that prevent this game from being a fundamentally and mechanically solid game, but the idea is definitely here and deserve credit for that, it's just the execution that fell a little short. Performance was overall good, but don't mix a mouse + gamepad the game will have serious performance issues if you do.either use mouse and keyboard or controller exclusively then you won't have issues with it.

_childDocuments_.review: For my full review please check out my channel! KILL KNIGHT is simply the steal of the year. For a very reasonable price you will be diving straight into this visceral experience dodging incoming projectiles, navigating hazardous terrain, and slaying countless enemies with a variety of weapons at your disposal. Make no mistake though, this game is not for the butcher, you must be artistic and measured in the manner you deal out each bout of violence as specific weapons will cause enemies to drop different items for your benefit. Consider the combat loop of DOOM as a very similar style, just with an arcade isometric perspective. I am very proud to say I had the 64th best score in the world for a very short period of time but that is quickly tumbling as strategies develop and people players identify the best way to clear levels in the most efficient and highest scoring manner possible. I strongly recommend this game and I hope other players can jump in on the challenge and see how far they can push themselves!
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: I tried giving this a fair shake but I just could not click into having a fun flow with this. There are a bunch of different gameplay mechanics going on, and that could be fine (Hades 1 and 2 do this very well!) but the controls in this are so clunky that it does not feel good to play. _childDocuments_.review: There's a lot going for this game, but what sets it apart is also it's downfall. In theory, adding more abilities sounds like a great idea. Others in the genre are fairly simple in operation, having access to more actions would surely make the experience better....right? Well in this case, not so much. After this experience I don't think that's the answer this genre needs to evolve forward. There's too many abilities & actions. Every button on the controller is tied to an ability or action, which you'll be required to remember and use while constantly using both sticks & making sure you don't get hit. If you decide to stick to one or two for simplicities sake, you'll be handicapped & will only make it so far. They've over complicated what makes these games great. This wouldn't have been such a huge issue if it wasn't for my next issue.You make very little progress each run, just getting a handful of currency once you die. Pieces of gear are 2k+ EACH while a run may land you something like 30-40 (if not less). You'd have to play for several hours just to unlock one thing using currency. The alternative is completing challenges to unlock pieces for free, but these challenges often have you play the game differently than you like & kills what little fun there is to be had. Not to mention challenges seem like an extension of the tutorial, really pushing you to use every button and ability at your disposal. It's overly complex, extremely slow on rewards, and repetitive with what appears to be one map that expands the farther you get. If you can't manage to pass a certain point, you'll never see a a different map. Not to mention each section looks similar to the last with a different shaped playing area.The atmosphere is great, graphics, art style, performance....so much is well done here it's a shame the issues mentioned are present.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like "boomer-shooters" or "fast paced FPS", ignore my review. This game might be for you.TLDR: This game confuses "fast and busy" with "difficult" or "intense".You have trillions of attack options and you must always be ready to dodge enemies at a split seconds, but yet feels more boring than slower paced, simpler top down shooters like Nex Machina, Helldivers 1, or even arcade bullet hell games like Dodonpachi/Touhou.Long review:It's a VERY fast paced twin stick, on top of that there is a lot of actions you can take.Your basic ranged weapon is joystick + right triggerthere's a secondary stronger shot that is another buttonYou have a basic sword slash as a face button, and a stronger finisher on another face button. The sword slash is necessary to replenish the secondary shot.You can enter "absorb mode" to collect pickups near your, and holding that mode + stronger secondary shot while having enough charge create a super shot that also creates health pickup.You also have dashes that give invulnerability frames.Ah and there's an active reload system which, if you time correctly, can give you either a melee boost, ranged boost, or absorb all pickups instantly.You almost run out of buttons to map all actions, and the game is so fast you don't get half a second to think much.The safest plan of action is to circle around the enemies while shooting at them, and it's what you'll be doing most of the time since melee is not strong.A level is "only" 7-10 minutes, but it feels very long and surprisingly boring because it is so repetitive. It's just constant barage of enemies.I've played two hours so far and reach the second level, I can't do more than 2-3 runs per session since I feel so burnt out after. It's difficult to progress in the game when you feel "You've had enough" after only 15 minutes of playing.Mind you: I love hard arcadey games shooters like Nex Machina, or more traditional bullet-hell/danmaku like Dodonpachi/Touhou (I've cleared the extra stage on atleast 5 of these games).What they have is pacing: You have fun showing your skills and killing low danger monsters, then the tension rises at the mid level, and it reaches it's peak/climax when you reach the boss/end of level. Then the next level has a different music/theme/visuals.After finishing a level in Kill Knight I feel "Oh it's finished?" instead of "Yeah I beat it!".  The end doesn't feel much different from the beggining, except from added enemies and lasers. If you want a very fast and arcadey twin stick shooters, play Nex Machina instead. If you want a twin stick shooter with a lot of options, that has interesting tactical plays/thinking but still gets your heart pounding and palm sweating, then play Helldivers 1.Kill Knight looked like it would have been for me, but only after experiencing the game do I realize it wasn't for me.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly can't recommend. The difficulty curve is just too steep for it to be accessible, and it hasn't quite seemed to nail the gameplay loop. You have a heavy weapon, which can be used to kill a lot of enemies. But it has finite uses, so you need to use your main light weapon and your sword (which really puts you in danger) in order to get ammo. But the problem is that in order to reach high scores, anything but your heavy weapon becomes obsolete. So most of the time you're left with these very weak dual pistols and risky sword desperately trying to get rid of smaller enemies and get ammo, while the bigger enemies are practically like minibosses until you finally get ammo for your heavy weapon. The fact that bigger hordes often need you to use your heavy weapon anyway, leaving you with nothing to use against the big enemies, is honestly just really frustrating. I love the overall theme and music of the game, but the combat loop just doesn't work on a fundamental level in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of these games where I’d like to have a neutral rating button.On the positive side for me are good visuals, really like the style a lot, the soundtrack is well done and doesn’t get on my nerves fast, controls are tight and responsive on my DualSense Controller and the game itself is pretty fun.So why am I not recommending Kill Knight?Though I like the option to switch between different difficulty modes, the base line on easy here is so hard that I am unable to finish the fourth of the five levels. Level selection is tied to your progress in the previous one, so I’ll never be able to see all of this game.  After nearly 20 hours I just gave up hope. I will try again and again, but I don’t truly see a way for me to finish Kill Knight. This feels like the game has never been tested by a wider audience than maybe hardcore twinstick / bullethell pros.Secondly, most of the unlockable equipment doesn’t do it for me. Either it feels too slow or too weak to consider.  Maybe it’s just my cognitive conditioning from years of gaming, but locking your weapons and armor behind either steep conditions or the slow grind of currency, should be rewarded with different and more powerful upgrades to the starting tools. In the current state, most of these items feel tacked on.My biggest gripe with Kill Knight is a bug that indicates this game has never been thoroughly tested. Launching this game right after I played something else, the game loads a black screen and just refuses to start everything else. I have to shut it down via task manager. A restart of my PC fixes this. This bug seems to have been reported multiple times since Kill Knights release on October 2nd 2024, but to this day (October 25) no patch has come out. I hope this gets fixed, but this reeks of a cash grab.Bottom line for me is, this game has potential, but for not being early access, this needs so time in the oven. I will continue to play, because I am stubborn and won’t let a game beat me. But, I can’t recommend this game to anyone else, at least in the state it is in right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Bringing back simplicity!My favorite thing about this game is how it draws you in and keeps you coming back. The game play is so heavily based on skill that as soon as you die you know what you did wrong. Maybe you should've opted for melee and used your shotgun instead of trying to evade. Maybe you should have used your ultimate, but you were hording it. You'll always want to adjust your strategy and try again. It's not easy, but it's simple, and fair. The leaderboards will also taunt you to try to speed up your runs to get that high score.The gameplay feels crisp and responsive, exactly what you'd expect for a game like this. All around I'd say Kill Knight is a no brainer if you're into this style of game. Just don't be surprised when you pick it up to play a quick game and find yourself 3 or 4 hours later wondering where the time went.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my top games of the year.  The mechanics are so finely tuned the gameplay is intense and fun.  I honestly can't recommend it enough.  I thought for sure when I started it would be impossible to beat on sufferance difficulty but I just beat it on sufferance AND sever mode (and got 14th place on the global leaderboard at the time of me writing this)When this game clicks with you, you feel like a god. It helps to have a good  build or game plan too going into it which can be hard to do when you're starting out but if you stick with it and really learn the mechanics, the weapons and equipment will come.  Its actually super important to understand how kill power and stuff works so I recommend revisiting the tutorials like a week after you first start playing to make sure you aren't missing some critical mechanic that could really help out.You do need to memorize the order of each level but thats part of the fun and challenge. Because it isnt random you can change your build to get around parts of levels that are giving you trouble.Eventually you'll find a build so good that once you get up to full kill power you're almost unstoppable.  And after dying a thousand times to some of the lasers and exploding pylons and freaking everything, it feels really good to feel unkillable.Can't wait to see where they take this because the ending left it open for more content!Absolutely love it.  I havent felt rage like this since my very first dark souls playthrough.  Where you know you lost because you ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up.  And where you know you win because you really did get better!

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it was time-warped to the modern era. It is ball-busting, it is unapologetic, it is kind of sadistic, it will bring the worse in you, but it's amazing for that!Kill Knight is an arcade top-down shooter (you can think of it as an isometric Asteroids) where the goal is to get as many points as possible, but that's only if you get to survive the waves of enemies coupled together with morphing arenas that will try their best to kill you.The gameplay is so polished it is never the game's fault, it will probably humble you and kill your ego in the process of digesting your frustration. Hell, it humbled me: I had to go down from Knight (Hard) to Acolyte (Normal) to finish the game because I was getting mad filtered by the laser grids, had to bite my tongue and accept defeat to advance, but I will finish this game on Sufferance!mf devs you'll get what you deserve(I love this game and wish you the best, pls make a sequel or another game with standard level progression and many bossfights, I will pre-order it).Edit: I did it. Fellas, it is peak.

_childDocuments_.review: I love that this game knows exactly what it wants to be and doesn't compromise it's vision. This is a pure twin stick shooter action game with deep mechanics that takes a lot of time to get better at. Tight controls and sick aesthetics. Totally my jam.The active reload system is pretty ingenious here - each time you reload, you have three different options: increase your next clip's firepower, perform a unique melee attack, or absorb red orbs to increase your Warp Drive meter. When you opt for the letter two, your next clip is weaker, but sometimes you need to melee to get more heavy ammo, or there are orbs that are too far out of reach (they disappear after a short amount of time).The point being, you are asking every second or two to make a split second decision as to what's the best course of action when you reload, and each option has trade-offs. That's the nugget of brilliant game design that keeps you thoroughly engaged at all times. And then the trade-off math changes when you update your loadout.THIS GAME ROCKS - 10/10
