_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - if you love challenging, unforgiving twin-stick shooter gameplay, knights with guns, and the unbridled, sheer amounts of swag this game delivers, KILL KNIGHT is a must-buy.KILL KNIGHT is an amazing, unforgiving twin-stick arena shooter that brings a fast-paced, intensive, and rewarding combat system, and perfectly delivers the power fantasy of ruthlessly mowing down brutal hordes of monsters... Having finally cleared the full game in just Acolyte difficulty and moving onto my Sufferance play through (and eventually trumping the Sever mode), after reading the (albeit sparse) negative reviews, I must clarify that this game is not for those unwilling to master the full arsenal across hundreds (and maybe even thousands) of attempts. Despite only having five stages to boot, the sheer difficulty and mechanical intensity of KILL KNIGHT will MAKE SURE you get familiar with each and every one of them. However, once your armour feels like second skin, slaying the masses will feel truly rewarding as you tactically swap between your options to fit your current position.Built upon one of my all-time favourite concepts, the timed quick reload system, KILL KNIGHT grants you the tools to cover all bases of offense and defense, but only if you can earn it. Aside from your primary, three components make up most of the combat of KILL KNIGHT; swords, heavy weapons and wrath bursts. Heavy weapons provide your main source of damage, and operate on a limited ammo basis that is regained upon killing enemies with your sword. This creates a back-and-forth dynamic where you need to alternate between your sword and your heavy if you want to maximise your damage output, encouraging you to take great risks for even greater rewards.Additionally, regaining health is also locked behind the wrath burst, a powerful alternative fire from your heavy weapon that can only be unleashed once the wrath bar is full. Filling this bar is done by absorbing blood gems, dropped by every enemy. However, absorbing blood gems for wrath forgoes building up the damage buff blood gems normally grant, meaning that you have to strategically decide between potential kill power/damage boosts or a powerful burst of damage and healing.Both your primary, absorption and melee attacks can be enhanced if performed within the quick reload time-frame emptying your primary provides, respectively over-driving your primary, absorbing all gems on the map or performing a stronger melee (with i-frames!).In conclusion, by making you weigh your options and keeping you under intense pressure, KILL KNIGHT's combat system provides you with a means to sweep, heal and cleave your way through your enemies, as long as your can prove your worthiness to wield it.Equipped with nothing but a basic loadout at the beginning, KILL KNIGHT's main form of progression comes from completing missions to earn more gear. However, just like the gameplay itself, the game will push you to your limits if you want to unlock them. These missions range from basic goals like completing a stage without failing a quick reload, to unique quests tied to your newfound strength after unlocking a new weapon. Whilst you may be stuck trying out a playstyle you're not fond of for a while, the game makes sure you are equally compensated and rewarded for your struggles and efforts....or you can just buy the next item with enough in-game currency, if you're a  (there's an achievement for buying something so go ahead actually)i am knight and i must killDo I think this game is amazing? Absolutely. For a fair price of 20 NZD or roughly 15 USD, KILL KNIGHT delivers on aesthetics, gameplay and the overall power fantasy of being a one-man army. In fact, is it deserving of an Overwhelmingly Positive review? I think so, and I'm doing my part to make it that way. Aside from suggesting a few minor changes, such as increasing how much currency you earn per run and adding UI visibility closer to the center of the screen, this game in my personal opinion is borderline (if not) perfect, and is a breath of fresh air amidst the current gaming landscape.Overall, if you love challenging, unforgiving twin-stick shooter gameplay, knights with guns, and the unbridled, sheer amounts of swag this game delivers, KILL KNIGHT is a must-buy.P.S. not  real knights use a gamepad. keyboard is fine, too.

_childDocuments_.review: This game rules. When I try to convince people to check it out I say that it's modern Doom turned into a run based, high score chasing twin stick shooter. Juggling different ammo types by using your arsenal of moves as effectively as possible is the core of the experience and getting into a flow where everything is firing on all cylinders feels awesome. There's a ton of unlockable equipment that drastically changes up your play style and mixing and matching items to clear specific levels, take on challenges, or just go for a new high score is a ton of fun. The game is hard as hell, so it's nice that there's a lot of options to play around with so that back-to-back-to-back attempts don't feel too repetitive. I think the bones of this game are good enough that it could have probably gotten away with a single weapon set, but the fact that they went above and beyond in that aspect just makes the game that much better. Still banging my head against the third layer, but I'm having a great time with it so far. Highly recommend checking it out.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I just want to say that I'm in my 40s and I've been gaming since the days of Atari 7800. I've owned just about every mainline console and have played several arcade shooters. This game right here is definitely something special. It is without a doubt, one of the best top-down, twin-stick shooters I have ever played. The movement is fluid, responsive, the controls are easy to pick up. It also plays great on the Steam Deck but I prefer to play on my PC because of the feeling of the bumpers L1/R1 on the Steam Deck. They feel a little off because this game as forced me to play with my Index and Middle finger on each side so I can press L1/L2 and R1/R2 quicker. I've never needed to play like that before on a controller with both fingers but this game is challenging enough where I've had to adapt this way. Its usually my Index finger pushing either button when needed.The graphics are simple yet comfortable. I appreciate the red tone of the levels and how they shift as you move to the next wave. The music is pretty awesome. Its not blowing your ears out but still has a tempo good enough to have you immersed in the world. I definitely recommend this game if you like top-down, twin-stick shooters. Its already my second favorite right after Vex Machina.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by confessing I'm not good at this type of games. I'll never be on top of the leaderboard but this game is so good I really don't care. I have fun beating my own high score and unlocking new weapons.It's a fun, nicely designed and really hard twin stick arena shooter. Biggest strengths are presentation (as a whole thing, even menus), music (it's doom 2016 mixed with arcade machine sounds) and cleverly intertwining mechanics. They basically force you to balance between ways of killing enemies and collecting stuff to power your character or arsenal. There are a bunch of items to unlock that will allow you to create a build that suits you best.I really hope this gets traction and devs will have the possibility to build something big on this great foundation. To sum it up, its Geometry Wars mixed with Doom. 5/5Things good to know (no spoilers):- Game is hard. It's Souls-like twin stick shooter. You need to get good to play it. It will mop the floor with you. (UPDATED After 10h).- Works  great on Steam Deck but eats battery fast- You can get hit and most of the time it won't ruin your run- Remember to blink

_childDocuments_.review: This feels as if Devil dagger/Hyper demon, Doom Eternal and Nex Machina made love and gave birth to an incredible baby.The game is a tough as nails twin stick shooter with abyss level of depth. Many many mechanics that are ALL essential to survival needs to be learned, assimilated and used on a second's notice. What might feel like mechanical bloat early one quickly turns into an arsenal of combat options that all make perfect sense. Nothing feels like an afterthought. This is where the Doom Eternal comparison comes from, think of how you must use everything in your arsenal to succeed, it's the same in Kill Knight.Unlocks are achievement based but you do gain in game currency that lets you unlock stuff should the game's difficulty be too much. There is endless loadout options and those I have unlocked so far all offer drastic differences in gameplay strategies.I highly recommend this game. It's minute to minute gameplay, the chunky sound effects, the gritty visual style, it's incredibly well made. If you want a perfect adrenaline rush game to be permanently installed on your steam deck for a quick burst here and there, this game is an absolute keeper.My only wish?  Please give us a nice Endless/survival mode with randomised level layouts/enemies... but this is a nitpick at best and I'm convinced it's in the cards already.

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what it says on the tin. I love me a good twin stick shooter, and by god does this one deliver in every way, Super tight controls, incredibly rewarding gameplay loop, meaningful challenges and gratifying progression & unlocks, incredible art direction, and absolutely oozing style in every single way. If you're after another rogue-like/lite in the vein of vampire survivors or enter the gungeon, kill knight might not be what you're after. However, if you love those games for the gameplay loop and not the rogue-like/lite elements (namely permanent progression outside of runs), then kill knight is almost definitely the game for you. I've seen some reviews criticising clunky controls - honestly, on a PS5 controller, the learning curve of choosing between movement, offence, and defence becomes totally natural incredibly quickly. Can't speak for mouse and keyboard or XBox controller, but with PS5? Chef's kiss. Whole game is chef's kiss. I haven't even talked about the music & sound design, but that's only because it's so immersive and enthralling that it barely even registers as a distinct segment of the game. TLDR: Oozing style from visuals to controls to gameplay loop. Very rewarding and gratifying. Do not mistake it for a rogue-like-lite. Possibly the best twin-stick shooter I've ever had the joy of experiencing.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great and a lot of fun. Had to get used to the keyboard controls. In the beginning it seems difficult - but once you get the mechanics you are full in flow.When you get upgrades it is really recognizable how the game play changes. My impression is overall that the developers have taken great care for this aspect - everything seems fine tuned to the T.You get the game while playing it - and learn to focus on the right things.My tips for people starting out:=======================- The pistol overdrive is your number one skill. That's the one in the second tutorial. You want to really recognize the sound when the bar appears and learn the rhythm and timing of it - and only focus on that. In the beginning its a bit hard to do that, because you become hectic if the screen is full - but believe me this clears the screen, and you can always dash to another location on the screen due to increased speed.- The second thing I use is shift - pulling the blood shards until I have one of the healing shard attacks. If it is full and not needed - keep it until you seem overwhelmed or need the healing. Could do the first level after some hours of gaming with these two aspects.- I tried to use the sword often in the beginning - but that didn't do so well. I would rather use it sparsely in the beginning. Same goes for the heavy attacks - those are live savers in some circumstances - so usually having one or two shots is good. But the wrath attack is just superior. That might change later on in the game.First Impression (and probably longer lasting one as well)=============================================So far, a great experience. Thank you, to the designers / developers. You did what Indie Devs should do and focused on mechanics and were very talented and hard working in doing so. It is really recognizable only after playing a couple of hours and getting the hang of it that this shines through - and it is not so well visible from videos.Of course I want to support such dedication. My candidate for Indie Game of the Year (though I did not play so many Indie-Games this year :)).Also the Vibe of the game is great. It is a mixture of hell, cyberpunk and goth. Quite unique scenario. I also like how they implemented the UI - really stylish retro tv screen kind of.When you die - this effect is just cool :D.The whole game is as if you have bought a new full price game in the golden era of gaming - a unique interactive piece of art, something new and different. Highly recommended buy - you won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: IT IS NOT A ROGUE-LIKE game.It's an twink-stick shooter and its great. The gameplay is really fun and doesn't feel repetitive due to the multiple loadouts you can try but it definitely can be overwhelming .I guess the bad things I could list is..-It'd be nice if equipment got some balance changes , there are options that are obviously much better than the rest... -And my biggest issue is honestly the UI. It is really hard to pay attention to anything but the center of your screen since you got all the timed-events and ofc you have to dodge a horde of enemies and projectiles coming at you. If there was a way for an alternative UI to be added where everything is in the center (minimized) or a way to increase the UI so it'd be easier to look at it in the middle of chaos , that'd be great.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very fun, its definitely a challenge. The music is excellent. It feels like this game is aiming for a particular type of player, the semi-hardcore to hardcore in both the time investment to become truly proficient and the challenge the game presents. There is a LOT going on, between the hazards, enemies and the 30 layers of interacting things you have to keep in mind as a player. There is a learning curve and you're asking a lot of your hands and your mind pretty much the entire time, which is something to keep in mind if you don't have the sort of time to invest in really learning the game and getting your hands used to playing it. As you get familiar with the process though, there is a decent amount of fun to be had for a pretty good price. There is also a pretty steep difference between the first and second difficulty levels, don't be too proud to lower the difficulty to explore what the game has to offer and build up some muscle memory if you're too stuck.

_childDocuments_.review: I dodge demon. I kill demon. Game good.Edit: changing to negative - lessened healing on Knight+ feels wrong and doesn't match the frenetic pace. Something has to give - either faster starting speed and less reliance on kill power for damage, speed, and dodge distance, slower-than-instantaneous enemy attacks, better attack telegraphing, or allowance for increased FOV to decrease off-screen hits. As it stands, this is an ankle-biting simulator in tight corridors. That gets old fast when most everything is unbalanced and you're forced to brute force and replay the same map for hours. _childDocuments_.review: The game is mostly about dodging incrementally harder/volumous stuff and balancing which type of reload you are doing depending on which resource you need the most. It rewards you for playing higher difficulties and assumes you will fail multiple times trying to unlock new equipment. The design is flawless, with dark fantasy in mind, as if MC from Blasphemous had been given guns and asked to descend into hell. Region priced and reasonably so, congratulations to the devs for making it accessible for everyone.I have no complaints, I just need to git gud, will put more hours into it for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: This game offers great value for its price, being easy to jump into while also having an impressively high skill ceiling. The difficulty scaling and wide variety of weapon and equipment options add depth. So far, the unlocked items don't feel significantly stronger than each other, but instead cater to personal and aesthetic playstyle preferences, which I love.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Kill knight is a breath of fresh air, its challenging and unique stylistically.It has a focus on gameplay, improvement and dopamine farming. After your second play through on respawn (you will be dying a lot) you can already feel the start of muscle memory forming and the satisfaction of building your skills up to face the greater and greater challenges. Its something so addictive that you search for but maybe find hard to find outside of classic dopamine farms like online competitive FPS's or MOBA's.Do yourself a favor and get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Action game aficionados, rejoice. We have another gauntlet of ultraviolence to conquer.Kill Knight takes the combat design of games like Returnal, Doom Eternal, and Rollerdrome and applies it to slick, highly stylized arcade twin stick shooting. If you like fast paced combat and score chasing, you will find plenty to love in this frantic, endless war against eldritch forces.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played through completely yet, but I am in love. It's like a combination of HYPER DEMON and a twinstick shooter, but with more structured levels than the typical score attack corollaries. The learning curve is steep enough that repeated attempts not only unlock new gear for variety but make the chase towards mastery rewarding along the way.Update:Playside has made something astounding. There are so many incredible touches that make this game shine. Later enemies ask for a deep knowledge of mechanics from the player, and higher difficulties match that knowledge level blow-for-blow.I find myself reflecting on my initial parallel to HYPER DEMON quite a bit. I think that the key difference with KILL KNIGHT is that the initial difficulty feels rewarding to conquer. In HYPER DEMON, there is nothing but the high score chase. In this game, clearing each level asks for a mastery so deep that high-scoring feels actionable afterward. I find myself routing enemy kills and managing resources to get a good-scoring run even while I've still yet to complete a level. For people who want a tough-as-nails arcade twinstick, this is excellent. For people who want a good high score chase on top of that, it's extraordinary. Cannot recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: WOW! I'm not really a big fan of twin-stick bullet hells but I have been unable to put Kill Knight down since I purchased it on its release.  $15 for a game with a very engaing gameplay loop and such a badass aesthetic is an absolute steal, highly recommend it!This game absolutely nails encouraging the player to enter a "flow state" amid all the carnage you will wreck. I would say the closest comparison is Doom Eternal as both games require fast-paced, delibrate decision in order to sustain yourself and sustain your slaughter. Having to balance clearing the hordes vs. recovering ammo vs. recovering health is really satisfying, especially as you get more and more efficient as you get closer to beating a given level. I am generally turned away from bullet hells because I don't really find dodging swathes of projectiles fun however Kill Knight doesn't actually do this (at least to the extent that other games in the genre do). Instead it throws hordes of enemies at you that you have to cut down. It can feel very much in the vain of L4D2, Vermintide, or DRG and while I do love coop horde shooters, I really like that Kill Knight offers a similar experience in a singleplayer package. This can be a challenging game. While I did enjoy the difficulty, I do feel like there was an extremely abrupt difficulty curve following the 2nd level however I was admittingly playing on Knight difficulty (hardest available during your first playthrough). This does kind of become a problem as each level has the same exact arrangement of enemies, spawns, etc. so if you're throwing yourself at a level over and over it might start to get a bit stale. This can be mitigated by experimenting with the various other equipment in your arsenal however unlocking equipment can be very expensive (or is tied to frankly tedious challenges) so this might not always be possible. Regardless, I still found the core gameplay loop so engaging that this wasn't a big damper for me. Also, the style of this game is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool. I love the brutalistic, hellish aesthetic of the setting. I love the glitchy, bold UI. While the tracks featured later in the game are not as strong, the menu music and the music in the first level (especially when the gameplay starts to get more chaotic) are absolute bangers. More than half the time I spent playing was on my Steam Deck and this game played flawleslly on it. I barely tinkered at all with any of the settings ingame or on the device and it ran at a very smooth 60 FPS, even during the more populated, chaotic moments. Overall, Kill Knight is a must-play if you are a fan of horde shooters or anyone looking for a fast-paced, high-intensity action.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Are you really into twin stick shooters?Do you like your games hard as ♥♥♥♥?Do you get a satisfaction for beating hard as ♥♥♥♥ games?Do you like a game you can jump into and play a quick level, or maybe you wanna sit down and grind out a new high score?Do you like the color red?Kill Knight might be the game for you.This game controls like a dream after you figure out the control scheme that works for you, everything is responsive for a game this fast paced. The tutorials are short and sweet and explain everything you should need to know to get started.  The weapons and armor you can bring into a level are all progress based on certain mission requirements (maintaining a streak, not letting your kill gauge drop in level), but you can grind out in-game currency to purchase those weapons if you find something too challenging.Very fun, very raw. This art style rules, this game rules. You actually cannot go wrong for 15 bucks.Buy Kill Knight. Master the Demon Within. Kill the Last Angel.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love how it feels like a modern take on an arcade game. I'm a busy guy, so I love that I can take 10 minutes, do a run, and get back to what I was doing. Simple game loop, easy to jump into it and start blasting, seemingly hard to master (I've only played 30 minutes so far. lots of attack strategies)...Stoked to keep playing.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions are off the charts. I've been in a huge twitchy/action lull and have zoned out on Vampire Survivors on every single console/platform that's available. The same is true with an old gem called Crimsonland which is more tactical  but action paced, albeit a relic at this point. Lets go back even further to my first love: Robotron 2084. Cave shmups, whatever I've been there but I've waited for this exact game all this time and didn't even know it was a thing until I saw a random promo ad on Metacritic, which I use to find out what's new. (f the actual reviews).This game does all that roguelike meta jazz and adds a layer of mechanics that have you thinking. I normally loathe "arena" shooters that force you into a box or send stuff off the edges of the screen but this one actually gives you the tools to get out of corners and the ability to ask yourself why the hell you put yourself in that bad situation in the first place. Charging up your beam cannon and nuking a crowd of enemies. Juggling the sword attacks to keep your heavy ammo brewing... the gameplay and pacing of this is insanely well crafted and in my short time has produced at least a dozen gratifying "hell yeah" moments. Ill have more to say about the longevity of it all later, but I'm too busy trying to not suck at this game. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED for twin stick shooter fans or maybe even roguelike fans that thought they could be more technical and on the challenging side.
_childDocuments_.name: KILL KNIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: KILL KNIGHT is an ultra-responsive arcade-inspired isometric action shooter. Condemned to eternal sufferance, deep within the voids of an eldritch arena, you must wield an arsenal of devastating weaponry to obliterate swarms of otherworldly horrors - and MASTER THE DEMON WITHIN.

name: SAMURAI WARRIORS 4 DX
detailed_description: A total of 55 different officers are featured in this rich depiction of the Warring States period. The new deluxe edition of 'SAMURAI WARRIORS 4' contains more than 150 previously released DLC, including costumes, weapons, customization parts, scenarios, BGM, and more. • Interact with 55 different officers, including Nobuyuki Sanada and Yoshitsugu Otani! In response to popular demand, Nobuyuki Sanada and Yoshitsugu Otani are now among the many officers featured in this vivid portrayal of the Warring States period. Takatora Todo, Naotora Ii, and Munenori Yagyu, who previously appeared only in Japanese releases, also appear for the first time in the main 'SAMURAI WARRIORS' series. In addition, character designs have been revamped and action elements have been enhanced for fan-favorite characters like Yukimura Sanada and Nobunaga Oda. The range of 55 unique officers, the greatest number of officers in a single game in the series, is a key component of 'SAMURAI WARRIORS.' • Journey through the colorful history of the Warring States period! In the main Story Mode, a tale based on historical events unfolds in two separate parts. While the regional stories focus on officers from regions across the land, such as Kyushu and Shikoku, the story of unification details the events leading up to the end of the Warring States period. Unlike previous 'SAMURAI WARRIORS' titles, this game features battles between each faction, allowing for a more dramatic depiction of the relationships between officers. Experience firsthand the convictions, conflicts, and complex feelings of these officers. • Experience the most exhilarating action in the entire series! The true thrill of this series, mowing down hordes of enemies in battles of 1 vs. 1,000, has been made even more exhilarating with the addition of new elements, including Hyper Attacks, which allow players to quickly close in on their enemies and cut them down, and Rage mode, which powers up attacks when the Spirit Gauge is full and allows players to perform the ultimate finishing move: Musou Frenzy Attacks. In addition, characters' attack types and the overall progression system have been revamped. These new elements offer an unprecedented variety of attacks, along with the strongest sense of exhilaration of any game in the series, all while maintaining the simple controls characteristic of the 'WARRIORS' series. • Travel across the land in Chronicle Mode! Explore the world of 'SAMURAI WARRIORS' in the new Chronicle Mode by completing various types of requests, meeting officers, and collecting items in regions across the land. Leave a lasting mark on the history of the Warring States period by customizing officers via Create Character in the upgraded editing mode. • Switch between characters in real time during battle! Use the Switch Character feature to switch between two different characters on the battlefield in real time as they strive for victory. By switching characters, players can gain an advantage in battle, discover hidden objectives, and receive various benefits. They can also set a detailed plan of action for the character not currently being played. • Utilize the strong connection between Morale and combat! Enemy camps are made stronger by higher Morale levels, but completing objectives and defeating standard bearers lowers enemy Morale and makes it easier to claim victory. As such, the player's actions have a drastic effect on battle conditions.

_childDocuments_.review: It is really heart warming to finally see this game on Steam, since it's official release in 2014, this has been the only Samurai Warriors that is perfect for the first starters of the SW series, since it's not a challenging game, but to 100% it, you gotta grind quite a bit.The Price is not too high nor too cheap, but considering this contains every DLC included, I think it's fair.THE MULTIPLAYER IS AVAILABLE!! Wow I honestly cannot believe it that Online Co-Op function, is also included, considering how they have removed it from Dynasty Warriors 8 and Warriors Orochi 3 Ultimate, I did not have high expectation for them to keep it, but I am super happy that it's here, good job Koei Tecmo!Although, this may not be my favourite SW in the series, it's still is the first introduction of it's new battle system along Dynasty Warriors 8, so it is an important title for the series, and it is way more enjoyable and longer than Samurai Warriors 5, the playAbility, the characters, the story, they are all far superior to Samurai Warriors 5, it's also a lot better than Samurai Warriors 4-II.First Warriors Orochi 3 Ultimate now this, please Koei Tecmo, consider porting the older titles from the PS2-PS3 era as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Not all Musou games are made the same, despite all of them sharing the overall premise of "kill thousands of popcorn mobs and watch numbers go up."  Some are particularly awful like Warriors All-Stars. Some are missteps like DW9, being pulled out of the oven too hastily. And some are just jam-packed full of awesome fun like DW8XL - a delicious pie stuffed with immaculate filling.SW4DX is, quite frankly, a delicious ****ing pie.  It's got over 50 playable characters, a truck-ton of named officers to destroy, a heap of story campaigns to go through and loosely explore Japanese history, a campaign for  your own custom character, all the extra costumes, songs, cutscenes and whatever you want. It even has you upgrading your weapons, hunting for gems and booster items, all in the name of getting insanely strong.  If a power fantasy is your idea of a good time, look no further than this game - you will go from a limited moveset to doing asinine battle dances in no time, and you get to have fun getting all 50+ characters to peak levels. It sounds like a grind, but it's not a chore because you're spending the entire time mowing down 100s of goldfish poop as you're doing it. You don't even have to think all that hard - just keep using the move you want to get better and it just gets better.And don't get me wrong - it's not completely mindless, either. There's tons of objectives to complete in each scenario and while you can usually ignore them and just keep hacking away at insignificant mobs, truly learning where to be and when to be there to nab all the objectives and their rewards adds a great element to each outing.  Not to mention that unlike older Musou games you have played (if you've been out of the loop for a while), you get to bring two characters to each scenario and flip between them on-demand to cover the map. Don't like where the AI  is taking your alternate? Give 'em new orders in 2 seconds and make sure they stick to where you want them to be. It's a tactical layer that's fun to mess with.If you've been out of the game for a while and want to hop back in, but see that SW5 or DX9 are out and , forget that. Get this or DW8XL.  These are top-tier Musou games and some of the most non-sweaty fun you can have. This is Koei having fun and letting you into the room while they do it.

The only thing that is missing to make it almost perfect, is ultrawide support.Bring more like this to steam, SW4 empires, Orochi Z, SW2, DW5 + empires. Would buy.The price could be a bit better all things considered, but is worth it nevertheless.

_childDocuments_.review: This is arguably the best Musou game you purchase on Steam and the best of the Samurai Warriors titles as a whole. I say this as someone who completed the original release on PS4 along with its semi sequel 4-II. The most important thing I appreciate about 4DX is how it manages to cover a large chunk of the Sengoku period by allowing the player to participate in multiple campaigns.That’s not to say I didn’t appreciate the more focused and smaller scale story of something like Samurai Warriors 5 (which centered primarily around Oda Nobunaga and Akechi Mitsuhide) but if you want a game that’s going to give you and extremely exaggerated synopsis of Japans warring states period, this is the one. It’s not a quick beat either as there’s the traditional story mode along with chronicle mode which lets the player create their own character and participate in largely “what if” scenarios. I’m really glad the DX version got a release outside of the Japan. Now if we can just port Dynasty Warriors Gundam: Reborn to Steam, I’ll be very happy.
_childDocuments_.name: SAMURAI WARRIORS 4 DX

_childDocuments_.review: Samurai Warriors 4 DX was shadow released by Koei and what a great addition it was to the PC Warriors library. This release specifically features all the content which was previously released for SW4 which includes additional scenarios and costumes but nothing from 4-2 so do mind that if you liked some of the additions from that instalment. Essentially the same type of release as Warriors Orochi 3 Definitive.The game itself is phenomenal and probably my second favourite Warriors game of all time. Gameplay is smooth and fun with every character feeling varied enough to try them out, the roster is great and one of the biggest in the Samurai franchise and personally had some surprise favourites who otherwise I would never have tried in an Orochi game or previous SW games.What truly elevates this game into greatness is the phenomenal storytelling and soundtrack, as for me those elements in games are always very important. I have played previous SW games such as the first one and 2 Empires but I believe that this was the peak of storytelling that the franchise reached, segmented mini stories for all characters who were easily likeable with some exceptions and showcasing their side of the conflict within the Sengoku period.I don't pretend to know that much about the actual era, but from what the game presents it looks like a comprehensive experience which showcases all aspects of that specific era, and for the first time moving past some notable events and exploring further into history.There is no main story as it is more like an over encompassing adventure but it can be said that the most effort went into the posterboy Sanada story, but none of the stories feel lacking in content or significance.The port itself is fantastic as it runs on a solid 60 FPS without error and only crashed once on startup so I can highly recommend this game for any Musou fan if you haven't previously played this. If you have experienced 4 in some form then I would say this release might not be for you, but the addition of all the DLCs in one package might alleviate that fact, even if the pricepoint is steep, it's highly worth it for the amount of gametime you can have with this release such as the main story and Chronicles mode which warrants replays.Thank you Koei for bringing this port to the PC and please keep them coming with a Samurai Warriors 3Z release or previous games' remasters as the Samurai Warriors franchise felt left behind in recent times.
_childDocuments_.name: SAMURAI WARRIORS 4 DX

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. A functional PC port from Koei-Tecmo?! It is quite a beautiful sight. And to shadow-drop it to boot. Fantastic. Worth every penny. The best Samurai Warriors, if not the best Musou game, ever made. Now updated and on your shiny new PC or Steam Deck. It feels like 5 Birthdays at once. I have yet to encounter a single problem. A+ 5/5 would burn Hannoji and disappear again.Framerate capped at 60 for gameplay, and looks like 30 for cut-scenes, and max 1440p.  (This is no problem for me.)Saw a review saying it looks great in 4k, however I do not see that option in the settings.Supposedly there is no Ultrawide support (I wouldn't know), and it won't let UW users play this Fullscreen or go past 1080p (not tested...).People seem to have a problem with the price. Some might find it worth waiting for a sale.Apparently, 4k should be available. K-T appears to be trying to solve that issue, although failing at it in fun ways.K-T's "fix" was to try restarting the game...lmfao.Yea, doesn't work (for me).Patch just dropped that included a fix to the resolution issue.

Just desperately want Samurai Warriors 1, 2 and 3 to get some love next... well and 5 Empires while I'm already wishing for things.For my First Impressions of Samurai Warriors 4 Dx check out my video here:

The only nitpick I have with this game is if you have multiple monitors with their own speakers, you can not switch where the sound comes from once you start and you will have to manually switch everything before you start up the game with you want the sound to go through a specific device.

_childDocuments_.review: I personally prefer older Warriors titles, in particular, the older Dynasty Warriors (DW) Games. Samurai Warriors (SW) always felt a bit jankier to me if that makes sense.This is the first SW Game I've played since SW2 Empires and I have to say I'm pleasantly surprised. I did not play this game on release and only can speak on this port exclusively.My biggest gripe with it is the lack of an English Dub. I feel it severely detracts from the experience given that if I want to follow along with the games plot, I have to put my full undivided attention into it and that's not what I want from a warriors game. But damn the game-play here is really solid, again I prefer the older "slower" combat of the PS2 era titles but this game feels electric.If there's one thing I want to be taken away from my review of the game, to KOEI,  port more of your older titles to newer hardware. And don't cheap out when it comes to bringing the games to the West. These games are so amazing but it feels like every-time we get the short end of the stick with these games. I feel like I'm getting a slightly lesser product since I can't understand this game, it makes it harder for me to justify buying this game. _childDocuments_.review: Samurai Warriors 4 (dont confuse it with 4-II) is finally on Steam. Gameplay-wise is pretty similar to 4-II (they even added some of the changes the sequel added) but with the stories and modes of 4.--"Ok, but I never played 4-II. What does that means to me?"--Just like every Musou, the game is a mix between Hack'n'Slash and strategy. You control two characters and you go arround the battlefield doing objectives and defeating enemies, while you keep some key characters (like maybe your commander) alive. Is simple in both fronts, but is pretty well mixed giving a lot of entertainment.About the modes, you have 3 modes:- Story: You play with diferent stories. History based ones, but heavely romanticed. Those stories deal with some of the different clans of the last years of the Sengoku era, begining with Oda's rise to power at Okehazama and ending with the Siege of Osaka, Yukimura's last charge and Ieyasu unification of japan.Depending of their importance in the greater picture they will be shorter (like 3-4 stages long) or larger. And as you complete some, you will unlock more.- Free mode: You can pick any mission you have completed on story, and play it with any character of you chossing. Great if you want to complete all objectives of a mission but you dont like any of the characters available to play on Story.- Chronicles mode: In this mode, you can play as your own OC (that you can use too in Free mode, but not in Story) and a secondary character of your chosing and travel around japan meeting people and doing short missions. The main goal is to get all biographies that you obtain when a character joins you. They also have "Friendship level" that you can get and unlock events with them.After that theres the typical settings option (no much to customize here, but being a 10-year old game, almost any recent PC should be capable of runing it without trouble) and a gallery to check every character unlocked, review events and cutscenes, music, etc.This version includes all the DLC of the game too, and thats A LOT. Of course, the majority of it is just new skins, music and armor parts for our OC (its all aesthetic, they dont effect the stats in any way), but some of them are self-contained new stages.About performance, once again the game is a 10 years old game so it should play fine. If thats not the case, you can still change some things like resolution, texture quality, shadows, etc. You can also cap the framerate to 30 FPS if needed.Lastly, at least in Steam Deck the game plays perfectly and is not going to give much trouble. Maybe the price is a little high for what the game is, but if youre curious about Musou's, this is still one of the best you can play.

_childDocuments_.review: Samurai Warriors 4 DX-------------------------------------------------------As a long-time fan of the Musou / Warriors franchise, I must confess that these games are a bit of a guilty pleasure for me. There's something irresistibly captivating about the blend of history, myth, and sheer over-the-top action that these games deliver. So, when Samurai Warriors 4 DX finally got localized, it felt like a dream come true.*Gameplay and Fun Factor:Samurai Warriors 4 DX is an absolute blast to play. The core gameplay remains as exhilarating as ever, with players taking control of legendary samurai and battling through hordes of enemies. The combat is fast-paced and satisfying, offering a seamless mix of strategic depth and button-mashing fun. Each character has a unique set of moves and abilities, ensuring that no two battles ever feel the same.One of the standout features is the Hyper Attack mechanic, which allows for rapid movement and chaining attacks across multiple enemies. It keeps the action fluid and dynamic, and it's incredibly rewarding to clear out massive groups of foes with a single, well-timed combo.*Content and Replayability:Where Samurai Warriors 4 DX truly shines is in its sheer volume of content. The game includes all the DLC from the original release, offering a staggering amount of characters, scenarios, and customization options. With over 50 characters to choose from, each with their own storylines and missions, there's always something new to discover. The Chronicle Mode is particularly engaging, allowing players to create their own characters and explore Japan in a more free-form narrative experience.Additionally, the game features an extensive upgrade system, encouraging players to experiment with different weapons and skills. This, coupled with the numerous difficulty settings, ensures that the game remains challenging and rewarding, even for seasoned veterans of the series.*Final Thoughts:For those who, like me, consider the Samurai Warriors franchise a guilty pleasure, Samurai Warriors 4 DX is a delightful treat that justifies every moment spent in its action-packed world. Finally having this game localized is a true gift, and it's one that I'll be enjoying for a long time to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Please bring back English voice acting to the Warriors franchise. Please. This is such a good game, but it lacks the character of the older games. The fact that all the voice acting is in Japanese makes it harder to relate to the characters when you don't speak the language. It also causes issues with trying to read subtitles when playing the game, and that's never easy or fun to keep in balance - it's like texting while driving. Even though there were mispronunciations and I'm sure mistranslations, the hokey voice acting is part of what made these games so memorable. I don't mean this as a jab against the voice actors either - they are wonderful and I love them.Other than that, this is one of the best Warriors titles available - especially on PC. I discovered this series with Dynasty Warriors 3, and this has a really good balance of what's good in the newer games as well as what really worked in the older ones. It's not anything terribly new to the franchise in terms of gameplay, but that's fine, it's a Warriors title. You know what you're here for, and it does it well.Folks are going to complain about the pricing all day long, but I don't think $49.99 is a terrible price for how much content you get, and I'm not talking about the DLC with the skimpy costumes for you anime weirdos out there. There is enough content here for Warriors fans to justify the price in my opinion.For anyone that doesn't like the Warriors titles, there is absolutely nothing here that will change your mind if you already don't like them. If anything this game embraces what the haters hate on, and I love it for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best pc port of a musou game, definitely the best port of one that I've played so far at least. Quick note, this game does come with the dlc weapons, however you need to unlock them first, which I think would is an interesting way of not breaking the game too quickly, however the unlock requirements are extremely vague. I unlocked them after finishing every mission in story mode with an objectives cleared rating of around 75%, although I've heard other people say they unlocked after just finishing the dlc missions (Secret Histories - I did these last so unfortunately I'm not able to add much to this) or reaching 80% objectives cleared.Onto the game itself, the soundtrack is phenomenal, easily one of my favourite game OSTs of all time. The combat is extremely fun and satisfying, although your mileage may vary based on your opinion of hyper attacks (personally I love them, but they definitely make the game significantly easier). Character switching is great, however its use as a traversal tool is somewhat limited by how effective hyper attacks are at moving around the battlefield. That being said, it's a great way to tie down a fleeing opponent or protect an important ally. There are 55 playable characters, and 3 main modes, story mode, free mode and Chronicles.The story largely sticks to the historical records of events, albeit with the usual exaggerations, whitewashing and gameplay concessions we've come to expect. This means that there are no hypothetical routes in this game, and the few branches in the story for missions such as Sekigahara still result in their historical outcomes. The story is broken up into several "Legends" that function as chapters, with most focusing on particular regions of Japan and the conflicts that occurred there, although there are a few that focus on a specific clan or individual. The region stories, such as Legend of Tohoku and Legend of Kanto tend to be around 4 missions, and mostly serve to set up characters from those regions in preparation for the larger conflicts, which mostly occur during the larger stories such as Legend of the Oda and Legend of a Land United.For me, much like many of the other entries in this series and Dynasty Warriors, the best part of this story was that it was interesting enough to encourage me to look into the real history that it's based on, but there are some fairly major issues I have with this story in particular. Firstly, the Legends can vary wildly in terms of significance, length and overall quality. The Legends of specific regions of Japan have considerably less to offer than the ones that focus more on specific clans or individuals, in large part because despite the names, the region stories tend to suffer from far fewer choices for playable characters in story mode, often only giving you two. Of course the playable character issue is largely solved by the existence of free mode, but to unlock these stages in free mode you still have to get through the story versions. Another issue with these stories is that many of them follow the same formula of spending the first couple stages fighting only generic officers, then around stage 3 or 4 one of the unifiers shows up with their army, and then it ends with a cliffhanger to push you towards one of the other Legends, usually the one featuring the unifier that showed up. The Legend of Chugoku is probably the most egregious example, although the only reason Tohoku isn't quite as bad is because I like the playable characters more.My second issue with the story is the way in which certain characters are portrayed, specifically the unifiers. Nobunaga has become an over the top cartoon villain, to the point where Nobunyaga from Warriors All-Stars feels like a more nuanced take on the guy. Hideyoshi, similarly to his depiction in the rest of this series, is presented as a goofball that everyone loves, which while it can be entertaining at times, is easily the most egregious instance of whitewashing history in the series. Ieyasu is probably the best out of these 3 portrayals, although I wish we saw a little more of what he was willing to do for the sake of bringing peace to Japan.Free mode is similar to other free modes throughout the series, letting you play through story missions as any characters you've unlocked. So far I've mostly used it either to grind levels for characters that don't show up as playable characters very often in the story mode or to do silly stuff like playing as Nobunaga on the Incident at Honnoji stage. Unfortunately, you can only play as the side of the battle that was playable in story mode, unlike some of the other musou games, but it's still nice to have.Chronicles is probably the most interesting mode on offer, although at time of writing I've only dabbled in it. The concept of it is that you create a character in edit mode, and then pick a starting region, and from there your goal is basically to meet and befriend as many characters as you can as you travel across Japan. Your primary character in this mode will always be your custom character, however as you meet and befriend the playable characters, you will unlock them as a secondary character in the mode. From what I've played, it seems like each character has quite a number of events with your character, where you are given occasional dialogue choices that can increase or decrease their opinion of you.While I spent a lot of this review focusing on the parts of this game I wasn't a huge fan of, that's mostly just because I had more to say about them, even though they are relatively minor blemishes on the overall experience. Overall, I think it has some of the most fun combat in the series and is one of the best musou games available on steam.

_childDocuments_.review: This is something of a comfort game for me, the gameplay of the musou games might not seem very deep or complex, and every game is a new take on the same historical tale, but I simply enjoy the very anime-like adaptation of the setting and historical figures. I originally bought a PS4 to play this and the Empires expansion, but having it now on PC is much more convenient, and contrary to Koei's reputation, this PC port actually seems to run well without issue, at least for me.What you're getting with this game is essentially an exaggerated adaptation of the end of the Segoku-Jidai period, from Nobunaga's rise to the Siege of Osaka Castle, with fantasy wushu magic and supernatural powers to anime caricatures of historical samurai, including figures that weren't warriors in real life but are made into fighters for the sake of Samurai Warrior's setting; such as my favourite character, Mori Ranmaru. The gameplay is simple hack and slash combat against large groups of enemies, with objectives and enemy officers to deal with, most of the difficulty comes from trying to complete every objective in a battle. Overall it can get very repetitive over time, the main thing keeping you invested will be the story and characters.Although this game was only re-released due to the anniversary of Samurai Warriors, I would still like to see more games brought to PC, such as 4 Empires, or more of the older PS2 Samurai and Dynasty Warriors games. This could be the start of a good trend for Koei, in bringing more of their older titles to PC for the sake of preserving them, and allowing new fans to play them for the first time, rather than having to emulate them. That said, there are still many PC ports of musou games on steam that still require updating and fixing.

_childDocuments_.review: "And here we have an artifact from the distant past! A game that's actually enjoyable! A game with attractive and cool looking characters! An offering of plentiful content for a rather fair asking price! Yet I should put it back in its' ancient vestments. Can't have the Proper-Protocol-Police arrest me for being in possession of dangerous wrong-think contraband! (Nervous laughter) Still,a neat little foray into a less civilized era of human development! Very "retro-sheik"! Very pre-modern-audience if you will!" ~Future archaeologist and anthropologist from the divergent dystopian time-line Tecmo Koei amuses me! I beat Samurai Warriors 4 II awhile ago. While it was enjoyable it did a lot of messed up things like putting all the extra outfits and character customization pieces behind a ridiculous paywall. From what I can tell vanilla samurai warriors 4 DX spins its' yarns based upon whole factions whereas SW 4 II told more independent personal stories. I'll level with you,both are about the same time period and the events in both unfold in very similar ways. Between them I believe DX is much better. You get all that juicy dlc "free" and character customization pieces get unlocked just by going through Chronicle Mode. (With the general consensus being it is better than the Nobunaga-tower-challenges from 4 11)If you are a musou fan you know what you are getting! If you are "not" a musou fan these games focus on historical heroes and historical heroines mowing down thousands of enemy soldiers on battlefields that shaped both Chinese and Japanese history. Each series has unique features and unique mechanics yet overall draw inspiration from the same well.What I mean by "history" is a very loose interpretation of it with much embellishment. Certain characters are decked out in gear that makes them look like overly flamboyant protagonists and antagonists from sentai shows like Kamen Rider! The fact you can become a moving grim-reaper possessed wood-chipper as you turn whole populations into so much mulch is part of the fun! In so many words I'm telling you to not go into this believing you are about to have a more grounded experience akin to Ghost Of Tsushima!Yet there is strategy mixed in with the absurdist power fantasies. Killing flag bearers can demoralize surrounding troops. Taking out barracks captains will populate that area with your troops instead of the enemy's. Striking down the messengers of your rivals ensures they will not find out what you are up to. Escorting supply caravans or siege engines safely will keep morale high. Morale will likewise drop if you let traveling merchants,engineers,diplomats,or certain officers die. My bro and best friend taught me the nuances of all this stuff when we played Dynasty warriors 5 in co-op ages ago! If it wasn't for him I would have thrown in my controller with this franchise as you can still lose if you refuse to pay attention to what is going on around you. You can kill a conveyor belt of infinite baddies but will still snatch defeat from the jaws of victory if key characters go unaided too long or you don't attack tactical locations swiftly and efficiently.Features specific to Samurai Warriors 4 DX include1. A type of rush-engaged hyper mode. You charge the enemy hordes fast as lighting whilst attacking large swathes of them simultaneously as they get conveniently bundled together. Remember the team-musous in Warriors Orochi 3 that would round up your foes into a single ball before they would all get shocked and rocked? Same here! 2. The ability to switch between two selected protagonists on different parts of the map at any given time. This will come in handy!3.You can give surrounding troops rudimentary commands such as "follow" "stay put" "attack" or "defend". It's not super in depth but it's a beneficial inclusion all the same.4. There is a "leveling up" system.5. There is an in game store where you can spend in game currency.6. You can collect and equip items that assign various positive attributes to your chosen character.7.Between missions you can select from multiple officers in your fraction to play as.8. Chronicle mode lets you make your own mercenary for hire and live out the feuding-states era from a more personal point of view. (More or less!) 9. There is a "Free mode" where you can repeat missions while playing as absolutely any character you want to.10. There are mounts. (War-Horses)11. It is controller compatible and I had no issues with the default button lay-out.12. Reacting at just the right time does a cool time-slowing evasive based dodge maneuver. Live your fantasies of becoming Sengoku era Neo! You are indeed the chosen one! 13. Weapons are upgraded by installing matching gems into rows of diamond shaped sockets. I preferred the weapon upgrade system in Warriors Of Orochi 3 Ultimate but what is here is fine!14.  One of the few cons is if you liked Naomasa Ii in 4 11 he is reduced to a less epic generic soldier in DX that you can recruit in chronicle mode.15. Each character eventually has two signature special attacks with the later one obviously being more devastating and flashy!And with that you know whether or not this is your jam! Of the Samurai Warriors titles a lot of fans like SW4 DX as much as the coveted best version of SW 2. All I can say is it's certainly better than SW 4 II to the point you wonder why they even bothered making 4 II as a glorified expansion pack. $49.99 is kinda steep for a game this dated but you are getting all the DLC bundled in with the package. It certainly is a lot more buyer-friendly than AAA games going for $69.99 and sometimes $130.00 if you buy the "Legendary rip-you-off edition"!If you want the "Tri force" of best musou titles on Steam I'd say this sits proudly next to Warriors Orochi 3 Ultimate and Dynasty Warriors 7 Extreme Legends. All these entries give you the most bang per buck with their extra content already accounted for!  (Careful Tecmo Koei,if you keep this up it might actually restore my faith in you and reignite the passionate fire in the ice-cold fire-pit where our love affair has hence resided! You're becoming dangerously "based" with these consumer-friendly deluxe re-releases!)

_childDocuments_.review: I am gonna say the negatives, then say why I recommend it anyway.This game is old as hell. The graphics are ugly. It's expensive. The gameplay is old. Archers are gimmicky but you get used to dealing them.I still recommend this game IF you like button mashers. If you don't, maybe this will change your mind, maybe it won't. It's not a "clicker," where the experience feels cheap. You're running around a battlefield beating the snoot off of people. It is glorious, and the repetitiveness is part of what feels good about it.The newer SW and DW games just don't feel as good. Something about how the controls feel, and how the enemies don't just instantly die at early levels just feels nice. You got time to do stuff, too. The map objectives in the early levels don't pass by so fast that they interfere with the rest of the playing experience, and a lot of them are optional.I would say the major differences are, and why I like it is, the attacks feel better when you hit people into other people. It's like knocking over bowling pins, it is great. The other difference is the Musou or "special attacks," these feel a TON better than the newer ones, those feel like 90% cinematic. This one has a little thing at the very end of the attack. but the attack itself feels a lot better, like you're actually playing the damn game. And you can manually charge it if you want to, which is nice.I haven't played multiplayer yet, so this is all based on single player.If you like the older KOEI "Warriors" games, I recommend.

name: ENDER MAGNOLIA: Bloom in the Mist
detailed_description: STORY Set in the Land of Fumes, this prosperous magical superpower is home to vast quantities of magical resources lurking underneath the surface. In hopes of advancing their kingdom's development, artificial life forms known as Homunculi came into being. Regrettably, toxic Fumes from the underground drove the Homunculi to madness, turning them into feral monsters. You play as Lilac, an 'Attuner' who possesses the power to save the Homunculi. Upon waking, you find yourself in a laboratory deep in the underground. There, you will become acquainted with the Homunculi closely involved in the kingdom's downfall. Together with the Homunculi, set out in search of your lost memories and precious friends in the Land of Fumes. Follow the journey of destruction and rebirth in a post-apocalyptic world, decades after the disastrous Rain of Death. SCENARIO ENDER MAGNOLIA is a dark fantasy 2D side-scrolling action RPG where you venture through the desolate Land of Fumes trying to save both humans and Homunculi. At the forefront of magical and mechanical development, the kingdom comprises of a hierarchical societal structure. Here, you'll come across abandoned cities, discover laboratories oozing with heinous mysteries, a grand Sorcerer's Academy, colossal factories, and much more. The hauntingly beautiful yet gruesome world of ENDER MAGNOLIA will unfold before you. Journey with Homunculi and help those who have lost their minds to the Fumes. Fight fearsome, powerful enemies, purify their souls, and rally your companions. Who will you save at the end of your quest — humans or Homunculi? GAMEPLAY ■ Experience the revamped battle system that elevates your gameplay and exploration beyond that of ENDER LILIES. ・Explore the mesmerizing yet grim world at your own pace and take on menacing enemies with the help of your companions. ・Find your battle style using 30 different unique skills acquired from your companions. ・Collect and upgrade loads of equipment, relics, and items. ・Featuring new difficulty levels, you can choose to have a challenging experience or enjoy the gripping storyline at your leisure. ■ Gorgeous 2D art, animation, and music all come together to create a whimsical world. ・Humans and Homunculi live together in the kingdom known as the Land of Fumes. ・Venture out, get to know people, and help one another while unraveling the mysteries of the world. ・Witness poignant cutscenes and enhanced character interactions with your companions. MUSIC After lending their sweet and somber music to ENDER LILIES, 'Mili' is back with new compositions that bring the mysterious world of ENDER MAGNOLIA to life.

_childDocuments_.review: Dark souls metroidvania with Jojo stands part 2: electric boogalooInstant purchase for me, probably the first one as soon as it dropped. CAVEAT EMPTOR:  Ender Magnolia is in Early Access -- it can be completed in 2 to 3 hours. If you can't wait for full release, play Ender Lilies first!Ender Lilies has always had a special place in my heart because everything worked so well. The dark foreboding setting, the beautiful music, the triumph of innocent children wanting to save the world, but accomplishing the bitter-sweet end instead. The stories of our youth, when we dreamed we could accomplish great things.I have no doubt the devs would recapture the magic yet again. I've done three bosses and it captures all the beauty in tragedy of the first game. Good people driven mad by a power beyond understanding, as your character defeats them you reveal their memories and grant them final redemption.The setting takes a slightly more colorful palette than the first game, but still portrays a world in decay. The music (Mili is back!) fits this perfectly, with theme and motiff encapsulating sadness in soft piano melodies.The game is in early access, but I have no doubt the devs will finish the game from 6 months - 1 year like the first game.One apparent change that they introduced into the game is the mini-map feature, it now displays what the level looks like instead of long hollow rectangles. Really helps in backtracking and looks great. I hope more metroidvania games adopt this design.

_childDocuments_.review: Felt obliged to write a quick review on the differences between Lilies and Magnolia. I loved Ender Lilies, and this game is shaping up already to be better or at least, just as good. Magnolia doesn't seem to be completely different, but there are many things it has done which has made it shine brighter than Lilies already. Here's a list of very nice changes: (The early access version gives us access only to the first 2 - 2.5 hours of gameplay) - There is no contact damage. Meaning you now only have to dodge the attacks the enemies make, you can walk through enemies safely now. - Instead of 6 total abilities, between 2 "pages". You now have 4 total abilities on 1 page. Makes combos easier, but slightly reduces your variety of abilities. - Abilities no longer have a set amount of uses. Instead they are defined by different categories. Main, Encore, Continuous, Cool down and Parry. I won't go into the specifics, as they are kind of self explanatory, the only difference to Lilies being that Encore-type is an ability that continuously activates as long as you hold down the button. - Not all boss enemies become available to use as abilities. A stark difference as all boss enemies became your spirits in Lilies. Now some give enhancement materials that can be used to enhance and expand your other "Homunculi". - You get your enhanced dodge very early into the game (Same time as double jump). In comparison you only got your enhanced dodge in Lilies at the 4th main boss. A small change, but makes it early game slightly easier (imo). You also get the QoL that is running as a default ability which is much appreciated. Considering we didn't really have a "running" ability in Lilies. - We now have Equipment, alongside Relics. Equipment is another way to boost your abilities, and we have 4 slots total. The equipment found in early access is only bracelets which only increases defence in different areas. Expected that further on, and other types of equipment will do different things. - THE MAP. It is much easier to read, and to navigate and backtrack using it. The rooms are now detailed and you are now told your position in the room. Any items or doors are now marked on the map as well. Rooms are connected with no mini loading screen between each one, with the exception of significant moves to other areas. (Still quite a few, but now each area feels like 1 big room) Fast travel is also now initiated anywhere using the map. instead of just returning to respite -> rest -> fast travel. - We now have NPCs we can interact with to gather information and lore from. Lilies only provided lore through Memories, Notes and Flavor text. NPCs are now a different way to get lore. These are all differences I took note of. Tried to not spoil much of anything, but there isn't much TO spoil in the first 2 hours anyway. I think Magnolia is already very well done, and excited for updates to come. I didn't encounter any bugs either. P.S The axe, that the axe throwing enemies use doesn't hurt you when it returns to them, unlike the wheel throwing enemies in Lilies. Not sure if that is a bug or not.

_childDocuments_.review: Some very good things:- NO CONTACT DAMAGE!!!- More customization, including equipment, homonculi weapons, etc.- No more use number spirits (we could get them in the final game)- Your character talks and has a personalitySome cons:- Art seems to be somewhat worse than the first game. Not the character art, but the background art. Could be improved for the final game.- Clunky menu controls. For some reason, the button you press to go into the menu, doesn't pull you out of the menu if you press it again.- Weird slowing down dodge animation. I can't put my finger on it, but the dodge animation (not the roll, the dash thing) is weird, you have iframes but it seems to slow down towards the end, and you can only start another one after the first one ends. It looks really weird and it breaks the fluidity of the game. Ender Lilies had much better dodge animation and mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is similar to Ender Lilies and overall does much of the same things well but there are a couple things I want to nitpick:- The dodge animation is slower than in Ender Lilies and it looks strange. It's seems more like a float with iframes than your character actually dodging out of the way of something. I would make it faster and make it cover more distance. In fact the combat movement in general seems very slightly slower than what it was in lilies but its noticeable.- a parry type move was one of the additions to the slightly different combat system. PLEASE don't remove the original parry from Ender Lilies it was so much fun and I can't count how many times I clutched because I parried just in time. The original parry is just too satisfying to remove.- there is a lack of lore collectables that actually tell me where I am. I don't really know much about the places (other than the small town) that I explored or what it was like to be there before I showed up other than that its the lowest point of the city and that it sucks to be there. Especially the area that was used as a safe haven for runaway homunculi. Beautiful area, but I didn't know what the area was for until it was told to me near the end of the area I forgot how it's been a while. The same goes for most of the bosses I didn't really know who I was fighting either. Then again it could be like Eleine in lilies where most of her lore is discovered after you fight her. funny thing is that this game actually has an advantage over Ender lilies in the lore explanations because there are people other than the MC who are still alive. If there isn't something to read about the place, have someone say something about the place. Of course these are the first few areas so most of the world building is going to be visual.- the art seems to be slightly worse than Ender Lilies in the background. I didn't do a comparison or anything but the art in lilies is sharper in my memory whereas in magnolia its a little out of focus and has less exposure. There are multiple great shots of the background within just the EA though so its not like the art is bad or anything, in fact its good that's why I wish I could see it more clearly while i'm playing.- staggering enemies seems pretty overpowered especially against normal enemies who dont have as much stagger resistance as bosses. that's pretty much the only bad stuff I can remember. the good stuff:- The UI is better IMO and QOL changes- the soundtrack quality is consistent with lilies (obviously)- the designs of the enemy's are cooler compared with lilies imo and there is lots of potential for new designs with the industrial theme. I love Nola's design in particular she isn't an enemy but still.- I prefer having less homunculi with more unique abilities than many spirits with one ability- there are some sounds like the dodge sound that I prefer in lilies but for the most part the sound design is improved- there is a clear sense of direction for the characters being that they want to go to the top of the city. Its a small thing but I find that when there is no sense of direction in these games I find myself wandering aimlessly wondering what I'm meant to be doing. Some people prefer it that way but not me. Lilies had this problem too since I honestly forgot that my objective was to find the priestess and I thought she was dead for the majority of the game. It was so much fun that I just wanted to go to the next area even though I didn't know what I was doing though.- there is a clear antagonist in the game being that one family I forgot the name of that's oppressing the homunculi. again it's been a while. It's not like Lilies needed an antagonist because the antagonist was the blight itself in a man vs nature type scenario, but its still cool to have one in magnolia especially because there are people still alive and because humanity has a way to combat the fumes without the help of the priestess.- The art direction is solid- nice things like dialogue at respites and cosmetic options- combat animations for attacks are improved in this gameand im sure there are many more nice things to say that I haven't said here

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? It will most likely be a masterpiece after it is finished.The predecessor Quietus of the Knights, released in 2021, is considered one of the best Metroidvanias of all time, on a par with the somewhat better-known representatives of the genre such as Ori and the Will of the Wisps or Hollow Knight. Quietus of the Knights was also first released in Early Access, only to delight us a few months later as a flawless and technically optimized little masterpiece. In the first installment, we accompanied Lily through a completely destroyed, corrupted world, redeemed our former friends from their suffering (and learned their skills in the process) and ultimately became a deadly fighting machine in order to free the world from the evil that has infested it.Bloom in the Mist is set in the eerily beautiful yet cruel world of Fumes. It takes us back to an apocalyptic world that has been destroyed by depressed, crazed artificial life forms (Homunculi). And we once again play a young girl, Lilac, with amnesia who wakes up in a destroyed ruin and has to save both the humans and the Homunculi. Decades after the events of Quietus of the Knights, homunculi - sad, artificial life forms - roam the land. As is so often the case, progress has ultimately led to disaster. The once highly developed realm of Fumes is full of magical resources that lie dormant beneath the surface. To drive progress, artificial life forms called Homunculi were developed. Unfortunately, the toxic fumes from underground drove the Homunculi mad and turned most of them into savage monsters.Lilac, a former student of the mage academy, can jump, roll, sprint, pull herself up from edges and strike with her sword from the very beginning. Other skills and weapons are only found in the course of the game or learned after successful boss battles. Battles bring experience points, which improve Lilac's character values (life and magic points, defense strength, attack strength, etc.). Enemies give a clear signal before they attack, which makes it easier to dodge or block. As a young girl, Lilac's resistance to damage is not very high, but she carries several healing potions with her. During her adventure, she acquires skills from defeated enemies and finds additional equipment. Relics (when worn) strengthen her even further. The world often branches off in different directions but, typical of Metroidvanias, some parts are impossible to enter unless Lilac has the necessary skills. Fortunately, there is an automatically drawn map. The bosses are visually impressive, they all require different mechanics to defeat.The game can be saved at park benches, as in Hollow Knight. This not only saves your score, but also restores your health - but also revives all enemies. The gameplay mechanics as well as parts of the visual design seem to be clearly inspired by Hollow Knight, which is a good thing. The gamepad support is flawless, the ultrawide screen resolution (21:9) works with black bars on the sides and cloud saves are possible. The music by Japanese band 'Mili', who were responsible for the soundtrack of the previous game, is surprisingly good.The game is still in Early Access and not complete. It plays fantastically, but it ends after four areas. The areas that are already accessible in the game are great. Lilac encounters an abandoned city on her adventures, discovers laboratories, explores a large magic academy and a huge factory. The developers plan to have the rest of the game ready in around six months. I'm excited! Fans get more of what has already made ENDER LILIES a top game and a fantastic Metroidvania. Exciting battles, great bosses, a destroyed, excellently staged world full of secrets, all combined with the excellent controllability of our young heroine. A must-have game for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to make this clear. I am not stating that ender magnolia is trash. The only reason why I put this review as negatative is that i have some important criticism that I feel needs to be changed for this game to be able to rival Ender lillies. Now lets get into itThe first thing I have to say is that gameplay wise this game has improved a lot. The different categories the different allies are put into are really helpful to differentiate between them. Another new and really good update is the upgrade system for each ally so that they can serve 3 different function depending on what the situation calls for. Really adds a lot of strategy and planning to the game which is really good. Personally I did not think contact damage was an issue in the previous game but since a lot of people complained its good that it was removed in this one. I also like the addition of the difficulty setting even though these kinds of games dont really need them. Now lets get into the critizism. First things first I feel like the story telling isnt as good in the previous game, The cutscenes you get for each character goes by way too fast and doesnt cover as much of their backstory as they did in the previous game. You dont really grow on your characters in the same way nor do you get as much infromation. Of course its made up by the small conversations that you have with each ally. The second problem is the worldbuilding. Deciding to put all the collectibles in really obvious spots and also allowing you to get basically all of them as soon as you go to the area removes the exploring aspect of the game. I also feel like the shop function destroys the exploring aspect as well since now you just buy most collectibles. This game also lacks the feeling of dread and that you are getting closer to the truth that the first game had.In summary I feel like the creators have sacrificed the good story telling, atmosphere quality and the exploring aspect of the game which were all VERY important to ender lillies and made it the masterpiece that it is. I dont really think better gameplay mechanics are going to be able to carry the game to the same heights as ender lillies if this goes on.
