_childDocuments_.review: In short:Early access part clearly outlines not just a worthy successor to Ender Lilies but a perfected and developed entity compared to the first part. Also it doesn't seem to require playing the first installment to understand the premise but still gives some intriguing snippets for those in the know.A longer overview:As much as I loved the first part (Ender Lilies) it still had a few rough edges and some inconsistencies. I expected them to be solved in Ender Magnolia hoping to see refined animations, gameplay mechanics and interactions as well as polished atmosphere conveyance (don't get me wrong: it wasn't bad in any way, but it still had some room to grow). I even replayed the original a few months before the early access release, which helped me define more specific changes that could be made.In my first 20 minutes I saw that Ender Magnolia addresses much more than my expectations (and I'm quite a nitpicky person, if my friends are to be believed). Apart from some obvious changes (like exemplary live animations and the primary aesthetic of world and UI) there are a lot of subtle changes help players in some smaller capacity (like an option to run and a more thorough tutorial with a slower pace). Simply put, early access went beyond my expectations in terms of refinement  of old and addition of new mechanics. And it was just the second day of early access, not a full version or even a big update later. Gotta give respect where it's due - developers have put a lot of their personal effort and time to make something they love and cherish, otherwise the content wouldn't be so thoroughly polished and thought out. Honestly, seeing this example of dedication and result warms my heart in our dark times when many studios are being laid off, some just after successful releases. I hope devs can keep doing what they love and wish them to get all the support that they will need ^_^

_childDocuments_.review: Another beautiful, desolate, wistful world from Binary Haze Interactive.If you enjoyed ENDER LILIES, then this will be an obvious follow up. If you are a fan of Metroidvania games, you certainly can trust this will be a strong one. The current early access content can probably be cleared in about two and a half hours, but it's two and a half hours of precise combat, beautiful ambiance, and compelling, wistful story telling. While there's still a lot more before the game is finished, I'm confident in recommending this as it already has all the solid bones of ENDER LILIES, but tells a magicpunk story in a fully realized world. You don't need to play ENDER LILIES to understand this game, though there are some references that will make more sense with memories of the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ender Magnolia is looking to be a promising sequel to Ender Lilies, a game I deeply enjoyed my time with (and coincidentally completed the day before early access released). As of now I have fully completed all of the content currently available in the early access and am eagerly awaiting the full release. However, in the game's current state I cannot recommend it to anyone but the most dedicated of fans. The game is highly lacking in content (only being a few hours long) due to its early access state. I fully expect this to change upon full release, at which point I intend to update my review to reflect the state of the game. For anyone who is interested in this game, I would recommend trying Ender Lilies if you haven't already and waiting for Ender Magnolia's full release.At this point I would like to share my experience and feedback with some of the more notable aspects of the early access version of Ender Magnolia (which will be abbreviated from this point on as "EM").The combat in EM is very similar to its predecessor, with some notable improvements. The general controls of combat feel smoother, the absence of contact damage is greatly appreciated, and the homunculi feel much more balanced than the spirits were in Ender Lilies. Although there isn't much oppurtunity to experiment with the homunculi upgrading system, it also has the potential to be a significant improvement over Ender Lilies.Unfortunately EM's combat also suffers from similar flaws as Ender Lilies. The two I want to point out are a lack of visual clarity and attack telegraphing. Due to the many effects that occur on screen, both from enemies and summoned homunculi, it is frequently difficult to see enemy attacks and/or Lilac. This makes it difficult to avoid damage during intense fights where all of your homunculi are acting in quick succession. This is further compounded by some of the enemies having poorly telegraphed attacks. The best example of this in the current version of EM is during Garm's boss fight. Garm only has a few attacks, but most of them share a nearly identical animation (raising his stake into the air before slamming it into the ground). This makes it nearly impossible to tell which attack he is using, which makes evading the attack and then counterattacking is frustrating at times.Overall the combat is very enjoyable and I'm looking forward to the more challenging encounters in the full game. Some improvements to visual clarity and perhaps some additional telegraphing would just help with reducing potential frustration and make some fights feel a little more fair.Exploration might just be the single most important part of a metroidvania game. Unfortunately its difficult to provide much meaningful feedback here since many of the most important aspects of metroidvania exploration (such as shortcuts, secret areas, powerups, and backtracking) are limited due to the nature of early access. I can only stress the importance of these aspects and express my faith in the development team to fulfil them.As for movement, so far it feels very responsive and I like that we get some basic movement abilities (such as the dodge and dash) right near the beginning this time. I can only hope that there are more movement abilities spread across the full game to keep traversal interesting and always expanding.The story of EM is gearing up to be very similar to Ender Lilies, both in content and in structure. Specifically both games are set in a land in the midst of an apocalyptic collapse caused by some ancient magic hidden deep underground, featuring a young amnesiac girl who has the special power to summon allies to her aid, with bits and pieces of information scattered around the world in the form of cryptic messages and dialog. While I do think that is a good thing, I also hope there are some surprises to be revealed in the full game. The addition of NPCs and a quest-like system have a lot of potential, but once again the early access is just too short to say much more than that.These are just some miscellaneous points that I don't have much to say about, but would be remiss to not mention.All things considered I can't wait to see what the full release has in store.

_childDocuments_.review: I was ecstatic to learn that ENDER LILIES: Quietus of the Knights was getting a sequel.When I found out that it was out, I soon bought and beat what was available in the early access. Binary Haze Interactive did an outstanding job improving the animation quality of the in-game/cutscene animations. Instead of the still imagery of ENDER LILIES' cutscenes, ENDER MAGNOLIA's animations have seemingly come to life. The base mechanics are relatively the same, except for the swapping of spirit sets, which was removed entirely for the early access. Spirits, what are now known as Homunculi, have different skill paths that you can devote resources into to give them different weapons/effects, making for far more build potential.The music is about the same as the first game, which is fantastic. Your character "Lilac" has just awoken and doesn't seem to have much memory of her own past. Seeing as this game is a SEQUEL to ENDER LILIES, albeit by a few centuries (supposedly), I'm hopeful to find pieces of lore/story about the blight and the canon ending of what happened to Lily.COME JANUARY 22nd! I also think that highlighting collectables should only be done if it is lore related as it "steals" from the experience.With that said, the fast travel and minimap are amazing, the fact that you can see details is a huge improvement from Ender Lilies.Other improvements are the removal of contact damage, it honestly frustrated me a lot, especially in boss fights.The equipment system feels ok, still need to see what they do with it.Changing relic description from "slightly" "moderately" and "greatly" to numerical values feels bad, I know that the clarity is nice, but it made me nostalgic, as it remembered me of Dark Souls.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Ender Lilies you'll likely enjoy the follow up, even what's available so far / while it's in Early Access.  Much will feel very familiar early on, but that's not necessarily a bad thing.  And what is new in the first few areas/hours is promising - including new depth to the upgrades, equipment, and skills.  There's a lot of promise / potential here, and an enjoyable framework to build off - but is very short compared to the first game / others in the genre currently.  To be fair this also feels much more like a demo than an evolving / updating near-final Early Access version; so hopefully it's barely scratching the surface.  The story seems intriguing so far and like it'll be an interesting continuation of the world / lore from the first game, especially with references to priestesses and Blight already sneaking into the first few hours.  The people of this world don't seem to have learned anything from the downfall of Lands End, and like we're in for another appropriately bleak adventure through a collapsing world - this time surrounded by more magic and steampunk(ish) visuals and vibes, instead of the more medieval / gothic settings, enemies, etc.  I dig it so far, and look forward to seeing how this all ties together in the world and story.  In the end, I'd recommend Ender Magnolia to anyone who liked the original, though others just looking for a new metroidvania may want to play the first one and/or wait for this one's full release.  It's still a good time and the price point is likely to rise on full release - so it's worth picking up now too, especially if you expect to play the final release eventually.

_childDocuments_.review: Within my (almost) 3 hours of game-time in the game's current EA form - I have managed to 100% what is currently available. I can quite confidently say that I am wholeheartedly excited for the full release of this absolute gem! I loved the first game and comparing the two, there is so much improvement already clearly visible. To break down some of the changes that I can recall (and please forgive me if I miss any major ones - it has been a minute since I last played the first game);Ender Lilies:- Enemies have contact damage if you touch them- Most spirits on top of having CD's, had limited uses (or just in general had limited uses)- Movement felt a bit more stiff (An example of this would be Ariel attacks not having any movement attached to them)Magnolia:- Enemies have no contact damage (Unsure if they intend to keep this change, but it sure as hell has saved from so many times once I finally realized I wasn't taking any contact damage by running into enemies)- All of the Homunculi currently in the game have unlimited uses, although most have very short CD's. In fact, there are some you can just hold down the button and they will keep attacking (Afaik, only the one with the gun can do this) And chaining Humunculi is exceedingly easy and feels quite smooth in most cases. Although there is some cases where it can feel a bit clunky or unresponsive.- Movement feels better than it did in Ender Lilies, but that might just be personal opinion. A major improvement in my opinion though, is that (at least in the case of Nola) you actually move forward while swinging in the air. I believe some places are only reachable if you use this mechanic to your advantage which I think is quite clever.I believe all three of these points to be considerable improvements over the first game, at least in my opinion at least lol.I will say that I also beat both (In the case of Magnolia, what is currently available) games using Mouse and Keyboard. I honestly think both games play perfectly if you changes a few key-binds here and there. For example; I have the first two Humunculi set to LMB/RMB and the 3rd/4th set to 1 and 2 - heal is on R and I believe those are the only keybinds I had to change to feel quite comfortable.Comparing both games, there is (at least again, with what is currently available) a lot of overlap with attacks and enemy designs, but I don't really mind it. The attacks and movesets I feel that are familiar are different enough that it feels quite fresh. In some cases, their attacks are expanded upon and I quite enjoy the almost nostalgic feeling I get when fighting certain bosses because of it. In terms of similar designs, there are actually few in number, and the models themselves are distinct and unique enough that I don't mind it at all.The game itself is quite difficult, or at least I believe it would be to a brand new player. It is likely due to the fact that I played a lot of the first game, but I rarely ever died. I first-tried pretty much every boss except for Gram. I fought him last and he actually gave me a lot of problems and I died quite a few times. Which is funny, as I believe you should actually kill him as your 2nd boss. In-fact, the whole area (The Mines) gave me a lot of issues as I would die to the guys who throw dynamite, particularly in one area where there is about 6 - 7 of them in a very awkward to navigate section. But, I believe that is just a massive skill-issue on my part lol.Overall, however, I really enjoy the combat, it is in my opinion, a huge improvement over the first game! Despite it feeling a bit gated or unresponsive - you can use multiple Humunculi at the same time seamlessly which I just think is so nice. Instead of having two resources to upgrade your Humunculi, each one has 3 different weapons or abilities that they can have. You start with the first one free and get a special resource to unlock the others. There is some over-lap with these resources, but as far as I have seen in the EA version - there is only two that share the same resource to unlock. To continue on from each one having 3 different weapons, afaik, you can select two (or probably all three) weapons an put them on the same bar which I think is quite cool and could def be really useful later on when the game is fully released and we have the full repertoire of Humunculi and their assorted weapons to chose from. The sheer amount of build variety that I can already envision in the future has got me quite excited for it!There is a ton more, crafting...equipment...relics, etc. but in general all of these things feel cohesive, and like they genuinely help you get stronger. Hell, when I finished the current content I was only level 15 by the end. But then again, I'm very much a fan of brute forcing these kinds of games without relying too much on careful strategy. The Humunculi with the gun however, I believe is a bit too good. He makes the game pretty easy as you can out range nearly every attack in the game bar from a very select few. It does a considerable amount of both physical and posture damage which is just way too good considering the range and how fast it can fire. It's so good it can genuinely trivialize some bosses. I had to stop myself from using it too much when fighting bosses as it would just make them feel like a cake-walk haha.That aside, every area - piece of music, the environments, and backgrounds all blew me away! I loved all of that in the first game as well, but this sequel delivers it just as good if not even better in most cases. Although I will say the cut-scenes, specifically for memories, I found a bit jarring to watch, the text sometimes not lasting long enough for me to read all of it in a lot of cases. But it was not a huge deal for me at least, even if at times I found it to be a bit annoying.But to conclude, I would whole heartily recommend this game, assuming you do not mind the (relatively) small amount of content it currently offers. And to that effect just to re-iterate, I cleared all of the content in just under 3 hours, but you might be able to do it faster if you are simply better at the video game than I. But, if not now, then please do keep an eye for its full release as I genuinely believe that this is an amazing game, and has huge potential to be a truly incredible game once it is finally complete!

_childDocuments_.review: Starting up Ender Magnolia years after finishing its predecessor, I felt like I’d never left. The protagonist I took control of might have been different, as was the location of this new journey, but the general feel of the world – its grim yet beautiful melancholy – very much remained the same, making me feel right at home, especially with the soundtrack’s lovely piano tunes and soft vocal backing in certain areas.All in all, I’m very pleased with the Early Access state of the project: it’s most certainly the kind of game that immediately grabs your attention with its gorgeous world and atmosphere, all the while tweaking and polishing what worked in Lilies. The combat system – that is, using “spirits” as weapons that fight for you – is as enjoyable as its counterpart was in the original, and the option to upgrade Homunculus abilities in order to diversify your lineup and try new play styles adds ample amounts of variety to gameplay. So far, Ender Magnolia very much seems like a worthy successor to Lilies, and I can’t wait to see more.For more honest indie game reviews, check out our Curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: Current early access build will only take you roughly 2-3 hours to finish, but it's already a great start. If you've played Ender Lilies before, then everything in this game - from the atmosphere, combat, difficulty, exploration - will feel at home, with some changes and QoL fixes compared to the previous game.A QoL I can't stress enough present in this game is the map is finally actually useful. Unlike Ender Lilies where the map is a bunch of boxes with lines connected to them to indicate you can go to that room from this room, the map now shows the layout of the area itself, including doors that require some key component obtained from the main story, and collectibles are also marked on the map too once it's visible on your screen. This game also retains the "area completed" QoL feature from the previous game too.In terms of combat, this game moves away from the consumable abilities the previous game had. All abilities (at least in current build) now have unlimited uses, but still subject to cooldowns. This game also streamlines the combat abilities, where instead of having a normal, heavy, and hybrid main attack seperated into 3 characters, all of them are now in a single character. This also does mean you cannot have a normal and heavy main attack simultaneously in your build like the previous game, so rip hovering in the air for a longer time spamming main attacks.There seems to be a difficulty option button, perhaps suggesting there may be an easier mode, but currently it is not available for now, so keep this in mind if you plan to buy this game while it's still in early access.Overall, this game definitely lives up as a sequel to the previous game. Either you wait for the full release or grab it now, this one is going to be a full recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Ender Magnolia is one of the best-reviewed games in the history of Steam for a reason.Everything great about Ender Lilies has carried over to Ender Magnolia. The world is massive, interconnected, and given life by hauntingly beautiful artwork. The combat is fluid, with innumerable weapons and upgrades that enable multiple unique playstyles. The bosses feel like they were taken from a FromSoft game. The soundtrack is so good that I found myself consistently taking damage because I was too distracted by Mili to defend myself. And while I won’t spoil it here, the lore is perhaps the most thematically dense of any metroidvania in existence.Just as importantly, though: from a mechanical/UX perspective, I’ve never seen a game improve so much from the first entry in a series to the second. Binary Haze fixed literally everything that I didn’t like about Ender Lilies. The map system, previously an albatross, is now the best map system of any game I’ve ever played. Our player-character, Lilac, gets sprint and dash within 30 minutes, instead of laboring with Lily’s flailing roll for 5 hours. Contact damage is gone; ability use limits are gone; ability statistics are made visible; and the list goes on. And devs didn’t stop improving there. Thanks to the upgraded fast travel system, I spent zero seconds of my playthrough backtracking – previously inconceivable for a metroidvania. Thanks to the new fourth ability slot, I could design a combat style that felt truly my own (not to mention more deadly than was possible in the prequel). The abilities and runes felt decisively more useful than their Ender Lilies counterparts. And, unlike in the prequel, I don’t think I encountered a single reskinned enemy during my entire playthrough of Magnolia. Finally, rather than just remastering Ender Lilies, the devs made sure to infuse Ender Magnolia with its own, unique personality. In contrast to the prequel’s desolate setting of Land’s End, Magnolia’s Land of Fumes is teeming with life and activity. Lilac encounters myriad NPCs who each have plenty to say about the joys and horrors of their lived experiences. And those experiences, in turn, are profoundly inflected by the social, economic, and political structures of Magnolia, which have evolved substantially from their feudal counterparts in Ender Lilies.I can’t begin to describe how grateful I am to Binary Haze for the work they put into this project. Every single person who helped make this game should feel deeply proud of themselves. It still needs to stick the landing – which is not an easy task! – but Ender Magnolia has the potential to be a genre-defining art piece in a genre that contains Hollow Knight. No notes. Brava 😊

_childDocuments_.review: I've played everything available at time of posting and I have a lot to go over.-NO CONTACT DAMAGE (THANK YOU!)-The map is amazing, I love seeing where I am on a relative scale, this is perfect-Enemy health/break gauges are much more clear-Animations are cleaner and easier to understand-No limitations on skill usage other than cooldown-Background doors to enter are visually more distinct-Relic descriptions give percentages instead of being vague-Attacking on slopes changes the angle of your attack-The "game feel" is somehow even better than Ender Lilies-Overall it feels like a step up in all regards-When attacking  immediately after a dash, the FIRST SLASH  should not move Lilac, or should move her much less. I've have many instances where I dash past an enemy, attack in the opposite direction, and now they're somehow behind me again because the slash moved me that far and the enemy gets a free hit-Having an ability on R1 is great, but not at the expense of losing the second set: I'll take 6 abilities even if it means swapping (Or have L2 swap abilities - a quick press to swap, hold to activate switches)-The dash feels like it doesn't go that far, it may be too late in development to change it because of puzzles and traversal, but I swear there seem to be attacks even from common enemies which are larger than the entire distance of the dash. Maybe increase ground dash distance but not aerial?-After dashing on the ground, there's this moment between the dash finishing and the run starting where Lilac almost pauses in place for a moment. Her animations don't transition smoothly either, this transition could do with some looking at-It feels like we're getting traversal/puzzle abilities quickly. If we have access to all of this from the start, it's going to remove the "oh, this ability lets me get to that one place 3 zones ago now!" moments. (Unless you have other such abilities planned, or this is just to showcase the demo)-When making the map full screen, a little more transparency to see the game behind it would be nice-Pausing and Unpausing are not the same button, for some reason. _childDocuments_.review: I only recommend it because the art and music, otherwise don't bother. Demo is waaaay too easy compare to the first one (honestly I am going to argue first one is also on the easier side compare to other souls-like metroidvania), in this demo the only difficult thing I've encountered is the mine area boss, but even then it wasn't that difficult like some of the bosses in other games (and the only reason it was difficult was literally because how much damage it does on the third phase, one rock hit 80% health gone). The rest of the game, literally no death. Mind you I am pretty average skilled so it's definitely not because I am really good at this. This game, compare to the first one, is too generous on almost every aspect, making the experience honestly a little boring. 1) Too many checkpoints. I am pretty sure I see a checkpoint most of the time before my heals even running out. And the checkpoints are too close to each other, if you have a bench every 3 minutes what's the point limiting the number of heals? And I can die without worry about anything, I am not losing my souls, I don't need to travel much, I can just die freely. Which might be a good thing for some, but this really kills the fun, I don't feel like the excitement or resource management pressure I had in the first game where I had to be cautious on my attacks, dodge etc. 2) Map showing you exactly where the collectibles are. So here is the thing, if I already know where the important stuff are on the map, why bother to kill all the enemies and explore the map? If I know the only collectible is on the upper left corner of this map, great, why do I need to kill everything else in the rest of the map? A lot of times I find myself check where stuff is, pick it up, and just want to skip the unnecessary enemies that's not on my path to the next area, I didn't because this is EA I want to test out everything so I did kill every single enemy, but I don't see myself doing this on official launch. Why bother killing them? What do I gain? I already have everything I need. And I am not sure why the devs wants to show the ENTIRE area layout before you explore. Like I said, if I already know the path to the next area judging by the layout, why would I kill anything that's not in my way?3) To make it even easier, enemies has a red flash before they going to attack. So you just press dodge when you see red it's pretty mind numbing, I don't really care what type of enemy, what's the difference? I just dodge when I see red.4) There is no contact damage. You can totally stand on an enemy without getting hurt. Combined with 3) where they literally tell you when an enemy is going to attack, I find it really hard to die even when they hit like a truck. 5) The abilities are given really early? Double jump is given to you like 5 mins into the game, without needing to beat anything. The fact that it's a separate skill but somehow you just get it makes me think it wasn't planned like this. It looks a lot like you are suppose to beat some boss or find it later in some area. I would rather get it later. I mean I still like the game, the art the music and all, but it's just straight way less fun compare to the first one. No exploration needed at all, no excitement since you don't worry about dying. I am also not saying you should make the game hard just for the sake of being "souls-like" or being difficult, but I think it does need some difficulty to make the game fun, to make not a walking simulator, and the first game does it well, not overly difficult, but also not a cake walk.

_childDocuments_.review: So my experience is limited to this game, and it is largely pleasant. The main thing that hits me about this game is the soundtrack and the animations / idle poses; I don't know, it's not often that a Metroidvania focuses so strongly on the fluidity of the animations and skills. It's usually simplistic and fluid, with a focus on the background or boss's spectacular effects. Not to mention the interconnected stories of each Homunculus and the universe as a whole. I don't usually care much about world building in these games, but it's quite intriguing that I can't help but want to meet more characters!The game includes leveling, unlockables, and particular upgrade options for each power you gain, all of which have their own unlockable weaponry, so there is a lot of variety here. It's not as if you're constantly going around with the same weapons and combo attacks; you may mix and match them whenever you like which is quite fun. So this is where my difficulties with the game arise. It's Early Access, which means it's not finished, so you'll see a lot of areas that aren't accessible right now. The bosses, for the most part, feel lackluster; they're generic so far for the first three, including their soundtracks, which all feel so docile and happy rather than tense and exciting. I'll put this down to the fact that it's being worked on, but that's really my only issue with this game is that it is Early Access. Unlike past Metroidvanias that I've played, which, although generally decent were all repetitive due to backtracking, getting lost, and not really connecting with anything in the world other than wanting to locate the next boss to go on and finish the game, this one has a lot of potential in that regard. You'll want to learn more, the game is relaxing in a not so challenging but not too casual visual splendour.

_childDocuments_.review: The early access is really great overall. I want to list out all the strength and weakness in the early access comparing to Ender Lilies. Strength:-Much better map: the map is a great improvement when comparing to Ender Lilies, and I don't think major changes are needed for the current map system in Ender Magnolia.-Animations: the bosses' and enemies' are so much easier to read and you can feel your attack actually making contacts when compare to Ender Lilies. Therefore, I don't think too much change is necessary for Ender Magnolia's overall animation.-Character/enemy varieties: there are so many varieties of enemies and NPCs, and I think having NPCs in Ender Magnolia is a great way to separate itself from Ender Lilies.No contact damage: this changes so much in engaging combat that playing in Ender Magnolia feels much more active than passive, and I hope the final game can retain that.-More diverse upgrade systems: the upgrade is so much more diverse in this game and it feels it adds more varieties to different kinds of builds/play styles. Cutscenes: the cutscenes feel much better and feel emotional than Ender Lilies. Also, I don't think voice acting is necessary for Ender Magnolia. _________________________________________________________________________________Weakness:-Enemies: the enemies feel a bit weaker when comparing to Ender Lilies. I am not sure is that due to having much more engaged stance system or Ender Magnolia's overall difficulty. Overall, I think regular enemies can be a bit stronger but not too much. Also, I think comparing the overall enemies' HP and difficulties in other metoidvania games can be some good comparisons to make. -Potential side quests and their varieties: if there are more side quests to be added in the final game. I hope there are more varieties for side quests. However, I think the side quests don't need to be as convoluted as those of fromsoftware's games, most notably side quests in Demon's Souls, Dark Souls trilogy, Bloodborne, Sekiro, or Elden Ring. _________________________________________________________________________________I also think the story and atmosphere in Ender Magnolia can improve if Ender Magnolia includes more story element or lore from Ender Lilies. Just make sure the story and lore from Ender Lilies does not confuse the new players and make sure the new players can still know what is going on even without playing Ender Lilies before. I think a good example to compare is the transition between original resident evil 1 and resident evil 2. Resident evil 2 followed the worldview and ideas from resident evil 1, but resident evil 2 and other games taking place in Raccoon City are their own things. On the other hand, not so good examples would be Yakuza Infinite Wealth and The Legend of Zelda Tears of the Kingdom. Both Infinite Wealth and Tears of the Kingdom can still be played without playing Yakuza: Like a Dragon or Zelda Breath of the Wild, but there are still some disconnected sections between the games feel confusing to new players._________________________________________________________________________________Overall, I think the early access looks very promising.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my very first Early Acess game and it ended way too early leaving me hungry and hooked for more :)Ender Lilies already was an atmospheric masterpiece.Spamming long range attacks like in Nier;Automata really takes the cake in Ender Magnolia.Gameplay is incredibly fun and versatile.You already get many different abilites in the beginning.I was VERY surprised to see how early you get double air jump in this game.I can think of no other metroidvania game that provides you with the ability to double jump in the first hour of playing (you cannot miss it). This is really noteworthy and incredible and I was like WTF.Because everyone wants to get double air jump as early as possible in a metroidvania - right? In Ender Lilies you could very easily miss a lot of amazing stuff (like upgrading the Knight) and I had to look up some things and even get some serious help with Ulv. I don't think this will be the case with Ender Magnolia. It's way more player-friendly.They improved on basically everything else like graphics and inventory/equipment depth.Fast travel also very well done.Discussion:Ori 1 is harder than Ori 2.Blasphemous 1 is harder than Blasphemous 2.Ender 1 seems harder than Ender 2.But maybe just because there was no difficulty mode to adjust in Early Access yet and - once again - because you already know the mechanics+patterns from the first game. So the second game seems easier.Would be interesting to see if someone played the second game first and then played the first game after that...Would he say the same about Ori, Blasphemous and Ender?! :)

_childDocuments_.review: So far, the design ethos of Ender Magnolias does not live up to its predecessor. The only improvements so far are its beautifully rendered artwork and slightly nimbler protagonist. And there's no contact damage in this game...that's good, but I also steamrolled through the first 3 areas. There isn't quite $20 of content here and might not be for at least another year. The final game needs to be about 7 or 8 times as long as the Early Access demo to match Ender Lilies.In most Metroidvanias (including Ender Lilies), most passages between regions are ability-gated. However, in this demo, we don't earn any abilities to get us through locked areas of the map. Instead, NPCs in the hub area actually hand us keys to locked areas after we defeat bosses. Why wouldn't the bosses be guarding the keys? That would at least be a little less disappointing. There ARE parts of the map that require new abilities to get through, but they aren't in the demo.Another indicator of poor pacing is that by the end of the demo (which is about 3 to 4 hours of content), (homunculi feature/skill spoilers follow)

_childDocuments_.review: from what i've played, as well as judging by other reviews i've read, it seems that the game as it currently exists is essentially a demo. i very much hope this means that the areas are going to get a full redesign at the actual release, because as it stands, it really feels like you're just walking through a linear corridor. in addition to that, the individual rooms feel rather soulless, as if they just kinda placed some enemies haphazardly and called it a day. in addition to that, whereas in the first game you really felt like you found something cool whenever you stumbled upon a secret, now they're just kinda strewn about in very easy to find locations.the above paragraph were things i think are going to get fixed after early access. what follows are things i think are significantly less likely to change. first, unlike ender lilies, there doesn't seem to be any attacks with limited use amounts in magnolia. i think this will be a positive change for the majority of players, myself included, but it's still a unique and bold design decision that was lost in favor of making a safer game, and i think that warrants mentioning. but there's one much, much bigger problem i need to talk about: why do you move so slowly? i even reinstalled ender lilies just to make sure, and yes, you move way slower ender magnolia. this has massive ripple effects on the entire feel of the game, by far the worst casualty of which are the bossfights. if you've played the first game, you'll remember that it had really good bossfights. the reason those fights felt so good was how smooth the game felt to play, letting the fights be very hectic. but because you move so slowly in magnolia, the bosses just end up feeling really clunky. maybe this get's better later on in the game from some upgrade, but i'm personally keeping my hopes low. when the whole game releases, provided it's at least as nonlinear as the first game, i'll probably change this review to positive.

_childDocuments_.review: -EARLY ACCESS REVIEW-One of the games that makes me wish steam had a middle ground review as opposed to "Yes/No" recommendations. I'm giving it a "Yes" as it is by no means a bad game but if I had a choice I'd give it a neutral "Meh"Cons:-Very Linear: As it stands the Early access as of this writing gives you roughly 3-4 hours of content to play through. This 3-4 hours of gameplay felt extremely linear, no real branching paths or sense of exploration. Go to area, clear out boss, get their ability and the key to the next linear area, never return to that area. Typically games of this genre I'd hope for some non-linear exploration of some kind. Hopefully whatever comes after early-access is less linear.-Slow and bland combat: Combat and movement feels very slow. Combat never felt engaging once to me during my time playing, slash your sword 3 times and move on, maybe mix in one of the over attacks you get as you progress but those sadly didn't make the combat any more fun for me. Your attacks, jumps, movement, and dodges all feel slow and overly weighty. We may be controlling a small girl but she sure moves like burly, large man. Made the already bland exploration feel like more of a chore than fun. Would love to see movement in general get a little speed boost.Story: What little bits of story we get after fighting a boss feels more like an after thought than an actual component meant to be engaging. Maybe it's just because it's early access but what is currently there is immediately forgettable.Pros:Art: This game has a very clear and well thought out art-direction. They've got their own flavor of dark-fantasy flowing through the art and the animations are fantastic. A lot of love went into designing an interesting looking and grim world.Music: The ambiance that the piano-laden tracks give is fantastic. It does a great job of selling the already great art by mixing in some meaningful and somber tracks.Stability: Runs fantastic on my machine and never saw any kind of performance issue. Great job on optimization.I'd say wait for Early-Access to end before picking this up. I may be an outlier in my feelings towards this game and perhaps I'm expecting too much but there's definitely a solid foundation here.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very good, has all of the strengths of the first game while improving upon its weaknesses. Even though its still early days, it's also apparent that exploration will be less tedious in the sequel, the maps provide more information and the player gets access to mobility skills much, much sooner than in the first game. Ender Lilies was a solid game, 7/10, but this one looks like it's going to be downright amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice Metroidvania, little bit more science-fiction like than the first one with a focus on machine, robots and a steam-punkish style and, as opposed to the first game, interaction with permanently existing npcs in hub-like city.Unlike the first one it has no real limitations on the use of companion 'spirits', which is one of the reasons the early access version feels a bit too easy in the normal levels. Often, you can stand out of reach of enemys and let your projectiles do the work. The bosses differ significantly, also like in the first one, ranging from easy to figure out to feeling frustratingly unfair with a weapon reaching nearly across the complete screen and being too fast to dodge most times.The gameplay feels really good in that inputs are not delayed, Lilac maneuvred exactly like intended during the whole playing time.That said, i'd recommend the game especially to beginners of the genre in the current version and hoping that it will be a bit more balanced in the final release.TL:DR- feels bit too easy in normal play through limitless helping spirits with no real cooldowns- one boss in particular being a total pain in the back, the others varying degree of satisfying fights- recommendable as a metroidvania with rpg elements and a steam-punk-like style

_childDocuments_.review: While you could argue it's too early to say if the game will end up being good in the end, considering you can only enter a handful of locations at the time and admittedly the couple last locations in the precedessor of this game sucked, it looks like the general theme of this game is "more of the same but better". The gameplay feels somewhat snappier, the animations are more fluid, the weapons are more fun to use, contact damage is gone and the enemy variety is very good. Even the soundtrack is relatively the same - boss themes suck (because for whatever reason Mili is fated to write exclusively slow piano songs for boss themes...) but everything else sounds marvelous. The whole "metroidvania in a fallen kingdom" schtick around which sadly Ender Lilies was centered, has been abandoned for a character that actually has something to say in a world with at least a handful of NPCs. All in all the early version looks incredibly promising and the game is shaping up to be one of the best metroidvanias on PC

_childDocuments_.review: Hmmmmmm, it def improved a lot of things over ender lilies. The game is kind of too short as it is for EA and there hasn't been much update since it was first released. Supposedly, the full game is being released in 4 months (Jan 2025) and there hasn't been any adjustment since Mar 2024 which is a bit concerning (so only one update since initial EA launch).While the combat is way better than the first game, it feels kind of clunky when switching between attacks. For example, let's say you're slashing the enemies and you want to switch into the fist or pistol attacks. You sort of have to wait half a second before the game recognizes the inputs. There's not a lot of backtracking which is kind of strange for this genre as well (hopefully they improve with GA). "i-frame" is a weird issue. I was fighting  the graveyard boss and it has an attack where it slams the ground and meteor balls come up. If you parry the initial attack, the follow-up attack instantly kills you and you literally haven't ended the parry animation by then. If you're in mid-air and you get hit, the enemy can still hit you as you fall which can suddenly end boss fights in a flash. I hope they can improve or add "i-frame".

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game with a lot of potential. The original Ender Lilies is one of my favorite games, but this game has the opportunity to outshine it by a long shot. It has better visuals, a more developed story, more complete gameplay, a more real world, and overall just a better experience.I will say, though, that this early access version is very overpriced for what you get. The entire thing is completable in less than an hour and there really isn't much to do. Unless you are a big fan of the first game like I am, just wait until it is released. There are a few things that worry me also. It's very easy. They say they will have difficulty options in the full release, which is good to hear, but a lot of the enemies have fairly predictable attack patterns which might not be fixable with a simple stat increase. There also aren't many secrets, each of the areas can be completed on the first visit with no need for backtracking. Maybe that is a plus for some people, but a big part of what makes metroidvanias rewarding is finally getting that one item you were missing to open up a bunch of secrets you weren't able to access before. I am really hoping that is changed before the final release.Overall while I am not so keen on this early access version, it makes me very excited for the eventual final product.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe I completed everything that the early access package had to offer. So far, I'm quite happy with what is available.I won't promise to have any sort of organization but here is some rough thoughts:- Music is amazing as always and game is even prettier than Ender Lillies imo.- Early game movement feels much better right off the bat since you get double jump/dash so early. Dash does feel a tad slow especially when I think about Ender Lillies movement, but the game itself feels like it's aiming to be slower with more accuracy. Though if things were faster paced, I wouldn't complain.- I do not claim to be an expert in game design, but I feel like you should be able to cancel attack animations with dash and jump. It just feels weird.- No collision damage makes for some interesting interactions but overall think it's a good thing since they seem to be designing around it.- There's an insane amount of UI QoL, even as simple as the map showing basic versions of what the area actually looks like instead of just boxes that represent the actual bounds of the area. I also really like the map becoming blue once all items have been obtained.- Points of interest being highlighted is nice but does make exploration a little too easy somehow? I probably would have looked something up if I got stuck anyway but still.- I like the spirits having different routes you could take. 50% of the spirits in Ender Lillies weren't useful and so I feel like I have a stylistic choice, which is nice. - I feel like I really like the visual representation with cutscenes, overall feel like there's more dialogue and I actually have an idea of what's going on without having to look to external sources. I literally had no idea what was going on in Ender Lillies until after I had killed the true ending final boss. The fact that I can look at the story and understand that there's points of interest and even an active role with attuners is nice. - I was relatively happy with the boss encounters, but a couple of them could use a bit more oomph. There were a couple that functionally only did a few mechanics and most resolved in the same way. I'm holding out criticism since it is the beginning of the game but even some early game bosses ♥♥♥♥♥♥ me up in Ender Lillies. I was quite happy when I had a couple bosses in Ender Lillies just have me dumbfounded for an hour until I realized which attacks were follow-ups and how to better read the tells. Overall, had quite a bit of fun. 8/10, obviously needs more content since the game is not complete but that's what we're here for. If more gets added, I'll update this review with continued thoughts.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is shaping up to be an improvement over the first one in every single way, positioning itself alongside some of the best Metroidvanias ever made!The combat feels familiar but they added different categories for abilities (some are cooldown based, there is a familiar you can summon and you don't need to worry about pressing the button again, some you can just hold the button and shoot projectiles). Another cool new feature is that all the Homunculi at this point on the early access can now be customized (I'll try not to spoil but just to give an example: you main attacker can change weapons, and others can be swapped between ranged or melee combat).There is also the removal of the limitation from the first game where some abilities had a set number of charges which makes me extremely happy!The story and the way that is told is similar to the first game (which I don't mind), but the setting being more modern and technological is enough to give the game a different mood when compared to Ender Lilies.The scenarios are still beautiful, the music is still top notch and characters and enemy design are some of the best out there.If you are a fan of Metroidvanias or just a 2D action platformer enjoyer this is a must buy!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the first things I noted when opening the game was that the movement feels much better. One of my few complaints with Ender Lilies was that moving around the world felt clunky, so I'm glad to see how this aspect has improved. The second thing I loved to see is that enemies no longer damage you just by occupying the same space. You actually have to be hit by an attack to take damage now. The early access version is very short as it is. You can see next to my profile that it took me 2.4 hours to see everything it has to offer. However, what has been done is quite good. The enemies are unique with the exception of a few basic enemy archetypes that are ripped straight from the previous game and I love the atmosphere which is enhanced by the soundtrack. I also love how there are other characters to interact with in the world as opposed to Ender Lilies where you were in a desolate kingdom with no one except your blighted spirits. Ender Magnolia has friendly NPCs and objectives/quests. It's nice that the sequel isn't just a re-skin of Ender Lilies.  Some criticisms I have are as follows. The map is too detailed. One of the things I love about metroidvanias is the exploration of an area and discovering things hidden away in cheeky corners or secret passageways. In Ender Magnolia, all the "secrets" or pickups are clearly marked on the map and the secret passages aren't discrete at all. Some other people have mentioned this as well, but all the boss fights are really easy. All things considered, it's a great demo for what we can expect in the full release and with a few tweaks, I think it can be even better than Ender Lilies.
_childDocuments_.name: ENDER MAGNOLIA: Bloom in the Mist

_childDocuments_.review: They just did it again.Ender Lilies for me was such a blast and Ender Magnolia is just as good as one of my favourite games of all time (Ender Lilies). Heck, there are small flaws in the animation, when you move with Lilac and the worldbuilding of Ender Magnolia isn't as sublime as it was in Ender Lilies, but at the end of the day, you have to remind yourself, that this is ONLY early access, meaning that the game will still get more content, will become better balanced, will become even better optimized. And that is so crazy to me, because in those 4 hours (to 100% the EA (even that room where you have to damage boost into it) I felt like I was playing a complete game. Once again the whole team did a pristine job in every aspect. The music was catching me once again by the heart, the artstyle left me hungry for more and it looks so good, the combat feels better with the Homunculi that you use compared to the spirits in Ender Lilies, while the movement of Lilac feels a bit sluggish at times and that is the ONLY aspect of those 4 hours that let me a little bit unsatisfied. I also very much like this idea of using spirits/Homunculi to defend yourself of danger, because by giving them their own stories, which still connect to the plot of the game, the player grows more accustomed to them, like they are fighting with you by your side and taking the burden with you, instead of just using plain weapons with no meaning, narrative or emotions. I applaud to this dedicated team and I know for certain, that by combining all those perfectly constructed aspects for this game, they will once again put out a damn good game and story in which everything just *clicks*, giving the player the perfect experience.Thank you very much for creating this sumblime experience of a short peek to a very good game that everyone will be happy to enjoy.P.S.: When I heard Mili's humming I just couldn't play anymore, it was so good that I had to stop playing for a bit and I just needed to hear to the soundtrack while I was wondering where the story goes next. There were many times where I just felt stunned by the visuals, music and story and the UI with the map was so polished up, that I can proudly say, that I have never once seen such a good map system in any game I have played prior to this.Thank you very much and I wish you a lovely day.

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid metroidvania enjoyer and ender lilies AND mili enjoyer i have to say this game is some absolute heat so far. Even as of right now the state of the game is a glorified demo at best, i still am looking forward to what binary haze is cooking. Besides a few hiccups and animation/jittering discrepancies, i have no issue with the game. BUT, something i do not like that i know some may disagree with me with is that in my opinion, the game is too light hearted. Like in the first ender lilies there were like no npcs to talk and converse with except the umbral knight and even then he didnt even talked that much. And when you woud purify blighted foes and gain their abilities, you didnt necessarily return them back to being human. We would only see a glimpse of their former will when they were alive or a slimmer of consciousness. We would see their whole backstory and understand why the characters are portrayed the way they were and come to an understanding of them. But in magnolia when homunculus are attuned, they basically get freed from whatever suffering they were in and its like a out of jail free card. There werent any consequences at all. And the way the story and plot is told is a little different as well. In the new one they kinda just tell you what to do and where to go. But in the og i feel like you were only told to save as many lives as you can knowing that most people were cooked and would basically find your own path at how to approach the game. I really enjoyed the solidarity of the world and how there were basically no sentient beings at all except lily and the knight. And most lore drops were way harder to find. In the new one they might as well be handed to you for free cause it is really not all that hard to find them. All in all i definitely liked the super vague story telling requiring the player to basically scavenge the entire map looking for documents and letting the player come to their own conclusions. magnolia like just dropped and even if the game does take a different method on its story telling im really not all that pressed cause either way i know binary haze finna cook regardless.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I just played Ender Lilies for the first time and 100% the game. I loved it so much and it was very refreshing. That being said, finding out there was a 2nd one released was a pleasant surprise. Even if it's limited due to early access.Playing through all the areas and bosses, I love the fact they took away contact damage. I also love the quality of life improvements like removing limited skill usage as it got me to play with the abilities more. Even if they decide to put a limit on skills again, it would not be bad.Music is still beautiful and sad with a hint of hope. The visuals are striking as I could stare at the background for a while and the character designs are still awesome. I took all sorts of screen shots in Ender Lilies. I imagine I'll do the same here when more gets revealed.I also love how the lore is slowly being woven in from the story of the first game. It's going to be interesting and a delight to see how things have progressed/came to be that the world is once again in ruin.I only have a few complaints, as I experience a few instances where there was a little input delay or the hit boxes were slightly off during one of the boss fights. (Could also be me just being human and messing up too, so that's up in the air.)I know many will not agree, but while it is nice to see the locations of secret items or notes, I actually don't like it. I want to be forced to explore the map and come back every time i learn a new ability. I don't like notes showing up on the map for you to just walk over and pick up. I think the mystery of seeing the area is not blue is enough to keep me searching till I am rewarded by finding it. What I might suggest is to perhaps allow us to mark the map as we go to remind ourselves to look back at locked walls and obstacles you know you can't currently access with your current skill set.Over all, beautiful and can't wait until more things are unlocked as the devs stuck to their guns and left the core mechanics alone, added quality of life improvements, and changed it up with the simple passage of time. Though holy hell that's quite a bit of technological advancement in a few decades vs what feels like centuries time difference.

_childDocuments_.review: Ender Magnolia is a sequel (and possible prequel?) to the 2021 game Ender Lilies, but it’s not necessary to be familiar with Ender Lilies to enjoy and appreciate what’s going on in Ender Magnolia. In fact, I’d say that Ender Magnolia is much more accessible to newcomers, at least based on what I’ve seen so far in the early access version. Meanwhile if you, like me, have done multiple playthroughs of Ender Lilies, Ender Magnolia still feels fresh and intriguing and worth checking out.Both the bosses and the minibosses are fun to fight, and Ender Magnolia seems to be quite balanced and linear in terms of challenge. According to the developer notes, the full version of the game will allow the player to customize the difficulty, but the standard setting worked for me. I still died a lot (affectionate) and was grateful for every character stat upgrade.Ender Magnolia is filled with NPCs who can be found in the central village and scattered across the map. The player can find scraps of text with background lore hidden in the environment, but there are also living people directly sharing their experiences. This world is in decline, but the player gets a sense that there’s still something to save. This game is also intensely atmospheric. There’s a beautiful city above, but you begin the game in the slums, which are filthy and decrepit. When the rusty browns of this aesthetic are interrupted, such as in an abandoned castle overgrown with brilliantly scarlet maple trees, it’s a sight to behold. I was motivated to overcome challenges simply so that I could see more of this ruined but beautiful world.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another indie metroidvania gem from the team behind ENDER LILIES: Quietus of the Knights!Following on from the success of their previous game, developers "Binary Haze" return with a familiar follow-up that so far feels distinct from its predecessor, but draws upon its best features. As expected, the art and design for the game is absolutely stunning, with detailed backgrounds, particle effects, and horrific (yet sometimes beautiful) character and enemy design. Combat still feels incredibly fluid, allowing the player to summon a variety of homunculi to aid you in combat. Where Ender Lilies included numerous summons to customise your combat style, Magnolia instead seems to opt for fewer summons but more detailed upgrades, with multiple abilities and weapons for each summon. Although still in early access, the combat feels incredibly polished, with several boss fights currently available for you to test your skills. Eager for more!And of course, it wouldn't be a follow-up to Ender Lilies without more gorgeous music from Mili. The few songs that are currently heard in the game are just as hauntingly beautiful as those you heard in the previous game. This is sure to be yet another incredible soundtrack!It's early days still for Ender Magnolia, but this is showing potential to be yet another brilliant metroidvania and a worthy successor to Quietus of the Knights.

_childDocuments_.review: A sequel to one of the most underrated Metroidvania titles ever made, Magnolia somehow manages to(thus far) outdo the first game in every way. Ender Lillies shined along side similar titles like the Ori series, Hollow Knight, and Deadcells - a feat that Magnolia is well on it's way to achieving. The gameplay is slower and more methodical, but still snappy and smooth, making combo attacks with your four chosen 'weapons' feel insanely gratifying. The combat can be difficult, but once you get the hang of each weapon and learn to combo your launchers with ranged attacks(most of which can be used independently of your melee abilities), you will look forward to every fight. I found myself resetting areas just to practice on trash mobs and having a blast.One of my favorite things about the first entry is that it was, in my opinion, one of the best games(tied only with Hallow Knight) for free-form platforming and Magnolia has already the same experience. You can perform trick jumps by combining double jumps, dashes and stalling attacks mid-air to reach places you might not have been meant to get to - and this is encouraged.  Try using  to gain height or get across gaps that look impossible to cross ;).Being an early access title, the available content is obviously short(I got through it in about 3 hours), so if you aren't itching to play until there is more to experience, I highly recommend adding this to your wishlist and keeping close track of the game's progress.Although Im sure no one will be reading it(lol), I will be adding a more comprehensive review of my experience thus far after another play through of the available content, as well as updating my thoughts as big updates come in.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so for context I 100% Ender Lilies and I completed as much of this game as possible before writing this review, I have a few criticisms but I wanna start with what I like about the game first.  Also just a heads up to anyone who reads this who hasn't completed Ender Lilies yet, there are some story spoilers in here so yeah.  First off, I really like how we can learn more about the Homunculi as we play through talking to them on while at rest spots, it makes them seem more like characters and less like tools, that is a big improvement over the blighted as the only context we really got for them was a few lines of dialog and a cut-scene (with the exception being The Knight of course.)I like the fact that the main character also talks, as we get to learn more about their personality as well, nothing wrong with LIly, but we get to learn more about Lilac that as simple yes or no cannot provide.The fact that each Homunculi gets their own different types of attacks is super cool, and I really like the equipment crafting system this game has as it adds more depth to what you can do with your "build" even if the options currently are quite limited.Now onto a few of my Criticisms:  Lilac doesn't show as much personality through her body language as Lily did, an example of this being their fighting animations, Lily's animations demonstrated that she herself could not fight, as most of her animations involved her covering her face, jumping back, ect.  Meanwhile Lilac's seem a lot more like the "stereotypical hero template" when it comes to her movement, things like the walking animation and the jumping animation don't show as much personality as they did with Lily, because Lilac's feel like they match half the other protagonists from other games, she also lacks facial expressions which I find strange considering one of our earlier interactions with an npc, and the fact that she found the doggo cute (valid by the way) but she just had a stone face on her model, it makes it feel like there is a disconnect from her actual personality and her body language.  The combat is cool however once I got bird man (forgot his name) I realized that a lot of the game was built around his range, which devolved into me just standing back and holding down his ability until the enemy's posture broke, in which case I ran up to them, attacked em a few times, then backed up and rinse and repeat.  The thing I liked a lot about Ender Lilies' combat is that it felt like I had to weave between the enemies attacks so I didn't take damage, and because of the limited usage on my abilities, it forced me to get up close and personal, it was challenging in a fun way;  and while yes I did feel this way with the bosses in Ender Magnolia, outside of the boss encounters the combat felt somewhat stale because half of it devolved into the above mentioned method.    Finally (and this is a story criticism so I won't dive too much into it as A: we haven't gotten too far into the game yet and B: I might have missed it) I'm very confused as to why the blight is back when Lily already sealed it, it kind of invalidates the efforts we went through in the first game and all of the hardship Lily went through, so I do hope to see an explanation in the future for why this is.  Overall I did enjoy this game, but I still enjoyed the first one more.  That however does not mean that Ender Magnolia is a bad game, it was a fun demo, I just worry that the few issues with it might effect the quality of the final product, which would really suck to see as I loved Ender Lilies and there is nothing I would want more than to love this game just as much.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so I have just finished playing through the entirety of what is currently on offer. I have played through the first plenty, and would consider myself a metroidvania connoisseur at this point. Let me do my best to summarize my feelings without being too lengthy.First off, aesthetically, gorgeous of course. Some animations lack a little polish, the one (1) other outfit you can get feels.... less than perfectly implemented, and the cutscenes feel jittery but assuming some improvement in full release, no notes. Same goes for sound design and music. Nothing I noticed worth mentioning.Story wise, the world is actually... alive. People in it and everything. A stark contrast from the first, and not frequently a direction I like, but that's just taste. I can't help but enjoy a depressing, melancholy-choked atmosphere. But, assuming I'm not the only one, I thought it worth mentioning.Gameplay is solid. If you liked the first, you'll probably like this one. A bit of QOL, a bit of streamlining the overall feel, I have no issues here. I will say that the mechanic of "every enemy you fight, you can get a friendly version" is not even close to present, which is a thing I really did like about the original, but its replaced by a mechanic that gives a lot more attention, in story and mechanically, to individual companions/summons/weapons (however you wanna view them), and it works for me just the same.Now my main issues so far are with world design, map, things of that nature. The map is *preposterously* detailed. Like, just a screenshot of the areas you're walking through detailed. I don't hate this, but it simplifies exploration dramatically, and asks minimal of you, the player, in terms of keeping track of where things are and how the map looks and feels to maneuver around. I am personally more a fan of a map that holds back, and doesn't give literally all the information, but I am also aware that's, once again, down to taste. Do with this info what you will.The other issue I had with exploration was just that everything felt very..... easy? Side paths had one little health upgrade and some resources, main directions were straightforward, overall, nothing felt risky, accidental, or overly rewarding as I went about anything. I felt remarkably in control of every direction I went, fully exploring 95% of rooms on the first walk through them. Now this could easily be chalked up to early access woes (especially when primary movement upgrades are just handed directly to you shortly after the tutorial), I am just a little bit worried this game will end up feeling a bit more hollow than the last. Too easy to be memorable for a continuation of an IP.I am still happy to recommend this game. I am more than comfy to give the devs some benefit of the doubt, and I had a ton of fun with what I played so far anyways. I am excited to see where this goes.

_childDocuments_.review: It warms my heart to know that the developer took previous comments from the first game into consideration. Thank you so much for that! It feels like a step up from the first part, so let's dive into it. Some points I'll be making are very subjective and some will be just nitpicking. Music and art style are top notch. I like the enemy design for each area and different attack patterns. I liked the shop system so far, relics and so on, glad they put enough resources this time. You can interact with the spirits and NPC, which was a nice addition. Combat system feels better. I kinda liked to have 2 sets, 6 abilities in total, but here you have only 4 and way more abilities to choose from. So you'll need to strategize more, I'd say. Which is definitely a neat way to make players engage more with various weapons and possibilities. No contact damage. I know that people complained about this a lot in the Lilies, but the problem there was that there were a loooot of enemies; with contact damage, it was mostly annoying than anything and felt unneccessary. Here in EM, however, I feel like the number of enemies also reduced, maybe they'll add up more. So, each level feels easy, I guess. It seems that there is a struggle to balance the difficulty. Bosses also have less health. I didn't die to any minibosses, I think. I managed to take down some bosses on the first try. Others took me up 5 attempts (my lack of attention lol). I can feel that the difficulty was tuned down significantly. Was it a good or a bad thing? Completely up to a player, I can see some people taking issue with it, others - not so much. What felt a bit odd was the amount of collectibles in every room. Even hidden areas were not so hidden. I spent 10 minutes banging walls looking for secrets lol only for them to be in the plain sight. You get double jump and dash really quickly, which made me a bit disappointed since the genre suggests a fair amount of backtracking and using new abilities to progress, I discovered everything on the available map. Again, maybe we'll get even more abilites or combos later. You will encounter 10 +- (mini)bosses here, each of them gives you a new ability or/and an upgrade. I've completely  unlocked variations of 4 weapons (12) and I have some additional spirits to that. It feels a bit overwhelming. I think they threw in most of it to test for bugs and general feedback. Maybe, in the full version things will be different, so it's too early to say.The only serious issue I have is the playtime. It's mostly 3 hours on avarage. If you are a skilled player it will take you 2 or even less. So, it feels like a demo, not an early access. A very packed 3 hours, given a rapid progression, the amount of collectibles and skills you get. They could have just removed half of the bosses and collectibles or even remove the whole Mines area, and it would be a very solid demo.  No bugs, but the game stopped responding to controls in the menu and crashed once. All in all, it was very nice to play the game. Can't wait for the updates and for the full version.

_childDocuments_.review: I find it hard to believe it's early access so far!The graphics are great, with a little more color added into it compared to the previous game. The story is looking good, with even some information found in early areas calling back to the events of the first game. Is it worth buying in its current state? Absolutely. The price for the game in early access is actually cheaper than it will be once finished. If you just want to buy it and leave it until it's finished, then at the very least you got it for a cheaper price, or if you want to play it and contribute your findings to help the game be completed faster, then that's great too! _childDocuments_.review: Ender Lillies was spectacular, which means Ender Magnolia has some big expectations to fill as its sequel. While this game is still in Early Access, what we have so far is promising:Combat is still curated and smooth as butter. Enemies are also varied and contribute to the atmosphere of each of the four areas currently accessible. Each playable summon (Stand? Persona? They're called homonculus I guess?) can use a variety of different moves so that weaponry and abilities can be changed while still keeping the same core of characters, which I am a big fan of and is also the biggest difference between this game and Ender Lillies. Each homonculus has their own present dialogue, including the main character Lilac, as opposed to the original game where Lily was a silent protagonist and most of the summons were just kind of there after you defeated them. This was fine in Ender Lillies since having a silent protagonist lent itself to the bleak atmosphere where everyone but her had already perished or succumbed to the Blight, but Ender Magnolia attempts a more character-driven plot which is evident in not only the dialogue but with the presence of communicative NPCs populating the world as well. The Land of Fumes feels more alive in general, although its on the brink of turning into a second Land's End. The use of a more vibrant palette also further differentiates Magnolia from Lillies, and my gawd some of the backdrops in this game are gorgeous. Mili also makes a return as the artist behind the BGMs, and they have killed it so far! I'm very excited for when the rest of the game comes out. That all being said, this game (at the time of this review) is in Early Access and is only 2-4 hours long. I can't really recommend the 20$ price tag unless you are someone like me who absolutely loved Ender Lillies (in which case it's an instant purchase). The full game will hopefully be finished sooner rather than later, but until then if you haven't played the OG Ender Lillies and are a fan of Metroidvanias I absolutely recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're wondering whether or not you should get early access at the current price, I'd say no. 3 hours of gameplay for this price is not justified if you're only in it for the gameplay alone. I personally got the game because I loved Ender Lilies so much and honestly just couldn't wait until the actual release of this game to see what it was all about lol.Regarding the story, there's still a lot more to be discovered, but we are just limited to a few areas at the current moment. The little notes that we can pick up to find out more about this world are very good though.The environment is spectacular just like in the previous game, with the music tracks being perfect for each area. However, I did feel like that certain areas were given a bit less character than some others, but I think that'll be remedied upon as development continues.Gameplay-wise, I felt like the combat was way smoother than Ender Lilies while at the same time being easier. Removing contact damage was definitely a good idea, but it made fighting enemies a lot easier than in Ender Lilies. You could honestly just stand inside an enemy and dodge when needed until they eventually die. I did die a few times to the bosses, but that was just because I didn't know their movesets at first. Maybe they'll become a bit more difficult as new updates come through (or I'll just increase the difficulty when the game releases).I think another thing that was great was the removal of numbered skill uses. I felt that it was a bit unnecessary to have in the previous game, but it did incentivize the player to switch over to their second skill set, which was removed in this game. Having these skills on cooldown really makes things easier and lets you keep combos going without worrying about running out of uses.Exploration was incredibly smooth, primarily because of the movement. It was really easy to 100% areas because the hidden items weren't particularly hard to access, with some just requiring you to head back a tiny bit later. However, I did not like how early you accessed abilities like the double-jump and enhanced dodge. I think it's just there to help players explore the game easily and test out the game, so it'll probably be given to you way later in the story in the actual release.Overall, fantastic game. Can't wait to see more. Not worth the money for the amount of playtime you get right now, but if you're like me and loved Ender Lilies + want to be a part of the development journey, definitely get it.
