_childDocuments_.review: After thoroughly enjoying Ender Lilies (see also my review on that if you're interested, great gane worth playing), I was quite hyped when I heard they were making a sequel. Though the early access is quite short as of yet (I think I got everything, and that took two hours), the experience is good.With the game unfinished, the story is unfinished as well. The story bits that are there however promise a story similar to the prequel in terms of setting and quality (which in my opinion is a good thing). The ambiance is amazing, with a similar vibe as the prequel as well.Unlike in Ender Lilies, there are actually living humans and homunculi to interact with, which makes the world feel a bit more alive (but just as miserable and dark).Ender Lilies is my favorite game soundtrack. Period. With what I have heard in the early access, that trend seems to continue with Ender Magnolia.This is the section where the game most deviates from its predecessor, using homunculi rather than spirits. Homunculi come in explicit, different categories: there are those that you summon and then ignore as they will "auto" target and attack enemies, those where you press the button for them to make one "attack" while further ignoring them, and those that you need to use "actively" (only one "active" homunculus can be used at a time, but "attack" homunculi can be used in tandem with them). There are no homunculi with limited ammo in the EA, which I appreciate, instead some of them have cooldowns and some have no cooldowns.In terms of impact on gameplay, Lilac (the protagonist) is a lot stronger than Lily. In general, attacks have significantly more reach and maneouverability durig combat is greatly increased in part due to there being an "active" homunculus that doesn't interfene with any non-dash movement. Mostly due to this maneouverability, bosses die quite a bit quicker and as a result the game thus far is easier (though I should remark that I have gotten better at these types of games and having played Ender Lilies doesn't make this game any more difficult either).In terms of feel on the other hand, throwing more attacks at enemies feels great, and the combat is extremely fluent. In all, I think this change a positive one (under the assumption late game will be a bit more difficult).Platforming is similar to the prequel, but you obtain double jump and dash at about the time you enter the second area. Curious to see if any new abilities will be added as well (while not in the EA, there is a button for hook, so that exists, as does swim).A shop system exists, thus far implemented quite well.Relics are back, serving a similar purpose.Mostly for the devs: while selecting a fast travel point using keyboard, you have to get quite close to the icon on the map before it snaps. Snapping it from a bit further would cut some time of trying to close in on the icon.Can't wait for this to be finished and play through the entire thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Ender Lilies was an excellent game, and Ender Magnolias is shaping up to be even better, with improved QoL and smoother movement. The map has much more detail than the first game, making navigation and collecting items that you missed easier. Movement options like double jumps and air dashes are very early in the game and there is a built in sprint to get around faster. All in all I really enjoyed the early access version.I have some feedback regarding the balancing and abilities:1. The "drill" which the bird boy has needs to be NERFED. This thing is way too strong. The posture damage is ridiculous, once I unlocked it I could essentially stand still holding the button down and let enemies come kill themselves on it2. Once you nerf the drill, nerf the default guns a bit as well, they are nearly as good at shredding posture and do so from a slightly further distance. IMO, These abilities should deal less posture damage and instead serve as a source of extra DPS, like the crow from the first game.3. Parry frames on the counter ability are too generous, but this isn't as big of a problem compared to the other abilities I mentioned.Overall feedback: The posture break mechanic feels more important in Magnolias than it did in Lilies, I felt that I deal comparatively little damage to the health bar, so it makes more sense to just shred the posture with the OP bird boy abilities since it's so safe and easy to do so, then DPS in bursts while they are down.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access Review:So far, there are massive improvements to the gameplay and exploration in comparison to Ender Lilies. You can choose to use advancing attacks rather than being forced to stand still and attack. This makes combat feel far more responsive and less floaty. Stagger can be abused a lot more with certain attacks, making it feel better to land staggers. Most importantly, contact damage is GONE! This was such an annoying feature in Ender Lilies, and I'm glad it's gone. In exploration, the room isn't entirely revealed when you enter it, and the map position marker tells you where you are in the room, rather than which room you are in on the map. Environments are prettier and the rooms feel more spacious.The one issue I have is that the music, which was a very big part of why I liked Ender Lilies so much, seems not as good. Maybe the mixing needs to be worked on, or rerecorded or something, but something about the music in Magnolia seems a little unfinished. If nothing is changed, that leaves me a little worried, as it is somewhat tiring to listen to whatever it is that is bugging me about the music. I have very high hopes for this game, and I hope we get the full release soon. SOON. SOON. SOON. SOON. PLEASE.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved Ender Lilies, learning about it's lore and the dark secrets of a kingdom brought to ruin by an unknown origin was very fun and thrilling, so I was naturally more than interested when I heard a sequel to that game was coming.I will go in depths to describe my 3 hours of gameplay to finish the early access to try and give you a review as polished as possible, so let's start.- The first thing we see about the game: It is pretty. The artstyle is still very similar to the one of ender lilies but with some improvements and great lightings, the environment and the artistic direction are beautiful. The animations are great too, though some are obviously not quite finished yet (it bugged me a bit to see Lilac glitch when turning 180 in a cutscene but it's bearable.) The one problem I noticed with the animations (which is very minor of course but still something that could be fixed) is during the beautiful cutscenes that happens to teach us about the lore, mostly coming after a boss fight, the text is small and leaves too fast for us to both learn about what the game wants to teach us, and enjoy the pretty visuals. It's a bit of a shame not to be able to watch it when the efforts put into it are this big.- Right after seeing the artstyle, we hear the music and I just have nothing much to say about it other than: it's Mili, they're super talented, they dropped yet another banger, I will get the soundtrack of the game the moment it's out, and the theme of that first town is beautiful enough to put me to sleep in seconds.- We then take control of our character, and the feel is somehow much better than in Ender Lilies, it feels much less clunky and more free, the attack animations of Nola aren't as heavy as the ones of the different blighted spirits of the prequel. Controlling Lilac and her homonculi is a pleasure.- Difficutly wise the game is fine-ish. I wish it offered a bit more challenge as some bosses have ways too much window for error and damage and I personally don't like to defeat a boss when I have made countless mistakes, I prefer to feel like I learned it's pattern to get this rewarding feeling.- The lore is very foggy and we don't know much about this world yet, but it still got me hooked on this whole universe and I HOPE that more links will be made with Ender Lilies, that's just a personnal need as I absolutely loved it, and seeing Ender Magnolia's story take roots on it would make me more than happy.If you are wondering if you should buy the game as of right now in Early Access? I'd say it depends. If you are a huge metroidvania fan and liked the prequel, go on, you'll have a blast. A short one, but a blast.Though if the game is finished? I can 100% lead you in. Parries can't block the rocks either, as after blocking the first one, any rocks that hit you during the animation will inflict damage. _childDocuments_.review: So I completed the game as far as allowed, while finding all items and upgrades on the map. Here is what I noticed, starting with the good things first:1. You can tell immediately that this is the sequel to Ender Lillies. It took everything EL did right and enhanced it in general, with some QoL changes as well.2. The design is very nice to look at. The character designs, areas and even the map have been refurbrished. Game looks beautiful to say the least. You can clearly see a lot of detail in the designs if you stop moving and look at the backrounds. Especially the backrounds for the boss rooms catch the eye immediately.3. It is more vibrant and alive than EL, there is other characters and the world feels less empty than in EL. Yes EL WANTED to have a world that felt like nobody was there, but I am glad this was changed. The interactions between characters at respites is a nice touch as well and adds life to the characters.4. The music is exactly on point. It really fits to each area and manages to enhance the overall experience. Really love the female vocals as well, you get immersed in the world, sort of what games like Nier Automata also did nicely. I also noticed the homage payed to one of the EL OSTs.5. The progression feels smooth and you do not really get stuck somewhere, something newer players will appreciate. More on this in a bit because smooth progression can go both ways.6. The fact you can still upgrade "spirits"(here homunculi) is nice, especially since each one has multiple forms to choose from. That gives the player more option as to how they wanna approach a specific boss or type of enemy.7. The mechanic allowing the player to swap between two separate sets of abilities was removed. Though this might initially sound like a bad thing, in EL it was not uncommon for players to accidentally swap during a boss fight and die due to it. Not having to worry about a mechanic that is supposed to be useful but could have you killed is a good thing overall.8. I will add a separate bullet here for the cutscenes. They look marvelous. Granted, the text could be a little slower, but it is all inside the boundaries of still being enjoyable to look at.Now, let us get to the "bad" things. Please keep in mind that the game is in early access and many things are due to change. Also none of those are world-ending things, there are games that are finished that still have those issues, so I will be very much hold back:1. In all honesty, at least so far, the game is absolutely and without a doubt WAY too easy. I sprinted through it in a little bit less than 2h(yes yes it is early access), but not only to the limited content so far. The fact enemies do not do contact damage in the sequel looks like a nice touch in the beginning, until you realize that you CAN easily skip whole areas without using a single ability due to dodging and double jumping. The game has so far never punished any of my mistakes that I deliberately made to test out if it would. But take this with a grain of salt since there will also be the ability to choose difficulties!1b. Some abilities are still outright broken. Braking the shield and staggering an enemy with one push of a button, even bosses, makes it non-interactive and a piece of cake. Also the scythe feels great to use due to the attack speed, but the dos also overall better than the sword due to the extra hit, so it removes any reason to upgrade that later(we do not know how all upgrades will be so I will add some benefit of the doubt here). So for future reference, please make sure to balance those out.1c. You end up being overleveled beyond reason by farming enemies that give good xp for how weak and squishy they are. This is also something EL did, difference is the big xp monsters were found in the late game content.2. You can literally farm currency very fast and buy out all of the items that are for purchase in the course of minutes. That is also something that not only encourages farming, but ends up having a character with far too many stats, thus manipulating the later game experience. This is something I actually liked in EL. Sure, you could farm XP but blight was limited to a fixed amount. This does not seem to be the case here. I went to the mines and had a field trip with farming, ended up not only overleveled but also rich in less than an hour.3. The progression is smooth and fast, which is nice, BUT it feels a bit TOO fast to be perfectly honest with you. I do not know how long the game is supposed to be, but if this was let's say 1/4 of it, then you are in for a maximum of 10 hours, faster if you do not really look for items.4. Speaking of items, I did not really have to look a lot to find things on the map. Some items are in plain sight and extremely easy to access, even for players with zero to none metroidvania experience. I am sure this will change though, still adding this for future reference.5. The bosses have a tendency to be those kind of big and immobile bosses. Takes a bit of interactions away but that is surely due to change with content still coming out. Hoping for somrthing that reminds me of Ulf from EL.6. The enemies. This is one of the things that sadly remained the same since EL. Areas are very limited to the enemies that inhabit it, which is logical yes, but if you are in one long room and you fight a horde of the same enemy,  it gets repetitive real fast. Variety is key and also something I missed in EL.7. Something else that sadly stayed in the game that artificially makes the game mechanics easy to abuse is the fact that after death, you keep "progress". By that I mean items you picked up, as well as levels and currency. This allows the player to basically not get punished for dying. The damage you take form enemies overall is not that small, but death is not punished, just like it was not in EL. You can run around and farm and if you are too lazy to use the respite warp mechanic, you just get yourself killed, re-spawning at a respite with a save point waiting for you right there.8. In EL you used to be able to teleport from respites to other ones. A very basic and useful metroidvania mechanic, there is absolutely nothing wrong about that. Problem: in Magnolia you can use this even outside of respites. I abused this multiple times when I felt like I wanted to teleport to the other site of the map. I did not have to seek out a respite, I just instantly warped. Yes, there is no meaning in having to run back an empty corridor to find refuge in order to teleport, but this mechanic also makes exploring less rewarding as a result. When I beat the shackled beast and found out I could not go further, I just instantly warped right next to the mines to continue there because I had figured that this is where I should be going next.To sum up, my overall experience was vastly positive. Keep in mind that I played tons of metroidvanias, so I am nitpicking at this point. What EL did well, EM does amazingly better. All good aspects of EL have been enhanced by a large margin and it is rather obvious that the developers actually listened to the community. But they might have listened a bit too much. My problem with the early access version is mainly that many mechanics that are indeed useful, result in making the game way too easy to actually enjoy it in the long run, so this is what actually has me worried right now. I am sure the difficcuIty will ramp up with more updates, but for now the game truly is extremely easy even for new players. I really want this game to succeed since I love EL very much. I see a huge amount of potential and an overall significant upgrade to the already amazing prequel. Please keep up the hard work, thank you for the sequel. I am really looking forward to the rest of the game. I will rate this early access version positively for now, with a huge recommendation to Metroidvania fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Promising so far, but as of writing - rather short. A handful of areas, several bosses and a decent variety of enemies so far. Decent level of challenge, a little more forgiving than, say, Blasphemous... Though one of the bosses gave me quite a bit of trouble, I'd somewhat neglected to check for upgrades before the fight; fast travel exists and is free to use from anywhere once unlocked, so that's really on me.Strong points: Beautiful scenery, art and animation; a gentle, bittersweet soundtrack to accompany the darkly beautiful setting. Gameplay is solid so far. Challenging enough if you move forward continuously, and if it gets too hard, you have the option of levelling up a bit by doing circuits around the areas, fighting regular enemies. Some ability to customize your fighting powers, which is nice and promising thus far; it does make a difference in how your attack patterns come out.Kudos in particular for allowing bosses to be affected by a freeze status stun, albeit it takes several freeze hits to inflict one; a nice, balanced way to make the classic "useless useful ability" (i.e. status effects that bosses are too often completely immune to, hence the 'useless' part) more useful again!Drawbacks: Currently quite short. Enemy death effects could use some polish. Some interactions (notably, when 'tuning' a defeated homunculus) feel like they need a sound to accompany them. Could be frustrating for someone not familiar with soulsy combat and progression in a 2D setting.Overall, recommended. The previous game, Ender Lilies, remains a wonderful work of art, and this looks to be shaping up to a worthy sequel. We'll have to see how it goes, but so far, so good!

_childDocuments_.review: So far, Ender Magnolia is a truly impressive sequel that iterates and builds on the success of its predecessor. The art and music are stunning, the story has me hooked, and a host of meaningful QoL features have been implemented.GREAT NEW FEATURES- Overhauled map that shows the shape and structure of each room- A new "sprint" mechanic that allows for quicker traversal- Options in the menu to hide gameplay UI- Extensive combat customizationIMPROVEMENT NEEDED- Homunculi cast direction is based on the START of the cast time instead of the END, which means it is very easy to accidentally cast them in the wrong direction.- Some cast inputs cancel each other out; for example, "encore" style homunculi will stop firing if you start casting another homunculi.- Boss cutscenes play every single time with no option to skip, which is pretty frustrating for bosses that take many tries.- So far, backtracking is virtually nonexistent; you can 100% complete nearly all of the current build with just the starting abilities.Super excited to see the game's progress during this Early Access period! I'm sure it will just keep getting better and better.

_childDocuments_.review: This is being written right smack dab at the launch of early access, so take some of what I say with the appropriate grains of salt. I imagine the game's performance might see a tune-up in the coming weeks or months, but it's unlikely there will be any massive changes to existing systems. I'll mostly be comparing this to Ender Lilies as well, which I am fresh off a completionist replay of.Right out the gate, the wonderful atmosphere of Ender Lilies is intact. The soundtrack so far has been as wonderful as its predecessor and I'm rather enjoying the extra electronic "oomph" (not a trained musician here) that's been added to compliment the more industrial setting. The backgrounds and environments are amazing as ever and I feel they are even more intricate than Ender Lilies already very impressive level of detail, though I can't quite put my finger on specifics. Character animations seem significantly more detailed as well. Liliac in particular seems to generally move and act with more purpose and frames of animation than Lily and the player's homunculi also seem more intricate in their actions. Comparing Yolvan's dual wielding of burst fire pistols to the somewhat similar Merchant or Eleine from the previous game feels like night and day to me. I'm also enjoying how much more (I hesitate to use the term) alive the land of fumes feels compare to Ender Lilies' world. Where the Umbral Knight in Ender Lilies was more or less the only character with dialogue for the entire game, here Lilac regularly interacts with her recruited homunculi and other people trying to get by. Your mileage may vary since some folks enjoy a solitary, lonely experience, but I think it's a nice change of pace.Actual gameplay follows in the footsteps of its predecessor, as one would likely expect from a sequel. The game is a Metroidvania with Soulslike influence. Combat behaves much the same way with a primary attack that largely halts player momentum for a multi-hit melee combo complimented by sub-attacks that behave independently of player movement. Interestingly, the limited uses of sub-attacks appears to have been removed entirely, though I have yet to see any far reaching difference that makes. Lilac is nowhere near as floaty as Lily. In Ender Lilies, aerial combos completely suspended Lily in midair, which in turn allowed the player to spend ridiculous amounts of combat time taking gravity as more of a suggestion than a law. In this game, aerial attacks give Lilac a bit of an upward boost to extend air time, but gravity continues to act upon her, reducing the player's ability to space out lengthy attack animations for maximum airtime.I could probably keep going on about all my other observations, but I figure I'll end this off with negatives in hopes it'll be seen by someone who can pass word along to the devs somehow. I've noticed frequent performance issues that were totally absent from Ender Lilies such as longer/highly irregular load times and lag. I'm not sure what triggers the load issues. Sometimes a room loads in about a second, sometimes that same room takes upwards of 6. Nowhere close to a dealbreaker for me, but it does strike me as odd. The lag is more of an issue and seems to be very consistently triggered by the crawling enemies that spew purple gas. Almost every time they attack, the animation lags the game for about a second while the gas appears.All in all, I'd say this is shaping up to be a very solid sequel to a game I really loved and I'm looking forward to more!

_childDocuments_.review:
Decades after the Rain of Death, a new journey begins in the Land of Fumes, where mystical powers lie beneath the earth. The kingdom's desire for conquest led to the creation of the Homunculi, machine-like artificial life forms prepared to execute the king's will. A recent resource-harvesting mission gone awry caused toxic vapors to emerge from underground, driving both man and machine to feral madness.

As the Homonculi devolve into dangerous creatures, guide Lilac - an "Attuner'' with the power to purify those infected by the fumes - on a quest to save the kingdom. With the help of friendly machines and spirits who fight in Lilac's stead, fend off mechanized legions of lunging carcasses, cannonball-firing corpses and chainsaw-wielding goblins terrorizing the land.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Ys (and Trails) for decades now, and it's easily one of my favorite JRPG series alongside Trails and Persona. It’s still surprising to me that Ys isn’t more popular in the West, but that’s a rant for another day. With Ys X, the series continues its tradition of smooth, fluid combat, a colorful cast, and epic, heart-pounding music. A heads-up, though: Chapter 1 is a bit of a slow burn, mainly serving as a tutorial. But once you unlock your full combat kit, the game really opens up.I’m a fan of the new Duo party system; it’s a refreshing shift from the old three-member setup. It feels like Falcom streamlined some of the previous complexities, keeping it distinctively Ys but giving it a fresh twist. On nightmare difficulty, the combat is tough without turning enemies into damage sponges, almost like an arcade-style souls-like, where dodging and blocking are emphasized differently from past games. The potion system is intriguing too. As you explore, you find bottles that you can fill with various potions, adding a bit of tension since your healing items are limited. Skills also return as Mana-driven attacks, and executing Duo skills is incredibly satisfying.So far, I’ve just finished Chapter 1, but I can see where this story is heading. The narrative feels like a blend of Ys VIII and IX, both of which had strong storylines. The focus on character dynamics, cast chemistry, and overarching mystery is still a staple. While there hasn’t been as much platforming as I’d like, I’m hoping that changes. The grapple from Ys IX makes a return and is used liberally in both combat and exploration. And as expected of Falcom, the soundtrack is top-tier. I recommend the Japanese voices over the English dub, which, unfortunately, doesn’t sound great. NIS’s localization has been a weak point in recent Ys games, and while it’s serviceable, the translations aren’t the most accurate.Even 2 hours into the game, I can give it a solid recommendation; especially after the ending of chapter 1 showed what Falcon really has in store for this game (I will update this review with my final thoughts once I've completed the game).  It also runs really well on the steam deck. If you’re hesitant to jump into Ys X because it’s the 10th entry, don’t worry. Each Ys game is self-contained, so you don’t need to have played the previous titles. Each story is presented as a chronicle written by Adol, our main character, years after the events, so the games don’t follow release order. Ys X, for example, follows Ys II chronologically and takes place before Ys: Memories of Celceta (Ys IV). Any references to earlier games are usually just Easter eggs. If you’re a fan of action RPGs looking for something fresh with surprises around every corner, jump into Ys with this one (or really any of the previous titles here on steam).
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Ed. note: I have added more notes in [UPDATE ...] notation after finishing my playthrough.I do not frequently buy games on day one at full price, but after playing the demo for _over 10 hours_ and given how excellent the past several Ys games have been (including the indomitable VIII), I figured Falcom has earned it. (Do note that demo saves carry over to the full release, so my total playtime is around 15 hours when writing this.)I will caution right now: in terms of gameplay, this is shaping up to be the weakest Ys game of the multiple-character-party era (i.e. out of Seven, Celceta, VIII, IX, X), and that alone warrants waiting for a sale before buying it.[UPDATE after finishing the game: While I don't necessarily regret playing through the game in its entirety, I do regret paying full price for it, purely because that feels like some sort of endorsement of the abysmal direction Falcom took the franchise with this entry.]=== The Good Parts ===The PC version runs great - even through Proton (which is how I'm playing it, in Debian).Graphical quality is easily on par with IX if not exceeding it. [UPDATE: With a big caveat: way too many areas look bland and samey.]There's TONS of work on dialogue (some voiced, some unvoiced [UPDATE: too much unvoiced, IMO]); that and the plot are presently the biggest motivators for me to continue playing. Both EN and JP voices are included.The OST seems promising so far; it seems to be getting stronger as I get further into the game. [UPDATE: There are some good tracks. It still pales in comparison to previous games. There are at most a couple of earworms in the entire OST. The most notable songs are primarily notable for emulating better songs in previous OSTs.]There's clearly still the exploration aspect of the past few games... but that's also a mixed bag which I have to drill into in The Bad Parts below.=== The Bad Parts ===Falcom clearly tried some new things with this game... and so far, they're all misses. Much of what I write about here is exhibited even in the demo, so try that first before buying if you're on the fence. (Again, demo saves carry over to the full game.)I could easily fathom this ending up having the longest playtime of any installment in the series. [UPDATE: I was correct.] Why is that under The Bad Parts? Because at the same time, it will also have the shortest playtime of any recent installment if you only count actual compelling gameplay that belongs in an Ys game. This game introduces way too much filler that feels like a slog.The ramp-up in this game is far more drawn out than other recent Ys games - which is probably a significant contributor to why the demo is so long. For example: side quests aren't introduced until 6+ hours in, whereas that concept is introduced much sooner in other recent Ys games.Seafaring is a boring slog. Your ship is also slow as molasses, and this is now how you complete the map, so congrats Falcom on turning map completion from something satisfying in previous games to something that feels like a chore in this one.[UPDATE: Another facet of map completion turns out to be dull searches for things that require a specific mana ability to find. This will involve backtracking to earlier areas once you obtain that ability if you want to 100%. I did not feel compelled to do this at all when I realized that's what was holding me back from 100%. I didn't even reach 90%.]You'd think seafaring might at least be a reasonable trade if it takes the place of the annoying wave-based combat arenas that nobody liked and yet Falcom made us suffer through in 2 games already. Well, bad news: they're making us suffer through those again a third time, and it's even more heavily phoned in this time - each wave warps in right in front of your face, with absolutely no effort made to make it seem at all believable.There are A LOT of invisible walls in this game, which seems especially egregious when you have an entire wide-open sea to explore (but there are instances elsewhere too). At least in VIII and IX there were usually at least slightly compelling reasons for these (e.g. needing more castaways to clear an impediment). More often than not, there aren't any compelling reasons in Ys X, it's just "but thou mustn't". [UPDATE: This gets particularly annoying when it ends up happening during plot-required sea battles. "Okay at least I have the entire gulf to maneuver within--oh hello magical blue barrier that wasn't here a minute ago." <followed by an enemy promptly also smacking right into it>]Battles also feel less satisfying. The rock/paper/scissors mechanic of slash/strike/pierce is gone. Instead, some heavier enemies have a break meter that _needs_ to be depleted before you can really do damage (and sometimes this needs to be repeated), and the break meter is susceptible to a separate stat BRK, alongside STR. I know this isn't the first game to try this sort of system; IMO it doesn't belong in an Ys game, as it makes fights feel way less dynamic and way more cyclic (see also: boring).Along with this is the new Duo system - which I am at least slightly amused by, because the default of binding it to the guard button feels like Falcom is calling me out specifically, as someone who always preferred evading over guarding. That being said, the Duo system makes me feel kind of disincentivized from ever bothering to use individual character skills during boss battles.There's also a new growth tree for stat bonuses that feels like it's trying to be Final Fantasy X or XIII, but it feels more like a waste of time rather than anything compelling. [UPDATE: There is also one aspect of the tree which the game never explains clearly, where lines don't grant bonuses under certain circumstances.]The first few acquired movement mechanics don't feel nearly as well-executed as in previous games. Mana String points can sometimes be easy to overlook, even when they're required (which the game seems to attempt to band-aid over by showing a prompt when literally anything stringable is in reach, even enemies). Mana Ride looks fun but is sometimes a nightmare to control [UPDATE: and often slows down to a crawl to the point where it's faster to just run unless you're going down a slope].[UPDATE about another problem with Mana String: the tutorial never explains that you can HOLD THE BUTTON to control or extend your swing. I got through half the game only ever tapping the button, and wondered why some jumps seemed to not really work and a couple of rooms were annoying as hell. Given that Mana String highly resembles an ability from Ys IX which only ever requires a tap, you'd think they'd want to be clear about this...]And whereas some movement mechanics sometimes added bits of metroidvania-esque backtracking in earlier games, Ys X hands out abilities practically before I know I'll need them. [UPDATE: The only big exception is the extremely dull searching-for-map-completion.][UPDATE: Level design was extremely bland for the most part, and only started getting at least a little interesting in the end-of-chapter maps during the back ~1/3 of the game.][UPDATE: Unfortunately, the plot also failed me in the end - it had nothing nearly as earth-shattering or grandiose as most of the other Ys games of the past 20 years, and the final plot twist was completely predictable.]=== Conclusion ===I can understand wanting to change the formula lest your games start feeling too samey for too long, but this seems like the sort of thing that would warrant external playtests on individual concepts to collect feedback before committing to so many bad ideas at once. It can still be enjoyable in spite of all this (depending on how patient you are for the parts that are a slog), but it's definitely a disappointing slide downhill from VIII and IX in terms of gameplay, and I can't really recommend it at full price relative to the high bar set by other recent Ys games.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this game a few minutes ago. This game is EXTREMELY fun to play through and has a great soundtrack. There is a lot of sailing, sidequests, and interesting character. Even the ship battles don't really get boring.If you want a great RPG to play through pick this one up. _childDocuments_.review: A magnificent game with a few flaws. The Naval traversal is not all that great. There are too many cutscenes. And I can imagine many people enjoying the combat of Ys 8 and 9 more than this. Nevertheless, it's an Ys game to the core, so the feeling of adventure is presented in all its greatness. And once you get used to the new style of combat, the flow is just the same as from those of the past. A brilliant game.

_childDocuments_.review: Im giving this a recommend because despite my many issues with it, its still a fantastic game thats way better than 90% of ARPGs out there. It's just, by Ys standards, Ys X is one of the weakest entries by far.The ship is neat on paper but in practice it takes so long to actually get anywhere that I find myself zoning out frequently. The ship combat is very basic and gets old pretty quick.The plot is pretty good. Nowhere near the heights of Ys VI, but its direction and characters keep me intrigued.Overall I'd give this an 8 out of 10, in a series thats mostly 9's and 10'sEdit: Redacting the bit about the controls as that was likely just a skill issue on my part, though my score doesnt really change as my biggest issue still has to do with how the ship traversal makes the world feel completely disconnected. A problem no other Ys game has.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't finished the game yet, But at about the 20 hour mark I can confidently say this is a great entry in the Ys series... Mostly. Nordics new main mechanic revolves around your ship. Ship fighting, sailing the ocean, upgrading your ship and crew. While the main gameplay loop is a lot of fun, personally I feel everything related to the ship is just terrible. It's sluggish, you sail like you're sailing through quicksand. I managed to eat dinner while going from point A to point B at one point. There's no reason why the ship needed to handle so poorly, or so positively slow.Despite this, everything else about the game feels fantastic. If you can tolerate that portion of the game, you're in for a great time. Pros:FishingGreat combo focused on tag teaming, but solo focus still viableMechanics that help boss fights feel like proper boss fights.FishingLots of characters with good personality.Lots of familiar returning completion and 'job' related chores for completion.Interesting build options.Music SLAPS.Fishing.And of course, Fishing.Cons:Ship fightsShip movementShip controlsShip everything really.way too many completion and 'crew building' chores.Some accessories offering insultingly awful 'buffs'.Hard to tell who has quests for you at times

_childDocuments_.review: Without having dived in so much. This game is awesome and I'm glad that the 10th instalment is finally here! Combat is surprisingly fun as I was bit scared of there only being two characters compared to previous entries. There a some cool dynamics with duo mode and the flow between single and duo makes up a lot of room to make variation to the combos. Port is flawless and just works straight out of the box running on a ryzen 1700 and rtx 2070 super on 3440x1440 resolution. Is this better than Ys 8 so far? Not exactly but it's a very awesome entry to one of my favourite franchises. Music is still a banger and story seems very appealing so far. I just get this nostalgic feeling playing through this games. If you are a Ys fan then this is definitively a worthy title to pick up and play.

_childDocuments_.review: Playtime: 47H/Diff: Hard Synopsis:Embark on a high seas adventure rich with action and exploration Experience the perils of Obelia Gulf through the eyes of Adol Christin and his unexpected ally, the pirate Karja Balta, as they help save the people of the gulf from the mysterious immortal monsters known as the Griegr.Plus:+back to more simple story line after many BIG adol adventures +the new Cross-system as the new gameplay after Party system+ revenge counter is broken AF+ Karja have a dynamic relationship with adol (and platonic too)+ sense of traversing seas with your own boat is fun + the mystery of normans and greigr is interesting+ Ys got new and cool cinematic cutscene+ gives us a lot more of lore and "foreshadowing" for the future adventures Minus:- the first time you got ship, the speed is very slow and sluggish until you got upgrade in mid-game - some mana gimmick activation is really janky- the "mana skateboard " cannot speed up in flat area, only on downhill or certain story spotMixed:= the latter part of story kinda rush and dull, but the final boss is epic = if you play after newest party system Ys, the cross system is like playing half speed of that= all your ship crew, only half of them is memorable enough include the main party that intertwined with the main story= The OST is good, but not memorable enough..= Weapon skin not change by upgrade weapon like previous game, instead by sidequest and story progressionNew adventure with new gameplay system for the next Ys game..by the timeline, Ys X is after Ys 1and2 but before Ys celceta..also we got the lore reason adol title adol the red and adol skill in modern game is flashy..quite interesting that 2 games in the row we introduce more norse side of myhtology after Ys 9..i hope Ys 5 remake is next tho..See on the next adol travelogue

_childDocuments_.review: It's very fun, it's a Y's gane. Probably the most fleshed out and polished one yet. Perfect on steam deck. _childDocuments_.review: I have been a die hard fan of the Ys series, but this game is quite frankly one of the worst.  It comes down to just the broken combat and boss battles.  Past games allowed you the freedom to bounce around dashing to do Flash Guards.  You would slow down time for a moment and could unleash attacks.  This would also replenish your SP so you could use more Skills.  Ys X guts that system for a clunky Duo system.  Gone are the Flash Guards and now the game forces you to use the Duo system for an insanely boring Block and Attack cycle.  Midway through these boss battles, they recharge their armor which turns them into a bullet sponge.  It simply makes the game unenjoyable.  I can only hope the developers go back to the amazingly fluid system they used to have.  If you enjoyed Lacrimosa of Dana and Monstrum Nox, you won't enjoy Nordics.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, very good port. Nothing really to say other than enjoy and play on hardest difficulty (becomes fun at 2nd or 3rd chapter). On that difficulty it kinda has those ER vibes, but with more arcade feeling. Multihit moves make it much easier because of damage reduction while you are doing them. Oh and perfect block is the king here, while dodge is barely used. And for the last and most useful tip: blue attacks are supposed to be run, not dodged (just run to any side to avoid them), they never mention it in the tutorial.

_childDocuments_.review: This game unfortunately falls short of what I'd expect from a typical Ys game. It is the true embodiment of the phrase "quantity over quality" because there are just so many new and unique mechanics being introduced in this game, and almost half of them are just there for show. To be perfectly honest, I prefer the simpler version of Ys games like they used to be in the past, with Ys VIII being Falcom's best-ever Ys game to date. I think that Falcom accidentally created a masterpiece with Ys VIII and couldn't replicate that same magic with any of their newer Ys games.I think this also boils down to the exploration aspect of Ys VIII which makes that game a magnum opus. For example, before we first arrive at the temple where Dana resided, we get to see a glimpse of the temple from afar, piquing the curiosity of most players as to what remains within the ruined temple. You don't get that same level of anticipation with Ys X. The only thing that could at the very least interest you in exploring the open sea is the islands scattered all around the ocean, which weren't even interesting or unique in the first place.Another aspect I don't really like about this game is the naval combat. It feels like a Temu version of Assassin's Creed Black Flag's naval combat. The controls are terrible and the enemy AI is just dumb. Despite the fast-paced naval combat, your attacks feel like they're impactless, and so does enemy attacks towards you. It doesn't feel as intense as you'd hoped it'd be. I don't want to compare this game to Assassin's Creed, but I can't help myself from making that comparison because of how terrible the naval combat is in this game, especially when it is among the focus/selling points of this game.I have to admit, controlling Adol and Karja is really fun, but the combat gets old really quickly. I think it's due to the bosses being less gimmicky compared to the previous Ys titles. The Ys series is known for its unique boss fights. Ys Origin was the first Ys game I played that got me into the series and it was among my favourite Ys games of all time simply because the bosses managed to surprise me with their sheer variations. In this game, even after reaching Chapter 5, there's barely any variation with the bosses. Most of them rely solely on parry and evasion mechanics. I guess you can say that Magna Diga is quite unique, but that was probably the worst boss in the entire game. And yeah, there are Quick Time events for certain bosses but even then the QTE is nothing special; it's terribly boring and forgettable so don't expect anything like Asura's Wrath level of QTE goodness.What's going on with Falcom these days? Why does the quality of their games keep deteriorating? I used to love their games during the Cold Steel/Ys VIII era but now it feels like they're running out of ideas. I believe part of the reason this happened is because they tried so hard to recreate the magic of their older games, but in doing so, they put themselves in a limbo of mediocrity. That's why their games never change, because they're too scared to innovate. They had to implement older mechanics in every single game they released in the past couple of years. In the end, the newer mechanics didn't get much of a focus, resulting in half-baked game mechanics like the naval warfare gameplay.Get it on sale instead, but definitely play the older games first before this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Ys X is Falcom's new prototype experimental game which forwards us into a new era of Ys X Gameplay Mechanics, it's just like how Ys Seven and Ark were the foundation to what we know today as, Ys Oath/Origin and Ys VIII and Ys IX, which perfected their own respective formula.I, for starters, have been a little skeptical at the current state of Falcom, who has been releasing quantity over quality with their Trails games recently, I was afraid that, with Ys IX, we'd be on to rough times for Ys games, and while Monstrum Nox wasn't necessarily a bad game, it had some issues here and there that played against it, rather than perfecting what Ys VIII granted us.Ys X Nordics gives us a new formula, and a taste of the greatest strengths of the Kuro's engine.Let's talk about the gameplay first.Ys X brings Sekiro to JRPG anime style game, with a bit of Ys speed to it, introducing a new block and counter mechanic that it's still a little rough around the edges and not as unforgiving as Sekiro, which would make for what I'd define as a Sekiro-lite power fantasy that Ys is known for. This guard mechanic is by far better than Flashguard, but still needs a little more polishing, such as guard stance breaking faster, it can totally break with tougher enemies and bosses, but you can pretty much bounce back any attack with little effort, and I would have liked if they make the time window a little more close.There's also an evasion techniques that comes to replace Flash Move, which also works well for the flow of combat.At the start, the game may feel a little slow, but that's merely due to the fact that you start with the bare minimum. Once the game let loose, it becomes just as fast as any Ys, and super satisfying too, specially as this time around, another of the core mechanics is a Solo/Duo mechanics, as our main duo takes the whole battlefield for each or both. Which makes up for a lot of great combinations and controlling the flow of combat for a display of epic powers and attacks that have the "Ys" Stamp on it because of how cool and flashy they are.The game also makes use of colored attacks, Red, for power attacks, which you block, and Blue, for fast attacks which you have to evade. Perfect Guard, and you'll see an epic flashy move, while raising another of this game's mechanics: The revenge counter, which will amplify your Duo Skills damage, take risks, and you'll be rewarded. As for the evasive measures, Evade a blue attack, and you're up for a counter attack, not as poweful as Duo Skills, and can sometimes trigger cool flashy moves that deals a lot of damage.The game hit jackpot with these colored attacks, and while it's far from perfect, I can see this becoming even more polished in a future Ys game, as Falcom perfects it's formula just like how they've done it before.We also have something other than ground combat, which is naval warfare!Same with the ground combat, it also starts slow, but as the game let's loose, there's a lot of new mechanics, including a lot of "Ys" Stamp Flashy busted ♥♥♥♥, that will make Sea warfare just as enjoyable as the ground combat, although I just wish it were a little faster, but hey!, if you were disappointed by how absurd Skull and Bones were, come join Adol and  Karja in it's pirate adventures into what would be a really compelling pirate sea warfare game.What can I say? I had a blast, the gameplay loop is really satisfying, and has a lot of things going on that keeps it from getting old, keeping the combat fresh with a lot of possibilities on the battlefield. The only thing I'd say that breaks the gameplay a little, is the fact that you receive less damage during skills, which is incredibly busted, Falcom must adjust this on higher difficulties to make it more balanced.Also, we needed far more dungeons, some islands were too short, and it would be great to have more challenging areas, but that's more of a nitpick, as I would have loved to play even more. But the game is not just gameplay, we've got other things too, like our cast of characters, which, honestly? they're a breath of fresh air, and Adol's duo, Karja, is a great co-protagonist and main heroine, among the best Ys has to offer, ruthless, and not as compassionate and lighthearted as Adol, but that gets a lot of spotlight and development that makes her among the finest heroines out there, puts the Boss in Girlboss. Her interactions with Adol is great, great chemistry and overall, makes up for some of the most expressive cutscenes in Falcom's history, which does a lot of wonders to Adol as a character, specially with a certain little something that happens at the epilogue, which would make any Ys Maniac lose their ♥♥♥♥ due to the implications.Steering aside from our great comrade in arms, we have a cast of side characters, all very lovable and with great side stories with them, and I specifically LOVE that the game went with the crew conversations, as it really adds a lot to them, as well as making them feel very alive, with their own aspirations, goals, and even reactions about the things that are happening, which makes up for a very lively cast of characters.And these crew conversations, I'd dare say they're just as good as Tales skits, I really hope that Falcom brings this back for future games, like Ys V Remake, or Ys 11, whichever happens first, having more character interactions outside of the main duo is something that many games often fail to do, and I'm glad Falcom returned to form with their excellent character writing for this game. As a story that is heavily driven by characters, their goals and motivations, Falcom nailed on this regard. Talking about the story, the story, while not as good as my beloved Ys VIII, is also a return to form for Falcom's fantastic writing that I've been longing for ever since Ys VIII  (and the good old Sky games) I enjoyed every bit of the story, because it just doesn't let go, with the exception of a certain few chapters that overstayed their welcome a bit with the side quests and other stuff, the story is full of relentless pain, despair, hope, and great scenes that really exhausts every bit of Kuro's engine to make really expressive cutscenes, epic attack montage of Coolness and what not. I'm really excited to see what the future of Ys holds for us, specially with the implications some of the key plot points this game delivered, as it makes it one of the most important Ys games out there. The only thing that left much to be desired, is the soundtrack. This is mostly an unpopular opinion, but Falcom glory days with great ost is but a sad husk of what it once was, and while it still has a bunch of great tracks, there are a lot of outsourced tracks that simply do not hold the quality of what Once Falcom stood for in the music department. There's still a little bit of hope, after the departure of Takahiro Unisuga, one of Falcom's best composers, Falcom got their hands on Shuntaro Koguchi, which seems to understand pretty well what the essence of Falcom games are in terms of music, and delivered a great amount of bangers. Here's hoping that Falcom treats their musicians better and we get to see more of Koguchi, as well as Jindo and Sonoda, instead of outsourcing their music as much as they've done it recently, which has increased to a ridiculous amount. All in all, Ys X is a glorious Return of one of my most beloved Action RPG franchises out there, and I'm glad to say that this was a great experience, excited about the future of the series.8.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Ys titles, this is a really strong one in the series!  If you've never played Ys before, that's OK cuz any of them are great jumping off points and this one in particular is an excellent one for that! It's a fun, snappy action RPG with a solid cast of characters that grows on you over its many hours, and pays off very well.My criticisms: it has a bit of a slow start IMO, and the balance between land adventuring, sea adventuring, and dialog sometimes skews a little too heavily towards one of the three for longer stretches than I'd prefer. Sailing around on the boat and sea combat is fun, and the characters are fun!  But there were a few occasions where I wanted the game to let me hack at things already. :DIt's also, as expected, not the nicest looking game in the world or anything, but it is an admirable effort for a game of its class, and to Falcom's credit probably the best production values for an Ys game to date.But yes, despite some critiques, I really loved this game!

_childDocuments_.review: (HEAVILY edited review from my first draft now that I've beaten the game with all achivements, but it's basically the same review with a bunch of stuff added in, so don't worry about the likes and stuff)Played through the Japanese version of Ys X on the PS5 when that came out and have just finished playing the English version on PC now, so I have quite a bit of experience with the game. With all achievements too (English only) (so yeah, I played through on Nightmare, but went back and did the superboss on Inferno also (which... isn't much different tbf)). Didn't really like it much on the first playthrough tbh, but having burned through the English version, gotta say I enjoyed it quite a bit! Not as much as Ys 8 or 9 mind you, but it's still good. Or, good after the final chapter 4 boss, at least... the early game is a really slow burn imo. A quick disclaimer btw but I actually did have to speedrun the game on Easy after my Nightmare playthrough due to missing 2 achievements (1 of which I know why). The Momina character notes seemed to be glitched for me and still are, so had to cheat that achievement sadly, since I couldn't be bothered after that (did everything as early as possible and spoke to her at every possible chance I had before anyone says anything). ANYWAYS, time to go over my thoughts on the game (I'll try to be as positive as I can): - GAMEPLAY: Gotta be honest, I hated the core duo system combat at first. Hated it for the whole of my Japanese playthrough (though I think a big reason for that is me not understanding the language, so I never really got how the combat worked properly), but actually came to enjoy it tbh. Well... again, come the end of chapter 4. Didn't really like the early game that much (mainly due to the lack of good STR and skills I guess). Actually like it quite a bit now. HOWEVER, I think it's still definitely my least favourite combat out of the main 4 in Ys (Bump, Napish, Party, Duo). Also, absolutely ♥♥♥♥ shield health bars to hell, it's awful game design. Didn't like it starting out and I still don't. You don't get any good break skills early game which makes it super annoying, and they're overdone to death late game (most notably the final and superboss bosses). Ship gameplay is AWFUL. Never liked ship gameplay much in Assassin's Creed, never mind here. I don't hate it, it's just a pure slog. Yes, your ship gets faster with the air currents and speed throughout the game, but it doesn't really help that much. Combat is also boring. Something you have to put up with though. If you're on PC like I was though, I suggest downloading a cheat table and using Cheat Engine if you want a faster ship, it actually works WONDERS! The (field) Mana abilities are pretty cool (in both a good and bad way, I guess)! Love the grappling hook (aside when you have to swing across certain bars where the hitboxes are awful). Crimson Line will always be cooler though. The Mana Vision is cool, but I hate that there's a bunch of new collectibles to get with it, kinda feels like padding for 100% and encourages backtracking (that's just me tho). The Mana Riding I thought was a sick idea at first, but when I quickly learned it's momentum based I quickly lost interest... you go SO slow half the time (like, even slower than normal running speed) and I found it annoying, though grinding rails is super cool with it! The time slow ability is really pointless imo since it's rarely ever used, and the waterfall climbing one should've been a thing from the start, since there aren't many places to use it anyway. Soooooooooo yeah. Exploration is nowhere near as good as Ys 8 or 9, mainly because of the linearity of things (again, just me), but it's still pretty decent. There's also a LOT of invisible barriers that just simply should not be there imo. Like half the time I wanted to jump over something or go under something for a shortcut or whatever, I just couldn't. It's actually stupid. And lastly a couple of nitpicks: Having to hold X to open chests instead of just press it can be annoying at times, although not that bad once you get used to it I guess. And movement speed in buildings is BAAD. Feels smooth with Cheat Engine modifiers but my GOD you move at a snails pace otherwise. - THE MANA SEED TREE Used to absolutely hate this in the Japanese version because I couldn't understand the language; thought it was overcomplicated. I understand how it works now and I still kinda hate it. To me it kinda feels like a lazy balancing excuse and they were kinda just like "just do it yourself lol". Cause I can guarantee if this was in 8 or 9 you'd probably be 1 or 2 shotting things even on Nightmare. Without it being in 10 you'd be doing baby damage on things. Just my take on it. - STORY AND CHARACTERS Not my favourite Ys story by any means, but the actually did kinda nail it, it's pretty damn good for what it is. There are certain moments that went HARD, and there are a few good cinematic moments such as the whale escape for example. As for the characters, I never really cared for any of them in my Japanese playthrough. Just based on designs I thought they were generic af. Upon playing the English version though, I love the majority of them! They all have their own cool distinct personalities and backstories. Also loved how even DR. FLAIR returns, pleasant surprise!! My favourite characters personally would probably be (any order) Rosa, Mirabel, Karja, and even Logr. Logr is a sick villain tbh and I'll die on this hill (Odr is alright too I guess, but not as much). Definitely feels like one I'd go for a drink with. The whole main group does feel kinda Ys 8 esque though, kinda feels like a big happy family on a big adventure or something and I love that. One thing irks me though, like a LOT... WHY ARE MAX AFFINITY EVENTS NOT VOICED IN THIS GAME (minus a line at the end)?? THEY WERE FULL VOICED IN 8 OR 9, IT JUST MAKES THEM LESS INTERESTING TO SIT THROUGH (though a few are pretty good tbf, just could've been better with voices). Please fix this for Ys 11. - OST Although not my favourite (probably not my least favourite either tbf), there's a lot of songs I love in this one. Lotta chill ones :)- OTHER STUFF Don't like how you can't toggle auto text outside of going into the options now. I like the QoL stuff with being able to skip more text and speed than usual. I missed the double jump in this game :( ...I like this game but I don't like how they pulled a new adventure after Ys 2 out of their a** and just slapped it on the timeline when there's absolutely ZERO references to it in future adventures whatsoever. I get that 9 felt really freaking climatic, but don't don't be afraid to do a sequel game. - FINAL WORD GOOD game but not GREAT imo. Definitely has some glaring issues, but still pretty fun nonetheless. Please though Falcom, FOR THE LOVE OF GOD, KEEP SHIP GAMEPLAY OUT OF YS 11 AND DON'T BRING BACK SHIELD HEALTH BARS AGAIN. Keep Duo combat by all means if you have to (I don't mind it), but personally would prefer to see how a solo Adol adventure plays out next time if possible, could be sick. If not though, bring the party system back but build upon Ys Seven's combat or something, cause the Flash system in that game was sick. Overall Ys X gets a 7/10 from me, possibly 7.5 if we're pushing it. Gonna leave this up as a negative review so it gets more attention though, as there are too many positive ones lol.

_childDocuments_.review: The best modern Ys action RPG yet.  Combat will take a bit to get use to and not as button smashy compare to previously. _childDocuments_.review: Ys X Nordics is the first entry in a while that goes back in the timeline, quite a bit actually, right after the events of Ys I and II, and it is really nice to see a very young Adol and Dogi finding new adventures in the lands of the Normans.As usual, the  of the PC version for this game is absolutely fantastic, being a port from PH3, and we have an extremely  game, packed with Settings.Coming back from their previous work with Trails Through Daybreak, we get Multisample Anti-Aliasing and the great Sparse Grid Supersampling Anti-Aliasing too.When both are combined, we get an extremely clean looking presentation, which really elevates the already pretty clean art by Falcom in this game, and the new Engine, of course.As far as performance numbers, on my , this game can be enjoyed at pretty good frame-rates at 1440p, 2x MSAA with SGSSAA and mostly Ultra Settings with a couple settings toned down (Shadow Resolution and Filtering) if you want, but not totally needed.The FPS at these settings tend to reach 120 quite often, only dropping a bit in intense cutscenes.Another option is to increase MSAA to 4x, and still be around 80-90 FPS, which is also pretty good like that, or we can lock the FPS to 60 FPS and forget about the FPS counter and just enjoy smooth gameplay all around, the whole game.At Default, console like settings, even 4K DLDSR is possible at 100 FPS or close to it.There’s plenty of room and scalability in the settings, both CPU and GPU scaling, to enjoy this game as best you see fit, because it is an excellent port.Moving on,  is also pretty smooth and responsive, as it couldn’t be any other way in an Ys game, and the new engine shows its muscle in the  department, both in regular gameplay, and particularly action .These cutscenes have an insane level of polish and animation never seen before in a Nihon Falcom game, only getting close are the latest entries in the Trails series, at least up to the one I’ve played.It is fantastically animated and, as usual in all Falcom games,  are actually quite expressive for this art style, which a strong point in their games, they manage to convey lots of different expressions and emotions via their very skilled animation on the characters’ faces, eyes, mouths, and bodies, even with the simpler graphics compared to other, bigger AAA productions.The  packs quite the punch too, ever since playing the Demo, weeks ago, some of the tracks have been stuck in my mind, and obviously now that I’ve completed the game, even more so. The OST does not disappoint, as expected, I always look forward to new Falcom games, particularly in their JRPG series, because of the soundtracks. (in English) is excellent, I recognize a few voices from other Falcom games, for sure, and some I don’t, and all of them did great.Our boy Adol has more lines than usual, haha, but he mostly remain the silent one we’re used him to be, don’t get your hopes up, but I was surprised hearing his voice more often than usual, it’s good and it fits the moments when we hear him.The   felt quite interesting and always making me want to keep exploring and adventuring and…yeah,  is what Ys does best, better than almost any  other JRPG franchise I know, that’s for sure.Having a Ship we can customize and improve and all the crew and stuff we can do on it…yeah that felt great, even if it’s not the first game that has done it, of course, it was nice to see Falcom’s take on the pirate ship shenanigans, instead of being on the other end and ending up stranded on some unknown island after a shipwreck :PAs for , it pretty much controls like most previous Ys games, with a couple new mechanics here and there, and the PC port has an , even for Menu Navigation, and this is great.I mostly played with my DualSense, but tried Mouse and Keyboard a few hours too, and it’s just naturally good, and easy to control, as we can quickly use skills without having to press a modifier.All in all, another excellent PC release from PH3 and NISA, I had a ton of fun with this new Ys game, explored every corner of the map, and it felt great.

_childDocuments_.review: The new combat is great, possibly the best combat system in the series. While it's definitely not perfect and still needs a lot of work (like the speed attacks, for example), it's a good evolution of the party system's combat. Additions like the skill chain, revenge gauge, and each character having their own SP bar felt like things that should've been there for years.Music is okay overall, kinda disappointing for an Ys game. There are some great tracks here and there, but half the soundtrack is taken up by mediocre music that gets really grating after a while of listening to it in-game. A far cry from Ys VIII where each track is a total banger.Characters were decent for the most part. Karja is okay, I felt like they tried a little too hard to make her likable to the point where she just comes off as too plain, if that makes any sense. I prefer having a bigger party where I can at least ignore the characters I don't like, but I don't really have that option here. Also because Adol is silent, Karja takes over most of the talking and it gets boring eventually, she's just not a fun character to listen to, especially for 40-60 hours. Grimson was cool and interesting, a couple of the Youth Brigade crew were nice too, my favorite being Grenn. Didn't care much for Rosalind, I think they fumbled her story and character, it felt way too rushed and she turned into a different character during that scene where she jumps to the ocean with Grenn and Cruz. You're saying she's meant to have a bit of mischievous, prankster side but for the rest of the game she acts like a cute waitress? Which character is she?The villains were nice, "Óðr" is perhaps one of the best Ys villains; his voice, actions, and boss fight make him steal the show whenever he's on screen.Speaking of characters, I think most of the character designs in this game were pretty bland compared to the last 2 Ys games and the recent Trails games. Again, I gotta criticize Karja; any girl from Daybreak (Agnes, Elaine, Shizuna, etc.) looks more appealing and better designed than Karja. Most of the NPCs look so...basic and boring, almost nothing about their designs is memorable or stands out. Not to say the game has any bad character designs necessarily, they're just serviceable at best.In terms of visuals, I was pretty disappointed. The character models, lighting, and animations are pretty good, but the environments (outside of a couple) are just so bland, and the game has a serious lack of variety when it comes to the environments, and this issue is even worse when you're out sailing. At times, the game can also look pretty damn ugly, which I guess is normal for an Ys game but still always something worth complaining about. Ys definitely needs better artists that could bring it to a similar level to Daybreak or the Sky remake. This is not really an issue of graphical fidelity, but art direction and environment art. Ys VIII somehow still remains the best looking game in the series.The PC port is incredible as expected, runs butter smooth and has a good amount of options. This is something I will never take for granted and will always praise and appreciate. The English localization is good too, and most of the English voice acting is well done. NISA did everything right with this release.This is a smaller thing, but this is the first Ys game to bring back proper towns since Celceta, and man are they bland. Besides the first town, none of them really stand out, they don't have any memorable NPCs, and you can't enter any of the buildings. I know this is more of a Trails thing, but I just thought it was worth mentioning. Good towns should be expected in any JRPG.The raids in this game have seen some kind of improvement. For one, you now have the option to skip them entirely, and now they kinda have level design since you go to the enemies instead of them coming to you. It's mostly just fancy hallways, but I guess it's better than nothing? Just stop bringing raids back.Some of the dungeons rely too much on hallways for my liking, and they all mostly look the same outside of a couple here and there. Overall they're still pretty good, but they don't reach the highs of Ys 8's dungeons. The final dungeon was especially disappointing, it's filled with reused enemies, it looks very bland, and it's very easy to traverse. There was one part I liked, but otherwise not much to write home about, which is odd cause Ys 9's final dungeon was great.The Mana abilities were cool, I didn't feel like I was missing the Monstrum gifts, but I do miss the double jump; movement just doesn't feel as good without it. The Mana hoverboard is easily the best one, it makes moving around fun and engaging sometimes. Mana string was fine, a bit too braindead and its range is too short when you want to use it for enemies. Mana sense sucks only because I hated spamming it over and over to get buried treasure, there was just too much. Mana burst is a cool way to bring back the charged attack, but again it's too braindead during exploration, "oh, vines? mana burst with adol" "a cliff I can't reach with a shallow pool of water? mana burst with karja" Not asking for Zelda level puzzles, but other applications for Mana burst outside of combat would've been cool.Also the lack of an Opening FMV is extremely disappointing. You're telling me Falcom can make an opening for Hajimari, Kuro 1, Kuro 2, and Kai (and likely Tokyo Xanadu K and Sky remake), but they couldn't spare one opening for 35th anniversary milestone Ys game? Piss off.But every issue in Ys X is minor in the face of this one: One of my favorite parts of Ys VIII is how satisfying and rewarding the exploration feels, and I'm sad to say that Ys X does not achieve this feeling most of the time squarely because of the sailing. What sailing does is that it forces Falcom to separate their maps into tiny chunks that are divided by the ocean, and then a lot of exploration is done through sailing which will really never be as interesting as exploring on foot. The ocean is empty and everything looks the same, and you're always railroaded to use the wind paths. And when you are exploring on foot, many of the islands are so tiny and end so quickly that I don't feel satisfied after I finish them, not to mention they are extremely linear with almost zero branching paths. The few moments in Ys X where exploration feels good (like that island with the fruits sidequest) show me that Falcom can still recreate the feeling of fun exploration if they try, so I hope for the next game they go back to world design that is more similar to Celceta and 8.What Falcom should've done for Ys X is to make lesser and bigger islands, that way they can feel satisfying to explore while also keeping the sailing - basically focus on the quality of the islands over the quantity of them. Think of how Kingdom Hearts handles the Gummi Ship and its various worlds. If it were up to me, each island would have several connected fields with branching pathways, caves, a dungeon, and maybe a town. But as it stands, the islands feel disconnected, hollow, and tiny, and there's nothing to tie together a larger narrative or experience like the Isle of Seiren.Overall, I'm actually pretty disappointed with Ys X. Making a game with good combat just isn't enough to make a great game, it has to excel in many more aspects. Lock in and stop bloating the games with unnecessary characters, systems, and mechanics. Hire people who can design appealing looking environments, attempt to make a connected world with branching pathways and rewarding exploration. Make more interesting and memorable characters that leave an impression, stop focusing on and amplifying aspects that don't make Ys fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Ys X: Nordics is yet another excellent entry in the series.The new combat system ditches the (in my opinion mostly annoying) Rock, Paper, Scissors affinity triangle of the Trio Team games and instead introduces a new attack stat: Break.Certain enemies are armored and need said armor to be broken before their HP can be reduced.The system is supported by having more freedom to build your characters. So you can focus one character on Break and the other on Attack or you can balance both out which plays into the games Skill Chain system, where consecutive uses of skills across both characters lowers their cost. All in all, while movement and dodging has been de-emphazised in favor of parrying, the combat system does not lack and of the series' staple speed or aggression. Story and characters are your usual Falcom fare. Well written side characters that all get their time in the limelight and a charming adventure story through this installments myths and lore.While it doesn't reinvent the wheel, the usual charm of the Ys series is alive and kickin'All in all, 50-60h of excellent adventuring fun!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a good time so far as a big Ys fan and I will for sure finish the game as it seems very close to Ys VIII which is my favourite of the bunch, there are however 3 things that I feel should've been addressed with a modern 2024 release.1.The outdated visuals and animations I can personally overlook as a fan but it can definitely be a turn-off for some people, the game has a great art style don't get me wrong but everything else looks like it's from 10+ years ago which has always been the case with Ys games. A new engine was a good time to finally go above and beyond but the end-result is an upscaled Ys VIII with better looking character models.2.The intro/tutorial before you get any freedom is 10 hours long, you have to do everything in these 10 hours in a very linear fashion before you can actually go adventuring, it does open up very nicely but man this is such a stopping point for people new to the series.3.The balancing is a bit off, this can be patched for sure but the boss Magna Diga was like I was playing on nightmare/inferno mode whilst playing on hard compared to anything else I had to face, it took such a long time before taking the boss down (I did not choose the weaken enemy option).So these issues aside, why would you play the Ys franchise if I got these critiques? The amazing music, the outstanding combat that always felt way ahead of anything on the market, the satisfying exploration, the characters that are well done and are all likeable to me (Karja is fantastic), the story I can't say too much about yet but these games have never let me down in terms of plot.The game also feels a bit more like the Tales of games to me compared to the previous entries which is a nice change!

_childDocuments_.review: Ys X: Nordics------------------------------------As a huge Ys fan, Ys X: Nordics totally hit the mark for me! This game brings back that classic Ys magic and makes it even better. The world of the Nordics feels fresh and exciting but keeps that fun, fast paced spirit that made me fall in love with the series in the first place. After Lacrimosa of Dana blew my mind and Monstrum Nox changed things up with some cool new mechanics, I was curious to see where Ys would go next and Nordics delivers big time.One of the best parts of Nordics is the combat. The new mechanics feel just right, blending in with that classic Ys action but letting you experiment with combined attacks. It’s a blast to figure out new combos and just go all in with Adol and Karja's moves! Speaking of Adol, I have to laugh this guy still can’t go anywhere without getting into massive trouble. But that’s exactly why we love him, right?There’s a small downside, though: the weapon variety isn’t there. You mostly stick with the same weapon throughout the game, you get new weapons, but they do not change visually. I was hoping for some more customization or cool weapon changes along the way, but it’s a small thing in the bigger picture.Ys X: Nordics still hits that sweet spot of adventure, joy, and non-stop action. The world feels alive, the combat feels fresh, and the whole experience is just a ton of fun. Every time I jump back in, I get that classic feeling of pure adventure that only Ys can give. It’s an epic journey and a must-play for any fan of the series or anyone who just loves a good, fast-paced RPG!Enjoy the game !!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful game. A must for Action-JRPG fans. The game clumsily starts from a narrative sense (there's a lot of talking at the start of the game, as it rushes to develop the tapestry of its narrative). However, the emotional pay-off for completing the story is fantastic for fans of the genre (and of anime). These games don't give that impression at the start, but they effectively build a connection to the story and characters over the course of the game.The ship controls seem to be a bit janky but with practice (and upgrading the ship) they became entertaining enough. I liked the sense of "adventure" that using the ship provided (a long-running theme of the series). The existence of a "world map" (in the 1990's sense) was welcome.Part of the charm is in the general simplicity of the visuals and the scenario design. I remember when the PlayStation Portable was released, it felt like one of the best systems because it mixed the design sentiments of PlayStation 1 games with graphics that (at times) rivalled PS2. The best of both worlds (almost). The Ys games exist as some sort of alternate universe where (in some ways) the developers didn't leave that time period. For fans, that's most welcome actually. It almost feels like a time-capsule to a previous generation. And for us who lived through that gameplay generation, it provides a nostalgia as if it came from that time period (which believe it or not, was around 20 years ago now). For younger players, this might work if they can appreciate "a simpler time" both in a narrative, graphics and gameplay sense.It's not a perfect game by any means; but I'm very glad that it exists. I'm definitely looking forward to the next entry.
