_childDocuments_.review: I found it very fun from start to finish (it took me 64 hours to finish it with everything completed)After having played several YS, in terms of gameplay it seemed to me the best of all.I loved that they dared to experiment with this new form of duo combatIt makes you want to fight and fight, it's very addictiveThe mechanics of sailing ships are really great, to discover new lands, sink other ships, and among other thingsAs for the plot I really liked it, it's my second favorite after YS VIII Lacrimosa of DanaThe characters felt very well written, even the secondary onesThe decisions are useless as always but it's not a negative thing, it's a good excuse for a moment of comedy as in all YSThe music is amazing, as usual in Falcom gamesThe final battle is phenomenal, you should definitely experience itOverall I'm very happy with this game, I recommend it even if you haven't played another game in the series, since the story is totally independent of the other games

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I would say I did like this over Ys 9, found everything on a high level to be really fun.  The story was plenty engaging and the characters are overall pretty charming, wouldn't say it's my favorite cast for Ys titles, but no one was really bad. _childDocuments_.review: Updated Thoughts after fully finishing the game: One of the best YS game I've played, definitely standing up there with Lacrimosa of Dana and Origins. It takes a while for the story to truly start but when it does it's hard to put the controller down. That final fight was probably the best final boss in the series when it comes to the feels! Some amazing cutscenes and story, I love my time with this game. Can't recommend it enough. Everything's great so far! Game is running quite well (had like 1 stutter during the very first cinematic, smooth sailing since then). The game feels quite different from the other entries in the Ys series thanks to the gameplay now focusing only on two characters, Adol and Karja. It's a treat to play so far, constantly switching characters to extend combos, guarding and riposting with both at the same time, I can definitely see how this is going to become even better with more skills and options later on. I only did the sea combat tutorial but from what I could see it's a very competant system. It's a lot slower than on foot but also much more centered around positioning. Also you can ram other ships so that's fun!I quite enjoyed the new characters so far, especially Karja, I do hope we'll have an option to switch back to her original vicking outfit though as it looks amazing. Exploration is what you would expect from previous games, plenty of stuff to find, except this time you also have an entire sea to explore. All in all this is already shaping out to be another amazing entry in the series! Also this one takes place quite early in the Ys timeline and as always you don't have to play any previous games before playing this one, only stuff you'll miss is some fan service. Also seeing a younger version of Dogi again after the last two games feels so weird ahah.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok. Buy it on sale if you're not a fan or if you're on the fence.If this is the first Ys game you have played, you might not be as harsh as I am about to be.Combat is ok but not worth mastering. Combat is block heavy and dodging isn't really useful anymore. The game is self-contradictory with how it wants you to play it. You can dish out attacks quickly but there's no animation canceling so you will have to slow down to not accidentally lock yourself into death. Enemies can have shield bars that will restore themselves which incentivize trying to do damage as fast as possible when it's down. Combat also doesn't feel good because the controls aren't tight enough to work for the combat. There's some input lag where guard doesn't activate even if you are in a neutral state so damage is unavoidable sometimes at no fault of your own. Locking on doesn’t feel good either because of how attack aiming works. Attack correction is turned off by default so you have to manually aim your skill attacks. This can lead to wiffing ranged attacks because you have no way to actually aim. You have the option to turn on attack correction but that leads to another problem where all of your attacks will change your orientation towards your target. Locking on is annoying and sticks you to your target too much and it's hard to tell when you are locked on or not.In general, it’s best to not take the combat seriously and play Nordics more as a Zelda than the Dark Souls they were aping.Story is weak. Nordics takes a while to get started and there’s alot of bad story to sit through before you get to anything worthwhile. Throughout the game, Adol will occasionally be forced into a side story in the middle of a dungeon or fight in order to do something completely unrelated. These are random interruptions that disrupt the flow of the game. Character banter and dynamics are fun but the script and writing is kind of dumb.Exploration is weak. Dungeon and world design are kind of flat and boring.The ship gimmick is whatever. I don’t think it was worth trading better level design for sailing.The worst thing I have to say is that I constantly kept thinking Ys 8 and 9 did things better than Nordics. 8 had better world design, exploration, and story. 9 had better movement skills and characters. Fishing was more fun in 8. Older Ys games do things better too such as better combat in the napishtim engine games or better pacing in Ys 1. Honestly playing Nordics just made me wanna play the other games more and that’s just the worst feeling a new entry the series can give a person.

_childDocuments_.review: Ys X is obviously intended as a new entry point into the franchise and might succeed at that. It's also the most far removed from many of the series' old strengths, with some of the highest highs and lowest lows. On paper I resonate with the mission statement of the new combat system. By narrowing the focus from a customizable party to a single pair of characters that act as one, developers can add complexity and explore it more through enemy designs, demanding varied and interesting actions from the player.The problem is execution, namely the balance between accessibility and veteran players and how absurdly long it takes to get going by Ys standards. It's not uncommon for RPGs to have a "slow start" but the Ys franchise has never had it THIS bad. You were always able to choose an appropriate difficulty and start getting your ♥♥♥♥ kicked in by the 2nd or 3rd boss.The new system makes it incredibly easy to stay invulnerable unless enemies have complex attack patterns, which they don't until the latter half of the game. Yet the difficulty modes are still purely about stats, resulting in the early game combat being completely cheesable in the most boring way. It only becomes interesting to veterans in a "time attack" scenario where learning boss patterns increases your DPS.All that said, the game IS no doubt designed this way for the sake of welcoming new players to action games, and my issues did go away in the latter half and I especially enjoyed Time Attack. I just hope future entries can revise their early game approach. is extremely slow at first and teased a potential bullet hell aspect that it never delivered on. If they are going to include a secondary main gameplay style like this, I'd like a bit more depth and mechanical exploration.Any  is bound to feel underwhelming after it was the primary focus in Ys IX, but the level design feels especially lacking here, with islands being simple corridors and the Mana abilities not seeing much use. The most fun I had was in deliberately avoiding a certain ability to have an actual platforming challenge.The "release line"  is weird because at first it seems to reward exploration, but being thorough results in outpacing the level caps really quick, causing entire layers to be unlocked at once. I think this is another case where they need to find a better balance in a sequel.This is the shiniest Ys game to date, which will probably surprise newcomers since the world looks straight out of the PS2. The series is infamously low budget and they seemingly did not make drastic changes between the Switch version and others, meaning it's capped by the Nintendo Potato's performance.Still, when compared to the previous 3D entries, the characters look great and even early bosses have much more oomph. Battle visuals and sounds are great, there's a bit more variety in boss music, jank is still there but I don't think it's any worse than the others.The new system brings about a problem that wasn't there before: Because Adol is silent, he can't exactly have good chemistry with the second main character. All the weight of the plot that used to be distributed among the cast now falls on Karja, causing this to feel more like her game where Adol tags along for the ride. It doesn't help that his voice acting is so infrequent it ends up distracting whenever it happens.Besides that, Karja was a fun protagonist, the plot presented several hooks that kept me going and it culminated in an extremely satisfying note, both story and gameplay-wise.However, although Falcom's baseline writing is still strong and I prefer it to most other JRPGs, most of the supporting cast isn't anything special. They serve to pad out the game because of modern expectations that games need X hours of playtime and Y amount of writing. It's still less egregious than its contemporaries but very noticeable for conflicting with the straight-to-the-point nature of classic Ys.Taken on their own, none of the issues with combat, exploration or yapping are deal breakers, but they do combine to make for the slowest start in the Ys series, something that ought to affect veterans more than newcomers.I'm glad I stuck with it because I got to experience one of the hypest moments in the series, and I hold out hope that the next entries will fix some of the transitional problems as they have done before.

_childDocuments_.review: Didn’t expect this game to be the GOTY for me, but boy am I happy. The game traded 'NEXT-GEN' graphic to slick and crisp combat with crazy good movement and super satisfying exploration. Story is gripping with a lot of heart in it. It has all the system you have already seen in an rpg but with a twist and creative improvements.  There is so much to love in this game, so much creativity in every aspect. 10/10 I do not regret picking this up full price at all.

_childDocuments_.review: So after playing through the whole game I have to say I can still recommend the game.I had a great time with it and can recommend it to anybody who is already familiar and likes the Ys series aswell as classic action rpg lovers. The soundtrack was decent, graphics were alright but my favourite part of this game (and the whole series in all) is that it all feels like grand adventures you set out on. You start to like the characters and wish to spend more time with them. They arent amazingly well written, but they have some depth in them. I really like the fact that there was only one character that you are playing with other than Adol. Since they were able to focus more on her. Because of that she had good character development and a well written story. The story was also enjoyable and was fun to work through, it is really straight forward but had a couple of twists that were pretty good. The combat has some problems like the fact that only near the endgame you get individual skills for each of the characters you play as, that are actually really viable. So until then you will most likely only be using the "Dual Mode". Also I think the game was pretty easy, even on the hard difficulty. I would have liked it to be a bit harder, tho there are still 2 other difficulties I haven't tackled yet. So I won't say this is a negative since you can cater the game to your liking.All in all it was a really enjoyable experience. Is it an absolute masterpiece? No.But it is still really enjoyable and that is what counts for me. I am definitely looking forward to the next installment (if one is being made).
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: note: played this game in nightmare difficulty. This game was a good try by the falcom team. The setting is very nice and the environment reminded me of Ys 8 which is a step back in the right direction. The new boat mechanic was cool at first but became tedious towards the end because of how repetitive it was. The combat was a surprising change of pace of the usual YS combat. It focused more on blocking rather than dodging. I do enjoy falcom trying to switch up the combat and not keep it stale throughout the series. This instance was a bit of a miss for me. I do appreciate the combat about how much more skill expression there is but I just can't get over the fact that everything (enemies and even most of the skills the karja and adol uses) moves so slow. Making the enemies so slow makes the game way too easy once you get the parry mechanic on point (it doesn't take long to master) you are basically unkillable. Its like I'm fighting in a matrix movie but not in a good way. I'm not saying the combat is bad just not for me. The control set up on controller was weird at first but you get used to it after a couple of hours fighting. As for the story, It was pretty tame for a YS series, especially after what we got from YS 9(that twist iykyk). Karja and Adols chemistry is very nice to see on screen, the rest of the other cast on the hand are painfully boring. Couldn't care less about their own side stories and honestly i doubt the writers did cause most of their stories were pretty bland. Its a good thing the 80 percent of the story revolved around Karja and Adol. Exploration in this game still doesn't top what we had in YS 8 but it still is nice to do. All in all, game was fun and definitely recommend it, had very high ups that make the game worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I had a great time, as usual Ys has a nice game feel that it's not easily replicated.I quite liked the combat, it flows really well and all the elements work nicely together (aside from the Mana String ability, I haven't used it much). Reading online there seems to be a lot of misconceptions about the combat system: I have read about people staying almost exclusively in Duo mode, never switching characters, not being aware of the Skill Chain multiplier, not being aware the the hyper armor during a skill animation... If you play like that, the combat system won't work.The intended way to play is to switch between Adol and Karja to keep the skill chain multiplier up, guarding/parrying as needed to build up the revenge gauge, and then unleash a Duo attack to do tons of damage/break. The game should have done a better job at explaining all these systems. But once it clicks, it's really fun, weaving skills, parries and duo mode never got boring for me.In general the boss fights were great! Those small boss specific combat cutscenes were cool too. The final boss is one of the best in the series.When it comes to exploration, the sense of adventure is still there as usual. Personally, I liked the ship sections and found them relaxing: it's true that the ship is quite slow at the beginning, but as long as you use wind lines it's not as bad as it sounds.The story starts to get interesting towards the end, but objectively it needs too much time to do so. The game spends too much time dealing with the immediate Grieger threat instead of focusing on the underlying mystery. I think I started to like it around Chapter 6/7, so well into the game. And while the cast of supporting characters start small, at one point you have around 25 people on your ship... That was a bit too much.As I did basically everything, I always had the materials for upgrades and whatnot, no farming needed!In the end the game is well worth playing, even more so if you played and liked the previous Ys games.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Planning to make a more in-depth review once I finish the game but so far here's my thoughts as a long-time fan of the series who's played all of the mainline games to date (minus the old original Ys 1/2/3/4)Gameplay wise Ys X is the start of a new style for the series, although still somewhat similar to the party system from SEVEN onwards, and with this game at this moment I'd call it a sidegrade which takes a few steps forward, and a few steps back. I really like the idea of focusing on two playable characters and how the fight in a synchronized way, and for the most part Ys X achieves it pretty well, the duo system is something I'm still getting used to but aside from feeling a little clunky at times, it's pretty dang satisfying, the abilities now feel more meaningful than in the older games because now they have more properties beyond just damage and range, but so far it seems like for bosses the duo skills are just too overpowered to bother with the single ones. I personally really like what they did with the guarding system, in concept, at least. Now it's not about landing that one parry every now and then and spamming, but rather timing multiple attacks in time and finding good openings to take advantage of the revenge system, kind of like a very lite sekiro. However the biggest gripe I have with the combat so far is how easy it is to keep reviving the other character again and again, hopefully the bosses become more punishing when it comes to mindless revival spamming later on. I also appreciate how they seem to have dialed down when it comes to how much you can heal, healing in action games while pausing is one of my biggest pet peeves so it's nice to see you can't just stockpile on a TON of healing items and trivialize everything.Story wise I'm enjoying it as well, it kinda sucks that we're back to young adol once again just for the sake of "appealing to younger players" as I just wanna see how things play out later in the chronology, but regardless the story that's being told feels pretty exciting and with high personal stakes, and as always it's great to see the lore of the world being expanded bit by bit, Karja is a pretty nice deuteragonist for the story, too, so definitely not a bad company to have around talking for the bulk of the experience. That said, even for someone who loves to play this series for the stories as well as the gameplay, the start can be pretty rough considering it's an action JRPG. Prepare for a LOT of cutscenes and dialogue before you can have any degree of freedom or substantial gameplay.For now I recommend it and I doubt my opinion will change, exciting to see where this game goes next!

_childDocuments_.review: With 8 hours in the demo and 8 more in the complete game I can already give a review. Thought I will add more when I finish it.It's a good game, and I LOVE IT, but it has flaws. PROS:Better graphics, animations look so much better, the characters has so much life! Textures look smooth and good but not all. Pretty anime style game as always!One of the best girls of the series, Karja, a strong woman with not much sexualization . I love DANA SO MUCH, she is my fav, but It's true that I hate her outfit. Fun combat, but nothing out of extraordinary, it has some new mechanics that are cool, like the duo system, it needed a bit more work but it's not bad.Exploration tools and new and different mechanics to spice things up are always positive! Including the ship!Story: I like it's inspired by vikings, I still has to finish it to give a proper review on this part.Music: GOOD, not the best, but GOOD.--------------------Now...let me explain the flaws better:CONS:The combat is not as good as in Ys VIII or Ys IX. That's a shame, and the duo system doesn't add much apart from blocking attacks. Evading mechanics are a step back instead of better. Gameplay is fun, but it's not the best of the series. In graphics department: characters look awesome, but those mountains.... what the ♥♥♥♥, Falcom. Fix those mountains.Another flaw is the lack of different enemies or different enviroments. No matter where you go with your ship, all the grass is the same, the threes, lack of flowers or details to the land, not much of different colors from one island to another... The villages seems all the same to me. They don't play much with light and shadows. I hope they continue improving tho! ♥Adol loses a lot ot centric narrative to put Karja, which is good, I love Karja, but I would love that Karja wasn't giving orders and making overall the most decisions in the game. I would have liked a bit more of characterization of Adol, like he had in IX or even in XIII. Aside from that, I don't really understand why they didn't continue with party members, because it's like they tried a middle ground between Adol going alone but it's not...not like how it should be, when you have Dogi there and characters like Gunnar or Phyllia, who have very good designs and are just in the back all the time. It's a lost oportunity, and again I do LOVE Karja. But It feels like, when you have so many characters around you all the time in a ship where you go here and there...that they don't go with you as a party, it's still a bit sad. The mana excuse I don't buy, since Adol have the same powers as Karja, someone else could have gotten them. But oh, well. it's done.The ship: combat is fun and awful at the same time because you can't move it very well, and you usually crash with barriers all the time. They should have let you a bit more of FREE exploration, less barriers... less "we can't go there". If you make a game with a ship of your own and you are getting inspiration from Vikings, pls, give me a viking ship, let me do a bit more... :CMusic department: Good tracks, but you don't have BANGERS. Quite like in Ys IX. But I do like the exploration soundtracks, just... when we will have an OST like Ys VIII or Felghana, or Ys 1 and 2 again? I love this series music and I know they can do better. Also, they could have used some... other instruments to make tracks more in line with the era of the "vikings" not all the music, but some tracks, you know? A bit more of... a touch more viking? Just a tiny bit???Designs: Not the best but not bad, I like that Karja is not "sexualized" thought that viking outfit with that skin of her thighs showing for no reason is... cringe. Give her normal pants for god's sake. And the purple outfit doesn't fit her character at all and I don't like it, so I just play with her viking outfit which is the one that makes sense for her and it's prettier. Adol looks perfect, but I miss a bit of more armor like the "warrior" he is. He comes from Ys 1 and 2, with a legendary armor and legendary weapons with magic...and he has this..."normal" look again? meh xD It doesn't makes more sense when you play all the games and it doesn't follow very well the lore.MY PERSONAL SCORE:Overall without finishing the game: 7/10I will add more review once I finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of the best action RPGs ever made. Falcom rarely misses, and like this game shows, when Falcom hits, they hit big. Ys is the GOAT of the genre, and Ys X: Nordics in particular is an extremely good entry. It's probably 4th overall if I was going to rank the series, but the 4th best Ys game is still way above entire franchises like Kingdom Hearts or Mana. Smooth, fast paced combat, great action controls, good enemy variety, tons of varied content, and extremely well balanced difficulties all make this game top quality. If you don't like action RPGs and you haven't played Ys, the series (including this game) will change your mind.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was such a disappointment for me.There a bunch of little things that I was willing to put up with, but then the ending was SO mediocre. Nothing of consequence happens in this entire game. That was ultimately what poisoned me against the game.Dogi is wasted yet again. The soundtrack only has about 2-3 excellent tracks, but all they do is reference other better games. The combat is a step back from 9. I still enjoyed it for the most part, but it is definitely not as good as 8&9. I played on hard. There were too many bullet sponges, and the break shields were just so tedious. The movement mechanics are also a step back from 9. Mana string is so slow that it is pointless to use in combat. The hoverboard was fun sometimes but its handling was very bad in a lot of situations. Being stuck in mud was also needlessly time wasting. Let me hop on the hoverboard instead of making me waste 20 seconds mashing dodge to get out of the mud. Adol talks waaay too much. I liked him being a silent protagonist, but they're slowly trying to do away with it. Both Adol and Karja do the ****** Jrpg thing where they have to announce that they see a treasure chest, and constantly tell you to use your mana vision while you're already using it to pick up a buried treasure. I hate that **** so much. The game is so full of padded sidequests and worthless dialogue with characters that do not matter. There are so many contrivances and conveniences that it was impossible to take certain conversations seriously. The best sidequests in the game were optional islands with unique story content on them, most of the rest were a waste of time. They replace your party with a bunch of random losers on your crew, and try to make you care about them, but fail massively. I personally hate party members and wanted to see a return to solo Adol adventuring, but apparently that will never happen again. But if Adol has to have a party, I would much rather them feel more like 7, 8, and 9. I actually cared about them in those games.But again, it all comes back to the pointlessness of the story. I don't want to spoil it, but it was just so lame. There are certain things that Falcom does that makes me think they're shallowly ripping of Persona, but they don't understand why it actually works when Atlus does it. It also feels like they fall victim to genre tropes because everyone else is doing it, not because it's actually good.I wrote this immediately after beating the game. I may update this review later as my thoughts become more clear. But I am feeling like this might be my last YS game. Maybe it's just not for me anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: is a fun game with great combat and smooth gameplay, offering an exciting world to explore.+ Combat is fast, smooth, and fun with easy-to-use controls.+ Two playable characters that work well together.+ Bosses and enemies are varied, with a break-bar system that adds strategy.+ Many abilities to customize how you play.+ The Souls system is enjoyable and helps improve your character's stats.+ The boat system is fun with upgrades and new abilities.+ Side quests are different and rewarding.+ You can find extra companions that help with the boat and add new features.+ The large map is interesting and gets better as you progress.+ The fishing system is simple and gives great rewards.+ Do yourself a favour and play it with the Japanese voice acting.- The villains have weak motivations and lack depth.- There are too many unnecessary dialogues that can be overwhelming.- The higher difficulty only increases damage, but enemy AI doesn’t improve.*Rating from lowest to highest: C, B, A, S.

_childDocuments_.review: Ys X: Nordics is the latest adventure of Adol we get to experience, and one of the earliest adventures Adol experienced, and I must say I very much enjoyed every bit of this game MUCH more than I thought I would. As the credits rolled I was left with that mixed feeling of sadness and emptiness that one would get after experiencing a wonderful work of fiction, and I am glad I chose to pick up this game out of some of the "possible" banger games that have come out recently near the end of 2024.Getting my issues out of the way, personally my only issue with this game was the controls and only at the beginning. It took some getting used to both on the field and the ship, but after a little bit of adjustment, everything felt fluid to me (I even changed a few keybinds because I was so used to certain actions on the gamepad from other games). Everything else is all love from here!The Ys series never fails to provide me with satisfaction in terms of action combat and exploration, that's a given, and for Ys X, it only got better with each chapter. Music was on point as well, which is nothing new from Nihon Falcom in general. I really enjoyed the simplicity of the Cross Action system and I do like the more balanced approach of combat and narrative to drive the story and game. The seamless weaving between solo and duo mode and the feeling and impact behind each skill was absolutely fun to play with, especially as you gain access to later skills.What really made this a wonderful and satisfying ride though, was the dynamic between Adol and Karja. From unlikely comrades to having complete trust with each other on and off the field, their development and bond was one of the best things I enjoyed in this game, and quite refreshing given the sibling-like relationship. This also extends to the crew on the Sandras. Each character has their own character story and fair share of struggles throughout the game, though not as deep invested as Adol and Karja's. Adol and Karja's importance to the story and the themes it presented really gave the game a strong finale and conclusion to Adol's adventures on the Obelia Gulf. The post-game title screens really tugs at you further!"No matter how much time goes by, we'll still be Shield Brother and Shield Sister."It is Ys entries like this that make me wish sometimes that Adol wasn't a "silent" protagonist, as I tend to get really emotionally invested in some of the characters that Adol meets throughout his adventures, but regardless, Ys X: Nordics is a new favourite of mine and I wholeheartedly recommend this to series new comers to veterans alike.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Ys series and have played through all of the Ys games that are available on Steam up to this point. To make my point short, this one may be my new favorite. I definitely recommend this game. It has a slow start, but if that doesn't stop you from enjoying a game, then I think you'll be in for a wonderful time.The new battle system is really fun. Switching between both Adol and Karja on the fly depending on who is better for the situation (or who I feel more like playing as) never got old and combining their attacks in Duo mode always felt great. There is a large emphasis placed on parrying attacks from enemies, as it fills your revenge meter, which you can spend by using a duo skill and dealing multiple times the normal damage. It's kinda like Royal Guard from the Devil May Cry series, albeit it is definitely easier to pull off a perfect parry here than in DMC. The combat is fast and keeping up the onslaught on enemies while parrying and dodging at just the right moments is always a thrill. Several boss fights in this game gave me a rush I rarely feel in games, and I treasure that. Gosh I love this battle system!Outside of land traversal, you now have a ship to sail around in. It starts off pretty slow, but you can use the currents to get around at a decent rate, and as long as you prioritize getting some speed upgrades early, the ship will be moving at a good pace in no time. I found naval combat to be pretty fun, but I do think it is too easy for about 90% of the game. I really enjoyed some of the late-game optional ship fights, though, as they forced me to use all of the tools at my disposal (except for items).As for the characters, there are some real great ones here. I liked most of the cast quite a good chunk (shout-outs to Dr. Flair and Father Cuthbert). That being said, the star of the show here is definitely Karja. I grew to like Karja quite a lot, and her and Adol's relationship becomes very endearing and got me really invested in the story of the game.Finally, to talk about the story, I will keep it short as I don't like spoiling stories for people on principle: it has a slow start, but I ended up being much more invested than I expected to be. It got its hooks in me, and it ended up being quite strong.TLDR; Play Ys X. Play other Ys games, too, if you have time. I love this game. Highly recommend. (:P.S. Definitely my Steam Awards Game of the Year nominee!

_childDocuments_.review: I greatly enjoyed Nordics. I think the battle system is much better than in Napishtim and Seven (the first games with their respective battle styles). I think it will be subjective as to whether someone likes it more than 8 or 9, but I personally like the new direction over perfect guards and dodges being as insanely powerful as they were. Parrying is still very strong and encouraged, but it's not all-consuming overpowered. You're still incentivized to play fast and loose via chain attacks giving you a skill point cost reduction.Obviously it's got to be said that this PC port is one of the best ones out there in the entire industry, period, and deserves only the highest praise. I think this is PH3's best work yet, and that is saying something. It is the definitive way to play Ys X, and that's not just by nature of it being on PC, but because of all the additional features added. The only minor thing I thought was curious to be missing is that there was no map supersampling, unlike in the previous few titles.Music, I also gotta get out ahead and say it's another fantastic soundtrack. Some tracks like "To Be Free", "Through the North Wind", "Heat Hazard", "Young Swordsman in the Eyes", "Destined to Keep Running", "If I Could Go Back to Those Days", "And the Adventure Begins", and several others (I really gotta stop before I name 20 tracks) instantly got added to my all-time classics list. I will say that some songs like "Depths of Gray", "Deep Inside Where No Light Reaches", and "Shield Brothers" probably get heard a bit too much, and it would be nice if some of the lesser used ones could have seen some more time. But it's a minor complaint.The cross action system is a bit on the unique side, and it will take a few hours at least to internalize it, but once you do it's a pretty satisfying system that allows for player expression in ways the series simply wasn't capable of before. The flow I mostly settled on was using individual skills or basic attacks to start, parrying when the enemy attacks, and then using duo skills once the revenge gauge built up enough for how i felt in the moment. I think the 2 biggest weaknesses are 1) the aerial combat is basically nonexistent and doesn't feel great, and 2) while skill animations are playing out you get something like a 90% damage reduction.For #1, I understand aerial combat being low on the priority list when you are making a new combat system in a new engine, because aerial combat has never really been a focus of the series. I'm glad they focused on the main combat feel, which is what REALLY matters, but would like for aerial combat and jumping in general to feel better in the future games.For #2, I'm guessing they made it this way for ease of casuals, because some of the skill animations are pretty sick looking and lengthy. But I don't see how this choice persists in the long term, because you should be forced to commit to a skill and eat ♥♥♥♥ if you chose poorly. They need to just make the skill animations shorter, I guess. Either that or allow you to animation cancel out of them. (Possibly both?)The ship combat, I don't see as a major selling point of the game. It exists primarily for thematic cohesion of the setting and a way to explore in a different manner to previous Ys titles. That said, the ship combat was never unfun to me. It was perhaps a bit on the easy side, but I was never upset to take several battles here and there. I think they perhaps introduce it in the worst light possible, because you are on a derelict ship that is nigh-unseaworthy, so it is slow as molasses and controls like garbage. Makes a lot of sense from a role-playing perspective, but again not necessarily the best first impression. There are a TON of upgrades though, and by mid game you will be zooming around like crazy, without even worrying about sticking to the jet stream currents. (Also fast travel exists once you've been somewhere, so it's not like traveling is tedious.) If this combat doesn't click with you, then you are practically never forced to engage with it, and can avoid all the encounters out on the sea—so I can't forsee it being a slog. (It is a very good source of ship upgrade materials though.)I'd say the story of at least 70% of Ys games are basically just an excuse to go on adventure. I feel like people tend to have nostalgia glasses on a bit too much when it comes to that. Does this one punch above that? Absolutely. It's a very strong premise to begin with. After that it kinda steps back, to being events that propel the journey forward in order to get out of the way of the gameplay and exploration. But in the final 30% of the game it comes back out of the shadows with a twist that I certainly wasn't expecting and a strong conclusion to the themes and main-focused characters. I think the side characters weren't quite as strong as in the previous couple games, owing a lot to them not being in the party. Some of them definitely had some shocking turns of events to their arcs I wasn't expecting though. Karja is definitely in the top few characters of the entire series. Also, there is a ton of lore to the Obelia Gulf region explored that I found very cool and interesting.For perspective, I've been the kind of guy who would rather silent protagonists slip into being a thing of the past—especially when it comes to Zelda, Persona, Dragon Quest and those kind of games. But for some reason in spite of that, I've still been okay with Adol being mostly silent for some reason. Maybe it's the way they handle it. I will say I'm kinda getting to the point where I'd be alright with him being fully voiced. It's not like they don't have the voice actor right there. I do hope they eventually do this in the future, but I will say I was genuinely impressed with how well Adol's goofy personality gets across in the game, and was shocked at how well they handled the bond between Karja and Adol coming through despite this massive limitation. So more power to Falcom.One place where the game can be inconsistent is the visuals. On the one hand, the main character models and animation work is better than ever. On the other, we have low texture work, much less post-processing and lesser lighting than Trails through Daybreak, and some of the environments are a bit lacking—especially land geometry out in the distance. I understand that Falcom were developing for the Switch foremost and lack the resources to truly retool for higher fidelity on multiplatform while doing a simul-release, and this is the reason for this. It's mostly not something that gets in the way of things, but it is at least something worth noting.Overall, most of my true complaints end up being the result of the game being small budget, small dev team, and short dev cycle—and developed primarily for the Switch. I also think the game is a bit too easy, but realize I should have played the game on higher than Hard. The superboss on Hard while doing a no heal challenge—oh man, now that was the type of resplendent challenge I was looking for. So I see that it's not that they don't know how to make a challenge anymore; it's more like Mario or Kirby where the challenge is left to optional endgame stuff in order to keep the game accessible to little Timmy down the street (and especially in this case where they don't have the dev resources to fully rebalance the game on higher difficulty). I'm definitely looking forward to replaying the game later this month on Inferno difficulty, and I think that says a lot. I'm also looking forward to how Falcom builds on this battle system in future titles!

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, I would give it a mixed review if I could but I lean more to the negative side for this game.The game itself is very slow. The movement is probably one of the worst in a Ys game. It feels very slow to move around in the overworld. There's a lot of tools for movement but they never feel as good as Ys 9. The ship is slow, the story is slow. Another annoyance is when fishing the character's would say something blocking the option to fish. So you'll have to wait 10 seconds or so before you can fish. Exploration is bad, the biomes are almost all the same and the islands themselves are pretty small and doesn't really contain anything of note. Since the game is so focused on the story as well, it never feels like you have a chance to just run around and kills mobs and find cool places. The combat is fine, you'll get used to the duo system. Not really my type of combat but serviceable .  The story on the other hand is okay, for how focused the game is on story it's nothing special. I personally really disliked the crew members and the rest of the npcs.Ultimately it's still a Ys game so you'll probably have fun, but it's one of the lower ranked Ys game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: As always solid Ys game. It was refreshing to be able to roam and explore world after mostly sitting city as in Ys IX. Story wise  I wouldn't say it's best or epic in the series in that regard Ys VIII is still my favorite but neverless it's one of the best in the series. I really enjoyed change in party and fight system and also co-op ability although not without issues is nice to have to enjoy it with friend. Abiliti to roam world not only on foot but also fare seas on ship was nice addon, although it is simple and maybe in some way primitive manages to deliver portion of fun. Falcom Sound Team as always did remarkable job with music.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful improvement from Ys IX which I thought was a bit of a low point compared to YS VIII. This is a step back up, not quite up to the incredible YS VIII, but a nice bounce back. Enjoyed the new combat system nice shake up from past games. Karja is one of the best characters we've ever had in Ys. I also enjoyed the ship combat, exploration. Getting to recruit and find different villagers is a nice touch and get to know each one more. Overall it's a great game and another falcom banger.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended. Gameplay is really fun despite a few irritations and the story is very good too, though mainly during the 2nd half.Building the combo meter while also balancing playing defensively is a very fun gameplay loop that never got old. The parry is very satisfying to do as well as it feels very impactful. Late game skills are also very satisfying to pull off because of how ridiculous some of them are. Not really any complaints with the combat system, though it does get a bit of a cluster♥♥♥♥ when fighting multiple enemies spamming different attack types that need different evasive manoeuvres to deal with. Really solid combat system overall.Really enjoyed the story. Karja was the real protagonist and she was a really great character with solid development. The writing is nothing mind blowing but it is just a very enjoyable story to go through, with good music accompanying some of the more memorable scenes. Unfortunately the first half isn't paced very well but it does pick up later on.Main flaws with the game for me were lack of environmental variety and some control issues. Needing to stand still to do a lot of actions interrupted the pacing a lot and was very irritating, especially when you need to also hold the button down.One of the best games of 2024, probably my favourite JRPG this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: This game honestly delivered a very fun and consistent experience throughout didn't feel like at any moment things were dragging along, the pacing is good and the characters and writing are very solid and likable. I highly recommend it for anyone whose into arpgs with a solid foundation like this. Combat: 9/10Story: solid 9/10Soundtrack: 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: really really enjoyed the duo-lead idea. honestly i think this should be the new template moving forward. the larger playable cast games are still good but i think this solidifies having a main character (aside from adol) much more clearly and lends a lot more narrative weight to the situation. karja's a great character and i think will join dana as a new fan favorite.that easter egg though in the epilogue in the lighthouse...(all achievements, played hard and NG+ nightmare)
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Ys X is my new favorite Ys game, in my book, it's even better than VIII which was my favorite alongside Oath in Felghana. Combat-wise, switching off my boi Adol the Red to make my chain multiplier higher instead of sticking to a character who has a type advantage takes a little bit to get used to but once it clicks it's great. If I were to nitpick, I'd say the mana burst ability felt useless in combat, I know certain accessories made them a little more useful but It's still more of an exploration skill to me personally. Love the characters, especially Karja, love the music and last but not least, love the boss-specific cutscenes when we manage to properly guard their special attack.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: I get it that the combat might not be for everyone, But for me, definitely love the Duo system. Though i do wish the system punish you more if you make mistakes. The Duo system is too overpowered and broken making the game too easy even on Hard (I am never a fan of game being too hard. played most Ys game on hard since most of the time it gave me a reasonable amount of challenge). The overall scale of the game is a bit smaller compared to 8. So don't expect much. Overall, it is still a fun game for me and i thoroughly enjoy the game from beginning till the end. 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very solid Ys game. Ys VIII and IX both have some parts that are better, but this is still great. The new battle system is a nice evolution on the old party of 3 system, and I look forward to its improvement in the next game. However, the ship stuff is alright at best, and I hope it's a one and done. Adol's supposed to be shipwrecked anyway; this is just unnatural.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all Ys games and love them all, except this one. It just isn't much fun. The pacing is off, the combat is poor (the new duo system is boring and uninspired), the sailing and ship battles are boring, and the story is awful. If you're new to the Ys series, please start with a different one; any of them would be better than this one.

_childDocuments_.review: ...So it's not that I disliked the game.  It's that it's inferior to Lacrimosa, Monstrum Nox, Celceta, even SEVEN was better than this.  And SEVEN was terribad.It would have been better served as a standalone with just Karja, have Adol make a guest appearance, but not call it Ys.  The problem, I think, is that this game has an identity crisis.  It doesn't know what it wants to be, and it presents as though the other games in the sequence didn't exist.  It also pulled punches and didn't want to really take any risks.  By the time the credits rolled, it felt like there were no real "stakes" to anything and they just played things too safe.  Monstrum Nox had a similar issue with this and it may just be the decline of the series overall.Adol in this game doesn't feel like "Adol".  He feels like a second wheel.  As if his presence isn't really a strong contributor to success.  In Lacrimosa, Adol's involvement was basically destined; there was a "larger than life" feeling to the involvement.  Monstrum Nox was more happenstance, but Adol was central to what was going on.  Here, it felt like you could have slapped anyone in this and not called it Ys and just shipped it as a new IP; in which case I might have been more forgiving.The graphics of the world aren't great.  In fact, I would argue that Ys VIII was superior in this category and it certainly wasn't that great, but that's how not-great Ys X's are in comparison.  Roughly equal to Monstrum Nox (better performance by far though).  Character graphics were decent good.There was too much time spent on the secondary NPC bit-players and their stories.  One of the things Monstrum Nox did well was to involve secondary characters without focusing excessively on them - here, the secondary characters get way more time than I think they should have, and it detracts from the protags.Every island was basically the same set of hallways.  While sailing around the sea was a bit fun, it was. a let down to see limited inspiration in the island layouts.Karja had two moments where it was obvious that she had feelings for Adol.  But the writers saw fit to de-emphasize this down to two tongue-in-cheek references, which is what made it obvious: instead of just going with it like they should have (two of the main NPCs were Shield Bretheren yet ended up getting married, which debunked the non-romantic theories), Karja goes from being a strong, largely independent female lead to someone who is struggling with all sorts of feelings.  But unlike with stronger characters like Laxia, it comes across forced and unnatural.  (FYI: Karja is the true protagonist of this game, and it would have been better served as a new IP with her alone vs. having Adol be part of it.  Not because Karja was really any good, but because Adol was pointless and having him there forced them to acknowledge a relationship, which came across stilted.  It would have been better to just focus on the one and not have Adol, who didn't contribute much in the first place.)The "big bads" get introduced as unstoppable threats, then get completely nullified with ease, then a plot twist happens with Karja that starts good but turns into a popcorn fart using "the power of friendship", and these previously unstoppable threats get turned into a generic plot device that felt completely crammed in to help explain the final sequences.  Which ended up being completely predictable because of one cutscene in the middle of the game where it basically spoiled the rest of it.Meanwhile, throughout the early part of the game, you're running into puppet creatures that hold a secret - and that secret is never really answered.  Not answered as to why it's happening, not answered as to who did what, or how you're solving it.  It just gets solved.  Yet there's a sidequest with the same situation, explained away as "we've been like this for too long".  Just lazy writing.I found myself favoring the island/unconscious sequences and dreading the regular exploration.  The island segments were actually interesting and that world felt more like Ys than the main world.  But those sequences start out frequent and end up less and less common, which (in my opinion) killed pacing.The battle engine wasn't terrible, but it wasn't as fun as Ys VIII, wasn't as energized as Monstrum Nox; not as frenetic as Celceta.  It felt a lot like Ark of Napishtim, frankly.  And some of the bug enemies were clearly inspired from that game.I clocked in with under 40 hours rushing.  There's a LOT of padding in this game, I don't mean sidequests, I mean fighting.  Enemies are HP sponges and it seemed like leveling up got increasingly more difficult the closer I got to level 60 for some reason.If it seems like I'm judging the game on its peers, I am.  If this were a standalone game not named Ys, it would be rated much higher and even recommended (just not at full price).  As such, I don't recommend this at full price.  At $30 it's probably fine.  But there just wasn't enough for me....Well, the island/unconscious segment part was decent fun.  I also liked the fish helper as well as the general sailing experience.  Voice acting was good.

_childDocuments_.review: Slightly over ten years ago I’ve played Ys Origin, which was my first experience with Ys franchise or Nihon Falcom games in general. And it completely changed my understanding of what an action RPG can be. Every single entry I’ve played since then, as they were gradually released on PC, was a pleasant experience. Even if not every single one of them were as fantastic as Ys VIII: Lacrimosa of DANA, which remains in my eyes the pinnacle of the franchise as of now. So when Ys X was first shown to be a new “phase” in the franchise, where gameplay will be changed and new mechanics and ideas will be introduced, I was beyond excited to see what Nihon Falcom will do next. …Ys X: Nordics turned out to be the most disappointing Ys game in the series I’ve played so far.The general idea behind Ys has always been a very simple, very mechanically accessible, but incredibly fun and exciting fast paced action RPG adventuring. Set in an alternative version of our Earth on the cusp of the Age of Discovery, it follows the adventures of Adol Christin – a redheaded self-proclaimed “adventurer”, who decides to explore Europe and constantly gets into crazy situations that involve magic and mythical beings that contrast the somewhat normal lives of that era people (just with a more fantasy flavour). Because of this very simple concept, the player is meant to fill the shoes of Adol as he is thrown head first into a new adventure and all of the series plots tend to be relatively simple and easy to follow. Which doesn’t necessarily make them primitive – while often involving lots of tropes, characters and storylines can still be very memorable and interesting, it just varies from game to game how interesting it gets.And mechanically, the simplicity has always been explored in various ways. I’ve said “phase” before, and what I mean by that is the fact that Ys games tend to have some sort of formula for how it plays for a few entries, until it’s switched to something else. And this has happened many times already, even with the entries that are available on PC and other modern platforms, ignoring most of the titles released during the 1990s (and Ys V, which is the only older game in the series without a modern remake or a remaster). However, all of these formulas are very pick up and play in how easy they are to understand. Previous one, for example, relied on extremely fast hack and slash combat with perfect dodges and perfect blocks and an ability to switch between multiple members of the team on the fly, as each of them focused on a specific damage type that was more or less efficient for the enemies you were fighting. Kind of a very simple rock paper scissors formula. It was fast, exciting, simple and allowed players to fully control the flow of combat.Which is what the new formula does not. While some of the basic ideas and controls from the previous “phase” were transferred as is, the new central idea in Ys X is the team of two, who can attack as one and perform special attacks. Type of damage isn’t gone entirely, but is simplified to the damage done to “armour” (that some tougher enemies and bosses have) and damage done to health. Perfect block remains but it’s main use is now to allow for counter attacks and restoring special attacks power faster. While perfect dodges only work on special colour coded “fast attacks”, and their benefit is now the same as for perfect blocks (though there is a very short slow motion effect when you hit it). Also cancelling combos with a block or a dodge now only works at very specific moments of the combination, usually closer to the beginning or the end of it, unlike older games.Sounds like something that should make the game simpler and more fun, but in practice this means that Ys X is now extremely specific about how you play with enemies controlling the flow of the combat more often than the players. You see – with the old system, you could chip damage a tough enemy, quickly dodge out of the attack to trigger a slow motion, perfect block to increase damage output, and control the pace of most of the fight. With the new system, your most consistent winning move is do nothing until enemy attacks you, perfect block it, counter attack, repeat the process until enemy dies. Which is the only way you will be surviving most of the first 10 or so hours of the game, with any enemy group. Until you become more versatile with your skills and the pool of health, that you can just ignore damage with normal enemies and do whatever, but still perform this boring “wait – counter – wait – counter” dance with every tougher enemy or boss until the game finally ends.But another big selling point of Ys X is supposed to be the fact that Adol finally gets to control a ship and explore the different islands on the sea, instead of being landlocked for the majority of his adventure. It’s a great idea and it could work, especially since Ys IX has shown that the team at Nihon Falcom could make moving around huge open world locations very fun with creative movement abilities. Unfortunately, the results are extremely boring. Exploring on ship is incredibly boring, not less because until the last 10 or so hours of the game ship will be painfully slow no matter how much you update it. Most of the islands, including the ones involved in the main plot, have no visual variety to them whatsoever. Combat is taking a page out of the mechanics first popularised with Assassin’s Creed III and IV, but strips them of all nuance, which leads to all naval battles being way too easy to be interesting and at worst just very tedious to go through. While all other movement mechanics in the game are just bad – why even introduce a magic surfboard if running is faster and more convenient in 85% of all situations? Why have a grappling hook mechanic which is worse in every single way to the one that already existed in Ys IX?..This game make so many choices that I cannot even begin to understand. Sure, this is a first attempt at a new formula, Ys haven’t really properly nailed those on the first try before. But even Ark of Napishtim or Ys Seven, for how flawed they were mechanically, were enjoyable games. Ones that you could see being improved in the future (as they were in future installments), but they were a solid enough base and a fun enough game. This isn’t the case with Ys X. It’s acceptable for the first 25 hours and becomes almost somewhat enjoyable in the last 10 hours… by general hack and slash action RPG standards. Which Ys series have always exceeded. But when put into context – even if I forget the best Ys entries exist and think only of the ones that are just solid, I’d rather recommend replaying those than playing Ys X. It’s simply not worth your time, when so much fun adventuring can be had with literally any other Ys game.

_childDocuments_.review: A good Ys game, lots of button prompts/combinations to learn, but once you get over the learning curve its fun to play. Has a brighter colour palette similar to Ys 8. Music is still recognisably Ys, but not quite as good as some of the other entries. As for what to love, the ship navigation and ship to ship combat is excellent. The same fishing mechanic is back from 8 & (maybe 9, cant recall of the top of my head). Island raids are a great ship combat/mini dungeon combination & being able to have shops on board your ship has been helpful to upgrade before an excursion on land. If I were to rate it relative to other Ys games I still love 1&2 The most, 8  second, 6 & 7 tied for third, Then 4 & Origins probably tie for forth, then 10 with 9 & 5 last. If the soundtrack was better, the ship mechanics would have bumped it up to third for me. Only my opinion, others are welcome to disagree and rate differently based on personal preference. I think the order and platform you play the games on matters for your taste, so mine is Ys 1 (SMS), Ys 6 (PS2), 7, 4, 3 (PC), 2 (NDS), Origins & 8 (PS4), then 9 on PS5 and 10 on PC.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 3: Steps forward and backward for the series. This one focuses so much on touchy-feely anime family, interpersonal moments and takes no risks that it brings none of the thrill Ys 9 had, as far as story and character. Too much comic relief and goofiness. Combat is more and less fun at the same time with devs who clearly wanted to slow things down a bit and make some kind of Soulslike system but didn't know how to implement proper pacing and timing. Speaking of pacing: the flash-sideways literally in the middle of tense action sequences to have to the mystery place aren't good design and aren't compelling. There's satisfaction to be had in playing this game, but it's a weak entry to the series in so many ways.EDIT 2: Just realized we went back to a game where the weapon appearance doesn't change. All the fancy newer graphics just to see the same basic sword and axe, even when swapping to weapons that have wildly different designs for their pictures in the shop. EDIT 1: Got a bit further in. Enemies are some magical, undead, dark, scary threat, but the monsters mostly have human voices and border on comic relief most of the time. Guess Nox spoiled me with its darker tone?Eh. Having just blasted through Ys IX Monstrum Nox and having very fond memories of Ys VIII Lacrimosa of Dana, I'm finding the beginning of Ys X to be... disappointing. It looks a little better, sound and voice acting seem better. But we ironically traded the "open-world-but-stuck-in-one-place" feel of IX where you could climb and fly and teleport all over the place to something that feels much more linear and on rails.I truly do appreciate their attempt and making the combat more thought out and less about spamming special moves over and over, but the counter system feels inconsistent and they changed a bunch of stuff on you (default attack to A from B (Xbox controller), LB dodge is now conditional, RB no longer defensive at all, RT is now a block system that's also conditional at times. The level design and movement leave me missing Monstrum Nox. We traded several very cool, very unique characters for 2 pretty bland characters (so far). We traded having a host of cool powers and traversal mechanics for [CHECKS NOTES] fishing and hoverboarding with lines of little shinies to pick up along the way, like I'm playing a Sonic game. For the BIG mechanic, we get sailing. Like the devs just played through Assassin's Creed Black Flag and thought it was the coolest thing ever and needed to get that into their game. So far it all feels a bit fun and a bit clunky. I guess I'll see where it goes.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: A departure from the systems we have come to know, Ys X is a subtle but indeed big change from what we know. Perhaps not the absolute strongest change of the series, the story is as rich as ever and the music is always bumpin'. The 2 player system would be AMAZING for online co-op if they could ever make it happen. Adol and Dogi co-op for Ys 5 do it. DO IT. I DOUBLE DOG DARE YA.A good Ys game so far, even if it's a smidge different. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Story: 5/5Gameplay: 4Graphics: 4Stability: 5Time Played: 80 Hours (40 in the demo maxing skills before release) One of the things I judge games on is how well they work. This is one of those games I never experienced a crash on despite adjusting graphics settings. There are some slight load times even on a m.2 drive, but I adjusted the video buffer to max for my card to speed up the transitions. ymmvThis is a fantastic ARPG for the fights and exploring on land. As with many YS titles the goal is to explore and much like the real world the sea is vast and mostly boring. You can opt to break up the pace with fights on the water or sail the few islands in each region to explore or do side quests. As one of the other reviewers noted, sea battles can be annoying. I'll note my playthrough was on hard difficulty and I was able to handle the side quest sea battles with ease and still manage an S rank. Nightmare or higher rank may provide more difficulty, but I haven't played it. Annoyances: Fishing. Not difficult by any means, just annoying having to do it for quest items. I find it more annoying to do fishing than the sea battles. Sea battles. Nuff said. DLC pricesPraises: Voice acting, they picked great voices for the player charcters. Especially despite Adol being a silent type hero for so long. Combat. YS has always been a fight and explore between story games and this game does all three well. I personally enjoy the growth the characters go through with their skills. A swing becomes multi swing, that becomes multi flame swings. Combat isn't punishing like a Souls game, but you can get by with hit it with the stick enough times. Don't recommend that since it would take forever with enemies with armor. Bosses are pretty formulaic though. Break down the armor, whittle some health, regains armor, rinse and repeat. Summary: If you like YS series, it is a great buy. If you're new this is a solid entry and no you don't need to play each game before. Chronologically, this game is about the third tale.

After buying and playing the full game, it has somehow managed to get better and better, helped by the fact that the new gameplay systems just clicked. The dynamic between Adol and Karja is pretty cool, too.Also thankful that despite having an ancient PC, I can still play this new game with great performance. Of course, a lot of that is also due to Durante and PH3. Thank you, PH3 GmbH.My only complaint is that I wish there were more costumes/cosmetic items, whether in the base game or whatever came in the DLC offerings.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game overall. Literally everything is good except for the fact that the combat (which is the most important part of an action rpg) is trash tier. Either you die to gimmick or it's so easy the fight is boring. No actual challenge just fight once to learn the boss gimmick and beat it while half asleep next try.Bosses' gimmicks are admittedly to be expected for a JRPG. But unlike soul games YS X also have hitboxes that make no sense and often hit places it shouldn't. On top of the fact that damage is done BEFORE the attack animation start which makes reactionary playing obnoxious. In the end the game expect yo to just stand in place and hold RT, very engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: The game overall is great, the combat/gameplay feels very fun to play & the new party system on this one compare to the previous Ys game is more manageable and rich.The Story/the character deisgn is good, but i was hoping more on the story :DNow, there are few point that need to be adress :First the graphic, it can be for most Ys player fine but for a game in 2024 the graphic is less than mid, The character design/FX on attack is really good but the environnement/landscape feel so poor compare  to the rest. Furthermore the level of detail in some zone are not consistent.For example there is one zone in the late game which is very beautiful and detail but when you compare to the first zone it's like night and day.Second the start is incredibly slowwwww like before 10h, the game is very linear.Ultimately the last point is the music which is mid, there is very few OST that i remenber after finishing the game.A lot of ambiant/sad/travel music are really good, but the battle theme or some epic boss theme are not there.Compare to Ys IX it's a step back in my opinion but i hope it will get better in the future.Still recommend the game because at least the game is really fun to play ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: To think this is my first review but this game is so damn good. Ys VIII is still my favorite but Ys X is pretty close through its amazing gameplay, story, and characters. The story wasn't the craziest thing ever but it is still on the better side more than anything. Played this on the highest difficulty (Inferno) and it is no joke but i don't regret it cause it made the gameplay even better for me. I had to be more aware of what moves the enemies were going to throw so i highly recommend it, unless you want to just play for the story and not be sweaty like me lol. Cons are the obvious outdated graphics and some few bs hitboxes but not really much to discard all the good things happening in this game. All in all one of Adol's best adventures in the series in my honest opinion. PEAK 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've always been a HUGE fan of the Ys series, always buy the most expensive version available on PC (I don't own any console). This new iteration is no exception.Pros:- Extremely satisfy combat per usual, though they revamped it a bit and I would say I prefer this, feel harder.- Great story, although starting a bit slow.- Relatable and memorable cast.- Graphics get a tremendous glow up, especially cutscenes holly molly.Cons:- Ship starts SLOW, I mean REALLY SLOW. It gets much better soon enough tho.- Only 2 playable characters is... fine. Ys VII, VIII, IX and Celceta are better in this regard.- Songs are not as good as Ys VIII and IX.- Travelling by a ship brings something new to the table, but overall I much prefer Ys VIII's sense of discovery and continuation of maps. I know that this has to be done to compensate for the original release on Switch. Well it is what it is then.TL;DR VIII and IX better but if Ys fan = buy.

_childDocuments_.review: it's ys, in spite of its departures. of the modern ys offerings on steam I'd put it slightly below 8 and well above 9.duo system is fun actually, and most of my gripes with it (and the game as a whole) were washed away by the back third or so. people will dump on the duo system and the armor system for being different but I vastly prefer it to the pierce/crush/slash triangle. flash step/block isn't as much of a loss as it seems like it would be. it could be better, sure, but I think for the first game after doing a huge overhaul they did a great job and wouldn't mind if they did the same thing for future entriesport is slightly jank (of course it is) so save often. I lost 12 hours of progress to getting softlocked into a ship fight. aside from that and the early game with the ship being actually horrible it's kamige as usualadol you moron stop adventuring and stay with a heroine. namely this one. no this isn't a spoiler.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a step to the right direction for graphics/character models. Hoping Falcom and improve on their new engine (IIRC it's a new engine they are using from the Trails series). A little slower pace from the other team based Ys games, but I do like it being less spammy than the other ones. Took me a bit to get use to the slower pace battles which Ys is know for a fast pace action RPG, but later on with more skills and equipment, feels like any other team based Ys game out there. The music, omg, as always, a banger of an OST! Last but not least - Karja's swimsuit and Raven outfit are amazing! So far the translations are alright, just some hick ups here and there, but I do appreciate them doing better on translating. I play on Japanese, but I do understand to a point where some things they say aren't what they really said, but it alright. I may be wrong about all of that, but I just "feel" like it's fine.Now let's talk about the performance... the performance is great too! Runs smooth and no crashes on my end. 1440P all ultra settings and 144 frames. At first, I was dropping down from 160 highest to 110 at the lowest from certain skills and areas of the map, which isn't bad, but with my computer's specs, I should be running the game flawlessly. I run Resident Evil 4 remake 144-160 frames without dipping down 144 frames with all the settings at ultra, but this game I had to tinker with my GPU settings for a bit to get those frames from dropping under 144 hertz. Wish it wouldnt drop frames like that without messing with my gpu settings. Other than that, game runs great if you set up your gpu correctly.The time you use your ship, it's really too slow for my taste and the ship battles are just boring for me. Other than the team based Ys games, Ys 8 is still my #1 but Ys X is definitely my second fave one. The feeling of exploration of the world is what I wanted from an Ys game, which greatly disappointed me Ys 9, being stuck mostly in a town.

_childDocuments_.review: Reached chapter 4 and it's a massive disappointment compared to Ys 8 and 9. Combat took a turn for the worst (duo link system forces Adol and Karja to hit slower but heavier, but it feels like a slog), endless crappy dialogue, ship gameplay is boring, story and characters are nothing to write home about (Karja is your typical tsundere character and nothing more) and questionable localization.Seriously, i can't find any enjoyment out of it. Kudos Falcom for ruining one of the best action RPG series.

_childDocuments_.review: It's... pretty good?  It has, thankfully, gotten away from the last few Ys games' team-play mechanics.  The duo-mechanic is not particularly well executed compared to the solo mechanics in the past four or five Ys games (Origins and Oath in Felghana were my favorites), but it *is* a neat new way to do things.  The duo mechanic is... really not particularly cleanly implemented.  I started playing on Hard, as a Ys fan, and thus far you either use Duo mode or you die.  Dash-dodging is pretty nerfed, and it seems like perfect guarding is the way to go now.Karja is an adorable cinnamon roll, and I really enjoy that Adol isn't treated as a thief.  I can't say enough good things about Karja, compared to IX's characters.The graphics and music are excellent... for Ys games.  The quality of life improvements continue.  It's an incremental improvement.  Compared to other sixty dollar games... the graphics are terrible.  The voice acting is amateur.  But nobody that's playing Ys games is here for those.Anyway, it's a really solid Ys game.  I recommend it, if you like Ys games.

_childDocuments_.review: So I just finished the game about 30 minutes ago, having put in close to 40 hours. The short version of how I feel is that it is a good Ys game. If you're an Ys fan, I feel like you're going to have a good time with the game... But that's about it.The long version is that the game feels like "junk food"; it's a good, but I'm not coming away from it feeling like it was amazing. I'm a "Johnny Come Lately" fan, having started with Ys VIII, and then started working my way from Ys 1 and 2, with a nice detour when IX came out of course, so I'm probably missing the context of someone who's been with the series since the 90's, but I'd give X a solid 7.5, which is perfectly fine, but disappointing to me given that I typically love sea-fairing pirate-y adventure. The crux of my argument is that the game just doesn't give itself time to breathe where it matters, and kind of drags on a bit in other areas where it doesn't.The characters are pretty weak to start. Naturally, Adol is our adventurous silent persona, so you aren't going to get a lot of human drama from his side, which leaves the heavy lifting to the supporting characters, which are really just... fine, I guess. Obviously this is just my opinion, but when I think of some characters in Ys IX like Yufa and Krysha, who go through a lot of struggles that you get to see and help develop, you don't really get that with the teens of Carnac. It's a typical "coming of age" story, which isn't bad in itself, just uninspired and bland, with or without the comparisons to previous games. There were some interesting potential with certain character conflicts, but, and this leads into my main criticism with the story, they don't really go anywhere, or in the best case, resolve way too quickly like certain BIG character developments that happen later in the main story. I would have liked the game to dwell on certain character conflicts a lot more. I feel like there could have easily been at least another 15 hours of game to account for that.Ys isn't just about its narrative (in fact, I'm sure some just consider that a bonus!), and while I enjoyed the combat initially, it starts feeling rote after about hour 20 maybe. I think a lot of it stems from the duo system, which is really fun, and I like perfect dodging and blocking to gain the advantage, but there's really only so much you can do with two characters. To be fair, they take it pretty far, but yeah... I think it ties really well with the narrative, but not feeling super connected to Karja, the new character you spend the most time with, I was kind of going through the motions after awhile. I played the game on hard, and the release line system felt pretty superfluous when added to the weapon upgrading and leveling systems. I dunno. It didn't feel worth it. Maybe in Nightmare mode it matters a lot more.Visually and performance-wise, there isn't really a lot to report here. It runs well, is pretty bug-free, and is in-line with what you'd expect from a modern Falcom title, which certainly isn't a bad thing. They're very pragmatic when it comes to pushing the graphical envelope, and definitely adhere to "if it ain't broke, don't fix it!" That said, there are certain areas where better animations would help the immersion, "believability", or whatever you want to call it of a scene much moreThis review has gotten way too large, so I'll end it saying that there's really a lot to like here. The game is very ambitious, but I feel like it misses the mark in some important areas. I finished the game and had to really try to remember what the last few scenes were, whereas I couldn't stop thinking about Dana from Ys VIII or the Monstrums from Ys IX for days.
