_childDocuments_.review: Ys X is even more of a visual novel than the prior games; it's almost like its job is to cover up glaring problems with the core gameplay. The enemy AI often cannot land a hit on you even when you're standing still; it definitely felt worse than in previous games, and it's actually so depressing. Hitting a flash guard is one of the more satisfying aspects of the game, but that doesn't matter when the enemy rather smashes into the ground behind you. You finish the game way before a good opportunity to explore the new release line system, which looks like it could make for some good food for thought, or at least a proper time sink, but the level progression falls dead in the water mid game like no one tested if you could even unlock all of it. Then they do this thing again where they soft lock your save game like a final "that's all folks!" and the last auto save that was made is missing like one hour of progress. It's such an unnecessary quirk for a game where otherwise your choices are completely irrelevant. How much suspension of disbelief do I need to want to progress my character in a role playing game? Why even have a leveling mechanic at this point? I could forgive this if the writing was consistently great, but we're dealing with mostly the same old obligatory glue dialog that the series has had for some time with only a few interesting bits sprinkled here and there. They're clearly completely unable to handle the amount that they are cramming in, and it has fully taken center stage with the actual game being haphazardly built around it. It's an effective strategy because character-centric story telling sells, and yeah the lead girl character is cute because of course she is, but I don't accept that as "good enough" when you are in the business of selling games. Oh, and you're on a really slow boat for half the game that makes you praise the lord every time you unlock a warp destination.

_childDocuments_.review: A new title in one of my fav. series and the one i have been fan of the longest, i was naturally excited for it...yet also wary, as i hadn't been exactly happy with Falcom for more than a few years now, and ....I 100%'d the game on Nightmare and my fears were put to rest for now.So let's talk about it, shall we?Bump Combat, Napish Era and party system. Those are the the combat systems most Ys fans are familiar with. And with X we are entering a new era of Ys combat that will probably accompany us for the next 2 - 3 titles.Our "Party" -if you can call it that- now consists of 2 members: Adol and Karja. You either control one of them at a time or both together at the same time in duo mode. In duo mode you move slower but get better attacks, and you can guard.Ah yes, speaking about guard....Flash guard and evasion are also gone replaced with a new guarding and evasion mechanic. Alongside their normal attacks, Enemies also have power (Red) Attacks and speed (Blue) Attacks. The first can only be guarded, the latter only evaded. Performing a perfect guard/evade against dangerous enemies and bosses also give you a cool combo attack/animation the first time you do it against them.I heard many people think that the combat is slow/clunky, and for the first hour or so i honestly thought the same...but once the combat clicks and you understand the flow, it ain't slower than usual Ys. To know when to use which character, when to duo and to chain skills together while evading/guarding makes for a fun and satisfying combat system. And ah, the revenge gauge needs to be mentioned as well. You get a damage multiplier on duo skill when guarding, with perfect guard filling the gauge by a lot.Well, controller remapping might also be needed as the standard control scheme honestly sucks XD.I do like the new system quite a lot, a nice change coming from the party system, but of course it's the first game with this system and it shows. Perfect guard timing i think is a bit generous, and imo shield should break faster without perfect guard. Adol and Karja could've also used some more differences between them. But just like Ark's system was perfected in Oath and Origin, and later 7's system was perfected in 8 and 9, this shall also develop and become better! Aside from our "standard combat" we also have naval combat - Boring at the start when it was slow but quite better later on!Raids are also improved now, with only offensive Raids being present and them being a 2 parter - a naval part and a mini dungeon part.Level and Boss design were generally cool - although wish there more variety on the former and stronger bosses in general.All together creates a very satisfying gameplay loop!Adol the red. The adventure-holic protagonist of the series. This time, his adventure wasn't even his intended target, as he basically got robed into it while in his way to Celceta from Esteria.Yup, this games take place between Ys 2 and Celceta. Adol didn't even get his adventurer title bestowed to him yet, and it's quite the contrast to the experienced punished Adol we got in Balduq - where he is at his oldest yet.The ship he was on on the way to Celceta get's boarded by pirates - led by this title's heroine and co-protag, Karja Batla, Pirate Princess of the Balta seaforce - the group that de-facto controls Obelia gulf - where our story takes place.And thus their fate was tied.Karja is a great character, and also a fresh one as a protag, as she is quite the opposite of a "Goody two shoes". With a striking introduction, she's someone who believes in strength above all else and "making the choice to live!". She has a different perspective on things than usual. Tbf, the Balta seaforce is not some super evil pirate group that pillage and blunder for the hell of it, but they are forceful, and occupy areas and collect tolls and stuff.And Adol and Karja play off well each other and together make for great leads. Adol here is at his most expressive yet, and he was already quite outspoken in 9. Karja goes the adventure alongside him and goes through great development herself. Don't wanna accidentally spoil much so i will say she's probably my 2nd fav. Heroine after Dana. You will see how she changes slowly through the game and develops as she learns more, and how Adol and Karja help each other through the journey and arrive at their answers.However, as leads, they of course need supporting cast to truly shine, for which we have the crew mates and a mysterious old man.Among the crew mates there is the "Youth Brigade". These are pretty much the party member equivalent in the party Ys games. They are not playable, but they do get quite a big focus during the journey, and accompany us during the journey as usual Party members would. They do get some good development and have a lot of banter and interaction between them - and with our leads.One thing that really makes the cast and their interactions shine are the shipboard convos. Convos you get while sealing the waters that i would compare to Tales' skits. They are great and add some much needed interaction between the members. Make sure to view em all!As for the story, it starts with "Monster attack Adol go slash them!" and then get's places and becomes really cool, especially while uncovering the history and myths of the Normans, and the conflict later on.The story is quite character driven, and we do have a pretty cool cast :DYs X offers a completely satisfying package of gameplay and narrative. A Masterpiece like Ys 8 this ain't, neither does it reach the gameplay heights of Oath and Origin, but it's a fresh take on the series with a gameplay loop that can and will trap you in it's seas, making you sail through it's adventure. Early game might be slow for some, but once you leave it and reach mid game, specifically chapter 5, it's honestly no breaks until the end from there. A satisfying end that leads into Adol's next adventure - Ys 4: Memories of Celceta.Ah, also, PC port by Durante - great as usual.RatingGameplay - ACharacters - AStory - B+/A-Music - CMiscellaneous - SScore: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game yet, but I think I've played enough to say with certainty that it's one of the weaker games in the franchise. It's actually like aggressively mediocre in many ways. The ship sailing is absolutely awful, it's worse than a budget version of Assassin's Creed 4. The ship combat also feels much worse than I was expecting. Not enough needing to position for broadsides. It's very arcadey and I frankly don't really like it.Aside from that, it uses the same skill spammy combat system that Ys Seven introduced to the detriment (in my opinion at least) to the series. I VASTLY preferred the combat style of Origin/Oath/Ark.The exploration is also so infuriating. I'm 26 hours in and the game is still hard railroading me. It'll tease you with a nice open area with your ship, but trying to explore without doing the story first in an area will have you hitting invisible walls in all directions. It's genuinely so awful.There's other incredibly annoying things that the game does as well, such as have you need to press the select button to do certain actions, this ranges from pulling out your fishing rod to talking to crew members while sailing to leaving the helm and going inside your ship. This would be fine, except anytime anybody is speaking, it blocks you from doing this. This, also, would be only a minor annoyance, except your characters always exclaims that there's fish in an area (that you can already clearly see) and you have to wait for the text box to disappear like 15 seconds later before the game allows you to pull out your fishing rod. Another notable thing that pissed me off; the devs decided that it was a good idea to put an NPC directly in front of the table you need to interact with in order to do ship upgrades, which means you need to walk in and then move around the room to the other side of the table before you can interact with it.Honestly, the only things I've thought were great so far are the soundtrack and Karja.

_childDocuments_.review: Played mostly on Steam Deck, where it plays great with some initial setup. It’ll drain the battery if you max everything out, so turn down a few settings. It looks a lot better on the smaller screen, and I’ll always think of Ys as a handheld series. I also played a bit via streaming from PC to Steam Link (the physical box) and it worked well on the TV with a DualSense. When swapping between PC and Steam Deck, the game save transferred via cloud, but the game settings for each were separate. So that kept graphic settings different for each device, but it also kept custom button config’s separate as well. Only a minor thing to deal with setting it for both.The programmers who ported this to PC have put a lot into optimization, and for such a niche series, it’s appreciated. They have also been known to make updates to these PC Ys games years after release, so this will likely continue to get some support for a while. I specifically bought it on PC this time for that and other reasons.Most Ys games are a slog at first and seem slow and disappointing initially. Stick with it. The usual character development and expanding story is here. It just takes time, and just like every other Ys game I’ve played in the last decade, I go through an initial period of disappointment until I realize the game is actually tons of fun and charming.This entry has some references to people and incidents from Ys I & II. You'll enjoy just a little bit more here if you've played those games first, however, it’s not critical to the story. Maybe read an overview of those games and it’d help. For story, this game takes place between Ys II and Ys IV: Memories of Celceta. This game expands on specific regions and histories not previously discussed much in other games in the series. This one has a LOT more English voice acting. There’s still a lot of text with no voice, but it’s an improvement to humanize characters more. There’s less of those jarring transitions where they voice act a few lines and then you gotta read the rest. It's nice to have a change of story-telling and gameplay style with only a two-person party with some new fighting features. It’s not a huge change from recent entries, but I was glad to not have six characters to play again, and I think it really helped build the development of the two playable characters. The fighting really hasn’t changed much, but I do like they tried something new, and while it took some getting used to, there is something interesting here with swapping characters on-the-fly to keep your SP skills going, and/or when to use the new duo mode skills instead. It’s not largely different in fighting style from recent games, but different enough to be fun. The more I played and practiced, I realized it was actually a neat new system with a lot of choice. If you’re just a button-masher, you probably won’t care.While some may not like this, I appreciate that this series still follows a semi-linear path. I am tired of every game needing to be open-world, and in a lot of games it just destroys the flow of the story. This is probably the most “open” Ys game, but it still guides and is fairly linear in a way. The ship part is the most open part of the game. The on-foot parts are more like prior entries with smaller sections to explore.The settings for PC are nice, including coop directly built in, which is super uncommon for this kind of game. The coop for the other recent games was a ton of fun. Even if the game wasn’t built for coop and it isn’t perfect, it’s a blast to share the game with someone else.I liked the inclusion of tips when idling. Since loading screens aren't long enough, sometimes I'd see these tips when idling to heal or coming back from as break. I also like they continue giving exhaustive button config settings, because these games have never had good button layouts. It took a lot of gameplay and fiddling to settle on a button config I liked, but at least they allow you to do it. They also included built-in settings for different button icons, such as Xbox, Playstation, and Steam Deck button prompts in-game.The icon art for the achievements is a lot of fun to look at. The Ys series continues to name places and things in ridiculous ways ripped off real life. I burst out laughing at "Walhalla" when it was first said out loud.The graphics are appalling. It doesn't need to be amazing, but this is pretty sad. The water seems worse than it was in Ys VIII: Lacrimosa of Dana, and this is a ship game. When these games were on handheld it looked charming. However now on PC with everything basically maxed out, especially while sailing and looking at the towns and islands from the ship, it looked like I was playing a PS2 game. Some places like the first town are not great in general presentation when walking around and seem barely populated or full of life (compared to the town in Ys IX: Monstrum Nox). Like most of my review, while some of it’s disappointing, you eventually get over it cause the gameplay and story are fun as usual. There are some areas that look great however, like inside places.The movement of characters also seems cheesy; more than recent games. For example, characters get done talking, and need to head a different direction, so they awkwardly pivot their whole body to a position, and then set off. It feels like PS2-quality animations of people. But don’t get me wrong, there’s so much voice acting, story depth, and character development, you eventually get over it.Additionally, I'm surprised at how limited some areas are. I don't need open world, but some areas are tiny and there's no shortage of invisible walls in places that might surprise you. It's not a deal breaker, but just a smidge more explorability would have been nice. However, I play these games for the stories character development, fighting, and the looting/leveling, so I've gotten over most of the graphics and cheese of the animations. You do get used to the graphics and the fun of the game takes over.They added fishing back in with this game, but they changed how you trigger it. You hit a specific button to pull up a top-left menu which ONLY contains an option to fish. Terrible design. This is also where character chat bubbles appear when running around on foot, and one of them ALWAYS comments when you’re near a fishing hole. The bubble disables the menu temporarily, so you have to wait until they shut up and the bubble goes away for the toggle to reappear in order to actually fish. A minor but consistent annoyance.When out at sea, some of the trigger points for sea battles do nothing randomly, and it just seems like a bug. Sailing feels slow early-game, and I mean REALLY slow, and so taking time to sail to a spot for it not to trigger is frustrating. Later in the game the ship upgrades make sailing and ship battles a lot more fun. Pay attention to people and side quests, as that is essentially how you upgrade your ship. You should definitely play this game, even if on sale. Every Ys game has faults, but they are always incredibly fun action RPG’s, and I will always appreciate their willingness to try new things with every entry in the series. These are my favorite JRPG’s, and I just have never seen the appeal of other JRPG series. They don’t do for me what Ys does.About 50 hours in I am probably barely past halfway. I am typically a slow player and like to experience everything though. Some day I will probably also try the harder modes in a replay.

_childDocuments_.review: Falcom had quite the task in front of them when it came to creating this game. Not only is their first (and as of writing, only) Ys game in their latest engine, but it also had to shake up the combat system a lot. They had been using the same combat system for 4 games total by now (7-9, as well as 4's remake), and while I absolutely adore Ys IX, and still consider that to be one of my favourite games ever made, it did become abundantly clear that the party system had run its course by the time Monstrum Nox's credits rolled. And for an RPG series that emphasises gameplay as much as Ys does, that's something you do NOT want to drag out.It's almost kind of fitting, what with this being the start of a new gameplay style, that Ys X covers one of Adol's earliest adventures. His second, in fact, if we're counting Ys I and II as one whole. And it did what it had to do: Enough. While I was hoping for a more significant shake-up, I do think the devs at Falcom made a very smart choice in having a more focused and specialised version of the party system: The Cross-Action system. (Or as I like to call it: The Duo system.) It's just Adol and Karja. That's it. That's all you're gonna get for the next 30+ hours. And the game is better for it. You control either Adol, Karja, or both at any given time, and it makes for one hell of a satisfying gameplay loop. I'd even argue it's the best gameplay the series has seen within the last decade and a half.Oh, and there's also taking the helm of a boat, to go explore the sea and battle other ships. It helps keep things a little fresh, even if I'm not really a fan of getting boat physics involved.When it comes to Ys games, I don't really view the story as all that important. There have been cases where I was really into the main plot itself (particularly SEVEN and IX), but when it comes to overall Ys narratives, I'm always more interested in the individual characters and their personality quirks, something Falcom tends to be really good at. I do think Ys X scores above average when it comes to its main plot, but it wouldn't be the same if Karja wasn't such a solid lead character. By the time the credits rolled, she had become one of my favourite characters in the series. She's a really fun character, and seeing how she grows and deal with the problems that come her way was engaging. Especially when factoring in her upbringing within Vikin- I mean Norman culture.Without going into spoilers, I also want to quickly mention just how much I love the game's final hours the more and more I think on it. I wouldn't be surprised if it'll be a long, long time until I see a finale executed in such a way in a game again. Hell, even while I'm writing this I'm growing more fond of it. I just really appreciate what the writers and other devs accomplished with it. It's really neat!One last thing I want to quickly mention is its soundtrack. I'll be honest, I'm part of the camp that has felt like Falcom OST's had been on a bit of a decline ever since their PSVita era ended. And I felt this especially with Trails through Daybreak earlier this year. So consider my surprise when I actually ended up enjoying more of the OST than I was expecting! So, composers, keep it up! (Just, uh, it wasn't perfect. Falcom, if you could keep you-know-who away from specifically the electric guitar, I'd appreciate it. He's fine otherwise.)ALL THAT SAID,I would consider this game: Great! Top 3 in the series if you ask me, taking VIII's place. But not enough to beat out Origin or ESPECIALLY IX for me. And with it being an Ys game without the roman number II in its title, it's a solid entry point if you're curious! The demo covers the first 20-25% of the game, if you're curious. So try it, see if it's something you like. And if it ain't, no harm done. As for me, though, I've loved every hour, and am very curious to see how the devs are going to iterate on this new style they've established!.......................(Get on remaking Ys V, pleez. It has so much potential.)

_childDocuments_.review: I reviewed the game thumb down midway through playing but as I now finally beat the game today in under 35 hours or so (steam hours isn't correct due to alt-tabbing) I still can't recommend this game or at least mostly mixed about it as it, not a bad game, it great I just personally didn't enjoy it as much as I wanted. This is mostly going to sound negative sadly but ill list off the sections of the game that I have the most problems with.This going to sound like a "boomer" take of “hating changes” but the combat system change from 7seven engine/party system to duo system is a weird one, but it is mainly with what they did with dodging and parrying. Dodging overall is the main issue as it feels like they made it the worse version overall as there is no longer invil frame while dodging, no flash dodge to give u invil for a period of time (same with parrying), and only able to do it for a very select few move in the game that is dodge only, even with that dodging just become "just hold sprint for auto dodge" moving the skill required for timing your dodge and feel like more of a gimmick move, its not THAT bad but it feels like a straight downgrade from 8-9.Parrying also is downgraded but is still good and feels pretty nice to hit however u now lose flashguard so no invil and 100% crit rate, so now u gotta make sure u parry everything but it also acts as a block button so just holding it will protect u from 100% damage. My problem outside of missing flash guard is the only reward u get is a counter hit and that it. I stop using it because it doesn't always happen, and the revenge gauge where your duo attack gets stronger the more you parry, it fine early but late game where u get more and more revenge it feels like it take a long time before u can fill it to use it to the max.Last is just the issue the new system added to make the game feel annoying to play at times, mainly for when the game has enemy with duo block require + dodge only require fighting at the same time with the added wind blowback it become a ♥♥♥♥ fest of getting cheat shooted and hit. Since u can't fully invil frame a lot of stuff, if some actions happen at the same time it becomes harder to not get hit or killed (since i played on nightmare) as u can't dodge a dodge only and be safe from other attack happening at the same time and same with parrying an attack and be safe from a dodge only move hitting you at the same time, what worse is some encounter have blowback into a unblockable (duo black required) making you getting CC into a hit which never feel good to play I just dreed the ship system so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ much, it's basic and bland AF for the majority of the game and it is SOOO SLOW early on that it kills the pace that ys game is normally known for being fast or at least decently paced, but ship just slow early on, all the enemy ship all feel the same and traveling speed is painful slow. The only time I actually had fun with the ship was doing the Final chapter ship quest side where u go fight 3 boss ship that actually have cool move and feel like the dev was creative about it vs how every other ship fight feels the same and extremely bland. It sucks that the ship is also around 1/3 to half of the game time spent making it one of the main reasons I can't recommend the game.  I honestly can't go in deep with this because I believe the story of this game overall  but going into deep with it for a story I stop caring for won't do any good.The characters however can give a deeper reason of just not caring about them and that is because the game did speedrun a lot of side character background story for the player to care and have a deep connect with them however the characters they pull that on have like 3 scenes of dialouge before they just dump a sad backstory. I didn't like any of the support side characters except maybe 1 or 2 of the other crewmates in the game.Katja is kinda a hit-or-miss character as they do build her as unlikeable early but turn over a new leaf, I'm indifferent about her.Grenn is a HATE or love character and i really really hate him, i hate that he has almost the most screen time vs other side characters as he is just a really annoying character.I do believe that this game at least with the "Teen" cast was supposed to be a party system, there was enough character for it to be a party of 6 + adol but they went to duo instead but wanted to keep the Teen cast super important to the main story. However me personally, I feels like Grenn and Cruz were the only ones that I can see being needed for the main story,MiscThe music was great and honestly, the more I played the game the more I got used to the combat system and realized the game isn't half bad I just feel like I'm a bit disappointed with the result, combat change is questionable, the story just didn't click with me (and I do think it just bad) and ship system was the weirdest addition for a fast pace action base game (at least fast pace for the past 3 titles). I almost dare say it is not even a Ys game but that is being too mean about it, I just feel like the stuff they added + change feels like the direction wasn't made with Ys fans in mind ....Sorry if this review sounds super ranty and rambly but it just that, Me ranting about this game, a franchise that I played all their other games (except 5) so pretty dumm out I didn’t enjoy this game as much as I wanted

_childDocuments_.review: Better than Ys 9, because Ys 9 was dripping dog poo, but the one third of this game that's actually an Ys game is buried under two thirds of tedious, longwinded nonsense that isn't worth slogging through. Don't give Falcom money for this.The devs were more concerned with hitting every single item on the Japanese Corpo List of Trends that must be crowbarred into  to come out of that country to actually make a good Ys game like most of them up through Ys 8. You see, Naruto was popular 20 years ago so now there  be a grossly bloated roaster of pointless, one dimensionally, shallow ancillary characters in hopes that one gets popular with the Rule34 goofs so we can sell them figurines. Calling them characters is a generous compliment, with so many unnecessary cretins involved, there's no time for most of them to be little more than Anime Personality Trope and a first name. And since Naruto was popular 20 years ago, one of the characters has to be an intolerable shrieking moron. That's Grenn, and he spends the game being the most aggravating idiot to ever blight any fictional medium.  His "character arc," no word of a lie, is to start as a clown as, become an even bigger, louder, more irritating wanton imbecile, and be rewarded for it. I've never seen anything like it.Most of the other character plots aren't necessarily "better," just less infuriating. Multiple times a character would exposit their own backstory directly at you, the player, to set up drama, only to have that drama resolved IN THE SAME CUTSCENE.  Set up, build, conclusion, all inside of 5 minutes with zero gameplay involved. They once interrupted the core plot on some wacky mystical island for inane family drama of inconsequential characters to do exactly that.  Again, I've never seen anything like it. It is Making this  worse is the way Grenn specifically, and everyone else to a lesser extent, talks.  There is zero attempt to "keep kayfabe," so to speak, of being a vaguely medieval fantasy world.  Unlike in previous, far superior Ys games, you now get treat to high school anime filler dialogue like "Oh HELL to the yeah!" Thanks, Grenn, please self apply Canadian healthcare at your earliest convenience.  That text was accompanied by him shouting (of course) "Get HYPED!!1!" I guess someone on the dev team had been watching Dr. Stone kindly @#$% off.  They try to compensate by having Karja say "aye" instead of "yes."  Because she's a pirate, you see. Didn't work.  if we didn't have this cumbersome roster of jackasses, there wouldn't be anyone to man the ship, which brings me toI've never played a game with a more half-fannied boat mechanic.  There isn't a sea.  There is a perfectly flat blue floor you slide along.  No waves, no dynamic weather or wind, shallow combat, all incredibly lazy.  It comes off as something I could slap together in Godot if I YouTube'ed enough tutorials.  It would barely be acceptable for a solo dev no budget indy game.  It's the "killer app," so to speak, of what's fronting as a Triple A game.  Sad!  The boat's a fat waste of time and the whole game would be better if it were designed and written to be almost entirely on land, where the game is at it's best.  Speaking of the game's relative strong suitThis is where you actually get some bits of an Ys game.  The two-character combat is pretty slick once you're up to speed with switching and throwing out wild anime skills.  Playing on Normal, which I am compelled to do after Normal on Oath In Felghana gave me PTSD, was entirely too easy.  ROLFstomping trash mobs is kinda fun, but there is zero challenge to it or most boss fights.  I accidentally blundered into the optional level 99 challenge boss at level 83 and that was the only time in the game I had to use any of the many healing items the game threw at me, and still won.As for the narrative and levels you're fighting through, they're quite mid. The Seabed Temple is the one place that feels like a Peak Ys dungeon, but everything else is a short jaunt on a generic island, interrupted by that stupid boat. The final dungeon is particularly lame.Then the narrative is The Karja Balta Game: Guest Starring Adol Christin.  Karja isn't even that bad in a vacuum, but good god  revolves around her at incredible length and it's a letdown for a series that typically revolves around dealing with some apocalypse or other. AND THEN she tells you that she was going on viking raids when she was ten because she's a super speshul pie rat princess once again @#$% off a ten year old girl is three and a half feet tall and weighs 60 lbs. I don't care if she knows the Kamameha Wave, she's not winning any fight.  Deliberately choosing to write something like that is completely deranged. This is all compounded by the fact that they inexplicably chose to set this game between Ys 2 and Oath In Felghana, meaning with the Tag Team core mechanic, the ONLY correct choice was to make Dogi the other playable character. But nah we need the waifu-bait character front and center while Dogi sits in the ship with his thumb up his ass.The whole plot itself in a general sense is a bunch of questions gradually building to a climatic payoff and resolution, like Oath In Felghana, Ys 7, and Ys 8. Unlike those games, the conclusion is a bit of a wet fart.To say ONE nice thing about the game, it all looks really good.  From characters to combat animations to lighting, great looking "Anime style" game.  Shame the actually game is so mediocre.Listen, don't buy this game.  Don't reward Falcom for such rote drivel.

_childDocuments_.review: FINAL REVIEW:Man I love Ys. Get into the series if you haven't, yet.EDIT:Having played for a while longer now, it's great. It's not quite at the level of Ys 8 so far, but that's a tall order. Between blocking and dodging and switchin between characters while using skills, combat can get a bit hectic, but it's fun and rewarding to take on a challenge boss twice your level.(OLD) INFO:I have yet to actually play the game, but it's Ys and I know that i like Ys, so the recommendation is purely based on that. I guess the config menu was nice, but I mostly jacked up the graphics and turned down the volume.However, I need to talk about the editions. Available are the base edition, the deluxe edition and the ultimate edition.The base edition includes the game and, during launch deal, an extra cosmetic pack as well as a mini art book, which is nice.The deluxe edition which I settled on additionally comes bundled with four extra cosmetic packs (one being part of the time-limited launch deal) as well as the OST (also part of the launch deal).Anyone who ever played an Ys game knows that the OST is absolutely awesome, but do not let yourself get fooled here. The OST comes with 8 tracks, and unless that is all the game has, that is a really weird choice that I am absolutely not happy with. I checked that beforehand, but imagine that being your driving factor to spend an extra 20€ on the game, and ending up with 8 tracks.The ultimate edition costs an additional 50€ over the deluxe addition and comes bundle with three bonus packs that look like they'd ruin your progression, as well as another art book that is only available during launch deal. I can't possible justify that as a purchase, but if you are hardcore about Ys art, maybe that's for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Ys X Nordics brings lots of new stuff to the table and is the 1st installment of the duo/pair system that replaces the party system we had with VII, VIII and IX.It's also the 3rd Adol's adventure right after Ys I and II, so Adol is quite young and we even have Dr Flair from Ys II (and Dogi of course)What i love about this game:- The combat system feels great and the duo system allowed Falcom to polish further attacks and moves used by Adol and Karja.- Ys X Nordics is vast and offers a big and rewarding world to explore that'll take you 50+ hours.- This is a modern Ys formula, i always liked what they brought with 7, 8 and 9, meaning a more story driven and characters driven approach to the story, it's still here in X (i still like oldies too, but they're not the same type of game to me).- Great music as always, while Falcom purists may say it's not the best because well team JDK is in a dire state to say the least, we have to give credits where it's due and Singa pulled some nice tunes, still, Unisuga is just missing once again.- New graphic engine, it's still nowhere near AAA titles but who cares, everything is crafted with care and we have improvements from the previous engine used in 8 and 9: better character models, full motion cutscenes.- Good PC port (minus HDR, you'll need a reshade mod for that because the implementation is flawed).- It's f*king Ys, if you're looking for fast paced action adventure RPG... look no further.What let me down a bit:- The naval combat: it's enjoyable once you upgraded your ship a little bit, but the start can be quite tedious.- The pacing: Ys usually excels at pacing combat, story and RPG aspects, here it's still good but i expected more: some island you explore can feel a bit out of place or short in length.- I would've liked more background story on Dogi and Dr Flair's reasons to follow Adol, this was the time to connect the dots!!My personal take:I still prefer the party system over this new duo system despite its advantages, just for the sole reason of having more variety in the combat gameplay and "main" characters that used to be very well developed as Falcom never fails to do, in Ys X we have this feeling that outside Karja and some few other characters we just have secondary characters development.But that's just a minor issue to me, Ys X is great and a breath of fresh air from IX that I also loved but felt a bit claustrophobic at times.Now the question... Is it better than Ys VIII? Not quite, and I think Falcom will have a hard time topping this masterpiece any time soon. Still Ys X is GOTY material, no doubt about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ys X: Nordics is the 10th establishment of the YS series taking place in between the previous titles of the YS series instead of a continuation of YS 9. First off the pricing was a bit absurd as it felt like a 40$ game at best for the base content, while the ultimate edition stretched all the way to 130$. Additionally, not including content from the Japanese version was another take away (Karja Battle Dress) at the current time of the review, everything else in the Japanese version is included however. That is the main two pre-game issues before getting into the game review.The story content and side quests takes about a total of forty hours or so without achievement completion hunting. This time Falcom opted for focusing on 2 main characters rather than the expanded roster of main characters like in the previous titles. Their story is very well crafted as it feels like a brotherly and sisterly feeling. Though it feels like the side characters didn't get a lot of effort and it kinda gave the can ignore them but they still are slightly interesting vibe. Some of the time while on the side characters dialogues or quests was wanting to get back to the main characters story progression instead. So ultimately your getting a game about 2 main characters who have a deep story arc. At the start of the game it is very slow and you can't even open world explore either until Chapter 4. Something new they tried this establishment was allowing Adol to finally get his own boat. Boating feels extremely dull until the late game chapters when exploring the waters. The boat is ridiculously slow, but the game gradually opens up ways to speed up your boat and make it more tolerable. Naval combat was alright, most of it was very repetitive. That said leading onto the next point this game has a lot of repetitiveness, especially during the boat areas of the game. The dungeon system is linked to the water exploration as they appear as islands you need to free in order to clear them. More or less it feels extremely lacking in terms of what YS8 offered in the dungeon setting diversity. The enemies in this game are also repetitive as you end up facing the same types of enemies called "Griegr" for the whole game. Dialogue had a tiny bit of repetitiveness as they used "for real" too much and it felt like they could've used other words in those places instead. That's pretty much it in the repetitiveness department. At the time of this review, weapon models do not change either expect the final weapons you get in late game. So there are only 4 weapon models. Which was slightly disappointing. One of the main highlights was the combat system as it provided many ways to expand how you want to traverse the game and you can customize your preferred stats in any way you'd like with the release line. Even though recommending this game it just felt disappointing than what YS8 and YS9 offered on the table, music too was kinda not there like previous titles, still passable however. It felt like the developers just focused on the 2 main characters for the whole game development period and forgot about what makes a YS game a YS game. For now leaving it at a 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Y's game for the book.  Definitely a fun game, but it definitely felt like it falls short of the same quality you get from previous game iterations.This one is placed in between leaving Esteria (Y's 1 and 2) and before getting to Celceta (Y's 4).Overall its a good story with good music, but I feel the whole ship combat and ship exploration were mediocre and gets boring really fast.  If you remove the ship travelling segments, then the game would be probably much shorter than previous iterations of Y's game, which just makes me feel as if ship movement was intentionally slow to drag out play time / cover the fact that this felt like a shorter game.Combat mechanics have changed from previous iterations with the removal of slash, pierce, and blunt damage types, but the skill system largely remains the same.  Flash move and flash guard now no longer cause slow time when triggered, which I like as a change, but one thing should be noted is that you can trigger flash move by just having the dash button held down when hit by a blue attack (no longer needing to time a perfect dodge), which I'm not a fan of.  But even with that, its still fast paced and fun to play.Like all Y's games, this one is a standalone without needing to play others in the series to get into it, and I would still recommend it to people who like this style of ARPG.

_childDocuments_.review: Another charming entry into the Ys series.  Not as pretty as 8 but better than the bland grayness of 9.  I enjoy the tighter party system compared to some of the others (7 & 9 esp.) where you ended up having a platoon of playable characters and benching most and only using them for specific parts that required them.  Karja undergoes some remarkable character development from bland, stereotypical "me sea raider!  Balta strongest!" like in the trailer to a much more approachable, not going to say "gentler" bc the girl loves a good fight but she's able to see the problems with how things currently stand and is kinder to people she would have held in contempt earlier. Sea travel/combat, as others have mentioned, is rough at first. Your ship will need several upgrades to feel anything like the Jackdaw from AC:BF, but that's an in-story thing as well - this ship was in drydock for decades and it's a not-so-minor miracle it didn't sink the first time she touched water again. Once you do, though, you can start mowing down enemy vessels like a fully-upgraded Jackdaw, and that feeling was good.Combat's fun, though it can be kind of basic if you play on Normal - "Block" covereth a multitude of sins in this game. Holding it causes Adol and Karja to dual-attack the target, and as long as you don't overextend or go somewhere the enemies are ten-twenty levels above you the two of you are essentially "the enemy runs face-first into a buzzsaw" and it can be ludicrously fun. You can fight singularly except for blocking if you prefer, and your partner will engage a different enemy so you don't get swamped.Overall, Ys Nordics is in my top 3 - 8, OiF and now 10 pushing Origins out. Will play again sometime.

_childDocuments_.review: Eh, bit torn between recommend or not.On the one hand it's a decently fun game, on the flip side the story is filled with everyone having mommy/daddy issues and cliché galore, the ship is extremely slow so the game showing "You can start exploring with the ship" only to lock you into a wide corridor with invisible walls feels misleading.I feel like it's initially super fun, but it quickly gets dull - Combat is extremely repetitive and doesn't switch anything up (You can one-hand 99% of fights since all you need is block button and attack button, movement is overrated)The ship feels out of place for Ys games, this title always was high pace with tight controls and challenging fights. Sitting on my hands waiting for a ship to slowly lug itself across the map and getting constantly blocked from exploration by invisible walls is plain dull and kinda frustrating.The high-octane gameplay from old Ys games feels like it just never found its way back into the game.I don't even do fights or explore anymore at this point in the game, bosses are just perfect block, riposte, rinse repeat - You don't need exp or upgrades for it. Kinda wish exploration gave proper rewards like older Ys games.If you try to play high octane á la the old games you just get destroyed because neither dodge nor block animation cancels your basic attack animations. It's just not worth doing anything else than riposte pretty much. Or big skills with slow timing. It just feels pseudo turnbased.The Ys I remember gave you permanent upgrades in secret little hideout locations, progression items etc., this is just you get the same item over and over and over and over again, the only thing that changes is its tier quality.Personally highly disappointed by the Ys title. As a separate game where you want a lot of whining about parents and family drama it's probably a decent buy. Don't get why so much conversation got added if all of it is the same daddy/mommy issue for every single one.Just feels meh, all of it once you realize how dull and repetitive the combat and story is.Wish story had a bit better writing, most events feel shoehorned and makes no sense really from the "Big bads". The main story writing is very clumsy for having so much dialogue in it.Disappointed, but it's not a straight up bad game. Just really really not a proper Ys game. Think ultimately I would still recommend it, it's a pretty cozy game - Just don't expect Ys.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: It's YS Series we are talking about. I will die supporting this series as long as it keeps going for the rest of my lives.For this entry, they took a special approach compare to previous entries, and I like every moment of it.Combat is the smoothest it has ever been. Story still kept me engaged. NPCs that are lovable and interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Not an impresive technical game, but it is still pleasant to explore the world with Adol. I have much loved the 8's episode less the 9 as this one. The introduction of ship battle is refreshing, but the battle system is a little tricky to master as your will mainly have a duo and will have to swith between duo and single attacks to refull your action points. Music are great, story is good, no bugs encountered.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a great entry to the Ys series, I had loads of fun. But with every entry with major changes, it comes with a lot of flaws that need to be worked on. I didn't care for the ship combat, and I believe they butchered evading a bit too much with their heavy handed focus on guarding. On the other hand I greatly welcome the departure from the weapon triangle based party system. The duo system felt fluid and the updated skill system adds an incentive for varied skill usage. I can't wait to see how Falcom improves on these new systems in the games to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm liking it, the new combat system works nicely, after a bit of getting used to it. Story and characters so far keep me interested, wonder how the team dynamics will proceed. There's only been one boss so far that's been a bit annoying, but one you have the pattern, it's mostly a question of patience. Besides that one, combat has been fun and dynamic, as expected from Ys.Performance, graphics and options are good, as expected from a title that Durante has worked on.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: - Too much water, literally. (Waaaay too much water both story and exploration)- Incoherent storytelling.- Annoying antagonists.- ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ plot out of nowhere interrupting the flow of the story.- Confusing combat mechanic when you only have 2 character in the party.- Confusing "release line" system (What is the point of this system in the first place, I wonder...)Ys game has never been so uninspired, unfun, with an uninteresting story like this.This is the first time where Adol don't get to be a destined hero to save the world like in the previous entry. You feel like you going to be that person, but nope. The villain will lead you there instead and you have no choice but to follow him (╯°□°）╯︵ ┻━┻The abrupt ending of CelcetaOr the monochrome Reshade Monstrum Nox is so much better than thisThe combat feels...off when there are only two people in the party as you almost always have to press RT to enter "Duo mode" to fight anything in this game ...it is more quicker and more effective, and you don't lose anything in doing so too. There is little to no incentive to fight in solo mode so all the unlocked skills is practically useless. The game engine clearly designed with a party of 3 or more people in mindBut then this is like a budget cut version of something trying to be Ys8 again but failed miserably.Also, It is like the team cannot decide whether they want the game to be before or after the event of Ys9 with the portrait character clearly showing teenage Adol but the actual model of him is so adulthood you will think this event happened after Ys9Still... recommended just for the Adol story (But please set you expectation very low)
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good story, characters and music. Pacing felt really good and not once did it feel tedious to explore the map and complete side quests. Ship combat is fun and new upgrades are always exciting, but its quite simple and not the main focus of the game.Ground combat is where the game really shines. Just keep in mind to use Adol for damage and Karja for breaking shields and freezing. Skill chains are your best friend, and duo mode should only be used to perfect block and make use of the revenge gauge damage multiplier.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: A very good game that kept me enterteined for a long time. I enjoyed the story and Karja is one of my favorite Ys Series characters ever, I even hope she'll be back in another future Ys game. However, having just two main characters felt like something missing. More playable characters would be cool and surely more costumes to choose from. That said, the thing that bothered me the most is that the gameplay and scenarios are a bit too repetitive. It would be nice to see more diversification. As for the graphics, they improved but I'm still hoping we can get something like Tales of Arise or Trials of Mana for future games.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Ys X: Nordics is easily one of the best entries in the Ys franchise. The fast-paced combat is exhilarating, offering a satisfying mix of strategy and action that keeps you engaged from start to finish. The music is absolutely phenomenal, staying true to the series' signature style while offering new, memorable tracks that perfectly complement the adventure.Exploration in Ys X is a great, with vast environments that make you want to dive deep into every nook and cranny. It’s a real treat to uncover secrets and discover hidden treasures. While the graphics may not be the most cutting-edge, this is a small issue in the grand scheme of things, especially given how much effort the developers put into everything else.I highly recommend this game to any fan of the Ys series, or anyone who loves fast combat, great music, and immersive exploration. It’s a must-play!
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: The latest title in the YS series actually certainly delivers more of the fun gameplay that you've come to expect from the series. This title even introduces nautical combat which is a neat addition to the gameplay. They simplified the party rotation by limiting it to two playable characters this time around, but that just keeps things simpler when you aren't juggling two whole parties worth of characters to level and all that like you had in YS 9. Its a definite must grab for fans of the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Ys universe ever since i played Ys VIII several years ago and now i got to play the latest game from the series and it delivers. The game has rich story with so many side quests that you can easily explore with some reasonable challenge. The game has also many mini games that are fun to play. Really recommend this game for people who loves good story and adventuring the open world
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked previous Ys games, you'll like this. Exploration is fun, Combat is fun, characters are fun, the world is fun, the story is fun - I normally never play Side Quests or do stuff besides the Main Story in JRPGs. Only here do I somehow care and want to do it all, I can't explain it better than that.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Every part of this game that isn't playing the game is the best in the series. Story, characters, and all that. Yes, even better than Ys 8. It's really good. Well, maybe not the music. But the musics still quite good.However, it's also a game that you have to play and in that regard it's the worst Ys game in a good long while. The sailing is not fun - they really captured that feeling of boredom while waiting to arrive at your destination. The combat is also not very good by Ys standards. At first it seems like there's plenty of options, and that it will be more skill based than the last few due to a lack of animation cancelling. In reality it turns out you just hold block while attacking and that solves 90% of the problems. It's very one-note and tedious.So overall it's a fine game, but far from great. Middle of the pack in the Ys series, perhaps slightly above average compared to other action-rpgs.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: A good Game  in the Ys series , really like the duo of Adol and Karja .Graphics are nice  , Story is good and enjoyable but not the best in the series .Combat is ok (blocking is nearly always king) , Ship Combat is weird but doable .I liked Ys VIII: Lacrimosa of Dana and Ys IX: Monstrum Nox a bit more but this one is still good . After finishing the game at the 54 hour mark.I say it is 8.5 /10
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Falcom once again delivers with Ys X what I've always loved about the series. It's just an all around good time. There is a certain amount of innocent fun that comes with Ys. From it's easy to pick up and exiting action game play to it's sometimes awkward and humorous dialogue, It's just simply fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Many, myself included, regard Lacrimosa of Dana as the best Ys game of the series.Well, for me, Nordics just clinched the throne together with Dana's tale.Where to even begin?!The tale of what happened to Adol and Dogi on their way to Celceta from Esteria is one hell of a ride.Storywise it's perfect.Great progression. Sweet pacing. Adol may be the semi-silent protagonist we know, but his interactions with everyone continue to cement him as my favorite JRPG hero of all time.And what amazing development and depth to the characters that tag along on his journey through those wild seas!Each and every character that forms the cast 'n crew of this game has their story to tell, both endearing and often tragic (Rafe, I feel you, bro); and all of them enrich the tale of Adol's adventure in the Obelia Gulf, two characters in particular stand above and beyond the others:Karja Balta is, together with Dana Iclusia, my favorite Ys heroine. The two of them are awesome characters in their own unique ways. I swear, the way Karja meshes with Adol and the crew, through calm waters and stormy seas, through bright times and tempestuous tribulations makes her such a compelling Norman Princess, who lives by the shield and the ax, fighting together shoulder to shoulder with her Shield Brother through thick and thin. I love her story.But especially THAT character. That one character who, by the end of the game won my admiration, and that of everyone of the cast is the perfect addition to the many amazing acquaintances our dear Red-Haired Adventurer has crossed paths with.VERY well written. I salute you.I love this tale. As much as I love Dana's tale.Gameplaywise...The new twist given to Adol's adventure with him and Karja fighting together is, in and of itself, a really fun way to work on a tangent to the now classic Ys battle system. So fast, dynamic, and addictive. Those duo techs! Beautifully crafted and executed, especially during those awesome climatic battles against those ultra cool bosses.But if there is one surprise jewel of gameplay that Falcom created, it's gotta be the ship combat!Yes, it is relatively simple in appearance, but SO. ENJOYABLE (it has a fully traverseable, interactable WORLD MAP! How I've missed a proper World Map!, Thank you, Falcom). The Sandras handles like a charm and is a force to be reckoned with. The Raids in particular are THE best.And while I can't wait to see the regular land combat battle system implemented in an eventual remake of Ys V (the only one of the old Ys games yet to be remastered), it is this game's particular ship combat system the one thing I hope Falcom develops further and makes into the core gameplay of a new franchise.I'm not kidding. This game's ship combat DESERVES to be built upon and taken to the next level: airship/spaceship combat (the "land" part of the Raids could be either mech or regular land combat, I drool at the possibilities!).It is how I wished Skies of Arcadia's ship combat were, and in Falcom's hands, with their skill to integrate it flawlessly into the narrative of the game... a whole new franchise could be created.No. A whole new franchise NEEDS to be created around it.Soundwise...It's Walhala.Crisp sounds that make the journey enjoyable.Stellar voice acting (in Japanese, I always play my JRPGs in their native language). Though I have to say, hearing Grenn's Japanese voice... great choice. No other Seijuu (Voice Actor) could've been better. You'll know why as soon as you meet the chap and see his story unfold.And Music that charms the heart! Team JDK continues to consistently be the gift that keeps on giving banger after banger after banger.Not just the classic fast-paced, guitar-shredding action tracks, but also the calm, sad, tense and happy tunes.In particular, Mitsuo Singa's "Those Who Live in the Distant Sea". That tune, with its longing flutes and plucking strings... Perfection! i find myself whistling it constantly.Replay Value.Guaranteed.To me, there are now THREE Ys games I play over and over again: Lacrimosa of Dana, Nodrics, and Ys Seven. Those are my Ys Holy Trinity.Verdict:This is what JRPGs should be. Games, and in particular, stories like this, are why I love fantasy.For me, Trails through Daybreak and Ys Nodrics are my GOTYs.I'm so sad this great adventure came to an end, but I know Adol Christin will strike again. Sooner that we expect, ready to take us into another epic journey.'Till then.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: A great and fun game, it has an enthralling history and many things to discover, the only thing is that outside the bosses the fights gets repetitive towards the end of the game Pros:-quick paced fights -interesting side characters -interesting storyCONS:-a LOT of back tracking-farming and combat gets repetitive towards the end game-can miss some trophies if you miss some conversations
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice fresh entry in Ys series that tries something different from previous party based Ys. The new combat feels really good and the exploration aspect is still fun. That said the ship combat is more annoying than fun and the story and characters aren't as good as Ys 8 or 9. Ys X still offers a pleasant overall experience and I hope that falcom will refine their new formula in Ys XI.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Another fun entry in the Ys series. Way more cinematic and as you go on the bosses get a lot of cooler and flashy. Falcom has really progressed in framing cutscenes to not just be static over the years which is great to see.The biggest issues I have are the massive lack of regular enemy variety and how awful the ship segments are. It takes a very long time in order to get the ship to not be a droll to play through. In general the sailing around is kind of filler more than anything. The only reason you really need to ever fight the open sea enemies is if you care about the 300 ships/pillars destroyed achievement. Aboardage is worthless and gives next to nothing for the effort. When you go back into NG+ to pick something up you might've missed they take all the upgrades away and you get reminded about how utterly slow and boring the ship content is.Played through on Nightmare and the game was overall easy if you relied and use Revenge and Duo Mode properly. Also you can pretty much always revive a downed party member if you immediately start reviving when it swaps over as you get invincibility frames.If you're on the fence about getting it then maybe wait for when it drops to 40 bucks but it was an overall fun 30 hours of play. It's all straight forward but if you care about getting everything done in 1 playthrough there are 10 missable Quests and 2 missable Person Entries (1 is very easily missed. Personally had to go back through to get just that 1 thing). Everything else is pretty much shown on the map and hard to miss.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: This is the second YS game I have played, I have always been a big fan of Falcoms Trails series and loved the stories and combat in those games, but this completely blew me away on everything, the graphics, the storytelling, the awesome characters (a bit cliche but loved all of them) and the absolutely amazing music that I started listening to before it even released in the west. Everything is just perfect in my opinion. It took quite a bit of time to get used to the weird control scheme they had but when you figure it out, it just becomes such an insanely satisfying combat system that lets you do really cool stuff, to this day I still feel like the parrying system is the best in an ARPG, it has such weight behind it and the counter attacks you do are really cinematic.Overall I would give this a 9/10, I would've given it a 10 but I really wanted more bosses with those awesome QTEs and crazy cutscenes, this was really a new peak for Falcom for me and I am very excited for Daybreak 2 and Kai.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: i do not enjoy the changes to the combat system, the boat is waaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaay too slow, and naturally your friend's ai is trash. Thanks to technically having two health bars, falcom has also made bosses do way more damage as well since you can now revive after getting to 0 hp. It's really not enjoyable if you get in a bad spot to be revive spamming. Probably the last ys game I buy, unfortunately. 9 was an incredible game that improved on everything that made 8 great. Go play those 2
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: The GoodAmazing experience, I've only played Ys 8 and a bit of Seven but X is on par with 8. I enjoyed Karja a lot as a co-lead, she's as good as Dana from 8 which surprised me. Adol is also very likable here though I think the game does a disservice to him by not giving him actual voiced dialogue in cutscenes. The story is quite predictable but it's done well enough and gets an emotional reaction as they do a really good job in making you like each and every single character. Also, the OST is 11/10 but it's expected from these Falcom games. The BadThe start is so very slow, the game doesn't pick up until you finish chapter 2. There's also quite a lot of yapping in the beginning which makes it even worse. After you get through the slog, the game is consistently good. Sea exploration is also slow at the beginning and you really want to get those mana sails upgrades, makes the experience so much more smoother. One of the permanent upgrades, the mana sense, should also be a toggle since it stays on for just a short duration and if you're 100%ing the map like me you need to press it every 2 seconds.Amazing game, with a good story and even better characters and music. Also, one of the best final bosses of any JRPG I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say that as an Ys game, Ys X is 1 step forward and two step back.  It's a fun action game from start to finish, but I didn't enjoy much of the new stuff.  The story was sub-par, even for an Ys game's standards.  The vast majority of the minor characters are just plain annoying.  Luckily, the main characters that revolve around Karja are generally interesting and well acted.  I'd avoid going for the 100% like I did.  It likely detracted from the enjoyment I got out of the game.  Still worth a purchase though, IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Beginning is pretty slow, especially the ship parts, it could do better there, especially for Ys veterans. Environmental variety is also very low, the vast majority of areas are either grassy island, or rocky island. It's understandable enough with the setting of the game, but especially since there's an icy area and also a Volcano, and we don't get to explore those save for one really small "hot spring" island, it's a shame.Still really fun though. I felt really attached to the characters and crew, the new party system I wouldn't say is "better" than the previous games but it was a nice little pivot, and everything else was at least meeting expectations
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game and a great entry in the Ys franchise. Goes in a different direction from the past few entries with its experimental dive into co-op and an attempt at naval combat. With what hiccups it has, it easily makes up for with its strengths. Would highly recommend whether you're new to Ys or you've been a longtime fan - It's all out of chronological order anyways, so now's a great time to dive in.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: This is a amazing game for the series easy a 10/10 for meThe story really got me hooked, the character are amazing the gameplay is smooth. The ability for the adol and karja were kool . The ship fights were fun and the upgrades really cool especially the finals upgradesthe side story were great too i would so recommend this game to order people and to people who love the series as a whole
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you so SO much falcom for making this amazing game and bringing the english version of Ys x to steam so fast!!This is definitely my new favorite Ys game to me personally its even better than Ys 8 in most aspect.Let me explain, My first Ys game is oath in felgana on PSP but back then im not a Ys fans and I dont even know what king of game Ys is, but on PC i started playing Ys 7, memories of celceta , 8 and 9. after that I became a fan of this game with Ys 8 as my favorite,but i realize something after playing Ys x, the party system on the other Ys games are so bad, 1st you are forced to change character depending on the monster weakness and sometimes the other characters are so bad to use (slow, low damage, or having a useless skills),2nd they give you too many characters, you can only use 3 anyway (1 for each weapon type) and one of them wll definitely will be adol so the other slash type characters are useless, unless on specific condition like in Ys 8,3rd if you try to use all of the characters let say you wants to 100% the game so you will have to use all the other characters, you have to manage all of their equipments swapping arround armors and accessories it is super annoying sometimes.And so after playing this game and looking at the other older Ys title i think Ys games are better with solo (like the olde title) or duo (like this game Ys x) and especially  duo in this game you just need to switch to one other character rather than to cycle through 3 character to swap to correct weapon type for monsters weaknessYs x also introduce a whole new combat system, you have solo mode (moves faster but less damage dealt) and duo mode (move slower but more damage dealt), they removing the broken flash move and guard with something even more interesting which are guard counter and dash counter these new mechanics are even more satisfying if you manage to pull it off and the window for these counters are more generous and if you manage to land the counter you are rewarded with revenge gauge which will multiple your damage to 5(max) times normal (outside of critical).Exploration is still there but its more of a sea exploration than a land exploration which is not that bad to be honest, sea combat also a fun little addition and also giving a great reward if you're lucky.Story is great there are some plot twist and a lot of heartwarming stories about "Family".I really recommending this game if you like action RPG games and especially if you're a Ys fans and i believe after you played this you will agree with me that future Ys games only need 1 or 2 playable characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! I don't think it's as good or as interesting as Ys 8, but it's still really good. The combat is nice even with the overemphasis of guarding, and I really enjoyed the story. Each time the game threatened to get stale I thought the story did a good job upping the ante. I finished in about 45 hours so it didn't overstay its welcome either. Ys almost never repeats characters, but Karja was awesome, would love to see her again.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom Line:Interesting attempt to introduce layers of decision making (instead of solving every problem with flash dodge or flash guard, doesn't matter which), but Duo System needs A LOT of work. Pick this up on sale if you love Ys.I enjoyed my time with Ys as always, however Falcom seriously needs to wake up. I would like to see Ys evolve as Trails has. Graphically, this is a very incremental upgrade over the previous games, and given the fact we have "lost" several playable characters, I don't understand the lack of weapon models. They never change until the the end of the game with ultimate weapons.Somehow the combat is more complex than the flash party systems, since you can't use one defensive option to solve 100% of problems, but at the same time it somehow feels simpler and easier. Not to mention the Duo system eliminates one form of jank and exchanges it for another.I really feel like Ys needs a much more radical change and reinvent itself. I understand there is no going back to the true glory days of top down battle, but flash party, as fun as it is, is overplayed, and this duo system is just not it. Not in the current form.I am not a Singa hater, so the OST gets a thumbs up from me, great tunes all around. Characters were easy to get invested in, and while the main story isn't anything world redefining or mindblowing, it is very personal and satisfying.Narratively, X feels very much pulled out of the hat, and Karja seems incredibly important to Adol after experiencing this journey together. Which makes it so strange that she was never ever mentioned or alluded to before. The setting makes no sense with regards to the location on Eresian map. It really should have been in the Baltic Sea, oh well, I guess they needed to put it between Esteria and Celceta, since they crammed it between 2 and 4.These are nitpicks, but I have come to expect a lot from Falcom's narrative and this feels like an unnecessary step back.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: It is better than Ys IX (not a high bar in my opinion) but not as good as Ys VIIIThe Ship at the beginning of the game is slow as hell and a drag to exploreI didn't care much about the story but the ending is pretty nice I guessI recommend picking this up on a sale if you're interested. Otherwise just go play Ys VIII
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good game. Pros: The story is fantastic, the world is very interesting and the combat is enjoyable when its challenging.Cons: Lack of enemy variety weigh down the gameplay and too many systems that are just shallow puddles that could have been omitted or blended with each other to make something interesting. (Mostly the crafting, skill trees, and stat potions.)
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: I seem to be in the minority of fans that liked Ys IX, lemmie say that right now.The new two-person party mechanic feels nice and different, allowing for big hits when you want or need them. However, they're too useful, I found myself using only them from about 30% of the game onward.I played on Hard.The main boat members were kinda boring, all said and done. Grenn was especially annoying. Or so I thought, then I changed the VA to Japanese. Suddenly, most of the annoying voices, like Grenn and Adol's weird Persona Navigator-esque barks, were not nearly as bad. I like how they characterized Adol, he seemed appropriately 'doe-eyed' and fresh to this whole 'adventure' thing, seeing as how this is, chronologically, his third adventure.Soundtrack, while good, wasn't as good as previous entries.I hope we have a Ys 5 remake using a revamp of these mechanics coming next.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: h2] not flawless, great focus [/h2]Game is fun, laidback hack'n'slashing untill the bosses humble you, play at least hard and if u played ys games before do not use the hero cape because its too op.The game gets harder if you rush through everything, the opposite is true as well. The game gets easier if you take ur time and loot everything.

_childDocuments_.review: The music was mid since it was filled with Singa music. One Unisuga track, I counted maybe 3 Jindo pieces, a few good ones from Koguchi who seems to be getting better, and typical Sonoda music thrown in. The music in the series is definitely getting worse and will continue to get worse if F Corp keeps outsourcing to cheap musicians.Really nice art style when in a field or town, but my god, island textures looked terrible when on the boat, breaking my immersion. You can tell this was made for the Switch.Story was solid, one of the best in the series. Karja seemed to completely overshadow Adol, but still, Adol got some quality development, especially if you consider the hidden runestone in the epilogue.For the first time, I played a Falcom game localized by NISA where the localization wasn't terrible for the first 6 months. They must have really stepped it up, as I didn't notice any typos or any weirdly formatted text. I 100%'d the game and talked to every NPC when there was new dialogue too.Maybe I'm in the minority, but the combat just wasn't doing it for me. I prefer the combat of Ys VIII with perfect dodges and guards. The naval combat was also really, really bad. _childDocuments_.review: Another adventure in Adol's book. This time, he and a Norman pirate / viking girl named Karja become bound together by magic cuffs, which don't allow them to move more than 10 meters away from each other.Compared to other Ys games I played that give multiple playable companions as you progress the story, this game only gives you Karja as your other option, and it seems to be a positive change to the story formula of Ys. Before, in Ys VIII and IX, some characters had limited screen time since they had to compete with Adol and 4 other characters. That somewhat forced them to be side characters. Karja, on the other hand, feels more like another protagonist. But why is it so important, and especially with Karja? Because she is an amazing character, a viking with a power to go berserk, which sometimes results in her attacking Adol. She also (not very often and mostly in the early game) talks about killing innocent people like it's a completely normal thing to do (let's just call it her starting point). Overall, the energy that she brings is great, and I really enjoyed her interactions with Adol and other companions and enjoyed seeing her grow. Unfortunately, the bad thing of having only Adol and Karja as playable characters is that the gameplay doesn't get more interesting as you unlock new characters. And the focus on parry mechanic that this game has feels more like a let-down (this mechanic makes the gameplay easy) but overall, Ys X is a great experience and I'm glad I picked it up.
