_childDocuments_.review: I liked the gameplay changes and how this game is more challenging than the previous ones. The overall movement speed of both characters and enemies was slowed down a bit, and now you actually need to learn the bosses' attack patterns. In some previous Ys games battles were too chaotic and winning them was often times a matter of having a high level and spamming your most powerful skills, dodging an eventual enemy attack here and there.The fact that now your party has only two characters instead of three also helps a lot to make gameplay more ballanced.The dual characters thing adds some new mechanics to battles. Holding one of the shoulder buttons (I think default is RB but I changed to LB) makes you control both characters at the same time, which in practice increases your attack and defense (it's the only way to guard) while significantly reducing mobility. I'm not a big fan of it, I still prefer just playing normally as one character and leaving the other one to the CPU, but some boss battles requires constant use of the dual characters' combined attacks/defense so I had to deal with it.Sailing: Ys X has a mechanic where you need to sail a ship and explore the sea to reach new islands. Other than the novelty of it (for the Ys series that is) these parts don't really add anything fun to the gameplay, as when controlling the ship everything is slow and clunky (which is kinda expected). This basically serves as an extra step you need to do before reaching a new area where normal gameplay proceeds.Other than that this is still the Ys I know and love, which means running across fields/dungeons while listening to some nice original soundtrack.Speaking of that, the music keeps the high quality standard which is present in basically every game in the series.Graphics: I'm not someone who expects amazing graphics in mid-budget/AA games, and I'm not comparing Ys X to AAA games, I'm comparing Ys X to Ys VIII and Ys IX, and as such seeing little improvement from the previous games is the reason why I consider the graphics to be disappointing.My biggest gripe is with characters' 3D models, they look very bland when compared to their 2D artwork versions. Maybe they need some outlines/cel-shading to have a more "true anime" look? It's something Falcom should consider for the next game. Previous games already had those bland looking 3D characters and I was hoping they'd be improved in the next iteration, which didn't happen.Backgrounds are a mixed bag, some areas look nice while others have lots of obvious low-poly stuff around making them look like something out of a PS2 game. Maybe that's a side effect of the game being made to run on Switch, but still.I know Falcom will never reach AAA quality in terms of 3D graphics, but at this point I think they should have at least improved significantly when compared to their previous two games. So it's time for them to improve or preferably change whatever engine they've been using. Heck, even a small team of indie devs with enough experience in Unreal Engine (or even Unity) can make graphics more impressive than this.On a positive note, many animations like running and attacking have significantly improved, now they look more natural/less robotic.Technical aspects: the game ran just fine on my PC. It has all the graphics, sound and gameplay customization options you'd expect for a PC release. I played with an Xbox controller and was able to fully customize it as well.I've read that the original PC release was problematic, but as of the writing of this review most or all of these problems seems to have been fixed.Final score: 8 out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm fond of Ys game for some years now. Ys 8 was my favorite. I felt a real passion in it. Ys 9 was a good experience but not really inspiring me as much. Ys X re-ignited that passion at some point. Not at the start though, sadly. The start was about getting used to the new combat system, handling an extremely slow ship... Expect to be slug on the sea until chapter 4 at least. And the way sometimes the story will make you move for 20 seconds, have a dialogue on you, move 10 more seconds, dialogue again, etc... in the early stages of the game. That's kind of a slow start. I didn't mind it too much though, the game was still entertaining.Once you're past that though... Oh boy. I was conquered by the game. Completely! And don't make me speak about the final boss... My favorite final boss of all Ys games. I was obsessed by it for a few days.Gameplay: the combat system is similar to the usual party system but you have only Adol and Karja. Also it's more about blocking with perfect timed block than dodges. No you're not rolling into hazards to proc invincibility anymore and to be honest I'm quite happy about it. Of course it requires a time of adaptation but it's fine. Fights can sometimes be very cinematic with special cutscene on the first perfect parry of some specific boss attacks. Difficulty-wise the game feels a tiny bit easier than Ys 8 or 9 but not by that much.Story: Intriguing at first it got me pretty invested as I was going on. The story is very much centered about Karja though so it might depend on how much you'll like her. The thing is... I liked her at least as much as I liked Dana in Ys 8. So it got me good.  In term of side stories, I didn't care about the side characters that you pick up along the way as much as I cared about the ones in Ys 8. Music: As with pretty much every Ys game there are many bangers. Final phase of the boss fight got me even harder than A to Z... that says something!Conclusion: this game definitely be one of my favorite Ys games with 8 and Origin. I already managed two people to give a try to the whole franchise by showing some parts of it so I guess the game somehow clicks with a broad audience as well. I can only recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: YS X: Nordics is a game that shocked me on a few levels, as we all know the YS games have been prone to change over the years in terms of both gameplay and difficulty, it's honestly a mix of refreshing and yet jarring at the same time to see these changes but they usually make it work and honestly despite peeps who clearly enjoy dark souls difficulty games (which not all games have to be guys N gals it's okay not to be a souls like even if they are great) it's a game with some interesting and superb mechanics, maybe a little too many to a degree as I started to feel like I was playing Doom eternal there were so many options for combat! XD but suffice to say it's clear they considered this when making the game and toned it down a little on difficulty depending on how you play, overall though it's a blast of a game that seems to have taken a stronger note from Falcoms Legend of heroes series in terms of both aspects of the visuals and the people you interact with which is super welcome dood!Okay now the big review! So YS X: Nordics is a rather interesting point of the games chronology taking place after I believe the second game, (because why not!? XD) the gameplay is similar to the more modern YS games but with a couple of twists, for starters there's now a proper and more clear block, dodging works a little differently too in that perfect dodges only exist with certain attacks and give a decently powerful long range counter, perfect blocks are still there and can work on any attack, with three outcomes, on guard breaking attacks you just block without being broken, on normal attacks it knocks them off guard for a heavy counter attack and the last? We will talk about next with the main new change to the game dood!So The next aspect of battle is Duo, this is a totally new thing for the series in which you team up with the second character you play with to both guard and attack with you in tandem, they even have unique team skills! In the past and even here we were used to each characters individual skills but now we have ones that can be used in unison, at first glance they probably seem a lot weaker and more costly to use but you see there's an extra function to it, the revenge gauge! As you block attacks it fills up for up to 5x the amount of damage (more or less even depending on what you've used and certain aspects of the game) perfect guards will raise it higher which also as the third thing I was going to mention will also deflect and raise much higher on red attacks, which also will give you a one time per individual opponent awesome visual special counter for high damage! What a bonus dood! (make sure to do that and perfect dodges on bosses for cool visuals!)So we've talked about normal combat but let's talk about the sea combat, as the game progresses you get a ship! (rather quickly actually which is one of two reasons I am fine with mentioning it) Boat combat starts off really slow but as you unlock certain things it becomes pretty fun, it's not the easiest to control with all the buttons you can use along with the placement of them but once you get into it you'll be having a blast! Literally!! You can even board big ships, it's a slow burn but they did a good job of it in the long run dood.As you travel you can find many islands, treasure and a few other things that are far enough off that I won't spoil, making it feel like a nice sea faring adventure! Hopefully they can survive Adols terrible luck on boats!! The music for the game during travels and the various islands and dungeons is as usual great, really giving that sense of adventure, they even expand aspects of how you travel in the game, I do feel that one thing could have used a boost function even if it cost SP to do it but I'll leave it at that and say it just would have been a nice bonus dood.As for the story? It feels like they had a stronger focus on it and the characters around you than ever, they've done it before granted but it feels more in depth here to the legend of heroes standard in fact, characters feel really fleshed out, not just the main two protags, granted that does mean there's a lot of story to go through as well as adventure but what is an adventure if not one big story of someone's exploits? It really made the world feel as alive in it's own way as Zemuria in the legend of heroes titles dood.Quests are labelled nicely and will only really be missable if you don't look around or check the maps per chapter which is stellar frankly, I needed no guide really, the only shame thing that's missable are character entries, so take it from me, make sure to talk to them each chapter!! Well at least if ya want all the achievements dood.So yeah that's YS X: Nordics, it's a blast, it can be hard or easy depending on how you want to play but either way it's a really fun time and a great new adventure to the series, it's kind of a lot to take in at first but as you get used to the combat system you'll be killing things and having good times a plenty! I look forward to more in the future! Thank you for reading and if you decide to get the game I hope you have a great time too dood!

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic addition to the Ys series. If you enjoyed Ys VIII: Lacrimosa and Ys IX: Monstrum Nox, then you'll definitely have a good time in Nordics. The change to a 2-character party with the Duo Mode system is definitely a departure from the norm when it comes to combat and gameplay as pretty much EVERY mainline Ys title before this has been a 3-character party with several characters you can choose from as the story progresses as Adol's two combat companions. It's still very much classic Ys hack-and-slash combat but with a few tweaks to the formula; mainly in the form of parrying and certain attacks that you're can only respond to with a parry or only respond to with a dodge that gives the combat a bit more depth than just mashing specials (especially on the 2 highest difficulties.) And none of that is to mention the NAVAL SHIP-TO-SHIP COMBAT that is a first for the series, which is very intuitive and enjoyable, but you're not forced to do it so much that it becomes overbearing. Overall, as a fan of Ys 8 and 9, I quite enjoy this game. The graphics aren't going to blow you away, but the story is well written despite the typical cheesy anime tropes that Ys tends to be known for, which can be charming depending on who you ask. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Both Ys VIII and Ys X are now my two favorite games from Falcom. Ys X is in my opinion an amazing step forward for the franchise full of great innovations that I can't wait to see future entries build upon. At the same time, after IX's different vibe, it returns to what many fans enjoyed about Ys VIII in several aspects (mainly when it comes to storytelling and atmosphere). Unfortunately with one glaring issue related to poor environments due to I'd say obvious resource constraints. I think that will lead to some unfair comparisons between VIII and X in favor of the former, as this one specific weakness of X is one of the strongest aspects of Ys VIII.  But Nordics still provides an amazing cinematic experience thanks to the production values of its boss fights alone, which have become some of my favorites in gaming, period. I've just had so much fun with them. =======When it comes to Falcom games, I've played the entirety of the Trails series as well as Ys VIII & IX. And for me personally, Ys X ended up being peak Falcom, with one pretty big flaw keeping it from being the absolute peak. After the more mystery oriented Ys IX, this newest installment returns back to what made Ys VIII so popular, and that is the feel of adventure.Starting with the non-combat side of gameplay, you can expect the standard Falcom Ys fare. You progress a main story chapter, unlock a new area with a bunch of treasure chests, other collectibles and 2 or 3 side quests, rescue a new NPC unlocking a new shop or service in your hub and then again move on with the story. Repeat until the end of the game. The small twist on that formula this time is that instead of travelling between connected areas for this content, these areas are now separated islands between which you travel over the sea with your ship. And some of the exploration is moved from the land to the sea, supported by naval combat system. I think this feature is very much a matter of taste, personally I'm kinda neutral to slightly positive on it. It fits the setting and I had fun with it, but there isn't a whole lot of depth to it.Now the (standard) combat side of gameplay is what I absolutely loved. I very much enjoyed the completely new guard-based duo combat system and I think Falcom is very much onto something here. This might again be a matter of taste, as unlike in the last few games, you're no longer double jumping and zipping around as if Adol had too much sugar, spamming flash guards left and right. Instead, the fights are a lot more grounded (literally) and focused on blocking/parrying and evading at the right moments. As someone who'd put Ys VIII's action combat as one of my favorites ever due to its speed, the above description of Ys X's combat system might sound disappointing. But the reality is the opposite and I feel like it's just a straight up improvement. The fights still maintain their high speed, with the main difference being that they feel less "spammy". Instead of chain spamming flash guards and skills, with the occasional spamming of healing/res items whenever the previous failed, I was now able to avoid 95+% of the boss damage on Inferno via well timed blocks and dashes, and haven't even used healing items the entire game (you literally don't even get standard healing items on higher difficulties).The best part is that in combination with the two character based combat, all of this allows for extremely cinematic fights, full of very well made special mid-fight cutscenes for blocks on every important boss. It just flows extremely well and feels very satisfying. The final boss fight especially is among my favorite boss fights ever, if not my favorite, period. But most boss fights in Nordics are an absolute treat and the game's strongest point.As for plot and characters, we are moving away from IX's focus on an entire party (both gameplay & story wise) and going back to a more personal story about a central character, Karja, similarly to VIII's Dana. Dana is a fan favorite, but despite that, I've already seen many people claiming that Karja is up to par, myself included. Not even remotely a copy paste, she has a much different personality, and not all of this setting's lore revolves as heavily around her. Her dynamic with Adol is central to X's storytelling, even more so now that combat and exploration involves only these two and nobody else. And I think Nordics nailed it as well as it could have, taking into account that Adol is a silent protagonist. I really wish he wasn't in this case though, it's difficult to do engaging dialogues when you have only 2 main characters and one is a wall. But Karja is great enough to still carry that on her own.Now for that one biggest flaw. The enviornments. Like I mentioned, Ys X returns the series back to its core, and that is the concept of adventure. This is supported by one of the youngest versions of Adol, by the setting of the story and by the non-combat gameplay mechanics like sea & island exploration. But that "support" pales in comparison to the absolute disservice and the damage caused by the total lack of interesting and varied zones. You thought you escaped the gray dullness of Monstrum Nox's prison city? Welcome to the endless dark blue sea of sameness with grays and mildly saturated greens on the horizon.I could take a screenshot of any of the game's tens of islands, be it from the prologue or the penultimate chapter, and you literally wouldn't be able to tell them apart. The sea isn't much better. The fact that after the last two games, this one doesn't have vistas/landmarks as one of the collectibles perfectly sums up the issue. The environments/levels are simply dull, uninspired, uninteresting and worst of all repetitive. They completely kill the spirit of adventure, only reinforce the monotony of an already formulaic gameplay loop and make the player get tired of the entire setting faster. It is understandable given the size of the company and the many higher priority innovations that were done in this entry. But the lack of resources allocated to this aspect is immersion breaking and leaves a big scar on the overall positive experience, especially when adventure and exploration were supposed to be back on the menu.

_childDocuments_.review: ---{ Graphics }---☐ You forget what reality is☐ Beautiful☐ Good☑ Decent☐ Bad☐ Don‘t look too long at it☐ MS-DOS---{ Gameplay }---☑ Very good☐ Good☐ It's just gameplay☐ Mehh☐ Watch paint dry instead☐ Just don't---{ Audio }---☐ Eargasm☑ Very good☐ Good☐ Not too bad☐ Bad☐ I'm now deaf---{ PC Requirements }---☐ Check if you can run paint☑ Potato☐ Decent☐ Fast☐ Rich boi☐ Ask NASA if they have a spare computer---{ Difficulty }---☐ Just press 'W'☐ Easy☑ Easy to learn / Hard to master☐ Significant brain usage☐ Difficult☐ Dark Souls---{ Grind }---☐ Nothing to grind☐ Only if u care about leaderboards/ranks☐ Isn't necessary to progress☑ Average grind level☐ Too much grind☐ You'll need a second live for grinding---{ Story }---☐ No Story☐ Some lore☐ Average☐ Good☑ Lovely☐ It'll replace your life---{ Game Time }---☐ Long enough for a cup of coffee☐ Short☐ Average☑ Long☐ To infinity and beyond---{ Price }---☐ It's free!☑ Worth the price☐ If it's on sale☐ If u have some spare money left☐ Not recommended☐ You could also just burn your money---{ Bugs }---☑ Never heard of☐ Minor bugs☐ Can get annoying☐ ARK: Survival Evolved☐ The game itself is a big terrarium for bugsYs X Nordics, the latest installment of the Ys series where our protagonist, Adol the Red, sets out on another adventure and again, getting caught in the crossfire of whatever is happening there. In this case, he's trapped in a land run by Normans, a viking-like pirates, and demonic beings known as Griegr, while trying to uncover the truth behind their appearance. I'll try to keep it simple and highlight the main features. Battle mechanics will be divided into land and sea (ship).Battle (land): By far this has THE BEST Ys party-based battle mechanics. There are only 2 party members and Ys X softly highlights the role of each member. The fight features fast-paced hack and slash, and now some enemies have "shield" bar on top of health bar where you have to deplete the shield bar first to damage the enemy. The 2 members' role is softly divided into "main damager" and "shield breaker" where the latter has better skillset for breaking the shield bar. Unlike previous Ys series, the block and evade mechanics are now revamped. They no longer slows time but other than their general uses, enemies will have unique attack patterns where you need to utilize both block/parry and evade to counter-attack. Battle (Sea): You don't like Assassin's Creed because it's too slow, but you like fighting with a pirate ship? Ys X has that, and it is splendidly simple, allowing you to maneuver around with a pirate ship, and using various weapon loadouts, battling against other pirate ships. Love it.RPG element: Party leveling is simplified to 1 level for both characters, so no matter who you use, they will level up together so there's no stress of leveling each and every one of them. Skills are learned through level and skill masteries, and there are TONS of skills to use. Stats development are comprised of a mechanic similar to Final Fantasy X's sphere grid, where every 10 level you will open a few orb nodes and insert orbs with various parameter (ATK, BRK for Breaking shield, etc). Put the same type of orbs together and you'll have additional effects, and none are too game-breaking. You can also upgrade your ship's parameters to make it stronger.Graphics: It looks...dated. Compared to Ys VIII and Ys IX, Ys X looks straight out of a handheld console, suffers the same fate with how Monster Hunter Rise is treated as a port from Switch. BUT for me it is still lovely and the game's only 6GB in size. Although, for a game that is released on 2024 (2023?), I was expecting an upgrade from Ys IX.Story: Oh man, the story is full of twists and turns, the main characters aren't cliche, and side characters offer a lot of depth to how everything runs in the world of Ys X Nordics and there are no corny ones. I keep forgetting how Nihon Falcom always has beautiful world-building. Dialogue feels impactful, and for me who always uses english dub for Ys X, I can honestly say Ys X has one of the best dubs, everything feels very emotional.Final Ratings: 8.9/10, I'd put this below Ys VIII storywise, but by no means is Ys X a letdown. Now I'm left with nothing again after I 100%'ed this game..

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game! Definitely one of my favorites in the series so far. The combat is a bit different from how the series was with other party games, but the improvement is one for the better. You can build both Adol and Karja to be more specialized to best utilize each of their playstyles (which are both very entertaining) and get the most out of both of them. The difficulty feels well-balanced, and it's largely a game of skill that challenges you to be thoughtful about your approach to battles. There's a ton to do exploration-wise, and going out of your way is usually quite rewarding! As for the story, it was fantastic hands down. I was gripped from start to finish- practically couldn't put the game down! This was also helped by the fantastic soundtrack to accompany it as well. Can't recommend this game enough to someone who wants to enjoy a fast, fun rpg with an emotional and gripping story!
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a few Ys games by now, Lacrimosa, Monstrum Nox, Celceta and now this one.Nordics was really fun.. I loved Lacrimosa and I think this game is tied with it for me. At first I didn't really dig the idea that we only had 2 playable characters but it grew on me quickly and now I adore Karja, she is a great character and she manages to carry the silent Adol easily, the secondary characters are also very nice.Weirdly enough I liked the whole ship idea, sailing and all, exploring the sea and reaching new isles was fun even if a bit slow at first. The story was good and kept me entertained, the combat is just what you expect from Ys with a few changes due to the fact that we only have 2 playable characters and the new duo mechanic. The game is very clearly not about graphics since that is its weakest point, the music was very good though and I enjoyed it.Be warned there's missables in this game! I would have 100% achievements if I didn't miss a People log in chapter 7 (curse you Lux), that being said there's not many of them. I feel like this game in particular leaned a little on the Legend of Heroes formula but it worked out fine imo. If you already know the Ys series and played a few of them before then yeah get this one, it's fun. If you don't know Ys at all and you are interested, starting with Nordics or Lacrimosa makes sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little JRPG, though it's piss-easy, especially if you do all the side content. Using your skills is the only real way to deal damage, and during skill animations you have hyper-armor and take massively reduced damage (<10%), so you can ignore most enemy moves and just cycle skills on them until they do a super move.Only exception is the hidden superboss that just covers the arena in heavily tracking AOE lightning making it impossible to stand still and actually hit the guy without getting stunned.The plot is pretty basic and rote, none of the twists are that hard to see coming, but the voice acting and general direction is good, so it's enjoyable nonetheless.Music is described by my girlfriend as "straight out of a sonic game", and it sometimes feels a little out of place, but it's usually fine.Graphics are relatively simple but very pretty, that makes it run great on a Steam Deck, which IMO is the perfect platform to play it on.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Ys Nordics is an excellent game if you're a newer Ys fan, but if you've been playing the series for a while like I have, you may have felt something just wasn't quite right despite the game being enjoyable. Though the setting has changed, the gameplay hasn't really budged from how it worked in Ys 8 and I think that's what holds the game back in my eyes.Everything from Ys 8 is still there: the character swapping, skill grinding, the base of operations, raids, exploration rewards, fish collecting to feed a critter, etc. I personally don't like that rolling for dodge slow-mo was replaced with "hold dash button to dodge blue moves", but having an improved block parry that's more rewarding is great. My biggest gripe is that as I play Ys Nordics all I can think is "I did this  in Ys 8 too". The "exact" part is the kicker; I love the gameplay loop of exploring and stumbling into challenging fights, but for example there was enough change in setting and type of challenge between Ys 1 and 2. Currently, Falcom is still rehashing the same minigames so we're still doing the same fishing quests, the same raids with only a thematic change, the same exploration of Nothingness™️ for Dogi Points™️, for the past three Ys games.One of the nice things about Ys Nordics is that they're trying to rein in the party mechanics. Managing 6 different characters that you may or may not use is overwhelming and you don't really get to use everyone fairly (for context I got all 6 achievements for exploring with each character in both 8 and 9) and the rock-paper-scissors counter system of attack types makes really large fights pedantic because you're constantly cleaning up chaff instead of doing anything skillful. At least with having Adol and Karja we're not stuck switching between counters for enemies all the time, and the duo attack system makes it easier to keep your AI companion in check.One of the lame things is that the gem & depth system is tedious to keep up with, and at the end of the day you can sorta skip past it by doing the old-school "buy the best weapons and armor you can and fully upgrade them" that the series has had forever. You get a bunch of skills through this gem tree so you do have to interact with it, and it's pretty easy to slot some gems in there that make sense and forget about it until you need to unlock some more skills again. Kind of a goofy system that doesn't really do anything for the game except be another feature that can be touted as "gameplay" because it impacts character stats.Falcom decided to start targeting the Switch as their default platform for release, but I don't think they've done the right prerequisite work art-wise to make sure that their art & asset direction scales up from Switch to PC. I double-dipped for the game and after playing it on the Switch and PC, I have to say that while the Switch version looks great and runs well for what the system is capable of, the art design limitations did not scale up well when played on my PC. There's something almost cheap-feeling about it versus something like Celceta which looks like it was designed for the Vita in mind but despite its origin platform still retains detail in its PC port.In turn, the music is as good as ever. There are also a few really great action setpieces and some of the bossfights are genuinely epic in scale. The supporting cast is as colorful as ever. . The final battle is crazy good and I like that they're keeping the "say goodbye to everyone" epilogue that gives everyone closure. Even though I like the extended interactions and character depth that Falcom's introduced into Ys, I've heard a few rumblings from friends who like the Ys games that the huge casts for the modern Ys games are overstaying their welcome. They yearn for a solo-Adol experience or at least limiting the co-op to Dogi. Gameplay-wise I think Falcom is falling into a trap where there are more systems and ways to approach combat, there are bigger fights vs mobs so the area of effect skills seem useful, and bosses are  bigger, but all of that is at the cost of interesting bosses and encounters. Increased boss sizes tend to turn into weird auto-correct fights where they'll swing and either their forward momentum will essentially dodge for you or they'll over-correct and still hit you. This doesn't really impact the difficulty of the fight except when you get free whiffs from the boss but it does take out a certain amount of control and strategy. At least I can say that Falcom learned lessons they'll never forget from from Dark Fact and Vagullion.At the end of the day, I still recommend Ys Nordics and will always try to get people into it. It's a great experience the whole way through but longtime fans may or may not take issue with a lot of the reused Ys 8 systems.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5 out of 10.One thing that Falcom does really well throughout the progression of the Ys series is that they are constantly trying to innovate the gameplay mechanics so that each game has its own unique feel. This title is no different, and the combat + exploration continues to undergo several changes.The party-based rock-paper-scissors approach to damage types and enemy vulnerabilities is gone, and is replaced with the dual character teamup of Karja and Adol. This time around, certain enemies can have a damage shield that must be depleted before they take damage to their health meter. Both characters dish out typeless HP damage and armor damage, but Karja is better at damaging enemy shields whereas Adol is better at dealing HP damage so you're encouraged to swap between them mid-combat. You can also easily enter and exit 'duo mode' where your character's actions are linked, you gain access to team-based attack skills with giant AOE effects, and Adol and Karja protect each other from incoming damage at the cost of slower movement speed.One major change to combat from past games is that holding the block/duo mode button will drop all incoming damage to 0 (as long as it doesn't come from certain special attacks that are obviously telegraphed), whereas in older games you had to hit that perfect block timing window to negate damage. However, you are still incentivized to block at the last second of an attack because it will make your next skill attack auto crit, and certain enemy attacks will stagger you out of your blocking stance unless you get the perfect block.The story also takes a slight departure from the typical Ys format: all the previous Ys games have had stories that involve Adol saving the world from existential doomsday threats, whereas this game takes the time to tell a more scaled down story that has a more personal touch to it. The stakes are still high, but this is a regional story with regional consequences. I found it a nice change of pace.The only thing that dropped this game down from a perfect score is the way the camera compensates very poorly when you're fighting a large enemy and you end up in extremely close quarters or up against a terrain boundary. Rather than making the terrain invisible to show both you and the enemy, it will zoom in so close that both you and the enemy completely disappear from view and you can't tell what's going on, or the camera will pan directly overhead and swing around wildly as the enemy moves about.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: While the previous entry left me disappointed, this one is at least as good as Dana or Celceta.Played the game once in the Nightmare difficulty, and it felt just right until the very end. Some boss took me some retries but did not feel impossible.The duo system with Break bar/Health bar make for a more interesting gameplay than the usual Pierce/Slash/Blunt with way more swapping character than usual.The Seafare is fun but let's be honest, not really challenging. Recapture mission are nice, I wish there were more.Overall, I enjoyed it a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Good addition to the series and probably the best PC port to ever be introduced into the series. Durante did an absolutely fantastic job with optimization as well as making sure FPS did not accelerate the game in unintended ways like previous ports had issues with.The game play is good once you get used to the whole duo mechanic. It took me a little to get used to it compared to the older games but it felt really good once I did. My largest complaint is that for the most part you cannot game over if a character goes due to having invuln during the forced character swap and if you just hold down the revive button 95% of the time you'll get off the revive. This leads to revive loops and hoping the one time you get it off you can just block or dodge. You can get super unlucky with enemy attack timing and get hit during that slight moment your char who's reviving becomes vulnerable and then you just kind of die (at least on nightmare). My biggest gripe is that it does not feel good to attack in solo mode versus duo mode but that might just have been a me thing. I found myself 99% of the time just attacking as a combo and then as the AA string gets close to done then I'd just find myself using my single skill.The story is pretty decent, very typical JRPG with a more dynamic ending. Some of the boss fights, especially the last one, are very well done and did not feel copy/paste of everything.Overall I'd give the game an 8.4, I really wish there was some post game content, you can 100% the game in a single playthrough which is nice but I would have just liked something.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: I played two chapters on hard and its too easy. I think the number one rule of this game is play on nightmare. It is very rewarding to learn all of the telegraphs and perfect block/dodge and learning how to use all of the combinations of skills. The game is very very forgiving you can hold the block or dodge button down or be rewarded by timing it better. I have died around 10 times, so this isn't coming from an elitist point of view. It doesn't feel that bad to die a bunch. The music is great like all YS games. The combat is extremely fun and the movement is the best I have ever experienced! If you just want to play the game and you don't want to go through all of the dialog you have the option to skip all of it. This game is what I have been waiting for!
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and well-made game that captures the feeling of adventure. The story and gameplay progression are very well paced with very little fat and you have a great degree of freedom to explore a surprisingly expansive map that I did not expect to see from a game with a file size that is just over 7gb. The ship combat is a bit slow at the start but quickly picks up after you begin upgrading the ship. The cutscenes, combat animations and general gameplay feel are a step-up from previous entries.Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off a bit slow but eventually turns into a good ol' classic Ys game where it's just straight up fun. The combat and mechanics this time around are quite a bit easier than usual though, which results in Nightmare/Inferno not really being that much of a challenge.The PC port is also excellent thanks to Durante/PH3 Games. The game itself has a few minor bugs, but nothing game breaking has been encountered. I just wish Falcom would take the next step in sprucing up their games already, because graphically this is nothing to write home about.Overall an excellent play. If you're not necessarily a fan of the Ys series but just want to play a solid action game, get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome Game!Without typing too much, awesome Gameplay and awesome story with good pacing, making you enjoy the ride from beginning till the end!If you're a fan of Gameplay similar to something like a more action-oriented Kingdom Hearts or Tales of Arise, you'll be in for a treat!Story isn't too overbearing, with good pacing, a cool team of characters who develop very nice over the course of the game.I'd very much recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: After going through 2 full playthrough session (Hard & Nightmare), safe to say that Ys X is my utmost favorite Ys title to date alongside with Ys VIII.The character dynamic between Adol and Karja is fantastic, the exploration at sea feels great, and the overall combat mechanic feels very fresh, yet familiar. In prior Ys titles, flash dodge tend to be my go-to when avoiding attacks. However, Ys X focuses more on perfect guarding and parrying attacks. The duo mechanic truly makes you feel like you are fighting as a team together. As such, the combat here feels very exhilarating especially on higher difficulties. Bosses provides a great challenge as well.Ys X is a bit more heavy on the story side, but overall it gives me a great satisfaction equivalent to that of Ys VIII. Overall, a fantastic Ys title and one that I would highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: It's the same Ys game I fell in loved it when I first played Ys Origin. With the addition of new systems like the sea battle and the duo fighter feature. Although I think it's been watered down from the combat experience of 8 and 9, where you have multiple options. But still, the music, fights, and the mechanics are still there. If you're a long time Ys fan or just a new one, I think it's a good place to start and continue. Let the music of the game hype you up from battle to battle.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing Ys game. My favourite battle system in the series together with the best final boss in modern Ys games. Great story. Fun exploration. PC port is great. Weaker points: side characters are less interesting than in previous games. The naval part seems a little too slow, especially in the beginning. Easy recommendation along Ys8 and Ys9.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing this on my steam deck and it's very optimized 60 FPS, though there are some fog and water scenery that makes it drop a few frames. Bosses battles the first chapters, takes a bit longer than I would have wanted on Hard. If you enjoyed Ys 8 or 9, you will love this game. Try the demo, it's quite long if you are unsure about buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: As usual, can always count on Ys for an action-packed good time.  Would recommend playing on harder difficulties to most as the guard feature has become notably easier to use.  Don't be put off by sailing in the early game - it is terribly slow and heavy but becomes a lot better after a handful of upgrades and mechanic unlocks.  Story is nothing special and voice acting is not the greatest, but I don't play this series for those aspects.  Probably stands with VIII and Origins as one of my favorite entries.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: I played Y's one on saga master system and have been a fan from that day to this one. I own them all, that said, Y's 8 was my favorite. Took until chapter 6 but this game has become a favorite, if not my favorite.  I payed full price for it and do not regret my decision. If you like Zelda and Skies of Arcadia this game is your dream come true.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Better successor to great YS 8 than YS 9 was. Slow starter with overloaded amount of mechanics and dialogues at start. Interesting boss fights don't happen until later half of the game. Story pacing however is on point and one of the better story in JRPGs I've seen in a while. Nightmare difficulty felt fair all throughout.Usually promising looking JRPGs are ruined by how repetitive game gets and how story just falls apart last ~30% of the game. This game I recommend because of last 30% of the game: Combat stays fresh, interesting map mechanics, and later boss fights make me want more. I was let down at start and excited by the time I finished the main quest line (They should've just dumped the sea aspect of the game and put those effort toward earlier dungeon/boss fights).Took 30 hours to finish all side stories and main quest on nightmare difficulty (for traditional Ys trophy, inferno balancing is way worse than previous Ys so I recommend nightmare). Probably won't bother to 100% as I couldn't really get into the world outside of main story and main characters. Biggest con is that I couldn't really relate to side characters or get interested in them as they brought little to no addition to gameplay/story, they were the repetitive part of the game actually.I want Adol to settle down for once Karja was great. Overall was a fun game would recommend 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Some things worked, some things didn't. It really felt like they were trying to recapture the magic of Ys VIII Lacrimosa of Dana.  and I think they did, for the most part. The story isn't as strong and the ship combat is a bit rough. There's also a lot more cutscenes in this game than any other Ys game. Maybe it's just been awhile, but 8 and 9 didn't seem like they were nearly as heavy handed with the cutscenes. Ofc, Ys is a series that barely relied on any cutscenes in the past. I think they could have trimmed a good 5 hours off and it would have been more effective.The combat system is a step back for me. There's a lot of stuff going on and it got too convoluted IMO. I appreciate they were trying something new, but it lacked the soul of the earlier games. You can hold one button to tank 90% of shots and only a few bosses really take advantage of guard breaks on you. This hot mess also came with a bizarre controller scheme, which I had to play around with to make it work for me. I think it's better than Ys IX (9) by default b/c it felt more like an adventure. Having Falcom's Trails series leak into this is not a good thing imo. 8 was the sweet spot, but it's getting too story heavy. and the story itself, well it's a bit tropey, to be generous. I think newcomers to the series are going to like this a lot more than long time fans, overall. It's a great action game that still holds that old school soul in a modernized package. It's hard to go wrong with any Ys game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: This is how you make an action RPG.  Simple, but effective comic book style graphics (low-poly even?) allow for complicated and fast paced action.  Hack and slash and collect and then get whomped by the boss.  And now there's pirate ship combat like AC4.Admittedly, I am a bit of a Falcom fanboy, but games like this are why.  To be honest, I was bit disappointed with Ys9 after how I much loved Lacrimosa of Dana.  But what I loved about the older Ys games, the exploration, the adventure, the fun characters, are all back here bigtime.  I always tell people Ys is like what I wish Zelda played like after number 3.  This entry continues to be what I wish Zelda played like.  Probably not true for everyone, but it is for me.PS: Please remake Faxanadu
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: In my top 3 of Ys games with VIII and Oath, Amazing game, love the Duo System, love the sense of adventure, only con is how there isn't much variety in locations, which makes sense because of the story but still, wish there was a volcano area or something to mix it up, either than that though I absolutely loved this game and it worked perfect 60fps on the steam deck
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: as a fan of this series, i like this game! (its a big step up from its last outing). gameplay is waaay better than when it was  originally released. Unlike the previous games however, the gameplay has been reduced from a 3 person team to a 2 person team. still not bad. my only problem i have is that there are a few glitches that i hope gets fixed asap. its mostly the load screen and sometimes the pause menu. sometimes the game will endlessly load when it transitions to a new area (i.e i fast traveled and it took so long to load that i seriously fell asleep during the game loading and woke up 2 hours later to it still loading) and sometimes pausing or going to the in game menu will sometimes freeze the game (or i should say the game freezes when you sometimes pause or try to access the in game menu), which really sucks when you have to access said menus to save. other than that its a great game
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Done and dusted!This is a good game: decent music, decent graphics, good gameplay, nice story, and some character growth is present as well. It doesn't overcome the sweet emotional damage incurred by Ys VIII, but there are nice plot twists nontheless. (Especially after dulling experience by recent Visions of Mana)
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Ys has done it again with a great tenth installment to the series. Placed after Ys I and II this adventure is mostly on boats (which is super ironic considering the rest of the series :). The cast was awesome and Karja makes for a great counterpart in combat which is insanely fluid. The story drew me in right from the beginning until the exciting end. This is a must have for Ys fans and I highly recommend others to try out this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10This is probably top 4 in the Ys series. It feels like they were trying to recreate the formula that they used for Ys VIII. Essentially you have a hub that you slowly build up and upgrade. A key part of upgrading this hub is to recruit new characters to it who will lend you their abilities and set-up a part of the ship with resources for you.This creates a found family kind of adventuring crew that you can do missions for and grow attached to. The story doesn't diverge if you fail to recruit some people but everyone's presence feels naturally included in scenes and you'll appreciate finding everyone that you can. A majority of the character writing and story revolves around this crew with everyone else in the world having some relationship to someone in your group and most the islands just being one off exploration areas for you to do missions for your friends. I believe Ys VIII tackled this more effectively but if you played and enjoyed that style of game then the feeling will be very reminiscent here.Onto the combat; there has been a big change from earlier entries in the series. Perfect dodging is mostly gone as it is reserved for special blue attacks and can't be used against any others. Instead shielding is king. If you shield an attack you build up a revenge meter which multiples the damage on your next duo skill. If you perfect shield an attack this meter builds up significantly faster and you regain a large amount of skill points used for your special attacks. Very often combat can boil itself down to guarding until your opponent does a swing that leaves them wide open and then hitting them with a hard punish. Your normal guard can be broken but I found you can just dodge out of most situations afterwards and a perfect guard can never be broken.I mentioned duo skills and that's another new addition. You have two main characters that you can swap between or you can enter duo mode where you control both characters at once. This system is neat in theory but in application it feels very all or nothing. If you play in solo mode you will use your high skill point (SP) moves with one character and then swap to the other. The character you're not currently playing gets a massive SP regeneration boost so you just swap between them so you can keep chaining your moves and spamming high damage skills. In this process there's very little reason to enter duo mode as it tends to break this flow and duo skills take SP from both members so if you try to mix in duo mode you will not have the SP for your solo mode shenanigans.You could instead just stick to duo mode as SP generates pretty quickly and normal attacks are very high damage. You'll also use this mode a lot for bosses because it's hard to stagger enemies so bosses are usually defeated by perfect guards and punishes than trying to combo them. In duo mode you can only use duo skills so you are completely locked out of your solo skills and in fact these skills have no impact on anything in duo mode. Passive effects on normal attacks will carry over to duo mode normal attacks and it seems to share your gear bonuses so it's definitely a strong mode. The problem is solo mode and duo mode just don't work well with each other or transition well into each other either.The combat could use just a bit of refinement but I really like the design goals within. I will say I miss flash guards and I wish perfect guard had some kind of safety. Very often I would be punished for landing a perfect guard because the duo skills all have long animations and can be interrupted by the enemy. Sometimes I would take my time to build up a 3+ multiplier on my revenge just to be smacked out of it after a perfect guard. It makes perfect guards feel underwhelming at times.There's also another type of combat; naval combat. This can mostly be ignored with only 3-4 mandatory ship fighting sections. The naval combat is not interesting. If you build up your ship then it will be very easy, if you don't then it will be very tedious. The combat doesn't have any challenge. You for the most part out-range and outmaneuver all your opponents. You just circle around them and pelt them over and over again until they sunk. The movement and control of the boat is painfully slow and the ocean sections in general feel oddly paced. Very often you will get conversations that are cut short if you are progressing at a normal pace to the next area. If you want to hear all the voice lines then you'll be stuck sitting at scene transitions as you let the characters finish their thoughts.The last section I'll talk about is the story. Just like Ys VIII, the main focus of the story is your female companion. This time her name is Karja and she is your other party member throughout the game. The story essentially sets up Karja and Adol as a special pair with the unique ability to defeat the greiger. An immortal race of malevolent beings. This means anyone who needs anything done is required to rely on the pair and they're the central force for change in the story. The themes of the story revolve around self-determination and self-reflection. Multiple character stories involve confronting their true desires. Familial drama is a recurring element present in a lot of story lines as characters ambitions are at odds with their legacy or expectations. The plot dips into some darker elements but doesn't pull the trigger often and wraps up almost all of the plot lines in the 'happiest' way possible. The antagonists here are a little weak here. They have strong personalities and can be fun to see but their motives and explanations are not very strong. There's a lot of "we do this because this is what we do". There are hints that there may be more nuance to the existence of the main opposing force but it doesn't go very far.Overall I rambled a lot but this game is fun. It's a light action filled adventure with solid controls and combat. There's always something to do and explore and they made a lot of effort into giving you freedom to tackle things as you want. There's almost always some marker or indicator for something to look into and there's a million and one sub-systems you can indulge in. If you don't like something however you can ignore it and not feel overly punished. Give this a shot if you like Ys. I can't imagine you'll hate your time playing the game but don't expect it to dethrone Ys VIII.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: My actual first non spoiler review of a game that I have mixed feelings about. I beat this game around 3am last night and man do I have my gripes. The story was somewhat engaging but around chapter 7 the potential some characters had went straight down the drain, Karja plot line was the only thing stringing me on. The main antagonist was very cool in concept but I went in 12 levels above them because the combat made any optional boss very doable regardless of the level gap. The combat. Kondo why. Ys 9 was a laughing stock with the way they handled flash guard and flash dodge, and it's still shocking to this day I think Felghana is the hardest Ys has to offer. As a friend said I paid $60 to block. Any difficulty gets shafted with guarding as a pair, why wouldn't you use it? Revenge gauge is broken but it works well enough when it comes to bosses regenerating their silly armor shield. Overall though. 6/10 game, I don't hate it, but I don't care for it overall. I say it's much more worth getting on sale, I may come back around and do the last 5 achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: This game is as mid as they come, combat system is kinda clunky, and coop is duck taped in. But it's fairly enjoyable, a lot of systems to explore. It just doesn't do anything to wow me. This game hits 360fps consistently. It's optimized well. This is a solid 6.5 out of 10 action RPG. I would play the demo first to see if it's your thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Different from the last entries in the series but still fun, chronologically this is the fourth(third if we only count Adol) game in the series so it a nice entry point too(if you don't want to start playing by I & II) and lastly, the port is really nice, the game isn't that demanding but it's still nice to see good port.The DEMO save carries over so I actually played the game for around 55 hours, it's a bit less content than Ys IX Monstrum Nox and that game is still my favorite 3D Ys but being a hard entry point into the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Ys X: Nordics

_childDocuments_.review: Great Combat system, Interesting story, nice feeling of progression. skills are flashy and make you feel badass. Playing on inferno but without heals cause I'm a masochist and I did it for ys 8 and 9. Only gripe is that you can cheese past almost anything by just holding the revive button as soon as someone goes down and you can use invincibility frames upon the forced character switch to revive with what feels like a 99% success rate.as a fan of the previous games this ones a 9.5/10 for me just for the combat alone. it keeps you engaged and is quite fun. beginning is definitely a slow start until after chapter 3 and is very dialogue heavy but it gives you a good chance to get a feel for the controls. the duo mode takes some getting used to so by the time you get to chapter four and have a bit more freedom you'll already be familiar with how it plays. highly recommend playing on at least nightmare or inferno for a fun challenge. (don't be an idiot like me and do it without heals, I love torturing myself

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the Ys series, and really enjoyed the Ys X Skies of Arcadia style gameplay of this entry into the series.  To make the review briefer I'm going to go with a plus and minus section.  If you enjoy modern Ys games or action RPGs I recommend buying it.  Plus:  -The ship portions of the game (upgrading, sailing, and battling) are satisfying-The play control remains tight-The player swapping and saving system in battles works well, and streamlines the experience-The graphics are colorful, and the character models are well done-The map system makes the game easy to navigate and backtrack.-No crashes, bugs, or visual issues in over 28 hours-The controls are easily mapable, and both keyboard/mouse, and gamepad control works exceptionally wellNegatives:-The music is good, but is more mellow than previous entries, causing me to take more breaks.  -Traversing the ocean in the early game has several limitations in traveling, and is slow.  It does improve.-The voice acting is overall good; however Adol seems to be finishing up puberty (very cracky voice), and Karja is rather unlikable in both her voice (screechy sometimes) and character.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an  game. I've been following the franchise for 36 years so of course I'm going to check it out. It doesn't really add much that's truly unique in feel. In other words, it plays just like  and  but with only two party members and some minor additions like sailing and the Unleash system. Falcom did get rid of the Slash/Strike/Pierce mechanics, which is a plus in my book because I never liked them. The story sucks you in, there are numerous places to explore that award you for your diligence, and the writing is excellent as always with Falcom games.My one major complain is the grind. Obtaining crafting materials, gold, and skill mastery wears on you because you'll need massive amounts of the first two to create runes for the Unleash system and the latter is all but necessary to defeat the final bosses. Not just Adol's and Karja's skills but the duo skills they use together. Prepare for that to take several hours in itself if you don't do so over several playthroughs.

_childDocuments_.review: A brand new adventure of Adol Christin freshly after the event of YS 1&2! (Adol is still 17 in this game)YS 10: Nordics blend the look and feel of Scandinavian within the YS world really well.Instead of control 3 party members like YS :Celceta, 7, 8 and 9, you get to pair with a viking princess instead.But those pair came with interesting mechanics throughout the game, so no more playing paper-rock-scissor or force to switch to character just to deal more damages.What surprise me is how fun and easy ship battle come to play; similar to Assassin's Creed 4, but more simple, and the sea is vast in this game. (Of course, there's a fishing section too!)The early chapter maybe a bit slow at first, but the pacing is getting better in the later chapter; you can expect a classic YS storytelling here.Overall, YS 10 : Nordics is a good old adventure that I'm glad we have for YS series.See you next in Celceta!

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Ys VIII, I really wanted to try this game out (I've had issues making my Ys IX litterally unplayable with no fixes available to my knowledge) and, while it is not as good as the masterpiece that is Lacrimosa of Dana, it's still a very good story, with a good cast of characters, but, the particularity of this game is, only two of them are playable, Adol, obviously, and the Pirate Princess, Karja.It is a gamble, because if you do not like her, you're still stuck with her for the approximately 50 to 60 hours of the game, and most of other characters are not as developped as she is. It is definitely her story.Personnally, I love Karja, she is a very cool and strong, and her character growth is really nice to follow and witness.Adol being quite litterally bonded to her opens the Duo mechanics and the gimmick of this game, allowing both him and Karja to attack in unison and unlocking exclisive combined skills, but also the ability to swap between the two to keep the combos up, reducing the costs of their skills. I never felt like the party was lacking, both of them being very satisfying to play.Overall, I absolutely loved Nordics and I hope you give it a chance as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Another great Ys game. I recommend it. It's no Lacrimosa of Dana but then again what is?Some Negatives:It's a bit too talky. Especially early on. You'll feel like you're being ferried from cutscene to convo to cutscene for a while. I highly recommend setting text speed to instant if you're going to be talking to every NPC (like you do.)Defensive options in combat are too strong. This isn't necessarily new, Flash Dodge and Flash Guard were beastly and extremely spammable in the last few games. Defense is less spammable now but nevertheless too easy and powerful.- You can straight up block a majority of attacks in the game, including ones from bosses. There's no chip damage and only specific attacks break through.- Even when enemies break through they frequently do not follow up on your vulnerable state.- Damage reduction while doing Skills is so high, using a skill and just tanking the damage is a very viable option. This is a real bummer. Skill spam becomes real strong.- Dodge is basically out of the equation unless an enemy performs specific blue coded attacks in which case sprinting makes you completely immune to them, trivializing these attacks completely.Otherwise the game is a blast, like the rest of the series. I don't really need to list Pros because if you're an Ys fan you already know why Adol's adventures are fantastic. If you're not, go play Lacrimosa of Dana.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I did not know what to think of this game. I immediately knew that it's better than Ys IX, but it felt slower than Ys VIII. It looked better than past games, but it seems not by much. And the voice acting had that same old NISA flavor that feels out of place in modern times, especially after playing Metaphor.But soon after, the game showed its true quality. Some of the battle mechanics weren't explained properly, but once you figure them out, you'll feel how good combat is. Right now, just after beating the game, it seems to be better than VIII, but I have to replay the latter to be really sure.What I'm sure of is how refreshing the story and the finale of the game are. No tired JRPG trope of saving the world by fighting a big bad monster here--there are other reasons to have a good fight, no? The last fight was the most satisfying, free flowing, and good looking fight video game fight I've had, I think ever. Finally, it's very well optimized. I beat it all the way on the Steam Deck, locked 60 handheld, and 60 most of the way docked at 900p resolution. It looked great either way.This game needs more love. I don't see enough people talking about it online or on Youtube. Definitely worth full price for the experience alone. Helping Falcom and PH3 out are just icing on the cake.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game through on inferno straight out the gate, probably took a total of 37 hours if we include the time I spent in demo. Overall, compared to VIII, it's not quite at that level (but then again, it's preeetty hard to beat that one), but in my opinion its as good as IX. The Good:- Game runs great- The game definitely got a huge improvement in graphics. Some of of the animations look a bit janky (specifically the running animation in some cutscenes) but overall, I think its a huge improvement over the previous titles- The combat. Now this one is a bit controversial. I'm on the side that it really is very good. They did away with the flash guard and flash dodge system so I understand that a lot of people were a bit upset. BUT, after getting used to building and maintaining the skill chain and sp discount, the flow of the fights becomes MUCH better. I really did enjoy the swapping between karja and adol and getting to use the heaviest hitters from both kits. Also the number of skills you get to choose from as well as the Duo mode skills; very fun.- Overworld exploration. It's different from the previous games because the main source of overworld exploration is through sailing to little isolated islands. It was fun and some of the islands actually have really good stories to them.- Music. Ys music always a banger. This one's no exception. Overall, I'd put it above IX but under VIII. This OST has its hits and misses but overall pretty good.The Bad:- Ship mechanics/combat. This is my only real gripe with the game that I think needs to be seriously overhauled. Early game ship handling is... pretty atrocious. It gets significantly better in the mid to end game when your ship is actually upgraded but most things to do with ship combat are just tedious. I don't think i did a single overworld ship battle that wasn't forced or a challenge encounter.The Mediocre:- The storyline is kind of middle of the road for me. Nothing too particular that I cared about throughout the majority of it. I did like the ending but that might have just been because I *very much* enjoyed the final fight. There were a few very good side stories tied to some of the islands but the main story was nothing overly special.- Mana skills. I thought these had a lot of potential, but the majority of them are used pretty sparingly. I was hoping for IX levels of exploration using them but sadly that was not the case. Just a bit of a disappointment. Tl;drIf you're a fan of VIII and IX, I definitely think you should pick this up and play it. It still has that adventurous ys gameplay feel that I love. But if the full price is too much for some (because seriously $60 NISA? I'm down for supporting falcom because I love their games but man, game prices just keep going up) definitely get it on sale. Still, no regrets buying it day 1.Here's to waiting for YS XI and HOPING that it gets a simultaneous worldwide release

_childDocuments_.review: Still early on in my playthrough, I will update my review if anything changes. Edit: Completed the game! Final spoiler-free review at the bottom.So far it's been quite fun! Music is amazing as always in Falcom games. Voice acting is hit or miss but no big deal. Combat feels smooth and responsive. The story-hook is promising, I already want to find out more.Graphics are not what you'd expect from a 60€ game but if you've played any Ys games before, you know that graphics are this series weak point. But the gameplay makes up for it.Edit: I have finished my Inferno-Run, cleared 100% and collected all achievements in about 55 hours playtime. Absolute incredible game, my personal GOTY so far! Story was quite fun, the writing is incredibly good, especially for a translated game. It felt believable, so did the characters. At no point did the game seem to drag on. The pacing is pretty good and the introduce new stuff all the time. Only the beginning is a bit slow but it picks up after a couple hours.Difficulty wise this is (in my opinion) one of the easiest Ys games, thanks to two gameplay mechanics which I'm not going to mention for the sake of spoilers. Ship-combat is pretty fun as well, but getting repetitive due to lack of depth. Thankfully, for the most part you can decide for yourself how much you want to engage in ship-combat. There is even a consumable item that lets you skip certain ship-combat encounters. This is one of the many reasons why I think this game really respects your time.Conclusion: If you're an Ys fan, go play this! If you like fast-paced semi-open world action games, go play this!

name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit
detailed_description: Retro Arcade-style Rally Racing in repurposed Parking Garages in big cities across the USA You said 'Parking Garage'? The “Parking Garage Rally Circuit” tour comes into a city, selects a parking garage, and temporarily turns it into an exciting rally course for a week-long competition. Each track in the game is styled as a unique parking garage that has been turned into a race course. Rally... Circuit?!? This is a hybrid of Rally and circuit racing. From rally it draws the jumps and “one racer at a time against the clock” time-trial format. However, the tracks are similar to circuit racing, with each race consisting of multiple laps around the same track (the track may change slightly from lap to lap, however) Controls are very tight, simple and arcadey, similar to Mario Kart (accelerate, reverse, steer, drift), but with a bit more dynamic “smash into things” physics. Seamless Leaderboards After beating the gold trophy for a course, ghosts from other players just barely ahead of you on the leaderboard are automatically downloaded to race against, getting you into that 'just one more' flow as you chase down rivals. Limiting the auto-download rivals to Steam friends only is also an option. Realtime Multiplayer Create or join a lobby of up to 8 players for realtime peer-to-peer non-contact racing! Split-screen Multiplayer Connect some controllers and relive the glory days of split-screen multiplayer for 2-4 players with contact and non-contact options. Retro Style Designed to look and feel like a long lost Sega Saturn game that could have been released in ~1998. This includes low-resolution, low-poly, chunky textures of course, but also extends to the audio, simple interface, and streamlined game scope. Oh, and CHEAT CODES too!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Game feels similar to drifting in Mario Kart. Took me 3 hours to 100% the game. Game would benefit from more cars and tracks in a future update. Multiplayer works fine. Runs perfectly on Steam Deck.-----------I love rally racing and I'm a fan of old-school graphics, like PS1 games, so I've been anticipating this game's release.The gameplay is similar to Mario Kart drifting, so if you've played lots of Mario Kart, this should be easy to pick up and play. There are a few little nuances and tricks that you have to figure out while playing. For example, drifting kind of magnetizes you to the ground, so drifting up a ramp is incredibly useful to prevent you from flying into outerspace.In terms of content, there isn't a whole lot. I unlocked and played through all of the content, 8 courses x 3 cars = 24 races, in 3 hours. All the achievements are reasonable and easy to earn, and that's how I like my video game achievements. In total, I earned all 15 of them also in about 3 hours. Multiplayer seems to work flawlessly. The actual gameplay of multiplayer doesn't differ from single player since in both instances you are racing "ghosts" of your opponents (multiplayer is actually real-time, but there's no collision). I had a really funny moment in a lobby where I was racing and an opponent flew through the air and dive bombed me like an airstrike, which made me laugh for a good 5 minutes straight. There's a replay tool that I made good use of to record that.I played all 3.4 hours at the time of this review on my steam deck. Works perfectly on deck and I never ran into any issues. In the near future, the steam deck compatibility on the store's page will probably change from "unknown" to "verified".I don't know if the developer has any more plans for this game, but I personally would enjoy a content update. Maybe more tracks and more cars, because the game is limited in that regard. What I would really love is a level editor, but that's too much to ask for and would take a lot of work. This is a well-made little game and I'm glad I wasn't disappointed because I've had it sitting in my wishlist for awhile waiting for it to come out. I think it's priced fairly in my region (10 USD) and I bought it for 15% off at launch.

_childDocuments_.review: I typically don’t go for games based solely on nostalgia, and given the price of the Sega Saturn when I was a kid, there’s no nostalgia to be had here for me. However, I love a good twist on the familiar and the idea of taking a rally race into a parking garage immediately interested me. But what surprised me was getting seemingly familiar racing mechanics taken to a deeper level than I ever anticipated.Abbreviated Review: Parking Garage Rally Circuit starts you out with a selection of what you want the game to look like. Each selection is an iterative step between something that looks straight out of the blocky, grainy early era of 3D gaming and something that feels more like it was inspired by that style but is easy to discern with high framerates. All of them run flawlessly, but I found the lower resolution, lower framerate options to be just a bit too difficult to parse. The full-screen higher resolution still has an aesthetic that will take you back to the feeling of the best the mid-90s could offer – with that handful of polygons and textures that look like you just zoomed out a bit on a quilt.Yet, with this dated but unique styling, the developer crafted eight pretty amazing tracks built around the idea of them all taking place inside, around, over, and through parking garages. It’s not just a set dressing either, each track feels like it has real aspects of parking garages throughout, and navigating those tight turns, low ceilings, and numerous parked cars is surprisingly intuitive. The best part for me though is that many of the tracks have some kind of gimmick associated with them. Whether it’s numerous jumps between paths, moving barricades, or boulders rolling down a hill onto the track, each dynamic element makes the tracks feel much more interactive. There’s even a part where lightning strikes taking out the power of a parking garage leaving you to navigate half the race in that dark with your headlights. It was incredible how much something so simple changed the experience.The driving aspect of Parking Garage Rally Circuit doesn’t seem all that novel. You’d be familiar with it if you previously played a Mario Kart game or something like it. You have a button that automatically sends you into a drift if you press it while turning and, as you drift, you’ll gain two levels of boost power upon releasing it. This, at face value, isn’t anything too impressive, but what is impressive is how well it’s implemented and the additions to the mechanics. Instead of simply trying to get standard boosts whenever possible, there’s some kind of ‘momentum’ mechanism built into your overall speed. The more boosts you chain back-to-back the faster you’ll end up going.In your effort to beat the ghost cars racing with you that represent first, second, and third place times, it’s often the case that making it to first place is only possible through this boost-chaining process. It not only requires a bit of effort to make happen, but a significantly higher amount of effort to maintain control over. The tight confines of the racetrack, numerous cars and obstacles, and the lengths to which you will be launched off jumps mean too much speed can leave you well off the proper path. Ending up in that scenario, even with the car reset option, usually puts you so far behind the collision-free timed ghosts that you’ll never catch up. So, the harder you try to accelerate to victory, the higher your chances of requiring a complete race restart.There’s a lot about Parking Garage Rally Circuit to love, but there are some quirks that make it a little bumpy. Sometimes it feels like the physics is from another dimension, especially when you start accelerating to higher speeds and collide with static and movable objects. You’ll occasionally be launched ridiculously or halted entirely when it doesn’t seem like you should. There’s also the fact there are only three available cars – and each one serves as more of an escalating difficulty level to loop through the eight tracks in the circuit. While that works well, it seems like it’s a missed opportunity to have at least a few vehicle options with different tuning. Even basic tuning options could add another layer to the experience.In general, though, the only noteworthy issue with this game is that it feels like there could be more of it. Yet, like with all arcade-style racing games, it’s less about the breadth of the content and more about the replayability – which this has plenty of. You can head back into the eight tracks with each of the three cars to chase and set record times, complete with online leaderboards and “top X%” tracking. You can also take on each one in endurance mode which lets you take laps around a course gaining seconds with each checkpoint until you run out of time. And there’s even a multiplayer mode if you want to compete more directly with your friends instead of just their times. The bottom line here though is this: for a little money, you get something that will either massage your nostalgia zone, entertain you with a unique setting and design, or challenge you with surprisingly engaging mechanics. It can easily do all three, but any one of them is enough to justify picking it up. Plus, it has a fun soundtrack as a cherry on top.

_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: To start this game is deceptively simple. The task of beating the gold medal is simple enough, just execute a couple of well timed drifts and remember your turns and you'll come out okay! However, as you progress the ghost cars don't even matter anymore. As you learn to chain the drifts you will be well ahead of them and your new competition becomes the physics engine. A poorly placed boost or a misaligned jump can ruin a run in milliseconds. I could see this being off-putting to some people, but it is quite rewarding to spend an entire race white knuckling it feeling like you're constantly on the edge of control and putting in a time that you know is at the very least top 20%. It is equal parts complete focus and praying to the physics engine to keep your car from getting too "slidey" as your momentum stops matching your direction of steering and the amount of time your wheels are in contact with the road become negligible.  So yeah basically I'm hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit
