_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely technical speed run racer with some insane physics and Mario Kart DS style snaking. _childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a great idea, and the controls and physics match it perfectly. Drifting feels tight and precise, letting you pull off constant U-turns and boosts along straight sections with ease. One of the coolest mechanics is chain boosting - you gain extra speed if you drift boost during an ongoing boost, and the exciting part? The speed is uncapped! This creates a balancing act where sometimes you need to slow down, otherwise, you’ll end up airborne. It can go both ways - either you end up spinning off the map and knocking down everything in your path, or you pull off an insane trick and find a hidden shortcut.The tracks are really well-designed too, each with its own unique gimmick. The ghost feature is a great touch too: it starts with regular bronze, silver, and gold times, but after you beat gold, it shows ghosts of players close to your leaderboard rank, making the climb up the ranks much more engaging. The music is another surprising highlight - it’s catchy and has hints of Sonic OSTs vibes, which feel perfect for a game this fast-paced. Plus, it’s awesome that the game offers both online and local multiplayer, which is always a welcome feature.It’s probably the first game I’ve seen that tries to capture the retro visuals of the Sega Saturn console, giving it a really unique look - and thankfully, you can tweak this visuals to suit your taste. I can’t wait to see DLCs and mod support added, as you can finish all the content in just a few hours. But those few hours are super engaging, so definitely give this one a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Short video review: Parking Garage Rally Circuit is a fantastic fusion of retro style, drift heavy arcade racing with modern feeling controls. The eight tracks all feel unique and have some crazy cool gimmicks and stage hazards. There's three heats which are basically difficulties, and you can either drive in a race against ghosts or arcade style, with checkpoints adding to your countdown time. It feels phenomenal to play with it's heavy emphasis on drifting. My only complaint is I wish there were more tracks!
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: It's a rare game where you feel you and the developer have near identical desires for what a game should be but for myself and Parking Garage Rally Circuit this was most happily the case. Drawing clear inspiration visibly from the bygone era of checkbox transparencies, truncated draw distances and 30FPS home ports (with options to alter all of these if you aren't a sicko). PGRC isn't actually the arcade checkpoint racing game it appears to be but cuts its own very specific route to success.Predominately a Time Trial racer with no cars to overtake or hurl randomized power ups at. For the most part you'll be racing to set the lowest lap time against the ghosts of other players in a way that evokes something closer to a low res Trackmania than you might otherwise expect from the 5th generation aesthetic. Cars dash around the tightest corners imaginable with a binary button based drift system not dissimilar from Mario Kart, drift longer to get blue sparks and in a bout of mad genius if you drift successfully in short order you'll lock in a new top speed for your car while you keep the drift chain up. Maintain the drift and you'll get faster and faster until you're practically travelling at the speed of sound. To stop you from rocketing off the course pressing the drift button locks your car onto the ground (usually) resulting in a furious game of juggling turns, drift and speed lest you witness the effects of high speeds off a short ramp. There's an incredible rush from nailing a tight sequence knowing that it was all player skill and tracks mastery. Those aforementioned ghosts also stop the track from getting lonely as you watch other players previous flailing attempts at racing.And yes, the Parking Garage thing seems strange until it isn't. Smartly thought out to offer unusual layouts - even the most basic car parks in the game are fantastical offering interesting routes of up and down overlapping pathing. Rapidly the tracks (of which there's something like 10) begin to spill out onto rooftops or bits of offroading to ensure things don't get too monotonous. PGRC knows when to add a bit of flavor and it nails it better than I was expecting. One of the larger criticism you could throw at the game here however is that your first run or three through a track will be pretty bumpy as the layouts can be elaborate and it's not always 100% clear where you need to go even with a track map in the corner - there's arrows and fences trying to point you in the right direction but when you're hurtling through a course a single subdued barricade is almost beneath notice.The music is categorically excellent in a way it didn't need to be. Avoiding chiptunes that tend to show up in retro themed games even when it's not period relevant - PGRC leans on a sort of Jazz/Ska fusion soundtrack with a sprinkle of honest to god vocal tracks waxing poetically about driving and going fast in a charmingly infectious manner that perhaps more than anything swings for the crown long held by racing game vocal king Takenobu Mitsuyoshi - perhaps it doesn't quite hit the level of Daytona but each track has its own theme and that rules.At the time of writing this review the developer is still making some planned additions to the game in the form of local simultaneous multiplayer so that's something to look forward to but it sounds more like a gimmick and PGRC is absolutely a full complete title without the need for more ongoing additions so I'm considering it complete regardless. Get this one and learn the joy, the thrill of racing... in Parking Garages.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: I am not huge on racing games (though I liked them more in my "youth") but I figured I'd give this a shot. This seems to be right up that alley (no pun intended?)The game drew me in more than I intended. I like to get the best scores, so found myself quickly restarting the maps so I could keep up with the gold "ghost" car. And boy, did that ever teach me how to play. It seemed like every step of the way I was forced to learn the technique of power-sliding everywhere. And it's _FUN_. I found myself going back to it during work breaks to try beating the next level or getting the next best time. It's easy to pick up and go, and I'm revved up (pun intended) about getting through all the tracks. I love the retro feel, and the consistency of the overall style of the game. Even for a not-much-of-a-racer type like me, I have enjoyed it immensely!

_childDocuments_.review: This is being typed up after completing the first car class, and unfortunately, the game has already left me utterly frustrated. But just to get it out of the way, most of the game is sound, and the presentation is absolutely spot on.The big problems with PGRC are twofold: the physics engine, and lategame level design.With the physics, it's not the drift handling that's the problem, because that's one of the things that the game, for the most part, nails. It's what the game does when it's not all four wheels on the ground that turns the game into an exercise in frustration. When compared to other drifty games like classic CTR, the airborne physics are much too complicated for their own good, and the end result is that it's all too easy for the game to just arbitrarily launch your car in a way that immediately ends your run. This also messes with Drifting, which is only Engaged via a single button, because there are bumps in the road on Course 8 that lie right on points where you are expected to start drifting. So if you try to Drift on the bump, it won't actually begin until you've landed, at which point you're likely trying to countersteer for a wide Drift and, instead, end up Drifting in completely the opposite direction.And it's the same with the collision physics, as the car has a huge tendency to get stuck on anything and everything. When combined with what happens when you leave the ground, you can easily be sent well out of the course and be forced to restart. And in many other courses, clipping an outside kerb (or the snowbanks in Course 7) will violently drag your car off-line in a completely unrealistic fashion (even by arcade game standards) and force a restart. Even hitting walls can literally lead to the car going into a full-on wallride that completely messes up the run, and a certain wall in Course 8 can cause the car to immediately spin the other way or completely vault over it.And then there's the course designs which, for the most part, are fine. The problem is that many of these levels have elements that punish the player for performing too well. You are expected to chain Drifts in order to increase your Speed and shave seconds off the end time, but then the game's level design forces you to slow down otherwise it becomes literally impossible to clear the level cleanly. This is made even worse by it being incredibly difficult to control the car's speed after several boosts, and the game's Tutorial doesn't explain that you're able to Brake while Drifting and still be able to get the boost after the fact (the Tutorial doesn't even mention how to do a Boost Start, and if there's any kind of Air Control in PGRC then that isn't explained either).The two biggest problem courses are, by some margin, Courses 6 and 8. 6 has many jumps across garage levels, with several of them causing the car to crash into the ceiling and end the run if you approach them too fast. And Course 8, Liberty Island, is the absolute worst. It's fine for about the first 25 seconds, and then you get to the worst part of the whole game, the rainbow corkscrew part. Not only are you approaching this part incredibly fast, touching any of the kerbs even slightly will immediately launch the car off-track. And if you go off the jump at full-tilt, you will completely overshoot the landing zone, so you HAVE to slow down. But slowing down for the jump is incredibly difficult, as you're forced to do a Boost because you just exited the corkscrew from a long drift. And even if you do manage to slow it enough, the airborne physics and the tight walls on the other side mean that, even if you actually manage to land on the road, you're either going to tumble and end up facing backwards, trip over the walls and fall off the road, or lose all your speed. And the worst part is that this section has no Checkpoints during this part. There's one at the start of the first Screw and the very end of the second Screw, and those are 20 seconds apart... when going at full speed, which is over twice the starting speed. If you end up Resetting, you automatically lose so much time that even Silver becomes impossible to get.It took me nearly three hours just to get a 'clean' run of Liberty Island with no Resets or significant loss of time. And when I did... it was a Top 10 time. And by then, my hands were an arthritic wreck on the controller.As it stands, I don't know if I can recommend this game. For something centered around Time Attack gameplay, its physics and level design work so vehemently against the player, that any semblance of fun I was having with the drifting was being quickly voided by the game arbitrarily deciding to yeet the car into the shadow realm. The airborne handling of the game needs to be much, much more predictable than whatever this is, because this is not enjoyable at all. Even if it looks the part.ADDITONAL: Another six hours later, and I was able to get one single clean run of secret level LD54. And that experience further cemented the truth that all the game's flaws are in the physics. The track layout, aside from the second checkpoint being way too easy to miss on Lap 2/3, is nigh-on perfect for what I would expect from a game like this. But every single ramp screws you over, messing with your drift timings and launching your car into the air if you're not either already Drifting or doing that and holding the Brake after Lap 1 (because you're going much faster by then), and the long downhill stretch near the end is almost complete RNG as to whether you actually make it down without being somersaulted into next week. And Lap 2/3 force you to learn how to slow the car's top speed down (just Braking isn't enough), otherwise the track will launch you when attempting to take the tight hairpin left.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic throwback to the 32bit era, and this game looks and feels like a Saturn or PSX game from back in the day. Although it's short to complete, you do have online multiplayer and online leaderboards to contend with, which is great.There are 3 car classes, the drift/boost mechanic feels really natural and works very well, the more you play the more you get used to flying around the tracks with ease. The skill variation is in being able to maintain a high speed from drifting and boosting without crashing.I thoroughly enjoyed my time playing, and will dip in now and then for some leaderboard action and fun. I hope the developer adds more tracks and cars at some point, and an official time trial mode would be good as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible experience with some calm casual appeal as well as the skill ceiling to make me want to lock in and climb the leaderboards. The game controls with a physics system unique to itself, mimicking more of the kart-racer style of Mario Kart with additional support for the rally style. Rather than aggressive combat items and butting heads, it uses the chain drift system to become an intense time trial based game where you're fighting for mastery of your vehicle as you set faster and faster lap times, using a powerful boost acceleration to encourage subtle braking and steering controls to maximize the top speed you can maintain before a slapstick style wipeout occurs. Visually great with a fun soundtrack, it's hard to find anything wrong in such a satisfying game. 9.5/10, if you think it looks fun then you'll have a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: PGRC is a fantastic little racing game with a nostalgic style but crisp modern feel. Walaber out-did himself creating a fantastic  game oozing with fun. _childDocuments_.review: I can respect a game that’s not looking to branch a sprawling narrative and just give people the happy brain juices they so desire.  Especially if you can find us sickos who play racing games that feel necessary, obligated even to shed any millisecond we can off of our lap time just to feel the gratification of doing so.  I got to speak to , now I get to see how it holds up!The Game Jam entry turned Godot Engine title is simple and quick: take rally cars of various weight classes and slap them into parking garages around the country for furious laps and impossible drifting corners to take home the Gold.  You get a choice of three different weight classes to traverse 10 different stages full of twisting turns, lap-specific obstacles, and plenty of shortcuts to put the best time you can on the leaderboards and collect some trophies along the way.But first, we gotta set up our car!  PGRC comes with three different classes of vehicles: Light, Heavy, and Ultra, that increase in speed and in turn the difficulty in handling the tight courses.  Each car comes with a handful of liveries to choose from and a color-changer that can be done via Hex Code, so the color combinations are limited only by your imagination.  Pick your favorite number between 0-99 and let’s get ready to race.PGRC’s stages take you all around the country, from Seattle to DC to Walaber’s own rendition of Rainbow Road, for 2-3 lap sprints around the curated courses.  The level of ingenuity of these is hilariously fun, from avoiding rolling boulders to navigating lightning-struck blackouts to criss-cross jumping in between two garages to doing an amateur recording of Gymkhana drifting past baggage carts and snowmobiles.  Each level is distinctly different and all carry a fun individual challenge to work around, especially when shaving a few seconds can get you a better cycle to navigate past obstacles better.Controls maintain the simplicity of the arcade and retro vibes: gas, brake, drift-drift.  Drifting for an extended time grants two tiers of boosts that slowly increase your car’s top speed so long as your boost is going, so chaining smaller and bigger boosts on turns is key.  Drifting also suction cups your car to the ground allowing for some tight corners to be taken at some breakneck speeds.  The controls handle nice and fluidly and in terms of response time and gameplay, it takes me back to old school Mario Kart days, which is never a bad comparison!While the controls stay fluid, the physics are anything but.  Boosts have a tendency to override actions so long as the boost is happening.  So if you try to brake while boosting, the boost will push you back to top speed if you don’t brake the whole way through.  Hitting a wall while boosting will slow you down while on the wall but tap you back to full speed the moment you’re off of it, and if you’re going fast while drifting and a wheel happens to catch some air, you’re going on a whirlwind ride as the engine doesn’t quite know how to handle cars that fast going sideways in a drift.The above can be a blessing and a curse.  If you’re cruising around playing stages for the fun of it or indulging in PGRC’s buttery smooth multiplayer, which consists of players racing for the fastest time but not sharing the courses together as these small courses were not meant for multiple cars at once, the results can be hilarious.  I’ve busted out laughing seeing my car barrel rolling through the sky or spin cycling because I drifted on a turn too hard and flew off the course in grandeur fashion.  But if you’re looking to climb the leaderboards and you have to push your car as hard as you can for every millisecond, the coin flips on whether or not the game engine will screw you can be maddening.  It all depends on how hard you’re trying on the game, but I can see the good, the bad, and the funny from the issues.Having 100% the game in a little over a few hours, your mileage may vary on replay value after the credits roll, but I had an absolute blast playing Parking Garage Rally Circuit.  The retro-dipped arcade racer lives up to the expectations of providing a snappy, ska-filled journey around the country skidding and sliding through garage floors and grabbing bragging rights from friends by hitting that sweet spot on each lap.  Enjoy the victory lap Walaber, I hope you’re not done with what you got here (can’t wait for that local multiplayer!).

_childDocuments_.review: Parking Garage Rally Circuit is an arcade-style racer with a heavy emphasis on drifting around tight spaces. It has a lot of fun ideas, chiefly that your top speed increases with chained drifts, and the overall game feel is mostly solid. The vehicles feel good to control and mostly go where you want them to, though at high speeds the cars do ragdoll around at the slightest touch on a wall or parked car, but you're trying to avoid those anyway.The game does not have a traditional time trial mode, but the "main" single-player mode is exclusively against ghosts that can't interfere with your racing line and your times are uploaded to a leaderboard, so replaying finished courses in that mode is TTs in all but name. There's also a nice arcade-inspired Endurance Mode where each checkpoint gives you a small extension to a countdown timer, and your goal is to see how long you can last before the countdown runs out. It has enough replayability that I see myself picking it up in the future when I'm in the mood to go fast for a few minutes.Especially considering the price, this is definitely worth picking up for fans of arcade racers and/or drift racers.

_childDocuments_.review: --Mixed Review--PGRC has a great atmosphere and vibe that unfortunately does more than its fair share of heavy lifting to support a game that can’t bear the weight of its janky and erratic handling system past the first hour.	The game produces an inviting, pick up and play, arcade atmosphere through its graphics, menus, and music. It also has a retro, low poly art style that looks great and doesn’t sacrifice any visual clarity to achieve it. Each location also has a somewhat distinct feel and are memorable.	The music also does a great job building upon the atmosphere due to a somewhat unique choice in Ska. It’s able to keep the energy up and also contributes to some great moments at the height of some of the lyrics that happen to match some sections of track that make it really memorable. The game owes a lot of its identity to it and would lose a lot of soul without it.	In general, the gameplay starts off very similar to Mariokart. You have to drift around corners and you charge up a boost the longer you drift, and as you play in Light class and are still learning the game, it matches expectations well. Though as you move up to Heavy and Ultra class, you’ll eventually realize it plays very different from Mariokart. Cars have an incredibly slow natural top speed that you never want to be at, so you eventually discover drift chaining (Getting the boost while still in the pervious boost) in order to stack drift boosts to properly increase your speed.         The problem is that you can’t properly manage your speed unlike Mariokart, here your brakes do next to nothing and aren’t even that useful for adjusting lines, lifting is a double edged sword since if you get on the gas too early it’ll accelerate you very rapidly, and if you stop drifting for any reason (finger accidentally slipped, double tapped, released slightly to early, wrong direction, etc..) before you get a boost you lose all of your stacks and get reset back to your natural top speed, which I cannot overstate how unbearably slow it is, and is also the only way to lose your drift boost. Ironically this makes spamming your drift button more effective than your brakes or lifting to slow down.         As you are able to chain drifts more and more, you’ll see the physics become increasingly erratic. Naturally you want to stack your boost as quickly as possible so you’ll snake a bit or chain drifts multiple times throughout the same corner, but you also have to keep adding to it to make upcoming turns and eventually you’re going too fast and inevitably lose control. Also, as you’re going this fast you’ll start to realize that the track design and the physics aren’t capable of facilitating these speeds since you’ll commonly: overshoot jumps, hit ceilings, hit walls, landing becomes super inconsistent, you can start driving on walls, you can spin out or fly off the track when drifting up inclines (the only way to properly take inclines), if your back contacts a wall when drifting it’ll start climbing up the wall, if any wheel doesn’t have even contact with the ground you’ll spin, and any slight contact with an object will send you flying across the map. It genuinely feels like all of these maps were designed for the Light class and the others were added as an afterthought. In fact, there is no small mistake at these speeds since you don’t even lose the drift boost for hitting an object (You can even drive head-on into a wall and not lose the boost) and the boost isn’t checking to see if you’re wheels are on the ground so the second they aren’t you fly across the map. 	The game just feels so frustrating to play as any mistake leads to an instant restart and I genuinely don’t think I’ve ever played a more punishing racing game. Many people have compared this to Trackmania (TM) due to the time trial (TT) aspects but this game is far too inconsistent and random to achieve the level of consistency and satisfaction that TM and other TTs can. I probably restart just as much if not more than in TM but the difference is, in TM I quick restart because I took a line that was a couple of tenths slower. In PGRC, I’m not even trying to improve by those margins, I’m just praying for a clean run so I can actually have a representative time and when I finally set one, I could’ve improved by so much more in TM with the time it took.	I’m well aware that there are people much faster than me on the leaderboards as the top 50 usually have times ranging from 10-30s faster than mine, but it’s not like I’m that slow. I can at a minimum get top 20% on every track and I know the feeling of being over 20s ahead of the gold time but it feels like you’re fighting the game at every turn, jump, and impact just to be playing at this level rather than one that facilitates it.	As much as I love the atmosphere, vibes, and concept, I’ve never played a game that’s felt so janky and so frustrating to play at a decent level. The game is decently cheap but I think $10 is a bit too much for the level of jankiness and only 3hrs of content, not to mention you’ll only have 1-2hrs before the cracks start getting large. And for $10 you can pick up something like Old School Rally or an older TM.

_childDocuments_.review: Parking Garage Rally Circuit is a 90s-styled arcade racer with one of the oddest places to have a rally in, a parking garage.Coincidentally, this game comes out during a year when many indie rally games were announced and released that strive for an early 3D console look, so does this game stack up to the sudden influx of competition?I figure we should talk about how well it captures the 90s first.This game doesn't really look like any of those fake retro games that very clearly try to imitate the look just to get more people interested in it. PGRC manages to not only resemble a 90s racing game, but it does it in a way that understands the audience. There are multiple presets that kind of emulate how this game would look under different circumstances. Going from original hardware, to how it'd look emulated, to even a very sharp modern PC port. A lot of options are available to cater to the style you want. It doesn't retract from the game in any way and offers lots of charm with whichever preset you choose.Additionally, the music is also great. It imitates the carefree 90s sound with some cheesy, but catchy lyrics and great tunes while you blitz through the circuits.The circuits themselves are surprisingly complex. You would assume parking garages look very similar, but there are a total of 8 tracks, not including cheat codes, and most of them feel unique, with some of them even having a gimmick to stand out. They're wonderfully designed, with some having posters advertising other indie games. Tracks range from being fairly simple and compact, to jumping between structures, leaving & reentering the garage, or different environments and environmental hazards.However, you can't deny that the number of courses is rather small. A total of eight tracks ain't a lot, and even if you include cheat codes, it simply isn't enough. In my opinion, the ideal number would've been 12 courses, especially because you see very early on how creative you can get with this concept.The mechanics themselves are where the game differs the most.This isn't exactly your usual rally game. This is a drift-centric game, with the drift feeling more akin to Mario Kart. Each drift has two levels, and you get a small boost each time you charge one. The challenge is not really drifting itself, but chaining together boosts to keep increasing your speed. Due to the parking garages being fairly dense structures, you need to make sure that you won't bite off more than you can chew, and avoid hitting walls or objects that ruin your drift streak. It is important to note that there are also some skillful moves you can do, like starting a drift before the end of an incline, to get additional grip and not jump, or to brake while boosting or drifting, to avoid overshooting a jump or driving into a wall. What makes it addicting is that you need to understand the circuits, having to route them where to drift, how many times, making sure you have just the right amount of speed to make it through the course quickly, without going too fast, or too slow. So getting a consistent route is the key to getting a good spot on the leaderboard, but of course, if you don't like to grind worldwide, you can still try to finish the courses before the gold medalist does.Furthermore, there are also obstacles, like cars or signs, that try to ruin your run.When I first saw the trailers, they looked fun to interact with. The physics seemed interesting, and it could've been great to find new shortcuts. In spite of that, that just isn't the case.The moment you interact with obstacles, the physics become unpredictable. Sometimes it's hard to move an object, other times it feels like it's spazzing out with a simple touch, making it hard to reliably come up with a plan to use them in routes. Occasionally, they also latch onto your car and ruin your time. Even the walls have questionable physics, giving you the ability to vertically drift.Now, you could say that this is a skill issue, and you shouldn't intentionally drive into something. However, even your car has similar problems. If you aren't on all four wheels, you might as well pick a god and pray, because at higher speeds, the car can just absolutely lose control in the oddest ways possible. Flipping over like an anime character after an elevation change, spinning out thanks to absolutely nothing, and the worst thing is ramps. Ramps are introduced early on, and landing these jumps is just a gamble at higher speeds. The car just keeps spinning, making me wish for the ability to air-brake, something Trackmania figured out decades prior to ensure that the idea of having your car jump wouldn't be a coin flip.Parking Garage Rally Circuit has a lot of charm and great ideas. It's worth a playthrough, but not the leaderboard grind, cause having to deal with inconsistent physics in a game where consistency is key makes the whole experience pure frustration. 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the Demo version much more then the final release product. The older demo had better physics that didn't yeet you into the sky. Also it was more rewarding to chain your drifts through out an entire track. The point of this game to me was being able to chain the drifts consistently through out and doing so would reward the player with constantly building speed. It was possible to keep this up and manage it over an entire race before which made the game a really fun experience that felt like you could just go faster with unlimited potential. It was a really fun feed back loop until I guess way later on the developer decided people who could skilfully navigate the entire race drifting should be punished harshly via the map design and newer physics that make the car feel really horrible to drive after specific speed is crossed. Also since the time for the trophy times are an absolute joke to beat if you have any sense of just basic game play and racing lines. The only thing left is to chase is the leader boards for better times. Then another major flaw of the game starts to show up with the physics just not being fun at all. Once you start to really try to optimise your run and push the bounds of the game. You'll find in so many places the game is designed to troll you and just mess up your run. The later tracks get really bad for this and lead to just an really frustrating experience over all.I really hope the Physics are reverted back to more closely resemble the demo version I played earlier in development, because that was a really great game and experience. I am really sad that the physics have changed to try and dumb the game down and make it so frustrating for top players to keep enjoying the game with out some random result screwing my race over. If I wanted to experience this kind of annoyance for speed running / leader board reasons there are better games to speed run. As of this time I cant really recommend this game anymore, which really sucks because I was touting this game as being really awesome and a great speed run game for leader boards but that has unfortunately changed.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a perfect arcade racing game, carried by intuitive mechanics and a PERFECT soundtrack, with some delightful map design as well! The gameplay loop revolves around constantly chaining drifts and boosts together, creating a natural progression through each race in which the balance of speed and control is constantly changing. It never feels unfair or unbalanced; every input is honored. At no point in my play time did I feel as though I was cheated out of a good lap because of odd physics; in fact, the physics interactions in the game are very natural and rarely feel obtrusive. When they do get crazy, you've already messed up enough to start back at a checkpoint, so flipping your car around wildly feels like a fun bonus for failure, rather than a frustrating time loss.The replayability of this is off the charts, too! There are in-built leaderboards for every race in the game, with each race representing a different city's parking structure. Each map is unique, sometimes with moving obstacles, strange architecture, or changes between laps to give them their own identity. Each race has a different song associated with it, and they are all perfectly scored, which makes grinding the individual levels a lot more satisfying. The game saves your best times, and uploads everyone's replays to the leaderboards, so you can compare strategies and watch people who have discovered some absolutely crazy skips. You also get to race against these replays when you go back to a race, which helps with variation. There's even a multiplayer mode built in so you can race your friends!There are only 8 tracks in the whole game, with a little bit of variation offered by the different weight classes of playable cars, though that variation doesn't feel like much of a difference sometimes. However, thanks to the attention to detail, soundtrack, and variable design of these levels, I was still happy with how much I got out of it, especially for the price. It's apparent that a lot of work went into each individual map, so you're getting quality over quantity.I haven't talked much about the visual design, but it is delightful. The game features a few different modes to emulate the look of older consoles. I played on the oldest one and had an absolute blast; the aspect ratio, graphics, and aberration all make for a really compelling visual style that helps sell the arcade vibe. A lot of games use the "classic visuals" gimmick to fluff up unimpressive gameplay, but in this case, they work extremely well together as a whole. I specifically really like the drift particle effects!Again, I want to give a special shoutout to Eric Daino and The Holophonics for the soundtrack. It's so charming, so fitting, and the amount of genuine care that went into each track is SO impressive. It helps bring a distinct feel to each map, and the songs are structured so well that you end up forgetting that they loop. A genuine achievement, which does not go unnoticed.Overall, this was a genuinely surprising and fun arcade racer! It's quick to pick up, and tough to put down. It also happens to cost less than going to the movies by yourself. Get this game so I can find out how multiplayer works!!!

_childDocuments_.review: While I had my fair share of fun with this game and wouldn't dissuade anyone from buying it (especially at such a low price), after doing everything the game has to offer I gotta say it's definitely not Overwhelmingly Positive material.I'm not expecting top-notch physics from a retro indie racing game, but each of the classic arcade racers are beloved by many because their physics are reliable and/or are what makes the game unique. While this game has a very interesting drifting mechanic in its favor, the physics are too unreliable and you're always at the mercy of a perfectly good lap being ruined by the game soiling the bed and making you lose speed for no reason upon landing from a jump, for example. You kinda get used to the game's BS over time, but still, that's not what makes a good game.In regards to content, I think what we have here is too little even for such a budget game. I'm not a good player at all and I still completely exhausted the game's content after six hours, I'm sure better players can do so in a fraction of the time, and I get that there are time leaderboards and such but no racing game should rely on such for its appeal to last longer than a day.At the end of the day, while a fun little game, it unfairly got a better score than dozens of better indie racing games around solely for its meme soundtrack and nostalgia factor. Don't get me wrong, the music is nice and I like me some ska punk, but catchy lyrics and retro graphics alone shouldn't give a game Overwhelmingly Positive status.

The UX around all of that is super nice and easy. If you're an accomplished racer, it probably won't take too long to beat all of the main challenges, but extra modes go a long way. I couldn't recommend this any more highly!

_childDocuments_.review: This is "on another level." It manages to capture the magic of creative 5th gen concepts while delivering an engaging racer. Its physics are easy to pick up at the start while rewarding you for mastering its drift boost mechanics over time. The low-poly art style is reminiscent of the Sega Saturn look it attempts to capture, complete with mesh transparencies and flat "VDP-2" elements. Tracks are fun to memorize, while making robust use of the parking garages across the U.S. Parking Garage Rally Circuit is a treat for any arcade racing fan, and it goes for a remarkably fair price. The only critique I have (and this is not on the dev) is I wish more people played online.

_childDocuments_.review: This gem is a beaut! Tl;Dr: drift fast surrounded by cozy, retro-inspired 3d-graphics to a banging ska soundtrack. Great arcady, but precise time-trial game. Both digital and analogue inputs are valid, yay retro! It has both online and split screen real time racesMore specifically: Imagine a more turn-heavy Mario Kart DS time trial mode with physics, where the drift-boosts add up over time rather than you having to wreck your thumb. While initiating a drift slows you down, the similar 3-step boost-system is different in the sense of not only giving you a boost, but also adding to your max-speed, only subtracting if you end a drift early or crash. It's a great, turn-centric, simplistic (number of inputs, so nothing negative) arcade racer. The gold medals are somewhat tough but fair, you don't need to be perfect, but you've gotta pay attention. The global leaderboards encourages some hard-nerding, snaking and pushing both the timing and the amount of drifts further and further. Here the physics come into play, as they are a double-edged sword. They allow for pretty extreme cuts, which can be cool, but they can also result in a ridiculous crashes and rolls should your brain go slower than your car (not gonna lie, it can be annoying at times, but it's neat). The default setting for the ghosts chooses the three times just above you on the leaderboard, makes it more focused about improving your own times rather than seeing Lightning McQueen himself just blasting ahead with multiple second splits. You can, however, choose any ghost from the leaderboard, with the great replay-feature giving you a seamless way to study lines and potential cuts in-game. The replay-feature allows for both player view, free-cam and the preplaced multiple camera thing, and has frame-by-frame skipping both forwards and backwardsLastly, for the luls: You can race up to 250 ghosts in a row if you think sight is overrated!
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: I think its a very good game, quite addicting, but I find myself getting frustrated going for faster time trials with a couple of bugs/issues:- There is intense stuttering when the game loads in player ghosts online, it happens on my main PC and my Steam Deck. It causes constant restarts and frustration during the start of every level.- The game encourages building speed through perfect tight turns, but then most levels punish you for going too fast with low ceilings or annoying barriers which cause the physics to totally flip out and ruin your runs. Would be nice to see more polish/playtesting and adjustment to fix really problematic levels (one really irritating low ceiling on Chicago is just bizarre, what is the point of building up speed only to have to slam on the breaks over a jump so you don't crash out?)- Sometimes level layouts are confusing, with it not being clear where to go. A bit more clearer signposting wouldn't hurt.

_childDocuments_.review: The gimmick of this time trial racing game is that every time you do a Mario Kart style drift boost, you get faster. But you keep getting faster, infinitely, if you can chain together your boosts. You even hit the brake the slow down, and you'll accelerate again at incredible speed if you have a high combo. This means the best possible time is one where you maintain a perfect chain through the entire two or three laps. That gets incredibly difficult as your car becomes uncontrollably fast, and you might need an entirely different braking and cornering strategy on your second lap compared to your first.The result is kind of unique. In most time trial racers like Trackmania, you're wondering how to get one tenth of a corner, and if someone has a leaderboard time seconds ahead of you, you might be scratching your head how to do it. In this game, I know EXACTLY what I have to do to be a whole five seconds faster: Just don't break my combo trying to go through THAT ONE CORNER with a 2.5x speed multiplier. Easy to learn, hard to master.It could use more tracks or a custom track builder to really be a game I'd come back to for months (for example: Trackmania has HUNDREDs of tracks and this has eight or something), but it's a very fun experience and the price is fair.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: A throwback to those older arcade-y racing games where the skill came from mastering the unique driving the game used. Learning how to chain boosts is THE way to get ahead, and while it's less about apex mastery and throttle control, it doesn't matter when you're going so fast through a parking lot that you fly off the map!A ton of fun in a simple to learn, hard to master game. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Strictly looking at the core mechanics, Parking Garage Rally Circuit is a time attack arcade racer. However, what makes it stand out is that the game is completely kitted out. Drifts and boosts can be chained, forcing the player to delicately balance going fast and maintaining control in eight hand-designed courses. The online features are surprisingly fleshed out, from the customizable lobby multiplayer to the various preference options for downloading player ghosts. The ska soundtrack by The Holophonics is icing on the cake, somehow breathing character into each stage while still being energetic enough to keep the gameplay tense. If you have ever gotten into time trials for an arcade racer, be it Burnout or Mario Kart, you should buy this game immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: In the top 5 of the Saturn Games! Parking Garage Rally Circuit is an unlikely surprise from another era, and yet so modern. Packed with references and details, as easy to handle as any racing game has ever been (especially on Steam Deck), the title takes you on board from the very first seconds, never leaving you along the way. You'll roll over, skid, go through doors on the edge, admire your replays and share your best screenshots, enter cheat codes to play with hidden cars...And behind it all, it's just a guy who one day thought it would be fun to race cars in a confined space in a Saturn style. The world of video games is wonderful.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the kind of racing game that will appeal to players who love to optimise their play. The controls are simple, accelerate, brake, and drift - with drift angle contributing heavily to how sharp or not your turns are. That's it, that's the entire game in terms of input. Your job is to manoeuvre three vehicles of varying weights and speeds across across imaginative parking garages (designed in a way to be fun in-game but would probably piss me off in real life), some of which have gimmicks too.Then you'll beat a level, and you're like, hey I got Gold! But also, maybe, the last lap was a bit slower than my earlier one. So let's jump back in and optimise that. Oh wait, in the middle of that rerun I messed up a part I nailed earlier. But wait, that part I messed up, if I intentionally fly in the air just right, maybe I can shave some seconds...and I can! But now I gotta redo this whole level with this in mind. But wait, what if I skip the need for the jump completely if I can enter with enough speed? That's great! But wait, that's actually a bit slower...but what if I slow down earlier so I don't have to slow down as I rapidly.......It's all about those little tweaks. And the ability to see your own ghosts and those of other players around a similar speed does help to keep that competitive feeling.The aesthetics are great too, with some earworms in there, and I especially love the "just like how my mind remembers it" 32-bit era graphics. This has quickly become my go-to game for "I'm not sure what I wanna play (for the long session) so I'll nip in and try to nail a few tracks." And then I'll play a different game, and suddenly in the middle of that I'll be like "Wait, if I do this bit a little differently...." and then be itching to come back in. Highly recommended, especially if you're an arcade game type of player who loves fine tuning a perfect run.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: This game rocks! It nails the nostalgia for those of us stuck on SEGA Rally games without trying to obviously try to emulate them.Controls are really tight and you go through all the stages of grief as you mature from "how do I fast" to "AAAA TOO FAST TOO FAST!!". The game has uncapped max speed (when boost-chaining) which means figuring out when it is indeed too fast is entirely on you!The physics engine makes you sign a blood pact where it will confiscate your car and send it to another solar system if you dare drift with even one wheel not touching the floor, which makes for some hilarious fails.All-in-all, every time I boot for this game I know every additional KM/H makes me scared ****less for my life, and if that isn't the rally experience I don't know what is.The soundtrack is dope too!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so, beyond, THRILLED for this year in video games. This is a GREAT year for racing game fans that have yearned for great, fun, addicting and replayable arcade racers, such as myself! Seeing arcade racing return by people who have dreamed and loved the legacy it left behind is truly a beautiful sight, as racing games have been on the decline over the past 3-4 years (thanks AAA industry -_-). Thankfully, the genre is far from over, with the help and power of the Indie scene.From Walaber, creator of the Jelly Car series, Pro Gymnast Simulator, Very Very Valet and lead designer of Disney's Where's My Water comes Parking Garage Rally Circuit! A retro-styled arcade racing love letter to the first generation of 3D video game consoles, more precisely the Sega Saturn.Gameplay: 10/10 Simple yet effective, PGRC emphasizes the importance of drifting, speed and precision to achieve the best times! A key mechanic you'll probably notice after a race or two is stacking boosts. The more you drift, the more boost you build, AND as long as you keep drifting after each boost, the higher your top speed gets. Do keep in mind, it'll get to a point where you go TOO fast. The handling is incredible, very arcade-like. Never sluggish or slow, always very fast, replayable and rewarding. The biggest identifier for the game is being able to race in... Parking garages? It sounds odd, but trust me when I say, it's such a unique layer of design for a racing game. Turning every-day parking spaces for malls, parkades and other parking lots into a circuit for rally cars sounds so interesting as an idea. Graphics: 10/10 A very meticulously-handcrafted visual aesthetic I absolutely love. PGRC aims for the visual style and polygonal sharpness of the Sega Saturn, and it does this beautifully. The dude even includes additional graphical options from CRT lines to rendering distance and hardware accuracy. It's incredible the lengths Walaber went to make sure the game's aesthetic is nailed down.Music: 9/10 I'll be honest, Ska is a pretty fitting genre for a game with this type of flair. The music is very good, on the account of a VERY small handful of songs I'm not the biggest fan of, but hey, that's more-so a me thing. I do wish were given the option to implement our own music into the game sometimes, and I mean that with zero disrespect to the musicians involved in the game's OSTContent and Features: 6/10 The game is pretty bite sized all things considered. Of course, this might change in the future, in hoping that it does, with the potential opportunity of making more tracks, cars, modes and mods in mind. The game comes with 8 courses (with cheats 10) across 3 vehicles (7 with cheats) and a fun set of cheat codes. I would LOVE to see more parking garages, lots and spaces based on Canada. I know the idea of making more tracks might be on the table after split-screen multiplayer comes out, so I hope that we do get more content over time. This game took an hour and a half to beat.Verdict: 8/10 With fast-paced arcade racing gameplay, nostalgic graphics and a fly (heh) soundtrack, Parking Garage Rally Circuit deserves a top 5 spot on my list of all time favourite racing games. All of this for $9 US!? Absolutely worth it. Please support Walaber, this game feels like only the beginning of a fun, tire-burning experience waiting to unfold!

_childDocuments_.review: An insanely fun arcade rally racing game with a satisfying gameplay loop of chaining drifts and boosts, allowing you to zoom across the map,though if you’re not careful, you might get flung off it. While the physics might be frustrating for some, for me, they led to some of the most hilarious moments during my playthrough. The levels are well-designed and progressively get more interesting and difficult as you advance. I’ve lost track of how many times I’ve restarted a track just to shave off a few seconds. Everything from the presentation to the gameplay is executed extremely well, and my only complaint is that there isn’t more of it. Even though it’s short, it’s still one of my favorite racing games in a long time. Definitely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this game so I'll recommend it with a Huge BUT: There are many faults, some minor others major.[ EDIT: I failed heavy class track 3, four times in a row, not even placing. I turned the music off and got gold. 100% music issue: the watered down christian rock grossness of the vocals and annoying horn midi pre and post race was psychologically affecting me lmao. 10/10, despite the rainbow road and game engine cult, game plays WONDERFULLY now,]A minor thing is the opening voice sfx and overall volume is extremely low. I can barely hear even the echo of the announcer's first line in the intro and the music isn't much louder. That's OK because the nature of having the same music sounds for every song and music element gets old fast. There's some refreshing variety in the song choices later on, and the overall music is fine, but using the same brass band for the race start/finish gets exhausting as the music is also the same band for the first 3 tracks. That does play into the old school way of how it was done, so I suppose it can get a pass.The controls are good, I can see the game getting sweatier and sweatier to get bronze 5 or 6 tracks in, to the point where over-drifting without skill or track knowledge can lead to a slower time than straight-up driving  and turning normally in some parts. And if you get off track, good luck because the reset button will usually send you 10-15 seconds back from where you were, before a curve series with a straight at the end, at least it did for me, every time. Even Mario Kart put you back on track at the same x position, losing only 5-7 seconds. Not to mention the physics of hitting a wall at speed will usually play the same spin-out animation that turns the car 180°, but that's a skill issue in that it isn't a 'full max throttle all the time' type of game, despite that being what a lot of older arcade-y race games were all about.A major issue are the corners themselves. At first, the arrows on the blue time gates were conflicting with the arrows on the yellow barriers. I had to consciously train myself to focus only on yellow and not look at the bright white arrows pointing in the opposite direction of the curves. That's fine, and there was only one single spot where the barrier arrows actually WERE pointed in the wrong direction of the curve, presumably because the object was also used on the opposite side of the barrier, so the arrows on both sides of the object face the same way, I assume to save space on a technical level in re-using the asset instead of a specifically redesigned one to be used only once. That means this trick could be used on a track further in.Then the lights went out. Now, one thing that race games have in common for the most part is letting the player know what type of major corner is coming up if it's drastically different from the current section. Conventional Rally driving does this by using a navigator sitting beside you to let you know the corner intensity that's coming up in 50m, 100m, etc because memorizing a non-linear track with a ton of corners that you can't really practice on isn't usually going to happen. Other games to this by showing a giant hairpin or dogleg etc. sign before the curve. When the lights go out here, good f-ing luck knowing where the corner is without a ghost in front. There was even one spot on that first no-lights track where I had no idea I had to turn because of the wall of black in front of me. tldr; fun retro-style game with a few roadblocks in repetitive music, visual corner/track navigation and off-track car resets.

It's easy to pick up and learn, and hard to master, with a very high skill ceiling and tons of room for improvement even after beating the hardest set times on every track. _childDocuments_.review: Parking Garage Rally Circuit is a racing game that ironically has nothing to do with parking a car.  Instead, you're racing around various location that just happen to be centered around parking garages.In single player, you start with the light car class and have to progress through 8 different tracks.  There are 3 things you need to know about how to drive.  Gas and break are pretty self explanatory, but there is also a drift button. When you turn and hold down the drift button, you start to enter a drift, obviously.  Sparks appear around your tires after half a second, and then when you release it, you get a small burst of speed.   If you've played any of the Mario Kart games, you should already be familiar with drifting.  But the one key difference is your drifting boosts can chain together back to back to further increase your overall speed every time.   In fact, there is technically no limit to how fast your speed can increase.  You can go well over 100 mph if you want.  Which sounds broken, until you realise you actually need to navigate your car through the course.  Which is why breaking also becomes essential if you wanna get a fast time among other players.   These courses have there own set of turns, jumps, parked cars, and sometimes gimmicks that you need to be aware of.You'll also need to navigate through various checkpoints placed on the course in order. That means you won't find any BS strat that allows you to skip 70% of a course. Thankfully the game is pretty lenient in the aspect of checkpoints, as you don't need to directly go through the center of the markers.  Just hitting the side of it with your car is good enough.  If you get a fast enough time, you can unlock new tracks and vehicle classes.   Beating the gold time in each course allows you to retry it, facing off against ghost data of multiple players around your skill level.   You can even select some of the best player ghosts and face off against them too if you want.There is a multiplayer mode where you can either join a lobby made by another player, or make your own.   The host of the lobby controls the car type used by all players, the track, and the amount of laps.  You can text chat with others in the room while you wait for the next race to start.  During these races, you face off against other players like you would expect, but there is no collision with their cars.  So while you're essentially racing against ghosts, these ghosts are still real time active players.There is a bit more I can talk about with Parking Garage Rally Circuit, but if you like what you've heard about this game so far, I'd say it's best to discover the rest for yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just delightful. It feels like a mix between drift-based arcade racers and Trackmania. From the former, you get your physics model: slow vehicles that can drift, and drifting for long enough gives you boost. There's a really neat twist, though; the boost you get from drifting increases your top speed without limit, so chaining drifts together lets you build up a crazy amount of speed. It can quickly become uncontrollable, and with how tight these courses tend to be it's easy to crash once you've built up that momentum. That makes for satisfying driving, where part of the challenge is seeing just how fast you can push the car before deciding to bleed some speed to maintain control.The Trackmania influence is felt in how the races are structured. In this game, everything is a time trial. All you race are ghosts, so there's no collisions. That's good, since these tight lanes can barely fit your car let alone allow for passing. Each course has a host of medal ghosts to beat, and after you beat them you can chase the ghosts of other players for a better leaderboard position. Instant restarts helps reinforce that chase, since there's no penalty for restarting. You've got as much time as you like to get the best run you can.Since everything is time trial based here, there's a lot riding on the quality of the race courses. I'm happy to say that each one is distinct and fun. Some offer interesting twists between laps, such as the Mt. Rushmore course with a boulder crashing down on the first lap. Others are straightforward, but those can be even more difficult with technical sections that really test your ability to manage your speed. The Chicago course comes to mind, with its long drifts that are perfect for building up tons of momentum paired with low ceiling jumps that will punish you for going too fast.Overall, this is a short game that's a blast to play the whole time. It's got a great theme, fantastic style, fun physics, and satisfying driving. I'd call that a $10 10/10 experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Stumbling upon Parking Garage Rally Circuit, I was fresh from two big losses of data. One was during a 40 hour play-through of Ring of Red for the PS2, the other was my 10 year old save file of Resident Evil Outbreak File #1. I was distraught, though at the time, I don't know WHY I was so affected. I would understand later. Crushed, I took just a day break from video games, anything to get my brain a bit of time from just losing all that progress. Looking for something to play, Steam recommends me Parking Garage Rally Circuit (PGRC). Being the ♥♥♥♥♥ for nostalgia for systems I have no real childhood connections to (my first gaming consoles were a SNES and PS2), PGRC seemed to be right up my alley. I adore RR4 and PGRC appeared to be the Saturn equivalent. The models were a dead ringer, the color palette was on point. In contrast to RR4's slick cool and cigarette smoke filled landscapes, PGRC seemed to be candy sweet. The energy and sauce that flowed from this package of seemingly good times and high speed racing action with satisfying drifts was exactly what I needed. I booted up the demo that was available and played PGRC. After some time of playing the tracks within the demo, I thought "Yeah, I'll pick this up when it comes out!" Added to my wishlist and went about my day. For about 10 minutes, until I booted the demo back up and kept playing. I never gave a ♥♥♥♥ about ghosts in racing games, even in my beloved RR4, I just ignored that aspect and raced for a better time. But for PGRC, I jumped back in and played some more. I started competing against ghosts. I started having a lot of fun climbing up the leaderboards! Soon, however, I was getting upset. I would barely get clipped by a wall and get sent careening and flying into the air. Immediately, I would reset. Figuring out little shortcuts or bits of tech from seeing ghosts zip past me. Let go of the drift button a quarter second too early and get lapped by three phantoms. Understand more about the physios of the game and how to avoid the jiggly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of grazing a wall and being sent 40 miles in the opposite direction. Give and take, give and take. Smashed table. Rising blood pressure. Gritted teeth. Sweltering heat. READY. SET. GO! Drift here, drift there. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ physics. Cut through barriers. Dirt trails. Scream of anguish as I fling myself into space because a parked car gently kissed my rear tire like the breeze. Scream of victory as I meek out a win and climb higher and higher. Can you hear me, heaven? i'm coming. Jacob, this ladder sure is handy. Three hours have passed. three hours of the same two tracks. I close the demo and eagerly await the full game. Months pass. The sun rises on this glory Earth of ours. The morning's cool wind feels good on the soul. Mother Ocean laps against the sand. I go to work. PGRC is live. Get home. Install it. I'm back in the hot seat. I grip the wheel. Walaber welcomes me back. READY. SET. GO! Off to the races. Push. Push. Push. I'm rusty. BANG. BAM. BOOM. SKID. SCREECH. SKIRRRT. CRASH. CRUMPLE. CRACK. CREAK. The chassis groans in pain. The engines roar to life. I forget that the physics invite you in with a hug and a kiss, hiding a knife behind its back. I rocket across pavement. I grit my teeth against the MPH.  It takes a while for me to get back into the saddle. PGRC's movement is floaty as all hell and the need to constantly drift chain adds stress upon me. I work my way through [LIGHT], the levels become more complex. More easily manipulated. More exploited. Less friendly. Go too fast? Get your head blow smoove off by the ceiling. Too slow? Your opponents are already on Lap 2. Balance is key. One must juggle handling and speed, as with all racing games. Gold trophies line up my walls. They are nothing, but dust to me. Like a man who has all the riches that can be found on Earth, my soul is empty. I shed my life for the leaderboard. This is new. I hate the leaderboard. Yet PGRC keeps me up. I think about it during work, as I sleep, as I wake. I see my past self, my own phantom zoom right past me. I fall behind. My peak is drifting and grinding its wheels against asphalt. My older self, barely minutes older struggles to catch up. I never was a fan of the OST, too happy, too much ska. I have too much Streetlight Manifesto in my brain anyway. Anthony1, Exodia and Sienna Sleep blast directly into my synapses, free of charge. I become vibration. The colors of Trance and HexD wash me. Baptism. The engine refuses to sputter into that good night. Restart. Again. Again. Again! ♥♥♥♥ the guy higher than me on the leaderboards, "he attacks enlightenment and perches twelfth-century fanaticism, posturing away there...". Perfection is but a twitch away. A singular, barely perceptible muscle spasm. Top 10%. Top 5%. I would get these positions on the leaderboards. 121. 49. 20. 58. Meaningless. I always strived to get all achievements in my games, do every single mode available, exhaust all options, play on the hardest difficulty. If I didn't, I felt like I didn't beat the game, I didn't experience it in its entirety. My brain is trapped by this line of thinking. Dissatisfaction and envy filled me. I always saw my skills are hardline mediocre. Contradiction was my shield. "If I'm bad at games and I got rank 78, surely everyone below me MUST be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and those above must be, at least, okay." Skewed negativity and narcissism as a human. I started up [HEAVY]. More gold trophies. My hubris grows. I think I understand the lay of the land. the sound of cylinders are my applause. The screech of wheels my cheers. My chains become heavier without my notice. I replaced Outbreak and Ring of Red with PGRC. A foolish man desperate to replace a loved one. Consumed by validating my own skills, I placed my hand upon the stove. Lessons are hardly learned by this old dog. 10%. 5%. [ULTRA]. My wings fall apart. I reach out to Father Sun, cracked skin and chipped nails. My worn hands feel the warmth of love before I descend further and further away from Heaven. Heads in my hand, I stare at Top 20%. 30%. 40%. I rack my brain,  During this leg of the game, I have never felt such anger in my body, so much bile spewed out of my mouth. Blood raced down my face. Time was a grainy film, lifelessly flickering on my retinas. Sound was muted. All that was present was the steady thump of Kaizo Slumber. In that moment, a question. Who was I? What meaning did my presence have at a time which this "film" so sadly beyond time now recalls? Validation from no one but myself. Some sort of other, my brain needed something to show that it exists, that I was just mediocre at the things I love. Breathe in. Breathe out. Breathe in. Breathe out. Should I give up? Learn to let go? Stop burdening me with this poison? Every game a struggle to prove that I'm good? Learn to enjoy games and not care about difficulty? Scoff at a challenge and learn to go at games at a leisure pace? Closed eyes are much more open in my opinion. Breathe in. Breathe out. Lessons are hardly learned by this old dog. It is surrender. Umile ebbrezza del contemplare. Lord forgive me, but it's time to go back to tha old me (literally just the me from two minutes ago). My only thought now. "♥♥♥♥ the guy above me!" Go beyond velocity. Godliness is only 120 MPH away. Ruin your hands. Destroy your bones. Dash away your nerves. Burn them off. Set yourself on fire. Awaken anew. Phoenix. Your body rises up. Banner-like, you are on the winds now. The blaring boom of music courses through your veins. Light fills me. I see it. I'm home... I hate you, PGRC, I hate you so much.See you next week, PGRC.Walaber! The turn on the fifth checkpoint on Seattle Airport is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ trash, dawg. Like be for real, man. ♥♥♥♥ is some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, ♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun, and very well made. Most of these gimmick type games I tend to doge, mostly because the gimmick runs thin after an hour or so, but the physics and controls for the car are have more depth than they might show at first. The mechanic of drifting to gain speed, a mechanic that is pretty well worn within various racing games, has been made the core mechanic; by chaining multiple drifts, your speed will continuously increase. Now, the tracks are in essence a car obstacle course, so by speeding you run the risk of overwhelming your control of the car and ending up spinning out. What makes this mechanic work is how much control you have over your vehicle, and how intuitively mechanics are to players. You can increase or decrease your cars arc by leaning out of or into the direction of the arc with movement joystick, allowing to adjust the arc moment to moment. You can also use your brake to further tighten arcs without ending drifts. Also, when you are drifting you cling to the floor, allowing the car to climb and descend ramps without losing control of the car.The game also does a very competent job at communicating information to the player. The speed of the boost is determined by how long you drift, and when you get to the first boost speed yellow sparks appear under the wheel, at the next speed level the sparks turn turquoise. Boost is indicated by the fire coming out of the exhaust pipes and speed lines. The track is indicated both by the track mini map and the markers that double as checkpoints. All of this is very easy to understand at a moment's notice, and is integrated smoothly into the game's visual and mechanical feel.This is a very good game. Would recommend. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: The games premise revolves around you drifting around parking worlds around the world. Think Mario Kart, where you have to spin up a drift boost, and the longer you hold a drift, the better the boost is. There are 8 different tracks and 3 car classes, resulting in 24 races for you to complete. The drifting feels incredibly tight and satisfying, and it’s a blast to zip zoom, trying to combo as many drift boosts as I can to get ahead of the invisible enemies. The levels have a lot of variety from one another, and each have a gimmick, reminding me of Sega Race TV. One stage has boulders and tree trunks that fall onto the stage, a rather large annoyance, but after a few restarts you end up memorising where they will land so you can avoid them. The music is also really nice, but by default the game is extremely quiet, and I genuinely couldn’t hear the music through my playthrough. There are a ton of graphical settings to make this game your own. You can upscale the game, to look less like a Saturn title, and more like a Model 2 arcade game. You can turn on fake CRT effects, and choose whether you want to play in 4:3 or in 16:9 / 16:10. There are also scaling options, which is useful for preserving the integer scaling on a higher resolution monitor. The game also scales to low resolutions, which allowed me to play the game in 640x480 on my CRT (though if I can make a suggestion to the dev, we need a way to remove the Saturn dithering effect and turn any fake transparency into a solid, as playing on a CRT with composite results in a lot of rainbow banding)The only thing that I dislike about this game are the physics, which can be wonky at times. Sometimes my car will randomly fly higher than normal, and sometimes it can get stuck on the walls. Also, the Seattle track is a b***h, it took me probably around 30 attempts to beat it because of the barrier separating the tracks.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, definitely worth the price. The two cars I've unlocked so far feel great to drive and play differently enough that make the tracks change slightly depending on which one you play. Track design is also fantastic. I love how its designed for one car and you compete with ghosts. Success or failure is determined by your execution of controls, not chaotic coincidence or sabotage. The soundtrack is fantastic as well.

_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: A game developed by Walaber, who created one of my favorite childhood iOS games, JellyCar. I saw him demoing this game on TikTok, and figured I'd check it out.This game is incredibly fun. The controls feel tight and fair, and getting up to 100mph+ is incredibly satisfying. Trying to maintain that speed through some tight corners while avoiding obstacles is surprisingly less frustrating than I thought it would be -- it just motivates me to try again.I have no nostalgia associated with this type of graphics and gameplay. Despite that, this game has been a blast thus far, and I'm excited to get a gold medal on every stage with every car type. Highly recommend if you enjoy fast-paced arcade-style games whose only goal is to continually strive to get better and faster!Works perfectly out-of-the-box on Steam Deck, by the way.

_childDocuments_.review: I can already tell I am gonna play this game a lot. It is like the time trials in Mario Cart but with extra drifting fun and a really nice online leaderboard. The best part is the three cars feel really different to play so it is like a completely different race even on the same tracks. _childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Fun! Feature rich, small packageRoll Daytona, Crash team racing (reserve boosts) and jellycar together and you get this. 8 courses that you run through on three weight classes. The gold ranks are very lenient so you can get all the achievements quick.I sort of assumed racing in narrow garages could be frustrating, but there are silly physics that give you some leeway (or send you ragdolling). The ska soundtrack lured me in. Snappy, slick and reliable drifting.The real challenge is in pushing the leaderboards, the game elegantly displays your percentile rank and seamlessly drops ghosts near your best score on each course, so I pushed for top 10 and 5% on a few favorites. Restarting a course is instant, and keeps you trying. Multiplayer is an unlock, don't expect to fill it, but its cool it exists. Chicago & to a lesser extent minnesota feel much too busy, feel like I'm getting too much air or trying much too hard to memorize stuff-- whereas I don't mind New Orleans at all, even with the lights going off. My favorites are San Francisco, New York, Wyoming, which feel great.I love little experiences like this that go a little beyond to feel complete. I don't really care for jelly car (their other game) but this was fun, cheers

_childDocuments_.review: fun hectic racing game, tracks are fun, the physics and driving feels good, feels awesome when you hit a sick line on a bunch of turns. and all the parked cars and props being the track and obstacles, as well as being able to push things aside to make shortcuts, all good stuff. hope it gets more tracks and features. def recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: a goofy retro arcade racer on the surface with hidden depth. the mechanics are easy to learn but difficult to master. the top speeds in this game are ludicrous, and the top of the leaderboards will seem laughably unattainable for all but the most furious racers. but dont let this deter you- this game is pure distilled fun. whether you want to drift your way to the top of the leaderboards or coast through the singleplayer campaign while bopping to old school ska, this game has a little something for everyone : )
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Insanely addicting! The drifting feels so fluid and clipping the apexes is extremely satisfying. Every lap I'm pushing how much closer I can get to the limit without flying off course. There's something about having two wheel's off course while clipping a checkpoint that's sooo satisfying. The controls feel really dialed in. Some courses can be difficult, but never overly frustrating in my opinion.Despite growing up in the 90's, I didn't play many games so I don't have much nostalgia for this style unfortunately (terrible of me, I know). Because of that, I usually find it hard to enjoy graphics like this, but this game has really changed that for me. It's so fun that it doesn't matter what it looks like and even then, I've really grown to love how it looks. So even if you don't have any nostalgia for retro games, this is still well worth your time!The soundtrack is also a lot of fun and matches the vibe perfectly. Hard not to have a smile on your face while drifting around to ska in the background! You can tell a lot of passion went into this game. I just hope more content gets added in the future. With more content, I can see me coming back to this game again and again. I will never look at parking garages the same way again!

_childDocuments_.review: Only played for 3 hours, but feels like I grew up on this glorious little game. The fact you're driving in super-tight parking garages really gets you to learn the tracks on another... layer.  Then, once you do, you really learn how to lean into the... drift mechanics.  The elegant simplicity of learning the track, the drift-chain-boosting, and where to use one boost vs. two is all so fun and robust that even the occasional moments of physics frustration can't bring me... to speak ill of this game.  Though, for all people praise it, I can't say I really noticed the soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Fun arcade rally game.It's super short at 8 tracks each, but you are able to unlock different car types that perform differently and can make courses more difficult if you're not careful.The controls are tight and courses even tighter, you need to master drifting, boosting, and approach jumps and corners with care, or else you'll find yourself being launched off course, potentially ending your run.The physics aren't too wonky for the most part, however you may find yourself sideways up a wall, or tilting forwards off a jump which is enough to send you flipping and spinning in a way that can be pretty frustrating.The big thing you need to learn to succeed in this game is drifting, which leads to boosts, and then chaining drift boosts to increase your speed, sometimes well beyond what is actually necessary, and to an uncontrollable degree.And once you have that down, it's all about when, where, and how to approach each turn and potential drift spot.Alongside the driving gimmicks, each course has its own hazards you need to watch out for, ranging from boulders falling to a complete blackout. You are going to fail a few times due to these, but that's the nature of the game. It's very much a retro game, in which you are encouraged to go back to it again and again in the pursuit of mastery.The OST is fantastic, and fits perfectly with the feel of the game. The ska soundtrack makes it feel very of the era, and sets the tone for each course pretty well.Overall, I'd recommend it. There's not a lot to the game, but finally getting that perfect run on a track, and racing alongside other ghosts with similar times is something that keeps me motivated to go one more round.I'd love to see more tracks in the future
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: An arcade racer with legitimately great driving physics. Super unique concept that just works, and the Trackmania-esque replay ghosts make for a lot of replayability.
