_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: They did such a great job making this game look and feel like a classic Sega style arcade game. There's a bunch of options to change the way the game looks, whether it be on a classic CRT or a remastered "PC Port". The controls feel really good. This is a super solid game and you should definitely give it a try if you dig that retro rally style.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: A short but very sweet arcade racer with a novel setting and a ridiculously fun drift/boost system! _childDocuments_.review: 9/10Too good for it's content! (I've just learn't that there is a new car and track hidden behind a cheat code!! the new car does have it's own campaign although it's not connected to any achievements. This is great news! I also heard there might be more cars but I don't know if they have their own campaigns too.)Too good for it's content!It took me a bit above 4 hours to beat this game (gold in all tracks with all cars). that's not great. There is a total of 8 tracks with 3 cars. the cars work more as a difficulty upgrade to the campaign. beat the light car and unlock the heavy car. then do it all again with the heavy car. This might sound boring.. and honestly, I was very disappointed when I realised the other cars didn't have their own tracks, but dang.. this game is so addictive and fun.. I must have spent about 1 hour in the title screen doing nothing and the rest of the time you see was me actually trying to beat online time trials.. something I don't remember the last time I've ever done in a video game. This game is f'ing fun! I'm still thinking of doing some more tracks to get my placement up on the leader boards now. Why am I doing this? well two reasons. One good and one bad. the game is way more fun than it has content for. I could honestly play this game for hours if only there was more content. I'm desperately trying to extend the time I am playing it by doing things I don't normally do like chase leader-board positions. There is another mode, "Endurance" but unfortunately it didn't make it to the campaign. It's a shame because I tried it once and it was a lot of fun. I would even settle for that as a new campaign. the "endurance" campaign lol. I'm not joking, I'd do the same 8 tracks all over again x3 cars for that mode :/ but it doesn't reward you for doing it. It does however have leader board positions which might extend the game a bit. But again, it's not as relevant even in the ui as the main mode so it just feels like it's not as important. This is the number one issue with this game but it was so cheap.. (it was launched with a %15 discount though).Almost perfect controls!The controls are almost perfect. I was so surprised because usually the controls are one of the things they never get right in racing indie games. It always ends up feeling cheap and nothing like those awesome arcade games from the 90s. This game however feels just like a big budget production from back then. the only issue is this weird mechanic where your speed is stored even through breaking. It's really hard to explain but you can accumulate speed boosts by sliding. When you have a ton of speed boosts the car goes much much faster. When you break you'd expect the speed to reduce a lot more and it does but if you release the break then it feels like the speed boost comes back in full. this is really annoying and awkward and if it's an intended feature I don't think it was well thought out. this makes some tracks really annoying (Chicago specially) but it's not enough to ruing the game.The dev has mentioned that he is putting mirror tracks and reverse tracks on his list of things to do. I only hope they won't be like endless and pushed to the back and that they won't have a campaign or any achievements associated with them. I think a great idea for extended content maybe in a dlc that i would happily pay for, would be sections to all the tracks that already exist sort of like ridge racer. You have 8 stages and they can be further subdivided into 3 or 4 stages. instead of having the campaign as is you could have short versions of all the other tracks except the starting track, then when you've beaten the shortened version mode you could  unlock the shortened versions mode in reverse and the rout bs. then when you beat rout b you unlock reverse rout b and rout c etc. Man. What else can I say.. give me content, give me dlc..make endurance modes have it's own campaign and chivies. i wanna play more!! absolutely deserves full price despite completing it in 4 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent arcade racing game that aims to capture the gritty, low poly aesthetic of Sega Saturn arcade racers like Sega Rally and Daytona USA.  Each track has a "gimmick" that sets it apart from the others, and the parking garage theme they all have provides some interesting verticality and lots of chances for ramps and jumps.  Has a drift-to-boost mechanic that has you sliding around any chance you get to accelerate ahead and stay at top speed, the longer you drift the more boost you get, with the level of boost indicated by the color of the sparks shooting out from your rear wheels in the vain of Mario Kart.  Ultra bouncy physics that can get a little frustrating once you reach the hardest difficulty, but are mostly fun to grapple with and get used to.  Also some excellent ska music, my two favorites being the songs with lyrics that play in the San Francisco and Liberty Island tracks.  Only major criticism is the amount of content is a bit lighter than I would like, doesn't bother me too much due to how replayable it is, but if it bothers you it might be worth waiting for a sale.  Otherwise, if this seems like the kind of thing you're into, it almost certainly is, definitely give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: You drive, you drift, you boost, you drift faster, you boost faster, you drift fastest, you boost fastest.It's a fantastic example of one of those 'simple' games of decades past, where pure, precise gameplay is all you need to enjoy it.Drive fast, tumble about, ram barriers and beat your time. What more can you ask for?
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Really love the "Sega Rally on the Saturn" graphics, makes it feel like you're playing a lost Saturn game. The sound track sounds like it could of been from Daytona USA, which is great! Great late 90s Sega goodness.After getting gold in all maps with all 3 cars, I gotta say I love the track design and game mechanics. Trying to find the perfect optimal route is a good challenge, a lot of depth to it which shows that the Dev knows how to make a good arcade game. Just like a good classic arcade game, the game is short, but the amount of time it takes to perfect your skills is where the real length of the game comes from. Getting gold was a frustrating (in the good way) but exhilarating experience, which made this game very worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright, it's a cute little racing game where the courses are largely a minute and a half long. The worst I can say about it is it's very easy to go TOO fast, and given you still go max speed but with basically no control while airborne it is very easy to go sailing either off the stage or into a barrier and the entire race is basically over as you recover.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually like racing games, but Parking Garage Rally Circuit feels like a perfect amount of arcade-y to toe the line and it was a blast. Only took me 3.5 hours to 100% so it's not too long, but there's replayability in trying to beat your own score or your friends/other players, and it has multiplayer lobbies which is a plus. super fun and feels great to play!
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun! Easy to learn and difficult to master. The blend of simple and approachable controls with the ramping speed as you chain drifts together, combined with some occasionally unruly physics, makes  excellent at being both a fun party racer and also a challenging speedrun grind for time trials. Trying to eek out an extra drift in every corner and then balance the absurd speed with the limitations of the track is a fun ebb and flow. The game also has plenty of charm, not just in its visual style and the many ways you can tweak it to your liking, but also being evocative of the Saturn era in its UI design and Ska soundtrack. Having a narrow scope allows the game to be filled with details that have you feeling the love poured into it, like the references to other indie games as posters in the mall stage or the choice of how the camera navigates the terrain when it zooms to you as a stage is loaded in.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute joy! The rally racing feels super smooth, and the power sliding mechanic is just so fun to master—you'll find yourself constantly trying to beat your best time. The bouncy physics add a bit of challenge, but it never gets frustrating, just makes it all the more rewarding. The retro vibe with its catchy soundtrack gives it that perfect nostalgic touch.And to top it off, Walaber, the developer, is incredible! They stream a ton of their development and are always engaging with the community. Honestly, if you love classic racing games, this one is a must-have!
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Well Done Walaber for bringing back a blast from the past from this lovely game, awesome old school 3d models and graphics, the soundtrack is an banger and awesome to listen to when racing against mates weather its online or by racing against the clock offline to place yourself on the leader board. the controls are smooth and easy to get into, the game replay ability is just spot on knowing that you want go bronze first to get the feel of the track then when you get the idea of how the game and the mechanics work then you can go for gold or for sliver, but i feel like there should be a platinum trophy ghost for gamers that really want to put there skills to the test would be an awesome addition for more challenges.Love the demo, and loving the full release of the game!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance, this game looks like the name and not much else, and I’ll admit it’s a bit light on the content side. That being said, I love the visual style and the soundtrack; those two things alone really sell the Sega Saturn / PSX vibe this arcade racer is clearly going for.If you’re looking for a fun car physics system to master however, that is where this game truly shines. The chain boosts from drifting seem to stack infinitely, and the game actually seems designed around this. There’s no rush quite like flying around a parking garage at 100 miles an hour, only for the game to call you out on your nonsense and wreck you. It’s downright hilarious on a bad run and a pure adrenaline rush on a great run. Racing game of the year? Honestly, pretty likely.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I have played all year. Recommended by the Team VVV YouTube channel and just by the look of it made me want to check it out, The graphics, gameplay and sound has everything good about arcade games from the 90's and it's addictive trying to beat a level and get to the next. I would like to see this game come to PlayStation as that's where I normally play games. Graphics 5/5 - Great - reminds me of Daytona. The level design is really interesting and the idea of rally driving in a tower car park is amazing.Gameplay 5/5 - Great - the controls are simple but it takes a while to get used to how the cars handle but the game couldn't be better.Sound & Music 5/5 - Love the music - reminds me of the arcades and the announcer voice is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and intuitive arcade racer. If you like racing and retro graphics this is those distilled to perfection. Keep in mind however the playtime you see here is how long it took me to "100%" the game. All (current) achievements. There are less than 10 tracks and 3 car types. The main appeal of the game is replaying these tracks over and over to improve your own time and your place on the leaderboard. So don't get mad when you play through every track in under an hour, its not designed for longevity. Although with the history this dev has I assume there will be minor content updates from time to time.Overall well worth the money though.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: game is phenomenal, very simple and easy to get started but has a surprising amount of depth in the controls (imo). Has the benefit of being fun for only short play times as well, I can boot this up to a youtube video on a lunch break etc. As someone who does not normally play racing games, I loved it from the start and would recommend it to anyone.  10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Parking Garage Rally Circuit is an awesome short tribute to SEGA Saturn racing games featuring a charmingly accurate art style and memorable soundtrack. The stages are creative, the controls are tight (but still fun to master and experiment with), and the realtime multiplayer support is a welcome surprise. Highly recommended for those who can't get enough of classic arcade racing games and their cheerful summer trip vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: (As of right now, I am the #1 endurance mode scorer on San Francisco in the RX2.)This is New York's hottest club, it has everything. Sega Rally visuals, Mario Kart boosting, wild offroad physics, crazy parking garage design, the fastest slowest cars, Tony Hawk's ska band, and to top it all off, the Statue of Liberty Rainbow Road.In all seriousness, this is an absolutely amazing game. It perfectly recreates the feeling of a lost Sega racing release. It feels so fresh to have a new retro racer that's not just an OutRun or Virtua Racing clone. It feels like the kind of game that would permanently alter your taste in gaming if you'd played it when you were a little kid. It's just that good. This is going down as an all time classic retro racer, and for $10 you just can't pass it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Just wow. Literally sat down and played 4 hours non-stop.If I combined Trackmania gameplay with Mario-Kart-DS-esk drifting mechanics, this is what I'd get and I do not regret buying this.Thank you <3EDIT: Things I'd add:* Let me pick the track I wanna play on please. I just started, but I already love grinding out Track 2 (Top 10 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥) & I can't go back and play it easily! That's actually what got me to stop playing lmao.* What I would give for a track editor...
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: The game just has so much character, it's fun seeing what curve-ball each level will throw at you. Love the car customization and fantastic replay mode. The game-play is smooth, art is consistent, an overall satisfying experience. After all unlocks you still have a competitive game-play loop trying to cut down time and find every advantage you can in a lap for online leaderboards. Well done! Haven't even tried multi-player yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend PGRC! It is well worth the price for a fun, racing arcade game. It has all the aesthetics of a game release for the PS1 in 1998. The gameplay is simple, (accelerate, reverse, turn and hand brake to drift) and you use these to master the maps and get the fastest time. The maps have tons of alternate routes and shortcuts and the physics engine give you the option to exploit turns to get better times. Replayable, fun and skill required.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Very short game, one that you can finish in one sitting, but simple and fun. Only 8 tracks, 3 different cars with different handleling and speeds, with the main goal is to win every race and then set the best lap records against other players. If you got the spare money and you're interested in the game after seeing the trailer, sure go for it.My only recommendation for the dev is to add a lot more tracks, if any updates are planned.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Everything it says on the box, and a lot of fun. Just finished playing it for the first time, and it's so quick to pick up, and will probably end up being a ton of fun to master. Would totally recommend for $10, great price. I love the crash-happy nature of the physics engine. That's why I love a lot of games, is because sometimes the engine is just a bit quirky and something goes way off course, like driving up a wall. Fun game, good time, good price, all 'round good idea.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody who grew up replaying racing levels on those old Playstation Magazine demo discs, I can't say enough great things about this game. Love the throwback visuals, clever level design, tight, responsive driving controls, and this righteous ska soundtrack? This game even made me nostalgic for parking garages. Not sure if others are having this problem, but the default music volume was set incredibly low? I didn't even realize this game had such ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥' tunes until I turned up the volume in the game's settings.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels so good to play. The cars ( of which I have currently driven 2) feel so good. Chaining together drifts has never felt this good. The aesthetics and physics of the game are perfect and it gives an incredible feeling of speed (You are always seconds from flying off the the side). If you are into a ska, you will deeply love this soundtrack as much as I have. If you aren't, its still good for channeling the Saturn vibe the game is going for. My only complaint really is that the final song that plays on the Liberty Island track has an obvious reset right before you finish that race that kinda kills the vibe. Otherwise, its an amazing game that does everything it sets out to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: For the price, its hard to complain. Incredible art style, solid handling model, fun track design. A proper throwback to the old arcade racing days while still trying some new things here and there to keep things refreshing. I am admittedly dissapointed by the small track and vehicle selection, almost wishing for the $60 dollar version of this game more than anything. Regardless, a ton of fun and an easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: This is totally unrealistic arcade racer and I love it!Outstanding aesthetics! I felt like playing a DOS game again! You can even change to 4:3 DOS era aspect ratio! They really nailed that aspect of the graphics and I really like it! It basically feels like a mix of Sega Rally, Destruction Derby, Screamer and Whacky Wheels. Some might say the graphics are PS1-like (Collin McRae Rally 1 era).The gameplay is also really fun! You get to drift in order to gain speed. The tracks are challenging and even though the theme is parking garages, there's plenty of variety. Some of the tracks even evolve over after each race.The game has multiplayer! That's great as well! Unfortunately, not a lot of people at the moment.I see three main downsides. The first one is that the checkpoints are too small and it's not uncommon to miss these. Once you miss one, it's pretty much game over. Devs probably could easily expand them (please?).The second downside is that there's no collision with other cars. I get that the tracks are really tight for such thing, but it would've been great, if this was an option still.And the third downside is the music. It's not bad, but not great either. It's just OK and you can mute it.For that price, that game delivers a lot of fun! Go grab it!
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun game! Expected to just try it out for a bit and got pulled in for much longer. Playing the levels with faster and faster cars is so well done. I'm glad I didn't have that much speed out the gate or I would have been in a concrete car sandwich. Super satisfying overall, I gotta try out multiplayer and more later! 100% recommend price, game play, graphics, MUSIC.
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

_childDocuments_.review: Retro Arcade Rally Racing... in Parking Garages?!? Precision driving with tight simple controls and arcade physics, all in a Sega Saturn style presentation
_childDocuments_.name: Parking Garage Rally Circuit

name: REYNATIS
detailed_description: Special Offer About the Game Liberate your world REYNATIS is a full-blown action-packed magical RPG in which two people with different perspectives fight for their ideals in a realistic recreation of modern-day Shibuya, Tokyo. ■World/Story The year is 2024. In Shibuya, Tokyo, the Criminal Magic Response Act has issued an order barring citizens from going out at night. However, it was quickly disregarded, and few enforce it. Marin Kirizumi is a wizard who grew up oppressed by others due to his magic. “If you become the strongest, you'll be set free.' Following those words left by his father, he arrives in Shibuya at night. When Sari Nishijima discovered her magic, she decided to use her powers to maintain order. She follows her own sense of justice to protect Shibuya from forces with dangerous ideals and illegal drugs that turn people into monsters. Marin, who seeks liberation. Sari, who treats the oppression of wizards as justice. The story of REYNATIS begins when the two meet in Shibuya, a place where cultures and ideas mix. ■Battle By properly utilizing Suppressed and Liberated states, anyone can easily execute show-stopping actions. In Suppressed Mode, you are unable to attack, but you can avoid any enemy attacks with the press of a single button. In Liberated Mode, you can go all out with your attacks, but you will be unable to defend, so timing is essential. Players can instantly switch between up to three different characters in the middle of battle. Each character comes with their own unique abilities. Pick your characters depending on the situation to gain the upper hand! ■Exploration The real city of Shibuya has been painstakingly recreated in REYNATIS. Walk around the city to find everything from famous landmarks such as SHIBUYA109 to hole-in-the-wall joints that only the savviest will know. While in Suppressed Mode, your identity and actions are concealed. As long as people don’t find out you’re a wizard, you can talk with normal civilians. During these conversations, you may receive exploration tips, as well as new quests. In Liberated Mode, you can use your magic to explore and move more quickly. However, there's a chance civilians will report you to the M.E.A., who will come after you in full force. ■Another Pockets of Shibuya contain Fog, gateways to an alternate magical world called Another that only wizards can access. This clandestine realm is managed by the anti-government organization known as the Guild. Those who cannot wield magic are unable to enter, and monsters run rampant due to the magic in the air. The expanse of Another contains not only forests and wilderness, but things resembling factories and museums, as well. What lies in its deepest recesses remains unknown. ■Lastly When Marin and Sari’s paths cross, a darkness that will transform the world descends. Wishlist REYNATIS today! We hope you'll look forward to the release! Scenario / Kazushige Nojima Music / Yoko Shimomura Character Design / Yasutaka Kaburagi Creative Producer / TAKUMI Steam Version Features 4K Resolution and High Frame Rate Experience REYNATIS in 4K resolution and smooth high frame rates up to 120fps. Enjoy every scene with enhanced clarity and precision. Keyboard and Mouse Control Support Customize your playstyle with full keyboard and mouse controls, offering greater flexibility and precision in combat and exploration. Selected Graphics Options Tailor your visual experience with a variety of graphics settings, ensuring the game runs optimally on your hardware. Playable on Steam Deck Take your Shibuya action-packed experience on the go! REYNATIS is compatible with Steam Deck, delivering a smooth gaming experience wherever you are.

short_description: Fantasy meets reality in Shibuya, Tokyo, where magic is something to be feared. In this action RPG, a young wizard seeks freedom through strength, and an officer seeks to control magic and restore order. When their paths cross, a darkness that will transform the world descends.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, if nothing, has a lot of soul. It's clear that, despite the low budget and resources, the devs were very passionate about Reynatis. Because of that, I have a hard time feeling bad about the lower quality of the game. It bleeds with that Tetsuya Nomura goodness, and it's no surprise, considering the director is such a massive fan. Having grown up playing games like Kingdom Hearts, Final Fantasy, and The World Ends With You, Reynatis carries on that same spirit in all the ways that matter. I want to support this game, and what it stands for, because I want to see more games made with genuine passion like this. A new generation of game developers, inspired by the same games that drive me to create. It's a wonderful thing to see. That's to say nothing of the game itself, though. A story that feels so Nomura-esque I can see his name in the credits if I squint (No surprise there, either, with Nojima in the writer's room). Fast, tight ARPG gameplay, which while it isn't all too depthy, feels great to pick up and master for the runtime of the game. Music by the legendary Yoko Shimomura, while not up to the impossible standard of the Kingdom Hearts games, still delivers, and hits wonderfully. I'll be playing this game for a while yet. And considering they plan on supporting this game well after launch? I couldn't be happier. Maybe the full-priced entry point might be a bit much considering this game's presentation, but it is absolutely worth the time. I recommend it whole-heartedly, if you can pick it up on sale. Not everyone is a freak for this kind of thing, like me.
_childDocuments_.name: REYNATIS

_childDocuments_.review: To those who don't keep track of Square Enix timeline and shenanigans that occurred... This game is based on Final Fantasy verses 13, a story that got lost due to the turmoil that struck SE during development that ultimately resulted to replacing the original director (Nomura) with Hajime. This change caused the original story to be scrapped in favor of the current Final Fantasy 15 story. Now, Nomura and the legendary team that helped Nomura with verses 13 kinda split but in a way work together to tell that story in their own respective ways.REYNATIS is essentially a spirit of the game once lost now coming back in a different medium by instead of Insomnia, we got Shibuya while instead of Noctis, we got Marin. Interesting enough, the name means "Sea" and the sky is often the reflection of the light that comes from the sea. In a way, Reynatis is a reflection of verses 13 in some sense.Current Thoughts as someone who bought the ultimate edition (release version) cuz f it and somehow speedran the game in a completionist manner unintentionally:Combat [Great] - Jarring at the start with the demo before release, but becomes really fun when putting the trust into the combat mechanics. You basically become Noctis with UI Goku levels of evasion. Some characters have unique methods of evading and approaches on attacking, but all have one thing in common... Intentionally not dodging while in melee range to counter, time it and you'll have the same feelings like a Jujitsu Kaisen sorcerer that tasted power and knowledge upon landing a black flash. Boss fights are unique in their own way, but the most terrifying force is the enemy you encounter by intentionally reaching rank 1 popularity (aka wanted system). Only issue I have is lack of unique combos to use without using abilities... Unless I am skill-issuing myself in the regards of basic combos.Environment Gameplay [Good] - While understandable that it lacks a bit, especially with the wanted system can be avoided entirely by moving to the next zone to reset it back to 0 and non-reported state. There is a lot to do, but there is a unique flaw worth addressing... The camera. I thought pictures can be taken on it, but does not seem to be the case as there are hidden items in the city that seems to require taking a picture to receive. However, the game somehow lacks the button to... you know... take a photo ingame? The wanted system can use improving, but given how terrifying it is to face that enemy even at endgame makes me wonder if the current state of the system is a blessing in disguise.Story [Wondrous!] - A story I long awaited for. While I do understand the game cannot tell the full story of Final Fantasy verses 13, it is a great story nonetheless despite my soul yearning for the original story scrapped. The characters can be easily attached to and some are enough to shed a tear, but I do understand that some English speakers have trouble creating that connection due to the language barrier in a auditory manner despite English subtitles.Graphics [Good] - While I understand some people would want top notch graphics. I don't want that as it causes games to sacrifice story and gameplay as a result... I mean look at most current day triple A game companies trying to release a game with the selling point of just graphics, it usually fails. Plus, I grew up around really old computers and the PS3, so graphics are less worth to me compared to if the game is actually playable & fun or not.System Requirements - Quite accessible for someone with a low end laptop that can run Team Fortress 2 and Metal Gear Rising Revengence with 60 fps framerate. Able to get a stable framerate on 30 fps, still very much enjoyable at that state.My Priorities when reviewing (1 is high, 5 is low):1 - Playable?2 - Gameplay3 - Story4 - Interactions5 - GraphicsOther games to look out for that may relate Final Fantasy verses 13 that will help piece together the other pieces of the story together:Kingdom Hearts 4 - Pretty much guaranteed to come out in Nomura's vision.Verum Rex - A spin-off game that is currently in a state of superposition where it exists of both reality and imagination, but we don't know if it will truly be developed and released. However, we will know in due time once Kingdom Hearts 4 releases.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start by saying that this game is really average. Some will have fun, other will find this game very boring.The game is very repetitive and the combat is really simple with no depth. It is 60€ in my country and it's really expensive for what it proposes. We are almost at AAA prices and it's not worth it for this quality. I will say 30€ would be more fair.Just try the demo and this is what you would have for the rest of the game. So I don't recommand the game unless you can have it at a fair price then it can be a filler game you can play between the games you are trully waiting.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to video reviewers this game is great its definitely budget and most people should wait for a sale but it has so much soul and heart combat isn't insanely complex but its really funthe characters are fantastic and while the story is predictable for the campaign it seems to be going somewhere interesting in the postgame updateswhich of the postgame updates the added superboss is extremely fun and difficult its a great challenge The director is so clearly a nomura superfan and im so excited to see what he does next and i PRAY this does well enough to justify a sequel with an actual budget whats here right now was made with the budget of a lemonade stand and they still made it specialIf you were a kid who watched the versus 13 trailer on repeat and tried to play kh2fm on a untranslated emulator in 2007 this game is for you

_childDocuments_.review: Reynatis is jrpg comfort food. The setting is great, character design is solid, music is good, and the real time combat is engaging. It seems off-putting switching modes but becomes second nature once you understand you can unload, switch character, unload, switch characters, and if you get out of mana just wait for the qte and hold the dodge button until filled for a huge Mana boost. It's fun enough and easy enough to avoid the frustrations of more complex systems. It also avoids the high of something like bayanetta or dmc as it lacks the complexity. For me this is a huge go for the moment as I'm between games and it fills a niche other games do not. It's kind of short, a bit basic, and lacks an English dub (which is a real shame as this would elevate the title considerably imo). That said, the game is fun and easy to play for long sessions. The chapters alternate between parties so it keeps it fresh and the story is suprisingly good. Overall a good game that runs like butter on the steamdeck. I will say the complete edition is a HUGE waste of money as the costumes are the same without a hat or a tiny recolor. They really did us dirty with this one lol. I also always get 5 stars in battle where in the demo it was much more difficult to get s rank. Maybe there was a hidden boost in the bonuses I missed? It makes me power level as I get a 30% XP boost permanently. Kind of confused on this one as I don't have an XP boost skill. Not a huge deal as it's fun either way, just thought I would mention it as the base game is all you need here. Hope this helps!

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the game so far, sure, the 3d models are basically made for the switch, but that was already confirmed by the developer, also furyu isn't famous for technical masterpieces, but I love all their games, and this one isn't an exception so far. the combat is fast and fun, the characterization of the various protagonists and the way they interact with each other is really good too.sure, maybe full price for someone it's a bit too much, but ay leat give it a chance in the next sale

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game, but advertising it as an action game was a mistake imo. The combat is 90% skills, 10% basic attacks, and I don't feel like that was made very clear to players starting out, seeing as you can't use skills until after the first chapter. It's also important to note that this is meant to be played as a jrpg, it's just not turn based like the usual games from that genre. The story was predictable, but it was pretty enjoyable regardless. I see a lot of reviewers comparing this game to Kingdom Hearts and saying it's bad because it's not Kingdom Hearts. I'm not sure what that's about, but you can just dismiss that and wait for a sale if you're unsure about the game but want to play more than the demo has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: REYNATIS

_childDocuments_.review: Reynatis looks like a PS3 game. And I was okay with that. Style choice. I played the demo and saw potential in the game so I picked it up on launch. Unfortunately, everything else feels like a PS3 game too. It's not just the models and textures, it's the animations, mission design, story pacing, UI and menus, physics...It might get better as it goes on, but after two hours I already felt like I was going through the motions with side quests. They're basically all the same thing - talk to someone to accept the mission, go kill someone (either a drug dealer or a drug user, which is plot relevant but still felt weird) on the other side of the map, and either return to that first person for your reward or immediately receive the reward when the fight is over. As for combat, it got a little samey for me. It is unique, and probably one of the highlights of the game though. Getting up to 3 people on your team really alleviated the issue of having to swap into defensive mode when your enemy only needed one more hit but you were out of MP. Each character had a different feel but at the same time felt pretty similar somehow too. The story felt like it was going to be very predictable, but obviously I can't be certain since I didn't get that far. Still, I felt like I could guess the ending within the first 20 minutes. Shibuya looked really good, but was broken down into very small sections with quick loading screens between each one, so again felt like a PS3 game. The Forest area was a long and skinny hallway with not much going on. Difficulty was super easy most of the time, but had occasional spikes in a few battles. Nothing too challenging that I saw.I feel bad leaving a negative review on a game that was clearly a passion project for the devs, but it's just not my cup of tea. I'd suggest trying out the demo, and if you enjoy it, you'll definitely like the full game as well. If it leaves you unconvinced, it's probably not for you. Ultimately, I requested a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: REYNATIS is just a 6/10 comfort Action RPG Junk food, that I'll recommend if it's on sale+(PRAISES)+ Characters’ drip is on point+ Learning magical spells by finding graffiti( called Wizarts ) is neat+ Using Shibuya’s map to spread around abilities, upgrades, resources, and portals for unmapped “dungeons” is interesting+ Although I have no attachment to “The World Ends With You” IP, I thought the collaboration mission was fun. Learning about some of Shibuya’s point of interest (Hachiko’s Statue, the 109 Building, etc…) was cool+ The in-game Group Chat is a nice budgeted way to give the main cast characterization( the text also feels natural too, kudos to the localization team )-(NITPICKS)- The in-game Group Chat is a poorly organized, and doesn’t provide a filter for read/unread conversations- I dislike how there’s a cooldown for switching characters-Despite the story being split from two character’s POV, the cliche edgy shonen male MC(Marin Kirizumi) is given more of the focus over time. While the idealistic police onee-san that wants to eradicate drugs, restore order, and serve some justice, feMC(Sari Nishijima) slowly becomes a supporting cast- The lack of hit-stun render ‘supposedly heavy-hitting characters’ useless- Enemies designs are bland and forgettable- The enemy type that is protected by a magic sphere and demands the player to “Full-Magic Circle” dodge it in [Suppression Mode] to deactivate the barrier are time-wasting annoyance- The Final Boss is a disappointing area-pollution enemy~(NEUTRAL)~ Combat ifor the most part Very Easy, except when fighting human Bosses~ Photo mode leave a lot to be desire bc of how limited it is~ Development of this started w/ the Nintendo Switch version, which explains the outdated visuals but this is a practice I’m in favor of bc versions from more powerful system are guarantee to have better framerate/performance~ The story seems too ambitious for its budget, character arcs and emotional scenes are rushed or loses impact due to the flat visuals… which is unfortunate bc I thought the Voice Actors gave it more than their all in the performances

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not gonna lie, Reynatis caught me off guard. I bought the ultimate edition blindly, not knowing what to expect, I basically free fall'd into the game. HALO Jumping into the storyline to the point where the game legit feels like a beautiful combination of Final Fantasy (Primarily), Devil May Cry, and Yakuza (in a way) with the rep like system via "Trending on social media" and "Malice Level". You start off as a police force that hunts wizards ( I always call them Mages in my stream. It's a habit). The animations and movements are beautiful, combat is fast and there's a time stamp after every battle you go into, this I like, I love to see how fast I can destroy enemies and what I can do to fix that (unless it's a boss fight). The dodge system is fantastic and the (I wanna say parry?) system to counter melee attacks looks and IS fantastic. Dialogues are wonderful as well, and there are definitely funny moments to lighten the mood, you just gotta be immersed into the dialogue and the environment.I legit recommend anyone who loves the series like Final Fantasy, DMC, and Yakuza. This game has a wonderful 10/10 from me which is surprising considering most games I gave (and they are stated why) they have lower scores than 8/10.I am seriously happy that I got the ultimate edition as I love to look at the artworks of the game, I even took a peak at the Japanese version!I've been streaming the game and so far I am really enjoying the story, when I'm done streaming the series I will definitely make a replay of the game!My absolute favorite characters are the M.E.A officers. Nishijima, Ukai, and Dogo. They are absolutely chill and they do have funny moments at times. While packing bad ass outfits.(one note for the developers, if they read this)For the devs: I'm not sure if it's just me or Kujirai doesn't have an idle animation during conversations in the office. I'm not sure how important that would be to fix but that's just something that keeps catching my eye.Thank you for taking your time to read my review, I hope all of you will have fun playing the game!

_childDocuments_.review: If you always wanted to know what Final Fantasy Versus XIII would have been like, then pick this game up. I mean, Reynatis is not one-to-one because the original Versus XIII trailers made Versus look more serious, dark, violent, and lonely. Reynatis, while it takes itself seriously, it doesn't appear near as dark and gloomy as the old Versus trailers were.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I'm a sucker for any game with Shibuya, so I enjoyed it. It has its technical shortcomings, and it's pricey for what it offers, but it's a cool experience with a lot of passion behind it and I personally liked it a lot. I haven't played the DLC chapters yet (UPDATE: I did! see below), but did play the TWEWY crossover and otherwise 100% the game. I got 30 hours out of it, including reading all of the reports, enemy bios, and non-voiced dialogue OUT LOUD, so it is short for the price. Some more detailed review below: Classic (though modern-styled) JRPG, I completely lost the plot at the end but that's to be expected. Think Nomura-levels of "what on Earth is going on", only slightly mitigated by the collectible reports. The more accessible part of the story provided a shockingly non-tropey and semi-realistic view on drugs, the police, and sensationalism of the public (flawed since it's a fantasy universe, but refreshing nonetheless). Otherwise, I enjoyed the messages the cast sent to each other- fleshed out their personalities and grounded the story in the modern day. Some dialogue seemed weird, which I assume was a localization thing. Also, some character motivations were strange, and again towards the end I stopped understanding what most bosses and some main characters were thinking. As everyone says, they're not great graphics for this day and age, but I honestly don't care. IMO it's a bit higher than standard for Switch, and I'm used to a lot worse. Some environments seem flat, but overall they make it work, even if it feels like you went back in time a decade or so. Load times were also fast, and I suspect the graphics contribute to that, so I'm actually grateful. Big exception to this is the TWEWY crossover- those models are, uh, really funny. And short. Couldn't stop laughing. (I love TWEWY. I thought it was really endearing, haha, but those poor models.) I played with mouse/keyboard, don't know about controller. I didn't actually know that you were supposed to be able to attack with mouse at all, so I never found that an issue, but I didn't like how some buttons weren't re-assignable. I ended up with a silly setup using mouse outside of battle for mouse camera vs both hands on keyboard (more buttons) for combat. So, little to no camera switching in combat, but it worked fine.  Combat was honestly pretty interesting! The attacking but was pretty standard, but having characters not preemptively dodge but rather right after when suppressed was new. Each character felt unique in combat which is awesome. Combat never was difficult though, and even the final boss was brute force with items that I picked up throughout the game. For Shibuya navigation, a large part of movement is liberation/combat/faster movement/item detection in populated areas that puts you on a wanted list. It is easily mitigated by just moving to a different area, but besides that I found it was a cool way to do some storytelling through mechanics- I'm sure there's some social commentary about self-defense or the mental toll of publicly being your true self when you're marginalized or something. Should be noted that an end-game item helps with item detection, so don't worry about having to find stuff in large public areas.Weird that selling items was introduced late in the game, and I do feel like a lot of mechanics weren't super developed (like, the shop mechanic was used for one thing and restaurants just sold different flavors of HP heal). Note that the settings provide an option to remove the confirm dialogue to make selling a lot easier and faster. Post-combat screens let you move while combat results are being displayed unless it was a story event, but there's this weird extra button press you have to make sometimes. Some of the UI transitions are a bit clunky. Also, game thinks I didn't sell a unique item I definitely did when mashing the sell button, so, uh, I wouldn't sell items too quickly? Then there's the mouse attack thing that everyone's talked about, but it didn't affect me. Genuinely surprised that music was by Yoko, as it felt very much background to everything that was going on. It worked with the game, but there wasn't any time when I felt like the music stood out or helped make a scene memorable, and that's a shame. There were some scenes where there was no music at all, and while it kind of worked, they could absolutely have put something in there to make it feel less dead. Characters are semi-voiced and only in Japanese, which is fine with me, but might be a turn-off for some. I learned, like, 2 phrases lol By the time combat becomes slightly difficult, the item and wizart DLC isn't necessary, and the costumes- well, I guess get those if you really care about how your character works. Again, haven't played the DLC chapters yet. (EDIT: see next paragraph :) ) Obviously if you're interested in the art/designer commentary or music you can get those respective things. Mini art book is in English, full art book has both Japanese and English versions.UPDATE: I played the DLC chapters (free, but downloadable content nonetheless). Sari's chapter is fine to play, but I wouldn't recommend playing the post-game ones unless you like being left on a cliffhanger for a few months or potentially forever if it gets cancelled (they're releasing a series of these chapters). The original ending can be satisfying enough, even though it leaves things to the player's imagination, and these chapters ruin that in spades. There are no dogs in this game, but there are cats. Interacting with them (I don't think it's a physical pet, just respectfully distant admiration of feline) removes your stress. meow

_childDocuments_.review: I like enjoyed this game. you can feel that they were trying to tap into that sort of PS2 Kingdom hearts energy here. The music definitely helps set the mood, the story has intrigue to set up another game and the characters help hold it all together. Bosses look grand the way you might expect for a JRPG and the game has flourishes to help expand on characters like text threads, giving them more personality and backstory in the main plot isn't quite enough.There are shortcomings here, the enemy difficulty isn't that challenging after a certain point and there attacks can feel too easy to dodge at times. while I like the character designs, the art direction for 3D character models isn't quite as proportionate in look as the 2D character portraits, as in, they don't look as nice. The animations for characters and enemies can appear rough or too simple and rigid as well. The story has you fight people afflicted by rubrum, these are not interesting enemies and in the story there is no hope for any of these people to recover. The problems caused by Rubrum are apparent and characters have a vendetta against the drug but the effects are not felt in the game's Shibuya, it looks very clean and the people don't seem bothered either.Knowing that this game is drawing from Final Fantasy Versus XIII and doing it's own thing is interesting to me and I would like to see it delved upon in a sequel. I want the team to have a chance to refine what is already established here and take it further. Marin Kirizumi can come off as a very bland sort of edge lord  the way he only wants to be the strongest but seemingly has no plan for what to do with that power. Much like Marin, the battle system, the enemy design and the plot, Reynatis has great potential, I just hope both with have another chance to unleash it. An interesting game if you like that sort of PS2 energy but waiting for a discount is always good

_childDocuments_.review: Great music. Story is somewhat interesting. Combat was kind of fun but you will hit a point in the game where you can cheese everything and it is button mashing gameplay until you run into 1 specific enemy towards the end of the game. That one is so annoying, you literally need to "disengage" and then do the perfect evade to remove its barrier so you can damage the enemy. This wasted so much time and they attack very slow so you are usually sitting there just waiting for them to do an attack that you can perfect evade. That enemy type literally made this game unfun to play. The characters were enjoyable in their own way. Anime trope AF I found myself skipping through a lot of unimportant dialog. Took me a little less than 20 hours to get all the achievements.I would not pay full price for this game. I think a fair price might be $20 USD if it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Reynatis is an action RPG leaning on the RPG side, so optimizing equipment and stats is more important than reflexes. It still is a fun action game but very easy as such; if you stock on consumable items to recover HP or counter bad stats you can take plenty of hits without dying. It has a just guard mechanic to revover MP faster which is decidedly RPG like in its execution and unintuitive for action game fans, which spawned much controversy. Basically you wait and react to a fullscreen prompt rather than the attack animation.It has a lot of unique ideas, like suppressed (defensive) and liberated (offensive) states, stress levels (which boost offense but lower defense and might force you into liberated state), public attention which draws the cops. These gameplay mechanics reflect themes of the narrative, which seems like a belated rendition of the canceled Final Fantasy Versus XIII. Much lower budget but also unfiltered by company politics. If FFXV was suppressed, Reynatis is liberated.The game is set in real world Shibuya at night, which is rendered in a beautiful color palette. It's not open world but segmented, which helps with escaping from bystanders taking photos of you on their smartphones and uploading it to social media after a battle. There are also portals to typical fantasy game like environments which have limited map access. A nice feature is that after a battle an arrow indicates where you were headed pre battle to avoid getting disoriented. You will spend a lot of time walking around Shibuya and another great idea is the Wizarts, graffitis you can spot on the walls to acquire eqippable skills and stat boosters. These as well as items which are only visible in liberated state make the environments very interactive, requiring you to look around, even when you are following quest markers.Character animation is lacking (no budget for motion capturing) and the characters and world are a bit low poly, but reasonably big and busy. Art design does offset these limitations and the BGM is top notch. FuRyu follows their usual strategy to hire big names, featuring scenario writer Kazushige Nojima, composer Yoko Shimomura and image art designer Yusuke Naora. Despite the low budget the game is reasonably polished with some exceptions, which boil down to minor annoyances:Sometimes you will accidentally escape a battle because your attacks move you over the batte area's border. Using fast travel can (very rarely) break story progression, in which case you need to return to where you last saw a quest marker. Subquests can be done at any time, even if characters involved shouldn't be able to participate at that time. In the latter half the difficulty bottoms out and makes the bosses push overs, which is cool in how much of a power rush it is though. After the incredibly low ratings the game got I was kind of worried for its quality. But if you don't expect an action game and aren't compulsive over graphics/open world the game is actually quite amazing and among my favs this year despite strong competition. It even compares favorably to FF7 Rebirth, the high budget Nojima game of 2024. Rebirth has an amazing open world and great character writing, greatly adding depth and new mystery to a known narrative. But it being the middle part of a larger story and so much optional stuff to do, the pacing is not well suited to the kind of narrative earlier FF was known for. And I really don't know how the Remake series hits for people who didn't play the original.Reynatis is self contained and thanks to its smaller world, the story moves at fast pace and gripped me in ways an open world, which is more enjoyable as a game but distracting from its narrative's direction, simply cannot. I want both of these types of games. Linear games with more limited interactivity/agency, which is used to close the gap between player and game character rather than trying to create an illusion of freedom, still have their place. True freedom in games will only ever exist outside the narrative.Reynatis concludes one part of its story but also ends on a cliff hanger. The free DLC episodes (3 out of 9 released at time of writing) take the story further and shake up expectations also game play wise. Reynatis is an amazing experiment not possible on AAA budgets, and so far the payoffs have been worth it. It remains to be seen how successful its last experiment will turn out: the post game episodic releases bridging into a sequel (?) or concluding the other side of the events unfolding.

_childDocuments_.review: I've released all my accumulated stress from being trendy in social media by petting a cat 10/10.In all seriousness, the game is good and fun, it has a lot of interesting points. I appreciate that the side quests give a better insight on the main story and world building rather than just being random requests, they are also nicely spaced out.I got this game recommended by Steam shortly after it released and decided to give it a try. _childDocuments_.review: It's a shame that I wouldn't recommend this game, really. The visual quality seems great. The gameplay seems reasonably interesting. The story is ridiculously anime, which is ok if that's what you're after. I do have a minor complaint about this being a $60 dollar game that doesn't have English voice-overs. Sorry, but at $60 you don't get to argue that it wasn't cost-effective to English voice actors. Plenty of games before this have pulled it off, it's clearly just to save the developer a buck. Still, that's not enough to make me not recommend the game.What is enough to make me not recommend the game is the blatant and large bugs that exist with key rebinding. This is on top of the fact that the default keybindings are awful (Honestly, I kind of expect that out of a decent chunk of Japanese games, I don't know why it is, but it's not exactly an isolated issue and it's easily changeable most of the time). It's also on top of the fact that a large portion of the keybinds are left off the keybinding menu and are not rebindable, a significantly bigger issue, but still not the worst thing in the world). Remapping any key on the keyboard disables the left mouse button from functioning as an attack key. Even with AHK, it's a bit unstable, and remapping the left mouse button causes erratic control behavior, sometimes even disabling the ability to navigate menus using the mouse (I believe it's assuming you're using a keyboard-only control setup, thus stops responding to mouse movement)If you use a controller, you might not run into this issue, but that's a huge issue for keyboard and mouse users, and consider that this is a $60 game with MASSIVE control oversights. It makes you wonder exactly how many other problems you're going to run into that you really shouldn't be running into in a game this price. Bugs happen, but this is such a blatantly obvious issue that it honestly makes me doubt whether this was actually intended to be a good game or just a cash grab making use of the anime style to attract players. Again, looking in the direction of the lack of English voice-overs and the presence of those pointless little DLC items that seem to be so common that reel incredibly out of place in RPGs. I seriously miss the days when RPGs didn't have a tutorial message telling you how to claim you DLC items. I'd have paid additional money for a launch-edition where the reward for paying extra is just the game never mentioning it has DLC items.It's honestly a damn shame because the game does actually look pretty good, but right out of the gate I have such a low opinion of it for such a ridiculous problem.

_childDocuments_.review: Reynatis is a great game 90% of the time, with the remaining 10% containing such terrible design as to ruin the whole. Very unfortunate, as I hoped it would be worthy to stand next to the Kingdom Hearts games -- which it draws much inspiration from -- but as it is, I can't recommend it to KH fans because of design issues and I can't recommend it to non-KH fans as it will simply appear strange and mediocre.
_childDocuments_.name: REYNATIS

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this game A LOT! The story is intriguing, the combat is flashy and the main character's and their design's are such a treat!!Edit: HOW COULD I FORGET TO MENTION THE MUSIC?? Do not even get me started, it is absolutely beautiful!Definitely think that Reynatis would've benefited from "something" to make traversing Shibuya and other areas feel less of a mundane task, my example would be to add platform-segments to make it more intriguing. The graphics are acceptable but what really carried the look of the game was the lighting & particle effects! I spent a lot of time just appreciating the areas I was in at times, both during and outside of combat, the photo-mode was therefore a great addition! Going for 100% completion was both fun and challenging, had to revisit some areas but it was enjoyable.Even though I recommend this game, you should wait for a price-drop. Paying 50$ or more for a non-AAA game is just not it, chief. This game is such an experience, I really hope we get to see more of Reynatis in the future. <3

_childDocuments_.review:
The year is 2024. In Shibuya, Tokyo, the Criminal Magic Response Act has issued an order barring citizens from going out at night. However, it was quickly disregarded, and few enforce it.

Marin Kirizumi is a wizard who grew up oppressed by others due to his magic. "If you become the strongest, you'll be set free." Following those words left by his father, he arrives in Shibuya at night.

When Sari Nishijima discovered her magic, she decided to use her powers to maintain order. She follows her own sense of justice to protect Shibuya from forces with dangerous ideals and illegal drugs that turn people into monsters.

Marin, who seeks liberation. Sari, who treats the oppression of wizards as justice. The story of REYNATIS begins when the two meet in Shibuya, a place where cultures and ideas mix.

name: King Arthur: Legion IX
detailed_description: Join the Discord About the Game 'This title is going to be great if you enjoyed Knight’s Tale, which a lot of people did, or you want a Roman themed campaign!” - Mortismal Gaming King Arthur: Legion IX is a turn-based, character-centric tactical RPG in the King Arthur: Knight's Tale universe - a dark fantasy version of the Arthurian myth. King Arthur: Legion IX welcomes new players to the mythical land of Avalon with an all-new story and heroes, also offering tough challenges to returning veterans. A new threat looms over Avalon as the long-lost, infamous Ninth Legion of Rome has set foot on the mythical island. Their commander, the fallen hero, Gaius Julius Mento was granted a demonic legion by their dead emperor, Septimus Sulla to find a way out of Tartarus. But when they accidentally arrive to the magical realm of the Lady of the Lake, Gaius Julius Mento decides to subjugate the island and establish Eternal Rome there. First, however, he must gather his lost legion… Play through a Roman-themed campaign as Gaius Julius Mento, a tribune of the undead Ninth Legion, as he discovers Avalon. Battle the monsters of nightmares, challenge the Pict tribes, the monstrous Fomorians and the cunning Sídhe. Experience the might of the Old Faith and Christianity and face the knights of Sir Mordred's Round Table through 15 handcrafted missions. Find, rebuild and protect the remains of the only Roman colony in Avalon and choose your path to victory. By the end of the campaign, you'll have to choose: do you want to become a powerful demon, or will you reject the might of Emperor Sulla and restore your humanity? A Role-playing Tactical Adventure Experience a unique hybrid between turn-based tactical games and traditional, character-centric RPGs. Manage and control a party of 5-6 heroes to explore and conquer the land of Avalon. Engage in deep tactical combat, tough moral choices, hero management, and the rebuilding of Nova Roma. Prove your Worth as a Tactician Every little move and every decision matters. Use covers, traps, flanking and an in-depth overwatch and opportunity system and turn the entire battlefield to your advantage like a master tactician. Sometimes meticulous planning, sometimes charging simply to combat will be the key to victory. The only difference between a successful or a failed quest may depend on the composition of your party only! Heroes Straight from the Abyss Legion IX introduces six unique heroes who have risen from the Abyss to conquer the mythical land of Avalon. Level up, gain skill points and unlock unique skill trees. Loot, equip and craft hundreds of artefacts and create the deadliest fighting force that has ever set foot on Avalon. Wide variety of Abilities Use unique skills, Ultimate Skills and World Abilities to overcome the toughest challenges during your quests in Avalon. Take risks and explore various tactical options as heroes don't face permanent death at the end of the missions. Test your skills in different difficulty modes, from laid-back storytelling to brutal, unforgiving battles. Not Built in a Day Build up and expand the city of Nova Roma. Make sure that your stronghold has the right facilities for your heroes that prepare them for different quests. But beware! Resources are scarce and you have to manage Nova Roma thoughtfully to keep it afloat. Regain your Humanity Your decisions have far-reaching consequences, influencing both gameplay and narrative. Through your actions, Gaius will either restore his humanity, or forever be transformed into a demon.

Test your skills in different difficulty modes, from laid-back storytelling to brutal, unforgiving battles. Not Built in a Day Build up and expand the city of Nova Roma. Make sure that your stronghold has the right facilities for your heroes that prepare them for different quests. But beware! Resources are scarce and you have to manage Nova Roma thoughtfully to keep it afloat. Regain your Humanity Your decisions have far-reaching consequences, influencing both gameplay and narrative. Through your actions, Gaius will either restore his humanity, or forever be transformed into a demon.
short_description: Dive into a unique blend of turn-based tactics and character-centric RPGs. Lead the skilled Roman tribune Gaius Julius Mento as he navigates through the dark fantasy realm of Avalon.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly - this is basically DLC and priced accordingly, but packaged as a standalone to be accessible to more players. It's not a full-size full-priced sequel, so shouldn't be directly compared to the main game as such.What it is, is a more streamlined, and much better balanced series of tactical battles. The 'strategy' layer of Knight's Tale (roster management etc) was the least successful part of it, and they've done away with most of it here. You're not choosing between different characters and different missions and balancing levels and XP and making semi-permanent skill tree choices. You're playing through a story with the same 5 or 6 characters that all level up after each mission and can respec for free whenever you like.The tactical gameplay is similar to the original, but the new classes (with a mix of new and old abilities) and the ultimate system give it a freshness and new depth. The balance is a lot better, with no stealth and fewer sources of AP-gain and damage ramping. To offset that you're given 5 or 6 characters for each mission instead of 4, and powerful ultimates that add a lot of tactical flexibility.They've also added a new difficulty level, 'Brutal', that takes things past the 'Very Hard' setting where Knight's Tale left off. It offers some genuinely challenging missions, but all very doable using the tools available. Some people try their first playthrough on Brutal and complain it's impossible. Others managed to do just that. I waited for my second playthrough, and after some early hurdles managed just fine. It's good to have a bit of a challenge sometimes, as it was a bit too easy to just start steamrolling everything after a certain point in Knight's Tale. Feels fun for a while, but soon gets old.There's an end game once you finish the campaign, where you stop levelling up and there's no more voiced scenes. What you do get is a lot more battles (some pretty unique), more high end gear to make different builds work, and a skill tome every now and then so you can still add a little bit of progression to one or two key characters.A couple of disappointments - most of the voice acting is pretty bad, with the notable exception of the female character who very much lifts the narrative any time she's involved. They still don't let you see the character screen during battles, so you sometimes lose track of some of the minor gear-based passives etc. And some of the achievements seem to be bugged.The music, by the way, is excellent.I've had a great time with this, and I'm over 100 hours from two playthroughs (Hard Ironman on the life path, Brutal Classic on the demonic path) and almost nothing's been boring (maybe just end game on Hard got a bit too easy).Despite making this standalone, for anyone who hasn't played Knight's Tale I'd still recommend that first. But for those of us who have, and want a fresh challenge, this is some of the best DLC I've played in a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who really enjoyed the previous title, I don't feel comfortable recommending this game seeing as in some aspects it's almost the same exact game with a Roman skin thrown on top, with even less depth and variability.It's a glaring realization when you're not only consistently running into the same enemies as the previous title, but even maps. I've even had a (quest/event) trigger during a particular mission that I remember being in the previous King Arthur, and should have clearly been removed as it wasn't initiated properly. There are FAR less heroes, who all have almost no depth either. There isn't much voice acting, and the bit that there is is unfortunately quite poor. The "story" in regards to the quests barely exists, and quite abruptly comes an end. After that point you are left with nothing but countless side quests one after the other that take place on more maps from the previous game. If you enjoyed the first King Arthur and just want something comfortable and more of the same, albeit with less depth, it couldn't hurt to pick this up. Otherwise I'd steer clear.

_childDocuments_.review: ► The STORY grabs the player. Especially as it goes beyond the traditional Arthurian legend with a Roman perspective. Apart from some blunt dialogue options, it is well written with an interesting morality arc that splits towards the end.► The shores of Avalon provides a fresh SETTING that adds to the mystical mood of the mythology. A compact GAMEWORLD of scripted locations is a suitable launch pad for missions to take place. Its a shame that nearly all the wonderfully crafted levels are used only once per campaign, as all the hard work in creating them feels wasted.► The CAMPAIGN is on the short side with a dozen plus, sequential missions. The only true branching comes with the final mission which depends on the morality pursued. The ENDGAME provides additional missions to more than double this count.► Handcrafted LEVELS look fantastic. Along with completing objectives; finding shrines that give buffs and loot chests entice real-time group-led exploration of maps. There's a substantial amount of NPCS to talk to, that adds to the immersion. Roman and mythical inspired points of interest give sections of these maps a themed feel, but those without them can ordinary. Strategically placed CAMPS are great, allowing limited health or armour recovery.► CHARACTER BUILDING provides a lot of tactical flexibility, but lacks a complete roster as classes are limited to x6. Active skills and passives are fairly diverse despite this. Most are melee driven. With a couple of classes for magic and ranged. Each completed mission raises characters level's by one, with a ceiling of x18. Micro-upgrades provide extra leeway to tailor builds towards sub-class. Respeccing skill points can be done for no cost at any time between missions.► BATTLES are the mainstay of gameplay and possess an orchestrated feel. They vary in composition due to different factions, but are fairly uniform in the terms of numbers and types. They consist of a mix of melee and ranged attackers with the odd surprise. Story-led battles field the strongest enemies. Compared to fillers these feel mundane.► TURN-BASED TACTICAL COMBAT is an IGOUGO affair on a grid. Important factors are health, armour and action points. The full regalia of abilities makes for involving, though formulaic action once a party setup is settled on. Even if a fair few are underwhelming. There is a reliance on specific characters to perform their roles. Positioning plays a central aspect to combat. Defence is abstracted into damage mitigation. Cooldowns stop the spamming of non-basic skills.► ENEMIES come in a good mix. From different factions in different configurations and an assortment of abilities to mirror the more common party ones. Most are humanoid. There are a fair number of mythical creatures. Mainly melee or ranged. Those that have magical abilities or summon temporary allies are few and stand out.► AI is mature given the number of games. Enemies focus on the nearest target, looking to surround them. They cycle through assigned skills or abilities in a scripted way. Healing is used sparingly on damaged AI allies.► The ENDGAME kicks in after the 11th mission is completed. These x9 or so extra missions have the hallmarks of fillers to prolong what is otherwise a short campaign.🔶 ACCESSIBILITY - Series of unobtrusive tutorials and info system cover basic gameplay, tactical mechanics and status effects. Combat mechanics have some some complexity.🔶 DIFFICULTY - x5 defined difficulty settings, plus a custom one with x6 parameters to decide upon. Overall normal difficulty is way to easy. Veteran TBT gamers should go straight for one of the top two difficulties.🔶 BALANCE - Is off. The first missions are too hard, but become a lot easier on standard difficulty. Made so due to the accumulation of skills which severely limits the damage caused by enemies. Expect higher difficulties to be better balanced. Especially given the fixed rate of progression for characters.🟨 REPLAY VALUE - Apart from the morality arc there are no real dynamic aspects to change-up the core experience of the campaign. Except perhaps loot rewards. Since changing character skills can be done on the fly, this only succeeds in establishing the player's preferred setup earlier than otherwise. The result of having a fixed party roster. 🟨 LONGEVITY - Two modes with one an ironman mode, an assortment of difficulties including a custom one and missed achievements provide the only motivation to replay.🟣 QUALITY - Numerous bugs reported and responded to by the devs. Some have been fixed.  A few affect achievements so they need to completed in the same action, not over the course of the campaign. It is possible to complete the game.🟣 STABILITY - No crashes experienced.🟣 STEAM - A mix of binary, story and counter achievements of which many can be missed. Cloud saving. Overlay screenshot capture. Limited controller support which was not tested.🟣 OPTIMISATION - Runs around 60 fps, if limit is set. Gfx card runs loud at default settings in a few places. There are notable slowdowns when transitioning to cutscenes, finding secret chests or when opponents spawn before encounters.

_childDocuments_.review: 2022's King Arthur: Knight's Tale, which wasn't about King Arthur and wasn't a knight's tale, was a fundamentally good strategy/tactics game utterly ruined by really, really bad level design, totally bloated beyond belief from a solid 15ish hour RPG to an unbelievable 30+ hour slog. Its missions were way too long, its encounters were way too samey, and there hadn't been nearly enough thought put into the totality of the campaign experience.The much shorter Legion IX promised to fix those issues, and having now beaten it (in about 7 hours, or maybe more like 6), I can report that it mostly has. Legion IX features vastly improved encounter design over the base game. The missions are way shorter (thank Jupiter). The encounters are way better designed; enemies no longer spawn in behind you magically, and there are now sometimes objectives to complete beyond homicide. The cast has been shrunk to six, but you always get six (or five) on a mission, rather than four; this is a great change. Characters have simpler and smaller skill trees. Knight's Tale had a bad story, with bad writing and very bad dialogue. Legion IX is way worse on both counts. But its gameplay is mostly improved. It's paced better, plays, better, and is definitely more fun. But it has lost something by stripping so much out. The simplification of base building is a shame, and while I think it was a good choice to remove the permadeath/injury mechanics, both thematically and mechanically, they haven't been replaced with anything. It feels like something is missing.I also miss the length of the skill trees. I thought they were too long last time, given the number of characters at your disposal, but with only six, these characters didn't seem to have nearly enough abilities.I managed to afford mostly everything, and where I put my points barely seemed to matter. As for the characters themselves, Mento is insanely OP--good--but the Flamen idiot has to be intentionally worthless, because I never found any use for him at all. He's a total joke, with a kit that makes no sense and feels underbaked. The Praetorian is similarly almost useless, because he lacks the mobility that Mordred and other characters had in the last game, and enemies almost never walk into his defensive spells.But the gameplay is still fun. It's tactically engaging while also tactile and satisfying. The worst thing about Knight's Tale was that it was too long. The worst thing about Legion Ix might be that it's too short. After two years, I had expected more. I haven't finished everything yet; after the credits roll, it's promised that the TRUE final boss is still forthcoming. I'll probably get to him eventually, but where I am now, my progress does feel kind of stagnant. Every quest I finish, a new one pops up, like I'm playing the Spooky Scary Roman Skeleton version of whack-a-mole with my pilum. If you're like me and enjoyed Knight's Tale but for its encounter design, I do recommend Legion IX. It's reasonably priced and decent fun. Just don't bother with the story, because the dialogue is really, truly horrible.Edit: I played a bit more in the post-game, and it's a huge treadmill. I'm not enjoying it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: Is it as good as the first game? No. Is it still enjoyable? Yes.The long version: as many others have mentioned here, Legion IX seems like a step backwards from Knight's Tale. A large amount of mechanics have been removed, the writing and voice acting are noticeably worse, and almost all the maps are copy-pasted from the first game. It might be best to think of this game as a DLC or very extensive mod. If you felt that the first game was too complicated, then this was made for you. If not, then you might be somewhat annoyed by the dumbing-down of the mechanics here.Positives and new mechanics:-Each character has unique abilities with no overlap.-Added the Larium, which applies significant modifiers to game mechanics.-The character that wields a two-handed weapon no longer feels so immobile as to be useless.-The "archer" has much better damage output and is now actually competitive. Overall, classes feel much more balanced.Negatives and removed mechanics:-No more roster management. Most missions are played with the same 5 characters. Some missions have a 6th.-Gear no longer has levels. An item gained in the first 5 missions could still be viable in the final mission. Instead, you can invest resources to upgrade a weapon or armor piece once.-Maximum character level is reduced to 18.-HP is no longer a major mechanic. It's now just armor and vitality, unless you use an ability for temporary HP.-No more lasting injuries or resting between missions.-The morality chart is now a morality line. Just plain good and evil.
