_childDocuments_.review: So.. Kongless: Survivor Instinct, adding a positive reaction out of good faith that 7Levels will take feedback out of the reception this game is gettingRight away it's safe to say this game isn't worth the full pricetag to be very honest, despite getting it as a gift from a friend, I would've waited for a bigger discount down the line. The game has its pros and cons, overall a neat experience that could definitely be more if it wasn't for the cons that keep dragging the experience down, so to go in parts:- The visuals in this game are gorgeous, it's easily the best thing the game has to offer, the level design artists did a great job to really flesh out the different stages of the destroyed city, where each bit of a building you explore has its own detailed rooms, be it a storage inside a hospital, a car workshop, or Monarch's bunkers. This isn't counting the eerie night sequences with Abaddon's webs all over the place or the Bay zones with Tiamat's acid.- The gameplay as a whole is quite basic, jump around, climb around, find a key for a door, find gears to repair a generator, move a box, it's nothing super crazy, but it does the trick. What annoys me the most though is the lack of fluidness to it, a lot of those actions work as preset animations that have to play till the end before you can do the next action. In theory this shouldn't be a problem as most of the gameplay is slow-paced, but it's atrocious once it gets to two parts, combat and the escape sequences..- The combat has to be the second worst thing in this game I've seen, the position-locking due the animations make that multiple enemies can easily take you down if you take a while to learn how to deal with the controls. Found myself dying quite often in the beginning because of that, it's a weird learning curve that doesn't really pay off, why? Well, 80% of the enemies in this game are mercs of the Hyenas, the main villain group of the story, they offer SOME variation as you progress such as using pistols, shotguns or shields, but this brings me to a core issue with this game.- For a game called KONG: Survivor Instinct, set within the Monsterverse, there's rarely much that makes it feel like it's meant to be a monster survival game, as said, most of the enemies are generic mercenaries, with only other two options being Abaddon's minions and baby Skullcrawlers. Both of which can die with one meele hit, so they're more of an obstacle than a real threat. If this was more balanced, had there be different types of those mini monsters scattered throughout the city, I don't know, make a version of Abaddon's spider that stays in the ceiling and shoots web? One that has some carapace and you need the hammer to take it down? Variation please!- The escape sequences, oh boy.. What is meant to be the most thrilling and coolest part of the game, running away from a giant kaiju as it tries to kill you inside a building, has to be the worst and most frustrating part of this game. Not because the sequences are bad per say, they're well varied and interesting, be it climbing a web-covered building fleeing from Abaddon, or going through a destroying bridge as Kong and Tiamat fight down.BUT, the stiff locomotion system of this game, alongside the awful aim of the grapple hook in the later sequences, drags these moments down so bad but so bad. I lost count of how many times I restarted the Kong vs Tiamat sequence due missing the hook aim, if the aim is ever so slightly lower than it should and you try to launch it? the whole animation will play, you gotta wait till it ends to then try again, all while Tiamat's body can just slam you and you gotta restart. It should be the coolest part of the game but it becomes the worst by sheer annoyance.- Last but not least, the story, or a fraction of it. I'm a huge Monsterverse fan, and ain't annoyed by human-centric stories at all like Godzilla 2014 or Legacy of Monsters, but those had a story at least, here the basic premise of the dad finding his daughter, alongside understanding why Kong, Abaddon and Tiamat are in the surface get quite vague and confusing. The story mostly boils down to the dad having to run away from the Titans or kill the mercs, go from point A to point B. There's Monarch logs that give extra context sure, but a lack of emphasis in this story that could've gone better in the actual dialogue sequences.. those of which have very mediocre voice acting, nothing that a second run in these audios for an update couldn't resolve me thinks. The story is barely different without Kong aswell, if anything Tiamat is the plot relevance, but of course a Tiamat titled game wouldn't sell as good as a Kong one, at least you got more monke scenes!Overall.. despite all these critiques, yesterday I still had a neat time to distract myself while playing this. It ain't perfect, it ain't great, but it ain't ♥♥♥♥ slop either, it's a neat game with nice concepts that certainly needed more time in the oven. 7Levels seems to have confirmed more updates so I hope some of these points are addressed. For now it's a 5/10 in my book

_childDocuments_.review: Not really a Metroidvania, instead it's a somewhat linear 2.5D action adventure game. You'll backtrack occasionally, but because you got lost not because you acquired a new key item etc. Survivor Instinct's main problem is that the basic gameplay loop is set in the first 30 minutes and it doesn't really change. There's some real epic high points here where you'll escape from Titans in sequences similar to the Ori and the Will O' The Wisp boss battles, but they're not that common and the majority of the game is spent trudging along from mundane electric puzzle to mundane electric puzzle. The combat is janky, the enemy variety is non existent, and the dialogue and story isn't worth talking about either.It's surprisingly pretty and any time the titans appear it gets a lot better, but there's just so much drudgery inbetween those moments that I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Soft recommend. I like what this game was trying to do, more so than how it ended up doing it. The environments are a bit generic, but quite detailed and good looking, there's a decent variety of stuff to do and to collect to go from place to place, although you don't really need to do crazy amount of backtracking to get to everything. The best and worst part of the game are probably the big setpieces where you escape from the Titans... on one hand thei're very cool, the game does a good job at conveying the scale and power of the monters... on the other they can be very frustrating, because you need to time perfectly every jump and movement, or you're dead and have to start all over. Also, the protagonist's voice actor is pretty decent as well... but the fact they have him voice most of the bad guys and side characters too feels very silly. If you can... spend a bit of money on an extra or two, next game xD Still overall, not a terrible game, and since it doesn't even ask full AAA price, I can't be really mad at it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's mediocre. For a tie in game it is fine. For a game as a whole it is just lacking.So first of all, I played on hard, which is totally fine. I like challenges. To the gameplay:I really dislike the combat. If you get all the counter, attacks and dodges right, it tries to feel rewarding...? But the combat does feel a bit boring and frustrating sometimes. Most of the time, you just have to wait for an enemy to do any attack while standing there, doing nothing. If you play offensive, you probably get punished. The frustrating part sometimes is, if one enemy does a melee attack and a shotguner attacks you too, you can only respond to one of the attacks. Same if two gunner attack you. You lose health. Not much choice there. That is the difficulty setting I guess? Still a bit frustrating and makes you wish to skip some of the fights. But using the environment to your advantage, like shoving enemies in goo or off a cliff is nice. The traversal is more fun. Exploring different areas and finding either health or ammo upgrades feels rewarding. The problem is that it starts to feel a little bit repetitive after a certain time. But with each new tool, you get new ways to explore different areas. And the data logs most of the time tell you things you probably already know but they add to the world building if you are interested in the whole Monsterverse. Especially to the newer Kaijus. Now there are side scroller parts in which you get chased by the monsters, similar like Scarecrow in the Batman Arkham games. They are the the most fun part for me, if they had better checkpoints (or any at all). I don't know if that is a part of the difficulty setting but if you die, you have to do the entire damn thing again. In fact, it started to get so frustrating, that I decided to write a review, because I am really torn about wanting to finish the game anymore.The story (slight spoilers):It's exactly what you expect. Guy searches daughter. Daughter does some shady stuff. Similar to the Monarch show, just with the family members inversed. But a character appears to tie more into the movies, which is pretty cool. However, some cutscenes make you wish for more kaiju action, because they rather decided to cut from certain confrontations away, instead of actually giving us what we are all here for: Kong, Abbadon and Tiamat; Giant Monsters All out attack. As a whole, it is not bad, but I wouldn't call it good either. If they ever decide to make another tie in game and learn from this one, I would absolutely be interested. If you are genuinely invested into the Monsterverse then I say that you could aswell watch a let's play, because you won't miss out on much. If you aren't interested in the Monsterverse, then you probably can ignore the game. If you still decide to play it for yourself, maybe wait for a little discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game when it first started, but it slowly got annoying and repetitive as I played. While there are positives, there are definitely more negatives. Is it worth playing? Maybe. Should you wait for a sale? Definitely. Due to the number of issues, though, I find myself giving it a thumbs down.You play as David, which is a pretty bland name for an equally bland character. He’s cheesy, probably tells annoying dad jokes, and repeats the same cliché phrases over and over throughout your journey. So much so that you wish the developers knew how to turn off dialogue repetition after a line has been spoken once. David doesn’t need to say “Why are you all so stubborn?” EVERY SINGLE TIME he kills a person. Silence would be fine, too.Then there’s the combat. Fun at first, but it gets repetitive fast. You have a melee weapon, and you’re supposed to dodge and parry attacks. The problem is that David’s actions often feel random. You try to hit an enemy, but instead, he kicks them away. There are also enemies with guns that tend to stand behind companions, forcing you to dodge bullets Matrix-style, which feels odd since David has no special abilities or powers. You do get a gun yourself, and this does make combat more bearable, but ammo is limited, so you still find yourself doing more melee fighting.And if the repetitive combat isn’t enough, exploration follows the same pattern. You do the same things over and over—find a key, locate a part, unlock a door, activate an elevator, turn a generator on or off, discover a glowing aura. Once you build up enough points, you can summon a titan to clear a path. The game claims to be a “Metroidvania,” and while you get a sense of that when you find a new weapon or item, it doesn’t happen frequently. There aren’t enough secret areas, there are few items to discover, and the game is pretty linear with minimal backtracking.Oh, and the game is called Kong: Survivor Instinct. I’m about 50% through, and I’ve encountered Kong maybe three times, and it was incredibly brief. There are other titans, but you see them so rarely that the game starts to feel more focused on the human enemies than on the titans.Finally, the game does have some chase scenes with the titans. While visually impressive, they’re frustrating from a gameplay perspective. The developers made these sequences so precise that one wrong move equals instant death, and you have to restart from the beginning of the chase. By the time I finally succeeded, I was too frustrated to enjoy the moment. It’s an example of prioritizing challenge over enjoyment.The good things:-The visuals are stunning.-Level design is well-done.-The titan scenes are the highlight of the game, but there aren’t enough of them—excluding the chase scenes, of course.Other than that, the story is bland, the dialogue is poorly written and acted, and David is an uninteresting and annoying character. Combat and exploration are repetitive, with minimal items, hidden areas, or upgrades to make it feel rewarding. Overall, try it at your own risk. You might enjoy it, but don’t forget—Steam does offer refunds.

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzle portions of the game are fun (but repetitive).  The story is thin.  The voice acting is some of the worse I've ever heard; plus, they main character keeps repeating the same lines over and over and over.  The worst part of the game, the part that makes this a Thumbs Down for me, is the constant stream of soldiers that you have to fight.  The combat in this game is awkward, clunky, and unresponsive.  Fighting soldiers is always a crap-shoot of whether or not your commands will register before you get hit or shot.  No matter how many of these guys you fight, every time seems like the first time.  By the end, I gave up caring how the "story" ended; I just wanted to be done with it so that I never had to play this thing again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game seems very heavily inspired by another game called Deadlight, but unfortunately Deadlight does basically everything better. I've only played the first 40 mins or so, so this is very much an early perspective:- The exploration in Kong Survivor Instinct is pretty good, although the animations are a bit janky and disconnected. There are plenty of places to explore but so far there's been nothing particularly interesting to find, just keys and medkits and ammo. Very occasionally you'll find a lore pickup, but it's all based on the films so if you've seen the films then it's information you already know.- The combat is pretty uninteresting. They've got parries and blocking and grabs but the way the combat animations are designed means you can rarely combo attacks smoothly - instead, you'll spend a lot of time chasing enemies down because your attack knocked them backwards. The gun makes combat easy as hell, enemies drop with one headshot, and since the gun is also necessary for exploration you'll find plenty of ammo so there's no scarcity of resources to worry about.- The story seems like pretty standard fare for Monsterverse stuff - it's a thinly veiled excuse to show giant monsters. The voice acting is incredibly phoned-in. The big set piece moments, like when Kong jumps into the foreground and starts trying to kill everyone, are pretty underwhelming.So far it's basically just made me want to replay Deadlight.
_childDocuments_.name: Kong: Survivor Instinct

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so this game is kind of a disaster lolSo, as someone who A) loves the Monsterverse, especially the more human-centric entries like Godzilla 2014 and Monarch: Legacy of Monsters and B) loves Metroidvanias, the idea of a Metroidvania set in the monsterverse with a street-level, human POV seemed right up my alley. There is so much potential inherent in the premise that goes WOEFULLY unrealised in the final product. Your arsenal is limited to a sledgehammer, a pistol, and a grappling hook. That's it. As far as metroidvanias go, that is a pitifully small toolkit. What about collectibles? Metroidvanias are known for having sprawling maps with lots of secrets to uncover, is any of that present here? Nope! The only collectibles to be found are basic health and ammo pickups, and lore entries for your datapad. In my playthrough I achieved a completion rate of 95% despite doing virtually zero backtracking or exploring, playing the game normally you will uncover pretty much everything it has to offer. A full playthrough of the game will take you about 6 hours. If you were playing on the hardest difficulty and going for 100% completion you could maybe clock 10 hours in this game, MAYBE. It is an absurdly short game with only 3 main areas to explore.The gameplay is pretty mundane, it's playable but that's pretty much the nicest thing I can say about it. Most of the game is just basic environmental puzzle solving, with no variety beyond "find the gears to repair this generator!" "find the key for this door!" "Move this box!". Very simple, very easy, you will not get stumped on a single puzzle in this game. Breaking up the puzzle solving are combat encounters against one of this game's 3 (yes 3) main enemy types: mercenaries, spiders, and baby skullcrawlers. The spiders are skullcrawlers are more like hazards than actual enemies, one hit from your sledgehammer or pistol and they're dead, no exceptions. That leaves the mercenary encounters as the only "true" combat in this game, and hoo boy are they bare bones. You can dodge, block, parry, and grapple, and at various points throughout the game you'll go up against these groups of 2-4 mercs, no variety, no miniboss type enemies, just you and 2-4 mercs, over and over and over. Granted your character is just some Joe Shmoe suburban dad so I wasn't expecting the combat to go gangbusters but utter lack of variety makes what little combat there is in this game a slog to get through.Let's talk about story: there isn't one. Okay there's kind of a story but it doesn't make any sense. Basically Kong went ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (no pun intended) and attacked a generic west coast city so you go to the city to find your daughter. Alan Jonah (the villain from Godzilla King of the Monsters) is back and doing generic eco-terrorist things including somehow making another ORCA, the bioacoustic device that can alter titan behavior. You steal the ORCA and Jonah spends the rest of the game hunting you, you uncover the mystery of your daughter's whereabouts aaaaand that's it that's the game. Also there are monsters sometimes. And yeah, "sometimes" is definitely the right word here because Kong and the other titans are barely in the game; they show up, ♥♥♥♥ around in the background for a few seconds, and then they're gone again. The game's major sections culminate in these platforming challenges where you're on the run from these monsters as they tear apart the building you're in. These sections are admittedly pretty fun and pretty tense, but they're few and far between, and that's really the only interaction you have with the titans in this game. Other than that, they're barely in it (this game is set in the MONSTERVERSE and is called KONG SURVIVOR INSTINCT btw)Final thoughts: the localization is all over the place: the dialogue and voice acting is just so...SO bad. Your character is chatty in the worst possible way, constantly chiming in with these cringe nothingburger dad jokes. I was irritated with him after the first couple hours. Thank god the game is so short otherwise he would be actually insufferable. What little dialogue there is is stilted and wooden, and I get that if I'm complaining about the dialogue in a Monsterverse project the joke is probably on me but it's just so bad, and it's really baffling to me because the lore entries you find scattered around the world are all really polished and well-written? It makes no sense, it's almost like they had different localizers working on the dialogue and the lore entries. The game technically has a plot twist but you can see it coming from a mile away so is it REALLY a twist? The music is pretty generic and bad, it's intrusive to the point of detracting from the game's atmosphere. I played most of the game with the music turned off because I found it made the game more tense and atmospheric. Last but not least, this game has hands down the WORST ENDING of any video game I have ever played.I would only recommend this game to DIEHARD Monsterverse fans and even then only at a STEEP discount. Otherwise, don't waste your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Kong: Survivor Instinct

_childDocuments_.review: Am I happy that they made a game based in the monsterverse? Yes. Could it have been better? Yes. Did I have a good time with this game? Yes. Kong: Survivor Instinct suffers from poor voice acting and terrible facial animations, but it does have an interesting story, cool environments, awesome titans, and some fun platforming action. It's overall a step in the right direction for the franchise, but the game does feel like it could have used some more time in the oven.

_childDocuments_.review: Kong: Survivor Instinct is a surprisingly solid "Monsterverse" metroidvania that features excellent level design as well as a decent combat system reminiscent of that in the Batman: Arkham series.The story is about as simple as it gets: One day the Titans (Kong, Abaddon, and others) suddenly attack an unnamed American city, leaving it in ruins.  An evacuation is ordered and you, David Martin, head out in search of your daughter after your calls to her go unanswered.  It doesn't take long before you discover that the Hyenas, a mercenary group led by Alan Jonah, are behind the Titan outbreak and... well, I'll leave the rest for you to experience firsthand.Despite its name, Survivor Instinct is  actually a survival game.  Instead, it's more of a traditional 2.5D metroidvania in which you must traverse nonlinear environments and return to previously-explored areas once you've acquired the tools necessary to unlock brand new routes.  There is admittedly some resource management in that health can only be replenished via health kits and pistol ammo is limited and therefore must be used sparingly.  However, make no mistake about it: Kong: Survivor Instinct is more about pushing forwards and advancing the storyline than scavenging for supplies and struggling to survive.My favorite aspect of the game is its aforementioned nonlinear level design.  Whereas some metroidvanias can be daunting and even tedious to navigate due to the sheer size of their worlds (see: Hollow Knight), Survivor Instinct is a much gentler experience in that it constantly nudges you in the right direction and frequently loops you back around to previous areas rather than forcing you to backtrack long distances.  There's also lots of platforming and lite puzzle solving, and it's all handled very well.  There are few, if any, frustrating jumps or climbs and the environmental puzzles are just complex enough to make you stop and think for a moment about how to proceed, but simple enough so that they never confuse or frustrate you.In addition to the platforming and puzzle solving, there are occasional combat encounters with mercenaries and deadly creatures.  The hand-to-hand combat with the mercenaries is the most fun, as it takes a Batman: Arkham-esque approach with parries, dodges, and grapples, making it possible to fight multiple bad guys at once without being hopelessly pummeled.  Although the combat isn't nearly as smooth or refined as in the Arkham games, it still manages to stay enjoyable from start to finish.  Grabbing and throwing enemies off ledges or into hazards like fire and electricity never gets old, and if you don't mind expending your pistol's limited ammunition you can even attempt to take them out with a single well-placed headshot.The only real complaints I have with the game are its chase sequences and voice acting.At key junctures during the game, you must flee from angry Titans as they demolish everything around you.  While these moments make for a nice spectacle and really ratchet up the tension, I found them to be overly reliant on trial-and-error.  If you make so much as one mistake, you're instantly killed and sent back to the beginning of the chase.  The only silver lining is that in addition to having unlimited lives, these sequences only occur roughly a handful of times over the course of the game.The voice acting is also rather poor across the board, with the main protagonist sounding borderline AI-generated and the supporting cast not being much better.  I felt this did a disservice to the story and prevented important moments from having any real weight or emotional impact.  Although the story itself isn't all that noteworthy to begin with, I still would have liked to have seen a stronger performance from the main protagonist since his voice is heard so often throughout the game.Overall, I recommend checking out Kong: Survivor Instinct if you're a fan of 2.5D platformers and metroidvanias.  While it might not feature Kong himself in the starring role, nor will it win over many people with its story or voice acting, it's a surprisingly well-crafted ~6 hour experience with levels that are fun to traverse and explore and a combat system that makes it satisfying to take down groups of bad guys.(Note: I received a copy of this game for free by way of a review code.  However, that in no way influenced my feelings for the game.  I was actually highly skeptical going into it and didn't expect to enjoy it much at all, but ended up being pleasantly surprised.  I hope that if you give the game a shot, you'll enjoy it as well!)

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so there are several things to mention. IMHO, this is a game for two types of people. Fans of the Kong Franchise and platforming/metroidvania gamers. Now, when we talk about rating the game based on those two categories, it's pretty easy to sum up. For those of the franchise, it's a fun little game that allows you to play the other side of the action in a platforming type game play. It's different than the Peter Jackson King kong game on playstation. That was more of a liner adventure game and this is a different take on that and of course a more simpler approach. For the platforming metroidvania gamers, this is a "kick your feet up" and enjoy game. It's simple, by the numbers, not really a challenge for seasoned vets, even on hard difficulty. So, many in this space many not find it fun. So with that being said, I think it's a simple game that fans should play and see what it's all about. From the different puzzles, fighting setups, resource management (ammo), to finding more health, it's an easy ride. I don't think it's a great game, but it's not a bad one either. Fans will like it, but not so much for the OG platformers. I consider myself both. I'm a fan of the franchise, ever since the original kong on VHS (dating myself), and I've played platforming metroidvania type games sense metroid, the first one....LOL.OVERALL SUMMARY:If you're looking for a simple game that's easy to pick up, won't stress you to go bald trying to prove your skills, and is associated with one of the coolest monster franchises, I'd say pick it up. But if you want a challenge, to test your platforming skills, find hints, explore on your own, and all that other jazz, it may not be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the MonsterVerse, this game is a must-get. But even if you're not, it's still worth picking up.Admittedly, I'm not the biggest MonsterVerse enthusiast myself, but this game still managed to impress me. The gameplay is polished and fluid, offering a smooth experience without any bugs or crashes.The graphics, while not groundbreaking, are solid for a 2.5D title, delivering a visually satisfying experience.One of the most immersive aspects of the game is how it showcases the Titans. Even as someone who isn't deeply invested in the MonsterVerse, I found myself captivated by their presence and background actions. It’s hard not to get drawn into the spectacle, and the fact that you can interact with the iconic Titan roars adds a fun touch of nostalgia for long-time fans.On the downside, the story is pretty underwhelming. It feels flat, the voice acting doesn’t quite fit, and the plot is predictable, with characters that are hard to relate to. There’s no emotional depth, but the game doesn’t rely on its story to carry the experience—it's the gameplay that shines.In terms of difficulty, it's relatively easy, even on the highest setting. Puzzles are straightforward and not particularly challenging, which makes the game feel a bit short. You can expect to finish it in 3-4 hours if you're collecting everything.Despite its shortcomings, I still recommend the game, especially considering how fun it is to play.Even as a non-fan, I found myself having a blast and finished it twice. For the price tag, it’s a great deal, and if you’re a MonsterVerse fan, it’s almost essential.Finally, we have a solid MonsterVerse game! Looking at you,

_childDocuments_.review: Kong Survival Instinct was already considered "iffy" when the game was announced. A developer no one really knew working on a major franchise IP while also being the first PC and Console in the Monsterverse series as a whole. And I'm gonna be blunt, for sake of story, you're better off looking towards Wikis or Walthroughs.-The GoodConcept: Honestly not a bad direction, I've had mutual and seen people in the community pitch the idea of playing as a Survivor trying to make their way to safety or meet with whatever potential goal they're after while the city in question is under attack by a giant monster. Putting it in a 2.5D Metroidvania style is not a horrible spin and did work pretty well.-The BadDialog: Story dialog wise is "okay" but what isn't is post combat dialog. MC and bad guys just say the SAME THING, OVER AND OVER AGAIN! The worst offender is when you fight off a Spider or a baby Skullcrawler where MC will always let you know that they are "gross."Combat: Slow, sluggish, and overall just "bleh." Not super difficult at least but even in the concept of a "survival-horror" combat definitely needed polish.Chase Sequence: This part should be the greatest draw to the game as you are trying to survive GIANT MONSTERS RAMPAGING A CITY! And thing is, it could have worked well considering the whole "concept" point. But some of these chase sequences feels "cheap." Not like in terms of budget, but the kind where you feel like "nil to none in chance." Keeping Spoils to a minimum, there's a chase that's actually you running while Kong is fighting another Monster, a moment that would be my bread and butter because Monster Fights are awesome. But this chase just tests precision to what feels like if you're not on it, your done and you have to restart the whole chase. And worse, these Chase Sequences has no checkpoints, so if you fail, sorry you're back at the start of the chase.-Final WordsI wanted to like it for what it is, shoot if anything I wanted to support this in hopes we get "that" game, "THE" game, the one like what Pipeworks did years ago with Godzilla 3 times. I wanted to show and even hope that there is a demand for Monsterverse games. But this game just doesn't stick. I'm certain the developers did everything they could to make the best possible game they could offer with their best intentions along with their resources. But for the first Monsterverse game debut for PC and Consoles... this isn't a good start.

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewed on Steam DeckLet me begin this review by saying that I’m not the target audience for this game. I don’t particularly enjoy metroidvania games and i don’t like the MonsterVerse. That’s not to say that I don't like Kong. I love the original 1933 movie and Peter Jackson’s remake, and i thoroughly enjoyed the 2005 Xbox 360 game based off of that movie, (wish it was in Steam☹️) but this game ain’t that. This game plays very well, it’s highly polished and well optimized for the Steam Deck. The default settings work incredibly well out of the box, so to speak. Credit to the developers. You get a rock solid 60fps and a good 3 hours of battery life. I experimented a bit and turned up all of the graphical settings to max and still received a solid 60fps although I could not discern any appreciable difference to the on-screen visuals, so best to leave them as they are and take the extra battery life. I found the on-screen text too small for my liking and had to turn them up to “Big” in the menu. I also found a spelling mistake in the text at one point. Instead of saying “signs of life” it read “sings of life.” I minor nitpick which I’m sure the developers will quickly correct. But for me the gameplay just didn’t grab me. I found the gameplay too stodgy and there wasn’t enough story to really grip me. Personally, story is everything to me. If a game has compelling characters and an interesting plot it will propel me to complete a mid game that is lacking in other areas. If you share my gaming sensibilities maybe give this one a miss, otherwise give it a shot. I love AA software and we need to give our support to developers making these smaller scale games otherwise our beloved pastime will implode under the unsustainable weight of AAA (AAAA if you’re Ubisoft) bloat. 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Kong: Survivor Instinct by 7Levels is a 2.5D action-adventure game that reminds me a lot of Shadow Complex back from the Xbox 360. It takes the Kaiju element and mixes in Metroidvania-style gameplay to give us a new foray into the Monsterverse. After the disaster of Skull Island: The Rise of Kong, I know people are hungry for a decent Kong game but will Kong: Survivor Instinct satisfy us? Not really, but it is getting us one step closer! That isn't to say that Kong: Survivor Instinct is a bad game, it isn't, but I don't think it is what anyone was really looking for out of a Kaiju game.Kong takes place after Mechagodzilla was defeated and Godzilla and Kong go their separate ways. Apex has been neutralized and Monarch is now focused on exploring the Hollow Earth. Unfortunately, this balance is short lived as Kong makes his return to the surface absolutely obliterating everything around him. The game opens with the news reporting on Kong's destruction and a man named Davis who is watching the report tries to reach his daughter Stacy on her phone but is unable to make contact with her. Fearing the worst, he heads straight into the wake of Kong to find her and get her to safety. Of course, David crashes his car and has to continue his journey on foot. As we make our way through the city, we must take advantage of our tools and weapons to get through different locals, avoid dangerous Kaiju, and discover what has happened to Stacy.After a brief section where we learn the basic controls of the game such as how to jump, how to crawl, and interacting with the environment, the game starts pretty quickly. As Metroidvania's tend to do, we will come across places that are inaccessible to us at first but we will unlock different tools that will allow us to briefly backtrack and continue our journey using our new found equipment. Along the way, David will meet a few different characters that will expand upon the story but most of the game is spent traversing the different locations such as city streets, skyscrapers, hospitals, and underground facilities searching for clues along the way. Eventually, David will find a piece of equipment that will allow him to collect bits of a recording of different Kaiju noises. After gathering all the noises to complete a roar of a famous Kaiju we can basically summon them to open the next section of the city.Along the way, we will come across puzzle solving sections that are very simple and straight forward. Shooting the locks off doors, shaking down bars, breaking down a boarded up door, and moving boxes to reach higher areas. There is nothing really innovative about the game, but it does what it is made to do. You want to make sure you are exploring every corner of the map however because there are medical kits that heal you, water bottles that increase your max health, ammo to reload your pistol, and extra magazines that will add to the max capacity of your gun without reloading. I did enjoy finding all of the hidden clues and making sure that I found all the upgrades.Outside of platforming and basic puzzle solving, there is a combat system as well to battle smaller monsters, mercenaries, and soldiers. The combat system is very straight forward, you can do a quick attack, a heavy attack, block, and counterattack. These battles are spread through out the game and can sometimes be difficult but nothing too challenging. I did die a few times at certain sections, but the combat system, while clunky, is serviceable. David is by no means John Wick. Making your way through the city is what fills most of your time with the game but these breaks keep the game engaging. The most challenging part of the game however are the Kaiju chasing portions. Every so often, one of the Kaiju will notice you and begin to hunt you down. Of course with them being the size of skyscrapers, it typically boils down to running through a partially destroyed building while their claws and fists are busting through the walls trying to get you. These chases are somewhat intense but also a bit cheap because it requires pretty precise timing in your actions so I expect most people to die in these sections. Dying isn't too bad as you typically respawn right at the start and just continue the escape.While the game is definitely a step in the right direction, I feel like the Kaiju element was somewhat lacking. Yes, there are several moments where you will see different Kaiju walking around in the background and they are always around either through story telling or the chases, but it just felt like something was missing to really bring it all together. I think I can speak for the majority of gamers that are also Kaiju fans, we want to play as them. The entirety of Kong: Survivor Instinct, we never get to BE Kong. We see him quite often but it just lacks that special moment that really gives us that "wow" moment when we get to destroy some buildings or even fight another Kaiju. We are just running around doing our thing while all the cool stuff is just happening around us. It really is a shame that there wasn't a least one moment as a payoff where we got to play as Kong and get to fight Tiamat or Abaddon to protect David. There are several opportunities where something like this could have been added to really give meaning to the Kong title. Like Shadow Complex, Kong: Survivor Instinct is a bit on the short side. My playthrough which was a 98% completion took about 6 hours to finish.I think that 7Levels did a fine job with Kong. It isn't a bad game, just a game that is somewhat lacking in a few areas to really make it stand out. I think that Kaiju fans might enjoy seeing some of their favorites appear in a game, but will overall wish they could actually play as them at least for a little bit. This is where the game is a double edged sword, if you are looking for a Metroidvania-lite, are interested in Kaiju, and are looking to support developers that are working in the Monsterverse you might find value here with Kong: Survivor Instinct.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm leaving the review as a negative but I do want to see more kaiju games set in the MonsterVerse, this game is just a huge misfire. Making the core gameplay a 2.5D linear metroidvania where you play as more or less some guy is not what I imagine when talking about the cinematic universe about science fiction giant monsters fighting.Visually, the game looks great, the two cutscenes in the game are well-rendered and look beautiful and the general game looks good but the actual animation of the game sucks a lot. Characters move so inhumanly and there is little effort to give the characters any lip-syncing. The animation and visuals clash so hard that I don't know if I can really say the game looks good. The background of the levels look good, especially in the cities where there are a lot of detail, I like how it looks and is probably the strongest part of the game, though its not a very important strength. The titans themselves look good enough, but the animation problem runs true with them too. There are a few sequences where you try to escape a building with the titan trying to get you, which I think is fine in the game but logically speaking very goofy, which reins true for many aspects of the game.The gameplay loop has three main areas, that being platforming, puzzle solving, and combat. The platforming is more or less okay, the main character's movement is pretty monotonous and very clunky to control (B to crouch? Really?), but I did get the hang of it eventually and the level design is alright for the most part. The puzzle solving is also just okay, but probably the weakest of the three. Seeing very articulated and conveniently placed boxes and explosive barrel dispensers doesn't make a lot of sense and isn't very cohesive with the environment we are in, and also doesn't make a lot of sense much of the time with the character only interacting with things in a straight line (and occasionally a titan in the background). The combat is also fine, I would like the system it was going for if it wasn't in this game, and every fight sequence is scripted in specific areas and ends up being very monotonous and boring. Even if you want to play this game for the lore, it doesn't give you a lot, if anything, and what it does give you is pretty boring. The game introduces a new titan to the series, but its very poorly fleshed out and generic as well as kind of being a rehash of other titans, being the MUTOs from Godzilla 2014 (burying and creating offspring). It also introduces the Tiamat titan's baby, Lahamu, at the end, and is meant to be why the main character's daughter cut contact from him, so-to-speak. Whether that mean anything in the future of the universe, I don't know.All in all, I think this game is just really lame and not really worth the play through, but as I said I want Legendary and/or Toho to consider making another game, possibly with a higher budget and a game idea that's more appealing. I think a fighting game with no lore implications is the strongest direction they could go for, or a first-person adventure on someplace like Skull Island, I dunno. I think they should try again with a game that's hopefully better than this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Kong: Survivor Instincts is a unique game that puts you in the shoes of an ordinary father, not Kong himself. You play as a civilian trying to find his daughter, Stacy, while Kong and other Titans cause chaos around you. The game connects well to the Monsterverse, as you feel small and vulnerable in the face of these massive creatures. It’s tense and thrilling, with plenty of close calls as you navigate through the destruction. If you enjoy the Monsterverse movies and want a different perspective, this game offers a gripping experience of survival and family.

_childDocuments_.review: I know everyone wants to play as monsters, but this is a great first step into gaming for the monsterverse IMO.  Gameplay is solid, it has lots of little lore snippets about the greater universe, and the monster scenes are honestly pretty good actually.  My only complaints are there should have been more monster scenes and boss fights, we don't need to play as them, but simply witnessing their powers and scale is awesome!  Also maybe have a bit more of an interesting main character and plot, as it is the main character is incredibly generic, and there isn't enough story fluff throughout the game to tell a story but I liked the twist at the end and the explanation for why the titans were rampaging!  Overall 7/10,  a great first entry into what is hopefully a longer line of games in the monsterverse.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a journey that's for sure.I’m currently stuck at a level near what I assume is the endgame, where two gears are required to proceed. Although I’ve attempted to backtrack, the limited fast travel options make it very difficult, compounded by repetitive AI spawns. This has made the experience increasingly frustrating, especially as I'm trying to make the playthrough enjoyable for viewers. At this point, it seems my only option may be to restart the entire game, which is incredibly disheartening. Adding to the disappointment, the lack of Kaiju action—a major draw for many of us—doesn’t help the game's overall appeal. We were expecting a game where you could control Godzilla and Kong, and with that in mind, I’m looking forward to loading up GODZILLA PS4 again. Unfortunately, I’d have to rate this a 6/10. _childDocuments_.review: I'll give this game a solid 7/10, I'll list the pros and cons of this game after I explain some stuff. The story itself is a decent one I would say. You are this dad named David who is looking for his daughter in this city wrecked by titans and along the way find out some... well I'll allow you to find out for yourself if you buy the game. _childDocuments_.review: As Monsterverse fans, we love our giant monsters. They're really the only thing that makes any of the Legendary movies worth watching. Nobody cares about the bland human characters who are just there to keep the plot moving along. We just wanna see a big lizard throw down with a big monkey. So when it was announced that the first proper licensed game was going to be a Metroidvania where you're just some lame regular-size guy looking for his lame most likely regular-size daughter? I noped out right then and there. "This is stupid," I thought. "Nobody asked for this!"Fast forward to October 22, I did what every self-respecting Monsterverse fan who's starved for content of the video game variety and has no restraint whatsoever would do:  I bought it anyway! And my verdict, having just finished it? It's actually way more fun than it has any right to be lol.That's not to say it's perfect; for starters the voice acting particularly for the main character is pretty bad, and the human characters and story in general are all entirely forgettable. But again, if you know anything about the Monsterverse why would you come in expecting anything more than that?No, the real star of this game is the game itself. The puzzles are fun, the combat is decent, and the level design is fantastic. From the ruined buildings to the underground Monarch facilities, every area stands out visually, and I had a fun time exploring every nook and cranny. That combined with the prospect of running into an angry Titan kept me engaged throughout, wondering what would be around the next corner.Speaking of the Titans, there is lore to uncover about the handful of monsters showcased in the game, which adds to the rewarding feeling of the exploration if you're into that sort of thing. Other things you can collect are health and ammo upgrades. Overall there's not a ton of backtracking required, and only a handful of tools you'll collect to help you advance to new areas. If you're paying close enough attention you can probably 100 percent it the first playthrough with relative ease. I think I finished with 97 percent. I've seen some debate as to whether it's more like Limbo or Metroid. I haven't played Limbo, but I feel like I'd consider this game like a Metroidvania-Lite. I'd give it a 7.5 out of 10. Would have been an 8, but the ending kinda left a lot to be desired. I felt like there was one final climactic chase segment incoming, but instead the game just kinda ended when my interest in what was going on was at its peak.Overall, while this isn't the first Monsterverse game I would have asked for, I enjoyed it far more than I expected to. I'd even go so far to say I wouldn't mind a sequel, especially one that focused on Godzilla. If you're into both Metroidvanias and Monsterverse, I'd highly recommend giving Kong Survivor Instinct a shot, especially at the introductory price. If you're only into one or the other though, I don't know if you'll get as much mileage out of it as I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Kong: Survivor Instinct pits the player in a action survival scenario in which they must use their combat skills and wits to search for their daughter, using the ORCA Σ to call upon the some of the Monsterverse's mightiest Titans, yet the game fails short of it's main goals: showing a spectacle of the monsters, showcasing a meaningful story that properly ties itself to Legendary's decade-old franchise,  expanding on the world-building, or providing a fast-paced action survival experience.—The Good—* The game controls and feels a lot like 11 bit studios' "This War of Mine" albeit faster, and for the most part, almost everything feels responsive.* The Titans look mostly faithful to their onscreen counterparts, and the introduction to Titanus Abbadon is also a nice treat, especially since Godzilla: King of The Monsters introduced a lot of off-screen monsters we never really got to take a look at aside from a few exceptions in tie-in comics.* The reintroduction of the ORCA as the ORCA Σ is a nice touch to the game, especially since it was shown how powerful of a device it was in both King of The Monsters and Godzilla vs Kong.—The Okay—* Combat is, more or less, meh. As previously said, the game feels a lot like This War of Mine, yet it feels like it lacks so much. For example, you can easily take out enemies if there are one, two or even three if they're all on the same side, but the moment they start coming from both in-front and behind, you have to put in the extra effort to get them all on one side, meaning you might have to use your resources more often.* There's a lot of going back and forth, much like a lot of Metroidvania games, but it feels like it's really flat progression. Half the time, you're looking for biowaves to call upon the power of the Titans to move or destroy things and even then, it feels like you've achieved next to nothing.—The Bad (and I mean, VERY BAD)—* THE STORY. The story feels almost nonexistent and it feels like a wasted opportunity. The protagonist: David Martin, feels like your generic disaster movie protagonist with no redeeming qualities. He has absolutely no backstory or professional history and they try and portray him as this man who can do anything and everything, and it really takes away from the atmosphere. Alan Jonah has been reduced from mass-extinction bio-terrorist to one-off black market dealer. We're talking about a man who killed thousands, if not, millions of lives during his debut movie, and he's ultimately reduced from international's most wanted to Saturday morning cartoon villain from knockoff Jonny Quest. And the ending, THE ENDING. I'm not expecting anything, but THAT'S IT?! THAT'S THE ENDING?! I'D RATHER HAVE INSTANT CUTAWAYS LIKE IN GVK OR GXK!* The Monsters. Remember when Godzilla X Kong: The New Empire came out and we were promised a buddy-cop dynamic from Godzilla and Kong from Adam Wingard after all the flack given to him for making the previous movie mostly Kong-eccentric, only to show Godzilla for eight minutes in the entirety of the film? Well imagine this, a 7-8 hour game to fully complete, and the most you ever get of the monsters is like...say five to ten minutes tops. The title is called "Kong: Survival Instinct" yet it feels like the monsters are heavily. HEAVILY underutilised. It feels like the Monsterverse brand was slapped onto an already in-development game 7Levels was already working on.* The grappling hook is one of the worst mechanics in the game. Half the time you try to use it, it fails and even then, it is not good for any of the chase sequences.* It feels like there are a lot of inconsistencies trying to turn this into a Monsterverse game, especially with one certain enemy unit.*THE ENDING. The final act of the game is, and I barely say this, hot garbage. Despite the complaints I had about the story, I did enjoy it to some degree...until I got to the final stage. Never have I been so disappointed in any game's ending that I ultimately tried to refund it. And the worst part? The developers had movies, books, and even comics to work off of to make a satisfying narrative and they still fumbled the bag.* The Pricepoint: at $24.99 USD, this is not a game I could recommend to others. As previously stated, it feels like the Monsterverse brand was slapped onto an already in-development game 7Levels was already working on. I'd probably pay $10 CAD at most for a game like this, especially since there are much better games by sole comparison.—Conclusion—This game falls short of what it was trying to accomplish as shown in the trailers. Kong ultimately got the treatment of being degraded to a side character like Godzilla was for the last two movies and 7Levels ended up releasing a knockoff This War of Mine with monsters slapped into it just to make a few dollars. I think this is one of the, if not, THE WORST piece of Monsterverse media to ever been released in the history of the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: 4/5Visuals: 5/5Music: 4/5Voice-lines: 2.5/5Story: 2/5-OVERALL: 6/10-The game ran very smoothly and I didn't encounter a single bug during my run; something that I really love considering how buggy most games tend to be nowadays (*cough cough* Until Dawn Remastered, Zoochosis *cough cough*).Game was great, loved the environment and atmosphere of the game; Gameplay was okay at most puzzles and map layout were fine, the combat is interesting for a 2.5D game and is pretty balanced personally speaking; Chase sequences were very difficult to navigate through and fumbling for a second during the chase can ruin your run but this is most likely a Me problem.I'm very mixed about the story but It does have a very small hand full of major twists and turns that make it interesting, personally speaking.My main gripe with this game is it's advertising, specifically how Abaddon was advertised; Even though he was advertised as the main antagonist Kaiju of the game he didn't serve a major role other then awakening and attacking the surface along with Kong and Tiamat and ended up becoming wasted potential, much like how a majority of Monsterverse Kaijus end up as.Kong didn't have a major role either surprisingly despite this game being a Kong game.Overall the game was decent and pretty polished; A very good game for a small indie-dev company. Although I don't think this game is worth 25$, if you want to play this game I recommend you buy it now while it still has a sale or wait for another, potentially bigger sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Kong: Survivor Instinct:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ The Titan Kong has resurfaced. He is looking for something, and he is cranky! The half-destroyed city is on high alert, and citizen are evacuating.. But not everybody has managed to escape from the central district. David Martin, a middle-aged oil rig worker, hasn't heard from his daughter since Kong unleashed his anger on the city. So, he decides to go to the city to find and rescue his daughter, Stacy. His journey will be difficult as he has to navigate the city ruins, fight mercenaries and creatures, and avoid Titans in this Monsterverse of Kong: Survivor Instinct!Kong: Survivor Instinct is a 2.5D platformer action game with some puzzle elements developed and self-published by 7levels on the 23rd of October 2024 on the Steam platform. The game is also available on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.The game starts with a very good cutscene with David driving his car towards the city after a news flash on the television explaining the situation. After crashing his car, he will find himself on the street where his journey begins. From here, you'll go through a short tutorial before finding a steel pipe, which will be David's first weapon.  You’ll also discover some sort of pad that will give you access to the maps and information found throughout the game. As I write this review, I have completed 90% of the game and am enjoying it, but there are some issues. I don't think it is a Metroidvania game because you don't backtrack or find your way from one point to the next; the direction will be written in yellow when you open the map on your device. But it is undoubtedly an excellent platformer game that has plenty of things going for it. The levels are well-designed, with plenty of obstacles to navigate; you’ll encounter electric cables on the floor, fire and lava, and creatures such as spiders and lizards will run towards you at speed. Doors will need keys to open them, and grid metal and trap doors will be chained with padlocks that can only be destroyed by shooting a bullet or smashing it with a large hammer. Make sure to check all walls and the floor as they may already be damaged, and you can destroy them with your hammer. You can also use explosive barrels to destroy walls, webs, and other strange obstacles that the Titans have sprayed around the levels. The puzzle side of the game involves finding gears to repair generators to open doors that need electricity to get by, and switching power on or off to access some areas.  Within each area, you need to reach the Bioware signals, which are pulsing energy fields. To unlock a new area, you’ll want to lure a Titan. You do this by accumulating a certain number of Bioware  signals and then matching segments of Bioware waves to form a complete wave. You'll find a few other objects while exploring the ruins: water bottles to increase David's health bar, medic bags to restore his health and magasines to increase the number of bullets he can load into his gun. There are ammunition cases here and there - you can't miss them as they will have the Monarch's symbol.    That brings me to the fighting system. It’s ok, but it could've been much better. The fighting against the mercenaries, where you have to hit enemies with a pipe or hammer and dodge their attacks, is on point. I did have a bit of trouble changing direction a few times when enemies were coming at me from left and right simultaneously. I like how easy it is to use David's gun; the aiming system is sound.  However, I did not like my encounters with some creatures that moved towards David at full speed while using the hammer as a weapon - the input is a bit off. You can use the gun, but the ammunition is always low. The same thing happened here and there when David was jumping from one platform to another - I don’t know on earth he reached it, he is so far from it!I immensely enjoyed the sections when one of the Titans chased David through the building ruins. That was fun! And when the big spider was chasing David, we twice had to despatch one of the speedy-Gonzales spiders! It took me a while to finish that one due to the under-performing input, which was frustrating. The graphics and sound effects are excellent. The story is just average, and I don't like David's voice-overs; it sounds like he is talking through a glass - horrible! The game has been translated into eleven languages and offers full controller support. It's recommended to play with a game controller.Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Good graphics+	The levels are well-designed and offer a balance of exploring, fighting and puzzle-solving gameplay+	The Titan chasing scenes are challenging but fair as well as fun+	AchievementsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	David's voice-overs are horrible-	A few issues with the combat input system-	Issues while jumping from one platform to another-	No trading cards as yetKong: Survivor Instinct has good graphics and well-designed levels, with challenging fights and escape segments from Titans. A Monsterverse platformer worth playing.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this review with that I enjoy Legendary's Monsterverse a lot and am happy to explore more of this universe.So Kong: Survivor Instinct is a 2.5D Metroidvania lite similar to Deadlight or one of the old War of the Worlds games from the 360 days, and for the most part I feel the developers did a good job with the game and expanding a bit on the narrative of the IP.The game play is fun though can get a little repetitive, and the traversal has some good variations with some nice locations to check out, including some nice set piece moments involving the Titans (though a particular one is a little infuriating with the mechanics used at the time).Visually and audio wise, the game is good for what I speculate was a low-mid AA budget, though it falters a little with the voice cast and the overall narrative. Overall, if you're a fan of the Monsterverse and looking for a good few hours exploring more of the universe then Kong will be a good option to do so, and I think it would be great to see this team get a second shot, maybe even with Godzilla involved

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an awkward one to review, but I don't think it fully deserves all the negative reviews, so I'm throwing one in myself. The main draw here is one thing -- do you like the MonsterVerse? If so, you should get it. Do you not care for the MonsterVerse? Do not buy it. (Also, I'll put this here -- if you don't pick Hard mode at the very start, you won't get the achievement for it. I picked Normal, then bumped it up to hard after the first 20 minutes, but did not get the achievement)This game is very short -- I finished the game (to 92% completion, apparently) in just shy of 9 hours. It's also not extremely complex. It's basically a neutered MetroidVania in terms of exploration and progression, with just a few items/upgrades that you will need to end up completing the whole game. The combat and movement tech is quite imprecise as there is no animation cancelling. One mistake in a boss encounter or one of the later fights will cause you to lose or take damage, and it feels bad. But I had fun! Movie tie-in games like this are something we should encourage. Despite being clearly a low budget title, I feel like it did well with what it was able to work with. If this game is ever on sale, pick it up and have a fun couple afternoons with it. Tiamat is cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Kong: Survivor Instinct

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a side-scroller based on the Monsterverse film series. I am really liking it so far-- exploration is fun, and I like the combat as well. Look at the screenshots and trailers to get a good idea of what to expect. I am satisfied with my purchase, and hope we will get more games like this in the future, both gameplay-wise and Monsterverse in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Kong: Survivor Instinct

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. The only thing i didnt quite like was that the combat felt a bit stiff sometimes and maybe the ending feels a bit too fast (that i dont really mind just felt a bit weird) . But other than that i really enjoyed it. It is a fun little game with a cool story that expands slightly on the lore of the monsterverse.  I would rate it at a solid 7.5/10 but i will bump it up to 8/10 because I love Tiamat <3. I probably will later try to get all achievements. And if anyone was wandering the game takes like 5-6 hours to complete the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Kong: Survivor Instinct

_childDocuments_.review: Kong: Survivor Instinct is a fun 2.5D metroidvania where you play as David and go for a mission in searching for your daughter stacy, during your walkthrough you will encounter different titans you've probably heard about before from famous movies franchises.The game has lots of puzzle solving sections in order to unlock different sections of the map, you will also encounter the hyena group with their multiple mercenaries that will want you dead, your combat skills will be tested.The bosses were very fun and will require lots of patience and timing with heavily focused platforming sections.The soundtracks were fine, but I enjoyed the story the most. This is a good recommendation if you're a metroidvania fan.Overall Rating 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Kong: Survivor Instinct

_childDocuments_.review:
A sudden Titan attack prompts massive evacuation efforts-but not everyone makes it to safety before the devastation ensues. Caught in the crossfire between battling monsters, many residents become trapped in the collapsing city - your only daughter among them!

Kong: Survivor Instinct is a 2.5D action-adventure game that combines realistic platforming, challenging combat, and metroidvania-style exploration during a thrilling quest of survival worthy of the Monsterverse franchise.

name: ROGUE FLIGHT
detailed_description: “With excellent art/presentation, exciting breakneck bullet-hell gameplay, an engaging story, and one of the best video game soundtracks I’ve heard in a while, it is impossible for this reviewer not to recommend Rogue Flight. Every aspect was clearly made with love, both for itself and for iconic series of the past, and I can’t imagine anyone trying this game and earnestly saying they didn’t like it.”  10/10 Try Hard Guides NEW MODE ALERT! Introducing the upcoming Caravan Mode—a fast-paced, action-packed challenge that takes inspiration from the iconic shoot 'em up genre! In this thrilling mode, players will engage in non-stop combat for two intense minutes, battling waves of enemies while striving for the highest score possible.  Caravan Mode delivers the perfect blend of adrenaline, strategy, and replayability. Get ready to test your skills and rack up those high scores in this exciting new mode. Rogue Flight is a breathtaking arcade space combat game inspired by the landmark style of 80's and 90's prestige anime. Traverse the Sol system and join a flight force voiced by a veteran cast, featuring Japanese talent from Sailor Moon, Neon Genesis Evangelion, Gundam, Naruto & One Piece, and English voice talent featured in Overwatch and Fallout 76, League of Legends and Marvel's Avengers. Jump into true stylish arcade action with a huge host of spacecraft upgrades, game modes and multiple narrative paths.                  It's been 3 years since the world burned. It was ARGUS; the interstellar watchman system given control of the Solar Defense Force. In a secret facility deep beneath the surface of the Earth, the last vestiges of humanity prepare to launch a daring counterattack. Take control of an advanced light space fighter and face hordes of enemies in a last-ditch effort to destroy ARGUS and restore peace to the Sol system. >> Featuring a retro 80's-90's analogue-video art style inspired by the golden age of prestige anime. >> Stylish high-speed arcade action set across 9 unique stages spanning the Sol system. >> Utilize incredible aerial acrobatic manoeuvres coupled with a dizzying array of weapon types. >> Experience a branching narrative path with multiple endings. >> Choose from standard arcade and unlockable roguelite game modes which offer greater risks and even greater rewards. >> Personalize your aircraft from over 100 unlockable liveries, as well as 24 badges with multiple color and style combinations. >> Customize your loadout from over 40 unlockable aero designs and 40 unlockable weapons from multiple classes with upgradable attributes. >> Featuring an original soundtrack featuring renowned video game sound design duo Fat Bard, additional music by Rinn, and an original opening theme with stunning vocals by J-Pop artist Itoki Hana. >> Fully voiced in English and Japanese by veteran casts, including English talent from Fallout 76, Overwatch, League of Legends & Marvel’s Avengers, and Japanese talent from Neon Genesis Evangelion, Gundam, Sailor Moon, Naruto & One Piece. >> Unlockable extras, accolades and more. >> Multiple difficulty levels for every player skill.
