_childDocuments_.review: ROGUE FLIGHT absolutely OOZES charm and mid-90s nostalgia from every corner. With poppy visuals and responsive controls that manages to keep everything readable and in your hands even in the most enemy saturated segments. Though I sadly found the bosses themselves to be a bit on the bland side; struggling to communicate their scale or really stand-out in any way. Still I'd be the third biggest liar in the universe if I said I didn't enjoy the game... so there you go... twelve gold-plated space whales out of ten.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: If Starfox and Ace Combat had a anime baby. Very good throwback to classic rail shooter/Shoot 'em up. A good amount of customization and unlocks, a great soundtrack and awesome visuals. The game is a little short, I was able to run through the whole thing in about 5 hours. There is a "Roguelike" mode, and you are able to go back and replay stages.Overall a very good game, just wish there was more
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty decent star fox style shmup that unfortunately suffers from a lack of variety at times. The core gameplay and visuals are great, the arrow has a really satisfying set of weapons, and a very unique melee attack thingy that i've never seen before. soundtrack is jammin all the time (there's even 2 vocal themes), and special shoutout to all the ship, character, and enemy designs, they're all really cool. The game's variety issue comes in two parts. It's enemy roster only changes by having stronger versions of already existing enemies, meaning you'll have seen pretty much every single enemy type after about 3 stages. The "branching narrative" is less a cool world map where differing mission performance will send you to different stages, and more a linear choice partway through each run where you pick between between 2 easy stages, 2 hard stages, or 3 of the previous with one new one, as well as a 4th "true" path that's just the previous path but with 2 alternate versions of previous stages. I do like the idea but pretty much having to play each of the same stages several times across what's supposed to be unique playthroughs makes the idea feel pretty eh. The ship upgrades are also not the most interesting, doing certain actions/using certain abilities well will give you points towards different categories to get upgrades for your ship's mobility and weapons/shields. At first its a cool choice between what you want to specialize in, when you likely only have significant progress in one/two categories, but the end goal is to just get an upgrade that gives you nearly max power on everything, making the other choices feel pretty redundant. It's also a decently short game, 100% achievements in 4.5 hours (though it's important to note that i'm an unhinged shmup and star fox enjoyer, you'll probably take longer) so your mileage may vary in terms of how worth it the game is for the price. Considering this is seemingly the dev's very first project i'm very impressed despite my criticisms, and the overall vibe of the game still made the $20 feel worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom line up front. A short but enjoyable rail shooter done up to look like the space opera anime's that were the best thing about anime from the late 70s-early 90s. Totally worth the 20 dollar asking price if you enjoy that sort of thing.Now as others have stated in their reviews the unit and level variety leave a bit to be desired and the length is quite short but the game play mechanics are solid and I quickly found myself trying to get higher and higher combos as I played through it. The voice acting is solid so props to the VAs who provided their talent to what dialogue there is and the overall look and design of the hero ship is quite nice. There is a nice bit of customization you can use in the look of the ship and there is some minor unlocks to let you tailor the ship to whichever of the various weapons you prefer but messing with it isn't really needed to enjoy the game. You'll also find a difficulty setting which might be needed as on the base difficulty it's not really too challenging. All and all a full recommend as something to scratch that rail shooter itch if you enjoy old classics like Panzer Dragoon and Star Fox.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: --Review updated after clearing story mode--From the moment you boot up Rogue Flight the game's charm and incredible sense of style bring you in. The overall experience (The story so far, the art and music, the voicework!) is all phenomenal. Levels have different lighting and shading depending on your story route, which is a nice touch.There's a wide variety of enemies right from the outset, and their designs and fire patterns are interesting, but the early bosses feel a bit frustrating to fight against as they take a lot of time without posing much threat. Later bosses start to become very exciting though!I didn't realise it initially, but the game has a permanent progression element where you can upgrade your ship's modules to improve your damage and shields based on the kind of fighting you've been doing, which made it much more fun to try different weapons and strategies, although the game doesn't offer much in the way of alternate weaponry for a while (at least stage 3)That said, the easiest and by far most abusable mechanic is the special move. Don;t get me wrong, it looks fantastic and feels incredible the first few times you use it... but it's unlimited, you get it back off cooldown almost instantly, and you're nearly invulnerable while performing it which combined with the slow-mo makes the "best" way to play to just crawl through the stage clearing waves spamming this move until you unlock more effective weaponry. I think it ought to be toned way down from where it is and it could be brought back to near it's current power level by the permanent progression.I definitely recommend this game if you're a fan of similar games such as Star Fox or Ikaruga*, and further as a beautiful art piece embodying and paying tribute to the late 80's aesthetic. For the price and with the potential of future updates it's more than worth it. But I would like to see the special move made less available (and thus more special), more variety introduced in the first stages of the game, and especially more interactivity to the early bosses.*I know Ikaruga is 2D, but the "one fighter versus an army" and anime aesthetic give it a similar vibe---Original review text below for context on developer response---The enemy variety even in the first two stages is quite wide, but the play pattern is unfortunately gets a bit stale. A few runs up to the second boss now and I have not been offered any new weapon or any other powerup besides missiles, which is odd considering the tutorial demos one immediately. The "screen clear" side special recharges almost instantly which makes clearing waves trivial, albeit incredibly cool looking. The bosses give you few ways to retaliate against their attacks, as you have to put yourself directly in the firing line to take shots. This is especially frustrating in the first boss, where you have to stay out of the engine wake but also shoot directly into the engines, which essentially boils down to wiggling a lot and hoping you don't slightly drift into the constant damage zone. Meanwhile the boss itself has little to no way of attacking you, making it feel like more of a passive obstacle. I hope to see more interactive and exciting enemies as I progress further into the game.EDIT: Having made it to a third stage, the enemy and boss attack patterns have become significantly more engaging and fun! Still no sign of any new weapons though...
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: 80's anime Starfox. Very stylish and visually pleasing with a fitting rock soundtrack for high speed space combat. Large variety of ship customization options flavour wise, decent variety gameplay wise (Though it's mostly upgrades you can choose to specialize in one of the weapons on offer.) The gameplay is fun if a bit simple at times, but that's the genre convention. Very good voice acting for the little dialogue there is. The game is rather short, but it has good replay value. Overall very much a great deal for the low price tag and there is little in this genre nowadays.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Star Fox 65 - Furry-Free EditionBut seriously, Rogue Flight is a compact homage to games like Star Fox 64 and Space Harrier. While it pushes the envelope mechanically in some key ways, it isn't quite as expansive as Star Fox (no subs or tanks in this game). It's worth playing if you're fan of Star Fox, though it would be nice if there was an option to skip the first 2 missions before the level split because seeing the true ending, assuming you clear each route on your first try, will have you play those missions 3 times each - which is 6 repeated missions.Overall, the game is recommended with a grade of: B
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable arcade space shooter with style! Music, visuals and voice acting are very good, gameplay is fun and suitable for a short burst of just one mission or to try and get through a complete run. Unlockable upgrades and different routes give variety to runs although there is some repetition of the early stages in order to get to the branching path each time. I played through it all on a Steam Deck OLED where it runs perfectly and is a great fit for the handheld. Some of it was in offline mode so I'd say overall it took me 6 hours for all the achievements.If you're a fan of arcadey shooters such as Starfox or Afterburner then check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Starfox but 80's anime.It may say I've played a 0.7-hour record but played offline on Steam deck. For 20 dollars it's good for what you get. Good combat for a flight game aside from just aim and shoot, there's a drift mechanic that can spice up the combat. The soundtrack is an absolute banger in my opinion. If there is a side story or a prequel to this game I can't wait for what the devs will cook.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Quite fun, great presentation and style. Nice and fun retro styled shmup to play through over a weekend. Basic gameplay loop works pretty well, and the story is just right for the games scope. The music, visuals, and controls are what sells it. I also never had any performance issues which is always a plus.The game asks you to repeat levels to get through the full story with all the endings. However the different routes and difficulty it gives you make repeated older levels get new additions and alterations so it's not overly repetitive. The unlocks and customization for the ship are surprisingly extensive, so thats another way to alter the gameplay between (and during runs).It's already gotten some updates with new enemies and modes so it will be interesting to return to it over time and try out different stuff that gets added.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed games like Starfox 64 or similar on rails shooters this is a really enjoyable game in that same vein with well done presentation and voice acting that runs perfectly on the Steam Deck .The campaign isn’t terribly long but has multiple routes and customization options in addition to a roguelike mode, it uses the old arcade style “three lives and then you start from the beginning” system but the devs offer multiple difficulty options in the settings menu.On the negative side, barrel rolling to parry shots works well as a mechanic but it’s something that you’re more encouraged to spam rather than it being a tactical option, and the use of red and yellow for enemy bullets makes the lava level that uses the same color palette a bit difficult to play when dodging. Otherwise it’s a solid game and worth the money to me, if you’re interested definitely try the demo.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet classic rail shooter, fans of the genre will probably enjoy. Both the English and Japanese voice acting are great, the story is simple and serviceable. I was a bit concerned about the advertised roguelite elements since I don't really want any of that, but you can ignore them, and in fact the modes don't even unlock until you finish an arcade mode playthrough.Things I wish were better:* Maybe bump up the standard/default difficulty by one. I died once in the plus route from careless lack of observation as my shield melted and I was just zoned out. I'll have to try the harder modes to see if they give a better feeling for challenge.* The drift attack / wing trail attack is too powerful and too slow. It's kind of this game's differentiating mechanic, and it's cool, but the incentives are to spam it. There's a slow-mo effect while it's in use, which is also cool, but after a while, especially when you get ships that recharge the special very quickly, it becomes annoying and slows the overall pace of the game down to a crawl.I think one possible fix would be to remove the slow-mo effect entirely, or make it an option, or only remove it on the harder game modes. making it much more like a fast melee attack that other shooters have. If the move didn't slow everything down, the overall pace of the game would remain high, which is where it should be.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: at first, i really thought this game wouldn't be for me - it's too fast, too bright, too busy, too confusing. i impulse bought it almost entirely off of the vibes alone. somehow, despite that, i ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ LOVE this game. it's super straight forward, yet manages to present some interesting ideas for storytelling between it's four (!) endings and really tight gameplay loop. by the end, i was hitting combos lasting four whole minutes, and capping off levels with 600,000 score!it doesn't have a groundbreaking story or revolutionary gameplay, it doesn't *need* to. it sticks to what it likes to do and it does it well, it doesn't overstay its welcome, it doesn't leave you wanting. excellent, absolutely excellent game. well worth it
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: A good fast paced shooter ala star fox. Controls great with a controller and the game feels good to play. The team did a good job making it feel like you're going at high speeds. It's on rails, so if you wanted to have free 3d flight, this ain't for you. But if you want to shoot up evil AI drones and simply save the world in cool spacecraft you upgrade along the way, go wild. Good performances from the cast across the board too, so there's also that. And really good music. Overall, this game has good vibes all over the place, and soul.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: It's not Starfox.  But it is VERY good with some added style points.  If you want a solid 3d rail shooter this is it.  Maybe I haven't played far enough yet but it is missing open levels ("all-range mode") like Star Fox had which may be it's biggest downside if you're making that comparison. Runs great on Steamdeck even though it's listed as "unknown" at time of this writing.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: It's good. Real good. The soundtrack is a banger. It oozes with 90s anime and video game VHS feel. UI is beautifully 90s as well, with "fighter plane console" aesthetic to it. The game also lets you select the colour of the UI... this is how you know they are making something special. :D (I remember the original Deus Ex did this, and I always wondered why more games don't do this... looking at you Elite: Dangerous).Some cons:- Compared to a 2D arcade SHMUP, this 3D rail shooter struggles with telegraphing enemy positions within the play volume, producing misses that look like they should be hits. I.e. the depth axis is unclear at times. The action being fast compounds the issue. It might also just be inherent to the rail shooter genre. - Boss battles are a bit tedious. Like in a 2D arcade SHMUP, they behave like levels, with weakpoints to shoot and attack patterns to dodge. But, because your ship moves where it aims, it makes it difficult to align a shot against a boss' weakpoint that also features some counter, which like the point above, doesn't telegraph where it'll hit you that well. For example, early on, you'll be shooting at the boss thrusters, which also puts you in harm's way of their burn. This all results in forcing the player to send pot shots at the weakpoint, breaking off the attack in time to avoid damage. It sounds like a standard arcade SHMUP design on paper, but Rogue Flight's implementation of it leads to a drawn-out fight. Compared to the boss battles from the many insanely challenging 2D arcade SHMUPs, this is challenging in all the wrong ways.I'm only an hour into the game, so some of these issues I have I might iron out via increased skill. But compared to other SHMUPs across subgenres, I still feel it's fair to offer this critique to the devs, and offer this as a consideration for players.That's it for cons. I love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: this game rules! It's not too hard, the art style, the music the voice acting, the unlockables, the story though very, very short is engaging enough. I literally played this for 8hrs straight I was addicted! Haven't played the extra mode yet I only have 2 critiques; I wish there was more levels and thus longer game and second the drift jet air slice thing on R stick is incredibly overpowered and in endgame can be spammed infinitely doing this slows down the pace of the game dramatically. I don't even care that it makes the game to easy, I prefer an easier ride. (bonus points for looking awesome!)P.S. the boss difficulty is weird. The Boss on level 2 is the hardest thing I've ever done but every other boss in the game is nice and chill, what's up with the level 2 boss, man?
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratches an itch I didn't even know I had, If your a fan of Star Wars: Rebel Assault, Starfox 1, 2 or 64, RayStorm (though that was top down) or especially afterburner 1, 2 & Climax you will love this game. If you also happen to be a fan of a short but sweet simple story that plays itself straight and serious, and Sythwave with rock insturmentals, 90s anime this game is a must play. As someone who remembers games like this and has been gaming since the early 90s this comes with my highest recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: A highly stylish shooter that has some killer aesthetics and great voice acting, but unfortunately is tied to an incredibly bland and ultimately boring gameplay experience.Each stage takes thrice  as long as it needs to, with fairly boring enemy patterns and capped off with a boss fight that has a tendency to use one attack pattern until you destroy bits and bobs, then shift into one more. None of the patterns are visually impressive nor are they interesting to deal with and the gameplay lacking excitement absolutely kills the mood the game is attempting to go for.It's really unfortunate because it has everything a shmup needs to be a killer game except for the actual game part. And the gameplay mechanics it attempts to add to spice things up ends up being little more than fluff. In many scenarios I'd be willing to look past the gameplay portion being lacking if it was trying to do something unique or different but what's here is a sub-standard shmup with poor stage design and even poorer boss design. I still hope you find success, but I cannot recommend it currently.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: What a blast. Arcade style shooter at its best. wish it was a bit longer but there are different game modes and such to try out.  flying feels amazing, the guns impactful and punchy and the special dodge attack, and parry/deflect system is very interesting and feels satisfying use. 9.5/10 for me. thank you for all involved. this was made with love and passion for a long lost genre and i wish it every success!
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: This game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rocks.In more detail: the art and sound design did everything right, the challenge is engaging and will beat you at first, and the devs keep adding little bonuses that they don't need to just to make it a little cooler.I usually don't like Afterburner clones, but this better than all of them including the original. It's a quick arcadey game that makes the best of it.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Easy 10 for me! This game hit me right in the feels with the sound track and combat. While i do think 20$ is a bit much for a game that is 4 hours long from beginning to 100% completion. It gives enough customization and detail for your spacecraft to want to keep holding down the trigger a little while longer.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Only played an hour but can tell this is a quality game. After browsing the forums I sense the developer is passionate over this game. That's a good thing.On rails shooter, looks and sounds fantastic. I'm a sucker for VHS effects! Also, the sideswipe is a genius idea.When I have some time to commit, I can see me playing and replaying for scores. Absolutely worth 15 quid.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Decided to check this game out after I saw Skillup recommend it in a video. I'm a big Starfox 64 fan, so as soon as I saw the gameplay I knew it was made for people like me.The good:- Awesome music. Tons of shreddy guitars.- Great voice acting- Artwork. Everything from the ship to the character portraits to the levels themselves look great.- Sense of speed. Feels like your really hauling ass through space.The bad:- It's really easy. There is one enemy type in particular that will destroy your health bar if you're not paying attention, but that's about it.- Boring bosses. I was expecting a little more spectacle, but most of them are quite boring and again very easy.Level pacing - Enemy distribution in the levels feels a bit off at times. There will be stretches where you barely encounter any enemies at all.Damage indicator - If you're not watching your health bar it can be very difficult to tell you're taking damage. A critical health audio cue would be really helpful.If you like Starfox or rail shooters, you'll probably have a decent time with this, but don't expect it to be much of a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very very difficult. Took me 15 mins to reach the 2nd boss, I shot it for 3 minutes and it didn't even progress the 2nd phase. I died on the second try and game over. I had to start from 0 again.I know it's roguelike but some games give rewards for better future run. But not this game, any progression you do each run means nothing, you have to start from the first stage with nothing.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that is absolutely worth your time & attention. Its a bullet hell rail shooter, so its already filling a unique niche that is underserved.Story goes harder than one would think it needs too, and I am all for it. This silly little bullet hell on rails has lore & characters straight out of an 80s space anime. If this game came out in the 90s it would've been a hugely popular title that started a whole franchise of games. Give this game some love and some money.
_childDocuments_.name: ROGUE FLIGHT

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: Rogue Flight takes classic elements from multiple video game genres and does a stand up job in the execution of its parts. 10/10 would leave atmo again.Roguelike Element: While death does mean the end of your run you do take back previously earned points and can change your Aero and Tact mod of your ship to better fit your playstyle. Bullet Hell: POV Bullet Hell Lite is a nice take on the scrolling shooter genre. Rogue Flight offers two choices of POV here: Cockpit view and 3rd person. Anime: The overarching story is very classic anime scene. it reminds me of Metal Gear.Personal aside: My first game near this genre was way back in the DOS era with Raptor: Call of the Shadows, followed by Star Fox 64 as was likely most people who have found themselves playing Rogue Flight. This game was exactly what I needed in 2024 to fill that gap.

_childDocuments_.review: pretty decent star fox 64 clone. the 80-90s anime aesthetic works really well. The drift feels really good to use and the weapons are all satisfying to use. The game is very easy tho. you can spam barrel rolls forever and health is easy to come by when most the enemy ships die in 1-5 shots and give health when you are in a combo. The thing this game is lacking most is variety. Every level is particles flying fast by you while the same 3 ships come attack you and then a boss. Was kind of hoping for more environmental movement. _childDocuments_.review: Rogue Flight is a fantastic throwback to the classic on-rails shooters of the 90s, like Star Fox 64. The game delivers tight controls, exciting combat, flashy visuals, and a nostalgic vibe that's hard to resist. Sure, it's on the shorter side—you'll probably see everything it offers in about two hours—but every minute is pure fun. Think of it as a 10/10 weekend rental: if that sounds good to you and you've got some spare cash, you're going to have a great time blasting through this a few times!

_childDocuments_.review: This game sneaked up on me as a YouTube recommendation four days before launch, and I am GLAD it did. The 80-90s anime aesthetic is ingrained into every facet of this game's art direction, and it's influences from games like Star Fox are quite clear. As of the time of this review, I have completed each branching path and New Game+, but have not tried the rougelight mode for the game. The action is fast paced and a visual spectacle, all accompanied by a good sound track and good voice performances (barring some weird audio mixing for Nadia's inner monologues). I particularly loved seeing the mouths move on character portraits, taking a CLEAR inspiration from Star Fox 64 portraits.It's a short experience (I completed all paths in roughly 4 hours of gameplay) but honestly, at 20 dollars, I feel like the game delivered on it's premise and I enjoyed each minute of dodging and weaving between enemy ships and attacks. Maintaining constant kills to keep your combo string is also encouraged, as your shield regenerates as long as the combo is maintained.If I had to criticize a few elements of the game, it's that the Drift system feels fairly overpowered. When you do a Drift, it creates a sort of energy blade attack that comes from the slipstream of the fighter jet, as well as a slow mo effect. If timed right, it's quite satisfying as it can wipe out a number of enemies on screen. The downside to this is that this move feels very overpowered at times, even in later stages of NG+ where the difficulty ramps up. (It may be needed if the Rougeflight mode is harder.)The other options are boost and braking; braking allows you to drag power ups to your ship, and can be useful for selecting enemies to shoot missiles at. That being said, the Boost function doesn't seem to serve too much of a purpose; best I can tell is that it allows you to pass certain enemies that may be firing from outside your attack range, but I almost never used it.All in all, it's a solid rail shooter that I highly recommend. I'm eager to see if the devs have more planned for the future with this game or any other projects.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Very good game, if Star Fox is a 5/5 I would give this a 4/5. My only real complaint is that it could use another level or 2. If you have any interest in it I would recommend at least trying the demo.A few weeks ago, Youtube's algorithm finally did something right and showed me a trailer I'm actually interested in. The second I saw the trailer I knew I was gonna get this game. Star Fox 64 has always been one of my favorite games and the 90's Anime aesthetic put me right in their target demographic. I'm happy to say I was not disappointed. I play through demo twice when it came out and didn't really click for me off the bat. However, after buy the game and getting to the 2nd and 3rd level, I started to understand that I need to go for combos more. The game has a similar system to Star Fox 64  *Hits*. In that game if you kill multiple enemies at the same time it give you more *Hits* that count towards medals. In Rogue Flight the game rewards you a lot for string kill combos together with you primary fire, missiles and jet stream attack. The bigger the combo the more shields and stat points you get.  Once I started on focusing on extending the Combos will all 3 attacks the game really clicked and any worries I had about the gameplay vanished. The game will also reward you with unlockable ship modules. To get them you will need to do things like parrying enemy fire, getting multikills with missiles and collect shield and missile drops with your vortex ability. Points are not spent, but rather the modules are auto unlocked at certain thresholds for each stat. Trying to max out each for the modules adds a lot of replay value. I just wish you didn't have to go to extras tab in the main menu to look at the stat descriptions. If you there was an option in the pause menu to get a that linked to the database descriptions of each stat and how to increase them that would be nice.I do have one other very small issue with it. Once you have played the story a few times and start unlocking ship modules the game can get a little to easy. Luckily there is a fix for this, in the setting tab you can change the difficulty to 2 harder levels (or 2 easier ones if you just want to chill to the music and story). -If the devs are seeing this, I really think it would be good idea to have the game ask you which difficulty you want after selecting the game mode. I totally missed seeing until I have beaten the game 5-6 times.If you pump the difficulty all the way up and still want a change the rougelike modes will give it to you. It took me 3-4 tries to beat the harder version of it and I admittedly got a little carried by getting one of the late stage weapon upgrades. Do keep in mind though that the Rougelike mode really just changes the modules you start with. From what I have seen it doesn't change the story or stages at all. I'm just going to group these together because there not much to say other than that they are perfect. Honestly, I bought this game purely from the music and overall aesthetic that I saw in the trailer. Once you have beaten the game a few time I would suggest looking in the Settings and Extras tabs. There are a few treats in there like a . The story and voice acting are pretty good, but a little short for my taste. Really the length is probably my only big complaint for the game as a whole. There are 7 stages (and a tutorial) with a few changes on each stage depending on the game mode and route you take in the story. If you are not watching the cutscenes I think a normal run will be about 30-40 mins for both of the short routes or 60-70 mins for the long route. If the game had just 1-2 more levels I would say its near perfect. Overall though I still really liked it and if your a fan of Star Fox I think your going to too. I would definitely recommend buying it and if your still on the fence you can always try the demo or wishlist it for a sale notification.

name: Abyss
detailed_description: Explore the abyss! Earth, 3024. Natural resources are scarce and the survival of the human race is in danger. Desperate to find new energy resources, the ASAN creates a biomechanical robot called Nep2no that is capable of withstanding extreme depths in the hope of finding new energy sources. After many years of exploration, a new energy source is found, code named 'Gaia'. Your mission will be to find the 'Gaia' energy stones by exploring the depths. To do so, you must control Nep2no by counteracting gravity and the surrounding darkness with the aid of a Light that will go out little by little. New features: - 12 Original missions plus 8 in Dark mode. - Competitive two-player mode. - New Graphic Effects and remixed Music. - Online Leaderboard. Local Multiplayer A controller is required in order to play local multiplayer.

name: Clock Tower: Rewind
detailed_description: Turn back the clock for one of the pioneers of the survival-horror genre. Translated and released outside of Japan for the first time, Clock Tower: Rewind is a revival of the terror-inducing 16-bit classic that dares you to explore the haunting confines of the Barrows family manor. As teenage orphan Jennifer, you must search every disturbing corner to find items, reveal secrets, and discover ways to evade Scissorman, a murderous, unstoppable, shears-wielding psychopath. Play Original mode to experience Clock Tower as it was when initially released in 1995, or play Rewind mode with extra content and improvements. Additional features include a new animated intro, opening and ending vocal theme songs, motion comics, creator interview, art gallery, border artwork, save states, and a music player. The clock is ticking...can you survive? Key Features: • The survival-horror classic, Clock Tower, officially translated and brought out of Japan for the first time • Choose from Original mode or Rewind mode, which features numerous gameplay additions and quality-of-life refinements • Run, hide, and survive as you attempt to evade the psychotic Scissorman • Atmospheric 2D art, detailed animations, and haunting sound effects augment the tense point-and-click gameplay • Multiple endings and randomized gameplay elements maximize replayability (and jump scares) • New animated opening, motion-comics with VO, and vocal theme song performed by Mary Elizabeth McGlynn • Featuring an art gallery, music player, behind-the-scenes creator interview, save states, and other modern inclusions

_childDocuments_.review:
Originally released on Super Famicom in 1995 in Japan, Clock Tower traps players in the haunting confines of the Barrows family manor, where they'll be pursued by Scissorman, a murderous, shears-wielding psychopath. As teenage orphan Jennifer Simpson, players will use a point-and-click interface to explore the mansion and search every disturbing corner to find items, reveal secrets, and discover ways to survive Scissorman's assaults. 

Without any offensive capabilities, Jennifer must rely on her wits and resourcefulness if she has any hope of escaping with her life and earning one of the game's multiple endings.

This enhanced version of the original 16-bit Clock Tower marks the first time this terrifying initial adventure in the popular horror series will officially be translated and released in North America and Europe.

name: Vigor
detailed_description: Vigor Chronicles: Genesis Unfold the Chronicles and revel in this genesis! A new era has reached the Outlands, full of exciting possibilities! In this update, you can explore Eikevjen in Encounters, try out the new Weapon Overhaul, and progress through a Battle Pass inspired by 80s action movies. About the Game Join the game that has been played by over 20 million players and explore the harsh and unforgiving Outlands, the shattered remains of what was once Norway. Utilize any means necessary to survive. Set in a post-apocalyptic atmosphere in the early 90s, the landscape of the Outlands is as deadly as it is beautiful, so be careful out there. Experience the thrills that Encounters have to offer, a high-stakes mode where survival is key. Extract the most valuable resources in order to build and upgrade your Shelter, or lose everything if you die! Choose over 60 different weapons and consumables to customize your loadout based on the play style of your choice - sneaky looter or deadly shooter. Change the pace of the Encounter and gain an advantage over your enemies by controlling tactical points on the map. Compete for Loot Events, special places that hold more valuable loot, and try to retrieve the Airdrop, the most precious haul in the Outlands. We dare you! Escape from specific exits at any time and avoid the deadly radiation cloud that sweeps over the map, killing everyone trapped inside it. Play alone in Shootout, a fast-paced deathmatch, or join a squad with your friends in Elimination, a 5v5 tactical, round-based teamfight. In Encounter, you can team up with a friend as a Duo, or compete as a Lone Wolf where the risk vs. reward factor is greater as you square off against other squads on your own! Identify as one of many groups of Outlanders that inhabit this broken world through various cosmetic sets. Choose between military, non-military and everything in between to instill fear in the hearts of your opponents. Your Shelter is your safe haven in the apocalypse and your central hub for information. By collecting resources from Encounters, you can build and upgrade your Shelter, which will, in turn, provide you with more options (craft better weapons and consumables, generate Crowns and other materials) that will be essential to your survival. Practice your marksmanship in the Shooting Range, craft your necessary equipment in the Armory, and customize your character from the wardrobe while you keep building your Shelter to maximize its potential.

_childDocuments_.review: I understand why everyone is a little ticked off with this game. As someone who had shilled $20 in 2018 to get Vigor in early release on Xbox to seven years later having to shill another $20 to get Vigor on Steam, I get it. Stings a bit. My thoughts to this whole conundrum is Vigor is absolutely worth it. It is worth spending 50 hours just knowing all my progress will be erased in a few months when the f2p method goes live. This game has something so unique to any  other extraction shooter; The sessions go fast! Compared to any other extraction shooter, you are in the "zone" or what have you for 40 to an hour. Vigor is easily 20-30 minutes of game play (if that). Fast game play is especially nice when you just want to loot and leave. I will say this game is absolutely beautiful, and with so many different weather condition for every map it never makes it feel like I am playing the same map over and over again. _childDocuments_.review: Vigor presents itself as a survival looter-shooter in a post-apocalyptic world, a concept that initially promises excitement and tension. Unfortunately, the game struggles to deliver on these expectations, falling short in several key areas that diminish its overall potential.Visuals and SettingOn a superficial level, Vigor is aesthetically pleasing. The game's visuals effectively capture a bleak, desolate environment, and the base-building mechanic provides a sense of personal progression. However, while these elements are commendable, they are ultimately cosmetic and do little to enrich the core gameplay.Gameplay and Balance IssuesThe heart of Vigor lies in its player-versus-player looting system, but it is here that the experience begins to falter. The matchmaking system is alarmingly unbalanced, often pitting newcomers against seasoned players equipped with vastly superior gear. This imbalance creates a steep learning curve that punishes less experienced players, making survival less about strategy and more about gear disparity.Monetization ConcernsMicrotransactions are unfortunately pervasive. While Vigor allows players to grind for in-game resources, the heavy emphasis on monetization is unmistakable. Cosmetic and gear purchases can give paying players a clear advantage, skewing the competitive fairness that should define games in this genre. This pay-to-win aspect undermines the integrity of the experience, alienating those who prefer skill-based progression.Repetitiveness and Lack of ContentOne of the most significant issues plaguing Vigor is its repetitiveness. After a few matches, the gameplay becomes formulaic, with little variety in the maps or encounters to keep the player engaged. The sense of risk and reward that the game strives to create is diluted by a lack of innovation and fresh content. As a result, the experience quickly loses its novelty.Technical ShortcomingsIn addition to gameplay flaws, Vigor suffers from technical issues. Clunky movement mechanics and sluggish combat responses hinder what should be fluid and responsive encounters. Furthermore, frequent server problems, including disconnects and extended load times, disrupt the player's immersion and progress, compounding the frustration.ConclusionIn theory, Vigor could stand out in the survival shooter genre, but its numerous flaws prevent it from reaching its potential. The game’s unbalanced matchmaking, aggressive monetization, and repetitive content all detract from what could be an immersive experience. Until these fundamental issues are addressed, Vigor remains a game that frustrates more than it engages, making it difficult to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Vigor: A Comprehensive ReviewVigor is a free-to-play looter-shooter developed by Bohemia Interactive, the studio known for titles like ARMA and DayZ. Set in a post-apocalyptic Norway after a nuclear disaster, the game offers a unique blend of survival, looting, and tactical combat, all within a tense multiplayer environment. The concept is intriguing: you play as an Outlander trying to survive in a world where resources are scarce, and every encounter with other players could be a matter of life or death.GameplayAt its core, Vigor is a third-person multiplayer survival game where players are dropped into large open maps to scavenge for resources and weapons. The goal is to loot as much as you can and extract safely before other players or environmental hazards take you down. What makes Vigor stand out is its tension-filled gameplay. Unlike traditional shooters, combat in Vigor is more calculated, with players often avoiding confrontation in favor of scavenging quietly.The maps are sprawling and atmospheric, each filled with dynamic weather changes that add to the immersion. Resources gathered in each match can be used to upgrade your base—a personal shelter that serves as a hub for crafting better gear and building your character's progression.CombatThe combat in Vigor is realistic but not as hardcore as DayZ or Escape from Tarkov. Gunplay is tight and responsive, with a variety of firearms, from pistols to assault rifles, and melee weapons. However, bullets are scarce, and each shot counts, which encourages strategic thinking. Do you engage that lone player or risk drawing attention to yourself and attracting others? This question forms the core of Vigor’s combat philosophy.Encounters are often nerve-wracking due to the unpredictability of other players. Some will hunt you down for your loot, while others might prefer to scavenge in peace. This "trust no one" atmosphere keeps you on edge throughout each match.Looting and ExtractionLooting is a major element of Vigor. You can find anything from weapons, ammo, and food to materials for base-building. However, the loot you gather can only be used if you successfully extract from the map. Fail to do so, and you lose everything. This high-stakes risk-reward system adds another layer of strategy, making extraction points hotspots for tense encounters.Some unique events, like an airdrop, make looting even more engaging. These events tend to draw players into conflict, creating thrilling moments of cat-and-mouse chases or full-blown firefights.Base BuildingYour shelter in Vigor acts as both a safe haven and a progression system. As you gather resources, you can upgrade your base, which in turn unlocks new crafting options and increases your ability to stockpile gear. The base-building mechanics are simple but satisfying, offering a tangible sense of progression between matches.Graphics and SoundVisually, Vigor does a great job of portraying a bleak, post-apocalyptic Norway. The environments are beautifully rendered, with detailed landscapes ranging from snowy mountains to dense forests. The atmospheric effects like fog, rain, and wind add to the immersive experience.Sound design is equally strong. The crack of gunfire in the distance or the rustle of footsteps nearby heightens the tension in every match. The absence of music during gameplay adds to the stark realism and keeps you focused on your surroundings.MonetizationAs a free-to-play game, Vigor offers in-game purchases mainly for cosmetics and boosts, but they don’t provide a significant competitive advantage. While the game avoids pay-to-win mechanics, the grind for better loot and shelter upgrades can sometimes feel slow, nudging players toward spending real money for faster progress. However, this is fairly balanced and doesn’t ruin the experience for free players.Community and MultiplayerThe Vigor community is somewhat small compared to larger looter-shooters, but it’s growing steadily. The player base is generally respectful, though you’ll encounter your share of griefers. Vigor does offer various modes, including team-based play, which can be enjoyable if you have friends to squad up with.DrawbacksOne of the biggest drawbacks of Vigor is its sometimes steep learning curve. The game doesn’t hold your hand, and new players may find themselves overwhelmed by the number of mechanics and systems at play. Additionally, while the tactical gameplay is its strength, some may find the pace a little too slow compared to other shooters. Matches can sometimes feel uneventful if you avoid combat or struggle to find worthwhile loot.Server issues and occasional lag can also disrupt the experience, although these problems are less frequent as the game has matured.VerdictVigor offers a unique blend of looting, survival, and tactical combat that stands out from more traditional multiplayer shooters. Its slow, tension-filled gameplay won't appeal to everyone, but those who enjoy risk-reward systems, careful planning, and intense encounters will find it highly engaging. The free-to-play model is well-balanced, with cosmetics and boosts available for purchase without giving paying players a distinct edge.While it has its issues, like a steep learning curve and occasional server problems, Vigor is a rewarding experience for those who enjoy high-stakes gameplay and the thrill of survival in a hostile environment.Rating: 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: So I played this for a few months back on console until the literal server lag and greed of the developers drove me away. Saw it coming to PC and Figured I'd grab this and try it out. They've went back and undid some of the greed but you still need to spend the ingame currency to get any decent amount of loot and considering you very quickly need hundreds of matts just for lvl 3 of 10-15 level house upgrades well I guess you better grind the in game missions and hope you extract lucky so you didn't complete 2 missions just to boost your loot by 50% once.First two hours ran pretty good. Deaths were justifiable, just unlucky, or mistakes on my behalf and I had good games and got some good loot. The majority of the matches I played until the radiation came in and sometimes never saw a player.The last hour has had me spawn hunted 4 times, and close proximity spawned to other players 3 times. Due to the fact that players often use the craftable item to reveal players around them and you can often just spawn by in game locations that will do that for you as well, having been shortly hunted after being spawned with no way to protect myself because I'm not at the point of being capable/worth bringing a jammer each run or skilled enough to react and catch a player who knows where I am and I don't know where they are first and kill them. Perhaps if these towers revealed everyone to everyone in the radius I'd feel a lot better about it, but considering if you don't spawn right next to it you might as well just run away from it imo. The only time I didn't die from being spawn revealed was because I saw them taking aim at me and got a headshot when they shot me in the body.Kill time is pretty quick, so unless you or your opponent just are inaccurate and having a bad moment, whoever shoots first wins. Which I don't think is necessarily a bad thing, but with being spawn hunted now in the majority of my matches it becomes less tasteful and feels like the meta gameplay is to camp loot locations from a hidden spot to kill someone.Since it's past the refund time I'm gonna try to play it some more and get my money's worth but if it keeps up and turns to the majority of my starts being spawn hunts and such I don't see myself staying around.**Edit**Yeah it proceeded the same. after about 10 or so more matches, longest matches are about 15 minutes and I only got 1 of those in about 90 more minutes of gameplay, it was mostly load in and die in the first 5 minutes. Even if you aren't spawn revealed and hunted, spawns are close to each other and radar towers revealing everyone are frequent on the map. Sure you can spend crafting materials to bring a jammer that you have to place and only jams a building sized area around it plus a little more to counter that, but it means little if you're pinged before you place it. Just feels like you either gotta sweat or not enjoy the game. Not sure why a grindy pvp extraction shooter on a small map would have personal UAVs.They've fixed some of the money grabby stuff they did back in console EA when I last quit playing (was free to play), but kept the ridiculous grind if you're not paying the premium currency to boost loot levels. If you get to escape that is. Sure you can complete weeklies to earn this and have a building that generates it (10 a day max level and one boost costs 30), but even at max level and completing it, you get about 6 or so boosts an entire week if you're hopping on every day?Matchmaking will be better when you can squad up with teams of 3, so you will be going against 3-8 enemy teams (solos can still join) and less likely to run into people rather than 11 enemies with a near guaranteed chance to clash even if not spawn revealed.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I break it down poetry style, tell you it's an AMAZING game ruined by lazy cheater bums.I cannot recommend this game in its current state, but as soon as they add a reliable anti-cheat, expect to see this review to be changed.Ah Vigor, how I loved you...In Norway's wilds, where shadows creep,Outlanders gather, their secrets run deep.With courage in their hearts, and eyes on the prize,In rugged terrains, bold destinies rise.The thrill of the chase, the pulse of the game,Now ruined by cheaters, the joy turned to shame.They twist a fair fight, with exploits so vile,Stealing Vigor's spirit, erasing my smile.From phantom opponents that vanish in thin air,To glitches that catch everyone so unaware,The quest for survival, so eager and bold,Can twist into chaos when the game's code won’t hold.Now that I've expressed myself enough, lets get down to brass tacks: I had origianlly played 166 hours of Vigor on Xbox One from roughly season 5 (September of 2020!) to about season 8, then just kinda got bored of the game and moved on. I moved to PC and tried Escape from Tarkov and other notable looter shooters but none of them quite scratch that itch that Vigor did for me. Once I saw it was free on PC I got excited to come back.I set my expectations too high, the nostalgia was too strongIt was just arcade enough to be a casual game session, but tactical enough where you had to pay attention or else it's back to the Shelter. I loved the progression of the Shelter, and I really appreciate the addition of the quick animation of your character upgrading the shelter once I could scrounge up enough resources. The guns feel so much better than they did 4 years ago! The game plays so much better and the controls feel so much more responsive.To sum it all up, I really wish this review could've been more upbeat and more appraisal of Vigor. As the game sits now, there is a lot of fun and cool gadgets to play with and guns to collect and master. Customization in this game is pretty cool too, but to be killed with a 1911 across the map instantly at the beginning of an encounter just to lose my gear is disheartening. To be shot through spawn's walls in the 5v5 Shootout is super lame, especially since you still can not leave those matches?! You're telling me I just have to sit there and take it for 5 rounds and then get emoted on? I am sorry but there are better games to spend my time on and that makes me sad for my younger self that loved this game in high school. I hope this review reaches someone and it makes any difference.Its a good game, it's just missing an anti-cheat.

_childDocuments_.review: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ (4/5)After 134 hours in , I can say that this game has truly captured my interest in a way few others have. It combines the thrill of survival with the excitement of multiplayer interactions, all set in a beautifully crafted post-apocalyptic Norway. Here’s why I find myself coming back for more:  offers a unique blend of PvPvE mechanics that keeps you on your toes. The tension of scavenging for supplies while avoiding or confronting other players creates a heart-pounding experience every time I drop into the world. The survival elements are well-implemented, and I love how every encounter can lead to both triumph and failure. Whether I’m sneaking around to loot an area or deciding whether to engage another player, every decision feels meaningful. One of my favorite aspects of  is the scavenging and crafting system. Collecting resources and crafting gear adds depth to the gameplay. The thrill of finding that rare item in a stash or successfully crafting a weapon keeps the loop engaging. I often find myself planning my next excursion, weighing the risks and rewards of different locations. Plus, the satisfaction of building and upgrading my shelter is a nice touch that keeps me invested in the game. The visuals in  are stunning, and the Norwegian landscapes are breathtaking. From snowy mountains to dense forests, each location feels immersive and alive. The art style captures the desolate beauty of a post-apocalyptic world, and I often find myself just taking a moment to appreciate the scenery. The sound design is equally impressive; every crack of a branch or distant gunshot adds to the atmosphere and tension. Playing with friends can be an absolute blast in . Teaming up to tackle objectives or defend against enemy players adds a layer of camaraderie that enhances the experience. However, I’ve had my fair share of frustrating encounters with solo players or teams that seem to take advantage of new players. While I appreciate the competitive aspect, it can be disheartening when you're just trying to enjoy the game. After 134 hours, I can confidently say that  has its ups and downs, but overall, it’s a solid survival game that keeps me coming back for more. The combination of scavenging, crafting, and intense player interactions creates an experience that is both thrilling and rewarding. _childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game since the Xbox Alpha days and I'm so happy they finally brought it to PC. The game (I would say) is very different than most extraction shooters and honestly gives me similar thrills as Escape From Tarkov without the time commitment. I do love the setting and world of Vigor as it's basically Winter Fallout set in the 80s-90s Norway.As new players I would recommend for you to just do your 3 games in "encounters" (raids), learn as much as you can about points of interest and the blue icons, maybe push them whenever it benefits you, and unlock the arena type modes to practise your aiming in TPP and FPP. A lot of people complaining that they don't understand how things work but haven't even completed the first 3 games.This is gonna be biased but I personally don't mind TPP games as I used to play titles like The Division and SW: Battlefront (classic) back in the day.Anyways,Its an extraction shooter where PVP is the main aspect and extracting with resources for your hideout and weapons is kinda secondary (at least imo). The game has pretty high skill gap in relations to map knowledge and weapon control. BTW there's a lot of weapons, and they all feel very different. You can practise with them at the shooting range once you bring em home at least once. The shooting range is super fun (imo).I would say the tutorial or "intro" games don't hold your hand at all and that's honestly a good thing imo as it lets you figure out the game yourself, feels a little more hardcore-ish and makes you take a more thoughtful approach to fights.Whether you wanna go in with just a pistol or knife and try score your luck on a "locked container" or go in with 2 primaries and try wipe lobby you can do that. But learn the maps before bringing, let's say, scoped weapons on a very bushy map.I would say the game is difficult at the beginning, as there are many things to learn, but you have to pay attention and know what your plan is when you get into a match of "encounters", as it can all go south VERY  quick.One thing I will say is a little clunky is menu navigation. While trying to equip gear, some functions are a little questionable but for me it hasn't been an issue, because of prior console experience. Learn how to navigate it and it wont be an issue, it's only a little different than what you would expect.Lot of people complaining about not understanding the game mechanics. If you just read what comes up on your screen when players perform world actions you might have a better chance. Learn the game before bombing reviews just because you don't "get it".The game is hard and you will come across POI (point of interest) campers and sometimes extract campers, but it honestly isn't THAT big of deal, as long as you play smart and not in an obvious way. It happens but it isn't as bad as, say Tarkov for example. It's an extraction shooter and they all play the same!You just have to be careful and know what you are doing and play it smart. There's many gadgets in the game that allow you to counter these type of players. But you have to learn the plays.Personally I would love to get my character/skins/progression from my Xbox account (((at least in the form of my cosmetics, as blueprints & gear would be a little unfair))) I put so much time and love into it on console, so personally feel this should be a feature in the game - having cross progression..Final point and my 2 cents are,Try the game, get a feel for it, play it like a hardcore extract shooter and you might enjoy it.I enjoy this game a lot but this can vary for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Bohemia's arcade, free-to-play, take on extraction shooter genre, running on Unreal Engine and with microtransactions. That kind of description seems rather wild, it sounds both like a great promise and a let-down. So, what's the deal with Vigor?Let's start with technical stuff - game runs on Unreal, instead of BI proprietary RV or Enfusion engines. For years some people in 'Hemia's community were saying that BI should ditch their own tech, and adopt one of the mainstream engines. Vigor does just that, and... it's not good. First off it just looks bad, I'm not sure if it's an issue with texture rendering, or maybe some post-processing that makes everything appear blurry. Performance seems fine for the most part, but then there are sudden, unexplainable drops that just kill your frames.The big issue is that the number of available graphical settings is close to nil, and... none seem to work. Changing frame cap, V-sync, few available post-process settings had no impact on what's on the screen, and how it's being rendered. It's a yuge warning sign tbh, ngl - that screams "non-competent developers". Oh, it's a console port too, so UI sucks when using a mouse, and there's more controller settings than keyboard & mouse ones (at least we can change keybinds, although I couldn't unbind some of the redundant options).As for gameplay: well, it sucks too. First off it's a third person shooter, which is both unrealistic help and hindrance. When camping corners, your third-person camera can see what's behind the obstacle even if it should completely block your vision. But on the other hand, when strafing your character gets in front of your crosshair, blocking your view of targets. When walking through foliage, branches of trees behind you will get between camera and character, again blocking your frontal view. You can switch to a proper aim-down-sight view, but it doesn't really work when moving.Speaking of movement - it's atrocious too. Well, it's a recent console port, so the whole anim set is made with controllers in mind, and mouse & keyboard somehow feel less precise than they should be. But that's not the worst thing. Neither is the fact that some of the moves feel awfully slow when compared to the rest of the game - especially walking in high ready feels too slow, and doesn't fit the pace of the game. But the thing which sucks is how our movement can be blocked by seemingly minor objects: stones, tree stumps, crates. Even though our character walks easily over way larger obstacles, he will stop dead when encountering some of the small clutter. And since it's third person game, you often won't see the thing that blocked you - as your character blocks the vision.Then there's gameplay itself, which is meant to be an arcade, "accessible" take on Tarkov experience. It just doesn't work. Everything is made to lower the time-to-kill: the maps are rather small, you can use various gadgets to find the enemies, round time is around 15 minutes (with radiation killing everyone too slow to extract), and when collecting goodies you become visible to everyone. In essence it discourages any tactics aside from camping and waiting for the sucker who got the drop first. Which is what every extraction shooter often devolves to, but here there's really no other way to play - last man standing is the one who wins. Well, unless you somehow won the spawn game, and are the closest guy to both the drop and the extraction point. Speaking of spawns - some are so dumb I wonder how they left the beta phase, especially the ones on shores/beaches, where you're visible from everywhere and often there's another guy 50 meters from you.So, if there's such a big emphasis on the "kill" part, how's the gunplay? Bad - there's really no difference in handling between various firearms, and I'm not just talking about difference among one type of them (eg. assault rifles). Your SMG handles as well as Mosin-Nagant, well, unless the gun is equipped with red-dot, or scope, then it gets awful sway comparable to having both arms broken in ACE mod for Arma 3. This makes iron-sights more accurate than scoped guns. Also, since game doesn't have trader mechanism, there's no sure (repetable) way to get guns, aside from buying blueprints in game shop for premium currency. Now you can earn that currency while playing, but the rate is painfully slow.Add to that problems with netcode (game uses P2P connection, and there's no regional matchmaking, so you're often fight against guys from the other side of the world with huge ping), reports about cheaters, and various other issues I'm too lazy to write... yeah, Vigor's bad man. And with the third person, arcade aspect, which clashes with the idea of extraction shooter, it could never be good, technical problems aside. Makes you wonder why it was even made in first place.Go check it out, it's free, but think of it rather as an entertaining train-wreck, than a good game. If you want a good extraction shooter - buy one, I don't think there's a good free alternative to Tarkov, Grey Zone Warfare or Hunt: Showdown. If you're just looking for fun, free-to-play shooter, well, Warframe is out there, what you're waiting for?

_childDocuments_.review: Pros-Free game-Variety of maps-3 different gamemodes at the time of this review-Variety of guns-No pay to win-Able to earn paid currency from normal play-Low entry specs, anyone can play-Lots of cosmetics, some a bit too good for camouflage but nothing too serious (No full dark hide in a corner type cometic)-Fun extra challenges at base, 5 per unlocked weapon-Decent base upgrading, making it rewarding for wanting to upgrade fast so you can get a lot of the materials passively-Lighting is not overwhelming, you can see clearly even when inside buildings and tunnels and you do not get flashbanged by the sun when outsideCons-Camping is more rewarding than travelling looking for fights-No PvE element to the game-Third person allows corner camping-Headshot from any range with almost every weapon results in instant death-No armor mechanic to allow you to survive gunfights-Game was made for console, this is just a PC port. A lot of the console mechanics are still present in game-Sound quality is awful. Gunfire can be heard from afar but someone full sprinting 10 meters from you is totally silent-No silent step without being aimed down sights and crouching. Unless you like proning everywhere-You do not feel rewarded for looting. Its just icons that go into your imaginary deposit when you return to base-Game rewards players that loot little to nothing and coward straight into one of the many open exit points around the map, given there is no mechanic that makes player need to wait before extracting-Graphics at high definition make everything look blurry from afar, lowering only worsens-No FOV slider. You feel trapped with your character filling half your screen when you aim down sights in third person-Switching from third person aiming to first person changes where you are aiming. Your reticule and your actual iron sights differ in position-Some bugs that were reported a couple years ago on console are still present in the PC release (Specially in missions)-Randomly spawned in the map, you could have a player spawned behind you or to the side, you run into a lootable area and all the sudden you are dead (For this, I tend to wait where I spawned and check my periferals, its just an hassle)-Time to actually enter the match is too big. It first waits for all players to load and then makes a ready check that takes quite a bit of time, specially if 1 person does not ready upGiven all this, I will probably continue to play the game. Even with all the bads, it is still fun. Playing in lone wolf mode (You fight against groups as a solo) makes leveling really fast and if you can get the drop on a group, you can kill them all (3x-4x headshots cleans them up). The base expanding is a rather fun mechanic that I did not expect to enjoy. The more you expand, the easier the game becomes. Technically, you are able to build every weapon with only parts when you get the blueprint for it so its just a grind until you can enter a match with any weapon you want. I would love to see an armor mechanic added to the game. The one shot headshot is a silly mechanic for 2024, specially given how randomly sprayed some weapons can get. Ayway, check out the game, you will find other positive aspects and other negative ones, you are not forced to play extraction, you can get most of the loot playing the side gamemodes trough crates. Have fun

Negatives- Feels and plays like a mobile game, if someone showed me this and said its the "new PUBG Mobile" I wouldn't lift an eyebrow.- The sensitivity is really weird on mouse and keyboard, and i can't figure out what. No matter how much fidgeting in the setting makes the weird feeling go away.- Menu sound design is awful, just slowly dragging the soundbar makes a horrible noise, and dragging the mouse over things also makes an annoying sound. - Going against trios while playing duos is so strange when they have the "lone wolf" thing, going 1 v 2 bu choice is fine, but not knowing if you'll go 2 v 2 or 2 v 3 is not okay.- Character movements are clanky and unresponsive. As said before, it feels like a mobile game.- Can't craft ammo for the guns i have. Thoughts I've had multiple times: "Oh i will bring this gun, never mind i don't have the ammo and i can't craft it, guess I'll grab the Thompson"- Sub-mid audio. Sometimes the footsteps are really loud, sometimes i cannot hear a thing. Guns from afar sounds nice, but when shooting them, it sounds like "pistol-sound.mp3" aka your average free gun audio.- Can't drop items to squad members (sorry team i pressed F instead of Space, no ammo for you)Neutrals/ You don't have to enter a match with good loot to get kills, although if you don't get a head shot you might as well run if the enemy has a real weapon. _childDocuments_.review: Note: While I am a Bohemia Interactive developer, I was not and still am not in any way involved in Vigor's development, the dev team is even based in a different city. I received the game as an employee benefit.I used to play Vigor on my Switch, but since I've never been any good with gamepads, I stopped playing after a month or two and was hoping we'd one day see a PC port. You have no idea how thrilled I was when the PC port was announced.The game is based in post-war Norway where you play a survivor (called Outlander) trying to manage their shelter and go into encounters for resources used to upgrade said shelter. The game contains several very nicely designed maps (after all, BI games are known for great environmental design) where your goal is to find as much loot as you can and get out alive before someone (or radiation) kills you. Before every encounter, you stock up on guns and tools in your shelter (which you need to craft first), then wait several minutes before it finds a server and then the fun starts. You and around 10 other players are placed in the encounter and it's up to you how it ends. You can play it safe, loot houses, cars, farmsteads and other locations and then make a run for your shelter, play it moderately safe by carefully looting special locations such as locked safes, or you can go all in, engage in nerve-wrecking shootouts with other outlanders, grab the airdrop and get the hell out of there. What makes it absolutely intense for me is the fact that unless you spend hard currency for insurance before every match, if you die, you lose everything that you found in the match and everything that you brought with you. It makes you think twice about your next moves, because you don't want to lose your epic weapon that you were gathering parts for in your previous encounters to a dude with a Thompson, just because you were careless.There are two other modes - Shootout (classic deathmatch where you don't use your hard-earned equipment - you don't lose anything) and Elimination (which is - as far as I understand, I've never played that mode - team deathmatch). These two are harder to get in, though, because the majority of player base plays classic encounters. The deathmatch is okay, I play it to improve my aim. I almost always die by getting shot in the back and only rarely see other players in front of me. While the classic encounters give me very pleasant adrenaline rushes, the deathmatch gives me unpleasant rage rushes. :D

The good;I enjoy grinding and building a base. I find it rewarding. I enjoy building a stash of loot. I enjoy doing quick runs. The guns themselves feel decent with a good selection to pick from. Loot comes second as a result, which completely voids any other method of playing. The terrain is awful with ankle high rocks and twigs stopping you dead in your track. The sound engine is some of the worst I have ever encountered with audio traveling through mountains. DLC that costs a grand total of ~$800 when the game is just released.. Very small rotation of maps and multiple of them are clearly designed around fighting as the primary thing to do while only a few serve as decent looting where it is possible to get to without guaranteeing death.It's a damn shame. The game is pretty. When your character is not being blocked by pebbles and twigs it feels smooth to move. _childDocuments_.review: Vigor is like the fruit of all the things Bohemia Interactive has been experimenting with throughout the years. Arma, Dayz, as if all of these games were meant to be practices to finally set the mind on a game that can reflect what the developer is really good with. Sure, the game has issues, bugs, matchmaking errors, UI needs some work... but all in all, Vigor is a fun game! I have been playing for a few hours, I know it's not much, but many extraction shooters I tried got me bored after half an hour. Vigor doesn't. It keeps me motivated to go on, try again, build my base, try new tactics, try the game modes, challenge myself on the field. Motivation, is what Vigor has, which I miss from many games nowadays. Graphics doesn't matter usually for me, but the game looks good, in my opinion. Very nice decision to put the fight on the norway mountains. Also, I love how active the developers are. Communication, addressing of issues and problems, listening to advices, implementing some suggestions into their game. Nowadays, as corporations tend to kick the players in the teeth, it's refreshing to see a team dedicated to provide. An other thing I like, is that Vigor has a casual touch. Extraction shooter is a genre I like, but I am really bad at them, since they require relentless determination, focus, tactics, precision, and what not. They were meant for the competitive gamers. But Vigor offers a few ways to be played comfortable for casual players as well, which is, for a player like me, is a huge plus!I can only recommend Vigor for the fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Vigor is an absolute gem in the realm of competitive gaming! From the moment I jumped into the action, I was hooked. The game brilliantly blends survival elements with strategic gameplay, creating an exhilarating experience that keeps you on your toes. The PvPvE mechanics ensure that every match feels fresh and unpredictable. The thrill of competing against other players while also facing environmental challenges adds layers of suspense and excitement. I love how the stakes are high with every decision you make—choosing whether to fight for that precious loot or to stealthily evade enemies keeps my heart racing!The graphics are stunning, and the sound design immerses you in the game's atmosphere, making every encounter feel intense and real. The variety of weapons and customization options allows for a personalized approach to combat, catering to different playstyles and strategies.What truly sets Vigor apart is the sense of community fostered within the game. The competitive nature encourages teamwork, yet the thrill of solo play can’t be overlooked. Each match feels like a mini-adventure where you’re constantly challenged, and victory feels all the more rewarding.Overall, Vigor delivers a perfect mix of competition and excitement that keeps me coming back for more. If you're looking for a game that will challenge your skills and provide an adrenaline-pumping experience, I can't recommend Vigor highly enough!

_childDocuments_.review: Vigor, initially a console game, has a smooth look, satisfying visuals, and immersive world-building. The sound design is excellent, allowing directional tracking with a headset. Gunplay feels satisfying with minimal lag. Downsides include the 3rd person free camera, which allows unfair peeking, and occasional instances of players getting headshots with hip-fired machine guns. The game offers multiple modes like PVP Extraction, Team Deathmatch, and Free for All. It's currently in Early Access on PC but will become free-to-play soon. Despite some issues, the captivating world, realistic gunplay, and responsive movements make it worth trying. However, the Early Access model provides excessive in-game currency, undermining the real experience."

_childDocuments_.review: Xbox Veteran who bought the Founders Edition back then. This review was originally positive but these developers are a joke.Gameplay is unique but rife with QoL and gameplay issues. Camping extracts and airdrops is super common and on some maps there is little to no counter to extract camping as only one extract is open out of the gate, the others requiring materials that are oftentimes hard to find.A lot of competitiveness and strategy is destroyed by people being able to just look around corners in 3rd person while being invisible. I've been killed and killed people using this, it feels unfair when you do it and feels unfair when you are killed by it because it honestly is. People have requested a first person only mode ever since this game came out on PC, and they never listened even though the game would've been wildly more successful if they did so.Airdrop and radiation system (combined with the aforementioned 3rd person cheesing) often forces you into long drawn out engagements, leading to nobody getting out with the airdrop and everyone losing all their gear because the fighting goes on so long there is no chance of escape from the radiation. This, or nobody goes for the airdrop because its viewed as too risky. There's a bunch of other gameplay issues and gun balancing issues but that's not what I am most mad about.Finally, I come to the treatment of the early access players. EA players got given 2500 of the premium currency to buy cosmetics, and access to the battlepasses.Come release, they wipe everything. Literally everything. Not just the guns or other gameplay items, they wipe cosmetics including the battlepass cosmetics people grinded for, and you can't get them back because they were a part of a battlepass that you can't get anymore even though you were there and grinded through it. One of the biggest reasons for buying early access? Gone. I wouldn't be so mad about this if it was a complete double standard. Xbox/Console players playing in unison with you get to keep all their cosmetics but you lose them for... paying to help test the game?Also, if you wanna re-buy the shop cosmetics that weren't in the battlepass, the closest equivalent currency pack you can buy (2700) is 50 dollars AND they increased the price of most of the cosmetics in the shop.Absolutely disappointing and sickening behavior. I was a major advocate for this game when most others were already writing it off. I feel like I can no longer trust these developers. They are clearly not ready for the PC Market. The Project Lead literally worked on ARMA 3, so how this was allowed to happen is an utter mystery to me.Do not buy this game unless you would like to be treated like dirt and have all your progress wiped as a paying customer, while people who played for free on consoles get to keep it. I have nothing against the console F2P players, but it's clearly unfair and a large double standard. Whoever on this team made these decisions should literally lose their job. Never purchasing another Bohemia game again until I see some redemption.
