_childDocuments_.review: Played about 10 games so far. It's not bad. I did come across a visual glitch when shooting someone on a ladder, it made them semi transparent and glitched their position all over the ladder and it then shot their corpse off of it. My only complaint so far is the interface is a bit clunky. Looting isn't an easy drop in drop out. You have to hold press on an item in your inventory to destroy it to make space for something else, which means you're just standing there waiting to swap loot and get shot. Comparing weapon damage in the loadout equip screen isn't easy, I haven't found a way to compare weapon stats between one equipped and one in the weapons list. I have to un-equip a weapon to compare stats on it. Same for weapons I find in the field, It'd be nice if an overlay showed up that showed +/- gains on something I'm hovering the mouse over vs equipped weapons. Definitely could use QoL improvements in that regards. All in all, it's been fun so far. Don't know how much longer it will be fun. Game time is very short, it could use a bump. Radiation spread is very fast and it comes out of nowhere after not that much time. So whatever you're doing, do it fast because there isn't much room to play around. It could use a few more gameplay dynamics, like stats to regulate such as hunger, more inline with tarkov but I think that'd only work if game time increased. Personally I'd like to see it lean more in that direction, just a little, and have it be a tarkov but without an overload of technical stuff while still having the feeling that there is a skill curve to master.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't give feedback on games, as most of the time no one cares anyway but I have a few minutes and I like the core idea of the game especially for someone like me who enjoys some solo survival like games. After playing for a while and extracting with the airdrop and opening crates etc. i realized (unfortunately) that if I don't buy "crowns" (in game currency that you'll probably be able to buy with real money) you'll never be able to catch up with someone who does.This is how it seemed to work (at least to my knowledge):You can earn crowns by playing the game and completing challenges also you'll get crowns through the daily login rewards (i don't think the amount is gonna be the same when the game launches  i got like 7k from these rewards which will be wiped i guess on release and then the numbers will most likely be a lot less)There is a pretty cool crafting system in place you find parts of weapons etc and if you got enough parts you can craft that weapon/tool whatever. There are bear trap parts to make a bear trap, pistolXY parts to craft pistolXY. But pistolXY part does only work for pistolXY so every weapon seems to have its own parts, even the bandage needs bandage parts, so very specific instead of like pistol parts for most pistols and medicine parts for bandages and pills, not a game breaking mechanic but also not really user friendly too many different parts to clutter up my inventory when I want to extract with loot.But if you have crowns there is an in game shop which lets you buy 'plans' for all weapons tools traps etc. When you have such a 'plan' you can craft without needing the parts but just 'Materials' which is much easier to come by and earn than the parts. You can generate 'Materials' via shelter upgrades passively even, that is nice. Downside of crafting with your 'Materials' instead of parts is the crafting is not instant (but can be made instant by using crowns) which is fine as its not a real advantage more a QoL, if i don't want to spend crowns aka money, I can start crafting a weapon play 1-2 games and it will be ready to pickup afterwards.The cost of these 'plans' ranged from like 50-900 crowns i think, depending on the rarity of the item and how powerful it is. There is a radio tower in your base that will generate 9 crowns a day on the lowest level if i remember correctly, also you'll need to login and collect them when the 'storage' is full so when on vacation you'll not have 100 crowns after 11 days just the 9 sitting there waiting to be collected. I can understand that decision somewhat but also feels a little bit strange to me could at least store like 5 days worth of crowns in the tower before it starts sleeping.Now to the point I actually wanted to make, you'll never be able to catch up with someone in the game if you don't spend money aka crowns. If you don't want to buy crowns you'll be at a huuuuge disadvantage unless you are really good at the game and kill everyone with cheap weapons, which is definitely possible but its gonna be tough especially when you get paired with more skilled people as you progress.So how can you get plans without spending money? Its random unfortunately. Some crates you open have a chance to drop you a plan, which is fine but either they disabled the drops of plans or the chance is just really low or I was really unlucky, i did not have a single plan in any of my crates and I opened quite a few. In all my playtime (not that much I know) I never got a plan not even the cheap ones for bandages and I did not have any more bandage parts left so I could not take bandage with me on my missions, the only option I had was to buy the plan so i can craft them or go into the encounter without a bandage which will reduce my chances of survival and extracting the airdrop to get a plan eventually.Now about the mechanics that lets you boost a lobby to get alot more rare loot and/or better airdrop loot, before an encounter starts you can boost either the loot found in the world and/or boos the airdrop itself with crowns, every person in the lobby can boost up to X amount depending on the size of the lobby to improve loot up to 700% or something.And there is a third option, called insurance for 60 crowns you can get in the encounter and youll not loose anything in your inventory except if you had the airdrop. So basically you pay for the safety to be reckless. You dont need to buy the insurance but youll play different if you know you cant loose ♥♥♥♥, but at the same time I dont want to pay real money to save virtual items from theft so i wont use it but will give people with access to more money an advantage. (Like in real life :D)TLDR: Buy crowns with money to progress like 10x faster and build+craft instantly or grind for a really long long time to maybe get the plans for the weapons you like playing or grind even more for crowns to buy a plan.Overall I like the idea and core mechanic of the game also the changing maps and weather, its quite simple and does not have a steep learning curve while still managing to be fun when fighting for an airdrop.I personally would add First-Person as a hardcore mode or something so you cant check corners with the invisible camera above your player model in third person view.Correct me if im wrong on how the crown system works.Thanks and bye

_childDocuments_.review: The game has been around for a while on the Xbox and there is a good reason for that. Finally it's coming to PC.People are salty that the Early Access is not free which is fair enough but for the price you are getting a tonne of gear and more than enough credits to buy a load of cosmetics as well as the season pass. I played this game for years without spending a penny on the Xbox and Switch so really i have no issue with this right now. It also thins out the crowds a bit at launch which i can imagine helps them sort out the servers. It's fair enough but if it bothers you just wait for the popper launch. Personally i don't mind getting in early and grinding out the battlepass that comes with the entry fee.It's one of the earlier Extraction Shooters that came out but offers a far more varied experience than Tarkov. What this means is that you don't always have to go in guns blazing and raise your blood pressure. You can do plenty of resource runs where you go in to gather what you need and then exfil without even engaging an enemy. I've done runs with no weapons and just stocked up on resources for my home base.  Other times i've snuck around out of sight stalking other players and then picking them off when they aren't expecting it.You can play this in a variety of different ways and each feels rewarding.The game does encourage stealth and camping to a degree, especially nearer to the early game when there are more enemy players but the game doesn't force you to engage. There are certain items on the map you can use to locate others or encite a duel but even when someone tracks your location it's brief and you can usually hide or evade..... or better yet.... wait and ambush them.Best moment so far was where some guy in the pre-game lobby boosted the air drop crate a whole bunch of times. I rested up near the zone and then watched a whole bunch of people having a shootout around the zone.  I picked off one or two enemies in the chaos completely undetected and then made off with a really good haul.There are some great moments of tension when you are outgunned and hiding in the dirt hoping the enemy doesn't spot you. Or when you enter a house and realise you aren't alone. I'm not a massive PVP player but i always appreciated how this game respects that and allows you to feel the tension of an extraction shooter without forcing you into combat and giving you ways to avoid it.

_childDocuments_.review: I would leave a neutral review but it won’t let me, chose positive because it is a game I continue to play.With that being said, this game needs MAJOR work. For those who say the game is Pay-2-Win, it’s because they are not doing their challenges, with that said, you can use in game currency (crowns) to swap seasonal challenges in order to find challenges that aren’t impossible but DO NOT do this, it’s not worth it in the long run. The main reason people try to complete all 50 seasonal challenges is for the SPECIAL SEASONAL REWARDS which are never worth it, it literally just gives you gold clothes for months of work, special seasonal rewards are not worth chasing AT ALL! So NEVER spend crowns on seasonal challenge swaps.Also the fact that you can open 300 gold supply crates and not receive one single crafting plan is INSANE!And lastly you have the CHEATERS, who are more obvious about cheating than any other game. They literally teleport to everyone and or insta kill the whole map in under one second. It also sucks with matchmaking, every round you have to re invite your team and if you take too long to start you all have to close game and re invite, then if you do start it and it looks for a match for too long then it puts the whole team in different matches away from each other. And if all this works out you have a high chance of something else going wrong or having a UE4 crash. The game just needs so much work but I don't think the devs care.Another small issue is how you get daily login rewards but it only lasts for 10 days, after 10 days in a row you never get another reward, this is just odd and dumb imo.Conclusion - The game is fun and is a great idea for a game, so as long as you don’t spend money on crowns (at least for seasonal challenges) and as long as you don’t mind cheaters, and as long as you don’t mind being annoyed by every grind feeling like a waste of time then this game is for you! I personally still play but I no longer try to do all seasonal challenges, I laugh at the cheating, and I no longer buy crown or try to unlock crafting plans, I just spawn in to shoot and loot. Hopefully game gets fixed or I’ll have to find another game.

_childDocuments_.review: I did NOT purchase cosmetics for this game before it was released as F2P so I do NOT have a negative bias towards it. The only thing I knew about this game prior to downloading: Bohemia's name is on it & my little brother used to play it occasionally on his console.I am not sure where any other negativity for this game is coming from as the rest of my experience has been pleasant.There are clearly some elements of the game that were designed with controller-players in mind, but that doesn't really take away from the experience.I have encountered 1 cheater. It was very blatant.Progress doesn't seem slow at all & the acquisition of "loot" is primarily for your crafting.There is no flea market economy in this game so, like the Native Americans, you use every piece of loot you pull out of each raid. I feel this system has inherently combated alot of RMT stuff you see in other extraction-shooters.The shooting challenges are also fun, but the difficulty still has controller players in mind.All in all: Very approachable extraction shooter experience. There isn't tons of convoluted systems to learn. The raids are rather quick. There isn't much to it; which isn't a bad thing. 144fps on Ultra, no hangups or hitches.This game is very chill in my opinion.EDIT: After playing for a bit and looking through all of the cosmetics for the game, I can understand why players were upset. There are tons of options for clothing and the pricing is a bit steep. I have played a fair amount of games now and only have enough "CROWNS" to unlock a default backpack. I can insure 1 kit. If you were to unlock every cosmetic item in the game it would be thousands and thousands of dollars.Bohemia should remedy this situation or I feel it will assist in the death of this title.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, So I've played this game since it was on the Xbox, played it on switch, PS4 and finally PC.Bought a pack on every platform I think.I've come and gone, missing the odd season here and there and its given me a real worrying perspective on the game development and possibly showing a trend with Bohemia.When I first played on Xbox it was a joy, my only complaint, wishing I could use my keyboard and mouse instead of controller but understanding why it wasn't implemented.Sure I had a higher Ping than I was used to, often above 200 but it was still extremely playable.The ability to generate premium currency over time was really cool and I enjoyed the business of upgrading my shelter.Sure you could crash if you tried crafting things to fast.Sure you could vault a railing and find yourself flung forwards and trapped in place.It was early days, those issues could be easily overlooked and were not incredibly common.Once I started playing it on the switch I hated using my tiny screen and played mostly on the dock.Other than that I was still really happy.The Loot Tables for the crates were still there, ensuring no doubles and a reasonable progression on blueprints.Still crashed you when trying to craft too fast.Still got you stuck vaulting a railing on rare occasions.Then I started dabbling on PS4.I didn't play too much as I was working but did get a few games in.See above for the switch minus the tiny screen issues.Now its come to PC (Hurrah!) and god am I seriously disappointed.The rates of premium currency gain seemed to have been squashed, providing much better gains early on in the antenna's leveling but seems to provide less late game by a solid margin.The worst ping I've dealt with so far, averaging 340-400 and rarely coming in at 240 Ping.Never 200<.Even considering the Ping, huge amounts of bullet reg issues.I can watch blood fountaining from 6-7 hits or try and slightly lead my target barely to make up for the latency and seeing at the end of the fight, I'm dead andthe game registered 1 hit.The Loot tables for crates are gone, just gone.I have never opened so many valuable crates by quantity and not received 2-3 blueprints.I currently have one.That Railing error that kills good runs is still there after 3 different platform ports..And why would that be Bohemia?It couldn't possibly be related to how you put them in the store for premium currency and made them fairly costly?Yes Bohemia, you can argue that it doesn't make it pay-to-win because you can buy them without spending a cent, That until you harvest enough materials to upgrade your workbench (more on this coming...) to the right level you cannot use the blueprints anyway.However I did notice another interesting thing in this current design of Vigor.You can now buy tickets to double the resources you extract at the end of the encounter,1 ticket at roughly 29.5 currency per ticket with the bundle of 2 will double your loot for one encounter, *IF* you escape successfully.Unlike other tickets such as the Increase loot tickets this only impacts the individual and is not a boon to every player in that match which otherwise would negating the personal Pay-to-Win advantage that could be seen.As it is I could not recommend spending money on Vigor.What was unique and made Vigor a more 'Value for Time spent' game in the looter shooter space has been eroded gradually in its development to a point where, despite having the energy for leveling my shelter through 3 other platforms I'm finding I'm missing the same drive here as I've come to discover the changes.Thankfully the game is free so I'd still suggest folks give it a shot, maybe with enough players the server problems as I experience them will resolve themselves but recommend is too strong a word by far.Its an enjoyable looter shooter despite its current flaws but the pattern in development does not give me strong hopes for its longevity at present.

_childDocuments_.review: i really like this game, its like short form dayz but without the jank and better shooting mechanics. the shelter aspect is addictive and a strong driving force to continue playing encounters. the maps are great and have at least doubled in quantity since the games console days. i wish the game had cross progression and i miss having the ability to walk but at least you can still do so with a controller which is a shame because walking can be a tactical advantage in some situations but the mouse will outshoot the controller everytime. that being said, ive put in close to 200 hours of playtime and have only manged to kill 9 people in encounters. i will admit shooting games arent exactly my favorite and i dont play them often but im not that bad overall, so i started spectating the people that kill me and ive found a surprising amount of people are in fact hacking. ive seen aimbot, teleporting, and walking through doors without opening them. its a pretty terrible feeling. ive tried the shootout mode but nearly every match ends with one guy on top with 20 or so kills and every one else has 1 maybe 2 kills. is everyone that bad or is this another example of hacking? the argument for the necessity of ranked matchmaking could go here. my next issue is the lack of proximity chat. i dont even think i need to explain how good that would be for a game like this. also there arent nearly enough gestures available to even begin to try to substitute the absence of proximty chat. the team up feature is really lacking as well. you cant visit eachothers shelters at all, thats a big let down. during a match you cant even drop a weapon for your friend or put it back in a box for them to grab themselves, once an item goes to your inventory you keep it or destroy thats it. im glad this game is free but surprised it was in early access as long as it was without any major changes, the gun overhaul is pretty unnoticeable to me. the game has a lot of potential and i will continue to play but unless the devs start rolling out meaningful updates quickly my interest is starting to decline.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is full of cheaters/modders so its impossible to progress. In encounters i got destroyed from other ends of the map through walls and behind hard cover. In the 5v5 game mode Elimination same issue you just spawn and lose. Played the game on console for years now and i must say the PC version is a let down due to these people having access to cheats so i highly encourage playing or even trying it on consoles with friends.General Feedback The game itself is great, progression takes time. Upgrading your shelter does give you a sense of achievement every tier you unlock with the materials you gather through out. Unlocking blueprints for weapons and consumables is something you'll always be chasing but the more you play and the more improved you become the easier it becomes. For character customisation you can either pay $$$ or unlock items from crates which you earn or unlock with season pass progression. some good some questionable its all personal taste. There is always someone better but the game is 80% luck as you can be the best but lose to that unlucky head shot which is an insta kill.  Some of the weapons are busted in the right hands and some weapons are just straight up spray and pray. The maps are very unique and great to learn when released. (Only one map has two styles) but otherwise they all vary. I have my favourites. The whole game is based on survival so some people will hide games and some run around looking to eliminate all players. Play it smart essentially, the more you play the quicker you figure out what type of opponents you have in lobbies. I wouldn't say there are try hards but there is some skilled players that have put time into the game. I'v been ganged up by teams of 3 sometimes winning and sometimes losing it just comes down to movement and luck honestly. You can play Encounters as Teams of 3 or Elimination teams of 5 and Shootout (Solo FFA). I'v had plenty of fun with friends and love playing solo in all game modes. Tips for new players;Don't corner campDon't crawl like a worm  (get spotted easily)If you hears crows as your approaching exits someone is nearby Save your high rarity weapons Play Shootout and Elimination for cratessometimes you do well sometimes you lose everythingalways have a back up plan Goodluck!Overall summary Console - 8/10 PC - dont bother

Besides that, the guns feel really good to shoot, the maps are GORGEOUS, the lore tidbits via cassettes and collectible items are incredible to me; Vigor has an atmosphere that no other game can really replicate, and I have had lots of fun with my friends so far. _childDocuments_.review: Has a lot of potential, but needs a lot of work too.-Balance the gun-play; the guns only feel like you need to account for the spread of the weapon, recoil & range is pretty non-existent.-Change the camera perspective so that I can look over my right shoulder as well, not just my left & center.-Fix the centers of the ADS function for the 1st & 3rd-person perspectives (1st-person ADS moves slightly off to the left of where you were initially centered when previously in 3rd-person).-Perhaps add a fog-of-war mechanic to the game to limit players' view when behind a wall or any other object to limit the annoyance of being 3rd-person peeked in almost every fight; fog-of-war being that players cannot see any moving objects in the game if their line-of-sight relative to their EYES is obstructed. Something similar to Project Zomboid's visual mechanic where the rest of the static world is still there, but anything that moves around in the environment would be 'invisible' to the player unless within their line-of-sight. (I'm tired of dying to 3rd-person corner peeking campers lol)Some improvements I would suggest would be to:-Allow early customization to the shelter, as it's the player's home & should reflect their personality a bit more; especially fun if players have other Outlanders come check out their personalized shelter.    -allowing players to further customize/personalize their shooting range would be amazing, including allowing them to create their own challenges for other players to attempt.-Clans could be added to the game, & a Clan Shelter could be an HQ for the clan members to meet up, hang out, or participate in clan events (raids, defenses, etc,).    -clans should have the ability to help one another out by donating items to each other. I guess if you wanted you could always monetize that option, only allowing VIP members to do it. I mean, it's a free game so the devs gotta make their money somehow, right?-Bigger or more expansive maps; I get tired of being killed so quickly after spawning in to someone who immediately ran over to my spawn. Doesn't always happen, but it happens often enough for me to feel the need to complain about it.    -maps don't need to be full of things, just put more distance between each player during spawn so we have the opportunity to gear up or run away (quick loot-n-extract) when we do empty-handed load-outs (since losing all of your guns in this game can happen pretty quickly).-Switching between 1st & 3rd-person (the game literally has this mechanic, but only for ADS in 1st-person).    -I'm already going to get cheesed by someone corner peeking in 3rd-person, so why no give me the option to see my demise coming in 1st-person?-Net code, but that's with most every game. Still though, I don't appreciate dying 2 seconds later when I've already gotten to cover. Feels... bad.Some things this game does pretty well:-Movement is actually pretty smooth in this game, albeit the only issue being the collisions with the world & objects (it's not too bad, doesn't affect game-play).-Aiming actually feels really nice in this game, despite not needing to ADS for most firefights. Particularly flicking is a fun aiming skill this game highlights (positioning is far more important).-Loot boxes actually give you some generally good loot, even some great loot. You also don't need to pay for these (though I'm sure you can), you can earn them from playing the different game-modes; easiest one to earn loot boxes in is Elimination (TDM).-Map design is pretty great too. Plenty of angles to hold, to get shot from, & to be paranoid of. -Decent tutorial.So, while I do like this game & would recommend it to others, it feels as if it needs a lot more polish before it becomes something great. It has the potential, though. Personally I think anyone should give it a try, all things considered it's free so no harm in it.

_childDocuments_.review: Vigor is more than just a game. It’s a story of survival, desperation, and fleeting hope set against the hauntingly beautiful landscapes of post-apocalyptic Norway. What makes it truly special is how it captures the raw essence of human nature when pushed to the edge.At its core, Vigor is a looter-shooter, but that description hardly does justice to the experience. It’s a game where every decision feels heavy, and every encounter with another player is filled with tension. Do you engage in a firefight, risking everything you’ve collected, or do you stay hidden, hoping the storm will pass? The weight of these choices sets Vigor apart. It’s not just about winning or losing but about surviving with purpose and consequence.

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade take on extraction looter shooter, where unfortunately low TTK and camping aggravate the experience.Third person camera also facilitates camping since you can peek without exposing yourself.You can use some premium currency to insure your loadout, then proceed with camping drops or extraction areas risk free, and even lay some traps to further improve your odds.This makes the whole situation camping situation worse and more rewarding, since it makes it even lower risk.Decent maps (a bit small and bloated with foliage at times, making camping situation worse), hideout upgrades give meaning to the grind, and streamlined looting that minimizes inventory management during gameplay.Also appreciated the multiple ways of detecting players in the map to avoid or pursue conflict.To have a better chance of looting and extracting, camp inside a bush - near some POI if you want to get 1-2 easy kills, then wait for the airplane to drop the crate. Doing this will make it so that at most you'll have to deal with 1 to 4 players in the lobby, improving your chances greatly.If you want to go full rat, extraction camping works as well as in ETF, just stay in a bush until someone tries to extract, kill, loot, and escape. Since the TTK is so low, the element of surprise wins 99.99% of the fights.Art, animations, UI/UX and SFX subpar and even terrible at times, but the performance is good.It's free but might as well pay for a better experience if you can, and there are more refined free options out there as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect in every way, shape, and form. The graphics are not only incredible in the visual execution, but also in their intended effect upon the player, the vague concept of the plot and surroundings leave plenty of room for imagination and also do not detract from the simplicity of the gameplay itself, and while being very excited about multiplayer capabilities in the near(?) future for this game, I am perfectly satisfied with the AI opponent that definitely keeps it interesting. Also, as someone who prefers games with more repetitive or similarly arranged levels at differing difficulties rather than storylines and long-term, evolving concepts in how the game is played, this is genuinely exactly what I want out of a video game.So, not only does this masterpiece align conceptually with a great many of my niche personal interests, it also has a flawless execution that, despite its simple gameplay idea, makes it stand apart from every other game I have put time into before. This was worth every cent of the 2.99USD I paid for it and more.Bravo, Klubnika. I hope to put many more hours into this game, and I will be informing everyone I know about Buckshot Roulette.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, and I cannot wait for it to grow as a game. This review is not negative it is just pointing out things that currently are in the game that I think could use tweaking. Much of the stuff I talk about this review will likely be fixed in the near future, as this game came out not even a week ago at the time of writing.First of all, I believe the dealer is inhumanly smart. The ai that the dealer has always makes the best decisions possible and always uses every single bit of info to its full potential. And I get that this is how the dealer should be as he's played this game of life and death his whole life, but I think that he's a little bit to good. In a game focused around risk, it would be more fun to see the dealer play a little bit more risky and even make mistakes here and there instead of always being perfect. On top of all this, it would also be good for the game because it introduces the idea of a hard mode, where the dealer gets better items, more health, and is always using all info to his advantage and always taking the best route.Another thing, i think for the double or nothing mode, specific items should be distributed with a higher chance depending on how many lives you and the dealer have and how many shells there are. Ex. if we start out with two HP and i get medicine and two beers while the dealer gets a knife, an inverse thingy, and a magnifying glass, I'm ♥♥♥♥♥♥. I believe its unfair that the dealer can just one shot you no matter what. There is a 100% I die even if I hit him with a live round. This could also be fixed by not allowing you to use specific items after other ones but I believe that's a bit of a stretch, I'm not quite sure how I would fix it but I know it needs to eventually get fixed one way or another.Also, WHY THE ♥♥♥♥ DOES THE GAME ALLOW YOU TO GET ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MEDICINE WHEN YOU START AT 2 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ HEALTH? ITS ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ USELESS! Lets say you get hit, if you eat your medicine, you have a 60% chance to die on the spot, if you do succeed, you only get one health so its just a worse cigarette. This could be fixed easily, let medicine over heal (only one heal over heal max) and reward the player for using medicine at one health (+3 health maybe?) In short, make dealer a little more dumb, don't give as many items in between rounds, make certain combos less strong, and buff medicine. Again, all of this is constructive criticism and all the goods outweigh the bads, just some things get very annoying after awhile. I know there are probably other issues I just can't think of any others at this moment, otherwise this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing and if you don't own it, buy it right now.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun for what it is. If you've heard about this game already it's probably because you saw someone playing it on Facebook or YouTube. It is exactly what it sounds like. You get a combination of blanks and live rounds that are loaded in a random order. You can point it at yourself to skip the dealer's next turn or point it at the dealer. It's an HP race to the death. In the first round, it's pure luck and probability. In the second round you get items that let you manipulate the odds. In the third round you get even more items. The problem with items is that you can use as many of them as you have and chain them together to great effect. So I can use the magnifying glass to see there's a live round, then saw off the barrel, then shoot the dealer. While the dealer can theoretically do this as well, the dealer is very bad at the game. He'll use items that reduce his odds, he'll make clear mathematical errors, etc etc. It's not a challenging game and when it's said and done the whole experience lasts about 20 minutes. It's fun and for $2.50 I can't complain, but I wish there was about 1/3 more content here... and that the dealer knew how to play.

_childDocuments_.review: To sum it up, I love it! The game revolves around you meeting up with the aptly named Dealer, signing your life away to a game of Russian Roulette with a 12 gauge, either winning around $70k, or dying. It provides a challenge that requires thinking, and The Dealer is really difficult, in a good way. The Dealer is an AI that is VERY smart, making good plays that you will fall into if you aren't paying attention (I'm learning this the hard way). I also like how he's characterized, with his expressive face and his alcoholic behaviors (always chugging a beer when he has one). However, sometimes it feels like The Dealer just knows what's next without any real incentive, which is my only real complaint, but I might get over it with time. In Double or Nothing, you really have to pay attention to The Dealer, as the Adrenaline can allow him to take anything you possess (typically really valuable tools).Next up, the items. The items provide a great addition to this game, as now not only does it require memorization, but it requires you to make the most out of the advantages you are given. In Double or Nothing, 4 items are in it that are exclusive to the game mode: The Inverter, Adrenaline, Expired Pills, and Phone. These items allow you to invert a round's properties, steal an opponent's item and use it immediately, gain 2 lives or lose one, and gain knowledge on a future round respectively.And now we get to Double or Nothing. Double or Nothing is a game mode where it plays out like any other round, however there are changes. Instead of getting items after the first round is complete, you get them immediately. Said items have many effects, as stated previously. After going through a game and earning money, you have a choice on whether to double your earnings through another 3 rounds, or keep those earnings for yourself. There is no limit to this, and provides a sort of endless mode.In short, it is a well crafted game with great mechanics, an advanced AI, and plenty of variety and content despite only having 2 game modes. I recommend you buy this game, as not only is it good, but it is a mere $3. And watch where you aim that gun. It could be your last shot...

_childDocuments_.review: "Buckshot Roulette" is a straightforward yet addictive game that puts a unique twist on the classic Russian roulette concept. You'll find yourself facing off against a dealer, armed with a shotgun and a heap of nerves, as you navigate the risky game of chance. What sets this game apart is its clever use of items, which allow you to bend the rules and manipulate your odds of survival.The game's atmosphere is spot-on, immersing you in the tension of the moment with every pull of the trigger. While the rules are easy to grasp and the controls are simple, they work seamlessly to keep you engaged in the high-stakes action.With the addition of the Double or Nothing feature and extra items, "Buckshot Roulette" offers plenty of replay value. You'll find yourself coming back time and time again, striving for that elusive big win and chasing down achievements along the way.That said, if you're not one for chasing high scores or completing achievements, you may find the gameplay a bit repetitive after a few rounds. However, given its affordable price point, this isn't a deal-breaker.In conclusion, while "Buckshot Roulette" may not offer endless hours of gameplay, its addictive nature and unique mechanics make it a worthwhile addition to any gaming library. Whether you're a thrill-seeker looking for a new challenge or simply enjoy testing your luck, this game is sure to deliver. Just keep an eye out for a good deal if you're on the fence.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing a mockup of this game in VRChat with a friend, I had to see the source material. I was blown away. I liked it so much I wrote this review to gush.A perfect game, like I'd classify Portal as a perfect game. Everything's there that needs to be there. The presentation AND execution are flawless. It doesn't outstay its welcome or try to be something it isn't. It does one thing really, really well.For $3? Go buy it. Then buy it again for a friend when it gets multiplayer.The gameplay, if you haven't heard of it, is simple but carries the game with ease.The dark and twisted atmosphere is so thick the 'cut through it with a knife' analogy doesn't work- it's as solid as stone.An excellent understanding of dramatic timing, and when to speed up, also keeps things tight- it understands the attention of the player and where attention needs to be.Despite playing for almost an hour it still feels intense. This absolutely scratches my itch of an atmospheric game.I especially like the strange 'items' that don't seem to perfectly relate to what they do mechanically, exactly how I'd expect an underground, life-or-death game to work. And the nice touch of the spent shells simply staying on the table... wonderful.

_childDocuments_.review: I wishlisted this game cause it looked interesting and then I saw it was only $3So I unwishlisted it and bought it immediately.There's a lot here for only $3!! It lands itself in a genre that I'm not quite sure even exists, which is weirdly cool. It's honestly hard to find words to describe the game as a whole. You and the Dealer take turns playing Russian Roulette with a 12-gauge shotgun, or, yknow, Buckshot Roulette instead. So each turn there's a predetermined amount of bullets, up to a maximum of 8. And those can be either live shots or blanks. You can see how many of each there are at the start of the turn, but the bullets are randomly slotted into each chamber. You also get a varying amount of health each round, from 2-4. You get a random amount of randomly selected items each turn. Turns go back and forth until you run out of shots in the chamber, at which point the shotgun is reloaded with a new random amount of bullets, and you get a new set of items. The round ends whenever someone runs out of health (ideally the Dealer!!! cuz if it's you ur just ded). There's a story mode which ends at the third round, or Double or Nothing which keeps going after every third round and resets back to round one. Until you cash out, or die.Despite what it seems like, there's actually a lot of strategy and decision making involved in your turns. It's not 100% RNG, though RNG does dictate quite a bit (mostly in terms of what items you get, and the order of the bullets). You have to plan ahead and think about how you're going to use your items, what items the Dealer has and how that's going to impact your gameplan, if they have Adrenaline and what they might steal from you, etc. THOUGH, sometimes the game will just decided "nah, screw you" and set you on a 2 health round and give the Dealer Magnifying Glass/Inverter/Handsaw though at which point it's just joever my friend ¯\_(ツ)_/¯Also not to mention the insanely cool and creepy and tense atmosphere. This lifeless dance club you've found yourself in. The grimy bathroom where you start. The music, the strange machinery, the smoking man, the Dealer. The waiver. The strange, creepy monitor that has some horrific pulsating Thing sticking out of the side. THE QUAALUDES.But boy, this game is intense!!!! Double or Nothing mode is insanely addictive. As you can probably tell from my hours played. Just don't go insane like I did chasing the two 1mil cheevos. Multiplayer is coming soon and I cannot wait for that. And remember, 99% of gamblers quit just before they make it big. u should b part of that 99% it's not worth it ok

_childDocuments_.review: Buckshot Roulette isn't just a game; it's a journey into the heart of the Wild West, where every decision could mean life or death. From the moment you step into this gritty, unforgiving world, you're thrown into a whirlwind of danger, strategy, and adrenaline-pumping action.The game's atmosphere is as thick as the smoke from a six-shooter, with stunning visuals and immersive sound design that transport you to a time when outlaws ruled the frontier. Whether you're riding through dusty plains or engaging in intense gunfights in the streets of a frontier town, every moment feels authentic and alive.But Buckshot Roulette isn't just about shooting your way through enemies. It's a game of strategy and survival, where every bullet counts and every decision can have consequences. Do you risk a daring bank robbery for a big payday, or do you play it safe and earn your keep through honest work? The choice is yours, but be prepared to face the consequences of your actions.One of the game's standout features is its dynamic world, where events unfold based on your choices and interactions with the characters you meet. Every NPC has their own story to tell, and your interactions with them can shape the course of the game in unexpected ways.Of course, it wouldn't be the Wild West without some intense shootouts, and Buckshot Roulette delivers in spades. Gunplay is fast-paced and satisfying, with a wide variety of weapons to choose from and plenty of opportunities to test your skills against bandits, lawmen, and rival outlaws.Overall, Buckshot Roulette is a thrilling ride through the untamed frontier, packed with action, strategy, and unforgettable moments. Whether you're a seasoned gunslinger or a newcomer to the genre, this is one Steam game that's sure to keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. Saddle up, partner, and get ready for the ride of your life.

_childDocuments_.review: What you'll get out of this game:A.  Memory Exercise.  How many rounds in the gun this time?  How many are live shells?   As the game progresses and you mentally tire, you'll find it easy to get distracted and lose track.  Memory plays big into deciding on your choices in tools.B.  Balanced attacks.  Experienced players have found the correct sequence of tool use to best counter the opponent's turns.  Do I attack this turn?  Do I reduce their healing instead?  Time to go sawed-off, or wait another round?  Learning and remembering the attack sequences and how to get the most out of your round  is amazing fun.C.  Unlimited repeat play.  You can go as far as your sanity and endurance will let you.D.  Classic pixel graphics add a sweet touch to the retro feel and dark mood.  SUGGESTIONS:  I'd change the German rave music in the dance hall to a revolving set of current royalty free bands.  Developers can change the mood with their music selections, and we'd get introduced to some new music before blowing the Clown's head to smithereens.Keep the pills.  They are irritating, but make you make tough choices.  Plus, I get a little thrill when the Clown pops a pill and loses a life.  DIE CLOWN DIE.  Ahem....sorry about that.

_childDocuments_.review: A good ol Russian roulette, I mean who doesn't like a eerie, dark game of gambling your life for money strategically. While I would've appreciated a story to such a unique and horrific game, I do realize that the developers main objective wasn't to make a story game. Comparing with Inscription, there definitely is potential to make an amazing story to the additional fun mechanics of the game. Either way I really enjoyed this game a lot. Can say with confidence I haven't seen anything like this before, so i'm happy to say for once in a while, this is indeed a unique and quirky game. The first layer to the onion is already a ton of fun and had me hooked from the start to continue playing. But I have to admit that the real fun began when I found out about double or nothing. The new items, higher stakes, & harder difficulty all blended into a delicious juice of excitement that definitely made me love the game more and be willing to trade in my limited time on this earth for the experience. I really love the choice to make it pixelated which adds horror to the already chilling atmosphere in the game. Overall I really dig the physiological horror aspect they were aiming for in this game. I do believe though this game would greatly benefit from adding a multiplayer feature, as seen commonly expressed in the reviews. I had a ton a fun with this game either way, and i'm sure over time, there will be more hours added to my record. This is a game I can confidently recommend to anyone to try out and know they'll enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I stare ahead as the dealer locks eyes with me. He gives a slight nod as he dumps the shells in the box on the table. "Ah yes" I think to myself, "8 bullets. 4 live. 4 blanks. 50% odds, I have first shot." I put the shotgun to my temple. *click*, the shot gun lets out a sigh of relief as the pressure hisses from the chamber, I stare forward eyes unblinking. I ♥♥♥♥ the gun, and a blank flies out."My turn again", I think to myself. I pop back a cold one with my boy (The dealer), and as he is distracted by my freakishly fast drinking of a cold Dos Equis, I recock the shotgun and watch as another blank flies out of the gun. I forcibly hulk smash a random magnifying glass as the shards go flying into his nose. As he picks out the glass shards, I decide to cheat and look at what shell is in the shot gun. I see a flash of red as I quickly pretend I never picked up the gun. I smile to myself as I pull out my Adam and Eve ^TM pink fuzzy handcuffs and tell the dealer to be a good ekitten and handcuff himself to the table. He obeys, as he always does. I pull out a small swiss army knife, and start to furiously saw the incredibly dull knife from Dollar Tree against the shotgun turning it into a sawed off shotgun. I proceed to pick the gun up and misclick shooting myself in the temple. I come back to life mysteriously as he calls me a slur and forcibly takes the gun from my hands.He then proceeds to do the most incredibly run of all time, chain smoking a cigarette and then popping expired Lexapro to get back down to one health. Forcibly handcuffing myself to the table, calling Dr Phil, chugging a Dos Equis, Inverting the shell, cutting the shotgun in half, and the grinning as he blows his brains out into the next game.10/10 would play.

_childDocuments_.review: Buckshot Roulette ReviewBuckshot Roulette is a thrilling, fast-paced game that lasts about 15-20 minutes, blending elements of classic Russian Roulette with the high-stakes gambling spirit of the Old West.What is Buckshot Roulette?In Buckshot Roulette, players face a virtual gun loaded with "buckshot" shells. Each turn involves a nerve-wracking decision: pull the trigger or pass the turn. The goal? Outlast your opponents without getting hit, creating an adrenaline-fueled atmosphere similar to Russian Roulette but with a twist of unpredictability due to the buckshot.Connections to Old West Roulette and Russian RouletteThe game channels the Old West vibe, where saloons were filled with games of chance. Buckshot Roulette captures this essence, focusing on luck and risk. Every decision carries weight, and the tension feels like a high-stakes showdown.The core mechanic takes inspiration from Russian Roulette, where players face a life-or-death situation. Buckshot Roulette offers a strategic twist without real danger, making it all about suspense and strategy.Who Will Enjoy Buckshot Roulette?Thrill-seekers: If you love adrenaline and risk, this game is for you. The mounting tension with every trigger pull will keep you engaged.Quick Decision-makers: Players who thrive on snap decisions in fast-paced games will appreciate the quick format.Gambling Fans: Those who enjoy casino-style games will resonate with its mix of strategy and chance.Social Gamers: It’s a fantastic choice for groups, allowing for bluffing and shared tension.ConclusionIn summary, Buckshot Roulette delivers a unique blend of chance, strategy, and suspense. _childDocuments_.review: (tl;dr, This game is fun, I recommend it)Well, this game graphics might not be that realistic, colorful, or clean, so don't expect it to be like that. Mike, the developer of this game is the expert of designing his video games to be industrial, rusty, dystopia like texture so the game will have aesthetic of unsettling feeling, and this game is not an exception. The design choice of this game graphics is something that I would say that it match the game, making this game graphics fairly good by aesthetic choice.Audio and soundtrack is also another thing that made me buy this game. Audio in this game are well crafted to match in-game objects/actions and industrial/rave soundtrack give a vibe of in the underground club's dance floor muffling outside the room which add very well into atmosphere of this game.This game is similar to Russian Roulette but with a shotgun and a choice to either shoot the dealer or players themselves. However, this game has unique gameplay of having items to use to have an edge over the opponents (for example: using handcuff to skip opponent turn, getting one more charge by smoking cigarette, add 1 extra damage with handsaw, etc), which making this game have a distinctive gameplay of strategic thinking and risk management over traditional Russian roulette game. You need to know first that this game, though have simple mechanic, but still have some challenge for player to carefully think before decide to shoot the shotgun. The dealer of this game can be describe as fair cheating, since it can used combination of item to make a sure shot of live rounds at player when it has a chance. However because what I describe about the dealer earlier, it can still blunder the well planned item using and shoot itself instead, which to the summary point of very well challenging difficulty, if the players themselves not messed up their plans.After Mike patch this game to have Double or Nothing mode, this game give so much more replayability for players to have more attempts of making high score and compete with friends in score ranking. More new items also introduced so the gameplay can be more fresh in Double or Nothing mode.You don't have to wait for discount! Just buy it full price since this game is cheap and affordable with its original price for this well crafted game (69 Thai Baht or 2.99 US dollars).From playing this game, I can say that Mike really put his love and care into making this game, making this one of his masterpieces that you can't missed. So overall, I would recommend to buy this game because of aesthetic choice of graphics, well made game audio, unique gameplay, challenging difficulty, and affordable price.

_childDocuments_.review: I can see why you'd enjoy this game, but personally, I just don't. Yeah, there's *some* ability to turn the odds in your favour, but there is way too much RNG around which items you get, when some of them are game-changing and some are either useless or even game-losing (the expired medicine in particular compounds this problem: there is no way it should take up an item slot).It's pretty mind-numbing for gameplay to have so many instances where you're essentially having to guess, where its only mode relies on you putting together long unbeaten streaks, especially when the dealer tends towards perfect play (sometimes bordering on the unbelievable) and it's possible for you to be totally screwed by items every single round.It's cheap, and that's to its credit: it's not pretending to be something it isn't. It's not a 'bad' game, it's well put-together and the art direction is really strong. But ultimately it's a simple concept without much depth to it and a tendency towards more moments of frustration than fun.

_childDocuments_.review: if youve ever wanted to play russian roulette, but the stakes of losing your real life are too high, or gambling doesnt give the same edge anymore, then buckshot roulette is perfect!let me start off by saying the atmosphere of buckshot roulette is amazing. you start in a dingy bathroom at a club, with a bottle of mysterious "double or nothing" pills on the counter (given that youve beat the dealer). upon leaving the bathroom and getting a view of the club below, you head into the dealer's room. the room is full of mysterious technology and the room is very dark (especially on the dealer's side). the dealer is something less than human, with black pits for eyes and a wide, toothy grin. the pixelated graphics add to this unsettling feeling, almost reminiscent of old horror games. sign your life away and get to shooting.unlike real russian roulette, buckshot roulette gives you second chances. if you die, youre resuscitated and back into the game. in the later stages of the game, youre given items than can increase your odds of survival, such as magnifying glasses (allowing you to see whats in the chamber), cigarettes (allowing you to regain a charge/health state), or other various items. upon winning, youre given a briefcase with your cash prize, and you can drive away to live another day. for such a low price, buckshot roulette is really well made and provides a great deal of entertainment

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game that I've purchased on itachi.io before it came out on steam. The game play is enjoyable and it is worth the purchase price. However I've been playing it recently and the recent item updates or balancing updates has made playing double or nothing to get the $1 million achievements almost impossible (I have achieved one of them) single rounds can take 10-15 minutes and when you're trying to get the achievement you need a streak of typically 18 rounds at minimum (if you get $31,250 - $62,500 first round) so for 18 rounds at 5-10 minutes each its 1.5-3 hours to get the achievement which is a massive commitment to a game where RNG is the major deciding factor not just skill or strategy which I would have no issue with but you can't "get good" with RNGAn example of bad RNG in the game is when you start a new round 2 lives each and 7 shells (3 live 4 blank) you're given a converter and smokes and expired medicine while the dealer is given a saw and phone and cuffs or something unbalanced like that, or bizarre RNG where you're given 2 saws and expired medicine while the dealer gets cuffs spy glass and adrenaline (not only is the dealers items unfairly advantaged but his ability to steal one of your doubled saws is annoying because you can't use saws twice in one turn so the dealer will steal your saw on his turn guaranteed)The biggest issues that keep people from completing the double or nothing challenges:1. First round score is based on time, not skill/item usage, so if you have 3 rounds with 3/4 lives each round you may as well restart the game because its going to take you 2-4 x the amount of time to win the first 3 rounds2. Bad RNG as I explained can kill a run at anytime even if you're on your second hour3. Dealer AI quirks, while overall I find the dealer AI fair, balanced and predictable sometimes I get suspicious that when it uses expired medicine it regenerates health a a higher success rate than the player (I experience a 30/70 heal/die rate while the dealer usually gets 60/40 or something similar which is why I never use it unless its a last resort EXCEPT THE DEALER WILL USE IT WHEN HE HAS 3/4 HEALTH ALREADY SO WHY DOES THE AI TAKE THAT RISK???) the dealer also gets suspiciously better when he uses the phone despite it only revealing one shells location but that might just be my imaginationThe online and campaign were enjoyable and a great value for the price, I just wish more balancing consideration is taken for the double or nothing game

_childDocuments_.review: normal review part: Game good, dynamic music godly, aesthetic great, animations are super stand out cool, and gameplay great. Only problems are nitpicks/accessibility.Autism rant/review part: I would have never expected it but this has become sort of a comfort game for me. I do this a lot with those simple yet effective indie games (Hotline Miami, SUPERHOT, Enter The Gungeon, Canabalt, sandtrix, to name a few.) If I don't know what else to play, I'm waiting on stuff, or even if I'm totally ready to hop in another game but I just want a little sort of appetizer first, I'll boot this one up. It's because of that that, I've come to think about this game a lot.and because I've been thinking about it a lot, I have a lot to say...actually important accessibility part: Can there be an option somewhere or maybe just an indicator in the environment to show the current load? I get that remembering how much of each shell type was present and which ones were fired is an important part of the game...but I am like on par with the blue fish in Finding Nemo that made Ellen Degenerous popular. As soon as those shells go into the tube, there is a 50% chance I will immediately forget the ratio and amount and the game will just be guessing from there on out. Again, something as simple as an indicator to show the initial load will help me, I don't need a huge handicap. Maybe the little flipping section of the table has just colored markers on it? They could be little checkers or something, that would still fit the aesthetic.nitpicks: Blanks don't click. A blank is a bullet/shell that doesn't fire a projectile, but still fires. Firing a blank at your chin would still nearly deafen, burn the skin, and/or kill you, depending on the amount of gunpowder inside. Kentucky ballistics actually has a video demonstrating this, and it is the first result I got when fact checking myself. In his video, a point blank (haha, very funny) shot with a halfshot 12 gauge blank blows open the ballistic dummy's skull. Obviously this isn't representative of all blanks, some might be significantly less forceful, but the point still remains that a blank is not a *click*. A blank is a big ol' boom, just like a regular.now, am I (a gigantic nerd) going to lambaste some game dev who has accomplished something super cool that I greatly enjoy for getting a detail wrong? No, of course not, but I would like to point out that the terms "Dummy" (a round made for training that is in no way reactive) or possibly "Dud" (A live round that has somehow not worked, possibly due to a defect in manufacturing) would be more accurate than blank.but thats all semantics, game is still great and you should play it if you haven't 9/10, would sign waiver again

_childDocuments_.review: A strategic game of Russian Roulette with a shotgun against an otherworldly opponent. Short but good atmosphere and use of items for different strategies and a recently added multiplayer mode.The match takes place over three rounds where both you and the "dealer" have an amount of health with you brought back when hit by blood transfusions or defibrillators. The first round has you both at three health where getting shot removes one, you are shown how many live and black rounds are being loaded into the shotgun and have to choose to fire at the dealer or yourself which will pass the dealers turn if you shoot a blank when aiming at yourself. Hitting the dealer or yourself with a live round gives them the next turn. Winning that first rounds moves you to the next segment where your life increases and items are added into the mix for both you and the dealer with them pulled randomly out of a box and set to your left and right side, able to be used at anytime during your turn. Items can range from healing items like cigarettes that give one life or expired medicine that can heal for two or damage you for one, handcuffs that prevent your opponent from acting by making them skip their next turn, adrenaline that lets you steal an item from your opponent if you use it right away, a knife that saws off the barrel of the gun making it do two damage for the next turn, and a variety of items to help you guess correctly if the shotgun has a live round or blank loaded. You can combine what you know about what was loaded into the gun and what was left with items that allow you to do things like remove the current shell, examine what is currently loaded, swap the type of shell currently loaded, or a phone call that tells you what is going to be loaded in the future.Some have mentioned the occasional issue with the dealer AI going through multiple items where they should know what is currently loaded before aiming the gun at their own head and shooting themself, but I thought that just added to the atmosphere and horror theme of the dealer. Completing the game once unlocks a double or nothing mode where you can enter into a new round to increase your final winnings.There's not a lot to the game but it has good atmosphere and style and the gameplay works well.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: Buckshot Roulette is a game I ultimately walked away from feeling very conflicted, once again making me wish that a middle-ground option was available on reviews.On one hand, the *very* small amount of time I spent with the game was fun; the aesthetic was pleasantly gritty, the tension was apt, and the Dealer has wonderfully sophisticated AI. _childDocuments_.review: The Dealer puffs smoke from a cigarette, leftover from the last bloody round. IT was simply enjoying the music pounding downstairs while IT waited for the next player.The moment of piece was ended with a loud bang. The new challenger walking through the newly kicked in door before sitting down.“Welcome! Welcome! Please, before we start, sign the waver…”IT handed the stranger a worn document with the signer device. He started looking through it. More carefully than most would.  As he read, IT started to study the stranger, something about this one seemed a little different.“So… what kind of player are you?”The stranger looks up from reading his contract, eyebrow raised. The Dealer just chuckles.“Sorry, Sorry. I just play this enough to see patterns in those who play. You see… there are only three kinds of people that come to my table. “The stranger stares at the thing across from him. IT is undeterred by the glare and continues.“The first kind is what I call the Gambler. Someone who has done all the math and thinks they know all the odds. Methodical, arrogant and so damn confident... right until they get their first mouth full of buckshot”The stranger turned his attention back to the form, but IT knew he was still listening.“The second is my favorite. The Thrill seeker. Someone who doesn’t really care about the money. just looking for the rush of putting a live gun in their mouth. Oh, they are so much fun… too bad they don’t last very long.”Three soft clicks could be heard being typed into the waver. The sound is almost drowned out by the music.“Then there are the broken. A person whose life is so messed up that they don’t care if they walk away from the table or not. If they win, great! The money will get them back on their feet. Lose? Then at least the pain is over.”IT leans onto the table.“What I find interesting is how it’s the Broken players that almost always come back for more rounds.”The waver is passed back to IT. The Dealer looks over the form before bursting into mad laughter.“So, tell me… God. What kind of player are you?”

_childDocuments_.review: Very addictive strategy game. Knowing your odds against the Dealer and utilizing your items while gambling whether both your memory and your luck are on your side is exhilarating and it feels incredibly rewarding when everything plays out in your favor. Highly recommend for anyone who's a fan of luck-based strategy where you have enough control to make informed decisions but are still playing off of a dice roll.With that said, the game doesn't come without a few flaws here and there. One of my biggest gripes is how the Dealer, regardless of stakes, will ALWAYS go for the most immediately successful outcome, wasting all of their items just to spite you. On one hand, it's really annoying that you're forced to do the same and waste all of your items because he will always use his own and steal your's. So there's no point in building up resources for later in the round since you might not get the opportunity to use them later. And if you get a ♥♥♥♥ hand and/or the Dealer gets a good hand, then you're just helplessly screwed. On the other hand, it makes it even more intense and exhilarating as it becomes a race to play every move you have or even eliminate potential options for the Dealer before the Dealer can do the same.Additionally, the main meat of the game "Double or Nothing" has to be re-enabled every run and you have to put in a name every time you restart. It would be much smoother and less monotonous if it simply restarted you at the table on round 1 every time you died. The game also loses a bit of replay value after you've beaten the 3-4 main achievements  as there are only 9 items available and no additional gamemodes. The game could easily have a bountiful amount of unique things to keep things engaging such as special unlockable challenging gamerules the player could enable to spice things up, more Dealers and arenas with different rules and behaviors, more items, maybe even locking some items until you've won/lost a certain amount of runs to create a sense of progression, etc to increase replayability. The upcoming multiplayer gamemode may alleviate this problem for awhile however.

_childDocuments_.review: ELDEN RING HOWLING STARFIST BUILD (LEVEL 150)A Dexterity Build that uses Fists to set Bleeding and to range down enemies with Beast's Roar.Class: AnyFlask Spread: Mostly HP some FPWeapon: Star Fist, Highland Axe & Frenzied Flame SealShield: NoneArmor: White Mask, and any other Armor that gives you lots of PoiseTalismans: Roar Medallion, Shard of Alexander, Lord of Blood's Exultation, Rotten Winged Sword InsigniaPrimary Stats: DexteritySecondary Stats: Vigor & EnduranceSkills: Beast's RoarSpells: Bloodflame BladeThe way this Build works is that you'll buff with Bloodflame Blade as necessary in order to add more Bleeding build up to your Star Fist, which you will be dual wielding. Attacking repeatedly will not only increase your Attack Power thanks to Rotten Winged Sword Insignia, but also because you will eventually trigger Hemorrhage, triggering White Mask and Lord of Blood's Exultation, further boosting Attack Power.Charged R2 attacks are very good with the Star Fist because they deal exceptional stance damage, and also count as two-hits, dealing incredible damage and building up Bleed faster than some other Fist R2s. Use them when you can.Beast's Roar is there to give you a ranged option. This is a Dexterity-based Ash of War, meaning you will want to change your Affinity to Keen on your Star Fist to get the most out of it. This Ash of War has tremendous range and decent damage, allowing you to shore up the weakest aspect of Fist Weapons, range. Use this when you can't get close enough to an enemy to be effective, or if it's just easier to range them down.

_childDocuments_.review: I  don't get the hype around this! Sure, it's cheap. But where's the fun?! It took me six tries to win the game. The first five matches I lost in the first round, with nothing to blame but randomness. Each try you have to walk back in the room, kicking in two doors on the way, watch the score board light up and the dealer reloading the same distribution of bullets. You pick one of two actions, based on whatever is more likely, and... pray to RNGesus. If you are lucky enough to make it to round two,  get added to the mix. I think there's 5-6 different ones – and while they allow you to mitigate the randomness at least a little bit, they don't change the fact that this still remains little more than a coin flip...

_childDocuments_.review: Buckshot Roulette is a thrilling strategy/luck based game revolving around a game of russian roulette but instead of a revolver it's a 12-gauge shotgun. With the goal of surviving and killing the dealer, you are tasked with memorizing a certain ratio of shotgun shells, with some being lives and some being blanks. As the bullets are loaded randomly, you must formulate a plan based on the ratio of the cartridges being used and by using various items wisely in order to ease your turn, whether that'd be cigarettes that give you an extra life, handcuffs which skip your opponent's turn, or even using a magnifying glass to check the current round is in the chamber. A great game for those who want to play a game about beating a challenge all the while beating the odds simultaneously.My only criticisms are that you cannot put the gun down once you click on it. You are forced to make the decision of either shooting the dealer or yourself when picking up the gun. The only other problem is that the dealer's AI can be a little repetitive/stupid at times. Seeing the dealer fire two blanks at himself and then kill himself with a live all in one go is pretty ridiculous when you consider the ratio of lives to blanks in some rounds.All in all, a fantastic experience! Not exactly horror, but definitely a thriller of sorts. Play this if you want your adrenaline pumping but still feel 100% in control of your actions as you narrowly escape death. 8.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Nice, weird aesthetics. Yet, the entire game is only a few screens.- The game has simple rules but it's fun. Drawing random tools from that box and moments of pure luck offer some dopamine doses.- Snappy, responsive controls and smooth animations.- Pretty good AI. Dealer plays smart enough.- Cool electronic music.The bad- It's too simplistic. It doesn't evolve, neither gets deeper. After a couple of hours its mechanics get repetitive and there's no point of playing more.- It gives you some in game clues to begin a search about its lore and meanings to multiple online sources and creator's previous games. Unfortunately there is no interactivity between the lore and the actual game and I find it too easy to just throw random abstract secrets here and there and let the players make all the assumptions and connect the dots.- Animations in between of each turn are a bit slow and boring.- Playing against a friend would be much more entertaining. Unfortunately, there is no online or couch pvp. A wasted opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: For 3 bucks it's maybe kinda cool but the best part of the game is its presentation. But that aspect is pretty heavily inspired by Inscryption, which pairs incredible presentation with fun gameplay. This game doesn't have the fun gameplay. There's a reason all the reviews are from people with 2 or 3 hours: it just doesn't have depth. _childDocuments_.review: This game just came out the same month as this review was posted, and it has all the elements of being a fantastic, small game. Atmosphere and music is really creepy, and always keep me on the edge of my seat. It's hard to describe but I always feel like I'm never really safe. Gameplay starts right away, and it makes russian roulette (with a shotgun) strategic and fun. It's always a great feeling when you feel like you've outsmarted or outplayed the dealer, or when he outplays you. While it is at it's core, a game of chance, it feels rewarding and the game greatly rewards strategic play and, of course, gambling.I'm very excited for when multiplayer comes to this game, and what these devs can cook up in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is short and sweet. You get what you paid for. But endless mode is for masochists only. _childDocuments_.review: A very fun and addicting roguelike that, while simple in it's mechanics and light in content, more than makes up for it in the quality and replayability of what it offers. The base game can be completed in under 30 minutes, yet the atmosphere and world it sets up through it's gritty, dingy and low-poly aesthetic pulls you in immediately and helps sell the feeling of playing a game of life or death; the small amount of breadcrumbs it gives you for the universe you're in made me think about not only what could be going on narratively but also thematically, such as who the dealer is or what he could represent. The real meat and potatoes of the game comes from the endless double or nothing mode, which can be played for hours on end trying to get a high score or all the achievements possible. With more content updates such as multiplayer coming soon and an ARG going on at the time of writing, for such a cheap price it's an experience more than worth trying and playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like this game. I saw it when it first released and thought it was such an interesting idea, but I just cannot recommend it. The game is way too unfair with the items, especially cigarettes, as they more than often just extend the duration of the game or just act as a free win. It also doesn't help that the dealer is either practically cheating or downright suicidal in how often he'll just dome himself for often no reason. The game is worth the sale price, but after the first play through gets annoying, especially in the 'double or nothing' mode. If the game wants to improve, then I suggest either heavily balancing the items or removing them entirely, as without them was actually quite fun and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting game of odds, memory and dangerous gun practices! It's great! Although, to be honest, I don't think Mike knows how shotguns work:1) Cutting off the barrel and mag-tube doesn't make a shotgun more powerful.2) Pump shotguns don't have ambidextrous ejection-ports.3) Shells open and flare at the ends after being shot....still, amazing despite my OCD attention to meaningless firearm details. Buy it! Play it!

_childDocuments_.review: Buckshot Roulette is exactly what the title suggests, Russian roulette with a shotgun. This game feels like a love letter to Resident Evil 7's DLC '21', and that is a huge compliment. I wouldn't say that it's as in-depth as Resident Evil's offering, but I feel that Buckshot's simplicity allows the player to settle in to its loop faster, which is a positive. Consumable items give some necessary variety, making subsequent attempts more interesting. The dealer can sometimes feel rigged, but I feel like it's normal to feel that way with game's that rely on RNG. I think the biggest complaint that I can levy at Buckshot regards the poor optimization, but I found that it was fortunately still playable. I'd recommend the game at this price point (2.50GBP), and I look forward to seeing what this developer releases in the future.7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful game. It's creative, has an original idea, charming design, and it takes me back to playing Albanian card games.That's because mathematically speaking, the game is structured just like a card game. You can map out the probability of your choices/uses of items, and rely on the same strategies as one would in a good game of cards. Not one of those Las Vegas casino games where it's just rigged probability, but like a proper social card game where having a good sense for calculated risks and remembering probability pay off in terms of skill input.Fantastic game. Easy to learn, difficult to master. Lots of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Some games just have the sauce and this is one of them. This game is gritty urban Inscryption. It is all grime and dirt, from the dealer’s grotesquery to its ecstasy-ridden club-music thumping, endlessly, in the background. Why do my hands shake? Is it the speed? Or is it fear?There’s not a super deep game here and that is by no means a bad thing. It is the dice games played in dirty city alleyways as a spectator sport, played for blood. This is a game of unease and dread and relief. It is a game of risk. It is a game of twitchy, nervous bluster and desperate pulls of a trigger. It is a game where making safe bets gets you killed. And I am all in.

So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he let me borrow his controller. Me and my son then played in turns and I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. _childDocuments_.review: Its a risk-or-reward game that gets you thinking a lot about your items and whats the best strategy to use.  Their tutorial is fun and easy to understand and the dealers difficulty is (in my opinion) balanced.  However, the best feature about this game by far has to be its audio:  the addicting music for the intro alone gets you hooked, the ambient music when you open the first door is fantastic, but the different audios for each level is genius.  Each level has a different audio and gets slightly more intense as the game goes on, giving you that proper "gambling" feeling.  Overall, fantastic game, highly recommend to other players, and cant wait for multiplayer to come soon!
