_childDocuments_.review: Buckshot Roulette is a great minigame for only $3. Optimal play requires combining strategy and probability and it's satisfying. It can be disappointing when you lose before $1 million because the dealer gets better items or RNG and it feels like you made no mistakes, but it makes it even more rewarding when you do reach it. It's a fun game and I'm excited for multiplayer.
_childDocuments_.name: Buckshot Roulette

_childDocuments_.review: Buckshot roulette at its core is a game of luck, probability, and strategy. The game takes the simple premise of Russian Roulette and advances it further as a random number of live shells and blanks are placed in the shotguns barrel by the games opposition - the dealer. In the second round, items are also given to the dealer and player creating another depth of strategy as probability and logical reasoning can be used to discover the best possible choice of move for the player. One of my favourite things about Buckshot Roulette is the music and visual design of the game. An unsettling atmosphere is created through these features as the dirty and grotty look of the surroundings and the chilling background noise of the music create suspense and fear. This combined with the fact that any run can end with bad luck even if the player chooses the perfect move every time makes this game very nerve racking to play especially if you're going for the hardest 2 achievements ("1000K" and "Know When to Quit") as you have to survive 15-18 rounds twice if you want both achievements.The only downside to Buckshot Roulette is that after 8 hours of playtime I feel as if I've accomplished everything that can be done in this game. Perchance I could try to improve the quantity of money I beat the 'Double or Nothing' mode with but I've already cashed out with 1000K so there isn't much point. The first play-through of the game can also be completed very quickly and for a casual player there's maybe only 1-3 hours of game-play. In conclusion, I would still recommend the game despite its short length as it's very cheap to buy and I found it to be a very fun challenge to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Buckshot Roulette

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that's only 3 dollars, it's so addicting. I can't stop playing it. The music is lit and I jam out to it, especially the first round music. The items are fun to use and there's a lot of strategy involved.Normal Mode is really for the tutorial. Once you get past that, Double or Nothing is where the real fun begins. New items to work with and once you start, you'll find yourself playing for hours.Multiplayer would absolutely work great for this game and the developer did confirm that it's coming, so I'm excited for that.

_childDocuments_.review: A memory testing game in roulette form. You need to best guess what bullet will be the next and decide to shoot yourself or your opponent. The key is taking good use of all the tools provided to reveal the bullet, to cuff your opponent, hear fortune teller, all ways at the end making real/hollow bullets not even so you get more than 50% chance to make the choice. _childDocuments_.review: After 8.5 Hours of Russian Roulette With A Shotgun, I must say the game is really fun with really basic repetitive techno music, the game takes place both above and below a night club with an entity the doctors call an "it" and "it" would like to dance with you, the shotgun and shotgun shells, over a highstakes game of life and death, there doesn't really seem to be any real plot and most of the gameplay is basic with really overpowered items that can deadlock or even nearly infinitely duress either you or "the dealer" the 50% chance stakes and watching the AI beat themselves up has been pretty entertaining and i'm happy to finally see this game get multiplayer after 7 months past the full release of the game technically the games been out since December 28th, 2023, so it's Been about 11 Months of waiting in total for multiplayer to finally arrive, playing shotgun roulette multiplayer with other real people from what i've seen should be fun since there will be 32 items at max at one time in play for all rounds, i'm certain there will probably even be item restrictions in the future or item balancing to limit how overpowered items such as handcuffs, and how devastating stacking items together in combination with each other can be with the shotgun, in multiplayer it would probably even seem unfair with how the ruleset of the game is laid out but besides the point it'll be fun to see where the game developer Mike Klubnika takes it from here.Additionally: The Achievements 1000K and Know When To Quit are the 2 hardest achievements of the game requiring you win 18 straight rounds of shotgun roulette minimum without dying once. meaning if either the odds stack against you, or the dealer has handcuffs or you count your blanks wrong, or if your items are bad, all these factors that make it so that you lose even one time and not declare victory 18 times in a row? _childDocuments_.review: Mike has created an unexpected masterpiece. The concept is so simple and so familiar, yet insanely refreshing with that refreshing twist. This may just be my favorite game of the year because you get so hooked onto it.Russian Roulette, but with strategy, that's what this game is about. Will you take the 50/50 chance on yourself or the dealer? Will you take a peek at the current loadout immediately or later? How can you use the items you've obtained to maximise the damage to the dealer? This game has the perfect mixture of luck and strategy.The main campaign is just a taste of what the game will offer you. It truly shines in the mode you unlock after you've beat it the first time (which takes like 15 minutes to do), Double or Nothing. More items, stealing items from the dealer side, switching the polarity of the bullet, literally infinite rounds until you wanna stop, there's so much thought in that specific gamemode that it deserves all the praise this game has. It even has leaderboards, really encouraging you to push for more, and apparently a multiplayer is coming up. I absolutely can't wait to see what it is about. You will most definitely, absolutely love this game, if you're even a little bit into strategy and horror.

_childDocuments_.review: Russian Roulette with a pump-action shotgun in place of the usual revolver? It sounds ludicrous, but it works well. Thankfully, you won't die instantly if you made the wrong decision unlike if you were to try this in real life (don't even think about it, bucko).  The story is minimal, but there's a lot of small details that paint a bigger picture. Especially if you played Mike's compilation game, which paints a bleak world that's even worse than you thought if you accept the idea that they all take place in the same universe.You're constantly thinking about whether you correctly counted the shells in the tube; whether you should take a chance and shoot the dealer, or turn the barrel on yourself. Items are introduced later to spice things up. You could set yourself up for victory, or waste a good setup if you're not careful. The Dealer is kind enough to take it easy on you in normal mode, but he's absolutely ruthless in Double or Nothing.If there's any criticism I have, it's that this kind of game could do well as a multiplayer. But I'm okay with keeping this as a single-player package and playing a knockoff if I wanted to duel a human. Other than that, this game pulls you in again and again to scratch the itch, and nothing else compares to the thrill it gives you. Ready for another round? I know you can't resist playing again...

_childDocuments_.review: Joking aside.... Russian Roulette may be pure luck, but swap the revolver for a pump-action shotgun, mix in live and dud rounds, and add Inscryption-esque items, and you've got Buckshot Roulette. Developed by Mike Klubnika, known for his eerie machinery horror games, Buckshot Roulette offers a more strategic take on a deadly game.In a dingy nightclub's back room, a demonic dealer awaits, loading live and dud shells into a shotgun in random order. Players take turns shooting themselves or their opponent. Dud shots skip the opponent's turn, while live shots take a life, revived by a clunky machine. The round ends when someone loses all lives, aiming for victory by the third round.The second round introduces items like the magnifying glass for peeking at loaded shells, cigarettes for life restoration, and handcuffs for opponent skipping. This adds depth reminiscent of Inscryption.Running the numbers on shell probabilities, deciding when to shoot or use items, Buckshot Roulette offers a simple yet engaging puzzle experience. The tone, weird machinery, and Inscryption-like feel make it compelling.Klubnika's signature weird mechanical devices are present, from the mechanical table to the shotgun itself. Every detail, from the whirring of hidden compartments to entering your name via an elaborate device, adds to the game's atmosphere.His games offer short, intense visits to unexplained places, building mystery and dread in a brief playtime. The contrast between vague mood and detailed devices grounds the experience. Rather than a conjured quill, you tap your name into a device printing letters on a liability waiver, emphasizing interaction with tangible reality in otherworldly settings.

_childDocuments_.review: Buckbuckshot Roulette is a unique and surprisingly fun twist on traditional roulette, combining the suspense of chance with a wild, Western-themed flair. It’s designed for players who enjoy a bit of randomness but also crave more of an interactive experience, reminiscent of a casino game meets shooting gallery.Gameplay and MechanicsThe setup is straightforward but fresh. Rather than betting on numbers alone, players take aim (metaphorically) at various targets, hoping to hit the jackpot while dodging the occasional "buckshot" that can send their winnings plummeting. The pacing is dynamic, and each round holds a sense of thrill as the outcome is revealed, often with unexpected twists.Visuals and SoundThe game leans heavily on its Western vibe with gritty, saloon-inspired visuals and a soundtrack that keeps you engaged, adding to the tension. The design elements are engaging without being overly complicated, allowing you to jump right into the game.ProsInnovative Take on Roulette: Adds layers to traditional roulette, keeping it from getting stale.Western Theme: The sound and graphics work together to create a great thematic experience.Quick Rounds: Ideal for short bursts of play, with rounds that resolve quickly.ConsLearning Curve: The additional mechanics can be a bit confusing initially.Randomness May Frustrate Some Players: Although the randomness is part of the fun, it can be a turn-off for players who prefer strategy over luck.VerdictBuckbuckshot Roulette is a solid, entertaining choice for anyone looking to mix up their casino-style gaming with a bit of shoot-em-up charm. It’s not a typical roulette experience, and that’s where it shines – just enough innovation to add excitement without veering too far into complexity.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun and short ride that is definitely worth its price tag. It has a few twists with the russian roulette gameplay that makes it more strategic but the decisions can still end up feeling a little shallow sometimes. Some items feel very powerful and others feel very weak. The randomness is definitely better than the pure roulette game but the randomness of item distribution makes it sometimes feel like the odds are just bad regardless. The visuals are phenomenal though with a grit and anticipation paired with every action. The most outstanding thing is the implementation of the soundtrack which is both extremely clever and effective at getting your adrenaline going. All in all, if this was some flash game with the exact same gameplay I probably would have quit sooner but the presentation is much higher than it had any right to be. It definitely sold me. If you're just looking to see the end, it's not too long but there is some fun to be had afterwards too. All in all, a good time!

It’s not just about the gameplay; it’s about immersing yourself in an environment that feels alive and exhilarating.And here's the exciting news: a new multiplayer expansion is on the way! I can't wait to see how they expand the chaos with new modes and features. If you love that Blade nightclub energy, Buckshot Roulette is definitely a game you’ll want to dive into!

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay of Buckshot Roulette revolves around a tense game of chance and strategy against a creature known as The Dealer. You gotta decide whether to point the shotgun at themselves or the dealer, with the outcome determined by the randomness of the loaded cartridges. The game includes different helpful items like trump cards, like a magnifying glass to peek at the next round, and cigarettes to heal. These elements add layers of strategy, making each decision critical adding tension.The game has a grungy, industrial visual style that gives it its eerie and unsettling atmosphere. The art style is like other dark, atmospheric games like Inscryption. The environments and set pieces, such as the club at the start and the bathroom you repeatedly wake up in, contribute to the game’s grim nature.10/10PS: the game might seem quite empty with content but a multiplayer mode will soon come :)

Here's a couple of tips that may help:There are also a few hidden achievements, one of which also requires a bit of luck to get (but not NEARLY as much as the two non-hidden achievements mentioned previously). One more tip, for those who don't know: If you want to see the hidden achievements for any game on steam, go to the "Global Achievements" section for it, and you can click on them to reveal them! Some games will purposefully have a non-helpful description on these to make them even more hidden, but Buckshot Roulette isn't one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Buckshot Roulette is not only a high-score chaser indie game, but with its newest multiplayer update it joins as another game in the "gamble your life with friends" genre. And while it has a lot of merit thanks to being so cheap & simple but fun, it has some really questionable issues. But first, let's talk about the positives.The most obvious thing anyone can mention about this game is its art direction and atmosphere. It's as bizarre as it's iconic. A weird-looking dude with only hands and a head, located on the top floor, next to an empty party, is an intriguing setting. The style really sets the mood with all its different odd-looking animations and the tidbits of lore you can find here and there. I love how stylized it is and how nothing is truly questioned about it, because there is no time when you're playing with your life.A gun is placed in the middle, with a varying amount of blanks and live rounds. They reload it in an unknown order, with the whole thing being about either shooting yourself or the opponent. Shooting yourself results in you either losing one of your set amount of charges to bring you back to life, but if you shoot a blank, you get another shot with a higher chance to make the dealer lose a charge. Of course, if you decide to shoot the dealer, your turn immediately ends, it doesn't matter if it's a blank or not. This simple loop continues until the gun is empty and has to be reloaded with a new set of blanks and live ammunition, or 'til the dealer dies, and you can move on to the next round. It makes for a fairly simple but addicting high-score hunt, trying to see how far you get by not only sheer luck but also by making educated guesses based on the amount of bullets in the gun.Not only that, but to really complete the mix of luck and skill in this game, you also get items after each reload. These vary from doing double damage, skipping a bullet, to even getting a look inside the gun. The way you use your items is just as important, creating a sort of skill ceiling that isn't entirely based on how much luck you have, but also on how well you use your items. It's basically a constant risk-reward system, with you being the factor for how risky you want to play. Do you want to use most of your items? Do you want to make sure you get a clean shot? Or are you just trying to stall to potentially get a healing item for the next reload? There are so many strategies, making it infinitely replayable.As great as the replayability is, the whole process of starting a new run is too long-winded. Having to load in, go through two doors, type your name with a mouse, and finally play doesn't sound like much, but it hurts a game based on replayability when you constantly see 30 seconds of the same animations with no immediate replay button.Another issue you could point out is the lack of any difficulty sliders or customization for the usual rounds, but I feel like it may be intentional to keep the high-score-chasing aspect simple.When it comes to  multiplayer, the lack of customization definitely becomes an issue, though.I held off writing a review because I was really interested in how this mode would turn out, and unfortunately, it's as bare-bones as it can get. You create a lobby with 2–4 people and try to shoot your friends for money. There are some small adjustments, like everyone getting their own masked floating head, and some items being removed or added to make the game flow smoother, but that's unfortunately about it. As much fun as Buckshot Roulette can be, the multiplayer update leaves a lot to be desired because you can't change a lot about it, resulting in it becoming really stale after a bit. For some reason, the game decided against giving the player a limited free camera view, meaning you can't really do silly head movements with your friends while staring down the barrel like in a similar game, Liar's Bar, but the bigger nuisance is that you can only look at the table where all the information is located when it's your turn, meaning you can't plan ahead or look for other viable strategies while it isn't your turn.The worst thing about this mode is the sheer lack of customization. You could get a lot of mileage out of simply adding more options to the multiplayer, by letting players choose their masks or by adding different settings with adjustable sliders. Stuff like item intensity, banning certain items, item usage per round, and the amount of charges are all things that inherently change the way you play the game, and for some reason they aren't present. It's really unfortunate how lacking and uninteresting Buckshot's multiplayer is, because it can be so much more than just going into a lobby and playing by the same rules every single time.All in all, Buckshot has a great gameplay loop, but the lack of a simple skip button and the tacky multiplayer really do it no justice. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Buckshot Roulette is a very flavourful take on the mainstream russian roulette-type game. It's just you, the dealer, and a shotgun- gambling to the death to see who wins. The game is divided into 3 rounds. Each round, you and the dealer are given a set amount of lives and take turns shooting each other. The gun has a random number of blank rounds and live rounds randomly inserted inside. Every turn, you can either shoot the dealer, or yourself. If you shoot yourself and it's an empty round, you skip the dealer's turn. If it's live, you shoot yourself and lose a life.. You win the game by winning all 3 rounds. To make matters more interesting, both players are given a random assortment of items throughout each round that can drastically manipulate the outcome of the game for you and the dealer, such as being able to skip the next shotgun round, doubling the damage of the next round, and seeing the next shotgun round. These items can be used in tandem with each other and provide endless replayability as well as giving an unexpectedly complex strategy to a predominantly luck-based game! If used correctly, these items can be used to make the gamble as safe as possible every single round, and you will still be pulling that trigger at the dealer's head and at your own... Every game is completely different, and will never be the same as the one before. Before you know it, you'll be doing maths in your to see which action gives you the best chance at winning, which items synergize the best to sway the odds in your favour the most, and overall, minimize the risk of the game as much as humanly possible to outsmart, AND outlive the dealer! New items have recently been added to the game to spice things up, and the developer has officially announced the workings of 2-player multiplayer, so soon, you can risk your life with a dear friend.For an extremely humble price of $3, this game is more than worth the purchase. You're practically robbing them!

_childDocuments_.review: An adrenaline pumping game where we take on the role of some random person down on their luck ready to risk it all. Step into a dark nightclub music blaring and get ready to sign over your life to the dealer. The main enemy of the whole game you fight against in a battle of luck and skill in order to make off with some good cash. At first you notice the game can be unforgiving in it's RNG sometimes you may lose 3-4 times in a row, but once you get to receiving items the whole game changes. Items let you do anything from checking if the round is live and ejecting the current shell. This really spices the game up and ups all the risk for both sides as the dealer gets these items as well and they are handed out at random. One very neat piece of lore was that when drawing items you have a chance to draw another persons liability waiver it was gods. We can assume that in this world god has sold his domain to the dealer and had lost and is now dead. Hence people constantly partying and gambling their lives for seemingly no good reason. One strong point the game has going for itself is a core mechanic its RNG. What makes the game so thrilling is never truly knowing what can happen without the use of items. Some times the dealer will end up shooting himself pretty much giving you the round. For its price you can get a good amount of play time and I think Buckshot doesn't overstay its welcome. With a recent update double or nothing you can now risk it for twice as much. Letting you double your winnings each time you make it through the ringer. The game itself is a thrill to play and brought a very unique twist on a well known all be it deadly game. 7/10Follow my curator page for more critical game reviews!

One side, You and the other side the dealer.- The Dealer will always the one perform reload with and I quote "Unknown sequences" reloading between blank buckshot and live buckshot.- The game will always let you take the first call. Its simple, You point the gun to the dealer and pull the trigger or you point the gun at your own face and pull the trigger.- You and Dealer each start the round with "Life point" or "Defib unit" Getting LIve round in the face and both party losing Life point hitting zero and that round end.- But don't worry, If you are manage to enter 2nd round. The game will kick up some notch and introducing you to the item. You and dealer get to pick equally amount for each round but the variation of item will be different. These item are to be used both on You and Dealer and if you play your item right. The game will turn from a game of chance into a strategy game where you will utilize the given items to favor your chance on winning the game.- It doesn't matter even if you won 2 round before, Each round are its own game, If you get to the last round and manage to win, You are still a winner (With less money to pocketing with)- Currently there are no actual system implementing the use of money or consequence from winning but I've got a feeling if this game steering into the right direction. It could be the next "Inscryption"And not to mention how dirt cheap this thing is right now. So grab the game and enjoy your time feeling like an adrenaline Junky while bobbing your head around with Techno Punk music.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay pulled me in. Seemed really fun.Brief DescriptionYou probably do not need it, because Tik Tok exists (for now at least), but this game is a really interesting roulette game with all sorts of items to make it fun and unique. Basically, if you want to be literal, you, a kind individual, cultured even, wake up in a bathroom in a club. You walk out onto the catwalk with the music blaring. You head inside this door and you are greeted by a very charming round young man with the teeth of a god and the nose of an Italian. He makes you sign a waiver to give up your rights to legal action in the case you die from this roulette game. Some refer to it as something called "Buckshot Roulette".To beat the game, you have to kill/beat the guy three (I believe, I forget) times and then you win.Pros-Polished. Not glitchy at all.-Fun gameplay! Very interesting neat little strategy game that does not take too long. Good to kill time. The items really spice things up and they introduce more after you beat the game.-Amazing art style. Gives creepy horror feels. Best part of the game aside from gameplay.-They have a whole double or nothing system and it tracks your profits. So there is replay value to some extent even after beating the game.Cons-Not a ton of content, but I expect more updates in the future.-Gameplay can get a little monotonous after a bit. Would not play long sessions of this, but I do not really thing you can help that-- and if you can its not a big deal its not like you need to play a game for a long time to enjoy it or for it to be good.Yeah, for the price I definitely recommend it and would play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: As a single-player experience, Buckshot Roulette is great, but ''it is ten times more enjoyable with friends in multiplayer'' i thought since the game came out. The multiplayer beta was released two days ago, and i have some suggestions for the developers.Firstly, since it's still in beta, a few of the animations are understandably bit off; they could use some smoothing out. Additionally, i think the game would benefit from a wider selection of items, and expired medicine also should be integrated to the multiplayer mode to give players more options. There should also be a feature allowing players to customize their health per round, adding a new layer of strategy.I've only spent around two and a half hours in multiplayer so far, but I've noticed that round order in the magazine could use some variation. Currently, it's maximal load is i suppose 6, either 4 live-2 blank or 4 blank-2 live, even though the magazine appears to have 10-round capacity. Also the sequences of live and blank rounds should be more randomized, as I've noticed that rounds of the same type often appear next to each other.That said, i don't need to go on about how fantastic the music and visuals are. Outstanding. Overall, i wanted to focus on a few areas that could use some polish. I definitely recommend blasting your friends heads in those 50/50 situations. Super fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Great short and simple game. Bumping soundtrack, nice grimy aesthetic, and very effective sound design all combine for a twist on russian roulette that will still make you wince when the gun is pointed at you. Like the real thing (I imagine) it's mostly luck-based but there's a decent space for skill in counting and tracking live vs blank shells as well as using items effectively to manipulate the odds. Once you beat it once you unlock an endless mode with a few new items and the aim is simply for high scores. But if you love the rush of gambling, with a little room for skill, and would rather not do it with your own life than this is the game for you! Also as of right now it's only player vs computer but the dev has promised PVP in the future and that should be really fun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is worth playing, if you like games where it's intense and you need to think a lot then this may be for you. This is basically Russian Roulette. You have a shotgun on the table, you have an opponent, you have 2 types off bullets that is a live or a blank (Live = Bullet with gunpower | Blank = Self-explanatory, nothing is inside). _childDocuments_.review: I have really been looking forward to play this, and decided to wait for the Steam release. This has two core game-modes: kicking down the door mode, and kicking down the door after getting high off pills. The first, being the core game mode, is really fun! The constant strategizing with the randomly distributed items is a great addition to the Russian Roulette gameplay (a not great game to play). I love constantly fighting with my own head over whether or not I shoot myself, which leads me to blow my head off (of course). I also really really enjoyed the latter mode, which is named 'Double or Nothing'. Having extra items, which are not present in the core game mode, makes it even more fun to strategize and makes the game a lot more interesting (pro tip: do not EVER take the medicine, it never works for you or the dealer). It makes the game have even more replay value, with the many different scenarios that are possible with different combinations of items. Oh also, it feels so good pulling off some big brain ♥♥♥♥ with the items.Was worth the wait and is worth getting! (especially since it has a launch sale get this game please)

_childDocuments_.review: Buckshot Roulette is a short dark Russian roulette game that aims to try to mess up with your opponent as much as possible while pushing your luck to the limit to win rounds in the most obnoxious way possible. The game is easy to learn and captivates the player's attention with the raw emotion of...gambling. Yeah, that's right! Gambling! But we gamble our lives, with shotgun shells. Having one real round in the chamber with two fake ones makes one heart pound when you go for that risky "I am gonna believe this round is real" and you shoot the dealer only to see that it was indeed a real bullet, giving huge satisfaction when making high-risk play. I like the items in the game as they add a "try to read your opponent's next move" layer to it and the possibility to create combos. The goal is to try to set up each turn and round maximizing your damage while reducing your opponent's moves.The only thing the game is lacking is multiplayer, which it needs BADLY because this is such an amazing little game that could get a lot of replayability when facing human foes. A single run can last from 30 minutes to 1 hour and the Double or Nothing mode adds a lot of new items to the mix with more challenging gameplay, so there is still some replayability even when it is only single-player. For 2,99 you cannot go wrong with this game that is bound to entertain you for a while!Note: In the future, the dev might add multiplayer!If you enjoy and find the review helpful, please follow my curator!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly love this game! I saw a ton of streamers play it and wanted to give it a shot, no pun intended, myself. I beat the game on my first try and beat the "double or nothing" mode on my first try as well. I will say that even though I beat it quickly and albeit really lucky, this game is awesome at replayability! I could see where you could do challenges with your friends or even want to strive for all the achievements. This game can be pretty difficult, but the abilities make it slightly easier. It really just depends how you play your cards. Overall, super fun game that I plan to come back to in the future and I would love to even see some lore added to this game as well!

_childDocuments_.review: Buckshot Roulette: A Nail-Biting Horror Experience!Step into the eerie world of 'Buckshot Roulette,' a short indie tabletop horror game that's as gripping as it is chilling. Developed by Mike Klubnika and published on itch.io, this game plunges players into a realm of gritty industrial visuals, setting it apart from the rustic charm of similar titles like Inscryption.Using the Godot game engine, Klubnika masterfully crafts an atmosphere of dread and suspense, enhanced by his own haunting soundtrack. Released on Steam by Critical Reflex, 'Buckshot Roulette' quickly gained traction, lauded for its strategic gameplay and high replayability.In this twisted game of chance, every decision could be your last as you navigate through its sinister landscapes. With its popularity soaring and sales hitting the million mark in just two weeks, 'Buckshot Roulette' is a must-play for horror aficionados seeking an adrenaline-fueled experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Russian Roullette with a shotgun and drugs and stuff to add random spice to the game. My favorite combo is inverter magnifying glass and saw. Glass lets you see the next round in the chamber. Inverter let's you turn a blank into a live round. And saw doubles the damage. This is just one combo that exists and it's a blast and a thrill trying to reach new high scores.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wondered what it would be like to try playing Russian roulette with a shotgun? Well, that's Buckshot Roulette in a nutshell - a game where you have to outwit (and out-luck) a bizarre creature in a back-room game of shotgun roulette, where the stakes are a briefcase full of money or a slug to the head.The first run acts as a tutorial. At the beginning of each round, the creature loads the shotgun with a random number of live and blank shells. It's up to you to try and follow the number of remaining shells of each kind, and on your turn, decide if you want to fire at your opponent or yourself.Once you have the basics down, the game introduces items you can use to help your chances. These include things like a magnifying glass that lets you see the current shell or a pack of cigarettes that restores lost health.After you complete the first run, you unlock the endless mode, where you can keep betting double-or-nothing for as long as you manage to survive.And… that's pretty much it? Once you master the basics - namely, counting the live and blank shots left in the shotgun and using your items strategically - the only thing left is to try out the endless mode and see how many points you can rack up on the leaderboard.With this in mind, I think Buckshot Roulette works better as an experience rather than a game. Although a short one (you can basically see everything the game has to offer in about 30 minutes to an hour), it's very interesting and atmospheric, and in my mind well worth the relatively low asking price.And if you're a completionist, there's always the leaderboard.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR at the bottomNow you may think my lack of playtime at the time of reviewing this game would discredit my opinion, but that's the thing, I cleared the story once and got turned into Swiss cheese in Double or Nothing twice (RIP Smelly and Cargo). This is a very short and small game, and for $3, I think it's perfect like that.To start, the positives.The game's art style is perfect. It feels very retro and indie, while still feeling well polished and expertly made. It's clear the developer knew exactly what he wanted and what his vision was for this game.The story also isn't delved into much. In an age of Bendy's FNAF's Poppy Playtime's whatever, over-explained lore utterly ruining the scary factor of a game has become commonplace. But nothing is answered here. What is the Dealer? How do some of these items work? Where are you (well a club but where is the club?) There's a lot of questions which adds to the uneasy atmosphere. If you liked Inscription, you'd love this game.The challenge varies. If you want a challenging but mostly easy-going experience, play the story. If you want The Dealer to make you into his newest wallpaper fashion choice at the slightest mistake, Double or Nothing. Above everything, this game is fair. If you won fair and square, The Dealer takes it and loses. If you messed up with your strategy or missed something, he will punish you for it. Same with the luck. Luck and The Dealer's AI seems to favor you in the story, but Double or Nothing it up and he stops holding your hand, that's what the handcuffs are for.The luck and by proxy, The Dealer. Given this game is literally Russian roulette but with a damn shotgun and weird otherworldly items like beer, you'd think The Dealer would pull some kind of trick to win, right? But no, he's probably one of the most honest antagonists you would find in media. He plays the game fairly and if luck decides it's his turn to take a wallop, he'll get hit. Heck, I won my first story playthrough by RNG deciding he wasn't going to win this time. Meanwhile in Double or Nothing, if he sees a win condition, he will take it and you will not see it coming until it starts and you have to watch as he slowly takes your life.THE MULTIPLAYERWith multiplayer out, the game has utterly transformed into a truly amazing game. The players are funny, the game's very casual-focused, the only downside I can think of is that if the host disconnects the game ends. But I promise it's worth it. Join the Discord, find a game with some guys in a VC, and have a hilarious blast messing around and having fun.The Multiplayer sells the game by itself. It's that good.Now, for the negatives.Honestly, I don't have any true negatives for this game. So instead here's some things that might be a turn off for you.The music. More a nitpick than anything, the music is repetitive and just a few notes. But it mostly is not present except for scant moments like the opening or during certain item uses. If you wan music in the background, you're gonna have to open YouTube or whatever and put some on yourself.Luck. Where I find positive, you may find negative. In the end of the day, no matter how smart you are with items and calling bluffs, this game will eventually ask you to flip a coin or roll a dice. And if you're not a fan of your defeat sometimes being out of your control, this game is not for you.TL;DR, Buckshot Roulette is a super short, cheap, and fun experience. It's very honest and to the point. I don't think it'd ever hurt to buy it even if it isn't for you in the end.Only thing keeping this from a 10/10 is that it's not really a legendary experience that I'll remember for a long time, but frankly that's not what it wants to be, so I can't detriment it for that. It's kinda just how my review scores work. I certainly recommend Buckshot Roulette.9/10

Buckshot Roulette is a game where you wake up in a disgusting cruddy bathroom in a nightclub, kick down a door to hear cool retro music, and then kick down another door to sign a waiver to play Roulette with a shotgun against none other than  himself. The Dealer is a fair player that plays by the rules and doesn't try to cheat or manipulate you in any way. He respects you and his maniacal game he so maliciously envisioned and constructed for our amusement. This game involves strategy, suspense, and pure luck to survive the night and head back to society in a very hurt and traumatized state while needing plastic surgery for your face. For the little amount of money this game charges, this game has a surprisingly good gameplay loop with tons of replayability, especially since a "double or nothing" feature was implemented into the game recently along with new items that won't be mentioned here. The AI in this game can either be smart by completely outplaying you in interesting ways or it could end up being stupid by shooting itself in the face knowing there were only live rounds in the shotgun. _childDocuments_.review: Buckshot Roulette is a very good example of taking a pretty simple premise and executing it in a fun, deceptively strategic way.The story: You start off in the bathroom of a club. Kick the door open to reveal you are on the top catwalk. Music and lights suggest the dancing below. A man leans against the railing smoking a cigarette. And there is a door in front of you. Open that door to find a grungy room with a green table marked with some grids. Seated across from you is a man? robot? demon?--whatever it is, it's got a creepy mask on and doesn't permanently die no matter how much buckshot you shoot it with. First you have to sign a General Liability Waiver (aka, this is your way of entering your name.) Then the game begins.The premise of the game is simple. The dealer shows you how many rounds of each type of buckshot you are playing with this load (it's random, although you generally start with 2 or 3 rounds and play with more as time goes on, capping at 8 rounds). Red means it's a live round; blue means blank. The dealer then puts the shells in a random order into the shotgun (though the dealer doesn't see the order it's putting them in either). A screen to your right displays a number of lightning bolts for the dealer and the player. A buckshot blast in this game, even to the face at point blank, isn't anything a little zap with the defibrillator won't fix. These are charges, which act as your lives. If you are shot, one charge is removed, and then it makes a check. If you still have at least one charge remaining, you'll be brought back to life with the defibrillator. If you don't, it's game over. The dealer is nice enough to give you one last zap to bring you back to life before booting you out of the game in the first two rounds, but in the third, you die permanently if you run out of charges. The dealer also has charges, but when it runs out, it is not game over, but the game advances to the next round.Here's where the key choice of each turn is: do you shoot yourself, or the dealer? Why would you shoot yourself? That sounds dumb, but shooting yourself with a blank skips your opponent's turn, giving you another shot. Managing the dealer's turns is a priority in this game. If you're good at remembering how many of each type of round are in play at any given moment, you can play the odds in your favor.If all the shots are expended and both players are still alive, then the shotgun is reloaded with a new random set of rounds and you start play again. If you win 3 game rounds against the dealer, you win a briefcase of roughly $70,000 in cash and you drive away (you even get to keep the shotgun!) and the game is over. If you're ready for a more advanced version, take the pills in the bathroom before opening the door, which activates Double or Nothing mode. In this mode, there's an expanded item list and every 3 rounds you win, you're given the choice of taking your money and ending your run or playing Double or Nothing with another game for more money.Now, the REAL genius of the game is in the items. In the second round in normal mode (or every round in Double or Nothing), you and the dealer are each given a random set of items to help you manipulate the odds and turn this educated guessing into real strategic gameplay. You can hold up to 8 items at once, and they carry over between reloads (though not between game rounds). You can play as many as you would like in a turn, with a few caveats (like not being able to handcuff an already handcuffed opponent or use adrenaline to steal an opponent's adrenaline). Every item is single use, and the dealer plays them with the same rules. Every time the shotgun is reloaded, you get some more items to add to your inventory. (Beware that if you fill all your slots, there is no trading; you simply lose any other items you draw that reload, so it isn't a good idea to hoard a bunch of items.)

_childDocuments_.review: Buckshot Roulette is a surprising gem that perfectly captures the thrill of games like Hunt: Showdown. What starts as a simple game with an unusual name quickly reveals itself to be an adrenaline-fueled adventure that keeps you coming back for more.The gameplay is straightforward yet effective. You dive into a risky endeavor where you can either win big or lose it all. This risk rewards each step with an intense surge of tension. The atmosphere is dense and dark, further intensifying the suspense.What particularly impressed me is the replayability. Every round is unique, offering a new challenge. You can never be sure what will happen next, adding to the allure of the game. The ability to earn points and level up encourages you to keep coming back to try your luck.Overall, Buckshot Roulette is an exhilarating game that captivated me from the get-go. It's a must-play for anyone who loves the thrill and enjoys embarking on an adventure. I can't wait to dive back in and see what the game has in store for me next.

_childDocuments_.review: If you play Buckshot Roulette just to beat the "story", then it will take about 20-50 minutes. This will be half an hour to an hour of mildly interesting gameplay that basically amounts to gambling. Nothing scary in this "horror" game, but the concept is surreal and the visuals and sound design are pretty great.If you try to get every achievement in Buckshot Roulette the rest of your journey will be wrought with disgusting levels of RNG in the "double or nothing" mode, where you will routinely get unwinnable rounds or just ♥♥♥♥ luck that will randomly kill you after a 30 minute run where you almost got to the 1.000.000$ required for the two godawful "1000K" achievements. If you're playing this game for a fun horror experience, don't, it's not scary, mostly middling quality wise and way too short. If you're buying it for achievement hunting–again–don't, instead of way too short, it's way too padded and RNG-based, it's literally just gambling.Games like this are where art goes to die and braindead entertainment takes its root. If you want a game like this, that has some actual substance to it (though unfortunately retains some of this game's worse qualities, too, especially in its mediocre Roguelite mode; so be mindful of that) then buy Daniel Mullins' "Inscryption".

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is short, as you can beat it in less than 30 or 20 minutes if you can already figure out how the game works from the start and you're used to playing games about manipulating probability chances.Many consider the base game to just be the tutorial though. The AI is terrible in the base game. After you beat the base game though, you unlock the game's endless mode, which has way more strategy involved thanks to the addition of new features, and the AI is way smarter, but also way more predictable. The only real "goal" for that is the game's achievements, which makes that part terrible since that would mean having to play the endless mode without losing a single round to reach a certain win streak. The odds to win rounds are usually in your favor, mainly thanks to the opponent's AI being predictable, but all it takes is one round of bad luck before having to completely restart it.At its core, the game is simply about picking the option with the best odds of success, as no matter how optimal your plays are, it all comes down to luck at the very end, as even with a 75% chance of winning, you can still get screwed over by that 25%.It's a massively glorified dice roll for less than 5 bucks. Why does beer allow you to eject shells? Why does smoking actually heal you? Why does sawing off the barrel of a shotgun do more damage to someone? It doesn't matter, the game's fun and cool looking.

I learned to like this kind of rustic atmosphere after playing Iron Lung. Buckshot Roulette has a fun spin on the good old Russian Roulette with a mysterious flying overcooked head. You really want to know what's the deal with the Dealer since You can do a single playthrough in pretty much just 20 mins like I did. There is however an "Double or nothing"-mode which gives the game some replayability if that's something you care about. I can recommend Buckshot Roulette just for the experience alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright.  is, well, a bit off center, and you've got to be a bit disturbed to enjoy this game.  :)It's a very simple premise. You are meeting up with what seems to be a demonic host (whose name is apparently Josh. LMAO) in a nightclub to play some Russian Roulette....with a shotgun, and an alternate set of rules. Winner takes all...the cash. The cash being actually meaningless outside of being the basis for the game's leaderboard (of which there is one), but at least you know you're leaving with something, lol. You begin in a disgusting bathroom, walk onto a walkway overlooking a grimy dance club, and finally enter the game room itself, which is equally dank and disturbing. You sign a waiver (lol) and the match begins.In this version of Russian Roulette, you can choose to shoot yourself or the host. You just have to decide if you believe the next shell is a blank or not. Each of you begins with a random but equal amount of health. One live round equals one health point. After taking a shot, you are defibrillated back into the action until your health is completely gone, after which you wake up in a grimy bathroom to start the process over. If you win, you begin the next round. Each match features three rounds. Additionally, you can unlock a 'double or nothing' phase, wherein after winning, you can choose to take your winnings or try your luck again for double the cash (points). And you can continue to decide to double or nothing until you eventually lose or cash out. Double or Nothing is engaged at the beginning of the game once unlocked by taking 'QuayLudes' btw.Each round features the shotgun with a randomly determined amount of live and blank shells which are revealed before the shotgun is loaded by the host. Neither of you know which order the shells are loaded. You are then given an also randomly determined amount of items which you can use on your turn to boost damage, heal, remove shells, determine which shell is next, and so on. You have eight slots that can be filled with items, and the RNG selection of items happens every time the shotgun needs to be reloaded (and each reload goes through the same random shell reveal process). You might get to grab two items, you might get to grab six items. Who knows? You and the host each get the same number of selections. Each item has two quick animations enabled for them. One is your animation, one is Josh's animation.Your only real objective is to survive, and to advance up the leaderboard, while also of course knocking out some achievements. If you are a disturbed individual, this is the game for you, lol. It definitely earns the $2.99 price tag, and I'd say this fits nicely into the presentation of horror you might expect from a Dread Collection or Szymanski-verse or some such.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, listen here, folks. Imagine you’re sitting in a dimly lit, smoky room with a guy who's half in the bag, flicking ash off his cigarette like it's going out of style. _childDocuments_.review: An incredibly clever little 1v1 game of probability and resource management. The art direction is wonderfully creepy and moody, the music is a delightfully moody pulsing club suite, and the gameplay is simple but shockingly stressful. _childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy math or games of odds, this is one for you. Strangely addictive, you'll find yourself constantly weighing your odds on where to pull the trigger as you use a variety of items to change the play condition: peek and see what round is loaded, call someone from the future to learn the status of a future round, heal yourself, use items to either eject a round or change it to/from a live round, and more. This is a game of math dressed up in a fun skin to trick you into not caring that it's math. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: After twelve hours of being missing after the initial search warrant went out, the police finally found my body and my stacks of cash I got from playing buckshot roulette. I'm finally free, but I now have tremors from my hands, a jacked up medical fee, and I'm also being sent to therapy because I keep getting traumatic flashbacks from medical equipment, loud noises (I hate the 4th of July even more now), and friendly little guys.Anyways, for people apprehensive about whether this version is better than the original; there's some bugs, which is granted for releases. Just stay on top of the bug tracker and read the thread just in case something's been solved already. From my understanding, Mike is the main dev and he's the only one looking at it, so for a fairly small game I don't want to be too harsh on the guy. I also think that, compared to the original, this has far more replay value.The new items added in this release are so fun. My favorite ties between the burner phone (very helpful), the inverter (solely because the dealer has a funny animation for it), and the expired medicine (also because the dealer has a funny animation for it). I'm also a big fan of the double or nothing mode, which is essentially just a randomizer gauntlet.The new items don't show up in the original campaign, only in double or nothing, which makes sense but also I kinda wish that there was, like, an extra-hard-mode mode with the items. By far the ACTUAL best item is adrenaline, which is super powerful in your hands but also extremely harmful if used by the dealer, which is a good balance to have. It always makes me cry-laugh when he steals my cigarettes.I'll probably return to this when the multiplayer releases. For a game that is $3 (and less at the time of writing), it is well worth its price and the gambling addiction I have thanks to it.

_childDocuments_.review: This dev clearly had a great idea and executed it flawlessly.This game is challenging but not hard. Unlike other games like this, the dealer doesn't cheat. As long as you keep track of how many live and dud rounds are in the gun and plan your moves ahead, you will win. There are RNG elements but they can be negated with enough skill.The dev seems to be adding every feature people want. Multiplayer, more story, online leaderboards. This game is excellent value for the price, one of the few Steam games I'd say might even be underpriced.==============================================================Edit 11/05/24:I'm very disappointed to see that the dev locked the much anticipated multiplayer mode behind Discord. I don't have a Discord account and I'm not making one just for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Though it is very fun, There are two achievements for reaching a million score in  mode. One for cashing out, and one for losing it all. If you go for these achievements, get ready for a several-hour-long exercise in tedium and frustration.However, I will still recommend this game as it's a pretty fun time when playing casually. If you don't care about achievements, definitely pick this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, and perfectly demonstrates the sad addiction of gambling and why it isn't worth it.  Everything from the items you can use to the shotgun shells being shown are metaphors of all the 'methods/ numbers' people use to get an 'advantage' of the house or Powerball.  At the end of the day you still don't know what happens next or 4 turns in, and that edge you had at the beginning is gone instantly.  Then to top it all off if you win, you just get ~30k. He 100% knows the order of the rounds (why else would he not look at the shotgun when he breaks the magnifying glass, or when he answers the cellphone he only holds it to his head for a couple of seconds before tossing it in a drawer?) and yet will shoot himself as if he didn't know, he doesn't complain when you use stuff on his side of the table nor does he protest when you handcuff him.  He gives you a fair chance to win, and he doesn't force you to play till you sign the waiver.  The game is $3 and is well worth the price, it might be short but it is certainly better than alot of games that are asking $70+.

_childDocuments_.review:
BUCKSHOT ROULETTE is a tabletop horror game that attempts to re-design the infamous game of Russian Roulette, replacing the traditional revolver with a proper 12-gauge pump-action shotgun. This extra firepower, and more importantly the different mechanics in handling a shotgun compared to a revolver, offers a fresh take on the classic and deadly game of chance.

The game takes place at the top of an underground nightclub, where the metal railings tremble to the pulse of long lost drum machines. A crooked AI dealer is waiting for you. Will you meet them?
